description:
Compliance made SME-asy: Employment basics with ATH Consulting, Are you confident in navigating the complexities of employment relationships in today’s ever-changing workplace? Join us for a comprehensive workshop designed for managers, employers, and business owners who want to deepen their understanding of employment fundamentals and people management best practices.
What You’ll Learn:
Foundations of Employment Relationships:
Explore the essential components that shape every employment relationship, including relevant legislation, terms and conditions, and the pivotal role of workplace policies and procedures.
Understanding Employment Types:
Distinguish between permanent, full-time, casual, and seasonal roles, and learn how each type impacts your obligations and management strategies.
Employment Legislation Essentials:
Get a practical overview of the 10 key employment laws that influence your workplace, ensuring you stay compliant and informed.
Good Faith and Agreements:
Discover the importance of acting in good faith and the differences between Individual Employment Agreements (IEA) and Collective Employment Agreements (CEA), including mandatory clauses and recommended “nice to have” terms.
Managing Change:
Learn best practices for handling variations to employment agreements and implementing effective workplace policies and procedures.
People Management Mastery:
Gain insights into the employee lifecycle, building a strong employment brand, and managing common workplace issues such as performance improvement plans (PiP), disciplinary processes, attendance, and health and wellbeing.
Leadership and Succession:
Identify the hallmarks of poor leadership and develop strategies for effective succession planning to future-proof your team.
Support Systems:
Know where to get help—learn when to trust your gut, when to rely on facts, and how to access the right support at the right time.
This workshop is your opportunity to build confidence, reduce risk, and enhance your leadership toolkit. Whether you’re new to managing people or looking to refresh your knowledge, you’ll leave with practical insights and actionable strategies for every stage of the employment relationship.
Don’t miss this chance to strengthen your employment management skills and connect with peers facing similar challenges. Register now and take the next step toward becoming a more effective, knowledgeable, and resilient leader.

Where: Carterton Community Courthouse (next to Events Centre) Holloway Street, Carterton

description:
Creative Careers Evening at Massey Wellington, Overview
Hear from graduates across our Screen Arts, Design, Commercial Music and Fine Arts programmes who are a few years into their careers.
What can you do with a creative degree?
College of Creative Arts | Toi Rauwhārangi graduates go on to build incredibly varied and inspiring careers across the creative industries and beyond. While creative study is sometimes questioned for its “employability”, the reality is that Aotearoa New Zealand’s arts and creative sector contributes $17.5 billion to GDP and makes up 4.2% of the total economy.
So where do our Screen Arts, Commercial Music, Design and Fine Arts graduates really end up?
Join us for a candid panel with recent graduates from Massey University’s College of Creative Arts | Toi Rauwhārangi and hear the real story of life after study: how they found work, what that transition looked like, and how they’re using what they learned in the real world. From building creative businesses and freelance careers to working in agencies, education, the public sector, and creative roles, our graduates are forging all kinds of futures.
You’ll hear from people working as:
artists and makers
designers and screen creatives
musicians and creative entrepreneurs
freelancers, contractors and sole traders
business owners and educators
creatives working both inside and outside the traditional creative industries
They’ll share the opportunities, connections and experiences that shaped their journey during study and beyond — including the realities of getting started in today’s economy.
We’ve scheduled this event for the evening before Open Day so students and whānau can attend together, especially if daytime commitments or travel make it harder to join us during the day. If you’re visiting from out of town, it’s also a great way to make the most of your time in Wellington.
And if you want even more of the inside scoop on studying at Massey, check out All Access — our student-run YouTube channel, where current students share what life at Toi Rauwhārangi is really like. https://www.youtube.com/@AllAccessMCA

description: Customer Service Excellence, A fantastic one-day course to get staff communicating professionally and confidently with customers. Keep your customers coming back by empowering staff with core communication and customer service skills along with a ‘can do attitude’. For the better part of every day, we are communicating to and with others. This workshop will equip participants with the skills and techniques required to transform how you manage relationships with customers, colleagues and stakeholders. Have you ever thought about how you come across to others and what it’s like to be on the receiving end of you? This workshop will help participants to understand the different methods of communication. Whether it’s the speech you deliver to your customers and work colleagues, the level of attention you give your spouse when they are talking to you, or the look that you give to the cat, it all means something! Each and every one of us serves customers, whether we realise it or not. Maybe you’re in a frontline position serving the people who buy your products. "Highly recommend."
"Inspiring."
"An amazing experience."

Founded on the research of Dr. Brené Brown, Dare to Lead™ is an empirically based courage-building programme, delivered by Boma New Zealand CEO and Certified Dare to Lead™ Facilitator Kaila Colbin.
Brené has spent two decades studying shame and more than seven years specifically looking at leadership. description:
Dealing With Difficult People & Situations, Transform conflict and difficult situations with co-workers and customers into opportunities by equipping your staff with the skills and techniques required to manage these situations with confidence, professionalism, and pride. Learn ways to resolve conflict with customers and co workers, influence successful outcomes and develop a peaceful workplace. We have all experienced the stress that comes from having unresolved conflicts with our customers and co-workers. Conflicts that are ignored or resolved poorly don’t go away, they cause people to feel resentful and to avoid each other. The effects on the business are a loss of productivity, turnover, and absenteeism. Wherever two or more people come together, there is bound to be conflict. This workshop will give participants a six-step process that they can use and modify to resolve conflicts of any size.

Participants will also learn crucial conflict resolution skills, including dealing with anger and using the Agreement Frame. Key Learning Outcomes: - Transform conflict into opportunity - Develop constructive strategies for dealing with difficult behaviour - Develop communication skills to diffuse the situation - Increase confidence and assertiveness in dealing with difficult behaviour - Manage your emotions and deal with stress - Understand the power of words and how to use them to your advantage Workshop Overview: - What are the behaviours that we find difficult to deal with? - Develop an understanding of how flight or fight reactions prompt difficult behaviour - Controlling your reactions and choosing how you respond - Strategies for staying calm and keeping your cool when dealing with difficult behaviour - How attitudes play a part – What’s it like being on the receiving end of me? How do I come across? - Dealing with the situation/problem, not the individual - Dealing with anger, your own and others – Be able to use basic anger management techniques - Developing communication skills, such as the agreement frame, active listening and open questions - Applying techniques to deal with difficult behaviour - Understand what conflict and conflict resolution mean - Understand all six phases of the conflict resolution process -Understand the 5 main styles of conflict resolution and be able to adapt the process for all types of conflicts - Speak up assertively and confidently when dealing with difficult behaviour To book: email info@biztraines.co.nz or call 04 974 8790.

description:
Designing exceptional volunteer engagement, Join international volunteer engagement expert Tobi Johnson in an interactive workshop to design a complete volunteer journey. 
Tobi Johnson is an internationally sought-after expert, consultant, and expert trainer in volunteer engagement. She is known for her modern thought leadership, highly practical evidence-based strategies, and innovative, “big hat” thinking around engaging, supporting, and acknowledging the work of volunteers. 
This workshop, to be held in Wellington on Tuesday 27 January, will guide participants through the complete volunteer journey using the Best Practice Guidelines as a framework for exploration. 
Through graphic facilitation, collaborative exercises, and practical brainstorming, you will develop creative and actionable strategies to design a volunteer experience based on the spirit of community. 
If you are a nonprofit that relies on volunteers – with lots of passion but limited resources – this workshop is specifically tailored for you. As community champions, this is an opportunity to explore, visualize, and co-create practical ways to strengthen volunteer engagement, grounded in the shared values that make volunteering in Aotearoa unique. 
About your facilitator Tobi Johnson:
Tobi Johnson is an internationally sought-after expert, consultant, and expert trainer in volunteer engagement. She is known for her modern thought leadership, highly practical evidence-based strategies, and innovative, “big hat” thinking around engaging, supporting, and acknowledging the work of volunteers. 
She is the President of Tobi Johnson & Associates, a consulting firm whose mission is to help nonprofit organizations make connections with remarkable volunteers. In 2015, she founded VolunteerPro, an online training and networking community for leaders of volunteers.  She is host of the Volunteer Nation Podcast and co-host of the Time + Talent Podcast with Jennifer Bennett of VolunteerMatch. In addition, she wrote Chapter 1 of Volunteer Engagement 2.0: Ideas and Insights for Transforming Volunteer Programs in a Changing World. She is also currently at work on a book for volunteers who lead to be published in 2026. 
Tobi has over 30 years boots-on-the-ground experience in nonprofit management, program development and start up, team leadership, training design and delivery and change management across a wide range of cause impact areas from arts and culture, youth development, employment and training, senior services, healthcare advocacy, homelessness, and more. 
Where: Wellington, in person. Level 2, 50 The Terrace (the VNZ offices), Wellington.
When: Tuesday 27 January - 9am to 5pm.
Tickets and pricing:
We have priced tickets based on organisation type, and offer a 25% discount to Volunteering NZ member organisations.
Community Organisations $199 +gst
Government or Business tickets $219 +gst
Limited low cost and complimentary tickets are available for those who need additional support to access tickets. These are aimed at organisations with an annual income between $0 to $140k.
Please contact us directly if you:
Are a Volunteering NZ Member and have not received the discount code of 25%, or
Want to enquire about scholarship or low cost tickets.
Email us on office@volunteeringnz.org.nz or phone us on 04 470 6006. Volunteering NZ member list here.

description:
ECD Emotional Leadership Development Course 20th November - Central Wellington, ECD Emotional Leadership Development 1 Day Certification Course
Become a Certified Emotional Culture Deck Leadership Practitioner
This course is designed to enhance leadership development by equipping leaders with the tools to understand and manage emotional drivers and dynamics within themselves, their people and their teams. The course focuses on developing emotionally aware leaders who can effectively foster a positive workplace culture. Participants will engage in practical activities that promote self-awareness, team cohesion, and emotional intelligence, all grounded in The Emotional Culture Deck framework.
"Emotional culture is shaped by how all employees—from the highest echelons to the front lines—comport themselves day in and day out. But it’s up to senior leaders to establish which emotions will help the organization thrive, model those emotions, and reward others for doing the same. Companies in which they do this have a lot to gain." – Sigal Barsade & Olivia O'Neil, Manage Your Emotional Culture

Why this course is a Game-Changer

In today’s fast-paced and complex business environment, the ability to lead with emotion is more critical than ever. Our ECD Emotional Leadership Development Course is designed to transform the way leaders understand and harness the power of emotions to foster a more dynamic and responsive workplace.
What to expect
This hands-on one-day course is designed for immediate application, ensuring that you can translate insights into action as soon as you return to your team or clients. 
What to expect from this 1 day course experience:
Understanding the power of emotions in leading others effectively
Development of effective emotion-led leadership strategies. 
Learning how to use and embed our ready-made Emotional Culture Deck Leadership Tools
Active learning through interactive activities and group discussions.
Exploration of personal leadership and team leadership.
What's included in this course?
Enrol in the ECD Emotional Leadership Development Course and unlock a wealth of resources including:
ECD Emotional Leadership Development Toolkit - Valued at 175 NZD: Get this invaluable toolkit filled with a robust selection of physical and downloadable resources designed for immediate impact. Its comprehensive nature will extend your learning and application of the course content well beyond the Course.
1x Emotional Culture Deck  - Valued at 155 NZD: Receive your personal ECD, an essential tool for applying courseprinciples in real-world settings, adding even more value to your toolkit.
Exclusive 60-Minute Group Coaching Call: Enhance your course experience with a group coaching call, scheduled six to eight weeks post-course. Hosted via Zoom, this session provides an opportunity to solidify your learning, address any questions, and ensure you're applying your new skills effectively. Whether you attend live or watch the replay later, this call is a key step in your continued development.
Continued Learning Discount: Enjoy a 50% discount on future purchases of The Emotional Culture Deck to support your ongoing practice.
ECD Emotional Leadership Certificate of Practice: A formal acknowledgement of your dedication to enhancing your Emotional Culture Deck skills. description:
Effective Business Analysis, Effective Business Analysis
Defining change with clarity and agility. Discover how to apply the core skills and techniques of elicitation, analysis, and communication.

About this Event


Description
The business world is demanding faster change, the ability to adapt and solutions that are fit for purpose. As a business analyst, you're counted on for your skills as a conceptual and practical thinker, a relationship builder, and a translator. You're relied upon to identify and describe the change required to address business issues. Sometimes there are problems that require a fix, opportunities that need to be realised or situations where the business simply doesn't know but is prepared to "give it a go" and experiment to gain insights to what it should do next.
In this course, you'll be introduced to a series of context aware, business-focussed approaches that you can apply to:
Work with stakeholders to uncover the business issue that needs to be addressed
Define the change required within its context
Prioritise and scope the requirements based on business value and
Specify requirements clearly to those delivering the solution
Designed and delivered by our Equinox IT team of practicing business analysts, this course covers how to structure your analysis activities based on the context and the issue at hand to describe requirements that fully represent the change required.




Outline
Day 1
Overview and concepts
What is business analysis?
Requirements analysis framework

Discover – understanding context
Understanding a business domain
Adjusting to different types of initiative
Stakeholders – identification, classification and engaging
Techniques (root cause analysis, 5 whys, diverge, converge, etc.)
The discovery canvas

Focus topic: Elicitation –gathering information and understanding
Purpose and context
Selecting the right technique (interviews, workshops, research, observation, brainstorming, etc.)
Planning a session
Running a session
Post session activities
Main exercise - role play

Day 2
Define – understanding the change required
Introduction to capabilities
Information and data – concept/domain Modelling
Business process – tips on modelling
Business rules – their relationship with other business concepts
Scenarios – use cases
Change strategy map
Change aspect map
Defining user and other stories

Scope – understanding priority and value
Helping the business to assess value
Techniques
User story maps

Day 3
Focus topic: Workshop Facilitation–gaining consensus
Being self-aware
Facilitation
Preparation
Group dynamics
Handling various situations
Main exercise - role play

Deliver – packaging for delivery
Backlog refinement
Developing good acceptance criteria
Understanding various types of solution requirements and contributing elements

Focus topic: Communication – telling the story
A brief overview of the difference between specification and communication




Learning outcomes
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to;
Analyse and understand the kind of business issue that needs to be addressed
Engage stakeholders and analyse their business needs
Define a change strategy
Define the aspects of change required
Understand various business models e.g. business process, information, business rules
Define a user story and associated requirements
Use effective techniques to elicit requirements
Understand how to plan and facilitate a requirements workshop
Understand scoping based on business value
Analyse, document and review solutions and detailed requirements
Define acceptance criteria
Understand how to communicate with a variety of audiences




Accreditation and certification
This course aligns with the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge v3.0®.




Audience
The primary audience for this course is business analysts, systems analysts and enterprise analysts of all experience levels. The course will also be of value to any project team members involved in requirements definition activities.




Prerequisites
There are no prerequisites for this course, however, some experience in business analysis will help.

description:
Get the Job: STARR Interview Technique and Preparation, Get the Job: STARR Interview Technique and Preparation
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
Meet the demand for excellence in the job market head on. Learn how to utilise the STARR technique in the way that recruiters use it. That is, to define and seek out the skills and qualities of the best candidate. Master the STARR skills and feel confident in your next job interview.

Familiarise yourself with the skills needed to ace your next interview. Learn the STARR method as an approach to responding to behavioural based questions. Understand how to use concrete examples from your life as proof that you possess the experience and skills for the job you are applying for. You’ll develop the key interview skill of being able to share your accomplishments through real-life examples.

In this course, you are taught how to identify specific example situations that are unique to you. You’ll learn how to confidently talk about the tasks involved and describe how you completed the key task and met its challenges. We’ll also consider the context of jobs you are interviewing for and how to choose examples that best show the desired skills interviewers are seeking.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Develop a higher level of confidence in approaching job interviews.
- Identify the different components of the STARR acronym and apply them to the job interview context.
- Identify what behavioural based questions are and why recruiters use them.
- Successfully answer behavioural based interview questions by applying the STARR technique.
- Develop skills in using real life examples to show transferable skills in the workplace.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.

(NZ Citizens and residents pay $29 with ID, all others pays $120).
AI tools are everywhere, but knowing which one to use — and how to use it well — makes all the difference. In this hands-on workshop, Jon Bell will guide you through practical techniques to make AI a genuinely useful partner in your work and life. Whether you've tried it a few times or use it regularly, you'll leave with real skills you can apply straight away, with no technical background needed.
We'll start with a quick tour of the main tools — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot — so you understand what makes each one different. (They're less different than you might think!) Then we'll spend most of the day going deep on Claude, which Jon considers the easiest to use, while also being the most powerful.
We'll cover real examples, answer your questions as they come up, and spend plenty of time experimenting together.
By the end of the workshop, you'll be able to:
- Write effective prompts that get clearer, more useful responses
- Use AI for research, brainstorming, writing, and creative work
- Understand the differences between the major tools and when to use each
- Recognise the tools' limitations (and how to work around them)
- Apply practical strategies for using AI in your personal or professional projects
- Confidently troubleshoot when AI gives unexpected or unhelpful answers
Please bring: A phone or laptop with ChatGPT and Claude installed and signed in to both. Enough battery to last the day.
A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

Hoake Tātou | Walk With Me Wellington Central, Tautoko Tāne is hosting Hoake Tātou | Walk With Me - a nationwide series of free presentations for agencies, service providers and professionals to share information and insights about working with male survivors of sexual abuse to get the support they need.
There will be two sessions on 12 November at Rydges Wellington CBD - 10am and 2pm.
The presentation includes:
Safe access and effective engagement of male survivors with support services
Dispelling some of the common myths about male victims of sexual harm
Navigate the misunderstandings that create barriers to engagement with support services
Highlight the role of lived experience as an effective engagement model
Collaboration and partnerships to welcome and embrace cultural and gender diversity within the male survivor community
Supporting complex trauma requires a shared response from several organisations, each with different skills and experience – no single agency or organisation can do it alone.
As more male survivors present with complex trauma, New Zealand will need even more collaborative sector partnerships to provide the wrap-around services necessary for recovery.
Hoake Tātou | Walk With Me is about bringing those different organisations together to hear from those with lived experience, and share information and understandings about working with male survivors of sexual abuse and violence, to help them get the support they need.

description:
Impactful Leadership, Impactful Leadership:
What do horses, mules and the All Blacks have in common? Hear a true expert break-down what really works when it comes to impactful leadership.
Welcome to the final conversation in our Women in Business series: four events that bring you important conversations led by Women in Business and heard by everyone. In partnership with Forsyth Barr, this bar-setting series is bringing hard-hitting topics into the conversational spotlight.
What good leadership looks like has changed, but many of the methods we rely on to deliver it haven’t. This conversation will showcase what horses can teach us about impactful leadership in modern workplaces, and how anyone can turn those lessons into action that delivers.
Why be part of this conversation?
In this thought-provoking session, BBC journalist-turned-leadership coach Janine Sudbury will share how she discovered what really works in leadership development, and why traditional approaches often fall short.
You’ll take away insights including:
The three secrets of the horse whisperer that unlock authentic, presence-based leadership
How to overcome Imposter Syndrome and People Pleasing to lead with clarity and confidence
Why horses give the most honest feedback—and how that feedback creates lasting breakthroughs
Who’s the speaker?
Janine Sudbury is the founder of Impact Leadership and the creator of a truly unique experiential leadership programme that swaps the boardroom for the paddock. specialises in helping women overcome Imposter Syndrome and People Pleasing Syndrome to lead with more confidence, clarity, and authenticity.
With powerful insights and unforgettable stories, including her work with former All Blacks coach Steve Hansen, Janine invites you to lead with more purpose, presence, and impact.
What’s in-store:
5:15-5:30pm – Arrival/networking
5:30-6:15pm – Janine Sudbury speaks
6:15-6:30pm – Q&A
6:30-7:30pm – Networking with drinks & canapes
Business card prize draw:
Attend the event and go in the draw to win a “New BMW for a Weekend” and a “New MINI for a Weekend” from Continental Cars BMW and Wellington MINI Garage.
This event is part of the Women in Business chapter from our “Join the Conversation” series - 4 events that spotlight important topics through conversation, led by the amazing women driving change within them.
Attend other events in the series:
17 July: Making money in the mess - How every woman can financially thrive in messy economic times
7 August: Strengths & Superpowers - Personal branding isn’t showing off - it’s taking ownership over how you’re perceived. Join a Masterclass in making yours standout among the rest
20 August: 3 Gals, One Beehive – live! - Hear three leading women take a week in politics, and turn it into the unfiltered commentary that you wish you’d hear on the 6 o’clock news.

description:
Industry Veterinarians Branch Meeting, Come along to hear insights from Animal and Plant Health New Zealand (APHANZ) CEO, Liz Shackleton, on what’s changing in the regulatory space and why it matters to you.
Thursday 30 October 2025
3-4pm followed by dinner
NZVA office, Level 2, 44 Victoria Street, Wellington
Meeting complimentary | Dinner at your own expense
Liz joined APHANZ as Chief Executive Officer in October 2023.
Her primary sector career spans various strategic leadership roles in biosecurity, regulatory and animal health sectors and clinical veterinary practice. Her work has included supporting teams and governance functions across private and public partnerships in the primary sector including leading the dairy industry team in the Mycoplasma bovis programme.
Liz is a chartered member of the Institute of Directors New Zealand, a veterinarian elected member of the Veterinary Council of New Zealand, past president of the Australian and New Zealand College of Veterinary Scientists (Pharmacology), and Institute for Strategic Leadership alumnus.
Liz hails from an Irish farming background and is passionate about our rural communities and supporting our sectors emerging leaders.
If you would like to attend this event, please register before the final deadline on Friday 10th October 2025. Places are limited and will be allocated on a first-come basis.

Registrations required. Full room details on registration. You will need to bring your own laptop. REGISTER HERE: https://tinyurl.com/mr2dzpjc
About the presenter:
Dr Fahimeh McGregor is the founder of DELTA Informed Decisions and a lecturer at Massey University Business School. With more than 20 years of experience across the public and private sectors, she specialises in AI readiness, data strategy, and helping organisations translate emerging technologies into practical and productive outcomes.
Fahimeh works with a wide range of organisations — from large institutions to independent business owners — helping them cut through complexity and integrate AI and digital tools into their operations in ways that are purposeful, time-saving, and responsible. Her focus is on building genuine capability rather than chasing technology for its own sake.
She is passionate about making AI accessible and practical for people willing to engage with it thoughtfully, and brings a practical, human-centred perspective to every workshop, consulting engagement, and classroom.

Introduction to Business Analysis, Introduction to Business Analysis
Get a pragmatic introduction to key business analysis concepts and the business analyst role, and apply what you learn.

About this Event


Description
This course provides a pragmatic introduction to key business analysis concepts and the business analyst role. It includes a number of hands-on exercises to apply what you learn. It is targeted at those who are new to Business Analyst roles or considering moving into this profession. The course is also highly suitable to subject matter experts, business representatives, and project roles that involve business analysis activities.
Business analysis is a broad and exciting profession and skill set. Your role is to understand businesses, their needs and their problems and then help assess and validate solutions to fulfil these needs or solve these problems. In the process you will be involved in a wide range of activities including analysis, requirements management, communication, solution assessment and validation, and planning.
The ‘Introduction to Business Analysis’ course is delivered by seasoned business analysis practitioner consultants who undertake business analysis activities on a daily basis.

New business analysts

Join NZ cricket legend Grant Elliot for some inspiration, a bit of networking and a drink.

About this Event

This month:
GRANT ELLIOTT is a renowned former cricketer, having played over 100 games for the Blackcaps. Grant enjoyed success on the international stage particularly with white ball cricket.
Widely regarded by his teammates as a hard worker and a reliable player who always put the team first, Grant was written into New Zealand cricketing folklore books when he hit the winning 6 which propelled the Blackcaps into their first ever World Cup final!
An entertaining and insightful speaker, Grant shares his knowledge of team culture, motivation and exactly what it takes to create a high performing team.

Leadership & Management Part 2, Learn how to make the transition from buddy to boss and lead a successful team. As John F. Kennedy once said, “leadership and learning are indispensable to each other”. description:

Friday 17th October 2025 | 8:30am–5:00pm
Location: Nairn Street Cottage, 68 Nairn Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6011

What this day is all about
Leadership Play Day is a full-day, game-based learning experience that takes leadership development out of the boardroom and into play. Instead of being talked at with boring slides, you’ll step into three carefully designed games that let you actually practice leadership.
You’ll be experimenting, problem-solving, laughing (a lot), and walking away with insights that stick because you’ve lived them, not just heard them.
This isn’t theory. It’s leadership in action.
Learn more at our website.
How it works
The day is made up of three 2-hour games. You can book individual sessions ($99 each), or join us for the full day ($297) to play all three and unlock The Leadership Playbook - a bonus 60-minute facilitated debrief where we connect the dots and help you take away a clear set of personal leadership shifts.
Here’s what’s on in Wellington:
The Moonlit Market (8:30–10:30am)
Pitch, trade, and negotiate under pressure. Build agility, creativity, and bold decision-making in a playful, high-energy marketplace.
The Broken Bridge (11:00am–1:00pm)
A fantasy quest to practice difficult conversations. Explore courage, clarity, and how you show up when the stakes feel high.
The Inner Tides (1:45–3:45pm)
Use the Emotional Culture Deck in a role-playing game to strengthen emotional awareness, resilience, and confidence in leading with empathy.
The Leadership Playbook (4:00–5:00pm)
Available only with a full-day pass. A guided reflection session to connect your learning, extract insights, and leave with a practical playbook you can use back at work.
Why you should join
Practical skills, not theory - you’ll walk away with tools and insights you can use immediately.
Safe practice, real challenges - rehearse tough moments without real-world consequences.
Energy + engagement - no sitting back, you’ll be on your feet, in the mix, learning by doing.
Unique approach - game-based leadership development you won’t find anywhere else in NZ.
Whether you’re a leader, facilitator, HR/People professional, or just someone curious about growing your leadership edge - this day is designed for you.

Full day pass (all 3 games + Leadership Playbook debrief): $297

Business owner brand

Welcome! I'm Rachel Klaver, content marketing coach, marketing strategist and small business owner.

I write a fortnightly column for NZ's Stuff newspaper on marketing, and have two podcasts: MAP IT Marketing, and Confident Content. )

So... would you like to come join me?

This two-day programme is just $2,000+gst per person.

Managing for value: building a strong financial advice business-Wellington, Building a valuable financial advice business means you have a resilient business to support your clients and a strong asset. Transactions – acquisition and disposal support the long-term growth and sustainability of financial advice provider businesses. Transactions take many forms, going concerns regularly acquire and dispose of clients, business units, lines of business, have investors buy-in, bring key staff together – and split businesses up. Only a small number of our transactions are the classic market exit.
Our aim is to spend time talking with advisers about how to grow their business and manage for value – making their business more valuable by explicitly thinking about valuation in addition to the other metrics such as profit and cashflow.

description:
Mauri Ora in Business: Leading with Wellbeing, Mauri Ora in Business: Leading with Wellbeing
In the rush of daily demands, it’s easy to forget that the most powerful tool you bring to your business is yourself.

About this Event

In the rush of daily demands, it's easy to forget that the most powerful tool you bring to your business is yourself. Mauri Ora in Business is a 3.5-hour interactive workshop designed for leaders and change-makers who know that true impact starts within.
At the heart of this kaupapa is a powerful truth: the most effective leaders lead themselves first. Using the Mauri Ora model and its eight domains of wellbeing from Te Rūnanga o Toa Rangatira, you'll be guided to reflect on your current leadership, unpack what's working, and explore how your own wellbeing shapes your business outcomes.
This isn't just theory — it's practical and deeply reflective. You'll move through guided self-assessment, meaningful kōrero, and dedicated planning time to build a personalised leadership plan that is grounded and immediately actionable. You'll also leave with a planning workbook and a follow-up session with our BizHub mentors to help you put it into practice.
What you'll walk away with:
A clear understanding of the Mauri Ora framework and how it applies to your leadership
Insight into your strengths and gaps across key wellbeing domains
A personalised leadership plan with practical next steps
Connection with like-minded leaders for support and accountability
Workshop details:
Tuesday, 12th May 2026 | 9:00am – 12:30pm (includes morning tea)
In-person, small group setting
Co-funded in partnership with Porirua City Council and WellingtonNZ through the Regional Business Partner Network — your pakihi may be eligible to attend at no cost. Reach out to us to check your eligibility and register to attend.

If you're ready to lead in a way that is grounded, sustainable, and aligned — this is your space.

NMHNZ CONFERENCE '26, NMHNZ CONFERENCE '26
Catalysts for Change : Naturopathy as Primary Care
Transforming lives and Redefining community healthcare
NMHNZ is proud to be at the forefront of Naturopathy as the leading Professional Organisation for Naturopaths and Medical Herbalists in Aotearoa New Zealand. This year our focus is on HOW we can position Naturopaths and Medical Herbalists at the forefront of health care in Aotearoa New Zealand, and beyond.
Our "Catalysts for Change" themed conference is all about putting our profession front and centre.We delved into our rich international heritage and explored the connections between the two, in 2024. We discussed how at the heart of Naturopathic and Herbal Medicine lies a profound respect for the wisdom of the past with a commitment to researching the benefits for our lives today.
2026 sees us looking outside the box at HOW we can be more active and visible.Our next step is to learn about integrating this knowledge and connection into primary health care.
Preventative health is at the forefront of everything we do, along with lifestyle, nutrition, and science. We want to redefine Community Healthcare using Naturopathic principles, Science & Research, and of course Nature.
This event will inspire and motivate you to get out & be a Catalyst for Change in your community.Our International speakers are renowned for delivering relevant and useable content, enabling our delegates to make use of every piece of information gathered.
Over two very full days, we will welcome speakers from around the globe. Along with delegates from Naturopathy, Herbal Medicine, and other Allied Health communities.

description:
New Zealand Vocational Education and Training Research Forum, Rebuilding together.
Ngā mihi nui ki a koutou katoa

Skills Group and BCITO are delighted to join forces to return NZVETRF as a unique national event to showcase and disseminate new and emerging research and innovation in Vocational Education and Training.
Since 2004, the NZVETRF has been the must-attend event for policy makers, researchers and practitioners engaged in vocational education, across all parts of the tertiary sector and industry.
The vocational education sector is transforming through both policy and technological change. Knowing 'what works' and what is emerging is more critical than ever as a new network of provision for vocational education and training is established.
Over a day and a half you'll hear from international and national keynote speakers, government and sector stakeholders, the learner voice, and debates on the hot topics, along with curated and competitively selected research and evidence presentations.

Places are limited - register now to secure your place at Aotearoa's pre-eminent cross-sector vocational education event.
Call for Abstracts Now Open
We now invite researchers, practitioners, and policy makers to submit abstracts for presentation at the Forum. As part of New Zealand's premier VET research platform, your contributions will help shape New Zealand’s future as our sector moves forward.
Submission Guidelines
Abstracts should be no longer than 300 words and outline your completed research and intended presentation. We particularly welcome submissions that address one or more of our key conference themes:
·       Workplace learning and Industry Training
·       Diversity, Access and Equity
·       Developing our Future Workforce
·       Technology and Innovation
·       Learner Journey and Outcomes
·       Collaboration and System Approaches.
Your research should demonstrate evidence-based outcomes, share good practice, support high-quality research networks, and inform policy development. We encourage submissions that honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi and incorporate Māori perspectives in VET innovation.
Submit your abstract here
Submission Deadline: 5pm, 17 September 2025
An assessment panel comprising representatives from Skills Group, BCITO, and an independent assessor will evaluate all submissions. Successful presenters will be notified by the end of September 2025.
Keynote Speaker Announcement
We are delighted to announce that Kathryn Rowan, Executive Director of Switzerland-based Global Apprenticeship Network will address the Forum.

Kathryn is a seasoned leader with a background in human resources and corporate social responsibility, who brings a wealth of experience from her previous role as Vice President of Human Resources, Zone Latin America, and Global Youth Lead at Nestlé. Throughout her career, Ms. Rowan has consistently demonstrated a passion for harnessing the power of business to drive positive change in society. During her tenure at Nestlé, in national, regional, and global roles, she promoted initiatives to strengthen leadership and capability building, diversity, and corporate reputation, while spearheading youth-focused efforts, including the Global Alliance for Youth.
The Global Apprenticeship Network was established in 2014 by ILO, the International Organisation of Employers (IOE), the Organisation of Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), and Business at OECD. GAN is governed by a private-sector led, multi-stakeholder coalition representing major global corporations and international organisations, GAN's primary role is to encourage businesses to implement apprenticeship and WBL programs and support the creation of an enabling policy environment.
Further programme details and speaker announcements will be made in coming weeks, so register now!
Your Co-Hosts
Skills Group is New Zealand's largest Private Training Establishment, supporting 17,000 learners and training across 33 industries, through both work-based and provider-based learning, across 15 campuses nationwide.
BCITO is New Zealand's largest provider of Apprenticeships, having qualified 55,000 tradies and counting, across 15 construction and allied trades.

Skills and BCITO gratefully acknowledge Ako Aotearoa, the Centre for Tertiary Teaching Excellence, for support and permission to carry this event forward. We acknowledge Ako's enormous contribution to VET research and this event over many years. NZVETRF is a taonga, and as co-hosts we are committed to upholding the mana of the event.

Partner with us.
NZVETRF is all about walking the talk on sector collaboration. We warmly invite interest from interested education and industry partners to join on as event supporters. Sponsorship and event supporter packages are available. Contact nzvetrf@skills-group.org for details.

description:
Painless Presenting - Tuesday 18th November, Full day presentation skills workshop in Wellington. Limited tickets available. Get in now so you don't miss out!
Who's it for?
You work in a technical field. You’re great at your job — but struggle to get your ideas across the business.
You often:
Dive into technical detail that loses or confuses your audience
Overload people with too much information, which makes it harder to get the results you need
Find it tough to explain complex areas of your role in a way others can easily understand
Spend hours planning presentations, yet still feel stiff and uncomfortable when delivering
Feel nervous when presenting, and wish you could speak with more ease and confidence
If this sounds like you, Painless Presenting will help you cut through complexity, present clearly, and build the confidence you know is vital for your career growth.
What you will learn:
A proven step by step process that will take the pain out of planning presentations and set the foundations for becoming a more engaging, natural and effective business presenter.

Participants are taught how to write a valuable business presentation, how to manage their nerves, design useful visuals and are given key delivery techniques to help deliver their presentations in a natural and engaging way.
You will come away with:
an understanding of how to use the SpeakerMap™ system, a step by step, proven approach to planning presentations quickly and effectively
a new appreciation of purpose when speaking
an understanding of how to quickly design useful presentation visuals
how to easily overcome the problems of speaking too fast, um-ing and ah-ing, and losing your place
a tailored strategy to dissolve the anxiety that so often accompanies presenting
three delivery tricks that will help you come across as credible and confident
Note: You will not need to present to the group on this course. If you are interested in a more intensive training option, including one on one coaching, check out our 2 day workshop The Effective Speaker.
What past participants say:

"Really great course, no pressure environment with a good mix of interactive and book work. Have walked away feeling more confident in how I am going to put my presentations together."

description:
Personal Brand Workshop | Wellington, Personal Brand Workshop Facilitated by Rochelle Moffitt
Wednesday 19th November 2025
10am – 4pm workshop
The rules of reputation are changing.
Today, visibility, credibility, and connection aren't just nice-to-haves - they're non-negotiables. Even established industries and respected professionals are realising they need to evolve to stay relevant and competitive.
That’s where this workshop comes in.

We’re here to help you take ownership of your reputation, tell your story with clarity, and build a personal brand that feels like you - and works for you.

We know that the real shift starts inside.
It’s not your LinkedIn. It’s not the algorithm. It’s the moment you believe you’re worth being seen .
This isn’t about performing or posting.
It’s about owning your story, claiming your space, and stepping into what’s next - with strategy and confidence.

What This Workshop Is About:
This is not a social media crash course. It’s a full-day, full-body recalibration of how you show up in the world - on purpose.
We’ll use Rochelle’s BANKABLE Framework to unpack what it really takes to:
Build a personal brand that opens doors and commands respect
Become the first name that comes to mind in rooms you haven’t even entered yet
Be strategically visible to the right people
Let your reputation do the heavy lifting before you even show up
Use social media to reinforce your authority, not just participate in the noise
This day is about shifting your mindset, sharpening your message, and building a brand that reflects your true value.

What Does It Mean to Be BANKABLE?
Bankable means your name carries weight. You’re trusted, referred, remembered, and respected.

You don’t just do good work. You’re seen as someone people want to work with, invest in, promote, or buy from.
It’s not about being everywhere - it’s about being in the right rooms, with the right presence, and the right message.
In this workshop, we’ll break down the BANKABLE Framework, which is built on the 8 core traits of people who consistently attract opportunity:
B – Belief
It starts with mindset. You believe you're worth being seen, heard, and valued. No shrinking.
A – Authenticity
Lead with your real story, not a polished performance. People buy you, not your job title.
N – Niche
You know what you stand for, who you serve, and why it matters.
K – Knowledge
You share your experience and insights generously - not to impress, but to connect.
A – Action
You show up. Consistently. You don’t wait to be discovered - you make your value visible.
B – Brand SignalsYour online presence aligns with how you want to be seen. There’s clarity, not confusion.
L – Leadership
You own your space. You influence through presence, not just position.
E – Equity
You’re building reputation, trust, and opportunity that compound over time. You’re seen as a valuable asset, not just a contributor.

Who It’s For:
Ambitious professionals, business owners, and leaders who are ready to:
Get clear on what they stand for
Build trust before the first conversation
Show up with authority and authenticity
Position themselves for the next opportunity, role, or revenue leap

What You'll Walk Away With:
✔ A mindset reset and brand strategy built using Rochelle’s BANKABLE Framework
✔ Your fully optimised LinkedIn profile that positions you clearly and credibly
✔ A personalised workbook with brand messaging, positioning, and action steps
✔ Clarity, direction, and the confidence to take up space

Extra Perks:
Morning tea, lunch, and afternoon tea are included
Investment:
Special community rate: $1,600 + gst (limited to 10 people)
Includes all content, catering, workbook, and post-workshop support

- Tash Fernandez

- Dauniika
"Morning Rochelle! Just wanted to a say a huge thank you for your session yesterday, it was truly fantastic. We had some fantastic conversations surrounding your content throughout the rest of the day, everyone is talking on your challenge!"

description:
Project Management 101, Dates:Wednesday 5 November, 9am-4.30pm & Thursday 6 November , 9am-4.30pm
Presenter: Paul Sutton, Nonsuch.
This two-day instructor led course has been designed to introduce the concepts of Project Management to help ensure a common understanding – regardless of whether you are a project manager, sponsor, team member or coordinator. The course covers the unique language, principles and tools of project management and builds a case for their application back at the workplace. This course will ensure you are equipped to manage your projects efficiently and successfully.
Ideal for individuals who have no previous experience with project management, or those looking for a refresher. Also ideal for those wishing to develop an understanding of project management as they progress into Project Administration and/or Project Coordination.
Learning Outcomes
At the completion of the 2-day course, you will:
Have a common understanding of what a project is and how it is different from day-to-day, business as usual work
Understand key terminology, principles and tools related to project management including how adaptive (Agile) and predictive (Waterfall) methodologies are different and how they work together
Understand the difference between project objectives, outputs, and outcomes
Learn and practice how to plan a project, based an output planning approach utilising Output Breakdown Structures, Output Flow Diagrams
Learn how to produce a project schedule including various estimation techniques
Gain practical techniques related to time, scope, cost, and quality
Learn practical techniques related to resourcing and costing on projects
Understand the importance of project quality and how to plan for it
Understand your role in a project and learn tips and techniques to help you manage your time and priorities
Understand a typical project organisation and the roles and responsibilities for each member of the Project Team and Project Steering Committee
Learn about the importance of stakeholders and how to use a stakeholder analysis to produce a robust Communications & Engagement Plan
Gain awareness of Risk Management including the difference between risks and issues
Have a general understanding of benefits, their importance to projects, and how to identify and quantify them
Talk through lots of real-life project examples to cement the learnings and identify traps to avoid.
Have a general understanding of the differences between project, programme, and portfolio management
No prerequisite is required for attendance on this session, but any prior experience or knowledge of project management will be a definite advantage
This session is a mixture of theory and discussion and practical group-based learning involving post-it notes, markers, flip chart paper. An easy to understand and practical case study is used throughout the course. No laptops are required, all learning resources are supplied.

description:
Putting the 'Where' into decisions: a 40 year journey with the enabling technology named Geographic Information Systems (GIS), During his IT career at Eagle Technology Group in New Zealand, Parker identified a number of software applications to import, sell, and support locally, including the GIS developed by US-based Environmental Research Systems Institute (ESRI).
From the late 1980s, he was involved in many ESRI GIS implementations across central, regional, and local government, DSIR/CRIs, and universities. When Parker retired from Eagle Technology 13 years ago, he founded GIS in Conservation (GiC), a non-profit charitable trust that provides GIS and other IT specialists and software to non-profit conservation and iwi groups at no charge.
In the Wellington region, GiC has supported organisations including Zero Invasive Predators Ltd (ZIP), Zealandia, and Capital Kiwi.
Parker’s talk will present real New Zealand examples showing how GIS has enabled a new way of understanding the world by putting the “where” into data.
This event is supported by voluntary donations. Please consider making a donation when reserving your ticket.
Biography
Parker was raised and worked on his grandparents’ Angus beef and cropping farm in Gloucester, Virginia. In 1976, he graduated from Methodist University, North Carolina, with a Bachelor of Administration, intending to continue towards becoming a Chartered Accountant.
He was instead recruited by Burroughs Corporation to work in IT sales for accounting solutions. Parker emigrated to New Zealand in 1983 and joined Pr1me Computers—now Eagle Technology Ltd—as an Account Manager, where he worked for 29 years until his retirement.
Parker has been a volunteer trapper for 22 years and continues to serve on both the GiC and MIRO committees. At MIRO, he coordinates the protection and study of the endangered Wellington Region banded dotterel population, assists with the little blue penguin project, and manages volunteer trapping at Parangahau Lakes.

description:
RETHINK Fundraising Wellington 2026, INTRODUCING AOTEAROA'S NEWEST FUNDRAISING EVENT: RETHINK
RETHINK Fundraising 2026 invites you and your team to look at your fundraising programme from a fresh perspective.
Join us for a full day of inspirational talks, panel discussions and practical workshops that will leave you energised, AND armed with a toolkit of actionable learnings to take your fundraising to the next level.
Date: Thursday, 5 March
Venue: Mākaro Room, Wharewaka Function Centre
Time: 8am-5pm
Cost: $249NZD (exc GST)*
Contact: Anna Shere anna@changeand.co
*If you prefer to pay via invoice, please email accounts@changeand.co.
THE PROGRAMME
For those of you who joined us for RETHINK Auckland 2025, please note that RETHINK Wellington will feature many of the same sessions from that event, with a few additions to the programme and two new guest speakers.
Branding blindspots 
In a sector focused on campaigns, conversion, and compliance, brand is often overlooked. But brand isn’t just a logo or a nice story. It’s how people feel about supporting you. And if it's not clear, engaging, or modern – you’re leaving both money and meaning on the table. This presentation from Tim Dove at re:brand will challenge a few norms and show some examples of it being done well. He’ll get you thinking about your organisation and how you can ensure you’re avoiding the ‘brand blindspot’. 
Rethinking charity comms 
When it comes to getting people enthused about our cause, too often we focus on the what rather than the why. Worse, we risk boring our audience to death with earnest, organisation-centric communications which neither inspire nor instruct. Dominique Antarakis from Change&Co will show you a new and fun way to look at your charity comms for maximum engagement and donor retention.  
Workshop 1 
Facilitated workshop which will provide the opportunity to take the learnings from the morning sessions and give you the practical branding and comms tools to take back to your organisation - and transform your fundraising! 
Lunch break  
Take a break, mix and mingle, and enjoy a fabulous lunch selection.
Data, behaviour, and hyper-personalisation 
This presentation from MIMO/DATAM will show you how to transform raw data into meaningful, multi-channel interactions across email, SMS, voice, and direct mail - all from a single platform. This session will challenge how you think about personalisation - it’s not just about names in subject lines or open rates in eDMs, it’s about burning down the old school campaigns and rebuilding around behaviour, context and connection. 
Lessons from the legacy frontlines 
Based on interviews with practitioners from organisations large and small, this session shares unfiltered insights from Gift in Will managers who are doing the work every day—what's actually generating pledges, where they're getting stuck, and what they wish they'd known sooner. description:
Rethinking Career: Find the Work You’re Meant For, Rethinking Career: Find the Work You’re Meant For

For many people, work feels heavy.
Something to get through. Something that drains more than it gives.

You might feel bored, frustrated, stuck, or quietly miserable — but also unsure what to do about it. Changing jobs can feel overwhelming. Will it actually make things better? Will it be worth the risk? Will I still feel financially safe?

This evening is not about rushing into big decisions.
It’s about understanding yourself first.

Drawing on the Career Dharma framework, this event offers a different way of looking at work - one based on human nature, psychology, and timeless wisdom. It starts from a simple but often overlooked idea: we are not all nourished by the same things.

In Career Dharma, enrichment is understood as wealth - not only financial, but emotional, creative, intellectual, relational, and spiritual. Each of us is sustained by different kinds of wealth. These are known as our prosperity types.

When our work provides the kinds of prosperity our body and mind actually need, work feels lighter, more meaningful, and more sustainable. When it doesn’t, even a “good” or stable job can slowly drain us.

Through guided reflection and practical exercises, you’ll begin to uncover:

What genuinely makes you feel fulfilled and energized at work

The types of prosperity that matter most to you

Why certain work environments exhaust you - and others don’t

How greater self-understanding can help you adjust your current role or make wiser choices about future work

This session isn’t about job titles or quick fixes. It’s about awareness - and how knowing what truly nourishes you can change the way you relate to work, without needing to have all the answers yet.

Please note this is one of two careers workshops this month. While they complement each other, each session is designed to be meaningful on its own.

A plant-based dinner and dessert are included in your ticket.
Both hosts are available to support those who wish to continue exploring their career path.

Meet your hosts, Sri Jiva & Chanchala
Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

Chanchala studied psychology and education and brings a coaching-based approach to career exploration. She supports people to uncover work they love by helping them understand what truly nourishes their nature and psychology. Chanchala’s work is grounded in curiosity, self-trust, and creating careers that feel sustainable and life-giving.

description:
Rethinking Career: From 9 to 5 to Thrive, Rethinking Careers: From 9 to 5 to Thrive

What if thriving at work isn’t about doing more — but about expressing who you already are?

This event explores how meaningful work emerges when we understand our natural temperament and disposition. According to the Career Dharma framework, each person is wired to create value in a particular way — driven by distinct motivations, values, and strengths.

This natural orientation is known as your field of work.

Rather than starting with job titles, Career Dharma identifies four archetypal fields of work, drawn from timeless wisdom about human nature:

Ideas – teaching, guiding, researching, healing

Government – organising, protecting, leading

Artistry – creating beauty, sensing emotion, responding to needs

Resources – building, managing, sustaining, and sharing value

When we work within the field that matches our nature, work feels purposeful and sustainable. When we don’t, even “successful” careers can lead to burnout or inner conflict.

Through guided exercises and reflection, you’ll:

Identify your natural field of work

Understand what genuinely motivates and drains you

See why certain roles feel heavy — and others feel more alive

Connect your disposition to real-world roles and possible pathways

This session isn’t just about fixing your career. It’s about learning the language of your own nature, and letting that understanding quietly guide what comes next.

Please note this is one of two careers workshops this month. While they complement each other, each session is designed to be meaningful on its own.

A plant-based dinner and dessert are included in your ticket.

About this Event

Rise & Shine: Kick-Arse Meetup for Wellington’s Women in Business powered by Wellington Beds and BNZ.

Join us for on Thursday 9th of April, at 6:00pm for an exciting in-person event designed for Wellington Women in Business.
Step into the dynamic and driven world of Rise and Shine, where the spirit of Wellington’s businesswomen comes alive with energy, ambition, and enterprise.
Hosted by Patrice Green and powered by Wellington Beds, this series is dedicated to supporting women who are building, leading and creating change in business.
We’re excited to connect you with Viv Conway, co-founder of Girls Get Off, at the beautiful BNZ Wellington Partners Centre, Level 1, 1 Whitmore Street. The entrance is on the corner of Featherston and Ballance Street.

When you know what you want and need, everything changes.

Join Patrice as she hosts Viv Conway this November to take the chaos out of 2026 and design a year that feels as good as it looks.
Viv is part of a new generation of founders building bold, high-growth businesses and challenging traditional ideas about women’s products and markets.
In this conversation with Patrice, Viv will share the story behind Girls Get Off and what it has taken to grow a brand in the women’s sexual wellness space. She will talk about the realities of launching and scaling a business in a category that has often been misunderstood or overlooked, and the resilience required to keep moving forward when the path is not always straightforward.
Her journey is a powerful example of what can happen when women identify gaps in the market, back their ideas, and build communities around products that truly serve women.
Expect an honest conversation about entrepreneurship, resilience, community building and what it takes to create something new in a space where the rules are still being written.

Expect to leave with insights, encouragement, and new connections.
Bring a friend or come solo. We’ll make sure you don’t sip your drink alone.

Each event is a vibrant venue for visionary growth, where trailblazing speakers share their paths and insights, paving the way for others to follow. It’s not just a meeting, it’s a movement fueled by ambition and the collective power of women who are ready to lead.
These sessions are designed to inspire, challenge, and equip you with the tools to take your business and personal growth to new heights. With a focus on forging lasting connections that grow into business opportunities, ‘Rise and Shine’ is a kick-arse community ready to welcome the next trailblazer - YOU. Get ready to be inspired, to inspire, and to turn every interaction into a stepping stone for success.
Beyond networking, this is a platform for vibrant, interactive conversations. Each event spotlights a trailblazing guest, introduced and conversed with by none other than Patrice herself. But here’s the twist: the floor opens to you, offering a chance to engage directly and ask questions.
At this meetup, you'll have the opportunity to have networking drinks and nibbles while sharing your experiences, ideas, and challenges with fellow businesswomen. It's a perfect occasion to gain valuable insights, learn from each other's successes, and build meaningful connections.

description:
The Inevitabilism Panel, We're told AI is Progress, progress that cannot be stopped, that it will change the way we work and live, from business to education and the commons. But who says? Whose progress and whose AI is it anyway? Is societal progress really bound to technological innovation, or are there other ways of reading - and even shaping - positive social change?
Technological Determinism is described as the belief system that social progress is driven by technological innovation, which in turn follows an "inevitable" course." This panel will take a good hard look at this 'inevitabilism' - its forces and politics - with a view to our shared future in Aotearoa and the Pacific.
Join us for a rigorous evening of discussion with a view to how we might gain more understanding - and more say - as to the reach and influence new technologies have over our autonomy, dignity, communities and cultures.

The Power of Successful Cross-Sectoral Collaboration: A Real-World Example, From Pilot to Powerhouse: The BEATS Research Journey
Presented by Dr Sandra Mandic
In a world where complex challenges demand bold collaboration, the BEATS Research Programme stands as a beacon of what’s possible when sectors unite with purpose.
Join Dr Sandra Mandic as she shares the remarkable 10-year journey of BEATS—an award-winning, interdisciplinary initiative that brought together academia, local government, schools, and communities across Dunedin. From its humble beginnings in 2013 to its international recognition by 2023, BEATS exemplifies the transformative power of shared vision, strategic leadership, and cross-sectoral teamwork.
In this session, you’ll discover:
🔍 How BEATS advanced scientific knowledge while serving real-world needs
🤝 What made its partnerships thrive across disciplines and institutions
🧭 Key lessons in leadership, adaptability, and long-term sustainability
🚀 Insights to inspire your own collaborative projects and research endeavours
Whether you're in education, policy, research, or community development, this talk offers a compelling blueprint for building impactful, resilient collaborations.
Explore the full story at AGILE Research – BEATS Programme
About Sandy
Dr Sandra Mandic, PhD, PMP is a transformational leader, innovator and award-winning researcher and author. Sandra’s personal and professional journey spans nine cities across five countries and three continents – including Europe, Canada, United States and New Zealand. She speaks four languages and has experience of working in academia, government and business sectors. Sandra was the founder and lead researcher on the award-winning BEATS Research Programme (2013-2023). She is also the founder and the director of the research consultancy AGILE Research Ltd. and the creator of the Compass Guide Research Training resources which currently include four books and over dozen research training and project management courses.
More information about Dr Mandic’s background and the link to her brief curriculum vitae:
https://agileresearch.nz/about-the-author/

Treasury Guest Lecture with Prof. Shiro Armstrong: IN-PERSON attendance, Treasury Guest Lecture with Prof. Shiro Armstrong: IN-PERSON attendance
Asia’s multilateral coalition for defence of the trading system

About this Event

Join us for the next lecture in our new seminar series
The rules-based trading system was designed to avert a repeat of the 1930s spiral of protectionism and conflict by anchoring trade in enforceable, non-discriminatory rules. That architecture—centred on the GATT/WTO—expanded prosperity and reduced the risks that arise when commerce becomes hostage to power politics. Today, outdated rules, weakened enforcement and growing willingness to bypass multilateral constraints are narrowing cooperation to trusted partners. In response, governments are adopting “second-best” economic security strategies—friendshoring, reshoring, industrial policy and selective restrictions—that can make sense individually but, in aggregate, accelerate fragmentation, slow growth and raise the costs of decarbonisation.
Asia is emerging as a pivotal coalition-builder for defending the trading system. ASEAN’s convening role, the scale and openness of RCEP and CPTPP, and the spread of workarounds such as the WTO’s Multi-Party Interim Appeal Arbitration Arrangement provide practical platforms to keep rules credible, markets open, and disputes manageable even in a more contested order. The coalition agenda is pragmatic: lock in equal treatment where possible, develop regional “pathfinder” rules on subsidies and security exceptions, and pursue mutual restraint and disarmament of economic weaponry—so that competition remains rules-based rather than coercive.

About this event
This will be a hybrid event. Please use this site to register if you plan to attend it in person.
If you would like to attend it virtually, please use THIS LINK to register.

About the presenter
Shiro Armstrong is Professor of Economics and Director of International Partnerships at the Crawford School of Public Policy at The Australian National University. He is Director of the Australia-Japan Research Centre, Editor of the East Asia Forum, and Director of the East Asian Bureau of Economic Research.
He is also a Visiting Professor at Keio University, Research Associate at the Center on Japanese Economy and Business at the Columbia Business School, Non-resident Fellow at the Research Institute of Economy, Trade and Industry, Japan and Research Associate at the New Zealand APEC Study Centre. Shiro is the recipient of the 2024 Nakasone Yasuhiro Award.
Professor Armstrong is a member of the Board of the Australia Japan Foundation and is on the Academic Advisory Council of the Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia (ERIA).

About this seminar series
New ideas, robust evidence, and insights from leading thinkers are crucial to strengthening the Treasury’s economic analysis and policy advice. Our new guest lecture theme — Navigating Global Shifts: Resilience, Challenges and Opportunities for New Zealand — invites us to reflect on how Aotearoa New Zealand can navigate an increasingly complex and interconnected global environment.
This series explores the major global forces that shape our economic landscape, including evolving trade relationships, geopolitical developments, and the global movement of people, capital, and ideas. Through these discussions, we aim to deepen our understanding of how New Zealand can build economic resilience, respond effectively to uncertainty, and harness our regional and international partnerships to support economic performance, productivity, and our living standards.
Our speakers explore strategies for mitigating the impacts of global disruptions — from pandemics and climate‑related events to geopolitical tensions and supply‑chain shocks – while also examining potential opportunities presented by rapid technological shifts, digital economy, and global innovations, to name a few. The series considers the role of government in supporting economic transitions, strengthening national resilience, and ensuring that New Zealand remains well‑positioned to meet emerging global opportunities. By bringing together diverse perspectives, this series seeks to inspire new ways of thinking about New Zealand’s economic future and to support informed, forward‑looking policymaking.
Please note that the views, opinions, findings, and conclusions expressed in the Treasury Guest Lecture Series are those of the individual presenters. They do not necessarily reflect the views of the New Zealand Treasury or the New Zealand Government.
For updates and our latest research visit: www.treasury.govt.nz

Keep in touch

Wairarapa Agritourism - November networking evening, Join us for another Agritourism networking event !

Wairarapa Agritourism – Exploring our opportunities
November networking evening.
This event is part of our agritourism network series, and is for anyone interested in agritourism within the Wairarapa and surrounding regions. This is a great opportunity to connect with like-minded people and become part of the local agritourism community.
We have two fabulous guest speakers at our November event, who will share their agritourism journeys and thoughts on the future.
Sonia Minnaar
Sonia Minnaar is co-founder of Canopy Camping Escapes. Canopy Camping Escapes partners with glamping hosts across New Zealand. Sonia will talk to us about the foundation and growth of Canopy Camping - how they started, what they do and how they work. We are excited to have Sonia Minnaar joining us for this event!
Their unique collection of hosted accommodation ranges from luxury safari tents to quirky off-grid cabins and modern luxe retreats – all immersed in nature and designed to help guests unplug and reconnect.
Sonia will share her insights around:
Industry trends and industry forecasts
Canopy Camping Guests (repeat/international) and Occupancy
Discussion around what make escapes successful
https://canopycamping.co.nz/
Tim Priest - Moonlight Peak
Tim & Summer Priest have owned the property near Carterton since February 2016. Tim is an Agri-Banker for Rabobank and a farmer. Summer manages Moonlight Peak accommodation, while also being a stay-at-home mum and a farmer.
For them, they love that the property is nestled just on the edge of the Tararua Ranges and overlooks the beautiful Wairarapa - from Mount Bruce all the way to the Cook Strait. It's the type of place where you feel like you're on top of the world, described as "somewhere between heaven and earth"!
The idea to set up glamping on their property came about when they came across Canopy Camping Escapes - and were inspired to set up their own retreat. Watching the moon and sunrise from the east above the Wairarapa is magical...and it's a delight for Summer and Tim to share it with their guests.
https://canopycamping.co.nz/moonlight-peak
