description:
Wellington - Building Science Summit New Zealand 2026, Wellington - Building Science Summit New Zealand 2026
Leading industry experts share practical insights and proven principles for advancing building envelope design and construction practices.

About this Event

Welcome to the Building Science Summit New Zealand 2026 in Wellington!
Join us on Wednesday 4 March 2026 at Te Papa, Wellington for a day filled with insightful discussions and networking opportunities. Bringing together leading industry experts from Aotearoa, Australia, Germany, and Canada to share practical insights and proven principles for advancing building envelope design and construction practices. Don't miss out on this exciting opportunity to connect with like-minded individuals and expand your knowledge.

Key Highlights:
Insights from international and local experts
In-depth discussions on building performance and durability
Case studies showcasing real-world solutions
Networking with industry leaders and peers

We are excited to welcome leading building science experts from New Zealand, Australia, Germany, and Canada. Including Brian Hubbs, Hartwig Künzel, Jess Clarke, Stijn Van den Eeden and Bernard Farrington.
Valid for 60 NZIA CPD Points.

We look forward to seeing you there!

Sponsors:
Nuralite, Oculus Building Science & Façades, Pro Clima, Outright Continuous Insulation, ROCKWOOL


Agenda


🕑: 07:50 AM - 08:20 AM
Registration

🕑: 08:20 AM - 08:30 AM
Opening message
Host: Peter Raimondo

🕑: 08:30 AM - 09:30 AM
TBA
Host: Bernard Farringon
Info: Bernard Farrington is a Laboratory Manager at Shelby Wright Test Labs while also working as a Senior Specialist at Oculus Architectural Engineering. He specialises in building enclosure performance, testing, and practical detailing, combining hands-on technical experience with consulting expertise to support high-performance construction and improved building outcomes.


🕑: 09:30 AM - 10:30 AM
TBA
Host: Stijn Van den Eeden
Info: Stijn has 25 years of experience in external envelopes and was involved in the design and construction of projects on 5 continents, before settling in New Zealand 15 years ago. His expertise includes building materials, façade system development, project delivery and remedial work.


🕑: 10:30 AM - 11:00 AM
Morning Tea Break

🕑: 11:00 AM - 12:00 PM
TBA
Host: Jess Clarke
Info: Jesse Clarke holds more than 15 years of experience in the construction industry. He holds the technical lead role of the Innovation and R&D Manager, servicing pro clima in New Zealand and Australia. Jesse is an active advocate for a holistic approach to the development of industry guidance, standards and codes.


🕑: 12:00 PM - 01:00 PM
Lunch Break + Networking

🕑: 01:00 PM - 02:00 PM
TBA
Host: Hartwig M. Künzel
Info: Prof. Hartwig M. Künzel is Head of the Hygrothermics Department at the Fraunhofer Institute for Building Physics (IBP) in Germany and an Honorary Professor at the University of Stuttgart. With a PhD in Civil Engineering, he has led pioneering research on heat and moisture transport in building envelopes for over three decades. Prof. Künzel is the creator of the internationally recognised WUFI hygrothermal simulation model and has contributed extensively to building standards and best practices for moisture control, energy efficiency, and indoor comfort. He has authored hundreds of publications and is a sought-after speaker at international conferences, sharing expertise that bridges scientific research and practical application in building physics.


🕑: 02:00 PM - 03:00 PM
TBA
Host: Brian Hubbs
Info: Brian Hubbs is a Founder, Principal, and Senior Building Science Specialist at RDH Building Science. With over 30 years of experience as a consultant practicing exclusively in the field of building science, he is a practical façade engineer and researcher. He has broad experience with a variety of building enclosure systems, delivering consistent innovative solutions. Brian brings a unique blend of theoretical and hands-on knowledge gained from designing façades for new buildings, as well as completing hundreds of forensic investigations, rehabilitation, and research projects. He has extensive experience with high-rise and iconic façade systems, components, and materials, designing new and innovative facade systems for high-rise wood and Passive House projects.

description:
Westpac Smarts: Beyond the AI Hype, Overview




Beyond the AI Hype: A 90-Day Practical Framework to Automate the Drudge and Protect Your Relationships.
Every Wellington business leader is hearing the same message: "Adopt AI or get left behind." But if you run a mid-market firm, a family business, or a non-technical organisation, the reality looks quite different. You do not have a corporate-sized budget, and you do not have an in-house Chief Technology Officer (CTO) to navigate the noise.
The good news? The best AI tools are no longer reserved for enterprise giants. The challenge is knowing exactly where to start to see a measurable return on investment without risking your most valuable asset: your customer relationships.
Join Asa Cox, CEO and Founder of Arcanum AI, for a highly practical session designed specifically for non-corporate business owners. Asa views AI not as a replacement for human capability, but as an "e-bike" the technology provides the propulsion, but your team still steers the route.
In this session, you will discover:
The 90-Day SMB Framework: A step-by-step roadmap to move from "we should look into AI" to clear operational deployment.
Eating the Drudge, Keeping the Relationship: How to deploy AI as a researcher, translator, and workflow amplifier to eliminate painful administrative boilerplate, while freeing your team to focus on client-facing, high-value work.
The "Goldilocks" Use Case: How to identify problems that are big enough to deliver real ROI (in finance, operations, or quoting), but small enough that they do not disrupt your core business.
No CTO Required: Practical steps to implement secure, private AI solutions using your existing staff and basic digital hygiene.
This is not a high-level futurist presentation or a generic tutorial on how to use ChatGPT. It is a down-to-earth briefing for business leaders who want to cut through the hype, reduce operational friction, and drive profitable growth.

Christine Douglas and Chris Benham from The Village Goldsmith will share the journey behind Floeting®, a world-first diamond setting technology developed in Wellington that’s a step away from traditional claws and clasps, allowing the diamond to appear to float.

Hear how this bold idea evolved into an inspiring story of global innovation, forged a landmark partnership with Tiffany & Co., and scaled to more than 50 countries - all while keeping design and IP anchored in Wellington.

How lower interest rates and policy changes are shaping buyer and investor behaviour

This session will provide a clear-eyed view of the risks, realities, and opportunities emerging in 2026, cutting through the noise with evidence-led insights and practical context.

description:
YEPN Wellington - Sustainable Aviation Fuel: A Strategic Approach, The Young Energy Professionals Network is pleased to invite you to our next Wellington event, proudly hosted by Z Energy at their waterfront offices.
This event will feature a panel discussion on one of the toughest – and most important – challenges in the energy transition: decarbonising aviation through Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF)*.
Aviation is one of the most challenging sectors to decarbonise and by 2050, it could contribute more than a third of Aotearoa New Zealand’s total emissions. Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is emerging as a critical decarbonisation tool, and momentum is building both locally and globally.
In this session, we’ll bring together voices from across the aviation ecosystem – industry leaders, suppliers and customers – to explore how SAF is being adopted, scaled and supported in Aotearoa and overseas. From feedstocks and policy settings to operational realities and investment signals, we’ll unpack what’s driving demand, what barriers remain, and where the biggest opportunities lie.
Whether you're curious about the technology, the economics, or the practicalities of adoption, this is your chance to take a deep dive into an important fuel in the energy transition.
Panelists include:
Julian Hughes, GM Supply, Z Energy
Billie Moore, Chief Executive, NZ Airports Association
Peter van Cingel, Business Development Manager, Channel Infrastructure NZ

Drinks and nibbles provided
Spaces are limited — register below to secure your spot.
* 'Sustainable Aviation Fuel' is an industry term used to describe fuels manufactured using waste and purpose grown feedstocks, including used cooking oil (UCO), tallow and canola oil, and can provide carbon emissions reductions on a life cycle basis.

description:
'WOMB WOMEN' Workshop for Women, IMAGINE...100 THOUSAND GRANDMOTHERS SPANNING BACK THROUGH 2.5 MILLION YEARS OF HUMANITY. ONE WOMAN GIVING BIRTH TO THE NEXT, ON AND ON THROUGH TIME, UNTIL HERE AND NOW.

This is AN INVITATION TO COME PLAY, to create with your own hands little Womb Women in honour of your own matriarchal lineage … with hands that have been created from the DNA of all your ancestors before you.
As I sit and sculpt each woman, I become deeply aware that the bone and flesh of my own hands hold the DNA of all my grandmothers. How many of them had their own stories of shaping clay, forming sculptural figures, moulding pots .. what was it my grandmother of 200 thousand years ago created I wonder. 
Through the evolution of humanity, the hands of approximately 100 thousand womb to womb women of my unique bloodline have given birth to my own. Our shared DNA forms these hands which are now shaping clay.
Each one of us has our own special womb to womb lineage, with a unique tone particular only to us, perhaps similar to another, however no one female whakapapa is truly the same.  
Perhaps you will have a particular mother or grandmother in mind as you create, imbuing their passed down wisdom into the clay figurine, perhaps the little woman you make will symbolize your entire line, calling up the flavour of your own unique lineage, or perhaps she is you and represents your own story … or maybe she will hold for you the wisdom of the ancient mother that resides within us all. 
DO COME JOIN US for an afternoon of making your own little womb women.
NO EXPERIENCE NEEDED, simply bring a curiosity and willingness to play, surrounded by other humans doing just the same.
PRACTACALITIES,
bring a cushion and blanket (you may prefer to sit comfortably on the floor as you make - there will also be tables and chairs available)
if you are already familiar with clay and have your own favorite hand tools please feel free to bring these
snacks and hot/cold beverages will be available
Workshop cost includes supplies, materials and firing. I will fire your creation then post it back to you, therefore postage will be extra and determined once packaged up.
PLEASE NOTE!!! This booking is for FRIDAY 5TH SEPTEMBER
                                              ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
“Within the DNA is written not only our histories as individuals but the whole history of the human race … patterns of DNA that have come down to us virtually unchanged from our distant ancestors – ancestors who are no longer just an abstract entity but real people who lived in conditions very different from those we enjoy today, who survived them and brought up their children.” ~ Bryan Sykes (The Seven Daughters of Eve)

description:
1835 Workshop with Tessa Russell, Last year Tessa began making full size one off polaroids, each held in a metal case that has been stamped with 1835, the year that He Whakaputanga was signed. She started this series in a state of frustration as “three privileged men who grew up in Aotearoa rapidly erase any progress we have made as a country over the last 189 years” but also out of hope as an act of resistance. She says that “while the images displayed in these wearable pieces may slowly disappear, the facts in our history will remain.” 
During this workshop, you will be guided by Tessa to create your own wearable artwork. Our hope is that you will take it out of the gallery and into the world—these are made to be worn, not stored. 
We ask that you wear this on Tuesday 21 October, the day He Whakaputanga was signed 190 years ago. Learn about He Whakaputanga through resources at Enjoy and by taking a tour of He Tohu at the National Library of New Zealand Te Puna Mātauranga o Aotearoa. When people ask you what your 1835 artwork is about, tell them about this kaupapa and put the responsibility back on them to educate themselves about He Whakaputanga. 
All materials and light refreshments will be provided.
This workshop is held during the first day of Chapter 5: Tessa Russell Waitirohia and George Turner, Under the Pasture. Read more here.

description:
2026 Wellington POCUS Fundamentals Course / EGLS Course, POCUS Fundamentals + EGLS
2 Days of Comprehensive POCUS education for Acute Care Clinicians
Take part in a flexible learning experience designed for real-world acute care:
Day 1: POCUS Fundamentals
Master the essentials – focus on AAA & eFAST.
Day 2: EGLS (Echo Guided Life Support)
Confidently assess and manage the shocked patient using focused cardiac and lung ultrasound.
Attend either day independently, or combine both for a complete acute care ultrasound experience.

Day 1 – POCUS Fundamentals
Focus on essential diagnostic ultrasound skills with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm (AAA) & eFAST (extended Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma) modules. This is ideal for clinicians seeking to build confidence and competence in core applications that can be immediately applied in clinical practice.
https://www.emugs.org/pocusfundamentals
Day 2 – EGLS (Echo-Guided Life Support)
Take your resuscitation skills to the next level with EGLS. Learn a structured, protocolised approach to using cardiac and lung ultrasound in the assessment and management of shock and respiratory failure. This course is designed to empower acute care clinicians with the practical skills to make rapid, life-saving decisions.
https://www.emugs.org/egls
Combo of Fundamentals + EGLS - Whether you're new to ultrasound or looking to enhance your skills, this comprehensive two-day course  is ideal for acute care clinicians aiming to integrate POCUS into daily practice.
You'll cover the core emergency medicine ultrasound modules: FELS, eFAST, AAA, and lung. The course aligns with ACEM and ASUM credentialing requirements for core ultrasound modalities.
By the end, you'll be proficient in four essential techniques: focused echo in life support (FELS), extended FAST, aortic scanning, and lung/thoracic ultrasound.
The program includes online pre-course work, brief lectures, image review, hands-on scanning, and networking opportunities—all within a supportive learning environment.
Suitable for all experience levels:
ACEM trainees beginning their ultrasound journey
Acute care doctors looking to upskill
Clinicians in critical care, rural, and urgent care settings
Beginners will build a solid foundation; experienced users can refine skills with expert feedback

description:
5 Days Figure Sculpting Workshop With Model, Working with a live model offers artists an invaluable opportunity to engage directly with the human form. The immediacy of the model’s presence encourages close observation and instinctive decision-making, leading to work that is expressive and real. This hands-on interaction brings a sense of movement and authenticity that’s hard to achieve otherwise.

The sculpting process typically starts by analyzing the model’s proportions and pose. A wire armature is built to support the structure, and clay is gradually applied to develop the form to a one-third life size, 750mm tall figure. From there, the artist refines the shapes focusing on anatomical accuracy and expressive detail that give the sculpture its final character.

Please visit the website to know more about the event.

With nearly 30 years of experience in traditional sculpture and the film industry, Javier is not just a sculptor — he’s a mentor. Trained in classical techniques, he studied fine arts and took anatomy courses at medical school, developing a rare combination of artistic and anatomical knowledge. He spent over five years at the world-renowned Weta Workshop, contributing to major films and exhibitions, and has worked across materials, scales, and digital technologies.

Material is included in the price.

Armature is supplied during the workshop.

You can buy our tools during the workshop if you like.

Tea, Coffee & snacks will be available.

We do share meals during the workshop.

description:
6-12 In person PLD, 6-12 In person PLD
The story of Communication and Signs is one of the five great stories which scaffold the learning in Montessori classrooms for the 6-12 year old child. It traces the beginnings of human communication and the development of writing.

How can we as educators encourage writing in our Montessori environments and ensure collaborations and an understanding of the basic writing processes, bring success and enthusiasm to the telling of powerful stories?

What are some of the stumbling blocks for children when researching? How can we provide strategies and structure to enable lively and informative information writing?

In this day-long face to face workshop, with a focus on guidance for narrative and information writing, participants will be invited into the world of learning to write. Strategies and exercises to stimulate interest and action for writers will be given, alongside challenges and advanced crafting lessons for more fluent writers in 6-9 and 9-12 classrooms. We will examine elements of structuring, elaboration, character and place, revision, and author techniques. Note taking and writing for research will be included in an information writing session.

Day 2: Sunday 14th September
Come prepared to share your collective wisdom while we align NZC History curriculum to what we do in our classrooms to ensure that everything is covered. By September we will also have a better idea of where the conventional system is headed with the new-look maths coming out. We will spend time unpacking the the WHY we do what we do.

This is an opportunity for you to discuss, share ideas and gain ideas for ways forward.

description:
A man of many parts: Isaac ‘Petatone’ Featherston — Part of Friends of the Turnbull Public Programme, Come along to this talk by historian and author John E. Martin to hear more about the life and work of Isaac Featherston, also known as Petatone, and his impact on colonial Aotearoa New Zealand.
Join us at the Library or online. Register for a Zoom link: https://dia-nz.zoom.us/.../WN_5PtO5NngRl2QyE4waFIhCw...
A lasting influence on Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington
John E. Martin, the author of Isaac Featherston — 'Petatone’: A Colonial Life, argues that Isaac Featherston (known to Māori as ‘Petatone’) was the most influential person in the development of the Wellington region from the 1840s to the 1860s.
Arriving as a ship's surgeon in 1841 and struggling with the lifelong affliction of tuberculosis, Isaac Featherston (1813–1876) was a doctor, newspaper editor, and a politician.
Come along to this Friends of the Turnbull talk to learn more about Featherson’s involvement with Māori, including land sales and with kūpapa during the New Zealand Wars. His story reveals the struggles of settlers and Māori in the colonial era, and the conflicts that followed.
A Friends of the Turnbull Library event
The Friends of the Turnbull Library, Ngā Hoa o te Whare Pukapuka Turnbull, offers a monthly programme of free public talks. These talks are held in the National Library in Wellington and on Zoom. Some of these talks will be repeated in Auckland. The public programme highlights the work of researchers who draw on Turnbull material for their projects and staff who care for and research the collections.

description:
AI Masterclass: Going Further with AI, AI Masterclass: Going Further with AI
(NZ Citizens and residents pay $250 with ID.)
You’ve been using AI for a while – maybe daily. You know how to prompt. But you’re still doing one-shot chats when your work deserves a proper system. This masterclass changes that.
Before you arrive, you’ll fill in a short intake form – what you do, what you want AI for, and what you can’t do (paste client data into public ChatGPT, work outside regulated tools, etc.). Jon reads every submission before class and shapes the day around the room. We won’t be doing a generic feature tour; the day is built to be a hands-on and customised workshop.
We’ll spend the day wiring AI into your actual work: the Claude desktop app, connectors to the tools you already use, a project built around your real documents and tasks, and Claude Design. You’ll leave with a working AI system to improve your life and work.
By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:
•     Set up the Claude desktop app with Chat, Co-work, and Code – ready for real work
•     Enable and use connectors (Gmail, Drive, calendar) – and know which ones to leave off
•     Build a Claude project around your own documents and tasks, with voice input and plan mode
•     Write operating rules for your workspace – constraints, verification triggers, what never goes in public chat
•     Discover and run Anthropic-provided skills on your real task
•     Stress-test your output with synthetic personas before you ship
•     Produce polished visual artifacts with Claude Design
•     Apply professional judgement: when to delegate, when to verify, when not to use AI at all
 Please bring: A laptop (Co-work and Code need a keyboard). The Claude desktop app installed and signed in. A paid Claude subscription (Pro or Team) – required for connectors, Co-work, and skills. Your intake form submitted at least 3 days before class. One real task you want to work on.
  A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

description:
AI, Information Protection, and 6 Practical Changes You Can Make Now, AI use is accelerating across Microsoft 365 – often faster than information controls, protection settings, and governance models are keeping up.
This practical, in‑person workshop is designed for people responsible for information, privacy, risk, or digital platforms who want to make progress without big budgets, new tools, or long programmes.
We’ll focus on what has genuinely shifted over the past 12 months, what’s working in real environments, and the low‑cost, high‑impact changes organisations can implement immediately to improve information management and privacy posture.
What the session covers
1. AI Autoclassification in practice
A grounded update on what’s actually working with AI Autoclassification (AIAC): what has matured, where organisations are getting caught out, and what to stop overthinking. We’ll share real‑world patterns from live environments, not theory.
2. Information Protection as AI use increases
Not policy theory. How protection, sensitivity, and access controls need to evolve in practice as AI becomes embedded in everyday work – and where many environments remain exposed.
3. Low‑cost, high‑impact changes you can make now
Practical configuration and governance moves that significantly improve information management and privacy posture, using the tools you already have.
What to expect
Real‑world patterns from live NZ environments
Practical examples, short exercises, and open Q&A
Grounded in New Zealand regulatory and organisational realities
No charge, no fluff – just things you can actually use
Who should attend
This session is for CIOs, risk and privacy leaders, Information Managers, and digital platform owners – particularly those working in high‑compliance or regulated environments – who want practical progress without adding unnecessary complexity.
What you'll get
You’ll leave with a clear, practical plan to manage and protect information as AI use accelerates – without big budgets or long programmes. This workshop focuses on what has genuinely changed over the past 12 months, what’s working in real environments, and the low‑cost configuration and governance changes you can implement immediately to reduce risk and manual effort. Grounded in New Zealand organisational and regulatory realities, everything shared is designed to be used straight away.

description:
AWE Partnership Masterclass for Violists and Violinists with Yura Lee, Join us for a Masterclass!
As part of our 2025 partnership with At the World’s Edge Festival, Orchestra Wellington will host AWE 2025 Festival Artist Yura Lee to present a masterclass for violinists and violists in Wellington.
Anyone can register to attend and observe the masterclass!
Visit https://orchestrawellington.co.nz/event/awe-masterclass-2025 to register to attend and observe the masterclass for FREE!
Violinist/violist Yura Lee is a multifaceted musician, as a soloist and as a chamber musician, and one of the very few that is equally virtuosic on both violin and viola. Her career spans three decades and takes her all over the world, captivating audiences through various musical mediums from baroque to modern, and enjoying a career that spans three decades and takes her all over the world. She has performed with major orchestras including those of New York, Chicago, Baltimore, Cleveland, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and given recitals in London’s Wigmore Hall, Vienna’s Musikverein, Salzburg’s Mozarteum, the Palais des BeauxArts in Brussels, and the Concertgebouw in Amsterdam.
At age 12, she became the youngest artist ever to receive the Debut Artist of the Year prize at the Performance Today awards given by National Public Radio. She is the recipient of a 2007 Avery Fisher Career Grant; she has received numerous other international prizes, including top prizes in the Mozart, Indianapolis, Hannover, Kreisler, Bashmet, and Paganini competitions. Yura Lee was the only first prize winner awarded across four categories at the 2013 ARD Competition in Germany.
An Incredible Partnership with At The World's Edge Festival!
As part of our 2025 partnership with At the World’s Edge (AWE) Festival, Orchestra Wellington is presenting a three-part series featuring AWE 2025 Festival Artist Yura Lee and AWE Artistic Director Benjamin Baker for a mini-series of concerts and a masterclass here in Wellington in addition to featuring these incredible artists' live performances with us on our subscription series concerts in September and October!

description:
Acing The Interview, Acing The Interview
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
People have skills which they want to offer to employers, however, low confidence and anxiety combined with a lack of interview experience results in them not gaining employment.
'Acing The Interview' is a 3-module one day workshop that provides practical, cutting-edge tools and techniques to prepare participants to 'Ace the Interview'.
The 3 modules are:
1. Resourceful You - Think
2. Managing You - Feel
3. Acing the Interview - Do
Explore how to manage your thoughts under pressure and control your critical voice. Understand how to manage anxiety and stress. Demonstrate your interview skills and use body language and well-formed responses to create a powerful and positive first impression.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
-  Manage your thoughts and critical voice under pressure
-  Visualise and mentally rehearse for success
-  Recognise your emotional reactions and manage your emotions under pressure
-  Utilise techniques to manage anxiety
-  Demonstrate interview skills and deliver well-formed responses to questions
-  Understand the STAR model and other communication techniques and how and when to use them
Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Thurs 12th March (7pm-9pm)
Thurs 19th March (7pm-9pm)

Relive the golden age of gaming by building your very own Arcade Emulation Console, complete with high-quality push buttons and joystick—just like the classic arcade cabinets you grew up with. The console runs "Batocera" on a built in Raspberry Pi board that connects easily to your TV or Projector.

Over three, hands-on sessions, you’ll:
- Assemble and wire your custom console using a Raspberry Pi Zero 2
- Choose the colours and look of your console to make it uniquely yours
- Install a wide selection of retro games (with instructions to add many more later)
- Learn how to connect to your TV via HDMI and power it up with the included USB power supply

By the end, you’ll take home your own fully functional arcade console—perfect for reliving your misspent youth (sadly, no fish 'n' chips included).

All materials, tools, and guidance provided. Just bring your nostalgia.

Only 6 Students Per Class.

You will learn the tools required, the basic technique of through-hole soldering, as well as assembling a small project you can take home with you. Along the way we will introduce the most common electronic components and their function.

Only 6 Students Per Class.

No experience is required. A great introduction class before tackling some of our larger projects.

Adult Class - LED Neon Sign, 4 Weeks
Mon 18th May 7pm-9pm
Mon 25th May 7pm-9pm
Mon 8th June 7pm-9pm
Mon 15th June 7pm-9pm

OR

4 Weeks
Mon 22nd June 7pm-9pm
Mon 29th June 7pm-9pm
Mon 6th July 7pm-9pm
Mon 13th July 7pm-9pm

During this course everyone will get to design and build their own awesome LED Neon Sign. The sign can be up to 50cm x 40cm and there are a range of colours available.

The design for the sign will be completed using the open source program 'Inkscape'. The frame will then be cut out of clear acrylic using our laser cutter.

The neon strip can be cut and soldered together to make sharp corners or bent into reasonably tight curves as shown in the images. Once all the neon pieces are positioned they will be glued then soldered together and powered by a standard 12 Volt wall adaptor (which is provided). There is also the option of incorporating a small dimmer circuit that allows you to control the brightness of your sign.

Only 6 Students Per Class.

Some prior soldering experience would be beneficial.

description:
Advanced Claw Setting in Two Days, This two-day class will run on two Sundays, 24 and 31 August, 10am - 1pm. It is designed for advanced students and focuses on teaching a range of claw setting techniques, along with straightforward construction methods to securely hold gemstones of various shapes and sizes. The emphasis is on mastering the techniques rather than creating polished, finished jewellery pieces.
Students are encouraged to bring along their own particular tools, metal and stones if they would like to. They can also bring their own half made ring shanks or other projects to set into.
They will start by creating claw settings for flat-bottomed stones on plate to gain an understanding of how claws work.
Students will then move on to faceted stones and be shown how to construct their own settings in a number of styles, and how to secure their stones in settings. Finally, they will be taught the dos and don’ts of finishing settings to a salable level.
The workshop will also look at how to use pre-made claw settings to best advantage.
Workshop fee $245, Early bird $221 till 27 July.
label: Classes & Workshops

description:
Advanced Flush Setting in Two Days, Advanced Flush Setting in Two Days
This workshop is ideal for advanced students who have already learned how to set cabochon stones. Over two three-hour sessions, 20 and 27 September, 10am-1pm, you will be given an understanding of the technique of setting faceted stones using a setting burr, hammers, punches and burnishing tools. This is the first step in learning to flush set facet cut stones so they sit below the surface of the metal.

Session 1 will cover the technique, demonstrations and the basics of preparing and cutting the setting. Students will be shown how to set their stones, and may begin to do this in class, but will then go on to repeat and practice the technique in their own time.
They can do this at home, or for a small extra cost, can stay on at the studio to practice setting for the afternoon.

Session 2 will pick up on the setting techniques, reminding and refining essential steps in the process. Troubleshooting can be covered in this class, as well as learning to clean up the settings. The principles of this setting technique will be covered in a few different scenarios, as some students may wish to take this skill into different styles or directions.

The option for students to have a half-day bench hire after class will also apply to this session.

What is provided: class fees cover your practice metal (copper) and stones (CZ) and detailed handouts that are useful for you to take away to refer to when practising and honing your skills.

Correctly sized drills and setting burrs will be provided in class, but students must purchase their own burrs for practice after class and any future bench hires. These are available for purchase in the studio.

What to bring: Advanced students can bring projects to set stones into, but please note the metal must be at least 2mm thick and we do not allow brass to be used as a project or practice for beginners. The metal must be copper or sterling silver.

Students should bring either a craft magnifier or magnifying lenses/glasses. If you have your own flex shaft tool you plan to use at home for drilling and setting, please also bring this along so that your tutor can advise on the best way to use it. We have two drilling machines in the studio, and these must be shared between the students, so if you have a machine, do bring it.

Practice bench hire after class $20 per person (till 4pm) must be booked in advance.

Workshop fee $195, Early bird $175 till 24 August.
label: Classes & Workshops

description:
Advanced Stone Setting: Stepped Bezel in 3 sessions, This workshop is ideal for intermediate-advanced students who have already learned basic soldering and how to bezel set cabochon stones.

A stepped bezel is a beautiful way to set faceted stones, creating a clean, elevated frame that both protects and highlights the gem. In our three-part Stepped Bezel Setting Class, students will learn the complete process of designing and fabricating stepped bezels using sparkling cubic zirconias in copper.

Designed for jewellers looking to refine their fabrication and setting skills, this hands-on workshop explores how to create clean, professional stepped bezels for faceted stones. Students will learn techniques for measuring, constructing, soldering, and setting with accuracy, while gaining a deeper understanding of stone fit and bezel design.

This is a technique class where you will learn techniques to practice in your own time or in regular block classes.

This class will run over 3 separate 3hr sessions and is working towards creating a simple band ring with a stepped bezel.

Session 1 will cover the technique, demonstrations and the basics of measuring and preparing the setting. Students will design their piece and begin the construction.

Session 2 will pick up on the setting techniques, reminding and refining essential steps in the process. Students can expect to be soldering in this class.

Session 3: Troubleshooting can be covered in this class, as well as learning to clean up the settings. Students may begin a second setting that they can continue in their own time.

We will be working in copper for this class ( silver is available for purchase, but we recommend making your first project in copper first). Students should expect to have at least one completed set project and possibly some other practice pieces begun by the end of the three classes.

What is provided: class fees cover your practice metal (copper) and stones (CZ) and detailed handouts that are useful for you to take away to refer to when practicing and honing your skills.

description:
Aerial Arts Silks Practical, IN PERSON, Wellington, NZ, Aerial Arts Silks Practical, IN PERSON, Wellington, NZ
Aerial Arts starts at the very beginning, teaching instructors everything they need to know about correct placement and technique so their students will have the building blocks to progress safely from one level to the next.

Aerial Arts Teacher Training and Certification courses provide extensive training in spotting and progression so the teachers feel confident, knowledgeable and inspired to teach Aerial Arts.

This course is offered in person and delivers the hands-on spotting and instruction of the syllabus from Primary to Level 6. For this course, you will be required to attend in person. Demonstrators will be provided by the host studio: you are welcome to bring a student of your own.

During the course you will:

-Learn to spot and teach the 7 levels of Aerial Arts syllabus; Primary - Level 6 including Strength, Technique, Balance, Drops / Slides, and Climbing

-Understand the teaching and spotting requirements of each level

-Learn how to safely teach and spot each skill in the syllabus

-Review anatomy and stability exercises to assist in the training of Aerial Arts

-Review safety and rigging tips for Aerial Arts

-Review how to maintain your apparatus

-Learn how to implement Aerial Arts lesson plans

Pre-requisites:

Teachers must have successfully completed Aerial Arts Silks Theory prior to attending this course.

Teachers must be a minimum of 16 years old to attend the course. Full certification will not be granted until the teacher turns 18.

Assuming successful completion of the exams, the teacher will be granted ‘Assistant Teacher’ status from age 16-17 and can teach classes with a certified teacher in the same room. Upon turning 18, full certification will automatically be granted.

Info + registration: https://www.acrobaticarts.com/training-courses/silks-practical-in-person/1801

description:
An Introduction to Zine Making, In this workshop you will be guided in making a classic cut and fold 8-page zine from a standard A4 sheet of paper - this is a clever design you can easily photocopy and reproduce later! You will be introduced to a range of techniques and approaches such as cut and paste photos and text, collage and drawing on paper.
If you’re keen to make more zines and share them with the world, there's a broad and growing community of Zine-makers and traders, as well as the well-attended annual Wellington Zinefest!
Paper, newspapers, magazines and basic drawing materials will be provided. We recommend you bring along a sketch book and any favourite drawing materials, newspapers, magazines or other interesting paper material to cut up and collage with in class.
Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
Cut and fold a classic 8-page zine format from a single sheet of paper
Brainstorm content ideas for your personalised zine publications
Arrange & compose text and images to fit a classic 8-page zine layout
Combine cut & paste magazine content with hand drawn/ written content
Create a draft zine of your personal interests

Operating out of his parents’ garage, growing it into a creative enterprise known for one-of-a-kind installations that capture international attention.
Andy’s journey has been one of continual growth and discovery, professionally and personally. Guided by a strong spiritual side and a firm faith in synchronicity and symbolism, he is driven by simple desires:

• To lift the energy in a room
• To design projects that make a positive impact
Through his creations, Andy reminds us that design can be a form of meditation- that, “true magic happens when art, nature, and spirit meet”.
Come along for this immersive and inspiring talk, meet like minded creatives, enjoy a light breakfast and register your spot today.

All materials provided.

Anyone Can Draw - Observational, Learn to create a realistic drawing from what you see. This introductory class teaches the technical skills of observational drawing using a variety of media, including pen and ink, charcoal, pencil and pastel.

Students will learn a range of formal skills through exercises in the following:

- Quality of line
- Accurate observation of shape
- Gesture drawing
- Use of negative and positive shapes
- Using tone well
- Direct observation of spaces such as interiors, buildings or landscapes

With expert guidance from Denise you will learn a broad range of skills that can serve as a basis for advancing into classes in painting and assist and finding your own means of expression.

Eight week course held on Tuesdays evenings, 28 July - 15 Sept, or Wednesday mornings, 29 July - 16 Sept.
Basic materials provided.

You must be at least 16 years of age to attend this course.

description:
Anyone Can Draw - Structural, In this course you will examine structural drawing with a careful helpful approach, focusing on simple perspective drawing and the value of geometric shapes and solids. Both these structural approaches contribute greatly to the success of your drawing.


Geometric shapes can simplify a subject, unify a drawing and make compositions dynamic. Geometric solids will help render any subject in three dimensions and transition to perspective.

A good working knowledge of the concepts of perspective will help you draw any subject with correct dimensionality. It can also help in your realist drawing, painting and invented subjects and environments. These concepts are also used in most two-dimensional art because it enables us to realise great spatial effects, making it an invaluable tool to add to your skill set.

In this course you will learn the following:

- Focus on geometric shapes and solids and how they contribute to both realist and abstract drawing
- Form an appreciation of geometry and shapes that can help with constructing a drawing
- The important tools, methods and concepts of one-point, two-point and three-point perspective
- Universal boxing, drawing ellipses
- Hints in locating helpful lines and axis to draw real subjects
- Introductory methods of working that blend perspective knowledge with real drawing situations

All basic materials supplied.

Eight week course on Wednesday evenings, 29 July - 16 Sept, 6:30 - 8:30 pm and Friday mornings, 31 July - 18 Sept, 10am-1pm.

You must be at least 16 years of age to attend this course.

Andy will guide you through both the practical techniques (composition, light, lines, verticals, details, context, people, dusk shooting, interiors, and more) and the deeper creative side of architectural photography: developing your own way of seeing, storytelling through space, emotion, rhythm, and the relationship between buildings, people, and place. After lunch, we’ll photograph inside Old St Paul’s, applying the same thoughtful approach. The day is followed by an online Zoom session where Andy will set a project and provide image feedback and Photoshop advice—helping you move beyond technical competence toward more meaningful, confident architectural images.

description:
Art History, Art History is a study of visual arts across time and cultures. It involves analysing artworks to understand visual language in its social, historical, political context, values and human expressions. It helps us to develop critical thinking to interpret how visual culture impacts the society and identity.

The focus this term will be as follows:

The first month will cover briefly the Prehistoric, Ancient, Greco- Roman art followed by the Renaissance period, looking at the works of the great masters like Donatello, Ghiberti, Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Raphael, Albrecht Dürer, Jan van Eyck and Hieronymus Bosch.

In the second month we look at Baroque, Rococo, Romanticism briefly, and then study Modern movements like Impressionism, Surrealism, Expressionism & Cubism, looking at artists like Monet, Degas, Manet, Cezanne, Seurat, Van Gogh to name a few. We also hold discussions on Dali, Matisse, Kandinsky, Mondrian, Rothko, Pollock and end with Picasso, among others.

Recommended materials - writing utensil and notebook

description:
Art Therapy for Well-Being: A Canvas for Self-Discovery, Art Therapy for Well-Being: A Canvas for Self-Discovery
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
Sometimes, our minds get stuck in habitual thought loops—endlessly cycling through the same worries, fears, and anxieties without ever finding a breakthrough. When words fall short, art therapy offers a different language. By shifting from thinking to creating, we bypass the noise of everyday stress and tap into an intuitive visual language that can surprise us with fresh insights, new perspectives, and profound meaning.
This workshop is a gentle, immersive introduction to a pathway of self-restoration, self-compassion, and self-worth—the vital foundations for true self-healing.
What you will experience:
A Shift in Perspective: Break free from repetitive thinking by engaging the creative, intuitive side of your brain.
Tools for Daily Coping: Learn how the simple act of making art can become a sanctuary for processing stress and finding grounding.
A Pathway to Wholeness: Explore how visual expression can reveal hidden strengths and foster a deeper sense of self-care.
Important Note: You do absolutely not need to be an artist or have any artistic experience to attend. This day is about the process of expression, not the final product. While this workshop is not a substitute for clinical individual or group therapy, it is a powerful, supportive introduction to the healing power of the arts.
What to Bring:
A journal and a pen or pencil. All other creative materials will be provided.  Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch and snacks and  photo ID.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

description:
Art and AI: Brit Bunkley in Conversation with Megan Dunn, Artist and filmmaker Brit Bunkley discusses the pragmatics and politics of making art with AI. Join us for a discussion in the Gallery, with insights into the making of his latest work Archive, commissioned for Messengers.
--
Brit Bunkley is a New Zealand-based artist and videographer whose practice spans sculpture, installation, and digital media. A recipient of the US National Endowment for the Arts fellowship, two NY state grants, and the Rome Prize Fellowship, his work explores the intersection of physical and virtual spaces, often blending surreal imagery with themes of history, politics, and environmental concerns. He has exhibited at the Museum of New Zealand Te Papa and internationally at Rencontres Internationales Paris/Berlin, FILE São Paulo (including 2025), and the Athens Digital Arts Festival. Recent exhibitions include Visions in the Nunnery, London (2022), Cybersculpture 2024 at Collège des Bernardins, Paris, and The Torrance Art Museum, LA (2025). In 2024, he won Best Art | Experimental Video/Film at the New York City Independent Film Festival. His work continues to evolve, embracing new technologies and alternative methodologies to challenge perceptions of reality and imagination.

description:
Artificial Intelligence past, present and possible futures: It’s not rocket science!, Bruce’s talk takes the audience on a brief tour of the history of Artificial Intelligence (AI), from early cons and ideas through Alan Turing, expert systems, early neural networks, convolutional neural networks used in computer vision, early chatbots, and today’s Large Language Models.
The talk then explores possible future scenarios for AI, including both the opportunities ahead and the significant societal impacts we may face. Audience members are encouraged to bring their questions, concerns, and strong views for the Q&A at the end.
This event is supported by voluntary donations. Please consider making a donation when reserving your ticket.
Biography
Bruce Aylward is originally from South Africa and grew up with computers in the home. He went on to complete a B.Sc. (Hons) in Computer Science.
Fresh out of university, his first role involved programming rockets to launch satellites into low-Earth orbit. His career has taken him to Cape Town, Johannesburg, Tel Aviv, and London, before his final move to New Zealand with his Scottish wife.

description:
Ask an Astrobiologist, Are we alone in the Universe?  Ask a NASA astrobiologist! 
Event Overview
In 2025, we mark a decade of astrobiology in Aotearoa New Zealand—a field of science that asks the biggest questions of all:
How did life begin?
Are we alone in the Universe?
What is our future beyond Earth?
We also mark 150 years of US-NZ scientific partnership. What better way to honour these two milestones than with a public talk by three eminent NASA astrobiologists and science communicators!
Join Dr Sanjoy Som, Dr Graham Lau, and Sarah Marcotte as they tell us about exciting current developments in astrobiology, plus get a chance to ask YOUR burning questions about life, aliens and the Solar System. 
Guest Speakers
🔹 Dr Graham Lau – “The Cosmobiologist”
Dr. Graham Lau, “the Cosmobiologist,” is an astrobiologist, science communicator, and host of NASA’s Ask an Astrobiologist. As Director of Communications at Blue Marble Space, he blends research, outreach, and education, inspiring global audiences. His Arctic geomicrobiology work informs life-detection strategies for Mars, Europa, and beyond.  
🔹 Dr Sanjoy Som
Dr. Sanjoy Som, planetary scientist and founder of the Blue Marble Science Institute of Science, studies planetary environments from early Earth to Mars. His work combines geochemistry, field expeditions, and science communication, fostering global partnerships in astrobiology while inspiring public engagement with the science of planetary habitability.  
🔹 Sarah Marcotte
Sarah Marcotte is NASA STEM Engagement Network lead at JPL, managing the Solar System Ambassadors Program. A specialist in Mars and planetary mission outreach, she makes complex space science engaging for public audiences through events, media, and educational programs.  
Proudly Presented By
New Zealand Astrobiology Network (NZAN)
Victoria University of Wellington
SpacewardBound New Zealand
With generous support from the US Embassy in New Zealand
🎟️ Reserve your seat now and be part of the conversation about life in the Universe!

description:
Astronomy vs. the Billionaire Space Race - Dr Samantha Lawler, University of Regina, RASNZ, WAS and the University of Victoria Wellington are co-hosting this year's Beatrice Hill-Tinsley Lecture.
Time: 6:00 pm, Date: Friday 13 May 2026
Venue: RHLT1, Victoria University Pipitea Campus
Available online via Zoom https://vuw.zoom.us/j/97988322365 if you can’t make it in person, but we strongly encourage in-person attendance for the best experience!
In February 2024, hundreds of pounds of potentially lethal debris from a SpaceX Crew Dragon trunk from a private astronaut mission fell on farmland near Regina, Saskatchewan. Later in the year, a piece of a SpaceX Starlink satellite was found in a lentil field in another part of the province. In September 2025, one of the handful of Starlink satellites reentering every week was witnessed burning up across the entire western half of Canada, with the reentry ending over Saskatchewan.
Dr. Samantha Lawler of the University of Regina has been studying the proliferation of satellites in orbit over the past few years, and has been stunned to learn how often space debris falls so close to her home. Come learn why Saskatchewan is the best place in the world to find space debris, and what happens when you find space debris on your farm and silent SpaceX employees show up in a rented truck to be greeted by an astronomer and a dozen of Saskatchewan's finest local journalists. The billionaire space race is well underway, and this has important implications for international law, the continued operation of satellites in Low Earth Orbit, atmospheric pollution, and the future of astronomy.
Samantha Lawler is a professor of astronomy at the University of Regina in Saskatchewan, Canada. She completed degrees at the California Institute of Technology, Wesleyan University, and the University of British Columbia, followed by postdoctoral fellowships at the University of Victoria (Canada) and NRC-Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre. Her discoveries in the Kuiper Belt and predictions for satellite pollution have been featured by BBC, CBC, CNN, NPR, BBC, Scientific American, The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, Wired Magazine, Nature, and many other international news outlets. She lives on a farm outside Regina and deeply appreciates the beautiful prairie skies.

description:
Astrophotography Masterclass: Capture the Southern Sky, Spend an evening under one of the world’s finest dark skies and learn how to photograph the Milky Way, constellations and deep-sky objects. This immersive masterclass is designed for curious explorers, hobby photographers and anyone who has ever looked up and wished they could capture what they saw.

Your instructor is an experienced astro-educator, and you’ll be taken step by step through the art and science of night-sky photography with DSLR or mirrorless cameras. You’ll learn how to focus at infinity, choose the best camera settings, build compositions under the Milky Way, and work with RAW files, noise control and exposure strategy. You’ll photograph live star fields and leave with images you can genuinely be proud of.

No astronomy expertise or prior astrophotography experience is required — just your curiosity. Bring a camera and tripod if you have them, but if not, you can still attend, learn from telescope-linked imaging feeds, and gain the skills and confidence to shoot the cosmos on your own.

Held at Star Safari, right in the Wairarapa dark-sky heartlands, this experience takes place under the same southern skies recognised by Lonely Planet as one of the world’s top stargazing destinations. If you’ve ever wanted to try astrophotography, this is the moment, and this is the place.

What you’ll gain:
- Confidence to shoot the night sky
- Proven camera settings and workflow
- Real photos of the Milky Way and southern star fields
- Knowledge you can use anywhere the southern sky is visible
- A rare, premium learning experience under a world-class sky

Perfect for couples, travellers, creatives, astronomy lovers, and anyone who wants a deeper connection to the night.

Spaces are limited to keep the experience personal.

description:
August's Nomadic Speaker: Rachel Young, Rachel Young is a freelance graphic designer, traveller, and occasional van-dweller who’s spent the last few years navigating the messy, beautiful reality of creative nomad life.
For Rachel, being a ‘nomad’ has never been just about travel, but a mindset. Since leaving her home in the UK in 2019, she’s moved across the world, worked remotely from a van, taught graphic design in China, and rebuilt her creative career more than once.
Today, she blends her love of design with a passion for helping other creatives navigate the highs, lows, and mindset shifts of freelance life, while inspiring those around her to pursue their own dreams.
In this Friday's talk, she shares the unfiltered truths of freelancing on the move - from creative burnout to financial uncertainty - along with the mindset tools that can make the journey not just survivable, but meaningful and joyful.

description:
Autumn Sandcasting Day, Join us for this wonderful intro to sand casting - it is a great opportunity to make some gorgeous lasting jewellery gifts for yourself or your loved ones!

The class runs from 10am - 4pm and there will be a lunch break.

Students are shown the ancient technique of sand casting, using a wax to make a simple hard model or found objects such as buttons or simple small forms - create your simple 2-part mould and melt and pour sterling silver or shibuichi (a mix of silver and copper) to cast into the sand.

The model you have made or found enables you to make multiple pours possible to create multiple pieces. Best suited to smaller scale items, both to keep the budget down and the amount of weight in a piece this technique can be used to create rings, pendants or small earrings. This is a fun process for those who just want to try their hand at it, or a very useful low-tech process for those who are making jewellery into a career or creative activity. Each student will be given opportunity to cast one or two items, and then time will be included in the day to finish up the pieces so you can wear them away.

This class uses a combination of tutor supervision and also a peer-buddy system so that students are also given opportunity to watch and learn from each other's casts and pours.

The class has a practical health and safety aspect to it as students are introduced to working with an oxy-lpg torch and molten metal.

Course cost does not include silver costs but students can expect to use around $60 - $120 worth of silver or shibuichi.

description:
Autumn Textured Pendants/Earrings, This quick, creative taster class is perfect for a fun outing with friends, a thoughtful gift-making session, or a treat just for you.

In just three hours, you’ll learn to craft a stunning pair of textured metal earrings from scratch. You’ll be guided step-by-step through heating and texturing the metal, then cutting and shaping it with traditional jewellery tools. By the end, you’ll have a beautiful pair of earrings to wear proudly or gift to someone you care about!

You will practice on smaller texture samples to work out what texture and what metal you want to go with, and then move on to creating your earrings in warm copper or yellow brass.

Your class materials pack includes everything you need for the class to make a super cool pair of shiny gorgeous earrings.
Using copper and brass as our main material allows us to have more creative fun and create larger earrings with less expense.

We do have a lovely range of sterling silver sheets that you can purchase as extra if you are committed to working in silver!

We use quality pre-made sterling silver and stainless steel earring hooks and hoops for these taster classes so that you can focus on making the main part of the earrings and know that your findings will be just perfect.

Kids aged 12 (or so) are welcome to attend the class, but an enrolled parent or caregiver must accompany anyone under the age of 16.

description:
Bailamos Bachata! Latin Dance Party (with free lesson), Please note: the event is free but it can only continue if we support the Southern Cross by buying food or drinks

Wellington’s favourite monthly Bachata Latin dance party

Join us for an awesome mix of bachata, focusing on the best sensual tracks and remixes, along with salsa and a smattering of kizomba and zouk. We welcome everyone, from the absolute beginner to the most experienced dancer. We’re all about the joy of social dancing together.
And what makes a free party with great people even better? A free beginners’ bachata lesson with some of Wellington‘s best Latin dance teachers. If you’ve never danced bachata, Latin dance or even any other dance style before then this is the perfect lesson for you. We will have you dancing like a pro in no time!
Bailamos Bachata is hosted free of charge by the Southern Cross. They love the atmosphere we bring but we also need to support them in return. We’re asking everyone attending to purchase soft drinks, food or alcohol from the bar. It’s vital we show our gratitude.
1800-1830 social
1830-1900 free lesson
1900-2100 social
Q&A
Q. What is bachata?
A. Bachata is a popular and fun Latin couples dance. It started in the Dominican Republic, then travelled to Europe and the rest of the world. It now includes a wide range of music styles and dance influences and is still changing and evolving.
Q. I haven’t danced before, is that a problem?
A. Not at all! That’s exactly what the lesson is for – everyone has to start somewhere and we’re a very welcoming crowd for beginners.
Q. Is bachata a difficult dance to learn?
A. Its origins as a party/community dance mean the basics can be learnt quite quickly, so you’ll be enjoying yourself in no time.
Q. Who are the capital bachata collective?
A. We are the combined Wellington dance schools and people teaching bachata and we really want to share this dance with everyone. We love bachata, we love our community and we want to share it with you
￼

description:
Bar Crossing Seminar - Manawatū (Foxton bar), Crossing A Bar? We Can Help
Bar crossings can be one of the trickiest, and riskiest parts of boating in Aotearoa. They change fast, they don’t always play nice, and they’ve caught out even the most experienced skippers. Each year, we see serious incidents and tragedies happening on our bars, so it’s super important to know your stuff before you head out.
That’s where we come in. Join us at Manawatu Marine Boating Club for a free and relaxed seminar. You’ll hear straight from local Coastguard skippers and boating legends who’ll share their real-world tips, local knowledge, and a few stories from the water.

Here’s what we’ll cover (and chat about):

Understanding the local features of your bar
Reading and interpreting the conditions when planning a trip
Getting your boat and your crew bar crossing ready
How to handle your boat while crossing
How to do a bar crossing report (and why it’s worth it)
What to do if things go pear-shaped
It’s interactive – so bring your questions, share your own experiences, and have a yarn with others in the boating community.
Bring your mates too – whether they’re brand new to boating or have been around since the days of paper charts and handheld compasses, there’s something in here that could save a trip… or a life.
 Why it matters:
In 2024, 23% of craft-related drownings happened during bar crossings.
5 lives were lost due to capsizing while crossing a bar.
Older blokes are still the most at-risk – but everyone can make safer choices with the right knowledge (and a lifejacket on).

description:
Beginner's Weekend - Afternoon session, A fabulous and fun introduction to jewellery making over two afternoons, this is our most popular short workshop! Give yourself a gift of a new creative hobby (or maybe even a career?) this spring!

The students start with basic ring making in copper or brass. We begin with ring making as this process teaches students many fundamental techniques in one project, measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting, soldering and finishing are all included in this one ring.

Students will learn how to measure their fingers to get an accurately sized ring, later they will also learn how to take sizing from existing rings. They are shown how to use a jeweller’s saw to cut their metal to the correct length, how to form it up and how to solder.

Then they learn how to shape their rings and finish them up into a wearable piece of jewellery, all in the first class!

In the first session they are also shown how to texture metals, cut and layer shapes, melt balls of silver and other techniques to create decorative elements.

Students can spend their evening thinking about and planning their design in silver for the next day. We encourage them to carefully plan this project and think about how they might make their piece before they begin, including creating drawings and notes. (We always say drawings don’t need to be “good”, they just need to make sense to the student and their tutor!). This project can be another ring, or earrings or pendants. We have a great selection of example pieces in the workshop so they can see what’s achievable in the 3-hour time frame. Sometimes students can make more than one silver piece if they have enough time.

Included in the class fee are copper and brass for practising on, up to 8 grams of sterling silver and all consumables such as sandpaper, solder and chemicals. Extra metals and chains are available for purchase in the studio.

description:
Being Tangata Tiriti: a Pākehā Project Taster #2—Te Whanganui-a-Tara, Being Tangata Tiriti: a Pākehā Project Taster
A one-day workshop exploring the beautiful restorative work of being tangata Tiriti in Aotearoa.
Who can we be for each other?
———————
We live in discombobulating times. And cracks are showing everywhere. So much that we thought was secure is shifting and changing. 
But here in Aotearoa, we have an extraordinary pou—Te Tiriti o Waitangi.
Come along for a day of depth; exploring the amazing potential that the relational space of Te Tiriti has for us all. This one is for tangata Tiriti who are deeply committed to an ethic of restoration in Aotearoa and want to go beyond an intellectual understanding.
Join Rebecca and Mel from The Pākehā Project for this one-day workshop exploring the mahi we as tangata Tiriti can do in the journey towards a Tiriti-led future. Using practices of Haumanu, a healing-centred approach to systems change, we’ll be inquiring into our own roles in reweaving the relational fabric that Te Tiriti o Waitangi offered to all people in Aotearoa, but that did not happen at the time.
We invite you into a space for gently inquiring into your unique place in the system rewiring itself. How do we show up where Māori are calling us to be? We'll be exploring relationality and worldview; the nervous system as map for working with activation; systemic racism, the orthodox Western worldview—its whakapapa and how it shows up in ourselves, our systems and society; and our roles in restorative systems change for a Tiriti-based future. It will be interactive, embodied, and nourishing.
Let's create islands of coherence in this turbulent world.
We'll host you upstairs at Vogelmorn Bowling Club, in the beautiful hills of Brooklyn, Te Whanganui-a-Tara. There'll be delicious kai, and a chance to resource yourself, in communion with others. We are so looking forward to welcoming you.
—————————————————————————
About the facilitators
Rebecca Sinclair (Pākehā—Scottish, English)
Rebecca is a facilitator, coach, and complex systems geek - helping her fellow Pākehā come back into the flow of life, and let go of colonial patterns that separate us from ourselves, each other, and te taiao. She is fascinated by the intangible, the improper and the in-between and how everything is always so much more extraordinary than we might think. She is an experienced tertiary educator, Co-founder of The Pākehā Project, Haumanu coach with Centre for Social Impact, a certified Warm Data Lab Host with the International Bateson Institute, and Honorary Research Fellow at Toi Rauwhārangi, College of Creative Arts, Massey University.
Mel Hare (Pākehā— Irish)
Mel is a highly experienced facilitator, consultant and leadership coach. Trained through Sydney-based IECL, Mel is an alum of the Pākehā Project Leadership Journey and a Haumanu coach, and weaves this critical perspective into her practice. She is deeply committed to restorative and relational ways of working and being. Mel was born in Sydney Australia, and her ancestors immigrated from Ireland. She acknowledges the Gadigal people of the Eora Nation, the traditional custodians of the land on which she grew up. Now her heart is in Aotearoa, where she lives in Wellington with her family.
Workshop prices
We are offering choice around what you pay for this workshop. 
Consider Option A ($250 + GST), if you:
own the home you live in
have investments or a retirement account
travel recreationally
have access to resources in times of need
work part time by choice
have a relatively high degree of earning power due to level of education (or gender and racial privilege, class background, etc.) Even if you are not currently exercising your earning power, we ask you to recognise this as a choice.
Consider Option B ($400 + GST), if you:
can access professional development budgets from your workplace or organisation for this workshop
are in a position to ‘pay it forward’ to cover the cost of those who are paying what they can
Consider Option C (pay what you can),  if you:
have significant personal levels of debt
are an elder with limited financial support
are an unpaid community organizer
are out of work, a student or otherwise limited financially.

description:
Bike Maintenance for Beginners, Bicycle Maintenance for Beginners
Have you recently started riding a bicycle and want to make sure you can take care of it properly? Or have you been riding for ages, but have always been scared to fix anything yourself?
Are you unsure of how to pump your tyres, or how much oil your chain needs? Find yourself fumbling for words when trying to describe that clunking sound to the guy in the bike shop?
This one day course lays bare the nuts and bolts of bicycle mechanics for absolute beginners, as well as those with a little experience. Through practical experience working with your own bicycle, you will find out what needs to be done to keep it running smoothly. We’ll cover what to look out for when things start to wear out, and how to check for problems, so you can be confident your bicycle is safe to ride. You will also learn how to fix some of the most common mechanical problems, and learn about the correct terminology and tools to use.
Those who feel intimidated in bike shops are especially welcome in this course. No question is a stupid question!
Bringing a bike to work on is essential, preferably one that you are riding regularly, because the best way to learn is by building familiarity with your own ride. E-bikes are welcome, although the extra weight can mean they are more challenging to work on. Regardless of whether your bike is in pristine condition, or desperately in need of TLC, it is welcome on the course – bikes showing a bit more wear can be useful for the learning of the whole group.
Bring your pushbike along on the day.  If you have the following, please bring them as well:  A multi-tool and pump; chain oil and rag; lightweight close-fitting gardening or rubber gloves.
Note: A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
(Please note this course is not exhaustive and is not a professional training course).
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Name most parts of a bicycle correctly
- Perform a quick safety check on any bicycle
- Fix a flat tyre
- Adjust your bike to fit your body
- Oil and clean your chain
- Identify and fix some common brake problems
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

description:
Biochar Big Day Out 2025, Char curious? Keen gardener? Orchardist? Lifestyler? Climate Champion? BBQ enthusiast? 
Come one, come all to this one-off opportunity to spend a day making biochar in a magical orchard, forest and garden. Thank you Kapiti Coast District Council (KCDC) and Paekākāriki Orchards and Gardens (POG) for sponsoring this event so we can offer subsidised tickets as part of Sustainable Spring!
You will:

Morning sessions (9.30-12)...
Sipping coffee and learning the basics of Biochar. 
Getting hands-on exploring the property and learning to source good burn material (stuff you can find in your own backyard or lifestyle block).
Building a char toilet - great skills for civil defence emergencies, or just camping!
Ignite the Char-B-Que and BIG 600l kiln, learn how to feed the flames and trap the carbon.
Cooking using char!
At lunchtime (12-1)...
Enjoy a BBQ lunch cooked on the Char-B-Que. 
Learn all about the magic of biochar and how to use it to fight climate change, feed your garden. 
After lunch sessions (1-3)...
Quenching (pour cold water on) a kiln and processing char by drying and crushing it.
Making a home fireplace mini kiln using a biscuit tin (please bring a tin if you have one or koha for some extra we will source and bring from op shops).
Making a char water filter.
At the end of the day (3 pm)
Grab some biochar to take home (BYO container e.g. ice-cream tub or a small bucket
The big kiln will be quenched later in the day (around 4pm). For those keen to level up their learning on the kind of kilns used for large lifestyle blocks and small farms you are welcome to stay on and participate in a small advanced group dicussion and actvities between 3 and 4.30pm. 
Important things to note: 
Sustainability: 
We encourage carpooling to the event. Please bring your own reusable cup for hot drinks
Health and Safety:
 Please note there will be tree nuts and hazards onsite such as hot kilns and flames. So please take the necessary precautions by wearing non-flammable (cotton, wool, natural) materials and bring any personal medication that you need. We will have a health and safety volunteer onsite.

Family Friendly:
 It is a family-friendly event (kids under 18 are free) but they must be supervised by their parent or guardian at all times due to the hazards on site. 
Workshop Leaders 
John Wraight - CharPae 
Our CharPae Operations manager and ‘inhouse’ Biochar subject matter expert John Wraight has been making and using Biochar for many years and has delivered a number of successful workshops using these kilns. He is a BioChar Network member. He leads local CharPae burns, Char-B-Ques and kiln hire.
Holly Norton - CharPae 
Our CharPae Project manager has been making and using Biochar for the past 2 years. She co-leads these workshops and has additionally been exploring char use in sustainable construction and civil defence. She is currently on a mission to use Biochar to transform a tennis court into a thriving kai production space. She is this event's coordinator should you have any questions.

description:
Book Group: The Grass is Singing by Doris Lessing, We return to Africa for our September book: Doris Lessing's first novel The Grass is Singing, which takes place in Southern Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe) in the 1940s. The novel opens with a newspaper clipping about the death of Mary Turner, a white woman, killed by her black servant, Moses. The bulk of the novel is the story of Mary's life and the divided society she lived in.

Lessing was born in Persia, to British parents, and moved to Southern Rhodesia when she was six. Many of her books are set in Africa. In 1949 she left the continent and arrived in London with her son Peter (leaving behind her two older children) and the manuscript for this novel under her arm. The Grass is Singing was published the following year. Lessing was awarded the Nobel Prize in literature in 2007.

This is a shorter book, fitting neatly between The Last of the Mohicans and W. Somerset Maugham's Of Human Bondage, which are both longer works. (Of Human Bondage was originally published in two volumes.) But The Grass is Singing packs a punch. Indeed, one Goodreads review begins: "Doris Lessing's first novel has the precision of a fine short story and the depth of a longer novel."

Do you keep meaning to read more of the great classics? At Wellington Classic Literature Club, we read works that have stood the test of time, whether they were written in 1780, 1880 or even 1980. We meet on the first Tuesday of the month.

VENUE

Wellington Classic Literature Club has been running for more than a decade - since the start of 2013 - and we have a great bunch of regulars as well as readers who join us for particular books or simply when it suits.

description:
Botanical Blues - Photographic cyanotype, Explore the historic photographic process of the cyanotype and create luminous blueprints of leaves and flowers.

In this workshop, you’ll discover the beautiful 19th-century photographic process of the cyanotype (often called a blueprint), known for its striking Prussian blue tones. In its earliest form, the cyanotype was used to record botanical specimens. During our workshop, you’ll collect plants or foliage from the garden (or bring your own) to create delicate contact prints on watercolour paper. We’ll coat paper with light-sensitive chemistry, expose your designs in the sunlight, and develop and tone your prints with tea (!) to add depth and variation to your series of finished images.

All materials included.

You must be at least 16 years of age to attend this course.

description:
Brazilian Zouk Dance Classes - Beginners Block B, Connect with other like minded people that have a love of dance.
Brazilian Zouk was developed in Rio de Janeiro in the mid 90s, and is now becoming more and more popular
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfhRHnEAbak
..............
This is stunning to watch and even more fun to dance! It is based on the original Lambada dance but adapted to more modern music with a slow-quick-quick beat. It can be danced to a wide variety of music including R&B, Rock and Pop.
In this block of 5 classes you will discover the fundamental techniques, movements and sequences of Brazilian Zouk to get you up and running on the dance floor.
This includes:
Week 1: Passo basico
Week 2: Lateral
Week 3: Io-Io
Week 4: Bonus
Week 5: Combination
They are designed so you can start this block as a complete newbie, or you can continue on as an existing student from the last block.
There are 4 blocks of classes (A, B, C, D) in the complete Fundamentals course. Once these are done, you can progress to the Improvers classes.

Breaker bay Raranga, Te Motu Kairangi, with the support of Breaker Bay Hall, warmly invites you to:
Monthly Flax Weaving Wānanga
Experience the joy of learning, sharing, and reconnecting with the art of weaving.
Whether you’re a first-time weaver or returning to refresh your skills, all are welcome. We’ll cover basic weaving techniques and tikanga (customs) and provide a supportive, creative space to connect with Māori arts and crafts alongside others.
Session Times
• Open session: 1:00pm – 5:00pm (pack down starts at 4:30pm)
What to Bring
• New weavers: 5–10 rau (blades) of harakeke, sharp scissors.
• An old towel
• Bring a bag, as you must take away leftover harakeke
• Returning weavers: 30–40 rau of harakeke and your weaving tools
• Some tools are available to borrow
• Shared kai (snacks) welcome but not required
• Bring a bag, as you must take away leftover harakeke
Koha appreciated, not required
If you would like to support the kaupapa, please email us at temotukairangi.huihui@gmail.com for koha details.
Come and enjoy weaving, learning, and connection in a beautiful, relaxed setting.

via facebook
