description:
Breathe & Draw 'Where creativity meets inner peace', Breathe & Draw 'Where creativity meets inner peace'
Breathe & Draw
Where creativity meets inner peace


Saturday 27th of September
10:00 am - 11:30 am
@Hey Coastie 42 Tutere Street, Waikanae Beach


Join our (totally beginner-friendly) Breathe and Draw workshop. An art class focusing on drawing itself rather than the outcome of your work. This month's class is all about turning inner chaos into calm, visual order through mindful drawing. Starting with simple, spontaneous lines and adding as we go.

Why people do it:
Reduces stress and anxiety
Helps process emotions
Supports mindfulness

We start each class with some interactive drawing exercises before we start our final piece.

description:
Business Continuity Planning, Overview



This practical Business Continuity Planning workshop helps small and medium-sized businesses prepare for disruption before it happens.
Could your business keep operating if something unexpected happened tomorrow?
Disruptions don’t wait until you’re ready. Severe weather, supplier delays, cyber incidents, key staff absence, power outages, cash flow pressure or system failures can all stop normal operations fast.
This practical workshop will help you understand what a Business Continuity Plan is, why it matters, and how to start building one that works for your business.
You’ll learn how to identify your most critical business activities, understand the risks that could interrupt them, and put simple steps in place to keep operating, recover faster and communicate clearly when things go wrong.
What you’ll walk away with
A clear understanding of what a Business Continuity Plan should include
A practical framework to assess, prepare, respond and review
Tools to identify your critical processes, dependencies and recovery priorities
Simple steps to strengthen your business resilience over 30, 60 and 90 days
Confidence to start your plan without waiting for it to be perfect
Who should attend
This workshop is designed for New Zealand small and medium-sized business owners, managers and decision-makers who want to be better prepared for disruption.
Why attend
Because a simple plan started today could make all the difference when disruption arrives tomorrow.

description:
CBT skills for physical health practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand, Cognitive Behaviour Therapy (CBT) is a psychological intervention initially developed for emotional disorders. It is now widely used in supporting people to deal with the challenges of physical ill-health. Professionals from various backgrounds can learn to use a simplified CBT skills set, and use of these skills enables them to be more effective in managing aspects of their patients’ distress.
The training is a mix of theory, skills demonstration and skills practice, giving participants a better understanding of the applicability of the skill set in their area of practice and providing some skills to take away. Training sessions are spaced to allow participants to use their new skills in their clinical practice. Each participant reflects on their learning and their work with a specific patient, and the whole group reflects on lessons learned. In this way, learning remains rooted in participants’ clinical practice. These CBT courses are consistently evaluated highly by participants.
The Course
Teaching will be commenced with 2 days of in person sessions. 19th and 20th Feb 2026 at Mary Potter Hospice, Wellington and subsequently 2 sessions on-line via Zoom. The online sessions will be on 8th April and 27th May at 5pm for 3.5 hours.
Attendance at all sessions is mandatory to complete the course.
The courses cost is $850 per person (incl GST).
The Trainers
Kathy Burn was a Clinical Nurse Specialist in Palliative Care who went on to train in CBT and to develop the CBT service at St Christopher’s Hospice, London. She now works in CBT in chronic pain, and she teaches and supervises CBT trainees at the institute of Psychiatry, London.
Kathryn Mannix was a Palliative Medicine Consultant and CBT therapist. She developed ‘CBT First Aid’ to enable palliative care clinicians to adapt skills from CBT into their clinical practice. She is an author. There are insights into her use of CBT in her books With the End in Mind and Listen.
Terms and Conditions
Attendance: In order to create a learning community for each course, it is important that each person on a course attends every session and is able to join in the discussions by keeping up with the course. By accepting a place on a particular course, you agree to attend all the sessions, to arrive on time, and to work alongside your group members during the session to support each other's learning. Each session builds on the last, and you'll be asked to put your new learning into practice in- between sessions. Building learning groups in this way means we can't add new trainees after a course has begun.
We are not able to run catch-up sessions for sessions missed. If you miss sessions, you may be asked to withdraw from the course and no refunds will be given.
Refunds/Canellations: Once you sign up and pay, we won't be able to refund your payment unless we can reallocate your place to another person before the course begins. The deadline for cancelling your place is 28 days before the day and time of the first session. If you cancel and we can fill your place with another person, we'll offer you the choice of a refund or a place on a future course, if places are available. We will do our best to fill your place, but we can't promise this. Refunds will incur an administration fee.
Dates and Times of Sessions: all dates and times are given in NZ time, and this varies over the year. It is up to you to check the correct time in your time zone: you may find this website useful to check your own time zone with Auckland NZ time on each specific date: https://www.worldtimebuddy.com/
Trainers: we have a team of trainers, all of whom are experienced CBT therapists and trainers, and all are familiar with applying CBT in physical health settings. Different sessions may be taught by different trainers, or by 'guest appearances' by some of our team. The team of trainers will ensure there is continuity of content and of learning as the course progresses.
Special circumstances: Sometimes, life events appear unexpectedly. If something unexpected prevents you from attending, please let us know as early as you can, and we will give consideration to how we might be able to support you to continue your training if that is what you wish to do.

“Openjamz is a collective born from friendship, held together by movement, and opened wide for anyone who wants to step inside.
It is a home more than a studio — a place where we teach each other, learn from each other, and let the music guide us.
Here, classes are not just lessons, they are exchanges. Jams are not just sessions, they are conversations”
WEDNESDAY 5th NOVEMBER:
Nay Nay (Waacking Choreography) @ 6:00PM - 7:15PM
“E noho ana au ki te Whanganui a Tara engari nō Tāmaki Makaurau ki te Tonga me Kirikiriroa ahau
He kaikanikani au nō Projekt Team me Two and a Half Brownies hoki
He uri ahau nō Ngāti Ranginui 
Ko Renee tōku ingoa

description:
Calligratherapy - Beginners, Calligratherapy - Beginners
Many of us live sedentary lifestyles, sitting for up to eight hours or more a day hunched over our keyboard - all the while rarely taking a proper breath! Even if we wanted to take a deep enriching breath into the lower lobes of our lungs, we are limited due to our posture. Often due to the stresses and strains of a busy work and life balance, our unconscious brain can develop a pattern of holding, irregular and shadow breaths.
Does this sound like your experience? 
Not being able to breathe properly is the key cause of many chronic respiratory diseases (Nestor, 2020)
Calligratherapy combines science journalist James Nestor's theory on proper breathing with the philosophy of ancient Chinese calligraphy to promote a state of optimal wellbeing.
Calligratherapy has been developed specifically for those who have never practiced calligraphy before and who are interested in deriving the benefits without having to learn the language or all the characters. It integrates the simple and intuitive act of inhaling and exhaling into calligraphy practice with Eastern philosophy behind it.
A range of different breathing exercises are embedded into each 90 minute session focusing on different calligraphy scripts.  Over the five weeks, you will develop and practice the awareness of healthy breathing, while learning new techniques of Chinese soft brush calligraphy covering five different scripts. 
All materials included in course fee.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
Start a new creative practice in Chinese soft brush calligraphy
Develop your own mindfulness strategy
Better manage everyday stress levels and access a calm, empowered and positive state of mind
Find ways to explore eastern philosophy and develop deeper connections with your spiritual self.

description:
Chain Maille Course, Our medieval materials expert Achille is ready to be your chain maille master. In this seven class course you will hone in on the chain weaves that incite awe and be bestowed with the agency to create a wearable piece or majestic object of your own design. On the mysterious journey towards mastery, Achille will take you through everything from the dexterity of proper ring closing, to practicing resolve through the depths of theory and mathematics that allow you to design and execute a piece of your very own creation. This is the perfect course to begin your foray into the craft of chain maille.

This course it taught by medieval enthusiast Achille. He is a creature of curiosity and crepes, having spent the last 14 years skulking around the capital publishing “woke leftist paper” as a founder of 5ever books. He has conquered our hearts, minds, and the specialty cheese departments of the local supermarkets. Achille is a master of chain maille, now offering to teach his craft to those willing to take up the challenge.

Some materials and tools are supplied. Depending on the project you choose to create there may be extra material costs, as well as the option to purchase tools for personal use. You are welcome to bring your own bent nose pliers and wire cutters if you have them.

There are variable pricing options, unwaged/student, waged, and generous. Please choose whichever option feels right for you and your circumstances! Note that this ticket is a commitment to the entire seven week course. No chain maille experience is required, just a will to delve into the depths of metal weaves. If you're unsure about committing to this craft, perhaps keep an eye out for a one off 101 chain maille class that may come in the future.

Course Outline:
Week 01 - 18th September
101: Basic Skills and Discovery
At this class we'll explore the basics of good chain maille practice.
Opening & closing rings properly
Trying out some simple structures
Begin exploring material options and how to make your own rings
Homework: keep an eye out for recycled or foraged materials that could be utilised in chain maille

Week 02 - 25th September
Play and Exploration
Gathering inspiration and looking into methods for individual projects
Playing with recycled & foraged materials
Homework: Choose a weave from the library to try out at home or explore during the next class

Week 03 - 2nd October
Mathematics of chain maille design, theory, and history.
Math of designing chain maille
Theory & pre-planning
Discussion about ideas for individual projects
Identify materials needed to execute individual designs
Homework: Choose your individual project, identify what materials you will need, and how we will source/make them.

Week 04 - 16th October
By this class you will have you project plan down. We'll be collecting/ making our materials or beginning the execution of our projects with the guidance of Achille.

Week 05 & 06 - 23rd & 30th October
These classes will be open working times to make use of tools in class, ask Achille questions or help with troubleshooting, and to share our progress, challenges, and solutions with each other.

Week 07 - 6th November
At this final class we will make finishing touches to our projects and celebrate our creations together! Perhaps including a catwalk of our chain maille wares, and sharing kai.

description:
Charlotte Grimshaw: The annual NZSA Janet Frame Memorial Lecture, In her 2025 NZSA Janet Frame Memorial Lecture, Charlotte Grimshaw will report from the frontlines of fiction and memoir, discuss veracity, integrity and clarity in a so-called “post-truth world,” and share ideas she’s formed about authenticity after a whole life lived in fiction.

Grimshaw will describe her ongoing quest for answers, including a recent personal discovery of material in the Turnbull Library archive that shattered some final illusions, and fuelled her determination to go on expressing ideas and writing accurate human stories, no matter what. Don't miss this one-off, very special event.

Presented in partnership with New Zealand Society of Authors Te Puni Kaituhi O Aotearoa (PEN NZ) Inc, and National Library of New Zealand Te Puna Mātauranga o Aotearoa.

This event is free to attend, and will be followed by supper and light refreshments. Please register to secure your place. All welcome.

Charlotte Grimshaw spent two decades publishing fiction after growing up in the family of a writer. In 2021 she published a bestselling memoir, The Mirror Book, about her experiences in the literary family. She described this as an account of the creation of her authentic self.  In her latest novel, The Black Monk (March, 2026), she has continued her exploration of authenticity, blending the “micro” interior world of guilt, truth and lies with the “macro” world of geopolitics and history. Charlotte is the critically acclaimed author of eleven works, including novels, two outstanding collections of linked stories, a best-selling memoir, journalism and book reviewing.

Charlotte Grimshaw is The NZ Society of Authors Te Puni Kaituhi o Aotearoa 2025 President of Honour. This prestigious honour is bestowed on a senior writer and long-serving NZSA member in recognition of their contribution to writing, writers and the literary arts sector in Aotearoa. Each year the NZSA President of Honour delivers the Janet Frame Memorial Lecture.

description:
Chemigrams: Making Camera-less Photographs with Chemistry and Chance, This weekend workshop will introduce you to the chemigram, a camera-less darkroom process that uses resists and chemistry to create striking abstract imagery on photographic paper.

In this day-long darkroom workshop, we’ll explore the abstract photographic process of the chemigram. We’ll use photo paper, photo chemistry, ‘organic’ chemistry (such as vinegar, baking soda, citric acid) and a range of resists, as well as potentially incorporating foliage or organic materials to create evocative and atmospheric camera-less photographs.

Popularised in the 1960s, the chemigram allows you to create abstract patterns and shapes, while exploring the fundamentals of camera-less photography – light, chemistry, surface, time – and the element of chance. You’ll leave the workshop with a series of engaging photographic abstractions and a new perspective on what photography can be.

All materials included.

You must be at least 16 years of age to attend this course.

Chess - Learn to Play, Chess – Learn to Play
Starting from the beginning you will discover how to play the 3000-year-old game of Chess. You will learn the principles that guide decision making in all parts of the game, learn algebraic notation and the ability to not only play a game anywhere, anytime, but also knowledge of where and how to play - both online and in person.

Description
Chess is an ancient game of strategy and analysis that hones concentration and focus, as you master the skills allowing you to win at this competitive recreation.

Join tutor, Ryan Hill to learn how to play this game from the beginning.

You will quickly go from understanding the basics to being able to engage in playing confidently and discover where to go for further training or to carry on playing – both in person and online.

Over 600 million people play this game that has remained popular throughout the ages – why don’t you become one of them!

Bring pen and paper to take notes.

By the end of this course you will be able to:

*Be able to use all of the chess pieces to play the game
*Be able to recount and use some of the most common openings and traps
*Recognise where to go for further training or to play
*Develop increasing levels of confidence in your ability to play and possibly win

description:
Colourful Enamel Jewellery Day, Learn to create beautiful enamelled jewellery with Lisa Sinclair.

Join us for a full-day enamelling workshop where you’ll explore colour, texture, and fire to create vibrant enamelled jewellery in copper or silver.

This hands-on class focuses on the fundamentals of enamelling, showing you how to apply, fire, and layer enamel to achieve rich, expressive surfaces. You’ll make a simple yet beautifully textured pendant or pair of earrings, then learn how to add a pop (or flood!) of colour to bring your piece to life.

Beginners to metalwork are very welcome - pre-formed shapes are available so you can focus on experimenting with colour, pattern, and mark-making. If you have some metalworking experience, you’re encouraged to take things further by creating and texturing your own metal forms before enamelling.

This is a playful, creative workshop and an ideal class for anyone who loves working with colour, surface, and experimentation - whether you’re new to enamels or keen to deepen your skills.

What you’ll learn:
The basics of enamelling on copper and silver
How to prepare metal for enamelling
Applying enamel using different techniques
Firing enamel and building up layers of colour
Creating texture and pattern in metal
Tips for achieving clean, vibrant enamel finishes

The class fee covers enamel materials but NOT metals. Students can choose from a range of pre-cut copper blanks or use their own copper sheet. Findings and chains are available to purchase at a range of good prices to suit all budgets.

Kids aged approximately 12+ are welcome. Any participant under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

For health and safety reasons, students must wear sturdy closed-toe shoes.

description:
Communicate Across Generations: Bridge the Divide, Communicate Across Generations: Bridge the Divide
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
 Discover why different generations prioritise different things in their interactions, from family group chats and face-to-face conversations through to workplace attitudes. Learn to decode the nuances, bridge the divides, and foster more effective communication in your daily life.
Learning Outcomes
Deconstruct Communication Styles: You will be able to identify and describe the typical communication styles, preferences, and values of different generations, including Baby Boomers, Generation X, Millennials, and Generation Z.
Mitigate Conflict: You will learn to recognise and resolve common intergenerational communication conflicts by understanding their root causes and applying effective conflict resolution strategies.
Improve Collaboration: You will develop practical skills to adapt your communication approach to better engage with people from different generations, leading to enhanced understanding and connection.
Foster Inclusivity: You will be able to appreciate and leverage the unique perspectives and strengths that each generation brings to the table, creating more inclusive environments in your relationships.
Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch and snacks, and pen and paper to take notes.

description:
Community Comms Collective workshop for NFPs: Social marketing essentials - communications that create change, How can we change or maintain people’s behaviour through marketing, and truly benefit the communities we serve?
This hands-on workshop will demonstrate how you can create behaviour change through social marketing. You’ll learn the basics of behaviour change marketing and communications, including best practice approaches to achieve behaviour change for social good outcomes.
Learn tools, tips, and strategies to help you:
·      Develop programmes or services that influence the communities you serve
·      Target resources effectively and choose tactics that have impact
·      Create communications and marketing campaigns that resonate
We are thrilled to have communications expert and social entrepreneur Tracey Bridges lead this workshop. She is a co-founder and director of The Good Registry, a social enterprise that directs consumer spending on gifts towards good causes. Tracey has significant governance experience in the not-for-profit space, including Whānau Āwhina Plunket and the WELLfed Charitable Trust, and is a fellow Public Relations Institute of New Zealand.
Tracey's insights are drawn from international and local practice, and a long career in behaviour change in social marketing, working on projects, including It’s Not OK, Sorted, Like Minds, Like Mine and many more.
Workshop presenter: Tracey Bridges
For out of towners or those who can’t make it on the day, this workshop will be recorded and shared on our website after the event, along with our other resources.
This is a free Community Comms Collective workshop for not-for-profits and collective volunteers hosted by Volunteer Wellington and supported by JacksonStone & Partners. We are grateful for their support and for our speaker for giving their time and talent pro bono.

description:
Community Herbal Workshop, Community Herbal Workshop
Learning and doing alongside our children is what we love. However, we appreicate this can sometimes be hard at times so we're trialing learning alongside each other at a community level.

Come join Earth School Aotearoa for our first community herbalism workshop. This is the first of quarterly sessions where you can come and make all your seasonal remedies either by yourself or as a family.

Bring the kids for no extra cost (adult ones too). These are grass roots, barefoot , children running around events where there's extra eyes and support to be able to learn and make what you need for your home based seasonal wellness remedies. There are experienced tutors there able to help, with their own children in attendance. If you have ever wanted to take more control of your remedies and are not able to afford the prices of some or generally just want to learn alongside others in a more relaxed environment then this is made for you.

This season is about immunity! The weather will start cooling, and it then becomes the time to have elderberries ready, firecider brewing and Mullein ear oil steeping. These are the three remedies we will be focusing on and why they’re go to's. Along with other common kitchen ingredients.

Ticket prices include the cost of ingredients but not vessels/jars. You will need to source and bring them yourself. More information will be emailed. Places are limited as we need to source ingredients in advance so sign up and bring the family (newborn or old).

Cost per ticket includes one mix of firecider, one ear oil and one elderberry. You will need to allow one hour of your time for the making, we have allowed a four hour session so you don't have to be rushed and can come around whatever life throws at you that morning.

You are welcome to stay longer/for the whole session. BYO lunch.

Where: Wallacville Church Hall , 11.30 - 3.30 on Saturday March 7th

Please message the page to book and reserve a spot for paying later or head here https://events.humanitix.com/earth-school-aotearoa-community-herbalisim

Coneheads Motogymkhana, Wondered what Moto Gymkhana is?
Keen to build confidence on your bike and improve your handling skills?
One of the hundred people who have "always been meaning to check it out"? Then this Thursday is your night! Come join us at the Tawa Outlet Mall for an evening of Motogymkhana.
All skill levels are welcome. We've designed beginner course for the summer, that isn't too technical and is a good introduction to the sport. (We've even tested it with a new rider!) Confidence In Public Speaking With Comedian Brendon Green, This workshop is designed for teens to develop their confidence in public speaking, through interactive teaching and guided activities.

Using evidence-based comedy and language techniques, participants will develop confidence in their public speaking abilities and their own sense of humour. A basic understanding of public speaking and comedic technique can enhance self-confidence, identity, and opportunity.

Realizing you have a unique world view and then being able to communicate that in an entertaining way is one of the most wonderful experiences you can have on your journey of self discovery and development.

Brendon Green is a creative communications specialist and storyteller who uses humour and empathy to help people connect, laugh, and learn. With over 18 years of experience in television, live events, and education, he creates thoughtfully crafted content with an emotional honesty that sometimes worries his mum.

He's helped write some of NZ's best loved Comedy TV, and his live stand up shows have been nominated for NZ Comedy’s biggest awards.

description:
Contact Improvisation with Eliza Sanders & Footnote Dance, Contact Improvisation with Eliza Sanders & Footnote Dance
Five-Day Intensive Workshop with Eliza Sanders

About this Event

This intensive week offers a rare opportunity to dive deep into the practical tools and nuanced territories of Contact Improvisation. Fresh from three weeks of intensive CI training in Thailand, Eliza returns with new wisdom and embodied understanding to share with our community.

A Unique Learning Community
This workshop brings together an extraordinary learning environment where Footnote's four full-time dancers will practice alongside independent dancers and community participants, creating a rich exchange of distinct yet equally valuable body wisdoms. Together, we'll explore the multilayered practice of Contact Improvisation in its depth and complexity.

The Journey: Progressive Deepening Throughout the Week
Through structured explorations and guided improvisation, we'll delve into the physical practice while also discovering the connections between how we move together and how we navigate life with greater ease and joy. As is Eliza’s style, we'll explore both the practical tools of the craft and uncover how this embodied practice offers insights for moving through the world with more presence and connection.
We'll venture into advanced techniques and principles of Contact Improvisation. Each day will build organically on the last, allowing for genuine integration and discovery. The specific focus will evolve from the insights and practices Eliza brings back from the Inspiral intensive in Thailand.



Who This Workshop Is For
This intensive creates magic precisely because it brings together diverse perspectives and experience levels. We welcome:
Graduates of Contact Improvisation foundations workshops ready to deepen their practice
Experienced movers curious about the broader applications of CI principles
Proffesional dancers eager to nuance and expand their practice
Community dancers eager to learn alongside professional practitioners
Anyone interested in exploring movement as a pathway to more effective communication and compassionate action
Those drawn to embodied practices for personal and social transformation
Prior Contact Improvisation experience recommended but not essential—our kaupapa embraces the wisdom that emerges when professional and community dancers share the learning space.

Practical Details
When: Monday - Friday, October 13-17, 2025 Time: 9am - 5pm daily Where: Footnote Dance Studios Capacity: Maximum 10 participants (alongside our 4 Footnote dancers) What to Bring: Comfortable clothes for dancing, long sleeves and socks recommended Included: Tea and snacks throughout each day (lunch not included)

Investment
Early Bird: $300 (until September 12th) Regular Price: $350

About Your Facilitator
Eliza brings years of dedicated Contact Improvisation practice and teaching, known for creating environments where technical skill development and personal discovery flourish together. Her recent intensive training in Thailand with internationally renowned teachers adds fresh depth to her already rich understanding of CI as both movement practice and life practice. Former participants consistently highlight her ability to create space where everyone—from newcomers to experienced dancers—can access new layers of understanding and embodied wisdom.

Come As You Are
The most profound discoveries in Contact Improvisation emerge from the unexpected—from the intersection of different bodies, experiences, and ways of moving through the world. Your unique perspective and embodied wisdom are exactly what this learning community needs. Come ready to explore, to be surprised, and to discover how the dance floor becomes a training ground for creating the more compassionate, connected world we all long for.
No perfection required. Just openness to the movement.

description:
Contemporary Realism, Whether you work from objects, the figure, or secondary sources, this is an opportunity to explore working more loosely, using oils or acrylics.

Justine will guide you through drawing and painting exercises to help loosen you up, and will discuss art historical techniques that may be relevant to your individual artistic style and context.

This course will increase your ability to represent perceived objects in a dynamic, painterly way. You will be guided through drawing and painting exercises to help you achieve accuracy of form, working loosely with oils and acrylics to create fresh contemporary paintings. The emphasis is on working with your chosen source material to create a `next level’ painting. This course is for those who have explored some of the basics of painting such as mixing colours, blending etc, but want to find a process that best expresses your unique approach and ideas. Skills learnt in class can be applied across all genres.

Materials are not included in this course.
Materials: Please bring your preferred range of oils, brushes and supports (paper, canvas, or board). A good basic set of oil paints would include cad and lemon yellow, ultramarine and cerulean blue, and cad red and alizarin crimson. Also, black and white. Inverlochy will supply Liquin and Gamsol solvent. No other solvents are allowed in this class. Please also bring a photocopied reference image in both black and white and colour.

Lunch break - 30 minutes. Bring a water bottle and packed lunch to enjoy in the historic Inverlochy house or explore the local cafes in Te Aro.

Contract Law Fundamentals for Non Lawyers Masterclass Wellington, Contract Law Fundamentals for Non Lawyers Masterclass Wellington
Register Today by contacting Crown Leadership International Group: Website: www.crownleadership.com.au Phone: +64 9 889 7217

About this Event

Contract Law Fundamentals for Non Lawyers Masterclass is an intensely practical guide through the essentials of contract law, exploring such details as when a contract will be required, when you have a contract (and don’t necessarily know it), what types of contract exist and the effect of legislation on your contractual arrangements.
This masterclass also scrutinises what happens when things go wrong, including how you can get out of a contract, options for assessing damages and remedies for breach and looking at the contractual implications of working in an e-commerce environment. You will grasp the crucial ingredients required for a good contract, and gain tips to better understand and manage your contracts.

Create some classic mouth-watering and flavourful Nyonya dishes. Come and discover how to blend ingredients with distinct spices and cooking techniques. You can easily replicate these dishes at home.

description:
Coptic Book Binding, Coptic binding is one of the earliest forms of creating a book, with raw simplicity you can produce a book of any size with the unique feature of opening out flat. No special tools or materials are needed and yet a wide spectrum of creative results can be created, from a notebook, sketch book and album to a highly crafted artwork. The books themselves can be made from found items, recycled material or quality art papers and card.

In this workshop you will be guided in assembling your chosen materials for your book, create decorative covers and learn Coptic binding - an elegant and simple binding that is unlimited in versatility. You will produce one bound book and one bound album. Once you have Coptic binding in your skill set you can produce your choice of books in any shape or form, for any purpose.

All basic materials supplied.

One hour for lunch. Bring a drink bottle and a packed lunch to enjoy in the historic Inverlochy House or explore the cafes in Te Aro.

You must be at least 16 years of age to attend this course.

description:
Courageous Communication™ | 1-day Workshop | Wellington | 11 Nov 2025, Courageous Communication™ | 1-day Workshop | Wellington | 11 Nov 2025
Get great at having hard conversations with Kaila Colbin

About this Event

Has this ever happened to you?
You’re sitting in a meeting and there are 50 elephants in the room with you that nobody is mentioning, and you’re doing the strategic plan but everyone knows it’s never going to work because the team don’t have the capability or the capacity and that one person never follows through and that other person thinks her work is better than it is, but nobody says anything and as you leave you think well THAT'S three hours I’m never gonna get back…
It’s hard to say the hard thing.
But saying the hard thing is the only way we can deal with what’s actually going on.
The number one indicator of a lack of courage is an inability to have hard conversations.
Hard conversations are scary. Our hearts start pounding, our tummies clench, our mouths go dry.
Hard conversations feel dangerous. If I say this thing, he’ll be offended! She’ll be angry! I’ll get in trouble!
Hard conversations are tempting to avoid. Nobody else is mentioning these elephants. Why should I?
But what if you were great at them?
What would it mean for your relationships?
What would it mean for your career?
What would it mean for your life?
Kaila Colbin has worked with more than 4,000 people to grow courage as a core competency and a clear framework has emerged from that experience.
In this 1-day workshop, you’ll build the skill and muscle to get great at having hard conversations.
We’ll cover the specific elements of how to communicate and what to communicate.

When: Tuesday, 11 November 2025, 9 am-4:30 pm
Where: Rangimarie Room, Te Papa Museum, 55 Cable Street, Wellington 6011
Lunch, afternoon tea and all-day tea and coffee are included in the registration.



Need help with the cost?
If you are an Educator or at a Not-for-Profit, you can automatically access a special rate of $745 + GST when you register (a $250 discount off our standard General Admission rates).



Our Health and Safety Plan
Boma is committed to delivering safe events. We follow best practices suggested by the New Zealand health authorities and work closely with our suppliers to prioritise health and wellbeing.
Our comprehensive health and safety plans ensure you can book with certainty and attend with confidence.



Our refund policy
For details on event refunds and transfers, please see our refund policy.


About the Kaila Colbin
Kaila Colbin is founder and CEO of Boma, an organisation building a world of intentional, intelligent, courageous leaders.
An award-winning leader renowned for impact, Kaila developed TEDxChristchurch into New Zealand’s flagship TEDx event and brought Singularity University to New Zealand and Australia, supporting thousands of people to engage with exponentially accelerating technologies and their impact on humanity. She trained with Dr Brené Brown as a Certified Dare to Lead™ Facilitator.
As a founder of the non-profit Ministry of Awesome, Kaila played a critical role in developing Christchurch’s startup ecosystem. She has extensive governance experience, and has been involved with mergers, capital raises, and company sales in the US and NZ.
A native New Yorker, Kaila’s work to champion Aotearoa New Zealand on a global stage saw her given the 2022 Kea World Class New Zealand “Friend of New Zealand” award. Her purpose in life is to be an uplifting presence.

If you have any questions about this event, please email us at .

description:
Creative Problem-Solving Workshop, Creative Problem-Solving Workshop
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
Through engaging puzzles, group activities, and proven creativity techniques, you'll discover how to tackle challenges from new angles and find solutions you might never have considered. Learn to break through mental blocks, generate innovative ideas, and lead groups to make better decisions together. This workshop draws on Neil's background in teaching, test-preparation, and creative thinking to help you unlock your natural problem-solving abilities in a supportive environment.
What You'll Get From This Workshop:
·       Simple techniques to generate ideas individually or in a group: brainstorming, mind-mapping, and more
·       Practice solving puzzles that sharpen your lateral thinking skills
·       Learn how to overcome blocks and restrictive thinking patterns
·       Experience effective group leading methods you can use with your own teams
·       Discover how to identify root causes of problems instead of just treating symptoms
·       Take home specific tools for approaching problems differently
·       Build confidence in leading problem-solving sessions with others
Who This Workshop Is For: This workshop is for anyone who faces challenges at work, leads meetings or teams, manages projects, or simply wants to become a better problem solver. Perfect for team leaders, community organizers, and anyone who's ever been stuck in an unproductive meeting wondering "there must be a better way!" No special background needed—just bring your curiosity and willingness to try new approaches.
What to Expect: A day filled with interactive activities, problem-solving challenges, and practical techniques you can use right away. You'll learn proven steps and while practicing facilitation skills to help groups make decisions more effectively. Neil creates a relaxed atmosphere where everyone feels comfortable contributing ideas and experimenting with new approaches. You'll leave with specific tools you can apply to your own challenges, plus handouts to help you remember what you've learned.
Neil's unique skill as an educator is his rare ability to blend evidence-based teaching techniques with the perfect dash of humor and storytelling, creating a learning environment where complex concepts become accessible and new skills feel immediately applicable to your real-world challenges.

description:
Creative Writing - A Tasting Plate, Creative Writing - A Tasting Plate
How often have you said, ‘I wish I could write’? There are many different kinds of writing. Starting is easy so why not give it a go by joining this creative writing ‘tasting plate’.
Each week we’ll focus on a different area of fiction or creative non-fiction. By the end of the programme, you’ll have tried your hand at writing a short story, a narrative poem, a travel memoir, a personal essay drawing from your life, an interview article, a story for children, a short film script and a piece of historical fiction.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
• Create works of fiction 
• Develop creative non-fiction text 
• Explore the natural inner spirit of writing 
• Discover your unique writer’s voice 
• Reflect on your own experiences in writing 
• Investigate different writing strategies
• Discover where your personal writing passions sit and what works for you.
Bring pen and paper or a laptop. 
This course is designed to help you improve your skills, to develop your unique writer's voice and to encourage you to take risks on the page. It is not a course where you'll be asked to read your work out loud, critique other writers work, or hand in your writing to the tutor. This is a safe place where you will be supported to do what writers do best - write.

The repetitive movements of crochet help the brain make more serotonin, which can decrease tension and feelings of depression. We’ll move through all the steps from the starting slipknot to reading patterns and diagrams and making your first crochet projects.

• Read a basic crochet pattern and recognise crochet terminology
• Choose yarns and hooks for projects
• Use a range of stitches with confidence
• Complete at least one project of your choice (granny square, keychain, garden decoration)

description:
Dolores Mosquera Wellington New Zealand May 2026, Day 1 – May 10, 2026 (9:00am–4:30pm)
Topic: Working with Dissociative Parts and Their Voices in Complex Trauma and Dissociative Disorders
Overview:
This seminar focuses on adapting EMDR for individuals with dissociative disorders, using the Trauma-Informed Relational Approach for Dissociative Parts (TADP) Dolores has developed. It provides strategies for working with dissociative parts and their voices and integrating a trauma-informed approach to inner conflict safely from early treatment stages.
Key Learning Points:
·         Identifying and working with dissociative parts and their voices.
·         Understanding the function and purpose of “hostile” parts.
·         Addressing dissociative phobias through EMDR informed techniques.
·         Managing resistance and treatment impasses.
·         Structuring work with dissociative parts effectively.
Program Description:
After many early cautions about the potential dangers of using EMDR with individuals suffering from dissociative disorders, limited methods have been offered for adapting standard EMDR procedures to this specific population. Based on these early cautions, EMDR is still considered by many clinicians as limited to the treatment of traumatic memories in high-functioning dissociative clients and only after a long preparation phase that depends on other treatment modalities. Confined by this conceptualisation, the use of EMDR is too often limited, and many survivors of severe traumatisation are unable to benefit from EMDR reprocessing and, if at all, only much later in the treatment process.
Dolores Mosquera developed (with AnabelGonzalez, M.D.) the Progressive Approach model for treating complex trauma and dissociation (2012) and the Trauma-Informed Relational Approach for Dissociative Parts (TADP) (2019, 2025). Using this trauma and AIP-informed models, clinicians can safely utilise a wide range of EMDR interventions (including BLS) from early in the preparatory phase of treatment for patients with dissociative disorders.
In this seminar, she will present her current practice of working with clients, including video demonstrations. Mosquera's deft clinical skills and ground-breaking innovative thinking teach a middle ground between "dissociation blind" aggressive EMDR interventions and overly cautious delays to the use of EMDR reprocessing.
Many dissociative clients have difficulty with hostile, critical voices. The internal conflict is sometimes so intense that the person even has difficulty carrying on an ordinary conversation. One factor that affects this conflict is how the patient deals with the voices or parts of the self.
Key Program Content:
Identify the internal system of dissociation and internal voices that are hostile and critical
How to read the function and purpose behind the saboteur parts of self
Using compassion and understanding to help deal with dissociative phobias within the internal system
Skills to reduce impasses and resistance that may complicate or reduce the efficacy of the treatment
Specific steps to organize the work with hostile parts and voices
 Days 2–3 – May 11–12, 2026 (9:00am–4:30pm)
Topic: From Fragmentation to Integration: A Master Class in Treating Complex Trauma and Dissociation
Format: 2-Day Masterclass: Three Clinical Cases from Start to Finish
Across two days, Dolores will present three distinct new cases illustrating varying levels of dissociation — including one with frequent switching and no initial Adult Self. Each session is interactive, highlighting the therapeutic process from assessment to completion.
Over two immersive days, this advanced master class offers a rare opportunity to observe and analyse complete therapeutic processes under the expert guidance of Dolores Mosquera.

Dolores will present three new and distinct clinical cases, each representing different manifestations of complex trauma and dissociation — including one client who experiences frequent switching and begins therapy without an integrated adult self.
Participants will follow these clients’ journeys from the initial stages of therapy through to treatment completion, gaining deep insight into decision-making, pacing, and the integration of EMDR strategies within complex systems. The format is designed to be highly interactive and reflective, combining video demonstrations, live commentary, and group discussion to deepen understanding of safe, flexible, and attuned clinical practice when working with dissociative clients.
This master class is ideal for clinicians seeking to refine their skills, expand their conceptual framework, and enhance clinical confidence when navigating the challenges of trauma-related dissociation.
Additional Details
·         Eligibility: Must have completed at least Part One of EMDR Basic Training (University of Otago or equivalent).
·         Certification: Participants receive a Professional Development Certificate of Attendance.
·         Dietary needs: Provided upon registration.
·         Parking: Paid on-site parking available.

description:
Dolores Mosquera Wellington New Zealand May 2026, Day 1 – May 10, 2026 (9:00am–4:30pm)
Topic: Working with Dissociative Parts and Their Voices in Complex Trauma and Dissociative Disorders
Overview:
This seminar focuses on adapting EMDR for individuals with dissociative disorders, using the Trauma-Informed Relational Approach for Dissociative Parts (TADP) Dolores has developed. It provides strategies for working with dissociative parts and their voices and integrating a trauma-informed approach to inner conflict safely from early treatment stages.
Key Learning Points:
·         Identifying and working with dissociative parts and their voices.
·         Understanding the function and purpose of “hostile” parts.
·         Addressing dissociative phobias through EMDR informed techniques.
·         Managing resistance and treatment impasses.
·         Structuring work with dissociative parts effectively.
Program Description:
After many early cautions about the potential dangers of using EMDR with individuals suffering from dissociative disorders, limited methods have been offered for adapting standard EMDR procedures to this specific population. Based on these early cautions, EMDR is still considered by many clinicians as limited to the treatment of traumatic memories in high-functioning dissociative clients and only after a long preparation phase that depends on other treatment modalities. Confined by this conceptualisation, the use of EMDR is too often limited, and many survivors of severe traumatisation are unable to benefit from EMDR reprocessing and, if at all, only much later in the treatment process.
Dolores Mosquera developed (with AnabelGonzalez, M.D.) the Progressive Approach model for treating complex trauma and dissociation (2012) and the Trauma-Informed Relational Approach for Dissociative Parts (TADP) (2019, 2025). Using this trauma and AIP-informed models, clinicians can safely utilise a wide range of EMDR interventions (including BLS) from early in the preparatory phase of treatment for patients with dissociative disorders.
In this seminar, she will present her current practice of working with clients, including video demonstrations. Mosquera's deft clinical skills and ground-breaking innovative thinking teach a middle ground between "dissociation blind" aggressive EMDR interventions and overly cautious delays to the use of EMDR reprocessing.
Many dissociative clients have difficulty with hostile, critical voices. The internal conflict is sometimes so intense that the person even has difficulty carrying on an ordinary conversation. One factor that affects this conflict is how the patient deals with the voices or parts of the self.
Key Program Content:
Identify the internal system of dissociation and internal voices that are hostile and critical
How to read the function and purpose behind the saboteur parts of self
Using compassion and understanding to help deal with dissociative phobias within the internal system
Skills to reduce impasses and resistance that may complicate or reduce the efficacy of the treatment
Specific steps to organize the work with hostile parts and voices
 Days 2–3 – May 11–12, 2026 (9:00am–4:30pm)
Topic: From Fragmentation to Integration: A Master Class in Treating Complex Trauma and Dissociation
Format: 2-Day Masterclass: Three Clinical Cases from Start to Finish
Across two days, Dolores will present three distinct new cases illustrating varying levels of dissociation — including one with frequent switching and no initial Adult Self. Each session is interactive, highlighting the therapeutic process from assessment to completion.
Over two immersive days, this advanced master class offers a rare opportunity to observe and analyse complete therapeutic processes under the expert guidance of Dolores Mosquera.

Dolores will present three new and distinct clinical cases, each representing different manifestations of complex trauma and dissociation — including one client who experiences frequent switching and begins therapy without an integrated adult self.
Participants will follow these clients’ journeys from the initial stages of therapy through to treatment completion, gaining deep insight into decision-making, pacing, and the integration of EMDR strategies within complex systems. The format is designed to be highly interactive and reflective, combining video demonstrations, live commentary, and group discussion to deepen understanding of safe, flexible, and attuned clinical practice when working with dissociative clients.
This master class is ideal for clinicians seeking to refine their skills, expand their conceptual framework, and enhance clinical confidence when navigating the challenges of trauma-related dissociation.
Additional Details
·         Eligibility: Must have completed at least Part One of EMDR Basic Training (University of Otago or equivalent).
·         Certification: Participants receive a Professional Development Certificate of Attendance.
·         Dietary needs: Provided upon registration.
·         Parking: Paid on-site parking available.
·         Accommodation: Discounted rates at a local hotel (discount code to be posted on the event site).

About Doug Lemov
Doug Lemov is a world-renowned educator based in the United States who has transformed classrooms with his teaching techniques. He helped found the Uncommon Schools (a nonprofit school management organisation) that has seen many students experience success.
His book, Teach Like a Champion (now in its 3rd edition), has sold over one million copies worldwide, and Doug has published several other books — most recently, the Teach Like a Champion Guide to the Science of Reading (2025).

description:
Draw the Moon: A Lunar Sketching Workshop at Star Safari, See the Moon like an astronomer — and draw it like an artist.
Join us at the Star Safari Observatory for a unique 90-minute experience where astronomy meets art. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll learn how to sketch the Moon directly at the eyepiece of our telescopes while observing its craters, mountains, shadows, and changing light in real time.

Using quality sketching materials (provided on the night), you’ll be guided step-by-step through:
- recognising key lunar features
- capturing contrast, relief and texture
- translating live telescope views accurately to paper
- fast sketching techniques for an object that’s constantly moving

You’ll have dedicated telescope time with our team, adjusting the optics for you and helping you get the sharpest possible view. This experience is designed to be accessible for beginners, while still rewarding for those with some astronomy or art experience.

Set beneath Wairarapa’s internationally acclaimed dark skies, this workshop offers a quiet, focused creative moment under the Moon. Whether you come for art, astronomy, or simply the pleasure of observing slowly and noticing deeply, you’ll leave with a sketch that is uniquely yours — shaped by the night and the light you saw.

Who is this for?
Adults and older children with an interest in drawing, the night sky, or simply trying something new.

Included:
✔ High-quality sketching pencils and paper
✔ Expert lunar observing guidance
✔ Dedicated telescope time
✔ Use of Star Safari’s professional viewing equipment

What to bring:
Warm clothing, curiosity, and any of your favourite drawing tools if you’d like to use them.

Take home more than a drawing — take home a moment of looking closely.

description:
Draw, Paint, Sculpt for Tweens & Teens, This is a beginner friendly course to help improve drawing, painting and sculpting skills.

Students will begin with drawing from still life using pencil; learning how to describe form through stroke direction and the layering of hatching. Next students will use lighting directed onto the still life, in order to heighten the tonal contrast, and make monochrome paintings of the illuminated scene. Understanding the image through tonal values, rather than outline, will enable student to draw and paint more realistically. Students will next experiment with colour, changing foreground and background colours to see how different colour combinations affect the focal point, mood and aesthetics of the overall image.

In the second half of the term students will sculpt in plasticine, making simple forms and learning how to render the surface to achieve the texture and form.

By the end of the course students will be able to:

- Describe form through light and shadow
- Sharpen your general observation skills
- Discover your personal drawing, painting and sculpting style

Suitable for ages 10 and above.

Eight week course on Thursdays, 30 July - 17 September.
Basic materials provided.

description:
Drawing And Painting A Portrait, Using the classic rules of proportion you will develop the skills to draw a portrait of a person. There will be steps to follow and many techniques to assist along the way.
You will work from a live model and from photographs drawing various exercises. You will use pencil and finally complete a portrait in watercolour paints.

Description
Using the classic rules of proportion you will develop the skills to draw a portrait of a person. There will be steps to follow and many techniques to assist along the way. Our experienced tutor and artist will demonstrate techniques to capture a likeness.
A live model will sit for us and you will apply those techniques to observe carefully and capture proportions and a likeness.
Next you will work from photographs and draw the model in various exercises, using pencil and paint.
Finally you will paint a portrait in watercolour using all the techniques and new found skills.

Please bring pencils and A4 sketch book to first class, all other art materials included in course fee.

By the end of the course, you'll be able to:
- Understand and apply some standard proportions for drawing the human face
- Build an understanding of great portraits and their attributes
- Use watercolour painting techniques to bring form to the portrait
- Complete a finished portrait in watercolour

4 weeks
Presented by Charlotte Hird.

description:
Drawing Into Print: Soundwalking, Join Gemma Thompson on a soundwalk from Toi Pōneke Gallery to Central Park in Aro Valley, finishing at Inverlochy House. Participants will draw inspired by sounds heard on the walk. These drawings will then be transformed into simple dry point prints using recycled Tetra Pak. Dry point is an intaglio printmaking technique where images are carved into a plate, inked, and then printed under pressure using a press to create richly detailed prints.
Tickets are $45. Spaces limited, book now!
All materials will be provided, but feel free to bring your own favourite drawing tools and a sketchbook.

Tāne, wāhine, and irawhiti are warmly invited to participate in a special day of high quality, affordable professional learning. This celebration of gender diversity in ECE will be held in a safe and supportive environment and is a fantastic opportunity to meet others in the profession, share your own story, and be inspired.
Gender Steretoypes in ECE - Mike Collin and Max Christie
What can gender stereotypes teach us about teaching and learning?
Early childhood education relies on diversity within teaching teams. Yet, gender stereotypes often shape how we see ourselves and each other as kaiako. This interactive session invites educators to explore the hidden assumptions that influence teaching roles and team dynamics. In this session, Max and Mike will unpack how stereotypes impact collaboration and how every kaiako adds unique value to teaching teams. Participants will leave with practical strategies to challenge bias, strengthen team culture, and celebrate the richness of varied approaches in ECE settings.
Autism NZ - Thecla Moffat
Men can change the dynamics of play in ECE benefiting autistic tamariki
Male kaiako often bring more energy in the ECE setting with an emphasis on more physical activity, outdoor play, "rough and tumble" play, and positive risk-taking, which appeals to both boys and girls and provides a different dimension to play than may be beneficial to most autistic tamariki. We now know that through fun and engaging interactions kaiako help enhance the autistic tamariki pivotal capacities for later learning. In this talk kaiako will get to know how men in ECE with their positive energy can make a difference through play for autistic tamariki in their centres. The kaiako will be given a few strategies of how to do that and some ideas to encourage tuakana-teina (peer play) between autistic tamariki and their non-autistic peers will be shared.

Mike Collin (B. Ed)
Being a new grad, Mike harnesses a fresh perspective underpinned by recent research and hands on learning. Mike is currently a kaiako within Heretaunga Kindergarten Association, nurturing the lives of our future generations to come.
Mike changed career paths having found his passion for teaching young tamariki. He believes in kaiako being the best versions of themselves to enhance positive and
meaningful learning environments for tamariki, advocating for the professionalism which early childhood kaiako achieve everyday. Mike strives for excellence in his approach to teaching and learning, seeking out the best outcomes for tamariki.
Max Christie (M. Ed)
Max brings over a decade of experience in early childhood education, blending academic expertise with hands-on leadership. Max currently lectures at EIT Te Aho a Māui, where he inspires future educators through a commitment to quality ECE for tamariki and whānau.
He began his teaching journey at Childspace Northland, where he also gained leadership experience and has facilitated PLD internationally and across Aotearoa. Max is deeply passionate about nature-based education, play, te ao Māori, leadership, innovative and affirming the mana of tamariki and kaiako.
Autism NZ - Thecla Moffat
Men can change the dynamics of play in ECE benefiting autistic tamariki
Male kaiako often bring more energy in the ECE setting with an emphasis on more physical activity, outdoor play, "rough and tumble" play, and positive risk-taking, which appeals to both boys and girls and provides a different dimension to play than may be beneficial to most autistic tamariki. The kaiako will be given a few strategies of how to do that and some ideas to encourage tuakana-teina (peer play) between autistic tamariki and their non-autistic peers will be shared.
Thecla Moffat (Early Intervention Manager, Autism New Zealand) is an educator who has been in the teaching field for over three decades. Thecla is passionate about inclusion and advocate for children’s rights and needs to be met in their educational settings.
Thecla has experience teaching from early childhood to primary school. She joined the tertiary sector in educating New Zealand’s teachers between January 2013 and October 2015 working as a lecturer at New Zealand Tertiary College. In her first year at New Zealand Tertiary College, she wrote the course guide for Inclusive Education Level 7. In October 2015 she joined the New Zealand Ministry of Education as an Early Intervention Specialist. In August 2019 Thecla joined Autism New Zealand to start their new early intervention services. She has a huge interest in inclusive education for children with diverse needs and promoting emotional and social competencies in the early years with special interest in autistic children. She has done research in inclusive early childhood education and promoting children’s social competencies. She sits on the Teaching Council Inclusive Education Advisory Group and currently sits on the academic programme board for New Zealand Tertiary College among other roles. She is a parent to three amazing children one of whom is neurodiverse. theclamoffat@xtra.co.nz OR thecla.moffat@autismnz.org.nz
Self-regulation & positive behaviour strategies - Robert Jensen & Nikki Wilson
ENGAGE is an evidence-based approach that supports the development of children’s self-regulation skills through intentional play. ENGAGE was developed by Professor Dione Healey (University of Otago) and has been widely researched in Aotearoa.
In collaboration with Methodist Mission Southern (MMS) and funding from the Ministry of Education, the programme is now being delivered across Aotearoa to equip tamariki with self-regulation skills to support successful navigation through school and beyond.
Robert & Nikki are ENGAGE facilitators for the Te Whanganui-a-Tara region.
Play is good for you! - Robin Christie
The reciprocal nature of learning between child and adult relies on a shared language - the language of play. This universal language is unspoken, and is strongest in the presence of curious, wondrous, joyous educators. You are already fluent in this language, and the amazing diversity of playful approaches you bring to your ECE setting is a huge strength of our profession! This entertaining and thought- provoking session will reinforce the importance of playful adults in children's learning, examine the research around the role of humour in human development, and share practical tips for staying playful every day.
Robin Christie is an early childhood teacher, playscape designer, and the co-founder of Childspace Early Learning Centres in Te Whanganui-a-Tara, Wellington, Aotearoa/ New Zealand. He is passionate about creativity in the early years, developing empowering learning environments, and getting more good men into ECE. You can get hold of him anytime on robin@childspace.nz .

description:
ESC September Asian Artist meetup, The Eastern Sound Collective is a growing community of creatives with pan-Asian roots, coming together to connect, collaborate, and support each other.
We’d love for you to join us for our next gathering on Thursday, September 4th at 6.30PM!
The evening will kick off with a workshop on Building Sustainable Art Practices with Jem Yoshioka:
About Jem:
Jem Yoshioka is an illustrator, writer and comic artist based in Pōneke, Wellington. Jem's debut graphic novel Folk Remedy Book 1 releases in September 2025, and she's busy working on Book 2. When not making comics you can find Jem dreaming up more story ideas and hanging out with her black cat. You can find her on social media @jemyoshioka most places (Instagram, BlueSky, TikTok, X)
Building Sustainable Art Practices:
In 2025 it feels like it's challenging enough to survive as a person, let alone thrive as an artist. But art has the unique power to nourish us in ways nothing else can. In this workshop Jem will share some of the strategies, habits and tools she uses to fit in making graphic novels alongside full time employment without burning out. This session is practice-agnostic, and is designed to facilitate discussion about what a sustainable art practice can look like, how to build one, and how we can support each other when things are tough. No resources required but feel free to bring any notebooks or tools you use to manage your art or your time

After that, we’ll share some kai (potluck style), have a relaxed kōrero
The gathering will be held at a cozy private space in Wellington CBD, easily accessible by public transport.
Message us for the exact location: easternsoundcollective@gmail.com
Or reach out on Instagram/Facebook: @easternsoundcollective

description:
EVENT: Presentation on Croatian Language, Culture, Science, Economy, and Language, A group of Croatian and Australian academics are touring NZ Croatian clubs in November, as a contribution to the celebration of the 1100th anniversary of the coronation of the Croatian King Tomislav. It’s a wonderful chance to engage with new ideas.
They will be at our club on Wednesday 26 November at 5.30pm (for a 6pm presentation). It is part of a project on “Science, Culture and Economy – Links between Croatian Communities in the World and the Homeland”.
The presentations are on:
- Brief history of Croatian standard language – Prof. Luka Budak (former Head of Croatian Studies, Macquarie University);
- World-renowned Croatian scientists and inventors – Dr. Marijana Borić, Scientific Advisor (Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts – CASA);
- The Croatian economy from 1992 to the present day – Prof. Tomislava Majić, Senior Lecturer (University North); and
- Croatian language recognition in Australia in 1970s – Prof. Ana Bruning (former lecturer at Croatian Studies, Macquarie University and long-time Croatian language teacher at the Croatian Schools in Sydney.
The presenters acknowledge the support of Croatian Studies Foundation of Australia, Central State Office for Croats Outside of the Republic of Croatia, Foundation of Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts.
Current timings for the event are:
5:30pm - gather for tea/coffee/drinks
6:00pm - Presentations
This will be followed by a question and discussion time, with a light supper and drinks.
All welcome! You don't need to be a member of the Club to attend!

description:
EVERYDAY POWER: WOMEN’S SELF DEFENCE WORKSHOPS, At Queen Margaret College, celebrating and empowering women isn’t something we reserve for one day a year- it’s part of who we are, every day. In that spirit, we are delighted to announce our Everyday Power: Women’s Safety & Self Defence Workshops, running this March in alignment with International Women’s Day (IWD).
WHO SHOULD ATTEND?
These sessions are open to all members of our QMC whānau, including:
• Students in Years 7–13
• Mothers, aunties, grandmothers, cousins, caregivers
• Alumni, friends, and QMC staff
• Individuals or groups- come on your own, with friends, or as a mother– daughter or family pair!
Please note: For younger students (Years 7-9), we strongly recommend the attend with a parent or adult caregiver. Sessions for younger QMC students will also be held in Term 2 and 3 as part of the Queen's Edge and Junior School afterschool programmes.
WHY YOU SHOULD ATTEND
We believe every girl and woman deserves to feel confident, safe, and in control– wherever they are. These workshops build real world skills to help participants:
• Navigate public spaces confidently
• Recognise and respond to unsafe or uncomfortable situations
• Protect personal boundaries
• Use effective physical movements for self defence
• Safely exit a situation and seek help
• Strengthen confidence, resilience, and situational awareness
WHY THESE SESSIONS MATTER
Regular incidents in Wellington and beyond remind us that girls and women still face moments where safety, comfort, or personal boundaries may be compromised - on public transport, on Courtenay Place, at social gatherings, or simply walking home.
While we hope none of us - ever face such moments, being equipped makes a difference: in awareness, in action, and in confidence.
ABOUT THE CLASS
- THREE HOUR DURATION WITH REST BREAKS
These workshops offer a practical, supportive environment where participants learn:
• Verbal strategies
• Body language techniques
• Awareness and prevention tools
• Simple, effective self defence movements
• How to stay safe in real world scenarios
Designed for all ages and abilities, these sessions are safe, empowering, and deeply confidence building.
ABOUT THE INSTRUCTORS
The workshops are led by Wil and the expert team at Tactical Survival Academy (Krav Maga). Their teaching is grounded in lived experience, real world scenarios, and a deep commitment to empowering girls and women. Since founding Tactical Survival in 2008, master instructor Wil and his team have trained thousands of New Zealanders, including members of the NZ Defence Force, members of the NZ Police, medical staff, diplomats, security professionals, and people with no prior experience with self-protection techniques.
WHAT TO BRING TO YOUR WORKSHOP SESSION
A light snack, a water bottle and comfortable clothing suitable for movement

description:
Early Childhood Centre Emergency Planning Workshop - Paraparaumu, Would you and your staff be confident in an emergency? Do you have a plan, and more importantly have you practiced it recently?

We are holding a free workshop for Early Childhood Education Centres in the Kāpiti Coast to come together to discuss your emergency plans.

This workshop is an opportunity for ECEs to share challenges and solutions and get advice from our Emergency Management Advisors.

It aims to help ECEs plan for significant events such as earthquake, tsunami, armed intruders and to share ideas and network around emergency planning.

This is an opportunity for Centre Managers, Directors, Health & Safety Representatives or Leads to:

- Share solutions, practical advice and learnings from recent events.
- Discuss your current plans with emergency management professionals.
- Learn more about our local hazards and important planning information including lessons learnt from the Christchurch Earthquake, Christchurch Mosque Attack and Cyclone Gabrielle.

Hope to see you there as we build safer and more resilient ECEs and communities together.

Places are limited to a maximum of 30 people attending each session. This workshop is endorsed by the Ministry of Education.

For more information, please email info@wremo.nz

We aim to make our community events inclusive to all people. If you are attending the event and have specific accessibility requirements, you can send us an email at info@wremo.nz with the event name and we will get in touch to see how we can meet your needs as best we can.
