description:
Easter Pole Weekend 2026, Easter Pole Weekend – WELLINGTON, New Zealand
Friday 3rd April – Monday 6th April
16 workshops – Pole Showcase – Pole Photoshoots
*
This Easter we have an exciting four-day Pole Weekend planned at Body Electric Pole Dance Studio!
On Friday 3rd, Saturday 4th and Sunday 5th April we run our workshops. We have invited Body Electric instructors plus guests to create something special for you – there is A LOT of variety to choose from: from Pole Tricks and Flow classes to Choreography and Twerk workshops. You can choose one workshop if you want! Or we would recommend jumping in the deep end and doing several! We have a package of 6 workshops for those of you wanting to be extra hardcore. We also have a special deal of 2 workshops plus a pole show ticket for $95!
*
On Saturday night The Pole Room Easter-themed showcase “Let There Be Light” will impress and entertain with workshop instructor performances plus special guests. $30 tickets from www.eventfinda.co.nz
Monday 6th April, is devoted to pole photoshoots! Book a session with talented pole photographer Dave Giles and get pics of your favourite moves. This shoot is suitable for pole students of all levels. Maree & Giada will be there to help you with poses. $120 for 20 mins (2x 10min sessions) 4 edited images.
*
PRICES
1 workshop - $40
2 workshops, plus a ticket to the pole show - $95
6 Workshops - $210
Pole Show Tickets - $30 through Eventfinda
Pole Photo Shoot with Dave Giles - $120 for 20 min shoot (2x10 min, with room between for a costume change). 4 edited images with the option to purchase more. Help will be given by Giada and Maree for posing.
Please email us to book: info@bodyelectricpole.co.nz
WORKSHOPS (Scroll down for more detailed descriptions of workshops)
*
Friday 3rd April
10.30am Pole Flow, Leg Rotations & Flexible Hips (Ana)
12 noon Belly Dance: Making It Slinky (Pip E-Lysaah)
1.30pm Sensual Awakening: Unleash your Inner Siren (Vixen Temple)
3.00pm Nail Your Inverts (Elisa Puccioni)
4.30pm Feeling the Floor (Karina Shann)
6.00pm Choreography Kickstarter (Maree & Giada)
Saturday 4th April
10.30am Chair Tricks & Choreo (Billie Jean)
12 noon Creative Practices For Freestyle (Rachael)
1.30pm Stripper Flow (Maddie May)
3.00pm Fonji 101 (Terumi Isogai)
4.30pm Tumbles & Drops (Terumi Isogai)
Saturday 4th April, 7.30pm, The Fringe Bar, Wellington
Pole Show featuring Teachers & Guests – “Let There Be Light”
Sunday 5th April
10.30am Booty Electric: Twerkshop (Emma Hopkins)
12 noon Bendy Bunnies: Stretch (Judith Dillon)
1.30pm Hula Hoop 101 (Dylan Daisy)
3.00pm Perfect Pirouettes (Gabrielle McElwee)
4.30pm Handstands with Julia (Julia Bromley)
Workshop details
Friday 3rd April
10.30am Pole Flow, Leg Rotations & Flexible Hips (Ana)
Leg rotations can create different shapes, lines and feeling to our movement. They can elevate our pole flow and are foundational to many transitions and moves. Leg rotations start from the hips. We can make them more comfortable and access more dramatic shapes by conditioning our hip flexors and increasing our range of motion. In this workshop we will learn:
•Conditioning exercises for our hip flexors that you can add to your regular practice
•The foundational movement of leg rotations and how they can elevate and create variety in our pole moves
•A variety of dance elements that use leg rotations, that you can add to your pole flow or routines
(All levels)
12 noon Belly Dance: Making It Slinky (Pip E-Lysaah)
The magic isn’t in the big tricks. It’s in the pause before them.
In Making It Slinky, we’ll dive into the slow moments that define a performance, the entrance, the exit, and every delicious transition in between. This workshop is all about how you arrive, how you linger, and how you leave them slightly unwell. We’ll explore controlled undulations, weighted steps, breath-led movement, and the art of stretching time so the audience forgets to blink. Less rushing. More reigning.
This is signature muscle isolation and control, the kind that makes a simple belly roll wave feel scandalous. We’ll break down my structured approach to belly rolls, arm waves, and wraps ... not just how to execute them, but how to layer and thread them so nothing ever “stops.” Everything melts, coils, and unwraps with intention. You’ll learn how to build tension through transitions, turning the space between movements into something almost indecent. If you’ve ever been told to “do more,” this workshop is about doing less… slower… and making it hit harder.
(All levels)
1.30pm Sensual Awakening: Unleash your Inner Siren (Vixen Temple)
Get out of your head and into your body with Vixen Temple! In this empowering workshop, you'll explore techniques to tap into your inner sensuality and trust your body. Harness your erotic energy to move with seductive fluidity and hypnotic flow.
(All levels)
3.00pm Nail Your Inverts (Elisa Puccioni)
Elisa will guide you into a series of exercises, precise techniques, and insider tips to help you finally master those elusive inverts and leg hangs. Whether it's refining your form, building strength, or gaining more aerial control, we've got you covered! This workshop is ideal for beginners who are starting with their inverts up to intermediate students that want to polish their inverting techniques. Don't forget to BYH (bring your heels!) for an extra challenge and added flair!
(All levels)
4.30pm Feeling the Floor (Karina Shann)
In this workshop Karina will utilize fundamental floorwork moves such as shoulder stands, rolls, duck dives and body lines to guide you through ways that you can accentuate parts of your body, move with intention and captivate the audience. She’ll teach transitions and combos incorporating the fundamentals that you can take away to elevate your floor game. Heels optional but recommended. Socks, leg warmers optional, knee pads necessary.
(Prerequisite – Backwards & forwards roll)
6.00pm Choreography Kickstarter (Maree & Giada)
This workshop is perfect to get you started on your performance journey.
• Practical exercises to unlock your creativity, start building combos for your routines, and practice transitions between moves.
• Talk through how to structure a routine, performance tips and tricks, how to deal with nerves and much, much more!
This workshop is suitable for students of all levels. If you are currently working on a dance for a show, we can help with that. But you don't have to have a performance in mind to get heaps out of this session!
Saturday 4th April
10.30am Chair Tricks & Choreo (Billie Jean)
A burlesque classic – Express! Let’s get our groove on to this banger. We will learn some cute chair tricks and transitions to sass our way through this choreography. Beginner friendly, this dance is suitable for all levels! Plus, progressions for those who want to get upside down.
Wear comfortable clothes, socks or dance heels.
(All levels)
12 noon Creative Practices for Freestyle (Rachael)
Freestyling is a fantastic way to develop your movement style. This workshop will cover various concepts like tempo, sensation, texture, intention. You’ll learn new approaches for practicing freestyling and have fun while gaining a new appreciation for the practice.
(All levels)
1.30pm Stripper Flow (Maddie May)
Learn how to slink around the pole in your own authentic way, focusing on embellishing movements, fluid transitions and musicality!
(All levels)
3.00pm Fonji 101 (Terumi Isogai)
This is an introduction course for fonji related moves. Starting with preparation exercises to get used to the movement. Learn the techniques to execute fonji safely and effectively!
(Prerequisite: Shoulder mount, preferably aerial)
4.30pm Tumbles & Drops (Terumi Isogai)
You climb up the pole, and now what? Learn fun ways to come down the pole!
(Prerequisite: Aerial invert. Leg hang)

7.30pm Pole Show – “Let There Be Light”
Sunday 5th April
10.30am Booty Electric: Twerkshop (Emma Hopkins)
Come along to Emma’s beginner Twerkshop where you will learn basic twerk moves from the floor to on the pole. We will cover different styles of twerking and then put them together for a sexy, bootiful routine. We need to protect our knees while we are popping it like it's hot so please bring kneepads. Sneakers are also recommended.
(All Levels)
12 noon Bendy Bunnies: Stretch (Judith Dillon)
Level up your flexibility this Easter with fun and creative ways to move your body. Whether you've got a dedicated practice or you've never tried stretching before, all levels are welcome - Judith will adapt poses for every level and ability.
In this workshop we will focus on partner assisted stretches and stretching with props (blocks/wall) We will work on breathing into deep stretches, relaxing into passive holds, as well as muscle activation for some fun duo poses.
(All levels)
1.30pm Hula Hoop 101 (Dylan Daisy)
Learn the basics of hula hooping. Start the spin, maintain your core tension and you’re off! Using different body parts to flow and transition make hula hooping a fun and dynamic art form.
After a lifetime of commanding stages and perfecting her craft, Dylan is a fantastic and skilled hoop performer who has become a favourite in the Wellington performing arts scene. Bring a hoop if you have one (We will supply some).
(All levels)
3.00pm Perfect Pirouettes (Gabrielle McElwee)
Keen to learn some smooth ways to turn, flow and transition around the pole?
Want to improve your dance fluidity?
Then this workshop is for you! Pirouettes are a MUST HAVE for any pole dancer, so this workshop will cover pirouette technique, a variety of fun pirouette patterns & transitions which build in level, ending with a short flow sequence. Socks are recommended.
(All levels)
4.30pm Handstands with Julia (Julia Bromley)
Come and get upside down with Julia! This class workshop will focus on the basic foundations of handstands and will give you skills and drills to continue to work on towards your upside-down goals. You will be guided through exercises and drills to maximise strength and technique needed to begin or extend your handstand journey. Julia has been teaching workshops and private lessons for over 7 years in both circus, pole and dance studios and loves seeing students gain the body awareness and technique to attain their goals!
(All levels)
*
Prices:
Single Workshop session: $40 per person
2 workshops, plus a ticket to the pole show - $95
Group package: 6 Workshops - $210

description:
Eastern Sound Collective - Asian Artist Meet up, The Eastern Sound Collective is a growing community of creatives with pan-Asian roots, coming together to connect, collaborate, and support each other.

We’d love for you to join us for our next gathering on Thursday, September 4th at 6.30PM!

The evening will kick off with a workshop on Building Sustainable Art Practices with Jem Yoshioka:

About Jem:
Jem Yoshioka is an illustrator, writer and comic artist based in Pōneke, Wellington. Jem's debut graphic novel Folk Remedy Book 1 releases in September 2025, and she's busy working on Book 2. When not making comics you can find Jem dreaming up more story ideas and hanging out with her black cat. You can find her on social media @jemyoshioka most places (Instagram, BlueSky, TikTok, X)

Building Sustainable Art Practices:
In 2025 it feels like it's challenging enough to survive as a person, let alone thrive as an artist. But art has the unique power to nourish us in ways nothing else can. In this workshop Jem will share some of the strategies, habits and tools she uses to fit in making graphic novels alongside full time employment without burning out. This session is practice-agnostic, and is designed to facilitate discussion about what a sustainable art practice can look like, how to build one, and how we can support each other when things are tough. No resources required but feel free to bring any notebooks or tools you use to manage your art or your time

description:
Eco Dye Workshop, Eco Dye Workshop
Impressions of Nature on Silk

Eco dyeing, also known as leaf or eco print, is a gentle, alchemical process where the natural pigments of leaves are transferred directly onto fabric, creating one-of-a-kind botanical imprints.

Join me for a full day of slow making and discovery as we explore this beautiful dialogue between nature and cloth. In the morning, we’ll forage around the hall, gathering leaves and foliage that speak to us. You’ll learn how to prepare and bundle silk with plant materials, drawing out colours and patterns from the landscape itself.

In the afternoon, you’ll design and dye your own silk scarf — a wearable memory of place and season, marked by the delicate traces of nature’s touch.

You will learn

• which plants and fibres work best for this method
• how to use an iron mordant to enhance colour and detail
• different bundling techniques and approaches

All materials and tools will be provided for use during the workshop.

Your workshop fee includes silk fabrics to explore and experiment with, one silk scarf to design and dye, and a detailed handout with information on mordants, dye plants, tips, and useful resources.

A ‘what to bring’ list (including suggestions for clothing and optional items) will be sent out closer to the workshop date.

Booking through my website (see link above)

description:
Explore Monoprint Workshop, Of all the print making methods, mono printing is the most spontaneous, responsive and versatile, being the medium for everything from abstract expressionism to hyper photographic realism. Simple and direct with the minimum of equipment and media, mono printing is approachable for any age or ability level, yet the creative potential is unlimited.

Planned here is a three day workshop to introduce mono printing from simple hand printing, spontaneous transfer methods through to working with presses and multiple matrices.

For people starting in printmaking and people already with an art practice in any media. We will experiment with a whole new method of mark making, transfer and texture to build skill level and also provide a cross discipline change to invigorate your existing art practice of painting or drawing.

Also you will be introduced to a progressive evolution development technique for learning and to push yourself into new areas of creativity that can be applied to other art practices and medias.

One hour lunch - Bring a drink bottle and a packed lunch to enjoy in the historic Inverlochy house or explore the Te Aro cafes.

Basic materials are supplied.

Two day workshop: Sat 25 - Sun 26 October, 10 am - 4 pm daily.

description:
Exploring Figure & Form, In this course we will study the human figure through drawing and sculpture. Both mediums use close observation as a focus and encourage the study of the curves, angles, and subtleties of the human body to accurately depict it.

Students will be guided in experimentations with size and volume, as well as exercises that will sharpen one's attention to detail, improving an artist's overall observational skills and enhancing their artistry across all subjects and styles.

In this course you will -

- Learn how to imbue a sense of the models personality into your drawing and sculpture
- Learn different approaches to rendering the surface of your sculpture
- Explore traditional working methods in both drawing and sculpting

Course fee includes model, tutor, air-dry modelling clay, necessary tools & equipment
label: Classes & Workshops

description:
Exploring Figure & Form, In this course you will study the human figure through clay sculpting from a live model. You will explore the fundamental proportions of the figure; the underlying rhythms to a particular pose that make it look dynamic and alive; and how to recreate the subtleties of the models character. The close observation of volume, curves and angle relationships will sharpen your attention to detail, improving your overall observational skills and enhancing your artistry across all subjects and styles.

This course prioritises hands-on skill development over producing a finished project. Students will focus on mastering sculpting techniques, materials and equipment rather than leaving with a ready-made sculpture.

In this course you will -

- Learn how to imbue a sense of the models personality into your sculpture
- Learn the fundamental proportions of the human figure
- Learn different approaches to rendering the surface of your sculpture
- Explore traditional working methods in sculpting

Course fee includes model, tutor, use of clay, necessary tools & equipment. Please note the following:

- If at the end of the course, you choose to keep your sculpture, there is a $25 additional charge for the clay.
- You also have the option fire your sculpture in the Inverlochy kiln at the end of the course for an additional $60. The sculpture will be ready for collection 3-4 weeks later depending on drying conditions. The $60 extra fee includes the clay, firing and a two hour workshop learning how to hollow out and prep your sculpture for firing. Date, time and payment to be organised at your final class.

This four week course runs on Saturdays, 8-29 Aug, 10am-1pm

description:
Exploring our Shared Humanity, Do you ever feel that you're just going through the motions? That life is a series of tasks, a pursuit of pleasure, or a race for self-improvement that never really satisfies? This isn't just a feeling; it's a fundamental human question about what it means to exist.

Description
Join experienced psychotherapist Rohit Grover for a six-week course that invites you to look beyond the surface of everyday life. In these two-hour sessions, we will explore the core tenets of existential therapy, moving away from the conventional focus on self and hedonism. Instead, we'll grapple with life's big questions:

What does it truly mean to live a value-driven life?
Do our personal values matter, or is the search for meaning just an illusion?
What is the "being" part of "human being" all about?

Through guided discussions, reflective exercises, and insights from classic existential thinkers, Rohit will help you navigate this profound territory. This isn't about finding easy answers. It's about developing the courage to ask the right questions, to confront the realities of freedom, responsibility, and meaning, and to discover a more authentic way of living.

This course is for anyone ready to step off the treadmill and begin a deeper exploration of what it means to be alive. Come and find out what it means to truly exist

Upon completion of this course, participants will be able to:

Differentiate between a life driven by external pressures or fleeting pleasures and one rooted in personal values and authentic meaning.

Identify and critically examine the core existential givens of human existence, such as freedom, responsibility, isolation, and the search for meaning.

Articulate a personal understanding of what it means to "be" a human being, moving beyond a purely functional or biological definition.

Arrive at sensing rather than thinking. Sensing this existence, this dance of life. Widen your view of existence.

What is the "being" part of "human being" all about?
Through guided discussions, reflective exercises, and insights from classic existential thinkers, Rohit will help you navigate this profound territory. This isn't about finding easy answers. It's about developing the courage to ask the right questions, to confront the realities of freedom, responsibility, and meaning, and to discover a more authentic way of living.
This course is for anyone ready to step off the treadmill and begin a deeper exploration of what it means to be alive. Come and find out what it means to truly exist
Upon completion of this course, participants will be able to:
Differentiate between a life driven by external pressures or fleeting pleasures and one rooted in personal values and authentic meaning.
Identify and critically examine the core existential givens of human existence, such as freedom, responsibility, isolation, and the search for meaning.
Articulate a personal understanding of what it means to "be" a human being, moving beyond a purely functional or biological definition.
Arrive at sensing rather than thinking. Sensing this existence, this dance of life. Widen your view of existence.

description:
Expressive Watercolour, Watercolour is special because of the fluid properties that produce spontaneous and unique results. The inability to anticipate exactly what the paint will do makes watercolour an exciting medium to work with.

In this course we will learn to set the conditions for surprising and beautiful accidents to occur on the page. By incorporating these looser abstract elements into representational paintings we can convey heightened emotions in our work.

Throughout the term we will cover the following:

- The wet into wet technique to achieve one of a kind paint interactions.
- Learn about transparent colour mixing to create luminosity in your paintings.
- Use marbling to find organic shapes and patterns.
- Study the relationship between line and colour and the different
- Ways they can be combined to find a personal style.
- Experiment with composition through collage.

Each class we will look at examples of historic and contemporary painting, and discuss how to selectively incorporate references into your work. Over the term you will build up a visual style and body of work.

Whether you’re new to watercolour or looking to expand your range, this course offers an opportunity to explore the expressive potential of watercolour.

Basic materials included. Students must be at least 16 years of age to attend this course.

Discover the wonders of Wairarapa Dark Sky Reserve and learn astrophotography with Fujifilm experts

About this Event


Rock Arch, Wairarapa Dark Sky Reserve
Photo Credit: Keith Molly




Nau mai, Welcome!

Join us for an evening under the stars as we launch the Wairarapa Dark Sky Reserve Photo Competition, a collaboration with Wairarapa Dark Sky Reserve and Fujifilm New Zealand.
The Wairarapa Dark Sky Reserve is one of the most accessible dark sky locations in the lower North Island, making it an amazing place for people to experience and photograph the night sky without needing to travel too far. This event is designed to inspire more people to get out there, enjoy the reserve, and explore what is possible with a camera under dark skies.
Whether you are completely new to astrophotography or already have some experience, this evening is a chance to learn, shoot, and connect with others in a beautiful and easily reachable dark sky location.


Your evening
6:30 – 7:30pm | Discovery talk at Pae Tū Mōkai O Tauira Whare presented by Charlotte Harding (Dark Sky Reserve Project Coordinator), Keith Molloy and JM Beltran (Photographers)
7:30 – 8:00pm | Transition to Lake Wairarapa (optional)
8:00 – 9:30pm | Hands-on night photography session by the lake, with hot drinks available for participants (optional, additional ticket required, limited to 30 participants)


Who this is for
Anyone wanting to discover and learn more about the Wairarapa Dark Sky Reserve
People curious about astrophotography
Beginners wanting to learn the basics
Intermediate photographers wanting expert tips
Fujifilm users and anyone interested in night photography


Fujifilm gear support
Fujifilm New Zealand will provide selected gear to touch and try during the event.


What to bring
For the outdoor session, attendees should bring:
Camera
Warm clothing
Headlamp or torch
Optional: Empty memory card (Fujifilm gear will be available try during this session, bring your memory card to take home your images!)
Optional: Tripod


Weather
This event is weather-dependent.
Back-up date: Saturday 13 June 2026
If the weather is not suitable, registered attendees will be notified of any changes.




Pūtangirua Pinnacles, Dark Sky Reserve
Photo credit: JM Beltran


Agenda


🕑: 06:30 PM - 07:30 PM
Discovery talk at Pae Tū Mōkai O Tauira Whare

🕑: 08:00 PM - 09:30 PM
Lakeside photography session (additional)

description:
Financial Planning for Retirement, Financial Planning for Retirement
Massey University's annual Retirement Expenditure Guidelines study (2019) found:
Just 40% of pre-retirees believed they were well-prepared for retirement, and 57% considered retirement to be a concern.  They also confirmed, New Zealand Superannuation is not sufficient to fund the retirement most people want.
Ministry of Social Development (2020):
22% of all people receiving New Zealand Superannuation also receive additional support payments, with over 44,000 superannuants receiving additional accommodation support,
And if you needed to obtain Government assisted accommodation, at the end of March 2020, more than 16,300 households were waiting for state or social housing.
Living in a motel or boarding house with strangers (who may have other vulnerable backgrounds) is not an ideal or safe location to spend your retirement years.   But for many, it is the only option they can afford.
If you have not planned for your retirement, then this course is you! 
This course has been developed for people in their 50’s or 60’s that are looking at retirement and have no idea if they can financially survive it: what to do, what $’s they need, how or where they can generate additional income, or even where to go to get help. 
It is targeted towards those that still have some time (for some - not much) to make adjustments, learn some basic financial skills, make some big decisions, and positively influence the quality of their pending retirement. 
You will be introduced to a simple step by step guide to developing a financial plan for retirement. 
You will work though a case study in class, and can then go away and repeat the process with your own data/details.  You will be provided with comprehensive course notes to enable you to update the case study information with your own information. 
At each step, key considerations and financial concepts will be defined, explained and discussed to help you understand the financial requirements of retirement.  
Are you ready for the retirement lifestyle you hoped or dreamed of?  If not, then this course is for you.
A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
Disclaimer:  The tutors are not financial advisors.  No investments, products nor specific recommendations will be provided.  A step by step planning process will be taught by working through a case study.  Key considerations that should be used by the participants when looking at their own options to bridge the financial gap between what is available through superannuation and what is required to meet lifestyle goals will be provided and discussed.  Product names may be used in examples and explanations to help participants understand the financial concepts and the planning process.

description:
Financial Planning for Retirement, Financially successful people don’t achieve their wealth by accident – they make and execute clear plans. Your retirement is on the horizon and research shows you’re most likely nowhere near financially ready for the retirement you desire and deserve! Get a complete and utterly practical financial plan, so you can have the retirement you want.

Massey University's annual Retirement Expenditure Guidelines study (2019) found:

Just 40% of pre-retirees believed they were well-prepared for retirement, and 57% considered retirement to be a concern. They also confirmed, New Zealand Superannuation is not sufficient to fund the retirement most people want.
Ministry of Social Development (2020):

22% of all people receiving New Zealand Superannuation also receive additional support payments, with over 44,000 superannuants receiving additional accommodation support, and if you needed to obtain Government-assisted accommodation, at the end of March 2020, more than 16,300 households were waiting for state or social housing.

Living in a motel or boarding house with strangers (who may have other vulnerable backgrounds) is not an ideal or safe location to spend your retirement years. But for many, it is the only option they can afford.

If you have not planned for your retirement, then this course is you!

This course has been developed for people in their 50s or 60s that are looking at retirement and have no idea if they can financially survive it: what to do, what $’s they need, how or where they can generate additional income, or even where to go to get help.

It is targeted towards those that still have some time (for some - not much) to make adjustments, learn some basic financial skills, make some big decisions, and positively influence the quality of their pending retirement.

You will be introduced to a simple step by step guide to developing a financial plan for retirement.

You will work through a case study in class, and can then go away and repeat the process with your own data/details. You will be provided with comprehensive course notes to enable you to update the case study information with your own information.

At each step, key considerations and financial concepts will be defined, explained and discussed to help you understand the financial requirements of retirement.

Are you ready for the retirement lifestyle you hoped or dreamed of? If not, then this course is for you.

Disclaimer: The tutors are not financial advisors. No investments, products nor specific recommendations will be provided. A step by step planning process will be taught by working through a case study. Key considerations that should be used by the participants when looking at their own options to bridge the financial gap between what is available through superannuation and what is required to meet lifestyle goals will be provided and discussed. Product names may be used in examples and explanations to help participants understand the financial concepts and the planning process.

description:
Founder Lecture: A thousand words: Photographic archives in Aotearoa, Join us for the annual Friends of the Turnbull Library Founder Lecture with Auckland Museum’s Catherine Hammond, who will share insights from her work with major photographic archives across Aotearoa.

Catherine's Founder Lecture will discuss the role and impact of photographic archives as complex repositories of memory and research.

Currently Director of Collections and Research at Auckland War Memorial Museum Tāmaki Paenga Hira, Catherine has more than 20-years’ experience working with artists’ archives in major cultural institutions in Aotearoa.

She will discuss the recent book and touring exhibition, 'A Different Light: First Photographs of Aotearoa', and reflect on archives and meaning-making in examples ranging from Marti Friedlander to Frances Hodgkins, feminist photographic practice and whānau portraiture.

Light refreshments will follow the lecture.

The Village NZ and Sparkle Fitness invite you to join a revitalising postpartum exercise class with Sierra Ryland, owner of Sparkle Fitness, at Karori Rec Centre, Wellington!

Sierra is a MumSafe, REPs (Registered Exercise Professional) and Safe Return to Exercise certified personal trainer, running and triathlon coach, and owner of Sparkle Fitness. As a mum herself, she knows how important it is to feel strong and confident in your body while also balancing the demands of motherhood.

This class offers a gentle, supportive approach to rebuilding your strength, focusing on pelvic floor health, core restoration, and functional movement. Whether you’re returning to exercise or just starting, this class is your space to recharge, connect, and feel at home in your body again.

What can you expect from this class?
- A 45min session
- This class will focus on the pelvic floor and restoring your core by teaching you proper cueing to help you activate the right muscles. A fantastic opportunity to make sure you start to heal and strengthen from the inside out.
- Functional strength and cardio exercises so that you can be confident each day.
- Small group size: up to 10 mums per class.
- A chance to connect with other Mum's like you, in a small and comfortable environment.

- Morning tea provided after the session and a chance to chat and ask questions.
What do you need to bring with you?
- You! Babies are welcome if you need to bring them along.
- A workout mat and your own water bottle.

This class is FREE, but registration is essential! Spaces are limited so register now to secure your spot https://wix.to/eWOqgl9

description:
Freedom and Responsibility in Science - WELLINGTON, Join the Royal Society Te Apārangi for a wide-ranging panel discussion about the many threats to the integrity of science around the world, how they can be addressed, and New Zealand’s place in the global context. The panel will feature expert guest speakers from the International Science Council’s (ISC) Committee for Freedom and Responsibility in Science.
Science today faces many challenges: Scientific and academic freedoms are declining worldwide as anti-science ideology becomes imbedded in many of the world’s governments; state obligations towards enabling science as a human right remain chronically ignored; irresponsible scientific conduct and governance of all kinds increasingly undermine science from within; and the tally of wars and crises which rob the world of the scientific talent held by entire nations is growing year by year.
At precisely the moment when scientific progress on some of the existential threats to humanity is most urgent, science itself is under more pressure than perhaps ever before. So, what can we do?
About the ISC Committee for Freedom and Responsibility in Science:
The Committee monitors trends related to scientific and academic freedom globally, advises the ISC on official statements and positions, and advocates for the Principles of Freedom and Responsibility in Science. The Committee also engages in major projects at the intersection of science, human rights, and philosophy, such as the ISC’s recent interpretation of The Right to Participate in and Benefit from Science.

description:
From Rags to Reuse - Up-cycling and Sustainability Workshop, Join craft artist and eco lifestylist Stella Carruthers for a day of practical textile upcycling and learning about sustainability in the context of low-waste living. Gain practical skills in rag rug techniques and engage with ideas around textile waste, green washing and actions you can take to make a difference in your daily life and the wider world.

Stella Carruthers, textile artist and eco lifestylist, will guide you on this one-day workshop to learn about sustainable living from a reduce and reuse perspective. Learn about textile waste as a global issue and explore rag rug-making techniques - you will leave the workshop with the skills to finish a project at home. Investigate the 8 pillars of the zero-waste movement and how they can inform low-waste living. Identify the key components of greenwashing so you can make informed purchases as a conscious consumer. Finally, leave the workshop feeling empowered to explore wider social and political actions as they apply to waste issues in contemporary society.

Most materials provided, but please bring a pair of small sewing scissors and sewing shears if you have them, a pen and paper, and your lunch.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Talk confidently about textile waste as a global issue and be empowered with the skills and ideas to reduce your personal textile waste footprint through recycling and upcycling practices
- have the beginnings of a cushion cover made using the rag rug stitching technique of couching, and the skills and knowledge to finish the project at home.
-Identify and describe the 8 pillars of the zero-waste movement and how they apply to recycling practices in contemporary Aotearoa New Zealand society.
- Understand what greenwashing is and have debunked some common greenwashing myths prevalent in society.
- Have learned some practical tips for living low waste in the city.
- Feel empowered to explore wider social and political action as it applies to waste issues in the modern world.

A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

description:
Fundamentals of Drawing for Teens, In this course you will learn the basics of structure and perspective so you can draw anything you like. Returning students are assigned additional challenges in order to promote continuous development of their drawing journey.

This course is catered to ages 13 years or older. Children under 13, please refer to the Tuesday afternoon course.

We'll be drawing on paper with pencils and pens. There's a strong emphasis on learning structure and perspective drawing, with the aim to feel more confident in drawing anything - real or imagined. We will be drawing things from real life, from photos and from our imagination.

What you will learn in the class.

- Perspective - learning the basics to help draw forms and spaces convincingly.
- Using perspective to draw organic forms.
- The structure of human faces - Constructing the face to understand it.
- The structure of human figures - Drawing the body from the skeleton out.
- The structure of animal and creature bodies - Seeing the similarities to humans.
- Shading and shadows - Understanding light as it hits objects.
- Composition - Arranging elements in your picture.
- Using different B&W mediums like pencils, pens, inks.

Eight week course on Thursdays, 30 July - 17 Sept.
Basic materials provided.

Discover glass fusing in this 5-week beginner course—create beautiful pieces, gain skills, all materials included.
Always wanted to work with glass? This five-week beginner glass fusing course is the perfect place to start. In this fun and interactive class you will be inspired to find answers to develop a simple makeover or design a grand new plan for your own outdoor area. Find solutions to problems and with creativity, develop your own design to suit your site and character.

description:
Garden Planting Design, Garden Planting Design
Spent a fortune on plants and still not achieved the dream? Can’t work out why some plants thrive and others barely survive? Ready to make exciting changes but no idea where to start and not much gardening background? This interactive and fun course will answer all your queries and give you confidence to create the garden you want with the right plants to achieve it. Style of garden, colour, plant palette – we’ll cover it all – and more.

Time permitting, we will look at photos of your gardens as “personal case studies” to help you get the most from the course.

• Identify and work with the site and climate conditions of your garden/outdoor areas to be developed; modify plant choices if necessary
• Accurately draw your detailed planting design on paper and to scale.
• Understand the role of colour and different plants in the garden and incorporate it into your design
• Learn how to improve your soil to guarantee success
• Use your final design to create a “shopping list” of plants
• Calculate anticipated expenditure / prepare a budget (to also include soil improving items)

Hardscaping design. This is available in a separate course.

• Recommending suppliers, service providers and retailers, although knowledge and experiences of the tutor and peers will be shared appropriately
• Pruning practices or plant disease management

description:
Genealogy - Basics of Ancestry.com DNA Tests, Have you done a DNA test with Ancestry.com? Don't know what to do next? This course will cover the basics of what your DNA results mean. We'll look at the tools available on Ancestry.com and other DNA websites to help you use DNA for your family's history.

Got your test results back and still wondering what a centiMorgan or a shared match is? Find out what the size of your match means and the tools available to help you work out possible family relationships.

We'll start by looking at Clustering and how the Grouping tool on Ancestry.com can help with this. We'll also look at the ThruLines and Common Ancestors tools to see how they can provide suggestions for knocking down brick walls in your research.

Also covered during this course are other websites you can upload your results to, how to manage other family member's DNA test results and other tools available when you get a bit more advanced - and just in case you need help in the future, we'll look at some of the places you could get this from.

Please note: This course will only cover DNA tests taken through Ancestry.com

Bring a USB stick and your Ancestry.com login details.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Understand the information provided by Ancestry.com about your DNA matches
- Use the Grouping, ThruLines and Common Ancestors tools on Ancestry.com
- Use the Shared CentiMorgan tool on DNAPainter.com
- Understand where to find other tools
- Understand the options for using other DNA websites
- Understand where to get further help

Prerequisites
For those who have already done a DNA test through Ancestry.com
You will need good computing and internet skills.

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Presented by Sarah Hewitt.

description:
Get Animated! Stop-motion Animation Workshop, Get Animated! Stop-motion Animation Workshop
Ever wanted to try your hand at stop-motion animation and bring inanimate objects to life? Now you can!

Join animator Steffen Kreft and storyteller and poet William Connor for a practical, hands-on workshop that will inspire and enable you to make your own magical stop-motion worlds and movies at home.

Supported by Wairarapa Library Service.

You’ll need to download an app on your smartphone, bring a desk-lamp, a snack, your fully charged smart-phone and charger, a steady hand and an open mind. All other materials provided.

Here's the (free) app to download on your smartphone:
i-Phone:
https://apps.apple.com/nz/app/stop-motion-studio/id441651297
Android:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.cateater.stopmotionstudio&pli=1

Ages 12 and up welcome – no prior experience required.
Places are limited to 16, so get animated!

Workshop 1-4pm, then a break, and at 5.30pm, we'll screen everyone's work.

Registration is required.
To register your interest, please email <events.waiword>.

About the tutors:

WILLIAM CONNOR
William Connor studied German, English literature, and Theatre at Victoria University in Welling-ton, where he completed his Master’s in creative writing in 2016. He lives between Berlin and Greytown, and works as a teacher, translator, editor, writer, and puppeteer. He has published numerous poems and short stories in several anthologies and journals, has written and per-formed in a number of plays that have toured New Zealand and Germany, and is the writer and cocreator of the intercultural comedy web-series Lifeswap, which explores and celebrates the differences between the German and New Zealand cultures.

STEFFEN KREFT
Steffen Kreft is an animation film director, illustrator, marionette maker and puppeteer. He was born in Münster, Germany and is currently living in Greytown in the Wairarapa.
When he first moved to New Zealand in 2007, he did his Masters in design at Massey University and co-founded the animation company National Park Studios in 2010. He taught design, animation and puppet making at Massey University and The Learning Connexion. In 2012, he directed and organised the Greytown Arts Festival and directed and made marionettes for the award winning adult puppet show “The Kitchen at the End of the World”. In 2014, Steffen and his partner William moved to Berlin for a few years where they started the popular animated web series Lifeswap about the cultural differences between New Zealand and Germany.
Now, he spends his time making short films for organisations like the French/German TV channel Arte, several New Zealand ministries, German museums and start-up companies or creates giant puppets and mesmerising marionette shows for festivals. He is also building a beautiful tiny house on wheels – apparently his most creatively challenging as well as satisfying project yet.
He has a passion for making things with his hands and while his projects are so varied, he can be very proud of the attention to detail that is obvious in all of his work.

description:
Get The Job - CV And Cover Letters, Are you looking to polish your CV and cover letter writing skills to nail your next job application? This course provides you with the tools to create a strong and updated CV and cover letter writing, using skills that are personalised to you.

Description
Explore how to appropriately structure and polish your CV and cover letter in order to achieve optimum results. This course prioritises you. Identify your key skills and weave these into your CV and cover letter to land you your next job interview.

Whatever job you are going for, there are key characteristics that should not be missed in your CV and cover letter. The focus of this course is to provide you with the same lens as a recruiter. By learning how your job application is reviewed by a recruiter, you will gain skills to streamline your CV and improve your cover letter writing. This will increase your chances of being a successful candidate and set you up to land an interview for your ideal job.

It doesn’t matter what previous experience you have - everyone has a range of skills that they can offer to their future employer. Fortunately, a strong and realistic CV and cover letter will showcase these skills and increase your chances for job success.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Recognise the features of an effective, well-crafted CV and cover letter and apply these to your own job applications;
- Apply different approaches, styles and techniques while writing your CV and cover letter depending on the context and job;
- Help others with their CV and cover letter writing (friends and whānau).

[Note: You must be a NZ citizen or resident to qualify for the free course fee option. A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

Courses need a minimum number to go ahead, so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email, so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Prerequisites
There is no prior knowledge or experience required. This course applies to all levels of candidate experience - it doesn’t matter if the participant is applying for their first ever job, or they are well-experienced in the job market. I tailor my content to empower everybody, regardless of their previous experience or job experience.

Whatever job you are going for, there are key characteristics that should not be missed in your CV and cover letter. The focus of this course is to provide you with the same lens as a recruiter. By learning how your job application is reviewed by a recruiter, you will gain skills to streamline your CV, and improve your cover letter writing. This will increase your chances of being a successful candidate and sets you up to land an interview for your ideal job.

It doesn’t matter what previous experience you have - everyone has a range of skills that they can offer to their future employer. Fortunately, a strong and realistic CV and cover letter will showcase these skills and increase your chances for job success.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Recognise the features of an effective, well-crafted CV and cover letter and apply these to your own job applications;
- Apply different approaches, styles and techniques while writing your CV and cover letter depending on the context and job;
- Help others with their CV and cover letter writing (friends and whānau).

[Note: You must be a NZ citizen or resident to qualify for the free course fee option. A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Prerequisites
There is no prior knowledge or experience required. This course is applicable to all levels of candidate experience - it doesn’t matter if the participant is applying for their first ever job, or they are well experienced in the job market. I tailor my content to empower everybody regardless of their previous experience or job experience.

description:
Get the Job: STARR Interview Technique And Preparation, Get the best results in job interviews. Learn how to approach behavioural questions and impress the interview panel. Ace interviews using the potent Starr method. Use it to your advantage by answering competency focused questions with winning replies.

Meet the demand for excellence in the job market head on. Learn how to utilise the Starr technique in the way that recruiters use it. That is, to define and seek out the skills and qualities of the best candidate. Master the Starr skills and feel confident in your next job interview.

Familarise yourself with the skills needed to ace your next interview. Learn the STARR method as an approach to responding to behavioural based questions. Understand how to use concrete examples from your life as proof that you possess the experience and skills for the job you are applying for. You’ll develop the key interview skill of being able to share your accomplishments through real-life examples.

In this course, you are taught how to identify specific example situations that are unique to you. You’ll learn how to confidently talk about the tasks involved and describe how you completed the key task and met its challenges. We’ll also consider the context of jobs you are interviewing for and how to choose examples that best show the desired skills interviewers are seeking.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Develop a higher level of confidence in approaching job interviews.
- Identify the different components of the STARR acronym and apply them to the job interview context.
- Identify what behavioural based questions are and why recruiters use them.
- Successfully answer behavioural based interview questions by applying the STARR technique.
- Develop skills in using real life examples to show transferable skills in the workplace.

Comedian, writer, and lifelong teacher Neil Thornton (seen on TV3’s After Hours) brings you a fun low-pressure comedy workshop.
Sign up here: https://www.nzcomedyschool.com/enroll

Everything you need to know to get a mic in your face:
-generating ideas

-effective delivery

Neil Thornton is an award-winning comedian with appearances on NZ TV and all over the world. In addition to his career as a stand-up comedian, comedy teacher, and writer, Neil has been teaching writing, creativity, and presentations for more than 20 years.

- A prime-time spot in a graduation showcase with a professional MC
- A high-definition video of your graduation performance to share with friends
Class is limited to 10 students, so enroll early!

description:
Getting the Most from ChatGPT: Practical AI for Everyday Use, AI tools like ChatGPT are everywhere, but how do you get the best out of them? In this hands-on, phone-based workshop, Jon Bell will guide you through practical techniques to make ChatGPT a more useful, reliable partner in your work and life. Whether you’ve tried it a few times or use it regularly, you’ll learn how to write better prompts, refine responses, and avoid common pitfalls without needing any technical background.
We’ll cover real examples, answer your questions as they come up, and spend plenty of time experimenting together so you leave feeling confident and ready to put your new skills to use.
Please bring: A phone with the ChatGPT app installed, and enough battery to last the day.
By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:
Write effective prompts that get clearer, more useful responses
Use ChatGPT for research, brainstorming, and creative work
Recognise the tool’s limitations (and how to work around them)
Apply practical strategies for using AI in your personal or professional projects
Confidently troubleshoot when ChatGPT gives unexpected or unhelpful answers
A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

description:
Gin and Clay Magical Blue Tile Workshop, A fabulous and fun workshop that combines creativity and gin tasting for a unique experience.

Create a stunning clay tile that will be fired and glazed in a vibrant blue just before Christmas, making it perfect for displaying in your home or as a thoughtful gift. Alongside that sip 3 delicious Gin samples from the Bond Store distillery where we will be working.

My clay classes are suitable for complete beginners or those with experience and are a wonderful way to relax, replenish and have fun. Working with clay is good for the soul! description:
Good Luck Craft Club, MONTHLY ASIAN CRAFT WORKSHOPS FACILITATED BY ROSE, JEM + JUN

FREE BYOC (Bring Your Own Craft) from 3pm - ticketed from 2pm for those needing guidance, $15 per person: email goodluckcraftclub@gmail.com to enquire/register

As Asian arts practitioners based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara, we know Wellington is home to more than a few Asian artists working across multiple disciplines. We also know many of us are searching for a way to forge a more sustainable sense of shared community. When we have had the opportunity to meet and connect as Asian artists here in Wellington, the space and conversations are always nourishing and invigorating, leaving us wanting more.

Join us monthly from 2pm for the ticketed workshops, or swing by from 3pm and BYOC for free - arrive when you like, leave when you want! We are also starting a Community Craft Box - help us fill it, or take some new-to-you supplies home.

Facilitators will host and ensure the comfort and safety of manuhiri, supporting and drawing connections between the people in the room as well as in the community.

Each event will have a main craft theme (Chinese knotwork, crochet, life drawing etc), but attendees can work on their own craft as well.

Hosts will provide some materials in line with the craft theme (i.e. yarn, paper, thread, scrap fabric, etc), We encourage participants to bring their own materials and projects of any craft or art form - all are welcome!

Good Luck Craft Clubs goal in providing a space for Asian arts practitioners in Pōneke is to remove as many barriers as possible, making it easy to connect. While some events may be themed around a craft or festival that aligns with a particular culture or identity, the focus is less on providing access to cultural experiences and more on providing access to each other.

First theme: Celebrate the Year of the Fire Horse with us and learn to make your own good luck (Pan Chang) knot with Jun.

description:
Google Gemini Academy: Educator Roadshow (Wellington), Overview
Join us for our annual edu roadshow! Join Steve (Google) & Jack (Fusion) to learn AI basics, prompting & responsible use in the classroom.
What to expect
This half-day workshop gives you a practical introduction to Google Gemini and generative AI in education, delivered by Steve from Google and Jack from Fusion Networks.
You'll leave with the skills and confidence to use AI in your classroom and admin work, and you'll sit the Google Certified Gemini Educator exam right there in the session, no pressure, no separate booking.
Who it's for
Teachers, school leaders, and support staff who want practical, hands-on AI skills. No technical background needed.
What you'll learn
Understanding Gemini and generative AI
What generative AI is and how it's different from other tech
How Gemini fits into tools you already use, like Docs, Gmail, and Classroom
Where AI can genuinely save you time (planning, grading, feedback, communication)
Using Gemini in your day-to-day practice
Writing prompts that actually get you useful results
Creating quizzes, lesson outlines, and rubrics with Gemini
Building your own "Gem" for repeat classroom tasks, like bell-ringers or feedback frames
Drafting emails and staff communications faster
Using AI responsibly
Spotting bias, errors, and "hallucinations" in AI output
Talking to students about plagiarism and responsible AI use
Building your own classroom guidelines for AI
Sit your certification exam on the day
At the end of the session, you'll sit the Google Certified Gemini Educator exam in a relaxed, supported environment, straight after covering everything you need to know. No exam anxiety, no need to book or study separately later.
Format
Half-day, hands-on session. Bring a laptop and your Google Workspace login.

Over this taster class, you’ll be guided through the process of heating and texturing metal, cutting and shaping with traditional jewellery tools. After completing this class, you will have one pair of beautiful earrings to wear away or gift to someone special!

You will practice on smaller texture samples to work out what texture and what metal you want to go with, and then move on to creating your earrings in warm copper, yellow brass and sterling silver - with solid sterling silver earring hooks or posts.

The earrings will be made with silver bonded onto copper, giving the bright flash of silver on one side and the dark tone of copper on the other.

Maybe your horse is still doing the things you ask, but the softness, willingness, or spark you used to feel together is missing.
Maybe you notice tension, hesitation, or subtle “no’s” where there used to be “yes.”
If you want to pay attention now; understand it, work with it, and strengthen your connection before the new year. Then this clinic is for you!

Setting your horse up to be relaxed, soft, and willing
Each rider works with me in two separate 1:1 sessions; on the ground or under saddle, depending on what your horse needs.

description:
How to Build a Daily Journaling Habit, Would you like to start a creative journal but don’t know where to begin?

Do you see beautiful examples all over social media but think that couldn’t possibly be you?

Or would you just like to make your existing journaling practice more aesthetic and visually pleasing?

Then this is the class for you!

Over the past decade Mira Bradshaw has built a daily journalling practice that has stuck. Mira has created daily entries every single day since 30 December 2023 (even with a baby in the house!) and she’s coming to NZ Stationery Festival to share her wealth of experience with you.

During this class you will explore:

- Different types of journalling and which might be right for you
- Practical tips for how to start small and manageable
- Ideas for how to evolve your journalling over time and stay creatively fulfilled
- How to stick with the practice when real life gets in the way!
- Ideas and hands-on practice on how to use daily items to make your journal personal and more creative

Together, you’ll explore prompts and ideas that allow you to build a daily journalling practice that you’re proud of and is personalised to your unique life.

You’ll receive some special creative supplies and you can take home whatever you don’t use in the class to keep the creativity going!

Supplies provided:

- 3 Sheets of Custom Stickers, designed by Mira (RRP $15)
- 1 x washi tape sample card prepared by Mira (RRP $9)
- Handout with key takeaways from the class, including links to helpful content and extra information

Students, please bring along: Any notebook & pen of your choice. Pop into The Stationery Festival or Mrs Blackwell’s Village Bookshop before the class and we’ll get you all sorted with these supplies if you don't already have them!

About your teacher:
By day, Mira is a data geek, happily working with numbers and advanced technology. Based in Auckland, she’s worked at Nielsen and Stuff, and right now she’s the Head of Data Governance for SkyCity. In her free time, Mira is a creative soul who enjoys a number of hobbies including knitting (knitting patterns as Cetus Knits) and creative journaling of all kinds.
Follow Mira on Instagram: @cetuscreates

Presented as part of The New Zealand Stationery Festival. Your ticket to this event does not include access to the Stationery Festival. Please purchase a ticket for The New Zealand Stationery Festival separately.

Hutt Valley (Upper Hutt/Lower Hutt) Mathematics Leadership Community 2025, Are you the maths lead in your school? Do you feel equipped to lead the roll out of the new mathematics and statistics curriculum? Would you like to be part of a group of like-minded leads?

description:
ITI Evening Seminar Wellington with Prof. Frauke Muller, Implant Overdentures for Old and Very Old Patients
In New Zealand there is an increasing number of older persons who retain their natural dentition until later in life. Accordingly edentulous patients will not only be older, they will also be also more challenging to treat. Implant-supported overdentures (IODs) may significantly improve the functional performance in most domains, particularly the bite force and chewing efficiency. They also significantly improve the patients’ OHRQoL. Their design should take into consideration the physiological signs of ageing, but also the morbidity and social context. The lecture presents step by step the manufacturing of age-adequate IODs with conventional and digital workflows. Digital techniques may also be employed to meet the requirements of very old patients with reduced neuroplasticity, as they allow to import successful features from an existing denture. IOD management may become a challenge at the onset of dependency when denture handling relies on the knowledge and skill of caring staff. At this stage, hygiene is even more crucial to prevent aspiration pneumonia. The “back-off” strategy aims at accompanying the functional decline. In summary, IODs significantly enhance oral function and denture satisfaction and therefore be considered a valuable mosaic in the dental treatment for older adults.

Learning objectives
1. Design an age-adequate removable prosthesis
2. Develop concepts for patients with reduced neuroplasticity
3. Know strategies to accompany future functional decline in very old and multimorbid patients

description: Inaugural Professorial Lecture - Professor Angela Ballantyne, Inaugural Professorial Lecture "Making things right". What does it mean to make things right? Medicine and science often turn to bioethics for concrete solutions to ethical challenges. But in reality, there is rarely a single, obvious ‘right’ answer. Human systems are inherently messy, and challenged by a legacy of injustice, unequal distributions of power, and declining social trust. This talk will describe the potential for bioethics to help clarify and navigate ethics dilemmas; pragmatically inching us closer to making things – if not right, then at least – better.

description:
Indonesian Gamelan - Introductory Workshop, Don't miss this one-off opportunity to be introduced to not one, but two of the most well-known musical traditions of Indonesia.

Wellington is the only place in Aotearoa where there is both a traditional court gamelan from Java (since 1976!) and a Balinese Gong Kebyar ensemble (since 2003), and the expertise to learn and perform these. Both ensembles are housed at the NZ School of Music at Victoria University of Wellington, which also offers a course for credit.

This is a hands-on session where you'll learn about the instruments, how the music is put together and have a chance to try your hand playing the instruments, including the most fantastic deep and resonant gongs. No musical background required, but there's also plenty to challenge accomplished musicians. Bring your curiosity and give it a go!

The workshop will be led by Budi S. Putra (a graduate of the prestigious tertiary institute of performing arts in Central Java) and experienced members of the two performing groups.

New members are always welcome, so if you enjoy the music, we'd love you to join one of the groups. There will be performance opportunities later in the year.

Balinese gong kebyar is a fast-paced exciting musical ensemble, one of many across Indonesia. The ensemble features beautiful deep gongs, shimmering bronze percussion instruments intentionally tuned slightly apart in pairs to create a beating sound pulse, and rapid interlocking patterns.

Javanese gamelan tends to be a relatively quieter, more meditative music also played on bronze metallophones and gongs, with a vertical fiddle (rebab) and wooden xylophone (gambang) in quieter repertoire and compelling vocals.

Directions: Come to Gate 7 of Victoria University of Wellington, Kelburn Campus. We are on level 1 of the NZ School of Music in room 303 (the Asia-Pacific Music Studio)

description:
Integrating Creative Writing Into Painting - 4 Week Course, Creative writing and painting are both powerful forms of artistic expression. By integrating creative writing into your painting practice, you can enhance your imagination, storytelling abilities, emotional expression, attention to detail, and personal style on the canvas. Please bring along a journal or laptop.

COURSE CONTENT
Each session presents a key idea backed by research or concrete examples, followed by practical writing exercises with optional sharing. We learn by doing and from each other.

1. Generating work from the interior: tapping into memories, conflict, emotion, and observation to generate art.
2. Figuring out what matters to you, then learning how to grow your fragmented ideas into something whole. For example, how do you turn a feeling, or a fleeting moment in time into a story? Into a painting? Into a work of art? What are the building blocks you need?
3. Inspiration from other creative sources: people, music, poetry, reading, random incidents. Ways to generate fresh ideas. How to clarify and focus in writing and art.
4. Structure and boundaries. Dreaming big but being real. How do you find and stick to a creative process? Understanding how you learn and what kind of feedback you need. Designing your next project.

description:
International Women's Day Lunch, We are very excited to bring to you the 2026 International Women's Lunch along with our supporting sponsor Wakefields Lawyers.
It's that time of year to get some friends, work mates together and come along, enjoy and celebrate International Women's Day 2026.
We are excited to be welcoming Suzanne Paul as our Guest Speaker for 2026.
Inspirational speaker Suzanne Paul arrived in New Zealand from the working-class streets of Wolverhampton in 1991 with just $18 in her pocket and a fierce determination to succeed.
Despite the challenges of a learning disability that brought anxiety and low self-esteem, Suzanne channelled her boundless optimism and natural gift for sales into building one of the country’s most successful direct marketing empires. Her iconic products, such as Natural Glow and the Suzanne Clip, became household names, and within five years, she had transformed herself into a multimillionaire and one of New Zealand’s most beloved public figures, complete with her own TV shows. In 2007, she further captured the nation’s heart by winning Dancing with the Stars.
Life took a dramatic turn at 50 when Suzanne lost everything and was declared bankrupt. Though tempted to give up, she instead drew on the same resilience and skills that had built her earlier success. Starting over from nothing, she rebuilt her life step by step, launching new ventures and embracing fresh challenges.
Among her many accomplishments since then, Suzanne developed a clothing line for petite women, opened a boutique in Remuera, and spearheaded the success of Thin Lizzy Makeup in both New Zealand and Australia. She also became a bestselling author with But Wait, There’s More, a book that shares her journey and practical wisdom on making dreams come true. A second edition is currently in the works, focusing on resilience and turning intention into action.
Now living her dream life once again, Suzanne Paul continues to prove that even in the face of adversity, reinvention is always possible—and that success is never out of reach.
Join us for a delicious lunch by Party Perfect, network and have a great time!

This workshop is a foundational step towards mastering interpretation and transforming visits into unforgettable experiences. Perfect for those working in museums, galleries, parks, zoos, heritage sites and tourist attractions.
Designed and presented by Lynda Burns this workshop offers a full day of immersive learning. With decades of experience as a practitioner, trainer, and mentor across Aotearoa and abroad, Lynda brings a wealth of knowledge and expertise and is a leader in the field of interpretation.
Throughout the day, you will: 
Experiment with new ideas and skills.
Share your existing knowledge with like-minded professionals. 
Explore the role of place interpretation in visitor experience. 
Learn how to reach the hearts and minds of visitors through meaningful story-sharing. 
Take a closer look at visitor demographics and behaviours. 
Discover the steps to start your interpretation projects, including research, goal setting, media choices, budgeting, and collection analysis. 
Gain basic project management tips to get things done efficiently. 
Explore how to work alongside iwi, stakeholders and managers. 
Please bring actual project ideas or content research to trial what you have learned throughout the day. This hands-on approach ensures that you get to test your new skills and leave with actionable insights.

It's important that the app/programme is installed on the student's device before the course begins, and that they have had a play on it to get used to how it works. This is so that the student is at least a little familiar with their chosen software so that it's enough to begin learning animation techniques on day one. Additional information found at our website.

Ross will advise you on a variety of animation apps/programmes available online to use, ranging in price from free to not very much. Note - A computer mouse can be used for 2D animation, but digital pens are much easier to use. Prior to the course commencing, you'll receive details of recommended programmes to use for the course.

description:
Intro to Musical Improv | A PopRox Improv Course, Musical improv can be absolute magic. Whether it's a whole musical show, or single song that bursts out of an emotional scene, music adds so much to our improv.
This course for improvisers will give an introduction to musical improv. We'll cover basic song structures, how to get into a song from a scene, how to support a song through chorus work, and why and when we use music to add to our improv.
Participants should be confident in scene-work and have at least 2 years improv experience. This course will not teach you how to approach scenes and characters, so you should have a solid foundation which you can add to with this new toolbox of musical skills.
The course includes 6 workshops which will run 6:30pm to 8:30pm on Wednesdays from August 6th to September 10th. As it is an intro course, we do not anticipate a showcase for this course.
ABOUT THE TEACHERS
LIA KELLY is a theatre-maker and teacher based in Pōneke. She is an established director, actor, improviser and musician and has been a part of productions across the city over the last 10 years. She directed One Night Band which won 'Most Original Production' at the Wellington Theatre Awards 2023, and performs regularly as both a player and musician for POPROX.
ISAAC THOMAS has been an improviser and improv musician for a decade in Pōneke and Whakatū/Nelson. He's played with Body in Space, Playshop, Poprox and been musical director for musical improv powerhouse The Pāua Ballads. He has worked with almost every major improv company around the city accompanying them through improvised piano, guitar and vocals.
THE STANDY-BY LIST
PopRox firmly believes that improv is for everyone, especially when it comes to sharing skills and knowledge. So we're offering "the stand-by list" for all our workshops in 2025. We'll giveaway any spots remaining a few days before the first workshop of the course, on a first-come-first-serve basis. No need to provide a reason, no questions asked. If the entry fee is a barrier for you to come along, then simply email poproximprov@gmail.com and we'll pop you on the SBL. Everyone on the list will be notified whether there was a place available for them 3 days before the first workshop.

Introduction to Lettterpress, This three and a half hour course is the perfect introduction to the traditional method of printing with lead type. Letterpress was the main method of printing for over 500 years from Johannes Gutenburg’s 1450s bible to recent times.

description:
Introduction to Taiko Drumming, Experience the power, rhythm, and energy of traditional Japanese drumming!

Taiko is a high-energy blend of powerful bass tones, synchronized group rhythms, and dynamic, full-body choreography. Often called "the heartbeat of Japan," Taiko is as much a workout as it is an art form.

Whether you're looking to try something new, get your heart racing, or connect with a centuries-old tradition, this one-off workshop is the perfect place to start.

In this one-off introduction to taiko drumming we will cover:
- Basic drumming techniques and simple rhythm practice
- Learn a simple piece of Taiko rhythm and play as a group

Workshop Details:
Cost: $15 (Includes a $10 discount for our upcoming 8-week beginners course starting 1 March 2026)
What to bring: Wear comfortable gym/movement clothes and bring a water bottle.
How to join: Spots are limited. Please register via our website to secure your place.

Taikoza is Wellington’s longest-running Taiko group. Founded in Hiroshima in the mid-1980s and calling Wellington home since 1991, we are dedicated to keeping the ancient spirit of the drum alive.
You may have seen our high-energy performances at Cuba Dupa, The Japan Festival, or at Blossom Valley. Most of our rhythms come directly from Hiroshima’s Taiko Hozonkai, preserving beats that have echoed through Japan for hundreds of years.
Ready to find your rhythm? Follow us on Facebook and Instagram for updates, or visit our website to book your spot today.

More info on Taikoza is available on the website.

description:
Introduction to the darkroom & camera-less photography for teens, Explore the magic of the darkroom in this hands-on, three-day photography workshop for tweens and teens. We’ll be exploring camera-less and alternative photographic processes, including the photogram, painting with developer, texture screens, and chemigrams.

On Day 1, you’ll learn how to safely use the darkroom and make your first photograms. Day 2 introduces positive photograms, where you’ll reverse tones by printing from your originals; we’ll also create painterly effects using different application techniques and texture screens. On Day 3, you’ll explore the chemigram process, working with photographic papers and chemistry to create expressive abstractions.

We’ll work with a collection of objects that play with translucency, texture, and shape, including foliage, feathers, lace, and glass. You’re welcome to bring small items from home – ornaments, jewellery, plants, or other treasures — to experiment with. This workshop gives you the opportunity to discover how light, chemistry, and imagination can come together to create unique photographic prints.

Recommended age for this course is tweens & teens ages 10 and above.

Duration: Three day workshop from Monday 12 January - Wednesday 14 January. 10 am - 2 pm daily.
Materials provided.

Come to St Michael’s Hall in Kelburn to meet new people and enjoy a great time in a friendly and welcoming atmosphere. No dancing experience needed, just a bit of coordination, some energy, and a big sense of fun!
Set dances are the traditional social dances of Ireland, and are so much fun to dance. Have a look here to see what it's all about: https://www.facebook.com/reel/1062173322541491.
No experience necessary, suitable for beginners and experienced alike. This is not Irish step dancing, not Riverdance!
Experienced teacher Helen Stonehouse will guide you through the moves and figures.
For many years she has taught Set Dancing at workshops and festivals across the UK, Australia, and Aotearoa. Our amazing Round The House Céilí Band, featuring Roger Stonehouse, Em Griffiths, and Thomas Stonehouse, will be playing lively jigs and reels and polkas for us throughout the day.
