description:
Jazz and Beyond Workshops 2025, Jazz and Beyond for students 19 and under
December 15–18, 2025
Coordinated by Chris Beernink, Dave Wilson, Daniel Hayles, and Lance Philip. Proudly supported by the Tauranga Jazz Society.
Take your playing to the next level at the Jazz and Beyond Workshops! Young musicians from across Aotearoa come together to dive into jazz and connected styles, working closely with some of the country’s leading performers and educators. In a friendly, inclusive environment, you’ll grow your skills, make new musical connections, and learn alongside other students your age from all around the motu.
Here’s what’s in store:
small group ensembles led by professional musicians
developing improvisation skills in supportive settings
an introduction to music production
listening sessions that expand your skills
inclusive jam sessions where all are welcome
ensemble performances at the end of week concert
And more!
If you're 19 or under with at least a year of experience on your instrument or in vocal training, you’re welcome to join. Choose from trumpet, trombone, saxophone, clarinet, flute, bass, piano, guitar, drums, vibraphone, or voice.
The workshops are held at the New Zealand School of Music—Te Kōkī at Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington. Follow the Jazz and Beyond Workshops on Instagram or Facebook for the latest updates. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com with any questions.
Schedule
The workshops run 9:00am–4:30pm Monday through Thursday, with evening activities including concerts and our inclusive jam sessions Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. Students perform in a closing concert on Thursday afternoon.
Accommodation
Students arrange their own accommodation. Often students from outside Wellington stay together in groups with a parent chaperone. Options for housing near Victoria University of Wellington include backpacker hostels and hotels. If you have a group of 15 or more, University Student Housing can been booked at Cumberland House. Contact info for this option is via email at Cumberland-House@vuw.ac.nz or by phone at +64 4 463 4770.
Meals
Lunch for the four days is available for purchase at many convenient locations on campus, or students may bring their own lunch.
Equipment
Provided equipment includes drum kits, guitar and bass amps, pianos/keyboards, microphones and PAs for vocalists.
All brass and wind players should bring their own instruments.
Drummers: you are required to bring your own cymbals, sticks, and hi-hat clutch.
Guitarists and bass players: you are required to bring your own instruments as well as cables (leads).
Preparation
All students with one year of experience on an instrument or in vocal training have the skills required to participate, so no musical preparation is required. On the first day, students will play a very short audition to be placed in an appropriate ensemble. Guidelines for this short audition will be sent to all registered participants in advance of the workshops.
Cost
Early bird price: $325 - register by 19th October
Standard price $350 - after 19th October
Registration is open to all until all spots are filled.
We are dedicated to ensuring all students can participate in the workshops without financial constraints. If the cost poses a barrier, please email us at jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com and we will find a solution to facilitate your participation!

description:
Jewellery Making - Faceted Gemstone Settings, Evolve and advance your jewellery making with beautiful faceted stone setting methods! Create jewellery embedded with precious glittering gems in copper, brass and silver - beginners welcome! All material costs included in the course fee.

Description
In this challenging and exciting workshop students will learn to set glimmering round-cut faceted gemstones into brass, copper and/or silver. Create a stone set jewellery project from a choice of simple earrings, a pendant, or a ring.

Students who have already done a Lost Wax Cast Rings class may bring their cast rings and try their hand at setting stones in those instead of starting a new project.

Students will learn ‘Flush Setting’, a method of embedding gems into the surface of metal without the need for solder or joins. The process is adaptable to a number of jewellery types and styles. Students with prior Flush Setting and soldering experience may advance to other methods and to try their hand at learning ‘Bead Setting’, or a simple form of ‘Prong Setting’.

Students may choose from lab-created Sapphires, Rubies and other high strength stones such as Cubic Zirconia in a range of colours.

The workshop is especially satisfying for the magpie in all of us, adding extra colour and shine to jewellery making.

While both beginners and returning students are welcome in the class, be aware that the tools and techniques require a level of fine motor skills, keen eye for detail, and strong hand control which take some patience, practice and perseverance to get the best results.

Our magnifying headsets, work clamps, and patient tutor will help you along the way.

Please wear closed-in footwear suitable for a workshop environment. bring a work apron if you have one or wear clothes you don’t mind getting a little grubby. Remember to bring your reading glasses if you have them.

By the end of the course, students will be able to:

Develop jewellery making skills with introductory faceted stone setting methods

Create a simple stone set project - either earrings, a pendant, or a ring.

Use Vernier Calipers to measure and calculate metal dimensions

Use files to shape brass, copper and/or silver components

Use a soldering torch to attach metal components such as jump rings

File, sand and polish brass, copper and/or silver creations into finished jewellery

description:
Jewellery Making - Lost Wax Cast Rings, Evolve and advance your jewellery-making abilities with exciting lost wax methods to create rings cast in copper, brass, bronze, white bronze and silver - beginners welcome! All material costs included in course fee.

Description
In this fresh 6-week jewellery-making course, you get a hands-on opportunity to develop new techniques creating rings with a sculptural and organic flair.

The lost wax process offers a wide range of creative outcomes such as 3D forms and textures, which are not achievable with fabrication techniques.

You will design and create a pair of rings in jeweller’s wax. These wax masters will be cast professionally for you, outside class, making them in metals of your choice - copper, brass, yellow bronze or white bronze.

Later in the course you will refine your new wax shaping skills and develop a ring to be cast in sterling silver!

In the second part of the course, you will sand and refine your casts into finished jewellery.

The class offers beginners a fun introduction to jewellery making, and for those with some jewellery experience it offers a great way to advance and expand your making techniques to new levels.

All materials included in course fee. Please bring pen and paper and your reading glasses (if you use these) and wear clothing and footwear suitable for a workshop environment.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:

- Evolve your jewellery-making abilities with new and exciting lost wax methods
- Develop and create unique sculptural ring designs
- Carve hard jeweller’s wax ring master designs to fit a chosen finger size for casting
- Sculpt and model soft jeweller’s wax master design to fit a chosen finger size for casting
- Combine hard and soft jeweller’s wax to create unique designs ready for casting
- File, sand and polish metal casts into finished jewellery

description:
Jewellery Making - Precious Stones in Cast Rings, Create sculptural rings studded with dazzling precious gemstones! Combine wax working and stone setting methods to produce a set of rings cast in your choice of copper, brass, bronze, white bronze and silver - beginners welcome!

All materials are included in the course fee.

Description

Expanding on the Lost Wax Cast Rings class, students in this course get to add precious gemstones to their cast jewellery process!

Experiment and create sculptural cast metal rings set with beautiful stones in a variety of colours.
This beginner-friendly jewellery class is also fun and engaging for returning students to diversify their skills and set stones in new ways.

Students will learn to work with a range of jeweller waxes, including hard wax, modelling wax, sheet wax, melting wax and more to create wax 'masters', setting stones in wax, as well as turning raw metal casts into shining, ready-to-wear jewellery.

Students choose their favourite wax masters to be cast professionally outside of class time, transforming the designs into their choice of metals, and are returned to students to polish and finish their casts in class.

The course fee includes a range of small precious gemstones, casting 2 rings in either copper, brass, yellow bronze, white bronze, and 2 rings cast in Sterling Silver.

The bold, organic forms and textures of the lost wax processes offer a wide range of creative possibilities beyond the scope of fabrication methods alone (soldering metal sheet and wire). Setting faceted stones in wax offers a simpler and more experimental way of adding stones to jewellery compared to fabrication settings.

All materials are included in the course fee. Please bring pen and paper, and your reading glasses (if you use these), and wear clothing and footwear suitable for a workshop environment.

By the end of the course, students will be able to:

Design and create unique sculptural ring designs

Carve a hard jeweller’s wax ring master design to fit a chosen finger size for casting

Sculpt soft jeweller’s wax master design to fit a chosen finger size for casting

Combine hard and soft jeweller’s wax to create unique designs ready for casting

Set faceted gemstones in wax for ‘cast-in-place’ setting methods

File, sand and polish metal casts into finished jewellery

Creative Experience: Design and create your own sterling silver jewellery with cast-in-place gemstones.
Expert Guidance: Learn from a certified jewellery maker in a supportive and inspiring environment.

Hobbyists and craft enthusiasts

Couples, friends, or mothers & daughters looking for a creative bonding activity

Guidance on creating a simple wax band

Use of all necessary tools

description:
Jewellery Making-Soldered Fidget Rings, Classic textured rings, with a unique and exciting twist! Learn to make your own fine jewellery fidget rings from copper, brass and silver - beginners welcome! All materials included in course fee.

Description
In this one-day workshop you are offered a hands-on opportunity to create custom rings with fun mobile components and unique textures. We'll also practice and build experience in the essential jeweller’s fabrication skills of sawing, filing, soldering, sanding and polishing.

What are fidget rings? Also known as spinner rings or stim rings, fidget rings have loose bands attached that can move and swivel around - it's interactive sculpture you can wear!

In this course you’ll be lead through the design and creation of custom copper and silver rings, with copper, brass and silver wire spinner bands adding novelty and movement to a classic ring design.

This course offers beginners a fun introduction to jewellery making, and for those with some jewellery experience, it offers a great way to advance and expand your making techniques to new levels.

All materials included in course fee.

Please wear closed-in footwear suitable for a workshop environment. bring a work apron if you have one or wear clothes you don’t mind getting a little grubby. Remember to bring your reading glasses if a have them.

description:
Jewellery-making On Monday Nights - 6 Weeks Block, Level 2+, Our popular weekend block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

This class is for level 2+ and advanced students. It is not open to beginners. It starts on Mon 20 April and runs for 6 sessions until Mon 8 June, 5.30pm-8pm.

Students must have completed at least two 4-week blocks or a 6-week fabrication block. If you are unsure of your level because you may have done a few different shorter classes, please contact us and we can advise you.

Students will be supported in further developing their jewellery-making skills in the areas that interest them.

Level 2 students learn to solder more competently on their own using chainmaking as a way to develop their fine soldering skills. They may create a simple stone setting or ring alongside this challenge project so they have something to hone their skills that they are familiar with, as well as taking on a new skill. Their project could be a pendant on a handmade chain, a charm bracelet or a more complex bezel setting - for example a teardrop or soft square stone to take on bezels with corners!

Level 3 and above students are encouraged to work on their design skills and try new and challenging techniques.

This class fee does NOT include materials for any student. All metals and stones as well as quality findings and chains are available for purchase each week in the studio. Students are encouraged to keep their silver scrap and find ways to use it thriftily in future projects!

Our booking system asks for payment to be made via credit card, Afterpay or PayPal on booking. If you do not have access to these payment methods or need to pay your course fee over time please email us to arrange this ;)

description:
Jewellery-making in 8 weeks - Tuesday Eve Mixed Level, This class is mixed level, allowing beginners to work alongside advanced students. It starts on Tuesday, 14 October and runs for 8 weeks till Tuesday, 2 December, 5.30pm - 8pm.
Our popular weeknight classes are the best way for beginners to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

Beginners start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering. Then we move on to making a practice-ring set with a Cabochon stone (cabochon means it has a flat bottom and a smooth domed top) in a Bezel Setting. The stone-setting process teaches you many fundamental techniques in one project! As you work through your practice-ring and setting, you can move onto working in silver and produce another ring with a cabachon stone that you really love. This way you will learn the basics as you go on your practice-ring, before taking the next step in costly silver.

Level 2 students learn to solder more competently on their own using chainmaking as a way to develop their fine soldering skills. They may create a simple stone setting or ring alongside this challenge project so they have something to hone their skills that they are familiar with, as well as taking on a new skill. Their silver project could be a pendant on a handmade chain, a charm bracelet or a more complex bezel setting - for example a teardrop or soft square stone to take on bezels with corners!

Level 3 and above students are encouraged to work on their design skills and try new and challenging techniques. They should prepare to have one or two simple projects they can work on self-directed in class: more chains or simple bezel settings are ideal - to help them strengthen their soldering skills - alongside a challenge project that might be a shelf setting (an adaptation of a bezel setting that can take faceted stones), a tube setting or a larger bezel setting for a box or brooch. Our tutors will work with you to discover your passions in the world of making, and to support your skills so you grow your understanding with each block you take. We recommend that students from level 3 and up take the occasional Technique class (for example - claw setting, enamelling, flush setting) and then bring those techniques into their projects in their block class to be supported in their practice and skill by their regular tutor.

This class fee does NOT include materials for any student.
Beginners should expect to spend at least $60 on materials for their ring making project.
All metals and stones as well as quality findings and chains are available for purchase each week in the studio. Students are encouraged to keep their silver scrap and find ways to use it thriftily in future projects!

description:

It starts Tue 23 June and runs for 8 weeks ill Tue 11 August, 5.30pm - 8pm.

Our popular weeknight classes are the best way for beginners to get into jewellery-making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

The stone-setting process teaches you many fundamental techniques in one project!

We start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering.

Then we move on to making a practice ring set with a Cabochon stone (a cabochon has a flat bottom and a smooth, domed top) in a Bezel Setting.

As you work through your practice ring and setting, you can move on to working in silver and produce another ring with a cabochon stone that you really love. This way, you will learn the basics as you go on your practice ring, before taking the next step in costly silver.

This class has all materials included in the class fee!

Each student receives a carefully curated materials pack including copper or brass, sterling and fine silver for your ring-making projects, as well as two stones from our supply so you get a good stone for your level of experience.

We have loads of gorgeous stones of a range of colours, and they are all appropriate for beginner settings.

Our booking system asks for payment to be made via credit card, Afterpay or PayPal on booking. If you do not have access to these payment methods or need to pay your course fee over time, please email us to arrange this ;)

description:
Jewellery-making in 8 weeks, Level 2+, This class is for level 2+ and advanced students. It is not open to beginners. It starts on Mon 2 February and runs for 8 weeks till 23 March.
Students must have completed an 8-week block with ring-making and bezel settings or equivalent. If you have not done one of our 8-week beginner’s classes or are unsure of your level because you may have done a few different shorter classes, please contact us and we can advise you.
This more advanced class is ideal for those who are already competent at soldering simple joins, annealing and basic tool use on their own.
A more advanced set of students means that your tutor can support you and the group to take on more exciting and complex challenges. They will work with the group to find appropriate projects for you and for the class as a whole. Each 8-week block may focus on a particular skill topic, rather than doing loads of different topics with each student over the block. This means the students will benefit from a more in-depth learning experience, supported practice and peer support from fellow students.
Level 2 students learn to solder more competently on their own using chainmaking as a way to develop their fine soldering skills. They may create a simple stone setting or ring alongside this challenge project so they have something to hone their skills that they are familiar with, as well as take on a new skill. Their silver project could be a pendant on a handmade chain, a charm bracelet or a more complex bezel setting.
Level 3 and above students are encouraged to work on their design skills and try new and challenging techniques. They should prepare to have one or two simple projects they can work on self-directed in class: more chains or simple bezel settings are ideal - to help them strengthen their soldering skills - alongside a challenge project that might be a shelf setting (an adaptation of a bezel setting that can take faceted stones), a tube setting or a larger bezel setting for a box or brooch.
This class fee does NOT include materials for any student.
All metals and stones, as well as quality findings and chains, are available for purchase each week in the studio. Students are encouraged to keep their silver scrap and find ways to use it thriftily in future projects!
Our booking system asks for payment to be made via credit card, Afterpay or PayPal on booking. If you do not have access to these payment methods or need to pay your course fee over time please email us to arrange this

description:
Jewellery-making on Saturday Afternoons for Beginners, 4 weeks, Spend your Saturday afternoons immersed in creativity, learning the timeless craft of jewellery-making in our warm, welcoming studio.

It starts on Saturday 22 August and runs for 4 weeks till Saturday 12 September, 2pm-5pm.

This short course is the perfect introduction for complete beginners, guiding you step-by-step through the essential techniques used by jewellers. You’ll start by working in copper or brass, building confidence as you learn to cut, heat, shape and texture metal. From there, you can choose to move into silver and bring your ideas to life in more refined pieces.

A beautiful textured ring band is an ideal first project, but once you’ve mastered the basics, the possibilities really open up—create earrings, pendants, or small bespoke pieces that reflect your personal style. You’ll learn how to solder using a jeweller’s torch, refine your finishing techniques, and polish your work to a professional shine. It’s a hands-on, deeply satisfying process, and there’s nothing quite like wearing something you’ve made yourself.

Materials are purchased as you go, so you can tailor your projects to your budget and ideas. Beginners typically spend around $50–$70 on metals over the course.

We set these classes in blocks of 4 weeks so students can easily stack their learning and move into projects like a stone set ring.

This block is ideal for teens and young creatives aged 12 and up.
Please note: anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

description:
Jewellery-making on Thursdays, 8-week block, Level 2+, Our popular weeknight block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. This class will be held at our new waterfront location, Market Lane!

The course starts on Thursday 25 June and runs for 8 weeks till Thursday 13 August, 5.30pm-8pm.

This class is designed for students who already have some skills and are ready to develop their craftsmanship in a lively, warm, and supportive environment. Guided by our highly skilled tutors, you’ll build confidence, refine your techniques, and gain the satisfaction of making jewellery that reflects your personal style.

If you’re brand new to jewellery making, we recommend beginning with our Tuesday Evening 8-Week Beginners’ Block, which gives a solid foundation in essential techniques before moving on to this class.

At Level 2, the focus is on precision and technique. Students explore the art of chain making, a classic jewellery making project that develops fine soldering skills and accuracy in construction. This project is an excellent way to build confidence with the torch and create a piece of jewellery that is both functional and beautiful. The finished chain can become a pendant, bracelet, or necklace, or you may choose to adapt it into a design of your own.

At Level 3 and above, the emphasis shifts toward creativity and design development. Students at this stage are encouraged to take on more complex projects, experiment with new and challenging techniques, and bring their own design ideas to life. With the guidance of our skilled and supportive tutors, you’ll learn how to push your skills further, problem-solve during the making process, and refine your eye for detail and design.

Evening classes are not just about the technical side of jewellery making - they are also a chance to slow down, enjoy the process, and be part of a creative community. Many students return term after term, finding the rhythm of regular making both mindful and rewarding.

Please note: this class does not include a materials allowance, giving you the flexibility to choose your own metals, stones, or other materials. You only pay for what you use, making it easier to customise your projects and work at your own pace.

Our booking system asks for full payment at the time of registration (via credit card, PayPal, or AfterPay). If you don’t have access to these options or would like to pay in instalments, please email us and we’ll happily arrange an alternative.

description:
Jonathan Kay - Massey University Lecturer/Master of Fine Arts Coordinator, Jonathan Kay is a photographic artist, researcher, and lecturer based at Massey University in Te Whanganui-a-Tara/Wellington. His work explores the intersection of art and science, using photography to reveal the unseen and challenge conventional notions of landscape. Over the past seven years, his research has focused on developing a site-specific and responsive approach to photographic interventions within the landscape.
Drawing inspiration from scientific 'fieldwork,' Kay’s practice involves close observation and data collection, using these methods to uncover new insights into specific environments. However, his approach extends beyond the typical scientific framework by leveraging the unique possibilities of the photographic medium. This process enables him to move beyond the traditional, idealized representation of landscapes, offering deeper, more complex interpretations.

description:
KOKEDAMA WORKSHSOP, Join Bonsai Master Rachi and create your own modern kokedama at our upcoming workshop.
Each participant will receive a complete kit with a pre-selected plant, moss, soil mix, and tools, and will learn how to create a kokedama and how to care for it at home.
Kokedama (Japanese for "moss ball") is a unique Japanese gardening art where a plant's root ball is wrapped in soil and covered with moss, forming a ball that replaces a traditional pot, often hung with string or placed on surfaces, offering an organic, pot-free way to display plants. Originating from bonsai, this technique uses a mixture of clay and peat moss, bound by string, creating a living sculpture that's both decorative and practical for indoor greenery.

description:
Karanga taonga, karanga tangata, karanga whenua |Reversing Cultural Amnesia: Activating Māori Practice in Museums, In 1947, Māori leader, politician, and scholar Apirana Ngata spoke to his scholarly peers at the Polynesian Society, announcing his greatest desire to revive Māori culture as a living force within communities, not be relegated to dead exhibits in museums (Ramsden 1948, 85).
This lecture acknowledges the concerns of visionary leaders and champions of cultural practice and their activation within museums. Through her work as a Māori curator, writer, cultural practitioner and post-doctoral researcher, Awhina Tamarapa advocates for cultural restoration as a form of liberation in a museum context. In her research, Tamarapa is exploring strategies for the recovery and reclamation of taonga puoro (singing treasures) and karetao (animated storytellers) for new generations.
There are challenges regarding taonga held by overseas museums. Concepts such as keeping taonga warm, and mana taonga, recognises the connection and authority of descendants to their taonga, that underpin this work.
The focus on the reclamation of Indigenous practice has been bolstered by working with First Nations, Canada BC. Led by Professor Bryony Onciul, University of Exeter, UK, Tamarapa was privileged to be part of a research project “The Future of Indigenous Rights and Responsibilities: Ancestral governance, environmental stewardship, language revival, and cultural vibrancy” funded by the Arts and Humanities Research Council, UK.
_________
The Michael Volkerling Lecture series is a partnership event with the Museum and Heritage Studies programme at Te Herenga Waka | Victoria University of Wellington, National Services Te Paerangi and Te Papa Tongarewa. This annual public lecture series recognises the legacy of the late Dr Michael Volkerling who was one of the principal architects of New Zealand's cultural and creative sectors.

After several SOLD OUT workshops in Wellington here is the next one... Oct 2025

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)

Monday 13th October - 10:00am - 12:00pm

Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. description:
Kintsugi Workshop, Discover the beauty in brokenness through the timeless Japanese art of Kintsugi- the practice of mending ceramics with gold, transforming cracks into shimmering lines of strength and history. Rather than disguising flaws, Kintsugi celebrates them, honouring the story that each repaired piece carries.

In this hands-on workshop, we’ll explore a modern adaptation of this centuries-old practice using gold dust and epoxy glue. You’ll learn the process step-by-step, practice the meditative process of repairing ceramic pieces (yes, there’s a moment of satisfying, gentle smashing!), and finish with your own golden-repaired piece to take home.

Kintsugi teaches us to embrace imperfection as part of life’s story- that cracks can become something to cherish, not hide.

Your ceramic pieces will be provided on the day. Feel free to bring along treasured items to be mended, and I will advise if they are suitable for a beginner's class. Or get in touch before booking to discuss.

description:
Knitting for Beginners, Always wanted to learn how to knit but never been sure where to begin? Join craft tutor Stella Carruthers as she teaches the basic principles of knitting in this fun, informative and supportive class. Come along and learn the essential building blocks of knitting, using only knitting needles, yarn and your hands!
Come and reap the benefits of a mindful and meditative craft-form. Meet other people interested in making things with their hands, chat over crafting and find out what the craft craze is all about.

Join crafter Stella as she shares her ten years plus knitting experience in this beginner’s knitting class that supports each student as an individual learner.

Master basic knitting techniques, learn how to cast stitches on and off the needles, explore the knit and purl stitches and practice how to hold the needles in a way that is comfortable for you - then learn how to knit in the English style.

Knitting needles and yarn are included in the course fee, but you're welcome to bring along your own 4-ply yarn if you wish.

By the end of the course you will have created two squares of knitting, one in basic garter stitch and the other utilising both knit and purl stitches to create the knitted fabric called stocking stitch.

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

description:
Korean language - Introductory One, This course is for those who are interested in Korean language and culture. You can learn how to speak and write Korean and expand your knowledge about Korea through the Korean culture. It will be fun! (NZ Citizens and residents pay $105 with ID, all others pay $205).

Korean - Introductory 1

(NZ Citizens and residents pay $105 with ID, all others pay $205).

Hangeul (Korean Language), Hanbok (Korean traditional clothing), Kimchi and healthy fermented food, K-pop, these all represent Korean culture. Korea is located in the very end of the continent of Asia. Its culture is rich and deep as its history goes back about 5,000 years.

This course is for those who would like to experience Korean culture and learn Korean language. If you are interested in Korea, it's for you!

A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

By the end of this course you will be able to:

- Read and write Korean alphabets.
- Read and write simple sentences in Korean.
- Introduce yourself in Korean.
- Speak daily expressions in Korean at a basic level such as; greetings, jobs, food, shopping, location and so on.
- Understand and use some Korean grammar such as; rules of pronouncing, words for questions, endings of verbs and so on.
- Count numbers in Korean.
- Expand your knowledge about Korean food and etiquette, Korean traditional songs, Korean traditional clothing, Hanbok and traditional game culture.
- Become more confident about the cultural aspects of these topics.

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. No prior knowledge required, just an interest in Korean language and culture.

description:
Laura Sessions: Positive psychology coach & writer, Did you get your ticket for our February event yet?
We’re excited to welcome our next speaker:
Laura Sessions (@laurainnz) is a positive psychology coach who helps people navigate change and move forward in their lives, work, and businesses.
Her work is grounded in the science of positive psychology, an approach that focuses on nurturing what’s already strong, rather than fixing what’s “wrong”.
Laura is also the general manager and senior writer at StudioC Design, a small Wellington and Christchurch-based design studio specialising in co-design.
For February’s theme, Camino – the Spanish word for path or way – Laura will explore how identifying your strengths can help you find your footing when the way ahead feels uncertain.
Through a simple, hands-on exercise, you’ll uncover some of your own creative superpowers. You’ll learn how to take a meaningful next step, even if you don’t yet know where your path leads.
Please bring along a notebook or paper + a pen or pencil to participate in the hands-on creative superpower exercise!

- Learn the basics of Taiko Drumming
- Learn the Repertoire: a number of traditional and unique Taiko pieces, basic taiko rhythms and rhythm practice.
- The Performance Experience: At the end of the term, you’ll have the chance to join us for a public performance! Show your friends and family what you’ve learned (performance is optional, but highly encouraged!).

Course Details:
- Start Date: 1 March 2026 to 26 April 2026 (no lesson on 29 March due to CupaCupa)
- Cost: $115 for the full 8-week term.
- Special Discount: Only $100 if you attended our Intro Workshop!
- What to bring: Comfortable movement clothes and water bottle

Why Learn with Taikoza?
Founded in Hiroshima in the mid-1980s and based in Wellington since 1991, Taikoza is the region's longest-running Taiko ensemble. By joining this course, you aren't just learning drums, you are becoming part of a tradition that stretches back centuries.
We’ve brought the thunder to Cuba Dupa, Newtown Festival, and Blossom Valley.

Lino-printing Koanga (Spring) Workshop - Pop-up Parlour 2025, Lino-printing Koanga (Spring) Workshop - Pop-up Parlour 2025
Join us for a fun-filled morning of creativity at Pukerua Bay Hub's Pop-up Parlour as we explore Māori design motifs using Lino-cut prints developed with artist Trixie Andrew.
Afternoon Tea provided. No experience needed.

The lino-cut prints will be provided with different design motifs and we will guide you through the process of printing your own items (clothing, bags, cards etc.) and creating your own small lino-cut to keep as well. Different kinds of paper stock will be available.

Māori design motifs are rich in symbolism and storytelling. These visually rich motifs are used in carving, weaving, and tattooing to convey cultural knowledge, history, and spiritual beliefs. These motifs are not just decorative; they are a vital part of Māori culture and identity. We will be exploring Koanga (Spring) for this session.

- When - 10-12pm Saturday 6th September 2025

Trixie Andrew (Ngāti Toa) has spent the past three years in Pōneke pursuing a Bachelor of Fine Arts with Honours at Massey University. She has paused this year to study the Heke Reo course at Te Wānanga o Raukawa, aiming to return to finish her degree after completing the Te Reo Māori Diploma. description:
Live & Work in Japan! Q&A Evening with JET Programme Alumni, Have you ever wanted to live and work in Japan?
Come talk
to some people who've done it!
Every year, a diverse range of New Zealanders representing a variety of backgrounds, ages, interests, and cultures start a life-changing adventure in Japan-and next year that could include you!
With applications for the New Zealand JET Programme around the corner, you may have questions about what it's actually like to be sent off to live and teach in Japan for a year or more!
The JET Alumni Association of Wellington, in coordination with The Embassy of Japan, have organised a casual evening event for prospective applicants to ask those questions, and hear some stories to help you make a better decision about if the JET Programme is right for you.
Q&A event details
Date: 6th October 2025
Time: 17:30 - 19:30
Location: Yoshi Sushi & Bento (Press Hall, Willis Street)
Doors open from 5:30, with Q&A starting from 6:00.
Enjoy free
courtesy of Yoshi Sushi & Bento.
(Drinks, including Japanese
will also be available for purchase).
So come along and bring your friends
to this great opportunity to meet a handful of the thousands of Kiwis who've taken part in this programme over the past 40 years
Anyone interested in applying is welcome to attend!

What is the Japan Exchange Teaching (JET) Programme, you ask?
The JET Programme is an overseas employment opportunity to live and work in Japan for a year or more! You could soon head abroad on the adventure of a lifetime, and get paid for it!
Programme criteria includes the following-are you:
A New Zealand citizen?
Already graduated?
Or will have your Bachelor's Degree/Teaching Diploma conferred by early July 2026?
Interested in international activities?
Interested in teaching English to young people and living in Japan?

Positions available:
Assistant Language Teacher (ALT)
ALTs help the Japanese foreign language teachers in class and help prepare teaching materials and class activities. They may assist in English language clubs and other extra-curricular activities. Knowledge of Japanese is not required to be an ALT.
Coordinator for International Relations (CIR)
CIRs work in local government offices and are involved in international activities, which might include editing publications, translation work, advising on the planning and implementation of exchange programmes, and interpreting at international events. A functional knowledge of written and spoken Japanese is required to be a CIR.
For more information about the New Zealand JET Programme, visit:
https://www.nz.emb-japan.go.jp/itpr_en/jet.html
https://www.facebook.com/JETProgrammeNZ/
We hope to see you there!

description:
Lost Wax in Three - Mitsuro Hikime Wax, Discover the magic of Mitsuro Hikime — the beautiful Japanese technique that uses a special stretchy wax to create flowing, organic textures unlike anything else in jewellery-making.

Over three inspiring sessions, you’ll learn how to transform this fascinating material into stunning wearable pieces using the traditional lost wax casting process.

Mitsuro Hikime wax behaves very differently from standard jeweller’s wax. Warm and pliable, it can be stretched, twisted and pulled into delicate ribbons and natural textures that resemble flowing water, bark, roots or molten metal. The results are beautifully organic and wonderfully unpredictable, making every piece completely unique.

During the first two sessions, you’ll learn how to handle and shape this traditional Japanese wax, exploring different techniques to create rings, pendants or small sculptural objects full of movement and texture. Once your designs are complete, your waxes will be professionally cast in the metal of your choice.

There is then a one-week break before the final session to allow time for casting. In the third class, you’ll learn how to cut, file, sand and finish your cast pieces, transforming them into polished jewellery ready to wear, gift or treasure.

This course is suitable for complete beginners as well as more experienced makers wanting to experiment with this exciting and expressive technique. More advanced students are also welcome to use the sessions to develop independent projects in a supportive studio environment.

Included in the class fee are all Mitsuro Hikime waxes, consumables, sandpaper and courier costs.

Please note that casting and metal costs are not included, as these vary depending on the size of your piece and the metal selected. Small castings generally cost around $6.65–$12, with metal costs ranging approximately from $8–$30 depending on whether you choose red bronze, white bronze or silver.

This class is great for young folks aged around 12 and up. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

description:
Make Your Own Robot at Old St Paul's, What does a robot look like to you? Your dog, Kākāpō? Humanoid like your grandmother, Meryl? Or more industrial like your dad’s vacuum cleaner? We’re putting on an art class for human children like you, and over two fun-filled hours you can create your very own robot!
Robots have been around for a long time, since the 1940s in fact, when American-born British robotics pioneer William Grey Walter built two robots called Elmer and Elsie out of old war materials and alarm clocks. They looked a bit like tortoises, and they moved by themselves in response to light.
Closer to home, in Aotearoa New Zealand, Eric Cummins from Rangiora has been making real working robots out of his garage since 1975. Some of the robots Eric designed now live in the Christchurch Museum of Toys & Collectibles.
In this art class you can manufacture a robot of your own design. We’ll provide all the materials, like boxes, aluminium foil, bottle caps, tubing, glue and so on, but you’ll need to bring along a real adult.
You’ll be creating robots for the future while appreciating the past in one of Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s most famously beautiful buildings – constructed by humans 160 years ago and now cared for by Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga.
For ages 6-12.
All materials will be provided.
Please note, children must be accompanied by a parent or guardian (free entry for adult assistants).
Spaces are limited.

description:
Make Your Own Roman Blinds, Come along and learn how to make your very own Roman blind, to give your rooms an elegant and streamlined look.

Description
Roman blinds are a perennial favourite because they use a lot less fabric than the usual pencil pleated or gathered curtains - as well as making your rooms look streamlined and uncluttered.

During the four weeks you will learn how to accurately measure your window to enable you to create very own customized roman blind.

Some hardware included in course fee but a list of all other materials (fabric, etc) will be sent out to you when the course is confirmed.

Please choose a narrow window for your first project - max 150cms wide.

By the end of the course you'll be able to

Accurately measure your window
Calculate how much fabric to purchase
Measure and cut out your curtain
Use appropriate machine skills to sew your curtain fabric
Use finishing skills to apply rings and cords to your curtain
Identify appropriate method to hang Roman Blind

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Prerequisites
This course is not for beginner sewers, you must to able to use a sewing machine in a competent manner.

description:
Mana Taiohi - in Wellington, Mana Taiohi Workshop
Mana Taiohi is a principle based framework that informs the way people who work with young people work in Aotearoa. Mana Taiohi has evolved from the principles of youth development previously expressed in the Youth Development Strategy of Aotearoa (2002). It is informed by the voice of young people and people who work with young people, Aotearoa based literature into positive youth development, and a Te Ao Māori worldview.
Matt was born and raised in Te Awakairangi, Wellington and his ancestors are Ngāti Porou - Tikapa, Ngāti Kahungunu - Wairoa, Ngāti Ruapani - Waikaremoana, Āti Haunui-a-Pāpārangi - Pungarehu and Gujurat. He has been married to his wife Rachel since 2016 - she’s Ngā Puhi, Japanese, and English and their son, Mana Tuku Iho, was born in April 2024 after a 7-year fertility journey.
Matt has been involved in youth and community work since 2005 and co-founded the 'Te Awakairangi Youth Development Network' with a team of superstars. Matt is currently the Pouwhakamana for Zeal Youth Aotearoa, Āpiha Kaiwhakahaere for Ngā Kaihoe, and the Kaiāwhina of World Vision New Zealand.
In 2019, the whānau moved to Tāmaki Makaurau to study a Bachelor's in Indigenous Theology (Māori/Pasifika), a Diploma in Māori Leadership and a Diploma in Te Reo Māori, completing these qualifications in 2022. These studies have been transformational for both their personal growth and their work in youth and community development, changing the way they engage with the world. Through storytelling, making connections, and wānanga, they share these insights with the people they meet.
Now, with the arrival of Mana, they are back in Wellington, closer to friends and whānau. They are excited to continue their mission to see Aotearoa lifted up and our people thriving to their full potential.

description:
Mana Up with Pio Terei in Wellington, Actor, singer, comedian, and storyteller Pio Terei joins The Village NZ for a transformative community kōrero: Mana Up - a deep dive into the real-life challenges that shape us and the real tools that can help us rise.
With his trademark warmth, humour, and humility, Pio guides us through the kaupapa that impact so many of our whānau:
Trauma
Relationships
Whānau dynamics
Grief
Anger
Alcohol & addiction
This is not a lecture. This is lived experience, shared with honesty and heart. Pio has a unique ability to speak with people, not at them. Creating a space where laughter and vulnerability sit side by side. His kōrero is grounded in te ao Māori, backed by simple, evidence-based tools, and designed for communities who are often the hardest to reach.
You’ll hear about concepts like Red Brain vs Green Brain, how trauma shapes behaviour, how to pause before reacting, and how to reconnect with the things that give us strength. These are tools people remember, take away, and use the very next day.
Why This Matters
Mana Up has been described as “an aha moment” for many who attend. One organiser reflected:
“An amazing workshop that was real, relevant, and so appropriate. Realising the whakapapa of trauma and being able to recognise behaviours as the result of such trauma really was an aha moment for a good percentage of the room.”
Another shared:
“The room spoke at length after you left, wanting more and asking for strategies to work on the trauma rather than just the behaviour. The feedback was exceptional -probably the best in my three years on the Executive Team.”
And perhaps the most powerful reflection of all:
“To have this delivered with such passion… I feel like there is hope for our ākonga, whānau, hapū, and iwi.”
These talks have sparked healing, shifted perspectives, and helped whānau feel seen, valued, and hopeful again. They are for everyone - parents, educators, community workers, youth, those impacted by trauma, those seeking reconnection, and anyone wanting to understand themselves and others better.

March Tech Talk - TECH FOR GOOD, Come and meet some of the French-led businesses that are having a positive impact on the community.
Talks in English and open for everyone within or outside the French Tech Ecosystem!
Keynote #1:
Adeline Bartoletti will be introducing us to Kelvius, an innovative technology turning industrial waste heat into storable and upgraded heat. 🔥
Industrial heat is about 40% of the global energy use, and about 30% is wasted. Kelvius harnesses the power of chemistry and offers modular thermal battery helping manufacturers to recover valuable waste energy, store this energy for long-term use, and upgrade it for reuse in high temperature processes. 🏭
Kelvius' solution helps reduce energy costs and decrease industrial OPEX, and improves site resilience and energy efficiency, decoupling from fossil fuels and electricity. 💡
Keynote #2:
Franck Natali from Liquium 👏🏻
Liquium is revolutionising the ammonia production process, helping it align with renewable energy, lower the cost of production and operation and have a broader scale for more applications. ⛽
With multiple awards under their belts, Liquium is currently challenging the status quo, attacking one of the most polluting chemicals on the planet. 🏆
Their goal? Reducing the green fuel premium for shipping lines and energy generators, and consequently the consumer. 🥳
Keynote #3:
Foucauld Thery, the CEO of Farm Medix Ltd, will tell us about the great work they are doing around mastitis diagnostics and lameness management. Farm Medix Ltd helps farmers protect animal health, improve milk quality, reduce antibiotic use, and boost performance with practical solutions and expert support. 🐄🐎
Their innovative approach delivers science-backed, practical solutions, helping farmers and horse owners improve animal wellbeing and herd performance, and delivering measurable improvement for the animals and the people who care for them. 💞
Our keynotes will be followed by a panel talk on Tech for Good. More information to follow.
Drinks and nibbles, and networking opportunity will follow!

description:
Mature Mountaineer's Talk: Geoff Spearpoint Reflects on His Journey, Doors open 1.30pm, talk starts 2pm

Geoff Spearpoint will present a very personalised view of his career so far, bringing his passion for remote places to a wide audience.
Geoff began tramping in 1966 when he was 15, which grew into a passion for transalpine trips and climbing. He has had a variety of careers however employment has mostly been a means to an end, and his real career continues to revolve around the mountains.
He has been on expeditions to the Northern Patagonian Icecap, Himalayas, Karakoram Range, Yunnan and Tibet and worked in the Dry Valleys for Antarctica New Zealand. However, in the background, there were always transalpine tramping and climbing trips throughout the Southern Alps, where he explored interesting corners including the Ngapunatoru Plateau, Olivine Ranges, Volta, Hooker Wilderness, Cook area, Godley, Gardens, the Bracken Snowfield, and other remote places.
Geoff is perhaps best known for the books he has written, including his latest, ‘The Great Unknown’, a photo and text essay of Southern Alps wilderness trips, designed to encourage and inspire more journeys, and for his behind-the-scenes roles in successful television series. In recent years, Geoff has been actively involved in the care of our back country assets and is a founding member of the Backcountry Trust Board.
Enquiries:
Dave Bamford, dave@davebamford.co.nz Tel 027 457 0313
Andy Carruthers, chair@wellingtonalpineclub.org.nz Tel 021 244 6051

Mature Mountaineer meetings are a NZ Alpine Club initiative providing an opportunity for older members of the NZAC & affiliated clubs to get together, share and hear stories (usually from an invited speaker), and have afternoon tea. The intention is to provide a social gathering for those less likely to go out to evening events. The concept has been successful in Christchurch (since 2006), Auckland and Wellington. The functions are open to all interested outdoor enthusiasts and are made possible thanks to support from Tūpiki Trust.

description:
Miramar Local History Event : Wonderland, Wonderland was Wellington’s first ever amusement park. Based in Miramar, it opened in 1907 and was located near the present-day Wētā Cave. At the time it was one of the biggest amusement parks in the Southern Hemisphere. Its various attractions were originally to be found at the New Zealand International Exhibition of 1906-1907 and were brought to Wellington after that exhibition closed. The park has a fascinating and interesting back story which the panellists will explore.
This very special event will be an unmissable treat for all local history buffs as well as a fabulous journey into Wellington’s and especially Miramar’s past, and features two of Aotearoa’s finest and most acclaimed historical novelists and Wellington City Libraries' own Local History Specialist.
Meet the panel:
Tracy Farr:
Tracy Farr's debut novel The Life and Loves of Lena Gaunt was long­listed for Australia’s Miles Franklin Literary Award, shortlisted for the Barbara Jefferis Award and Western Australian Premier’s Book Awards. Wonderland is her third novel and is set in and during the time of Miramar’s Wonderland.
Philippa Werry:
Multi-award winning historical fiction writer Philippa Werry’s most recent book Iris and me about the travels of Robin Hyde won the Young Adult Fiction Award at the NZ Book Awards for Children and Young Adults. Her numerous other works include award winning fiction, non-fiction, picture books, plays and poetry, with a special emphasis on children and young adults, and a particularly strong focus on Aotearoa / New Zealand stories and history.
And to complete our illustrious panel we have Wellington City Library’s Local History Specialist, Gábor Tóth.

Beginners start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering. Then we move on to making a practice-ring set with a Cabochon stone (cabochon means it has a flat bottom and a smooth domed top) in a Bezel Setting. As you work through your practice ring and setting, you can move on to working in silver and produce another ring with a cabochon stone that you really love.

Level 2 students learn to solder more competently on their own using chainmaking as a way to develop their fine soldering skills. They may create a simple stone setting or ring alongside this challenge project so they have something to hone their skills that they are familiar with, as well as taking on a new skill.

Level 3 and above students are encouraged to work on their design skills and try new and challenging techniques. They should prepare to have one or two simple projects they can work on self-directed in class, alongside a challenge project.

This class fee does NOT include materials for any student.

Beginners should expect to spend at least $60 on materials for their ring making project.

description:
Moving Meditation: Attention, Space, Endurance, and Hip Articulation with Djibril Sall, Moving Meditation: Attention, Space, Endurance, and Hip Articulation with Djibril Sall
This series of workshops explores movement as a form of meditation by training attention through the body, space, relational awareness, and endurance. Participants are guided through slow floor-to-standing warm-ups, spatial orientation exercises, group navigation tasks, and sustained hip articulation practices. The workshop emphasizes clarity, choice, and duration, making it accessible to participants with varied movement backgrounds. Previous movement experience is helpful but not required. Participants are encouraged to work at a self-determined pace and level of intensity.
Djibril Sall is a queer Senegalese performer, choreographer, and writer whose work sits at the intersection of racialized migration, belonging, and in-betweenness. Born in Dakar and raised in a working-class family in the Deep South of the United States, his practice is shaped by movement across classed, racialized, and geopolitical borders. Drawing from his own migration history, he asks how trauma might become a departure point for pleasure, disclosure, letting go, and open-hearted connection.

description:
NZCFS Wellington Branch March Meeting: Blossoming Patterns: Minnan Tiles, The Confucius Institute at Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington will be hosting an interactive workshop at our early March meeting.
This workshop explores encaustic cement tiles from Minnan (southern Fujian). Far from being simple copies of European designs, Minnan tiles have formed through cross-regional exchange and local use, evolving as different communities adapted and reinterpreted them. Using a cultural-computing lens we will trace how tile patterns travelled from Europe to Southeast Asia and into Minnan, and how they changed through selective adaptation and local creativity.
Participants will also create their own tile-pattern compositions in a simple hands-on workshop, including structural deconstruction, color selection, and your own reinterpretation.

description:
Narrative Refresh w. Austin Harrison | A PopRox Workshop, Sharpen your narrative tools in this one-off workshop with PopRox improv.
Refresh and restock your narrative toolkit to create a satisfying arc for your improv- be it within a scene or across a whole show. We'll unpack what a narrative arc is, and the simple tools and choices you use to help keep a scene/show on track.
This is a refresh intensive, so folks should have some experience with improvised scene work and have taken a workshop in narrative before- to get the most out of this workshop.

ABOUT THE TEACHER
Austin Harrison is one of Aotearoa's most prolific improv performers, producers and teachers. He's a founding member of PopRox, a 6-time winner of Late Night Knife Fight and a Wellington theatre Award winner. Past shows include Ungartered Territory, Pudgy Mediocre White Men Solve Your Problems, and Magnus Steele. He's taught with Improv Connection, WIT, Voice Arts and was recently appointed Artisitc Director of the New Zealand Improv Festival. Austin specialises in interactive and narrative work and loves the full spectrum of joy improv has to offer!

THE STAND-BY LIST
PopRox firmly believes that improv is for everyone, especially when it comes to sharing skills and knowledge. So we're offering "the stand-by list" for all our workshops in 2025. We'll giveaway any spots remaining a few days before the first workshop of the course, on a first-come-first-serve basis. No need to provide a reason, no questions asked. If the entry fee is a barrier for you to come along, then simply email poproximprov@gmail.com and we'll pop you on the SBL. Everyone on the list will be notified whether there was a place available for them 3 days before the workshop.

description:
Natural Textured Rings, Craft a beautiful, personalised ring - a perfect treat for yourself or a thoughtful gift for someone special! This 3-hour taster class is designed for absolute beginners, though all skill levels are welcome to join the fun.
You will be guided step-by-step through the core techniques of silversmithing. You'll start by practicing basic texturing, cutting, and shaping with traditional jewellery tools using copper or brass. Once you’re comfortable, you'll move on to crafting your final piece in sterling silver.
In this hands-on workshop, you will learn to:
Measure your finger and cut the metal strip to the perfect length.
Create unique surface textures using a rolling mill, hammers, punches, and even natural elements like feathers or leaves. You can stamp names, dates, whatever you like.
Work safely with a jeweler's torch for heating and soldering the metal.
Finish your ring with sanding and polishing techniques.
By the end of the class, your beautiful, custom-made sterling silver ring will be ready to wear.
This is an ideal activity for individuals, groups of friends, or visitors to the city looking for a creative experience.
What's Included:
All practice materials (copper and brass).
A strip of sterling silver for your final ring.
All necessary consumables (sandpaper, solder, chemicals).
Use of all tools and equipment.
Important Note for Young Makers: Kids aged 12 and over are welcome to attend, but anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

description:
Nature Journaling with Sandra Morris, Observe, draw, and write from nature. 9 November.

Reconnect with the natural world in this mindful workshop led by award-winning botanical artist and illustrator Sandra Morris. Set in the historic garden and visitor center of Nairn Street Cottage, you’ll learn how to observe, draw, and write from nature, whether for identification or simply for pleasure.

Nature journaling invites us to notice the intricate relationships between plant and creature, decay and growth, and the quiet beauty often missed in the rush of daily life. Through sketches, diagrams, poems, lists, or prose, you’ll discover your own way of recording the world around you.

All materials provided, however, please feel free to bring your own preferred drawing tools, such as watercolour pens, colour pencils and your own journal if you already have one underway.

Sunday 9 November, 10am-12:30pm
Tickets $65.00
Bookings essential

Sandra will also be doing an Introduction to Botanical Drawing and Plant Inks workshop on Saturday, 8 November. Make a weekend of it and book both to receive a $20 discount. On the booking details page, you’ll have the option to add a second workshop with Sandra Morris. When both are selected, the discount will be applied automatically.

description:
Needle Felt a Mini Cat Scene, Description
This one-day course will guide you step-by-step from a fluff of wool to a small wall hanging.

What You’ll Learn

Felting Fundamentals: Understand the tools of the trade, including different needle gauges, wool roving types, and safety techniques.
Sculpting with Fiber: Master the art of 2D needle felting to create depth, realistic textures, and smooth gradients.
Capturing the Details: Learn how to bring your cat to life by detailing expressive eyes, delicate whiskers, and soft, dimensional fur.
Who Is This For?

Absolute Beginners: No textile or drawing experience required! Needle felting is incredibly forgiving and easy to pick up.
Craft Enthusiasts: Anyone looking to add a unique, tactile medium to their artistic repertoire.
Cat Lovers: Anyone who wants to make a cute cat picture through a beautiful, handmade keepsake!
Note: All materials provided and you will leave with a felting needle, backing board and enough wool to complete your project if you have not had time to complete during the session. Many people will complete their art work in the course time, but it is possible that you may need to complete it at home. If so, you will be given enough wool to complete it.

Tea and coffee provided for your breaks, please bring your lunch and snacks.

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. description:
Neurodiversity Workshop, Neurodiversity Workshop
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
This one-day workshop introduces you to the topic of neurodiversity and considers some of the key conditions that people live with. We look at:
•ADHD – Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder
•Autism
•The “Dys family” – dyslexia, dysgraphia, dyscalculia, dyspraxia (Development Coordination Disorder)
•OCD – Obsessive Compulsive Disorder
•Tourette’s Syndrome
Tik Tok creator and public speaker on neurodiversity, Nigel Sutton, will introduce the subject and facilitate you in discovering the definitions and impacts of each of the key kinds of neurodiversity. Working together with other participants, you will consider many key commonalities that those living with various neurodivergent conditions  experience. We will expose the realities of being neurodivergent in a “neurotypical world” and this will allow you to develop empathy and practical strategies to support neurodivergent people to be their best. 
New Zealand’s leading dyslexia expert Mike Styles, will provide an interactive and participatory session to assist you to understand and support a family member or friend who has dyslexia or a similar learning difference. 
You will be able to ask anything you want with our neurodivergent hot seat session.
Find out from those offering “lived experience” what it is really like to have a different kind of brain. This one day workshop is: ”Neurodiversity in a Nutshell” – whether you know a little or a lot, whether you are a relative, employer, partner, friend, or just interested to know more about neurodiversity – this workshop is for you!

description:
New Zealand and the heroic age of Antarctic exploration, A New Zealand perspective on early Antarctic expeditions.

Come along to this Friends of the Turnbull Library event for an opportunity to learn about the pivotal role New Zealanders played in early 20th century voyages to Antarctica.

In his book, 'South by South: New Zealand and the Heroic Age of Antarctic Exploration', Charles Ferrall tells the thrilling story of New Zealand’s key role in ‘the heroic age’ of Antarctic exploration.

In his research for the book, Charles explored a collection held in the Alexander Turnbull Library that was donated by Sir Joseph James Kinsey. Sir Joesph was a Christchurch businessman, collector, noted Antarctic enthusiast and New Zealand agent for the Antarctic expeditions of Sir Ernest Henry Shackleton and Captain Robert Falcon Scott.

description:
Oil & Cold Wax Landscapes Workshop, Discover the rich possibilities of oil paint and cold wax medium in this one-day workshop exploring atmospheric and expressive landscape painting.

Through a series of guided exercises, you'll learn how to build layers, create texture, and develop a sense of depth and distance using colour, tone and mark-making. The emphasis is on capturing the essence and feeling of landscape rather than detailed realism, allowing plenty of scope for personal interpretation.

During the workshop you will explore:

- Layering techniques using oil paint and cold wax medium
- Creating atmosphere and depth through colour and tone
- Building texture to suggest landforms and natural elements
- Using tools such as palette knives, brayers and squeegees
- Balancing abstraction with recognisable landscape forms

The day begins with smaller studies to build confidence with the materials before progressing to larger works where you can develop your own compositions.

What you'll take home
By the end of the day, you'll have completed a number of landscape studies and larger works on oil paper, giving you the opportunity to explore a range of techniques and approaches. You'll also receive a comprehensive Oil & Cold Wax Student Guide to support your continued exploration of the medium at home.

All materials and tools are provided, including oil paints, cold wax medium, oil paper and a variety of mark-making tools, allowing you to experience this versatile medium without needing to purchase supplies beforehand. For those who decide they would like to continue working with cold wax after the workshop, additional cold wax medium will be available for purchase on the day.

Suitable for beginners through to experienced artists, this workshop is ideal for anyone wanting to loosen their approach to landscape painting or explore the unique qualities of oil and cold wax.

What to bring
Please bring a piece of cardboard and some baking paper to transport your artwork home safely. As oil and cold wax paintings take time to cure, your work will still be wet at the end of the workshop.
Wear an apron or old clothes.

Half hour lunch break -bring a packed lunch to eat in the historic Inverlochy House or explore the local Te Aro cafes.

25 Feb (Wed) 2:30–4:30pm

27 Feb (Fri) 3–5pm

It’s not about being perfect – it’s about backing yourself, having a go, and discovering what you’re capable of alongside a group of incredible women doing exactly the same.

description:
Overcoming Imposter Syndrome for Creatives, Overcoming Imposter Syndrome for Creatives
There is a widespread ‘lack of confidence’ epidemic among creatives, and if you have ever felt like your work is not good enough, hesitated to submit your art to competitions, or doubted your skills when applying for creative jobs, you are not alone! Creatives often feel imposter syndrome most acutely. Unlike other industries, those in the creative field produce something new every time, and sharing this with the world can be daunting, even for established artists.
 This pervasive self-doubt, known as imposter syndrome, affects countless artists and creators, often holding them back from realising their full potential. This concise workshop is designed to help you uncover the roots of this inner voice of insecurity and provide you with effective tools to overcome it. Through engaging activities and practical exercises, you will learn how to transform self-doubt into a source of strength, empowering you to confidently share your unique talents with the world.
 What you won't find in this masterclass: This is not a session about general self-growth or self-confidence, and it does not include positive affirmations or self-talk. All the information provided is based on scientific research and is applicable to all creative sectors.
Bring along some examples of your work on the day (eg a painting, a photograph of your work, etc).
 By the end of this workshop, you’ll be able to: 
Identify and challenge the origins of your imposter syndrome.
Apply practical techniques to silence your inner critic.
Share your creative work with increased confidence.
Turn self-doubt into a motivational tool.
Recognise and celebrate your achievements as a creative professional.

description:
PADI Advanced Open Water Course, PADI Advanced Open Water Course
“Your Next Step in Underwater Adventure”
Exploration excitement and experiences are what the PADI Advanced Open Water
course is all about. And no you don't have to be "advanced" to take it - it's designed
so both new and experienced Open Water Divers can sign up and develop better
diving skills and techniques straight away!

The Advanced Open Water Diver course helps you increase your confidence and
build scuba skills to become safer and more comfortable in the water. It’s also a great
way to get more diving experience under the supervision of a PADI Instructor.
This course builds on what you've learnt and develops new capabilities by
introducing new dive activities and ways to have fun scuba diving. You will complete
5 different types of dives to build your confidence and develop your dive skills. The
dives include the basics of Deep Diving Underwater Navigation - and your choice of
Peak Performance Buoyancy Naturalist Fish Identification Wreck (weather dependant)
Enriched Air * Photography or Night during winter.

Complete the theory online then join us for a weekends diving. After the 5 dives
over the weekend you will qualify as a PADI Advanced Open Water Diver. This is the
minimum requirement for many of our dive adventures and a prerequisite for the
PADI Rescue Diver course.

If you have any questions please call so we can help you.

description:
PADI Rescue Diver Course, PADI Rescue Diver Course
CHALLENGING And REWARDING. The BEST Dive Course You Will EVER Take…
These words probably best describe the PADI Rescue Diver course. Building upon what you’ve already learned during your diving to date this course expands your knowledge and prepares you to deal with any problems you may encounter on and under the water.
The Rescue Diver course is the perfect opportunity for you to develop your personal self-rescue dive skills help tired divers administer first aid and rescue distressed divers under the guidance of your PADI Instructor.
During the online theory you’ll learn how to think like a rescue diver and preview skills you’ll practice with your PADI Instructor. After you have completed the Rescue Diver theory online you come in and spend a weekend with us practicing the skills and concepts you learnt about first in the pool then out in the ocean in progressively more challenging situations. We also take you through the Medic First Aid practical if you don’t already have a first aid and CPR certificate.
The Rescue Diver will start you looking differently at diving being more aware of the divers around you as well your own safety and dive gear. It is a prerequisite for the Master Scuba Diver Rating (the most prestigious recreational rating) as well as the Divemaster program (the first step in the professional dive ratings). It is commonly viewed as the most important dive course people take.

description:
PET First Aid Course - Wellington, PET First Aid Course - Wellington
Our Pet First Aid Courses educate both pet owners and those working in the industry on animal first aid and emergency situations.
Studies show that 90% of all pets will experience at least one emergency situation in their lifetime!
- Would you know what to do if your pet choked on their toy?
- Would you know what to do if your pet stopped breathing?
- Would you know what to do if your pet was hit by a car?
Most people would not, which is why PET First Aid & Training (NZ) Ltd developed a concise, New Zealand focused first aid course that was available to everyone.
The course covers 23 different situations and it is hands on for all attendees. Using specially imported mannequins from the USA you will learn CPR and rescue breathing. You will practice your bandaging skills on live animals. Learn to recognise everyday poisons, the symptoms and how to help stabilise your animal until you can get professional help. This course will empower you and give you confidence in an emergency situation.
Each person receives:
- Full Colour Manual
- Emergency Response Plan
- Poisonous Food Fact Sheet
- Poisonous Household Item Fact
Sheet
- Poisonous Plants Fact Sheet
- Certificate - valid for 2 years
Course attendance is limited to 10 people to ensure that everyone gets the opportunity to get involved. As places are limited book in quick not to miss out!
Accredited for NZVNA CPD
Accredited for Duke of Edinburgh Hilary Award - bronze skill section
Animal Evac NZ partner - discount available for volunteers
The course runs for 6 hours and costs $189.00 per person / $160 per student (group rates available, please inquire).
To book:
www.petfat.co.nz

description:
Padi Advanced Open Water Course, Exploration, excitement and experiences are what the PADI Advanced Open Water (AOW) Diver course is all about.

The AOW course is designed for both new and more experienced Open Water Divers and is best attended as soon after your Open Water Diver course as possible. That way you will increase your confidence and build scuba skills to become safer and more comfortable in the water; all under the supervision of a PADI Instructor.

The AOW course consists of five dives that includes a: Deep and an Underwater Navigation dive. Popular local options for the remaining three dives are: Peak Performance Buoyancy, Naturalist, Wreck, Fish Identification, Imaging, Night, *Enriched Air or *Dive Against Debris (* conditions apply).

You may choose to add the 'Enriched Air' and/or the 'Dive Against Debris' specialty qualifications to your weekend experience. Simply ask to: include these dives as part of your five dives, complete the on-line study and a short practical, pay a small fee – and go diving. These Specialties count towards the prestigious PADI Master Scuba Diver rating.

Pay your deposit and you can begin the AOW theory. Make sure your dive medical is current, then join us for a weekend's fun diving. After everything is completed, you will qualify as a PADI AOW Diver. This is the minimum requirement for our dive adventures and a prerequisite for the PADI Rescue Diver course.
If you have any questions, please call so we can help you.

Padi Rescue Diver Course, CHALLENGING And REWARDING - The BEST Dive Course You Will EVER Take…
These words probably best describe the PADI Rescue Diver course. Building upon what you’ve already learned during your diving to date, this course expands your knowledge and prepares you to deal with any problems you may encounter, on and under the water.

The Rescue Diver course is the perfect opportunity for you to develop your personal self-rescue dive skills, help tired divers, administer first aid and rescue distressed divers, under the guidance of your PADI Instructor.

During the online theory you’ll learn how to think like a rescue diver and preview skills you’ll practice with your PADI Instructor. After you have completed the Rescue Diver theory online, you come in and spend a weekend with us practicing the skills and concepts you learnt about, first in the pool then out in the ocean in progressively more challenging situations. We also take you through the Medic First Aid practical if you don’t already have a first aid and CPR certificate.

The Rescue Diver will start you looking differently at diving, being more aware of the divers around you as well your own safety and dive gear. It is a prerequisite for the Master Scuba Diver Rating (the most prestigious recreational rating) as well as the Divemaster program (the first step in the professional dive ratings). It is commonly viewed as the most important dive course people take.

PADI Rescue Diver Course Information:
Digital Theory – PADI Rescue Diver eLearning or tablet course (about 11 hours)
Full Weekend – Practical rescue skills and scenarios in the pool and open water

Prerequisites:
PADI Advanced Open Water Diver certification or Adventure Diver with Navigation (or qualifying certification from another agency)
12 Years of age or older

What To Bring:
Diver Medical | Participant Questionnaire (completed in the last 12 months). Other languages – click here
Your PADI Advanced Open Water Diver card or Adventure Diver with Navigation
Your eLearning completion form
First Aid & CPR certificate (can be taught in conjunction with the course)
