Panel Talk: Interconnected [Breathe | Mauri Ora], Discover how art, science, nature, and Indigenous knowledge converge as Marshmallow Laser Feast and experts share insights inspired by Breathe | Mauri Ora: An Immersive Journey into Nature by Marshmallow Laser Feast.

Hosted by Miriama Kamo, Interconnected brings the relationships of art, science, nature, and mātaurangagloss to life in a panel discussion where London-based art collective Marshmallow Laser Feast joins leading researchers and curators for an evening of sharing how we understand the world and ourselves, inspired by Breathe | Mauri Ora.

This thought-provoking kōrero explores how technology makes the invisible visible, and how creativity, science, and Indigenous knowledge together can transform how we see our planet and our place within it.

Featuring
* Representative from Marshmallow Laser Feast – artist/director
* Dr Dan Hikuroa – Earth systems scientist and expert in integrating mātauranga Māori
* Dr Huhana Smith – artist, curator, and researcher exploring climate adaptation and Māori knowledge
* Dr Rebecca Rice – Senior Curator Art at Te Papa
* Dr Thom Linley – Curator Fishes at Te Papa

The panel will explore
* How technology and art reveal nature’s hidden systems
* The meeting of mātauranga Māori and the scientific method
* Ethics and responsibility in an age of ecological change
* Reimagining humanity’s relationship with the living world
* Future visions for the next generation’s environmental consciousness.

Programme
* 6pm to 7pm – Exhibition Viewing
Experience Breathe | Mauri Ora after hours – an internationally acclaimed digital art exhibition that reveals the unseen forces connecting all living things.

* 7.30pm to 9pm – Panel Talk
Audience Q&A and closing reflections.

Spaces are limited – book your ticket today.

description:
Panel talk - Libraries and archives leading change, The inspiration for this panel talk is Rūaumoko, the atua Māori (Māori god) associated with earthquakes, volcanoes and the movement of the land. In this context, Rūaumoko represents disruption, but also transformation and creativity.

In our world, disruption is not an exception; it is becoming the norm. For libraries and archives, one of the challenges is not to stand apart from disruption, but to become places of convergence — of memory, access and trust, ultimately leading to transformation of communities, service and access.

Facilitated by Te Pouhuaki National Librarian Rachel Esson, this lively kōrero features a panel of international leaders from libraries and archives in Australia, Canada, the United States of America and Aotearoa.

The panellists are:

- Anahera Morehu, Poumanaaki Chief Archivist at Archives New Zealand Te Rua Mahara o te Kāwanatanga
- Leslie Weir, Librarian and Archivist of Canada at Library and Archives Canada
- Dr Marie-Louise Ayres, Director-General at National Library of Australia
- Simon Froude, Director-General at National Archives of Australia
- Robin L Dale, Deputy Librarian at the Library of Congress, United States of America

Light refreshments will be served after the panel talk.

This kōrero will also celebrate the opening of our new heritage campus — Te Kahu on 25 March 2026.

Te Kahu brings together the new archival building and the National Library building in Wellington. It brings together Aotearoa New Zealand’s documentary heritage in one modern, purpose‑built place.

description:
Photography - Unlocking the Secrets to Captivating Images, Why do some photographs linger in our memories while others seem forgettable and repetitive? Why do we scroll through Instagram and barely recall what we saw five minutes later?

This course will help you find the answers to these questions and show you how to transform your photographs into extraordinary, captivating, and memorable images

Elevate your photography from ordinary to extraordinary and ensure your work stands out in the digital age. Creating captivating photographs and understanding what makes a photograph engaging is something every photographer should master.

Camera settings are essential, but once you know them, you need to learn how to take photographs that stir emotions, impact your audience, and leave a lasting impression.
After all, isn’t that the true purpose of photography? People don’t want to see the same landscapes or flowers they’ve seen thousands of times. But how do you turn what you love into something that makes people go, "Wow"?

Captivation in photography means stopping a viewer in their tracks, making them look, feel, and connect. It’s about delivering a photograph that enthrals, evokes profound emotions, and shifts perspectives.

In a world brimming with images, only a few have the power to truly captivate and linger in our memories.

This pioneering course is your gateway to mastering the art of creating captivating photographs at a time when AI-generated images are saturating our visual landscape. Create something genuine and memorable—images that spark curiosity, evoke emotions, and inspire changes in perception. It's time to define your unique style, refine your vision, and make your mark.

Course Outcomes

By the end of the five-week course, you’ll be able to:

-Identify the foundational elements that transform an ordinary image into a captivating one.
-Create photographs that make people say "Wow" by applying techniques that add a spark of wonder to your shots.
-Infuse your photographs with curiosity, making each frame a source of intrigue and interest.
-Understand why some images linger in memory and how to make your photographs unforgettable.
-Develop a unique style and vision that sets your work apart in the crowded digital landscape.

Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Prerequisites
This course is perfect for you if you:

Aim to elevate your photography from good to mind-blowing.
Are eager to discover the secret ingredients that make photographs unforgettable (all backed by research and science).
Feel passionate about photography but need fresh ideas on what to photograph and how to truly stand out.
Wish to explore and evolve your genre and style.

5 sessions, 4 x Thu 5:30 PM – 7:30 PM plus a Saturday field trip
Wellington High School

description:
Plan Your Page - Journaling Creatively, Are you inspired by the aesthetic journals you see online but don’t know where to begin?

Do you feel like you need a never-ending list of supplies to make something that looks appealing?

Do you want to stretch your creative muscles more when you journal?

If you wish for more clarity on putting together a page that is creatively satisfying, aesthetically pleasing, and reflects your unique style, then join Mira for this action-packed class.

This special class will explore:

- How to play and find your unique journalling style
- Key things to think about when laying out a page
- How to make your style more cohesive and speed up your creative process
- Using clear, acrylic stamps in your journaling process
- Dos and don'ts to have you stamping like a pro!

We’ll work through a guided creative activity to make a journal spread about The New Zealand Stationery Festival and you’ll leave the workshop with a page structure well underway and ready to complete with all the day’s highlights when you get home.

Your class fee includes a generous kit of supplies for you to take home:

- An MD Notebook - A5 Grid (RRP $24.90)
- A Clear Stamp Set (RRP $39.90)
- An Acrylic Stamp Block (RRP $12.90)
- Two Custom Sticker Sheets, designed by Mira (RRP $10)
- Washi Tape Sample Card (RRP $9)
- A loop of DingDing PET tape (RRP $15)
- Shachihata Mini Stamp Pad (RRP $9.90)
- A NZ Made Ruler (RRP$3.90)
- Handout with key takeaways from the class, including links to helpful content and extra information

Students, please bring along:

- A pen in a neutral colour (can be a black gel pen or marker, or a fountain pen)
- A pair of scissors (any size)

About your teacher:
By day, Mira is a data geek, happily working with numbers and advanced technology. Based in Auckland, she’s worked at Nielsen and Stuff, and right now she’s the Head of Data Governance for SkyCity. In her free time, Mira is a creative soul who enjoys a number of hobbies including knitting (knitting patterns as Cetus Knits) and creative journaling of all kinds.
Follow Mira on Instagram: @cetuscreates

Presented as part of The New Zealand Stationery Festival. Your ticket to this event does not include access to the Stationery Festival. Please purchase a ticket for The New Zealand Stationery Festival separately.

description:
Please Let Me Remain, 
Please Let Me Remain, is A/Motion's debut work as an emerging project-based contemporary dance collective, founded by Aylin Atalay. The work is an intimate exploration of sisterhood through the lens of Aylin's roots and identity as a Turkish/Pakeha woman.
Five dancers will explore how sisterhood affects the individual and the group as one entity. Women together in comfort, sharing the same mundane experiences.
The games we make up, the‬ ‭future we see together, the life we romanticise. The culture we are all at the root of, and the‬ hope there are better days ahead.
Taking influence from Turkish traditions and Aylin's interest in reflecting the human experience, the audience will witness intertwined female connections that hold up the group and carry stories, memories and values. Viewers will observe how this culture stays rooted in the individual while they are alone and how sisterhood is a bond that keeps things moving. 
It is a journey of surrendering to the space together and enjoying simplicity, nostalgia, and the tangents relationships have. In contrast to this, it holds a melancholic quality when a dancer is alone. We are a result of the women who raised us. How do we continue to carve this path for others?

description:
Posture Perfection Is Possible, Are you a computer slouch, feeling stiff and tense at work? Do you find it difficult to maintain a good posture? Does your posture cause back, neck or shoulder tension? Would you like to enjoy more freedom in everyday activities?

Under the guidance of an experienced teacher, we'll explore movement in ways that help you reduce tense unhelpful habits. Movement lessons are done on the floor or sitting on a chair and are based on the pioneering work of Israeli physicist and engineer Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais. This workshop is suitable for all ages (over 16) and fitness levels.

Outcomes
By the end of the workshop, you'll be able to:
- Identify and reduce muscle tension
- Move with more lightness and freedom
- Improve your posture
- Describe some basic anatomy
- Have tools to use at home and at work

Bring two blankets (or a mat and a blanket) and wear loose, warm and comfortable clothing. Tea and coffee provided but bring your lunch.

Please note that instructions are given verbally rather than by demonstration, so good hearing and understanding of English is required.

1 Day
Presented by Sue Field.

description:
Produce like a Pro - A Workshop for Theatre and Comedy Makers, This full day workshop deep dives into the fundamentals of producing, marketing and touring theatre and comedy in Aotearoa New Zealand. Led by two of the country’s leading independent producers, we’ll take you through a series of practical tips and resources to help you make more professional work, and less stressful production processes.

Whether you have a fresh idea for next year's fringe circuit, or an existing show planning its next steps- we'll cover everything you need to know with plenty of time for tailored feedback and advice.

The Workshop will cover:
- Key producing decisions and creating the right timelines and production plans for your work.
- Assembling the right team, contracting and looking after your people.
- How to manage budgets and expenses without losing your mind.
- An overview of the funding and partnerships landscape in Aotearoa, and how to get the most out of your time spent in this area.
- Identifying your target demographic and the best ways to get in front of them.
- A general guide to marketing and publicity in 2026.
- Touring in New Zealand and beyond.

The workshop can be attended in-person or online. Online attendees will be sent a link in advance of the workshop day (keep an eye on your spam folder, just in case).

Pricing is Pay What You Can from $50, but we reckon it's worth may more than that. Paying what you can afford, helps to make it more affordable for those for whom it's a stretch. If payment is a barrier, we're open to service exchange and other koha options so feel free to get in touch.

ABOUT THE FACILITATORS

NINA HOGG
Nina is a comedian, tour manager, performer and producer based in Pōneke. She has worked as a full-time producer and tour manager for The Theatre in Health Education Trust (Sexwise), The National Theatre for Children and Young & Hungry, managing and/or producing eight full scale national theatre tours.

She also regularly tours her own works around NZ and Australia with her queer comedy duo Ginge & Minge and Mon Platon’s touring production Coro- which toured to the Edinburgh Fringe in 2025. Her accolades include “Best Show” at the Wellington Comedy Awards 2025, “Comic Originality” at NZ Comedy Guild Awards 2025, and “Best Hustler” at NZ International Comedy Festival 2026.

Nina also leads marketing and publicity for PopRox Improv, Mon Platon Productions, Ginge & Minge and currently manages social media for Wellington icon Shut Up and Dance.

AUSTIN HARRISON
Austin is one of Aotearoa's most prolific performers and producers, having worked on over 800 live events. He's won a Wellington Theatre Award, “Favourite Comedian” at Dunedin Fringe 2026, and “Best Newcomer” at NZ International Comedy Festival 2026.

Austin is the Artistic Director of the New Zealand Improv Festival, and lead producer of Mon Platon Productions and Ace-ssential Workers (an independent company telling Aspec/asexual/aromantic stories on stage). He’s toured work from Gore to Whangārei, to the Melbourne International Comedy Festival, Adelaide Fringe and the Edinburgh Fringe.

description:
Professor Brian Cox - Emergence, After performing his smash-hit show ‘Horizons’ to nearly half a million people across the world, Professor Brian Cox is back with his new world tour Emergence.

Brian has appeared in many landmark science programmes for BBC radio and television over the last 15 years, from the Peabody Award-winning Wonders of the Solar System to the world-wide hit series The Planets.

In the winter of 1610 Johannes Kepler was crossing Prague’s Charles Bridge when he noticed a snowflake land on his arm. Why, he asked, are all snowflakes six-cornered? “I do not believe,” he wrote, “that even in a snowflake, this ordered pattern exists at random.”

400 years later, we have part of the answer. Snowflakes are made of water molecules, which are made of atoms, which are made of quarks and electrons – which might be made of superstrings – all held together by forces of nature described by quantum theory. But how does such delicate beauty emerge from such abstract simplicity?

Emergence is a celebration of the intricacy of the Universe and an exploration of the laws of nature that sculpted it. From the largest structures in the known Universe – the rivers and flows of galaxies that trace the cosmic web – to Earth’s interlinked ecosystems and the structure of the human brain – from black holes to snowflakes – we observe a world of dazzling complexity underpinned by magnificent simplicity.

How did a quarter of a million-year-old species of great apes on one small planet amongst trillions orbiting around a middle-aged star in an average galaxy figure all this out, guided by curiosity, mathematics and an aesthetic sense of symmetry and beauty? And what might we become if we can hold onto the ideas of the enlightenment so successfully developed and deployed by Kepler and his contemporaries and successors – ideas that have allowed us to begin to read the story of the Universe and carried our spacecraft to the edge of the solar system and outwards to the stars.

Professor Brian Cox said: “I’ve loved creating Emergence – it’s the most ambitious live show I’ve ever written. I’ve been very lucky to collaborate with a wonderful group of scientists, musicians, filmmakers and graphic artists to bring cosmology, biology, philosophy and history to the largest and most advanced LED screens available, with the best sound and lights I could find. I hope the show is an all-encompassing experience, and I hope it leaves everyone, whether they love science or music or history, or simply contemplating the beauty of Nature, with something new to think about.”

It's about understanding the psychology behind how you spend or save, and discovering how we can make preparing for our future easier and more enjoyable. Once you understand how you regard money, you can take control of yours!

Managing finances should be empowering and enjoyable, yet traditional methods often make money a stressful, taboo topic—even with your closest loved ones. In this workshop, we're not here to tell you to cut your budget or skip your favourite treats. Instead, we’ll come together to design a financial plan tailored to your unique needs, making you feel confident, excited, and in control.

In this workshop, you’ll explore the psychology of money and how it influences your financial decisions. Through real-life case studies, step-by-step guidance, and collaborative exercises, you’ll design a financial system that suits your lifestyle, reduces stress, and helps you achieve your goals.

If you want to simplify your finances and live without the worry of every dollar spent, then this is the workshop for you!

This workshop will be a confronting one that will expose you to the risks that children face in this modern overindulgent world. Many have become used to being the constant centre of attention and are unable to delay gratification and aren’t competent in everyday skills. They have few self-care skills and skills relating to others, can’t take personal responsibility and don’t know what is enough or what is “normal” for others – these children end up having a difficult time of it in life and you will too.
 You’ll take away new insight and knowledge plus strategies that you can apply that very night to help your child to be a responsible, likeable and respectful person.
By the end of the session, you’ll be able to:
• Reflect on the current context parents are faced with today
• Find the relevant research
• Practise the parenting tools and discuss the model
• Know where to go to get support
Aimed at parents, grandparents and caregivers of children of all ages.

description:
Real Kids, Real Complexity: Teaching at the Intersection of Neurodiversity, Culture and Development, Real Kids, Real Complexity: Teaching at the Intersection of Neurodiversity, Culture and Development
Teaching has never been more complex or more important. Every classroom is a dynamic mix of neurodiversity, cultural identity, language, trauma, and rapid societal change. Educators are being asked to do more, with less - often caught between policy pressures and what they know is right for children.

This new national workshop from Longworth Education acknowledges that complexity and offers practical, evidence-informed strategies for navigating it.

This is not a one-size-fits-all model. Instead, we explore what it means to teach in ways that are developmentally responsive, neuro-affirming, trauma-aware and culturally sustaining, all while managing the daily realities of the classroom.

Designed for teachers, leaders, SENCOs, learning support staff and anyone working in education, this workshop will support you to:

Better understand the developmental, neurological and relational needs that shape student behaviour and learning

Recognise and respond to complexity, without becoming overwhelmed by it

Strengthen inclusive, identity-affirming practices that work in diverse, real-world classrooms

Learn practical ways to hold onto both rigour and humanity in your teaching

Leave with tools, frameworks and language you can use the very next day

Whether you're new to this way of thinking or looking to deepen your practice, this workshop will meet you where you are and support you to move forward with confidence, clarity and care.

Join us as we mark ten years of Longworth Education’s commitment to child-centred pedagogy and celebrate our recognition as one of HundrED’s Top 100 Global Education Innovations for 2026 and Aotearoa's leading expert in play pedagogy across the school sector.

description:
Retirement Reinvented, Retirement Reinvented
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
In your middle years, working, retired or somewhere in between? What’s next? Life is about much more than work or leisure, but most of us have given little thought to what “retirement” might mean.
It’s difficult to speculate what may happen in the future – but we can be proactive and take control.
This course offers insights into how to make the most of our time once we’re less focused on career and/or childrearing. It covers many of the issues people face when considering a move from current employment to a different lifestyle that includes more time to do the things we’ve always promised ourselves we’d do – “when we retire”.
After the workshop, you’ll be able to identify a number of common issues and potential ways to manage them when considering and planning your “rejuvenation”, rather than a retirement. We won’t cover financial planning, but will focus on some of the personal growth opportunities for living and making a conscious contribution to your community.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
By the end of the day, you’ll have:
Developed your own perspective on ageing and retirement in the 21st Century and identified what’s important to you
Completed a personal life audit exercise and considered your values and your strengths
Considered options to include a sense of purpose and explore choices that can provide you with that sense of purpose
Explored possibilities in the major aspects of your life and identified potential challenges and strategies for overcoming them
Begun to develop your blueprint to maximise the best years of your life and have considered a “future proofing” downsizing plan.
Bring pen and paper.

We won’t cover financial planning, but will focus on some of the personal growth opportunities for living and making a conscious contribution to your community.

By the end of the day, you’ll have:
- Developed your own perspective on ageing and retirement in the 21st Century and identified what’s important to you
- Completed a personal life audit exercise and considered your strengths
- Explored possibilities in the major aspects of your life and identified potential challenges and strategies for overcoming them
- Developed a blueprint to maximise the best years of your life and developed a “future proofing” downsizing plan
- Considered options to include a sense of purpose and explored and implemented choices that provide you with that sense of purpose
Bring a pen and paper.

1 day, Sat 9:30 AM – 4:00 PM

description:
Richard Dawkins — 50 Years of The Selfish Gene, Richard Dawkins is a world-renowned evolutionary biologist. When published in 1976, his book, ‘The Selfish Gene’, reframed our understanding of life, behaviour, and human nature. Now, 50 years later, he is coming to Wellington to reflect on the book’s revolutionary legacy. He explores what fifty years of science has confirmed or challenged and explains why its core questions are more urgent today than ever before. 
‘The Selfish Gene’ has remained a cornerstone of modern science. It introduced the gene-centred view of evolution and coined the now-ubiquitous concept of the ‘meme’. The ideas in it ignited global debate and five decades of subsequent research. Richard Dawkins is one of the most consequential scientific communicators of our time, so don’t miss the rare opportunity to hear him speak in person.

description:
Riding Blind, Riding Blind
We all know trucks have huge blind spots—right in front, beside, and behind—that can completely hide motorcycles? In New Zealand, many crashes happen simply because riders are unseen.
But it’s not just visibility — impairment from alcohol or other factors can drastically slow your reactions and decision-making on the road.

As part of Motorcycle Awareness Month, join us for a free event on Thursday 18 September at 5:30 pm at NZ Motorcycle Centre to learn:

*Where motorcycles are most at risk around trucks.
*How to stay visible using lane positioning and following distance.
*How impairment affects your riding — test it out with our “beer goggles” activity.

Food and cold drinks will be provided, with barista coffee and hot chocolate available to purchase.

Book your Ride Forever course with code MAM25 between 1 Sept and 15 Oct and get it for free — plus go in the draw to win one of three Muc-Off Helmet Care Kits!

A huge thank you to ACC and all our supporters for making these events possible.

The Motorcycle Collective is a DIY workshop and community for all riders — a place to hang out, find support, give support, and pay it forward. Learn more at: motorcyclecollective.org.nz

description:
Sandcasting Day - Summer, Join us for this wonderful intro to sandcasting - it is a great opportunity to make some gorgeous lasting jewellery gifts for yourself or your loved ones!

Students are shown the ancient technique of sand casting, using a wax to make a simple hard model or found objects such as buttons or simple small forms - create your simple 2-part mould and melt and pour sterling silver or shibuichi (a different mix of silver and copper) to cast into the sand.

The model you have made or found enables you to make multiple pours possible, until you either get the result you are after or to create multiple pieces. This is a fun process for those who just want to try their hand at it, or a very useful low-tech process for those who are making jewellery into a career or creative activity.

Course cost includes 9g silver but students can expect to use extra $50 - $70 worth of silver or $20 - $30 of shibuichi.

This course aims to allow students to all have at least one successful cast, and to learn the finishing techniques for the pieces they cast, allowing you to leave with a gorgeous finished piece of jewellery.

description:
Sat Afternoon Jewellery Making - Beginners, Spend your Saturday afternoons immersed in creativity, learning the timeless craft of jewellery-making in our warm, welcoming studio.

This short course is the perfect introduction for complete beginners, guiding you step-by-step through the essential techniques used by jewellers. You’ll start by working in copper or brass, building confidence as you learn to cut, heat, shape and texture metal. From there, you can choose to move into silver and bring your ideas to life in more refined pieces.

A beautiful textured ring band is an ideal first project, but once you’ve mastered the basics, the possibilities really open up—create earrings, pendants, or small bespoke pieces that reflect your personal style. You’ll learn how to solder using a jeweller’s torch, refine your finishing techniques, and polish your work to a professional shine. It’s a hands-on, deeply satisfying process, and there’s nothing quite like wearing something you’ve made yourself.

Materials are purchased as you go, so you can tailor your projects to your budget and ideas. Beginners typically spend around $50–$70 on metals over the course.

This block is ideal for teens and young creatives aged 12 and up.

description:
Scottish Country Dancing, Scottish Country Dancing
Why do Scottish Country Dancing? Great music and amazing ‘brain gym’ for body and mind! Scottish Country Dancing is a very social form of dancing, danced in "sets" usually with four "couples" - unlike Highland Dancing which is usually solo dancing. Have fun and meet new people, while getting fit!
It’s suitable for all levels of fitness, and is a great way of meeting and socialising with new people. Scottish country dancing is a common pastime for thousands of dancers in many countries, whether you’re in Japan, Germany, the US or Scotland itself.
Wear soft flat shoes and loose clothing and bring a bottle of water. No partner is needed – we change partners for every dance!
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
• Name and perform to beginner level the five major steps of Scottish Country Dancing
• Name and perform ten simple formations
• Participate in five simple Scottish Country dances, in strathspey (slow) and reel/jig (fast) tempo
• Clap rhythm to reel, jig and strathspey tempo
• Have the confidence and skills to join a club to progress your social dancing 
[This is a physical activity that involves an element of risk.  While all possible measures are taken to prevent accidents or injury, please note that participation is at your own risk].

description:
Screenprinting taster workshop Nov 15th - print a tote bag, Design and screenprint your own tote bag, no experience needed!
Join artist and designer Greta Menzies for a fun, hands-on introduction to screenprinting using paper stencils.
In this 2-hour session you’ll design and cut your own stencil, then print your artwork onto a tote bag (included in your ticket).
Want to make extras? See the 'what's included' section below.
What you’ll learn
How to create and screenprint your own design using paper stencils
Tips and tricks from Greta’s years of experience as an artist and textile designer
(Greta is happy to answer any questions about printing methods and help you find resources)

What’s included
All materials provided, including one tote bag
Extra tote bags will be available on the day for $6 each. They make great gifts!
You’re also welcome to bring your own light-coloured fabric or fabric item to print on, just make sure it’s at least 50% natural fibre (cotton or linen is ideal).
The max print size is A3.
Can I print more than one bag? Or multiple colours?
Once your design is on the screen you can print a few multiples if you'd like.
The workshop is set up for participants to make one bag with a single colour print, but depending on how fast you work, (if there is time) you are welcome to add another colour.

Who it’s for
This workshop is for anyone curious about screenprinting, no experience required.
All ages welcome! (Under 13s will need an adult to join them.)
Accessibility
The space is wheelchair accessible.
The process is adaptable for all abilities. If you can use scissors, that's excellent, tearing paper also works. Greta is happy to help with cutting if needed.
Details
Date: Saturday November 15th, 2025
Time: 10.30am - 12.30pm
Location: Mt Cook School, 160 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington
Cost: $85 per person
Class size: Max of 10 participants
What to bring
Yourself and your ideas!
Wear clothes you don’t mind getting a little paint on (or bring an apron)
Optional: light-coloured fabric item to print on (at least 50% natural fibre, cotton or linen is ideal)
Water bottle and snacks if you like
Extra tote bags available on the day for $6 each
(random colours and limited selection, unless you want to email me ahead of time and order something specific: greta.menzies@gmail.com)
About Greta
Greta Menzies is an artist and designer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has taught art and design workshops since 2015, in galleries, schools, community studios, and at Massey University. Greta first started screenprinting with stencils in her garage at 17, making hoodies and t-shirts for her mates. Over the last few years, she’s refined her accessible, low-impact printing method while teaching school groups - and now it’s time for all ages to have a go!

description:
Scriptwriting, Scriptwriting
During this course, you will develop and build on your writing skills so you can confidently produce scripted narrative. You will learn how the basics of scriptwriting work, whether it be for stage or screen.
 Topics discussed and practised include the three act structure, script format, the differences between writing for film, theatre and television, creating dialogue, world building and more.
 We’ll take part in exercises, watch clips and have group discussions. In workshops, you’ll give and receive feedback, developing your scriptwriting skills through both. By the end of the course, you’ll be ready to finish your script, and take the next steps toward bringing it from page to stage (or screen!).
 Bring pen and paper.
 By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Analyse film, television, and theatre with a new lens for the way scripted stories work
- Develop character arcs and dynamics
- Create and build worlds
- Write effective dialogue and work with subtext
- Develop and implement a writing routine that works for your life
- Give and receive constructive feedback on your writing
- Have the confidence to put your work out into the world

description:
Sculpture - Intro to Creature Sculpting, Join us in an exciting new introduction to creative sculpting - a hands on class to produce unique creature figurines and miniatures to bring your imagination to life! - Beginners welcome! All material costs included in course fee.

Description
Whether you want to make creatures cute, creepy, in the style of pop-toys, figurines, or a one-of-a-kind character in your own style, this is the class for you!

Working with air dry clays, oven bake polymer clays and wire, armatures this workshop offers a variety of modelling methods and approaches - a great opportunity to turn ideas into tangible 3D forms. With modern clays we can create translucent, flexible, and even glow-in-the-dark elements to add more realism or a touch of the surreal into each creation!

We’ll kick off working with traditional air-dry clay to get a feel for modelling a few simple forms.

Once familiar with the materials, we’ll go through some basic design elements, guided by animal anatomy and morphology. From here the tutor will show and chat with the group about ways we can transform the creatures from our imagination into unique sculptures full of character.

Students will be coached through designing and creating a series of small-scale creature sculptures, beginning simple, and building to a more complex final form as we gather practice.

The class offers beginner students a fun introduction to sculpting organic forms from scratch, and for those with some hands-on creative experience, it offers a great opportunity to experiment, hone and advance your making skills to new levels.

Please wear closed-in footwear suitable for a workshop environment. bring a work apron if you have one or wear clothes you don’t mind getting a little grubby. Remember to bring your reading glasses if a have them.

description:
Sea Glass Jewellery Making - 3 x evening workshops, Design and create a unique ring with foraged sea glass ‘gems’ while learning and developing core jewellery fabrication techniques. An opportunity to engage in creative recycling by turning seaside flotsam into precious wearable treasures. Experiment with ring textures and forms in silver, brass and/or copper, then set your unique glass ‘gemstone’. Finish up with your choice of polish, including high lustre gloss, steel brushed satin, or darkened antique finishes.

If you can, please beachcomb and bring along some sea glass options - ideally around 1cm wide, and with a flat back. Glass provided if you are in need.

Techniques:

- Create a ring with one bezel set foraged sea glass ‘gem’
- Use jeweller’s callipers to measure and prepare metal
- Use jeweller’s saws or snips to cut and shape metal
- Use files and sanding to refine and smooth metal edges and surfaces
- Use jeweller’s flame torches to solder join metal pieces
- Use Dremel & bench polishers to refine & finish metal casts into wearable jewellery

Materials Supplied: Sea Glass, Copper, Brass, Sterling Silver

Project of one ring to be completed over 3 x Friday evening sessions on 14,21 & 28 November, 5:30 -7:30 pm.

with storyteller and arts educator Tanya Batt
www.imagined-worlds.net
Join acclaimed and experienced storyteller, Tanya Batt (creator of the Gingerbread man Blues and the Magic Playdough), as she shares a guide for interactive storytelling; organising process dramas; imaginative group activities - songs, movement  and full bodied story telling set within a framework for celebrating the changing seasons.
A highly interactive, practical workshop that will give you cause for celebrating.
 " What a magical experience it is to attend a workshop of internationally renowned storyteller, writer and educator Tanya Batt. Seasonal Storytelling, combines Tanya’s expertise as a storyteller and arts educator with her profound respect and understanding of the natural world. Weaving pūrākau, waiata and whakatauākī with stories and songs from cultures around the world, Seasonal Storytelling offers imaginative and practical ways to help tamariki celebrate and connect with the seasonal changes in Aotearoa. It also provides teachers with helpful suggestions around working with tamariki through storytelling and the arts."
Moira Wairama - storyteller, writer and teacher

description:
Secure Development Training - September 2025, Have you been to a Kawaiicon and found yourself realising that you want to know more? Are you a curious developer who wants to know what happens if you prod a web application? Are you a QA looking to take the worst path possible through an app?
Maybe the PrivSec Secure Development Training is for you!
Agenda
The training is a one day course consisting of the following:
A detailed overview of the OWASP Top Ten Web Application vulnerabilities.
Multiple real world examples and case studies of exploited vulnerabilities.
Hands on experience exploiting these vulnerabilities on a custom web application
Techniques and tooling to identify and exploit these bug classes, using both source code analysis and dynamic testing techniques.
Remediation steps and techniques to mitigate and avoid these issues.
Outcomes
By the end of the day, you will have an understanding of tools and techniques used to compromise web applications and hands on experience in exploiting multiple vulnerabilities in the OWASP top ten.
About the Trainer
Training will be led by one of our Senior consultants, Jack Moran and supported by Sriram Jayaraman
Jack is a Senior Consultant at PrivSec Consulting. He has worked in the offensive security space for the better part of a decade, focusing on web and mobile application testing, along with code reviews and security configuration reviews. He has a number of CVEs credited to himself, and his enthusiasm towards security security is infectious.

description:
Self Defence Foundations - 2hr Introduction, Being prepared is smart. Come be prepared with protective and self-defence skills that will last a lifetime.
Imagine enjoying the peace and freedom of no longer feeling caught without options in threatening and unsafe situations, for the rest of your life. Whether working day to day, going on travels, or simply talking to your kids about their safety, you will be armed with knowledge, tactics, techniques, physical conditioning, muscle memory and a sharpened sense of awareness from mental conditioning, that you can take with you where ever you go. Your Krav training will become like a ‘practical toolkit for protection’ that will accompany you for the rest of your life.

That process takes only a few minutes so there is plenty of time in this 3-hour class to complete your projects.
Beginners start with simple pendants, earrings or charms. It is much easier to start with flat projects so we leave the rings for the advanced class!
Jewellery pieces can be textured and shaped however you like, and if you don't like your piece simply squish it and start again - Precious Metal Clay is the ultimate recyclable material!

Sip & Kintsugi Workshop in Wellington // The Bond Store Distillery, Sip & Kintsugi Workshop in Wellington // The Bond Store Distillery
Come and experience this unique Sip & Kintsugi workshop at the lovely Bond Store Distillery. You will get a gin tasting tray on arrival with three different gins with tonic. And why not come a little earlier and grab a bite to eat beforehand. (Must be 18years +)

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)

Friday 26th June - 5:30pm - 7:30pm


Ema has been teaching Kintsugi for 5+ years and regularly travels to Japan to study and learn new techniques. Ema's illustrations and ceramic works sit in many of our countries best galleries, and whose products and merchandise sell in the most stylish design stores and gallery shops. Her style is enchanting - quirky, feminine and colourful, and clearly influenced by her travels throughout the world, usually off the beaten track.

Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.

Kintsugi
It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:
A finished artwork piece
A understanding of Kintsugi
Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

description:
Sir Ian Athfield Memorial Lecture 2025 | Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington, Te Kāhui Whaihanga New Zealand Institute of Architects are excited to welcome Ian Moore to New Zealand to present this year’s lecture series ‘The Past Needs a Future’ which will focus on adaptive reuse.
Ian is the principal of Ian Moore Architects, established in 1990. The practice has won numerous Australian and international awards and has been published and exhibited widely, including at the Venice Architecture Biennale in 2008 and 2012.
Initially studying civil and structural engineering at the Auckland Technical Institute in New Zealand, Ian moved on to study architecture at the University of Technology, Sydney, graduating with honours in 1988.
Ian has taught at numerous universities and been a speaker and guest lecturer throughout Australia as well as internationally.
Ian has also been a member of awards juries in Australia, New Zealand and at the World Festival of Interiors in 2013 and the World Architecture Festival in 2015. In 2003, Ian was the inaugural Creative Director for the Australian Institute of Architects annual conference.
About the Sir Ian Athfield Memorial Lecture
The annual Sir Ian Athfield Memorial Lecture commemorates the late Ian Athfield, a singular and much-loved figure in New Zealand architecture.
Affectionately known as ‘Ath’, Ian was knighted in 2014 and was one of New Zealand’s most influential architects. He won more than 60 national and international architecture and design awards and the lecture series was established to honour his legacy and celebrate his larrikin spirit.
In keeping with that spirit, each year the lecture is given by a person with something to say – someone who is challenging orthodoxy and a business-as-usual approach to practice, and life.
During his career, Ath designed many significant buildings, none more so than his own home in Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington, which enraged the neighbours, perplexed the Council and inspired the city for decades.
Ath was talented, original, insightful, opinionated, provocative, and sometimes outrageous. His architecture is stimulating, challenging, ever-changing, but never careless.
In 2004, Te Kāhui Whaihanga New Zealand Institute of Architects awarded Ath the Gold Medal for career achievements, noting at the time “What defines Athfield above all is his contagious enthusiasm, his devotion to architecture, and his unswerving belief in its possibilities. Believing architecture to be a civilising force, he has demonstrated a strong commitment to architecture’s public realm: the streets we live in; the urban centres we inhabit; the countryside we love and so often abuse.”
The Sir Ian Athfield Lecture Series is proudly sponsored by Resene and GIB.

An excellent, fun class if you have already taken one of our Stacking Rings or Textured Earrings classes and fancy adding to your jewellery collection.

You will learn to create a tapered pattern for a ring to fit your finger. You will get to practice in copper or brass first then make your masterpiece in solid golden bronze. You will measure and cut the bronze, then apply a beautifully shiny, sparkly hammered finish using carefully polished hammers. Then you’ll be guided through soldering and forming up your tapered band, before carefully cleaning it up and applying the finishing touches to make this a ring that will be coveted for generations.

All materials supplied, optional upgrade to solid sterling silver - silver sheets in a range of thicknesses are available for purchase in the workshop.

*If you really love your bronze or brass ring and want to elevate it with a thin sterling silver liner, a 4 or 6 week block is ideal to take your piece to the next level.

Included in the class fee are copper for practising on, and sterling silver bar to create your twist ring and all consumables such as sandpaper, solder and chemicals. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

presentation.
Actions that build rapport with your audience.
Strategies to maximise the impact of your words, voice, and body language.
Mindsets and actions to reduce stage-fright and appear more confident.
Memory techniques and strategies for impromptu speaking.

description:
Spring Container Planting Workshop, Grow Your Own Kai - In Containers From Your Own Compost

Want to grow your own fresh kai but only have a balcony, patio, or courtyard? This hands-on workshop will show you how to grow spring vegetables and herbs in containers - a flexible, low-cost way to turn even the smallest space into a productive garden. Following on from our winter edition, this is the second workshop in our seasonal container growing series, with a focus on getting your spring garden thriving using your own compost.

This workshop will cover:
- What to grow in spring, including leafy greens, herbs, and root vegetables
- How to set up containers - choosing the right size, drainage, potting mix, and using your own compost or bokashi soil
- Feeding your plants with DIY fertilisers, spotting nutrient gaps, and refreshing tired soil
- Creating ideal growing conditions with sunlight, watering tips, wind protection, and natural pest control
- Keeping your garden productive by harvesting, replanting, and rotating crops throughout the season

Please bring your own container(s) - buckets, storage bins, flexi tubs, or old drawers all welcome. We will show you how to safely repurpose them.

Spaces are limited, book now to get growing this Spring!

description:

Spring Solstice, Spring Solstice
**Contact me to purchase tickets ❤️ $50 person**

We’re welcoming the change of season with something truly special, and we’d love you to be part of it. Our Spring Solstice Celebration is all about renewal, connection, and stepping into the brighter months with intention and joy.

We start the night with our main retreat leader, spiritual guide and life coach Amy cleansing our energy, we then move on to a woman's circle before planting our intentions for the future by sowing seeds (you get to take home), gentle meditation and then we start weaving our flower crowns. Also included will be a small gift basket of local produce and handcrafted goodies!

This event is $50 per person so if you're interested let me know and book your spot!

description:
Stacking Rings - Christmas session!, Create your very own ring stack from copper, brass and sterling silver in this fast, fun and highly rewarding festive workshop!

Guided by our experienced and supportive tutors, you’ll be introduced to the fundamental skills of jewellery-making while creating a small collection of rings to take home and treasure.

During this 3-hour class, you’ll learn how to measure your finger, cut metal to size, and add textures and patterns using hammers and punches. From there, you’ll be shown how to solder your rings together with a jeweller’s torch before finishing them with filing, sanding and polishing techniques. Along the way, our tutors will share tips and tricks, patiently guiding you so you feel confident every step of the way.

By the end of the session, you’ll have crafted two sterling silver rings and two copper or brass rings, and if time allows, you can make even more!

Each ring you make is completely your own, whether you keep them sleek and simple or experiment with texture and pattern. You’ll leave not only with a stylish, wearable ring stack, but also with the joy of having made something truly unique with your own hands.

This class is perfect for beginners, groups of friends, or visitors wanting a memorable creative experience. Many students find jewellery making a wonderfully mindful activity - slowing down, working with their hands and enjoying the calming rhythm of making.

Your class fee includes copper and brass for practice, sterling silver for two rings, plus all consumables such as solder, sandpaper and polishing materials. Extra silver and other metals are available for purchase in the studio if you’d like to expand your collection.

Children aged 12 and up are welcome, though anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

description:
Star Sense: Find Your Way by the Stars, Learn the ancient art of celestial navigation under one of the world’s best night skies.

This Summer of Space, Star Safari invites you to rediscover something humanity once knew instinctively — how to read the night sky as a living map.

Under Wairarapa’s internationally celebrated dark skies (featured by Lonely Planet as one of the world’s top stargazing destinations), you’ll learn how explorers, navigators, and storytellers used the stars to orient themselves, travel across oceans, understand seasons, and pass knowledge through generations.

Guided by Hari Mogoșanu — TEDx speaker, former NASA intern, and creator of the planetarium film Ngā Tohunga Whakatere — you’ll gain practical, confidence-building skills in southern-sky star-literacy:

You’ll learn how to:
- Find south using stars and sky geometry
- Identify the key constellations of the summer sky
- Trace the Milky Way and understand its structure
- Read seasonal sky patterns and stellar motion
- Tell planets from stars
- Navigate using asterisms and star-hops
- See the sky through multiple cultural perspectives
- Understand dark-sky ethics and the importance of gentle lighting

This experience focuses on unaided stargazing — learning to understand the sky with your own eyes. By the end of the night, you’ll be able to step outside, recognise what you see, and use the stars to find direction anywhere in the world.

What’s included:
Guided instruction, southern-sky star map, orientation techniques, constellation recognition, navigation principles, cultural stories, dark-sky awareness, Q&A.

Recommended age: 10+
Duration: 2.5 hours

Come and learn the ancient skill of sky navigation — and leave with a deeper sense of place in the cosmos.

Star Sense. Find Your Way by the Stars.

Welcome to the Philosophy In The Park Summer Series !

Each session takes a different shape—sometimes small-group conversations, sometimes a single open circle—but all are rooted in the Socratic Method: asking questions, listening carefully, and thinking together rather than trading speeches or debating winners and losers.

Discussions can be on everything from Politics to Pop Music, Ideology to Identity, Markets to Marxism, Feminism to Faith, Aesthetics to Anarchy, Capitalism to Consciousness and beyond...

In the spirit of “Philosophy in the Public Sphere,” the group is open to everyone. No academic background required—just an open mind, a willingness to ask questions, and respect for different perspectives.

This short course is the perfect introduction for complete beginners, guiding you step-by-step through the essential techniques used by jewellers. You’ll start by working in copper or brass, building confidence as you learn to cut, heat, shape and texture metal. From there, you can choose to move into silver and bring your ideas to life in more refined pieces.

A beautiful textured ring band is an ideal first project, but once you’ve mastered the basics, the possibilities really open up—create earrings, pendants, or small bespoke pieces that reflect your personal style. You’ll learn how to solder using a jeweller’s torch, refine your finishing techniques, and polish your work to a professional shine. It’s a hands-on, deeply satisfying process, and there’s nothing quite like wearing something you’ve made yourself.

These Sunday sessions are also perfect for returning students and more experienced makers who want dedicated studio time, guidance on more ambitious projects, and the chance to be part of a friendly, creative community.

Materials are purchased as you go, so you can tailor your projects to your budget and ideas. Beginners typically spend around $50–$70 on metals over the course.

description:
T-Rescue Training, Key objective of the session is: to train other people in carrying out T rescues in mildly rough water
The expectation is that the trainer is the person in the water and the trainee is in the kayak cockpit so the trainee is warm for most of the session. Only at the end will we ask the trainee to fall out and be rescued, and that's voluntary so that they can have that experience to inform their own ability to rescue others.
Key areas of focus:
Managing the swimmer around the kayak
Lifting the kayak onto the spraydeck � ideally we would have some weight in the bow so that this is hard
Holding the kayak on edge to support the other boat � this is the single item that people have most trouble with
Safety
No need to run safety in protected water but in the rough water we will reserve one trainer for safety

Towing

description:
Te Reo Māori - Intensive Wananga, An opportunity for beginners, or those with a little te reo, to take part in an intensive language and cultural experience.

Description
Te Reo Māori - Intensive Wānanga
Course is free for NZ citizens and residents (please bring photo ID when attending workshop). If you are not a NZ citizen or resident a fee of $120 will apply, please phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

During this one-day workshop we’ll use as much te reo as possible to immerse you in the language and introduce you to te ao Māori (the Māori world), its language, culture and traditions.

The wananga is aimed at those who are new to te reo or who have attended a basic course already but would like a refresher and a one-day intensive experience.

Please bring kai to share at lunchtime.

By the end of the day, you will:
- Be introduced to the Māori spiritual and natural worlds and our important connection to them (mana whenua and manu atua)
- Be able to identify and connect with underlying Māori values and customs such as tikanga, manaakitanga, whanaungatanga and whakapapa
- Have participated in singing group waiata and understand its cultural function
- Be able to identify the sounds of Māori letters and pronounce important letter combinations correctly (whakahua)


NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable. This is a stand-alone course and will not qualify as a pre-requisite for the Intro 2 Te Reo.

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Prerequisites
For beginners or those who may have completed the Introductory 1 course and are looking for a refresher course.

description:
Te Reo Māori - Introductory 2, For those who have completed Te Reo Māori - Introductory 1 recently or have equivalent knowledge. [Please see the Te Reo Māori - Introductory 1 course description for an indication of what is covered]. Course fees: If you are a NZ citizen or hold a NZ Resident/Permanent Resident Visa the course fee is $99 (evidence of eligibility required). If you are here on a Work Visa/Working Holiday Visa the course fee is $189.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Discuss our responsibilities as a bi-cultural nation under ‘Te Tiriti o Waitangi’ and identify underlying Māori values such as: whanaungatanga, pepehā and tikanga
- Discuss the significance of whakapapa as a fundamental Māori world view and confidently describe your family and relationships through this lens
- Form simple sentences to describe parts of your face and body
- Discuss protocol on the marae
- Recognise the importance and use of karakia and be able to recite one correctly
- Recognise the cultural values inherent within different whakataukī (proverbs) and kīwaha (idioms) and be able to correctly recite one of each

Prerequisites
For those who have completed an Introductory 1 course, or equivalent. Note: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and for statistical purposes, some additional information is required as part of the enrolment process.

description:
TechWomen and AWS - Career Mindset Workshop: Own Your Energy, Kick off 2026 with a transformative mindset experience that will enable you to set and execute the right intentions for your career throughout 2026 and beyond.
The TechWomen and AWS teams invite you to begin the year with a special mindset workshop designed for women in tech, hosted by Candice Murray, a leading NZ based career mindset coach. In this interactive session, you'll choose a positive emotional state you want to strengthen - whether it's calm, confidence, self-belief, or focus - and learn practical, evidence-based techniques to access it whenever you need it most.

description:
Telescope Mastery, Our Telescope Course is back!

You already own a telescope, but...

If you already have a telescope and would like to learn more about how to use it, how to collimate it and any other maintenance they need, what type of eyepieces are the best to buy and any other equipment.

BRING YOUR TELESCOPE ALONG!
OR

You don't have a telescope, but...

would like to learn how to use one, don't fret! We have 14, and you can learn all about them.

Your instructor:
Sam, our resident astrophysicist.

Sam is skilled in explaining the intricacies of telescope operation and makes learning both accessible and engaging. Our course offers hands-on experience with our diverse collection of 14 telescopes, ranging from classic reflectors to sophisticated refractors and versatile catadioptrics.

Where: Star Safari Observatory - 10 minutes from Martinborough


There's no "but" after our course. You'll know exactly:

- Where to start?

- What to do?

- How to get the best out of your telescope?

- What must you consider if you wish to plunge into deep-sky astrophotography?

You get:
A collimation cap - no more guesswork on how to collimate your telescope. With this tool, you can keep your telescope sharp.

Tea and coffee - refreshments.

Bring your lunch and a picnic blanket! We have a spectacular setting at Star Safari Observatory, and we will stop for a lunch break to enjoy our Moon garden and the surroundings.

Take the giant leap; reach for the stars!

At the end of the course, you'll learn all about the types of telescopes available and mounts, attachments, and eyepieces. We cover the whole lot. We have been using telescopes for a long time and now have an excellent range for our public sessions and at our home observatory.

We're not affiliated with retailers, so our advice is unbiased and based on our years of experience with lugging telescopes around the world, maintaining them and using them.

description:
Textured Bracelets - New Class!, This fast and fun workshop is ideal for beginners, but experienced students are also welcome to come make their own bangle!

Students will practice making a simple textured or polished bracelet in either copper or brass using heavy-gauge wire, then move on to making a 3mm wide flat silver bracelet from start to finish. They will learn measuring, texturing, soldering, and finishing techniques to make a personalised beautiful and wearable bracelet.

Students can choose their textures or stamps - this is perfect for stamping names and dates, lines of poetry, or giving a hammered, beaten finish. It's all up to you!

More experienced students may wish to make a wider bracelet using flat strip or extra bangles in silver wire. There will be a cost for extra silver wider metal, but the basic silver allowance is included in the course fee.

This is a taster class aimed at either providing a fun experience with a great result, or an excellent place to begin absorbing basic jewellery techniques for those wanting to pick up the activity.

The expected outcome for students is one bracelet in copper or brass and one bracelet in sterling silver. Additional bracelets can be made should time and the group's needs allow.

Course fee includes materials for the basic project.

Extra materials are available to purchase in the workshop or you can upgrade your silver to a wider strip.
label: Classes & Workshops

description:
Textured Bracelets - Taster Class, This lively, hands-on workshop is designed for complete beginners, but it’s also a great opportunity for more experienced students to enjoy a creative session making their own unique bangle!
Everyone will leave with a beautifully finished bracelet of their own preferred texture.
We’ll begin by experimenting on a sample strip of copper, where you’ll practice creating textures using hammers, punches and stamps. Once you’re confident you’ll move on to your main project: a 3mm wide flat strip bracelet in either sterling silver or copper, crafted entirely by you from start to finish. Along the way, you’ll learn essential jewellery making skills including measuring, texturing, soldering, shaping, and finishing.
Students are free to personalise their bangle with textures or stamped designs. This could be a simple hammered finish, decorative patterns, or meaningful words, names, dates, or poetry lines - making your bracelet truly one of a kind.
Beginners will work with the 3mm strip provided, ensuring a rewarding project that’s manageable to complete. Wider metal is much harder to form and solder, so we are learning to walk before we can run
Copper is included in the course fee, if you wish to work in silver you can purchase it on the day.
Experienced students may choose to challenge themselves by making a wider bracelet from flat strip or by creating additional bangles in silver wire. (Please note: extra silver for wider bangles is available to purchase at the workshop for experienced students only, and let us know if you wish to go wider so we can make sure we have the strip in stock).
This workshop is a taster class: perfect for anyone seeking a fun, creative experience with a beautiful result, or for those looking to dip their toes into jewellery making and build foundational skills.
SPECIAL PRICE $115.

description:
Textured Pendants and Earrings - Taster, This quick, creative taster class is perfect for a fun outing with friends, a thoughtful gift-making session, or a treat just for you.

In just three hours, you’ll learn to craft a stunning pair of textured metal earrings from scratch. You’ll be guided step-by-step through heating and texturing the metal, then cutting and shaping it with traditional jewellery tools. By the end, you’ll have a beautiful pair of earrings to wear proudly or gift to someone you care about!

You will practice on smaller texture samples to work out what texture and what metal you want to go with, and then move on to creating your earrings in warm copper or yellow brass.

Your class materials pack includes everything you need for the class to make a super cool pair of shiny gorgeous earrings.
Using copper and brass as our main material allows us to have more creative fun and create larger earrings with less expense.

We do have a lovely range of sterling silver sheets that you can purchase as extra if you are committed to working in silver!

description:
Textured Rings - Welcome Spring!, Make your own personalised ring - a gift for yourself or someone special! :-)

Learn the basic technique first in copper or brass, and then craft your final piece in silver!

Over this taster class, you’ll be guided through the process of heating and texturing metal, cutting and shaping with traditional jewellery tools. Use feathers, leaves, or fabrics to create a unique texture for a beautiful ring!

Learn to measure your finger, cut metal to length and texture it without rolling mill, hammers and punches. Then use a jewellers torch, sandpaper and polishing, and your beautiful new ring will be ready to wear.

This 3-hour class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends and visitors to the city.

Included in the class fee are copper and brass for practising on, a sterling silver ring strip and all consumables such as sandpaper, solder and chemicals. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

Kids aged 12 (or so) are welcome to attend the class, but any person under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

description:
The "Other" Curriculum Roadshow - WELLINGTON, Multiple Choice: Wellington Screening and Education Discussion
Join the Aotearoa Educators Collective (AEC) for a pivotal evening of discussion focused on the future of education with colleagues in Wellington. We are proud to host a screening of the compelling documentary, Multiple Choice - see the trailer here.
This film explores the profound and often challenging impacts of high-stakes, standardised testing on students, teachers, and the entire education system. Following the screening, we will open up a vital conversation about how we assess, Curriculum reform, and celebrating what is great about what we are doing now in Aotearoa New Zealand.
Your Voice Matters
This event is a crucial opportunity for educators, policymakers, parents, and community members to engage directly with key issues shaping our local schools and kura. We aim to:
Spark informed discussion about the role of assessment and qualifications.
Reflect on the implications for the ongoing redevelopment of the New Zealand Curriculum, national testing, and NCEA.
Encourage collaboration across our sector to reimagine equitable, future-focused pathways for all learners.
The Event Plan
Come together for a social networking event and evening of insight, hosted at St Patrick’s College.
The event will include:
A screening of the documentary Multiple Choice (approx. 1 hour).
A dynamic DRAFT Panel Discussion featuring a mix of local and national leaders:
Panel Convenor - Mark Potter | Principal of Berhampore School
Ragne Maxwell | Principal of Porirua College
Lynda Knight | Principal of Glenview Primary School
An Audience Q&A to foster broad community dialogue.
This is your chance to connect with peers and contribute your perspective to the national conversation. Secure your spot today!

The Anatomy of a Portrait with Nicola Jackson, Join artist Nicola Jackson for a masterclass exploring techniques and influences in her approach to portraiture. Nicola uses paper mâché, anatomical illustrations and vibrant colours to create unique and identifiable works. description:
The Art of Mending - Micro Mill, When it comes to the clothes we love, every rip, stain, and imperfection is an invitation to exercise agency, expression, and an opportunity to show the garment how much we appreciate it.

This class is cared for by the whimsical Aisha, a multidisciplinary artist with a passion for empowering the mending process. Each month on Wednesday evenings Aisha will introduce us to a different technique for reviving our beloved textile pieces. If you're like us and have a box of clothing in need of repairs that never seems to empty... this is the club for you. With three events a month we'll inspire each other to creatively care for those pieces we love! This club is also perfect for anyone who loves learning new skills. Techniques we'll cover are lino printing, patching, darning, felting, embroidery, beading, sashiko, fabric painting and more! All materials and tools are supplied at each class - but you are welcome to bring your own. We highly encourage bringing those clothes or other textile items that need some love and repair.

There is no need to attend every class. We can catch you up on the skill at which ever class you choose to join us at. There are single class tickets or monthly sign ups available. Both of these have variable pricing options, unwaged/student, waged, and generous. Please choose whichever option feels right for you and your circumstances!

In August we are Lino Printing!
Class 02: 20th August
At this class Aisha will take us through the process of designing and cutting our own lino to print with! You're welcome to keep going with the pre cut designs as well. Lino and carving tools will be supplied.

Class 03: 27th August
This class will be open to what you want to work on! Bring in larger project items, print with the lino cuts you made in the previous week, or cut some fresh ones!

In September we are patching!
Class 01: 10th September
Aisha will take us through the process of sewing on patches. Patches that we printed in the August classes will be available for this. You're welcome to bring your own patches as well. Please bring something that needs a patch up or a little bit of decoration.

Class 02: 17th September
At this class we will learn how to appliqué, the process of using scrap fabric to make decorative patches. This is a great way to elevate a rip or stain with some visible mending.

Class 03: 24th September
At this last class of the month we'll be open for all the patching needs. Hang out and finish projects we've started or mend some extra items.

Be sure to check our website or here for updates about techniques coming up in the following months.

description:
The Bible Course, The Bible can feel big, complex, or hard to navigate, but it doesn’t have to. This winter, St John’s in the City is hosting The Bible Course, an eight‑week journey that helps you see how the whole story of Scripture fits together and why it matters for life today.

This is the first time The Bible Course has been run in New Zealand, and we’re delighted to partner with Bible Society NZ as their pilot group ahead of a national launch during Bible Month in July. Over 140,000 people in the UK have already taken part, finding it accessible, engaging, and confidence‑building.

Whether you’ve read the Bible for years or are just beginning to explore Christian faith, you’re warmly invited.

Each Sunday evening includes:
- A shared meal to begin the night together
- Childcare for preschool and primary-aged children
- A 20‑minute video teaching session
- Time in small groups to talk, ask questions, and explore the themes
- A physical guidebook to use throughout the course (optional purchase: $10)

Spaces are limited, registration is essential

These will be like-minded whiskies going head to head, but as we know, often these are the most informative comparisons, casting a light on the subtle nuances of cask, age and distillery style. Cadenhead's Enigma 'Speyside Single Malt' 16 years old 53.6% (Manzanilla Hogsheads)
GlenAllachie 'PX Hogshead Single Cask' 2012 / 12 years old #1029 58.3%

description:
The Curl Next Door with Anthony Bayer WELLINGTON, Anthony Bayer is an Auckland-based stylist who’s made his mark at New York Fashion Week and in top NZ and Australian editorials. Known for his approachable teaching style, he’s all about helping stylists find their unique style and gain confidence.
Join Anthony Bayer for an immersive look and learn workshop focused on the artistry of curly hair. This session will equip you with the skills to create styles that celebrate natural curls.
We'll explore three dynamic techniques: "The Heidi" for sculpting long, defined curls; "The Tori" for shaping the effortlessly chic French Curly Bob; and "The Emma" for crafting bold, textured Curly Pixies. Each technique brings a unique vibe, reflecting the individuality of clients.
Throughout the workshop, we'll also discuss curl care, styling techniques, and how to use color to enhance the natural beauty of curls. Perfect for stylists eager to expand their expertise and deliver exceptional, personalised curly hair results.

description:
The Digital Minefield: AI, Misinformation, and Detox, Are you feeling overwhelmed by the non-stop flood of AI headlines, viral deepfakes, and notifications on your phone? The Digital Minefield: AI, Misinformation, and Detox is a practical, engaging workshop designed to give you a deeper understanding of the modern digital world, building your confidence to engage with the technology and know how to put it down. (NZ citizens and residents free with ID, others pay $120.)


Description

Together, workshop participants will demystify how artificial intelligence actually works, acknowledge some of the harms of this new technology, learn about the characteristics of mis/disinformation, build resilience against fake news, and explore why our brains weren’t built for the infinite scroll. You will walk away from the workshop with a better understanding of the hidden forces shaping your screen, equipped with real-world tools to cut through the digital noise.

Dr. Andrew Chen is a leading New Zealand specialist at the intersection of digital technology ethics and public policy. With a PhD from the University of Auckland in Computer Systems Engineering, Andrew brings a deep technical understanding and applies it towards systemic issues and interventions. With extensive experience advising public agencies and private companies on governing emerging technologies, Dr. Chen translates complex technical concepts into clear, accessible insights for the community. He is passionate about helping people understand technology's societal impacts, and thinking more deeply about what’s happening behind the scenes, so we can all navigate today’s complex digital landscape.

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

This course is free for NZ citizens and residents. Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.

If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

description:
The Four Pillars of Excellence™ Workshop, How to Move Forward When Life Feels Too Much

This is the first in-person Zammtopia workshop, designed to give you something practical, thoughtful, and immediately usable in your daily life.

If you have been moving from one demand to the next, holding a great deal and rarely getting a moment to hear yourself think, this workshop was made with you in mind.

It offers more than a breather. It gives you a space to stop, reflect, and recognise how much of your energy has been going into everything and everyone else. And it gives you a way to use some of that time and energy for yourself — to sort through what is happening, and learn how to carry the load and care for yourself better.

After the workshop, you will leave with a practical tool you can use immediately — one that helps you manage your load more clearly and begin putting some of your energy back into yourself.

And for those two hours, the workshop itself becomes part of that shift: a space set aside for you to pause, reflect, and acknowledge how much of your energy has been spent elsewhere. It is a chance to spend some of that energy on yourself, in a way that helps you carry life better and care for yourself better, too.

Limited Seats. Intimate Setting. Optimal Learning.

description:
The Joy of Improvisation, Discover your creative potential and enjoy improvising scenes and stories in a safe, positive group environment with the Wellington Improvisation Troupe [WIT].

Description
Improv is theatre without a script and a fun way to build your skills in many areas, including team work, public speaking, storytelling and on-your-feet creative thinking.

This is the perfect place for absolute beginners to get acquainted with the joy and art of improvisation, inspired by the generous creative philosophy of Keith Johnstone. It's also a great place to get back into improv if you've been away from it for a while.

WIT has been teaching this course in association with the CEC for almost 20 years now. It uses fun games and structured exercises to teach the foundation skills of improv. These are a prerequisite for further courses and membership of WIT (www.wit.org.nz), as well as useful in themselves.

If you have questions about the course, please contact WIT directly on info@wit.org.nz.

By the end of the course, you'll have:

- Explored basic principles of improvisation
- Enjoyed interacting in a friendly, positive and supportive environment
- Developed more confidence, presentation and communication skills
- Experienced joyful moments of improvisation

The course will end with a directed demonstration of class exercises for invited friends and family.
