description:
The Power of Slowing Down - meditation course, The Power of Slowing Down - meditation course
The Power of Slowing Down - meditation course
with Kadam Birgit

It seems fair to say that we’re in a distraction crisis these days.
Or perhaps you’ve been too distracted to notice.
The world seems to be (is!) moving ever and ever faster, throwing more and more things into our path.
And our natural instinct is to move just as fast in order to keep up. And good luck with that.

Buddha is a b-i-g fan of the Slow Down Movement.

When we slow down in meditation, for example, we give ourselves the chance to absorb.
When we slow down in daily life, we give ourselves the chance to respond to people, events, thoughts, etc. with wisdom and empathy.
We regain crucial control over our own mind and our own actions. If you feel that your world is slipping out of your control, please join us for some teachings on Buddha’s advice for how to shift into a lower gear, in life and in meditation.

Everyone is welcome.

WHAT TO EXPECT
These classes are based on Buddha’s teachings on the mind, but you do not need to be a Buddhist to attend, or to benefit from them. There is no physical exercise involved and you can choose to sit either in a chair or on a cushion. These classes are suitable for all levels of experience.

Registration starts at 9:30am. This course includes a vegan, wheat-free morning tea (we cannot guarantee gluten-free).

description:
The World of Ikebana - Tension and the Beauty of Space, Have you ever heard of Ikebana, the Japanese art of flower arrangement?

With a history spanning over 1,400 years, Ikebana is far more than decorative floral design. It is a refined art form that expresses space, balance, seasonality, and life itself. Today, Ikebana is internationally recognised and practiced by enthusiasts around the world.

Through careful techniques such as proper water preparation and pruning, flowers can be enjoyed for weeks, subtly changing their appearance over time.
This event invites you to explore the history, philosophy, and aesthetics of Ikebana, followed by a hands-on workshop where you can experience the art firsthand.
By engaging with flowers, space, and silence, participants are encouraged to sense the changing seasons and reflect on the essence of life.

Part I: Lecture & Demonstration, Q&A
Part II: Workshop

description:
The Write Way: A Smooth Introduction to Fountain Pens, Curious about fountain pens but not sure where to start?

Join Andrea Darbyshire for a low stress introduction to the joy and elegance of fountain pens.

In this informative, 45 minute session she will cover:

- The main types of modern fountain pen and their parts
- How to fill a pen: bottled inks, cartridges and converters
- Cleaning and care for you investment
- Ink & Paper: welcome to the rabbit-hole!

We will have a sample set of Esterbrook pens that you can try, fitted with the standard nib sizes: Extra Fine, Fine, Medium, Broad and 1.1 Stub. While our sample set is exclusively Esterbrook, everything you learn in the session will apply to almost any other modern fountain pen on the market.

BONUS: Purchase an Esterbrook fountain pen at the NZ Stationery Show and we'll credit your $25 course fee toward your new pen. Sorry, we can't credit the Eventfinda fees.

This is an absolute beginners class. No experience necessary, just bring along your curiosity. Suitable for left and right handers.

About your teacher:
Owner of more than a hundred modern and vintage fountain pens, you’re in experienced hands with Andrea Darbyshire. Her appreciation for fine writing instruments goes beyond collecting, Andrea also delights in sharing her knowledge with others and connecting with fellow enthusiasts. She is a regular at the Wellington Fountain Pen Meetup. By day, Andrea is the Cataloguer & Metadata Librarian at Masterton Library, where her love of ink and paper naturally complements her passion for books and learning. When she isn’t isn't busy inking a new pen, you’ll likely find her working deftly with a pair of knitting needles, creating something beautiful one stitch at a time.

Presented as part of The New Zealand Stationery Festival. Your ticket to this event does not include access to the Stationery Festival. Please purchase a ticket for The New Zealand Stationery Festival separately.

description:
Thriving As a Nation of Readers: Strengthening Reading Communities, As part of NZ Children’s Book Week 2026, Te Awhi Rito Reading Ambassador Kate De Goldi will chair a Panel session on why reading for pleasure matters and why strengthening our school reading communities is so important.

Having the skill to read is much more powerful when it’s paired with the will to read. Reading for pleasure is the foundation for full literacy. It builds vocabulary, knowledge, critical thinking and imaginative power.

It also develops an understanding of self and others and contributes to wellbeing. However, in Aotearoa New Zealand there is a steady decline in the numbers of young people reading for pleasure.

Join us at this free event where the panel will explore the current reading landscape. They will discuss the ways schools, libraries, families and whānau, and other organisations can collaborate to build reading communities that support and inspire life-long reading for pleasure.

The event is for educators, librarians, researchers, and anyone interested in engaging young readers.

This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
Cultivating true resilience is an intentional practice of the mind, body, and soul. It is rooted in deep self-knowledge and personal empowerment. In our rapidly changing world, the ultimate question we must ask ourselves is: How can I unlock my unique strengths and capacities to not just survive these demanding times, but truly thrive?
By implementing a "living" practice of mindful strategies, creative expression, and physical awareness, we can empower our thinking, elevate our emotional well-being, and bring a renewed vitality to our life's work.
What to Expect
This workshop offers you a rich tapestry of practical tools, storytelling, and collaborative discussion. Together, we will explore diverse pathways to foster courage, helping you shift from a state of survival to one of thriving—even while navigating the daily pressures of stress, grief, anxiety, or the fear of an uncertain future.
What You Will Take Away:
Mindful Strategies: Daily, actionable practices to anchor your thoughts and reduce overwhelm.
Creative & Physical Outlets: Expressive tools to release tension and process complex emotions.
A Personal Roadmap: A clearer understanding of your innate strengths to help you navigate future transitions with confidence.
Details & What to Bring:
Duration: Full-day workshop
What to bring: A personal journal and your favourite pen or pencil. (However, paper and pen will be provided if you need).
Step out of the survival loop. Join us to reclaim your inner strength and cultivate the courage to thrive.

description:
Titanium Earrings - Wellington, In this super-fast 3-hour class, you will make a pair of earrings fit for a superhero!
Titanium is an amazingly light metal that can transform from a subtle grey to a whole range of super vibrant, or sleek and pale colours, from gold, pink, purple or deep blue, to light blue, palest green and subtle grey.
You’ll begin by practising fundamental metalworking techniques on copper, then experiment with flame-colouring titanium to understand how heat transforms its surface. With these skills, you’ll craft your own earrings, exploring texture and colour.
We’ll use a rolling mill to imprint natural or abstract patterns into the titanium sheet, shaping pieces into clean geometric forms—rectangles, diamonds, triangles, or squares. You can also experiment with layering elements for added depth and variation.
Finish your design with a choice of comfortable hooks or hoops, and leave with a unique, wearable piece.
Titanium is hypoallergenic, and your findings options include surgical stainless steel and gold-plated stainless steel.
You should take this class:
- If you like large earrings that are bold and badass
- If you like earrings to be feather light
- If you like colourful earrings that will really make a statement
- If you like pastel blues and simple shapes
- If you love earrings and want to try something new
- If you’re curious to learn more about using Titanium in your jewellery making - this is an ideal way to dip your toes.
The course fee $135.
Kids aged 12 (or so) are welcome to attend the class, but an enrolled parent or caregiver must accompany anyone under the age of 16.

description:
Toi Art Saturdays: Guided Slow Looking (FREE), Take a closer look. Join free, student-led sessions that invite slow looking, reflection, and thoughtful conversation around art.
Going to a gallery can sometimes feel a bit overwhelming with so much to see – on average, people spend less than 30 seconds viewing a work of art!
At these relaxed sessions, local high school students will guide you in slow looking. This is an approach gaining traction around the world that invites us to linger and look closely, letting our responses unfold. You’ll make your own discoveries and create your own meanings, with some discussion and fun along the way.
Each session will begin by looking at Traffic Cop Bay by Bill Hammond, followed by another surprise artwork. No two sessions will be the same!
No booking required. Meet at the session start time on level 5 in the Toi Art galleries – we'll be waiting in the reading space at the top of the main stairs.

Torch Fired Enamels - 4 Weeks course, This is a 4 week's block focusing on beautiful glass enamels on copper and silver using the Torch Fired Glass Enamel technique. It is a wonderful way to add colour to your work! The course starts on Sun 4 October and runs for 4 weeks until 25 October, 10am-1pm.

Beginners to jewellery work can use pre-formed shapes to apply their enamels to so they can focus on creating an excellent result. They will be shown how to apply textures and small alterations to the pieces using either hammers or roll printed textures before prepping the metal for the glass enamel.

Those with some metalwork experience can take on a more advanced piece, exploring more complex techniques such as cloisonne.

High quality silver findings are supplied for one to two projects and more are available to purchase if required.

Sterling silver chains are also available if you want to complete the finish of a pendant.

Build your foundational jewellery making skill with this deep dive into enamel technique!

Beginners and advanced students are welcome.

description:
Vocal Blokes Over the Hill and Still Singing, Wellington Vocal Blokes return to Greytown
– Older, Bolder, and Still Singing
Greytown, you asked for an encore — and we couldn’t resist.
Wellington’s Vocal Blokes are crossing the Remutakas once again for a full day of music, laughter, and good company on Saturday, 22 November.
Our concert last year was such a hit that we’ve decided to do it all again — only bigger and better. This time we’re adding two singing workshops led by our young and inspiring music director Paddy Shanahan, before rounding the day off with the 4:30 pm concert Over the Hill and Still Singing at the St Andrews Union Church Hall.
Workshop 1: Finding Your Voice (11:30 – 1:00 pm)
Think you “can’t sing”? Paddy Shanahan would disagree.
In this light-hearted session, he’ll show how singing is really just “talking on pitch.” Starting with Reviewing the Situation from Oliver!, you’ll discover how expression and rhythm turn everyday speech into music. No solos, no pressure — just an easy, encouraging space to let your voice come alive.
Workshop 2: Singing Together (2:00 – 3:30 pm)
Once you’ve warmed up, it’s time to build harmony.
Drawing inspiration from Jacob Collier’s version of Coldplay’s Fix You, Paddy will guide the group in shaping simple “oohs” into rich, layered sound. It’s less about perfection and more about listening, blending, and feeling the joy of shared music.
If you take part in this second workshop, you’ll also be invited to join the Vocal Blokes on stage for one song at the afternoon concert — a true “community choir” moment.
Workshops cost just $20 each or $35 for both, and if you enrol for both you get free entry to the concert.
The Concert – Over the Hill and Still Singing
At 4:30 pm, the St Andrews Hall doors open for a concert that promises to be every bit as joyful as last year’s — maybe even more. Over the Hill and Still Singing is a playful nod to our journey from Wellington to Greytown and to the fact that most of us are, well, not exactly in our twenties anymore.
But that’s the beauty of it — we sing for the sheer love of it. Expect songs about travel, friendship, and meeting new people, all delivered with our trademark mix of heart and humour.
We love performing for Greytown audiences because you listen, laugh, and sing along in all the right places. There’s something special about this town — the warmth, the curiosity, the way the hall fills with energy before the first note.
Come Join the Chorus
So whether you’re a shower-soloist, a closet crooner, or simply someone who enjoys good company and great music, come spend the day with us.
Bring your voice, bring a friend, and rediscover how good it feels to sing together.
Workshops at 11:30 am and 2:00 pm.
Concert at 4:30 pm — St Andrews Union Church Hall.
Because being Over the Hill just means you’ve found a better view.

description:
Voices from the Moana: Amplifying Pacific stories of healing and resilience, Talanoa Tai Learning is a new collection of learning experiences. They're designed to help you build your cultural responsiveness and improve your ability to engage meaningfully with Pacific communities. Talanoa is a Paciﬁc style of deep dialogue, with a focus on how we connect to each other and strengthen relationships, while still being able to share honest and eﬀective insights. Tai refers to ocean waters, which represent your opportunity to rise through the ebb and ﬂow of this learning journey. If you want to strengthen your capability in this space, to create transformational change, and to enhance your relationships with people from diﬀerent communities - this workshop is your chance to grow.
What will I gain from Voices from the Moana?
In Voices from the Moana, you will explore and share rich narratives of healing and resilience from different Pacific nations and perspectives. The Pacific ocean is a diverse place and we have our own unique stories of healing through traditional practices, beliefs and methods. This Talanoa Tai learning experience invites reflection on your own understanding of different healing modalities from the Pacific and the impact it has on your worldview. It will equip you to advocate for social justice through Pacific voices. You'll gain practical tolls and insights that you can apply directly to your work.
This is a 3 hour in-person learning experience.
Who is this workshop for?
These learning experiences are for both Paciﬁc professionals and those from other communities. You don’t need to have prior knowledge or experience in this area - we’ll meet you where you are and provide a welcoming, supportive environment for you to learn.
Cultural responsiveness is for everyone. Whether you’re in social work, education, government, community sectors or beyond, these learning experiences have been designed to help everyone build their skills. If you think this professional development might be right for you, it is!
Cost
When work is busy and budgets are tight, cultural responsiveness can often take a backseat. But this is an aﬀordable investment that will help you address the challenges that so many of us share, like how to build engagement and trust, and avoid relationship missteps. It’s not a buzzword; it’s a vital skill if you want to better meet the needs of the people you serve. Price: $170 (inc GST) per person, including morning tea.
 Facilitator
Our team’s extensive research and experience feed into these sessions, with a focus on interactive activities and practical, real-life examples. Our team has decades of experience across a range of ﬁelds, in particular social development, education, and research. We have worked with organisations and businesses across the Paciﬁc, and our engagement with diﬀerent Paciﬁc languages, cultures, and communities means we oﬀer robust, informed perspectives. Fa’aeafale’upolu (Polu) Samuelu is the facilitator of this Talanoa Tai Learning experience.

description:
WIDance Open Classes term 4., Come dance with us!
Join the WIDance team as we slide, bounce, wiggle, roll, and dance our way into Term 4, 2025!
Whether you’re a seasoned dancer or just starting out, our classes are designed to be accessible, engaging, and fun for everyone.
Our classes offer a safe and inclusive space to find joy, laughter, and creative expression through contemporary dance, improvisation, dance-based games, and composition. Through Movement, we build body and space awareness, confidence, and connection.
Open Class
Our open class has been running for 15 years and is a vibrant, welcoming space where dancers of all experience levels come together to move, create, and express themselves. Each session blends technique, improvisation, and choreography, giving you room to explore your own rhythm and creativity.
This year, our technique work now includes exercises from Stopgap Dance Company’s UK-based IRIS syllabus — an inclusive, dynamic approach that supports strength, awareness, and artistry for everybody.
"IRIS is an inclusive dance syllabus that gives teachers a framework to develop the disabled dancers of tomorrow. It is a consolidation of Stopgap’s experience of training professional disabled dancers, and it contains tried and tested methods that the company has been developing since 1995.
IRIS is divided into four levels: Include, Respond, Integrate and Specialise, each having its own set exercises, guidelines and assessments. IRIS will give disabled children and young people the same level of structure, balance and rigour of dance education as their non-disabled peers and provide the opportunity to accumulate skills and experiences necessary for the professional industry".
Term 4 runs for 6 weeks, on the following dates:
Saturdays: 11 am to 1 pm , 8th November to 13th December.
Cost: $120 waged. $85 unwaged. casual $20 per class
New option: Technique class only, 11am to 12pm, $60.

Who are we?
WIDance is one of Wellington's leading dance providers for disabled and non disabled dancers, striving to provide equal opportunities for all to dance. Established in 2010, we run open classes, workshops, and performance events throughout the Wellington region.
Our mission is to provide equal opportunities to dance experiences for diverse communities, advocating for access and empowerment

We are holding a free workshop for Early Childhood Education Centres in Carterton to come together to discuss your emergency plans.

description:
Wankernomics — Just Touching Base, At work, do you struggle with simple tasks like using the phrase “circle back” in every email? Have you never used the word “synergies” in a LinkedIn post? You might be a failure at office life and need a pep talk. Luckily, some Australian satirists have a solution. ‘Wankernomics — Just Touching Base’ live at The Opera House reveals the secret to workplace success through the ancient art of being annoying.   
The shows are hilarious and include many ‘oh-my-god-that’s-exactly-what-happens-at-my-workplace’ moments. You’ll get a demonstration of the buzzwords, bureaucracy, banality, and baloney of modern working life. You’ll get tips on how to speak at work, how to look like a genius in meetings, and how to get promoted by simply dropping the phrase ‘360 degree all-hands ideation session’ into an email to your boss. 
So, pop some time in the diary for an outcomes-focused, value-added, best-practice, deep-dive into the realities of the working world.

description:
Water Cast Pendants Taster - Spring, This is a super quick 3-hour session, and is great fun to do with family or friends.

Water casting is a really hands-on low-tech casting method that results in surprising and fun little forms that can be turned into pendants with amazing textures and shapes.

You will be guided through melting silver and pouring it into water to create little charms.

Experiment with pouring at different heights to create different shapes.
Choose one or a few of your favourites to have drilled and turn into simple pendants or earrings, or new charms for your bracelets!

We will use hardened jump rings to attach your water-cast pieces to either colourful cord or you can choose sterling silver chains which you can purchase for extra.

The technique will be demonstrated with important health and safety practices, then students will be guided to do at least a couple of casts, and should expect to have at least one successful item to clean up and finish in the class.

A basic amount of metal allowance of a small amount of silver is included in your course costs, and if your projects go over that amount you can pay for the metal you use on the day via internet banking or cash.

This course is open to complete beginners and advanced makers. Extra materials such as chains and findings are available to purchase.

For health and safety reasons class participants must wear sturdy, closed toe shoes and have their hair tied back.

description:
We are not one people: From Parihaka to a Pākehā myth, On the morning of the 5th November 1881, an Irishman called Andrew Gilhooly formed up alongside other members of the Armed Constabulary at the entrance to Parihaka pā; he was there for the invasion, the occupation and — much later — for the farming of land taken from Taranaki iwi.

But those events dropped out of the family stories handed down to Gilhooly’s descendants; neither do they feature in national narratives of fairness, egalitarianism and equal treatment.

In this presentation, Richard Shaw, one of Gilhooly’s descendants, will explore the relationship between historical amnesia amongst (some) descendants of settler families and the stories we tell each other of the nation we live in.

Wednesday Morning Jewellery-making In 8 Weeks, This NEW block of morning classes is the best way for beginners to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. It will run from Wednesday 17 September for 8 weeks until Wednesday 5 November from 10am - 12.30pm.

This class is mixed level, allowing beginners to work alongside advanced students.

Beginners start with basic ring making in copper or brass, students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering.

Then we move on to making a practice ring set with a cabochon stone (cabochon means it has a flat bottom and a smooth domed top).

Once your first setting is completed you can move to working in silver and produce another stone set ring with more interesting design elements.

Level 2 students explore chainmaking as a way to develop their fine soldering skills. Their silver project can be a pendant on a handmade chain or a piece of their own design.

Level 3 and above students are encouraged to work on their design skills and try new and challenging techniques.

Included in the class fee are:
Beginners: a materials pack that includes copper and brass for practising on, 2 gemstones and enough sterling and fine silver to complete the cabochon ring project.
Advanced: students receive a generous credit to spend on materials as they choose. All consumables such as sandpaper, solder and chemicals are also included. Extra metals and materials are available for purchase in the studio.

Description: My journey from banks to BioTechs
  About John Robson:
JR is the Managing Director of cell therapy company, BioOra Limited. BioOra addresses both access and scale issues by providing an affordable and accelerated pathway to market for CAR-T therapies via lower cost, high throughput, GMP licensed manufacturing capabilities from clinical trial through to registration and commercialisation.
 JR is also the General Manager of Bridgewest Ventures in New Zealand, and he holds an executive position within the Bridgewest Group, a San Diego based privately held investment company that focuses on disrupting industries through innovation and with investment assets in excess of US$4 billion, and JR is responsible for the deep tech investment programme in New Zealand.

description:
Why there are two biological sexes and what this doesn't mean, Arguments about the number of sexes have recently become heated, part of the culture wars of the twenty-first century. But what do biologists mean by male and female? The standard definition is surprisingly simple: male means making small gametes (sperm); female means making large gametes (eggs). Nevertheless, some biologists are unhappy with this view, arguing that dispensing with it would both lead to better science and support progressive social change.
I argue, along with philosopher of biology Paul Griffiths, that such a move would be a grave scientific error. It would deprive biology of one of its most powerful tools for explaining biological diversity. I give several examples of the utility of the standard definition in evolutionary biology, such as an explanation for why there are, in fact, just two sexes, and how different characteristics become associated with different sexes in different species.
I then identify some of the errors the critics make. Most notably, they assume that the scientific value of sexual categories depends on females sharing some essence of femaleness (and similarly for males). But this “essentialist” approach is rejected by evolutionary biologists, since it plays no role in the models that explain the evolution of sexes and sex-associated phenotypes. Moreover, the concept of biological sex is critical for understanding the evolution of the human reproductive system and why humans differ from other species.
It is important to realize that the standard definition of sex does not imply that there are just two sorts of (human) individuals. Because sex is different from “sex roles”, gender and cultural practices, I also point out that biological sex is no constraint on human diversity.
Finally, I note that keeping the standard biological definition of sex does not mean that (i) gender is binary, (ii) gender is biologically determined or (iii) scientists have not used sexist language and stereotypical concepts.
In short, this talk aims to help us to navigate a knotty problem of our time.
Biography
Hamish Spencer is Emeritus Sesquicentennial Distinguished Professor in the Department of Zoology at the University of Otago. Educated at the University of Auckland and Harvard University, he has broad research interests ranging from modelling genetic changes in human, animal and plant populations to using molecular-genetic methods to study the evolution of flora and fauna. In collaboration with historians, he has written about eugenics, first-cousin marriage and Robert FitzRoy.
In 2009, Hamish was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand and in 2016 won the Society’s Callaghan Medal for science communication. That same year he was appointed Science Advisor at MBIE, a position he held for five years. He was awarded a James Cook Research Fellowship by the Royal Society Te Apārangi in 2022 and was elected a Fellow of the International Science Council in 2023.

“Relationships are all there is. Everything in the universe only exists because it is in relationship to everything else. Nothing exists in isolation. We have to stop pretending we are individuals that can go it alone.” -Margaret J. Wheatley
You aren't alone. In a world of screens, finding genuine, in-person connection can feel surprisingly tough. But building a supportive network and circles doesn't require a total personality makeover—it starts with who you already are.
This hands-on, high-energy workshop is designed to help you map out your unique strengths, passions, and existing ties to build a community where you truly belong. We skip the generic networking advice and dive straight into practical, real-world tools to help you spark meaningful relationships.
What you’ll walk away with:
Your Personal Connection Map: A clear overview of your unique interests, strengths, and hidden community links.
The "Icebreaker" Blueprint: 1–2 simple frameworks to confidently shift casual small talk into deeper, more rewarding conversations.
The "Reach Out" Breakthrough: Break the ice right then and there by sending two messages or writing a letter during the session—getting the hardest part out of the way!
A Ready-to-Use Action Plan: A customised roadmap to connect with 1–3 new or existing friends, with your first milestone already crushed before you leave.
"Networking is not about just connecting people. It's about connecting people with people, people with ideas, and people with opportunities." — Michele Jennae
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. description:
Women's Krav Maga Self Defence - Intro Night, We believe every woman should feel strong, fearless and confident for life. Krav Maga has proven to be highly empowering for women all around the world. We offer this course to women to learn to deal with women-related challenges, encouraging every woman to overcome anxiety or fear, with confidence, skills, strength.
In an ideal world, women would not need to learn to protect themselves. However, until some deeply ingrained societal problems are resolved, it is smart and necessary to have some skills to be able to look after yourself and loved ones with. In the meantime, we encourage every women to approach this training with personal development, personal growth, enjoyment and empowerment being the motivating purpose.
We understand women often prefer to train in a women's class. This is our Women's (13+) class called ROAR.
Beginning in 2018, this program was created to provide a safe, holistic and supportive class where women can experience empowerment through training. You will learn to find your voice, inner strength and resolve, while learning physical skills such as how to escape and overpower an assailant, counter grabs, abduction attempts, chokes, hair grabs, pushing and shoving, being hit, being pinned to the ground and sexual assault attempts. We will help you unleash your protective feminine fighting spirit.

description:
Women's MINDSET Self-Defence Workshop - Wellington, Women's MINDSET Self-Defence Workshop - Wellington
Our women's workshop is probably the most intense, comprehensive, enjoyable & hands-on self-defence syllabus in New Zealand & Australia.

About this Event

The workshop is rated R13 so only those aged 13 and above can attend due to the content taught. There are a limited amount of spaces available so book early.

Don't let the price deceive you; we're firm believers that every woman and family deserves the opportunity to participate in workshops like this without having to break the bank.

So, what sort of things can you expect to learn at this workshop?

You learn the vital parts of the body - parts of the body that are vulnerable & easy to attack.
Learn how to block an attack confidently.
Learn how to defend yourself against slaps, punches, pushes & grabs.
Learn to defend yourself against headlocks, hair grabbing, and wrist grabs.
Learn how to defend yourself against chokeholds, and bear hugs.
Learn how to defend yourself on the ground.
Learn effective rape defence techniques.
Learn how to use your hands, legs, knees & elbows as weapons.
Learn to defend yourself against many other types of attacks with confidence.

Plus, lots, lots more. (depending on the time allowed & the participant's progression)
What we teach is how to deal with the worst-case scenario, when the awareness, avoidance and de-escalation have failed, it all turns physical, there's no obvious way to escape & you must fight back.

"... a massive shout out to Charlie Riley for all the amazing work he does. Charlie, you are a champion among champions. Thank you. Ladies, if you loved #reebokunleashed or if you missed out, please check out Charlie and find a course near you."
Zoe Bell - Hollywood Stunt Woman, Actress & Producer

This is the sixteenth year that we've been running our women's workshop for the community in New Zealand and this is the second year in Australia. All you need to take with you is a positive attitude, comfortable clothing, a drinks bottle & towel plus something to eat during the breaks. Please note that the workshop takes people out of their comfort zone & can be both physically & mentally demanding at times if unsure seek your doctor's advice before undertaking any form of physical training or have a word with the instructor.

description:
Working With Colour workshop, Working With Colour workshop
This workshop is about mixing colour to produce satisfying and exciting colour combinations in your paintings. We will work with top quality GOLDEN acrylics, and you will learn about how to achieve overall colour harmony in your work. We will also cover working with complimentary colours, ‘loud and quiet’ colours and our personal colour cravings. The workshop will be more about practice than theory, although special attention will be given to colour value (its place on a grey scale) and chroma (brightness). You will also learn about the pigment realities that are often neglected in theory-based colour teaching, in other words, pigment selection for the cleanest and brightest possible mixes. The morning will concentrate on developing your own personal palette and by the afternoon you will be using this palette in an abstract painting inspired by the exciting dance-like colour works of Chinese artist Mimi Chen Ting. We will also take inspiration from the colour works of well-known NZ master colourist Sandy Adsett. Class numbers are limited to 6 and the day is suitable for beginners to art as well as experienced painters. Cost: $180

About this Event

Join us for a relaxed, whānau-friendly cyanotype / printing workshop led by exhibiting artist Claudia Jowitt.
Inspired by her exhibition Uana / Carried by the Waves, this hands-on session invites tamariki and adults to play with light, water, and natural materials while learning the simple, magical process of cyanotype printing.
Cyanotype is a sunlight-based printing technique that produces striking blue images. With Claudia’s guidance, you’ll arrange flowers, leaves and other natural shapes—echoing the motifs that flow through Uana — and watch your prints develop before your eyes
.Open to all ages and experience levels, this workshop is a fun, creative moment for the whole whānau. description:
Workshops with Jethro: Social Big Apple, Sugarfoot Stomp is excited to offer two Social Big Apple Workshops with guest facilitator, Jethro!
Jethro has been travelling, studying, experimenting and teaching Social Big Apples for years now and there's so much he wants to share about this dance. The fundamentals, a ton of brand new tricks, and for the advanced dancers - he'll be teaching how to call so you can keep doing social apples! The first session is open Level. The second requires good experience with swing outs.
The Social Big Apple (aka swing rueda) is an extremely fun way to explore, learn and teach Lindy Hop. But mostly, it's just a fantastic game to play at social dances. So if you want to join the party, this workshop will give you everything you need to have a crack when they spontaneously erupt at the next swing event.

*Why is the Social Big Apple key for Lindy Hoppers?*
With roots dating way back, even before Lindy Hop (earliest recording is from 1840), African American churches held Ring Shouts. Everyone danced in a circle, slowly making their way around. As people shuffled and stomped and shouted, African rhythms like the call and response was a part of the dance. If you have ever been to a dance that had a caller, (like casino rueda, square dance, ceili) this tradition likely came from these African American communities and the Ring Shout.
Later in the 40s, the Big Apple craze swept through America. A circle of dancers had a caller, calling out charleston and swing moves/sequences that everyone did in unison. Frankie Manning heard about it over the phone which is when he choreographed the Big Apple routine that we still do today.
*Class Details:*

Saturday, 1 November.

Workshop 1 | 1:00 pm – 2:30 pm (doors open at 12:50 pm)
Workshop 2 | 2:45pm – 4:15 pm

Workshop 1. Open Level. This class is an intro to the fundamentals of called, Social Big Apples. All you need to know is the 6 and 8 count basics, plus a couple of beginner moves. Intermediate and advanced dancers that join this class will also be challenged with added variations and the chance to learn to be a "Caller"

description:
You Spot It You Got It: Unpacking cultural conditioning and turning the mirror inwards, Talanoa Tai Learning is a new collection of learning experiences. They're designed to help you build your cultural responsiveness and improve your ability to engage meaningfully with Pacific communities. Talanoa is a Pacific style of deep dialogue, with a focus on how we connect to each other and strengthen relationships, while still being able to share honest and effective insights. If you want to strengthen your capability in this space, to create transformational change, and to enhance your relationships with people from different communities - this workshop is your chance to grow.
What will I gain from You Spot It, You Got It?
In You Spot It, You Got It, you will deepen self-awareness by being encouraged to recognise some of your own conditioning and impacts of this in your daily life/practices. When we are not conscious of the things that might not sit right within us then we unknowingly or knowingly project them onto others. What we reject, we project. By examining patterns and recognising our conditioning, then we can truly understand how we can live in more conscious ways. This Talanoa Tai learning experience offers space for talanoa, tools and exercises to facilitate introspection and personal growth by turning the mirror inwards.
This is a 3.5 hour in-person learning experience. The day will start with a mihi whakatau to welcome you into the space.
Who is this workshop for?
These learning experiences are for both Paciﬁc professionals and those from other communities. You don’t need to have prior knowledge or experience in this area - we’ll meet you where you are and provide a welcoming, supportive environment for you to learn.
Cultural responsiveness is for everyone. Whether you’re in social work, education, government, community sectors or beyond, these learning experiences have been designed to help everyone build their skills. If you think this professional development might be right for you, it is!
Cost
When work is busy and budgets are tight, cultural responsiveness can often take a backseat. But this is an aﬀordable investment that will help you address the challenges that so many of us share, like how to build engagement and trust, and avoid relationship missteps. It’s not a buzzword; it’s a vital skill if you want to better meet the needs of the people you serve. Price: $170 (inc GST) per person, including morning tea.
Facilitator
Our team’s extensive research and experience feed into these sessions, with a focus on interactive activities and practical, real-life examples. Our team has decades of experience across a range of ﬁelds, in particular social development, education, and research. We have worked with organisations and businesses across the Paciﬁc, and our engagement with diﬀerent Paciﬁc languages, cultures, and communities means we oﬀer robust, informed perspectives. Fa’aeafale’upolu (Polu) Samuelu is the facilitator of this Talanoa Tai Learning experience.

description:
Your Life's Purpose - Discover Your Emotional Needs, Your Life’s Purpose – Discover Your Emotional Needs and Core Values
. (NZ Citizens and residents pay $49 with ID, all others pay $120).

Ask the big question – what is the ‘Why’ of your life? Reflect on your emotional needs. Learn how to identify an overarching purpose and a wider meaning that is larger than yourself. Work with your personal values to develop a life purpose statement and goals that can guide how you live, work and play.

Put in the hard work on this one day Saturday workshop and experience the benefits of self-knowledge. Let the emotional knowledge you gain inform not only how you live your life but also how you feel about living it. You’ll be asking the big questions about not only how you live your life, but also why. Discover the tools and scientifically-based information to inform the exploration of your life’s purpose.

Consider your emotional needs and how they relate to personal meaning. You’ll unwrap the concepts of emotional nutrition and be shown how to be guided by your values and start to think of them as a compass directing the journey of your life. To do this you’ll identify your values hierarchy and learn about how this framework can inform how you live your life. Once you can apply a spirit of consistency to your self-identified larger purpose, as well as your needs, then your life’s purpose, emotional needs and core values, will align. It’s quite a transformational day!

Bring pen and paper. Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch/snacks.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:

Develop a Life Purpose Statement
Perform an Emotional Needs Self-Assessment
Elicit Your Core Values
Align your goals with your life purpose, emotional needs and core values

Zentangle® Method - Beginners, Zentangle® Method - Beginners
The Zentangle® method is an easy-to-learn, relaxing and fun method to create amazing images by drawing structured patterns.
In this course you will learn to make beautiful art, following the 8 steps of the Zentangle® method from a certified Zentangle teacher.
Discover your creative side, even if you think you don’t have one. You might surprise yourself!  If you can hold a pen, you can do this.
Creating Zentangle patterns is super relaxing and a creative form of mindfulness. Increase your awareness and focus, get absorbed and feel more confident while making your own unique and original art.
Learn about borders, strings, and shading. Learn your first tangles and discover the world of Crescent Moon, Hollibaugh, Printemps, and Florz. It feels great to have creativity flowing. Anything is possible one stroke at a time. There are no mistakes to make here!
After a step-by-step introduction you will take home your amazing images and have discovered a new way to relax.
All art materials are included in course fee.  Tea and coffee is available but please bring your lunch/snacks.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
-    follow the 8 steps of the Zentangle® method.
-    make beautiful structured black and white drawings.
-    explain why creating Zentangle patterns is a relaxing form of creative mindfulness.

During the first 2 classes, beginner students will complete a variety of putiputi (flowers).

We provide harakeke for you if it is your FIRST class and we will teach you how to harvest for yourself during this time and what to harvest for your next class.

After that, if you would like us to harvest for you, purchase the add-on - "Please harvest for me" for an additional fee.

Moving forward, you will start making kōnae (2 corner kete - basket), kono (4-sided kete), tapawhāroa and more.

- Develop your pūkenga (practical skills)

Our kaiako will have made it clear to you when you can advance to this level from beginners.

If you are new to Ōtari but have experience please reach out before committing.

Projects are planned in advance of each wānanga to help us move forward together as a rōpū and awhi one another while working on similar taonga.
Please check your emails beforehand so you know what to bring.

Waenganui Wānanga are an important step toward joining our Tuakana Rōpū, who will often be attending these wānanga.
While they work on their own taonga projects, they are a valuable source of support for learners—happy to kōrero, share advice, and offer inspiration along the way.

Projects may include new closes for your kete timata, kete waikawa, puritanga, pīkau and pōtae.
We will teach you preparation, preservation and storage of harakeke - important especially over winter months. Additionally, we will induct you to the Ōtari Pā Harakeke when ready.

With regular attendance, you will deepen the mātauranga gained from beginner classes and share your learnings with others. (Refer to below for a reminder)

What’s included in your intermediate ticket?
- Three+ hours weaving class with our tuakana weavers and raranga rangatira.
- Limited access to tools, as you are expected to have your own kete mahi (tool kit).
- You are expected to bring your own harakeke.
- We encourage you to harvest for yourself, but if you are unable to harvest for class, we have ‘Please harvest for me’ options in addition to your ticket at least three days before class.
- Light refreshments are provided, and we encourage you to bring kai to share

- Waenganui Rōpū are expected to harvest for themselves, but if something unexpected pops up we have add-on services available during the ticketing process. A minimum of 3 days notice is required.

- At our discretion, tickets are fully refundable or transferable.
- If class numbers are too low, we may have to cancel (and will offer a refund or transfer), so please check your emails before class.
- We offer concession tickets for students, unwaged, seniors, and those with disabilities.
- It is important to us that our classes are accessible to all. If ticket costs are a barrier for you, please visit our website to enquire about our reduced-cost or free tickets.

description:
Ōtari Raranga Weavers - Raranga for my Valentine, Otari Raranga Weavers – Te Rā o te Aroha
Weaving Gifts from the Heart – A Valentine’s Day Celebration

With the support of Wellington City Council, Wellington Gardens, and the Ōtari team, Otari Raranga Weavers warmly invite you to Te Rā o te Aroha – Weaving Gifts from the Heart.

Set against the beauty of Ōtari Wilton’s Bush, we gather to share mātauranga Māori through traditional weaving and healing practices, guided by the rhythms of nature and the taonga of our ngahere. Our kaupapa is rooted in connection—honouring aroha, nurturing creativity, and bringing our local community together in a spirit of learning and togetherness. For this special Valentine’s wānanga, you will create putiputi (flower) bouquets to gift to your nearest and dearest. We will provide whakakano (dyed) harakeke to add colour, vibrancy, and personal expression to your weaving.

Two classes available:
• 11:00 am – 2:00 pm
• 2:30 pm – 5:30 pm
(Places are limited and high interest is expected for our first sessions of the year)


No experience required – all levels are welcome

Please arrive on time for karakia (opening blessing)

Raranga for sale - A range of woven taonga will be available to purchase. Cash or bank transfer accepted.

Drop-in welcome:
Feel free to pop in anytime during the day to see what we’re up to, connect with our weavers, and purchase heartfelt gifts.

Kai & Manaakitanga - Rongoā (Māori healing) tea and light refreshments will be provided. We’ll also have snacks on the table, and you’re welcome to bring a plate or baking to share.

Whānau friendly - Children under 14 must be accompanied by an adult with a ticket.

Stay connected - Follow us on Facebook & Instagram: Otari Raranga Weavers

www.otariraranga.co.nz

Tūngia te ururua kia tupu whakaritorito te tupu o te harakeke.
Set the overgrown bush alight and the new flax shoots will spring up.

description:
🩷 Dance for Kanan: 24-Hour Dance-A-Thon Fundraiser 🩷, 🩷 Dance for Kanan: 24-Hour Dance-A-Thon Fundraiser 🩷
***NEW DATE***
Join us for an unforgettable 24 hours of movement, music, and magic as we come together to raise funds for our beloved Kanan’s unfunded breast cancer treatment.

Last month, Kanan received the shock of her life when she was diagnosed with HER2 positive breast cancer, an aggressive sub-type of breast cancer that can spread and grow rapidly. Unfortunately, the targeted treatment isn't funded, and Kanan is looking at costs of approx $35,000-$40,000.

This is more than just a dance event — it’s a celebration of her community, strength, and the power of showing up.

We’ve rallied an insanely talented team of 20+ dance professionals, each donating their time and energy to teach a class. From hip hop to heels, contemporary to line-dancing — there’s something for everyone.

Thanks to the generosity of Hannah from Sweet Studios, we’ll be dancing non-stop on the Kapiti Coast, and we want YOU to be part of it!

💃 4 Ways to Join the Movement:

🕚 Mini Movers (5 hours, Year 1-4)
Take on the mini challenge by getting sponsored while you learn some new styles of dance and how to present yourself on a stage!

🕛 Half-Day Hero (12 Hours, Year 5 - Year 8)
Get sponsored for every hour you dance — rally your supporters and groove for a cause. Can be done individually or split between a group!

🕘 Full-Day Fighter (24 Hours, Year 9+)
Take on the full 24-hour challenge and let your sponsors pledge per hour. Every step helps Kanan get closer to healing. Recommended todo this as a group!

🩰 Drop-In Diva ($25/class)
Choose any class that speaks to your soul and join us for just $25. No strings, just good vibes.

Register here: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfEhUtS2rawbqzFrAQUDKtrjTZAG2e4iXZuwDMZCzWWS3B3Gw/viewform?usp=sharing&ouid=103696675397207234907

Let’s dance with purpose. Let’s dance for Kanan. 💕

Follow this page for the full class schedule, teacher lineup, and donation links, all coming soon!

Tag your dance crew, share the love, and let’s make this a night (and day!) to remember.

If you would like to make a donation that is not in relation to this event we have a givealittle page to go towards medical treatment!

As part of the wider Wellington Heritage Festival, this 2-hour author-led walking tour of the CBD guides you through highlights from the new Te Papa Press book, 'Capital Trees'. ABOUT THE BIG BASH

First held in 2020, Orchestra Wellington's Big Bash is an annual mass play-in event which brings together hundreds of instrumentalists from across the Wellington region in a glorious afternoon of music-making.

Conducted by Orchestra Wellington's Music Director Marc Taddei, together we will rehearse then perform a selection of much-loved works. This year's repertoire includes Tchaikovsky's Romeo & Juliet Fantasy Overture and 1812 Overture!

Anyone is welcome to come along and watch both the rehearsal and the performance entirely for FREE. Rehearsal runs from 1-3pm with the concert starting at 3:30pm.

FOR PARTICIPANTS:
There are some important things to note before you arrive for this year's Big Bash:

👉 Location: Lower Hutt Events Centre at 30c Laings Road, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010.

👉 Timings: Please arrive no later than 12:45pm. Rehearsal runs from 1-3pm, then a short break before our free concert for community, family, and friends at 3:30pm.

description:
A Change Is Coming Walk Tour, 2026 marks the 40th anniversary of the passing 1986 of the Homosexual Law Reform Act. The legislation set out to decriminalise homosexual activity between consenting adults and make it illegal to discriminate against someone based on their sexual orientation.

But this wasn’t the first attempt at homosexual law reform. Join us on this special 90-minute free walk tour to celebrate the people and movements that fought for a brighter future for rainbow communities.

Our journey begins at the location of the first public meeting in New Zealand, advocating for homosexual law reform in 1967. This was two years before the Stonewall uprising in the U.S., which went on to ignite Gay Liberation around the world.

The tour ends at Parliament, where we honour the Members of Parliament who have championed equality over the last five decades.

Along the way, we’ll reflect on some of the difficult realities rainbow communities have faced, from the injustices of the legal system, to the stances of the medical profession, churches and the military. As the late activist Ralph Knowles recalls, “As far as medicine was concerned, it was sick. As far as the law was concerned, it was a crime. As far as the church was concerned, it was a sin.”

Though at times the stories are challenging, this walk tour is ultimately uplifting, as we pay tribute to our amazing rainbow kaumatua and allies who led the way.

description:
ANZAC Day - 2026 Open Day, NEWS RELEASE :
FOR IMMEDIATE USE - April 2026
ANZAC DAY - OPEN DAY- SATURDAY 25th April: 10AM - 4PM.
Wellington’s historic Wrights Hill Fortress in Karori is open for public inspection again on ANZAC Day, SATURDAY, April 25th. The World War Two coastal battery first opened to the public in 1989 and will be accessible between 10am - 4pm.
On ANZAC Day people are invited to self-guide themselves through the tunnels and gun emplacements. The walk usually takes about one hour. Bring a torch with you for some fun!
Visitors will be able to explore the 620 metres of underground tunnels with a free map and history pamphlet. They will see the engine room, shell stores, plotting rooms and the huge gun pit where Gun Number 1 used to stand, as well as a replica of the 10-metre-long gun barrel.
Also on show will be historic photos, and a DVD of how a 9.2-inch gun operates will be showing as well. The World War Two Fortress will also have period themed displays. It’s only open to the public on four Open Days a year.
Wrights Hill Fortress was built from 1942 to protect Wellington from Japanese bombardment. In the early 1960’s, the guns were cut up for scrap and sold, ironically, to the Japanese.
Admission is $20 for a family of two adults and three children under 15, or $10 per adult and $5 per child. (Sorry no EFTPOS -CASH ONLY) Access is via Karori Road, Campbell Street, and Wrights Hill Road. All proceeds go to the continuing restoration of the Fortress. There is limited car parking at the summit of Wrights Hill. Please Park sensibly and use walking tracks.
Visitors to the Fortress in Wrights Hill Reserve can also enjoy picnic sites and panoramic views from the top of the hill. There will be a BBQ sausage sizzle and soft drinks on sale. For safety reasons no jandals please.

description:
Adopt a Plant: Begonia House Fundraiser, Support the Friends of Wellington Botanic Garden and grab yourself a bargain. We’ve kept the plants we need for propagation, but we have healthy plants left over that we can’t fit into our nursery. That’s where you come in – take home one of our plants and help the Friends fundraise to go beyond the basics with amazing new features like exterior landscaping and internal fixtures for the renewed Begonia House.
These plants are from the display end and thrive in indoor conditions (they are coming from a glasshouse after all). They should do just fine in your house. Have too many house plants? Wrong. You can definitely fit just one more. It’s for charity after all.
We’ll have some available for loose change and others for a minimum donation that won’t break the bank. Payment by cash or bank transfer only (no EFTPOS). All proceeds go to the Friends of Wellington Botanic Garden to put towards the Begonia House enhancements http://givealittle.co.nz/.../the-begonia-house-the....
Get prepped:
- Share the love! 3 plants max per person.
- Plants come as they are – we practice integrated pest management but you may need to give them a quarantine before joining your other plant pals at home.
- Swap your pot – there will be a station where you’ll swap your plant to a different pot. We need all our A+ pots for our future plants. We’ll be around to help.
- BYOB – bring your own bag or box for transporting your new friend home.
- Early bird gets the plant – no holds.
We’ll post an update in our Facebook event page a few days out of what plants will be for sale. Make sure you RSVP to get notified.

An Evening for Palestine, An Evening for Palestine
Please come along to a fundraiser evening to benefit The UN's Occupied Palestinian Territory Humanitarian (OPT) Fund. The fund supports NGO's and UN partner organisations on the frontline of the humanitarian crisis in Gaza - more information here https://crisisrelief.un.org/en/

It's an opportunity to give back and to share kai, and spend time with community. We have immense privilege in Aotearoa, and cooking and sharing food is a way that feels important (to me - Nicole) as a way to bring people together for a good cause, in the face of what often feels like endless global and local injustice, oppression and catastrophe.

All ticket sales from this fundraiser will go to the OPT Fund, to support the people most in need when they need it.

Included in the ticket sales are:
-a three course family style meal (menu released closer to the date, vegetarian and vegan option)
-tunes from some of Wellington's local musicians
-discounted beverages on the bar (with sales going directly to the Fund)

Invite your friends! Bring your colleagues!
Tickets here: https://events.humanitix.com/an-evening-for-palestine

Doors open 5:30, music from 6, dinner from 7.

We're currently sourcing donations from local sponsors to make the event possible. If you would like to participate, get in touch.

An Evening with Dr Hinemoa Elder, Nau mai, haere mai! Join us for this very special event to meet Dr Hinemoa Elder and hear all about her latest book, Ara: A Māori guidebook of the mind, published by Penguin NZ.
Dr Hinemoa Elder will talk about chapters in Ara, and how she has delved into a unique exploration of how to think about thinking, rooted in the wisdom of Māori culture.
In Ara, Dr Hinemoa Elder introduces us to a profound journey guided by Hinengaro, Māori goddess of the mind, leading us through 23 specific rua, caves, into the unfamiliar depths of Papatūānuku, our earth mother, and back to the surface again.
Hinengaro offers us a dedicated path to gather insights, face challenges and help us navigate the complexities of our minds.
Hinemoa will be signing books.

In 2025 (YES I KNOW I’M LATE THIS YEAR) we're celebrating;
My 34th Birthday.
A DECADE living in Aotearoa New Zealand.
My new side hustle/hobby/passion, where I managed to produce 34 shows (actually wtf.)
Doing stand up for the first, second, third, and fourth time ever.
Rufus’ life, and his newly evolved form.
Finally biting the bullet on moving to the UK and announcing my resignation at work (effective in feb but whatever we’re counting it.)
This Anne Day I’m doing something a bit different - while I’m still accepting/exceptionally keen on receiving haikus and bawdy limericks as gifts, what I really want is support getting myself and Sexy Ghost Boy to Australia. But I, always a giver, am not just going to ask for your money with nothing in it for you.

And so? Anne-Themed-Fundraiser-Quiz-Night.

Brush up on New Zealand politics, Josip Broz (Tito)’s Yugoslavia, The Rocky Horror Picture Show, Kākāpō biology, and the History of Rufus. There will be prizes! 

Important details
Tickets $10+bf each, but any additional koha appreciated <3 
Teams of 4-6, feel free to bring +1s and +mores that I don’t know. 
Can’t make it but still want to send some aroha my way? Donate direct to the fundraiser here:  https://www.thearts.co.nz/boosted/projects/sexy-ghost-boy-goes-to-australia

description:
Art Therapy for Well-Being: A Canvas for Self-Discovery, Bypass the mental loops and discover a new language for healing. Join us for a one-day creative journey to quiet the mind, release stress, and unlock a powerful pathway to self-compassion—no art experience required. (NZ citizens and residents free with ID, all others pay $120).

Art Therapy for Well-Being: A Canvas for Self-Discovery

This course is free for NZ citizens and residents. Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.

If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

Sometimes, our minds get stuck in habitual thought loops—endlessly cycling through the same worries, fears, and anxieties without ever finding a breakthrough. When words fall short, art therapy offers a different language. By shifting from thinking to creating, we bypass the noise of everyday stress and tap into an intuitive visual language that can surprise us with fresh insights, new perspectives, and profound meaning.

This workshop is a gentle, immersive introduction to a pathway of self-restoration, self-compassion, and self-worth—the vital foundations for true self-healing.

What you will experience:

A Shift in Perspective: Break free from repetitive thinking by engaging the creative, intuitive side of your brain.
Tools for Daily Coping: Learn how the simple act of making art can become a sanctuary for processing stress and finding grounding.
A Pathway to Wholeness: Explore how visual expression can reveal hidden strengths and foster a deeper sense of self-care.
Important Note: You do absolutely not need to be an artist or have any artistic experience to attend. This day is about the process of expression, not the final product. While this workshop is not a substitute for clinical individual or group therapy, it is a powerful, supportive introduction to the healing power of the arts.

What to Bring:

A journal and a pen or pencil. All other creative materials will be provided. Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch and snacks and photo ID.

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

description:
Art and AI: Brit Bunkley in Conversation with Megan Dunn, Art and AI: Brit Bunkley in Conversation with Megan Dunn
Artist and filmmaker Brit Bunkley discusses the pragmatics and politics of making art with AI. Join us for a discussion in the Gallery, with insights into the making of his latest work Archive, commissioned for Messengers.

--

Brit Bunkley is a New Zealand-based artist and videographer whose practice spans sculpture, installation, and digital media. A recipient of the US National Endowment for the Arts fellowship, two NY state grants, and the Rome Prize Fellowship, his work explores the intersection of physical and virtual spaces, often blending surreal imagery with themes of history, politics, and environmental concerns. He has exhibited at the Museum of New Zealand Te Papa and internationally at Rencontres Internationales Paris/Berlin, FILE São Paulo (including 2025), and the Athens Digital Arts Festival. Recent exhibitions include Visions in the Nunnery, London (2022), Cybersculpture 2024 at Collège des Bernardins, Paris, and The Torrance Art Museum, LA (2025). In 2024, he won Best Art | Experimental Video/Film at the New York City Independent Film Festival. His work continues to evolve, embracing new technologies and alternative methodologies to challenge perceptions of reality and imagination.

Learn more here > https://citygallery.org.nz/events/art-and-ai-brit-bunkley-in-conversation-with-megan-dunn/

IMAGE Brit Bunkley, still from Archive, single channel video, 2025

description:
Asia After Five: Experiences in Taiwan, About the event
The Asia New Zealand Foundation and the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office Wellington are hosting an evening of stories and insights from New Zealanders who have studied, worked and lived in Taiwan. Hear from the Foundation's Leadership Network members and Taiwan alumni as they share their experiences and reflect on future opportunities for Kiwis in Taiwan.
Our Asia After Five events are interactive. You will have a chance to ask questions, network with others and learn more about Asia.
Event details
Date:  Thursday 25 September 2025
Time:  5:30pm-7:00pm
Venue:  Asia New Zealand Foundation, Level 16, Fujitsu Tower, 141 The Terrace (access to building via Cable Car Lane before 6pm)
This event is free to attend, but please RSVP for catering purposes.
This event is a collaboration between the Asia New Zealand Foundation Te Whītau Tūhono and Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in New Zealand (TECO).
Our speakers
Ema Kato
Ema Kato is a recent graduate from Victoria University of Wellington with a degree in Communication, specialising in intercultural communication and Mandarin. Having lived in Japan, Taiwan and New Zealand, Ema is passionate about cross-cultural exchange and will return to Taiwan next year to pursue advanced language study and a master’s program at National Taiwan University with the Huayu and Taiwan Scholarships.
Tom Durkin
Tom is currently based in Auckland, working in Private Wealth at Craigs Investment Partners. Having studied Mandarin as a part of his degree at the University of Otago, he has long held an interest in Chinese language and culture. Tom spent two months travelling in Taiwan at the end of 2023. During this time, he joined parts of the Taipei Hui with the Asia New Zealand Foundation Leadership Network, worked with a farmer in Chiayi and spent two weeks at Fo Guang Shan Buddhist monastery in Southern Taiwan. His participation in the recent Shanghai Hui with the Asia New Zealand Leadership Network sparked a desire to re-engage and immerse in Chinese culture. Tom has recently been accepted to study at the National Taiwan Normal University - Mandarin Training Center from later this year. He's looking forward to sharing his experiences and hearing more on others' perspectives of the New Zealand-Taiwan relationship.
Lauren Pattermore
Lauren Pattemore is an early-career journalist based in New Zealand, with contributions to Stuff, the Otago Daily Times, Crux and Radio New Zealand. She recently completed a media internship with the Asia New Zealand Foundation in Taipei, working with TaiwanPlus. In 2024, she was named runner-up for Best Up and Coming Journalist at the Voyager Media Awards. She holds a Bachelor of Communication from Massey University, where she specialised in expressive arts and journalism.
Rob Eland
Rob was the sole New Zealand recipient of the Taipei City Chinese Learning Scholarship in 2018, selected by Mayor Justin Lester. With the scholarship, he took a sabbatical from work and travelled to Taipei, where he lived from mid-2018 to early 2019. During this time, Rob studied full-immersion Chinese at NTNU's Mandarin Training Center (MTC) and took part in several New Zealand–Taiwan cross-cultural activities, including supporting then-Deputy Mayor Jill Day and a group of New Zealand performing arts students during their visit to Taiwan. Rob returned to New Zealand in 2019, but he looks forward to heading back to Taiwan again soon.

description:
Authentic Dating Wellington, Authentic Dating Wellington
“Thank you so much for creating a space in which such well-aligned people could come together. I can't think of the last time I met so many wonderful, open-minded people in one go like that. It was a real pleasure” - John


Tired of endless scrolling?


Over the superficiality of app culture?


Ready to connect with real people and talk about what truly matters?


Here’s your chance take a break from the apps and connect more openly and authentically with those both like-minded and different. After a long break, it's returning to Wellington this February for Valentine's weekend!


You’ll have several encounters throughout the night. Each will be carefully guided, inviting you to be yourself, to communicate openly, and and explore multiples layers and flavours of connection. Come spark a new summer flame! 🔥


Authentic Dating welcomes all men, women & non-binary people aged 18+, both monogamous & non-monogamous. We will aim to pair you with a gender different from your own.


Is this event for me?

If you are seeking....

✨ Deep & meaningful conversations without small talky chit-chat

✨ Exciting new connections, both romantic & platonic

✨ An opportunity to explore & challenge your assumptions

✨ A substance-free environment

✨ Playful & sincere communication activities

✨ Skills you can apply to your dating life beyond the event

✨ A space to simply be yourself

....then this event is for you!


What will actually happen? 🥰

You will be invited to explore four unique interactions, some of which are randomised and some of which you can choose. Each will involve a new set of instructions to help you communicate about topics that really matter to you.

Each interaction will last 10-15 minutes. At the end of each interaction, you will have the opportunity to share a contact detail on a piece of paper in a way that is both cute and discrete ~ please bring your own pen!

Consent is important: you always have the agency to choose how deep you go. You will never be forced to share information that you don't want to.


Why are tickets sold by gender? 👫

To ensure that the gender balance is as even as possible, it is important to keep track of how many men/women/non-binary people are signing up. If a particular gender is over-represented in the run-up to the event, we do our best to ensure that under-represented gender(s) also sign up.

While we aim to achieve an even balance of genders (and ages), this is not always possible. However, what is guaranteed are skills that you can apply to any connection. Simply come with an open mind and ready to connect.


The facilitator 💁‍♂️

Laurie King

I'm Laurie (he/him), a queer British-Kiwi who’s current home-base is Berlin. My passion is creating spaces that cultivate healthy, thriving human-to-human relationships, helping people take off their masks, feel their sensations and celebrate their aliveness on Earth. Since 2019, I have organised and facilitated hundreds of Authentic Relating, Dating and Embodiment workshops in Oceania and Europe.

My training includes The Embody Lab, Authentic Revolution, Body Electric, Connection Institute and World Peace Yoga School. I have facilitated at internationally acclaimed festivals such as Stretch and Ignite, and organisations such as ART International and Authentic Bay Area.

My workshops have sparked thousands of nourishing connections, turning many strangers into life-long friends. I look forward to holding space for you!

I also offer online Holistic Coaching sessions, inspired by Authentic Relating, Positive Intelligence and Somatic Experiencing techniques.


For more information, check out itoiauthenticrelating.com.


For my Instagram, check out @itoiauthentic.


i to i Authentic Dating has already been a big hit in Wellington, as well as Auckland, Christchurch, Berlin, Amsterdam, Melbourne, Sydney, Vienna, Copenhagen, London, Bristol, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Montreal.


Here’s what others have said:


"This has been the most positive experience I've had in meeting genuine souls with the intention of finding love/romance for over 6 years" - Luca


"Laurie led us through a series of games and exercises that allowed us to open up and create very real bonds with others and with our own selves. Many emotions were felt in the safest, most welcoming environment" - Jason


“What a wonderful workshop you ran last night. I walked away with a sense of renewed self worth and also questioned why I don’t articulate comfortably what I want. It’s the perfect antidote to app culture.” - Imogen


“Laurie created a beautiful, safe space in no time, making it an ideal environment to be present and engage meaningfully with the activities. Even though all participants were strangers to me, I felt a deep sense of belonging developing over the evening.” - Tim


“Thank you so much for creating a space in which such well-aligned people could come together. I can't think of the last time I met so many wonderful, open-minded people in one go like that. It was a real pleasure” - John


"I love Laurie’s energy, wisdom, execution and light touch. I felt super safe to open up and connect while he was holding the space" - Tess


"Authentic Dating re-opened an old window for me in a new way. Heaps of fun too! And I did meet a very special person. Highly recommend for anyone curious and keen to connect with depth & joy" - Samantha


Practicalities:

Cost:

$35 for Low income

$45 for Regular income

$55 for High income

*

Location: Wellington Meditation Centre, 31 Hobson Crescent, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand.

When: Friday 13th February, 7.30 - 10pm. Please be on time as you may not be let in if not.

Dress code: Whatever you're comfortable in. The venue is shoes off and (mainly) seating on the floor.

Intoxicants: This is an alcohol and drug free event. There will however be plenty of tea available.

Refund policy: No refunds available. If you cannot make it you may transfer your ticket to a friend or use it as credit for a future i to i event.


* Why are tickets sold by income? 💰

In order to make the event as accessible as possible, there are three ticket types available, depending on the level of income you feel you have. It is up to you to decide how much you would like to contribute to the event.

If you would really like to attend but do not have the funds for the lowest ticket option, please get in touch and we can figure something out!

Limited spaces available through Humanitix. Book early to secure your place!

Author Talk | Lynley Edmeades with Claire Mabey, Author Talk | Lynley Edmeades with Claire Mabey
Unity Books Wellington and Otago University Press warmly invite you to an author talk featuring Lynley Edmeades in conversation with Claire Mabey about Lynley's new book, 'Hiding Places'.

Hiding Places is a compelling and beautifully written meditation on early motherhood and creativity. Told through a series of fragments that range from raw and troubled to delightful and hilarious, this remarkable book responds to the unexpected shocks and discoveries of becoming a mother, drawing on excerpts from family letters and secretive medical records, and advice contained in Truby King’s 1913 tract, Feeding and Care of Baby. Resonant with, yet distinct from, the works of writers like Maggie Nelson, Kate Zambreno, Olga Ravn and Chris Kraus, Hiding Places is an inspiring read for anyone interested in the dangerous yet fruitful zones where life and art overlap.

Bailamos Bachata! Latin Dance Party (with free lesson), Bailamos Bachata! Latin Dance Party (with free lesson)
🔥 Please note: the event is free but it can only continue if we support the Southern Cross by buying food or drinks 🔥


🌟 Wellington’s favourite monthly Bachata Latin dance party 🌟


Join us for an awesome mix of bachata, focusing on the best sensual tracks and remixes, along with salsa and a smattering of kizomba and zouk. We welcome everyone, from the absolute beginner to the most experienced dancer. We’re all about the joy of social dancing together.

And what makes a free party with great people even better? A free beginners’ bachata lesson with some of Wellington‘s best Latin dance teachers. If you’ve never danced bachata, Latin dance or even any other dance style before then this is the perfect lesson for you. We will have you dancing like a pro in no time!

Bailamos Bachata is hosted free of charge by the Southern Cross. They love the atmosphere we bring but we also need to support them in return. We’re asking everyone attending to purchase soft drinks, food or alcohol from the bar. It’s vital we show our gratitude.

1800-1830 social
1830-1900 free lesson
1900-2100 social

Q&A
Q. What is bachata?
A. Bachata is a popular and fun Latin couples dance. It started in the Dominican Republic, then travelled to Europe and the rest of the world. It now includes a wide range of music styles and dance influences and is still changing and evolving.

Q. I haven’t danced before, is that a problem?
A. Not at all! That’s exactly what the lesson is for – everyone has to start somewhere and we’re a very welcoming crowd for beginners.

Q. Is bachata a difficult dance to learn?
A. Its origins as a party/community dance mean the basics can be learnt quite quickly, so you’ll be enjoying yourself in no time.

Q. Who are the capital bachata collective?
A. We are the combined Wellington dance schools and people teaching bachata and we really want to share this dance with everyone. We love bachata, we love our community and we want to share it with you
￼

description:
Beacons of Hope walk tour (World AIDS Day special event), ** FREE - but please register at https://walktours.nz/book **

Join us for a special event marking both the 40th anniversary of the founding of the Burnett Foundation Aotearoa and the 40th anniversary of the death of Bruce Burnett – one of Aotearoa’s pioneering HIV activists and educators.

Bruce was instrumental in co-founding the AIDS Support Network in the early 1980s, which would become the New Zealand AIDS Foundation in 1985, later renamed to the Burnett Foundation Aotearoa in 2022.

Walk Tours NZ, in association with the Burnett Foundation, is hosting a very special walk tour to commemorate these two significant anniversaries. Starting outside the Āwhina Centre on Willis Street, we’ll walk through central Wellington, stopping at various locations to pay tribute to some of this country’s HIV pioneers.

Learn about personal and collective responses to the epidemic, and hear short archival recordings from those who experienced the early years first-hand.

As part of the walk tour, we’ll return to the Āwhina Centre where the Burnett Foundation team will talk about the current state of HIV in Aotearoa and show a couple of panels from the New Zealand AIDS Memorial Quilt.

Behind the Headlines: Talking Books with Mike McRoberts, Mike McRoberts (Ngāti Kahungunu ki te Wairoa) is one of New Zealand's most respected journalists and broadcasters, with an award-winning career spanning four decades. Join us to hear him talk about the books that have shaped his life at this special fundraising event for Katherine Mansfield House & Garden.

After anchoring Newshub's 6pm bulletin for 20 years and reporting from conflict zones and natural disasters worldwide, Mike is a familiar face in New Zealand homes. His work involves telling other people’s stories, but what stories have influenced him? Books have played an important role in Mike’s life, taking him from student librarian to author of two books himself.

Mike’s latest book, Speaking My Language | Te Kōrero i Tōku Reo, explores his deeply personal journey into Te Reo Māori and Te Ao Māori - captured in his acclaimed documentary, Kia Ora, Good Evening.

The evening will begin with a glass of Hunter’s Wines’ award-winning MiruMiru™ and delicious canapés. A non-alcoholic option will also be available.

This event is being held to raise funds for our Category 1 Historic Place and writer’s museum in Thorndon, which is open six days a week. We offer an annual programme of events and activities designed to encourage creativity and we host school and tour groups to share the life, literature and legacy of Katherine Mansfield.
