description:
Behind the Scenes: Napier Port & Mainfreight Learning Adventure, Behind the Scenes: Napier Port & Mainfreight Learning Adventure
Have you ever driven past Napier Port or watched trucks moving through Hawke's Bay and wondered what really happens behind the scenes?

Every day, thousands of tonnes of cargo, products and supplies move through systems most of us rarely get to see.

Yet these operations quietly keep our region connected to New Zealand and the rest of the world.

This is a rare opportunity to step behind the gates and discover two of Hawke's Bay's most fascinating and important operations.

Join us for a special Learning Adventure that takes you inside Napier Port and Mainfreight Hastings, guided by people who know these organisations better than almost anyone.

Our day begins with an exclusive guided tour of Napier Port, one of New Zealand's busiest maritime hubs. You'll hear stories of the port's history, watch the operation in action, and gain a new appreciation for the scale and complexity of what happens there every day.

After the port tour, we'll gather for a relaxed waterfront lunch at Madame Social in Ahuriri — a chance to enjoy great food, good conversation and wonderful company.

In the afternoon, we'll head to Mainfreight's Hastings depot for a behind-the-scenes look at one of the country's most innovative logistics operations. From live freight tracking and electric forklifts to sustainable building design and workplace culture, you'll discover what makes this Hawke's Bay business such a success.

Along the way, you'll meet interesting people, hear remarkable stories and see parts of the region that most people never get access to.

Meet Our Guides 🎤

Tony des Landes spent more than 50 years working at Napier Port and is one of Hawke's Bay's leading maritime historians. His knowledge of the port, its history and its role in shaping the region is unmatched.

John Mackay is Hastings Branch Manager at Mainfreight and brings deep insight into the day-to-day operations, innovation and culture that have helped make Mainfreight one of New Zealand's most respected companies.

What We'll Explore
• A rare behind-the-scenes tour of Napier Port
• The history and evolution of Hawke's Bay's maritime industry
• How goods move through New Zealand's supply chains
• Innovation, sustainability and culture at Mainfreight
• The people, stories and systems that keep our region connected

description:
Belmont Historic Bunker walk, Step into history and explore Belmont’s WWII munitions bunkers at Belmont Regional Park.

Join us for a unique opportunity to explore Aotearoa New Zealand’s WWII history at Belmont Regional Park.

Built in 1943, the Belmont Munitions Depot was once the country’s largest ammunition storage site, chosen for its strategic location near shipping routes and Trentham Military Camp, and its safe distance from populated areas. The depot originally held 62 magazines storing anti-aircraft shells, mortar rounds, grenades, and other munitions—including 1,500 tonnes of mustard gas, believed to be the largest store of chemical weapons in New Zealand.

This self-led, easy 2.5 km circuit walk follows the well-known Magazine Mile, winding through open farmland with expansive park views. Along the route, historians will be on-site to share stories and insights into Belmont’s vital role in supporting New Zealand and U.S. troops in the Pacific during World War II.

Walk at your own pace as you explore historic bunkers, uncover wartime secrets, and discover how this quiet landscape helped shape the Pacific war effort.

Time: 10.00am – 1.00pm
Meeting point: Belmont Regional Park, Hill Road entrance

Please note this event is limited to 60 car parks, so we encourage people to carpool where possible. To help us manage car park capacity, each registration is for ONE vehicle only (if you wish to register for more than one vehicle, please complete additional registrations)

Bob Ross Landscape Painting Workshop, NZ’s first Certified Bob Ross Instructor, Malcolm Sime, will prove to you that if you can hold a pen and write, you can hold a brush and paint. Come along and create a landscape oil painting from scratch to take away at the end of the day!

Description
If you don’t already know who Bob Ross is then Google him, and you will be amazed at how he creates fantastic paintings using simple tools. You can too!

Wear old clothes, come with nothing except your lunch, and go home with an oil painting completed 100% by yourself.

All materials are included in course fee – a 16x20 inch professional canvas, Bob Ross oil paints, brushes, and all equipment, as seen on NZ TV and YouTube.

This is a unique technique of wet-into-wet oil painting, which is ideal for those who have never painted before, as well as more experienced artists.

Please note: Suitable for all adults - please make sure you have a method to transport your wet oil painting home at the end of day. Each workshop focuses on doing a specific set landscape painting - the whole class group does the same painting.

(Please note there is no wheelchair access to this venue).

description:
Book Group: The Last of the Mohicans by James Fenimore Cooper, Celebrating its 200th anniversary this year, James Fenimore Cooper's 1826 novel is an unforgettable portrait of fierce individualism and moral courage, set against the bloody French and Indian War. The events of the book take place in 1757 in a very early America - in what we now know as Upstate New York - and only two decades before the Revolutionary War. The Last of the Mohicans has been described as a trailblazing text that helped establish early Americans’ shared sense of identity and purpose.

James Fenimore Cooper was one of the first and greatest literary giants of the New World, read in America and Europe, and stands alongside Nathaniel Hawthorne and Edgar Allan Poe as one of the forefathers of American literature.

Do you keep meaning to read more of the great classics? At Wellington Classic Literature Club, we read works that have stood the test of time, whether they were written in 1780, 1880 or even 1980. We meet on the first Tuesday of the month.

RSVP
Bookings essential. Get your free ticket by clicking 'Register' above. Limited places.

If you've signed up, but things change and you're not going to be able to make it along, please email classiclitwgtn@gmail.com as we may be able to make more spaces available for others.

VENUE
We meet in the ‘Games Room’, The Library bar's private area overlooking Courtenay Place. After you enter the bar, head to your right (up the step) and through a smaller space with booths to the large carpeted space beyond (behind the big wooden sliding door).

ABOUT US
Wellington Classic Literature Club has been running for more than a decade - since the start of 2013 - and we have a great bunch of regulars as well as readers who join us for particular books or simply when it suits.

description:
Book Launch: Hoods Landing by Laura Vincent, Join Unity Books, Āporo Press & Whitireia Publishing for the launch of the highly anticipated novel, Hoods Landing by Laura Vincent (Ngati Mahanga, Ngapuhi)!
- - - - -
Rita considered the dead. Shut her eyes. Rolled their names around her brain. Stacked each person in order like folded laundry, warm and crisp from the sun. She wondered how her name would sound amongst them.
In the rural reaches of Auckland, the women of the eclectic Gordon family gather for Christmas. They may push each other’s buttons, but know precisely when to offer tea (or a tipple). Rita, the 50-year-old baby of the family, is planning to tell them she has cancer. Drifting between past and present, she considers the lives of women in their community and reckons with what it all means for her future and her family.
Featuring elderly lesbians, twins who aren’t twins, and several dogs named Roger, Hoods Landing is about shoddy pasts, ambiguous futures and the imperfect bonds that tie family together.

Noho Tahi | 和平共處 is the inaugural residency project for The Dan and Una Chan & Laywood and Joyce Chan Residency at Wai-te-ata Press. The Residency’s focus is on “projects that enhance understandings of and engagement with Chinese Aotearoa, whether historical, social or cultural.
Speakers on the night are: Etienne Wain 黃義天 , Juhyeon 주현, brenda wang, Brecon Dobbie 布雷肯.
This multimedia collection reflects on noho tahi | 和平共處, peaceful co-existence between cultures — an emerging invitation for Hainamana/NZ Chinese communities to reorient ourselves towards Tangata Whenua in ways that uphold Tikanga Māori, Te Tiriti o Waitangi, and the diversities and complexities within Hainamanatanga (Chinese ways of being in Aotearoa).

description:
Book launch | NOVA, Join us for the launch of NOVA, a wise and joyful new novel by Tim Corballis. The book will be launched by pip adam.
Tuesday 9 June, 6pm
Unity Books Wellington
Free event – all welcome!
Nobody is very used to organising a world.
From the author of Our Future Is in the Air and R.H.I., NOVA is a genre-defying novel that imagines a future in which people and their worlds talk to each other.
Set on NOVA, a self-contained world launched into deep time, the novel unfolds through conversations between Kalla, a former councillor uneasy with consensus and ceremony, and System, the voice of all NOVA’s mechanisms and processes. System is curious and anxious – and seems to know about every aspect of life on NOVA, but in some ways knows nothing at all. Kalla is sceptical, smart and increasingly troubled by what can and can’t be measured. Together, System and Kalla circle around questions of democracy, labour, memory, entropy and love.
As it moves between scenes of work, public ritual and speculative reflections on systems theory and time, and as NOVA itself coasts, rotates and persists in its unknowable form, the novel asks disarming questions: what might it mean to have on-demand access to the voice of the world? What would we do with that knowledge? And is it possible for a world to be meaningfully organised at all?
‘This novel is such a wise, far-reaching, and funny reflection of organised societies and the relationship between humans and machines. What an ambitious, enlightening, and strangely joyful book.’ —Alice Miller

Bride Of The Year 2025, For 55 years, Wairarapa Bride of the Year has been a mainstay in the events calendar in the region. The event returns to the Wairarapa Events Centre for 2025, where brides who were married between 1 July and 30 June and were married in the Wairarapa, and/or have lived or are living in the Wairarapa, and/or whose spouse has lived in the Wairarapa, will get the chance to relive the magic of their big day, donning their gowns again, all while raising much needed funds for Te Awhina Plunket Wairarapa.

This event is unique in its focus on Wairarapa’s flourishing wedding industry. It is a great opportunity for couples planning their own weddings to look for inspiration from other local couples, for friends and families of brides to reminisce on the weddings. It is also an excellent opportunity to support Wairarapa Plunket and the service they provide to our community.

In 2024, the funds raised through Bride of the Year went towards purchasing equipment for use for Plunket rooms across Wairarapa along with purchase .

A ticket to Bride of the Year provides you with a night of glamour and celebration of love, all while supporting Wairarapa Plunket and the service they provide to our community.

description:
Celebrating 132 years of women’s suffrage — special lunchtime tour and kōrero, Join our kaimahi for a special lunchtime tour and kōrero, highlighting the 1893 Women’s Suffrage Petition | Te Petihana Whakamana Pōti Wahine, which paved the way for women’s suffrage in Aotearoa.
Tour and kōrero
Mark your calendars for 19 September, the anniversary of the 1893 Electoral Act that granted New Zealand women the right to vote in parliamentary elections.
To celebrate Suffrage Day, join a 45-minute kōrero and tour of the 1893 Women’s Suffrage Petition — Te Petihana Whakamana Pōti Wahine.
Tours are open to visitors of all ages (age 6+). Booking is not required.
Please meet at our waka reception desk on the ground floor before the start of the tour.
The ongoing struggle for equal rights
Come along to the National Library to learn about the journey New Zealand women took to gain the right to vote and about the ongoing struggle for equal rights.
View the 1893 petition that led to the creation of the Electoral Act 1893, which was signed into law on 19 September 1893.
Hear stories about wāhine toa like Meri Te Tai Mangakāhia (Te Rarawa) and suffragists Kate Sheppard, Ada Wells and maybe an ancestor of your own.
label: Community & Culture

description:
Celebrating Mahuru Māori: He wheako reorua o He Tohu and Pipitea walking tour — Mahuru Māori 2025, This Mahuru Māori, join a reorua (bilingual) He Tohu experience and hīkoi around Pipitea to celebrate te reo Māori and the unique hītori (history) of Pipitea. Deepen your understanding about ingoa tūturu (original place names) and the wāhi where He Tohu currently sits.
A reorua | bilingual tour of He Tohu and Pipitea
Join us and embark on a haerenga (journey) together to connect to the ancestors and our shared past. The tour will begin at He Tohu — a permanent exhibition of three iconic constitutional taonga that shape Aotearoa New Zealand.
* 1835 He Whakaputanga o te Rangatiratanga o Nu Tireni — Declaration of Independence of the United Tribes of New Zealand
* 1840 Te Tiriti o Waitangi — Treaty of Waitangi
* 1893 Women’s Suffrage Petition — Te Petihana Whakamana Pōti Wahine.
These taonga are significant because they shaped who we are as a nation and will shape what we become in the future.
"Ka mua, ka muri | Walking backwards into the future"
A hīkoi around Pipitea
After the He Tohu tour, join us on a half-hour bilingual hīkoi (walk) around key sites in Pipitea of cultural significance.
There are slight inclines in places, but we will be walking on the pavement for the tour. If the huarere (weather) is looking inclement, please bring warm clothing, a raincoat, or an umbrella. If the weather is too bad, we will postpone the event, so please register so that we can notify you about the cancellation.
Shared kai
During the kaupapa, knowledge, pātai (questions), and reflections will flow between us. At the end we’ll have kai timotimo (snacks). You are welcome to bring snacks to share.

description:
Chinese footprints: A Lunar New Year walking tour of Wellington, Join Oral History Advisor Lynette Shum and historian Nigel Murphy on a walking tour exploring the rich history of the Chinese in Wellington. The tour will also draw on images, ephemera, and oral history from the collections of the Alexander Turnbull Library.
Celebrate Lunar New Year exploring Wellington’s Chinese heritage
Celebrate Lunar New Year with Chinese footprints, a walking tour led by Lynette Shum (Oral History Advisor, Archives Library New Zealand) and historian Nigel Murphy. The tour will draw on images, ephemera, and oral history from the Alexander Turnbull Library's collections.
Meet at the Wellington Trades’ Hall Building for a brief introduction, before heading out to explore sites of significance for Wellington’s early Chinese community. These include businesses, eateries, and Haining Street’s ‘Chinatown’ — heritage largely erased and now invisible to passers-by. The tour concludes back at the Trades’ Hall Building with a pot of Chinese tea.
A koha of $10 is suggested to help cover the cost of running the tours.
RSVP now for your spot
Spots are limited, so book your place now by emailing ATLOutreach@dia.govt.nz.
Can’t make this date? We’re also running the tour on Saturday 21 March 2026.
About the speakers
Lynette Shum, third-generation Poon Yue Chinese New Zealander, is Oral History Advisor for Archives Library of New Zealand. Her first home was on the fringes of Chinatown, yet she was unaware of its existence until researching what would become the Haining Street Oral History Project. She has completed an MA on the topic.
Nigel Murphy has been researching, writing, and lecturing on Chinese New Zealand history for almost 40 years. His interests include the politics of Chinese New Zealanders, their organisations and associations, social and cultural lives, home villages, and transnational connections with other Chinese overseas communities.

description:
Colossal Squid: Freaky Features, Colossal Squid: Freaky Features comes to Cobblestones, Greytown

The ever-popular Te Papa exhibition Colossal Squid Ngu Tipua opens at Cobblestones on 11th December 2025 and runs through until 1st February 2026.

The Colossal Squid is so rarely seen that only eight adult colossal squid have ever been scientifically reported. Now venue name, in co-operation with Te Papa, is set to reveal some of the fascinating science and wonderful secrets of one of New Zealand’s most significant natural history specimens.

Te Papa's Head of Natural History, Phil Edgar, said, “In learning about this weird and mysterious creature, we hope visitors will have a greater appreciation for life in the deep sea, much of which remains undiscovered.”

The Colossal Squid is one of the most iconic specimens at Te Papa, and while touring the complete specimen is impossible, some of the important parts of the squid have found their way to Cobblestones.
Te Papa’s Curator of Invertebrates, Dr Rodrigo Salvador, explains how important the Colossal Squid has been for the science community, and how popular it has been among the public.

“Te Papa’s Colossal Squid has been a major source of information for scientists and the museum’s most popular exhibit since its debut. They live in the deep Antarctic waters, and despite being one of the largest invertebrate species in existence, they are very rarely captured”.

Colossal Squid Ngu Tipua centres around an interactive table displaying many different objects, including the lens from an eye of the Colossal Squid, part of a tentacle, and a complete tiny squid, a miniature of its colossal relative. Touchable rotating models of a squid’s tentacle hook and the Colossal Squid's beak are also on display.

The exhibition also displays two documentaries which show life in the depths of the Southern Ocean, and how the most complete Colossal Squid ever found ended up at Te Papa.

The public can continue the experience and learn beyond the exhibition with a new Te Papa press book for children, Whiti: Colossal Squid of the Deep, and online Te Papa resources, including a free downloadable Colossal Squid Activity Book.

“Thanks to the support of WBS and Te Papa, Cobblestones is delighted to be bringing this fascinating exhibition to Wairarapa during the summer holidays. It’s a must-see exhibition for the young and young at heart to learn about this fascinating creature, its world, and habitat.”

Colossal Squid Ngu Tipua is developed and toured by the Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa.

For further information, please contact:
Cobblestones Museum - 063049687 or cobblestonesmuseumgreytown@gmail.com

description:
Communicate Across Generations: Bridge the Divide, Tired of miscommunications with your Gen Z niece or your Baby Boomer parent? This one-day workshop will equip you with the tools to navigate the diverse communication styles of today's multi-generational world. (NZ citizen and residents free with ID, all others pay listed price).

This course is free for NZ citizens and residents. Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.

If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

Discover why different generations prioritise different things in their interactions, from family group chats and face-to-face conversations through to workplace attitudes. Learn to decode the nuances, bridge the divides, and foster more effective communication in your daily life.

Learning Outcomes

Deconstruct Communication Styles: You will be able to identify and describe the typical communication styles, preferences, and values of different generations, including Baby Boomers, Generation X, Millennials, and Generation Z.

Mitigate Conflict: You will learn to recognise and resolve common intergenerational communication conflicts by understanding their root causes and applying effective conflict resolution strategies.

Improve Collaboration: You will develop practical skills to adapt your communication approach to better engage with people from different generations, leading to enhanced understanding and connection.

Foster Inclusivity: You will be able to appreciate and leverage the unique perspectives and strengths that each generation brings to the table, creating more inclusive environments in your relationships.

Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch and snacks, and pen and paper to take notes.

description:
Community Evening Tri 2, Ignite Consultants is a student-run charitable organisation that provides free and creative advice to charities and social organisations across Aotearoa. All of our consultants are passionate and talented student-volunteers who are driven by their desire to foster social change. Our vision is to help organisations to maximise their impact through harnessing the fresh perspectives of university students.
We run two project cycles per year which coincide with the university semesters, each lasting for a duration of 9 weeks. Each team consists of a local charity, 5-6 students, a project manager (a person who has been through the Ignite Consultants experience before) and a professional mentor who has experience in consulting and/or the industry the organisation works in.

Ignite's Community Evening is a special occasion where our consultants share what they have learnt, created and experienced over the past nine weeks. This event is an opportunity to learn about the remarkable charities we have collaborated with this semester, to enjoy delicious food and to extend our heartfelt thanks to all our supporters.
This semester, attendees will get to hear presentations from the teams who have worked with WELLfed, Take10, Orange Sky, PACE and The Charitable Recycling Trust.

Our grandmothers would never be caught without a selection of home-baked biscuits, a slice or two and at least one type of cake or loaf. Today many of those skills are no longer being passed on.

In this workshop you will get back to basics with some of the Kiwi baking classics which, made well, are delicious and widely loved.

A pretty, delicate Louise Cake and
melt in the mouth Afghans.

Explore different kinds of lentils and create recipes that make the most of this versatile and nutritious food staple. All ingredients included in course fee.

Description
The lentil is perhaps the world’s most versatile and indestructible food. It has significant health benefits from lowering cholesterol to supporting weight loss – and lentils are delicious when cooked well. Enjoy this half-day course that will show you how to cook lentils properly and make the most of this nutritious staple ingredient. Discover spices to complement and enhance lentils and create some mouth-watering dishes.

All ingredients included in course fee. Please bring your apron, a couple of teatowels, a sharp knife and leak-proof containers to take your food home in.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:

Recognise some different types of lentils.
Cook some delicious lentil dishes.
Understand some spices that will work well with lentils.
Follow simple recipes.

description:
Coven: Butch, Coven: Butch
For butches and butch lovers! This night sets to make two things clear:

1. We love butches!
2. Get enough sapphics and queers in a room and anything can become a competition

Join us for axe throwing, games, kai, and as always at our events impeccable vibes. Spot prizes for the best butches, drink on arrival, and a room full of hot babes? Need we say more, so get your fits checked and grab your ticket before they go. This event has limited capacity.

Not a butch? No problem, all butch and butch appreciating Coven members of all flavours welcome.

No dress code! Come as you are, celebrate butch fashion or your queer identity and expect a fun chill night with your community.

More info about Coven:

Coming Solo? You’re Not Alone.
Don’t be nervous if you’re planning to come on your own – Coven is built for connection. Whether it’s your first queer event or your hundredth, you’ll be surrounded by a community that gets it. From the moment you arrive, there’ll be friendly faces, welcoming vibes, and plenty of chances to mingle, and connect. Coven is about belonging – and there’s a place here for you.

Coven Kaupapa
For queer women and gender minorities, spaces like this are rare, vital, and sometimes, life-changing. In a world that constantly centers cishet norms, Coven offers a space where we are the default – where you can fully show up as yourself, be seen, celebrated and surrounded by YOUR community.

For many in our Coven, this is one of the only opportunities we feel comfortable enough to experience nightlife free from the male gaze, tokenism, fear, or the need to shrink ourselves to fit in. It’s a space where sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people aren’t just welcomed – we are centered. It’s for those who are often pushed to the margins, who rarely feel represented in “inclusive” spaces that still cater to the mainstream.

This night exists because we need it – and because we create it, together.

Accessibility
This event is located on the ground floor. Have specific accessibility needs? Reach out directly to the Whisky & Wood team at

If you made it this far... Good girl / Good they / Good boy / Good YOU!

description:
Crime & Punishment Tour, We’ll take a wander to find those who were responsible, in the earliest days of the settlement of Wellington (and our country) for creating and enforcing the law, those who sat in the law courts, and those who kept incarcerated the people who failed to observe the law. There’s a duellist, lawyers galore, police and military law enforcers, and even a criminal or two.

Tours start at the Bolton Street Cemetery Museum, Lower Bolton Street, and will last 1.5 hours. Cost $10 per person, but free for children. Each tour will be limited to 30 people, so book early to avoid disappointment.

This event is not suitable for wheelchairs. Please wear sturdy shoes, as some of the paths are steep and can be slippery.
label: Community & Culture

description:
Crime and Punishment, Extraordinary stories about people who broke the law, as well as lawyers, policemen, jailers and judges. There's even a murder or two!
Hear stories about the jailers, judges and policemen who were dealing with criminals, as well as some of the villains and murderers that shocked earlier generations in Wellington. Find out about the duelling pistol that was involved in the deaths of a lawyer and a magistrate; and about an unsolved murder on a quiet farm road. There’s even a criminal or two.

Booking is REQUIRED.
Cost: $10
Booking info here: https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/.../crime-and.../

Health & Safety:
Please keep to the paths and always follow the directions of your tour guide. This is a heritage cemetery with very old headstones and fragile railings. Wear sturdy shoes and take care.

We've had wonderful support from grants and community funding over the last two Crop Up seasons - now we need to fundraise as this funding is no longer available. Please join us (grab 3 friends for your table of four!) for a cracking Crop Up Quiz Night at The Offering in Greytown on 14th November. Enjoy dinner and drinks from 6pm with the Quiz from 7pm.

Crop Up has become Greytown's Saturday morning meeting place for our village to feed itself from local gardens, enjoy freshly caught fish, taste straight-from-the-oven bread, pick up meadow-laid eggs, try locally grown wheat flour and provide a place where we can gather, eat brunch, drink coffee and get social with our neighbours. It's a community check in spot, a place for fundraisers to sell their home baking, or a spot to collect Greytown's garden flowers to fill our homes with.

description:
Cèilidh Dance Fundraiser for WMC, Get your dancing shoes on and bring the kids! The Wellington Music Centre invites you to join a vibrant and lively evening of traditional Scottish and Irish social dancing, featuring the sensational VicFolk band! This beginner-friendly, all-ages partner dancing event is designed to bring families and the community together for a night of fun, music, and connection, all while supporting the Wellington Music Centre.

Details

12th September 2025
6 - 9pm
St Patrick's Hall, 17 Rongotai Road, Kilbirnie
Ages 0-99
Tickets:
https://www.wellingtonmusiccentre.org.nz/.../wmc-ceili-dance
(door sales will be available)
Activities
Traditional Partner Dancing: Learn and enjoy traditional Scottish and Irish dances, led by the VicFolk caller*, making it perfect for beginners and families.
Live Music: Dance the night away to the energetic and foot-stomping tunes provided by the sensational VicFolk band.
Raffle: Grab a ticket to our raffle for a chance to win fantastic prizes!
Silent Auction: Bid on unique items and experiences donated by local businesses in our silent auction, including tickets to Roxy cinema, and a family pass to Wēta Workshop, with all proceeds supporting the Wellington Music Centre.
Food and Drinks: Food and beverages are available for purchase throughout the evening. This is an alcohol-free event.
*the caller leads the band and calls out instructions for the dancers, usually with a good sense of humour! They make sure everyone is having a great time, especially those who have never attended a cèilidh dance before.

Supporting Wellington Music Centre:
A cèilidh is about more than dancing, it’s a place to enjoy time with your family and connect as a community. At Wellington Music Centre, we are passionate about bringing joyful and affordable musical experiences to kids and families in South and East Wellington. Proceeds from the event will directly benefit the Wellington Music Centre, helping to fund our great programmes, including the Peninsula Family Choir, the Miramar Kids Choir, the Wellington Music Centre Orchestra, our foundational music courses: Music Explorers and the Ukulele Ensemble, and our free twice-a-year community events.
You can read more about the Wellington Music Centre and our fantastic programmes on our website:
https://www.wellingtonmusiccentre.org.nz/

description:
DEBRA NZ Conference and Family Camp 2025, Kia ora DEBRA New Zealand whanau !
Save the dates - DEBRA NZ Conference and Family Camp, Wellington, Friday 22 - Sunday 24 August 2025.
We are very happy to announce that we are planning a get-together for the NZ EB whanau and a few Aussie families in Wellington in August. We really hope you can join us - it will be wonderful to see you!
This event is a great opportunity to meet other families, connect with old friends and make wonderful new ones, learn from each other and from valuable talks about EB issues, and have time to relax and enjoy a couple of days in Wellington city - the creative capital! We're keen to hear about any particular topics you would like to hear about.
Everyone is welcome including extended family and friends, caregivers, and healthcare professionals.
Dates: Friday 22nd August (check-in from 3pm with informal meet and greet from 5.00pm), to Sunday 24th August (finishing 2pm after a farewell lunch)
Event location: Wellington City, venue to be confirmed
Registration will be launched in early May - please stay tuned for further details!
Your registration fee will cover the conference, meals and children’s activities from Friday evening to Sunday lunch time, but it does not cover accommodation (amount to be confirmed), travel or airport transfers.
DEBRA NZ will provide some limited assistance with accommodation and travel costs if needed, subsiding flights for the person attending with EB.
Please contact debra@debra.org.nz if you would like to apply for this support.
There will be more information soon.
We need an idea of numbers so please get in touch as soon as possible!
Email: debra@debra.org.nz with any questions and let us know if you are interested in attending.
Nga mihi nui,
Anna, Lea and the DEBRA NZ team
debra@debra.org.nz

description:
Day of the Dead Celebration - Dia de los Muertos, Join Claudio for this special occasion we will be celebrating one of the most important holidays in Mexico, the day of the dead or “Dia de los Muertos”.

The Day of the Dead is one of the traditions that has remained alive throughout the centuries; the main holidays are November 1 & 2, which UNESCO designated and cataloged as an Intangible Heritage of Humanity in 2003.

This special celebration dates back to prehispanic times before the arrival of Europeans to America, and has been alive and widely celebrated over the years.

Expect:

Cleansing copal and herbal welcoming.

An opening ceremony to acknowledge the Tlalmanalli (offering and altar) with the deep sound of the conch shell in the four directions and drums sounds.

History of the day of the dead celebration.

Explanation of the altar, and the main elements for an ofrenda.

Storytelling: learn of Mexican legends like Catrinas and Xoloitzcuintle (the Mexican dog that helps the dead to find their way to Mictlan, the Aztec underword).

Remembering and sharing histories about the loved ones that passed away (optional but encouraged)

Traditional Mexican chants for remembering the loved ones

Atole de Chocolate, a traditional prehispanic drink - amazing in flavour, consumed cold or hot

Music to invoke emotion and imagery of contemplative natural and mystical environments

Finish with a shamanic atmosphere of relaxation and traditional chants.

description:
December Full Moon Drumming, Please remember this is a ZERO WASTE and *NO ALCOHOL* community gathering.
Kia ora!
Full Moon Drumming Wellington is a registered public event with the Wellington City Council. We are a group of humans from all walks of life who gather under the full moon each month to connect through drumming and dance around the fire. This gathering is participatory, that means if you made it to the circle you are part of the circle. As in Africa, there is no audience! Everyone is invited to participate as part of the ‘chorus’ (singing/clapping), dancing, or drumming.
The event is weather permitting, we check the forecast a few days prior and aim to make a decision the day before the event, although this is not possible and sometimes we make the decision on the day. All updates are posted on the event page.
This gathering is entirely run by volunteers, if you'd like to contribute in any way please get in touch.
There are a few things that we need help with:
- FIREWOOD: Please bring dry firewood as a koha, no wood no fire! Please NOTE we DO NOT burn pallets (due to nails) or treated timber. Driftwood from nearby south coast beaches is often abundant, feel free to post or reach out if you have a vehicle and are keen to help gather firewood on the day of the event.
- BEAUTIFYING THE CIRCLE SPACE: Anyone has fairy lights, oil burners, or is keen to make some signs?
NOTE: We hold a fire permit for this event. For safety reasons we don't allow participants to feed the fire, and while is generally okay to roast some marshmallows early in the evening we don't allow the use the fire for cooking or heating food.
This is an **ALCOHOL FREE EVENT**, please help us uphold this kaupapa and remind those who are unaware and might be new to the event. As hosts we are responsible for your safety and we take that responsibility seriously, especially given that the event is authorised through both fire and event permits. Large, public, all ages gatherings require administration and logistics so please respect this and the guidelines provided.
Princess Bay is within Taputeranga Marine Reserve (https://octopus.org.nz/taputeranga-marine-reserve), we are welcomed to gather each month in this special place so let’s all make sure there is NO RUBBISH LEFT BEHIND and that we take care of the space. Dogs are NOT ALLOWED at the gathering - there are Korora (Blue Pinguins) nesting under the rocks nearby and we've had issues with dogs in the past.
Children are welcome at the fire, though, especially after dark, please make sure that all children have adult supervision, that the supervisors are aware of the children they are looking after, and that the children are aware of who is looking after them.
Feel free to bring:
- Your friends.
- Drums or any percussive instrument.
- Warm clothing; jackets and wool blankets are good.
- Something to seat on (otherwise sand is often wet)
- Drinking water.
- Food, tea to share.
- Your lovely selves.
- Fire spinning kit and fuel.
FIRE SPINNERS: Please take all precautionary safety measures and make sure to set up fire-spinning downwind from the fire circle.
PARKING: There's a parking lot a few hundred meters from the fire circle where there's also public toilets. Please also be aware of our neighbors driveway opposite the stairway and do not park directly in front of it.
CARPOOLING: If you don't have a way to get to Princess Bay, or if you have spare seats in your car, feel free to post it on the event page. The less cars driving the better.
Feel free to share the event page and send an event invite to whomever you feel would be interested, not everyone sees the notifications and advertising

Don’t: How using the right words will change your life - an author talk, Thursday 23 July, 5.30-6.30pm
Te Whare Ngārara Community Room 1 (Mezzanine level), Te Matapihi ki te ao nui Central Library.
Join us for a talk from Bob Selden, author of Don’t: How using the right words will change your life.
The words we use every day are quietly working against us, and we don't even know it. Every "don't," every "you always," every "I will" is programming our brains in ways that sabotage our relationships, our habits, and our future.
Struggling with difficult conversations? Discover how positive parenting scripts, clean language techniques, and better self-talk dissolve conflict before it starts.
Whether you're navigating couples repair, managing workplace feedback, or trying to change negative thinking, the tools here are concrete and proven. From coaching questions that unlock deeper understanding to the science of why "I am saving" beats "I will save", every chapter builds your emotional intelligence habits and transforms how you connect with the people who matter most.
Bob Selden's book, Don’t: How using the right words will change your life, first published in 2016 and now revised, has been described as "ground-breaking" in developing positive conversations, relationships and personalities.

description:
Echoes in the Room: A Lecture with Dr Pamela Gerrish Nunn, When Frances Hodgkins settled in England after the war, she brought with her a rich stock of European sources gathered during her time in France. This talk by Dr Pamela Gerrish Nunn introduces some of the lesser known artists Frances Hodgkins drew for the art she forged in the 1920s and ’30s.

Dr Pamela Gerrish Nunn, formerly professor of art history at the University of Canterbury, is well known internationally as a specialist on women artists of the 19th and early 20th centuries. She has published articles and given conference papers on Frances Hodgkins, curated an exhibition of Hodgkins’ works at the NZ Portrait Gallery and contributed to several Toi MAHARA exhibitions.

The lecture will be held at Waikanae Community Centre, 28 Utauta Street, Waikanae

Free entry but rsvp required. Drop into the gallery or rsvp here: https://form.jotform.com/253427149566869

description:
Fat Queers Eating Cake!, Fat Queers Eating Cake!
There’s so much strength and solidarity in members of marginalised communities getting together to have a joyous good time. Fat Queers Eating Cake! is a shared meal (please bring food to share, if you’re able), where you can gather with friends old and new, free of any diet talk or body shaming.

TLDR:
- Saturday 14 March 12pm -2pm
- Please bring some food to share, if you are able
- Venue to be confirmed
- Free, but please register once the ticket link is set up
- Please take some time to read the full post below for more information

WHO
This is an event for you if you’re fat, any gender and any flavour of queer. Please be assured that fat is absolutely a neutral term referring to body size in the same way that tall or brunette are also neutral terms. It’s our word to use how we like - just like queer.

There’s no tape measure at the door to determine if you’re ‘fat enough’, we just ask that smaller fats acknowledge they may have more privilege in various ways than larger fats.
- Kids: We don’t want childcare to be a barrier to attending, but this event is not specifically designed for children.
- Allies: if you don’t have fat and/or queer friends to bring with you, and you’d be worried about coming alone, feel free to bring an ally with you.

WHAT

Think of it as an inside picnic (which isn’t weather-dependent and is more accessible for those who might not be able to sit on the ground). Bring some food, pop a label on it so those with dietary requirements can nibble safely, make yourself a cuppa and grab a seat!

This event is absolutely free. We ask you to bring some kai to share if you’re able, but if you can’t, please don’t let that stop you from attending.

FOOD

We use cake in the event title because it’s got a decadent ‘sinful’ reputation it’s fun to subvert, but all food is good food, so bring whatever makes you happy. Love to bake? Excellent, we’re into that. Garden overloaded with veges? Bring those! Learned to make amazing hummus because you don’t support genocide? Lovely! Only got time to pass by a dairy? Grab some potato chips. We will have ingredient labels to put with your food.

Please note: During the event, what you eat is your business, what anyone else eats is their business. The only kind of comments appropriate would be “oh this __ is so delicious” NOT “oh I couldn’t eat that, I’d have to go to the gym”.

WHERE:

To be confirmed ASAP. It may be in the Hutt or it may be in the central city.

ACCESSIBILITY

Full details will be provided once the venue is finalised, but accessibility will be a top consideration.

- COVID-19: please take a RAT before attending, and stay home if you or anyone in your household is sick. If you’d like to come along in a mask, but wouldn’t feel safe to remove it to eat, you are still absolutely welcome to join in the chats.

- Alcohol: this is an alcohol-free event, to allow younger members of the community to attend.

WHY

I used to organise fat liberation events with my ethical clothing company House of Boom. I’ve folded that now, but still want to help provide spaces for our community to get together, have some fun, and work to overturn fatphobic bullshit at the same time. Now that I've joined the board of Wellington Pride, specifically to help make events more accessible to the 1 in 3 members of the Rainbow Community who are disabled, I thought this would be a particularly fitting event to host. Join us!

HOW

Please register for a free ticket so we know how many will be attending - once the ticket link is created.

description:
February Full Moon Drumming, Please remember this is a ZERO WASTE and *NO ALCOHOL* community gathering.
Kia ora!
Full Moon Drumming Wellington is a registered public event with the Wellington City Council. We are a group of humans from all walks of life who gather under the full moon each month to connect through drumming and dance around the fire. This gathering is co-creative and participatory, that means if you made it to the circle you are part of the circle. There is no audience, everyone is invited to participate as part of the ‘chorus’ (singing/clapping), dancing, or drumming.
The event is weather permitting, we check the forecast a few days prior and aim to make a decision the day before the event, although this is not possible and sometimes we make the decision on the day. All updates are posted on the event page.
This gathering is entirely run by volunteers, if you'd like to contribute in any way please get in touch.
There are a few things that we need help with:
- FIREWOOD: Please bring dry firewood as a koha, no wood no fire! Please NOTE we DO NOT burn pallets (due to nails) or treated timber. Feel free to post or reach out if you have a vehicle and are keen to help gather firewood on the day of the event.
- BEAUTIFYING THE CIRCLE SPACE: Anyone has fairy lights, oil burners, or is keen to make some signs?
NOTE: We hold a fire permit for this event. For safety reasons we don't allow participants to feed the fire, and while is generally okay to roast some marshmallows early in the evening we don't allow the use the fire for cooking or heating food.
This is an **ALCOHOL FREE EVENT**, please help us uphold this kaupapa and remind those who are unaware and might be new to the event that alcohol is not permitted. As hosts we are responsible for your safety and we take that responsibility seriously, especially given that the event is authorised through both fire and event permits. Large, public, all ages gatherings require administration and logistics so please respect this and the guidelines provided.
Princess Bay is within Taputeranga Marine Reserve (https://octopus.org.nz/taputeranga-marine-reserve), we are welcomed to gather each month in this special place so let’s all make sure there is NO RUBBISH LEFT BEHIND and that we take care of the space. Dogs are NOT ALLOWED at the gathering - there are Korora (Blue Pinguins) nesting under the rocks nearby and we've had issues with dogs in the past.
Children are welcome at the fire, though, especially after dark, please make sure that all children have adult supervision, that the supervisors are aware of the children they are looking after, and that the children are aware of who is looking after them.
Feel free to bring:
- Your friends.
- Drums or any percussive instrument.
- Warm clothing; jackets and wool blankets are good.
- Something to seat on (otherwise sand is often wet)
- Drinking water.
- Food, tea to share.
- Your lovely selves.
- Fire spinning kit and fuel.
FIRE SPINNERS: Please take all precautionary safety measures and make sure to set up fire-spinning downwind from the fire circle.
PARKING: There's a parking lot a few hundred meters from the fire circle where there's also public toilets. Please also be aware of our neighbors driveway opposite the stairway and do not park directly in front of it.
CARPOOLING: If you don't have a way to get to Princess Bay, or if you have spare seats in your car, feel free to post it on the event page. The less cars driving the better.
Feel free to share the event page and send an event invite to whomever you feel would be interested, not everyone sees the notifications and advertising

description:
Forest & Bird WALK a New Reserve - Mātai Moana / Watts Peninsula, Join us for a guided walk over Mātai Moana / Watts Peninsula (North end of Miramar Peninsula). This guided walk will celebrate the Government announcement (September 2025), that the 72 hectare area is now a Public Reserve and DOC land.
The area's attractions include:
1. strong historical, cultural and military values, (several kainga and pā, and military history from 1880s), and has hosted several prisons, including a prison garden
2. some superb 360 degree views of Wellington Harbour
3. no major animal pest species and while much of the land is grass or in pines, there are several sizable and growing areas of regenerating native bush.
Moderate fitness will be needed. Our walk is expected to take a little over 2.5 hours. It will traverse a mixture of sealed roads and walking tracks with some uneven ground and two quite steep sections, from sea level to 163m above sea level. One section has a gradient of 30 degrees for a short section. There are some stiles to climb over.
Meet opposite the steps up to Massey Memorial at 130 Massey Road, Point Halwsell, Mapuia, Wellington, 6022. This is about 450m south of Point Halswell, and 500m north of the northern end of Shelly Bay. Location of the meeting point: approx 41°17'15" S, 174°49'26.5" E. A Forest & Bird Flag will be on display. See map for meeting spot and car parking suggestions. Please arrive in time to confirm your attendance and receive a quick pre-walk briefing.
Arrive by 12.50 p.m. on Sunday 22 February 2026. Please register on EventFinda in advance - limited to 40 walkers. All aged 10 or more, are welcome - you do not have to be a Forest & Bird member. All children must be accompanied by an adult who takes responsibility for them. Please bring your own sunhat, sunblock, snacks, any personal medications plus water bottle and wear good walking shoes/boots. There is no public transport to the meeting point.
If weather is wet/unsuitable, a decision to postpone will be made by 11:00 a.m. on Sunday 22 February 2026, and a group email will be issued to all those who have registered. Contact Ken New on ken.new@branch.forestandbird.org.nz for any enquiries.
Please register on EventFinda.

description:
Free BBQ and chat with Council & Kāpiti Mountain Bike Club, Council staff and Kapiti MTB club have been around Waikanae Park hill, checking out some of the do-it-yourself bike tracks that have been popping up. We’ve been walking the hills (and jumping into a few of the holes!) to get a real sense of the terrain, the steep drops, and the jump locations, and yes, photos never quite do the scale justice!
While some of the current tracks and features are unsafe and need to be removed, we get it, this isn’t about shutting down fun. It’s about ensuring the space can work better for everyone, now and in the future, through best practices.
That’s why this Sunday, we’re inviting local young riders and their whānau to come down for a Free BBQ and kōrero.
Meet the crew, share your thoughts, and be part of the conversation about what mountain biking in the park could look like moving forward, using the NZ MTB guidelines to inform good track-building practices.
Where: Waikanae Park, end of the rugby fields
When: Sunday, 5 October at 12pm

description:
Friends of Karori Cemetery - 2025 Wellington Heritage Festival: Gallows Tour, Crime, Justice, and the Final Walk.
Delve into the complex history of capital punishment in Wellington with this thought-provoking tour through Karori Cemetery. Gallows shines a light on the people behind the process. Discover their roles in shaping justice, the cases that defined their careers, and the human stories behind a system of ultimate consequence.
Each tour is $10 per person (plus non-refundable booking fee). Children under 12 are free.
Our tour has a maximum capacity of about 15 persons. If there are insufficient tickets remaining for your party, please email us at info@friendsofkaroricemetery.co.nz to check if we can accommodate you.
Please note:
If we have to cancel a tour due to inclement weather or sickness, we will notify you on the day 1 hour before the tour starts by email and on our Facebook page. The booking fee is non-refundable.
This tour is approximately 2 hours long.
This tour contains a number of adult themes and some graphic descriptions so is not suitable for everyone.
Please dress appropriately for the conditions.
While we do our best to guide you on a safe walking route, during the winter months the ground can become slippery in places.
Some of our walks require a moderate degree of fitness and are not suited for those with limited mobility.
There is only one toilet which is located by the cemetery office at the main entrance.
If you have purchased tickets for other people can you please pass our tour information on to them as well.
Please meet us at the shelter (shown as the Historic Chapel on the map at the main entrance)
We look forward to welcoming you to Karori Cemetery.

Embark on a captivating journey through the history buried in Karori Cemetery with our tour showcasing the remarkable lives of Wellington's women.

Be inspired by the incredible impact of these women's lives in early Wellington.

description:
Friends of Karori Cemetery - Evening Tour (April 2026), Evening Tour
Would you like to join us and explore the beauty of Karori Cemetery in the evening?
This tour is for anyone who would like to see the Cemetery through a different lens, as the landscape settles in from dusk to darkness. On this walk you'll be accompanied by two guides who will take you on a wander through some of the most magical parts of the cemetery, with a story or two of early Wellingtonians along the route. We might even spy a Ruru/Morepork or two! The tour does not have any scary themes. There are points on the tour where we may pause and turn off our torches to enjoy the landscape in the darkness.
The tour is of approximately 1.5 hours duration and starts and finishes at the Main Chapel on Rosehaugh Avenue, where there is plenty of easy parking.
Each attendee needs to bring their own torch that they can comfortably carry for the duration. No head torches please for the comfort of your fellow walkers.
The route mostly follows paved surfaces but there are some areas of unevenness. Surefootedness is required. This tour involves approximately 2km of walking, with some slow paced but uphill stints.
The tour is not suited for children under the age of 12 or unaccompanied minors. There are no toilets on the route.

Each tour is $10 per person (plus non-refundable booking fee).
Our tour has a maximum capacity of about 15 persons. If there are insufficient tickets remaining for your party, please email us at info@friendsofkaroricemetery.co.nz to check if we can accommodate you.

description:
Friends of Karori Cemetery: Hangman's Noose Tour (March 2026), Hangman's Noose Tour
In total, 85 people have been executed for crime in New Zealand with the first in 1842 and the last in 1957. Seventeen of those men were executed in Wellington and 11 are buried in Karori Cemetery.  This walking tour will visit some of their graves to account their crimes, trials and convictions. It will also visit the plots of some of the victims.

The graves are unmarked and placed in remote and disparate locations making this a tour about 2.5 hours long. The route is 2.5km and requires reasonable physical fitness due to the steep terrain and unsealed paths in places.
The tour contains a number of adult themes and some graphic descriptions and so is not suitable for everyone.
Each tour is $10 per person (plus non-refundable booking fee). Children under 12 are free.

Friends of Karori Cemetery: Military Tales from the Services Section (April 2026), Military Tales from the Services Area
Come and hear tales from our military history. The Servicemens Cemetery was opened in 1916. It was the first and remains the largest such cemetery to be established in New Zealand.  The tour has about 25 brief stops and includes prominent army leaders Major General Sir Howard Karl Kippenberger, Major General Charles William Melvill, Lieutenant-General Sir Leonard Thornton, Major General Sir Keith Lindsay Stewart, and army nurse commander Hestor Maclean.

description:
Friends of Karori Cemetery: National Monuments (Dec 2025), The two main stops on the tour are the Cemeteries’ two national Monuments – the Tangiwai disaster and Prime Minister Peter Fraser.  We will review what happened at Tangiwai and especially the bravery of the trains crew and in addition, what the court of inquiry found about the safety of the bridge. 
Peter Fraser is generally regarded as one of NZ’s best Prime Ministers of the 20th century, and we explore his initiatives in public health and education and also his leadership during WW2.
These are just two of the several stops we will make.
Each tour is $10 per person (plus non-refundable booking fee). Children under 12 are free.

description:
Friends of Karori Cemetery: SS Penguin Tour (Feb 2026), On the 12 February 1909, the SS Penguin sank in Cook Strait in a raging southerly storm with the loss of 72 lives, one of the worst maritime disasters in NZ history.  Many of those who died were woman and children, as their lifeboats capsized in the wild sea. 
Although the Captain was heavily criticised, it is still not clear what the ship hit nor where, as the wreck of the Penguin has never been located. 
The tragedy stunned Wellington and a day of mourning was called for 16 February.  The city came to a standstill as many of those who died were brought up to Karori Cemetery for burial in a long procession of cabs and lorries.
To commemorate this tragedy the Friends will be undertaking a guided tour of most of the Penguin graves on Sunday 8th February. 
The tour duration is approximately 2 hours long.
This tour is suitable for people with moderate fitness. The route mostly follows paved surfaces but there are some areas of unevenness. Surefootedness is required.

Each tour is $10 per person (plus non-refundable booking fee). Children under 12 are free.

description:
From Boots to Dragons - Photo Walk, Join us for a timed photographic adventure from the heights of Mount Victoria to a legendary dragon’s lair.
Beginning at the Tararua Tramping Club, we’ll stroll downhill along footpaths with sweeping harbour views, colourful houses, heritage buildings, and plenty of Wellington character. Along the way, you’ll tackle creative, slightly cryptic photo challenges designed to spark imagination rather than speed.
No technical expertise required — just a camera (or phone), comfortable shoes (the route will cover 2-3 kms, mostly downhill), and a sense of fun.

description:
From Pemberley to Pipitea: Celebrating Jane Austen's 250th Birthday, From Pemberley to Pipitea: Celebrating Jane Austen's 250th Birthday
Marking 250 years since Austen’s birth this romp through her irreverent Juvenilia is spliced with deliciously pompous gems from Aotearoa’s earliest newspapers.

From the drawing rooms of Georgian England to the dusty streets of Victorian Wellington – the pretensions of polite society never change.

To mark 250 years since the birth of Jane Austen, her wildly funny Juvenilia is brought to life, including The Beautifull Cassandra, The History of England, Love and Friendship – and more.

Between Austen’s sharpest barbs you’ll hear genuine gems from New Zealand’s early newspapers, courtesy of Papers Past: gossip, pomposity, early etiquette advice, and scandalous society mishaps.

The result? A sparkling, one hour romp proving that the absurdities of status, marriage and manners travel across oceans, continents and centuries.

Performed as a series of readings with lightning character swaps, sly narration, and just a hint of scandal, this is Austen as you’ve never heard her: young, bold, and perfectly at home in 19th century Wellington!


Booking is REQUIRED.
Cost: $25
Booking information here: https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/from-pemberley-to-pipitea-celebrating-jane-austens-250th-birthday/

description:
GROUNDWORK: an author talk with Michele Leggott and Catherine Field-Dodgson, Join us to hear authors Michele Leggott and Catherine Field-Dodgson discuss Emily Cumming Harris, the subject of their book 'Groundwork', and one of Aotearoa's most significant female artists of the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
Just as Emily Harris’s beautiful paintings occupy a liminal space between scientific botanical illustration and art, so this book occupies a shifting ground between biography and imagineered monograph. The result is often moving and always intriguing. Importantly, it restores to Aotearoa art history a figure who had almost disappeared.
Emily Harris has been examined alongside her artist peers Sarah Featon and Georgina Hetley, but until this book neither her distinctive voice nor her almost 200 surviving images have been heard or seen in any quantity outside of archival or online spaces.
Her life story is remarkable and her diaries, letters, poems and paintings constitute a fascinating legacy. In 'Groundwork', with its compelling text, they are lovingly brought together for the first time.
Michele and Catherine will be bringing copies of Emily's hand-coloured book 'New Zealand Flowers, Berries and Ferns' to display.

description:
Georgina Beyer - Diamonds are Forever Walk Tour, In 2004, Georgina Beyer, the first openly transgender Member of Parliament in the world, famously confronted members of Destiny Church during the Enough Is Enough rally on the grounds of Parliament.

Never a bystander, Georgina faced down the bigots, telling them straight, “Your hatred is totally intolerable!” This was just one of many significant moments that shaped the life of the extraordinary Georgina Beyer.

Born in Wellington, Georgina went on to have an unprecedented local, national and international impact through her commitment to equality and her desire to give everyone the opportunity to reach their full potential in society.

Join us for this special 90-minute walking tour as we pay tribute to the late Georgina (1957–2023) by visiting locations around central Wellington that shaped her journey. Along the way, we’ll honour some of her heroes and listen to first-hand archival audio clips that showcase her humour and resilience.

Georgina’s story is defiantly optimistic – confronting hardship and using her lived experience to change the world for the better.

Accessibility information: the tour is on flat public footpaths. Tours are limited to approximately 20 walkers.

Time/Date: 1pm, Saturday 21 March, 2026
Starts: meet outside St Peters Church, 211 Willis Street
Ends: Vivian Street
Duration: 90 minutes
Cost / Bookings: the tour is free but you do need to register

PLEASE REGISTER AT https://walktours.nz/book/
(if there are no registrations the tour won't go ahead)

Image courtesy of the amazing Kym Strathdee

Join us for our annual edu roadshow! Join Steve (Google) & Jack (Fusion) to learn AI basics, prompting & responsible use in the classroom.
What to expect
This half-day workshop gives you a practical introduction to Google Gemini and generative AI in education, delivered by Steve from Google and Jack from Fusion Networks.
You'll leave with the skills and confidence to use AI in your classroom and admin work, and you'll sit the Google Certified Gemini Educator exam right there in the session, no pressure, no separate booking.
Who it's for
Teachers, school leaders, and support staff who want practical, hands-on AI skills. No technical background needed.
What you'll learn
Understanding Gemini and generative AI
What generative AI is and how it's different from other tech
How Gemini fits into tools you already use, like Docs, Gmail, and Classroom
Where AI can genuinely save you time (planning, grading, feedback, communication)
Using Gemini in your day-to-day practice
Writing prompts that actually get you useful results
Creating quizzes, lesson outlines, and rubrics with Gemini
Building your own "Gem" for repeat classroom tasks, like bell-ringers or feedback frames
Drafting emails and staff communications faster
Using AI responsibly
Spotting bias, errors, and "hallucinations" in AI output
Talking to students about plagiarism and responsible AI use
Building your own classroom guidelines for AI
Sit your certification exam on the day
At the end of the session, you'll sit the Google Certified Gemini Educator exam in a relaxed, supported environment, straight after covering everything you need to know. No exam anxiety, no need to book or study separately later.
Format
Half-day, hands-on session. Bring a laptop and your Google Workspace login.

description:
Greytown Heritage House & Garden Tour, Greytown Heritage House & Garden Tour
Greytown is renowned for charming settler houses and lush gardens that thrive on rich alluvial soil.
The 2026 Greytown Heritage House and Garden Tour offers an opportunity to explore some of the town’s most remarkable properties.

Greytown Heritage Trust’s self-guided tour takes you through the gate and over the threshold – some of these houses will be opening publicly for the very first time.

So, spend an indulgent summer day weaving through the picturesque town’s streets, exploring our evident history. In joining us, you will be actively supporting the conservation of our heritage.
label: Community & Culture

description:
Greytown Heritage Trust House and Garden Tour 2026, This is another opportunity to explore charming Greytown houses and gardens where the owners have valued and enhanced the integrity of the building and its environment, and so nurtured Greytown's heritage.

Greytown Heritage Trust offers this self-guided tour, unveiling nine remarkable properties along with three destination events. A newly opened countryside café, spoiling with on-site baking, offers a pause looking out towards the Tararua range. A barbecue in a bucolic Waiohine setting. A fête, nostalgically redolent of yesteryear, selling perennials, crafts and home produce. There will be Devonshire cream teas and Wairarapa Rosé and bubbly, bunting, adventure and indulgence. How could you resist?
The houses are further flung than the previous tour and we listened hard to feedback – fewer destinations but greater distances will mean you’ll more comfortably explore this charming town and it’s houses and gardens.
You’re invited to spend a summer’s day exploring remarkable houses and gardens in this attractive town. In so doing you will contribute to a fundraiser for the refurbishment of Greytown's colonial-settler Kōuka Cottage (c1860) at Stella Bull Park, 113 Main Street, Greytown. This cottage and its maintenance are important in fostering Greytown's architectural heritage.
Receive with your ticket:
Access to 9 of Greytown’s significant private homes & gardens. Access to a fête, a café and a countryside barbecue.
A quality keepsake folding map & information poster. These will be posted to you nearer to the date.

General information & conditions
Properties are open from 10.00am until 4.30pm. This tour is self-guided; you can visit the properties in any order you wish.
Each ticket holder will be sent a map and wristbands for entry, by post. It is absolutely critical that you include your address on your Eventfinda registration and purchase of tickets.
At each venue you’re asked to present your wristband to the volunteers at the entrance to gain access. Please ensure that you are wearing your wristband during the tour as this will ensure your entry at each address. The wristband isn't transferable to other people during the tour events.
The houses, of course, are private homes. Photographs are available on the Greytown Heritage Trust’s media sites and we ask that you don’t take your own photographs inside houses, nor touch furnishings or items. Some areas will be inaccessible and signed accordingly. Some gardens may also be off limits for photography but this will be indicated at the venue.
Keeping people and property safe is important, this tour is reserved for those aged over 15. We’re also asking that no animals are brought to the visits unless they are mobility-trained and certified. Accessibility is compromised variously in houses and some gardens.
Greytown public toilets will be marked on the map.
The tour will proceed regardless of rain or other moderately poor weather but there may be a cancellation in the event of Met Office amber or red warnings. In this, what we hope is unlikely, event we will communicate with you by email and on social media sites.
Cash sales and some eftpos facilities will be available at some properties. The proceeds or proportions of these sales will also contribute to the fundraiser.
The Trust is grateful for your support, and wish you a wonderful day exploring and enjoying Greytown’s heritage properties.
Links
Website (for more heritage info):
https://www.greytownheritagetrust.co.nz/
Social Media (for sneak peaks of the tour):
https://www.instagram.com/greytownheritagetrust/
https://www.facebook.com/greytownheritagetrust

description:
Greytown Tales on Foot, Take a Walk Through Greytown’s History
This leisurely guided walk explores the early stories, streetscapes, and standout characters that shaped the town. We’ll begin and end at two of Greytown’s historic pubs — but along the way, you’ll also hear colourful tales of the ones that have disappeared from the streetscape. From original town-acre-allocations and early churches to hidden corners and colourful transformations, each stop brings the past vividly to life. We’ll pause at key sites to share visuals and stories that reveal the town’s unique beginnings and evolution.

Whether you’re a local or a visitor, you’ll come away with a fresh appreciation for one of New Zealand’s most historic town.

description:
Guided tour of the historic Bolton Street Cemetery - Tiptoe Through the Tombstones, Guided tour of the historic Bolton Street Cemetery - Tiptoe Through the Tombstones
Explore historic Bolton Street Cemetery in central Wellington (just off The Terrace) with experienced guides. Hear entertaining and surprising stories with Tiptoe Through the Tombstones.

Tiptoe Through the Tombstones, starting at the Seddon memorial on Sundays at 2.00pm. A fascinating tour of Wellington's early history. The stories go far beyond well-known names from history, giving glimpses of ordinary people who made their home here.

Seize this opportunity to learn more about NZ’s oldest town cemetery and the lives of some of its many and varied occupants, people who lived in nineteenth-century Wellington. Hear wonderful stories from our colonial past as well as a reminder of the disruption caused by the construction of Wellington's Urban Motorway. Settlers and Māori were buried in this beautiful heritage cemetery, and their headstones can give us intriguing information.

All Sunday tours leave from the Kinross Street entrance to the Cemetery. The tours finish at the little museum in lower Bolton Street, just off the Terrace.

Children 12 & under: free (no ticket required).

Well-behaved dogs on leads welcome.


Booking is REQUIRED.
Cost: $10
Booking information here: https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/guided-tour-of-the-historic-bolton-street-cemetery/


Health & Safety:
Follow the directions of your tour guide, and stay on paths. Old headstones and railings around graves can be unstable.

Please wear good shoes and dress for the weather. The tour may be cancelled in bad weather.

description:
Heritage tour at the Haunted Inverlochy House, Celebrate Halloween with a cuppa and a historic tour of the haunted Inverlochy House. Inverlochy House is a Victorian mansion designed by local architect Thomas Turnbull for a prominent local family in the late 1870s. In the early 1900s until 1980 it was divided into nine flats and known as the Inverlochy Flats. Since 1987 it has been the home of Inverlochy Art School. Inverlochy House has had a reputation for being haunted since the 1970s and has been the subject of an ongoing paranormal investigation by several NZ and international groups over the years.

Tour runs for approximately one hour. Stay in town to enjoy dinner at the local cafes in Te Aro.

description:
How do I learn? A lecture by Kimberley Moulton, Overview


Curator Kimberley Moulton reponds to how do I learn? in her lecture as part of AGENCY: A curatorial intensive in three questions.
This lecture is presented as part of AGENCY: A curatorial intensive in three questions How do I learn? How do I act? How do I imagine? presented by Artspace Aotearoa and Te Pātaka Toi Adam Art Gallery. Read more about the full symposium programme.
How I Learn: Restoring the Spirit of Collections and Place, an Indigenous space-time curatorial methodology.
There is a continuum of knowledge that manifests through contemporary practice and when artists and community activate object, space and place. These objects and sites can act as mnemonic portals of which we can walk between Ancestral space and today. In this lecture I will consider Indigenous temporality in relation to place and Ancestral belongings in museum collections and the role of contemporary artists in re-storying these spaces beyond the historic past and colonial centre. This Global Majority inter-cultural and space-time dialogue will consider an approach to curatorial work through my framework of restoring the spirit and consider deep-time relational ecologies and materialities that guide me in my practice. Sharing examples of recent projects that meet at the intersection of contemporary art, historical archive and place I will consider the way in which I learn from Country, community and collections.
Workshop participants already have a reserved place at this lecture and are not required to RSVP.
AGENCY: A curatorial intensive in three questions How do I learn? How do I act? How do I imagine? is presented by Artspace Aotearoa and Te Pātaka Toi Adam Art Gallery and supported by Chartwell Trust, Goethe Institut, National Services Te Paerangi, and Toi o Aotearoa Creative New Zealand Te Manu Ka Tau International Delegates Programme.

Biography
Dr Kimberley Moulton is a Yorta Yorta woman from Australia and a curator and writer. Kimberley is a respected international curator working across modern and contemporary art and historical collections. Leading research and curatorial practice in the field of connecting knowledge, histories and futures at the intersection of historical collections and contemporary art, her work centres regenerative re-worlding of art histories and ecological, cultural and relational Indigenous and Global Majority creative practices. She is currently Senior Curator Exhibitions at RISING, the Melbourne international arts festival and most recently held tenure as the Adjunct Curator Indigenous Art Tate London (2023-2026). She has a PhD in curatorial practice from Monash University Melbourne and in 2023 was appointed Curator Emeritus, First Peoples at Museums Victoria.Working with artists to amplify underrepresented art histories, her practice foregrounds connecting communities to collections, through rematriation and re-spiriting collections and place beyond the colonial past. This work has positioned Moulton at the forefront of local and international curatorial and writing praxis which supports contemporary art across multidiscipline areas to re-frame a new dialogue between object, place and community. Kimberley’s research interests include Indigenous rematriation, Ancestral belongings and restitution, Indigenous space-time cosmologies and embodied knowledge in contemporary art practice.Along with her curatorial work Kimberley is currently Deputy Chair of the Board for Australia’s leading regional art gallery, Shepparton Art Museum and Director of the board for the Adam Briggs Foundation.

description:
International Day of the Girl - 2025, You are Invited to our inaugural International Day of the Girl Fundraising to celebrate the work of Heartprint Cambodia.

The AquaPura Project is raising funds for a new Safe Water installation, and an Emergency Rapid Response Kit for Heartprint in Cambodia.
Heartprint is wholly aligned with AquaPura's mission to educate and provide technical training for girls to be safe water system installers and maintenance leads, so they are provided an opportunity to succeed in a male-dominated industry of essential water provision services.

The theme of International Day of the Girl Child 2025 is:
"The Girl I Am, the Change I Lead: Girls on the Frontline of Crisis". 

This theme was developed in consultation with girls' organisations, UN partners, and girls themselves.

This theme emphasise the leadership potential of girls and their role in driving positive change, particularly in the face of crisis. 

The International Day of the Girl, observed annually on 11th October, aims to highlight the challenges girls face globally, and promote their rights and empowerment. 

The 2025 theme specifically acknowledges the unique experiences and contributions of girls during times of crisis, recognising them as agents of change. 

This fundraiser will be led by Girls, who deeply understand the importance of delivering Safe Water for Every Child.
Heartprint is a not for profit organisation committed to improving living standards of underprivileged families in Cambodia. Heartprint takes a holistic approach to charity by building the Heartprint Community Centre. They are able to provide the support that looks at the whole family structure, not just the basic living needs, but also addressing their overall physical, emotional, social, and spiritual wellbeing.
