description:
Randell Cottage writers-in-residence 2025 — Part of Randell Cottage writer-in-residence series, Join author Saraid de Silva for an evening of conversation, readings, and video reflections from past Randell Cottage writers-in-residence, including Titaua Peu and Hinemoana Baker.
Join us at the Library or online. Register to receive a Zoom link: https://dia-nz.zoom.us/.../WN_p6_8lW8vSyOLAnFYTHhOgw...
A conversation with author Saraid de Silva
This year’s Randell Cottage writers-in-residence are Titaua Peu (French writer-in-resident) and Saraid de Silva (New Zealand writer-in-resident).
Join Saraid de Silva in conversation with Randell Cottage trustee Francis Cooke. Saraid will also read from her new novel, which promises to be very different from her first and acclaimed book Amma. But how different will it be from Amma’s stories that follow three generations of South Asian women? Saraid says her Untitled Second Novel is a revenge thriller about two best friends in a stolen car, crossing the country to crash a New Year’s Eve party.
Video reflections from former writers in residence
Following the conversation, French Cultural Counsellor, François Bockel, will present the latest in the series of short videos of writers-in-residence reflecting on their experience at Randell Cottage. Titaua Peu was the French writer-in-residence earlier this year, and New Zealander Hinemoana Baker was the 2024 New Zealand writer-in-residence.
The videos form part of Randell Cottage’s recorded oral history, designed to capture the essence of those writers and their interests while undertaking their fellowships.
RSVP to let us know you are coming
Light refreshments will be provided so RSVP before 1 December to info@randellcottage.co.nz.
Randell Cottage writer’s residency
Wellington’s historic Randell Cottage has been a writers’ residency for New Zealand and French writers since 2001. The Randell Cottage Writers Trust is supported by the New Zealand-France Friendship Fund/Arts Foundation of New Zealand, and the Wellington City Council. It works in close partnership with the Embassy of France.
About the speakers
Saraid de Silva is a Sri Lankan Pākehā writer and arts worker based in Tāmaki Makaurau. She was the co-creator and co-host of Radio New Zealand’s podcast and video series Conversations with My Immigrant Parents and has recently worked as a storyliner, script writer, and script editor on New Zealand television shows. Her first novel, Amma, was released in New Zealand and Australia by Hachette New Zealand in March 2024 and in the UK by Weatherglass Books in April 2024. It was long-listed for the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Literature in the Ockham Awards and the UK Women’s Prize for Fiction.
Titaua Peu is a Tahitian novelist who stayed in Randell Cottage during the first half of 2025 as the French writer-in-residence. She is working on a new series of books that present a near future marked by a reverse migration, one in which inhabitants of Aotearoa have migrated north to the island of Mangareva in French Polynesia following a great war. The first laureate from French Polynesia, Titaua is considered one of the principal French-speaking voices in the literature of the Pacific, with her writings focusing on Polynesian society, the impact of colonialism and the place of women.

description:
Retirement Reinvented, Whether you’re already retired, or planning ahead, this practical workshop will help you to reflect, re-envision and re-vitalise your life and develop a plan for your future, on your own terms. (NZ citizens and residents free with ID, all others pay $109).

In your middle years, working, retired or somewhere in between? What’s next? Life is about much more than work or leisure, but most of us have given little thought to what “retirement” might mean.

It’s difficult to speculate what may happen in the future, but we can be proactive and take control.
This course offers insights into how to make the most of our time once we’re less focused on career and/or child-rearing. It covers many of the issues people face when considering a move from current employment to a different lifestyle that includes more time to do the things we’ve always promised ourselves we’d do – “when we retire”.

After the workshop, you’ll be able to identify a number of common issues and potential ways to manage them when considering and planning your “rejuvenation”, rather than a retirement. We won’t cover financial planning, but will focus on some of the personal growth opportunities for living and making a conscious contribution to your community.

By the end of the day, you’ll have:
- Developed your own perspective on ageing and retirement in the 21st Century and identified what’s important to you
- Completed a personal life audit exercise and considered your strengths
- Explored possibilities in the major aspects of your life and identified potential challenges and strategies for overcoming them
- Developed a blueprint to maximise the best years of your life and developed a “future-proofing” downsizing plan
- Considered options to include a sense of purpose and explored and implemented choices that provide you with that sense of purpose
Bring a pen and paper.

1 day, Sat 9:30 AM – 4:00 PM
Wellington High School
Presented by Angela Robertson

description:
Robert Orr Historic Homestead Open Day, Robert Orr Historic Homestead Open Day
Step back in time and explore a piece of Lower Hutt’s past. Built in 1885, the home features artefacts collected by the family over generations.

Come and experience one of Lower Hutt’s hidden heritage treasures at our upcoming Open Day!

This 19th-century two-storey Italianate villa was designed by Charles Petrie for Robert Orr and built by Stephen Strand between 1885 and 1887. Constructed from native timbers—totara, rimu and matai—the house features a symmetrical design with two square bay windows flanking the main entrance. The once 17-acre estate became a thriving market garden employing up to 40 people, with most of the property then being subdivided in the 1960s.

Still a cherished family home, the villa is tucked away from the street and surrounded by beautiful historic gardens. During the Open Day, visitors are welcome to explore the home and grounds at their own pace with a self-guided visit. It’s the perfect opportunity to relax, discover, and connect with Lower Hutt’s rich past.

Miriam Tong, an artist and heritage enthusiast, will be on-site to illustrate a portrait of Robert Orr Historic Homestead. She is happy to stop and chat, but also happy for visitors to watch her working in fine ink pens, to capture the heritage house in its beautiful surroundings. Miriam has been drawing commissioned house portraits for 10 years and is gifting her time and artwork to the Wellington Heritage Festival Trust.


Cost: Koha

Event information here: https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/robert-orr-historic-homestead-open-day/

description:
Sacred Rewilding Forest circle 🎶 W ❤️ Shared picnic, Sacred Rewilding Forest circle 🎶 W ❤️ Shared picnic

What to Expect: Sacred Women's Circle


🌸Welcome, Sister. If you are feeling a pull in your heart to join us, that calling is your initiation.
Trust where you are being led. The circle lives within each of us.
Sacred Women's Circles have been used for thousands of years to build supportive communities, encourage authentic self-expression, and remind us that we are never alone on our journeys.

This is a dedicated, women-only gathering to honor our womb energy and embrace our sacred sisterhood.
Together, we step into a safe container to lower our walls, let our facades drop, and form real, authentic relationships rooted in vulnerability and trust.

✨ Meet Your Host: Crystal Mihinui
Your space is held by Crystal Mihinui, a dedicated practitioner with over 40 years of profound experience in music, frequency, and energy work. Crystal weaves her extensive background into every circle to create a deeply safe, transformative container for your healing. Her unique medicine includes:
Reiki Master: Channeling universal life force energy to restore balance and harmony to your body, mind, and spirit.

Music Therapist & Classically Trained Pianist: Using a lifetime of technical mastery and a deep understanding of musical psychology to shift emotional blocks and soothe the nervous system.
Sound Healing Practitioner: Blending acoustic frequencies to guide you into profound states of meditation, relaxation, and inner awakening.

🌿 The Journey & Flow
Gathering at our beautiful, secret forest spot surrounded by native trees, birds, and mountains, our flow includes
Sacred Circle & Oracle Cards: Opening our space with Archangel cards, inviting in nature spirits, and honoring our ancestors.
Womb Healing: Activating our deep feminine intuition using womb mudras and sacred mantras.
Shamanic Sound Journey: A deeply restorative guided meditation powered by crystal singing bowls and energy healing from the realm of the Fae.
Sisterhood Sharing: Returning to the circle to softly share our experiences, stories, and wisdom.
Ritual Releasing what no longer serves us by offering our written words to the sacred forest.

Forest Bathing & Journaling: Immersion in the healing frequencies of nature.📍

Location & Meeting Points
We have two meeting point options, both provided upon booking.
You can choose to:
Meet at our cozy home-based studio to rideshare together
Or meet directly at our beautiful outdoor location in Rivendell.☔

Rain Plan: If the wild weather joins us, we will move to our beautiful indoor alternative (details provided upon booking).🎒

What to Bring
A shared vegetarian dish to enjoy together during our gathering
A journal and pen for your reflections
Comfortable clothing suitable for the forest.
Swimming gear (if you would like to take a dip! 🏖).🎟

Investment & Inclusivity Children's Tickets: Children are very welcome to join our sacred space and are half price.
Community Services Card: Concession tickets are gladly available; please bring your proof of entitlement on arrival

Cancellation Policy: As a small, heart-led family business, our time is precious. Tickets are non-refundable, but you are deeply welcome to gift your ticket to another sister if you cannot make it.

description:
Salsa Magic’s Friday Fiesta - Palladium Edition, Join us for another fun night of social dancing with DJ Rafa, playing the grooviest Mambo, Salsa, and Bachata tracks! Emphasis on the MAMBO
Tonight we celebrate the Palladium era of Latin dance! Known as “the home of the Mambo,” the Palladium Ballroom was America’s most important venue for the development of Latin music and dance throughout the 1950s.
Mambo music and dance were co-created at the Palladium where Puerto Rican, Cuban, Dominican, Italian, Jewish, Irish, and African American patrons danced nightly to music from the “Big Three” Latin orchestras: Tito Puente, Tito Rodríguez, and Machito.
You can expect lots of Mambo and all-around good vibes!
$12 entry
DJ Rafa
Something classy or flashy (totally optional)
BYO drinks (but please keep them off the dance floor)
Salsa Magic's Friday Fiestas are held on the second Friday of every month and are a staple in the Wellington Latin dance community. All levels of experience and styles are welcome!

description:
Sapphic Speed Dating Dinner Party, This 4-course sapphic experience is more like a big gay dinner party than a traditional speed dating event (it even features fabulous local performer, Ginger Velour, as the MC to guide you through the evening!) With each course in the meal, you’ll switch tables and sit with a new group of 4-6 cute strangers—although it’s Wellington, so no guarantees it won’t be your ex. There will be conversation question cards on the tables if you get stuck on what to say, but your best chats will come from just being yourself!

And don’t stress about asking a hottie for their number if you’re shy—we’ve designed this experience to be as easy and low-stakes as possible. Each attendee will have a paper bag “mailbox” that you can slip a note into at the end of the night to avoid any awkward face-to-face interactions. Whether you both want to connect after that is up to you, but this is the time to shoot your shot!

After purchasing a ticket, you will be sent a short questionnaire. Please fill it out promptly! This helps the organisers place you in groups with similar interests so you have the best chance at finding what you’re looking for.

No TERFs no SWERFs. This event is open to all people 18+ who identify as sapphic/lesbian/queer. Bi, pan, questioning, and ace folks are all welcome.

Additional info:
- Most dietary requirements can be accommodated by the amazing chefs at Everybody Eats. Please include your dietaries when prompted in the questionnaire.
- Accessibility: Everybody Eats is up a flight of stairs and does not have wheelchair access. There are gender neutral bathrooms inside the restaurant and all chairs have backs. If you'd prefer not to stand up and move around the space after each course, please email the organiser with any mobility requests at goldenhourgigz@gmail.com

description:
September Full Moon Drumming, Please remember this is a ZERO WASTE and *NO ALCOHOL* community gathering.
Kia ora!
Full Moon Drumming Wellington is a registered public event with the Wellington City Council. We are a group of humans from all walks of life who gather under the full moon each month to connect through drumming and dance around the fire. This gathering is participatory, that means if you made it to the circle you are part of the circle. As in Africa, there is no audience! Everyone is invited to participate as part of the ‘chorus’ (singing/clapping), dancing, or drumming.
The event is weather permitting, we check the forecast a few days prior and aim to make a decision the day before the event, although this is not possible and sometimes we make the decision on the day. All updates are posted on the event page.
This gathering is entirely run by volunteers, if you'd like to contribute in any way please get in touch.
There are a few things that we need help with:
- FIREWOOD: Please bring dry firewood as a koha, no wood no fire! Please NOTE we DO NOT burn pallets (due to nails) or treated timber. Driftwood from nearby south coast beaches is often abundant, feel free to post or reach out if you have a vehicle and are keen to help gather firewood on the day of the event.
- BEAUTIFYING THE CIRCLE SPACE: Anyone has fairy lights, oil burners, or is keen to make some signs?
NOTE: We hold a fire permit for this event. For safety reasons we don't allow participants to feed the fire, and while is generally okay to roast some marshmallows early in the evening we don't allow the use the fire for cooking or heating food.
This is an **ALCOHOL FREE EVENT**, please help us uphold this kaupapa and remind those who are unaware and might be new to the event. As hosts we are responsible for your safety and we take that responsibility seriously, especially given that the event is authorised through both fire and event permits. Large, public, all ages gatherings require administration and logistics so please respect this and the guidelines provided.
Princess Bay is within Taputeranga Marine Reserve (https://octopus.org.nz/taputeranga-marine-reserve), we are welcomed to gather each month in this special place so let’s all make sure there is NO RUBBISH LEFT BEHIND and that we take care of the space. Dogs are NOT ALLOWED at the gathering - there are Korora (Blue Pinguins) nesting under the rocks nearby and we've had issues with dogs in the past.
Children are welcome at the fire, though, especially after dark, please make sure that all children have adult supervision, that the supervisors are aware of the children they are looking after, and that the children are aware of who is looking after them.
Feel free to bring:
- Your friends.
- Drums or any percussive instrument.
- Warm clothing; jackets and wool blankets are good.
- Something to seat on (otherwise sand is often wet)
- Drinking water.
- Food, tea to share.
- Your lovely selves.
- Fire spinning kit and fuel.
FIRE SPINNERS: Please take all precautionary safety measures and make sure to set up fire-spinning downwind from the fire circle.
PARKING: There's a parking lot a few hundred meters from the fire circle where there's also public toilets. Please also be aware of our neighbors driveway opposite the stairway and do not park directly in front of it.
CARPOOLING: If you don't have a way to get to Princess Bay, or if you have spare seats in your car, feel free to post it on the event page. The less cars driving the better.
Feel free to share the event page and send an event invite to whomever you feel would be interested, not everyone sees the notifications and advertising

 🏗️ The Process: How raw materials like cement, aggregates & water are mixed to create concrete
⚙️ Batching & Mixing: How mix designs are selected and adjusted
📏 Quality: Quality controls & production oversight, including testing & slumping
🚚 Dispatch:  Loading, scheduling & delivery coordination

description:
Site Visit - Studio of Pacific Architecture - Te Aro Double-Header!, Join us on Wednesday 20 August, for an exclusive NAWIC members-only site tour of two very different but geographically close projects in Te Aro. The National War Memorial and FPC Martin Square are both undergoing major refurbishment - join us for a look behind the scenes!
National War Memorial: Refurbishing a Wellington Icon
Step behind the scaffolding and witness the National War Memorial Project – a complex seismic strengthening project where heritage sensitivity is of utmost importance. With construction works being carried out by Maycroft Construction, join us for the rare opportunity to explore a significant piece of the capital’s cultural fabric.
Known to many as the backdrop of ANZAC Day commemorations, this national memorial is undergoing a meticulous refurbishment to ensure its legacy endures for generations to come.
 What’s Happening On Site:
Seismic strengthening of the tower and bell frame 
Stone remediation to preserve its historic façade
Asphalt roofing works
The real challenge? Balancing modern engineering with heritage preservation. Every upgrade is being carried out with deep respect for the building’s historical significance.

Then, just around the corner, we will move on to another refurbishment project – at a much different scale and for a very different purpose!
 FPC Martin Square: from Workshop to Office Space
Leading industrial design-and-build specialists First Principles Constructors are celebrating seven years of innovation with a bold move - into a brand-new headquarters in central Wellington. Take a look inside the transformation of a former engineering workshop into the new HQ for FPC. With exposed services, raw materials, and an industrial aesthetic, this compact yet clever refurbishment shows how much can be achieved in a small urban footprint. Construction is well underway by Aoraki Construction, with completion coming up in September.
What’s Happening On Site:
•     Structural steel installation, new roofing, cladding, a new concrete mezzanine slab
•     Interior fit-out works
•     Full building services upgrades

Our event kicks off at 6.30pm with a drink and a mingle before we split into two areas of the restaurant for the serious dating

description:
Social Sewing Saturday - April, Social Sewing Saturday - April
Come join us for a fun-filled day of sewing and socializing at Karori Arts & Crafts!

About this Event

Come join us for a fun-filled day of sewing and socializing at Karori Arts & Crafts!
Come join us for a fun-filled day of sewing and socializing at Karori Arts & Crafts! Whether you're a seasoned pro or just starting out, this event is perfect for anyone who loves to sew. Bring your latest project or start something new - either way, you'll have a blast chatting with fellow sewing enthusiasts. Bring your current project or get inspired by others' creations at our friendly gathering. Share tips, tricks, and stories while working on our projects together.
Don't forget to pack your sewing machine, fabric, and any other supplies you'll need. We can't wait to see what you create! You will need to bring your own machine and materials. Please bring an extension lead and multipoint box if you have one. (Don't worry, though—we have some in the centre, too!) We'll supply an iron and ironing board to share, as well as a table and relatively comfy chair each. There are also spare cutting-out tables at a taller height. You are welcome to come along and work on hand-sewing projects.
A kitchen is available on site and supermarkets as well as cafes are very close by.Parking is free and there are 3 dedicated spaces for the centre as well as others closeby.
Cost: Free for members of the Karori Arts Centre or $15 per person payable directly to KACC. (Membership of the centre is $105 annually and also gives you reductions on classes and access to other groups)
Please do NOT attend if you are sick (even just a little bit!)

Social-quizm: A May Day Quiz Night, Join Unions Wellington and Reception (the new organising space in Trades Hall) to celebrate International Workers Day (“May Day”) with a pub quiz!
Hosted by comedian and union organiser Tim Keats, this May Day event is sure to rival the heady summer of ‘68.
Drinks, dinner and new merch available!
Win swagged out union prizes by aceing the quiz or through sheer luck in one of our raffles!
Proceeds will be split between Unions Wellington (to run their general election and Wellington Works campaigns) and Reception (to keep the lights on).
Ticket info:
Snacks will be provided on quiz tables.
You can purchase a ticket that includes dinner (if you do not preorder dinner, you may be able to have leftovers, but we will not be doing dinner tickets on the night)
Tickets can be individually purchased, or you can buy a team ticket, max team size is 8 people.
If you don’t have a team of 8 - you can still quiz as a smaller team OR we can add other team members to your team on the day for you.
If you are an individual - we will match you with an existing team, and/or support you to create an alliance with other individuals.
Drinks, Merch and Raffle tickets will be sold separately at the event!
When: 6:00PM Friday, 1 May 2026
Where: City of Wellington Pipe Band Hall, corner Stoke/Hanson St, Newtown
Who: Anyone who wants to support two great union causes.

description:
Soiree at the Zoo; A Night for our Whanau and Animals, Are you ready to take a walk on the wild side? Be a rebel with a cause?
Join Ronald McDonald House Charities® New Zealand (RMHC® NZ) and Te Nukuao Wellington Zoo for our joint fundraiser, 'Soirée at the Zoo: A night for our families and animals.’ RMHC NZ and Wellington Zoo have a long history of working together in the community. We wanted to secure the future of the work we do by hosting this fundraiser, as we approach nearly a decade of partnership.
We are excited to bring you an epic night of glitz, good vibes and an action-packed live auction with some fabulous prizes, all to raise much-needed funds for RMHC NZ and Wellington Zoo.
Date: 22 November 2025
Time: 6.30pm – 11.00pm
Location: Wellington Zoo, 200 Daniell Street, Newtown, Wellington 6021
BUY TICKETS NOW to secure your spot and get ready to:
• Explore the zoo after hours
• Enjoy delicious canapés with a complimentary welcome drink
• Feel the electric excitement of the live auction and raffle
• Let your hair down and hit the dance floor with some choice local music
• Mix and mingle with your friends and some familiar Wellingtonian faces
• Be captivated by the journey of a local RMHC NZ whānau and Wellington Zoo
• And much more!
By attending our Soirée, you'll be making a real difference as all proceeds raised will be shared equally between RMHC NZ and Wellington Zoo.
Every day, RMHC NZ provides families with a child in hospital a ‘home-away-from-home'. RMHC NZ supports over 4,400 Kiwi families every year, keeping them together during their toughest times.
Te Nukuao Wellington Zoo welcomes families using RMHC NZ services to the Zoo for free, through our community partnership. Each year, over 400 adults and kids come to spend time with animals in nature. The zoo is a place of healing for over 250,000 people each year, including whānau from RMHC NZ.
Get ready for an unforgettable evening that makes a real impact! With only 150 tickets available, make sure you seize the day and secure yours!
We can’t wait to see you there!
label: Community & Culture

description:
Soirée at the Zoo: A Night for our Whānau & Animals, Te Nukuao Wellington Zoo and Ronald McDonald House Charities® (RMHC®) New Zealand invite you to an exclusive fundraising event: Soirée at the Zoo: A Night for our Whānau & Animals.

Join the two charities for a refined evening of celebration and generosity, where compassion for people and care for wildlife come together in a truly unique setting.

Buy your tickets now!

Guests will experience Te Nukuao Wellington Zoo after hours, enjoy elegant hospitality, and take part in an inspiring night of entertainment and giving, all in support of Wellington families and animals.

What to expect:
- A rare opportunity to explore Wellington Zoo after hours! Join an exclusive Zoo tour and discover the Zoo from a whole new perspective.
- A complimentary welcome drink and delicious canapés throughout the evening
- An engaging live auction and raffle with exceptional prizes
- An entertaining MC, live local music and a chance to dance the night away
- Opportunities to connect with friends, colleagues, and familiar Wellington faces
- The moving story of a local RMHC® NZ whānau
- An insight into Te Nukuao Wellington Zoo’s vital conservation mahi in Aotearoa and around the world

This fundraising event will make a tangible difference to Wellington families and animals. All proceeds from Soirée at the Zoo will be shared equally between Ronald McDonald House Charities® New Zealand and Te Nukuao Wellington Zoo.

Every day, RMHC® NZ provides a home-away-from-home for more than 100 families, offering comfort, care, and stability during difficult times. Your attendance — and your generosity on the night — will directly support families with essential accommodation and meals.

Through their community partnership, Te Nukuao Wellington Zoo welcomes RMHC® NZ families to the Zoo at no cost. Each year, over 400 adults and tamariki visit the Zoo to reconnect with nature and the restorative power of wildlife, joining the 250,000 people annually who experience the Zoo as a place of wellbeing and inspiration.

With only 150 seats available, this will be an unforgettable evening of purpose and celebration.

Secure your place today and be part of a night that supports whānau, wildlife, and the community that connects us all.

Buy your tickets now!

Invoicing options are also available; please email venues@wellingtonzoo.com for more information.

Please note: Event data will be shared with both RMHC® NZ and Te Nukuao Wellington Zoo.

description:
Soldier Stories Walk, Join eminent historian Neil Frances for a not-to-be-missed walk exploring the history of the Featherston Cemetery and the men who lie at rest there. The cemetery contains 182 Commonwealth war graves, the bulk of them of men who died in the Featherston Military Camp from 1916 to 1919, including many deaths from the November 1918 influenza epidemic. Each tour is limited to 30 visitors.. Tour limited to 30 visitors. Free entry.
A Featherston Heritage Festival Event

description:
Solo travellers: casual hangout in Wellington (4pm), No pressure, no plan—just new friends

Whether you’re visiting Wellington for the first time, recently relocated, or simply love connecting with curious people, this weekly meetup is the perfect way to share stories, make friends, and go explore, as a group, the magic that Wellington has to offer

What to expect?
• Casual & hostless: no formal host, no schedule: just show up, be yourself, meet fellow solo travellers & expats and decide as a group where you feel like going
• Central meeting point: it is surrounded by cultural landmarks, cafes, and restaurants, making it a convenient and safe starting point.
• Open to everyone: whether you are a local, an expat or just passing through for a few days, you are welcome to join. (English is the primary language, but feel free to switch of course)

How to talk with strangers?
(and create meaningful connections)
To help you get started, I curated a little game of ridiculously good questions you can ask to break the ice, shift the conversation from dull to intriguing and fun, and eventually create meaningful connection quickly. I hope this helps!
www.pierrebonvalot.com/good-questions

The only things you need to do are…
• Leave a message in the comment section to let the others know that you will actually be there (I don’t want you to end up alone there

• If you can’t make it anymore, no problem! But please update your RSVP to let the others know
• Please be gentle and patient with each other. We all want to make good friends here.

Why join?
• Meet open-minded travellers and locals who are keen to connect, learn and have fun together.
• Experience Wellington... as a group.
• Be part of a global community that celebrates solo travelling and meaningful connections between foreign and locals.

How does it works?
1. Arrive at the meeting spot at the scheduled time.
2. Look for other joiners—friendly faces and curious explorers.
3. Introduce yourself, connect with others, and decide as a group where to go.

When & where?
• Day: every Sunday
• Time: 4:00 PM (meetup sometimes displays a different time zone: but it’s always 4pm local time)
• Location: in front of the Albatross Fountain
Hostless: I am setting up the event for you all to meet, but I won't be there myself this time

Hi my name is Pierre
I created this Meetup group because I want to see more human connection happen in the real world. I feel many of us want this, but don't exactly know how to go about it. I hope this helps a little bit.
I also work as a coach: I help people who feel stuck in their life to reconnect with themselves, create real change and ultimately live more fulfilling lives.

We’ll provide scrapbooking materials, but we encourage you to bring your own treasures. Items like stencils, photos, poems, and Aotearoa-inspired artwork are all welcome.
Join us to highlight shared culture through art, music, hopeful messages, and reflections on solidarity here at home.
This drop-in session continues the spirit of our Nakba Day gathering - connecting, reflecting, and expressing care. Expect warmth, soup, bread, tea, incense, beautiful music, and space to stay until late. This event is open to all ages.

description:
South Wairarapa Half Day Tour - Afternoon, Journey with us through the breathtaking landscapes of South Wairarapa, where every hill, river, and breeze carries a story. Our guided experience weaves together the rich history of the land, the life-giving waters, and discover the ancestral stories. Learn about the deep connections between people and environment. Our half day tours invites you to see, feel, and respect this region in a way that stays with you long after you leave.

This tour is a travelling tour. We pick you up from Featherston Train Station 10 minutes before the event starts and we will deliver you back to Featherston Train Station on finishing.

Please ensure you bring comfy shoes, warm clothes and sun protection. Water Bottles are encouraged and refreshments will be provided throughout the trip.

Speed Puzzle fundraiser for CanSurvive Dragon Boat Club, Join us for CanSurvive’s very first speed puzzling event!
Each team receives the same 500-piece puzzle and races to complete it as fast as they can.
You can have up to three people in a team and there’s a two-hour time limit.
Our unique puzzle design is top secret and stays covered until the timer starts and you can rip into it! What we can tell you is that we’ve created a beautiful new design in collaboration with New Zealand artist Lori Davis, and it’s been produced by New Zealand’s premium puzzle company, PieceHouse.
The best bit… anyone can join in! Whether you’re a speedy puzzler or prefer to take your time over a cuppa, you won’t regret giving it a go.
So, what are you waiting for? You can puzzle solo or team up with family and friends to meet like-minded puzzlers - and a few dragonboaters! - for a fun afternoon you won’t forget.
As well as the main event, we’ll have bonus puzzles on the go for the super speedy, there’s a kitchen on site for refreshments and there’ll be a raffle and CanSurvive goodies to buy, including our new puzzle - because why share the puzzle that's included with your ticket when every team member could have their own?

description:
Spring Céilí Dance with The Great Beag Céilí Band, Spring has sprung, the days are getting longer, the rain is falling sideways. Must be about time we had another céilí! Join The Great Beag Céilí Band at St Michael’s Hall in Kelburn for a rousing evening of dancing to foot-stomping celtic tunes. Our Autumn céilí sold out so make sure you get your tickets early!
If you’ve never been to a céilí (or ceilidh) before, fear not - céilí dancing is very easy! No fancy moves or any previous experience required: our caller will explain each dance, and we’ll all walk it through a couple of times before adding the music.
This is social dancing so bring all your friends! No need to bring a specific partner - there’ll be lots of friendly people to dance with.
Discounted online tickets are available on Humanitix until midnight on September 26th: $24 / $16 concession
https://events.humanitix.com/beag-ceili-spring-ceili-2025
Some door sales may be available on the day: $30 / $20 concession (cash only)
—
Doors open 7:30pm
Adults and age 10+ welcome. Under 16s accompanied by an adult.
Light refreshments will be available. We recommend bringing a water bottle to grab a quick drink between dances - hydration is key!
This is an alcohol-free event.
Getting here: St Michael’s Hall is located at 81 Upland Road in Kelburn Village, just behind the church.
There is very limited on-street parking in the village. We recommend public transport: the 4, 18, 21, and 22 buses stop regularly right outside coming up from Te Aro or down from Northland and Karori.
Be safe online: Tickets are only available online from the Humanitix event. Do not buy tickets from other sources such as Facebook comments or resale sites - these are always scams. If you can no longer attend, please contact us via Humanitix, our socials, or email to discuss refunds.
Health notice: Céilí dancing is a great way to meet lots of people. If you are feeling unwell then please stay home and rest this time, we will see you at the next one.

Mr. Gerry Brownlee M.P., Speaker of the House of Representatives is delighted to host IBNNZ, The Irish Business Network of New Zealand and The Friends of Ireland - The Tara Trust at a special gala luncheon celebration of St Patrick’s Day, on Tuesday 17th March 2026 from 12 – 2pm. The luncheon will be held in the Legislative Council Chamber at Parliament with all proceeds of this event going to support the work of the Tara Trust and the Friends of Ireland.
The Tara Trust is a registered charity and exists to support the Irish Community in New Zealand through its support of Irish arts, culture and the welfare of the Irish diaspora.
Join the Rt. Hon. Mr. Gerry Brownlee M.P., Speaker of the House of Representatives, and our special guests H. E. Ms. Jane Connolly, Ambassador of Ireland to New Zealand, along with Mr. Noel Grealish, T.D., Minister of State at the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine, and IBNNZ for this special celebration of Ireland and New Zealand’s strong and shared links.

description:
Suffrage Day Walking Tour Bolton Street Cemetery, It's Suffrage Day on Friday 19 September, marking the day in 1893 when New Zealand became the first self-governing country in the world to grant women the right to vote in parliamentary elections.

To celebrate our pioneer women, and those who signed the Suffrage Petition in 1893, we're taking a walk through the cemetery, talking about the roles of settler women from 1840 onwards.

We'll meet at the Seddon Memorial at the top of the cemetery (by Anderson Park) in time to set off at 11.00am, and we'll finish at the Museum in Bolton Street about 12.30pm.

This tour is suitable for all ages, but full mobility is required. Cost $10 per person, children under 12 free, and good dogs on leads welcome.

description:
Sunset Guided Tour, Experience Stonehenge Aotearoa at its most breathtaking — as the sun dips below the Wairarapa horizon.
Our Sunset Guided Tour blends astronomy, storytelling, and the natural beauty of twilight for an evening you will never forget.

Led by one of our knowledgeable guides, this 90-minute experience explores how ancient cultures used the Sun to track time and mark the turning of the seasons. You’ll discover the scientific and cultural thinking behind the Henge’s unique Southern Hemisphere design before watching the sunset alignment from inside the stone circle.

Weather permitting, you’ll witness how the setting Sun interacts with the structure — a striking moment that links ancient knowledge with the rhythms of the natural world.

Duration and Schedule
• Allow: Approximately 90 minutes
• Start Time: Begins one hour before sunset
• Availability: Offered any day with advance booking

Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui opening weekend, Join us over the opening weekend to celebrate the return of our much-loved central library, Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, and the reopening of Te Ngākau Civic Square.
Be amongst the first to explore the incredible new spaces to read, work, meet, relax and create – our new Makerspaces, galleries, recording studio, Tō Tātou Pōneke (new home for City Archives), Nōku te Ao Capital E's play space, OnTV and Media Lab, rawa (commissioned artwork), the new Reading Room and Ngā Pou Ruahine, our specialist collections including those for Tamariki Children and for Taiohi Youth, and of course all the books!
Take a moment to enjoy the revitalised plaza area of Te Ngākau Civic Square, featuring new landscaping, seating, play areas, and water features.
On offer throughout the weekend will be exhibitions, live jazz, taonga puoro, storytelling and waiata, as well as demos and tours of the new spaces.
The new cafe, Central Ground, will be open on the ground floor from 10am-4pm for food and beverage purchases (the cafe is cashless).
At 10am on Saturday 14 March, the Mayor will formally open Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui outside the building in a brief civic ceremony. A massed choir of 300+ singers will then welcome the first Wellingtonians as they come through the doors.
It might get busy at Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui over the opening weekend, so please be patient if there is a queue.
Visit tematapihi.govt.nz for more details.
Make sure you visit us over the weekend!

description:
Tension in Te Matapihi - Mystery in the Library, Are you a fan of great storytelling? The Ngaio Marsh Awards, in association with Wellington City Libraries, invites booklovers to a fascinating and fun evening of criminally good conversation at Te Matapihi Central Library featuring terrific Kiwi writers.
Two-time Ngaio Marsh Award winning author Jennifer Lane will chair fellow Ngaio winners Brannavan Gnanalingam (Best Novel for SPRIGS), Claire Baylis (Best First Novel for DICE), and 3x winner Michael Bennett, along with Verb Festival founder and kids' author Claire Mabey, and debut novelist Jennifer Trevelyan for a thrilling kōrero about how they craft memorable characters and page-turning storylines, and infuse their tales with deep insights into people and society. We're excited to whisper there has been a very special last-minute guest added to the panel.
WHEN: Thursday 30 April 2026
WHERE: Te Matapihi Ki Te Ao Nui | Central Library, 65 Victoria Street, Te Aro, Wellington
WHEN: 5.30pm
This is a free event.
Brannavan is a Wellington novelist, freelance writer, and property lawyer who was born in Sri Lanka and grew up in Lower Hutt. He's written eight novels, been listed for the Ockham New Zealand Book Awards three times, and won the 2021 Ngaio Marsh Award for Best Novel for SPRIGS, which examined the aftermath of a brutal act of sexual violence. His latest novel is political satire THE LIFE AND OPINIONS OF KARTIK POPAT, published in late 2024.
Claire Mabey is a children's writer, books editor for The Spinoff, and founder of literary festival Verb Wellington. In 2020 Mabey received a Ghost Light Award at the Wellington Theatre Awards, and has been described as "a force of nature in the Wellington arts community". Her middle-grade novel THE RAVEN'S EYE RUNAWAYS won Best First Book at the 2025 NZ Book Awards for Children and Young Adults, among other accolades. The sequel, THE RAVEN'S EYE REBELLION will be published in April 2026.
Jennifer T has a background in photography and children's publishing, and is now a full-time writer living in Wellington, with her husband, son, daughter, dog and cat. When not at her writing desk Jennifer can be found in the garden. Her debut novel A BEAUTIFUL FAMILY became part of a bidding war by global publishers, and was published internationally in 2025.
Claire Baylis is a Rotorua author and legal researcher who won 2024 Ngaio Marsh Award for Best First Novel for DICE, a courtroom drama written as part of her PhD in creative writing from the Institute of Modern Letters. Claire studied then lectured in law for 12 years before moving to Rotorua, where she's been a researcher for the Trans-Tasman Jury Study and set up a water safety programme focused on low-decile schools.
Michael is an award-winning filmmaker and novelist (Ngati Pikiao, Ngati Whakaue) who has won three Ngaio Marsh Awards, across nonfiction and fiction categories - for his true crime work IN DARK PLACES (2017 Best Non-Fiction), detailing the story of Teina Pora, as well as his first two novels starring Māori sleuth Hana Westerman, BETTER THE BLOOD (2023 Best First Novel) and CARVED IN BLOOD (2025 Best Novel). He is co-writer of Irish-NZ crime drama The Gone, and his crime novels have been translated into several languages, been shortlisted for the Acorn Prize for Fiction and several other awards on four continents.
Jennifer Trevelyan is a Wellington short story writer and novelist who was born in rural Australia but has now spent more of her life in Aotearoa. Her debut ALL OUR SECRETS won a Ngaio Marsh Award for Best First Novel, and Jennifer also contributed to crime and thriller anthology DARK DEEDS DOWN UNDER 2. Her novel MIRACLE won the 2024 Ngaio Marsh Award for Best Kids/YA.

description:
The Coven Ball: Leather & Lace, The Coven Ball is Back – And Naughtier Than Ever!

Get ready to unleash your inner vixen at Coven: Leather & Lace – our most seductive event of the year returns for its second spellbinding edition!

Expect a night full of provocative delights: dazzling burlesque performances, flash tattoos, a spanking booth (yes, really!), and tantalizing treats lurking around every dark corner. And don’t forget – there are spot prizes for the fiercest looks, so bring your best Leather or Lace fantasy.

Who’s it for?
Coven is a celebration crafted exclusively for queer women and gender minorities. Whether you’re sapphic, trans, nonbinary, genderqueer – this is your night to shine.

Evening Highlights:
- 7pm Cocktail Hour: Fabulous arrival photos, sip on our sexy drink specials and soak in the vibes with live sapphic music.
- An evening of entertainment from burlesque, to the kinkier kind, and flash tattoos by an incredible local artist
- Our infamous dessert grazing table

Tickets are strictly limited – and they WILL sell out. Secure yours now and don’t miss the queer event everyone will be talking about.

Coming Solo? You’re Not Alone.
Don’t be nervous if you’re planning to come on your own – Coven is built for connection. Whether it’s your first queer event or your hundredth, you’ll be surrounded by a community that gets it. From the moment you arrive, there’ll be friendly faces, welcoming vibes, and plenty of chances to mingle, and connect. Coven is about belonging – and there’s a place here for you.

Coven Kaupapa
For queer women and gender minorities, spaces like this are rare, vital, and sometimes, life-changing. In a world that constantly centers cishet norms, Coven offers a space where we are the default – where you can fully show up as yourself, be seen, celebrated and surrounded by YOUR community.

For many in our Coven, this is one of the only opportunities we feel comfortable enough to experience nightlife free from the male gaze, tokenism, fear, or the need to shrink ourselves to fit in. It’s a space where sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people aren’t just welcomed – we are centered. It’s for those who are often pushed to the margins, who rarely feel represented in “inclusive” spaces that still cater to the mainstream.

This night exists because we need it – and because we create it, together.

Accessibility
The event is held upstairs at Whisky & Wood, a stunning venue with gender-neutral bathrooms and lift access (note there is a small bump as you enter). Staff will be ready to help if needed. Have specific accessibility needs? Reach out directly at hello@whiskyandwood.co.nz.

Community Tickets
We want Coven to be for everyone. At checkout, consider donating toward our community ticket fund. Can’t afford a ticket? Email willysmackntush@gmail.com with the subject “Free for Me” and your preferred name. We’ll be gifting free tickets on Friday 18 October.

If you made it this far... Good girl / Good they / Good boy / Good YOU!
Get ready for a night of queer joy, sexy surprises, and community magic.

description:
The Epic Life of Kahe Te Rau-o-te-Rangi, Te Waka Huia Wellington Museum is excited to have Miria Pōmare share the beautiful tāonga of her family’s story for Wellington Heritage Festival.

Miria comes from a long line of influential wāhine Māori. Her namesake, Lady Mīria Pōmare (1877-1971), was a community leader who spent much of her life advocating for the benefits of both Māori and Pākeha. In 1918, Lady Mīria was appointed an OBE for her service to the Māori Soldiers’ Fund which was established to help provide soldiers with comfort (food, knitted garments, letters) while they were away from home. Lady Mīria Pōmare’s story is shared in a display in the Attic of Te Waka Huia.

Hear the life story of modern-day Miria’s tupuna and great Rangatira Kahe who was one of five women who signed Te Tiriti in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. Nau mai, haere mai to hear more about this Mana Wāhine and her truly epic life.

Join us on this free 90-minute community walk-tour as we trace Carmen's Wellington years (1967-1980). We'll visit some of the remaining inner-city business locations and imagine some of those that are no longer here: Le Balcon, Carmen's International Coffee Lounge, The Peacock, Cleopatra's Coffee Lounge, Carmen's Bazaar, The Gazebo massage parlour, The Cottage brothel and Carmen's Curio Shop.

Learn about Carmen's landmark 1966 court case, her race to become Mayor of Wellington in the 1970s, and how she supported and offered a safe harbour to Wellington's Takatāpui LGBTI Rainbow communities.

“I would more or less hypnotise all my guests like a black widow spider and trap my clients caught in my web. As people left my coffee lounge at 6am or earlier I would splash them with Carmen’s exotic juice which meant that they would be back another night for more. The scent would guide them to me. Some would hear my voice calling like an eerie whisper from the depths of darkness.” [from Carmen’s autobiography]

Accessibility information: The tour is on flat public footpaths. Tours are limited to around 20 walkers.

Starts at the rugby sculpture, Jack Ilott Green, corner of Harris Street & Jervois Quay (just by Civic Square)
Ends: Upper Cuba Street

Cost: FREE
Please register (for walker numbers): https://walktours.nz/book/
DURATION: 90-minutes

The Festive Flyer, The Festive Flyer
Join us and celebrate Christmas with a delicious lunch and a day out on the train! Saturday 6th December 2025

Get into the festive spirit with Steam Incorporated—perfect for celebrating with colleagues, friends, and family!

Jump onboard our heritage train departing Wellington Station, and nestle down into your seats for a relaxing journey up the coast behind one of our heritage Da class locomotives.

After arriving at the private entry at Tatum, you'll take a short walk across the car park and follow the music into the Pavilion, where we settle in just in time for lunch!

Immerse yourself in a well-crafted meal, created by the talented chefs there. The menu is set to be a classic kiwi style Christmas buffet feast with all the trimmings!

There will be plenty to keep you entertained such as outdoor games, live music, and 2 dinner sittings, so there is plenty of time to tour Tatum, check out Tatum House, and relax in the gardens on the Tatum House Lawn with a drink. You will be advised of your sitting time prior to arrival.

Departing Tatum, climb on board, head to the Lounge Car, grab a drink from the bar and enjoy the journey home. This unforgettable ride hugs the dramatic coastline along the famed Kapiti escarpment, offering sweeping views of the Tasman Sea and rugged cliffs. It’s a rare chance to relive the golden age of rail in one of New Zealand’s most scenic rail corridors as the sun begins to set.

This excursion will be hauled by our 1955-built diesel electric locomotive, Da 1410, and consist of our steel carriages.

Fares (include your return train travel, meal and entertainment)
Adult 13+ yrs - $229
Child 2-12yrs - $189
Infant 0-2yrs - FREE

Thinking of a larger event, or your corporate Christmas Function?
We're pleased to be able to offer some fantastic packages for large groups, or corporate functions with our friends at Tatum. This all inclusive train ride and Christmas lunch combo is a great way to celebrate 2025 with your team! Please contact us via email or call us on 0800 783 264 for a personalized group package.

Please be at your boarding station minimum 10 minutes prior ready to roll, with your tickets, carriage letter and seating allocations at the ready.

Limited Mobility Disclaimer
Tatum does NOT have a platform. This means you must be able to board and disembark the train from ground level with little to no assistance.

Due to the age, design and nature of our heritage carriages, these are not suitable for passengers with limited mobility. If you have any concerns, please contact us on 0800 783 264 to discuss options with our bookings team!

All tickets and seating allocations are sent via email, within 48 hours prior to the departure of this excursion.

Prior booking is essential, make sure you reserve your spot now to avoid missing out on this experience.

description:
The Highs and Sighs of selling in India, The History of Anglo-Indians: a Graphic novel, Keith Butler, who identifies as an Anglo-Indian, reveals how his community grew up without being taught its own history. Discovering that Anglo-Indian history was probably never taught at school level in India, Butler set out to not only to expose this absence, but to correct it.
His response was The History of Anglo-Indians, a bold, accessible graphic novel created for readers of all ages and nationality.
Following its launch in India in January 2026, 300 copies sold in just three weeks, confirming a powerful appetite for a decolonised telling of Anglo-Indian history. Interestingly, it wasn’t only the community who purchased the book but Indians of many other persuasions.
In this talk, Butler shares the highs and sighs of taking that story on the road—selling a reclaimed community history while India itself is re-examining its national narrative. Honest, engaging, and resonant also of the Māori experience in New Zealand, this is a conversation about memory, identity, and who gets to tell history.

description:
The Stories of Our Bodies Wellington [LGBTQIA+ cohort], We often believe we can know something about other people based on what we see of their bodies. Before we’re even conscious of it, we label, compartmentalise or judge - and it can be a real struggle to relish our own bodies when this judgment happens in front of a mirror. 
The Stories of Our Bodies is an affirming and liberating circle, firmly
held in dignity, that redirects this judgement towards positive body image and bodily autonomy. This workshop builds on the living lineage of Australian Radical Faerie elder Uncle Teacosy. It is shaped from gay men’s survival of the 90’s AIDS epidemic, evolved to uplift queer&trans communities and has been offered internationally by only one facilitator.
Each participant is invited into deep connection with their body and then in turn, we share the stories of our bodies from birth til now, removing as many articles of clothing as we choose. Stories often include histories of illness, injury, gender affirmation, addiction, aging, intentional modification, shape, ability or size
What stories can the marks and folds of a body tell when witnessed in belonging and respect? How can we uplift each story and every storyteller?
This circle is for participants from the Takatāpui, MVPFAFF+, LGBTQIA+ communities, active in engaged consent and includes partial or full nudity in a non-sexual atmosphere.
Your Facilitators: Eleven Greenstones and val smith
Eleven Greenstones (she/they, Pakeha) is a cultural worker, community educator, researcher, gardener and facilitator who seeks deep and fertile justice by cultivating rich soil and robust, adaptive communities. For three decades, Eleven has informed and performed behind a radio desk, on stage, in community centres and cultural hubs. Her work spans the Pacific Ocean including in Aotearoa, Australia, Timor Leste, China, Korea, Mongolia and the US: educating in high schools, AOD rehabs, hospitals, police stations, co-housing cooperatives, squatted warehouses, international language schools and mentoring in arts workshops and community gardens.
Eleven is a life-long student, recently in decolonial Fieldwork with Leah Manaema Avene and with Héctor Aristizábal, founder of ImaginAction. They’ve studied post-activism with fugitive philosopher Bayo Akomolafe, Generative Somatics and Undoing Racism® (People’s Institute for Survival and Beyond). They’ve been mentored by First Nations ecologists to work for a living planet, Undoing White Supremacy Austin (Texas) to design and deliver anti-racism ‘unlearning circles’ and by Radial Faerie elders to facilitate liberating spaces for the LGBTQIA+ community.
val smith (Pākehā, they/them) is a choreographic artist-researcher and educator based in Tāmaki Makaurau, Aotearoa. Their practice engages critical somatics and friendship-based collaboration to explore the socio-political dimensions of whiteness, queerness, and transness within the cultural context of Aotearoa. Recent performance work investigates more-than-human kinship, queer intimacies, and temporalities in relationship with marginal urban places.
val’s teaching and facilitation engages with community, secondary and tertiary learning environments. They have a Postgraduate Diploma in Dance and Drama Secondary Teaching, and have worked with kids, young people with disabilities, the Disability dance sector, older folks, as well as queer and trans communities. They teach somatic practices, improvisation, performance skills, critical dance, yoga, creative practice and research methodologies.
A recipient of the Arts Foundation Laureate Award (2019), val was also the 2016 Caroline Plummer Fellow at Te Whare Wānanga o Ōtākou, University of Otago, where they undertook a community dance project with the local queer community.

description:
Tour Toi Māori, Overview






Exclusive behind-the-scenes tour of The Dowse's collection store, exploring Toi Māori, taonga care, and Things We Don't Talk About.
Go behind the scenes at The Dowse with this tour of our collection store, featuring a special focus on our Toi Māori collection and explore our exhibition, Things We Don't Talk About.
Join Collections Manager Jo Wehrly and Director Karl Chitham for an exclusive look at how we care for, store, and preserve these important taonga.

Things We Don’t Talk About
Land rights, modes of masculinity, rates of incarceration, and the negative impacts of religion are among the topics that are often difficult to discuss. This exhibition draws attention to the challenges faced by Māori communities in Aotearoa through powerful artworks from The Dowse's collection. It highlights unspoken and unheard moments of cultural tension and sadness from recent decades, while also sharing stories of resilience, perseverance, and hope for the future.

Featuring work by 21 artists including Hiria Anderson-Mita, Zena Elliot, Russ Flatt, Ngahuia Harrison, Abigail Aroha Jensen, Rangi Kipa, Maureen Lander, Peata Larkin, Matthew McIntyre Wilson, Fiona Pardington, Michael Parekōwhai, Reuben Paterson, Diane Prince, Ngaroma Riley, Hariata Ropata-Tangahoe, Kereama Taepa, Wi Taepa, Te Mohoao, Terri Te Tau, Areta Wilkinson and Wayne Youle.

//Image: Kereama Taepa, He Pukaea [detail], 2019. Photo: Jess O’Brien

description:
Towards modernism: The Walter Cook collection at Te Papa, Towards modernism: The Walter Cook collection at Te Papa
Curator and author Justine Olsen will explore Te Papa’s Walter C. Cook Collection of Decorative Arts. Walter intended to trace modernism’s roots from the Arts and Crafts Movement to post-war designbut, but how did he achieve this aim?

Join us at the Library or online. Register for a Zoom link:

Modernism through the eyes of a collector
Between 1965 and 1990, collector Walter Cook built up an extensive collection of British and European decorative arts, mostly purchased in Wellington. In 1992 he gifted the collection to Te Papa, significantly adding to the museum’s holdings of international decorative arts.

In the research for her book, Towards Modernism: The Walter Cook Collection at Te Papa, Justine Olsen drew on Turnbull and National Library collections, including the Wises Street Directories and Papers Past, to understand market trends through the flow of design from Europe to the market in New Zealand.

In this talk, Justine will explore the story of the market and changing taste, both at the time of production and half a century later, when these objects were sought after by dealers and collectors.

The Walter C. Cook Collection of Decorative Arts
The collection was built up over a twenty-five-year period by Walter Cook, a discerning and determined collector of modest means. The glass, ceramic, and metal objects — by designers including Susie Cooper, Clarice Cliff, William De Morgan, Christopher Dresser, and Inge-Lise Koefoed — track the evolution of design from the Arts and Crafts movement through to the British and European modernism of the 1970s.

A Friends of the Turnbull Library event
The Friends of the Turnbull Library, Ngā Hoa o te Whare Pukapuka Turnbull, offers a monthly programme of free public talks. These talks are held in the National Library in Wellington and on Zoom. Some of these talks will be repeated in Auckland. The public programme highlights the work of researchers who draw on Turnbull material for their projects and staff who care for and research the collections.

About the speaker
Justine Olsen has been Curator of Decorative Art and Design at Te Papa Tongarewa the Museum of New Zealand, since 2009. Her special interests include late nineteenth and twentieth century design, and contemporary New Zealand craft especially ceramics and jewellery. With history curator Michael Fitzgerald, she developed the exhibition ‘Walter Cook: a collector’s quest’ in 2012.

Image: Justine Olsen, author of The Walter Cook Collection at Te Papa.

description:
Tram 17 Inauguration (Fathers Day 2025), Join us at the Wellington Tramway Museum as we put our latest restoration project into active service at the museum!
Tram 17 was built in 1904 by the Wellington City Council Tramways as a four wheeled box (Palace) style tram. By 1917 the system had grown and 17 was rebuilt into its current form adding a set of trucks converting the tram to 8 wheels. Tram tram saw regular service until the 1940’s where it was eventually use for peak time travel, before being withdrawn in the late 50’s.
It was then sold, and taken to Bell road in Raumati on the Kapiti coast where it served as a beach hutt until the 80’s where it was donated to the Wellington tramway museum for display and eventual restoration.
2014 a conservation and restoration plan was put together, and the tram was shipped out to the Wheelwright Shop in the Wairarapa for a full body overhaul. It was transported back to the museum in 2017 and put on public display until new trucks (wheelsets) could be manufacturedby A&G price in Thames.
Since 2019 the tram has undergone new wiring, and extensive testing and running in and is now ready to take passengers along our museum.
Tram 17 is a wonderful achievement by all
Those involved, and we cannot wait to welcome you this Father’s Day to enjoy a ride on this heritage tram, saved from the scrap heap, and then saved again from rotting away.
Please note: We intend to run tram 17, however due to the nature and style of the tram, its operation is weather dependent. If we deem that the tram cannot run, we will advise accordingly.

Jane Jacobs was a well respected urbanist of last century who valued the organic nature of cities and successfully worked to stop motorways through central New York and Toronto.

description:
UHC class of 2000 - 25 year reunion, UHC class of 2000 - 25 year reunion
Luke Vilain here - I’m putting together a school reunion for our year. Key details:

Where - UHC fields (probably somewhere behind the astroturf, maybe near the pine trees if shade is needed) - Mrs Van Maren (who is now the deputy principal) has said we can use them 😊
When - Saturday, January 10th, from midday until the food
Food - please BYO picnic and drinks. I'll be organising some toilets and some spare water, as the school won't be open at that stage, therefore no staff to open up the facilities
Activity - it’ll be a relaxed day - with some “back to school” races (egg & spoon, sack race, that sort of thing)
Families / dogs / hangers on - if you’ve got kids, it would be great if you could bring them along – the more chaos, the better 😄

Please forward this event to people that you know that went to UHC! They don't need to strictly have been in the 2000 year, or even have stayed in school until 2000 - the point is to have people come together who haven't seen each other in a long time, but have a shared connection in our teenage years

I'll likely be reaching out to people asking for contact details (like your name, facebook profile, cell phone, vague location), so those that are happy to share with others can do so - I've had a couple people already mention that they'd like to follow up with people and reconnect after all this time. This will obviously be optional (the privacy act and all that 😄)

Really looking forward to seeing you all! Any questions please shout and I'll update the event 😊

description:
URGE BLACK, URGE BLACK
Unleash your inner dark side at URGE BLACK. The pulsating rhythms of liberation meet the sultry allure of leather-clad revelry. This isn’t just a dance party; it’s a sensorial odyssey that transcends age and convention. Prepare to be captivated, challenged, and ultimately liberated in an atmosphere where every shimmy and shake is an act of personal revolution.

URGE doesn’t just throw parties; we craft transformative experiences that celebrate the raw, unbridled essence of gay culture. Leather, fetish, uniform, gear, sports kit, etc.

Let’s dance and celebrate our authentic selves!

URGE tips:
Doors open at 9:00 PM.
Door sales are limited and $60 (cash only) if the event has not sold out prior.
Peak times: Queues can form if everyone arrives at once. We work to get you in quickly, so please be patient and courteous to our staff.
Dark Room: Located out back. Explore it if you’re feeling adventurous!
Your DJs:
Winner Mick
DJ K-OTIK
Everett Wayne
Event Rules:

This is a safe space: have fun, be kind, spread love, and look out for each other.
Follow instructions: Listen to staff and volunteers—they’re there to keep everyone safe. Ignoring their directions may result in removal from the event.
ZERO tolerance for harassment: This includes racism, transphobia, homophobia, sexism, misgendering, xenophobia, ableism, and fatphobia.
CONSENT IS KEY: Consent must be explicit and enthusiastic and can be withdrawn at any time.
- - - - SEE YOU ON THE DANCE FLOOR - - - -

description:
VOGELMORN'S BEST QUIZ, Secure a spot and come jump in on a classic, family friendly quiz night at your favourite new local. This will be a reoccurring event on the last Thursday of every second month!
~~~ How it works ~~~
-Pre-register by emailing ordishquiz@gmail.com
-Turn up from 6.30pm for a 7pm start
-Max 6 people per team
-$5 per person, then $30 for a 6 members team (bring cash!)
-We have a maximum number of teams so best to get in quick or try your luck on the night
-Awesome prizes to be won

The bar will be open from 3pm with a great selection of local tap beers, wine and non-alcs. Happy Hour from 3pm to 6pm.
Smoked and Pickled will be dishing up delicious kai to keep your brains switched on! You can book your dinner in advance.
Vogelmorn Bowling Club is not a accessible building
Don't forget to pre-register by email at: ordishquiz@gmail.com
Not quizzing? No stress, we will still be open to the public!
"Vogelmorn Upstairs is not a wheelchair accessible building. There is an accessible
bathroom in the space. This is an all ages venue but those under the age of 16 must be
accompanied by a designated adult after 8pm. The Vogelmorn Precinct is a community
space located in a residential area. With that in mind, the team ask that you be kind to
others' and that when you leave the gig, you do so quietly to avoid disturbing our
neighbours.”

description:
Visit the Upper Hutt Blockhouse (8th & 9th Nov 2025), Visit the Upper Hutt Blockhouse (8th & 9th Nov 2025)
This Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga property is not open to the public often, so bring the family between 11am and 1pm.

About this Event

This Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga property is not open to the public often, so bring the family between 11am and 1pm!
Come visit the Upper Hutt Blockhouse between 11am-1pm as part of the Wellington Heritage Festival 2025.
"The Upper Hutt Blockhouse is one of the few remaining buildings associated with the New Zealand wars, as well as a monument to Pākehā settler anxiety, built in fear of an attack by Māori that never came. Visit today and you’ll get a sense of the defensive ‘last stand’ mindset. On both floors you’ll find a series of balistraria, tightly angled gun slots through which members of the militia would defend their posts. Keep an eye out, too, for an exposed panel where you can see the fine gravel that was packed between the exterior weatherboards and inch-thick interior boards to absorb the impact of answering gunfire. Don’t be fooled by the windows – they were added later. Originally, the loop holes you’ll spy on the walls were the only way to see out."
Inside the Blockhouse, there’s an exhibition from Whirinaki Whare Taonga, telling the early story of Upper Hutt and its Blockhouse.
We will have some knowledgeable people available to share stories, answer questions and some light refreshments. Drop in between 11-1pm and stay as long as you like!

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Castlepoint Welcome to Wairarapa Walk, Join us for a special day out at one of Wairarapa’s most iconic coastal spots, in partnership with the Red Cross Settlement Team and led by Atta-Ul Muneeb. This event is all about building connections, community, and friendship while enjoying the beauty of the outdoors together.

We’ll meet at 9.30 am at the Tranzit Offices on Queen Street, Masterton, and travel together by bus to Castlepoint Beach. Once there, you’ll have the choice of several guided walks: climb to the historic lighthouse for sweeping sea views, enjoy a stroll along the beach, or explore part of the nearby nature reserve. Each walk option takes about 30 minutes, making it easy to find one that suits your fitness level.

After exploring, we’ll gather for a BYO picnic and fun beach games before heading back. Buses will depart Castlepoint at 2pm, with an expected return to Masterton around 3pm.

This event is family-friendly and open to all — walkers of all ages and abilities are welcome. A number of spaces have already been reserved for former refugees. There are 30 free places to be reserved here on Eventfinda for migrants, newcomers to Wairarapa, and members of the public who’d like to build connections and help make everyone feel welcome. The return bus trip is included, thanks to discounted bus costs kindly provided by Tranzit Group.
This event is possible due to the generous support from our sponsors: Masterton Rotary Club, Masterton South Rotary Club, Carterton Rotary Club, South Wairarapa Rotary Club.
Practical details:
- 5-hour round trip
- Walk options: beach (flat), lighthouse and reserve (moderate fitness, steps/uneven ground, not suitable for prams or wheelchairs)
Bring: warm clothes, waterproof jacket, sunhat and glasses, food and water, sturdy shoes with good tread
- Children under 14 must be supervised at all times

Photo Credit: Jet Productions.

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Martinborough Heartbeat Friday Walk, Join the Martinborough Friday Walkers, Martinborough Community Board, and Wellington Free Ambulance for a relaxed local walk to discover where Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs) are located around the village. The route is flat and mostly suitable for pushchairs and prams, making it a great outing for all ages and fitness levels.

The walk finishes at the Waihinga Centre with light refreshments and an opportunity to chat with Cheryl from Wellington Free Ambulance about AEDs. You’ll also be able to register for upcoming Heartbeat training courses.
Martinborough is well served with around 12 AEDs across the village. A new map showing their locations—along with details of the AED Locator App—will be available and distributed to local businesses.

This event aims to raise awareness of AED locations and highlight the free training opportunities provided by Wellington Free Ambulance, thanks to the Lloyd Morrison Foundation. Don’t forget to wear something red!

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Papawai Marae and Eels Hikoi, A guided walk at Papawai Marae provides an opportunity to explore one of Aotearoa New Zealand’s most historically significant marae, near Greytown. Papawai is the home of Ngāti Moe hapū and it also served as the centre for the Kotahitanga Māori Parliament movement in the late 19th century. Manuhiri exploring the marae grounds will learn about the important gatherings held there in 1897 and 1898, during which significant decisions - such as the resolution to end Māori land sales - were made. The walk reveals the stories behind the meeting houses and highlights notable figures such as Hāmuera Tamahau Mahupuku and Premier Richard Seddon. Participants also discover the significance of the 18 tōtara whakairo (carved figures) that face inward, rather than the traditional outward-facing stance. A short walk behind the marae visitors will find Papawai Stream teeming with tuna (eels). The waterway has been planted up to restore its health and biodiversity thanks to locals and a stream restoration group.

This 45minute walk is mainly flat with some moderate inclines.
label: Community & Culture

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Walk in the Dark Carterton, This session is held at the Carterton Golf Course.

Step into the beauty of the night with this unique new offering for the Wairarapa Walking Festival. Hosted on the manicured grounds of a local golf course, this gentle evening stroll allows you to experience the magic of darkness without worrying about uneven paddocks or rough terrain.

As we walk together, the transition from dusk to dark will naturally unfold, helping us acclimatise to the night. For those new to walking in the dark, handy red-light torches will be provided to keep you comfortable. This is less about distance and more about slowing down, stepping slightly outside of your comfort zone, and embracing the calm of night.

Along the way, we’ll reflect on the value of darkness - its role in history, its impact on wellbeing, and its importance for the environment. We’ll then pause to share hot chocolate and, if the skies are clear, look up in awe at a canopy of stars. With star charts in hand, we’ll explore what the November night skies have to offer and why protecting them matters.

As we walk together, the transition from dusk to dark will naturally unfold, helping us acclimatise to the night. For those new to walking in the dark, handy red-light torches will be provided to keep you comfortable. This is less about distance and more about slowing down, stepping slightly outside of your comfort zone, and embracing the calm of night.

We’ll then pause to share hot chocolate and, if the skies are clear, look up in awe at a canopy of stars. With star charts in hand, we’ll explore what the November night skies have to offer and why protecting them matters.

The evening concludes with simple, practical ways we can all help preserve our night skies - because our environment doesn’t end at the treetops, it stretches all the way to the stars.

description:
Waitangi Day 2026 - Open Day, Waitangi Day 2026 - Open Day
FOR IMMEDIATE USE – JAN / FEB 2026
WAITANGI DAY– OPEN DAY
FRIDAY 6TH FEB, 10AM- 4PM

Wellington’s historic Wrights Hill Fortress in Karori will be open for public inspection again on Waitangi Day, Friday, February 6th. The World War Two coastal battery first opened to the public in 1989 and will be accessible between 10am and 4pm.

On Waitangi Day people are invited to self-guide themselves through the tunnels and gun emplacements. The walk usually takes about one hour. Bring a torch with you for some fun! Strong footwear and no jandals!

Visitors will be able to explore the 620 metres of underground tunnels with a free map and history pamphlet. They will see shell stores, plotting rooms and the huge gun pit where Gun umber 1 used to stand, as well as a replica of the 10-metre-long gun barrel. Also on show will be historic photos, and an assortment of military memorabilia. A DVD of how a 9.2-inch gun operates will be showing as well. The World War Two Fortress is the only one of its type in New Zealand available to the public on four Open Days a year.

Wrights Hill Fortress was built from 1942 to protect Wellington from Japanese bombardment. In the early 1960’s, the guns were cut up for scrap and sold, ironically, to the Japanese.

Admission is $20 for a family of two adults and three children under 12, or $10 per adult and $5 per child. (CASH ONLY please-NO EFTPOS). Access is via Karori Road, Campbell Street, and Wrights Hill Road. All proceeds go to the continuing restoration of the Fortress. There is limited car parking at the summit of the Hill.

Visitors to the Fortress in Wrights Hill Reserve can also enjoy bush walks, picnic sites and panoramic views from the top of the hill.

There will also be a BBQ sausage sizzle and soft drinks on sale. No booking required.

The International Wave of Light invites baby loss families, friends, loved ones and supporting organisations from around the world to join in honour and remembrance of all loved and longed for babies gone too soon.
No matter where you are in the world, you can light a candle at 7pm in memory of your baby or babies to be part of the wave of light that begins here in Aotearoa and wraps around the globe.
Wherever you do this, you will be joining a global ‘Wave of Light’ in memory of all the babies who lit up our lives for such a short time.
This is a family friendly event, please be mindful pregnant families, babies, children, as well as health professionals wishing to support our community may be in attendance

Have you ever wondered what goes on behind those 'staff only' doors? Join our guides for a peek behind the heritage curtain.

Join guides from Porirua's City Centre Library and Pātaka Art + Museum to take a 'behind the scenes' tour of the heritage collections. They will reveal how the objects in the collections are being looked after and what is available to tell the stories of Porirua's history.

Free, booking required, please visit the Wellington Heritage Festival website to register: https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/porirua-libraries-behind-the-scenes-tour/
label: Community & Culture

description:
Wellington Heritage Festival - Crematorium Open Day, Built in 1982, Whenua Tapu Crematorium is a beautiful facility that has served thousands of families.

Hear about the history of the chapel and what it’s like to operate a crematorium from the staff that operate it. You can also do a walk-through of the crematorium (optional).

Cremation is the common choice in NZ when it comes to death, with over 70% of Kiwis choosing it. Traditionally Māori and Pacifica families always chose burial, however there is a slow change happening in that space also. We are passionate about de mystifying what cremation is so families can feel informed about the choices they make.

Come along as we open Whenua Tapu Crematorium to the public and answer any questions you may have.

description:
Wellington Heritage Festival - Porirua Cemetery walk, Porirua City Council is undertaking a project to memorialise over 1700 unmarked graves.

Come along to hear about the history of Porirua Cemetery and the Porirua Hospital (Asylum) and how this has resulted in hundreds of unmarked graves.

Hear stories of some of those people that died while in the hospital care and hear about the project underway to remember these people with funding from the government.

This is a direct result of funding available from the Royal Inquiry into Abuse in Care.

Parking on roadside, tour will start at the Cemetery Chapel.

Please wear good shoes and dress for the weather. The tour will happen rain or shine, we have a small chapel on site to host the talk if it is wet.

description:

His talk will focus on these projects and the research resources he discovered; he will also discuss issues around making information publicly available through social media.

description:
Wellington Heritage Festival - Sharing Stories, Porirua Libraries would like to discover new stories about Porirua, inspired by its photograph collection or yours.

Looking at a photograph can bring out memories from the past that provides a connection to a place you called home. Porirua's City Centre Library would like to capture those memories by recording people talking about a photograph in the library's collection, or bringing in their own.

The image and recording will be added to the library's catalogue for everyone to share. Book a time to visit and share your memory.

To book a time to visit, contact ruth.barrett@poriruacity.govt.nz
