This event is a Bus Tour around the Porirua Region to visit and learn about the sites that are so significant to Ngāti Toa Rangatira.

Site of Significance Tour / Itinerary will include:
• Whitireia Park, Titahi Bay
• Takapūwāhia Marae
• Ngāti Toa Domain, Paremata
• Hongoeka Bay, Plimmerton
• Battle Hill, Pauatahanui.

Koha entry, booking required.
To book your space on the bus, please email communications@ngatitoa.iwi.nz

description:
Wellington Heritage Festival - St. Joseph's Pāuatahanui, Hear the stories, with accompanying photos and maps, which bring to life the families who founded this beautiful church 147 years ago.

Brian Murphy, a descendant of the Murphy family who built St. Joseph's church, will lead this talk. A small community of closely-linked families, with many coming from Roscommon in Ireland, established farms at Pāuatahanui and donated funds to build this timber Victorian-Gothic church.

Brian will relate stories which lie behind the graves and unique windows of St. Joseph's.

Koha entry.

description:
Wellington Spring Festival – Government House Garden tour, As part of Wellington's Spring Fetival, explore Government House gardens with the BARK garden team (90 minute tour)

Government House was opened in Newtown in 1910, and its extensive gardens have been in continuous development since then. As part of the Spring Festival, the Government House garden team is offering guided walks through our gardens. Tours will go ahead regardless of weather. Tours will not enter the main house.

Bookings are essential for the free tour. Places are limited: https://gg.govt.nz/government-house/government-house-wellington/government-house-tours/upcoming

Some parts of our grounds are not mobility friendly. Please contact the Visitor Centre direct if you have any questions regarding accessibility.

Groups wanting to organise a garden tour or house tour can email our Visitor Centre team direct: bookings@govthouse.govt.nz

If you have any questions or need more information, please email us at bookings@govthouse.govt.nz, or call us at 04-382-0837. You will receive a reminder email 24 hours before your tour.

description:
Wellington Vintage Machinery Open Days, Wellington Vintage Machinery Open Days
Get a close look and hands on experience with machinery of yesteryear. Weather permitting, we will have our Fowler Traction engine in steam too!

Find the machine that was used to make the 1950 Empire Games medals. Many of the machines have a association with the Wellington area.

Take a nostalgic trip through the vintage kitchen and other displays of household, and retail items from the past. Wellington Vintage Machinery is housed in an old Cheese Factory built in 1925. The factory has had an interesting past from cheese factory, to milk bottling plant, munitions store during WWII, and other uses before becoming home for the vintage machinery.

The building is one of the few remaining dairy factories designed by architects Duffill & Gibson of Hawera and built by CE Roebuck of New Plymouth.


Cost: Koha
Event information here: https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/wellington-vintage-machinery-open-days-25/


Health & Safety:
Please wear closed toe footwear and keep an eye on any children that you bring along.

Most of the display is wheelchair accessible, and an accessible toilet facility is also available.

description:
Wellington: Te Matapihi Central Library Tour, Te Matapihi/Wellington Central Library Tour with WCC and Athfield Architects

RICS invites members to a site visit of Te Matapihi ki te ao nui, Wellington’s soon-to-be-completed Central Library. Delivered in partnership with Athfield Architects, LT McGuinness, and Wellington City Council, (with Aurecon, Tihei, Fire HQ, Rider Levett Bucknall & RCP), this event offers a look at the revitalised civic space following completion of the main contract works (public opening scheduled for early 2026, following soft fit out).

The project includes extensive seismic strengthening—base isolators, new foundations, and structural upgrades, making Te Matapihi one of the most resilient public buildings in the city. It also targets a 5-star Green Building rating and will house the Library, Capital E/Experience Wellington, Council Archives, and Council Service Centre, in a single integrated facility.

PPE Required: Hard hat, Hi-Vis and steel toe cap boots.

Contact:
For more information on this event please contact Caleb Steiner (RICS Member Engagement Lead) at csteiner1@rics.org

description:
Welly Clubs Winter Quiz 2026, Brought to you jointly by VUWTC, NZAC Wellington and WTMC, join us on Tuesday 28th of July at the Hunter Lounge for a night of Wellington outdoors community quiz fun. We'll be raising funds (and glasses) for Land Search and Rescue Wellington - with some mega quiz and raffle prizes thrown in too!
The Quiz

Come along to test your knowledge, share a drink with friends, and make a meaningful contribution to a charity doing incredible work to ensure Aotearoa's outdoor enthusiasts
Tickets will be sold per team: $85 for a student team, and $175 for a non-student team. Each team ticket comes with a bowl of fries and a large Hunter Lounge pizza! Each team can have up to 6 people in it - we encourage you to fill up your team to the full 6 people! The number of teams will be strictly limited, so make sure your team buys a ticket to reserve its spot - individual places can be filled later (liaise with your clubs to help you find some team mates). Buy your tickets here: https://www.vuwtc.org.nz/Event/13465
Arrive from 6pm at the Hunter Lounge for a 6:45pm sharp start to the quiz. We would recommend arriving early to ensure you have time to buy your raffle tickets, buy-an-answer coupons and any drinks you may want, and find your allocated table before the quiz kicks off. Keep an eye on our event page on Facebook and follow your club on Instagram for more details!
The Raffle & Buy-An-Answer

Coupons are $5 each (i.e. $5 per question), with a maximum of 10 coupons being able to be utilised throughout the quiz (maximum 2 per round). Coupons will be available for sale on the night only (strong preference for cash).
Food and Drink

The Hunter Lounge offers some fantastic food and drink and will be serving all night. Team tickets include one bowl of fries and one pizza already, but feel free to order extra food and drinks as well! Tables will be allocated so ensure you know your table number before ordering.
A chance to have fun, win big, AND support a great cause? You don’t want to miss this one. Grab your buddies and let's get behind a good cause. We can't wait to see you there!

description:
Welly On Wheels - City to Island Bay: Confidence & Skills for Biking, Join Wellington City Council, Pedal Ready, and Switched On Bikes for a guided bike tour along the cycle route from central Wellington to Island Bay. Build your confidence and skills to ride safely and efficiently by paihikara (bike), explore the latest cycleway improvements, and learn practical tips for night-time commuting.

The ride starts and finishes at Switched On Bikes HQ near Waitangi Park, heading to Shorland Park in Island Bay. You are welcome to finish the ride at Shorland Park or ride back to Waitangi Park. Note: the event may be postponed in the case of adverse weather.

Duration: Please allow around 2 hours for the ride.
Arrival: Arrive 30 minutes early if you’re renting a bike.
Preparation: Bring clothing suitable for changing weather conditions.

These rides are ideal for people who:
- Can ride a bike but haven’t yet started biking regularly in the city.
- Already ride in the city but want to gain confidence.
- Want to learn how to use Wellington’s cycleway network safely and efficiently.

Who can join: Open to riders aged 18+, or 13+ if accompanied by an adult. Younger children are welcome on cargo bikes or bike seats provided by participants. If you’d like to borrow a bike seat, please contact Switched On Bikes directly.

Bikes and bookings:
An electric bike is strongly recommended. Thanks to Switched On Bikes and Wellington City Council, you can rent one for only $10 if you don’t have access to your own. Please book your e-bike separately here: https://switchedonbikes.rezdy.com/642002/electric-bike-hire-welly-on-wheels

After the tour, you can either leave your bike with us and catch a bus back to the city or keep riding if you’re feeling energetic! You’re welcome to return the bike before 9am the next day at no extra cost or hold onto it for the following day at a discounted rate of $39.

If you’d like to learn to ride a bike away from traffic, check out the free Pedal Ready courses on their website.

For any pātai (questions) about the tours, please email info@pedalready.org.nz.

Privacy Statement:
Information collected for this ride is used for booking and safety purposes. Your name and emergency contact details will be deleted within 14 days after the tour. Other provided information may be stored anonymously to support project evaluation. Your email address will be kept for up to 4 months so we can share follow-up information about biking in Pōneke and invite you to give feedback about your experience.

You have the right to request access to or correction of your information. To do so, please email tours@wcc.govt.nz.

description:
Welly On Wheels Kilbirnie - Confidence & Skills for Biking, Wellington City Council and Pedal Ready are teaming up to run social bike tours of the cycle routes in Kilbirnie and the surrounding area. Build confidence and skills to travel safely and efficiently by paihikara (bike) while getting to know the cycle routes in Kilbirnie!

Rides start and finish at Switched On HQ on the waterfront. A great way to exercise your newfound cycling skills and confidence on a fun social ride!

Please allow 2 hours for the ride. Arrive 30 minutes early if you are renting a bike.

These rides are suitable for people who:
- Know how to ride a bike but aren't yet travelling by bike in the city; or
- Those travelling by bike in the city but would like to gain confidence; or
- Those who want to learn how to use new infrastructure.

Open to riders aged 18+ (or 13+ if accompanied by an adult). Families are also welcome to bring younger children on cargo bikes or bike seats provided themselves. Please enquire directly with Switched on Bikes if you'd like to borrow a bike seat for the tour.

An electric bike is strongly recommended to participate in this ride. Thanks to Switched on Bikes and Wellington City Council, you can rent an electric bike for just $10 if you don't have access to one. Please book that separately here: https://switchedonbikes.rezdy.com/642002/electric-bike-hire-welly-on-wheels

You can either leave the bike with us after the tour and make your own way home (there are regular buses that depart regularly to the city from the Kilbirnie bus depot) or come back with us to Switched On HQ. If you're feeling extra enthusiastic and want to extend your ride overnight, you're welcome to hold onto the bike for free and return it before 9am to Switched on Bikes. You can also hold onto the bike and return it at the end of Thursday at a discounted cost of $...! You can decide what you'd like to do as late as the end of the guided ride on Wednesday.

If you would like to learn to ride a bike away from the road, check out the free Pedal Ready courses on their website. Any pātai (questions) about these tours please get in contact: tours@wcc.govt.nz.

PRIVACY STATEMENT: The information you shared in signing up for this ride is used for booking and safety purposes. Within 14 days after the tour, your name and emergency contact details will be deleted. Other information provided may be stored anonymously to support our project evaluation. Your email address will be stored for up to 4 months following the tour. Within that time, we may contact you with follow-up information about biking in Pōneke, as well as feedback opportunities about the ride and the impact it has had on your travel around Pōneke. You have the right to ask for a copy of any personal information we hold about you and to ask for it to be corrected if you believe it is incorrect. If you would like to ask for a copy of your information or to have it corrected, please contact us at tours@wcc.govt.nz.

description:
Whenua Tapu Crematorium Open Day, Whenua Tapu Crematorium Open Day
Built in 1982, Whenua Tapu Crematorium is a beautiful facility that has served thousands of families.

Hear about the history of the chapel and what it’s like to operate a crematorium from the staff that operate it. You can also do a walk-through of the crematorium (optional).

Cremation is the common choice is NZ when it comes to death, with over 70% of Kiwis choosing it. Traditionally Māori and Pacifica families always chose burial, however there is a slow change happening in that space also. We are passionate about de mystifying what cremation is so families can feel informed about the choices they make.

Come along as we open Whenua Tapu Crematorium to the public and answer any questions you may have.


Cost: Free
Event information here: https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/whenua-tapu-crematorium-open-day/

description:
Women of Pōneke February 2026 Event, Women of Pōneke : Big dreams for a cool Capital
26 February |5-7.30 | Te Ahumairangi Foyer
National Library 70 Molesworth St
We begin the year by inviting you to Dream Big!
We love Wellington for its quirk, culture, connection to nature and its infectious energy. In your wildest dreams what would our future capital feel and be like? How would you live in it and what would you want it to stand for on a world stage? — How can we create a city future generations will love to live in?
As Eleanor Roosevelt once said  “ The future belongs to those who believe in the beauty of their dreams”
Who better to dream than the Women of Pōneke!
We are delighted to have the team behind Dear Wellington – Claire Sharpe and Sophie Jacques from Warren & Mahoney and Helen Milner associate at Think Place — to share their dreams for our city in inspired visual imaginings and letters from a future Wellington. They will invite you to join in re-imagining our cool little capital, express your hopes and think about how we can turn ideas into action. 
This is an event where you can surround yourself with great company, enjoy delicious food and wine - unleash your imagination, connect and spark action.  We can’t wait to see you there! 
Tickets are limited to 180 guests.
Get your tickets now! 
Numbers are limited due to space, so we recommend you get in and quick! We are limited to 180 only. 
We will be serving wine, beer and amazing non-alcoholic drinks, inclusive in the ticket price. Platters will also be shared throughout the evening. 
So grab your ticket now and share with at least one amazing woman (and/or ally) in your life.
To cover our costs, we are charging for this event. We know that things are tough at the moment for many, so if this is a barrier for you to attend, please contact us and we will do everything to support you to attend. 
Help a woman in need
If you wish to support someone else who may have a financial barrier, please buy one of the "Buy-One, Give-One" tickets, so we can support more of the amazing women of Pōneke to attend.
Get in quick!
Tickets for previous events have sold out fast. For this event we are capped at 180 people attending and we will be updating our social media channels on the progress of the ticket sales, so get your tickets quick.  
Accessibility
The Te Ahumairangi Foyer, National Library is fully accessible. If you are not able to use the steps on Molesworth Street, you will be able to access the venue via the lift off Aitken Street. There will be staff at the door to be able to support and guide you to the venue space.
A bit about us 
Me.We.Pōneke is our signature quarterly event designed to inspire, connect and raise the voices of our wonderful community of Wellington women, and people who identify as women. 
We believe that magic happens when women come together. We’ve seen it. We’ve felt it. And we want to create more of it with regular events that are open, welcoming, supportive and empowering for the women of Wellington.
Come along, bring a friend and join us as we continue to raise the voices of Wellington women and invite you all to be part of Me We Pōneke.
You can join our mailing list from our brand new website, thanks to our amazing partner Springload. Check it out here and make sure you sign up to our mailing list: https://www.womenofponeke.org....
We are also on Insta! Follow us here: https://www.instagram.com/wome…

description:
Women's Circle: Threads of Thought, Women's Circle: Threads of Thought
A women’s circle for reflection and sharing, using prompts to guide honest conversation, connection, and deeper understanding.

About this Event


Women’s Circle: Thread of Thought
This Women’s Circle is a a space to gather, reflect, and explore the beauty and depth of the feminine experience.
The evening offers a slightly different approach to our usual format. You’re invited to arrive with something in your heart or on your mind - a thought, reflection, or question you’d like to place into the space. These will be written down, gathered into a basket, and passed around, becoming the prompts that guide our conversation.
From there, the circle opens for sharing. Each woman will have the opportunity to speak, reflect, or simply listen as different threads of thought unfold and weave through the room.
There is no pressure to perform or explain yourself here. Some may share openly, others may simply sit and listen. Both are welcome. The circle is held in a simple way that allows honesty, presence, and genuine expression to unfold naturally.
When women gather in this way, something quietly meaningful happens - stories are witnessed, voices are heard, and a sense of shared understanding begins to emerge.




A nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert will be shared afterwards, offering a warm and grounding way to close the evening together.




Meet Rasesvari, your host
Rasesvari (pronounced Rah-say-shwari) has always remembered feeling connected to healing, the inner world, and what helps people feel well and in alignment. Growing up, she spent many hours tucked away in libraries, reading about philosophy, plants, and anything that felt meaningful or life-giving.
Her path took a few turns away from the usual route, leading her to spend six years in an ashram setting focused on self-development and spiritual life. During that time, she explored meditation deeply and had space to focus on her own healing. This naturally opened the door to learning about Traditional Chinese healing, Ayurveda, sound healing, bioresonance, and a lot of self-study along the way.
Her loving aim is simple: to create spaces where people can finally feel comfortable in themselves again and and have room for their own growth and healing.



Agenda


🕑: 06:00 PM - 06:15 PM
Arrive to Bhakti Lounge

🕑: 06:15 PM - 07:15 PM
Women’s Circle: Thread of Thought
Host: Rasesvari

🕑: 07:15 PM - 08:15 PM
Plant-based dinner and dessert!

description:
Worser Bay Boating Club Centenary Weekend Celebrations!, Worser Bay Boating Club Centenary Weekend Celebrations!
https://www.wbbc.org.nz/events/worser-bay-centenary-weekend
Worser Bay Boating Club Centenary Weekend
Celebrating 100 years of sailing at Worser Bay.

Date & Location; 30 Jan 2026, 5:30 pm – 01 Feb 2026, 4:30 pm
WBBC, Karaka Bay Road, Seatoun, Wellington 6022, NZ

About the Event;
Toast 100 years of sailing at Worser Bay at The Worser Way book launch

Friday 30 January 5.30pm to 8.30pm

We kick off the weekend's events with the launch of "The Worser Way" history book. The proof copy has arrived in the country and it is stunning. There are 343 pages, 24 chapters, and 100s of photos tracking the history of sailing in Worser Bay from early Māori settlement through to the current day. If you haven't done so already place your order for a book then get a ticket to the launch where you will be able to pick up your copy.


Centenary club day and BBQ dinner

All day Saturday 31 January with BBQ dinner and drinks from 4.30pm onwards.

Saturday is going to be a big day at the club. The morning will kick off from 9.00am with 'Optisquad' and 'Blue Fleet sessions with our latest crop of new young sailors learning the ropes in the bay. From 11.30am we will have the usual weekend supply of pies and sandwiches available from the kitchen for lunch. Racing gets underway from 1.00pm with two races back to back for for all classes. Then from 4.30pm onwards the bar will be open and a buffet style BBQ dinner will be available for everyone from 6.30pm. Come down for part or all of the day and experience what club life is like after 100 years.


Centenary celebration lunch

Sunday 1 February from 11.30am onwards

“An opportunity to share tales from days when the wind was stronger and the bay worser”

To cap off the weekend, we are hosting a centenary celebration lunch at the club. Bring your partners, your memories, and settle in for an enjoyable buffet lunch. This will be an opportunity to reconnect, reminisce and share tales from years gone by. We’ll have a couple of speakers and we’ll mix up seating between courses so you get a chance to chat with a range of people. Everyone welcome - current members and old salts alike!

https://www.wbbc.org.nz/events/worser-bay-centenary-weekend
Register here!

Come and play tabletop games and practice your te reo Māori at the Newlands Community Centre.

All levels have been participating - beginners and fluent speakers. So please feel comfortable to come along.

There are games suited to all levels, and info sheets to help beginners. Playing games is a fantastic way to pick up new kupu and phrases and use what you have already learned.

Kēmu include: Kaupapa, Tākaro!, Kāri Māori, Wero, Whare Whare, Kupu Rorirori, Ko Wai Koe? and any others you bring along.

A free activity with supper provided. Parking available right outside.

description:
[FULLY BOOKED] Georgina Beyer – Diamonds are Forever (Wellington Heritage Festival), ** THIS EVENT IS NOW FULLY BOOKED **
STARTS: 1pm, SUNDAY 2 NOV
In 2004, Georgina Beyer, the first openly transgender Member of Parliament in the world, famously confronted members of Destiny Church during the Enough Is Enough rally on the grounds of Parliament.
Never a bystander, Georgina faced down the bigots, telling them straight, “Your hatred is totally intolerable!” This was just one of many significant moments that shaped the life of the extraordinary Georgina Beyer.
Born in Wellington, Georgina went on to have an unprecedented local, national and international impact through her commitment to equality and her desire to give everyone the opportunity to reach their full potential in society.
Join us for this special 90-minute walking tour as we pay tribute to the late Georgina (1957–2023) by visiting locations around central Wellington that shaped her journey. Along the way, we’ll honour some of her heroes and listen to first-hand archival audio clips that showcase her humour and resilience.
Georgina’s story is defiantly optimistic – confronting hardship and using her lived experience to change the world for the better.
Time/Date: 1pm, Sunday 2 November 2025
Starts: meet outside St Peters Church, 211 Willis Street
Ends: Vivian Street
Duration: 90 minutes
Cost / Bookings: ** FULLY BOOKED **
Accessibility information: the tour is on flat public footpaths. Tours are limited to approximately 20 walkers.
Image courtesy of the amazing Kym Strathdee
This tour is part of the amazing Wellington Heritage Festival - https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz

description:
tipsy trails #10 Wellington, Hello, welcome - stoked you found us. We’re tipsy trails. We’re on a mission to get more people in their 20s outdoors and turn an online community into an epic in-person one.
We meet once a month and walk together along some of New Zealand’s most stunning trails while chatting with new and old mates. 
We’re a club built on the idea that getting outdoors doesn’t have to be super serious or intense - it should be accessible, with a bit of fun. You don’t need fancy gear. You don’t need to be “outdoorsy.” You don’t even need a group to come with - rocking up solo is totally normal here. All paces and abilities are welcome. You just need to show up and enjoy the rest.
So, what do you say? Put down your phone and come outside with us.
TRAIL INFO
Where: Ataturk Park, Miramar Peninsula, Wellington
Length: Approx. 7km, 220m elevation gain, around 2.5 hours
Difficulty: Moderate
WHAT TO BRING?
Water bottle (make sure it’s full!),
trail snacks (interpret this however your heart desires),
comfy walking shoes,
a warm layer for during/afterwards,
hat, sunglasses, sunscreen (fingers crossed for sunshine), 
a raincoat (just in case)
swimming togs & towel (fully optional),
and a bag to throw everything in! (maybe a backpack or little side bag)
MEETING POINT
Meeting details and timing will be emailed once you’ve registered.
Keep an eye on our Instagram and tipsy trails Facebook messenger group chats for any updates or weather changes.
POST-HIKE PLANS?
With the trail wrapped up and the afternoon still ahead, we’ll head to a nearby pub for a well-earned drink and bite to eat 🍻
NEED / CAN OFFER A LIFT
Carpooling is available for anyone who needs a lift or can offer one. You can connect with others in the Facebook messenger carpool group chat, share your area, and organise pick-up details directly.
REGISTRATION
This is a free community hike, with limited spots available, so please register to join us.
Any questions? Our DM’s are always open on Instagram @tipsy_____________

description:
‘Amethyst outlook’: Exploring Katherine Mansfield’s queer identity, Part of the 2026 Wellington Pride Festival | Tū whakahīhī e Te Whanganui-ā-Tara
“From the amethyst outlook my situation is devilishly fascinating, but it cannot be permanent.” – Katherine Mansfield, 1907
Following the success of 2025’s The Magic of Her Body: Readings of Katherine Mansfield’s Queer Writing, dive deeper into Katherine Mansfield’s queer identity from the perspectives of two generations of Wellington writers.
Gill Greer CBE MNZM is a respected Mansfield scholar, who has also led organisations focused on human rights and health. In 2005, she was appointed a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit, for services to family planning and literature. In 2012, she was made a Commander of the Order of the British Empire, for services to international health and women’s rights.
Joy Holley completed her MA in Creative Writing at the International Institute of Modern Letters in 2020 and her debut collection of short fiction Dream Girl was published in 2023. She was the 2024 Verb Wellington Writer in Residence at Katherine Mansfield House & Garden. During the residency, Joy worked on a first draft of her second book; a Gothic novel about a group of young, queer women living in a haunted flat in Te Whanganui-a-Tara.
This event is free, but registration is required due to limited space in the house. Please note that this event will take place upstairs, see the Accessibility page of our website for more information.
You can either attend this event in-person or online via Zoom. If you register to attend via Zoom, a link will be sent to you at least 24-hours prior to the event start time.

🎄🎅🏻Christmas at the Club🎅🏻🎄, 🎄🎅🏻Christmas at the Club🎅🏻🎄
You are invited to the 14 Dec 2025 Christmas lunch for the Croatian Cultural Society Wellington. It is the club’s biggest day of the year, and we look forward to seeing you there.

Bookings are now open at our Google Form (Link in comments) – we need bookings and payment by 30 November.

The main course will be largely catered, but we have volunteers making ćevapi, octopus salad and punjene paprike/stuffed peppers and also invite members to bring a dessert plate to share, whether it’s from Croatia, NZ or elsewhere.

We are planning to cater for different dietary requirements, so please put down any needs on the booking form.

Timing
11am - Croatian Mass
Fr Bozjak is coming down from Auckland to give a Mass in Croatian at St Anne’s Church (22 Emmett St, Newtown). He will join us for lunch afterwards.

12pm - Club doors open
The club doors open at 12pm at 32 Hania St, Mt Victoria. Father Christmas - Djed Božićnjak 🧑‍🎄visits before lunch is served (parents, don’t forget to bring a named and wrapped gift for your child to pop under the tree for them).

About 12.30pm Lunch starts
A buffet main course will be served. Dessert will be served after the main and members are welcome to stay and enjoy the day.

Payment:
The Executive keeps the costs as low as possible to make sure we get a good cross-section of members, including young families.

- $30 per person for Financial and Life Members of the Club
- $15 per person for member's children aged 12–17, free for those aged under 12.
$50 per person for non-members or non-financial members

For catering purposes, please book and pay by Sunday 30 November

Account: 06-0561-0017339-00,
Account name: Croatian Cultural Society Wgtn Inc
Reference: Xmas
Code: your initials & surname.

Fill in the form with the names of those attending and the amount paid.

Volunteers are still welcome for cooking the day before and for tidying up at the end of the lunch.

Any questions or to volunteers your services please email

description:
🥋 MF Hutt Valley End-of-Year Social! 🎉, 🥋 MF Hutt Valley End-of-Year Social! 🎉
🥋 MF Hutt Valley End-of-Year Social! 🎉
Saturday 13 December, 10:30am – Hikoikoi Reserve, Petone (weather dependent)

Howdy Team! 👋
What an amazing year it’s been — we now have over 50 smiling, sweating, super students across our Petone and Trentham schools! The support from our students, parents, and community has been incredible — thank you all ❤️
Let’s celebrate with a fun, lightweight, and informal End-of-Year Social!

Plan for the day:
🥏 Round of Disc Golf (golf with Frisbees!)
🍔 Kai and picnic
🏊‍♂️ Optional swim (for the brave!)
💬 Jibber-jabber and good vibes
Bring a Frisbee, some kai to share (I'll check if there's a community BBQ available nearby and let you know), and your summer spirit — let’s wrap up the year together in style 🌞

Things I’m celebrating this year:
• Launching our schools with support from Aussie colleagues, family & fighting friends.
• Learning and implementing MF programmes.

description:
2025 Annual South Coast Cleanup, Welcome to the 16th annual South Coast Cleanup, 10:30AM-12:00PM 13th September 2025.
As well as caring for our coasts and oceans, it’s all about community! Join us at any of our cleanup locations for a morning of litter collection and family fun.

WHEN
We kick off at 10:30am on the 13 September. We host clean up sites at 12 locations between Owhiro Bay to Breaker Bay on the Wellington South Coast. All rubbish will be gathered up around 12.15pm and taken to Lyall Bay by the playground to form one huge rubbish mountain that will be collected by the council.

Pitch in for a rubbish pile up at 12:30 at Lyall Bay playground where we will mound up our rubbish and admire our collective efforts! Then we will head to Parrotdog for a drink / kai after!

WHERE
Our fantastic friendly volunteer groups will be scattered along the coastline between Owhiro Bay and Breaker Bay. You can turn up at any of our volunteer sites:

Site 1 - Owhiro Bay hosted by Project Jonah
Site 2 - Dive Wellington hosted by Dive Wellington

description:
AlterCOP30: Climate Fresk Workshop in Wellington, Do you want to be part of the solution to tackle climate change but don’t have the time to become a climate scientist? Join us for a 3-hour interactive workshop to explore the causes and consequences of climate disturbances.
Based on the IPCC report and played by over 2 million people worldwide, this collaborative workshop allows you to understand the key issues of climate change to empower you to take action.
How it works:
The workshop is based on a 42-card game. Each card represents an element, a cause or a consequence of climate change.
In teams, guided by your facilitator, you are encouraged to find the cause-effect relationship between the different components of climate change. Collective intelligence will get you from one deck of card to the next!
This step-by-step reconstruction provides keys to understand the complexity and develop an overview of climate change.
Agenda:
Introduction, 15 mins
Fresk Card Game, 1 1/2 hours
Debrief and Actions, 1 hour 15 mins
Climate Fresk is an excellent opportunity to understand the key elements of climate change and what you can do to be part of the solution. No previous climate knowledge is needed.

Tea, coffee and snacks will be served during the short break. Workshop run by Climate Training Co. Ltd.
Donations are welcome to support climate education and action!
In solidarity with AlterCOP30, this November we’re running a series of climate events across Aotearoa - bringing communities together to learn, connect, and take action for a just and sustainable future.
AlterCOP is a Global Initiative founded by The Matcha Initiative and The Transmutation Principle, locally brought to you by Climate Club, Climate Crew, and Climate Training Co.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
AlterCOP30: Digital Collage, Led by Climate Training Co. and Jean-Philippe, the Digital Collage is a fun 3-hour workshop centred on collaboration and collective intelligence. 
The aim of the workshop is to raise awareness and train participants on the environmental issues of digital technology. The workshop also outlines solutions for a sustainable digital technology, and allows open discussions amongst participants on the important and timely topics.
A true team-building tool, allowing participants to come together and delve into the sustainability of our digital world, and engage with the solutions. 
It is built on the same theory and structure that underpins the Climate Fresk.
Benefits of this workshop for your organisation:
Build a shared understanding of digital sustainability 
Understand the problems and threats 
Find solutions that you can implement 
This workshop is rigorously sourced from data sourced by ADEME, Green IT, EcoInfo CNRS and the Shift Project’s reports and references.
How the workshop operates:
Understanding: in teams of 4 to 8, the participants identify and then draw the links between the cards of the game to build a “Collage” 
Personalisation: they visually express their key messages and link their work to their context: to take ownership of the content and create a team spirit
Debriefing: each group explains their title and decoration, then the facilitator makes a detailed summary of the whole system
Solutions: a solutions based exercise finishes the workshop, which stimulates discussion, reflection, and action around a sustainable digital world
If you're looking to build awareness and explore real solutions around digital sustainability in your organisation, this workshop is a great place to start.
In solidarity with AlterCOP30, this November we’re running a series of climate events across Aotearoa - bringing communities together to learn, connect, and take action for a just and sustainable future.
AlterCOP is a Global Initiative founded by The Matcha Initiative and The Transmutation Principle, locally brought to you by Climate Club, Climate Crew, and Climate Training Co.

description:
Awa After Dark: Spotlighting at Kumutoto Forest, Kelburn, Awa After Dark: Spotlighting at Kumutoto Forest, Kelburn
Explore your local awa with freshwater experts from our Wai Connection team at this spotlighting event at Kumutoto Forest, Kelburn. With your gumboots and a torch, head off on an evening hīkoi to your local waterway to ‘spotlight’ and observe freshwater species in their natural habitat. Learn about the health of our waterways, freshwater conservation efforts in your neighbourhood, and some of the ways that you could become a kaitiaki of your local awa. Due to the delicate nature of this awa the observations will be stream-side as we walk along the banks and bridges of the stream.

This event is in collaboration with the Kumutoto Restoration Project, a restoration group that has been working on restoring and enhancing the biodiversity within and around the ngahere and awa at Kumutoto.

Book here: https://events.humanitix.com/awa-after-dark-spotlighting-at-kumutoto

Awa After Dark events take place in the early evening, they’re perfect for the whole whānau.

This event is free, but bookings are essential. These events are very popular, please let us know if you have booked and can no longer make it so we can reallocate your spot.

Outdoor event:
This event is outdoors, please dress appropriately (gumboots and warm clothing recommended). If the weather is really bad, we'll let you know we’re cancelling via the email you've provided us.

Location:
The streams we spotlight often don't have an 'address'. On the day before the event, we'll email you all the details you need to find our exact meeting location on the night.

What is spotlighting?
Ever played spotlight with a fish? Heaps of our native freshwater critters are nocturnal. Scientists often visit freshwater areas at nighttime with a torch, it’s the best time to see exactly who’s living in our awa!

What is Wai Connection?
Wai Connection is a national programme delivered by Mountains to Sea Wellington aimed at connecting local communities to their waterways to improve them. We support communities and mana whenua with the knowledge, tools and expertise to monitor and care for their local freshwater places.

description:
Battle Hill Community Planting Day, Battle Hill Community Planting Day
Date: Sunday 26 July 2026
Time: 1pm – 4pm
Place: Battle Hill Farm Forest Park - meet at the Woolshed
Join us for a rewarding afternoon helping restore Battle Hill Farm Forest Park at our community planting day.
Greater Wellington and the Friends of Battle Hill group will be planting in two key areas — the new oak wetland and the airstrip wetland — helping to improve biodiversity and strengthen these important habitats for future generations.
We’ll wrap up the day with a BBQ to celebrate your mahi.
This planting day is perfect for those who enjoy a bit of physical activity as you’ll be carrying plants and digging holes.
What to bring and wear
• Sturdy boots or gumboots
• Long sleeves and pants, and a waterproof jacket
• Warm layers — a hat or beanie is a good idea
• A spare change of clothes (the site can be very exposed)
• Your own spade and gloves if you prefer your own
• Water bottle and snacks
We’ll provide
• Plants and planting tools
• Gloves
• An experienced team leader
• Health and safety briefing and support
• Hot drinks and a sausage sizzle

description:
Botanical Insights talk - Ancient plants, This talk, which partners a major pictorial display at the Tree House, starts with a look at landscapes preceding the rise of trees. It then focuses on the Silurian, Devonian and Carboniferous geological periods, characterised by the appearance of the likes of scale trees, seed ferns and calamites.….and the swamp forests that gave rise to the production of coal. Then it advances to the Permian period, including Gondwana prior to its eventual breakup, and the beautiful, strange, gymnosperm Glossopteris that was widespread in the ancient southern continents, embracing what is now New Zealand/Aotearoa. Finally, it progresses to the world of ‘living fossils’ such as ginkgo and the even more primitive horsetails. Attention will be drawn to some of the animals that populated this ancient world.

Located in the Treehouse Seminar Room, Wellington Botanic Garden ki Paekākā.
Free of charge. You’re welcome to bring along your own ‘brown bag’ lunch to enjoy during the talk.

The speaker is Reg Harris, a volunteer guide [botany] at Wellington Botanic Garden.
Reg delivers botany lectures for diverse audiences, delving into plant interactions, adaptive radiation, tropisms, and more. As a dedicated volunteer guide at Wellington Botanic Garden (WBG), he pioneered collaborations between WBG and Victoria University, organising annual field labs for biology students.

description:
Botanical insights display - Ancient plants, Ancient plants and a few animals

A boom in ‘modern’ palaeobotany started in the early 19th century and continues to the present day. A pictorial display at Wellington Botanic Garden’s Tree House highlights key discoveries in this long trek, and also gives us a glimpse of some of the animals that shared the world with plants.
The display is in two halves. From 1 November to mid-December, the ‘scene’ is set, and includes a look at the landscape preceding the rise of trees. It then moves on to the Silurian, Devonian and Carboniferous periods, characterised by the appearance of the likes of scale trees, seed ferns and calamites…. and the swamp forests that gave rise to the production of coal.
The mid-December to 31 January half focuses on the Permian period, including Gondwana before its eventual breakup, and the beautiful, strange, gymnosperm Glossopteris that was widespread in the ancient southern continents. It then, finally, progresses to the world of ‘living fossils’ such as ginkgo and the even more primitive horsetails.
A public talk associated with the display will be held at the Tree House on 2 December.

description:
Challenges in a Changing World – what kind of future do we want?, Public Talk & Workshop

Humanity is at crossroads
One path into the future leads to increasing social and economic division, environmental destruction, war and planetary peril. The other path leads to increasing social harmony, economic and environmental balance, a golden era of peace.

Throughout history, especially at times of crisis, great spiritual teachers have emerged to show humanity the next step forward.

According to British artist, author and esotericist Benjamin Creme, a group of such spiritual teachers is now living in the modern world ~ Maitreya, the World Teacher and The Masters of Wisdom ~ to help and inspire humanity in its task of global transformation ~ to create a civilisation based on sharing, justice and peace; for humanity to act - to share and save our world.

From ancient times, a body of spiritual teachings known as the Ageless Wisdom has been handed down from generation to generation. A systematic and comprehensive account of the evolution of consciousness in humanity and nature, it describes how the universe came to exist, how it operates, and humanity’s place within it.

As humanity matures, further aspects of this previously hidden knowledge are released in a wider, more open manner. Throughout the last 100 years, the Ageless Wisdom Teachings have been communicated through individuals such as Helena Blavatsky, founder of the Theosophical Society, and later by Alice A. Bailey and Helena Roerich; followed by Benjamin Creme.

Along the lines of these teachings, humanity is once again at a critical point in its further development, now with a growing awareness of the necessity for unity, justice and peace.

According to these teachings, Maitreya – known as the Teacher for this coming Age of Aquarius – will emphasise the utter necessity for peace, and that the complete renunciation of war can only be achieved by trust. Sharing alone, Maitreya will affirm, can engender that trust.


~ followed by short Transmission Meditation session ~

description:
Climate Fresk Workshop in Wellington, Do you want to be part of the solution to tackle climate change but don’t have the time to become a climate scientist? Join us for a 3-hour interactive workshop to explore the causes and consequences of climate disturbances.
Based on the IPCC report and played by over 2 million people worldwide, this collaborative workshop allows you to understand the key issues of climate change to empower you to take action.
How it works:
The workshop is based on a 42-card game. Each card represents an element, a cause or a consequence of climate change.
In teams, guided by your facilitator, you are encouraged to find the cause-effect relationship between the different components of climate change. Collective intelligence will get you from one deck of card to the next!
This step-by-step reconstruction provides keys to understand the complexity and develop an overview of climate change.
Agenda:
Introduction, 15 mins
Fresk Card Game, 1 1/2 hours
Debrief and Actions, 1 hour 15 mins
Climate Fresk is an excellent opportunity to understand the key elements of climate change and what you can do to be part of the solution. No previous climate knowledge is needed.

Tea, coffee and snacks will be served during the short break. Workshop run by Climate Training Co. Ltd. Donations welcome!

description:
Climate Friendly Composting, Registrations essential. Please register by emailing community@kaicycle.org.nz
This event is hosted as part of Climate Festival Pōneke 2026 & Composting Awareness Week.
It’s well known that composting is a lot better than throwing food scraps in landfill - reducing greenhouse gas emissions, returning nutrients to the soil, improving soil health and microbiology, sequestering carbon in the soil, and growing more kai. But... composting still produces greenhouse gas emissions. The recipe and the composting method used can hugely affect the amount of greenhouse gases emitted during the decomposition of organic materials, and the quality and biological composition of the resulting compost can have climate implications too.
Join us at Kaicycle Urban Farm to learn about a range of composting methods and the climate impact they have, and find out what practical techniques you can use to minimise emissions from composting at home and make the most healthy compost possible.
Welcome to join for any other part of the day -

description:
Community Agency - a conversation with Markus Luczak-Roesch and Gerhard Reese, Two scholars share their perspectives on Community Agency and discuss the links between the Global environmental and global mental health crises.
  Gerhard Reese
Gerhard Reese works as Associate Professor for Climate Change at Te Herenga Waka - Victoria University Wellington in Aotearoa / New Zealand. Before, he was Professor and head of the Environmental Psychology Research Unit at the University Kaiserslautern-Landau in Germany since 2016. He got his PhD in Psychology from Friedrich Schiller University Jena, Germany, in February 2010. His research focuses on individual, social and systemic catalysts and barriers of pro-environmental behaviour and the nature-health nexus. He attempts and sometimes succeeds to spend more time outdoors than indoors and he still is a serious competitor in Super Mario Kart.
Markus Luczak-Roesch
Markus Luczak-Roesch is Professor of Informatics and the inaugural Chair in Complexity Science at Victoria University of Wellington’s School of Information Management. He is also one of two Co-Directors of Te Pūnaha Matatini, Aotearoa New  Zealand’s Centre of Research Excellence in Complex Systems. He founded and leads the Complexity & Connection Science Lab, an interdisciplinary group developing theories and computational tools to understand how complex systems unfold over time. His research investigates how structure and meaning emerge in systems - from language and brain activity to online communities and the environment - using models that reveal meaningful coincidences and unexpected system-level behaviors.

description:
Community Open Day - Pēpuere / February, Respecting Papatūānuku is a way in which we can all do our bit under Te Tiriti o Waitangi, so join us this Waitangi weekend to get your hands in the māra and learn about our methods to leave this whenua better than we found it.
Have you been looking for a chance to visit Kaicycle Urban Farm? Come along our Community Open Day regularly in spring, summer, and autumn! Each open day includes a working bee, shared lunch, koha workshop, and compost sales. Come along for as much or as little of the day as you would like!
9:30am - 12.30pm COMMUNITY WORKING BEE - Registrations required
Many hands make light work - come and get your hands in the māra - with a bunch of us we'll be able to get a good chunk of mahi done, plus you'll take some skills home for your own māra! Register at www.kaicycle.org.nz/volunteer
12:30PM - 1:30pm, KAI BREAK
Bring a picnic lunch and join us for koha coffee, tea, and cake.
1:00pm -1:30pm FARM TOUR
If you haven't been to our urban farm before, this is a great opportunity to find out what we're all about and how our farm and community composting works.
1:00pm - 2.30pm KOHA WORKSHOP: KAICYCLE'S HUA PARAKORE JOURNEY- This Waitangi weekend, get some information about Kaicycle's Hua Parakore journey! Hua Parakore is a Māori led organic growing verification system, open to home gardeners and commercial growers! Kaicycle has been on the Hua Parakore waka for 3 years, learning about growing and composting on this Māori whenua in a way that respects Papatūānuku and tino rangatiratanga. Come along to this workshop whether or not you're interested in joining the Hua Parakore waka; explore the pillars of Hua Parakore, built around te ao Māori; hear about Kaicycle's experiences; and get tips for running your own māra and composting in a whenua respectful way.
Registrations required - email community@kaicycle.org.nz to sign up.

description:
Community Planting Belmont Regional Park, Help us reforest the hills of Belmont Regional Park. By planting native trees and shrubs, we will restore the native ngahere/forests and create an ecological corridor for wildlife to travel between Wellington, Porirua, Kāpiti and the Hutt Valley.

We have partnered with GWRC, PCC, and local iwi to restore the hills of Belmont Park. Starting on the west hillside, our aim this year is to plant 5,000 native plants to create a forest for the future! This project aims to bring the community together to restore the hillsides of the Belmont Regional Park.

We provide all the tools and training, no prior experience needed. We can even provide transport to the site. Just bring your energy and lunch. We will provide you with a yummy morning tea.

Come have some fun planting with us and TAKE ACTION FOR NATURE!

This event is part of Conservation Week 2025 - www.doc.govt.nz/conservationweek

Sign up for this event on our website ConservationVolunteers.co.nz or email Wellington@cvnz.org.nz

description:
Community Snorkel, *New Location: Scorching Bay Beach*
--------------------------------------------------
Dive into a free snorkelling event this summer!
Beginners welcome! We provide all necessary gear and experienced guides to ensure your safety and enjoyment in the water. Participants just need to be at least eight years old and confident swimmers. Those under sixteen must be accompanied by an adult.
Registrations open at 9.45am. Come down to book a snorkel time for the day, as spots may fill up quickly. Bring your togs, towel, refreshments and make a day of it exploring the activities and environment at Scorching Bay Beach.
This free event is brought to you in partnership with Greater Wellington Regional Council.
Cancellations/Postponements
Events are weather dependent. Stay updated by checking MTSW Facebook event listings for any cancellations, postponements, or location changes.
A note on water quality- We are keeping a close eye on the situation at Moa Point Wastewater Treatment Plant and the impact to Wellington's South Coast. As this event is taking place in Wellington Harbour, there are currently no concerns to water quality due to the Moa Point spill. As well monitoring the impact of this spill, please be assured we are always monitoring water quality ahead of snorkel events. Often, after heavy rain, water quality can dip due to runoff via stormwater pipes. This affects not only visibility, but in-water safety. MTSW only ever operates when LAWA shows a green (safe to swim) water quality rating.
Accessibility
There is accessible parking and toilets at Scorching Bay. There is access via beach wheelchair to the beach area and the area in front of the beach is fully accessible. We have a variety of options to enable a more comfortable experience in the water including flotation aids and 1:1 support from our trained guides. Please get in touch with us at events@mtsw.org.nz in advance of the event to discuss your accessibility requirements, including to enquire about beach wheelchair assistance, we love helping people to experience our marine environment!
The snorkelling in this event is run under the Health and Safety of the Mountains to Sea Conservation Trust programme Experiencing Marine Reserves. Adventure Activity Certified - AA0534.
Photos: Kristine Zipfel

description:
Conservation Kōrero: Caring For Cats Indoors, Join us at Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne for an engaging and balanced kōrero about one of the more challenging conversations in pet ownership today – indoor cats.

Whether you’re the owner of a roaming cat, have a “catio” setup, are thinking about your next feline friend, or are simply wildlife-conscious, this is a chance to hear from veterinarian Brendon Bullen of Kelburn Vets about the facts, the challenges, and the practical options available to current and future cat owners.

We’ll explore how to keep cats happy, healthy, and enriched indoors, while sharing practical tips, surprising cat trivia, and myth-busting insights.

Come along for ideas, open discussion, and a fresh take on feline care and conservation.

This event will be held in the Pāteke Room in the Visitor Centre with light refreshments provided. Doors open at 6.00pm, parking is available at both our Visitor Centre and overflow parking area on Birdwood Street.

description:
Conservation Kōrero: Dark Skies, Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne and the Wellington Astronomical Society have teamed up to bring you an evening of ‘Dark Skies’.

Astronomer Holly McClelland will begin the evening with a talk on the importance of dark skies, both to the natural ecosystem and to human health.
Illustrated with stunning image from the Cretney Observatory near Martinborough, Holly will introduce us to the night sky, so the next time you are looking to the stars you can not only find the Southern Cross, but also the Galactic Kiwi.

Weather permitting, we will then have an hour of telescope viewing from the Zealandia carpark. Alternatively, if the weather isn’t ideal, you’ll get the chance to get an up-close look at some of the incredible astronomical equipment used by the Wellington Astronomical Society. WAS members will be available to answer your questions.

About Holly:
Holly is an astronomer and science communicator. She has a Bachelor of Science in Astronomy from the University of Canterbury, was a senior astronomy guide in Tekapo, leading groups on once-in-a-lifetime stargazing experiences. Holly is also on the council of the Wellington Astronomy Society, helping to make events like this possible.

description:
Conservation Kōrero: Discoveries in Dragonflies, Recent summers have seen the sanctuary humming with damselflies and dragonflies-a positive sign of our freshwater restoration projects. These incredible apex predators of the insect world are masters of flight, but aspects of their lives are still shrouded in mystery and intrigue, especially when it comes to some of the more elusive and unique species of Aotearoa.

Join us for a kōrero/talk led by dragonfly ambassadors Ruary Mackenzie Dodds and Kari de Koenigswarter to hear more about dragonflies and damselflies, and learn about their latest discoveries in the secret lives of the bush giant dragonflies!

This event will be held in the Pāteke Room with refreshments provided. Doors open at 7.00pm.

Speaker bio:

Ruary Mackenzie Dodds F.L.S.
Ruary is a “Dragonfly Ambassador” for the British Dragonfly Society with several published books and many public lectures and radio segments both in New Zealand and the UK under his belt. He has been carrying out research in and around the Pencarrow Lakes, south of Eastbourne, and alongside his wife Kari and Dr George Gibbs is currently working on a night filming project of the elusive Bush Giant dragonfly and its previously unrecorded nocturnal activities.
Ruary’s aim is to publicise the importance of dragonflies as bio-indicators to New Zealanders, how they can be used as a simple way to detect the health of freshwater spaces, and highlight their amazing life-cycle, extraordinary behaviour, and the threats they face.
For more details about Ruary, see www.ruarymackenziedodds.com.

Kari de Koenigswarter
Kari is a full-time artist and a specialist in the study of dragonfly larvae. She has worked alongside Ruary every step of his dragonfly journey. She has personally designed and run many Odonata Larval Identification courses in the UK, including for the UK Environment Agency.
Kari’s work in New Zealand has included identifying exuviae at Lakes Kohangapiripiri and Kohangatera in order to establish proof of breeding of species there. Quite apart from time spent staring down a microscope, this has involved standing knee-deep in lake water for up to an hour and a half at a time!
For more details about Kari, see www.karidekoenigswarter.com or @karidekartist on Instagram

description:
Conservation Kōrero: Discoveries in Dragonflies, Recent summers have seen the sanctuary humming with damselflies and dragonflies-a positive sign of our freshwater restoration projects. These incredible apex predators of the insect world are masters of flight, but aspects of their lives are still shrouded in mystery and intrigue, especially when it comes to some of the more elusive and unique species of Aotearoa.
Join us for a kōrero/talk led by dragonfly ambassadors Ruary Mackenzie Dodds and Kari de Koenigswarter to hear more about dragonflies and damselflies, and learn about their latest discoveries in the secret lives of the bush giant dragonflies!
This event will be held in the Pāteke Room with refreshments provided. Overflow parking is available on Birdwood Street. Doors open at 6.45pm.

description:
Conservation Kōrero: Roots of Resilience, Climate anxiety is becoming increasingly common, particularly among people who care deeply about the future of the environment and society.

This thoughtful Conservation Kōrero explores how we can navigate uncertainty without becoming consumed by fear, helplessness or burnout. Through reflections on resilience, values and the restorative effects of nature, Dr Ivan Lin discusses how confidence can emerge from staying present and taking meaningful action aligned with what matters most.

Dr Lin is a medical doctor, speaker and workshop facilitator with experience delivering public and professional wellbeing programmes focused on resilience, emotional wellbeing and the relationship between people and the natural world.

This event will be held in the Pāteke Room on the Visitor Centre, with doors opening at 1.45pm. Parking is available outside the Visitor Centre, along Waiapu Road, and at our overflow carpark on Birdwood Street. Zealandia's free shuttle will be running it's usual schedule.

Photo: Scott Langdale
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Conservation Kōrero: The Transformation of Mana Island, Mana Island is one of Aotearoa New Zealand’s conservation success stories. Farmed off the coast of Porirua for more than 150 years, the island is now covered with forest that is overflowing with an abundance of endemic birds, lizards and insects. Some of our own species translocations at Zealandia can be traced back to Mana Island!

In our next Conservation Kōrero natural history curator Dr Colin Miskelly describes the transformation from farm station to thriving island sanctuary.

This event will be held in the Pāteke Room with refreshments provided. Doors open at 7.15pm, overflow parking is available along Waiapu Road and at Birdwood Street carpark.

description:
Conservation Kōrero: Under The Mistletoe, Join us this December for a kōrero exploring the complex lives of native mistletoes in Aotearoa New Zealand.
Leading mistletoe expert and hands-on conservation practitioner, Trevor Thompson, will share insights into the ecology of these beautiful yet elusive plants, how he is propagating them, and the challenges they face across our landscapes.
From habitat loss to seed dispersal and browsing impacts, learn what is threatening the survival of these special plants and what’s being done to protect them. Come along to deepen your understanding, ask questions, and discover how we can help ensure these special species remain part of our ngahere for generations to come.

description:
Conservation Kōrero: Underwater Forests of Wellington, Towering seaweed forests and colourful sponge gardens lie just beneath the surface of Wellington’s coastline. Like forests on land, these underwater habitats support a remarkable diversity of life, including treasured kaimoana species. Yet they face growing pressure from human activity and environmental change.
Dr Nicole Miller will take us on a visual journey through Wellington’s Blue Belt, exploring current conservation successes and challenges. Drawing on years of diving, photography and local restoration work, Nicole will highlight the beauty and fragility of these ecosystems and why it’s more important than ever to bring changes to the surface.
This event will be held in the Pāteke Room in the Visitor Centre with light refreshments provided. Doors open at 6:00pm, parking is available at both our Visitor Centre and overflow parking area on Birdwood Street.
Nicole’s seaweed artworks will be on display at Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne from 1 August to 30 September, with all profits supporting Explore Your Coast: www.exploreyourcoast.co.nz/docu.

description:
Conservation Week, Skink and Gecko Live Show Reino Grundling will talk and show slides illustrating the mostly unrealised role that lizards (skinks and geckos) had in our pristine ecosystems, with some 130 or more different species! And what makes this presentation so marvellous is that he will have a number of living examples there for all to see! Great for the kids!

Conservation Colouring Competition The Masterton Library is celebrating the importance of conservation with a colouring competition—and there are some great prizes up for grabs. There will also be an informative display featuring conservation-themed resources you’re welcome to take home with you.

Dr Marie Doole Biodiversity Funding Talk Dr Marie Doole will discuss the pros and cons around nature/biodiversity credits, an emerging option for funding the protection of biodiversity, particularly on private land, by investors, whether corporate or philanthropic. Worth attending if you've been following the media hype.

Think Like a Forest Film Forest and Bird are showing this film, starring Sam the Trap Man, in three locations. The Regent have generously offered to show it where it will have the most effect—on the big screen! The film is produced by Pure Advantage who have an aspirational programme around landscape-scale restoration of native forests called Recloaking Papatūānuku.

Kōkako Morning Hikoi Join us for a special one-off tour and experience the magic of the kōkako at Pūkaha. Follow our expert guide to a kōkako hotspot and enjoy the rare opportunity to possibly see and hear kōkako. After your walk, return to the centre for a hot drink and morning tea.

Waihinga Bridge Planting Morning Ruamāhanga Farm Foundation is hosting a morning of planting and a celebration of children's voices at the start of the soon to be opened Waihinga Bridge Walkway. Tools will be provided and all ages and abilities are welcome!

Exploring Ngahere Under Story and Campfire Talk The Tramping Gently Club Art Collective (TGCAC) takes up temporary residency at Te Whare Whakapapa Raranga to explore human-centred warning systems and ngahere's role in mitigating danger. Join us in bringing the understory into te whare through kōrero and creative exploration.

description:
Dark Sky Trek Wainuiomata, Dark Sky Trek Wainuiomata
We’ve teamed up with the Wellington Astronomical Society to bring you this exclusive FREE behind-the-scenes event.

Walk deep into untouched native forest, through some of the oldest trees in the Wellington region as darkness falls. You may even hear the calls of kiwi and rūrū (morepork). Explore an area not normally open to the public, including a glowworm-filled tunnel that links to the Orongorongo Valley.

The Wellington Astronomical Society will share insights on Dark Sky awareness and preservation and provide a telescope for viewing the Moon and the Southern Cross. Talk to Remutaka Conservation Trust volunteers about their Kiwi release programme and nest monitoring efforts.

Wainuiomata Regional Park is working towards dark sky reserve accreditation, one of only three in the Southern Hemisphere. Light pollution from the city washes out most stars, but the park offers one of the best stargazing experiences in the region.

What to bring:
• Torches/headlamps (red lenses preferred)
• Sturdy waterproof footwear
• Warm and wet weather clothing

Note: This event includes a steep hill walk in the dark. A moderate level of fitness is required, and it is not suitable for children under 15.

This event is strictly limited to 30 people. Registrations for this event will be on a first in first served basis and opens at 10am on Tuesday 14 July via this link:

Denniston - a place worth fighting for., The Denniston Plateau is one of Aotearoa's most unique landscapes and is rated by the Department of Conservation as a key ecologically valuable site. It is a unique ‘lost world’ ecosystem home to a remarkable array of life. A fast-track application to mine 20-million tonnes of coal in the area is expected to be filed this year.
Join us for an engaging session to:
Hear from experts about Denniston Plateau’s extraordinary biodiversity and ecology.
View a photo exhibition by West Coast photographer Neil Silverwood capturing the Plateau’s beauty.
Learn about the proposal to expand coal mining in the area
Wine, beer and appetisers are provided. You may be asked to show proof of identity upon arrival.

description:
Designing Tomorrow: The SDG Blueprint for Built Environment Futures, Designing Tomorrow: The SDG Blueprint for Built Environment Futures
📅 Wednesday, 1 October 2025
🕔 5:00–7:30 PM (Networking from 5:00 PM | Panels 5:30–7:30 PM)
📍 Te Aro Campus, Faculty of Architecture and Design Innovation, Victoria University of Wellington (139 Vivian Street)
The built environment is at the heart of Aotearoa’s response to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals SDGs). The way we plan, design, and construct our cities influences how we live — and how we tackle challenges such as climate change (SDG 13), sustainable cities and communities (SDG 11), affordable housing and equity (SDG 10),
responsible consumption and production (SDG 12), and partnerships for action (SDG 17).
This event is part of SDG Action Month 2025, a global campaign that highlights how communities, institutions, and industries are accelerating progress toward the 2030 Agenda.
For Aotearoa, the conversation is urgent: how can planning, design, and construction shape a sustainable, equitable, and climate-resilient future?
The evening will open with a keynote address that sets the stage with global perspectives on sustainability and the role of the built environment in achieving the SDGs.
Two panels will then explore critical themes:
• Planning + Place + People — equity, housing futures, cultural identity, indigenous leadership, and policy alignment.
• Materials + Methods + Innovation—construction technology, green standards, digital tools, and carbon-conscious practice.
Alongside the discussions, attendees can view a Student Showcase from the School of Architecture and the School of Design Innovation, and contribute to a Blueprint Wall by writing their own pledges on SDG Commitment Cards, ensuring the event concludes with collective action as well as ideas.
📌 Free to attend | Open to all | RSVP required

description:
Destination Earth, Expect your senses to be stirred in a new art installation. Destination Earth aims to inspire climate action through art. It incorporates satellite data, real-time generative music, and responds to audience movement in real-time. Using video and immersive sound, audiences will be challenged to reconsider the rhythm of living as humans. 
You are invited to dive into the flow of the Southern Ocean and explore the pulse of the Antarctic circumpolar current. Participate by adjusting your walking patterns and breathing to ‘regenerate’ the world around you. Motion sensors will pick up your activity and adjust the environment to suit. At a sensorial level the effects of climate change will come to life. 

Destination Earth is a collaboration between Cellule Studio (UK) and Victoria University of Wellington. The work, by artist Salome Bazin, mixes art, science, and technology. It emphasises the urgent need to slow down human activity.  

A bi-cultural perspective is also central to the experience. Māori symbolic views of the ocean are included, offering a richer narrative of the global climate.
 
Image credit: Cellule Studio, directed by Salomé Bazin.

description:

Meet at the Founders' Entrance, Glenmore Street.
Cost: $10 or Free for Friends – bookings required (you’ll get the option to choose your ticket type after clicking ‘Buy Tickets’)

This is part of the regular walks run by the Friends of the Wellington Botanic Garden. They run throughout the year with a different topic every time.

Join the Friends for only $30 a year and all the walks will be free, as well as other great benefits.

description:
Dragonflies & Damselflies are Amazing and Important - Forest&bird Talk, Ruary Mackenzie Dodds and his wife Kari de Koenigswarter are rated as Dragonfly Ambassadors by the British Dragonfly Society. Although they have recently been involved in the setting up of a Dragonfly Hotspot at Exbury Gardens in Hampshire, England, their work currently centres on New Zealand where awareness of the significance of dragonflies is possibly behind that of the U.K, which has a growing understanding that dragonflies are a key indicator of the health of waterspaces. In this talk, Ruary takes his listeners back to basics on the amazing life-cycle of these insects. He outlines typical preferred dragonfly habitats, and touches on identification of New Zealand species. In addition to Ruary’s talk, Kari’s larva demonstration table shows actual examples of the larval stages on NZ species.

In their New Zealand work, Ruary and Kari are carrying out survey work on behalf of the Greater Wellington Regional Council, and are preparing a dragonfly education pack for schools. They have also carried out five summer seasons of night-filming an endemic dragonfly species – the Bush Giant – that lives in a burrow! A Radio New Zealand Our Changing World programme has been devoted to their work. (https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/ourchangingworld/546925/dragonflies-masters-of-flight).

Ruary and Kari have been working with dragonflies since 1985. They opened Europe’s first Dragonfly Sanctuary in 1991, and founded the National Dragonfly Biomuseum in Northamptonshire in 1995. They and their team of volunteers continued work with the National Trust at Wicken Fen in Cambridgeshire, and were instrumental in the setting up of the Dragonfly Centre there in 2009. Their adventures were published in Ruary’s memoir, The Dragonfly Diaries (Saraband, 2014). Kari and Ruary have also published a how-to book, Dragonfly-Friendly Gardening (Saraband, 2024). Ruary is a Fellow of the Linnean Society. He has given talks in eight countries. He has appeared on both television and radio, and was awarded BBC Springwatch’s ‘Dragonfly Geek’ award. He has been featured in BBC Wildlife Magazine, The Scottish Field, and in Wildlife Trust and National Trust publications. Kari specializes in the larval stages of odonate life, while – even after over forty years – Ruary’s heart lifts at the sight of a dragonfly in flight, and he loves sharing this enthusiasm with his listeners!

description:
EBANZ Natural Building Conference 2025, EBANZ Natural Building Conference 2025
This year’s EBANZ (Earth Building Association of New Zealand) national conference will see industry leaders, innovators and enthusiasts come together to profile the latest ideas, technologies and projects shaping the future of low carbon, high performing, sustainable building in Aotearoa.

Set at Te Wānanga o Raukawa and the Forest Lakes Conference Centre on the Kāpiti Coast, the earth building conference will see builders, designers, researchers and earth-building enthusiasts explore how traditional and contemporary earth construction methods are shaping resilient, sustainable futures in Aotearoa and beyond.

Themed ‘Earth, Culture and Community’, the three-day conference in mid-November will include presentations, hands-on workshops, site visits and kōrero with leading voices in natural building, indigenous knowledge, climate-responsive design and regenerative practice, while also profiling New Zealand’s own set of earth building standards (NZS 4297, 4298 and 4299) 2024.

A ‘Professionals Day’ on Friday 14 November at Te Wānanga o Raukawa is aimed specifically at architects, engineers, inspectors, builders and designers interested in earth and natural building techniques. It will dive into the Tennent Brown Architects-designed Pā Reo campus at Te Wānanga (a Living Building Challenge project) and presenters will include Rau Hoskins of designTRIBE, Verena Maeder of Solid Earth and Sigi Koko, founder of Build Naturally USA.

Friday will be followed by the in-depth weekend conference at Forest Lakes, featuring talks and presentations aimed to inform and empower people on different aspects of earth and natural building as well as hands-on workshops in different methods and materials, including clay-based plasters, cob, rammed earth and adobe, straw bale and hempcrete. House tours will feature different building techniques, including straw bale and rammed earth, adobe, natural plasters and more.

description:
Edible Weeds Foraging Workshop 23rd November 2025, Join expert forager Felicity Joy of Wild Botanica for a comprehensive Wild Edible Weeds Foraging Workshop in the beautiful community gardens of Mount Victoria, Wellington.
This inspiring experience will open your eyes to the abundance of edible wild plants growing right under your nose.
We’ll unlock the secrets of foraging, connecting with the land, and turning humble "weeds" into delicious, nourishing food. You’ll gain confidence in identifying common edible plants, learn their botanical names, and understand their medicinal and nutritional benefits. We’ll also explore ethical foraging practices, how to spot toxic lookalikes, and share simple, practical ways to incorporate wild foods into your daily meals.
This isn’t just about food: it’s about sustainability, resilience, and reconnecting with the environment in a meaningful way. You'll leave with a deeper appreciation for the land, new skills to support local food security, and the knowledge to make your own simple meals from wild ingredients.
Class sizes are limited, so book early to secure your spot.
For more details and bookings, visit

follow @wild.botanica.nz on social media.

description:
Electrify Porirua: how to save money on your energy bills feat. Mike Casey, It keeps getting more expensive to heat our homes and water, cook our meals and get around. But there is a way to avoid those rising costs and Electrify Porirua will show you how.  
Most Porirua homes could be saving thousands on their energy bills each year, while also slashing emissions, simply by upgrading their gas and petrol machines to the electric equivalents available today - and ideally powering them with solar and batteries for more self-sufficiency in case of power cuts or natural disasters.
Porirua has crossed the “electrification tipping point” where homes, farms and businesses can now save money and reduce their emissions by going electric. It’s a massive win-win and a lot of people don’t know about the potential savings that are hiding in their cupboards, kitchens and driveways. 
Rewiring Aotearoa is trying to change that and we’re supporting grassroots action across the country. Community electrification groups are popping up all over the place and helping to raise awareness about the benefits for their local region and helping locals through the process. Now, it’s time to bring the buzz to Porirua.
Come along to hear from Mike Casey, who is saving tens of thousands a year on his all-electric solar-powered cherry orchard, and find out how electrifying Porirua is the smartest, cheapest, and healthiest way to power our lives.

description:
Evening meeting - A mycology of New Zealand in 10 fungi, Speaker: Dr Geoff Ridley. Fungi are often overlooked. Most people only become aware of them when there is a problem, the bathroom ceiling goes mouldy, the roses need spraying because of the black spot, mushrooms sprout all over the lawn. The bigger role that fungi play in our lives is missed. This is the story of ten little-known fungi that are important biologically, culturally, historically, and economically in Aotearoa.
Geoff is a mycologist who studied the larger fungi in the Ōrongorongo Valley for his PhD at Victoria University of Wellington, and as a forest mycologist and pathologist at the Forest Research Institute in Rotorua. He currently works in the nationally significant collections of fungi held by Manaaki Whenua – Landcare Research. His personal interest is in discovering the fungi of the Kaiwharawhara Valley in Wellington.

Let's give the trees a bit of summer love, so they can return us a kai in Autumn!

We'll just be doing some mahi to prepare the trees for the hot months, at our two sites around the corner from each other in Titahi Bay. Weeding, feeding and maybe a little mulch if we can get some! We will also listen to some tunes and continue to figure out how to save the world.

We'll start with the trees at the top of Tireti Rd site (walkway entrance: https://maps.app.goo.gl/r6atPhuZECgS5XAn7). We'll do a quick tidy up there, until about 11.

Then at about 11-11.30 we'll head to the Pikarere Reserve site (Top of Pikarere, almost at end of 220 bus line: https://maps.app.goo.gl/TmDKyr4JsXgkjoeY8).

It's the last session of 2025, so we'll have a bit of a shared kai to enjoy the fruits of the year. Then we'll get back into it until the place is looking good!

The plan is for us to catch back up later in summer, and in Autumn we'll come together again and celebrate our harvest together, from our community trees to our backyards!
