description:
Friends AGM with guest speakers, Join the Friends of Wellington Botanic Garden for our Annual General Meeting and a pair of inspiring botanical presentations. You don’t have to be a member to attend — everyone’s invited!
Programme
Each presentation is 30 minutes, with time for questions.
Paul Bell-Butler
Botanist and PhD candidate, Paul is delving into the hidden world of leafy liverworts (family Lophocoleaceae). His research combines modern molecular techniques with traditional botany to reveal how these overlooked plants shape ecosystems and influence seed germination.
Clare Shearman
Plant Collection Team Manager at Wellington Botanic Garden, Clare brings a career spanning historic English estates to iconic New Zealand gardens. Fresh from the prestigious Longwood Gardens Fellows program in the USA, she shares insights into garden design, conservation, and how public gardens nurture wellbeing and connection.
Come along to hear their stories, celebrate our beautiful gardens, and meet fellow plant enthusiasts.
Located in the Treehouse Seminar Room, Wellington Botanic Garden ki Paekākā.
For more info about the Friends: https://friendsofthewellingtonbotanic.wordpress.com/

description:
Future Architecture of the Network (FAN) Conference 2026, Kia ora!
Electricity and electrification are seen as the significant enablers for decarbonisation of our nation. The Future Architecture of the Network (FAN) | Te Whatunga Hiko programme aspires to meet the challenges the electrical power system will face as we journey towards sustainable decarbonisation.
Our vision is to provide an infrastructure paradigm through a hybrid AC/DC transmission and distribution system that meets the needs of tomorrow’s efficient, low-carbon, reliable and resilient electrical power system.
Funded as part of the New Zealand Government’s Strategic Science Investment Fund (SSIF) on Advanced Energy Technology Platform (AETP), the research team is investigating what the future electrical power system might look like.
Hear about the team’s latest achievements as we approach the final phase of the programme.
Attendance is in person at Victoria University Wellington.
Ngā mihi nui,
Prof. Neville Watson,
Science Leader
The detailed programme will be circulated closer to the event.
 More information on the research can be found at https://www.fan.ac.nz/
If you have any questions, please contact futurearchitecturenetwork@canterbury.ac.nz

description:
GDNZ 2025 Shelly Bay Cleanup, *POSTPONED TO 18TH OF OCTOBER*
Join Ghost Diving New Zealand for a community cleanup!

This will be an ocean and shore based clean up targeting rubbish in and around the Wellington foreshore.

Scuba divers, free divers and shore crew all needed! Be prepared to get wet and dirty!

9.00am - Registrations open
9:45am - Briefing
10.00am - Divers in the water
2.00pm Clean-up and pack down

Scuba and Free Divers must provide their own gear and tanks. If you also have your own catch bag(s) or float boat for collecting rubbish, please bring this along and ensure they are named.
If you would like to join in the fun and participate as part of the shore crew, you will need to make sure you are wearing fully covered shoes and bring a pair of gardening gloves... also be prepared to get dirty!

ALL PARTICIPANTS, SHORE CREW AND DIVERS MUST REGISTER ON ARRIVAL.

PLEASE NOTE:
• This is a free, family friendly event, but children must be supervised at all times by an adult.
• Closed toe footwear must be worn for safety.
• Please bring your own hand protection (gardening gloves or similar).
• Don’t forget your own water bottle and bring sunscreen if it’s a warm day.
• Dress for the weather (warm clothes and jackets)
• There will also be plenty of work for non-divers to get involved.
Should the event be cancelled due to circumstances out of our control, notification will be given on the Facebook page the night before. Please remember to check prior to the event.
We look forward to seeing you there!

Roll up your sleeves and join us for the Great Big Waterfront Clean-Up 2026. Help clean up our waterfront and keep trash out of our harbour.

What to bring:
Sturdy footwear

Sun-smart gear
Raincoat (just in case!)*

Haewai Catchment Climate Adaptation Workshop, Join us for coffee, kai, and conversation at a relaxed, family-friendly community event in Haewai Houghton Valley. This is your chance to share your thoughts, ideas, and local knowledge about how our community can respond to the challenges of climate change.

We’ll be running interactive activities for all ages, including a colouring contest and lego building for kids, while the adults can share their ideas, experiences and knowledge about the neighbourhood and explore what makes Haewai Houghton Valley special. Whether you’ve been involved in local projects for years or are new to thinking about climate adaptation, your voice is important.
Plus, everyone who takes part goes in the draw to win a 200-litre emergency water tank - a fun (and practical!) way to get your household prepared for anything.

This event is part of the Paekawakawa / Haewai Local Climate Adaptation Pilot, where Council, mana whenua, and the community are working side by side to shape a shared vision for a resilient and thriving Houghton Valley.

description:
Hua Parakore Soil Health Wānanga, Looking to build healthy soils, grow healthy kai and take care of the wellbeing of your whānau, whenua and future generations?
Learn to apply hua parakore approaches in your own māra with our very special Hua Parakore Soil Health Wānanga in May.
The two-day wānanga is led by hua parakore food grower Dr Jessica Hutchings and will take place in Te Whanganui-a-Tara.
Join Jessica to learn how to:
- Reconnect and re-member soil as an ancestor - as Hineahuone.
- Explore how hua parakore supports soil health beyond productivity by focusing on balance, vitality and intergenerational care.
- Learn the six key hua parakore principles and how these inform nurturing soils without synthetic inputs.
- Understand how to observe environmental signs and work in alignment with natural and seasonal cycles.
- Reflect on your own relationships with soil and place.
- Understand how hua parakore can be applied within marae, community and whenua-based contexts to support seed, soil and food sovereignty.
For just $40, you’ll be able to join Jessica for two days, as well as enjoy kai and a resource kete.
When: Saturday 2 May 10-4pm and Sunday 3 May 10-3pm.
Where: Inner Most Gardens, Mt Victoria, Te Whanganui-a-Tara.
Spaces are limited to just 35 participants.

It is a wonderful welcoming monthly community gathering to share the abundance from our kitchens and gardens!
Been madly making chutney? Silver beet going crazy? Been collecting flower seeds? Got some foraged berries or a delicious cake to share?
Come along for a kōrero with our friendly community and enjoy free coffee, usually with a scone or muffin that someone has brought along. Everyone is welcome - with or without something to share.

1:30pm - 3.00pm KOHA WORKSHOP: Climate Friendly Composting -
https://www.facebook.com/events/1704614757650028/
Registration required - email community@kaicycle.org.nz to register.
It’s well known that composting is a lot better than throwing food scraps in landfill - reducing greenhouse gas emissions, returning nutrients to the soil, improving soil health and microbiology, sequestering carbon in the soil, and growing more kai. But... composting still produces greenhouse gas emissions. The recipe and the composting method used can hugely affect the amount of greenhouse gases emitted during the decomposition of organic materials, and the quality and biological composition of the resulting compost can have climate implications too.
Join us to learn about a range of composting methods and the climate impact they have, and find out what practical techniques you can use to minimise emissions from composting at home and make the most healthy compost possible.
This is a koha workshop and we ask you to pay what you can afford. If that’s a gold coin that is completely fine! If you can afford more we really appreciate it - we are a charity and rely on donations to be able to carry out our mahi. Koha can be paid in cash or by bank transfer.

Join us for this introductory workshop on seed saving. Seed saving is an ancient practice and an essential tool in creating a circular and resilient food system and enabling kai sovereignty. It also allows us to select for seed that will thrive in our micro-climates, strengthening crops year by year. We'll wānanga about the importance of saving seed, understanding the whakapapa of seeds and plant reproduction, and what you need to know to start saving seed yourself. description:
Launching in-store: Capital Trees by Susette Goldsmith, Join us in celebrating the recent launch of Capital Trees: The Arboreal Legacy of Te Upoko-O-te-Ika the Wellington Region by Susette Goldsmith, author/editor of Tree Sense: Ways of Thinking About Trees.
"The significance and meaning of trees engagingly explored through the way they have shaped our capital.
From the fossil forest of Tītahi Bay and the ageing oak on Plimmer Steps, to the karaka grove on Wellington’s waterfront and a threatened stand of lowland beech in the Hutt Valley, Capital Trees journeys across the region to trace the living legacies of the city’s rich tree heritage and the many people who have shaped, protected and challenged it.
These legacies include arguments around heritage tree listing, the native versus exotics debate, biodiversity, attitudes towards heritage authenticity, trees as monuments and more, explored through facts, anecdotes and field notes.
Illustrated with contemporary photography and specimen illustrations of the species and individual trees covered, this book is a must for all who live in the Wellington region."

description:
Lunch & Learn with David Trubridge, Join us for a very special Teulo Lunch & Learn, where design, sustainability, and community regeneration come together.
Hosted by Häfele and Teulo, this intimate event features internationally renowned designer David Trubridge and the global launch of his newest portable light: Dusk.
Enjoy lunch and conversation with peers from across the design and construction industry, with MC DK guiding the session.
What to Expect
Keynote: Think Like a Tree
In his 20-minute talk on biophilic design, David Trubridge shares how we can learn from trees and forests to design healthier, more sustainable spaces.
Film Screening: Think Like a Forest
This short film from Pure Advantage highlights the Recloaking Papatūānuku movement, an ambitious initiative to restore more than 2 million hectares of native forest and wetland in Aotearoa. Featuring Sam the Trap Man and local kaitiaki, it’s both an inspiration and a call to action.
Global Launch: The Dusk Lamp
Be among the first to experience Dusk, David’s most portable light yet, inspired by his collaboration with Pure Salt’s Tamatea Art Project in Fiordland. A new short documentary will showcase the story behind the design and the environmental partnership that shaped it. A portion of all sales will support Pure Salt’s conservation efforts in Dusky Sound.
Local Conservation Panel
Hear from organisations leading vital regeneration work, including the Maraetōtara Tree Trust, Esk River planting projects, and Te Mata Peak Park restoration, and learn how you can get involved.
Why Attend?
This Lunch & Learn is more than a product launch or film screening — it’s a chance to connect with the design community, hear from one of New Zealand’s most iconic designers, and explore practical steps toward a regenerative future.

We are in this for the long haul and a forest that contains a wide range of plant species will, in turn, attract a wider range of birds, lizards, and invertebrates. A wider range of plant species also allows for the forest to naturally regenerate and helps prevent weed species from establishing.
Tools are provided, bring sturdy shoes and a water bottle, Working bees are held every Sunday in June (except June 1st - Kings Birthday Weekend) and August 2025.

description:
October Just Sew, Join us for our Just Sew - October edition!

Got a tear, a missing button, or a hem that’s come undone? Don’t toss it - fix it! Our monthly Just Sew sessions are all about giving your clothing and textile items a second life. This is a great way to take climate action in your own life – and learn new skills along the way.

Book online and bring along 1-2 clothing or lightweight household items (cushion covers etc) for repair. We will have sewing machines, needles, thread, and a selection of patches and buttons ready for you. If you have something special you would like to use, feel free to bring it along.

Our skilled volunteers will be here to help with repairs such as holes, tears, hems and missing buttons. Whether you are completely new to sewing or just need a bit of guidance, we will support you through it.

These sessions are held at Te Aro Zero Waste on the first Saturday of every month, from 1-4 pm.

Bookings are prioritised, but we will do our best to fit in walk-ins if there’s space.

description:
Oriental Bay Tugboat Cleanup 2026 - GDNZ, Join Ghost Diving New Zealand for our first cleanup of 2026!

This will be an ocean and shore based clean up targeting rubbish in and around Oriental Bay
Scuba divers, free divers and shore crew all needed!

DATE: Saturday 2nd of May
TIMES:
9.00am - Registrations open
9:45am - Briefing
10.00am - Divers in the water
2.00pm Clean-up and pack down

LOCATION:
Oriental Bay Tugboat - look for the GDNZ signs.

Scuba Divers who wish to participate must have a minimum of 30 dives and can produce a dive log and be comfortable working in low / zero visibility.

Scuba and Free Divers must provide their own gear and tanks. If you also have your own catch bag(s) or float boat for collecting rubbish, please bring this along and ensure they are named.

If you would like to join in the fun and participate as part of the shore crew, you will need to make sure you are wearing fully covered shoes and bring a pair of gardening gloves... also be prepared to get wet and dirty!

ALL PARTICIPANTS, SHORE CREW AND DIVERS MUST REGISTER ON ARRIVAL.
PLEASE NOTE:
• This is a free, family friendly event, but children must be supervised at all times by an adult.
• Closed toe footwear must be worn for safety.
• Please bring your own hand protection (gardening gloves or similar).
• Don’t forget your own water bottle and bring sunscreen if it’s a warm day.
• Dress for the weather (warm clothes and jackets)
• There will also be plenty of work for non-divers to get involved.
Should the event be cancelled due to circumstances out of our control, notification will be given on the Facebook page the night before. Please remember to check prior to the event.

We look forward to seeing you there!

description:
Parangarahu Lakes Community Planting Day, Join us for a day of planting at these nationally significant lakes.
The Parangarahu Lakes are important to the surrounding environment and are home to native taonga. This includes a range of wetland plants, īnanga (galaxias maculatus), manu (birds), and our native freshwater mussel, the kākahi.
This planting day is perfect for those who enjoy a bit of physical activity, as you’ll be carrying plants and digging holes.
What to bring/wear:
• Sturdy boots or gumboots
• Long sleeves and pants, and a waterproof jacket are essential. Layering and wearing a hat or beanie is a good way to stay warm. This site can be very exposed, so it is a good idea to bring a spare change of clothes.
• Feel free to bring your own favourite spade and gloves.
• Bring your own water bottle, and snacks.
We provide:
• FREE transport from Burdan’s Gate, Eastbourne, along the rugged coast to the Lower Pencarrow Lighthouse at the harbour entrance and onto the entrance of the first lake. Please book your seat as we have limited numbers. No private cars will have access.
• Plants and planting tools, gloves.
• An experienced team leader, health and safety management and training.
Meeting point: 507 Muritai Road, Eastbourne, Lower Hutt.
Booking is essential to secure your seat on the bus to the lakes.
Follow this link to register: https://forms.office.com/r/VDGJcRJLww

Plant Diversity & Human Impacts On Endangered Plants - Guided Walk, In this easy 60-minute downhill walk we will obtain a perspective on plant biodiversity and human impacts on endangered species.

Species radiation in the Southern Hemisphere with New Zealand examples - Kōwhai, Hebe (Veronica) and Kauri.

Examples of rare and endangered species owing their situations directly to human activities. These plants include:

- Three Kings kaikomako (Pennantia baylisiana),
- Bartlett's rātā (Metrosideros bartlettii)

Reimagining Construction: Participatory, Circular, and Open by Design, This presentation examines how the principles of participatory, circular, and open design can transform construction by bringing human and ecological values into the heart of how we build.
Drawing from both ancient timber framing traditions and modern innovations, it demonstrates how modularity and standardisation unlock flexibility, efficiency, and customisation while supporting sustainable, locally-rooted solutions.

description:
Resilience and Emissions Reduction Workshop for Not-For-Profits | Blenheim, Ready your not-for-profit for the future
Do you know you need to take action to address climate change but don’t know where to start?
Do you want to strengthen your organisations’ planning and readiness for change?
Do you want practical tools and support to measure, assess, and report on your organisations’ impact?

In partnership with Rātā Foundation, our Earth+ Resilience and Emissions Reduction programme has been designed to flip the script on climate change, centering your organisation as agents of change and kitting you with the tools, support and community to make a difference; and it’s free of charge!
About the programme
With the support of the Terra Nova team and other programme participants, you will be guided to identify how your organisation is uniquely placed to contribute to the resilience and wellbeing of people and planet, and the opportunities and obstacles to creating positive change.
The programme is accessible and suitable for everyone, from those just starting on the journey, to those who have steps in place but are looking to gain access to further resources. This programme is not intended to add extra workload or deliverables for your organisation, it is an offer of support to integrate an Earth+ approach into your BAU; an answer to the question “what can we do about climate change?”
We know that every organisation’s capacity is different, so our support is available for you to utilise it when you need it until the end of 2025. This includes:
Access to a dedicated online community where you can connect with the Terra Nova team, other Rātā grantees and specialised partners. Ask questions, find resources and share your journey.
A toolkit of resources and impact sessions to develop your knowledge and connect you with the expertise and support to build resilience and tackle change in a range of impact areas.
Complementary access to the Cogo carbon emissions measurement tool, providing you the ability to quantify and report on your emissions impact and providing recommended actions for emissions reduction and cost savings, in an easy-to-use format.
It begins with a 1-day interactive workshop to kick things off. By the end of the workshop, you will walk away:
Feeling more empowered about the future, with a deeper understanding of resilience and climate change as it relates to your organisation’s context.
Having explored how you can make change positive and achievable, centered on the needs of your community and team. 
With free access to Cogo carbon manager, an emissions profile, report of your carbon footprint and practical action you can take to reduce your emissions.
Having built a network of support and gained free-to-use practical tools and templates.
Note: we will be running multiple workshops throughout the year; you only need to attend one workshop to join the programme. If you prefer an alternate date, please head to our Humanitix profile to find the corresponding event. 
The programme is fully funded for not-for-profit organisations and registrations are now open for 2025! Register for the programme and secure your spot in a workshop through this Humanatix event, and a member of the Terra Nova team will be in touch to confirm your enrollment. For more information about the programme and workshop, visit the Terra Nova website.
We look forward to welcoming you into our community of changemakers!

description:
SCUBA: Subterranean Critters – Understanding Biodiversity Aotearoa, Join Julia Kasper, Lead Curator Invertebrates at Te Papa, as she talks about Subterranean ecosystems - some of the least explored habitats on Earth. Globally, scientific knowledge of cave and groundwater invertebrates remains fragmentary, with most regions having only sporadic surveys or taxonomic treatments. Many cave systems host highly specialised faunal assemblages - troglobionts, stygofauna, and other obligate subterranean species - that often display extreme adaptations such as reduced pigmentation, elongated appendages, or complete loss of eyes.

The Subterranean Critters: Understanding cave Biodiversity in Aotearoa (SCUBA) project brings together the expertise of a wide range of researchers and cavers to better understand the biodiversity and ecology of faunal communities in caves in Aotearoa New Zealand. Novel sample collection, combined with reviews of the literature and presently available natural history collection holdings, will enable species discovery and improved understanding of the distribution and conservation status of cave taxa, as well as the abiotic factors that influence their distribution, ecology, and abundance.

Located in Tāne Whakapiripiri, Ōtari Visitor Centre. Gold coin donation. No need to book, just turn up!

This seminar is part of the Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush Trust’s annual seminar series. This year, they are on the first Tuesday of the month, March – November, to celebrate 100 years of Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush.

Ōtari 100: Celebrating 100 years of native plants, conservation, and community. 1926-2026.

description:
Spring Edible Weeds Foraging Workshop 12th October 2025, Join expert forager Felicity Joy of Wild Botanica for a comprehensive Wild Edible Weeds Foraging Workshop in the beautiful community gardens of Mount Victoria, Wellington.
This inspiring experience will open your eyes to the abundance of edible wild plants growing right under your nose.
We’ll unlock the secrets of foraging, connecting with the land, and turning humble "weeds" into delicious, nourishing food. You’ll gain confidence in identifying common edible plants, learn their botanical names, and understand their medicinal and nutritional benefits. We’ll also explore ethical foraging practices, how to spot toxic lookalikes, and share simple, practical ways to incorporate wild foods into your daily meals.
This isn’t just about food: it’s about sustainability, resilience, and reconnecting with the environment in a meaningful way. You'll leave with a deeper appreciation for the land, new skills to support local food security, and the knowledge to make your own simple meals from wild ingredients.
Class sizes are limited, so book early to secure your spot.
For more details and bookings, visit
www.wildbotanica.co.nz
follow @wild.botanica.nz on social media.
For questions, email felicity@wildbotanica.co.nz.
Join my email newsletter to hear about upcoming foraging workshops: https://www.wildbotanica.co.nz/pages/newsletter

description:
Spring Floral Display Accessible Self-Drive Tour, Gather your friends, whānau, or neighbours who might find it tricky to access the gardens, and enjoy a relaxing, self-guided drive through a spectacular spring floral display at Wellington Botanic Garden ki Paekākā.

Simply drive along the one-way route past the Display Garden and soak in the colours of tulips, forget-me-nots, dianthus, primulas, chrysanthemums, daffodils, and more.

How it works:
- No registration needed — just turn up and enter through the Glenmore Street gates.
- Follow the designated one-way route through the gardens, keeping within your vehicle at all times.
- Exit through the West/White Gate to return to Glenmore Street.
- Feel free to enjoy the route as many times as you like during opening hours.

Please note:
- Drive slowly (maximum 10 km/h), and watch carefully for pedestrians, especially children.
- Stay in your vehicle for the entire tour to keep everyone safe and comfortable.
- Follow all signage and do not turn around within the garden grounds.

This event is self-guided and unstaffed. If you need assistance during your visit, please call 04 499 1400.
For enquiries, email treehouse@wcc.govt.nz or call 04 499 1400.

description:
Summer Wild Edible Weeds Foraging Workshop, Explore the wonders of Wild Edible Weeds Foraging Workshops, situated in the scenic community gardens in Mount Victoria, Wellington.

Embark on a journey into nature, uncovering a world teeming with wild, edible plants. This workshop, centred on abundant, delicious, and nutritious edible weeds and commonly found plants, will leave you enthusiastic about foraging in your own backyard and local neighbourhood.

During this immersive, outdoor, multi-sensory learning experience, we will:

Delve into the basic principles of sustainable and ethical foraging and wild harvesting.
Learn the botanical names of plants along with their various common names.
Confidently identify 10-20 wild plants, including details about lookalikes and toxic plants to avoid.
Explore the nutritional and medicinal properties of each plant, discovering how to prepare simple healing remedies at home.
Understand how to prepare each plant for maximum nutrition and flavour, discussing easy recipes and cooking tips.
Uncover the folklore and history of each plant, hearing fascinating and often amusing stories that help us connect with the plants and our ancestors.

Leave the workshop feeling empowered with the skills and knowledge needed to deepen your connection to food, bolster local food resilience, and enhance security throughout the natural cycles of the seasons. Say goodbye to the supermarket; instead, gather your own wild greens on the way home for a delightful dinner.

For more info: www.wildbotanica.co.nz
or email Felicity@wildbotanica.co.nz

Te Hononga hikoi: Taupō Swamp, Te Hononga hikoi: Taupō Swamp
Te Hononga hīkoi enable our members to connect with others in the Wellington Catchments Collective. It's pretty inspiring seeing the activities happening in other catchment groups.

The next Te Hononga hikoi will be at Taupo Swamp in Porirua on the morning of Sunday 21 September at 10am – 11.30pm approx.

Come for a spring stroll and bring friends and family. Bring water and own snacks or fuel up at nearby cafes in Plimmerton.

We will meet in Ulric Street by the pedestrian bridge entrance to the dog park (plenty of parking)

Friends of Taupo Swamp & Catchment Inc was formed in 2018 by a group of Porirua residents. Restoration activities have been focused on the part of the wetlands that is owned by Porirua City Council.

Back in 2018 there was a lot of blackberry on the site. Now, some of the 2019-20 locally sourced plantings by volunteers are 5 metres high. By the end of the current planting season FOTSC will have put in 18K plants. An adjacent planting programme around the Plimmerton Domain coordinated by the local Rotary Club and the Porirua City Council has resulted in 22k trees and plants.

Please register your interest/intention to attend by flicking a short email to . In the event of bad weather we will advise cancellation by 8am and rescheduling for a week later.

description:
The Future of Conservation Hui, Forest & Bird - The Future of Conservation Hui
Nature Can't Vote, But You Can
Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington

Who is giving nature a voice this election?

Aotearoa New Zealand's protected conservation land is under threat. Forest & Bird's maps of at-risk land have sparked a national conversation - and this election we have an opportunity to show politicians how many of us value nature. Join us in Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington this August, to hear from conservation experts about what's at stake, and your political candidates on what they plan to do about it.

The Election Conversation - Evening Event
Who: Open to the public
When: Saturday 1 August 2026, 6pm–9.15pm (programme starts 6.30pm)
Where: New Zealand Parliament Buildings, Banquet Hall
Cost: Free
After networking and nibbles from 6pm, the programme features a keynote address on local conservation issues, hear an overview of what's at stake for nature this election - including what the Conservation Amendment Bill could mean for the region, and a moderated political panel with representatives from across the spectrum. Audience questions will be put directly to the panel, giving you the chance to hear how parties plan to tackle the issues that matter most for nature.
Come along, get informed, and be part of the conversation this election.

Mobilise for Nature - Afternoon Session
Who: Priority access for Forest & Bird branches, networks, members, and volunteers - open to anyone who wants to get involved
When: Saturday 1 August 2026, 1pm–5pm (optional networking from 5pm–6pm)
Where: New Zealand Parliament Buildings, Banquet Hall

Goodlife Collective, Sustainability Trust and WEAll Aotearoa are proud to be co-hosting Dr Amanda Cahill, founder of The Next Economy
Don't miss this opportunity to hear Amanda's insights from her work in Australia, which demonstrate how acting on climate change can help catalyse fairer, more regenerative wellbeing economies.
Amanda has worked at the intersection of government, local councils, big companies and communities for 30 years, to support communities to transition to a thriving future.
Amanda is the Founder of The Next Economy, where she supports regional communities across Australia to manage the impacts of decarbonisation and climate change in a way that builds more equitable and regenerative economies. Most of this work has been in coal and industrial regions, where she has brought together government, industry, workers and community groups to co-design transition strategies despite deep-seated tensions. Her work draws on 30 years’ experience working with changemakers across the world to address economic and health inequalities, environmental degradation, women’s rights and climate justice.

About WEAll Aotearoa: WEAll Aotearoa is a non-partisan and independent ‘think and do’ tank working to redesign Aotearoa New Zealand’s economy around the wellbeing of our people and te taiao. Amanda is the Founder of The Next Economy, where she supports regional communities across Australia to manage the impacts of decarbonisation and climate change in a way that builds more equitable and regenerative economies. Most of this work has been in coal and industrial regions, where she has brought together government, industry, workers and community groups to co-design transition strategies despite deep-seated tensions. Her work draws on 30 years’ experience working with changemakers across the world to address economic and health inequalities, environmental degradation, women’s rights and climate justice.
Amanda is a Churchill Fellow and has a PhD from ANU in human geography. She is also a Research Fellow at the University of Melbourne, an Industry Fellow at the University of Sydney and a co-editor of the recently published book: Regional Energy Transitions in Australia: From impossible to possible.

Next Economy works with government, industry, investment and community to create the conditions for a rapid, responsible and fair transition to a climate-safe, regenerative and socially just Australian economy.

description:
The permaculture design process for a sustainable lifestyle, We invite you to spend a day at Doris & Bob's, experiencing how permaculture can help you design more than just your garden! Applicable in all situations of life, no need to own your own place.
Doris will share her journey of integrating the permaculture design approach into her life's questions, her diverse home and community projects in Paekakariki (eg. PaeCycle, a food scrap collection set up and Pataka Kai, the public cupboard to give and take food abundance), and as Trustee of Toru Education: Motivated by an sense of urgency and responsibility to take care of our finite resources and to care for our environment with all its diverse wildlife and each other. Through storytelling and practical examples, we'll explore how these principles can help shape our lives and communities for the better, and how we all can contribute as individuals. Every choice we make matters.
We also will take a stroll through Doris's garden and engage in some hands-on activities to experience some of the principles in action. Of course, we will spend some time at the various compost heaps (Compost is Doris' middle name!). Regenerating soil with home made compost! Making compost involving food scraps (closely predator managed) or from garden waste (free standing heaps). 
Lunch will be provided—feel free to bring a small contribution to go with the homemade bread if you'd like (but not expected).
After lunch, we will explore the design process of creating a base map for your specific setting, whether it be a your home garden, personal question such as 'What's next?' or a community project.
No prior experience in permaculture is needed. We hope you will leave with new ideas and connections, practical inspiration for your own compost making and an enhanced understanding of how many ways you can apply the permaculture design process and create community, one compost heap at the time!
There will also be a crop swap table where we practice the permaculture approach of reciprocity of 'give and take'; you might enjoy bringing seeds, seedlings, produce from your garden, and walk away with something unexpected (again, don't feel obliged to contribute).
Spaces are limited to 15 spaces to fit into our living room, so make sure you reserve your spot. We are at 59 Wellington Road, up the driveway on your right. Don't follow google directions as that would take you down to the beach. Just come on down Wellington Road, and we are up on your left. Please park below by the lay-by and walk up. description:
Tipping Points in the Cryosphere, Tipping Points in the Cryosphere
Public panel discussion featuring world leaders in cryospheric sciences as part of the international 'Climate in the Crysophere' conference

About this Event

The accelerating loss of the cryosphere, which holds 70% of the world’s freshwater in all its forms – sea ice, lake ice, mountain glaciers, the polar ice sheets and their ice shelves, snow and permafrost - is one of the clearest planet-wide consequences of global warming so far.
The loss of even parts of these key components of the cryosphere would result in severe impacts for coastal communities, infrastructure and ecosystems through permanent inundation of the lowest-lying areas and by increasing the frequency of flooding, and requires an extensive and long-term commitment to adaptation to limit these impacts. By the end of the century one billion people living in coastal areas could be impacted (IPCC 2023).
There is ample evidence for abrupt change in the past, especially for the glaciers and ice sheets. Moreover, changes in land-ice are, for the most part, are irreversible on human-to-glacial timescales. In fact, both the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets show strong hysteresis behaviour, meaning that once certain parts of the ice sheets are gone, it would take much colder temperatures to regain the ice.
What characterises tipping dynamics in the cryosphere most, however, are the nested timescales, and possibility of tipping cascades between elements, ranging from mere hours-decades in the sea-ice, up to millennia for the ice sheets with consequences on a range of spatial scales: as global warming accelerates, there is an increasing discrepancy between the rapid forcing, and the comparably long response times in the cryosphere. This clash in timescales gives rise to a massive gap between the observed and committed impacts, in particular when it comes to sea-level rise. While typical projections focus on sea-level changes within this century, recent evidence suggests that the bulk of sea-level rise - even while triggered within this century - will unfold over hundreds, if not thousands of years.

Otaihanga

Speaker Mike Joy - see Bio below

Mike is a Senior Research Fellow and Lecturer in Environmental Science at the School of Geography, Environment and Earth Sciences, Mike’s research includes ecological modelling, freshwater bioassessment, environmental policy, biophysical limits to growth and the role of energy in society. He is publicly outspoken about the decline in freshwater quality and ecosystems, especially the impact of nutrient pollution from intensive dairying on New Zealand's "100% Pure", clean, green image.
Mike is an outspoken advocate for environmental protection in New Zealand and for this has received several awards including an Ecology in Action award from the NZ Ecological Society, the Charles Fleming Award for environmental achievement in 2013 and in 2023 the Callaghan Medal for science communication from the Royal Society of New Zealand. In 2015 he was awarded the Morgan Foundation inaugural River Voice Award and in 2017 the inaugural NZ Universities Critic and Conscience award. His book 'The Fight for Freshwater' is a memoir that provides a rare first hand look at those whose voices question the health and future of our waterways.

description:
Wainuiomata Old Forest Walk - January, Wainuiomata Old Forest Walk - January
Explore ancient forests on a guided walk in Wainuiomata Regional Park

Step into a world few get to see. This exclusive guided walk takes you deep into a 1,000-year-old forest in Wainuiomata Regional Park—an area normally closed to the public. Wander beneath towering native rātā and rimu trees and discover a sanctuary for North Island brown kiwi and other native birds.

Led by one of our experienced park rangers, you’ll hear stories about the park’s natural heritage, conservation efforts, and the history that makes this place so special.

Registrations are extremely limited. Each walk is capped at just 20 participants, with a maximum of two registrations per person. If you’ve joined this event before, please consider letting someone else experience this unique opportunity.

Wainuiomata River Community Open Day, Wainuiomata River Community Open Day
Get to know your local awa at this drop in day with Mountains to Sea Wellington’s Wai Connection team!

Take part in water quality and species identification activities from the Wainuiomata River, learn about ways you can take part in conservation mahi going on in Wainuiomata.

We’ll be running water quality monitoring (including SHMAK test demonstrations) and identifying fish and macro invertebrates living in the awa!

Our catchment co-ordinators will be onsite to chat about other ways you can get involved in conservation in your area too.

This event is for the whole whānau, drop in anytime between 10am-2pm

Register via Humanitix for updates https://events.humanitix.com/wainuiomata-open-day

description:
Wainuiomata Water Walk - February, Explore ancient forests and waterways on a guided walk in Wainuiomata Regional Park
Join us for a special guided walk through beautiful native forest in Wainuiomata Regional Park, exploring areas not usually open to the public. Led by our knowledgeable park ranger, you’ll learn about the Wainuiomata water collection area and how this pristine water makes its way to Wellington’s taps.
This is one of our most popular summer events, and places are limited to just 30 participants. If you’ve attended before, please consider letting someone else experience this unique opportunity.
The walk will follow the Orongorongo Pipeline Tunnel and visit the historic Morton Dam—one of New Zealand’s largest concrete dams and a remarkable example of early engineering innovation.

To book: Due to the overwhelming popularity of these limited capacity events, we allocate bookings via a ballot system. A ballot will open for registrations via the link below at 10am on Tuesday 27 January and close at 10am on Thursday 29 January. description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Aorangi Forest Park Old Mill Track, Join the Aorangi Restoration Trust and South Wairarapa locals for a walk along a recently restored track in Aorangi Forest Park. Follow an old logging road to the historic mill site and take in the beauty of the regenerating forest along the way.

Aorangi Forest Park stretches between Martinborough in the north and Cape Palliser in the south, covering much of the Aorangi mountains. By road, the park sits about 80 km south of Masterton and 100 km east of Wellington.

The park is located on Department of Conservation land and features a rich variety of native bush. Beech forest dominates the northern range, while hinau and matai are common in the hardwood forests at lower altitudes. Mahoe thrives on moist soils in gullies and along stream banks. Other species include fuchsia, makomako, heketara, kohuhu, titoki, rewarewa, rimu, and miro, creating a diverse and vibrant landscape.

Walk Format
Meet at 16 Kitchener Street, Martinborough for shuttle transport to the start of this route. The walk itself is a 10km return trip, expected to take 5 hours. It is a fairly easy tramping track - with about 500 metres of more difficult terrain due to the unformed nature of the track and moderate slope at the start. The remainder is gradual slope on a good benched track. We will return to 16 Kitchener Street between 4pm and 5pm.

Important
Once registered, please check your email for the gear list. This walk is partly in cellphone coverage. This walk will be postponed till Sunday 23rd November if there has been significant rain and the river is too high. Tickets will be refunded if cancelled.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Cavelands Walk, Discover a hidden gem of Wairarapa on this scenic 5km walk that winds through native bush, past historic glow worm caves, and up to vast hilltop views.

You will be led by Joseph Potangaroa and Belinda Cranswick, who will guide you through the environmental and historical aspects of this route. This 5km guided walk begins beside the scenic Taueru River, following its banks for approximately 1km. Early on, you’ll pass a picturesque pond surrounded by a mix of native and exotic trees. The route continues to a unique and historically significant feature — the glow worm caves. Here, you'll pause for a short discussion about the history of the caves and their ecological importance. This area is protected under a QEII National Trust Covenant, ensuring its preservation.

Throughout the walk, you’ll encounter a rich diversity of native flora including mānuka, kānuka, tītoki, kōwhai, ngaio, tōtara, and kahikatea. The track then ascends a relatively steep farm trail to a hilltop vantage point, where you’ll be rewarded with sweeping views across Bull Hill, the Ponatahi Hills, and the Remutaka Ranges. Another QEII covenant can be seen on the south-western slope.

From the ridge, the track descends with stunning views across surrounding terraces and flat paddocks, before returning to the starting point.

Walk Format:
Approx. 5km return with well-formed tracks + one fairly steep uphill section. This walk is for all ages, but bear in mind the length and terrain.

What to Bring:
- Sturdy walking shoes or sneakers with good tread (no jandals or sandals)
- Warm clothing and a waterproof jacket
- Sunhat, sunglasses, sunscreen
- Food and water
- Koha (donation) — the landowners welcome contributions to Life Flight

Important:
Please check your ticket confirmation email for the exact meeting point and directions.
This event is weather dependent, and will be cancelled if the river is too high.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Holdsworth Restoration Trust Walk, Led by volunteers from the Holdsworth Restoration Trust this walk highlights community-led restoration in Tararua Forest Park. Walk leaders will guide participants along trap lines and share their knowledge of the pest control project — including how often traps are checked, which pests are targeted, and how bird and animal populations are monitored. Keep your eyes and ears open for native birds such as tomtits, early evening ruru, grey warblers, North Island riflemen, and the ever-present pīwakawaka, tūī, and kererū.

Volunteers will also share their knowledge of native flora, including towering rimu, northern rātā, and miro, which rise above a canopy of kāmahi and beech. The forest is one of the finest examples of mixed podocarp–broadleaf forest in the Tararua Ranges and supports a wide range of indigenous biodiversity. Walkers will also learn how to identify native fungi, understand five-minute bird count monitoring, and discover how to get involved in pest trapping.

Walk format:
This slow-paced walk is suitable for most fitness levels and ages 5 +. The path is mainly on a flat track, however the ground can be uneven with tree roots - not suitable wheelchairs. Note, there is no cellphone reception on this walk. No dogs allowed.

Depart the carpark at 6pm, cross the bridge and along the track, breaking into 3 groups at the Gentle Annie junction. The 3 groups all take a different route along a trap line track, meeting at Donnelly Flat for a hot chocolate and snack before continuing the walk around the loop track and back to the carpark at 8pm time.

Image credit: Jet Productions
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Hāpua Farm, Discover the beauty of Hāpua Farm, a property that combines rolling farmland with wetlands, native bush, and sweeping views of the surrounding hill country. Led by Michael Birch, a member of the Ruamahanga Restoration Trust, the walk begins on the farm’s airstrip, offering beautiful views of the Tararua Ranges before descending through farm tracks, open paddocks, and bush trails.

Along the way, explore wetlands created by large landslides 11,000–12,000 years ago, and continue east to two protected QEII covenant areas of native bush. Here, you’ll encounter towering totara, matai, and kahikatea, as well as abundant birdlife including kererū and tūī. Last year's participants had rave reviews of this walk!

Walk Format:
The walk covers around 6 km. You must be able to climb over fences and walk for 3 to 4 hours over uneven ground. Some climbing is involved - this is a hill country farm. This walk is partly in cellphone coverage. This walk will be cancelled if it has been raining heavily in preceding days. You must arrange your own transport to this walk.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Kiriwhakapapa Loop Track, This guided walk follows the 2km Kiriwhakapapa Loop Track in Tararua Forest Park, about 16km north of Masterton. The track is well-graded with a gentle 50m incline and includes bridges across the Kiriwhakapapa Stream. Walkers will pass through regenerating native forest and a stand of exotic Redwoods.

The walk will take approximately 2 hours and is led by members of the Masterton Tramping Club and Wairarapa Walking Festival Committee, who will also provide information about other tracks in the area.

Walk details:
Meet at 13 Church Street (carpark next to Masterton Police Station) if you’d like to carpool. The track is generally flat, with a 50m incline. Note uneven forest floor and tree roots. No cellphone coverage in the area.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Longbush Cottage Garden Ramble, Enjoy a gentle afternoon garden walk at Longbush Cottage, perfect for those who prefer a more relaxed pace. Set across one hectare, the gardens feature a series of beautifully designed spaces, each with its own planting theme, all at their best in November.

This two-hour ramble includes plenty of time to explore, rest, and take in the surroundings. With numerous seating areas throughout the garden, it is well suited to participants with limited mobility. Two large glasshouses also provide sheltered spaces to enjoy should the weather be less than perfect.

Afternoon tea is included, with garden creator Luke on hand to share the story of Longbush Cottage and answer questions. Guests can also browse the onsite emporium, offering a selection of garden-themed gifts.

Photo courtesy of Longbush Cottage.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Millennium Native Forest Reserve, Led by volunteers from the Friends of Millennium Native Forest Reserve, this walk offers a fascinating insight into how a once-degraded farmland has been transformed into a thriving native bush and wetland. The Millennium Native Forest Reserve is a community asset established by Masterton South Rotary on land leased from Masterton Trust Lands Trust. It is maintained by a committee called Friends of Millennium Native Forest Reserve. Walk leaders will share the Reserve’s inspiring history — from its beginnings in 1993 as a community-led project to restore local biodiversity, to its official opening in 2000 as part of a nationwide millennium celebration. QR codes placed at key spots offer short films presented by local college students, bringing the Reserve’s stories, conservation work, and unique ecology to life. Along the way, participants will hear how volunteers have reintroduced native plants and nurtured a habitat for native birds, insects, and aquatic life.

As you explore the urban Reserve’s meandering tracks, keep an eye out for tūī and kererū - with a bit of luck, you might also spot a gecko basking in the sun, a darting skink, long and short finned eels in the waterways, koura beneath the shallows, dragonflies, and even wētā tucked away in the undergrowth. You’ll gain an appreciation for the dedication it takes to maintain the Reserve and discover ways to get involved in its ongoing care.

Walk format:
This easy-paced walk is suitable for all fitness levels and ages. The tracks are 2.6km of largely limed winding tracks, with sections of boardwalks. Note: there is no toilet available at this reserve.

We’ll depart from the Hillcrest St Reserve entrance at 2pm. The group will pause at key points to hear stories, scan QR codes, and observe wildlife. Expect 1 - 1.5hr walk.

Photo credits: Friends of Millennium Native Forest Reserve.
This walk is part of the Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Photo Walks with Walker - Fensham, Join photographer and Adobe Community Expert Geoff Walker for a creative evening walk at Fensham Reserve. Starting at 6pm, this two-hour session will focus on exploring new perspectives and learning practical techniques to capture stunning images with your mobile phone camera.

With the reserve’s bush tracks and open spaces as your backdrop, you’ll discover how to make the most of evening light while sharpening your photography skills in a relaxed, supportive setting.

Image credits: Geoff Walker
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Poetry at Dorset Square, The artist collective Tramping Gently Club invites you to welcome undergrowth and fertility at Dorset Square. Join a thought-provoking walk through Dorset Square, part of the Featherston Walkways and Reserves. Along the way, discover a participatory artwork featuring the poetic voices of South Wairarapa youth —where walkers are invited to take part in Poems Against Sustainability.

This unique card-game artwork opens space for sometimes challenging but important conversations about climate change, our relationship to the land, and working with nature. First presented at Featherston Booktown 2022, and later developed during a year-long residency at Turere Lodge in the Remutaka Forest Park, this participatory artwork explores big ideas through creativity and play.

Set within the accessible Dorset Square—the most accessible of four urban bush reserves in Featherston. This walk is an opportunity to connect with a re-emerging under story of kawakawa. Once a paddock used as a training area for the Fire Brigade's competition team, the reserve now offers cool shade in the hot Wairarapa summer and an emerging low flammability undergrowth.

Walk Format:
Walkers can expect a gentle walk - 1hrs in total. Maximum 20 participants. All ages.

Image Credit: The Tramping Gently Club Art Collective

This event was previously advertised to be held at Pigeon Bush - however public access here is now restricted and the walk has been relocated to Dorset Square.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Ruamāhanga Awa Sundowner Walk, Back by popular demand after delighting festival-goers in 2024, this unique twilight walk returns for 2025. Led by Jane & Rod from the Ruamāhanga Farm Foundation, the journey begins with a sensory—and at times silent—stroll along the Ruamāhanga River before entering the majestic Waihinga Bush, one of the finest examples of podocarp forest near Martinborough.

As the sun sets and the forest darkens, take your place beneath the towering trees and be transported by a mythical tale of how this special forest came to be. A truly atmospheric experience, blending nature, story, and stillness.

Registration cost will be donated to Ruamāhanga Farm Foundation.

Walk Format:
This 4km walk is predominantly on flat track, with mown grass underfoot, however the ground can be uneven.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Te Whenua Tapui O Whakamairu Reserve, Discover one of Masterton’s hidden gems with a gentle walk through Whakamairu Reserve, a 1.4-hectare pocket of established native bush within the town boundary. This designated Scientific Wetland, protected by Greater Wellington Regional Council, is home to 200-year-old kahikatea and swamp maire, alongside younger native plantings that signal the ongoing restoration of the reserve.

The boardwalk has recently been renewed by Masterton District Council, and the restoration work continues with the help of the Solway Community Group and local school children from Chanel College and Douglas Park School. Together, their efforts are gradually returning this special site to its original state.

The track is flat, with a mix of boardwalk and limed paths, making it easily accessible for prams and wheelchairs. To access this reserve, head to the end of William Donald Drive off High St. Solway, and park near the junction with Driving Range Road (private road).
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Tinui Food Forest Tranquility, Discover the beauty and abundance of the Tinui Food Forest, a four-hectare property near Castlepoint. After a warm welcome and short introduction from owners Deb and Ray, enjoy a guided walk along meandering springtime paths lined with blossoms and alive with bird song. Children will love feeding the alpacas and exploring the maze, while adults can learn how this flourishing food forest was established and why.

Following the walk, sample seasonal produce and preserves in the farm shop, including Deb’s homemade specialties. This two-hour event is suitable for all fitness levels, including families with preschoolers, and offers a peaceful experience in nature. We’re grateful to Deb and Ray for generously offering discounted tickets for this special Walking Festival event.

Walk Format:
Allow 2 hours. Flat track, but some muddy patches — wear sturdy shoes or gumboots. Dress for the weather. Note, some areas have no cellphone reception.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Waihinga Bridge Wetland Walk, Journey through a landscape of renewal on Ruamāhanga Farm. This guided walk with Jane & Rod leads you into a restoring wetland, through an ancient tī kōuka grove, down to the Ruamāhanga awa, and past areas of recent riparian planting. Along the way, pause at key sites to listen to curated recordings of tamariki involved in Te Reo o Te Wai—a multi-arts project connecting communities with the health of Wairarapa Moana.

This dusk walk invites reflection, learning, and connection. It is ideal for those curious about wetland restoration, multi-disciplinary approaches to education, or simply experiencing nature in a new way. Parts of the route will remain open to the public after the Festival.

The walk is mostly flat on mown grass, with six hand-held stiles to cross, two scrambly riverbank sections, and the possibility of some boggy patches. Walking boots are recommended.

We would welcome koha towards Ruamāhanga Farm Foundation education programmes.

Delivered in partnership with Wairarapa Catchment Collective and the Ruamāhanga Farm Foundation.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Waiohine to Holdsworth Overnight, Note this is an overnight stay, starting from 9am Friday 21st November and finishing on Saturday 22nd November.
This guided overnight hike is the perfect introduction to tramping in the Tararua Ranges. Beginning with a spectacular crossing of the Waiohine Gorge suspension bridge — 94 metres long and 35 metres high — the walk follows fairly gentle terrain alongside the Waiohine River, through lush native bush, and without any steep climbs.

After a 9 am bus departure from Tranzit in Masterton, we travel to the Waiohine road-end (pickup available along the way at Carterton Station, timed to meet the train from Wellington) and set off on an 8 km walk to Tōtara Flats Hut. This Department of Conservation hut has bunkrooms with mattresses, cooking stoves, rainwater taps, a woodstove, and a long-drop toilet. We have booked most of the hut’s 26 bunks. On Day 2, wake to the sound of native birds before continuing on an 11 km walk to Holdsworth Lodge, where the bus will return us to Masterton.

What to bring: Good shoes or boots, rain jacket, backpack, sleeping bag (in a waterproof bag), overnight clothes, toiletries, any personal medications, food, cooking pot, plate, cutlery, toilet paper, water bottle, and snacks. Optional: togs and towel, battery bank. All rubbish must be carried out.

Important:
If you would like extra information and your gear checked, please attend an information session with your walk leader on Sunday 2nd November 6pm, at the Carterton Courthouse.
Must have a good level of fitness. Dogs are not permitted. There are no river crossings except by bridge, but one section requires walking along the riverbank to avoid a slip. If the river is too high, the walk will enter and return via Holdsworth. The walk leader will carry a Personal Locator Beacon, lighter, newspaper for the woodstove, and a basic first aid kit. No refunds except in exceptional circumstances or if the walk is cancelled.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Wairarapa Moana Wander, Join local freshwater ecologist, Dr Katie Brasell from Kahungunu ki Wairarapa, on the northern shore of Lake Wairarapa. On this 3-4km stroll, you can take in the fresh South Wairarapa air, learn what treasures the moana holds and how local kaitiaki (stewards) are helping to restore mauri (life force) to this jewel of our region.

Meet at the Lake Domain Reserve just south of Featherston. The walk will begin with a brief history of the lake’s importance to mana whenua by the Lake Domain camping area. Continuing for about 1km east across the top of the lake, you’ll hear about the locals favourite native shellfish, kākahi, and what the annual counts are telling us. A few hundred meters away, we’ll take a look at a myriad of aquatic plants (good and bad) and how restoring native species in the lake could turn the tide on this degraded ecosystem.

Walk Format:
This walk is suitable for all fitness levels, and is expected to take 1.5hrs. Children are welcomed but must be accompanied by parent/guardian.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Water, Wind and Wood - Part 1, Join us on a musical tour in the Botanic Garden, listening to music and discussing the plants that are used to make musical instruments.

Meet above the Children's Playground for this 60-minute walk
Cost: $5 (cash only, please). or free for Friends.

This is part of the regular walks run by the Friends of the Wellington Botanic Garden, they run twice monthly throughout the year with a different topic every time.

Join the Friends for only $30 a year and all the walks will be free, as well as other great benefits.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Water, wind and wood - Part 2 - Guided Walk, On this walk we will continue our musical odyssey in the Botanic Garden, listening to music and discussing the plants used to make musical instruments. Meet at the Duck Pond for this 60-minute walk.

Meet at the Duck Pond for this 60-minute walk.
Cost: $5 (cash only, please). or free for Friends.

This is part of the regular walks run by the Friends of the Wellington Botanic Garden, they run twice monthly throughout the year with a different topic every time.
Join the Friends for only $30 a year and all the walks will be free, as well as other great benefits.
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Weeding Bee 18th October, Weeding Bee 18th October
Kia Ora Koutou

Now we have finished planting we are turning our attention to the all important W**d releasing.
This is essential to keeping the seedlings we have planted this winter from being overwhelmed by grass and weeds.
Also mulching to help with moisture retention over those hot summer days (hopefully we get a summer!)
Meeting at the Nursery on Hana Udy street at 9am
Gloves, tools and sunscreen provided along with a morning tea and an update on the Reserve afterward.
Hope to see you there !



Health & Safety Notice: When working in the Reserve, please ensure your clothing and footwear are appropriate for expected weather conditions (cold, wet or hot) and the terrain (such as holes, hidden objects, blackberry, overhead branches). Trip hazards and slippery tracks are a possibility. Stay clear of waterways. Be cautious if you have allergies and carry the necessary medication. Enjoy your time in the Reserve and please avoid blocking pathways used by other users. Report any accidents, injuries or possible hazards to the H&S Coordinator (021 071 536)
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
Wellington Climate Fresk Workshop, Do you want to be part of the solution to tackle climate change but don’t have the time to become a climate scientist? Join us for a 3-hour interactive workshop to explore the causes and consequences of climate disturbances.
Based on the IPCC report and played by over 2 million people worldwide, this collaborative workshop allows you to understand the key issues of climate change to empower you to take action.
How it works:
The workshop is based on a 42-card game. Each card represents an element, a cause or a consequence of climate change.
In teams, guided by your facilitator, you are encouraged to find the cause-effect relationship between the different components of climate change. Collective intelligence will get you from one deck of card to the next!
This step-by-step reconstruction provides keys to understand the complexity and develop an overview of climate change.
Agenda:
Introduction, 15 mins
Fresk Card Game, 1 1/2 hours
Debrief and Actions, 1 hour 15 mins

This inspiring experience will open your eyes to the abundance of edible wild plants growing right under your nose.
We’ll unlock the secrets of foraging, connecting with the land, and turning humble "weeds" into delicious, nourishing food. description:
Wellington Foraging for Wild Edible Weeds Workshop, Join Felicity of Wild Botanica for a wander around the edges of the Innermost Community gardens to learn about commonly found, wild, edible weeds. Build a relationship with a natural world that is overflowing with abundant, wild, edible, nutritious, medicinal plants. Learn their names & get to know them, along with folklore & stories from the past.

By the end of the workshop you will:
- understand the basic principles of foraging, including sustainable harvesting
- feel confident in identifying 10-15 wild edible plants
- know about their nutritional & medicinal benefits
- know about common toxic/dangerous plants to avoid when foraging
- know about the best ways to prepare your foraged greens for maximum nutritional benefit & flavor
- feel empowered to include foraged greens in your everyday diet

Walk away with hands on, practical skills & knowledge that you can use in your own life.

Investment includes hands on wild weed walk & discussion, cup of foraged herbal tea & wildly delicious foraged snack.

Whānau Day, Join us for a FREE day of family activities exploring the connection between the whenua (land) and the moana (sea).

Discover raumati (summer) through workshops, performances, and hands-on activities. Learn about seaweed varieties, native plants, and how we can protect our natural environment for future generations.

Activties:
* Identify diverse seaweed species with Mountains to Sea
* Drum and dance to Tokelau rhythms with the Kupega Affect
* Create Moana-inspired crayon pāreu designs with the Pacific Climate Warriors
* Enjoy a live reading of I Love My Island by Moemoana Asfa'ato'a Schwenke, narrated by Inangaro Vakaafi
* Grow native plants and take a cutting home with Te Rito Gardens
* Get your face painted with sea and land creatures by Daizy Designs
* Paint watercolours inspired by botanist and seaweed expert Nancy Adams
* Explore Te Papa's Collections with our art and botany curators

This is an important site for Karori Kaitiaki, as it's the home of the future Birdwood Reserve track. Volunteers can either climb down the gully to help clear weeds, or can comfortably work on the street-level planted areas around the carpark.

2-4pm, Sunday 1 March 2026
Birdwood Reserve, opposite the Zealandia overflow carpark

The KāKā team

description:
Workout and working bee with Hypha, Hypha and Zealandia are teaming up to clear out the lungs and clean up Te Kaiwharawhara!
Kick off the day with a morning workout, followed by a working bee to remove rubbish from Te Kaiwharawhara stream behind the Hypha building.
Never done something like this before? This one's for you. The workout will be a strength and conditioning session and open to all levels, ages and stages. Following this we're getting into a working bee from 9:30–12:30pm (after coffee of course) where we'll be cleaning up Te Kaiwharawhara stream along School Road. description:
World Ocean Day Fundraising Quiz - Mountains to Sea, Whale-come back for another instalment of the Mountains to Sea Wellington World Ocean Day Pub Quiz!

Brush up on your ocean trivia, put on your pirate hats, and join us for an unforgettable night of community sea-lebration!
Thanks to our friends at Parrotdog Bar, we’ll be back on the south coast this year for this annual sell-out fundraising event... get your tickets fast!

All proceeds from the night will support Mountains to Sea Wellington’s marine programmes, providing opportunities for folks of all ages to get up close and personal with te taiao through our education programmes, restoration projects and community events.

We’ll have a range of quiz topics, themed around the ocean (and other topics for the less ocean-savvy). There’ll also be mini games, raffles, spot prizes and more!

‍Be the best dressed:
Don your most sea-purb costumes and join the catwalk to compete for …the best in shoal!

Tickets on sale NOW! Get in quick before they are gone.
Tickets are $25pp or $150 for a team table (maximum 6 per team), with options to pay more if you’re feeling like making a bigger splash to support us.
If you book a single ticket, we’ll set you up with team mates on the night.

This event is part of World Ocean Day celebrations. Learn more about World Ocean Day here:https://worldoceanday.org.

description:
Ōtari Glow Worm Tour, Take a guided night tour through Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush and discover some of the fascinating night-time residents on your way to see the titiwai/glowworms. Enjoy the tranquil beauty of the bush after dark and witness the magical glow of these unique creatures.

This outdoor night-time tour takes just over an hour.
The tour requires a moderate level of fitness; the route includes numerous steps and a steep incline to and from the glowworms.
No dogs, and not suitable for babies and young children.

Meet at the Ōtari Visitors Centre, 150 Wilton Road. Wrap up in warm clothes, wear sturdy walking shoes, and bring a torch or head lamp.

Glow Worm Tour Ticket Refund Policy:
• No Refunds: We do not offer refunds for Glow Worm Tour tickets.
• Ticket Transfers: If you can’t attend your booked tour, with 2 weeks notice we can put you on a future tour, subject to availability.
• Weather Conditions: Tours operate rain or shine. In the event of extreme weather or unsafe conditions, we will reschedule your tour or provide a refund.

For any changes or enquiries, please get in touch with us in advance at Treehouse@wcc.govt.nz or call 04 499 1400.

This tour is operated by the Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush Trust. Join the Trust from only $20 a year and the glow worm tour is free, plus you’ll be supporting the amazing work the Trust does. Join today at owbt.nz/membership-donations/
label: Conservation & Nature

description:
🛠️🌿 Hands-On Conservation: Trap-Making with NAWIC🌿🛠️, Join us on Thursday 9th October, from 5:00pm – 7:30pm at MenzShed Hataitai for a hands-on evening of teamwork in the spirit of conservation. Let's protect our local native wildlife by building pest traps to donate to Predator Free Wellington in support of their mission.
With materials and ready-to-assemble kitsets kindly sponsored by Aoraki Construction, we’ll roll up our sleeves and assemble traps at MenzShed Hataitai - all tools and materials provided. No experience required.
After the mahi, we’ll come together to share fish 'n' chips and fizzy drinks on the bowling green, kindly provided by NAWIC. It’s a chance to connect, give back, and make a tangible impact on our environment.

80's Day Disco: Wellington 🪩, 80's Day Disco: Wellington 🪩
Tickets selling fast → https://www.fatsoma.com/e/vb6j5pqr/la/qwmu

Get Ready to Groove at the Ultimate 80s Day Disco! 🎉

Step into a time machine and relive the magic of the 80s with a day filled with the biggest disco anthems and synth-powered hits of the decade. Whether you’re a true 80s fanatic or just here for the nostalgia, this party is all about electric vibes, funky beats, and non-stop dancing! 🎧🕺✨

What to Expect:

🎶 Nonstop 80s Classics: Dance to the timeless hits that defined the decade—from disco grooves to rock anthems and synth-pop bangers.

🕺 Retro Dance Floor Energy: Show off your best moves under the dazzling glow of neon lights and shimmering disco balls.

📸 Totally Rad Photo Ops: Capture the moment with throwback props, vintage backdrops, and all the 80s glam.

🌟 Feel-Good Vibes All Day Long: Celebrate the music, the energy, and the nostalgia with great people and iconic tunes.

Let’s make it a day to remember—80s style! 🎶💿✨

Expect to hear music from:

Michael Jackson ⭐ Madonna ⭐ Prince ⭐ Whitney Houston ⭐ Queen ⭐ George Michael ⭐ David Bowie ⭐ Tina Turner ⭐ Elton John ⭐ Phil Collins ⭐ Cyndi Lauper ⭐ Bon Jovi ⭐ The Police ⭐ Bruce Springsteen ⭐ Duran Duran ⭐ Journey ⭐ Billy Joel ⭐ Lionel Richie ⭐ Eurythmics ⭐ Depeche Mode ⭐ Aerosmith ⭐ U2 ⭐ The Cure ⭐ Van Halen ⭐ Hall & Oates ⭐ AC/DC ⭐ The Smiths ⭐ New Order ⭐ Fleetwood Mac ⭐ The Bangles ⭐ Rick Astley ⭐ Spandau Ballet ⭐ Roxette ⭐ Simple Minds ⭐ Guns N’ Roses ⭐ Billy Idol ⭐ Tears for Fears ⭐ Bryan Adams ⭐ A-ha

FAQ’S

🗣️ Why do the tickets come in different price tiers?

Whilst there is no physical difference. There is only a limited amount of tickets we can sell. Therefore we operate a festival style ticketing model. The earlier you buy your ticket the cheaper it will be.

🗣️ Do you do group discount? Stag/Hen etc

Yes, we offer a discounted ticket price for groups of 10 or more. These tickets can be found listed as the “Big Group Package!” above, orders for these tickets are restricted to a minimum of 10.

🗣️ Will there be more tickets available if the event is sold out?

Once this event is sold out, there will not be any additional tickets released. In addiction to this we will be unable to sell them at the door due to maximum capacity and health and safety regulations.

🗣️ Is the venue accessible?

Our events take place at a variety of locations across the UK and Ireland. As each varies please ensure to check the specific venue's website for accessibility information.

🗣️ Can I resell my tickets?

Yes, if you are unable to attend an event you are welcome to sell your tickets on. We do not use names on tickets as a condition for entry.

🗣️ Are your events 18+?

All of our events are strictly 18+. A valid photographic ID may be requested on entry.

🗣️ I have more questions?

If you have additional questions and wish to contact us directly, don’t hesitate to drop us a DM on either Facebook (Daytime Disco) or Instagram (@daytimediscoevents)

Refund Policy:
In-line with normal consumer standards for ticket purchases, tickets for Daytime Disco events are non-refundable, on the condition that we not moved the event or canceled it. If you are no longer be able to attend the event, you are of course welcome to gift or sell your tickets onwards as we do not use names on the tickets as a condition of entry.

A Celtic Christmas by A Taste of Ireland - Wellington, “Jingle Jigs, Reels a Treat.”
Ken Longworth – The Newcastle Herald
Direct from its Off-Broadway season, A Taste of Ireland - The Irish Music & Dance Sensation, presents its holiday spectacular, A Celtic Christmas. Prepare to be enchanted with some of the world’s finest Irish dancers and musicians bringing the spirit of Christmas to life, in a show that will make you laugh, cry, and sing into the night.
After captivating audiences across the USA and around the world, A Celtic Christmas by A Taste of Ireland returns to New Zealand this festive season following a highly successful 2022 tour. Experience the magic as world-class performers blend melodic folk mash-ups, acapella tap battles, and heartwarming storytelling in one truly unforgettable performance.
Featuring former World Irish dance champions and stars from Lord of the Dance and Riverdance, A Celtic Christmas delivers a holiday spectacular packed with Irish wit, traditional tunes and heartfelt ballads, alongside all your favorite carols. The show’s exciting mix of electrifying rhythms and extraordinary talent promises an evening brimming with Irish charm and enthralling entertainment, all in one powerhouse event.
Immerse yourself in a traditional Celtic landscape and let the magic of an Irish Christmas transport you to a world filled with excitement and wonder, where vibrant music and dance embody the heartbeat of the festive season.
With over one hundred and fifty 5-star Facebook reviews and over 150,000 followers, A Celtic Christmas by A Taste of Ireland promises 100% live singing and dancing as it bridges the gap between energetic folk music, Irish dance, and modern tap styles.
Don’t miss your chance to see this magical show as it tours New Zealand for a strictly limited season. Get your tickets now before they sell out.

description:
A Century Celebration!, A Century Celebration!
In 1926, at a meeting at the Accounts Chambers in Johnston Street, Wellington, Mrs JW Bell (and her husband) offered to lease three sections of her land for the purposes of establishing a tennis and bowling club in Titahi Bay.

Well Mrs Bell, thanks to your kind offer, we are still here 100 years later and don’t we have some stories and memories to share of those years gone by!

Over the course of Wellington Anniversary weekend (16-18 January 2026), we invite current and former members of the Titahi Bay Tennis Club to come and join us in celebrating this incredible milestone!

In coming months, we will update this post with more information about events planned for the weekend. In the meantime, please put this in your diary, share with friends, family, or perhaps use it as an opportunity to reach out to a former interclub team mate you haven’t seen or heard from in a while and tell them you’ll see them there!

We hope you can join us for what should be a great occasion!

description:
AR Monthly Concert - Laldy and Owen Hugh, AR Monthly Concert - Laldy and Owen Hugh
Laldy; Wellington-based fiddle player Rachel James and guitarist Donald James combine forces for one mission: to play folk and “gie i' laldy”, meaning to do something with gusto or great enthusiasm. With Welsh and Scottish roots, they are inspired by Scottish, Irish and Scandinavian music traditions.
Laldy brings to the stage a set which weaves together contemporary and traditional folk tunes and songs with original writing and arrangement. Playing a selection of sweet songs, modal grooves and traditional bangers, Laldy are a lively and danceable offering to the New Zealand folk and festival scene.
Owen Hugh - has been writing songs since he was 16 though it
took him 3 years of trying before writing a decent one. He has just remastered all his albums and they are available on sites such as YouTube, Spotify and Apple music. His music always touches the soul and contains Celtic, Rock Folk and Blues influences. He cut his teeth at folk clubs in NZ and the UK in the 90’s and has played Edinburgh Fringe Festival 4 yrs in a row as well as several festivals in UK. Once described in the American Press as a cross between “Billy Connolly and James Taylor”, be prepared to laugh and cry possibly at the same time. After a period of writer’s block he is now recording and road-testing new material.
Entry: $20/$15 for members. Cash only (no eftpos facilities). Note: The concert will be on the first floor, with access via stairs or the lift. (Yes, the lift is back in action!) You may have to press the button at the side of the door to gain access to the building.

This three-day event will bring together barbershop singers, quartets, choruses, and enthusiasts from across the region for a celebration of harmony, performance, and community.

Attendees can look forward to a full schedule featuring competitions, workshops, coaching sessions, mass sing-alongs, and showcase concerts highlighting both emerging talent and seasoned performers. Tākina’s world-class facilities provide an ideal setting for vibrant performances and social gatherings, all within walking distance of Wellington’s cultural and culinary attractions.

The convention aims to inspire musical excellence, foster connection within the barbershop community, and offer an unforgettable experience for performers and audiences alike.
