description:
Beervana 2026, The world's weirdest and most wonderful beer festival returns to Hnry Stadium, Wellington on 21+22 August 2026!
For two glorious days - across four massive sessions (Friday and Saturday, morning and afternoon) - Hnry Stadium transforms into a full-blown beer universe celebrating craft beer, creativity, chaos and bloody good times!

Expect fresh pours from legendary breweries, one-off festival beers, delicious eats, roaming entertainment, hidden surprises and the kind of joyful mayhem only Beervana can deliver. From weird and wonderful brews to unforgettable festival moments, there’s nothing else quite like it.

Beer lovers travel from across New Zealand - and around the world - to experience the hoppiest place on earth. Whether you're a seasoned beer aficionado or just here for the vibes, expect the unexpected at Beervana.
label: Festivals

description: Beervana, Based at Hnry Stadium on Wellington’s magnificent waterfront, Beervana attracts over 16,000 people over two days. About 50 breweries set up shop on the covered concourse that surrounds the stadium. They represent a selection of beer brewers from around New Zealand, Australia, and further afield. Revellers can make a full circuit of the building and not miss anything. Visit stalls, taste some uniquely brewed beers, chat to the brewers, and catch up with mates. Adding to the atmosphere are food stalls and multiple live music performances. There are four sessions spread across the weekend. Each runs for five hours so there is plenty of time to enjoy the vibe, learn something new, and discover an amazing brew.
label: Festivals

description:
Beervana, New Zealand’s boldest, hoppiest, and most delightfully weird beer festival. This is no ordinary tasting event, it’s a full-blown sensory adventure where brewers go wild, food gets fancy, and the unexpected is always on tap. 

Expect more than 60 breweries pouring over 300 unique brews—from hazy IPAs and fruited sours to beer cocktails and non-alcoholic surprises. 

But Beervana isn’t just about the beer. It’s a feast for all senses: think whitebait fritters from Boulcott St Bistro, Korean fried chicken, Mahurangi oysters. Add in live music, quirky brewery stands (yes, there’s a Best Stand vote), and unexpected entertainment and you’ve got a festival that you'll come away from with a greater knowledge of great beer, a belly full and plenty of fun memories with your mates.

description:
Bloomsday 2026, Bloomsday 2026
Join us to celebrate Bloomsday!

June 16 is the day on which James Joyce’s groundbreaking Modernist novel, 'Ulysses', is set. In Dublin there is a whole festival dedicated to Bloomsday and it is marked all around the world with events just like this one.

Cherie Jacobson, Director of Katherine Mansfield House & Garden, will share her experience of Bloomsday in Dublin last year, and Jane Connolly, Ambassador of Ireland, will share a reading from Ulysses. Food and music are important in 'Ulysses', so we’ll also be offering a taste of both.

Participants in Bloomsday often dress up, from a simple straw boater like James Joyce wore or the bowler hat sported by his character Leopold Bloom, to full Edwardian garb. So don’t be shy about dressing for the occasion!

Katherine Mansfield and James Joyce met for a cup of tea in Paris; now you can meet in the birthplace of one Modernist icon, to celebrate the work of another.

This event is free but registration is required via our website due to limited space in the house. Please note that this event will take place upstairs, see the Accessibility page of our website for more information.

In partnership with the Embassy of Ireland, New Zealand.

description:
Blossom Valley: Wellington's Cherry Blossom Festival, Blossom Valley: Wellington's Cherry Blossom Festival
Wellington's annual spring cherry blossom festival is back this September 🌸 A must-see event with 350+ cherry blossom trees creating a sea of pink 🌸

⭐ 'After Dark' evening light experience tickets now on sale.

📷 Capture gram-worthy photos and videos under the blossoms, and find our viral style photo spots including a giant living love heart, a swing, a boat (new this year!), a giant frame, and more

🛏️ Book a night in our chalet accomodation and wake up to a sea of pink 🌸

☕ Pre-purchase a delightful high tea alongside your ticket for the full experience (bookings required)☕

Weekends often sell out so make sure you have pre-purchased tickets online to secure your car park as spaces are limited. We hate to have to turn cars away when tickets are sold out so please do pre-purchase your tickets this year for weekends!! 🚗

🌸 New This Year - Flexi Passes
This pass allows you to come on whichever day you like. Not sure about the weather or at what level of blossom the trees are then this is for you. Purchase this ticket and come during the day on whichever day and time you like. (These tickets do NOT cover the After Dark experience).

Shuttles are available from Wellington, Palmerston North, Masterton or (anywhere!) with Capital Shuttles. With bookings available from 1 person, up to a 54 seater bus, they are the ideal way to get to and from Aston Norwood Gardens 🚌

Our in house photographer Lilia will be back again offering affordable professional photography sessions - perfect for family photos, couple photos, solo, friend groups, or even secret engagements! 📷

🌸 Blossom Valley is more than an event—it’s a fleeting moment of beauty, peace, and connection with nature. We can’t wait to share it with you. 🌸

-
In 1994, inspired by visits to Japan, owners Mark and Fiona Rammell planted over 350 Sakura Cherry Blossoms and are now seeing their dream burst into life each Spring.

Blossom Valley is an annual spring celebration sure to put the spring in your step as you explore the 14 acres of garden with New Zealand’s highest number and density of mature cherry blossom trees in the one place. For just a short amount of time each year at Aston Norwood Gardens in Kaitoke, Upper Hutt, hundreds of cherry trees come alive creating a canopy of pink blossom.

The event is carefully scheduled around the natural blossoming of the trees, with data from previous years informing the date selection. While the team at Blossom Valley do their best to ensure the ultimate blossom experience the timing of the bloom is up to mother nature.

Bodgies to Bogans, Bodgies to Bogans
This Festival event runs from the 18th October to the 9th November 2025.


'Bodgies to Bogans' tells the story of the juvenile delinquencies and teenager rebellion of the 1950s to the Bogans of the 1980s.

Whether you were listening to rock and roll, riding motorcycles and drinking milk shakes at milk bars in the 50s or growing a mullet and thrashing out the leathers to heavy metal in the 80s, this exhibition documents the history of youth culture in Upper Hutt, and New Zealand.

Curated and developed by Whirinaki Whare Taonga.
Proudly supported by The Rimutaka Trust.
Open 10am–4pm, seven days a week.


Cost: Koha
Event information here: https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/bodgies-to-bogans/

Bookshop Day 2025, Mark your calendars, Bookshop Day takes place on Saturday 11 October! Bookshop Day is a one-day nationwide celebration of independent bookstores, highlighting the cultural importance of books and bookshops, and the people that bring the two together, our amazing booksellers.
This year marks 10 years of Bookshop Day in Aotearoa – that’s 10 years of dress-up competitions, live music, storytimes, regional bookshop hops, author readings, spot prizes, teddy bear sleepovers, giveaways, arts and crafts, scavenger hunts, delicious baked goods, and many, many more activities and offerings!
Bookshop Day is run by the Booksellers Association of New Zealand to encourage book lovers, like you, to celebrate your local bookshop.
Head to our website to explore our Bookshop Day event calendar and see what your local bookshop has planned this year: https://www.booksellers.co.nz/bookshop-day-2025-events

description:
Carnival of Chaos, Myth, chaos, murder, alchemy, mystery, and devils are afoot in this four-night festival featuring six short retellings of classic works with strange new twists! We invite you to THEA 303’s ‘Carnival of Chaos’ in Studio 77, premiering hybrid works from the House of Echoes (1 & 3 October): The Odyssey, Medea and The Devil is a Lover, and the House of Secrets (2 & 4 October): Rope, The Taming of the Shrew  and  God’s Gift.

Each adaptation has been directed, designed, produced, choreographed and managed by the students.

House of Echoes (Season A): Performs on the 1st and the 3rd of October

The Odyssey – An adaptation of Homer’s The Odyssey
Odysseus just wants to get home to his true love, but the journey isn’t exactly smooth. The streets after 2 a.m. and too many beers are alive with obstacles; cops are grumpy, goth girls are tempting, and the help of the Gods is nowhere to be found. Meanwhile, back home, a dangerous polycule is getting cozy with his Penelope…

Medea – An adaptation of Euripides’ Medea
Medea lives her perfect 1950s white picket fence dream! When her husband starts taking new pills “Conservatol, the wonder drug for traditional love” she learns that traditional love means different to what she thought. Betrayal, hurt, and anger push her to the edge making her act in ways she never thought she would. “Heaven has no rage like love to hatred turned, nor Hell a fury like a woman scorned.”

The Devil is a Lover – An adaptation of William Shakespeare’s Love Labours Lost and Ben Johnson’s The Devil is an Ass
Satan and two devils, Beelzebub and Pug, make a pact to travel to a 1920s speakeasy on Earth and abstain from corruption for 3 years. As the narrative combines absurdist actions with Shakespearean dialogue, the three devils quickly learn of the difficulties present in avoiding corruption and the effect their devilish meddling has on humanity.

House of Secrets (Season B): Performs on the 2nd and 4th of October

Rope – An adaptation of Patrick Hamilton’s Rope (1929)
Not a whodunnit, but a howdoyahideit? Marion and Melanie are sure they’ve committed the perfect murder by killing their friend Norman and hiding his body in a chest, a chest their select group of friends have been invited over to have a murder mystery games night around. It’s foolproof, until the over analytical Constance comes to play…

The Taming of the Shrew – An adaptation of William Shakespeare’s Taming of the Shrew
In 1970's Aotearoa, sisters Katherina and Bianca find their love lives complicated by their father's order that one may not pursue romance unless the other follows suit. The sudden appearance of a charming factory owner and friend of Bianca's beau could mark a new hope for the two, but will this lead to an ocean of love or does something far more sinister lurk beneath the surface?

God’s Gift – An adaptation of Ben Johnson’s The Alchemist
The Carnival has come to town in 1615 London. Lovewit has gone to see the show, leaving her manor in the hands of Jeremy the Butler, the “Alchemist,” and Dol, a hardworking prostitute. Lovewit’s house becomes a place for schemes, with ample opportunities to take money from foolish men. Will Dol be happy with her split of the money? Or will a surprise visitor shake things up?

Content Forecast: mentions of and implied sexual violence and domestic abuse, mentions of drug use, strobe lighting, violence, coarse language, loud noises, haze, and smoke.

description:
Cheep Frills (Live) x Rare Specimens, Born on East London’s dancefloors and forged across Aotearoa New Zealand’s club and festival circuit, Tempo Schmempo finally lands in Te Whanganui-a-Tara for the first time, with a vibrant series of parties for the winter months.
On a bi-monthly basis, expect carefully curated lineups of the country’s finest underground electronic artists, designed to showcase the fantastic talent that thrives across the motu.
What’s more, each party will be punctuated by a double A-side release from the two artists performing on the night - to be released a week before the party.
And to top it off, we've teamed up with Duncan’s Brewing Co. to pour an official Tempo Schmempo beer on tap for the night.
For the first instalment, we’re proud to introduce Cheep Frills (Live) and Rare Specimens.
About the artists:
Cheep Frills is a genre-bending live act from Marcos Alonso and Dolphin Therapy, fusing electronic production with vibrant vocals and playful performance. Their shows deliver high-energy dancefloor stompers, cheeky reinterpretations, and unexpected sonic detours that keep crowds moving and grinning. Equal parts musically tight and joyfully loose, Cheep Frills is a guaranteed mood-lifter for any stage or setting.
As Rare Specimens, Nick Munday, Pete Green, Matt McPhee and Dan Rainey have become firm fixtures in New Zealand’s underground electronic scene, balancing playful eclecticism with dancefloor precision during their unique back to back performances. United by their love of disco, italo, acid house, Detroit techno, Balearic sounds and UK club culture, the group combines road-tested experience with finely tuned taste acquired through decades of crate-digging and DJing across the globe.
Expect only the finest musical selections, lovingly curated from dance music’s rich history — plus more shenanigans than you can shake a stick at.
See you on the dance floor.

Vamos a celebrar este 18 de Septiembre como corresponde! ✨

Los queremos invitar a celebrar estas fiestas con la comunidad en el bowling de Seatoun.
Vamos a tener dos parrillas prendidas, juegos tradicionales (gymkana, carrera de sacos, la silla musical, una pichanga y hasta karaoke), además de música y baile pa’ que no falte el zapateo . 🎶⚽🔥
La idea es que cada uno traiga algo para la parrilla y algo rico para compartir: puede ser un postre, unas empanadas, sopaipillas, ensaladas o lo que se les ocurra. En el local se podra comprar bebestibles varios, incluso terremotos!!! 🍷🍻
Y porque no hay primera sin segunda ni segunda sin tercera… 🎉
Este año vamos a celebrar con varios panoramas:
⦁ Sábado 13 de Septiembre: celebración en el restaurant Puro Chile desde las 12pm a 7pm .

⦁ Sábado 20 de Septiembre en la noche: seguimos la fiesta en el barrio con DJ Descontrol.

⦁ Domingo 21 de Septiembre: en el bowling de Seatoun con nosotros desde 12pm.

También para los que quieran ir a apoyar y ver el show de Puku Rangi Tea (Grupo de danza de Rapa Nui) en Wellington.
⦁Martes 16/09: Performance en Scots College Wellington. FREE 7pm.
⦁Jueves 18/09: Presentacion en el musel Te Papa Tongarewa. FREE 1pm

¡Así que vengan con ganas de pasarlo chancho y celebrar juntos este 18 toda la semana!!!

Nos vemos pronto!!!!!!


Let’s celebrate this Chilean Independence day the right way! ✨

We’d like to invite you to join us for our celebration with the community at the Seatoun Bowling Club.
We’ll have two barbecues going, traditional games (gymkana, sack race, musical chairs, a friendly football match, and even karaoke), plus music and dancing so we don’t miss out on some good cueca steps. 🎶⚽🔥

The idea is that everyone brings something for the barbecue and something tasty to share: it could be a dessert, empanadas, sopaipillas, salads, or whatever you’d like. Drinks will be available for purchase at the venue, including Chile’s famous cocktail, the Terremoto.🍷🍻

And because one party is never enough… 🎉 This year we’ll be celebrating several events:

⦁Saturday, September 13th: Celebration at Puro Chile restaurant, from 12pm to 7pm.

⦁Saturday, September 20th at night: we keep the party going in El Barrio with DJ Descontrol.

⦁Sunday, 21 September at the Seatoun Bowling with us from 12 pm.

Also for those who would like to go and support and watch the show by Puku Rangi Tea (Rapa Nui Dance Group) in Wellington.
⦁Tuesday 16: Performance at Scots College Wellington. FREE 7pm.
⦁Thursday 18: Performance at the Te Papa Tongarewa Museum. FREE 1pm.

So come ready to have an amazing time and celebrate this Chilean Independence Day/Week together, not just once but several times!

See you soon. 🎉🎉🎉

description:
Chillax 2026, Chillax 2026
January 16–19th. Unplug. Unwind. Unleash.

About this Event




Get ready to CHILLAX - JAN 16-19th 2026!
Unplug. Unwind. Unleash.
This January, escape the chaos and step into a world where nature, music, and good vibes rule. CHILLAX is your long weekend paradise — a four-day off-the-grid camping festival set in stunning natural surrounds.
What to Expect:
Live Music from sunrise sessions to late-night jams
Cool off with a river swim
Farm Walks to reconnect with the land
Star Gazing under skies unspoiled by city lights
And the ultimate highlight: The Tropical Lotus Bell Tent Party - a vibrant explosion of colour, rhythm, and wild tropical energy!

No WiFi. No deadlines. Just freedom, fresh air, and a whole lot of fun.
Leave your phone. Bring your soul.
CHILLAX – The name says it all.

Our Chillax Festival gets better each year with the support of our wider Chilled whānau, it grows, matures, blossoms and develops into something new and exciting. We can't wait to see where this journey takes us next.
Without all your support, we wouldn't be able to add little extras each year - so THANK YOU ❤

Our Mission:
At the Chillax Festival, we provide a platform for new up and coming artists to present themselves and grow confidence in front of a friendly non-judgmental group of Chilled Kiwis! To bring happiness and enjoyment, surrounded by the beautiful nature our country has to offer, while focusing on sustainable, safe, chilled events.
Stansborough is a beautiful hidden farm, encompassing 2300 acres of hills, valleys, swimming holes and bush. At the Chillax Festival you can forget the rest of the world exists and leave all your worries behind.
Come for the day or stay the entire weekend it is up to you.
____________________________________________________________________________________________________



Enjoy live music over the long weekend from our 2026 Muso line up!
Our 2026 line up and onsite food options, will be confirmed 3 months prior to the event.
All ticket holders will be notified and kept up to date with all new information.
Here is a snaek peak of what we can confirm!...
Our 2026 Newest Guest Artist is "Raia"
Based in Palmerston North, Raia is a young, confident artist with an amazingly pure voice. By far our youngest performer yet, she has a voice and stage presence that far exceeds her age. Raia performs covers and original songs - both contemporary and old school - layering smooth vocals and charming arrangements across everything she does. Raia is excited to bring her artistry and love of music to this years Chillax Festival.
Our guest band for 2025 'The Archer Project' loved it as much as we loved them - so they are definately coming back!
Of course we will also have some of our other favourites returing! ____________________________________________________________________________________________________


ITINERARY


FRIDAY -

If you are extra keen to make the most of the whole weekend, why not join us on Friday. Arrive from midday and once you are set up you can enjoy the scenery, explore the lake and bush valleys, swim in the river, walk the hills and tracks or climb to the top and see the sea. Wind up the evening with some good company chilling in the barn.



SATURDAY - Event day #1


If you're not already enjoying our company, arrive anytime, pitch your tent, or simply park your car, familiarise yourself with the surroundings.

Live music throughout the day from a range of artists and mixed bands - some regular favourites and some new amazing talent! Maybe even some surprises for the kids.


We have another food truck attending this year, so bring cash if you want a break from the BBQ! Our wonderful friends from Sajitarian IceCreams will be selling their amazing Ice Creams, so bring cash and don't miss out!


This year the main tent will be open for everyone to enjoy throughout the weekend. I great place to relax, sit quietly and get out of the sun.

Saturday evening you can enjoy our CHILLAX tent party - 2026 is 'TROPICAL THEME' so don't forget your Hawaiian shirts and Tropical skirts!


After dark make sure you get in some amazing star gazing in our beautiful dark sky zone!



SUNDAY - Event day #2

Another chillaxed day with plenty of live music from bands.


Appreciate the beautiful rural setting, take a gentle stroll or a hike to the top of the hill to see the sea or simply chill out by the river in the sun with friends. Play a game and listen to music - the choice is yours. How about an evening Comedy Fest in the tent?!


MONDAY - Wellington Anniversary

Appreciate the beautiful rural setting, take a gentle stroll or a hike to the top of the hill to see the sea or simply chill out by the river in the sun with friends. Pack up when you are ready and then we look forward to seeing you all next year!

____________________________________________________________________________________________________

Parking will be provided by the camp site. Once you are set up you can enjoy the scenery, explore the lake and bush valleys, swim in the river, walk the hills and tracks or climb to the top to see the sea.
Fridges in the cottage will be available, so you can put your (clearly named) food in them to store. You may want to bring a chilli bin and ice for beverages.
For lunch and dinner on Saturday, the BBQs will be back for everyone to use. We are also trying to lock in a food truck to add a bit of variety for everyone, so bring your cash so you dont miss out!


WHAT YOUR TICKET INCLUDES
A line up of Live Entertainment over the long weekend by a variety of live singers, musicians and music under the stars.
Use of toilets (Tidy Eco toilet units with solar lights)
Use of BBQs and shared fridges and cash food truck options!
An amazing chilled weekend or day out and the additional option of off-the-grid camping on a beautiful private secret site in the Wairarapa!
Live music, great company, laughter and good memories!
____________________________________________________________________________________________________
Tickets to each consecutive event, will be offered first to those who attended the event previous, so be one of the first so you don’t miss out.
'Ms Magnifique Events' are invitation only and limited numbers are limited so don't miss out. This enables us to keep these events special, exclusive, desirable and personal.
If due to weather the festival must be cancelled, there will be a postponement date or the choice for a refund (minus a small admin fee). All funds are held by Eventbrite until the event date incase of cancellation and refunds.


WHAT TO BRING
Enough food for your group for the duration of your stay or money for onsite food options. There are NO shops close (only a very handy and exceptional cafe 10 mins drive away - but you will need to check opening hours!) You need to make sure you do not run out of food, drinks and WATER. We will have some spring water available which is ok for drinking, but most people prefer to bring bottled water.

BYO drinks and water
Eating and cooking utensils (plates, bowls, cups, cutlery etc)
Cash - for onsite food options
Tent, sleeping bag, pillow and bedroll (if you want one) - If you have a camper van or pop up you are also welcome to bring them.
Togs and towel for river swimming - 3 great swimming holes to choose from
Insect repellant, sun block and antihistamine
Happiness, laughter and awesome dance moves
Please bring bottled water if possible (we don’t suggest drinking the river water)
Torches (there is no power at the camp site so once it’s dark it is super dark! Unpolluted night skies with loads of stars and satellites)
Oh and don't forget, again......BYO water!


IMPORTANT INFO
Notes:
NO POWER at camp site.
NO CELL COVERAGE OR INTERNET (unless you climb to the top of the hill/mountain or visit the local cafe)
NO PETS (as there will be farm stock around)
ABSOLUTELY NO SMOKING (we don’t want to start a bush fire, and you would unfortunately be liable)
POP UPS OR CAMPER VANS are ok, but please note there is no power or waste dumping available.

Closest 'Homewood Storeroom Cafe' 10 minutes drive down gravel road (we suggest you check opening hours) - a great cafe!
Closest basic shop - Riversdale (30 minutes on gravel road )
Closest supermarket - Carterton
Last petrol station: Carterton (we suggest you fill up there)
2 hours drive from Wellington (last 20mins on gravel road)
Exact address on google search ’Stansborough farm cottage’ Kaiwhata valley road, last 20 minutes is gravel. We will put ribbons up along the way for you to watch out for, so you know you're heading the right way.
There is an emergency phone at the farm house.
Make sure to grab a map of the property (will be provided on arrival) which highlights points of interest on the property.


Responsibilities:
Parents are solely responsible for their children at all times. Adults are responsible for themselves at all times, especially if drinking alcohol! Be aware the property and site of the event, is a working farm and there are hazards all around (rivers, lakes, cliffs, valleys and animals) so be careful and responsible.
The nearest medical facility is 50 minutes drive away.
When guests leave, we ask that you please take all your own rubbish with you and leave behind only flattened grass and the site as you found it.
If you are purchasing a Festival Day Pass only you will need a designated driver if any alcohol is consumed. The road to the venue is tricky and gravel in part. We DO NOT recommend anyone drives that has consumed any alcohol or is tired.

Click here to see videos and images from Chillax 2025:

description:
ChoctoberFest, Porirua is the home of New Zealand’s favourite chocolate — Whittaker's. So it's only fitting it has a festival celebrating all things chocolate. During September and October, the city is serving up a range of tasty treats for ChoctoberFest, all featuring Whittaker’s chocolate.
More than 30 local businesses will be competing in the Whittaker’s Bake Off and Top of the Chocs. Head in to participating spots, and try unique chocolate drinks and amazing baked goods. You can then vote for your favourites.
Indulge your tastebuds and try special drinks such as a whipped white choc biscoff latte, or a coldbrew shot choc maltini. For a sweet snack, how about a molten embrace, kunafa chocolate croissant, or a banoffee flossy pie? There are plenty of options for all chocolate lovers, including vegan and gluten free items.
As well as voting for your favourite items, you can join the fan club, share reviews, and be in to win. Up for grabs are 100 Whittaker’s Peanut Slabs, an exclusive tour of the Whittaker’s factory, and ChoctoberFest vouchers for local cafes and bars.
The festival has been running since 2022, and is a highlight of the local hospitality scene.

FAQ’S
🗣️ Why do the tickets come in different price tiers?
Whilst there is no physical difference. There is only a limited amount of tickets we can sell. Therefore we operate a festival style ticketing model. The earlier you buy your ticket the cheaper it will be.
🗣️ Do you do group discount? Stag/Hen etc
Yes, we offer a discounted ticket price for groups of 10 or more. These tickets can be found listed as the “Big Group Package!” above, orders for these tickets are restricted to a minimum of 10.
🗣️ Will there be more tickets available if the event is sold out?
Once this event is sold out, there will not be any additional tickets released. In addiction to this we will be unable to sell them at the door due to maximum capacity and health and safety regulations.
🗣️ Is the venue accessible?
Our events take place at a variety of locations across the UK and Ireland. As each varies please ensure to check the specific venue's website for accessibility information.
🗣️ Can I resell my tickets?
Yes, if you are unable to attend an event you are welcome to sell your tickets on. We do not use names on tickets as a condition for entry.
🗣️ Are your events 18+?
All of our events are strictly 18+. A valid photographic ID may be requested on entry.
🗣️ I have more questions?
If you have additional questions and wish to contact us directly, don’t hesitate to drop us a DM on either Facebook (Daytime Disco) or Instagram (@daytimediscoevents)
Refund Policy:
In-line with normal consumer standards for ticket purchases, tickets for Daytime Disco events are non-refundable, on the condition that we not moved the event or canceled it. If you are no longer be able to attend the event, you are of course welcome to gift or sell your tickets onwards as we do not use names on the tickets as a condition of entry.

Courtenay Carnival - The Biggest Dress Up Party in the Universe, Wellington’s most electric street celebration is back! The Courtenay Carnival transforms Courtenay Place into a dazzling hub of music, food, dance, and community spirit. From day to night, experience an unforgettable fusion of live performances, street eats, parades, and cultural showcases—all in the heart of the capital’s entertainment district.
What to Expect
Live Stages & Street Performers – From DJs to drumlines, salsa to soul, and everything in between, Courtenay Place bursts with energy. Expect a vibrant mix of circus performers, roaming comedy acts, drag artistry, and pop-up surprises throughout the precinct.
Entertainment Lineup
• Kids Disco – A fun, high-energy dance zone for tamariki.
• Circus & Comedy Acts – Jugglers, acrobats, and comedians bringing laughter and spectacle.

description:
Coven: Wet - Pride Party, Follow the siren song to Ivy Bar this Pride Festival and get pool ready for a night that will leave you dripping. This is a pride dance party for sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people, so let's get wet with pride.
You don’t want to miss the tantalising surprises we have planned… Follow us on Instagram for more teasers.

Coven is pay as you wish or koha on the door.
More info about Coven:
Coven Kaupapa
For queer women and gender minorities, spaces like this are rare, vital, and sometimes, life-changing. In a world that constantly centers cishet norms, Coven offers a space where we are the default – where you can fully show up as yourself, be seen, celebrated and surrounded by YOUR community.
Coming Solo? You’re Not Alone.
Don’t be nervous if you’re planning to come on your own – Coven is built for connection. Whether it’s your first queer event or your hundredth, you’ll be surrounded by a community that gets it. From the moment you arrive, there’ll be friendly faces, welcoming vibes, and plenty of chances to mingle, and connect. Coven is about belonging – and there’s a place here for you.
For many in our Coven, this is one of the only opportunities we feel comfortable enough to experience nightlife free from the male gaze, tokenism, fear, or the need to shrink ourselves to fit in. It’s a space where sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people aren’t just welcomed – we are centered. It’s for those who are often pushed to the margins, who rarely feel represented in “inclusive” spaces that still cater to the mainstream.
This night exists because we need it – and because we create it, together.

Does Irish music get your feet tapping? This is your opportunity to get up and dance to some cracking tunes at our evening Céilí on Saturday 18th of April.

Come to St Michael’s Hall in Kelburn to meet new people and enjoy a great time in a friendly and welcoming atmosphere. No dancing experience needed, just a bit of coordination, some energy, and a big sense of fun!

description:
Daffodil Express 2025, Carterton’s Daffodil Festival in the early Spring creates a great day out for the whole family. Why not travel there in style by a heritage train, let Steam Incorporated take the stress out of travel as you take the train to the Wairarapa. This year, our train has reduced capacity, so be sure to book in quickly!
Hauled by our heritage locomotives, take a glimpse into the bygone era of train travel as we clear the rush of Wellington, racing through the suburbs of Petone, Lower Hutt & Upper Hutt. After picking up the last of our passengers at Upper Hutt, we will race through the 8.8km long Rimutaka tunnel. This tunnel remains the longest in New Zealand with scheduled passenger trains, and has just been subjected to a full track relay for the first time since it was opened in 1955.
Passing through Featherston, we head east and navigate the rolling hills towards Carterton.
Arriving into Carterton, you'll have a few hours to disembark and go and explore Carterton's annual Daffodil Festival , before jumping on the train for the return journey home.
The Daffodil Fields and Festival
Located in the heart of the Wairarapa, Carterton’s popular Daffodil Festival offers an abundance of activities ranging from the famous Daffodil picking at Middlerun Farm, markets along High and Holloway Streets, the Big Wai Art sale in the events Centre, live music, and loads more family fun.
Shuttle buses will run from the town centre to the daffodil fields. There will be a lot of people for these buses, so please be patient. The bus transfer is free.
Here you can pick your own daffodils for $5 (Cash Preferred) that is a fundraiser for Wellington Free Ambulance and Whānau Āwhina Plunket, Wairarapa region. While stocks last!
The fields are not suitable for walkers or wheelchairs due to uneven grounds.
Prior booking is essential, this is an annual sell out event!
Fares
Adult (13+) - $125
Child (2-12yrs) - $90
Infant - Free
For more information & tickets, head to https://steaminc.org.nz/book-train-trip/daffodil-express/

¡Celebra con nosotros el Día de los Muertos con música, baile, comida tradicional y altares conmemorativos!

About this Event

Welcome to the Day of the Dead - Dia de los Muertos Celebration at AWHI Yoga & Wellbeing! Join us for a vibrant and colorful event filled with traditional live music, storytelling, rituals for remembering the dead and delicious prehispanic Mexican cacao drink. Honour your loved ones at our ofrenda, or altar, and learn more from our faciltator, Claudio Escutia, about this rich cultural tradition.
Let's come together to celebrate life and remember those who have passed in a joyful and meaningful way. Don't miss out on this special celebration!

Cleansing copal and herbal welcoming.
An opening ceremony to acknowledge the Tlalmanalli (offering and altar) with the deep sound of the conch shell in the four directions and drums sounds.

Traditional Mexican chants for remembering the loved ones 
Atole de Chocolate, a traditional prehispanic drink - amazing in flavour, consumed cold or hot
Music to invoke emotion and imagery of contemplative natural and mystical environments

description:
Dia de los Muertos - Day of the Dead Celebration with Claudio Escutia, Dia de los Muertos - Day of the Dead Celebration with Claudio Escutia
Join Claudio for this special occasion we will be celebrating one of the most important holidays in Mexico, the day of the dead or “Dia de los Muertos”.

The Day of the Dead is one of the traditions that has remained alive throughout the centuries; the main holidays are November 1 & 2, which UNESCO designated and cataloged as an Intangible Heritage of Humanity in 2003.

This special celebration dates back to prehispanic times before the arrival of Europeans to America, and has been alive and widely celebrated over the years.

About the Day of the Dead
The Day of the Dead tradition dates back to pre-Hispanic times, when a tribute was paid to death; the tribute took place from the last week of October to the first days of November.

Prehispanic Mexicans conceived Death as the beginning of the journey to Mictlán (the Place of the Dead), during which the soul of the deceased had to overcome various obstacles before reaching Mictlantecuhtli (the Lord of the Dead) and Mictecacíhuatl (the Lady of the Dead). Upon reaching the gods of Mictlán, an offering had to be made to them in order to obtain eternal rest.

What to Expect
Claudio will explain why it is important to celebrate and take the time to honour and remember the members of your family, ancestors and loved ones who have passed away. He will also explain the mysticism and spirituality around the Day of the Dead celebration.

We’ll also learn how to set up your ofrenda, or altar, and which elements are important for it (as well their meaning).

It's very common for an ofrenda of the dead to be placed inside Mexican homes, decorated with papel picado, food, traditional sweets, and photos of loved ones. Candles and marigold flowers are also placed as a sign of welcome for our loved ones.

Feel free to bring photos of your beloved ones that have passed away, fruits and flowers for the altar and anything that your beloved ones valued / loved when they were here with us. We will place those on the altar.

The Evening’s Schedule
Cleansing copal and herbal welcoming.

An opening ceremony to acknowledge the Tlalmanalli (offering and altar) with the deep sound of the conch shell in the four directions and drums sounds.

History of the day of the dead celebration.

Explanation of the altar, and the main elements for an ofrenda.

Storytelling: learn of Mexican legends like Catrinas and Xoloitzcuintle (the Mexican dog that helps the dead to find their way to Mictlan, the Aztec underword).

Remembering and sharing histories about the loved ones that passed away (optional but encouraged)

Traditional Mexican chants for remembering the loved ones

Atole de Chocolate, a traditional prehispanic drink - amazing in flavour, consumed cold or hot

Music to invoke emotion and imagery of contemplative natural and mystical environments

Finish with a shamanic atmosphere of relaxation and traditional chants.

Details
When: Saturday 1 November, 7pm -9pm

Where: AWHI Yoga & Wellbeing - Level 2, 15 Johnston Street, Wellington CBD.

Investment: $55 (first 5 enrolments - $45!); Children under 16 years old - $35

Haere Mai!
Everyone is welcome including kids (see special pricing). No previous experience or knowledge is required. As this is an evening of learning and exploration, come wearing comfortable clothing! Bring an open heart and mind willing to learn and receive.

description:
Diwali Festival of Lights, Diwali Festival of Lights is an exciting cultural celebration with fun activities for the whole whānau . Experience the colours, tastes, and sounds of India and South-East Asia. TSB Arena and Shed 6 will host a variety of performances and plenty of activities to keep you entertained. Take part in henna painting and lantern-making. Feast on delicious regional cuisine, explore Indian fashion and jewellery, and meet local community groups. Most importantly, enjoy this important and joyous festival. 
At the end of the night, enjoy the fireworks show as the event goes out with a bang. The fireworks display will start at approximately 8:50pm on Wellington Harbour (weather dependent). 
Diwali is a significant annual festival that marks the triumph of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance. It is celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs, and Jains in communities all over the world. It’s marked with candles, lanterns, and fireworks. It is also known as Deepavali and is one of India’s most widely-celebrated holidays.

To celebrate the 80th Anniversary of Vietnam’s National Day (2 September), Viet Hub NZ proudly presents

description:
Ecstatic Dance Wellington, Ecstatic Dance Wellington
💫 Move. Release. Connect. The first Ecstatic Dance Wellington is here — come celebrate our launch at Vogelmorn with DJ Kimba Jade on the decks. 🌙❤️

🌟✨ Ecstatic Dance Wellington – Launch Event ✨🌟

With DJ Kimba Jade @ Vogelmorn, Wellington

Kimba Jade & Bernie Cruise are thrilled to bring Ecstatic Dance Wellington to life! 🎉 This is the launch event, and we can’t wait to co-create the first of many transformational dance journeys with you.

💫 What is Ecstatic Dance?
A freeform, drug- and alcohol-free dance experience where you move however your body wants. The music flows like a wave — starting slow, rising to ecstatic peaks, then softening into stillness. It’s therapeutic, uplifting, and a powerful way to connect with yourself and community.

Please note, that this Ecstatic Dance is not verbally guided, we let the music guide you 😊. Dance freely how your body moves you.

🎶 This Dance Floor
Guided by DJ Kimba Jade, expect an immersive journey through deep bass, tribal rhythms, and global soundscapes that awaken both body and spirit. With over 24 years behind the decks—including 8 years dedicated to Ecstatic Dance—Kimba crafts transformative spaces of joy, release, and connection. Originally from Auckland, she curated Alchemic Dance Floor events for 5 years, now co-runs the Ecstatic Dance Festival, and leads Alchemic Ecstatic Dance DJ Trainings. She’s thrilled to share her magic and move with you on the dance floor!

🎶 The Sound System
Here at Ecstatic Dance Wellington, we believe in using a phat sound system with lots of bass for our dances. We will be bringing an ultra vibey and super bassy experience for you!

description:
FRUIT LOOP FESTIVAL, Fruit Loop Festival
Marlborough’s freshest music festival!
About the Festival
Fruit Loop Festival is Marlborough’s juiciest new summer gig! A full-blown celebration of music and dance, kicking off under the sun and well into the night. Think open-air energy - blending Marlborough's summer magic with a full-scale music festival. An insane line-up of DJs and live performers with production to match! From the first drop to the final track, it's where the beat hits harder and the drinks taste sweeter.
Fresh, wild, fierce - Fruit Loop is the party Marlborough has been waiting for.
The Line-Up
DICK JOHNSON: The heart of NZ’s electronic scene, Dick Johnson is a true house music heavyweight. With remixes for global icons like Fatboy Slim and Claude VonStroke, plus Kiwi favourites L.A.B and Tiki Taane, he’s spent over two decades electrifying dancefloors worldwide. A relentless force behind the decks - and music director for Synthony - Dick brings the fire every time.
SIN: Co-host of George FM Drive, Sin is plugged into the pulse of the dance scene and has quickly become a revered authority on all things electronica. She’s torn up stages at Rhythm & Vines, Homegrown, Hidden Valley, and international festivals from Fiji to the UK. With supports for legends like Fatboy Slim, Groove Armada, and Netsky, Sin brings high-energy house, techno, and ravey curveballs to every set.
KITA MEAN: Kita Mean is New Zealand’s award-winning drag superstar, known for her infectious charm, razor-sharp wit, and high-camp aesthetic. With a career spanning 15+ years across stages and screens worldwide, she’s wowed audiences from Aotearoa and Australia to London, Canada, the USA, and beyond. Winner of the very first RuPaul’s Drag Race Down Under and co-owner of the iconic Caluzzi Cabaret, Kita continues to dazzle with colourful looks, flawless mug, and hilarious timing. Quirky, kooky, kitsch, and quick - Kita Mean isn’t just a queen, she’s an experience.
PETE GREEN: Originally from the UK, Pete is part of the vinyl-digging collective Rare Specimens. His love for deep, worldly electronic sounds brings low-end warmth and an infectious energy to the dancefloor. Along the way, he’s supported artists such as Crazy P, Psychemagik, Audio Jack, and Christopher Tubbs, playing festivals and parties from Creamfields and Rhythm & Alps to Tempo Schmempo. Expect a set seasoned with Italo, ambient, and deep house flavours, dusted with disco, and finished with a splash of techno.
Event Details
Date: Saturday 28 March 2026
Time: 2pm - 10pm
Location: The Fancy Cow, Marlborough
R18 event - Photo identification will be required.
Return Bus Service:
Getting to and from the festival is easy with our return bus service. Pick-up points will include Redwoodtown Woolworths, Seymour Square, and Countdown Springlands. Purchase a return bus ticket when you nab your ticket.
A full timetable and bus information will be announced closer to the event.
Parking is strictly limited at the festival. Drop off recommended.
Tickets
Tickets are limited — don’t wait. Secure yours now!
Door sales may be available.
Have your ticket open and ready to be scanned at the gate.
Kaupapa
Fruit Loop is a safe, inclusive space where everyone belongs. If you can’t celebrate diversity, respect others, and bring good vibes, this festival isn’t for you.
Harassment or discrimination of any kind will not be tolerated. Anyone behaving this way will be removed.
Refunds and Cancellations
Fruit Loop Festival is a rain or shine event. The festival will proceed regardless of weather conditions, except in circumstances where safety is compromised or conditions make it impossible for the event to continue.
No refunds will be given for changes to the programme, line-up, or advertised performers.
Stay Connected
Follow us for line-up drops, updates and key event information: @fruitloopfestival on Instagram

description:
Gates to Memory - Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance: CANCELLED, *TICKETS TO THIS EVENT ARE CURRENTLY ON HOLD*

Gates to Memory is a contemporary dance work that premiered at the Kia Mau Festival 2025. The work explores the connection with entities and embodies the messages, wants, and connection with our physical world.

Gates to Memory invites audiences to witness the intimate act of remembering—of reclaiming lost stories and forging new ones through embodied performance. It is a call to honour those who came before, to hold space for those yet to come, and to respect the ones who will always be.

The strength of this work lies in the unspoken but strongly felt spiritual presence that comes from openness to access messages that are not ours but from ancestors from spirit worlds. To the creators, these messages come in the form of music, movement, and intuition.

Gates to Memory is performed and directed by Caribbean and Brazilian afro-descendant artists Ella Williams and Stela Dara, lighting designer Elekis Poblete and CreaTech sound designers Kevin Licorish and Jeanelle Frontin . All who wish to connect with their spirituality and the cultural intertwining of traditions and entities.

Presented as part of the Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance 2026.

description:
Greytown Apple Harvest Festival 2026, Molewood Orchard is hosting the third annual Greytown Apple Harvest Festival on Easter Saturday, with the support of Greytown Country Village Heaven. Bring your family and come along for a day celebrating all things apple!

Entry to the orchard is free. The festival will be held in the orchard's idyllic picnic area, Molewood Meadows.

Pick your own apples (and possibly pears), carriage rides, face painting, food trucks, stalls, apple baking, cider and fruit wine samples, live music, games and activities for kids.

Please bring your own bags or buckets to pick into.

Access to the orchard is at 17 Mole St Greytown, or else from our “secret” door in the shelterbelt at the end of Farley Ave (this area has plenty of parking and is closest to the centre of Greytown).

Follow us on Facebook or Instagram for further details, or check out our website.

The rain day is Easter Monday, 6 April.

Greytown and its surrounding areas are home to an extraordinary concentration of diverse creative talent, producing a unique and vibrant range of artistic expressions. What better way to showcase this than with a local celebration of the arts?

description:
Greytown Lands Trust Big Switch Opening Night @ The New Zealand Festival of Christmas, Greytown Lands Trust Big Switch Opening Night @ The New Zealand Festival of Christmas
Kick off the New Zealand Festival of Christmas 2026 festivities on Saturday, 27 June, with a spectacular rural celebration.

Main Street turns into a Town and Country show of sorts, where you can cheer on your favourite backyard hero in our Ride on Lawnmower Grand Prix, play old school games, and once it gets dark, see the magical lights get switched on for the first time, and enjoy the much-loved Light Up Tractor Parade as it rolls through the village.

What to expect:
- Entertainers throughout the village
- Artisan Night Markets with arts, crafts, food, and festive treats
- Outdoor dining at Truckstop, The White Swan Garden Bar and Food Truck Central
- The first switch-on of magical Christmas lighting
- The beautiful Community Christmas Tree, featuring adorable Ruru Morepork decorations by local children. Thanks to Greytown Lands Trust.
- Snowfall returns — by popular demand - thanks to FreshChoice Greytown! Every 30 mins from 6pm - 8pm
- Spin the wheel to win a meat pack

Browse the Night Markets and sample delicious food truck treats, grab a hot chocolate or mulled wine, enjoy the entertainment, the snowfall and festive music through the streets.

Main Street will be closed to traffic so you can roam freely and soak up the atmosphere. Throw on your winter coat or your Christmas jumper and join us for an opening night to remember, thanks to Greytown Lands Trust.

IMPORTANT INFORMATION
Some Festival of Christmas events involve flashing lights and light projections, which may affect people with light sensitivity. Please stay within designated safe zones and follow the directions of our traffic marshals.

description:
Greytown Through the Ages, Greytown Through the Ages
DATE: All Weekend
LOCATION: various retail shops & eateries in Greytown Main St.
AGES: All
COST: Free
Step back in time with Greytown Through the Ages, a unique, immersive event where visitors can explore the town’s rich history simply by strolling along its charming Main Street and local shops. Participating businesses throughout Greytown will display historical photographs — some dating back as far as the 1850s.

Wander into cafés, boutiques and eateries to discover black-and-white snapshots of rarely seen archival images showing what Greytown once looked like. From dusty horse-drawn streets to early main street storefronts of eras gone by, each location offers a different window into the past.

Many photographs will be matched with the current buildings so visitors can compare then and now, sparking conversations and nostalgia and soak in the legacy of one of New Zealand’s most historic towns.

www.greytownarttown.com

HARD OUT, Hard Out — Jungle Juice is dropping their first-ever Hard Techno party, and it’s gonna go off.

We’re talking straight-up belters, raw sounds and heavy energy, just pure underground sound for the real techno whānau.

Pull up, bring your crew, and get ready for a full-on sesh — loud, sweaty, and proper hard out.

Heavy pulse of the underground. Jungle Juice has been shaping Wellington’s dance floors, and now they’re turning up the pressure — faster, harder, and unapologetically raw.

Lose yourself in the kick. Feel the weight of the bass. This one’s for the ones who live the night — Aotearoa’s true techno heads.

• DANI — 22:00–23:00
• MALWARE — 23:00–00:00
• DJ BY ACCIDENT— 00:00–01:00
• VNESS — 01:00–02:00
• GASPAR — 02:00–03:00

Venue: Red Square — 26 Blair St, Te Aro, Wellington

Get ready, Wellington — this is Hard Out. No compromises, just pure Hard Techno.
Important Information
This event is R18. Valid photo ID will be required for entry.
Respect each other and the venue.
We will not tolerate any form of discrimination.
Look out for each other and please report any antisocial behaviour.
Consent is key – always.
Lighting & Visual Effects: Please be aware that strobe lights, lasers and other flashing
visuals may be in use throughout the night. These effects may not be suitable for everyone.
Photos & Video: Our crew will be capturing the energy of the night through photos and videos. By being here, you’re part of that magic and may appear in content we share to celebrate and promote future events.
Have fun and please find the crew if you have any issues.

Havelock Mussel & Seafood Festival 2026, Havelock Mussel & Seafood Festival 2026
Marking its 22nd year, the Havelock Mussel & Seafood Festival has been an integral part of Marlborough's vibrant summers and is back Saturday the 14th of March!

Indulge in the freshest catches straight from the ocean and savour the mouthwatering flavours of Marlborough's finest seafood delicacies.

Experience live music from kiwi legends & local artists, cooking demonstrations from local experts and Celebrity Chef, fascinating industry displays, and a Kids Zone to keep the little ones entertained. And, of course, be part of our Guinness World record attempt for mussel opening!

For our out-of-town festival-goers, worry not! We have arranged convenient transport options as ticket add-ons, ensuring a safe journey to and from the event.

More than just a festival, we are a community-minded, not-for-profit event with a mission to celebrate and support the local seafood industry.

By joining us, you contribute to a cause that gives back to the heart of the local community.

Let's celebrate the bounty of the ocean together!

Get ready for an explosion of colour, music and joy at Horowhenua Holi – Celebration of Colour. Join us on Saturday 21 March, 1pm–5pm at Levin Adventure Park for an afternoon packed with vibrant fun for the whole whānau.

Entry to the festival is free, with colour powder available to purchase on the day, so grab your packets, gather your crew, and get ready to paint the sky in every shade of happiness.

What’s happening on the day

Colour Throws – Countdown together and launch your colours into the air!

Food Stalls and Food Trucks – Tasty bites and sweet treats to keep you fuelled

Music and Dance – High-energy beats and performances to keep you moving

Bring your friends and family and experience the magic of Holi together. Wear white, bring your festive spirit, and get ready to celebrate in a cloud of colour!

Things to know

Wear old white clothing – colours may stain

Choose comfortable, flat shoes you don’t mind getting colourful

Parking is limited – plan ahead where possible

description:
Hutt Japan Day 2025, Hutt Japan Day 2025
Hutt Japan Day is back!
Join us for a vibrant celebration of Japanese culture at the Hutt Japan Day festival, held at the Lower Hutt Town Hall, Dowse Square & Dowse Art Gallery on Sunday, 9 November.

Celebrating 30 Years of Friendship
This year's event is extra special, marking 30 years of partnership with Minoh City, our sister city in Osaka, Japan. The festival is organised by the Hutt Minoh House Friendship Trust, with support from the Hutt City Council and the Embassy of Japan.

What’s on offer?
• Be captivated by an array of Japanese performances and demonstrations
• Engage in hands-on activities and workshops
• Immerse yourself in the exhilarating rhythms of taiko drumming
• Indulge in delectable Japanese cuisine from one of our food vendors/stalls
• Explore our market area for unique Japanese treasures

Get Involved!
To participate in this special celebration as a performer, artist, cultural group, demonstration, market or food vendor, please visit our website for more details and registration forms: https://www.huttminoh.org.nz/participate-in-hutt-japan-day-2025

Save the Date - Sunday, 9 November 2025
Lower Hutt Town Hall, Dowse Square & The Dowse Art Museum

We look forward to celebrating the richness of Japanese culture with you!

description:
Irish Set Dancing - day of dance 2026, Does Irish music get your feet tapping?  This is your opportunity to get up and dance. 
Set dances are the traditional social dances of Ireland, and are so much fun to dance.
 No experience necessary.  Suitable for beginners and experienced alike.   You just need a bit of coordination, a sense of fun, and some energy.  (This is not Irish step dancing, not Riverdance!)
You can come along without a partner, there will always be someone to dance with.
Age 10 upwards.
We recommend smooth soled shoes if you have them.
 Experienced teacher Helen Stonehouse will guide you through the moves and figures.  There are 2 workshops on Saturday and on Saturday evening we have a Ceili when we'll dance some of what you learnt in the workshops plus some more Irish ceili dances.
Anyone is welcome to the Ceili without having been to the workshops.
 Our amazing Round The House Ceili Band will be playing all the jigs and reels and polkas for us throughout the weekend.
 Good music, fun and friends.

description:
Kapiti Tattoo & Arts Festival 2026, Get ready, Kapiti – something bold, creative, and totally unforgettable is coming your way. On Saturday, 7th March 2026, the Kapiti Tattoo & Arts Festival makes its explosive return at the Paraparaumu Memorial Hall, bringing together the ultimate fusion of ink, art, and live entertainment for one epic day of creativity and connection. Whether you're a tattoo enthusiast, an art lover, or someone who thrives in high-energy, artistic environments, this festival is your ticket to something truly extraordinary.

This isn’t just another tattoo expo — it’s a full-blown creative takeover. Expect to see over 40 talented artists under one roof, from the regions leading tattooists to visionary painters, sculptors, illustrators, and local craftspeople. You’ll witness live tattooing, explore interactive art installations, shop handcrafted works, and dive into workshops designed to spark your imagination. Plus, with non-stop local entertainment on the main stage — from musicians to performers and DJs — the atmosphere will be electric from start to finish.

What makes this event truly special? It’s powered by the team at Kapiti Castles — the creative minds behind the popular Kapiti Wedding & Events Expo. Known for producing vibrant, community-driven experiences, Kapiti Castles has crafted this festival as a platform for creative expression, community connection, and artistic inspiration. Whether you're an artist looking to grow your brand or a visitor eager to explore the region’s creative heartbeat, this is your moment.

The Kapiti Tattoo & Arts Festival is more than an event — it’s a movement. It’s a chance to meet incredible artists, get inspired, celebrate culture, and maybe even walk away with some fresh ink. With something for everyone — from art collectors to curious newcomers — this is a must-attend event for 2026.

So mark your calendars for 7th March, gather your crew, and get your tickets now. The Kapiti Tattoo & Arts Festival 2026 is where creativity comes alive, and you won’t want to miss being part of it. Tickets are on sale now — don’t miss your chance to be part of Kapiti’s boldest new festival.

Keep Hush X Twisted Frequency | Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington, Keep Hush X Twisted Frequency | Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington
Twisted Frequency is teaming up with Keep Hush to bring a slice of Aotearoa’s outdoor festival culture into the city and broadcast to the world.

For the uninitiated, Keep Hush started as an intimate underground club night in London and has grown into a global platform celebrating underground dance music through live streams, pop-ups, and parties in unexpected places.

These folks have such a fantastic kaupapa that resonates deeply with what we are doing down here in Aotearoa and we couldn't be more stoked to work with them and share a bit of the Twisted community's creative passion with the world.

Featuring a carefully selected lineup of talent who are dedicated to creating original homegrown tunes, all representing a unique aspect of the country’s bass music melting pot. This will be a journey of sound from dub-infused taonga pūoro to home mulled jungle breaks and all stops between.

description:
Kia Mau, Kia Mau is an arts festival that showcases innovative Indigenous performances. Held every two years, the festival lights up Wellington's winter. See contemporary performances by leading Tāngata Whenua , Tāngata Moana, and global Indigenous artists. The two-week festival includes dance, theatre, music, and visual art. Audiences can expect to be challenged and thrilled by new work from Aotearoa and beyond.
Kia Mau was first held in 2015, founded by two leading Aotearoa creatives. Hone Kouka (Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Kahungunu, Ngāti Raukawa, Kai Tahu) is the Artistic Director and Chief Executive. Mīria George (Ngāti Kearoa, Ngāti Tuara, Ngāti Awa, Ngāti Kūki ‘Āirani) is the Executive Director.
Hone and Mīria describe themselves as innovators. They push boundaries, redefine forms, and forge new paths. They say the festival is not just a platform for presentations, it’s a hub for kōrero and whanaungatanga . The festival has a strong influence on many artists and plays an important role in shaping New Zealand’s contemporary arts scene. “Kia Mau has continued to thrive because of the imagination and commitment of our artists. And of us to them,” says Mīria.

Krakerjack, Krakerjack
Krakerjack is a seven-piece band infusing a Kiwi twist into traditional Polish and klezmer tunes, celebrating these unique cultural traditions by fusing authenticity with innovation. Our pieces showcase soul-stirring vocal harmonies alongside virtuosic instrumentals, poignant ballads and lively dance numbers. We have been gigging since 2022 at various Polish community events, Newtown Festival, Slavfest and have started to perform outside of Wellington, including in Palmerston North at the Festival of Cultures.

LOVE - ALL Colter Carson, LOVE - ALL Colter Carson
Join us on the tennis court for an afternoon of great local drinks, food and a soundtrack provided by Colter Carson

About this Event

Love-All

Join us for the first instalment of our summer series LOVE-ALL

We're opening up centre court to bring you a refined wind-down to your week amongst the gardens. Gather your friends to enjoy a music led Sunday session in the lush surrounds of Barewood. Championing the music you’ve never heard but wish you had, all effortlessly merged together by our carefully selected guests.

Our first Guest selector : Colter Carson (Craiglist/Public Possession)

Colter is a lifelong music lover, DJ/producer and graphic artist living in Ōtautahi/Christchurch. Growing up in a musical household, playing instruments and collecting music from a young age sparked an infectious passion for music and strong desire to share. His productions and DJ approach strike a careful balance between leftfield eclecticism and dancefloor functionality.
In 2024, Colter brought out a self-titled EP as the first release on Eden Burns’ new ‘Big Beat Manifesto’ (a sub-label of Public Possession based in Munich) and performed at TwoMinds festival, Christopher Tubbs’ Body Electric night and Port Noise. He also started a regular Mouthfull radio residency with Max Rodhouse (Rhythmic Ceremonies).

Available on the day:
A wine & beverage list selected and served by local award winning Sommelier Arthur Griffoul of Soif Wine Shop.
Incredible local private chef Mark Wilson Diu will be curtsied serving a reinvention of the sausage sizzle. We’re talking king crab and wild venison.

description:
MATA MATA - Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance, AWAKENING THE TANIWHA, HONOURING THE RECLAMATION. MATA MATA is an offering through the act of solo dance. A summoning of the ancestral spirits that reside deep within the awa. As the taniwha stirs just beneath the surface, memory begins to flow from skin into whenua. Awakening the blood memory that is present here. Becoming a sacred ancestral ritual, allow yourself to slip into this journey of returning. Acknowledging the physical body as a vessel to conjure spirit, mana, and memory. MATA MATA is the honouring of Whakapapa and identity and the holder of space to witness the sacred act of awakening this reclamation.

Presented as part of the Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance 2026.

About the artist:
Harrison Cook is a contemporary dancer, choreographer, and writer of Māori (Kāi Tahu) and Pākehā descent, born and raised on Ngāti Hauā Whenua in the Waikato region of Aotearoa. He is currently based on the lands of the Whadjuk Noongar people in Boorloo (Perth). Harrison is a graduate of the Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts, completing his Bachelor of Arts Dance (2023) and Bachelor of Performing Arts Honours (Awarded a First Class Honours) (2024). During his honours research year, working under the mentorship of Jo Pollitt, he developed and produced his thesis work ’Te Wakahuia: Coming to Know Lineage through Dance Improvisation and Archival Poetics’ which included a body of movement and film work under the name ‘HōtokeWynter ~ ComingToKnow.’ This experience of producing this written and movement practice left Harrison feeling pulled to continue this ongoing artistic enquiry into whakapapa, ancestral memory, and the uncovering of the body as a living archive. His developing choreographic practice centres on research-based improvisation, exploring relationships between land and water, ancestral voice, and embodied lineage. Harrison’s solo work MATA MATA has become a sacred part of his practice and artistic offerings and has been developed and supported through the PILOT Choreographic Program with Enneagon Movement and will premiere as part of The Blue Room Theatre’s 2026 Annual Season through the EVOLVE Program with STRUT Dance. His artistic development has been supported through residencies with The Blue Room Theatre and PICA (Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts), where Harrison was given time and space to continue developing his ongoing practice and project 'THE RETURN'. Through his evolving practice, Harrison continues to explore and understand the connecting to dance becoming a sacred site for remembering, reconnecting, and embodying the stories of our past.

Join us on Saturday 21st March from 10am–3pm for our Harvest Festival - a special launch event in partnership with Upper Hutt Food Week.

HARVEST FESTIVAL ACTIVITIES INCLUDE:
- Local Mangaroa Lunch / BBQ
- Live music & good vibes with Carlos Riegel & Casual Healing
- Garden tours (Very Limited Spaces — Sign Up Now)
- Permaculture Orchard Tours
- Kids Zone with face paint & craft activities
- Local vendors & marketplace
- Coffee cart
- Sheep dog demos
- Sheep shearing

ABOUT FOOD WEEK

Upper Hutt Food Week is coming to life for the first time, 21st–29th March 2026 - a celebration of local food, culture, and community. Think of it like the Upper Hutt Arts Trail, but with kai.

All across the region, organisations, cafés, foodbanks, schools, community groups and marae will be putting on a rich spread of workshops, shared meals, foraging walks and events. We’re proud to be kicking it all off at Mangaroa Farms.

It’s a moment to mark the changing of the seasons, celebrate the harvest, and deepen our connection to kai grown here in Upper Hutt. Whether you’re a grower, a cook, a food lover or just curious, this is your chance to meet others who care about where our food comes from and where it could go next.

Then from 22nd–29th March, Mangaroa will continue to host a range of food-focused workshops and experiences across the week - with some wonderful guest facilitators. Details to come.

Martinborough Music Festival 2025, Bringing the world to Martinborough for chamber music in the heart of South Wairarapa.

Join us for four exciting concerts over three days, featuring stunning New Zealand and international artists including Natalia Lomeiko (violin), Yuri Zhislin (violin/viola), Matthias Balzat and Ashley Brown (cello), Jian Liu (piano), Wilma Smith and Donald Armstrong (violin), Simon Brew (saxophone) and Caroline Henbest (viola).

These artists will bring to life extraordinary works including Zoltán Kodály's Duo for Violin and Cello, Op. 7; JS Bach's Goldberg Variations for string trio; Shostakovich's Piano Quintet in G minor, Op. 57 and Mozart's String Quintet No. 5 in D major, K.593.

The Sunday afternoon concert will also include the world premiere of Shifting Worlds, a piano quintet by renowned New Zealand composer Louise Webster, who has special ties with South Wairarapa.

Visit martinboroughmusicfestival.co.nz for more information about artists, programmes and links to ticket sales.

Matariki herenga waka – for all of us.

Kia ora Paetūmōkai whānau, Wairarapa Moana communities. and manuhiri, it's time for us to start planning our Matariki celebrations again.

Soon we will put the call out; for those of you who are storytellers, pumpkin choppers, kawakawa gatherers, kaumatua and kuia chauffeurs, chair putter-outers, table decorators, steam pudding makers, sweepers, child wranglers, photographers, leftover hangi dispersers, fairy light arrangers; our small town makes wonderful things happen when we gather together. If you have helped before, thank you, and if you can help again- thank you- but if you need to rest, we understand. If you haven't helped before- nau mai, haere mai, welcome- and in advance, thank you!

This year’s theme of "Matariki herenga waka" is all about inclusion, and encouraging ALL people to celebrate Matariki together. The theme has strong connections to multi-culturalism and the sharing of cultural practices; we can ALL connect to the core values of Matariki and embrace the celebration of the holiday.

The Māori New Year is a time of reflection, celebration, and preparation. It is a time to remember loved ones, come together with whānau to give thanks to what we have and look forward to the promise of a new year.

In the meantime; here's a new Matariki waiata to get your heart singing. Don't worry, there'll still be the Matariki Macarena!

🦇A Day of Decadence, Darkness and Delights 🕷️

Join us from midday until the shadows stretch long, as Brewtown transforms into a haunted haven of unholy delights for NZ Brewers Fest 2025 – Monster Mash!

🍻Fiendishly good Beer!
It wouldn’t be NZBF without great beer, and this year 20 of Aotearoa’s best breweries will descend on Brewtown to pour every style you could possibly desire, from crisp Lagers, cold IPAs and hoppy Pale Ales, to funky Sours, smoky Porters, rich Pastry Stouts – and everything in between!

Visit Brewtown’s own custom Unimog Bar for 13 beers handpicked by our craft beer experts, but get in quick – we only have 1 keg of each, and they won’t last long!

🍸Haunting Spirits & Wine!
New for this year! Step into our haunted cocktail bar for some seriously spooky spirits! Our mixologists have been hard at work creating some devilishly delicious drops just for you.

We’re bringing in some of the best wines the Wairarapa has to offer, so whether you prefer a crisp Sauv, a fruity Pinot or a refreshing Frosé there will be something to enjoy.

Still not enough for you? Then head down to the Everything Else Bar, for NZ crafted ciders, as well as bourbon, rum, gin and vodka alongside a range of low and no alcohol beers, cocktails and soft drinks.

🌮Monstrously Good Kai!
The NZBF food court hosts the region’s top foodies, bringing you big, bold, flavour-packed festival eats that’ll satisfy both the living and the undead.
Watch this space as we announce our festive foodie lineup!

⚔️Enthralling Entertainment!
Lose yourself in a cabaret of the bizarre, where the performances are as dark as they are dazzling. Expect sultry burlesque, twisted characters and moments that will thrill, chill, and have you begging for more.

Witness the brutal thrill of buhurt armoured combat, as warriors face off in full medieval kit in a raw display of might and mayhem.

Dance the day away at the main stage, as Welly’s top talent smash out tune after tune, all building up to a headline show from Brewtown favourites, The Blueprint – as they bring a special set just for Monster Mash! Trust us, you haven’t seen them like this before…

Grab your mates and get stuck in at the Games Zone, where a bit of friendly rivalry meets festive fun, and the loser buys the next round.

Enjoy dressing up? Go all out in your most terrifying, theatrical or jaw-dropping costume — and you might just take out the crown in our epic Best Dressed Competition, with spooky-good prizes up for grabs.

With affordable return coaches from Welly and Petone and great discounts for group tickets it's scarily easy to get involved!

description:
NZCFS Wellington Branch October Meeting: Mooncake Making, The Mid-Autumn Festival (simplified Chinese: 中秋节; traditional Chinese: 中秋節), also known as Moon Festival or Mooncake Festival, is a traditional festival celebrated by Chinese people and also other East and Southeast Asian people. It is the second-most important holiday after Chinese New Year with a history dating back 3,000 years.
The festival is held on the 15th day of the 8th month of the Chinese luni-solar calen-dar with a full moon at night. On this day, the moon is at its brightest and fullest size, coinciding with harvest time in the middle of Autumn. This year, the Moon Festival is on 6 October. We will be making mooncakes at our October monthly meet-ing to celebrate this festival.
Our secretary Vera will demonstrate the flaky Suzhou-style savoury mooncake with pork. We will also make some sweet ones using redbean paste filling.
If you are coming to the session, please bring $5.00 entry fee, a plate and cutlery for the mooncake tasting.

description:
National Celebration - 40 Years of Homosexual Law Reform, National Celebration - 40 Years of Homosexual Law Reform
40 Years of Homosexual Law Reform – Community Celebration at Parliament

Join us in the historic Banquet Hall at Parliament as we come together to celebrate 40 years since the passing of the Homosexual Law Reform Act — a landmark moment that helped transform Aotearoa New Zealand into a more inclusive and just society.

This special evening will honour the courage, determination, and advocacy of those who fought for equality, while celebrating the vibrant and diverse rainbow communities who continue that legacy today.

The programme will feature speeches from past and present activists, sharing reflections on the movement, the challenges faced, and the progress achieved over four decades. Guests will also enjoy performances from talented members of the community, bringing music, storytelling, and creative expression to the celebration.

More than a commemoration, this event is also an opportunity to connect across generations of the rainbow community and allies. Join activists, community leaders, supporters, and friends for an evening of reflection, celebration, and whakawhanaungatanga in one of the country’s most significant civic spaces.

Together, we honour the past, celebrate the present, and look toward a future where equality and inclusion continue to grow.

Open Air are excited to return to a day/night adventure at the weird and wonderful Carlucci Land in Happy Valley.

We are planning a fully immersive production again with an amazing range of artists.

3-430pm K-oTik
430-6pm NotMySister
6-730pm Everybody
730-9pm Donna-Marie
9-1030pm Greg Churchill
1030-12am Takas


2nd Stage to be announced soon!


Our friends from Cosa Nostra food truck will be back serving fresh pizzas and also have a range of soft drinks available.

We will not be offering ticket refunds or swaps for this event, if you can no longer make the event, you can on-sell your own ticket - buyers please be sure about who you are buying from as there are lots of scammers around!


Consent is always required at any event to ensure that everyone is kept safe and boundaries are not crossed. Please ask before any hugging, touching of any sort, taking photos, etc. We operate a zero-tolerance policy to bad behaviour. If you see something that doesn’t seem right, you have a responsibility to do something. And remember, if it’s not an enthusiastic YES then it’s a NO.


Open Air reserve all rights and have a zero-tolerance approach.

description:
PA2026 Opening Night, Haerenga Moana: voyages of separation, transformation, reconnection
You’re warmly invited to open The Performance Arcade 2026 with us on Wednesday 25 February, 6.00pm, on Wellington Waterfront behind Te Papa.
Now in its 16th year, Performance Arcade returns as a free gathering where performance art, live music, movement, sound, and video converge within a temporary architecture of shipping container. This vibrant site is a waka activated by more than 40 artists.
Opening night is a moment to pause before the rush: to acknowledge the artists, the journeys they carry, and the shared waters we’re about to enter together for our 2026 kaupapa - Haerenga Moana: journeys of separation, transformation, reconnection.
Join us to welcome the festival, feel the mauri of the site, and begin this voyage in good company.
Meet us at the DVB Music Stage, between Te Papa and Chaffers Marina.
Music on opening night includes Te Kahureremoa, Jitsvinger (from South Africa), Riki Gooch Pirihi, with UMU closing the evening.
Everyone is welcome—please bring your whānau and friends.
Programme available here:
https://www.theperformancearcade.com/programme

description:
POP Go the Festival Singers: Island Bay Presbyterian Church, POP Go the Festival Singers: Island Bay Presbyterian Church
The Festival Singers invite you to a enjoy unforgettable music in POP go the Festival Singers – a dazzling celebration of popular songs from the 1920s right through to today.

Expect energy, variety, and entertainment as we journey through swing, rock ’n’ roll, Motown, disco, soft rock, and contemporary pop.

The programme sparkles with classics and favourites: a Beach Boys Medley full of surfside sunshine, Ruru Karaitiana’s iconic Blue Smoke, Elvis Presley’s Hound Dog, and Bobby Darin’s Beyond the Sea.

We’ll groove with Pharrell Williams’ Happy, cheer to Survivor’s Eye of the Tiger, and celebrate Kiwi pride in Crowded House’s Weather with You.

Heartfelt beauty shines through Simon and Garfunkel’s Bridge Over Troubled Water and Billy Joel’s And So It Goes, while fun abounds with The Lion Sleeps Tonight and Gershwin’s sultry Summertime.

Swing makes its mark with Glenn Miller’s Chattanooga Choo Choo and In the Mood. We also sing rousing medleys of songs by Queen and ABBA.

Along the way, enjoy contemporary sparkle with Dua Lipa’s Levitating and the timeless artistry of these unforgettable hits.

With the incomparable Jonathan Berkahn at the piano, every piece shines with character and style.

This concert promises nostalgia, joy, and toe-tapping fun – a true trip down memory lane with something for everyone.

Join us and be part of a celebration of music that entertains, connects, and uplifts.

Book here:
https://events.humanitix.com/pop-go-the-festival-singers-island-bay-presbyterian-church

Our kaupapa:
Paekākāriki Pride exists to support Takatāpui and Rainbow communities in the Kāpiti Region and beyond.
We firmly hold the position that trans women are women and trans men are men, and that non-binary identities are valid. We recognise the harm caused by colonisation to Takatāpui communities. As an organisation we work to become better Treaty Partners
