description:
Prophetiae Sibyllarum [Paraparaumu], Prophetiae Sibyllarum [Paraparaumu]
The Tudor Consort celebrates its 40th birthday in 2026 and we have an incredible season planned to celebrate. Collaborations with five different ensembles, a debut in Auckland, three premiere performances, and of course a performance of Thomas Tallis’ 40 part masterpiece Spem in alium. Make sure you visit our website to get all the details and secure your tickets!



We will be taking part in our third Aotearoa Festival of the Arts with SoundCathedral on Sunday March 1, an incredible re-composition of Orlande de Lassus’ Prophetiae Sibyllarum by Michael Norris, written especially for our anniversary and the 25th birthday of Stroma contemporary music ensemble. We celebrate going ‘over the hill’ in style in our May 2 concert XL, featuring two 40 part works by Tallis and Mäntyjärvi. We have two concerts with our friends Orchestra Wellington - Leonard Bernstein’s energetic Chichester Psalms as part of W:Ellington on 30 May, and Victoria Kelly’s brand new opera Ocean on 28 November. A debut in Auckland with NZ Barok sees us performing Lotti and Handel, and we finish the year with Messiah with Australian virtuoso harpsichordist and director Erin Helyard.




This is one of the most exciting seasons in our history, and I hope very much you can join us as we celebrate!

description:
Puku Rangi Tea – Rapa Nui Music & Dance Tour in Marlborough, Experience the vibrant culture of Easter Island as Puku Rangi Tea tours for the first time in Marlborough to closing the Welcoming Week Celebration!
Since 2012, they have been dedicated to preserving and showcasing traditional Rapa Nui music and dance. Their vibrant performances include the Hoko warrior dance, resonating with the spirit of the Māori Haka, storytelling through Takona body painting and ancestral narratives, Kai Kai string games and the rhythmic sounds of Tahitian ukulele and drums.
Puku Rangi Tea currently performs three shows a week at the Tahatai Hotel in Hanga Roa, Rapa Nui, and has participated in various festivals throughout its history, including:
Indigenous festival 2023–2024, San Juan de la Costa, Chile.
World Gathering of Folkloric Associations 2020, Lima, Peru.
International Festival 2018–2019, Málaga, Spain.
Chapultepec Forest Festival 2018, Mexico City, Mexico.
Second Workshop on Rapa Nui Music and Dance 2018, Mexico City, Mexico.
Rapa Nui Dance and Music Show 2018, Mexico City and Morelia, Michoacán, Mexico.
First Workshop on Rapa Nui Music and Dance 2017, Mexico City, Mexico.
Rapa Nui Dance and Music Show 2017, Mexico City, Mexico.
Indigenous festival 2016–2020, San Juan de la Costa, Chile.
Cultural Market 2017, Mexico City, Mexico.
12th Pacific Arts Festival 2016, Hagåtña, Guam.
Carnaval 2016, Arica, Chile.
Summer Festival 2016, Valdivia, Chile.
Oktoberfest Chile 2015–2017, Malloco, Chile.
Gala Puro Chile 2015, Miami, United States.
The tour holds significant cultural importance due to Rapa Nui deep ancestral connections with Aotearoa, offering a unique opportunity for cultural engagement and community connection.
Their itinerary includes high-profile engagements, such as:
Music Workshop on Friday 12 at 4pm - Koha Entry - RSVP Required
Dance Workshop on Friday 12 at 6pm - Koha Entry - RSVP Required
Concert: Live music and dances on Sunday 14 Spetember. Doors open at 3:30pm, Event start at 4pm
Koha - Entry - RSVP Required (Limited Capacity)
We are also excited to feature the local guest band "Matices", who will open the concert with a vibrant performance of live Andean and Latin American music.

description:
Rathkeale Christmas Fete 2025, Welcome to the Rathkeale Christmas Fête 2025! Walk through the gates of Rathkeale College on 1st November and be welcomed by a diverse range of colourful stalls, the aroma of freshy cooked food and plenty of festive inspiration.

Now in its 22nd year, the Christmas Fête has become a must-do event on the Wairarapa spring calendar. Stallholders travel from around the North Island to sell their wares and offer Christmas shoppers loads of inspiration. From festive decorations, clothing, arts and crafts, to flowers, toys and plants – there is something for everyone.

Gourmet food is always a highlight at the Fête - think freshly made gourmet burgers, lamb & mint sausages, wraps, curry, salads, and the ever-popular berries & ice-cream - there is always a huge variety of flavours to tempt the taste buds. Devonshire Teas and home baking served in the Rathkeale Homestead rose garden is a time-honoured tradition while refreshing cold drinks can be sipped on as visitors listen to live music performed by students at various times throughout the day. The popular Christmas cake stall features again this year - but visitors are encouraged to get in early as the cakes often sell out by midday.

The beauty of this Fête is that it’s a day out for the whole family. In addition to the 120 plus stalls, there is plenty to entertain the children including facepainting and magic shows throughout the day.

Visitors can also explore the beautiful, expansive grounds of Rathkeale College including the school gardens designed by Alfred Buxton, the Greek Amphitheatre and the 3km eco-trail which weaves through large stands of native trees, including ancient kahikatea.

Eftpos is available, but we strongly recommend that visitors bring cash.

Koha/gold coin entry.
Rathkeale College is a five-minute drive north of Masterton in the Wairarapa.
label: Festivals

description:
Rathkeale College Christmas Fête 2025, Rathkeale College Christmas Fête 2025
Welcome to the Rathkeale Christmas Fête 2025!
Now in its 22nd year, the Fête offers shoppers loads of inspiration. Stallholders will be selling festive decorations, clothing, arts and crafts, as well as flowers, toys and plants – there is something for everyone.
Gourmet food is also a highlight – with freshly made gourmet burgers, lamb & mint sausages, wraps, curry, salads, and the ever-popular berries and icecream available for purchase. Devonshire Tea served in the Rathkeale Homestead rose garden is a time-honoured tradition while refreshing cold drinks can be sipped on as visitors listen to live music performed by students at various times throughout the day. description:
Resonant Rave, ✨ A Night for the High Vibe Dancers ✨
Love the energy of a club night — the music, the lights, the freedom — but not the hangover?
Craving that connected dance floor feeling… completely sober?
Welcome to our Resonant Rave — where we get high on music, movement, and community. 🪩💫
No booze required — just pure vibes, connection, and the freedom to be fully you.
Whether you’re sober, sober-curious, or simply want to experience dance in a new, elevated way — this night is for you.
Come dance. Come connect. Come as you are.
Expect bass-laden melodic grooves, warm smiles, and the kind of connection that happens when everyone’s really there.
Move sober. Dance deeper.
Let the resonance move through you.
🎧 With special guest DJ:
SORCHALULA
Mysterious, mercurial and multi-faceted. SorchaLula has as many shades to her music as she does to her personality. A dynamic producer/DJ, she flows from slinky sensuality, to fierce filth, to the uncompromising underground. Every set features her original tracks, many melting with honeyed vocals by singer Samuel (Cecilia’s Crop). In tune with what the body needs, she entwines beauty with bravery, sinuous melodies with hefty bass, lush peaks with decadent darkness.
She has played many top festivals around Aotearoa: Northern Bass, Shipwrecked Festival, Twisted Frequency, Aum Festival NYE, CubaDupa, Taniwha’s Den and more. She is highly rated by some of the biggest names in the scene for her taste, depth, and intuitive understanding of dancefloors. As founder of The Sensonauts she created events exploring the senses, music, dance, and music education with a focus on inclusivity.
Link to music
https://soundcloud.com/sorchalula
🪩
🎧 As well as:
KIMBA JADE
Kimba Jade has been lighting up dancefloors for over 20 years with her signature blend of deep, funky, and globally inspired grooves. A master of musical journeying, Kimba weaves bass-driven beats with tribal, melodic, and soulful sounds that move both body and spirit.
With a deep passion for Ecstatic Dance and the power of music to connect and uplift, Kimba brings that same vibrant, heart-opening energy into clubs and bars. Her favourite styles to play are Tech House infused with Indie Dance and Techno, blending rhythms with emotive melodies to create a sound that’s both driving and deeply immersive.
After years of spinning in Sydney and Auckland’s underground scene — from conscious dance floors to late-night sessions — Kimba is now based in Wellington, bringing her signature fusion of rhythm, soul, and bass to local venues. Whether behind the decks at a festival, Ecstatic Dance, or a packed club night, Kimba’s passion is the same: to create an unforgettable atmosphere where freedom, rhythm, and connection collide.
Link to music
https://soundcloud.com/kimba
@djkimbajade
🪩

SGCNZ VUW Wellington Regional Shakespeare Festival, Shakespeare Globe Centre New Zealand Regional Shakespeare Festival Wellington is one of 24 similar regional events across New Zealand. These Regional Festivals involve more than half the secondary schools, home schoolers and community youth drama groups in the country. During these Festivals, students perform their reimagining of Shakespeare's plays, in their 5-minute and 15-minute scenes, between late March and the end of Term 1. A Group from both categories from each region is selected from these to go on to participate in the National Festival over King's Birthday weekend in Wellington.

The Festival provides a wonderfully eclectic mélange of the creativity of the imaginative rangatahi of New Zealand. A large percentage of the scenes are student-directed. Come and see the way they relish explore and present the Bard's works!

Salsa Magic’s Friday Fiesta - Palladium Edition, Salsa Magic’s Friday Fiesta - Palladium Edition
Join us for another fun night of social dancing with DJ Rafa, playing the grooviest Mambo, Salsa, and Bachata tracks! Emphasis on the MAMBO 💃

Tonight we celebrate the Palladium era of Latin dance! Known as “the home of the Mambo,” the Palladium Ballroom was America’s most important venue for the development of Latin music and dance throughout the 1950s.

Mambo music and dance were co-created at the Palladium where Puerto Rican, Cuban, Dominican, Italian, Jewish, Irish, and African American patrons danced nightly to music from the “Big Three” Latin orchestras: Tito Puente, Tito Rodríguez, and Machito.

You can expect lots of Mambo and all-around good vibes!

description:
Slow Grind Fever [AUS] - Wellington Jazz Festival, Express from Melbourne, Australia and crossing international waters for the first time this October, Meow is excited to welcome the slowest, spookiest, smokiest and swingin-est club night Wellington has ever seen: 'Slow Grind Fever'.
For this one-night-only episode of SGF Wellington, founder Richie1250 (106.7 PBS FM) will be joined by fellow Melbourne radio alumnus Dr. Popalotacorn (RRR, 98.1FM Raglan) and Wellington's own belle of the airwaves Miss Juliet (RadioActive.FM Americana)
Slow Grind Fever was born in 2012 when Richie1250 hired a Russian Cultural Centre ballroom and threw a slow dance party for his 30th birthday, and it's been running as a regular monthly club night ever since. Richie and his friends play the slowest, sleaziest, spookiest, sweetest, swinginest old records they can find, and people dance real slow in a haze of smoke and dim red light. It's a good time.
In the last few years Richie has taken Slow Grind Fever on the road, with regular dances in Sydney, Hobart, Darwin and Alice Springs. They post up a monthly Slow Grind Fever mix in the week before the party every month, and have collaborated with Stag-O Lee Records in Germany on a series of Slow Grind Fever LPs and CDs.
Enjoy the music and if you feel so inclined, get down to Slow Grind Fever - Wellington at Meow on Friday 17th October.
Listening to the MP3 mixes is nice, but when you’re in the room all
wrapped up in smoke with the music sizzling right off the old records, through the speakers and into your brain, well, there's nothing quite like it…
http://www.slowgrindfever.com/
https://www.instagram.com/slowgrindfeverclub

Are you ready to take a walk on the wild side? Be a rebel with a cause?

Join Ronald McDonald House Charities® New Zealand (RMHC® NZ) and Te Nukuao Wellington Zoo for our joint fundraiser, 'Soirée at the Zoo: A night for our families and animals.’ RMHC NZ and Wellington Zoo have a long history of working together in the community. We wanted to secure the future of the work we do by hosting this fundraiser, as we approach nearly a decade of partnership.

We are excited to bring you an epic night of glitz, good vibes and an action-packed live auction with some fabulous prizes, all to raise much-needed funds for RMHC NZ and Wellington Zoo. 🌟✨

📅 Date: 22 November 2025
🕕 Time: 6.30pm – 11.00pm
📍 Location: Wellington Zoo, 200 Daniell Street, Newtown, Wellington 6021

🎟️ BUY TICKETS NOW to secure your spot and get ready to:
• Explore the zoo after hours
• Enjoy delicious canapés with a complimentary welcome drink
• Feel the electric excitement of the live auction and raffle
• Let your hair down and hit the dance floor with some choice local music
• Mix and mingle with your friends and some familiar Wellingtonian faces
• Be captivated by the journey of a local RMHC NZ whānau and Wellington Zoo
• And much more!
By attending our Soirée, you'll be making a real difference as all proceeds raised will be shared equally between RMHC NZ and Wellington Zoo.

🏡 Every day, RMHC NZ provides families with a child in hospital a ‘home-away-from-home'. RMHC NZ supports over 4,400 Kiwi families every year, keeping them together during their toughest times.

Te Nukuao Wellington Zoo welcomes families using RMHC NZ services to the Zoo for free, through our community partnership. Each year, over 400 adults and kids come to spend time with animals in nature. The zoo is a place of healing for over 250,000 people each year, including whānau from RMHC NZ.

Get ready for an unforgettable evening that makes a real impact! With only 150 tickets available, make sure you seize the day and secure yours!

We can’t wait to see you there!

St Patrick's Festival on the Waterfront, St Patrick's Festival on the Waterfront
The St Patrick's Festival on the Waterfront Parade and Concert is back for 2026! Come and join the Irish Communities of Te Whanganui-a-Tara on Sunday 15th March, and invite your family and friends. Everyone is welcome.

This year the parade starts from Te Papa. Paddy McCann will be there from 12noon to get everyone's toes tapping to Irish music until St Patrick and St Brigid lead the Parade along the waterfront. As always everyone is welcome to walk alongside the county flag that is special for them.

Be under the sails at Queen's Wharf for the concert from 1:30-4:30pm. This year's entertaiment includes music from Crossroads, Sláinte, Hutt Valley Children's Singers, and dancing from Gregan Irish Dancers, Kerry School of Irish Dancing and the Ryan-Dorris School of Dancing.

Come prepared to join in the craic. The ceílí is back, along with the crowd choir, and who will be this year's best dressed in green? There'll be face painting, art and crafts, storytelling and icecream for the kids. The GAA will be back on the sausage sizzle so bring some cash.

This year, we end the day with a special prize draw and make sure you're there to lift the sails with everyone joining in Fields of Athenry.

Street Eats and Beats, Masterton Street Eats & Beats

Formerly known as Thursday Night Food Trucks, Masterton Street Eats & Beats is Masterton's favourite weekly food truck and community event, bringing together great food, live music, and a relaxed family-friendly atmosphere every Thursday evening.

With a rotating lineup of food trucks and street food vendors, no two weeks are ever quite the same. From gourmet burgers and international cuisine to sweet treats, coffee, and local favourites, there's something to satisfy every craving. Add live music, plenty of seating, and a welcoming community vibe, and you've got the perfect way to kick off your weekend early.

Whether you're catching up with friends, bringing the family out for dinner, or simply looking for an easy meal after work, Masterton Street Eats & Beats offers a fun and affordable night out for all ages.

Event Details
Every Thursday
4:30pm – 7:00pm (rain or shine)
Outside the Masterton Club, Chapel Street (SH2), Masterton
Free Entry

What to Expect
• rotating food and beverage vendors throughout the season
• Live music and entertainment
• Family-friendly atmosphere
• outdoor seating available or bring a picnic blanket
• New vendors regularly joining the lineup
• EFTPOS and cash accepted by most vendors

Food truck and street food vendors are always welcome to enquire about joining the event.

Come hungry, bring your friends, and enjoy one of the Wairarapa's favourite weekly community gatherings.

description:
Summer Camp Launch Party | Half Angel and King Hit , San Fran Summer Camp is back for 2026!
Join us and some of Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s finest artists over five nights across January and February with tickets from $10 or a season pass for $40, featuring drink specials and cocktails thanks to our sponsor Jameson.

Start your new year off right with two of this city's premier alternative acts! 

Half/Angel toe the line of alt-rock, post punk & ambient psychedelia. They unpredictably juxtapose intimate, soft, vocals and delicate instrumental passages with raucous, high-energy outbursts. They’re exciting to listen to, and their singles ‘Debt Collector’ & ‘Boat Ramp + Jitterbug’ will have you struggling to put them in a box and itching to hear what’s next.
New noise in the scene, King Hit, is a Te Whanganui A Tara based four piece that blends together the jarring-ness of shoe-gaze, the punch of hardcore, with the sombreness of midwest emo. After a successful release of their debut single ‘asterisk’, King Hit are poised to release their follow up single ‘Sap’, an grungy-yet-ethereal longing love song.

description:
Summer Camp | Sam Fowles and Elly Mae , San Fran Summer Camp is back for 2026!

Join us and some of Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s finest artists over five nights across January and February with tickets from $10 or a season pass for $40, featuring drink specials and cocktails thanks to our sponsor Jameson.

Our penultimate night features two of Pōneke’s finest songwriters from two separate sonic worlds… their combination is sure to be a treat!

Sam Fowles makes music that moves the body, speaks to the heart, and touches the soul. Driven by groove and the desire to find meaning in the moments on this journey we call life, the musician, songwriter and producer has a signature sound that stands out and stuns. Fowles would describe his music as psychedelic soul laced with blues and funk. It resonates with deep grooves and driving rhythms created by vintage drum sounds, digital sonics, and electric guitars that build and blaze into billowing soundscapes. At its core is his unique, soulful voice and the punchy, heartfelt lyrics he wears on his sleeve.

Elly Mae crafts songs that encapsulate the bittersweet ache of growth, the quiet unraveling of time, and the soft glow of nostalgia embedded within. Her music is an amalgamation of folk, dreampop, indie, shoegaze, and anything in between. From lullabies that make you feel weightless to being wrapped in a blanket of sound, Elly Mae's folk/country melodic guitar style is accompanied by experimental, spatial bass from Arran Cargill-Brown and textured pocket drumming from Sasha Francis-Murray. 


San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

description:
THREE JOYFUL HOUSES - AOTEAROA FESTIVAL OF ARCHITECTURE - SUNDAY 28TH SEPTEMBER, THREE JOYFUL HOUSES by IAN ATHFIELD
SUNDAY 28TH SEPTEMBER @ FUTUNA CHAPEL - KARORI
Three joyful houses, three families and three client stories about the commissioning, designing, building and living in homes designed by Ian Athfield.
SPENCER and DIANE LOGAN
1974 - 1978
WINDY POINT – EASTBOURNE
Photographer unknown
Spencer Logan and his wife Diane will talk about the commissioning of their first new home, its design, construction, the cleaning of thousands of bricks, and living in this unique collection of a pair of recycled brick towers with timber clad ‘saddlebags’. 
ROSS, CUSHLA and TESS JAMIESON
1974 - 1978
MAHINA BAY
Ross and Cushla have lived in their home on the Eastern hills above Mahina Bay for 48 years. They will, along with their youngest daughter, recount their experiences of working with Ian Athfield in the commissioning of the design of their home, the construction process and then living in this hillside hugging collection of building, and how this home may have influenced their living and the raising of a family of four children.
JONATHAN CUSTANCE   - THE CUSTANCE HOUSE 1981 – 1982
HAVELOCK NORTH
“The Custance House replaced an early modern home that burnt to the ground in 1981 leaving only the swimming pool unscathed.  Ray and Ann Custance, who were friends of the Athfields, sought a bold replacement.  With their son, industrial and interior designer Jonathan Custance, they prepared a four page brief for a new building….. “
Text taken from Athfield Architects by Julia Gatley 2012 AUP.
The Trust looks forward to welcoming architects, designers, graduates, students and interested members of the public to attend this event and support the Trust in its work.
The Futuna Trust is a charitable organisation and all funds raised from the Futuna Lecture Series go towards the ongoing care, maintenance and operation of Futuna Chapel and also to support various initiatives undertaken by the Trust.

There will be 15 Design CPD points available for NZ registered architects attending the event. Please include your NZRAB registration number when registering for Architect tickets

Our mates from RNZPBA Wellington Hawkes Bay are back to curate their all-new take on traditional pipe and drum comps with some of the finest musicians in the country.

Join us on The Greenspace for our very own family friendly, FREE to attend salute to those earth-shaking instruments of war (literally) and all things Highlands and Islands!

It won’t just be Pipers and Drummers competing for glory. Brewtown is delighted to welcome some bonnie boogying in the form of Scottish Highland Dancing, as dancers from up and down the country wow the crowd with traditional dance.

So, get behind these incredible young athletes and show your support at this years Tartan Up The Green!

The Daffodil Express, The Daffodil Express
All aboard for one of Steam Incorporated’s most popular events of the year!

Join us on our annual Daffodil Express — a special heritage train journey to Carterton’s much‑loved Daffodil Festival in the heart of the Wairarapa.

Travel in vintage style behind our beautifully restored locomotives and carriages, with convenient boarding available at Wellington, Petone, Waterloo and Upper Hutt.

Sit back and enjoy the journey as we leave the city behind, race through the Hutt Valley suburbs, head through to the Wairarapa — including the famous 8.8km tunnel, one of the longest on New Zealand’s passenger network.

Once in Carterton, you’ll have time to explore everything the festival has to offer, including stunning daffodil fields at Middle Run Farm, bustling street markets and artisan stalls, live music and entertainment, food, crafts, and family-friendly fun.

After a relaxing few hours, simply hop back onboard for the return journey — no traffic, no parking hassles — just a great day out by rail.

Make it a day to remember — gather your friends and family and experience this iconic Wairarapa tradition the best way possible: with Steam Incorporated.

Details to follow closer to time, but already got a few new ideas for the 2026 edition.

Description from Inaugural 2025 Edition FYI:

I would like to acknowledge the support of The Island Bay Festival, which will be celebrating its 40th year of bringing the community together this year, and thank them for giving me a space in The Park this Sunday at The Day in The Bay to showcase and celebrate The Italians of Island Bay, their history and their contributiion to the community, business and culture.

#supportlocal
#celebratelocal
#celebratecommunity
#islandbayfestival

The majority of Island Bay Italians are Neapolitan from the hill top town of Massa Lubrense and surrounds on the Sorrentine Peninsula, followed by Sicilians from the small volcanic island of Stromboli in the Aeolean sea.

When you think of The Italians of Island Bay you might think of their involvement and contribution to the Fishing and Food (and related) Industries, but it goes much wider than that..

Books that will on display:

- Alle Fine del Mondo by Paul Elenio
- Le Famiglie Strombolani by
- Food & Family by
- Family Business by Vincent Moleta
- Angelina by Gerard Hindmarsh
- Unsheltered by Clare Moleta
- Umberto Saba : poetry & prose selected & translated, with notes by Vincent Moleta

Just a few days to go till the big Day in the Bay on Sunday. I'm unexpectedly in Perth for family reasons, so have had to piece this together organically long distance, with the help and contribution of my mum's childhood girlfriends from The Bay, for which I'm extremely greatfull.

My Back-Story:

On my mother's side I'm double 4th generation Strombolana-Kiwi and 2nd generation Dutch-Kiwi on my father's side (RIP).. thus my long and unusual name..

Rosina Maria Giuseppina van der Aa.

All 4 of my biz-nonni (great grandparents) bravely sailed to the ends of the earth (alle fine del mondo) in search of a better future.

My maternal great grandfather (Bartolo Barnao) and his elder brother(Giuseppe) initially fished and slept under their fishing boat in Makara, before returning with their Strombolane wives who were also siblings (Giuseppina and Maria Concetta Pirera) to set up shop literally (a fish shop) in Palmerston North before then moving to No 64 The Parade Island Bay when my Nonna Rosina was 17 circa 1934.

My paternal great grandparents (Angelina Criscillo and Vincenzo Moleta) along with Vincenzo's brother (Antonino) and Angelina's cousin (Rosa) settled and tamed D'urville. My Nonno (Leslie George Moleta) spotted my Nonna (Rosina Elvira Barnao) at the Zino-Toscano wedding where she was a bridesmaid. They had two children, both named after their grandparents as was the tradition. My uncle Vincent Bartolo and my mother Maria Josephine The rest as they say is Family Business..

The Most Wuthering Heights Day Ever Pōneke - 2026, Put your red dress on and join us for The Most Wuthering Heights Day Ever Pōneke!�
A joyful community recreation of Kate Bush’s iconic Wuthering Heights dance.
Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui (Wellington Central Library)
Sunday 26 July 2026
2pm–3pm
Whether you’re a lifelong Kate Bush fan or you’ve never danced a step in your life, you’re welcome.
This wonderfully dramatic, low-pressure community event brings people together to dress in red, learn a few simple moves and recreate Kate Bush’s iconic dance together, find joy, and bring some light to the dark days of winter!
No dance experience required. Participation over perfection is very much the vibe.
WHAT TO EXPECT
• Optional community workshops in the lead-up (stay tuned for more info!)
• A couple of practice run-throughs on the day
• One gloriously dramatic group performance
• Lots of laughter, connection, and mid-winter joy
The Most Wuthering Heights Day Ever! all started back in 2013 in Brighton, UK, by the awesome @shambushevents. It has since become a worldwide phenomenon, with thousands of people in cities around the globe donning red dresses and dancing together.
Last seen in Pōneke in 2016, we’re bringing it back!
So grab your red dress, gather your friends, and come join the joy this July.

#themostwutheringheightsdayeverpōneke #wutheringheights

The New Zealand Stationery Festival, Join us in beautiful Greytown for the first New Zealand Stationery Festival, a boutique celebration of the love of pen and paper!

Opening in our historic Town Hall, this is your chance to explore an inspiring collection of premium international stationery brands, along with handpicked local makers, all under one roof. Featured brands include ArtGecko, A. T. Cross, Esterbrook, Ferris Wheel Press, Lamy, Letts of London, MD Paper, Milan, Moleskine, The Superior Labor, Traveler’s Company, and many more.

From 10 am to 2 pm: Exclusive access for ticket holders to the show, with first-in-line chance to purchase products and take advantage of show special offers. Plus ticket holders also receive a collectable NZ Stationery Festival AS Colour tote bag; this one is going to be very sought-after!

From 11 am to 2 pm: Access for door sales, as capacity allows.

Between 2pm and 4pm: Festival opens for free public access (no entry fee, no totes).

Throughout the day, join creative workshops designed to spark ideas, improve your skills and deepen your love of stationery and creative journaling. See below for a summary of our creative workshops.

The New Zealand Stationery Festival will be intentionally intimate to fit within our wee town; a small but perfectly formed gathering focused on beautiful paper goods, pens, inks, journaling and creative tools, and the wonderful people who enjoy them.

Just an hour from Wellington, Greytown’s charm makes it the perfect setting for a day with your fellow ink lovers, journalers and stationery enthusiasts. Join us for New Zealand’s inaugural biggest little stationery festival!

The New Zealand Stationery Festival 2026
Saturday 10 January 2026, 10 am - 4 pm
Greytown Town Hall, 89 Main Street, Greytown
Creative Workshops:
11am - 11:30am: What the Washi? Introduction to the Creative Uses for Washi Tape
11:45am - 12:45pm The Write Way: A Smooth Introduction to Fountain Pens
1pm - 2pm How to Build a Daily Journaling Habit
2pm - 3pm Plan Your Page - Journaling Creatively
3pm - 4pm Writing to Reveal
Buy workshop tickets here: https://www.eventfinda.co.nz/tours-festivals/2025/new-zealand-stationery-festival
Please note: Event tickets do not give you access to Stationery Festival. Please buy a seperate Stationery Festival ticket, or you can enter for free between 2pm - 4pm (as long as capacity allows).

The Runholder Presents A Boutique Festival of Wine, Gin, Food & Music, The Runholder Presents A Boutique Festival of Wine, Gin, Food & Music
Join us under a canopy of trees for an unforgettable afternoon that blends flavour, sound & celebration. Set against the stunning backdrop of Martinborough’s rolling hills and vines, this curated gathering brings together our favourite makers, movers, and shakers - ready to pour, plate, and play their hearts out.

Sip iconic artisan wines, swirl small-batch gin and savour signature gourmet bites by culinary legends.

On stage we welcome the soulful stylings and powerhouse vocals of Hollie Smith, the retro glam and infectious energy of The Beat Girls, and the genre-spinning magic of Sweet Mix Kids, interspersed with sets from DJ Takas. The only thing smoother than the wine is the soundtrack.

Our Saturday session promises an elevated, intimate atmosphere - where the wine flows, the beats drop, and the good vibes carry you through an afternoon of dancing, right into sunset.

With invited friends: Martinborough Vineyard, Te Kairanga, Escarpment, Ata Rangi, Schubert, Palliser Estate, Halite Wines, Lighthouse Gin, Mt Difficulty, Vavasour, Martinborough Brewery, Antipodes Water, The Crab Shack, Wharekauhau Estate, Shed 5, SOUL Bar & Bistro and Martin Bosley's Oyster Saloon.

Elevate your festival experience with VIP hosting at The Runholder Cottage. Indulge in premium and library wines poured by the winemakers themselves, impeccably paired with gourmet food offerings from Auckland Viaduct’s iconic SOUL Bar & Bistro. As a VIP guest, you’ll enjoy all-inclusive food and beverage with menu service for any onsite vendor, exclusive access to the dedicated VIP area with priority stage sightlines and premium hosting amenities for your comfort and convenience.

Take advantage of easy transportation options with return bus add-ons from Wellington, Masterton, Carterton, Greytown & Featherston ($30-$60), and free shuttles to and from Martinborough Square, so you can sip responsibly.

description:
The Spring Fling Express, Celebrate the season in style aboard the Spring Fling Express.

This heritage rail journey whisks you from Kapiti through the lower North Island’s most breathtaking landscapes.
Tailor your day with two delightful options: jump off at the iconic Taniwha Daffodils to wander through vibrant golden fields, or continue to Waipukurau. In town, explore the bustling Spring Market or opt for short "shuttle" train trips to discover our charming neighbouring townships. Combining nostalgic rail travel with the very best of country hospitality, this is the ultimate springtime escape.

Hop aboard the Spring Fling Flyer for a delightful short-haul heritage rail experience during the festival's launch weekend!
Operating as charming shuttle excursions from Waipukurau, these trips offer a nostalgic journey to both Ōtāne and Takapau, connecting communities and celebrations along the line.

While at the station, don’t miss 'Tracks through Waipukurau', a platform exhibition celebrating 150 years of journeys, stories, and connection.
It is a fun, flexible, and scenic way to immerse yourself in the Spring Fling festivities while experiencing the golden age of rail.

TICKET INCLUDES: Nostalgic heritage 1-day train travel from Paekakariki to Waipukurau and return.

KEY EVENT INFO: All ages welcome
Service operates in wet weather
Due to the age/design of heritage carriages, this experience is not suitable for passengers with limited mobility; please contact the Steam Incorporated bookings team to discuss options if you have any questions.
Meal options available and caters for a range of dietaries (including gluten free/vegetarian/vegan).
______________________________

Your Spring, Your Way

Running throughout September- and October, this year's Spring Fling is a curated showcase of our district's finest heritage, hospitality, and heart. Whether you're seeking a long, indulgent lunch in a historic garden or a heart pumping coastal trak, there is a Spring Fling experience crafted specifically for you.

Central Hawke's Bay is a hidden gem waiting to be discovered, come and experience the warmth of our hospitality and the magic of our landscapes.

description:
Tora Bombora - 2027, Tora Bombora - 2027
The Return of Tora Bombora.

Wellington Anniversary Weekend, 22 - 24 January, 2027

After five incredible festivals and a four year hiatus, Tora Bombora is returning for the sixth edition - Tora Bombora Ono

For four summers, the paddocks sat quietly. The stages slept, the winds kept moving across the hills, and the coast returned to its familiar rhythm. But some things never really leave. They simply wait.

————————————————————

Ticket System and Key Dates

'Tora Bombora Whānau'
To keep the community close and the kaupapa even closer, if you have attended Tora Bombora in the past, you are already 'Tora Bombora Whānau' which gives you first access to tickets (keep an eye on your inbox). The remaining tickets will be released to people who sign up via our website to become a part of the 'Tora Bombora Whānau'.

How it works
1. Enter 'Tora Bombora Whānau': Sign up to the Tora Bombora waiting list and join the whānau before the link closes.
Link opens Monday, 6th July.
Link closes Sunday, 9th August.

2. Keep an eye on your inbox: Once the link has closed, you'll receive an email with a 'Tora Bombora Whānau' access code that gives you access to purchase tickets to Tora Bombora before they are released to the general public. Each whānau member may purchase up to four tickets.
Whānau ticket access and lineup out 10th August

3. General ticket release
Tuesday, 11th August - If any tickets remain after the whānau link has been sent out, they will be released in a public sale.

If this sounds like your kind of gig, put your name in the hat. The coast will do the rest.
All other info can be found at www.torabombora.co.nz

————————————————————

CAMPING: This is included in your ticket price. The festival begins at 3.00 pm Friday the 20th Jan. The camping zone will be situated on-site, right on the Pacific Ocean where you can swim, fish, surf, play and chill out.

FOOD AND SHOPS: Tora is isolated. This means no shops for 45 minutes so please make sure you bring more than enough food and gear as Martinborough is the nearest town. There will be plenty of food trucks at the event.

————————————————————

Festival Terms & Conditions:

*THIS IS AN R18 EVENT & RIGHT OF ADMISSION IS RESERVED.

**WASTE POLICY IS BRING YOUR OWN, TAKE YOUR OWN.

————————————————————

LOCATION

313 Te Awaiti Road, Tora Beach, Martinborough, South Wairarapa, Wellington, 5782

Drive time from Wellington: 2 hours 15mins.

Ultimate Tribute Fest 2: Dimebag & Ozzy Memorial Show, Ultimate Tribute Fest 2: Dimebag & Ozzy Memorial Show
Featuring Tributes to: Pantera, Ozzy Osbourne, Megadeth, Faith No More and more bands TBA.

About this Event



Ultimate Tribute Fest 2: A Memorial for Metal Legends

Rail Records, Wildkiwi Distillery, Women's Refuge, and Riockstock present a monumental night of heavy metal in honor of two of the genre's most important and beloved figures: the legendary guitarist "Dimebag" Darrell Abbott of Pantera, and the recently departed Godfather of Metal, Ozzy Osbourne.
Join us on Saturday, December 6th, 2025, at Wildkiwi in Upper Hutt for a memorial show that will shake the foundations. This date holds a special importance to us metal heads, falling just three days after what would have been Ozzy's 77th birthday (December 3rd) and just two days before the anniversary of Dimebag's tragic passing (December 8th, 2004), giving us all a chance to raise a glass and celebrate both legends in the loudest way possible.
This is a night to pay tribute to the artists who defined a generation of heavy music. From Dimebag's revolutionary groove and unmistakable harmonic squeals to Ozzy's haunting vocals and iconic stage presence, their impact is eternal. We invite the metal community to come together for an unforgettable evening of remembrance, unity, and blistering riffs.


The Lineup
Prepare for a full-throttle sonic assault from four of New Zealand's premier tribute acts, performing the anthems that have become the soundtrack to our lives:
•Hell's Wrath delivering the ferocious power of Pantera
•Zombie Stomp (ft. Danny Rascal) channeling the madness of Ozzy Osbourne
•Angel Dust performing the eclectic genius of Faith No More
•Demon Foetal Harvest unleashing the thrash mastery of Megadeth
(More acts to be announced!)


Event Details
•Date: Saturday, December 6, 2025
•Venue: Wildkiwi, Unit 13/27 Blenheim Street, Maidstone, Upper Hutt
•Time: Doors open at 6:00 PM
•Age Restriction: This is a strictly R18 event. ID will be required.
•Charity: We will be accepting donations at the event and at point of sale on behalf of Women's Refuge. Your support is greatly appreciated.


Ticket Information
Secure your spot to witness this massive tribute event. Tickets are on sale now!
•$20 Early Bird (+GST/BF) - Limited quantity available! Grab them before they're gone.
•$30 General Admission (+GST/BF)
•$40 Door Sales/Lates (If not sold out prior)


VIP Table Experience - Only 6 Available!
For the ultimate night out, gather your crew and secure a VIP table.
Price: $240 per table (includes 6 tickets - works out to $40 per person)
Perks:
•Guaranteed reserved seating for your group of 6.
•Early venue access from 4:00 PM to settle in and have a meal.
•10% discount on delicious bar food from the Wildkiwi kitchen.
•First dibs on the merch table.
•Check out soundcheck and meet the bands (where possible).


Limited Edition Merchandise
•Exclusive Event T-Shirt: $30
•Commemorate this special night with a limited edition T-shirt. There are only 20 of these shirts being made, so this is a true collector's item. Available as a ticket add-on. Don't miss out!
This show is a tribute, a memorial, and a celebration. Get your tickets now and be part of a historic night for New Zealand's metal scene.

ULTRA Worldwide has just announced the inaugural ULTRA New Zealand, which will take place at Wellington Waterfront in Wellington on Friday, April 10, 2026. In celebration of this historic debut edition, ULTRA New Zealand will transform the country’s capital into a multi-stage experience featuring world-class electronic music talent. ULTRA New Zealand will be held at an idyllic waterfront location, promising to channel the signature spirit of ULTRA’s flagship Miami festival and deliver a landmark moment for both ULTRA Worldwide and New Zealand’s live music landscape.

ULTRA Worldwide’s arrival on the Wellington Waterfront brings a sense of grand spectacle to the capital - an event launch that will create an unprecedented atmosphere for New Zealand. Set against the harbor’s sweeping backdrop, ULTRA New Zealand will be an electronic music playground that elevates Wellington City onto the global stage of dance music culture.

ULTRA New Zealand is part of the ULTRA Worldwide family, which continues to cement its status as the world’s most international music festival brand. Boasting active events on all six inhabited continents, including the flagship Ultra Music Festival in Miami, the global festival brand is heralded for delivering an unparalleled combination of top-tier electronic talent, cutting-edge technology and large-scale productions.

Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025 Opening, We’re kicking off the Wairarapa Walking Festival with a celebration on one of the region’s much-loved gems—the Greytown Rail Trail. Originally a branch railway line between Greytown and Woodside Station, the line was disused from the 1950s until local residents formed a trust in 2010 to transform it into the walking, running, and cycling track we enjoy today.

The Rail Trail offers a level, 5km route on a smooth, limed path - open in places, tree-lined in others - and winds through farmland with views across to the mountains. Popular year-round with walkers, cyclists, visitors, and locals alike, it’s the perfect spot to launch our festival.

The festival site opens at 9:30am, with coffee available to purchase thanks to Gracias Coffee. Meet the friendly teams from Masterton Foot Clinic and Masterton Shoe Clinic who will make sure you’re ready to walk. At 10:00am we’ll officially open the festival with a karakia, before inviting you to meander, stroll, or stride along the trail.

Look out for special treats along the way from the Greytown Lolly Jar, and celebrate your efforts at the finish with a sausage sizzle hosted by the Greytown Rail Trail Trust.

Walk Format
Meeting Point: Greytown end of the Rail Trail, Cotter Street.
Trail: 5km one way, flat lime path
Who it’s for: All ages and abilities. You’re welcome to turn back at any point.

No registrations required for this walk.
Photo credit: Greytown Trails Trust

description:
Waitangi Day 2026 - Open Day, FOR IMMEDIATE USE – JAN / FEB 2026
WAITANGI DAY– OPEN DAY
FRIDAY 6TH FEB, 10AM- 4PM
Wellington’s historic Wrights Hill Fortress in Karori will be open for public inspection again on Waitangi Day, Friday, February 6th. The World War Two coastal battery first opened to the public in 1989 and will be accessible between 10am and 4pm.
On Waitangi Day people are invited to self-guide themselves through the tunnels and gun emplacements. The walk usually takes about one hour. Bring a torch with you for some fun! Strong footwear and no jandals!
Visitors will be able to explore the 620 metres of underground tunnels with a free map and history pamphlet. They will see shell stores, plotting rooms and the huge gun pit where Gun umber 1 used to stand, as well as a replica of the 10-metre-long gun barrel. Also on show will be historic photos, and an assortment of military memorabilia. A DVD of how a 9.2-inch gun operates will be showing as well. The World War Two Fortress is the only one of its type in New Zealand available to the public on four Open Days a year.
Wrights Hill Fortress was built from 1942 to protect Wellington from Japanese bombardment. In the early 1960’s, the guns were cut up for scrap and sold, ironically, to the Japanese.
Admission is $20 for a family of two adults and three children under 12, or $10 per adult and $5 per child. (CASH ONLY please-NO EFTPOS). Access is via Karori Road, Campbell Street, and Wrights Hill Road. All proceeds go to the continuing restoration of the Fortress. There is limited car parking at the summit of the Hill.
Visitors to the Fortress in Wrights Hill Reserve can also enjoy bush walks, picnic sites and panoramic views from the top of the hill.
There will also be a BBQ sausage sizzle and soft drinks on sale. No booking required.

description:
Wellington Jazz Festival, Soul, funk, jazz, fusion, rhythm and blues — it’s a celebration of sound across the city this spring. The annual Wellington Jazz Festival is back. The event packs over 100 gigs into five days in venues around the city. 
The festival features two major international acts making exclusive New Zealand debuts. Wellington will see two-time Grammy Award-winning jazz vocalist and bandleader, Gregory Porter and five-time Grammy Award-winning jazz singer, Samara Joy. Gregory Porter’s unique and timeless sound blends jazz, soul, and gospel. His influences include Bakersfield Southern Gospel and jazz legend Nat King Cole. At just 25 years old, Samara Joy has become a breakout jazz sensation. She’s redefining 21st-century jazz with a rich, mature tone and refined phrasing. 
The treats in the programme continue with Australian First Nations soul singer Bumpy, and a commissioned work by New Zealand/Congolese drummer, composer, and rhythm master  Myele Manzanza. He’ll be performing with international supergroup, lvdf. The Rodger Fox Big Band returns with a tribute to Ray Charles, and the Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra has its inaugural performance with a Duke Ellington arrangement of Tchaikovsky’s The Nutcracker Suite. Many of the hospitality venues in Courtenay Place and its surrounding streets are planning intimate jazz gigs across the festival. Follow the sound of saxophones to find a spot to park up for the night.

Wellington Pasifika Festival 2026 🌺, Wellington Pasifika Festival 2026 🌺
Experience the sights, sounds, and flavours of the Pacific at Wellington Pasifika Festival 2026 🌸🌴🥥

Come along to this free, whānau-friendly festival and join us to celebrate our unique Pacific communities. From art and language to performances and food, the Pasifika Festival is all about acknowledging the richness of our Pacific brothers and sisters.

📅Saturday 7 February 2026, at Waitangi Park, Wellington
⌚12pm-6pm for the main event. Come from 1:30am for the opening ceremony.
📍Waitangi Park, Wellington Waterfront

The 2026 event theme is ‘Arrival’, which will be represented through explorations of migration stories and is a celebration of and a welcome to the Pasifika communities who have made New Zealand their home. You can also view the carving has been taking shape since the 2024 festival and talk to artist Leo Semau about the artwork.

Plus... The popular Pasifika Cuisine Cook-Off competition is back for another year, with food stalls submitting their best dish for judging by a celebrity panel.

The festival will open with a blessing followed by stage performances from various Pacific Island groups. There will be food stalls, craft, and sponsor stalls, a Kids’ Zone, and Pacific Media Network 531pi FM and Āti Awa Toa radio activations.

You can also take part in a festival wide activation based on the card game ‘Lalaga’, designed by Torisse Lalau, which uses Pasifika wisdom (talanoa) to foster empathy and connection through sharing stories.

We’d like to thank the Pasifika Patrol who will be helping out on the day. Gather your friends and family for a fun day out–be transported to the Pacific Islands for the day! ❣️

To see the full programme, head to 👉 https://wellington.govt.nz/news-and-events/events-and-festivals/pasifika-festival

description:
Wānaga Matariki, Wānanga Matariki: Matariki Herenga Waka is a special Matariki evening kōrero exploring the traditions, knowledge and future of waka voyaging in Aotearoa and across the Pacific.

Presented by the crew of Ngahiraka-Mai-Tawhiti and Te Kura Waka, this free public wānanga brings together experienced navigators, cultural leaders and storytellers to share insights into traditional celestial navigation, ocean knowledge, waka hourua traditions, and the intergenerational revival of indigenous voyaging practices.

Through personal stories, cultural perspectives and discussion, speakers will reflect on the past, present and future of waka navigation, and the role of mātauranga Māori in reconnecting communities with whakapapa, te ao Māori and the moana.

The evening features respected speakers and facilitators including Tainui Stephens, Manihera Forbes, Hinerapa Rupuha and Tamahau Tangitu, each bringing extensive experience in Māori storytelling, cultural leadership, traditional navigation and Pacific voyaging.

Suitable for adults, educators, cultural practitioners and anyone interested in Māori knowledge systems, navigation traditions and contemporary indigenous storytelling.

Booking is recommended.

This event is wheelchair accessible. Please note that variable lighting may be used during the event.

description:
XCOMMUNICATE, The formidable powerhouse duo COMMUNICATE return to Wellington in November with their clubnight, XCOMMUNICATE, for one night only.
Known for their long sets that incorporate decades of sound, Cyril Orson and Heylady have been punishing dance floors across Aotearoa since they joined forces 3 years ago. Off the back of a monstrous summer, which saw them play 19 shows up and down the country, the pair have spent most of 2025 in the studio finessing their own brand of audio alchemy and preparing to release their label, also named XCOMMUNICATE.
Usually XCOMMUNICATE is a 6 hour journey though decades and sonic realms, however as Heylady is still recovering from a mighty dose of burnout they’ve roped in a couple of their good friends, who happen to be some of Wellington’s finest, to join them as they lay down four hours of four to the floor.
Halo is a mainstay on Wellington dancefloors and it was a no brainer asking her to be on this lineup. A DJ since 2000, she has played festivals across the country and never fails to rock her slot. Her set at Taniwha’s Den last summer was a big highlight and one of the best of the festival. Halo’s ability to drive forward thinking sound and her clever construction of sets are just two reasons you need to be on her floor.
DJ Coda is the godfather of techno in New Zealand. With a career that spans decades, he isn’t just a DJ but a dedicated promoter and one of the trustees of NZ’s longest running student radio station, Radio Active. Part of the COMMUNICATE family from the get go (and a longtime collaborator of Heylady’s), DJ Coda is a master of his craft and never fails to deliver. Armed with knowledge , taste and a hefty love of Detroit, DJ Coda is the man when it comes to rocking the dance floor.
First release tickets are on sale now, grab yours before they are gone and come and dance the evening away with four of the best. We recommend arrive early so you don’t miss out on any of the sets, they are all going to be killer.
IMPORTANT INFO:
Our event is a safe space for all. If you or someone you know is feeling unsafe or harassed, please approach one of the DJs or bar staff. If you are behaving badly and impacting others ability to have a good time safely, you will be removed. Please act with respect and care for your fellow attendees at all times, no means no and this goes for conversations as well as more intimate requests.

description:
XL: 40th Anniversary Concert, Come celebrate out very special 40th anniversary!
N.B. There will be a pre-concert talk from 7pm in the Cathedral.
The Tudor Consort celebrates its 40th birthday in 2026 and we have an incredible season planned to celebrate. Collaborations with five different ensembles, a debut in Auckland, three premiere performances, and of course a performance of Thomas Tallis’ 40 part masterpiece Spem in alium. Make sure you visit our website to get all the details and secure your tickets!
We will be taking part in our third Aotearoa Festival of the Arts with SoundCathedral on Sunday March 1, an incredible re-composition of Orlande de Lassus’ Prophetiae Sibyllarum by Michael Norris, written especially for our anniversary and the 25th birthday of Stroma contemporary music ensemble. We celebrate going ‘over the hill’ in style in our May 2 concert XL, featuring two 40 part works by Tallis and Mäntyjärvi. We have two concerts with our friends Orchestra Wellington - Leonard Bernstein’s energetic Chichester Psalms as part of W:Ellington on 30 May, and Victoria Kelly’s brand new opera Ocean on 28 November. A debut in Auckland with NZ Barok sees us performing Lotti and Handel, and we finish the year with Messiah with Australian virtuoso harpsichordist and director Erin Helyard. 

This is one of the most exciting seasons in our history, and I hope very much you can join us as we celebrate!

🌑new moon at moon 🌑a summer solstice celebration 🌑

the end of 2025 is approaching fast, and what better time to gather with others to celebrate this shift than a new moon??

with several live solo electronic artists this new moon at moon gig will be the perfect opportunity to reflect and celebrate your progress this year, (or to dance away blocks stopping you from moving forward!) and connect with others.

🌻this new moon also coincides with the summer solstice, marking the halfway point of the tauhou māori, making it an even better time to gather with others, celebrate, reflect and bask in the joy of the sunshine + renewed energy that comes with summer ! 🌻

🌑the artists who will be guiding you through this night are: 🌑

✨hazel elder
✨vanessa tottle (AUK)
✨talmar (AUK)
✨modern dialogue
✨beet-wix

but as well as music there will be…

💫koha tarot readings
💫 a raffle
💫 koha second hand clothing

with profits going to Outline Aotearoa

https://outline.org.nz/

while this time of year can be a wonderful time to reconnect with your roots, this same exact reason can make the holidays an especially rough time for some - particularly for some LGBTQIA+ / queer people who may not be supported by their families / be feeling disconnected from community at this time.

to recognise this at the gig we will be having a second hand clothing rack + raffle as a fundraiser for Outline Aotearoa, a charity that provides mental health support to Takatāpui, MVPFAFF+ and Rainbow communities, their friends, whānau, and those questioning.

some profits from the tickets will also be going towards Outline Aotearoa as well as supporting local queer / femme and trans artists !


🌟accessibility info / general tikanga for gig 🌟

please come if you are nice and stay home if you are not. this is a queer-friendly space and we will not tolerate racism, homophobia, transphobia, sexism, ableism or general shit behaviour of any kind.

please do not come if you are sick. sickness spreads like hell at gigs and we want to keep our vulnerable communities safe. there will be masks available for those who would like them.

venue is wheelchair accessible and has an accessible bathroom. please contact Lucky / beet-wix at if you have any further accessibility enquiries

☀️ come along, help support a great cause and gather with everyone in queer community to celebrate this shift in our year ! ☀️

2-Day Kali Seminar with Stephen Brown from Inosanto Academy in CA, Want to learn the exact martial art skills as used in the Bourne films? Wellington this is your chance...
Tactical Survival Academy is hosting Senior Instructor Stephen Brown from the renowned Inosanto Academy of Martial Arts in Marina Del Rey, Los Angeles!
With over 40 years of martial arts experience and 36 years training under Guro Dan Inosanto, Stephen is one of only two instructors currently teaching Kali classes at the academy alongside Guro Dan Inosanto himself.
Stephen specializes in the Filipino Martial Art of Kali, as passed down through Guro Inosanto’s lineage. His training background also includes extensive experience in Muay Thai, Silat, Western Boxing, Jeet Kune Do, Savate and Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu.
Over the decades, Stephen has worked with:
* Multiple branches of Law Enforcement, Military units and Special Forces.
* Actors, stunt performers, and executives in the film and television industry.
* As a fight choreographer for screen productions.
Known for his precision, adaptability, and deep respect for the cultural roots of the arts he teaches, Stephen brings a wealth of knowledge and embodied experience to every seminar.
Currently based in Marina Del Rey, CA, Stephen is excited to share the Kali method of Guro Inosanto with the New Zealand martial arts community.
• Location: Mt Cook School Hall, 160 Tory Street, Te Aro
• Dates: Sat Sept 6 + Sun Sept 7

description:
A Life on Our Planet: Climate Change Film Screening, Overview

Join us for a powerful climate documentary screening and discover how we can protect our planet for future generations.

Join the Nelson Youth Council for an inspiring screening of A Life on Our Planet, presented by renowned broadcaster and natural historian Sir David Attenborough. Through breathtaking footage and powerful storytelling, the film explores the impact humans have had on Earth's ecosystems while offering hope and practical solutions for creating a more sustainable future.
Following the screening, attendees will have the opportunity to reflect on the film's key messages, discuss climate change with others, and explore simple actions that individuals and communities can take to make a positive difference.
Whether you're passionate about the environment or simply curious to learn more, everyone is welcome to attend this engaging and thought-provoking event.
Arrival Information!
The film screening will be held in the Library at Nayland College.
Please enter through the Front Office (Reception), where staff or Youth council members will be available to direct you to the library.
Why Attend?
Learn about the causes and impacts of climate change.
Discover practical ways to reduce your environmental footprint.
Be inspired by real-world solutions that are helping protect our planet.
Connect with others who care about creating a more sustainable future.
Who Can Attend?
This event is open to everyone—students, families, young people, adults, and members of the wider community. No prior knowledge of climate change is required.
Why This Matters
Climate change is one of the greatest challenges facing our generation. Understanding its causes and impacts is the first step toward creating meaningful change. By coming together to learn, discuss, and take action, we can all play a part in building a healthier, more sustainable future for people and the planet.

From September to November, a selection of Thursdays will be your chance to slow down, sink into a beanbag, sit back in a chair, and lose yourself in the magic of cinema. This one is our special School Holiday screening - something fun for you and the kids to do, and on a budget. Afterwards, we'll chat with Chantelle Murray about her processes in bringing to life The Lost Tiger and what it means for her as an Indigenous woman in film.

Teo is a plucky young tiger and one of the last of his kind. Found abandoned and wearing a mysterious crystal necklace, he is adopted into a big, boisterous kangaroo family of travelling wrestlers. After receiving visions from an unfamiliar land, Teo must suddenly embark on an epic quest to reconnect with his heritage and save his homeland from the clutches of destruction. --- Cary Scott is a well-to-do widow gradually re-entering a social life amongst her mostly dull country club peers. Her only apparent enjoyment in life comes from weekend visits from her college-age children. Cary then meets a handsome younger man, Ron, who owns a small landscaping business. A follower of Henry David Thoreau's Walden, Ron enjoys a life focused on nature and is deliberately uninterested in the gossipy opinions of others. Their romance causes clashes and tensions between Cary, her children, and the country club. ---

Atsuko Okatsuka — The Big Bowl Tour, She’s been described as having one-of-a-kind humour, boundless energy, and infectious charm. Comedian and actress Atsuko Okatsuka is heading to Wellington with her latest show, ‘The Big Tour’.   
With podcasts, television and film acting, and standup specials on streaming platforms, Atsuko has gained a huge following. Her previous tour, ‘Full Grown’, sold out over 200 shows across 20 countries. Her latest standup special, ‘Father’, premiered on Disney+ and has made it onto its Top 10 list. 
Atsuko’s viral moments are as legendary as her stand-up. She has ridden a Jeepney (a type of public utility vehicle) in the Philippines and started the #DropChallenge, which helped bring Beyoncé’s ‘Partition’ back to the charts. She’s become a true queen of the internet with clips from her live-filmed show, The Intruder, racking up over 100 million views. Fans even turn up to her shows wearing wigs styled as her signature bowl cut as a form of homage. Humour has no borders when you’re that funny.

Banff Centre Mountain Film Festival World Tour 2026 - Pōneke Wellington, Banff Centre Mountain Film Festival World Tour 2026 - Pōneke Wellington
Banff Centre Mountain Film Festival World Tour presented by the NZ Alpine Club - Wellington Screenings

About this Event

The New Zealand Alpine Club with Presenting Partners, World Expeditions, La Sportiva, NZ Mountain Safety Council and Osprey, bring the Banff Centre Mountain Film Festival World Tour back to Pōneke Wellington this May and June!

Banff Centre Mountain Film and Book Festival is one of the largest and most prestigious mountain festivals in the world! Hot on the heels of the Festival that is held every fall in beautiful Banff, Alberta, the Banff Centre Mountain Film Festival World Tour hits the road. With stops planned in over 600 communities and more than 40 countries across the globe, the Banff World Tour celebrates amazing achievements in outdoor storytelling and filmmaking worldwide.

From the over 400 entries submitted to the Festival competition each year, award-winners and audience favourites are among the films that are carefully selected to play in theatres around the world. Travelling to remote vistas, analysing topical environmental issues, and bringing audiences up-close and personal with adrenaline-packed action sports, the 2025/2026 World Tour is an exhilarating and provocative exploration of the mountain world.
Be moved. Be inspired. Don’t miss out. Reserve your tickets today. For more information visit and follow our Facebook page for updates.
This screening is a fundraiser for the New Zealand Alpine Club.


PROGRAMME
We will be screening two programmes, Ruapehu and Tasman. over 4 nights. All screenings start at 5.30pm with doors opening at 5:00pm.

description:
Big Bike Film Night, The Big Bike Film Night is on a mission – bringing the best short cycling films from around the world together for you.

Showcasing 2.5 hours of mesmerizing bike films that have everything a cycle-centric audience could want – action, drama, humour, and plenty of inspiration. The evening is unashamedly and utterly, utterly, utterly designed and devised to delight the two-wheel devotee!

The 2026 treasure chest of films includes:

a dazzling mountain bike ride exploring the breathtaking landscapes of Norway, embracing the magic of the midnight sun • a life-changing experience for two adventurous women as they embark to cycle to all the ski-fields in New Zealand in one gigantic attempt
an inspiring film that captures the wettest, most miserable riding conditions imaginable
a film that playfully delves into the world of those taking cycling to new heights – celebrating fun, silliness, and creativity that comes with pushing boundaries on two wheels
a compelling story about perseverance, showcasing the challenges and triumphs of navigating daily life following a life-altering injury, and how adaptive design has transformed and enriched the journey forward
a moving movie that follows a father and son’s journey as they take on one of life’s most meaningful milestones- riding a bike together as a family
a bold and uplifting story of an adventure activist, attempting to break the 24-hour Guinness World Record in downhill mountain biking- all to raise funds for reforesting foothills around Queenstown, New Zealand. Her relentless pursuit not only pushes the limits of endurance but also becomes a powerful symbol of resilience and environmental commitment
and crowning the night off… we all love an underdog tale. This charming, funny, heartfelt film inspires us to believe that we all have the capacity to be unlikely heroes in our own stories. The audience is transported back to the nostalgic 1990’s, to the slopes of the punishing Mont Ventoux, in Southern France, to witness the drama of a battle between two giants
ALL in the mix!

These short films are a great reminder of why we love to ride our bike; with stories that captivate us, stories that move us, and most importantly of all – inspiring us to get out and ride. All celebrate the fun, adventure, and joy that cycling enables.

So…listen to the voice inside you; it’s telling you to go. Grab your mates, GO ON… grab your bike and come along for the ride!!

PREVIOUS ATTENDEE’S COMMENTS:

“One of the most inspiring events of the year”

“If you only have one night a year out, make it this!!”

“The Big Bike Film Night is always a wonderful, eclectic, wacky mix of films and I love it!”

“If you haven’t experienced the cinematic excellence of The Big Bike Film Night – then YOU MUST!!!”

description:
Bogan Film Classics | The Warriors, Goodbye Pork Pie, and The Castle, Mullet, muscle cars, and movie mayhem. In conjunction with Bogan Day out Bogan Film Classics is a loud and proud celebration of the big screen at its roughest and rowdiest, from cult NZ favs to over-the-top action flicks.

Brought to you by Aro Video
.
The Warriors
Saturday 14 March 8.30pm
Director: Walter Hill | Year: 1979 | Length: 93 minutes | Rating: R16 violence & offensive language

The Warriors promises an awesome retro night at movies. Set among youth gangs of New York who each have colourful names and uniforms, it’s a film faithful to its comic book origins by never pretending to be ‘real’, and with exciting action that never feels mean-spirited. It has a timeless ‘futuristic’ vibe that makes it still feel modern, and yet the story is based on an ancient Greek text that says something about the eternal nature of man and the troubled times we are now living through.
.
Goodbye Pork Pie
Sunday 15 March 1pm
Director: Geoff Murphy | Year: 1981 | Length: 105 minutes | Rating: PG Violence

Proudly flying its Bogan Kiwi flag on the car aerial of a humble yellow mini, this road comedy classic was made in our own back yard with the undeniable #8 wire ingenuity and larrikin spirit of director Geoff Murphy. It’s a maverick-fuelled grand tour from Kaitaia to the Bluff, though it’s the mainland section where it really carries its audience towards the absolute ripper finale. “I’m taking this bloody car to Invercargill!”
.
The Castle
Sunday 15 March 6pm
Director: Rob Stitch | Year: 1997 | Length: 84 minutes | Rating: M Offensive language

Regarded as Australia’s favourite movie of all time, this true-blue Bogan classic is up there in the hearts of Kiwis as well, full of quotable lines that have become immortalized in both of our cultures. Many of you will have seen it many times, but don’t let that stop you seeing it with a room full of fellow fans and members of a new generation keen to see what the fuss is about. It’s a film about family, after all!

description:
British and Irish Film Festival - A Room with a View, A Room With a View captured the attention of the world upon its release, bringing the novel by E.M. Forster to dazzling life in the Florentine countryside and in the well-appointed homes of the English Edwardian upper classes. A comedy of manners with a quick wit and impeccable comic timing, A Room With A View is also a portrait of the quiet solitude that lies beneath Forster’s characters, and of the need for human connection in a world of rigid convention.

The young Englishwoman Lucy Honeychurch (played by Helena Bonham Carter), arrives in Florence on a Baedecker-style grand tour with her aunt Charlotte Bartlett (Maggie Smith). Through a series of events involving English expatriates Miss Eleanor Lavish, an unflappable novelist (Judi Dench), and the Emersons, a free-thinking father and son (played by Denholm Elliot and Julian Sands), Lucy’s life is changed forever under a loggia in Florence and in the Tuscan countryside.

Ivory’s delicate and playful direction spirits us from an adventure in the back alleys of Florence, lost with Dench and Smith, to the lace-parasolled rigidity of English lawn parties. Shot on location in and around Florence (including unforgettable scenes in the Piazza della Signoria and at Giotto’s frescoes in Santa Croce), A Room With A View made stars not only of Bonham Carter, Day Lewis and Sands, but of the Tuscan landscapes and Puccini arias (as sung by Kiri Te Kanawa) featured throughout.

Director
James Ivory

Producer
Ismail Merchant

Cast
Maggie Smith, Helena Bonham Carter, Denholm Elliot, Julian Sands
label: Film & Media

description:
British and Irish Film Festival - Beat the Lotto, - OFFICIAL SELECTION: Dublin International Film Festival 2025 -

Beat the Lotto is a rip-roaring tale about the mathematician who, along with a ragtag syndicate, plotted to fix Ireland’s National Lottery in 1992, captivating the nation and sparking rabid debate.

In Ireland, the public became obsessed when the National Lottery arrived, none more so than mathematician and avid stamp-collector Stefan Klincewicz. Using mathematical analysis, he reckoned the system could be beaten if he could just gather enough people to form a syndicate to buy every single ticket combination – and front up all the cash, of course.

Director Ross Whitaker fashions this unbelievable true story into a gripping thriller, mirroring the tension felt by the public as the lottery authorities caught wind of the plan.

With insightful interviews and fantastic archival footage, Beat the Lotto is a look back at Ireland in the 1990s and a compelling tale of one man’s attempt to outsmart the system.
Director
Ross Whitaker
label: Film & Media

description:
British and Irish Film Festival - Broken English, - OFFICIAL SELECTION: Venice International Film Festival 2025 -
- OFFICIAL SELECTION: BFI London Film Festival 2025 -

Broken English is a bold and imaginative documentary portrait of the inimitable singer, songwriter and icon Marianne Faithfull.

A survivor, provocateur and true original, Marianne spent more than six decades defying expectations, releasing over thirty-five albums while constantly reinventing herself.

Made with her full involvement, Broken English is an intimate and unflinching exploration of a fractured yet unbreakable life shaped by fame, creativity and relentless public scrutiny.

The film unfolds within the “Ministry of Not Forgetting”, an imagined, cinematic institution where memory and mythology collide. The Ministry is presided over by Tilda Swinton as The Overseer, and George MacKay (also starring in & Sons at this year’s Festival) serves as The Record Keeper, poring over Faithfull’s life and career.

Broken English is a genre-defying act of resilience and rebellion — Marianne Faithfull’s final fearless declaration, her defiant swan song.
Director
Jane Pollard, Iain Forsyth
Cast
Marianne Faithfull, Tilda Swinton, George MacKay, Zawe Ashton
label: Film & Media

description:
