description:
The Art of Adventure, Doc Edge Festival 2026

A vintage road trip that fuelled a lifetime of wonder.
In 1957, renowned wildlife artist Robert Bateman and spirited biologist Bristol Foster set out on a global expedition in a rugged Land Rover they called “The Grizzly Torque”. Starting in the UK, their travels took them to the far corners of the earth. From the lush rainforests of the Congo to the vibrant landscapes of India, Bob painted the wonders they encounter, while Bristol filmed on his 16mm Bolex camera. Blending original 16mm footage with reflections from later life, the film traces how their journey shaped two remarkable paths: one through art, the other through science. A heartwarming, inspirational love letter to friendship and the adventure of life.

description:
The Big Bike Film Night 2026 - Blenheim, The Big Bike Film Night 2026 - Blenheim
Let the good times ROLL! The screening sensation known as The Big Bike Film Night is back in '26 for your bike films fix!!!

Monday 30th March screening times:-
5:00pm
6:30pm

What's it all about??? The Big Bike Film Night is on a mission- bringing the best cycling short films from around the world together for you.

Showcasing 2.5 hours of riveting bike films that have everything a cycle-centric audience could want - action, drama, humour, and plenty of inspiration; the evening is unashamedly and utterly, utterly, utterly designed and devised to delight the two-wheel devotee!

Our Promo Trailer
https://bit.ly/Big_Bike_Film_Night_2026_Promo_Trailer

The 2026 treasure chest of films includes:
• a dazzling mountain bike ride exploring the breathtaking landscapes of Norway, embracing the magic of the midnight sun
• a life-changing experience for two adventurous women as they embark to cycle to all the ski-fields in New Zealand in one gigantic attempt
• an inspiring film that captures the wettest, most miserable riding conditions imaginable
• a film that playfully delves into the world of those taking cycling to new heights - celebrating fun, silliness, and creativity that comes with pushing boundaries on two wheels
• a compelling story about perseverance, showcasing the challenges and triumphs of navigating daily life following a life-altering injury, and how adaptive design has transformed and enriched the journey forward
• a moving movie that follows a father and son’s journey as they take on one of life’s most meaningful milestones- riding a bike together as a family
• a bold and uplifting story of an adventure activist, attempting to break the 24-hour Guinness World Record in downhill mountain biking- all to raise funds for reforesting foothills around Queenstown, New Zealand. Her relentless pursuit not only pushes the limits of endurance but also becomes a powerful symbol of resilience and environmental commitment
• and crowning the night off… we all love an underdog tale. This charming, funny, heartfelt film inspires us to believe that we all have the capacity to be unlikely heroes in our own stories. The audience is transported back to the nostalgic 1990s, to the slopes of the punishing Mont Ventoux, in Southern France, to witness the drama of a battle between two giants
ALL in the mix!

These short films are a great reminder of why we love to ride our bike; with stories that captivate us, stories that make us think, and most importantly of all- inspiring us to get out and ride. All celebrate the fun, adventure, and joy that cycling enables.

The New Zealand 󠁿2026 National Tour is brought to you by our PRESENTING PARTNERS
CYCLE JOURNEYS, and Destination Queenstown | Lake Wānaka Tourism

NATIONAL COMPETITION*
When you buy a ticket to attend a Big Bike Film Night New Zealand you can enter our National Competition to win some incredible prizes

Thanks to our Presenting Partners, Cycle Journeys, you could WIN a day ride for two on the new Kawatiri Coastal Trail, the prize includes 1 night's accomodation in Westport + breakfast
Website https://cyclejourneys.co.nz/kawatiri/

Thanks to our Presenting Partners, Destination Queenstown and Lake Wānaka Tourism you could WIN a biking holiday for two in Queenstown and Wānaka - New Zealand’s ultimate mountain biking and cycling destination.
Website https://www.queenstownnz.co.nz
Website https://www.wanaka.co.nz

Thanks to our Supporters, Ground Effect Cycle Clothing, you could WIN some awesome CYCLING KIT and 6 x $100 gift vouchers
Website https://www.groundeffect.co.nz

*Terms and Conditions apply


PREVIOUS ATTENDEE’S COMMENTS:-
“One of the most inspiring events of the year"
“Wow! If it comes to your town do NOT miss it. Something for everyone.”
“The Big Bike Film Night is always a wonderful, eclectic, wacky mix of films and I love it!”
“Inspiring | Breathtaking | Heartwarming | Quirky | Bonkers | Funny as F##k!"

HEALTH WARNING: Watching this collection may cause you to want to ride for no less than 1 second and no more than 24 hours per day. Potential side effects could also include buying a bike, bike gear, bike clothing, bike travel books, etc., etc., and longing to get lost with your bicycle. In addition to being entertaining, this event will inspire and lead to activities that improve your physical and mental well-being.

What's it all about??? The Big Bike Film Night is on a mission- bringing the best cycling short films from around the world together for you.

Showcasing 2.5 hours of riveting bike films that have everything a cycle-centric audience could want - action, drama, humour, and plenty of inspiration; the evening is unashamedly and utterly, utterly, utterly designed and devised to delight the two-wheel devotee!

Our Promo Trailer
https://bit.ly/Big_Bike_Film_Night_2026_Promo_Trailer

The 2026 treasure chest of films includes:
• a dazzling mountain bike ride exploring the breathtaking landscapes of Norway, embracing the magic of the midnight sun
• a life-changing experience for two adventurous women as they embark to cycle to all the ski-fields in New Zealand in one gigantic attempt
• an inspiring film that captures the wettest, most miserable riding conditions imaginable
• a film that playfully delves into the world of those taking cycling to new heights - celebrating fun, silliness, and creativity that comes with pushing boundaries on two wheels
• a compelling story about perseverance, showcasing the challenges and triumphs of navigating daily life following a life-altering injury, and how adaptive design has transformed and enriched the journey forward
• a moving movie that follows a father and son’s journey as they take on one of life’s most meaningful milestones- riding a bike together as a family
• a bold and uplifting story of an adventure activist, attempting to break the 24-hour Guinness World Record in downhill mountain biking- all to raise funds for reforesting foothills around Queenstown, New Zealand. Her relentless pursuit not only pushes the limits of endurance but also becomes a powerful symbol of resilience and environmental commitment
• and crowning the night off… we all love an underdog tale. This charming, funny, heartfelt film inspires us to believe that we all have the capacity to be unlikely heroes in our own stories. The audience is transported back to the nostalgic 1990s, to the slopes of the punishing Mont Ventoux, in Southern France, to witness the drama of a battle between two giants
ALL in the mix!

These short films are a great reminder of why we love to ride our bike; with stories that captivate us, stories that make us think, and most importantly of all- inspiring us to get out and ride. All celebrate the fun, adventure, and joy that cycling enables.

Kia ora! 
We have an update on the eras tour movie we need to share with you. In the past East Coast releases have meant a Friday 5pm release for us in New Zealand, which would have been fine for our Saturday screening of the FINAL SHOW (trailer here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S1MO3bRG9qw).

We'd also LOVE if you could share the link with family & friends, we still have some tickets to sell and would love to raise the funds, and have a fantastic dance party vibe with you. (https://events.humanitix.com/the-eras-tour-movie-a-swiftie-birthday-screening-for-a-cause)
Apologies for this hick up and change of plan. Mara broke her foot 3 weeks ago and has had surgery, so we are getting used to pivoting and changing plans this summer. We appreciate your understanding!

EVENT OVERVIEW:
Calling all swifties! Come along to a fun, action packed, dress up, sing-along on Taylor's birthday on December 13th. A one time screening only, of Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour Movie at Penthouse cinema. There are three ticket price options to pay, Budget Swiftie, Generous Swiftie, Big Spender Swiftie. Each ticket gives you the same access, its just about how much you want to donate. Every ticket also comes with a Taylor Swift themed goodie bag. All of the funds will go to supporting families and children in need in Palestine through Aotearoa 4 Gaza. So ...Are you ready for it?
There will be a Taylor birthday cake, goodie bags and a few Swiftie spot prizes!
Information about cause:
The Aotearoa 4 Gaza mutual aid fund was set up last year to directly support families in Gaza. We are a grassroots collective based in Aotearoa standing in unwavering solidarity with Palestinian families in Gaza. Through consistent, direct mutual aid, we send $100 at a time (usually once a week) to families who are living through unimaginable hardship under Israel's occupation and genocide. These contributions go straight to verified recipients, without intermediaries, ensuring urgent support reaches those who need it most. The fund is fully volunteer run and is led by Emily Writes. Nobody takes a cut. Every cent goes to our families. Every donation is a lifeline, and a stand against violence and genocide. We invite you to contribute, to share, and to stand with us in this act of collective care and resistance.

The Red Shoes (1948) screening - Powell and Pressburger, This is a screening for Wellington Film Society members only - to join grab a three-film sampler member ($40) or a full year membership ($120). https://wellingtonfilms.nz/join/
This film is playing twice - first at 6pm on Monday 24 November and then again at 8.30pm on Tuesday 25 November.
“The Red Shoes plays in my heart” – so says legendary director and cinephile Martin Scorsese, who personally assisted and championed the 4k restoration of the 1948 Powell and Pressburger epic which concludes our theme “Dancing on the edge” and closes out our 2025 programme.
Real life ballerina Moira Shearer stars as Vicky Page, a ballerina who rises to stardom under the watchful eye of svengali Boris Lermatov. Vicky is cast in Lermatov’s new production, “The Ballet of the Red Shoes”, based on the Hans Christian Andersen fairytale of the same name. In the prevailing gender norms of the 1940s, Vicky must choose between her career and her marriage – but will the mysterious power of the red shoes mean they have the final say?
The Red Shoes revels in its glorious Technicolor aesthetic, and for Scorsese offers the perfect synthesis between colour, sound, editing and cinematography. Nowhere in the film is this more evident than in the legendary 17-minute ballet sequence, which uses all aspects of filmcraft to weave between the action and Vicky’s psychological state. The influence of this sequence is clear in films like Hitchcock’s Vertigo (1958).

description:
This Is Congo - Free Screening (Congo Week), Please join us for a free/koha in-person film screening of "This Is Congo", to raise awareness for Congo Week. There will also be an optional group discussion and light snacks provided (feel free to bring your own snacks too).
You can find more info below (including how to support if you can't attend).
NOTE: As we will be viewing and discussing potentially sensitive topics, this event will have an Open Door Policy. You may leave the venue at any time, for any reason, and will not be judged for doing so.
ABOUT THE DOCUMENTARY FILM:
"A whistle-blower, a patriotic military commander, a mineral dealer, and a displaced tailor share a glimpse of life amid Africa's longest continuing conflict."
WHAT IS CONGO WEEK?
Congo Week is on 19-25 October, where we commemorate the millions of lives lost in this ongoing genocide in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). It is also a time to celebrate the enormous humanity and environmental potential the beautiful country DRC has.
WHY ARE WE HOSTING THIS IN TE WHANGANUI-A-TARA, AOTEAROA (WELLINGTON, NEW ZEALAND)?
We are holding community film screenings during Congo Week to talk to each other as a community, and to help each other learn. As we support other causes/issues in Aotearoa/NZ and worldwide, we would like to increase solidarity for Congolese people.
We are buying, consuming, and benefitting from tech products/AI usage through child slavery and genocide of Congo. As long as there are customers of minerals found in the DRC, corporations will have an incentive to continue exploiting Congolese people for these minerals to be used in jewellery, batteries, e-cigarettes, and tech products like our phones and computers.
HOW MUCH IS THE TICKET?
The film screening is free but we appreciate koha for the Panzi Foundation (more info below).
WHY WOULD I WANT TO JOIN THE FILM SCREENING?
The film screening is for anyone keen to learn/watch a documentary film, wants to share their experience through optional group discussion, or wants to meet new people.
This event welcomes people from all walks of life who are willing to learn, listen, or contribute (LGBTQ+ friendly).
Before 7:45pm: Set up
7:45-8pm: Karakia, health and safety, organisers' introductions, brief explanation on Congo Week
8pm-9:30pm: "This Is Congo" screening (people can come and go at any time)
9:30pm-9:40pm: Moment of silence/meditation
9:40pm-10pm: Quick group discussion with optional participation (TBC if we can extend)
By 10pm: Pack down
WILL THERE BE MORE IN-PERSON/VIRTUAL FILM SCREENINGS IN THE FUTURE?
Yes, will most likely be in 2026 instead of this year. We would love to collaborate with other people/groups, so we can share our skills and knowledge collectively.
I CAN'T ATTEND. HOW CAN I SUPPORT?
Please spread the word via social media stories, reposting, wheatpasting, or sharing to people who don't use social media (Instagram post here).
If you click RSVP, there is an option to donate without getting a ticket. We sincerely appreciate this.
You can RSVP to the 22 Oct 2025 film screening here.
If you click "Contact host" below, feel free to send us your email address and we can email resources after the event, e.g.:
Use refurbished tech products (instead of new ones)
Alternatives to Google/Microsoft mail/maps/calendar/forms/etc
Alternatives to Spotify/Apple Music
Reducing generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) usage at work/personal life
If using Google as your search engine, add "-ai" at the end of your searches (to stop showing AI results)
Actions and Instagram accounts to follow
WHERE WILL THE KOHA GO TOWARDS?
Koha that we receive will go to the Panzi Foundation.
The Panzi Foundation has opened hospitals, mobile clinics, and the City of Joy, a sanctuary where women learn healing, empowerment and leadership through their traumas. Rape is a weapon of war used against the Congolese people.
The Panzi Foundation is one of the largest African-led nonprofits and is committed to addressing the devastating impacts of sexual and gender based violence through a holistic, survivor-centred approach.
The Panzi Foundation was founded by Dr. Denis Mukwege, who is considered one of the leading experts in injuries of rape and was awarded a Nobel Peace Prize in 2018, 6 years after an assassination attempt on his life.
WHO ARE THE EVENT ORGANISERS?
This event is organised by ordinary community members affiliated with Te Tai-Tētēkura (an indigenous, youth-led group in Aotearoa/NZ).
Te Tai-Tētēkura is founded on the principles of revolution through education and restoration of power to the people. They hold a foundational community-based kaupapa that prioritises uplifting, connecting, and empowering our communities.
Te Tai-Tētēkura's founding is based on the socialist and revolutionary politics of the Black Panther Party, which rose to prominence during the Black Power Movement in the U.S. They combine the Black Panther Party's ideas with Te Tiriti o Waitangi, and their own landback and decolonisation principles.
Through community initiatives, Te Tai-Tētēkura shows the people that we as a community can take care of our society.
We stand in solidarity with indigenous peoples in Aotearoa/NZ, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), and across the world facing injustice.
Please click "Contact host" if you have questions/feedback/concerns or if you can't attend anymore.

description:
Toitu: Visual Sovereignty film screening, Toi Tū Toi Ora: Contemporary Māori Art was the largest Māori exhibition in the history of Auckland Art Gallery and attracted attendance levels not seen by the gallery since 1989. Chelsea Winstanley’s documentary follows the journey of curator Nigel Borell as he navigates the constraints between institutional authority and Māori self-determination.
Chelsea Winstanley’s documentary follows the journey of curator Nigel Borell as he navigates the constraints between institutional authority and Māori self-determination. Borell’s curatorial vision is clear – Māori art must be authored, not simply advocated for. For the artists, this represents a chance to be seen on their own terms and is an initiative that ultimately leads some to the global stage of the Venice Biennale. 
But as the scale of the exhibition grows, so does the institutional resistance. The result is a reckoning: whose story is being told, and who holds the pen? With many of the artworks exploring the legacy of colonialism, the making of the exhibition itself becomes a living reflection of that very struggle. Laying bare behind-the-scenes conversations rarely seen on screen, TOITŪ Visual Sovereignty lifts the curtain on the inner workings of an institution and examines the cost of visibility without control – and the quiet power of walking away. — Heperi Mita 
The screening will be followed by a Q and A with Director Chelsea Winstanley.

description:
Twin Peaks: Fire Walk With Me, "Faster and faster. And for a long time you wouldn't feel anything. And then you'd burst into fire" - Laura Palmer
TWIN PEAKS: FIRE WALK WITH ME.
DAVID LYNCH | USA & FRANCE | 1992 | 135mins | R18+| 4K DCP PROVIDED BY JANUS FILMS DISTRIBUTION
Join us for this very special community fundraiser screening of the prequel to the critically acclaimed series, "Twin Peaks".
ABC cancelled the original series after season 2 but a month later, Lynch announced he was "not yet finished with the material" and principal photography for the full length prequel film, began on September 5th 1991 at a caravan site in Snoqualmie Washington. Which became the "Fat Trout Trailer Park" where the story of the last 7 days of Laura Palmer begins.
Since its showing at the 1992 Festival De Cannes, no other Lynch film had polarized audiences to such an extent. Fans that wanted more "Cherry Pie" and "Donuts" from the TV show were served a much darker, unflinching and unforgiving work - in Lynch's own words, a movie about "the loneliness, shame, guilt, confusion and devastation of the victim". Derided by critics and many fans at the time it was a commercial box office flop.
Yet in the years since the initial reaction, a gradual wave of reappraisal and appreciation began. With time it's brilliance came into focus with growing acknowledgment, that the film is a more accurate, complex and powerful account of trauma. Combining the dramatic ferocity of Sherly Lee's tour de force and the beauty of Angelo Badalamenti's score, Lynch reclaimed full ownership of the material creating a harrowing, compassionate and enigmatic hymn to Laura Palmer.
As we approach the films 34 year anniversary and since Lynch's passing in 2025, it is now regarded by critics and fans worldwide, as a revered epilogue, essential predecessor to "The Return", and Lynch's most chilling, terrifying, and yet empathetic and humane cinematic masterpiece.
WHERE: The Roxy Cinema. 5 Park Road. Miramar. Wellington.
Cinema 1 - The big cinema upstairs with the massive screen, red italian leather sofas, and of course those red curtains!
WHEN: Wed 25th Feb 2026. Seating is unreserved so arrive early to check-in at the table upstairs, enter the raffle and get seated.
8:15pm - Doors close and the film starts. (no trailers)

COST: Tickets are $20 per person. (plus booking fee). This is a not for profit community screening put on for the pure love of Twin Peaks and the fans. All proceeds go to help pay for the cinema hire and licensing the film with any extras donated to charity. So spread the word and come celebrate "Twin Peaks Day 2026"!
TWIN PEAKS RAFFLE: Check-in at the desk upstairs and get a complimentary raffle ticket, to enter into the draw for 1 of these companion books.
The Secret Diary of Laura Palmer - By Jennifer Lynch with foreword by Mark Frost & David Lynch (paperback, 2012 edition)
Fire Walk With Me: Your Laura Disappeared - By Scott Ryan with foreword by Jeff Jensen (paperback, 2022 edition)
Laura's Ghost: Women Speak about Twin Peaks - By Courtney Stallings with foreword by Sheryl Lee (paperback, 2020 edition)
Cutoff to enter is 8:10pm and prizes drawn just before the start of the film.
RULES:
1. Tickets are per person. There will be NO door sales at the Roxy, so DO purchase it beforehand please. 
2. The film is classified R18+. All attendees MUST be 18yo + and have ID
4. The Roxy have strict no BYO food/drinks. Only Food/drinks purchased at the Roxy can be taken into the screening.
3. This is a safe, friendly, INCLUSIVE place. There is ZERO tolerance for discrimination, disrespect or creepy gross behavior of any kind. By attending you agree to the Code of Conduct.
4. Arrive early to enter the raffle before the cutoff if you want to be in it to win it. Good Luck!
Thank you and Happy Twin Peaks Day!
Join us for more Twin Peaks community screenings at:
www.facebook.com/fishinthepercolator
www.instagram.com/fishinthe.percolator

description:
Victorian Photography Workshop with Brian Scadden, Victorian Photography Workshop with Brian Scadden
DATE: Sunday Sept 28
TIME: 9:30am-1:30pm
LOCATION: Cobblestones Museum, Greytown
AGES: Over 18
COST: $135 per person. Max 5 people.
Come and have a go at wet-plate collodion photography, using authentic materials to produce your own heirloom image as were made 170 years ago. This almost lost art produces one-of-a-kind images on tin or glass plates, which you create and have an image you’ve crafted to take away.

Brian Scadden will be your instructor for this workshop. Brain has been passionate about photography for over 40 years, beginning his career at the National Film Unit in the 1970s before joining Park Road Post Production as Head of Laboratory, Head of Picture, and Restoration Manager. His work in film sparked an interest in early photographic techniques, prompting him to master wet-plate collodion photography. In 2006, he was invited to assist leading wet-plate experts in the USA and has since taught many New Zealanders this challenging process. Jane, who attended Brian’s workshop in 2014, later married him in 2019 and completed a photographic project in Carterton in 2016.
Although Brian retired in 2015, he returned for short-term assignments at Park Road Post and part-time work at Archive NZ, supporting film archiving until mid-2023. Both Brian and Jane continue to shoot with 35mm and 120mm film using vintage cameras from their collection.

description:
Visual Takes: An evening with Getty Images (Wellington), Visual Takes: An evening with Getty Images
You know the story you want to tell. Getty Images will help you find the content to bring it to life.
After a successful event in Auckland, we are bringing this kaupapa down to Pōneke! Come along for an insider's look at Getty Images' comprehensive suite of services designed for directors, producers, art departments, researchers, and creative professionals across the industry. Whether it’s scripted or factual, Getty Images helps find the right content (fast), access archival gems or fresh contemporary visuals, navigate licensing and clearance, negotiating and pricing, and much more.
Our panelists are:
Arran Birchenough For over 25 years, Arran has been working with TV and Film producers in NZ, Australia, and APAC, and has been based in NZ for the last 20 years. Arran is responsible for the teams at Getty Images that support producers in NZ and across APAC with the range of Getty Images services and support, including free access to content to support getting funded, free research including from the TVNZ, BBC, NBC and ITN archives, advice on clearance, copyright, legal and licensing, and developing offerings to meet the needs of scripted and unscripted producers alike.
Sarah Bailey-Harper from Tenzing, The Luminaries and Sparticus joins to bring perspective from the art, set design, costume and textile departments of scripted productions, sharing her experience and knowledge when using creative content in pre-production and production.
Ruth Korver is an experienced producer who has worked across the full spectrum of content. Her production company Useful Media focuses mainly on factual content. Ruth has produced a number of TV series, documentaries and feature films for TV and cinema. Her most recent work includes feature documentary The Stolen Children of Aotearoa for Awa Films and premium factual series Hua Parakore - Fixing our broken food systems for Storybox. Ruth was a senior producer at creative agency Storybox for eight years and in that time worked on a number of commercial campaigns and visitor experiences.
Date: Wednesday 15th October
Location: Wētā Workshop Group Space, 129 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington 6022, New Zealand

Waifilmfest Presents Never Forgotten: the Marines of Masterton, Never Forgotten: The Marines of Masterton – Special Screening

After sold-out shows in May 2025, we’re bringing back Never Forgotten: The Marines of Masterton for one more special screening in Martinborough!

This feature-length local documentary tells the story of the United States Marine Corps’ 3rd Defense Battalion, who were stationed at Solway Showgrounds in Masterton in 1943 during World War II. Director Mark Pacey explores the Marines’ visit, the deep connections they formed with the local community, and their lasting legacy—including the journey to constructing a memorial in their honour.

Presented by Waifilmfest in partnership with Circus Cinema, Restaurant & Bar and the Wellington Historical Festival 2025, this is a unique opportunity to experience a powerful story of history, community, and remembrance.

Come and be part of this special event — one last chance to see it on the big screen!

Wairarapa Cinémathèque 2026 Presents METROPOLIS (1927), Metropolis (1927)
Sunday 5 April 2026, 7:30pm
Dir. Fritz Lang | Germany | 2h 3m | Silent | Sci-Fi | Drama

A towering achievement of early cinema, Metropolis is Fritz Lang’s visionary silent masterpiece: a film that continues to shape how we imagine the future.

Set in a vast, futuristic city sharply divided between privileged elites and oppressed workers, the story follows the ruler’s son as he meets Maria, a prophetic young woman who calls for understanding and compassion between the classes. What unfolds is an extraordinary spectacle of monumental design, groundbreaking special effects, and a deeply human moral vision.

Both epic and intimate, Metropolis is a powerful meditation on class, technology, and empathy. It is one of the most influential films ever made.

This special screening of METROPOLIS is presented in cooperation with the Goethe-Institut New Zealand.

Join the Wairarapa Cinémathèque. Memberships are available now, giving access to a curated programme of classic and significant films throughout 2026. Set amid the ruins of post-war Vienna, The Third Man follows pulp novelist Holly Martins (Joseph Cotten) as he investigates the suspicious death of his old friend Harry Lime (Orson Welles). With its iconic zither score, shadow-drenched cinematography, and unforgettable final act, this noir classic explores moral ambiguity in a fractured world.

This screening is presented as part of the programme for the Wairarapa Cinémathèque 2026.

Wairarapa Cinémathèque is dedicated to celebrating film as part of our artistic and cultural heritage. We value the communal experience of cinema, bringing people together through curated screenings, discussions, and the sharing of films of significance. Your membership ensures access to this shared experience, while providing benefits such as exclusive screenings and partner discounts.

Dir. Billy Wilder | USA | 2h | Comedy, Romance, Crime

After witnessing a Mafia hit, two Chicago musicians (Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon) flee the city disguised as women in an all-female jazz band bound for Florida. Chaos, romance, and mistaken identity follow; including Marilyn Monroe at her most luminous.

Hilarious, subversive, and endlessly quotable, Some Like It Hot is widely regarded as one of the greatest comedies ever made. Billy Wilder’s razor-sharp wit, dazzling performances, and audacious gender play still feel astonishingly fresh more than 65 years on.

This screening opens the 2026 Wairarapa Cinémathèque season.

description:
War on Drugs Film Screening, In remembrance of the victims of human rights violations and extrajudicial killings during the War on Drugs in the Philippines, please join us for a free/koha screening of "On the President's Orders" documentary in Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

NOTE: For a list of trigger warnings, please see this document. Since we will be viewing and discussing potentially sensitive topics, the event will have an Open Door Policy, which means that you may leave the venue any time, for any reason, and will not be judged for doing so.
WHAT IS THE WAR ON DRUGS?
Spearheaded by the former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte, the War on Drugs is a violent anti-drug campaign which killed nearly 30,000 Filipinos, most of which were urban poor (Karapatan, Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch).
WHAT ARE EXTRAJUDICIAL KILLINGS?
"Extrajudicial killings, or extrajudicial executions, happen when someone in an official position deliberately kills a person without any legal process" (World Organisation Against Torture).
WHY IS IT IMPORTANT TO TALK ABOUT TODAY?
Human rights violations and extrajudicial killings are still on-going in the Philippines under President Bongbong Marcos, the son of the dictator Ferdinand Marcos Sr. who proclaimed Martial Law in 1972, and Vice President Sara Duterte, the daughter of former President Rodrigo Duterte (Karapatan).
WHY WOULD I WANT TO JOIN THE FILM SCREENING?
The film screening is for anyone who is keen to learn about the War on Drugs, wants to share their experience during the War on Drugs (or something similar) through group discussion, wants to meet new people, wants to watch a Philippine film/documentary, or just wants to have snacks.
I WANT TO JOIN BUT I'M FROM TĀMAKI MAKAURAU / CHRISTCHURCH / THE PHILIPPINES.
We will stream the film through Zoom for viewers outside Te Whanganui-a-Tara, however, there may be internet and other technical difficulties during the event itself. Also please make sure to select the "Online" ticket option when RSVPing.
HOW MUCH IS THE TICKET?
The film screening is free but we appreciate koha for the venue/snacks/donations to Philippine non-governmental organisations (NGOs).
NOTE: This is an LGBTQ+ friendly event.

This panel brings together practitioners, academics, and critics, and will reflect on the role of film and television in helping us understand ourselves and each other.
Does film and television give us the chance to examine our values and culture? If the answer to this question is yes, then how are we doing? What have our stories on screen had to say about us in the past, and what are they saying about us now?

A fight for land, life, and the next generation.
Set deep in the heart of the Amazon, Indigenous chief Juma Xipaia fights to protect her people’s land from exploitation and destruction. Spanning years of activism and six assassination attempts, the film captures Juma’s historic appointment as Brazil’s first Secretary of Indigenous Rights, under President Lula. Hugo Loss, her husband and a former Special Forces ranger-turned-unwavering ally, leads dangerous operations against illegal gold miners. When Juma discovers she is pregnant, her battle takes on new urgency. Navigating impending motherhood, rising political responsibility, and Hugo’s high-risk missions, she is forced to confront the personal cost of resistance.

description:
Yo (Love is a Rebellious Bird), Doc Edge Festival 2026

She built a world to keep their story alive.
After Yo’s passing at 89, her 41-year-old friend, Anna, spends a decade obsessively building a detailed 1/3-scale version of Yo’s house with a miniature puppet of her inside. Anna re-constructs a magical space where Yo’s stories unfold, and their relationship continues. The film juxtaposes intimate vérité of Yo’s last year with Anna’s creative interpretations of her dramatic life stories. Born in Switzerland in 1924, Yo lived life on her own terms, defying expectations around sexuality, mothering, aging, and even death.

10 February 2026 Whisky Tasting, Whisky Tasting: 10 February 2026
Hosted by Matt Mueller

Let's get 2026 off to a great start by answering the question: "What affordable, 12 year-old whisky should I have in my whisky cabinet at home?" - a classic conundrum at an affordable price.  Having a look at a few classics, some new challengers, and a mystery bottle is going to be our way of welcoming in the New Year with our first whisky tasting of 2026.
Bunnahabhain and Glendronach are the stalwarts that always rise to the top of these type of lineups, but they will have challengers from Glenturret, Tamdhu and Tomatin!  Plus a mystery will be in the lineup to cause some havoc and challenge our expectations...

description:
11 November Whisky Tasting, Whisky Tasting: 11 November 2025
Hosted by Matt Mueller
On November 11, we will dive into the penultimate whisky tasting of the year: New Zealand whiskies!
New Zealand has a long and complex history with single malts, stretching all the way back to the earliest Scottish settlers in the 1830's.  Government regulations shut that down in the 1870's, however, it became revitablsed in the 1970's at the Willowbank Distillery in Dunedin.  Willowbank  shut down in 1997, but we have an early 1990's bottle to take a look at!
The New Zealand single malt industry started growing again in the mid-2000's and now has a thriving craft whisky scene on both islands.
In addition to the older style of whisky, we'll sample some contemporary whiskies from the likes of 8 Wired, Pokeno and a few others...
Please join me at the Seatoun Clubhouse at 7:30pm on November 11th, for this special tasting.  $60 per seat.  See you then,
Matt

description:
9 September Whisky Tasting, Whisky Tasting: 9 September 2025
Hosted by Matt Mueller
In September, we'll get back on track, away from the International Whiskies of our August tasting, and on to the Eastern Highlands of Scotland: Glendronach.
Named for the valley of the brambles surrounding the distillery, Glendronach was the second distillery to gain a legal whisky license, and is currently under the stewardship of Dr. Rachel Barrie, a legend in the whisky industry. Dr Barrie has recently revamped the Glendronach lineup, and we're going to see how she's doing: we'll try the previous 12 and 15 year--old bottlings against her new releases. She's worked her magic at Ben Riach, and we'll see how she's doing at Glendronach (I suspect quite well!). Additionally, we'll try the highland peated Glendronach, a departure from the familiar smokey peat of Islay. We'll expect a sweeter, softer style, bolstered by some sherry maturation.
Please join me for this wonderful tasting of Glendronachs:

description:
96 Originals, Celebrate a quarter-century of culinary excellence at Logan Brown’s 29th anniversary lunch, where the past meets the present in a delicious fusion of food and stories. Join Steve Logan and Shaun Clouston, alongside original Logan Brown team members Francois Febvre (La Cloche) and Shepherd Elliott (previously of Ti Kouka, Leeds Street Bakery, Shepherd, Concord and The Test Kitchen), for a special afternoon filled with fantastic kai and plenty of memories.

As the doors of Logan Brown first opened in 1996, it quickly became one of Wellington’s most beloved dining destinations. Now, this unforgettable event offers a chance to reminisce with the chefs who helped shape the restaurant’s legacy, sharing tales from the early days while serving up a feast of flavours inspired by their storied careers.

For any longtime Logan Brown fan or someone curious to the whakapapa of Wellington food, this is a celebration of the friendships, milestones, and moments that have defined one of New Zealand’s most iconic dining experiences. Expect a menu that reflects Logan Brown’s rich history, prepared with passion and paired with great conversation, laughter, and a few tall tales.

This six-course degustation alternates between the rich, wheat-based dishes of North India and the light, spicy, rice-based specialties of South India, reflecting centuries of regional tradition and coastal influence.
Each course is introduced by Chef Sushil, who shares the stories and family traditions behind the recipes that have been passed down over generations. Guests will enjoy a seated dinner where each dish highlights the iconic techniques, spices, and flavours that define its region.
The ticket includes the full six-course degustation, chef-led introductions, and a take-home gift bag with treats.

Inspired by the wines that grace state banquets and formal royal occasions of the British Royal Family, this intimate gathering draws from producers associated with the Royal Household. Bottles will be chosen for their pedigree, poise, and quiet authority. For one exclusive evening, Noble Rot’s cellar reflects the mysterious spirit of Buckingham Palace’s own, offering a rare opportunity to taste wines in the style of those served to the Monarchy and its most esteemed guests.

description:
Alexia Urban Winery Presents Bonjour Gimlet!, Alexia Urban Winery Presents Bonjour Gimlet! (A Sparkling French Affair)

Alexia is bringing a touch of France to Greytown with their sparkliest cocktail yet…the Alexia Bonjour Gimlet!

Sure, the original gin and lime juice Gimlet was invented by British Royal Navy surgeon Sir Thomas Gimlette to prevent navy sailors getting scurvy, but it was the French who made it classy with the addition of elderflower liqueur.

Alexia is taking their Gimlet a step further, giving it an effervescent twist – combining Greytown Distilling gin, the floral notes of elderflower liqueur, and fresh lime juice… then topping it off with Alexia Blanc de Noirs Méthode Traditionnelle. With a French-themed food menu to match, this is a Gimlet worth saying Bonjour to!

The French flags will be flying, the croque monsieurs will be magnifique, and the berets will be positioned at the jauntiest angle possible! This is your call to cancel all boring plans for March 21 and say ‘oui!’ to an afternoon of French joie de vivre at Alexia!

Always a Bridesmaid, Step into the world of <i>Bridesmaids<i> for a three-course feast that brings the film to life, literally. Zephyr is serving up a cinematic dining experience where every bite is perfectly timed with the on-screen action.
Expect to start with Annie’s mum’s famous artichoke dip, and an entree inspired by Lillian and Doug’s engagement party then get ready for the main event: the Brazilian feast (but guaranteed to be without the unfortunate side effects). And for dessert, it’s that cookie. The giant one. Gorgeous to share or go full meltdown mode — it’s your call. All paired with cocktails and drinks that complement the evening perfectly. After all, as Megan says, "I'm gonna climb that like a tree." And yes, by "that," we mean the drinks list. Mocktails available.
Like an exclusive invite to Lillian’s Parisian bridal shower, these tickets will disappear fast. So grab your besties, your worsties, or your slightly terrifying but well-meaning Megan, and join us for a night of food, film, and absolute chaos. Because sometimes, life calls for laughing until you cry, eating until you're full, and toasting to the love of your friendships that survive it all.

Expect a rotating spread of 10 to 15 pintxos built on Amuse’s sourdough baguette, topped with combinations like bacon and egg tortilla, pork belly with persimmon relish, seared tuna with kawakawa aioli, and classic gildas. Snacks are served quickly from the yellow window, ready to eat, with sticks tallied at the end.

Drinks stay close to the theme, with New Zealand vermouths, Spanish reds, and house cocktails designed for grazing. Drop in, eat well, and stay as long as you like.

description:
Art Flow: Dine & Discover, Following the success of the award-winning 'ArtFlow' programme at DoubleTree by Hilton Wellington, we invite you to join us for the third chapter of 'ArtFlow: Dine & Discover'; an intimate evening where visual art and culinary craft come together in a truly unique setting.

Developed in partnership with the New Zealand Academy of Fine Arts, 'ArtFlow' has recently been recognised with the Innovative Collaboration Award at the 2025 HM Awards, celebrating its distinctive approach to bringing together artists, hospitality, and the wider community. For this chapter of 'ArtFlow', Elder Pinot joins as an associate partner, bringing a curated selection of their wines to complement the evening’s culinary experience.

Learn more about the programme and award here:
https://nzafa.com/art-flow-winners-2025-hm-awards
https://www.cordonbleu.edu/news/participating-in-the-award-winning-art-flow/en

For this special evening we welcome Lynn Blann, whose artistic journey traces back to Auckland’s vibrant creative culture of the 1960s and 1970s. During this influential period, shaped by the Peace, Anti-War, Women’s and Māori rights movements - artists, writers, poets and musicians gathered in galleries such as the renowned Barry Lett Gallery. Surrounded by the emerging works of figures including McCahon, Hanly and Twiss, Lynn developed a deep connection to the artistic energy of the time.

Today, working in acrylics, charcoal and pastels, Lynn continues to translate these influences into contemporary abstract forms on canvas. Her work reflects a lifelong engagement with New Zealand’s creative culture, recently recognised with a Merit Award at the 2025 Academy Prize for Visual Art.

The evening begins at Grazie Italian Restaurant with a welcome drink and an opportunity to meet Lynn and fellow guests. A thoughtfully curated three-course dinner follows, with dessert prepared by Chef Aman Khanna and the team at Grazie Italian Restaurant, celebrating the culinary artistry that complements the visual experience. Selected wines from Elder Pinot will accompany the entrée and main courses in tasting portions, offering guests a refined introduction to the character and craftsmanship of this distinctive New Zealand wine label.

As the evening unfolds, guests will gain insight into Lynn’s artistic journey and inspirations before continuing the experience with a guided tour through the hotel’s 'ArtFlow' exhibition spaces, where the artworks come to life within the hotel’s beautifully restored heritage interiors.

Event Programme:
• Welcome drink on arrival
• Mix & mingle - meet featured artist Lynn Blann
• Three-course dinner at Grazie Italian Restaurant **paired with a range 'Elder Pinot' wines.
• Guided ArtFlow exhibition tour with the artist

**Wine pairings will be served as tasting portions. Guests are welcome to enjoy additional wines from the Elder Pinot range, available for purchase by the glass on the evening.

'ArtFlow: Dine & Discover' offers a rare opportunity to experience art beyond the canvas bringing together artists, cuisine and conversation in an elegant and intimate setting.

description:
Aurora Distillery Gin Experience, Create, make and take home your own gin with us at our Gin Experience sessions at our beautiful Wairarapa site, just 10 minutes from Martinborough. Our experienced distillery staff are on hand throughout to guide you through the process and give as much or as little advice as you want. We have hundreds of satisfied customers who have made some really exciting gins.

You’ll begin by foraging in the distillery gardens then we move to the gin-making room to learn about the gin making process and the ingredients involved. You’ll sample loads of botanicals then you will choose what you want to put in your very own gin recipe. After weighing out your recipe, you’ll move to your very own still and begin distilling!

While your gin is distilling, we’ll do a gin tasting of some of our own Arrival brand gins and some surprises from our other spirits.

At the end of the session you’ll bottle and seal your own 500ml bottle of gin to take home!

Please note each Experience attendee must have their own ticket. To ensure all participants have a great time and get our full attention we cannot accept spectators.

Bellbird Sings at The Dowse, A musical journey through art, stories, and seasonal food, with a touch of opera. 

Bellbird invites you beyond traditional dining into a sensory experience shaped by music, storytelling, and contemporary art. Inspired by the haunting song of the korimako (bellbird), you'll explore purakau (stories) through art and opera. Two-time Burger Wellington winner, Chef-owner Chetan Pangam crafts a menu celebrating Aotearoa's seasonal abundance: thoughtful integration of native ingredients, local produce, and refined Indian influences, all presented with an artistic lens. 

You'll arrive at Bellbird with a welcome drink and specially selected canapés, then move to the Dowse Art Museum for a private, behind-the-scenes guided tour with the gallery director, unlocking unique stories on display. A five-course sit-down dinner follows inspired by the art, matched with wines from Mishas Vineyard. Conversations flow from table to table, and each course reveals a new layer of meaning tied to land, memory, and identity. 

Your ticket includes a welcome drink, canapés, a five-course dinner, and five glasses of matched wine. Additional drinks available for purchase.

Join VHNZ Cuisine for a hands-on cooking workshop featuring Broken Rice with Grilled Pork Chop, Shredded Pork Skin & Egg Meatloaf (Cơm tấm sườn, bì, chả trứng) — one of southern Vietnam’s most loved comfort dishes.



In this session, you’ll learn how to prepare each key component: marinated grilled pork chop, fragrant shredded pork skin, soft savoury egg meatloaf, and perfectly cooked broken rice. We’ll also share the cultural story behind cơm tấm and why this humble dish holds such a special place in Vietnamese everyday life.



This is a relaxed, community-led workshop where you’ll cook together, learn traditional techniques, and enjoy a shared meal at the end. No prior cooking experience needed — just curiosity and an appetite.



To help keep these classes sustainable and support ongoing community activities, there will be an additional $10 contribution per class.

This helps cover:

• Facilitator effort and preparation

• Admin and coordination work

• The ability to continue running and expanding community workshops



This class is delivered in collaboration with I Love Viet Food, and made possible thanks to the generous support and sponsorship from:



* Hutt City Council

description:
Bánh Mì Workshop: Open to all VUW Staff & Students, Bánh Mì Workshop: Open to all VUW Staff & Students
To commemorate the 81st National Day of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, we invite VUW staff and students to a hands-on Vietnamese Bánh Mì workshop. Come together to celebrate culture, community, and cuisine through one of Vietnam's most beloved street foods.

WHAT THIS WORKSHOP COVERS

- The history and cultural significance of bánh mì
- Learn how to make Vietnamese chicken liver and VEGAN paté, egg yolk and VEGAN mayonnaise, pickled carrot and daikon
- Prepare and assemble your own bánh mì

WHAT YOU WILL GET

- Hands-on guidance in making an authentic Vietnamese bánh mì
- A freshly made bánh mì to enjoy during the workshop
- A take-home recipe card with ingredients and step-by-step instructions
- Opportunities to connect with fellow VUW staff and students in a fun, inclusive environment

FACILITATOR

This workshop is facilitated by Yung Nguyen from I Love Vietfood, in partnership with Viet Hub NZ.

SUPPORTING COMMUNITY THROUGH FOOD

Your koha helps support our VUW Chaplaincy venue host and Viet Hub NZ's community initiatives, including free community meals, cultural activities, and educational programmes.

Join us and celebrate the sweetness of tradition, creativity, and community

Join cake expert, Lina, for a hands-on cake building and decorating workshop where creativity meets craftsmanship!
With over 20 years of experience in the culinary and hospitality industries - from managing restaurants across Europe and Asia to running her own cake design business - Lina brings not only technical expertise, but also a genuine passion for sharing the joy of decorating.

description: Capital of Kai, How did Wellington become a culinary paradise? Capital of Kai tells the story through 100 years of Wellington's food creatives, restaurant workers, and café culture. It's a love letter to the hospo whānau who have shaped the city. Walk through galleries of heritage treasures: the Green Parrot's working griddle, Hiakai's light-up signage, Il Casino's couch, Shanghai restaurant's 1980s menu, the Matterhorn café's cowbell. You'll see the arc from 1930s British hotel dining (roast mutton, boiled vegetables, milky tea) through European influences brought home by migrants and travellers, and the diverse cuisines - Chinese, Malaysian, Indian, Syrian, Greek, Māori - that define Wellington now. Hungry for more? Feed your curiosity at Capital of Kai.

Central Vietnam Fish Noodle Soup | Bún Cá Miền Trung, If you love light, fresh, and vibrant food, this workshop is for you.
Join Viet Hub NZ for a hands-on cooking experience inspired by the coastal summers of Central Vietnam, where bowls of Bún Cá Miền Trung are enjoyed to cool down, reconnect, and nourish the body. This fish noodle soup is fragrant yet gentle, packed with herbs, tomatoes, and clean flavours that feel perfect for warmer days.
In this workshop, you’ll cook alongside others in a relaxed, welcoming space — learning not just the recipe, but the story, rhythm, and balance behind the dish. It’s the kind of food that feels comforting without being heavy, and exciting without being complicated.

• Fresh, summery flavours that are easy to recreate at home
• Beginner-friendly, hands-on learning
• Cultural stories woven into the cooking
• A shared meal that brings people together
• Take home what you cook to enjoy later

description:
Chance Luck & Magic 2024 Release, Be the first to taste Chance, Luck & Magic 2024, the latest iteration of one of our proudest achievements.

On Saturday 18 October, you can come and taste the beer in our Wild Workshop, the place where it was made. Brewers Pete and Dave will be on hand from 2pm to raise the first toast and tell you all a little about how this year’s blend came to be. We’ll also pull a couple of other goodies from the cellar to keep you and CLM company.

And, to top it off, our friends at Nomames Tacos will be here for the edible pairings.

This beer is the ultimate expression of Wild Workshop’s inner-city terroir, and the 2024 bottle is no different; a blend of five years of 100% spontaneously fermented brews, aged in French oak. The result is a complex and truly unique drop that harnesses the natural character of Pōneke.

We love this beer, and we’re so chuffed that other people do too - we’re very honoured that Chance, Luck & Magic, in its various vintages, has garnered global recognition and become one of our most prestigious creations:
Silver medals at both the 2023 and 2024 World Beer Cup (huge!)
Four consecutive gold medals at the New Zealand Beer Awards, as well as two trophies for Champion European Ale, and the Champion Beer title in 2022
Champion International Beer at the 2024 Australian International Beer Awards

The release of each new edition has become a landmark annual event for us, a chance to take a moment and appreciate the beautiful things that come from the wild workings of the environment.

Come and celebrate with us!
label: Food & Drink

description:
Chapel o' Burnin' Love, Elvis has left the building and he's now in Titahi Bay, running a wedding chapel just for you. This is a truly unique experience where you can either live out your dream of getting married in a Las Vegas wedding chapel either just for fun, or legally. Arrive in a convertible Cadillac with bubbles in hand, step into a sanctuary where the King himself is celebrant, MC, photographer, and musical send-off rolled into one gloriously ridiculous evening.

After the ceremony (legally binding or symbolic, your choice), newlyweds are seated for a refined take on Elvis's signature sandwich: peanut butter mousse, candied bacon, and banana on brioche. Tater tots on the side. A slice of red velvet wedding cake to cut and share. Elvis karaoke and Elvistravaganza festivities carry the night forward, because what else would you do after getting married in a chapel run by the King?

Wedding packages vary; you can have an Elvis commitment ceremony just for fun, a vow renewal for a bit more seriousness (with a bit of help beforehand) but also
an Aoteroa New Zealand Legal wedding/union is available - ticketholders will be contacted to make confirm all the details are just right - and will get extra pre-time with the celebrant to get all the proper legal details done.

Wedding tickets are per couple and include: transport in the Cadillac, glass of travelling bubbles, wedding ceremony and certificate, breakfast, wedding cake, photographs, wedding album, sandwich, sides, cake slice, and one cocktail or non-alcoholic alternative. Additional alcohol is available for purchase.

description:
Cheesemaking - Brie And Queso Fresco, During this intensely practical, hands-on workshop, you will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Double Cream ‘NZ style’ Brie. You will also be shown how to make Queso Fresco cheese which you will get to sample afterwards. All ingredients included in course fee.

The ultimate class in practical cheese making! Learn all you need to know to replicate making NZ style Brie and Queso Fresco at home. You will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Brie. Then, while the Brie is ripening and setting (don't worry, all terminology will be explained!), we will make Queso Fresco together.

All ingredients are provided as are recipes and detailed handouts to take away with you. Bring an apron, a dishcloth, 3 or 4 tea towels, a pen to take notes and a 2 litre container and plastic re-sealable food bags to take your cheese home.

During the workshop, the following topics will also be covered: Milk and where to source it, hygiene and sanitation, equipment required and the origins of the cheeses you are about to make. You will also receive comprehensive instruction on how to mature your Brie cheese over the next few weeks.

A small break will be provided and you will have the opportunity to purchase equipment and cheesemaking ingredients after the workshop should you wish to replicate the experience at home.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Make Brie and Queso Fresco
- Recall the best milk to use and where to source it from
- Name and identify what equipment and ingredients you need to make Brie and Queso Fresco

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

1 Day
Presented by Alexis Murti.

During this hands-on workshop, you’ll be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of farmhouse style cheddar.
The fee includes a cheese press (value $95.00) which can be used every time you want to make a hard cheese. It holds up to 6 litres of milk and this is what you’ll be taking your cheese home in to press for 12 hours after the workshop. All ingredients, recipes and a full set of course notes are provided.
You’ll also receive comprehensive instruction on how to wax (if you choose to) and then mature your cheese over the next five weeks. Alexis will also demonstrate how to make halloumi cheese which will then be grilled for you to enjoy! There’ll be a short lunch break and cheese making supplies such as wax will be available to purchase.
By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:
• Describe the basics of sanitisation and hygiene
• Recognise the difference between raw and pasteurised milk and know where to source them
• Make a round of cheddar cheese using a cheese press
• Describe how to wax and mature the cheese
• Describe how to make halloumi, following a demonstration

This intimate, hands-on experience is designed for anyone who loves good food, great company, and, of course, cheese!

description:
Chicken Porridge with Shredded Chicken Salad | Cháo Gà cùng Gỏi Gà, Cháo gỏi gà is a comforting Vietnamese classic that pairs two contrasting elements on one table:
• Cháo gà – a light, nourishing rice porridge slowly cooked with chicken, ginger, and aromatics
• Gỏi gà – a refreshing shredded chicken salad with herbs, onion, and tangy dressing
Together, they reflect a very Vietnamese way of eating: balance, simplicity, and sharing. This dish is often enjoyed when families gather, when someone needs comfort, or when the weather calls for something gentle yet satisfying.
What You’ll Experience
• Learn how to cook smooth, flavourful chicken porridge from scratch
• Prepare a fresh Vietnamese shredded chicken salad with herbs and dressing
• Understand the cultural meaning of serving cháo and gỏi together
• Share a warm meal and stories around food, just like at home
Who This Is For
• Anyone curious about Vietnamese home cooking
• Families and community members looking for a relaxed, hands-on experience
• People who enjoy healthy, seasonal, and comforting food
No prior cooking experience needed. This is a welcoming, community-led workshop.
Ticket Information
• $10 per person – contributes to ingredient costs and facilitator effort
• Optional koha/donation welcome to support VHNZ Cuisine community programmes
Acknowledgements
With thanks to our community partners, volunteers, and supporters who make it possible for VHNZ Cuisine to continue sharing Vietnamese food, stories, and connection.

description:
Classical by Candlelight, Candlelight is the only way to experience centuries-old music properly, and The Night Watch, Wellington's premier early music ensemble, know this. So for one night only, in collaboration with National Candles, in a concert steeped in candlelight, this is your chance to go back in time. Keep your phones pocketed and let the modern world recede for a few hours.

Bringing together Australasia's top specialists in early music, The Night Watch perform on period instruments: harpsichord, viola da gamba, and others from a tradition that predates the modern orchestra entirely. The evening features countertenor Austin Haynes and soprano Carleen Ebbs, two of New Zealand's top vocalists. Heard live in a candlelit room, you'll experience this music beyond anything a recording could do. The candles themselves are courtesy of National Candles, one of New Zealand's oldest candle makers, handcrafting their wares for over half a century.
At The Runholder in Martinborough, a three-course family-style menu built for sharing and unhurried conversation. The food is warm and generous: rich winter flavours.

Your ticket includes a welcome drink on arrival and three courses. Additional drinks are available to purchase on the night.

description:
Club Tropicana, This August, Beach Babylon becomes Club Tropicana, a retro, romantic escape inspired by 1960s tropical honeymoons, classic tiki bars and vintage beach glamour. Picture golden sunsets, flamingos, thatched umbrellas and the carefree buzz of a sun-soaked getaway, right in the heart of Wellington. No passport required.

The menu is vibrant and full of escapist flair. Start with coconut prawns and banana blossom kokoda, then dive into mains like mango glazed  pork rib rack or the tropical tofu paneer curry. Save room for dessert: pineapple upside-down pudding or a coconut rum fondue to bring the tropical fantasy to a sweet finale. Behind the bar, the tiki and kava-spiked cocktails flow freely, from Blue Hawaiian’s to retro rum punches, all dressed to impress with flamingo stirrers, umbrellas and tropical garnishes.

A golden-age soundtrack sets the mood, featuring the smooth calypso of Harry Belafonte, beachy vibes from The Beach Boys, and sun-drenched classics by Astrud Gilberto.

Club Tropicana is a winter getaway, fun and fabulously over the top.

description: Cognac vs Armagnac, Noble Rot sommelier Maciej Zimny has a undeniable passion for brandy, and he is yearning to share that with you. Maciej will guide you on an educational journey through this fascinating world focusing on the most prestigious French regions for brandy production: Cognac and Armagnac. He’ll provide detailed insight into the appellations, distillation and ageing processes, differences in oak maturation and why one region focuses on vintage expressions while the other ages blends for several years in barrel. But don’t worry, this isn’t a classroom affair—they'll be pouring 8 different spirits paired to a unique three-course menu to showcase Maciej’s knowledge, and he’ll even teach you the sommelier’s techniques for how to taste spirits correctly. Fall in love with brandy, find your favourite and next time you’re ordering a nightcap you can show off your new-found knowledge to your friends.

description:
Cooking Class: Sri Lankan cutlets, Cooking Class: Sri Lankan cutlets
Sri Lanka has been hit with devastating floods, and thousands of families have lost their homes and livelihoods overnight. 100% of this events proceeds will going to disaster relief in Sri Lanka.

Come join us, learn the art of Sri Lankan cutlet-making, eat well, and make a difference at the same time. Good food. Good people. A real impact when it’s needed most.

For any questions, please email

Can You Stop at One? (We dare you!)
A Sri Lankan cutlet is history disguised as a snack. European croquettes crash-landed on the island centuries ago, and Sri Lankans didn’t just borrow the idea — they rewired it. Fish and potato for thrift, chilli and mustard seed for heat, curry leaf and lime for brightness, all sealed in breadcrumbs and fried in coconut oil. One bite tells you everything about the island: layered trade routes, colonial collisions, ingenuity in the kitchen, flavour turned into defiance. It’s super-tasty — crisp, molten, impossible to stop at one.

Now you get to make your own and learn a bit about Sri Lankan culture.

We’re running a hands-on cutlet class where flavour is learned by instinct, not measuring spoons. You mix, taste, adjust, and chase that perfect balance of heat, comfort and citrus brightness. We bring every ingredient; you bring an appetite and the willingness to get your hands involved.

We’re being hosted by the crew at The Beer Engine — and their Yuzu Hazy is the move. Bright and citrusy, it slices through the richness and wraps around the spice in a way that makes you sit back and swear under your breath. When the frying’s done, we sit together and eat your creations with simple rice and Aiyō dhal. Big flavour, cold beer, good people. The kind of night food lovers remember.

description:
Cooking Classes, Authentic Indian cooking classes in Wellington with panaromic views over Wellington Harbour.

In each class, you will learn 4-5 recipes like: potato stuff roti, roasted eggplant curry, wholemeal, roti, naan; shahi paneer; dhal, samosa; palak paneer; gourmet chickpeas; vegetable korma; gulab jamun; kheer; mango lassi; masala chai, and many more...

The classes start at 6 pm or 10:30 am on weekends and weekdays with a 2-hour session followed by a dinner or lunch afterwards. The ingredients, copies of recipes, organic karma drink will be provided with a full course meal in a banquet setting. Custom made classes available for gluten free, dairy free and any other food intolerance and dietary requirements.The ingredients, recipes, complimentary organic karma drinks will be provided with a full course meal.

There are 2 to 8 people in each class in purpose built cooking studio. Also a private cooking classes available.

The menu for the class can be:

1) Spicy potato stuffed paratha and roti, rajasthani tomato relish, aalu matter or spicy peas- potato curry, roasted cumin yogurt raita and fresh mint- coriander chutney.

2) Shahi Paneer (cottage cheese cubes with spices and rich tomato-cashew gravy), garlic coriander naan, cumin jeera basmati rice and sweet fragrant rice pudding with cardamom. Also I will teach how to make fresh paneer.

3) Roasted eggplant curry, plain whole wheat chapatti or roti, jeera aaloo or potato curry, Tuar dahl (split yellow lentil) and Basmati rice with homemade pickle.

4) Palak paneer (creamy spinach curry with cubes of paneer), jeera rice (basmati rice with fragrant spices, panjabi chhole or spicy chickpeas curry and mango lassi. Also fresh paneer making.

5) Khadi (chickpeas fritters in yogurt and chickpeas flour soupy gravy), Aloo-Gobhi (cauliflower and potato curry),  savoury wraps with herbs and spices, fresh pickle and basmati rice.

The total cost is $130 per person, this includes ingredient cost. (As an alternative we also sell cooking class gift vouchers.The food options are unlimited and the class provides fresh and best ingredients)
For booking a class please contact indiancooking@xtra.co.nz

Just bring your taste buds! and Enjoy!!

description:
Crying Tiger, Charcoal smoke, sizzling meat, and you're in Nong Khai, a small northeast Thai town where families gather around the grill for Crying Tiger steak. Beef steak marinated 48 hours in coriander root, garlic, black pepper, oyster sauce, palm sugar, whiskey, and mandarin juice, char-grilled until the meat weeps with its own juices.
The chef grew up cooking this dish with family and friends. It arrives with sticky rice and a Northern Thai Isarn dipping sauce of tamarind, lime juice, ground chillies, and fresh coriander. Alongside: a sharp granny smith apple salad dressed with chilli and fish sauce, topped with prawns; and tom zapp, slow-cooked pork soft bones that melt into a soup fragrant with kaffir lime, lemongrass, and ground rice.

Named after her hometown of Delhi and her home postcode, this special menu is a deeply personal tribute to her upbringing and a childhood immersed in the rich culinary traditions of North India. Chandrika brings the heart and soul of Delhi to Wellington with a generous, share-style multi-course menu featuring bountiful vegetarian plates and an exceptional lamb raan.

Expect an explosion of flavour, with exotic spice blends, saffron, citrus and native berries woven into every dish. In North India, condiment is king, and this feast will be served with a vibrant array of chutneys, pickles and relishes. To complete the experience, Chandrika has also designed a beautifully curated drinks menu to complement the bold and fragrant dishes.

description:
Dark Beer Week 2026, Dark Beer Week 2026

Got milk? We have! The cows have finally come home, they’re all here, and it’s time for Dark Beer Week 2026.

Head to GP Aro and GP Kingsland between June 2-8 for a week stacked with velvety stouts, porters and their kin.

Headlining Dark Beer Week this year is a brand new release and your new favourite stout: Black Milk. A good, honest imperial oat milk stout, sweet and creamy and full-bodied and loaded to the teats with rich, malty character. It’s your first chance to try this addition to our core lineup. Get to know each other before it hits the supermarket aisles.

But that’s not all:
Black Denim will be appearing as a limited-release smoked maple pecan porter
Sova is making its first foray, a Czech dark lager, cold-conditioned at length and perfectly suited to the side-pour taps

And, to top it all off, a bevvy of beloved rebrews: Cereal Milk Stout, Aro Noir, Iron Pig, Dr Pete’s and Snug all on tap, Great Deluge and 12 Anniversary Quad as bottle pours, and even Tiny Stout for a non-alcoholic treat.

description:
Dessert First, For Chef Shuchi dessert has always been the most emotional part of a meal. It's where people slow down, and where conversation softens. For this event you're encouraged to skip right to dessert for this five course dessert tasting menu each tied to a memory. Some from Shuchi's life, some shared in our collective memories, all rooted in the small, often overlooked moments that shape how we experience sweetness.

Raspberry panna cotta tastes like school lunches and summer berries. Rich brownie with hazelnut mousse is the sweet thing you crave after a long day. The lemon cake that became Le Ciel's bestseller without anyone realising. Apple crumble soufflé carries memories of Shuchi's grandmother. Passionfruit posset brings the taste of home from Tanzania. Each course is plated with technique and restraint, refined, but never losing its warmth or intent. You'll spend an evening in the warm, slow space where dessert deserves to be.

Your ticket includes five plated courses plus one palate cleanser.

description:
Dinner With Dionysus, For this five-course degustation, Head Chef Nicolas Mentzas draws on his Greek heritage to present the flavours and textures of home through a refined, fine-dining lens. Often perceived as relaxed and informal, there is a quiet depth to Greek cuisine. It is shaped by season, coastline, mountain herbs, and generations gathered around the table.
Dinner unfolds as a carefully composed menu that honours tradition while embracing precision in one of the world’s oldest wine cultures. Rather than a shared feast, expect elevated dishes rooted in Greek culinary history, reinterpreted with elegance and detail. Each course is paired with Greek wines, highlighting distinctive indigenous grape varieties and the growing confidence of the country’s modern producers.
Throughout the evening, the Noble Rot sommelier team will introduce each pairing, exploring how Greece’s food and wine traditions complement one another in perfect harmony, at the highest level.
Your ticket includes an amuse bouche on arrival, five courses, an arrival wine, and seven Greek wines paired throughout the evening.

Join us for an interactive tasting led by wine writer and educator Joelle Thomson, as we explore a curated selection of Te Muna wines from a variety of producers.

You will be picked up from the Square in Martinborough and driven to the stunning Escarpment vineyard. Joelle will guide you through a tasting of twelve of Te Muna wines. The experience concludes with a relaxed opportunity to revisit some of your favourites while meeting several of the producers, before being transported back to the Square.

description:
Discover Te Muna - Explore the Wines, Te Muna means secret place in Maori. We want to let you into the secret of the Te Muna Valley wines.

Te Muna valley, just east of Martinborough, is not the easiest place to grow grapes. The winds and the temperatures test us.  But the micro climate and the unique soil structure help us produce exceptional wines with a distinctive style.

Join us for a small group, interactive tasting led by wine writer and educator Joelle Thomson, as we explore a curated selection of Te Muna wines from a variety of producers. Craggy Range, Escarpment, Big Sky, Blue Earth Estate and more.

You will be picked up from the Square in Martinborough and driven to the stunning Craggy Range Te Muna Estate vineyard where Joelle will guide you through a tasting of twelve of Te Muna wines. The experience concludes with a relaxed opportunity to revisit some of your favourites from the tasting while meeting several of the producers, before being transported back to the Square.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Discover Te Muna - Go Behind the Scenes in April, Join us for a full-day immersive experience in the viticulture, winemaking and wines of Te Muna Valley. Walk the vineyards, meet the producers, go behind the scenes and taste exceptional wines right where they are made.

Tickets are limited to twenty people to ensure that this is an intimate experience, taking you to places that are not normally open to the public.

Your tour begins with pickup from Martinborough Square, leading to a special start at Big Sky Wines. Kath and Jeremy will take you through a hands-on experience of their vineyard and winery. From there, visit the stunning Blue Earth Estate vineyard and olive grove. Margaret and Mike will entertain you with stories of their journey and explain how they grow their olives and grapes. You will then indulge in a long, relaxed lunch accompanied with a glass of wine. Some of the region's winemakers will join us to share their stories and answer your questions. The adventure continues with an insiders' look at the state of the art winery at Escarpment. Rowan will walk you through the process of how grapes are transformed into their wines. description:
Dragons Is My Uso, Chef Jessica Tang and legendary home chefs Litia Lefaoseu and Iutita Mallon are drawing on the century long fusion of Chinese and Samoan cuisine and the way food expresses love, ai, and alofa. In the late 1800s, small numbers of Chinese settled in Samoa and became part of a growing multicultural community. There they influenced local customs, made an enduring contribution to Samoan cuisine introducing contemporary favourites such as sapasui (chop suey), keke pua‘a (pork buns) and of course laisa (rice). 

Dragons celebrate this cultural and culinary fusion by showcasing these favourites and presenting new dishes highlighting the shared love of culinary staples such as taro and noodles, rice, fish, and pork, the magnificent spectrum of Chinese herbs, spices and flavours. Through cooking and sharing food together the chefs honour their culinary heritage, strengthen our connections to one another and celebrate the big and little moments in life. This is a shared-style meal, served banquet style on lazy Susan turntables. 
Dragons is My Uso was one of the sell-out hits of the 2024 festival - don't miss out!

Discounted tables for 10 available for $1000, so get the whole aiga together!

description:
Due Isole, Join Chef Giulio Ricatti for an extraordinary evening celebrating the bond between two islands — Sardinia and New Zealand. Through a carefully curated nine-course dinner, this event offers a personal and heartfelt exploration of identity, place, and the connection between land and sea.

Raised in Sardinia and now at home in New Zealand, Chef Ricatti shares his story through a menu that bridges the wild, untouched landscapes of both countries. Each course is crafted exclusively with New Zealand ingredients, reflecting the rich bounty of our land and sea, yet inspired by the timeless traditions and bold flavours of Sardinian cuisine.

Accompanying the meal is an expertly selected pairing of wines from Sardinia and New Zealand, highlighting the unique characteristics of each region while celebrating their shared essence. The thoughtful combination of food and drink creates a dialogue between the two islands, offering diners a chance to taste the harmony of contrasts.

More than just a meal, this is an evening of storytelling. Chef Ricatti invites you to journey with him as he reflects on the places that have shaped his life and the meaning of finding a home across oceans. His philosophy of embracing the present moment is woven into every dish, making this event a sensory and emotional experience.

Whether you’re a lover of fine dining, an admirer of Sardinian culture, or simply curious about the connections between food and identity, this dinner promises a night of discovery. Step into the heart of two islands and savour their soul in one unforgettable evening.

Découvrez Orléans - Workshop & Tasting, Overview



Join us and learn more about this beautiful town!
🌿 In the heart of the Centre-Val de Loire, along the banks of the Loire river, lies Orléans. A historic city of medieval streets, grand cathedrals and a legacy that helped shape the destiny of France.
This is the France of Jeanne d'Arc: the young heroine who, in 1429, freed the city from siege and helped turn the tide of the Hundred Years' War so decisively at the Battle of Patay that the French expression "mettre la pâtée" (to thrash someone) is said to trace back to it. Wander through the medieval old town, admire the soaring Cathédrale Sainte-Croix, the statues honouring Jeanne d'Arc, the lively place du Martroi and its historic carousel.
Join Lou for a fun and immersive workshop (en français !) and step into the history, traditions and art de vivre of Orléans from the famous Fêtes de Jeanne d'Arc to the Festival de Loire, and the region's culinary treasures: the wines of the Centre-Val de Loire, Orléans mustard, and the beloved Pithiviers.
And of course, we'll wrap up with a tasting of delicious traditional treats from the region!

description:
Edible Idioms, Language and food belong together, add history and the story deepens into something altogether different. Lustre's taking the words we use every day and turning them into dishes. Cool as a cucumber becomes a palate cleanser, a piece of cake arrives as something entirely new, and every course speaks to the way culture lives in how we talk about food.

Seven courses of interpretation, each one teasing out a different idiom from around the world. There's a German one about sausage and indifference, an Indian one about something fishy in the pulses, moments where the kitchen challenges and entertains in equal measure. One surprise dish waits mid-evening, your job is to guess which idiom it is. The menu shifts with the seasons and the whims of Lustre's local farms, but the game never changes: food as language, language as history.

Your ticket covers the seven-course Lustrous banquet menu and an idiom-inspired arrival drink. Alcohol is available to purchase.
