description:
Entre Calles, Cuba Street Tavern owner Rich spent eight trips wandering Barcelona's backstreets, finding treasured and memorable venues, not because they were advertised but because someone leaned in and said, "trust me, you need to try this place". Entre Calles recreates that feeling through shared tapas, Spanish-inspired drinks and music. 

Tapas arrive in waves across shared tables while DJs spin Spanish tracks. Nobody's ordering from a menu, plates just come, each one designed for passing and picking at, the kind of eating where the conversation flows as easily as the Spanish-inspired drinks. Expect pinchos that hit hard, dishes that layer and surprise, and the feeling of being somewhere because someone recommended it rather than because you planned. It's tight, vibey, and a little chaotic in the best possible way. 

Your ticket includes eight courses of shared tapas and three paired Spanish-inspired drinks.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Escarpment Launch & Long Lunch, Be one of the first in the country to taste the 2023 vintage single vineyard wines from Martinborough's Pinot Noir superstars, Escarpment. From the gravels and windswept terraces of Martinborough, Escarpment has built a devoted following through word of mouth, shared by locals, championed by sommeliers, and remembered long after the last glass. 

Presented by winemaker Tim Bourne against the wild outlook of Boomrock's coastal position, you'll sample their wines paired with locally sourced wild ingredients including wild boar, Cook Strait snapper, tītī (mutton bird), venison, and Wairarapa cheese. 

The afternoon opens with Rosé on arrival and canapés of wild boar arancini and ceviche, then moves to a three-course long lunch. Expect leek, tītī, and Mānuka honey pasta with kawa kawa butter; tart cherry venison loin with purple kūmara gratin and Kikorangi Blue; and a Wairarapa cheese course with dark chocolate and blackberry jelly. Each course is matched with Escarpment's range, celebrating the magic of Wairarapa. Your ticket also includes return bus transport.

description:
FILIPINO RESTAURANT WEEK, From October 20 to 26, 2025, Filipino cuisine will take center stage in Auckland, Wellington, Christchurch, and Dunedin for the first Filipino Restaurant Week (FRW). This week-long event introduces foodies to the rich and diverse flavors of the Philippines, with Filipino restaurants showcasing traditional and modern dishes that tell stories of heritage and community.
Participating restaurants will offer fixed-price menus featuring Filipino dishes like adobo, kare-kare, and halo-halo, giving diners a chance to experience the rich culinary traditions shaped by centuries of history. These menus highlight the unique fusion of indigenous ingredients and global influences in Filipino cooking.
Filipino Restaurant Week is a celebration of heritage, an invitation to unity, and a singular opportunity to savor Filipino cuisine. It celebrates New Zealand’s diverse cultural tapestry, deepens cross-cultural understanding, and strengthens community through the universal connection of food.

The Ukrainian Gromada of the Wellington Region warmly invites you and your family to join us for a wonderful afternoon of connection, creativity, and delicious Ukrainian traditions! 💙💛

This family gathering is a fantastic opportunity for both children and adults to come together, meet new friends, reconnect with our community, reflect, share ideas, and enjoy a fun-filled Varenyky Workshop. 🥟✨

Together, we will learn how to make traditional Ukrainian varenyky (dumplings) from scratch:
🥣 Prepare the dough
🥔 Make delicious fillings
🥟 Shape the dumplings
🍽️ Cook them to perfection
😋 And, of course, enjoy tasting them together!

Whether you’re making varenyky for the first time or you’ve been making them for years, everyone is welcome! It’s a fun, friendly, and delicious way to experience and celebrate Ukrainian culture. 🌻

🥗 Please bring a plate to share, along with your favourite fillings for the dumplings. We’d love to see a variety of delicious ideas!

💛 There is no cost to attend, however, donations towards the venue hire would be greatly appreciated.

We can’t wait to spend this special afternoon with you and your family.

See you soon! 🇺🇦💙

Bring the whānau along for an afternoon of swapping, shopping, and sustainable fun at the Greens Family Market Day! Feast of Five Fishes, The ocean sets the tone for this five-course degustation, where fish and seafood take centre stage from first course to final bite. Drawing loosely on the spirit of the Italian Feast of Seven Fishes, this is a communal appreciation of the ocean's jewels, exploring the breadth and finesse of premium ocean produce with precision and care.

Each course reflects a thoughtful approach to seafood, drawing on seasonal catch and sustainably sourced ocean produce from around New Zealand. Throughout the evening, enjoy six unique canapés and six meticulously crafted drinks, each inspired by the work of a different artist. Each exhibit reflects the raw power and beauty of the natural world, as local artists push boundaries to bring these elements to life in real-time.

As you journey through Foxglove’s Secret Wardrobe, you'll be surrounded by live artistry unfolding around you, creating an environment filled with raw creativity and vibrant energy. Aphrodisiac-inspired canapés and expertly paired beverages complement the visual experience, bringing each artist’s medium to life while celebrating Wellington’s rich and diverse creative community.

This culinary and sensory pairing will transport you deeper into the world of artistry, blending food and creativity in unexpected and delightful ways.

This event goes beyond simple exhibition — it’s a celebration of Wellington's local talent where the boundaries between food, art, and sensory experience are beautifully blurred. Whether you’re an art aficionado or a culinary enthusiast, this immersive experience promises to engage your senses in an unforgettable way.

description:
Field to Feast, Set on a working regenerative farm just outside Wellington, this long-table dinner brings you as close to the land that produced your meal as possible. The vegetables and pasture-raised meat will come directly from Mangaroa Farms and other local suppliers, shared in a cosy winter-dinner setting designed to spark conversation, curiosity, and connection around food. This is an interactive dinner experience that blends food, conversation, poetry, live music and inner-enquiry into one cohesive experience.
You're welcomed with whakawhanaungatanga, a warm welcome drink and canapés to acquaint your taste buds to the land. You'll gather in the yurt for a multi-course regenerative meal, with stories from the farmers and producers who grew the food. Woven through the evening will be live music from Casual Healing, poetry and reflective questions to open the table. Designed to foster a single, focused conversation, this Jeffersonian style dinner invites conversation across the table. You'll talk with strangers and leave with friends. 

Your ticket includes a snack and drink on arrival, a multi-course farm-sourced dinner complete with fresh baked bread, local sides and dessert with non-alcoholic beverages throughout the evening.

In that time we’ve released dozens of new wines, held scores of pop-ups, become a wine bar, and spent many hundreds of hours working towards becoming one of NZ’s few in-house Méthode Traditionnelle producers.

To celebrate we’re delving into our cellar and hosting a fun, informal tasting of some of the wines that have defined our urban winery (and us!). There’s a story behind each one.

Take a seat, hear the stories, and taste the love put into each wine as Alexia co-owners Jane (also winemaker) and Lesley spend an hour traversing five whirlwind years of a little urban winery on a Greytown back street.

Ticket includes all tasting pours.

Tasting:

Méthode Traditionnelle (an advance look at a yet to be released vintage)

2019 Chenin Blanc – that wine that showed us Wairarapa’s Chenin Blanc potential

2017 Chardonnay – 6 barrels that lit the urban winery fire

2020 Pinot Noir – the heartbreak grape from the loneliest vintage

2025 Lagrein (from the barrel) - the wine that’s been on Jane’s mind since the 1990s

description:
Foraged Flavours : From Wild Greens to Plate, Foraged Flavours : From Wild Greens to Plate
~ Foraged Flavours: From Wild Greens to Plate ~

Step into a full-day, hands-on workshop at Mangaroa Farms, just 40 minutes from Wellington with Expert Forager Felicity Joy from Wild Botanica.

You’ll explore seasonal edible wild greens, learning to identify them, discover their properties, and turn your foraged finds into simple, delicious creations. In the farm’s fully equipped kitchen, you’ll make a range of hands-on preparations: fresh wild green spreads, infused butters, vibrant salads, and pickled or preserved treats, all designed to showcase the flavours of the season.

During the day, we’ll enjoy a shared wild feast together, tasting the seasonal dishes you’ve prepared in a relaxed, beautiful farm setting. This workshop is interactive, practical, and sensory, a chance to deepen your foraging skills, connect with nature, and celebrate the flavours of the wild. All ingredients, tools, and guidance are provided, so you can fully immerse yourself in the experience.

Perfect for those who’ve already attended Wild Botanica’s Foraging Workshops, this is the next step: taking your wild plant knowledge into the kitchen. Also suitable for total beginners, no experience needed.

When: Saturday 18th October
Time: 10 am – 3 pm (5-hour immersive experience)
Location: Mangaroa Farms, 40 minutes from Wellington

What’s included:
~ Full-day, hands-on experience: foraging, plant ID, cooking, and tasting
~ Access to a fully equipped kitchen and all tools
~ Guidance from an expert forager and cook
~ A shared wild feast using seasonal foraged ingredients prepared during the workshop
~ Educational insights into the nutritional, medicinal, and culinary properties of wild greens
~ Beautiful farm setting for a relaxed, sensory experience

description:
France vs New Zealand, France has long set the benchmark for fine wine. New Zealand, by contrast, is young, confident, and still defining its place on the world stage. For this five-course degustation, Noble Rot places the two side-by-side in a focussed tasting of classic pairs that asks a simple question: has New Zealand earned its seat at the table?

Each course is a head-to-head. A French classic meets its New Zealand counterpart. The food is classic, designed to let the wines show their differences. Expect thoughtful comparison across the varieties, regions and styles that shape both countries’ reputations. The emphasis is on quality producers and wines that speak clearly of place. Five courses means five comparisons, each one letting you taste whether New Zealand's found its own voice or is still chasing France's shadow.

Your ticket includes an amuse bouche on arrival, five courses, ten wines matched head-to-head throughout the evening.

From the Fisher's Mouth, Tom and Cole of Strait Speared have been supplying Wellington's best venues with spear-caught butterfish for four years using methods that have minimal impact on the ocean. Knowing your fisherman matters, and tonight they're coming to the table to talk you through why. 

A nine-course degustation using all the parts of the butterfish: fillets, collars, roe. Each preparation different, each one revealing something new about the fish and the selectivity it takes to harvest responsibly. You'll chat with the fishermen about their work, with the chef about different butterfish preparations, and with the people beside you as course after course unfolds. This is what transparent seafood looks like when the person who caught it is sitting across from you. 

Your ticket includes nine courses and one welcome drink on arrival. Additional alcohol can be purchased.

description:
George Motz: Burger Scholar, Calling all burger lovers. Class is in session as world-renowned smash burger expert George Motz brings a masterclass to Visa Wellington On a Plate. George has devoted his life to the humble burger, tracing its origins from 13th-century Mongolia to its current place as an American staple. He has made films, written books, and even taught university courses dedicated to the dish. In 2023, he opened Hamburger America in Manhattan, a tribute to regional burger styles and the stories behind them. Now he is bringing that knowledge to this burger loving city, at the bottom of the world, to share with all of you.

On stage, George will guide the audience through his ‘History of the Burger’. Expect a few surprises, along with the kind of detail only a ‘burger scholar’ can deliver. 

For the main event, George will cook his take on the Oklahoma onion burger live, sharing the methods that have earned him a global following. Every step is projected overhead, so you will not miss a thing. From the sizzling onions to the final stack, it is part cooking demo, part storytelling session, and a celebration of a classic. 

The evening wraps up with a Q & A, giving you the chance to ask George about his travels, techniques, and favourite burger joints. 

Whether you are a dedicated burger fan or just curious about what makes a great one, this is a chance to hear from one of the world’s leading voices on the subject.

Your ticket includes the presentation, live cooking demonstration and Q&A. No food will be served. A cash bar and merch will be available to purchase on the night.

This International Chef Collaboration is proudly supported by the New Zealand Government’s Events Boost Fund.

description:
Grilled Chicken, Turmeric Sticky Rice & Pickled Vegetables, Grilled Chicken, Turmeric Sticky Rice & Pickled Vegetables
Vietnamese Feast: Grilled Chicken, Turmeric Sticky Rice & Pickled Vegetables

Join Viet Hub NZ and I Love Vietfood for a hands-on cooking workshop featuring a vibrant Vietnamese meal that is often enjoyed at family gatherings, celebrations, and special occasions.

In this workshop, you'll learn how to prepare:

� Grilled Chicken (Gà Nướng)
Marinated with aromatic spices and grilled to perfection for a delicious balance of smoky, savoury, and slightly sweet flavours.

� Turmeric Sticky Rice (Xôi Xéo)
A beloved Vietnamese sticky rice dish known for its golden colour, rich aroma, and comforting texture.

� Pickled Vegetables (Dưa Chua)
Fresh, tangy pickles that add crunch and balance to every bite.

Together, these dishes create a meal that is colourful, flavourful, and deeply rooted in Vietnamese food culture.

Whether you're new to Vietnamese cooking or looking to expand your culinary skills, this workshop offers a welcoming environment to learn practical techniques, share stories, and enjoy a delicious meal together.


WHAT YOU'LL GET

� Hands-on cooking experience
� Recipes to take home
� A shared meal to enjoy together
� Insights into Vietnamese food traditions


FACILITATOR

This workshop is facilitated by Yung Nguyen from I Love Vietfood, in partnership with Viet Hub NZ.


SUPPORTING COMMUNITY THROUGH FOOD

Your registration fee helps provide a koha for our facilitator and supports Viet Hub NZ's community initiatives, including free community meals, cultural activities, and educational programmes.

Come hungry and discover the flavours of a Vietnamese feast!

description:
Hands-on Sourdough Workshop (Neil's), Sourdough for Beginners - $120 (paid via internet banking)
Come join us for a hands-on, in-person sourdough workshop at Willow Corner Collective headquarters (aka my home)! This workshop is currently the only hands-on sourdough workshop being offered in the Nelson region - I teach and demonstrate to you and then you get to mix and practice on your own dough as we go along.
Whether you're a seasoned baker or a beginner, this event is perfect for anyone looking to master the art of making sourdough bread, learning from someone who has 10+ years of experience. Perhaps you've found all the Youtube tutorials and Instagram how-to's overwhelming and are keen to learn via an in-person class. Then this is for you! I've baked hundreds of loaves in the last year alone, sold at a market, and hosted a pop-up shop. However, my passion really lies with teaching others to bake their own sourdough in their own homes, for their own families (or small businesses - one day!).You will be taught, demonstrated to, and then you get to have a go yourself; whilst learning my tips and tricks along the way. Plus we finish by sampling some delicious, fresh artisan sourdough with some favourite toppings!
You'll go home with all you need to make a good loaf of sourdough bread:
Knowledge
Student Guide, including recipes and troubleshoot guide
Bowl, liner, bowl scraper, and razor blade... all the tools you'd need to make sourdough
Dough made in class to bake the next day at home, to wow your family/friends
Confidence to continue the process yourself
Healthy, bubbling starter to continue your journey at home
Continued support and encouragement via our own private Facebook community group, for class attendees only
Note: You will have your dough to take home after the workshop that will need shaping around 6-8pm, so please ensure that will work for you that day.Also, please double check the date when booking. If for some reason you are unable to attend on the day, due to time constraints, I am unable to refund your ticket. I am happy for you to send someone in your place, though. In extenuating circumstances I may be able to hold your ticket for a future workshop; this is decided on a case-by-case basis.
*Payment to clear in bank account two days after ticket bought, after which time your ticket will be released on to someone else. Please pay immediately upon purchasing ticket.
**All workshop info you need to know ahead of time is in the confirmation email. Please ensure you read this down to the bottom.
***I recommend you already have a pair of digital scales, and a cast iron dutch oven at home to bake your loaf with as this makes the best, artisan sourdough, with great rise. Alternatively, a large, lidded casserole dish or enamel roasting pan work also. (The lids are a necessity).
"Sarah’s sour dough class is for real life! Achieve beautiful delicious bread easily in your own kitchen. Sarah teaches you how to fit sourdough into your busy life. She clearly and passionately gives the essential information, tips and tricks to make your own loaf. I loved getting to have a go at each step in the process. I love Sarah’s catchy philosophy “The goal is good bread, not perfect bread.” This took all the pressure off, for me, and I left the class empowered with all the knowledge and skills needed to give it a go at home. I appreciated the thoughtful and well prepared resources Sarah gave us. Thank you!" - Megan
"Sourdough with Sarah was a delight! From feeling overwhelmed and giving up on the idea of ever making my own loaf of sourdough, to dancing with joy as i watch a beautiful perfect sourdough loaf get nice and golden in the homewood stove!The information was packaged in bite sizes with hands on practice in between, where we all got to experience each step of the whole process, which was cleverly condensed and prepared so that despite normally having waits in between, we were able to see it all play out in a short few hours!The process was beautifully organised with attention to detail that had us fawning, came away feeling so blessed and privileged!Sarah's glowing personality made all the information feel easy and palatable, it was so fun!Such a lovely time, great environment to learn with ease." -Melody
label: Food & Drink

description:
Hidden Ferments, Indian fermentation has long lived in home kitchens and ancient texts, yet rarely takes centre stage in restaurants, especially on the global stage. This collaborative event invites you into that quieter, largely unseen world as chefs Saavni Krishnan and Sriram Aditya from Melbourne's Saadi restaurant, and chef Vaibhav Vishen, from Wellington's Chaat Street, bring a fine-dining lens to India's deep fermentation traditions, set against Wellington's wild, coastal produce. Across an intimate evening, the menu combines age-old techniques and new terroir: cultured grains, pickles, kanji-style ferments, and lacto-preserved fruits.

For both chefs their cooking is rooted in memory and comfort but expressed with restraint, clarity, and precision. Think fermented rice and lentil batters reimagined as delicate snacks, vegetables transformed through lactic fermentation to echo both Indian aachar and Wellington's coastal flora, and broths built on aged, cultured bases for depth and length. The journey traces a loose path from the grain and pulse-based ferments that underpin everyday Indian eating, through preserved vegetables and fruits, to experimental applications responding to Wellington's climate and producers. 

Your ticket includes a five-course tasting menu with thoughtful beverage pairings designed to echo ferment-forward flavours. Non-alcoholic options feature pickled, infused, and cultured elements without overpowering the palate. This event has shared seating.

The person who guesses the most correct ingredients will receive an $80 Dragonfly voucher and bragging rights as the ultimate flavour detective.

An exploration of contrast; crunch and softness, spice and sweetness, tradition and innovation.

description:
I-Sarn Thai KanTok, Join Daeng from Tuk Tuk Thai for a deeply personal culinary journey to the heart of E-Sarn, the north-eastern region of Thailand she once called home. This one-night-only event celebrates the traditional Kan-Tok style of dining – a communal meal served on handwoven bamboo trays and shared amongst family and friends. This event is made to be shared, the ticket price is for a shared menu for two. 

Growing up in the small town of Tha Bo near the Mekong Delta, Daeng’s childhood was filled with stories of rice farming, village generosity, and dishes cooked from what the garden offered. In E-Sarn, meals were acts of love, shared daily around the Kan-Tok with laughter, music, and warmth.

Now, Daeng invites you to gather at her table and experience the flavours of her upbringing. You’ll be served nine traditional dishes on a beautifully crafted bamboo tray, designed for sharing, just as they are in her village.

On the Kan-Tok:
Hor Mok Salmon – Steamed salmon in banana leaves, marinated with herbs, spices, and coconut milk
Mok Nor Mai with Pork Belly – Pork belly steamed with bamboo shoots
Larb Gai – A celebratory chicken mince salad with fresh herbs and toasted rice
E-Sarn Sausages – House-made, spiced and fermented in true north-eastern style
Nam Prik Tomato – Roasted tomato dipping sauce with chillies, garlic, and shallots
Som Tum – Green papaya salad with a sweet, sour, spicy kick
Sticky Rice – Soaked overnight and steamed in traditional bamboo baskets
Fresh and Steamed Seasonal Vegetables – To enjoy with sauces and mains

Dessert:
Kanom Chan – Thai layered jelly cake
Kanom Mun – Tapioca and coconut pudding

Pull up a seat at Daeng’s table and discover the stories, flavours, and traditions that shaped her childhood.
Single tickets or odd numbers unable to be catered to.

description:
Keiko Kuwakino + Joe McLeod, For one night only, two forager-chefs from opposite ends of the Pacific will bring you - Kai meets Shoku - as they cook together at Pipitea Marae, for an all inclusive six course dinner that could only happen in Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

Pipitea Marae has always been a place of gathering and welcome. For generations, Te Āti Awa ki Te Whanganui-a-Tara has offered manaakitanga to those who arrive by sea, by land, and now, from across the Pacific.

On 29 August, that tradition continues with a dinner bringing together two chefs whose life's work is rooted in the same conviction: that honouring culture and history is best done via the puku.

The story of this harbour is one of guardians, pathways, and the meeting of worlds. Te Āti Awa have long understood that the sea connects rather than separates. What began as a relationship across the Pacific between Te Āti Awa and Japan finds its expression at the table, where two Indigenous cultures share their stories through food.

Chef Joe McLeod (Ngāi Tūhoe) brings more than 40 years' experience as an international chef, alongside six decades spent researching, recording, and reconnecting Mātauranga Kai Māori, returning traditional food knowledge to marae across Aotearoa. One of the foremost authorities on traditional Māori cuisine, Chef Joe's kaupapa is grounded in the belief that food carries whakapapa, and that restoring a people's relationship to their kai is an act of cultural survival.

Chef Keiko Kuwakino travels from Satoyama Jujo in Niigata, Japan, where her Michelin-starred restaurant reflects a practice rooted in wild mountain vegetables, fermentation, and the rhythms of Japan's snow country. Her cooking begins with the land she forages. For Keiko, cuisine starts with the land itself, her role simply to listen carefully to nature and translate its story through food.

Hosted by Te Āti Awa at Pipitea Marae, Kai Meets Shoku is a partnership between Wellington Culinary Events Trust, Te Rūnanganui o Te Āti Awa, and E Kai Māori, supported by MBIE.

Your ticket includes five courses, matched beverages for all courses, and Māori and Japanese entertainment

description:
Kumutoto Kai me te Kōrero, Kumutoto Awa was one of the living streams of Pōneke long before the city buried it underground in 1866. This four-hour guided hīkoi traces its path from the Kelburn hills to the waterfront, connecting it through kai, kōrero, and the people who are working to restore the place of the awa in the city's future – The Kumutoto Restoration Project. You'll start with a light lunch and cocktail at Graze in Kelburn which will be a collaboration between Chef Max Gordy and the Kumutoto Community Orchard founder and avid forager Milan Magan. You will also meet your hosts Martin and Micheline who will regale you with stories about Wellington's lost streams. From there, the group walks to the only remaining stretch of the Kumutoto stream still visible above ground, where soup waits alongside more kōrero about the whakapapa of the awa. The route then follows the buried path of Kumutoto down the Terrace to Bert's Bar for a final cocktail created with a foraged ingredients from Kumutoto before finishing at the mouth of the awa on the waterfront. All food and drinks across the event are included in your ticket, with ingredients foraged from the Kumutoto Community Orchard and ngahere. Wear comfortable shoes and dress for the weather. The route covers approximately two kilometres and includes steps.
The ticket price includes an optional foraging workshop with Milan Magan. You'll spend an hour in the orchard and ngahere learning about what you'll be eating and drinking the following day. Saturday 1 & 29 August 9-10am.

description:
Le Marché Français at GP Leeds St (MELTED CHEESE GALORE!), We love Le Marché Français. They're tres chic and one of the greats when it comes to fromage (cheese). It's always a treat having delicious French food on deck to class the place up, and it pairs so well with beer.
On Sunday 14 June, Le Marché Français is coming to Leeds St for the afternoon to present to you lucky folks their raclette baguettes - it's a Raclette Lunch!
Huge wheels of specialty French cow's milk cheese, slowly melted and then loaded straight onto fresh baguette, with a range of accoutrements on the side (cornichons, Dijon mustard, radish and Saucisson) so you can build each perfectly-balanced bite to your personal preference. Have you seen raclette IRL before? It's the closest food gets to performance art, and it takes skill and experience to execute.
Lucky for us, Le Marché Français are pros - you'll feel like you've been transported straight to fair Paris ("Paree") or a quaint village square in Provence. There's a fuel crisis on - let the world's delicacies come to you!
Sunday 14 June, from 12pm
$30 a head gets you a raclette baguette with sides + a drink (beer, wine and non-alcoholic options)
Vegetarian option available
No gluten-free, dairy-free or vegan options (it's cheese and bread!)
Bookings available, and recommended
Walk-ins welcome - but you'll be taking your chances
Book your spot now using the link above!

description:
Le Petit Chef, InterContinental Wellington proudly presents the first official Le Petit Chef experience in New Zealand - an extraordinary fusion of theatre, storytelling, and fine dining.

Step into the whimsical animated world of Le Petit Chef, the world’s tiniest and most determined chef, as he embarks on a globe-trotting quest to source the finest ingredients. Using groundbreaking 3D projection mapping technology, your table transforms into a magical stage, where continents shift, spices fly, and the art of cooking comes thrillingly to life before your eyes.

As the journey unfolds, a five-course menu is served in perfect harmony with the story. Highlights include Wairarapa crayfish bouillabaisse, corn-fed chicken with Perigord truffle, and a decadent Valrhona chocolate dessert. Choose from the Grand Menu ($180), Classic Menu ($140), Vegetarian Menu ($140), or a dedicated Kids Menu $70). While each menu offers a distinct culinary experience, the stunning visual show remains the same for all guests and is centered around the Grand Menu storyline.

description:
Love Bites, Modern dating is a minefield, so Beach Babylon and local comedians Mike Fowler and Anya Rzhevitskaya have turned it into a laugh-filled dining event not to be missed. 

Love Bites is a three-course comedy dinner centred on the chaos of modern relationships: red flags you clocked and ignored, situationships you still can't explain, and texts that should've stayed in drafts. Across the night, Mike, and Anya will take very different angles on love and dating as the courses land, from early sparks and suspicious charm through to full-blown hindsight. The menu mirrors the arc perfectly: entrées spark connection (think love bombing fondue and I'm hooked prawns), mains explore the situationship (steak with main character energy or fish soft launches), and dessert brings the happily ever after. It's loose, social, and just self-aware enough. 

Your ticket includes three courses and a welcome cocktail. Additional drinks available for purchase.

description:
Madeira My Dear, Madeira has been too often overlooked. It sits in grandmother's cabinet waiting for cooking or forgotten entirely. But Madeira is built to last, it's a quietly complex wine that deserves discovery. Noble Rot will spend an afternoon proving it to you.
The afternoon begins with a welcome cocktail before settling into a three-course long lunch served sharing style at the table, in the traditional Mediterranean spirit. Generous plates are designed to encourage conversation and a slower pace. Across the meal, guests will taste six Madeiras, exploring the spectrum from dry and saline expressions through to richer, caramel-toned styles, with insight into grape varieties, ageing methods, and the oxidative character that gives Madeira its unique flavour profiles and remarkable longevity.
Your ticket covers a themed arrival cocktail, three generous sharing courses, and six Madeira wines paired throughout the afternoon.

description:
Maille à Maille, Since 1747, Maille has been synonymous with French gastronomy. The supplier to the court of King Louis XV, it remains one of the most recognised French condiment brands in the world. This August, Maille teams up with Le Bouillon Bel Air for Menu du Jour: a special collaborative bistro series served every Sunday throughout the month.

Step into a classic Parisian-inspired dining experience and enjoy a three-course menu where Maille's signature mustards feature throughout each dish. Begin with a leek terrine dressed in a Dijon and wholegrain Maille mustard vinaigrette, followed by Poulet Gaston Gérard—chicken in a rich Maille mustard and cream sauce. Finish with a dark chocolate mousse accompanied by brown butter crumble, poached pear, and a mustard-sesame-honey tuile. This exclusive three-course menu is available for $85 per person, every Sunday in August.

As you sip, savour, and share your impressions, you'll hear the makers talk through the shapes they chose, the clay they selected, and the ideas that guided their hands. Then the shakers reveal the stories behind each serve — how they matched flavour to form. It's the kind of collaboration you'll remember for years to come, each time you reach for your new favourite drinking vessel.

Light canapés will keep things grounded, and a market stall will offer additional handcrafted wares straight from the makers' studios. The buzz from the last two sell-outs came purely from word of mouth. Come along, and you'll understand why.

Your ticket includes a welcome drink, three bespoke cocktails, light canapés, and three handmade ceramic vessels to take home.

description:
Mastering Paella Workshop, Learn to authentically create Paella by Spanish Embassy Special guest chef, Edrick Corban-Banks, from Casa Paella.
In collaboration with the Embassy of Spain in New Zealand and Casa Paella, we are proud to offer a one-day workshop taught by the award-winning chef, Edrick Corban-Banks.
Chef Edrick is the owner of Casa Paella, Casa Paella holds the official ICEX “Restaurants from Spain” quality seal, recognising its place within Spain’s international network of restaurants committed to authenticity, quality, and the promotion of Spanish gastronomy. This is rare opportunity to learn the culture and traditional Valencian techniques of Paella from a master artisan.
You will spend the day in Teams of 2 as Chef Edrick guides you through the creation of the award winning Arroz con Salmón.
Date: 25th July
Time: 9:30am – 3pm (light lunch is included with a glass of Albarino white wine)
Location: Level 2, 52 Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington
Allergies: Ingredients in this class contain the following allergens: Fish, Shellfish/Crustaceans, Molluscs, and Sulphates. This dish will be Gluten Free.
You Will Create:
Arroz con Salmón (Salmon Paella featuring Ōra King Salmon)
First developed in Tasmania using Petuna ocean-grown salmon and awarded the
Tetsuya Wakuda “Best Plate” prize at Taste of Tasmania, this paella is designed as a
technique-led masterclass in stock construction, rice absorption, and heat
management. A concentrated seafood fumet—prepared from shellfish and fish
frames—builds depth and structure, allowing the character of premium local salmon
to remain the centre of the dish.
Course Details: During the workshop, you will learn the following skills:
Prepare a fresh seafood stock using fish and shellfish frames
Build flavour through sofrito, saffron, paprika, and olive oil
Cook Valencian paella rice correctly so each grain remains separate
and full of flavour
Manage heat, evaporation, timing, and liquid levels
Understand the difference between cooking “rice with seafood”
and creating a true Mediterranean rice dish
Develop the prized socarrat — the golden crust at the base of the paella
Finish and serve your paella in the traditional shared style
Course Includes: All ingredients and equipment supplied, at the end of the class, participants will sit down together and enjoy the paella they have created with a glass of Albarino white wine.

What is a Le Cordon Bleu Workshop? A Le Cordon Bleu Workshop is a hands-on culinary training session delivered in our professional teaching kitchens. Be personally guided by world class chefs and taught key techniques step-by-step, with chef feedback throughout. This workshop includes a light lunch, and is designed to give you skills you can repeat confidently at home or in a professional setting.
Contact Details: +64 4 472 9800 | nz@cordonbleu.edu
label: Food & Drink

description:
Mediterranea, At Cicio Cacio Osteria, the Mediterranean comes to the table in an intimate dinner shaped by memory and place. Inspired by the owner's childhood on a Mediterranean island, this dinner traces a path from Italy to Spain, across Greece and into the Middle East, with dishes from each region reflecting the shared spirit of the Mediterranean: the sun, the sea, the music, the nostalgia, the being in the moment. The food is uncomplicated and entirely enjoyable, simple, fare focused on freshness and simplicity, letting the ingredients speak for themselves. Expect the most perfect hummus with grilled pita, the best Spanish tortilla, uncommon seafood like octopus and sardines, couscous, lamb, and goat, pastas, and colourful salads, a true insight into the Mediterranean spirit. 

You'll be seated at a long communal table in front of a real fire for a progressive nine-course menu, each plate paired with a matched wine selected to reflect its origin and character. Throughout the evening, the chef shares stories behind the dishes, offering insight into flavours, traditions, and personal history. You're invited to come into the kitchen and share the secrets of each recipe, cooking alongside the chef. A final musical touch ends an evening dedicated to the beauty, spontaneity, and simplicity of the Mediterranean. 

Your ticket includes nine courses, nine matched wines, storytelling, hands-on cooking, and recipe sharing.

This exclusive event will offer an intimate exploration of Chef Newell's evolution as a chef and restaurateur, showcasing iconic dishes from four pivotal periods in his career.

Set in the elegant Napoleon dining room inside the historic Martinborough Hotel, each course represents a defining moment in Chef Newell’s career. Paired with fine wines selected by in-house Sommelier Carl Fraser, this evening is designed to be a feast for both the palate and the mind.

Course 1: 1980s – Claridge’s Hotel, London
A taste of the refined sophistication from one of London’s most prestigious hotels.
Course 2: 1990s – Le Gavroche, London
A nod to the classic French techniques that helped shape Chef Newell's early career.
Course 3: 2000s – Zibibbo, Wellington
A celebration of New Zealand’s finest ingredients and a significant step in his culinary journey.
Course 4: 2010s – Union Square Bistro, Martinborough

This evening offers guests a unique chance to experience the evolution of one chef's journey through extraordinary dishes paired with wines that elevate each moment.

description:
Micro Aperitivo - Neighbourhood Vermouth Bar, Alexia Urban Winery x Greytown Distilling Company present: Micro Aperitivo - Neighbourhood Vermouth Bar

Aperitivo – it’s the Italian pre-dinner beverage ritual designed to open the palate, open the stomach, and open the conversation.

Wander past any Italian bar as the sun goes down, and you’ll see the locals sipping martinis and negronis, while engaged in animated discussion!

The common ingredient in these cocktails…and conversations is vermouth – a delicious, aromatic, botanical-loaded, fortified wine. Wine, you say? That’s where we come in. Alexia has been working with Greytown Distilling to create a vermouth for them right here in Greytown, and they’ve asked us to host something fun to celebrate its release for the Greytown International Cocktail Festival!

We’re channelling vermouths Italian roots and transforming into a little pop-up Italian neighbourhood vermouth bar!

We’ll be serving the most intriguing (and cutest) cocktail flight in town to showcase the beauty and versatility of vermouth… the ‘vermouth micro-trio cocktail tray’ - a cocktail broken into three micro parts: micro vermouth on the rocks, micro gin martini, and micro negroni.

All the Alexia wines will be available too, of course, and it’s Italian all the way in the kitchen, with guest chef Caleb Kloeg turning out crispy arancini and gelato soft-serves so delicious you’ll be transported to Italy.

Cocktail inspired? You’re in luck. Greytown Distilling will have a little pop-up shop on the night, selling all the essential cocktail-making accessories too.

It’s neighbourhood Italian bar vibes on a Greytown backstreet, and we can’t wait… so get on your vespas, pump up the tyres on your Bianchi, rev those Fiats and get to Alexia!

Vermouth micro-trio cocktail tray

The most intriguing cocktail in town…a single cocktail broken into a micro-flight showcasing the beauty and versatility of vermouth: micro vermouth on the rocks, micro gin martini, and micro negroni. Shrunken, not stirred…

Essential details: 4pm – 8pm, Friday 27 March, Alexia Urban Winery, 197 West Street, Greytown. No bookings required, just turn up. GF? Yes. Vegan? Yes. Leashed dogs ok. This is a rain or shine event, so don’t miss out!

The Greytown International Cocktail Festival is proudly sponsored by Greytown Distilling Co and The White Swan.

description:
Next Gen Cook Off, The Next Gen Cook Off returns for its fifth year, and things are heating up at Everybody Eats.
Every Monday in August, four of Wellington’s freshest young chefs will go head-to-head in a high-energy kitchen takeover, serving up epic three-course dinners using rescued food.

Each chef will be given the same protein, generously provided by Meat Direct, but everything else is a surprise—ingredients are revealed that morning, based on what’s come in. Menus are created on the spot, and dishes are served to a buzzing, hungry crowd. It’s fast-paced, creative chaos with serious culinary skills on display. Guests get a front-row seat to the action, while supporting a truly game-changing enterprise.

4 August — Jessie Gibberd, Loretta
Originally from rural Waikato, Jessie Gibberd made the move to Wellington to study, but it was the buzz of hospitality that captured her heart. Swapping textbooks for tongs, she left her degree behind to dive headfirst into the kitchen. Now a chef de partie at Loretta, Jessie brings a grounded, fresh perspective to one of the city’s most beloved eateries.

11 August — Felipe Molina, El Matador
Hailing from Chile, Felipe Molina is a professional chef with over 15 years of experience in kitchens around the world. Having worked in several countries and world-class restaurants, Felipe brings a global sensibility to his craft. With a passion for seafood, meats, and bold, expressive flavours, his cooking is shaped by travel and tradition, blending international influence with creativity on every plate.

18 August — Zane Gupwell, Graze
Zane Gupwell began his hospitality journey at just 15, washing dishes at a local café in Mount Eden. From there, he headed to Queenstown, learning from a wide range of chefs and kitchen styles before challenging himself with a move to Wellington. Since then, he’s worked at some of the city’s top restaurants and now brings his thoughtful, evolving style to Graze Wine Bar.

25 August — Lulu Temmuyin, Mr Go’s
Lulu Temmuyin is a chef who loves pushing boundaries, even when they’re unexpected. Lactose intolerant but obsessed with cheese, and not a fan of lamb but winner of a lamb cooking competition, Lulu is all about surprises. At Mr Go’s, she brings bold, sustainable flavour to the forefront, blending personality with punch in every dish.

Everybody Eats runs on a pay-what-you-can model, transforming food waste into gourmet meals and bringing the community together over good kai. The Next Gen Cook Off celebrates and champions this mission, proving that rescued food can be next-level delicious.

The Next Gen Cook Off is proudly supported by The Gas Hub.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Next Gen Cook Off, The first four Mondays in August, an up-and-coming chef takes over the Everybody Eats kitchen at LTD and delivers a three-course dinner built from rescued food, cooking it their way and style. Walk in, take a seat, and let the Everybody Eats volunteers whānau take care of the rest. No bookings. Pay what you can. 
Sixth year running, and the model stays simple: good food, good company, and a room full of people making a difference one plate at a time. Every course uses rescued ingredients, because eating is fundamental and everyone deserves access to something . 

3 August — Oscar Little, Hummingbird
Oscar Little started his culinary career five years ago as a commis chef at Shed 5 and The Crabshack, where he learned what it means to commit to a team. He’s since worked his way up to chef de partie at Hummingbird. Along the way he’s volunteered with Everybody Eats, and it’s that spirit of giving back to the community that drives him to compete this year.

10 August — Brayden Puketapu, Koji
At 22, Brayden Puketapu is already developing a cooking voice that’s distinctly his own. Working at Koji, he’s drawn to the creative challenge of transforming overlooked ingredients and putting his own stamp on both classic and contemporary dishes. His heritage is central to that identity, grounding his food in something personal while keeping it fresh and inventive.

17 August — Eugenous Evan, Rosella
Indonesian-born Eugenous Evan came to Wellington five years ago and hasn’t looked back. After stints at Shepherd, Hillside & Daisy’s, and Supra, he’s now chef de partie at Rosella, where he’s been for just over a year. For Eugenous, cooking is an act of care: a way to share something of himself with every person who sits down to eat.

24 August — Aryan Dhankhhar, Mosaic Venues (Mr Go's, Kisa, Ombra, Parla)
Aryan Dhankhhar’s love of food started young, holding weekend cooking competitions with his sister and himself in their family kitchen in Haryana, India, with their mother as judge. Since then he’s built a career spanning hotels, restaurants, and catering, working across techniques from sous vide to traditional barbecue. A highlight: leading the team at Wilson Barbecue during Wellington On a Plate 2024, where they set a world record selling over 6,000 burgers in a single day. Now at Mr Go’s, he brings that same drive and precision to every plate.

Next Gen Cook Off is proudly supported by The Gas Hub.

description:
Once Upon a Time in Wellington, We are hosting some very special guest chefs over a 2 week period, with each chef joining us for a 2 night collaboration. Their identities won't be reveiled until the day before via Instagram. Speculate, believe the rumours, start the rumours for all we care! Three local legends, one from outside Wellington, and a roster that reads like the highlight reel of modern cooking in this country. It will be a small a la carte format during our usual trading hours.  Walk ins are encouraged but bookings for groups of 4 or more it is highly recommended. The menus will be small and à la carte throughout. 
Guest #1 (4-5 Aug) The Taipan
Our first guest is a previous collaborator, you know him, you love him, we love him. If you've eaten his food before, you know subtlety isn't on the menu. Expect bold and aggressive flavours, and probably some offal. 
Guest #2 (7-8 Aug) The Kodiak Bear
Lover of restaurants and a wizard with words on paper. We are very excited to introduce this guy and give him a creative platform to show Wellington something special from a unique perspective. 
Guest #3 (12-13) The Suzumebachi
Joining us from the Hawkes Bay, This man brings a tempered approach to cooking from his time cooking in Japan. Now an established award winning chef in New Zealand, and someone we consider at the pinnacle of modern cookery in this country. Expect Japanese flavours and techniques utilizing the some of the best produce NZ has to offer.
Guest #4 (14-15) The Bighorn Ram
With many curls in his horns, this guy has been pivotal and arguably one of the most important chefs Wellington has ever known, setting the stage for many of us who followed. An award winning chef who pioneered modern cuisine in this City, you wont want to miss this. Expect a measured and wise approach to fun flavour combinations with precision.

description:
Otto Wine Club: Schubert Wines, Join us for the launch of Otto Wine Club – a new monthly wine tasting series celebrating some of New Zealand's best wineries.

Each month we'll welcome a different winery to Otto, where you'll have the chance to meet the winemaker, hear the stories behind the wines, and taste a curated selection from their range.

Our first event features Schubert Wines, one of Martinborough's most respected boutique wineries. Drop in anytime between 5:00pm and 7:00pm to enjoy your guided tasting.
Your ticket includes:
- A tasting flight of five Schubert wines
- The opportunity to meet the winemaker and learn about the vineyard and winemaking process
- A relaxed after-work atmosphere with plenty of time to ask questions and discover your new favourite drop

Whether you're a seasoned wine enthusiast or simply keen to explore something new, this is a fun, informal way to discover great New Zealand wine.

Spaces are limited, so book early to avoid missing out.

About Schubert Wines: https://www.schubert.co.nz/wines/
After graduating from the German Viticulture and Oenology University Geisenheim Kai Schubert and Marion Deimling travelled the world in search of the perfect terroir and conditions for viticulture, especially their favourite variety – Pinot Noir. Their quest took them to the wine regions of France, Germany, Oregon, California, South America and Australia and ended in Martinborough in the beautiful Wairarapa Valley.

Here they found the perfect climate and conditions for producing low yields and excellent quality grapes. Since 1998 Schubert Wines have been growing and producing wines with intense and complex character that are now nationally and internationally award winning.

PICKLE WEEK - Garage Project Wellington, All hail the mighty pickle: Pickle Week at GP
Few foods inspire greater fervour than the pickle. Pickles are a strong flavour, no argument there, but they’re refreshingly unique, undeniably interesting and a reliable support act for any culinary affair. They deserve some goddamn respect.
To honour this Tilda Swinton of the condiment world, we’re throwing a week-long celebration around International Pickle Day that puts pickles front and center. We’re talking:
Pickle Beer
Spicy Pickle Beer
Pickle micheladas
Pickle platters
Snacks featuring interesting pickles
Pickle tattoos (temporary, but could be made not temporary)
Pickle merch
Pictures of you as pickles
Pickles
If you have any affection for pickles greater than ‘indifferent’, you’re going to love this.
No tickets required, just turn up, ready to pickle out.
Pickles - they’re a pretty big dill!
When:
Tuesday 11th to Sunday 16th Sunday
Where:
Garage Project Taproom
Garage Project Leeds Street
Garage Project Aro
Garage Project's Wild Workshop

description:
Paint & Sip with Mandy Emerson, Enjoy a fabulous night of creativity and great company paired with delicious food & refreshments!

Mandy Emerson is an established NZ artist from Riversdale Beach in the Wairarapa. She started her paint workshops over a year ago and they have been such a success she continues to be fully booked out.

It is The Offering's absolute pleasure to host her here in Greytown. Enjoy a glass of bubbles on arrival, select a delicious dish from the curated menu and settle in for some creativity. The workshop will then pause for dinner.

Mandy's work is mixed media, feminine with florals and she has won awards for her works and exhibits all over New Zealand.

Her biggest success came from exhibiting at the NZ ART SHOW in Wellington which she still continues to be a part of and also attending ARTMELBOURNE in Australia. Visit her website www.mandyemerson.com

description:
Paint and Gin Weekend Afternoon - The Great Wave, Join us for a fun adults’ painting class at The Bond Store – a vibrant distillery in the heart of Paraparaumu, known for its award-winning New Zealand craft spirits. No painting experience is needed – your friendly artist will guide you step by step in a relaxed, judgement-free environment.

This event is all about creativity, conversation, and having a great time while unleashing your inner artist.

Your ticket includes a gin tasting tray, giving you the chance to sample some of The Bond Store’s specialty gins while you paint.

Whether you’re coming with friends, planning a date night, or flying solo, this is your chance to unwind, get creative, and experience the joy of painting with Paintvine.

What is Paintvine?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality canvas, acrylic paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit (or find some at the bottom of a glass). At the end of the night you will leave with your own painting ready to hang up on your wall.

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website ⇒ paintvine.co.nz

description:
Paritua, The Botanist & Sea Shepherd!, Paritua, The Botanist & Sea Shepherd!
We've teamed up with Paritua Vineyard and Sea Shepherd NZ to bring you a fantastic evening of dining and drinking excellent wine! We'll be serving a four course plant based dinner, matched with Paritua wines, in support of Sea Shepherd New Zealand.
⁠
Each dish draws its inspiration from the sea with a kiwi twist, designed by our head chef Stephanie Hinton. Stephanie has recently moved back to New Zealand after 16 years cheffing in London, and running acclaimed vegan businesses there. Each course is paired with organic and vegan wines presented by Ollie Kettle and Josh Pointon of Paritua Wines. Proceeds from tickets sold will be donated directly to Sea Shepherd to help protect our oceans.

Numbers are limited, so gather your friends and book early for an unforgettable night of food, wine and ocean conservation.

description:
Pass the Glass, This is an intimate guided tasting exploring the conversation between chocolate and wine. Across five curated pairings, taste each element individually before bringing them together, uncovering how sweetness, tannin, texture and origin transform one another.

From Pacific-origin chocolate to expressive fortified wines, each match tells a story of how it was found; through experimentation, happy accidents, and recommendation. Led by Gabe Davidson (co-founder and bean-to-bar maker) and Josh Pointon (one of the country's top sommeliers), this is a structured, indulgent tasting designed to be flavour-focused and genuinely educational. 
Your ticket includes five chocolate pairings and five wines.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Pasta Giapponese, Taste the dishes driving Japan's newest food obsession: pasta made with Japanese ingredients, techniques and instincts. Think Wagyu bolognaise, Yakitori Aglio e Olio, shiso pesto, and mentaiko cream — dishes that feel completely familiar and entirely new at the same time.
It's a combination that's been quietly building for decades, ever since Japanese chefs trained in Italy brought authentic technique home and discovered how well their own ingredients responded to it. What's emerging now is something neither culture could have made alone. 

Your ticket includes two courses and a glass of organic Marlborough wine.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Perfect Pairs: A Journey Through Wines of the World, A Wine & Food Pairing Night at Cuba St Tavern

Join us at Cuba St Tavern for Perfect Pairs - a special evening celebrating great wine, good food and the people around the table.

For one night only, we’ll be pouring five standout wines from around the world, each paired with a dish designed by our kitchen to bring out the best in every glass.

Guiding the evening is Brandon Nash, from Importer and Distributor Dhall & Nash Fine Wines, who will introduce each wine throughout the night and share a little about the regions, producers and stories behind the pours.

From English sparkling to Central Otago Pinot Noir, this lineup takes guests across some of the world’s most exciting wine regions - all enjoyed in the relaxed, social atmosphere of the Tavern.

Expect a night of great wine, thoughtful plates and good company in the heart of Cuba Street.

Wines Featured
England - Digby Fine English Brut
Austria - Laurenz V Grüner Veltliner
USA - Duckhorn Chardonnay (Napa Valley)

Phở Real! Vietnamese Cooking Class – Special 2/9 Edition (FREE), Join us for a hands-on cooking experience as we celebrate Vietnam Independence Day with one of our most iconic dishes — Phở!

description:
Pickle Week, All hail the mighty pickle: Pickle Week at GP

Few foods inspire greater fervour than the pickle. Pickles are a strong flavour, no argument there, but they’re refreshingly unique, undeniably interesting and a reliable support act for any culinary affair. They deserve some goddamn respect.

To honour this Tilda Swinton of the condiment world, we’re throwing a week-long celebration around International Pickle Day that puts pickles front and center.

We’re talking:
Pickle Beer
Spicy Pickle Beer
Pickle micheladas
Pickle platters
Snacks featuring interesting pickles
Pickle tattoos (temporary, but could be made not temporary)
Pickle merch (potentially reup of bottle openers)
Pictures of you as pickles
Pickles

If you have any affection for pickles greater than ‘indifferent’, you’re going to love this.
Pickles - they’re a pretty big dill!

description:
Pāua to the People, For many of us, pāua is widely known, yet rarely tried beyond fritters, or the classic creamed version. Get it right, though, and it deserves a place at any kiwi table. Get it wrong and you may as well sole your boots with it. 

Join a collection of chefs, fishermen, and locals for a deep dive into the life, nutrition, and uses of our most iconic seafood. The masterclass starts with local wine, then into demonstrations of technique in the despatch, preparation, and cooking of pāua, and open forum discussion as you explore ultimate expressions of this taonga. Roll your sleeves up to learn techniques first-hand at a grazing pace, with refreshments to hand. A communal meal follows, celebrating our local oceans and prepared by masterful chefs. Pāua appears eight ways, kelp in all its glory, and smoke, fire, and fish take centre stage. 
Your ticket includes welcome beverages, eight courses featuring pāua in multiple expressions, matched wines or non-alcoholic options throughout.

description:
Pōneke Pony, Middle-earth has found its way to Oriental Bay. For August, Beach Babylon hosts a tavern pop-up that feels like somewhere you stumble into wandering hobbits and stay longer than planned, candlelight, conversation, a space removed from the everyday.

The menu nods to tavern traditions: Shire comfort, Rohan indulgence, Gondor richness. Food that leans generous and satisfying, designed for settling in rather than moving on too quickly. Hobbits eat early and often. Dwarves favour bold, indulgent flavours. Rangers keeping things simple and well chosen. And somewhere in the mix, the quiet suggestion that a certain ring might not be entirely accounted for. The drinks keep things grounded. Local craft beers, classic pours, and a few special concoctions for those with a sense of adventure. Choose your path through three courses, entrée, main, dessert, with options that work whether you're a hobbit or a ranger. Costumes welcome. Just arrive hungry.

description:
Rodney Scott: Pitmaster, Rodney Scott has been cooking whole-hog barbecue over coals since he was eleven years old. By seventeen, he was working the pits full time. What began as a kid helping out at his parents' roadside business eventually became one of the most celebrated careers in American barbecue. In 2018, Scott was named Best Chef: Southeast by the James Beard Foundation, the second pitmaster ever to win a James Beard chef award. He has appeared alongside Anthony Bourdain in Parts Unknown, and in 2020 was profiled on an episode of Chef's Table: BBQ, showcasing his South Carolina whole hog style. 

Boneface Brewing in Upper Hutt will be transformed for the occasion: American cars out front, whole hogs slow cooking over a fire pit, long trestle tables set up beer-hall style inside, live music, flash tattoos, and a specially brewed Boneface collaboration beer made for the day. Scott will be cooking his signature whole hog alongside a second protein, two hot sides, two cold sides, bread, and condiments. Staff will be dressed for it. So should you!

Your ticket includes food and entertainment. Beverages and flash tattoos are payable on the day.

This International Chef Collaboration is proudly supported by the New Zealand Government’s Events Boost Fund.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Roots of Ceylon, From the irrigation kingdoms of ancient Ceylon to the smoked-meat traditions of the Veddā people, Sri Lanka's indigenous cuisine carries centuries of survival, ritual and ingenuity. Most of it passed down by word of mouth and nearly lost to modernity.
Each course of this meal tells a different chapter: royal chicken porridge, coastal family curries, festive millet sweets, and more. The menu drawson local ingredients, ancestral techniques, and the ayurvedic principles that shaped how Sri Lankans have eaten for generations.
Your ticket includes five courses and tea-based beverages throughout the evening

description:
Sconnoisseur, Get ready to master the art of making Wellington's iconic cheese scones at Pravda Café. Widely regarded as the home of the city's best cheese scones, Pravda's creations are so beloved, they often sell out before you can blink. Now, you can learn the secrets behind their mouthwatering scones firsthand.

In this hands-on workshop, you’ll be guided through mixing and preparing your own batch of Pravda’s famous cheese scones. Once your dough is ready, you'll hand them off to be baked to crispy flaky perfection. While they cook, relax with a cup of tea or coffee, and once your scones are ready, you’ll enjoy the fruits of your labour fresh from the oven.

The best part? You’ll get to take home the coveted recipe, allowing you to recreate these legendary scones in your own kitchen whenever you want. This is a perfect opportunity to learn a piece of Wellington’s culinary history and enjoy a deliciously rewarding experience.

description:
Signature High Tea's | Steam Incorporated, Step aboard for an elegant afternoon unlike any other, where heritage rail travel meets refined indulgence.

Introducing Steam Incorporated’s Signature High Tea Experience — an exclusive journey designed for those who appreciate the finer things. Departing from Paraparaumu and Waikanae, this carefully curated steam excursion offers a relaxed and luxurious escape, all within the space of a single afternoon.

Travel in style behind our beautifully restored steam locomotive, Ab 608 Passchendaele — a remarkable 111-year-old engine that brings history to life. The gentle rhythm of steam and the nostalgia of classic rail travel set the tone for an experience that is as timeless as it is memorable.

With limited numbers onboard, this is a more intimate journey — unhurried, comfortable, and distinctly premium.

Our destination is the picturesque Tatum, where you’ll be welcomed for a classic High Tea in a tranquil countryside setting. Indulge in a selection of finely prepared sweet and savoury treats, accompanied by freshly brewed tea and coffee — the perfect complement to a leisurely afternoon.

This experience has been thoughtfully designed as a shorter, refined outing — ideal for those seeking something special without committing to a full day. Whether you're celebrating an occasion, catching up with friends, or simply treating yourself, the Tatum High Tea offers a memorable blend of heritage, hospitality, and indulgence.

Experience Highlights

Steam-hauled return journey from Paraparaumu & Waikanae to Tatum in the heart of the Horowhenua
Steam hauled by Ab 608 ‘Passchendaele’, a 111-year-old heritage steam locomotive
Exclusive experience with a relaxed, premium atmosphere
Classic High Tea at Tatum, featuring a curated selection of treats
A short-format afternoon escape, perfect for a refined day out

Fares
$149 per person — includes return steam train travel and High Tea experience at Tatum, boarding at either Paraparaumu or Waikanae.

description:
Snacks Amore, When the host brings you bread, instead of a red flag...Snacks Amore!
Amuse Snack Bar invites food lovers to ditch the dating apps for one delicious night of light-hearted speed dating and snack-based bonding at their Euro-inspired aperitivo haven. Whether you are after a snack (human) or a snack (sustenance), you're guaranteed to leave with a full heart and a satisfied appetite.
Each attendee will enjoy 12 mini dates and 6 courses of Italian-inspired snacklets – cacio e pepe, agrodolce, pasta alla norma, porchetta, and zabaione, all served in perfect bite-sized form. A glass of Lambrusco kicks off the evening, with a cheeky mini tiramisu maritozzo to take home. Throughout the event, wines curated by the charming Richard Klein of Artigiano Imports will be on offer, alongside Amuse’s house spritz, Negroni, and Parrotdog Lager.
The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming – more aperitivo hour than high-pressure matchmaking. The Amuse team, also musicians, will guide the evening with playful icebreakers, musical moments, and a light-touch structure that makes meeting new people easy and enjoyable.
Two themed evenings allow guests to choose their best fit:

description:
Songs from the Deep, LBQ drops anchor for one night, trading its usual warmth for something saltier. Long communal tables, low light, rope and timber, and the Pōneke Shanty Club leading the room through some rousing singalongs.
Sea shanties were never written down. They travelled port to port, voice to voice, and that's exactly how the evening works. By the second set the room is carrying the chorus. Between the music, anonymous dockside confessions are read aloud and become part of the night's folklore.

Food is hearty and built for winter: slow-braised beef cheek and dark ale pie, or roasted kūmara and caramelised onion pie to start. Char-grilled market fish or a smoked mushroom and lentil wellington to follow, and a spiced rum sticky pudding or dark chocolate and sea salt tart to close.

Your ticket includes three courses and three drinks. Choose from curated beer, rum, or non-alcoholic ginger beer.

description:
Sunday Curry Sunday! - With the Multicultural collective, Sunday Curry Sunday! - With the Multicultural collective
So this time we are doing a bit more hands on...


D'ya like curry? D'ya like cooking?

Come make cutlets Srilankan style and eat them with curry!

Fuelled by Aiyo and the Multicultural collective of Porirua, a select few are in vited to Join Kushal and bang out some amazing Srilankan cutlets , whip up some severely tasty curry and hoover them down with a nice cold Springblossom Yuzu White Ale! Cooking spots are limited so get in quick!

Reserve a space here:
https://events.humanitix.com/cooking-class-sri-lankan-cutlets

from Aiyo and the MCC:
Can You Stop at One? (We dare you!)

A Sri Lankan cutlet is history disguised as a snack. European croquettes crash-landed on the island centuries ago, and Sri Lankans didn’t just borrow the idea — they rewired it. Fish and potato for thrift, chilli and mustard seed for heat, curry leaf and lime for brightness, all sealed in breadcrumbs and fried in coconut oil. One bite tells you everything about the island: layered trade routes, colonial collisions, ingenuity in the kitchen, flavour turned into defiance. It’s super-tasty — crisp, molten, impossible to stop at one.

Now you get to make your own and learn a bit about Sri Lankan culture.

We’re running a hands-on cutlet class where flavour is learned by instinct, not measuring spoons. You mix, taste, adjust, and chase that perfect balance of heat, comfort and citrus brightness. We bring every ingredient; you bring an appetite and the willingness to get your hands involved.

We’re being hosted by the crew at The Beer Engine — and their Yuzu Hazy is the move. Bright and citrusy, it slices through the richness and wraps around the spice in a way that makes you sit back and swear under your breath. When the frying’s done, we sit together and eat your creations with simple rice and Aiyō dhal. Big flavour, cold beer, good people. The kind of night food lovers remember.

From delicate hand-pressed pieces to beautifully rolled varieties, you’ll watch each step come to life in an engaging demonstration that’s both practical and inspiring.

Balarama’s grounded and approachable style makes the process easy to follow—even if it’s your first time exploring sushi-making. There’ll be space for questions throughout, and plenty of tastings along the way—so come hungry!

On the menu for the demo:

* Hand-pressed sushi (Nigiri)

* Sushi rolls (Maki-zushi)

* Tofu pocket sushi (Inari-zushi)

Afterwards, stay on for a full vegan dinner and dessert, freshly served and enjoyed in good company—a deliciously relaxed way to spend your evening.

Meet Balarama, your chef & host
Say hello to Balarama, our amazing chef who’s always meditating on his next culinary creation. At Bhakti Lounge, he’s known for mastering a range of cuisines—from comforting classics to vibrant international dishes. Lately, he’s been exploring the delicate and artful world of Japanese cooking, crafting plant-based sushi that’s as beautiful as it is flavorful. Balarama’s goal is to make food that feels nourishing, thoughtful, and easy to enjoy—like a home-cooked meal made with heart. With his calm, down-to-earth style, he makes even the most intricate dishes feel approachable.

description: Sweet Sensations, Noble Rot wants to sing the praises of sweet wines and help you to learn that they aren't just one note. They'll showcase a range of wines from around the world that lean towards the sweeter side without leaving a cloying sensation on your palate, enhanced by a specially-curated five-course degustation menu from entree to dessert. If you would like to explore your favourite level of sweetness in wine, this event is for you. The knowledgeable Noble Rot team are here to show you that sweetness is one of wine’s most versatile assets, as well-balanced sweetness in wine can be delicate, elegant and complementary to both sweet and savoury dishes. Discover how some grape varieties are more suited to producing sweeter wines and how their level of sweetness is achieved. If you're into the sweeter things in life, this one is for you.

The estimated time to enjoy the full Le Cordon Bleu 5 course dining experience is 2 hours. We invite you to sit back, relax and enjoy our students' creations.




What is Brasserie Le Cordon Bleu?
Brasserie Le Cordon Bleu is our training restaurant where our students get practical experience in a real restaurant environment - all under the expert guidance of their chef lecturers. In the kitchen, we have students from our Diplôme de Cuisine programme. In the dining room we have our Bachelor of Culinary Arts and Business students serving you and putting their theory skills into practice.

description:
THE WAY OF TEA Workshop, The Way of Tea is a traditional Japanese art—a ritual that embodies the mindful practice of harmony and tranquility in everyday life. Our Herbal Tea Ritual is our interpretation of the Way of Tea, infused with the therapeutic benefits of herbal medicine, bringing traditional knowledge into the modern world. You will be expertly guided by our knowledgeable herbalists in the art of mindful herbal tea blending.
You will discover the therapeutic qualities and unique tastes of nine medicinal herbs, focusing on their calming, grounding, uplifting, healing, balancing, and energising properties. From these, you will select your favourites to blend into your own unique tisane—a medicinal infusion.
Throughout the workshop, you will take time to reflect on the tastes, sensations, and effects of each herb as you infuse and taste your new herbal blend. You will leave with a tranquil mind, 50g of your custom tisane, a stainless steel infuser, and the embodied experience of this mindful ritual to invoke each time you brew your blend.
To complement your tea tasting, enjoy a selection of handcrafted bites from the Oatery.

description:
Talanoa for Tomorrow: Rethinking the Way We Live - 20 Aug, Overview

What if creating a better future starts with rethinking the way we live today?

FREE EVENT: Join us for an evening of conversation, connection, kai, and practical ideas for building more sustainable and resilient communities.

Who is this for? Anyone interested in creating a more sustainable and resilient future, whether you're already taking action or simply wondering where to start.

We'll bring together leaders, changemakers, and community voices to explore:

🌿 What can we actually do at home?
🌏 How can we build stronger, more resilient communities?
💡 What new ideas and innovations are making sustainable choices easier?
🤝 How can we learn from each other and turn ideas into action?




6:00–7:00 PM: Talanoa, panel & audience Q&A

7:00–8:00 PM: Kai, connection & networking




Talanoa for Tomorrow is taking place across four Wellington sessions, with a different panel of speakers at each event.




We are excited to announce for this session we have:

Rose Dohig is a Community Farm Manager at Kaicycle, where she has spent the last three years connecting people to the whenua and to each other. She believes that community building is one of the most effective tools for tackling the impacts of climate change and loves bringing this vision to life through her mahi. Kaicycle is an urban farm and composting initiative in Newtown that has been operating since 2015. The initiative connects people of all ages with the whenua, shares knowledge and skills on regenerative Hua Parakore growing practices, collects and composts food scraps from local businesses and households using e-bikes, and donates both grown kai and compost to local community programmes. Their education programme connects tamariki and rangatahi to food systems, climate action, kai, and the whenua.




Joshua Peauafi is a Pacific leader, social impact advocate, and co-founder of Potplant Studio. Passionate about relational leadership, diversity, equity, and inclusion, Joshua uses nature and plants as a vehicle to spark meaningful conversations around wellbeing, mental health, and community connection across Aotearoa New Zealand.


Can't make this date?

Check out our other sessions and find a date that works for you:

Tuesday 18 August
two/fiftyseven, Wellington

Wednesday 26 August
Wellington Chamber of Commerce

Thursday 27 August
two/fiftyseven, Wellington




With different speakers and perspectives at each session, there will be something new to discover:




Let’s talanoa about fresh ideas to reduce waste, rethink how we live, and create a better tomorrow together.




Spaces are limited




Hosted by POTPLANT STUDIO, in partnership with Wellington City Council.

description:
Talk Truffle To Me, Executive Chef Carl Maunder has spent two decades with truffles: exploring, refining dishes that let them truly shine, building an entire culinary philosophy around one ingredient. 

Indulge in five courses built around Périgord and Bianchetto truffles at the height of their season. Hand-prepared scallops with truffle, beef fillet Rossini reimagined, house-made truffle brie. Every course carries the same special ingredient, yet every course reveals something different about this heady ingredient. Carl shares insights throughout the long lunch: why this preparation, why this wine, what makes a truffle matter enough to shape a chef's craft. You'll taste the earthy weight of it, catch the aroma before the plate lands, understand the precision behind each dish. Each course is paired with a beverage chosen to meet the truffle's character.

description:
Tanzanian Dinner, Tanzanian Cuisine Dinner – Returning for a Limited Season

After winning Best Event at last year’s WOAP, our celebrated Tanzanian Cuisine Dinner is back — for two weeks only.

Experience an evening designed for discovery, comfort, and generous sharing. Guests are invited to order as many dishes as they wish from a specially curated menu showcasing classic Tanzanian flavours, traditions, and vibrant spices. This is not a set menu, but a relaxed dining experience that encourages exploration at your own pace.

To complement the food, an optional pairing menu featuring wines, beers, and thoughtfully crafted non-alcoholic beverages will be available each evening.

Event Dates:
May 7th, 8th, 9th
May 14th, 15th, 16th
June dates added due to high demand!

Time:
6:00 PM – 8:30 PM

Join us for a warm, flavour-driven dining experience that quickly became one of our most loved and awarded events.

Seats are limited.

We are offering a tasting menu with 5 tasting plates for $62 per person, or the main event, a 5-course dinner for $82 per person.

OPTION 1: TASTING MENU
5 Tasting Plates — $62 per person
Option to order extra plates at additional cost!

Course 1: Mshikaki ya Ng’ombe
Charcoal-grilled beef skewers
Marinated in garlic, ginger, lemon and pili pili.
Served with fresh kachumbari (tomato–onion salad).

Course 2: Viazi Karai

Golden fried, dusted with masala,
served with tamarind-coconut chutney.

Course 3: Maharage ya Nazi
Slow-simmered red kidney beans in coconut cream
Fragrant with turmeric and cardamom.
Served with turmeric basmati rice.

Course 4: Kuku wa Kupaka
Grilled chicken in rich coconut curry sauce
Charred first, then simmered in spiced coconut gravy.
Served with chapati.

Course 5: Mandazi
Traditional doughnut
with mango passion curd.

Plated Culinary Experience — $82 per person

This version is more structured and elevated — designed like a progressive tasting journey from coast to mainland.

Amuse-Bouche

Lightly spiced coconut doughnut
with mango and passionfruit curd.

Entrée

Tamarind & Lime Sorbet
A bright palate cleanser.

served with fragrant Swahili pilau rice,
kachumbari and pili pili sauce.

(Vegetarian option: Mchuzi wa Mboga – seasonal vegetable skewers)

Grilled chicken in rich coconut curry sauce
Charred first, then simmered in spiced coconut gravy.
Served with chapati.

Dessert
