description:
Taste & Create - A Painting with Sugar Valentine Affair, Taste and Create a palette of passion at the historic Inverlochy house. Join us in indulging in hand-crafted pastries by the renowned Maxine Schecter of Sugar Flour while working with Inverlochy's skilled tutors to create a piece of art in your choice of medium (drawing, printmaking, pastel painting, ceramics). Pastries are paired with refined tea and non-alcoholic bubbles.

The exact pastries are going to be a surprise (we'll drop hints along the way in the lead up to the event)! So pastries pictured are not what you'll get. The pastries will be incredibly seasonal and fruit focused (if anyone has any fruit allergies they’re unsure of you can can contact Maxine directly before booking). Maxine can also offer gluten free and gelatine free options for the dietaries too.

About the team:

Maxine Schecter is a French trained pastry chef who has worked in restaurants and patisseries in Wellington (Logan Brown), Paris (Gâteaux Thoumieux), London (The Fat Duck and Sketch) and is the author of Patisserie Made Simple: The Art of Petits Gateau.

Inverlochy Art School offers a broad range of high quality art classes and workshops, taught by a community of enthusiastic and talented practicing artists all year round. We believe in art for art's sake and allow students to find freedom in creative exploration.

description:
Te Kanapu: the grid blueprint for Aotearoa in 2050, Overview

Join YEPN Wellington to tackle key questions to help Transpower and New Zealand prepare for the electricity system of the future

What should Aotearoa's electricity grid look like in 2050?
Wellington YEPs, help us tackle key questions to allow New Zealand to prepare for the electricity system of the future.
After a fantastic turnout last year, Transpower and YEPN are teaming up again to invite you to another evening of big ideas and good company on Thursday 30 July.
You'll throw your ideas into the mix, meet people from across the sector, and feed into Te Kanapu, Transpower's programme developing a blueprint for a reliable, resilient and affordable grid for the coming decades.
As the next generation of the energy workforce, we've got a real stake in these decisions. This is our chance to get involved.
We'll kick off with an update from Future Grid leaders John Clarke (Executive GM), Tania Lund (Programme Director) and Andrew Sykes (Technical Director), before moving into a fun and interactive workshop.
We're keen for voices from every corner of the industry, whether you’re an economist, engineer, policy pro, regulator or out in the field.
Came along last year? We'd love to see you back for round two. New faces just as welcome.
As always, the evening will finish with drinks and nibbles so we can keep the convo going.

description:
Tea & Chocolate Tasting Event, Join Libertine Blends and Baron Hasselhoff’s for an inspiring and delicious evening of tea and chocolate tasting!

To celebrate the launch of our Tea & Chocolate Tasting Gift Box, we’ll guide you through 8 pairings of small-batch organic tea and exceptional bean-to-bar chocolate.

Hosted by local chocolate expert (and tea lover!) Luke Owen Smith and Baron Hasselhoff’s ‘Chief Chocolate Disciple’ Clayton McErlane, this event will celebrate the quiet magic that happens when tea and chocolate combine. description:
The Cake Club Picnic 3.0✨️, The Cake Club Picnic 3.0✨️
Love cake? So do we! Join us at The Cake Club Picnic – a one-of-a-kind gathering dedicated exclusively to cake. You don't want to miss it!

About this Event

Welcome to The Cake Club Picnic! 🍰
By popular demand and our first cake picnic was a success, we are happy to host another epic Cake Picnic!
Join us for a deliciously fun day out at Bellevue Gardens Hotel on Sunday, November the 8th, 2026.
Whether your a professional baker, a passionate home baker, or simply someone with a sweet tooth, The Cake Club Picnic is the perfect event to indulge your love of all things cake!
Entry requires both a ticket and a cake - one per person.
Everyone attending must bring a cake of their own. No cake, no entry - no exceptions. This rule keeps things fair and fun for everyone involved.
Even if you're bringing a guest under tickets you have purchased, they must bring a cake too. Sharing one cake between two people won’t cut it. We appreciate your understanding and commitment to the cake-loving community!
🎂 What to Expect:
A relaxed indoor and outdoor garden setting - enjoy the space rain or shine!
A shared cake table filled with baked goodies brought by everyone attending - taste, share, and show off your creations!
Chill vibes and great company - meet fellow cake lovers, swap stories, and make sweet memories.
Picnic-style seating - bring a blanket, find a sunny spot, or grab a seat indoors.
A self-service tea and coffee station to keep your cup full as you sample cakes.
Cake Size Requirement:
Please bring a cake that can generously serve at least 12 people. Think full-sized bakes -enough to share and make sure everyone gets a proper slice (or two)! 🎂✨ - REMEMBER - CAKE ONLY!
Cake Set-Up:
You’re welcome to do final touch-ups at the venue, but please avoid full setups or major decorating on-site. Display tables will be shared with other guests, so we want to keep things smooth and stress-free for everyone.
Serving Tools, cake detailed label & Cake Stands:
Please remember to bring your own serving tool so guests can easily cut and enjoy your cake.
We will provide you with a cake label card and card insert stick for everything to look uniformed!
Want to show off your creation? Feel free to bring a cake stand to elevate your cake-literally and visually! 🍰🔪✨
Boxes & Utensils:
We've got you covered! The host will provide boxes for you to pack up cake slices during the event, along with forks, spoons, napkins, and water to keep things easy and enjoyable. 🍴📦💧
Rubbish:
Let’s keep the vibes sweet and the space clean! Please use the bins provided on-site and help us leave the venue just as lovely as we found it. We also kindly ask that you take any leftover rubbish or personal items with you when you head out. ♻️🧼💛


Disclaimer & Event Guidelines
This is a community-friendly event, and all participants are expected to behave in a respectful and responsible manner toward others. By attending, you agree to be patient, follow the event rules, and respect everyone's space, time, and contributions.
If you are bringing a homemade cake, you confirm that it has been prepared in a clean and safe environment to the best of your ability. Please note that food is consumed at your own risk, and the event organisers and venue accept no responsibility for allergic reactions or food-related illnesses.
Cakes that contain common allergens (e.g. nuts, dairy, eggs, gluten) must be clearly labelled to help others make informed choices.
This event will be photographed and filmed for use in future marketing, content, and social media promotion. By attending, you grant permission for your image and likeness to be used across both online and offline platforms by the event organisers.
You attend this event at your own risk. The organisers, volunteers, and venue are not liable for any injury, loss, damage, theft, or illness that may occur. Please keep an eye on your personal belongings - you are responsible for them.
Thank you for helping us keep this a fun, safe, and inclusive experience for all! 🍰💛
Bring your appetite, your friends, and your best bake. Everyone is welcome - just come ready to relax, connect, and enjoy a truly sweet day out!


Agenda


🕑: 11:00 AM - 03:00 PM
How the Cake Club Picnic Work
Info: You’re welcome to arrive from 11AM to set up your cake and take some time to admire everyone else’s beautiful creations before the event officially begins. Cake Cutting & Group Rotation-

To keep things fun and relaxed, all participants will be grouped by coloured wristbands, which you’ll receive at the registration table.

When it’s your group’s turn, you’ll have 5 minutes to browse and slice a piece from any cakes you’d like to try. This helps make sure everyone gets a fair and enjoyable experience sampling all the amazing creations.

Once all groups have had their turn, feel free to go back and enjoy any leftover cake! ?


Important: Please don’t take or use other people’s serving utensils or display stands - these belong to the cake owners and need to be returned to them. Thank you for being respectful and keeping the cake vibes sweet!

description:

If you’ve ever looked at the flow chart for partial triple distillation, you’ll know that this sort of thing can be pretty complex!
But fear not, I promise we won’t be getting too scientific - and we’ll taste an interesting mix of official and independently bottled crackers, across a multitude of ages from some all-time fave distilleries; Mortlach, Benrinnes, Bunnahabhain and Amrut.
Here’s the lineup…
Bunnahabhain 12 years old 2023 Cask Strength Edition 60.1% (Sherry casks) WB 87.27

Benrinnes Adelphi 13 years old 55.5% (1st Fill Oloroso Sherry Hogshead) WB 88.19
Amrut Triparva Triple Distilled 50% (casks as yet unknown) WB 87.19
Mystery whisky WB 88.11
I hope you can join me for another tilt at five tip top drams!

The Cheese Bar, After a barnstormer last year, Garage Project and Le Marché Français return with Cheese Bar, a carefully selected cheese and beer experience popping up for three nights at the Wild Workshop.

This is à la bonne franquette: no bookings, no set menus, just exceptional French and locally sourced cheeses matched beautifully with beer.

Build your own board from a counter display of soft, washed rind, bloomy rind, alpine-style, goat's milk, and blue cheeses.

description:
The Flipper, Bright lights, laminated menus, and paper-lined trays. Nate Auld, head chef at Mr Go's, rewinds the clock at LTD. with a 1990s New Zealand–style fish and chip shop, seen through a knowing lens. It's nostalgic and a little tongue-in-cheek: a highbrow, lowbrow take built for people who grew up on battered everything. 
Book a table or walk in for a one-hour sitting between 5–10pm and order from a succinct menu that treats the classics with care, without taking them too seriously. Mussel fritters that actually crunch, battered or crumbed fish done properly, hot dogs in their finest fried form, pineapple fritters dusted in cinnamon sugar, not shit chips, plus proper seasonings with lemon and housemade sauce. Drinks are there to smash back: Spritzes, crisp whites, and Waikato from the chilli bin. Dishes and drinks range from $6–$16.

The Great French Potluck by French Touch Welly, Kia Ora & Bonjour everyone!
Ready to kick off the summer season with delicious food and great company? Join us for a convivial French Potluck at the beautiful Botanic Garden!

Let's gather together, share our favorite dishes, and enjoy a lovely evening surrounded by roses.

description:
The Grower's Champagne, Champagne takes on a different voice when it comes from the hands of the grower. In conjunction with Truffle Wine Imports, Noble Rot presents a premium degustation menu dedicated entirely to Grower Champagne. These are wines crafted by the families who farm their own vineyards and bottle under their own names, often in very limited quantities.
The evening unfolds over five courses, each paired exclusively with Grower Champagnes. Expect individuality, texture, and precision, with some bottles rarely seen beyond their cellar doors. These are wines shaped by site, season, and personal philosophy, offering a clear expression of place rather than a large-scale blended house style.
Throughout the evening, the Noble Rot sommelier team will guide each pour, exploring what sets grower producers apart and why their Champagnes have become some of the region’s most compelling, coveted and sought-after wines.
Your ticket includes an amuse bouche on arrival, five courses, and seven grower champagnes paired throughout the evening.

description:
The Kava Experience - February 2026, Bula Vinaka and Welcome to Kava Culture, New Zealand’s newest destination for authentic Fijian Kava!
We are thrilled to invite you to another relaxing Kava Experience night. Whether you're a curious newcomer or a seasoned kava enthusiast, our dedicated team will warmly guide you through every step of this unique journey.
At Kava Culture, we offer a premium, traditionally brewed kava experience designed for wellness-focused individuals seeking natural relaxation. We pride ourselves on sourcing our kava directly from small Pacific Island farms, ensuring unparalleled quality and authenticity.
Immerse yourself in the rich traditions of the Pacific as you enjoy our exquisite kava in our calm, serene location at Kaitahi, beautifully illuminated by ambient lights. This is more than just a drink; it's an opportunity to connect with others, promote genuine stress relief, and celebrate ancient island culture with modern comfort.
Join us for a night filled with community, connection, and tranquility. Let Kava Culture transport you – no passport required!
Choose your journey:
* Mini Experience: $30 (1.5 hours)
* Full Experience: $50 (3 hours)
We can’t wait to welcome you!

description:
The Lock INN, Before late licences and 3am closes there was the lock-in.
When the doors officially shut, the real night began. If you were in the know, you stayed. Curtains were drawn, doors were locked and glasses filled. For one night only, The Thistle Inn is bringing that spirit back through an after-hours evening of drinks, canapés, long-table dining and live music. 
The Lock INN is a modern take on the after-hours tradition - an evening that begins with drinks and canapés before guests gather for lavish long-table dining once the doors close to the public.
Think generous shared plates, flowing drinks, and the kind of feast that’s built for passing, pouring and lingering at the table. As the evening unfolds, a live band shifts the atmosphere as the night carries on, as things move into a more social close.
It will be a little indulgent, a little rebellious and entirely unforgettable.
Your ticket includes canapés, a five-course shared feast, four drinks served throughout the evening, and live music.

description:
The Rumour Lounge, At The Rumour Lounge, you'll arrive to the sound of jazz and step into an intimate speakeasy-style dinner party with performances by one of Wellington's premiere drag performers. The night unfolds in three phases: roaming canapés as guests settle into the space and mingle; a move to luxuriously styled long tables where generous shared dishes arrive, rich, warm, enhance flavours designed for conversation and passing plates; and finally, dessert canapés circulating through a lounge-style setting as the space softens into something even more relaxed. 
Between courses, your host returns with moments of performance, theatre, and playful storytelling, keeping the energy alive and guaranteeing your dinner companions will no longer be strangers by the end of the night.

description:
The Seasonal Forecast Series: Winter, The Seasonal Forecast Series continues with Winter.
A four-part exploration of ingredients at their peak, highlighting the flavours & textures that capture the distinct character of Autumn, Winter, Spring & Summer.
For our Winter release, we've brewed a Belgian Stout with chocolate, cherry & rye. Dark chocolate & cocoa create a fuller, rounded mouthfeel, balanced by subtle cherry aromatics that help dry the finish. Rye contributes a restrained bready depth, layered with nutty biscuit undertones.
We'll also have Autumn's Rhubarb Farmhouse Ale pouring alongside it, offering a chance to revisit the bright, tart character of the season before.
Join us from midday on Friday 12 June for the next chapter in The Seasonal Forecast Series.

Drinks will flow throughout the evening, inviting guests to indulge as the magic unfolds.

Expect seafood aplenty, drunken waffles and hearty tavern fare. description:
The Trinity Hill Vintage Escape, The Trinity Hill Vintage Escape
The Trinity Hill Vintage Escape 🍷

Welcome spring in style and step aboard The Trinity Hill Vintage Express for a magnificent, all-inclusive rail and epicurean adventure. We are heading to Hawke's Bay for an exclusive winery experience at one of New Zealand's most prestigious estates.

Sit back and indulge as our majestic steam locomotive sweeps you through changing landscapes, winding its way through the dramatic scenery of the Manawatū Gorge toward sunny Hawke's Bay. There is no better place to experience the romance and grandeur of mainline steam than from our open-air viewing platform. It is the ultimate vantage point for taking stunning photos, capturing the thunderous echo of the engine, and taking in the fresh spring breeze.

Throughout the entire journey, our onboard licensed café carriage will be at your service. You can purchase a range of premium alcoholic and non-alcoholic refreshments, fresh hot coffees, teas, and sweet treats to enjoy right from your seat as the scenery rolls elegantly by.

Our tracks lead straight to Hastings, where a private coach awaits to escort you directly to the legendary Trinity Hill Vineyard in the globally acclaimed Gimblett Gravels district.

This exclusive afternoon centers completely around celebrated viticulture:
- Behind the Cellar Door: Go on an insider's tour to discover their world-class winemaking craft and rich heritage.
- Curated Artisan Lunch: Unwind on the stunning estate grounds with a premium lunch box featuring your choice of a hand-crafted sandwich (such as the bold Beef and Kraut with pickles and cheese, an elegant Chicken and Tarragon, or a vibrant Salad and Hummus with salsa verde).
- Perfect Pairings: Accompanied by a savory scone, sweet slice, and fresh fruit, your estate lunch is paired perfectly with a complimentary glass of Trinity Hill's flagship Hawke's Bay Collection Wine.

Your ticket covers your return rail travel behind a genuine steam locomotive from Kapiti, Horowhenua, or Manawatū, complete with reserved premium carriage seating offering panoramic views. You will have full access to our open-air viewing platform for unbeatable sightseeing and photography, alongside entry to our fully licensed café carriage throughout the rail journey. Seamless coach transfers will also be waiting in Hastings to transition you smoothly from rails to vines.

Once at Trinity Hill, you will enjoy an exclusive winery tour exploring Trinity Hill’s history and winemaking craft. To complement the afternoon, you will receive a curated estate lunch box featuring a premium sandwich, savory scone, sweet slice, and fresh fruit, paired perfectly with a complimentary glass of Trinity Hill's premium Hawke's Bay Collection Wine (or a non-alcoholic alternative).

description:
The wines of the South, An Evening of French Terroir
A Wine Dinner Featuring Provence & Bordeaux Thursday 5th of March 6.30pm
Join us for a refined culinary journey through two of France’s most celebrated wine regions. This exclusive wine dinner pairs a thoughtfully curated four course menu with exceptional selections from Domaine Peyrassol in Provence and Château Malescasse in Bordeaux.
Domaine Peyrassol – Provence

Nestled in the sun-drenched hills of Provence, Domaine Peyrassol crafts elegant wines that capture the essence of the Mediterranean landscape. Known for their refined rosés and expressive whites, these wines offer vibrant freshness, delicate fruit, and a whisper of coastal minerality.


Château Malescasse – Bordeaux

From the prestigious Haut-Médoc appellation of Bordeaux, Château Malescasse produces structured, expressive reds rooted in gravelly soils and generations of expertise. Expect layered aromas of dark berries, subtle spice, and velvety tannins that speak to classic Bordeaux character.


The Evening
Aperitif on Arrival;
4 course seasonal tasting menu
Guided wine pairings and tasting notes
Insight into the history and philosophy of both estates
This is more than a dinner—it is a celebration of craftsmanship, terroir, and the timeless harmony between food and wine.
Reserve your seat and savour the flavours of Provence and Bordeaux.
$150pp

description:
This is How We Eat, Chow celebrates the most powerful recommendation of all: the one shared across a family table.

Jimmy Mahakit (Isaan, Thailand) and Kunpheng “Ricki” Zhu (Jiangsu, near Shanghai) have each spent a decade as Sous Chefs at Chow. For one night, they cook together, presenting dishes learned at home through observation, taste, and guidance at the stove. These are recipes passed down through families, remembered rather than written. This is word of mouth in its purest form.

Jimmy’s cooking is bold, herb-forward, and grilled, with chilli heat and fermentation. Ricki’s focuses on balance, braising, clarity, and precision. The evening unfolds as a generous shared dinner, finishing with dessert.

Food  is made to be shared.  What begins as dinner evolves into a true Chow party, with matched cocktails flowing and a DJ building the energy.

Your ticket includes a shared dinner and matched cocktails. Additional drinks will be available for purchase.

Top 10 Rosé selection by Candice Chow, Candice Wine Chat

Rosé summer

Expect a relaxed, fun, sit-down evening — perfect for all levels of wine lovers ✨

Truffle Hunt and Taste Experience, The winter truffle season runs from June through August, making it the ideal time to join and watch skilled dogs in action and savour the rich, earthy flavours of freshly unearthed truffles.

This Truffle hunting experience has you enjoying a relaxed mid-morning hunt through Fiona and John’s truffle orchard of Oak and Hazel trees - Akura Truffles. Accompanied by their trained truffle dogs, they want to share this short but wonderful season and experience with you.

When you've found some of these treasured delicacies, pop around the corner to Le Gra Vineyard and Winery for a fun and interactive lunch inspired by these little black beauties.

You'll learn how best to infuse the truffle flavour into your food, taste some of the Opaki's finest and freshly hunted in delectable dishes, and, if you so choose pair them with local wines.

There are only 10 spots per hunt, ensuring a truly intimate and real hunting and tasting experience. Don't miss out; choose the date to suit your diary now.

description:
Tulsa Meets Martinborough, From cattle country to oil fields, from dive bars to dinner tables. Tulsa's food tells the story of America's heartland. General Manager Adam Cruz continues his "meets Martinborough" series by bringing the bold, smoky soul of Southern cooking to the Napoleon dining room's intimate fireplace. 
Five courses trace a culinary exploration: start with a Reuben egg roll (sauerkraut, corned beef, Russian dressing), move through fried pork ribs that legend is made of, followed by biscuits swimming in sausage gravy, and then slow-smoked BBQ pulled pork served with cornbread, fried okra, and black-eyed peas — sides that honour the agricultural plains. Strawberry pecan pie closes out the night. Each course pairs with a Martinborough beverage: hand-crafted brews from Martinborough Brewery, award-winning Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from Palliser Estate, a botanical gin from Margrain, and a Noble wine to finish with pie. 
Your ticket includes five courses and four standard drinks (low and non-alcoholic options available).

description:
Tītahi Bay Spring Community BBQ, Tītahi Bay Spring Community BBQ
It's (nearly) summer so it's time for a BBQ! Come and join us at 43 Kapiti Crescent (St Matthew's Hall) for a BBQ on the lawn. If it's bad weather, we will move into the hall.

All welcome! Dinner will be served from 5pm; we will make dinner, so just bring yourselves!



FAQ

Who is this for? Can I come along?

Yes absolutely, please come, we would love to have you. This dinner is for all the people who live in the beautiful community of Tītahi Bay!

What if I can't make it until a bit later?

That's all good, we will be serving a rolling dinner from 5 to 6.30pm so come whenever suits you. If you can only come a little later than 6.30pm, we will likely have more than enough so come anyway!

Can I bring my kids along?

Yes! In fact, please bring your kids along. We will have some games in the room and some options for crafts on the tables along with the food.

Do I need to bring anything?

Nope! Just yourselves, all are welcome just as you are.

But I really want to bring something to contribute?

If you would like to bring a salad to contribute to the BBQ, feel free to email us at and we can chat! We really just don't want this to be a barrier to anyone coming along.

Can I help?

Yes absolutely, this is a community event so help is always appreciated. It is also a great time to meet some other people. We will have some tasks for set up and also some for packing down and cleaning up. If you are interested in helping, flick us an email at

Will my dietaries be met?

We will make sure there will be options for these dietaries: vegan, gluten free, dairy free, and nut free.

If you have a dietary that isn't on there, feel free to check and flick us an email.

Can I bring my friend(s) along?

Yes, please bring your friends along, especially if they live in Tītahi Bay!

Who is this hosted by?

This idea is hosted by us, the crew who run Tītahi Bay Anglicans, but it is run with the help of our friends around Tītahi Bay. The hope is that this can become a recurring community event where others can join in on hosting this.

This is at a church, will I be preached to?

No, we promise that this isn't a Tupperware party bait and switch. While we definitely are a church, this event is for the Tītahi Bay community as a whole to be able to come eat together and connect.

description:
Tết Cooking Workshop - Celebrate Lunar New Year Through Food, Step into the flavours of Vietnamese Lunar New Year with a special hands-on workshop that brings tradition, community, and storytelling together.
Join us as part of the Lunar New Year Festival 2026 for a delicious cultural experience!
✨ What We’ll Make Together:
🍃 Bánh Tét / Bánh Chưng – iconic sticky rice cakes wrapped in banana leaves, symbolising family reunion and prosperity
🥒 Dưa Món (Pickled Vegetables) – crunchy, colourful pickles that balance the richness of New Year dishes
🍖 Thịt Kho (Caramelized Braised Pork) – tender pork simmered in coconut water, a dish that brings comfort, warmth and the taste of Tết
This workshop is designed for all ages — beginners, families, food lovers, and anyone curious about Vietnamese culture. Learn the meaning behind each dish and how they come together on every Vietnamese New Year table.
💛 Why Join?
• Experience authentic Vietnamese Tết traditions
• Learn recipes passed down through generations
• Connect with community through shared stories and food
• Take home what you cook
• Celebrate culture in a warm, hands-on environment
Sponsored & partnered with Pomare Taita Community Trust, E Tū Whānau & Hutt City Council.

description:
Unwrapped, Unwrapped: Whittaker’s since 1896 invites Chocolate Lovers behind the scenes to discover how a local maker became a global name. Set within the wider history of cacao production, the exhibition traces Whittaker’s story—from J.H. Whittaker’s founding vision and the iconic products that followed through to the company’s ongoing commitment to quality, beans-to-bar manufacturing and ‘Good Honest Chocolate’ values.

The exhibition unwraps the story of New Zealand’s Most Trusted Brand and features objects to delight all the senses. Visitors will encounter nostalgic memorabilia and classic advertising, a scent station that reveals chocolate’s layered aromas and artworks made in collaboration with contemporary creatives.

2026 marks 130 years of Whittaker’s. What began as J.H. Whittaker’s small family business in 1896 has grown into a world-class chocolate manufacturer, still proudly family-owned four generations on and based in its original Porirua factory.

Urban Wine Walk | Pōneke Wellington (NZ), The streets and laneways of Pōneke Wellington are set to come alive this Spring as a line-up of eight venues each play host to an incredible winemaker, who'll be there ready to pour and chat you through an unforgettable afternoon.

HOW IT WORKS
Kick things off at your chosen starting spot with something to eat, and then let the adventure unfold. Wander at your own pace, glass in hand, discovering incredible wines and venues along the way.
With a stellar line-up of winemakers, good vibes at every stop, and a guaranteed sell-out crowd, the Urban Wine Walk is the ultimate self-guided tasting experience you and your crew won’t want to miss!

PARTICIPATING VENUES & WINEMAKERS
1 - Choice Bros Ft. Coney Wines (NZ)
2 - Glou Glou Ft. Halite (NZ)
3 - Little Beer Quarter Ft. Hopes Grove & Aard (NZ)
4 - Lulu Bar Ft. Margrain Vineyard (NZ)
5 - Noble Rot Ft. VALLI (NZ)
6 - Panhead Tory St Ft. The Good Way (NZ)
7 - The Arborist Rooftop Bar Ft. Matawhero (NZ)
8 - The Tasting Room Ft. Tettonica Wines (NZ)
*Please note that traditional venue menus may vary due to the nature of the event.

TICKETS
Vino Lover Pass – $79 + Booking Fee (Limited Availability)
WHAT’S INCLUDED
Wine Tastings – Up to 3 wines per winemaker along the trail
$10 Food Voucher – Redeem at your nominated starting venue (before 1pm)
$25 Wine Voucher – Put towards event-day wine orders (six-pack minimum, participating producers only)
Event Essentials – Your official wristband & keepsake tasting glass

EVENT REGISTRATION & COLLECTION
Before heading to your nominated starting venue, swing by the official registration point to collect your wristband, tasting glass & vouchers.
Where: Panhead Tory St (1 Tory St)
When: Saturday 18th October | 11am – 1pm
Please note: The Urban Wine Walk officially runs from 12-4pm. Arrive early to grab your event pack and avoid the rush!

REFUND POLICY
Tickets are non-refundable (we’re all in for good times rain, hail or shine!). The only exception is if the event is cancelled or postponed by the organisers – then we’ve got you covered.

GETTING AROUND
One of the best parts about the Urban Wine Walk...? It’s totally self-guided! After checking in at your nominated starting venue, the day is yours! Wander at your own pace, discover new spots and sip your way through the trail however you like.

**Sorry kids, Urban Wine Walk is strictly 18 Years and Over!

About this Event


This 5-Course dinner expertly prepared by our Superior Cuisine students is not to be missed.

Join us for a romantic evening in the heart of Wellington, enjoy a complimentary glass of bubbles on entry and savour your loved one's company as our chefs and students prepare a delectable 5 course menu.

description:
Valentine's Day High Tea in the Flower Farm, Relax and enjoy some time out with a loved one, your partner, your mum or your good friend.

The High Tea consists of a selection of delicate finger sandwiches, savory and delightful, sweet treats accompanied with your choice of tea or coffee PLUS one fresh bouquet of flowers to take away.

BOOKINGS ARE LIMITED.
BOOKINGS ARE ESSENTIAL.
Your booking is for High Tea for 2 Adults and includes 1 bouquet of flowers to take away.

The venue Lavender Magic Flower Farm. The lavender has been harvested but the sweet calming scent still lingers. We are officially into the flower season - if you love dahlias then this is the place to visit.

High Tea in the hills, with a loved one is an ideal way to create a lasting memory blending tasty indulgence with natural scenery.


Nestled in a charming country garden, Lavender Magic offers breathtaking views of the Tararua Ranges, creating a stunning backdrop for relaxation and discovery. Whether you’re picking flowers, strolling among the lavender, or simply soaking in the peaceful atmosphere, this is the place to unwind and reconnect with nature.

Come see the magic. Lavender Magic — where tranquility blossoms and the stars are brighter.

Lavender Magic is a Lavender farm and a Cut Flower Farm. It has about 5000 lavender plants and grows a range of cut flowers. In season you will find pockets roses, lilies, sunflowers, zinnias.

Discover over 100 dahlias in the display gardens, all labelled so you can see the plants in situ. If you intend on buying dahlia tubers, rather than checking out catalogues come see for yourself, the size of the plant, the true colour and size of the bloom. Your visit may save you money from purchasing something that not quite right.

Since 2007 Lavender Magic has won many awards for the quality of their lavender oil, which can be purchased on site along with balms, creams and sprays in the small farm shop.

Plan your visit: Lavender Magic is a great place to take time out, relax and recover.
Wear - Good footwear to explore the lavender field and surrounding gardens.
Wear - Sunglasses and slip, slop, slap on if a sunny day as we get full sun.
Bring - Your pet, if you are a responsible owner and promise you will pick up its mess and will not let it annoy others.
Bring - A camera to capture some of the magic and create memories.
A toilet is on site.

Bookings are essential for this event.

Lavender Magic is a scenic drive, about 60 minutes from Upper Hutt and 75 minutes from Palmerston North.

If you want something a little more private, we do hire out our property for photography and special events, contact Pauline on lavendermagic@outlook.com

How to get there:
Drive past the pizza place to get to Lavender Magic - Pizza at the Water Mill Bakery is open (Friday Only 5pm-9pm). Make a day of it - Other things to do in the Mt Holdsworth area - Fernado Oscar Calligo may have Choripan the Argentinian Food Cart open (Check socials for dets) Paul Melser Pottery (Weekends Only), Jackie Pearson's Fine Art Gallery (Check for details), Rivenrock Mountain Biking Park (Check for details) and DOC walks (24/7) as Holdsworth is the main entrance to the eastern side of the Tararua Forest Park.

Mt Holdsworth, Carterton, Wairarapa is a great place to visit.

description:
Vietnamese Crab Noodle Soup - Bánh Canh Cua, Vietnamese Crab Noodle Soup - Bánh Canh Cua
Join Viet Hub NZ for a comforting winter cooking workshop featuring Bánh Canh Cua, a rich and hearty Vietnamese crab noodle soup known for its thick, silky noodles and flavourful seafood broth.



In this hands-on session, you will learn how to:



• Prepare and season a traditional crab-based broth

• Work with thick tapioca or rice noodles

• Balance flavours and textures with crab meat and fresh herbs

• Present the dish beautifully, Vietnamese style



Bánh Canh Cua is a beloved Southern Vietnamese dish, often enjoyed as a nourishing family meal. Its naturally thick broth and delicate sweetness from crab make it perfect for cooler days.



Participants will cook together, share stories, and enjoy tasting the finished bowl as a group.



To help keep these classes sustainable and support ongoing community activities, there will be an additional $10 contribution per class. This supports:



• Facilitator preparation and effort

• Administration and coordination

• The continuation and expansion of community workshops



This workshop continues our collaboration with I Love Viet Food and is made possible thanks to the generous support of:



• Hutt City Council

• E Tū Whānau

• Pomare Taita Trust

• Te Mako Community Centre

• Newlands Community Centre



Spaces are limited to ensure a quality, interactive experience.



Come warm your hands, learn a new skill, and celebrate Vietnamese heritage through food.

description:
Vietnamese Pâté Chaud (Bánh Pa-tê Sô), Join Viet Hub NZ for a free Vietnamese cooking workshop celebrating one of Vietnam’s most-loved pastries — Bánh Pa-tê Sô (Vietnamese Pâté Chaud).
In this relaxed, hands-on session, you’ll learn how this golden, flaky pastry is made, explore its key flavours, and hear the cultural stories behind a snack many Vietnamese families grew up with. The workshop is beginner-friendly and designed as a welcoming space to cook, taste, and connect through food.
What makes this workshop special is not just the recipe, but the sharing of culture, memory, and community. Whether you’re new to Vietnamese cuisine or reconnecting with familiar flavours, you’ll leave with new knowledge, warm food, and a deeper appreciation of Vietnamese food culture.
Free to attend | All ingredients provided | Limited spaces – registration required
Come cook with us, meet new people, and enjoy a meaningful cultural experience through food.
This workshop is proudly delivered by Viet Hub NZ, in collaboration with Te Tai Ohinga | Central City Youth Hub, supporting accessible, inclusive spaces for cultural learning and connection ❤️.

description:
Vintage cake masterclass, Step into the charm of classic pâtisserie and learn the art of timeless cake design in our Vintage Cake Masterclass.

In this guided, hands-on session, each guest will receive a 10cm mini chocolate cake — beautifully prepared and ready for decorating. You’ll begin with a live demonstration by Chef Shuchi Bhardwaj, who will walk you through the techniques and piping styles that define elegant vintage cakes.

Then, with expert guidance, you’ll recreate the design on your own cake, icing and piping step by step to achieve a stunning, nostalgic finish.

All materials are thoughtfully provided, including:

• Freshly baked mini chocolate cake
• Buttercream icing
• Decorations and piping tools
• Cake box to take your creation home

Whether you’re a beginner or a baking enthusiast, this interactive class is designed to be relaxed, creative, and enjoyable.

Gluten-free options are available.
$70 per person, including a hot beverage of your choice.

Come for the experience, leave with new skills — and a cake that looks straight out of a vintage bakery window.

description:
WELLINGTON Speed Dating For Ages 26-44 by Cheeky Events New Zealand, Overview


Get ready for a night of fun and connection at WELLINGTON'S hottest speed dating event!
Let’s ditch the apps together and embrace real connections. Say goodbye to the dating apps and hello to your very own Cheeky Love Story!
What’s included: Your first drink is on us—let’s toast to great company!
How It Works:
Before the event:
If you have the App store on your phone make sure to download the Cheeky Events App to set up your profile and upload a photo. The app is not avilable yet on Google Store so if you have a Google phone then save and use this web browser link instead to enter who you like and receive any matches:
https://app.cheekyeventsaustralia.com/

P.S. Don’t worry—it’s not a dating app! We’ve skipped the chat feature because we’re all about real, in-person connections.
During the event:
Check in to grab your name tag and free drink token.
Arrive on time to enjoy 15 minutes of casual pre-mingling.
Ladies stay seated while men rotate every 5 minutes—don’t forget to rate your matches in the app!
Take a quick 15-minute break before the next round.
After the rotations, feel free to stick around for some extra socializing!
After the event: Stay for extra mingling and check the app for your cheeky matches 12 hours later!
For more details, check out our blog: What to expect
Who knows? You might just find your next spark!Our IRL singles events (single mixers and speed dating events) are happening across Australia & New Zealand.
About Cheeky Events
We host fun, inclusive singles events across Australia & New Zealand! Whether you’re in your 20s, over 40, looking for love, or just looking to meet new people, our events are designed to bring people together. Whether you’re seeking romance, new friendships, or even networking, we’ve got something for everyone!
Follow us on Instagram:@cheekyeventsaustralia @cheekyeventsukandireland @cheekyeventsnewzealand @cheekyeventsukandireland @cheekeventsus
Visit our website: www.cheekyevents.net or download the Cheeky Events app to get started.
We can’t wait to see you at one of our events soon!

description:
Watercolour Paint and Wine Night - Wildflowers in Vases, Looking for a unique night out in Wellington? Join us for a beginner-friendly watercolour painting event where you’ll explore fluid colour mixing, delicate brushwork, and create your own watercolour artwork … in a bar!

Our artist guides you step-by-step through the watercolour process, so absolutely no art experience is needed. You’ll be encouraged to add your own personal touch along the way, making each painting uniquely yours. It’s the perfect excuse to try something new, switch off, and enjoy a relaxed night of creativity and good vibes.

Drinks: No drinks are included in the ticket price, but drinks are available for purchase.

Food: A delicious menu will be available to purchase throughout the event.

What is Paintvine?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality watercolour paper, watercolour paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit. Our events are held in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip on while you paint. At the end of the night, you’ll leave with a watercolour painting you created yourself – you might even surprise yourself with what you can achieve!

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website ⇒ paintvine.co.nz

Celebrate the final day of Visa Wellington On a Plate and the end of winter with the ultimate comfort food: mac 'n' cheese, served all day long.

Two of Wellington’s legendary food rescue and community dining champions, Everybody Eats and Kaibosh, are joining forces to serve piping hot mac 'n' cheese, raising funds to help feed the community. As official charity partners of the festival, they are turning comfort food into real impact.

For just $10, each bowl will help fund a three-course meal for someone in need through Everybody Eats or provide a day’s worth of food for a family via Kaibosh.

Customise your mac with a range of toppings and flavours, all made from rescued food, showcasing just how delicious food recovery can be. In the lead-up to the event, Everybody Eats and Kaibosh will be calling on their social media followers to share their favourite mac 'n' cheese combos, with the top picks featured on the day.

Diners can enjoy their meal seated in the Everybody Eats restaurant or opt for takeaway to share with the whānau or flat.

The goal is to serve 2,000 bowls and fund 2,000 meals for the community. Join the celebration, enjoy incredible kai and help make a real difference.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Whisky Galore Tasting: Kilchoman 20th Anniversary Tour, Founded in 2005 by Anthony and Kathy Wills, Kilchoman was the first distillery to be built on the island of Islay for over 120 years. In the 20 years since its founding, the Wills family remain driving force behind Kilchoman, keeping the traditions of farm-to-bottle whisky making alive on Islay.

Since their first visit to New Zealand in 2007, the Wills and their whisky have garnered an enthusiastic following, and it is with great pleasure that the team at Whisky Galore announce the 20th Anniversary Tour of Kilchoman, proudly presented by Catherine MacMillan, Brand manager for the distillery.

Join our very special guest Catherine MacMillan, all the way from the Isle of Islay in Scotland, for an evening celebrating the 20th anniversary of Kilchoman. This tasting is a celebration of all things Kilchoman for the past 2 decades, including several of the brand-new, limited edition 20th anniversary whiskies.

description:
Wine World Cup, This year, as the world turns its eyes to the football world cup, Noble Rot brings the competition to the table. For one night, the drama of football is reimagined in the glass, with each course framed as a head-to-head clash between two wine nations.
The evening begins with a welcome pour before a five-course degustation unfolds in match format. Each course is served with two wines presented side by side. It could be Argentina vs Chile or Italy vs France. You're invited to compare style, structure, character and flair across the world’s leading wine countries. The final course delivers one last decisive pairing to close the evening. The Noble Rot sommelier team will guide each “match,” sharing insight into regions, rivalries, and defining characteristics that give every wine its competitive edge.
Your ticket includes an amuse bouche on arrival, five courses, an arrival wine, and nine matched wines served head-to-head throughout the evening.
label: Food & Drink

We begin with a grounding meditation and explore five mindful techniques that awaken each of our senses before heading behind the scenes on a private tour with owner and winemaker Josh Scott.

The morning concludes in the Bistro with a guided sensory wine and food pairing that deepens our appreciation for flavour, texture, and the stories within each glass.

Spaces are limited! Reserve your place for a morning of calm, curiosity, and connection among the vines.

description:
Winemaker's Long Lunch, The return of an annual favourite. Each year, the Winemaker’s Long Lunch brings friends of Noble Rot together around a shared table, and rather than focussing on one region, this time they're welcoming legendary names from across all corners of the New Zealand wine community.
Settle in for an afternoon shaped by conversation, generous hospitality, and wines poured by the people who made them. Winemakers will join you at the table, sharing bottles from their own cellars and the stories behind them. Such as the significant vintages, the vines they grow, and the decisions that define their style. The atmosphere is relaxed and intimate, with time to taste, and ask questions over a glass (or three).
A relaxed three-course long lunch will be served sharing style, thoughtfully designed to complement a line-up of outstanding New Zealand wines poured throughout the afternoon in this fitting celebration of wine and friendship.
Your ticket includes three courses and wines poured throughout the afternoon by the winemakers themselves. This is an afternoon of genuine hospitality.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Wines of Poland, Poland's wine scene barely appears on most people's radar, which is exactly the point.  For this special evening, Noble Rot sommelier Maciej Zimny turns the spotlight toward his homeland’s emerging wine scene and the wider momentum of Eastern Europe.

Four courses of refined Polish culinary tradition will be served, each dish interpreted with precision to complement the wines and let them shine. Maciej shares his personal story throughout, the vineyard sites he knows, the producers finding their voice, the momentum building across a region that's changing in real time. This will be a wine education that feels more like conversation rather than lecture. Guided by Maciej’s passion for Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, alongside varieties long enjoyed across Eastern Europe, guests will be the first in New Zealand to taste bottles imported specifically for this event. Expect cool-climate purity, bright acidity, and distinctive expressions from a region finding its voice with growing confidence. 

Your ticket includes an amuse-bouche on arrival, four courses, six matched Polish wines, and Maciej's personal guidance.
label: Food & Drink

Whether you’re new to whisky or already have a favourite dram, this is a relaxed and approachable experience designed to be enjoyed by everyone.

As we cruise around on the Southern Hemisphere’s first fully electric passenger ferry, you’ll have the chance to enjoy good company, great whisky, and a different perspective of the city.

Join the Nelson Youth Council to make reusable beeswax wraps, reduce waste, and learn sustainable everyday habits.
🐝 Event Overview: Beeswax Food Wrap Workshop
Hosted by: Nelson Youth Council
Arrival Information
Please arrive at the Nayland College Reception (Front Office). A Nelson Youth Council volunteer will be there to welcome you and guide you to the workshop room.

Join us for a fun, hands-on workshop where you'll learn how to make your own reusable beeswax food wraps while discovering how small lifestyle changes can make a big difference for the environment. When attendees arrive, they'll be welcomed by Nelson Youth Council members and introduced to the purpose of the workshop. A short presentation will explain the environmental impact of plastic food wrap, how beeswax wraps work, and why reusable products are an important step toward a more sustainable future.
Participants will then move to workshop stations where they'll:
Choose from a variety of 100% cotton fabrics.

Watch a live demonstration before creating their own beeswax food wraps.

Every reusable beeswax wrap can replace hundreds of pieces of single-use plastic wrap over its lifetime. By teaching this practical skill, the workshop helps reduce household waste, encourages environmentally friendly habits, and empowers the community to make simple but meaningful changes.

opportunities to connect with others interested in environmental action

description:
2025 Taiwan Update Lectures, 2025 Taiwan Update Lectures
Join us for three talks by experts on different aspects of Taiwan

About this Event

Taiwan’s Multidimensional Energy Security Challenges
Professor Chyungly Lee
A stable and reliable energy supply is essential for a nation’s economic growth and development. In selecting fuel sources, nowadays almost all countries have taken climate change into account, adopted sensible clean energy transition plans, and designed a schedule to meet the goal of Net Zero. While pursuing a 3-E (energy-economic-environmental) balanced energy supply strategy, Taiwan, lacking indigenous resources, faces unique challenges of supply disruptions from over dependence on energy imports and possible blockade, quarantine, or invasion from Beijing. Any disruption of power supply or surge of energy costs could not only threaten Taiwan’s competitive edge in the global high-tech market but also undermine Taiwan’s internal stability and the nation’s survival. In this talk, Dr. Chyungly Lee will first present fact sheets on Taiwan’s energy status, summarize Taiwan’s current energy strategy, and then discuss dilemmas and vulnerabilities that Taiwan might face in the next few years.


What does Taiwan’s two-level politics tell us?
Professor Alex Tan
This presentation examines Taiwan as a critical case study for understanding the evolving challenges to democracy in the 21st century. Arguing that Taiwan serves as a “canary in the coalmine,” the analysis highlights how the island’s early and persistent political polarization—rooted in identity politics and the legacies of authoritarian rule—prefigures trends now visible in established democracies worldwide. The research explores how deep divisions between the Kuomintang (KMT) and Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), reinforced by institutional and social factors, have led to legislative gridlock, declining trust in political institutions, and a “democratic ceiling” that constrains further democratic development. Taiwan’s precarious geopolitical position, facing constant pressure from the People’s Republic of China, intensifies the dilemma of balancing national security with the protection of civil liberties. The presentation analyzes Taiwan’s innovative responses to disinformation, foreign interference, and public health crises, illustrating both the resilience and fragility of democratic systems under external and internal stress.


Gaming Taiwan: Indigenous Epistemologies in Play
Associate Professor Chia-rong Wu
This research explores how Indigenous knowledge systems in Taiwan are being revitalized through video games. Far from mere entertainment, these games draw on tribal traditions, ancestral stories, and deep connections to the land to create meaningful digital experiences. By blending oral storytelling with interactive gameplay, Taiwanese Indigenous game developers are preserving cultural memory while challenging colonial legacies. Titles like Princess Baleng, Tayal, VuVu, and Gadvia show how games can empower communities and pass down wisdom to younger generations in innovative and engaging ways. Gamers not only play a game but also immerse themselves in digital environments shaped by Indigenous perspectives and values. This study encourages all engaged audiences, including educators and students, to consider video games as powerful tools for cultural resurgence and learning. Focusing on Indigenous Taiwan, it highlights how digital games integrate historical consciousness and interactivity to reimagine the past and future of the island.

description:
50yrs Misuse of Drugs Act: What impact & what next?, The 1975 Misuse of Drugs Act (MoDA) has failed to deliver. Data from the United Nations Office for Drugs and Crime indicates the demand for drugs is greater than ever, while the supply of drugs knows no bounds. The failure and harm caused by the so called 'War on Drugs' is acknowledged globally and witnessed first hand here in Aotearoa New Zealand.

Back in 2011 a comprehensive review of the MoDA conducted by New Zealand Law Commission recommended the MoDA “should be repealed and replaced by a new Act …administered by the Ministry of Health”. HRCA wants to see that recommendation enacted.

New Zealand has a history for bold world leading policy reform: Woman’s Right to Vote; Decriminalisation of Sex Work; National Needle Exchange, Same Sex Marriage and most recently Drug Checking.

This half day Symposium will provide clear evidence why major law reform is necessary and detail the foundations upon which Aotearoa NZ can once again be innovative and lead the way with new drug laws based on evidence, research and experience -providing a safer environment for future generation.

Harm Reduction Coalition Aotearoa are delighted to have assembled a group of respected independent thinkers with vast experience of drug policy in Aotearoa and beyond, to reflect on the impact of the MoDA and to identify the principles and values needed to underpin new drug laws.

Warren Young: Prof. of Law & Former Deputy President New Zealand Law Commission.
Kirsten Gibson: Chair of Harm Reduction Coalition Aotearoa and Qualitative Researcher.
Fiona Hutton: Associate Prof. Institute of Criminology, Victoria University of Wellington.
Adam Dorsett: 40 yrs Living/Lived Experience of Prohibited Drug Use, 25yrs in Prison.
Julian Buchanan: Former UNODC Advisor and Criminology Professor.

This event is free and open to the public on a 'first come first served' basis.
However, eventfinda ticket holders will be guaranteed a seat.

description:
A Place of Firsts, Globally, citizens assemblies are widely used as an effective way to involve local people in deciding how to address complex issues such as climate change. Despite the repeated failure of standard policy processes, citizens assemblies have only recently made it to New Zealand. Register for this event to find out more about the Porirua Assembly on Climate and its innovations. 
Porirua is known for community-led innovations in governance and delivery, and the Porirua Assembly on Climate continued this tradition by being:
the first climate assembly in New Zealand,  
the first assembly co-designed and organised by an iwi authority and a community group, 
the first assembly process designed to honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi by using a tricameral design,  
the first New Zealand assembly to include children and young people, and 
by creating a new local governance body - the Porirua Community Leaders Forum - that sponsored the Assembly, holds its recommendations and can instigate ongoing community dialogue on local issues. 
Panellists will share learning on the Porirua Assembly’s innovations, talk about why the standard citizens assembly model was modified, dig into what enabled so many firsts and how these worked out in practice. They will reflect on this legacy and possible future impacts. Might these democratic innovations strengthen local democracy elsewhere in Aotearoa New Zealand? 
About the Host and Speakers
Jodi Watene is a Systems Change Lead at Te Rūnanga o Toa Rangatira Incorporated, was the project manager for the Porirua Assembly and is helping to establish a New Zealand Community of Practice on Indigenous Citizens’ Assemblies.
Makerita Makapelu is a Team Leader for Wesley Community Action in Porirua with a background in performing arts and youth work. She specialises in community-led development and grassroots systems change, and was one of the Porirua Assembly facilitators.  
Cally O'Neill was a participatory designer of community spaces until 2019 when she shifted her focus towards advocating for Te Tiriti-based deliberative democracy to address the climate and other contemporary crises. She is a founding member of Te Reo O Ngā Tāngata/The People Speak and was one of the Porirua Assembly facilitators. 
Future Unity, a youth climate group formed during the Assembly process will be represented by Orini Rokx-Taratu and Santino Morehu, who were participants in the Assembly’s youth and community streams.  
Emily Beausoleil is an Associate Professor at Te Herenga Waka - Victoria University of Wellington. Her research as a political theorist centres on the dynamics, conditions and challenges of democratic engagement in diverse societies. She is conducting an independent evaluation of the Porirua Assembly process.

description:
AI in Education: Part 1, Sovereign AI in NZ Education is a two part series that invites educators, AI developers, wh`ānau, students, and other interested people to consider how we - in Aotearoa - can design, build, and use AI tools. The goal of these sessions is to spark and support the creation of AI tools and practices that best serve the aspirations of our students and whānau, and blend well with the skills and insights of New Zealand's educators.
Part 1:
Generative AI is already in Aotearoa’s primary classrooms.  It is used by many teachers for planning and by ākonga both in and out of school.  However, policy, training, and culturally safe practice haven’t always kept pace.
In this talk, David Coblentz will provide research-based insights into:
teacher adoption patterns,
what students say they’re doing (and worrying about), and
where schools are missing guidance.
We'll also discuss what AI sovereignty could mean in education in Aotearoa New Zealand.
Then we can close with some practical steps for boards, leaders, kaiako, and whānau to support constructive and equitable AI use in Years 5–8.
*While the formal (and online) event will finish at 5pm, those attending in person are encouraged to stay on for snacks and drinks to share. Stay till 6pm or later, and get into the ideas more deeply, in a room full of good people.
David Coblentz is a Senior Statistician at NZCER. In addition to an undergraduate degree in Mathematics and Physics, David holds advanced degrees in Biostatistics (MS), History (PhD), and International Studies (MA) from the University of Washington in Seattle. Prior to coming to NZCER and transitioning into an educational research career in 2021, David worked as a biostatistician, data analytics director, and statistical consultant. David also has university teaching experience in history. His areas of interest include data analysis and data science, history education, evaluation, and AI in education.
Part 2 will follow within two weeks of David Coblentz's presentation. It will be an online event that features two or three local AI in education developers, talking about their current development projects.
We intend to record both parts and make them available via our community site - https://community.sovereignai.nz/

Accountability in War: International Justice and Accountability for Ukraine, Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has posed an unprecedented challenge to the international legal order — raising fundamental questions about accountability, reparations, and the enforcement of international law.
This expert roundtable brings together three visiting Ukrainian legal and civil-society practitioners for a focused discussion on the international justice mechanisms being developed in response to Russia’s aggression, and the role that partners such as New Zealand can play in supporting them.
The discussion will explore recent progress on:
the international compensation mechanism for Ukraine, including the Register of Damage and the newly established International Claims Commission;
ongoing efforts to ensure individual accountability for the crime of aggression, including the establishment of a Special Tribunal;
the broader international response grounded in the rules-based international order.
The roundtable forms part of the Oceania Fora on International Justice and Accountability, and is organised in collaboration with the Embassy of Ukraine in Australia, during the Ukrainian delegation’s visit to Australia and New Zealand in February 2026.

Date: Tuesday 17 February 2026
Time: 2:00 – 3:30pm
Venue: The Wellington Club
Format: Roundtable discussion
Afternoon tea: 3:30–4:30pm, following the roundtable.
Places are limited. Register if you wish to attend.

description:
Activists, Allies & Beyond: 40 Years Since Homosexual Law Reform, Activists, Allies & Beyond: 40 Years Since Homosexual Law Reform
Join us at Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Central Library for a free event celebrating the 40th anniversary of the Homosexual Law Reform Act 1986. We’ll be joined by Trevor Mallard, Linda Evans, Bill Logan, Onjei Bond, and host Gareth Watkins for a panel discussion exploring the social and political climate, and the long history of community activism that contributed to the landmark 1986 reform passing through Parliament.

The panel will discuss the political processes behind the bill and the opposing community campaigns that emerged during a deeply divisive period in New Zealand’s history. We’ll hear about the personal impacts this had on members of the rainbow community, the resulting legacies of the reform, and the ways it continues to shape the lives and rights of queer people in Aotearoa today.

Sunday 14 June, 2-3pm
Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Central Library (65 Victoria Street)
Ngā Pou Ruahine, Level 2
Free event, all welcome


About the Speakers:
Trevor Mallard was an MP for 35 years and served as a Minister and Speaker. More recently he was our Ambassador to Ireland, is now retired and spends his time gardening, walking his dog and helping with grandchildren. Trevor acted as “whip” for the Homosexual Law Reform Bill. His role was to keep a day by day count to help ensure the numbers were there to make sure it became law.


Linda Evans has been an activist in lesbian, feminist and gay politics in Te Whanganui-a-Tara since the 1970s. She was involved in the ongoing campaigns for homosexual law reform and anti-discrimination laws in the 1970s and 1980s. Linda is a trustee and voluntary curator for Kawe Mahara Queer Archives Aotearoa.


In 1985 Bill Logan was a radical Wellington bookseller and involved in the Gay Switchboard and the response to the Aids pandemic. He became one of the organisers of the Homosexual Law Reform campaign to decriminalise sex between men. He remains engaged in socialist and community activism, and now works as a counsellor and marriage and funeral celebrant.


Onjei Bond is a recent Master’s graduate in Museum and Heritage studies, interested in the queer history of Aotearoa. He has recently finished a six-month research project focused on documenting and preserving the queer history of the Taranaki region – in collaboration with Pride Taranaki and Puke Ariki.


Gareth Watkins (he/him) founded the non-profit community website PrideNZ.com in 2009. It has become the largest online audio repository of local Takatāpui LGBTQIA+ Rainbow histories. The site now holds over 1,000 audio recordings of events and life histories, along with thousands of related news items dating back to the early 1900s—all freely available to a global audience. From day one, the website’s kaupapa has been to capture a snapshot of local communities, make that content easily accessible to the public, and help safeguard Rainbow heritage by ensuring the collection is available to archives in the future. In 2017, Gareth and his husband Roger Smith also founded Walktours NZ – a volunteer group that has run over 100 free, accessible, inclusive and community-focused walking tours exploring the city’s rich queer heritage.

We’ll be joined by Trevor Mallard, Linda Evans, Bill Logan, Onjei Bond, and host Gareth Watkins for a panel discussion exploring the social and political climate, and the long history of community activism that contributed to the landmark 1986 reform passing through Parliament.

The panel will discuss the political processes behind the bill and the community campaigns that emerged during a deeply divisive period in New Zealand’s history. We’ll hear about the personal impacts this had on members of the rainbow community, the resulting legacies of the reform, and the ways it continues to shape the lives and rights of queer people in Aotearoa today.

About the Speakers:
Trevor Mallard:
Trevor Mallard was an MP for 35 years and served as a Minister and Speaker. More recently he was our Ambassador to Ireland, is now retired and spends his time gardening, walking his dog and helping with grandchildren.
Trevor acted as “whip” for the Homosexual Law Reform Bill. His role was to keep a day by day count to help ensure the numbers were there to make sure it became law.

Linda Evans:
Linda Evans has been an activist in lesbian, feminist and gay politics in Te Whanganui-a-Tara since the 1970s. She was involved in the ongoing campaigns for homosexual law reform and anti-discrimination laws in the 1970s and 1980s.
Linda is a trustee and voluntary curator for Kawe Mahara Queer Archives Aotearoa.

Bill Logan:

He became one of the organisers of the Homosexual Law Reform campaign to decriminalise sex between men. He remains engaged in socialist and community activism, and now works as a counsellor and marriage and funeral celebrant.

Onjei Bond:
Onjei Bond is a recent Master’s graduate in Museum and Heritage studies, interested in the queer history of Aotearoa.
He has recently finished a six-month research project focused on documenting and preserving the queer history of the Taranaki region – in collaboration with Pride Taranaki and Puke Ariki.

Gareth Watkins:
Gareth Watkins (he/him) founded the non-profit community website PrideNZ.com in 2009. It has grown into the largest online audio repository of local LGBTQIA+ Rainbow histories, with more than 1,000 recordings of events and life histories, alongside thousands of related news items dating back to the early 1900s. The material is freely available to a global audience. description:
Are Prisons Obsolete? A future we make for ourselves., People Against Prisons Aotearoa is an organisation that calls for a transformation in our approach: not just towards what we'd call criminalised behaviour and people, but towards organising the whole of society to support human flourishing.
The carceral system is an industry that does not produce a product, but a world of limited potential. While in the immediate future the cessation of harmful practices such as solitary confinement or abusive 'boot camps' for youth might not require alternatives, abolitionists like Ruth Wilson Gilmore argue that abolition is brought about by building something new. Some alternatives have already been attempted, such as restorative justice, but these programs are routinely discontinued even when they show signs of success. Other alternatives, such as Turuki! Turuki! https://www.beehive.govt.nz/.../2019-12/Turuki%20Turuki.pdf or #CareNotCages, are an imagined future, where education and community involvement transform lives for the better, in contrast to the so-called 'Justice System' limiting them far beyond reason.

Professor David Capie is Director of the Centre for Strategic Studies and Professor of International Relations. He is also a Trustee of the Asia New Zealand Foundation.

Australia, New Zealand, and a post-American Asia, Foreign and defence policy in Australia and New Zealand needs to grapple with the likelihood that the US won't compete with China for regional leadership. Canberra and Wellington thus need to develop strategies that emphasise self-reliance, yet Australia in particular is pursuing ever-closer integration with the United States.
Sam Roggeveen is Program Director of the Lowy Institute’s International Security Program. He is the author of The Echidna Strategy: Australia’s Search for Power and Peace and Our Very Own Brexit: Australia’s Hollow Politics and Where it Could Lead Us. Before joining the Lowy Institute, Sam was a senior strategic analyst in Australia’s peak intelligence agency, the Office of National Assessments, where his work dealt mainly with North Asian strategic affairs, including nuclear strategy and Asian military forces. Sam also worked on arms control policy in Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and as an analyst in the Defence Intelligence Organisation. Sam writes for newspapers and magazines in Australia and around the world, and is a regular commentator on the Lowy Institute’s international magazine, The Interpreter, of which he was the founding editor from 2007 to 2014. Sam also serves as lead editor at the Lowy Institute, and editor of the Lowy Institute Papers.

Tuesday 7 October, 6pm
Unity Books Wellington
All welcome!

'Existing views of Featherston are fragmentary, negative and not very satisfactory. He was the “little Doctor”, a single-minded despot wielding tyrannical power and casting an oppressive shadow. As I began to understand more of his life, I realised that there was little appreciation of a man who had contributed so much.’ —John E.Martin

Isaac Featherston was at the heart of some of the most significant developments in New Zealand from the 1840s colonisation by the New Zealand Company to the abolition of the provinces in 1876. A doctor, newspaper editor and politician, he advocated for the provinces against the domination of central government, while also being primarily responsible for the relocation of the capital from Auckland to Wellington in 1865.

Known amongst Māori as ‘Petatone’ and with a reputation for directness and honesty, he was at the very centre of Pākehā–Māori relations, and in his 1857 official portrait is depicted alongside leading rangatira Te Puni and Wi Tako.

About the author: Dr. John E. Martin has researched and written about New Zealand history since the 1980s, teaching in universities and employed as a historian in the public sector. He was parliamentary historian in the 2000s and 2010s. His publications include rural and labour history, the history of science and engineering, and social and political history. His books include The Forgotten Worker (1990), People, Politics and Power Stations (1991 and 1998), Holding the Balance (1996), The House: New Zealand’s House of Representatives, 1854–2004 (2004), Parliament’s Library (2008), Honouring the Contract (2010), Illuminating Our World (2017), A Colonist’s Gaze (2018) and most recently Empire City: Wellington Becomes the Capital of New Zealand (2022).

About this Event

The next Café des Idées, organised by and , is honoured to host Wendy Nelson and Kevin Hackwell for a captivating discussion on the shared scientific and environmental connections between France and New Zealand in the subantarctic marine world.

Wendy will be talking about important marine collections made on French expeditions of discovery to the NZ subantarctic in the early 1800s that are housed in the Herbarium of the Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle in Paris.
Wendy has been collaborating with Professor Line Le Gall (Departement Origines et Evolution) and for two weeks in October they worked to locate and document these important specimens - uncovering answers to some long held questions about the identity of species described over 180 years ago and not found subsequently.
In this talk she will take you into the Herbarium of the Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle, Paris - and highlight some of the remarkable treasures housed there.
(This work was supported by funding from the French Embassy in Wellington and the Royal Society of New Zealand Te Apārangi.)
Kevin will talk about the importance of the marine protected areas in the subantarctic and initiatives that have been taken to protect critical habitat for southern seabirds and connections between French and NZ in this critical work.

Wendy Nelson is a botanist and marine biologist, currently Senior Research Fellow Auckland Museum Tāmaki Paenga Hira
Kevin Hackwell is an ecologist, formerly Chief Conservation Advisor for Forest & Bird, a sister organisation to LPO (Ligue pour la Protection des Oiseaux)

description:
China and the Media Landscape in the Pacific, Over the last decade, the People’s Republic of China has sought to deepen its ties with Pacific Island countries. Beijing’s efforts to cultivate influence in the region have included expanding economic, diplomatic, and security ties with Pacific Island nations, as well as expanding China’s footprint in the region’s media landscape. This talk will present the findings of recent research on China’s efforts to shape reporting, media coverage and narratives in the Pacific Islands and put Beijing’s efforts within the context of the region’s rapidly evolving information landscape.
 About the speakers:
Heidi Holz is a Senior Research Scientist at CNA. For close to two decades, her work has focused on PRC strategic communications, propaganda, and influence efforts. She is a graduate of Georgetown University’s School of Foreign Service, where she received a master’s degree in security studies and a bachelor’s degree in Chinese and East Asian history.
Genevieve Collins is a research specialist in the China Studies program at CNA, where her research focuses on the behaviour of China’s state-run media and its reactions to US military operations and activities.
 Barbara Dreaver (Discussant) has been the Pacific Reporter for TVNZ 1 News since 2002, breaking stories uncovering social and economic issues affecting Pacific people living in New Zealand and the Pacific Islands. In 2020, she created a two-year training programme through Pacific Cooperation Broadcasting Ltd to support new Pacific journalists across the Pacific region. In the 2024 New Years Honours she was awarded an ONZM for services to investigative journalism and Pacific communities.
 About CNA: CNA is a non-profit, non-governmental research and analysis organization dedicated to providing independent and objective analyses to the U.S. government and the public. This talk will build on previous CNA research on China and the Pacific Islands media landscape which you can find at www.cna.org.

description:
Community Information Day - Upgrading the Cook Strait cable, Transpower is hosting community information days in Makara and Picton about the work we’re doing in the coming years to upgrade Aotearoa’s electricity link between the North and South Islands. This session will be held in Makara.
New Zealand’s High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) Link has been in service since 1965. It helps keep our electricity system reliable and stable and allows Kiwis to access the lowest-cost electricity across both islands. It’s a critical piece of our national grid. The current HVDC cables were installed in 1991 and have an expected 40-year lifespan, so they need to be replaced by the early 2030s.
As well as replacing the three existing cables and adding a fourth cable, Transpower’s planned renewal programme includes building new cable termination stations at Oteranga Bay and Ōraumoa/Fighting Bay. This work is expected to start in the summer of 2027/2028.
Construction is still some time away, but we want to share our plans with communities near our sites and hear from them about how we can best understand and manage possible impacts.
Come along to Makara Community Hall on Sunday May 3, 10am-2pm.
Grab a coffee and cookie and meet some of the Transpower team
Learn more about the thinking and planning behind the HVDC Link renewal work
Quiz us on HVDC history (our specialist topic!)
Learn how we will update you on our plans

description:
Connected Theatres or Fractured World? Emerging Threats and Collective Responses Across the Euro-Atlantic and Indo-Pacific, Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 it has become clear that threats in the Euro-Atlantic region and the Indo-Pacific are profoundly inter-connected. North Korean troops and weapons have helped Russia’s war effort and Chinese technologies have sustained its military industrial base. Ships registered in the Pacific have been part of Russia’s sanctions-busting ‘shadow fleet’ and implicated in cable-cutting activities in the Baltic Sea. Conversely, Russia has transferred advanced weapons technologies to North Korea, and lessons from the war in Ukraine have implications for Indo-Pacific flashpoints, including across the Taiwan Strait. But if cross-theatre links are clear, forging collective responses has become much more complicated. The recent US National Defence Strategy points to a more limited US role in Europe and expectations that in the Indo-Pacific allies and partners will have to do more. International order is in flux. What does all this mean for New Zealand, for our region, for partners, and for global security? 
Confirmed speakers:
Prof Nick Bisley (LaTrobe University, Melbourne)
