description:
Beyond Sight: An Authentic Relating Experience, Beyond Sight: An Authentic Relating Experience

What happens when we set aside small talk, social roles, and even sight itself?

In this special evening, you’ll experience Dyad Meditation a simple practice of authentic relating. In pairs, you’ll take turns sharing and listening. One person speaks from the heart, the other listens with care and attention. No interruptions, no advice, no fixing — just the rare experience of being fully seen and fully heard.

The twist? You’ll be blindfolded

By removing the sense of sight, we soften our usual ways of navigating the world and allow ourselves to listen more deeply. to our own inner experience and to the person in front of us. This creates space for vulnerability, openness, and a raw connection that’s rarely felt in everyday life.

The atmosphere is warm, relaxed, and supportive - an opportunity to connect in a way that feels human, sincere, and refreshing, without pressure or performance.

You don’t need to come with anyone. Arriving on your own is warmly welcomed, and pairings will be created on the night, offering a chance to connect beyond familiar faces.

After the meditation, you’re welcome to stay back for a wholesome plant-based dinner - all included in your ticket!

Meet your host, Andre
Andre has been holding spaces for meaningful connection since his teenage years, when a rite of passage in Golden Bay first opened his heart to the power of circle work. Since then, he has continued to create experiences that feel safe, heartfelt, and deeply human. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and breathwork facilitator, Andre brings warmth, creativity, and sincerity to all he offers — guided by a quiet curiosity about what it means to truly meet one another.

description:
Beyond Sight: The Power of Dyad Meditation, Beyond Sight: The Power of Dyad Meditation
What happens when we strip away the surface layers of small talk, social roles, and even sight itself?

In this unique evening, you’ll step into the practice of Dyad Meditation — a powerful form of authentic relating where two people take turns speaking and listening in complete presence. One person shares, the other simply listens. No interruptions. No fixing. No judgment. Just the rare experience of being fully seen and fully heard.

The twist? You’ll be blindfolded.
By closing our eyes to the outer world, we drop our guards and tune into something deeper. This creates space for vulnerability, openness, and raw connection that we don’t often experience in daily life.

Expect an evening that’s real, grounding, and surprisingly freeing — a chance to connect with yourself and with others in ways that go beyond sight.

You don’t need to bring a partner or a friend — in fact, coming on your own is part of the experience. Everyone will be paired up on the night, so it’s all about connecting beyond familiar circles.

Afterwards, we’ll share reflections over a nourishing plant-based dinner, keeping the conversation alive in a relaxed space.

Meet Andre, your host
Andre has been exploring the art of authentic connection since his teens, when a rite of passage in Golden Bay first sparked his passion for circle work. Since then, he has been creating spaces that invite honesty, vulnerability, and depth — guiding people into experiences of being truly seen and heard. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and breathwork facilitator, Andre brings creativity and presence to all his offerings, inspired by the question of what it really means to be human.

Body & Soul PD Day, Body & Soul: Somatic Practice PD Day
Join counsellor, trainer and equine therapist Courtney Brown for a day of professional learning and personal rejuvenation. Courtney brings a dynamic, compassionate and playful approach to her work at the leading edge of somatic theory and practice.
Nervous system regulation is a major focus of research and interest for the power of the mind-heart-body connection to release stress and aid trauma recovery. Courtney integrates this with a passionate Christian faith through with her rich experience working with people and horses to calm the stress response and build resourcefulness.
Saturday 2 May, 9.30am-3.30pm (5 hours PD)
Fully catered.
An event of NZCCA Wellington, Rōpu Tohutohu Kairaitiana
Suitable to counsellors, pastors, chaplains, and anyone interested in holistic wellbeing and trauma.
Courtney Brown, MNZCCA, Holistic Horse Wisdom
https://holistichorsewisdom.com/

description:
Breathe Bro Workshop, Breathe Bro Workshop
𝗕𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗕𝗿𝗼❟ is a grounded no-bulls**t!

Breathwork Workshop/Journey created to support men with their mental heath, emotional resilience and overall wellbeing. This space is design for the brothers, father's, uncles, grandfather's who are ready to release stress, reconnect with their bodies and breathe through the pressure that life stacks on their shoulders.

Through a guided breathwork journey, somatic releases, and simple tools you can take home. Breathe Bro helps you reset your mind, regulate your nervous system and step back into your life with clarity, strength and presence.

A space for men to breathe, feel and heal together.

𝗕𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗥𝗢 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗠𝗘𝗗𝗜𝗖𝗜𝗡𝗘 𝗢𝗙 𝗕𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗧𝗛

Breathwork is an ancient, evidence-informed practice used to support healing, regulation, and expansion by bridging the nervous system, body, and mind.

Through conscious, circular breathing, altered states of awareness naturally arise. These states allow stored stress, emotion, and somatic tension to move through and release — without force.
Breathe Bro works directly with:

• Nervous system regulation
• Somatic intelligence
• Emotional processing
• Mental clarity and presence

As the breath deepens, the body’s own chemistry shifts. Breathwork influences brainwaves, cerebrospinal fluid, and the body’s innate capacity to reset.

Gamma brainwaves — associated with deep meditation, heightened awareness, and peak cognitive function — may be activated.

Some research suggests correlations between breathwork, gamma states, and the body’s natural production of endogenous DMT (often referred to as the “spirit molecule”). While experiences vary, many men report effects similar to deep meditation, emotional release, insight, and renewed clarity — without the use of substances.

Each journey is unique and meets you exactly where you are.

𝗕𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗥𝗢 — 𝗕𝗘𝗡𝗘𝗙𝗜𝗧𝗦

Men attend Breathe Bro to support:

• Stress, anxiety, and burnout
• Emotional regulation and resilience
• Improved sleep and recovery
• Increased energy and vitality
• Lower blood pressure and improved circulation
• Nervous system balance
• Releasing stored tension, stress, and emotional weight
• Trauma release and PTSD support (trauma-aware, non-forcing)
• Improved body awareness
• Greater emotional capacity and presence
• Mental clarity and focus
• Pain and restriction relief
• Increased confidence and self-trust
• Reconnection to intuition and inner guidance
• Purpose clarity and grounded direction
• Creativity and self-expression
This is not about “fixing” yourself — it’s about creating the space to reset, regulate, and come back into alignment.

𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗜𝗡𝗗𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦 & 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗬

Breathwork can create intense physical, emotional, and neurological responses.
For your safety, it is essential that you inform the facilitator prior to attending if any of the following apply:

• Severe PTSD or unresolved trauma
• Current use of recreational drugs
• Recent surgery
• Medications that alter brain chemistry (e.g. antidepressants, anti-anxiety, ADHD, OCD medications)
• Detached retina or glaucoma
• Kidney disease
• High blood pressure
• Cardiovascular disease (including previous heart attack or stroke)
• History of aneurysm
• Uncontrolled thyroid conditions
• Diabetes
• Severe asthma (mild/moderate may attend with discussion and inhaler)
• Epilepsy or history of seizures
• Bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or previous psychiatric diagnosis
• Any condition that may impair participation in deep emotional or physical release

This space is trauma-aware and integrity-led. Adjustments may be possible just reach out.

❓ 𝗙𝗔𝗤’𝗦

Q. What actually happens in a Breathe Bro session?

A. You’ll be guided through breathwork after a clear explanation of the technique, what sensations may occur, and how to stay regulated. There’s space afterwards for reflection, questions, and grounding.

Q. I’m not very emotional — is this still for me?

A. Yes. Breathwork meets you exactly where you are. Some men experience emotional release, others experience calm, clarity, insight, or deep relaxation.

Q. What if I have one of the contraindications?

A. Contact Tara via email () beforehand. She’ll let you know if adjustments can be made or if it’s best to wait.

🎟️ 𝗧𝗜𝗖𝗞𝗘𝗧𝗦 & 𝗦𝗣𝗔𝗖𝗘𝗦

Limited to 15 men — to maintain safety, presence, and integrity of the space.

• Standard Ticket — $55 per person ( Limited to 10 spaces)

• Koha / Flexible Pricing — (Limited to 5 spaces)

• Pay-It-Forward / Donation — Supports another bro to attend (This is advertised on IG @breathe.bro.nz - tag a bro)

𝗔𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗧𝗮𝗿𝗮 𝗚𝗼𝗱𝗱𝗮𝗿𝗱 — 𝗙𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿 & 𝗙𝗮𝗰𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿 𝗼𝗳 𝗕𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗕𝗿𝗼 🤙

Tara Goddard, from Wainuiomata, Wellington, New Zealand, she is a Sacred Ceremonialist, facilitator, and teacher, bridging esoterics and science together through spirit-led guidance, informed through lived, embodied experience.

She is the founder of Esoteric Medicine Pathways and Breathe Bro, creating grounded sacred spaces that support mental health, emotional resilience, and holistic wellbeing.

Tara’s breathwork lineage comes through HineHau BreathWav, an IPHM-accredited modality founded by Shannon Rose. BreathWav uses circular connected breath through an open mouth to activate the body’s natural, inbuilt healing intelligence.

This approach does not force cathartic release; instead, it honours the wisdom of the body by gently riding the waves of what naturally arises. Each session is intuitively crafted as Tara attunes to the group’s magnetic field, shaping the ceremony in response to the collective energy in the space.

With many years of experience across multiple modalities including Breathwork, Quantum Healing Hypnosis (QHHT Level 2), Sound Therapy, Energy Healing, Intuitive Readings, Plant Medicine, and Coaching & Mentoring Tara holds grounded yet multidimensional spaces that support nervous system regulation, emotional processing, and deep reconnection to self.

Tara’s work is trauma-aware and community-centred, supporting individuals navigating stress, burnout, grief, and mental health challenges. Through breath, presence, and embodied practice, she offers pathways that foster resilience, connection, and self-trust. Her facilitation gently reminds people that they are not broken they have always been the healer, and the medicine they seek already lives within them.

Tara is devoted to guiding people to bridge their inner knowing into embodied, everyday life, empowering them to reclaim their wellbeing, sovereignty, and sense of belonging to themselves, to each other, and to the world around them.

🫁 Breathe. Reset. Carry less ❤️

description:
Breathwork: A Gentle Reset, Breathwork: A Gentle Reset

Take a pause from the noise of daily life.

This breathwork journey begins with gentle movement to awaken the body and open the breath. Through slow, mindful stretches, we begin softening tension and grounding into the present.

You’ll then be guided through two styles of breathwork — each offering a unique pathway inward. There’s no pressure or expectation, just the freedom to explore what feels right for you:

A dynamic, connected breath for those who wish to build energy, move emotion, or break through internal blockages

A slow, rhythmic breath for those seeking stillness, calm, and deeper grounding

Both approaches invite a sense of spaciousness — physically, mentally, and emotionally — while supporting nervous system balance and inner clarity.

To gently close the session, we’ll move into a quiet, nurturing meditation to support integration and leave you feeling steady, clear, and connected.

Afterwards, stay and enjoy a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, lovingly prepared to complement the experience — because healing is also about how we feed and care for ourselves.

Why Breathwork?

Breathwork has helped so many shift from a state of tension and overwhelm into a place of ease, clarity, and resilience — often after just one session. It’s a simple, powerful practice that reconnects you to your body, your breath, and your inner stillness.

You’ll leave feeling more grounded, more present, and more like yourself again.

Meet Karla, your host
Karla is a breathwork and trauma-somatic facilitator based in Aotearoa (New Zealand), originally from Malta. With over a decade of experience in Reiki and three years facilitating trauma-informed, science-based breathwork, Karla combines holistic tools, meditation, and conscious breathing to support nervous system regulation and deep emotional healing. Her offerings help release stored trauma, reduce stress and anxiety, and activate oxytocin—the “love hormone”—fostering connection, vitality, and a sense of wholeness. She currently holds regular classes, workshops, and transformative retreats that nurture the mind, body, and spirit.

Breathwork has helped so many shift from a state of tension and overwhelm into a place of ease, clarity, and resilience — often after just one session. It’s a simple, powerful practice that reconnects you to your body, your breath, and your inner stillness.
You’ll leave feeling more grounded, more present, and more like yourself again.
Meet Karla, your host
Karla is a breathwork and trauma-somatic facilitator based in Aotearoa (New Zealand), originally from Malta. With over a decade of experience in Reiki and three years facilitating trauma-informed, science-based breathwork, Karla combines holistic tools, meditation, and conscious breathing to support nervous system regulation and deep emotional healing. Her offerings help release stored trauma, reduce stress and anxiety, and activate oxytocin—the “love hormone”—fostering connection, vitality, and a sense of wholeness. She currently holds regular classes, workshops, and transformative retreats that nurture the mind, body, and spirit.

description:
Burnout to Balance - Proven Techniques to Pause, Recover & Return!, This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
In today’s high-pressure world, burnout is often worn as a badge of honour—until the physical and mental toll becomes impossible to ignore. True recovery requires more than just "taking a break"; it requires resetting the nervous system from the inside out.
Led by Simon, a former high-stakes litigation lawyer who successfully navigated his own severe burnout, this workshop bridges the gap between understanding stress and actively healing from it. This practical, evidence-based workshop is designed to take you on a journey from chronic depletion to sustainable balance. You will explore what burnout actually is, identify your personal triggers, and master powerful physiological techniques to pause the stress response, recover your vitality, and return to life and work with renewed resilience.
What We Will Cover
Part 1: Understanding the Burnout Cycle (The Setup)
Before we can fix the problem, we must understand it. We begin by unpacking the foundations of chronic stress to help you map your own journey.
What is Burnout? Defining the psychological and physical parameters of exhaustion.
The Root Causes: Identifying the systemic, professional, and personal drivers of chronic stress.
The Nervous System Hijack: How prolonged pressure traps the body in a constant "fight-or-flight" state, impacting sleep, digestion, and cognitive function.
Part 2: The Science of Physiological Recovery (The Solution)
While mindset matters, burnout lives in the body. We will introduce the fastest, most effective tool for resetting a hijacked nervous system: Functional Breathing Training.
The Three Dimensions of Health: How biochemical, biomechanical, and psychophysiological breathing patterns dictate your stress levels.
Measuring Your Stress Tolerance: Learn how to assess your current breathing efficiency and physiological stress baseline.
Immediate Relief vs. Long-Term Resilience: Practices that offer instant calm during acute anxiety, paired with lifelong training to rebuild your nervous system.
What You Will Walk Away With
By the end of this one-day workshop, you will:
Recognise the Warning Signs: Deeply understand your own burnout triggers and early warning indicators.
Interrupt the Stress Response: Master proven, discreet techniques to pause the "fight-or-flight" response in real-time.
Improve Everyday Well-being: Know how to optimise your breathing patterns to combat poor sleep, fatigue, and brain fog.
A Personalised Recovery Plan: Walk away with a practical toolkit to integrate self-regulation and physical recovery into a busy professional life.
What to Bring: Please bring a notepad and pen to track your personal pacing metrics, record your breathing patterns, and map out your recovery strategy.
Participant Self-Management & Safety
This workshop is designed for adult learners. It is a supportive, respectful space where you are encouraged to engage at your own comfort level and self-manage your energy throughout the day (including taking breaks to decompress as needed).
Please note: The advanced physiological recovery techniques practiced in this workshop are highly effective for nervous system regulation. No prior experience with breathwork or yoga is required.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Burnout to Breath: A Somatic Reset for the Nervous System, Burnout to Breath: A Somatic Reset for the Nervous System

If you’re running on fumes, stuck in overdrive, or feeling wired and tired, this session is for you. Even if you’ve tried resting, you might still feel tense, foggy, or emotionally flat. This session is designed for those ready to reconnect to their body, regulate their nervous system, and rediscover their energy.

You might notice these signs:

Waking up tired, even after a full night’s sleep

Overthinking decisions and feeling emotionally reactive

Craving peace but feeling disconnected from your body

Often feeling “on” and unable to fully relax

Workshop Details:
Through guided somatic breathwork, gentle movement, and nervous system education, you’ll be supported to safely release stored tension, calm your system, and access clarity from within.

What to bring/prepare:

Comfortable clothing for movement

Water bottle and journal

Yoga mat provided

Optional: blanket, eye pillow, essential oils

Arrive: 5–10 minutes early to settle in

Unwind further with a wholesome plant-based dinner and dessert, a nurturing way to ground yourself and enjoy a sense of calm and connection after the session.

Contraindications for Breathwork:
Breathwork can be a powerful tool but may not be suitable for everyone. Please consult your healthcare provider before participating if you have:

Cardiovascular issues (e.g., high blood pressure, heart disease)

Respiratory conditions (e.g., asthma, COPD)

A history of seizures or epilepsy

Diagnosed mental health conditions (e.g., schizophrenia, bipolar disorder)

Pregnancy (some breath patterns may need modification)

Recent surgery or physical injuries that limit movement

You are always welcome to participate in the somatic and movement elements without engaging in deep breathwork—your safety and well-being are our priority.

About Lynofuro:
Lynofuro is an Integrative Somatic Coach and Breathwork Facilitator who helps intuitive, high-performing people overcome emotional burnout and restore energetic balance. Her work blends somatics, breath, and energy alignment to support lasting transformation.

description:
CBT skills for physical health practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand, Cognitive Behaviour Therapy (CBT) is a psychological intervention initially developed for emotional disorders. It is now widely used in supporting people to deal with the challenges of physical ill-health. Professionals from various backgrounds can learn to use a simplified CBT skills set, and use of these skills enables them to be more effective in managing aspects of their patients’ distress.
The training is a mix of theory, skills demonstration and skills practice, giving participants a better understanding of the applicability of the skill set in their area of practice and providing some skills to take away. Training sessions are spaced to allow participants to use their new skills in their clinical practice. Each participant reflects on their learning and their work with a specific patient, and the whole group reflects on lessons learned. In this way, learning remains rooted in participants’ clinical practice. These CBT courses are consistently evaluated highly by participants.
The Course
Teaching will be commenced with 2 days of in person sessions. 19th and 20th Feb 2026 at Mary Potter Hospice, Wellington and subsequently 2 sessions on-line via Zoom. These will be either 18th or 19th March an 22nd or 23rd April 2026.
Attendance at all sessions is mandatory to complete the course.
The courses cost is $850 per person (incl GST).
The Trainers
Kathy Burn was a Clinical Nurse Specialist in Palliative Care who went on to train in CBT and to develop the CBT service at St Christopher’s Hospice, London. She now works in CBT in chronic pain, and she teaches and supervises CBT trainees at the institute of Psychiatry, London.
Kathryn Mannix was a Palliative Medicine Consultant and CBT therapist. She developed ‘CBT First Aid’ to enable palliative care clinicians to adapt skills from CBT into their clinical practice. She is an author. There are insights into her use of CBT in her books With the End in Mind and Listen.
Terms and Conditions
Attendance: In order to create a learning community for each course, it is important that each person on a course attends every session and is able to join in the discussions by keeping up with the course. By accepting a place on a particular course, you agree to attend all the sessions, to arrive on time, and to work alongside your group members during the session to support each other's learning. Each session builds on the last, and you'll be asked to put your new learning into practice in- between sessions. Building learning groups in this way means we can't add new trainees after a course has begun.
We are not able to run catch-up sessions for sessions missed. If you miss sessions, you may be asked to withdraw from the course and no refunds will be given.
Refunds/Canellations: Once you sign up and pay, we won't be able to refund your payment unless we can reallocate your place to another person before the course begins. The deadline for cancelling your place is 28 days before the day and time of the first session. If you cancel and we can fill your place with another person, we'll offer you the choice of a refund or a place on a future course, if places are available. We will do our best to fill your place, but we can't promise this. Refunds will incur an administration fee.
Dates and Times of Sessions: all dates and times are given in NZ time, and this varies over the year. It is up to you to check the correct time in your time zone: you may find this website useful to check your own time zone with Auckland NZ time on each specific date: https://www.worldtimebuddy.com/
Trainers: we have a team of trainers, all of whom are experienced CBT therapists and trainers, and all are familiar with applying CBT in physical health settings. Different sessions may be taught by different trainers, or by 'guest appearances' by some of our team. The team of trainers will ensure there is continuity of content and of learning as the course progresses.
Special circumstances: Sometimes, life events appear unexpectedly. If something unexpected prevents you from attending, please let us know as early as you can, and we will give consideration to how we might be able to support you to continue your training if that is what you wish to do.

Welcome to an hour and a half of uninterrupted YOU time!

Lift your energy with ceremonial cacao, dance into joy with an energizing movement practice, and close with yin inspired stretches and meditation - a journey of connection, movement and renewal.

Hosted by Heidi Firth & Kae-Lynn Sorensen.

What to expect:
Cacao - Ceremonial Cacao drink to foster heart-opening, emotional connection, and creative flow. We'll open with mindfully drinking "Cacao Ambassador" Cacao to bring awareness to our hearts & bodies.

The Movement - Easy to follow choreography with modifications. Where intentional movement meets empowering music.
Think of it as an hour just for YOU – to sweat, move however you need to, laugh, release and feel amazing in mind, body + soul.

A space where you can leave your judgements at the door, reconnect with yourself and have some fun!

Yin Yoga - A slow-paced style of yoga that emphasizes passive stretching and longer-held poses. It targets the deeper connective tissues of the body, such as ligaments and fascia, rather than the muscles, promoting flexibility, joint health, and relaxation. The practice encourages mindfulness and introspection, creating a calming contrast to more vigorous, dynamic forms of yoga.

I love holding spaces that feel like a deep exhale, where we can melt into Yin shapes, sip cacao, and let our whole system soften. My love is supporting people to feel good in their bodies and to remember that health can be both deeply healing and beautifully simple.

Hello I’m Kae-Lynn!

I lead The Movement because, I believe everyone deserves a non judgmental space to catch their breath and, be reminded of their spark.

When Mel first shared The Movement with me I was so I was burnt out, numb, and deeply disconnected. I was busy trying to love and please everyone else that I completely lost myself.

During my first class something shifted. The music — the movements — Reminded me of that spark within me. It felt like my soul finally had permission to shine again. For that one hour, I could breathe. No pressure, no expectations, no noise from the world or my mind. Just movement, music, and freedom to be me.

I believe fitness should be intentional, empowering and fun.

description:
Chit Chat with a Kit Kat (Free Event), Chit Chat with a Kit Kat (Free Event)

Chit Chat with a Kit Kat and Coffee!

This is for 'all women' of all ages and from all walks of life who just need to be heard, and to share their worries, burdens, stresses, grief, sadness, loss etc.. and my friend and myself are realising there are alot of us out there experiencing these emotions for a myriad of reasons, be it loss, be it menopause, be it grief, stress, anxiety, depression, financial, family stuff, so my beautiful friend and I thought it would be a great idea to extend our little sessions that we have been having to more women who are in need of just being free to feel what we feel, to be honest, raw and open and not feel judged for our thoughts and emotions in a safe, loving, caring, understanding space, where we can support each other to be "Brave Bold and Beautiful" under pressure

We are human beings doing the best we can with what we have in a world that has sort of gone a bit pear shape hey, so this 'Beautiful Woman', is about allowing you and me to speak our truth amongst like minded women in a safe space who are experiencing similar feelings and emotions with no judgement, just love and understanding

The positive of this, is when we vocalise and communicate our worries, concerns, hurts, disappointments, sadness, anger, frustrations, annoyances, we actually let go toxic energy from our mind, body, soul which actually improves our health and wellbeing mentally and physically, fact and truth!

Studies and Statistics have proven that 80% of illnesses are caused by STRESS, so let's just do something kind, caring, loving and healing for us, and let's get together and get raw, real and natural, and chit chat about whatever it is you want to chit chat about, no judgement of course within reason lol :)

What do you think? Sounds fab? :)
If so then Direct Message me or email to confirm, and i'll book you in on the 3rd of December or if you are just one of those bizzy Lizzy's like me and you forgot to book, then just feel free to rock up or text me, which i will give you access to when you email ,but prefer confirmation due to space being free to use

Toxic confusional states like delirium are common in people who are dying.
Delirium is a common distressing symptom at end of life for patients, family, whānau and carers. This session will focus on understanding the types of delirium, the risk factors, causes, prevalence & incidence, and will include best practice assessment and management.

description:
Conceptions of Identity & Their Implications, Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars

Conceptions of Identity & Their Implications

Whether we are aware of it or not, how we perceive ourselves and what we identify with has a profound impact on the quality of our inner and outer experience. Life inevitably presents us with challenges, complexities, and difficulties. Our sense of self and identity can either empower us, helping us navigate these challenges with resilience, or disempower us, leading to confusion, hopelessness, or depression.

In the second chapter of the Bhagavad Gita, readers are encouraged to deeply contemplate the true self—our consciousness. By exploring life through this understanding, we can cultivate a greater sense of meaning and connection with the world, our loved ones, and everything around us.


Hosted by Sri Jiva and Smita:

From a young age, Smita was drawn to music as a means for reflection and self-expression. Following university, she lived in an ashram for several years, where she was introduced to the wonderful practice of bhakti yoga and its wisdom. Inspired by her practice, she regularly hosts kirtan (mantra music meditation) sessions at Bhakti Lounge along with her husband Sri Jiva.

Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

6.15pm Tuesday 10th February

End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.

description:
Confident & Competent Suicide Prevention Training Series - Te Whanganui-a-Tara-Wellington (CC2026/02), CONFIDENT AND COMPETENT SUICIDE PREVENTION TRAINING
To reduce the high rates of suicide in this country a workforce confident and competent in assessing risk and providing ongoing support to suicidal people is essential.
Recent coroners’ findings highlighted the need for workers in the health, social services and counselling/psychotherapy sectors to regularly update their knowledge and competency in suicide risk assessment and intervention. This training should be a core component of practitioners’ ongoing professional development. Advanced practitioners such as counsellors, psychotherapists and clinicians should not only be knowledgeable about suicide risk assessment but also highly competent in undertaking an assessment and assessing the level of risk. The training attended should match the worker's scope of practice. Those working in the non-mental health sectors must be also be competent in making an informed referral to crisis services.They must also be up to date in their competency and capability to engage with the suicidal individual.
This advanced-level workshop address the concerns raised by coroners and are designed for clinicians counsellors and psychotherapists. Rather than a siloed approach to assessment and support strategies, this training emphasises the interconnection of the two and presents them as part of the continuum of suicide intervention and care.
Designed specifically for the New Zealand context, this training is being recommended by counsellors all over the country as a must attend workshop.

description:
Conscious & Connected Breathwork, Conscious & Connected Breathwork

Step out of autopilot and into your own rhythm — this session is about tuning in again.

We begin with gentle movement and mindful stretches to awaken the body, open the breath, and release tension. You’ll then be guided through two complementary styles of breathwork, allowing you to explore what feels most nourishing for you:

A dynamic, flowing breath to energise, release emotion, and move through internal blockages

A slow, steady breath to cultivate stillness, calm, and deeper grounding

Both approaches create a sense of spaciousness — physically, mentally, and emotionally — while supporting nervous system balance and clarity of mind. The session closes with a quiet, nurturing meditation, helping you integrate the experience and leave feeling steady, connected, and present.

Stay afterwards to enjoy a wholesome plant-based dinner and dessert included in your ticket — a simple way to nourish your body and complement your practice.

Meet Your Host: Karla

Karla is a breathwork and trauma-somatic facilitator based in Aotearoa (New Zealand), originally from Malta. With over a decade of experience in Reiki and three years facilitating trauma-informed, science-based breathwork, Karla combines holistic tools, meditation, and conscious breathing to support nervous system regulation and deep emotional healing. Her offerings help release stored trauma, reduce stress and anxiety, and activate oxytocin—the “love hormone”—fostering connection, vitality, and a sense of wholeness. She currently holds regular classes, workshops, and transformative retreats that nurture the mind, body, and spirit.

Spaghetti with roasted capsicum, sunflower seeds and sun-dried tomatoes

Stuffed focaccia

Salad with pear

description:
Cultivating Calm: Positive Psychology & Mindfulness, Cultivating Calm: Positive Psychology & Mindfulness
Cultivating Calm: Positive Psychology & Mindfulness

Develop the tools you need for navigating stress, anxiety, and overwhelm.

Mary Rose Dias - Positive Psychology Practitioner (MSc), Yoga Therapist, and Certified iRest®️ Meditation Teacher - will be leading a nourishing and practical evening exploring how mindfulness and positive psychology can help us cultivate greater calm, resilience, and inner steadiness.

Life can be demanding, and when stress builds in our system, it can become difficult to access clarity, ease, and perspective. While we can’t always remove life’s challenges, we can learn to shift our relationship with stress and develop tools that help us meet it with greater awareness and self-compassion.

Through guided meditation, reflection, and experiential practices, you’ll be introduced to accessible tools to help you:
•⁠ ⁠Regulate stress and settle anxiety
•⁠ ⁠Connect with a deeper sense of inner safety and steadiness
•⁠ ⁠Clarify intentions and reconnect with what matters most
•⁠ ⁠Access practical resources for greater calm and wellbeing in everyday life

Together, we’ll explore grounding practices drawn from mindfulness, meditation, and positive psychology, beginning and ending with guided meditation to support integration and deep rest.

This is more than just developing a mindset, you’ll be leaving with something practical to draw upon long after the evening ends.

Open to all - no prior meditation experience needed.

Plus - there is an amazing plant-based dinner & dessert included in your ticket! Stay back for the good food & great company.

Meet Mary Rose
Mary is a Wellington-based holistic therapist, meditation teacher and yoga practitioner whose work gently weaves together evidence-based psychology, ancient yogic wisdom, meditation practices and a whole lot of unconditional love and respect for each person’s unique journey. With over 15 years of experience in wellbeing, counselling, coaching, yoga and meditation, she is deeply passionate about creating nurturing spaces that support healing, self-discovery and inner calm.

Her heart-felt calling is to support others in accessing greater health, healing and happiness. While based in her birthplace of Aotearoa New Zealand, Mary’s dedication to wellness has taken her around the world, including Hawaii, Australia, Ireland, the Czech Republic and the UK, where she has trained with internationally recognised teachers in yoga, meditation and positive psychology. Through private sessions, workshops, courses and retreats, she offers a grounded, compassionate and holistic approach that honours both modern psychology and timeless wisdom traditions.

description:
Dad Bod Reset, Dad Bod Reset
Free your spine. Strengthen your core. Keep up with your kids.

About this Event

There's a myth in the dad-world that getting older means getting stiffer, sorer, and more limited in how we move.
It doesn’t.
This 90-minute, hands-on workshop is designed to help dads reconnect with their bodies, restore spinal movement, and rebuild a strong, functional core that supports everyday life.

Who this is for
This workshop is for dads who:
Feel stiff, tight, or sore (especially through the back, hips, or neck)
Sit a lot for work and feel “locked up”
Want to move with confidence again
Want to keep up with their kids without hesitation
Want better performance in sport, training, and life
No experience needed. No ego. Just practical tools that work.

What we’ll cover
Freeing up your spine
Learn simple mobility exercises to restore movement, reduce aches and pains, and take pressure off your lower back.
Deep core activation
We’ll focus on switching on and strengthening the muscles that stabilise your spine and pelvis, not just surface “abs”.
Strength, power, and confidence
Build a body that feels capable again… whether that’s lifting your kids, training in the gym, or simply enjoying a walk in the bush.
Better rotation and performance
Improved spinal movement and core control means better efficiency for things like your golf swing, running, and day-to-day movement.
Everything in this session is practical, repeatable, and designed to slot easily into real life.

Details
Date: Thursday 26 February
Time: 6:30pm
Location: Studio 2, Les Mills Hutt City
Duration: 90 minutes
Cost: $25 per person
10% of proceeds will be donated to the Push-Up Challenge in support of Mental Health Foundation New Zealand.

Theme: Welcoming new possibilities
Learn how to listen to your feelings and find guidance from within, using a gentle powerful tool called Interactive Drawing Therapy.

This single workshop focuses on the theme of welcoming new possibilities, great if you are going through change, wanting to transition or entering a new phase.

You will be guided by Lara Phillips, a trained creative facilitator in Interactive Drawing Therapy, through drawing prompts (similar to a guided meditation or journaling) to draw out where you are at and draw out your own inner guidance. No art skills are needed, more simple mark making.

This gentle yet powerful tool uses drawing and writing as a way to access your subconscious and to listen to your heart rather than your head for guidance. A tool often used in therapy, it is made accessible for self-care and community wellness through these workshops.

About Lara Phillips
Lara Phillips is a creative facilitator trained in Interactive Drawing Therapy. With a 20 year career in creative copywriting in design and communication, she shares drawing and writing as a mode for wellness and self-care, to promote preventative and proactive mental health measures through creativity.

“We all have the wisdom within to help ourselves, if given the space.”

For more workshops or to book individual sessions visit www.drawitout.co.nz

Draw It Out offers creativity for wellbeing. It is not intended as therapy nor does it replace counselling, therapy, or any other medical or clinical professional help. Participants are guided to draw out where they are at, whilst drawing out their own inner resources for support and guidance.

Participants understand it is their own responsibility to manage their mental and physical health during sessions, to opt in and out of activities as they see fit, and make the facilitator aware if further support is required.

description:
Dying Matters Week Wellington Region, Dying Matters Week Wellington Region
Dying Matters Week connects people across Aotearoa to start conversations in a safe space, learn from local experts and seek support to plan for later life and end-of-life and to navigate grief and loss.

Dying Matters Week will occur throughout the Wellington Region with different events occuring over the week. Dying Matters to us all because, it will happen to us all. How it happens and how we deal with it can make the biggest difference to both us and the people who love and care for us. This week is designed to expand the conversation and provide information and resources to enable all of us to be empowered around death and not to be frightened of it. Individual events will be featured on this page with details about how to access each event.

description:
Dying Matters Week, Dying Matters Week
Coming up at the Community Centre next month. 2 sessions totalling 1 hour in length.

Monday, 1st at 2:00pm Final Farewell: Your Legacy Your Way with Alina Reed
Ever wondered what your send-off might look like? A haka, a playlist, a tree planting? Join us for a 20-minute kōrero on the importance of documenting your funeral wishes — with heart, humour, and a dash of practicality. Let’s talk about how to make your final farewell truly yours.

Monday, 1st at 2:30pm Mary Potter Hospice with Imelda Coleman
You may know hospice through fundraising events like street appeals or strawberry fairs – but hospice is so much more than that. Join us for a short 20 minute session to learn about the holistic care Mary Potter Hospice provides, supporting not only patients but also their whānau. Discover how hospice care uplifts, comforts, and brings dignity at the most important time of life.

There is a link to the website here: https://gowithgrace.nz/dyingmatters/wellington-events/wellington-central/, you can pre-register here or come on the day.

Sarah Bradnock is a local multi-modality practitioner of energy, bodywork, plant medicine, now working utilising the the breath with SoulSide Breathwork.

Book your space today! Only 10 available.
$55 per person
bring a friend (2 tickets) $100

Registration closes on Wednesday 23 September, if not sold out before then!

What do you need to bring:
- yoga mat or other mat to lay on
- bolster (optional)
- eye pillow
- socks
- jersey or warm top
- water bottle
- journal and pen

If you've never participated in breathwork before, here are a few contraindications:
Physical Contraindications
-Cardiovascular issues
-Glaucoma
-High blood pressure (Over time, if untreated, it can cause health conditions, such as heart disease and stroke) Deep-breathing lowers blood pressure.
-Epilepsy
-Detached Retina (Retinal detachment separates the retinal cells from the layer of blood vessels that provides oxygen and nourishment).
-History of strokes or seizures
-Aneurysm or family history of aneurysm. (Burst blood vessels in the brain).
-Blood thinning medication. (Unfortunately, the blood thinners used to prevent such blood clots can increase the risk of bleeding in the brain, a cause of hemorrhagic stroke).
-Pregnancy or possible pregnancy
-Asthma
-Mental Contraindications
-Substance dependence & addiction (Deep breathwork journeys are not always appropriate for those who are still addicted to a substance, as it tends to raise suppressed or repressed material for processing. However, if you’re currently in recovery, this can be extremely healing, and help you discover the deeper patterns that gave rise to this addiction. (Grof, 1985: 267 – 268).
-Bipolar disorder, schizophrenia or psychosis
-Hospitalisation for emotional crises in the last 10 years
-Psychological conditions and diagnoses, which preclude safe emotional release.

If you are affected by any of the above, please inform Sarah.

*Tickets are non-refundable, but are transferrable with 24 hours notice required.

description:
Emotional Mapping: Making Sense of Your Emotional Patterns, Emotional Mapping: Making Sense of Your Emotional Patterns
Have you ever noticed that when emotions arise, you tend to react in the same ways over and over again?
Some of us shut down, disconnect, or tell ourselves we’re “fine.”
Others overthink, become emotionally overwhelmed, or feel responsible for everyone else’s feelings.
These are emotional patterns, learned ways of relating to emotions that helped us cope in the past, but can leave us feeling anxious, reactive, disconnected, or exhausted.
Most of us were never taught how to understand emotions in a healthy way.
Instead, we learned to avoid feelings, get stuck in them, or stay hyper-aware of the emotional states of others.
Emotional literacy offers another path.
It helps us recognise what we’re feeling, understand the needs underneath those feelings, and respond with more awareness and self-compassion.
In this workshop, we’ll explore common emotional patterns, what they can look like in everyday life, and how we can begin shifting them over time.
You’ll leave with:
•⁠ ⁠a clearer understanding of your emotional patterns
•⁠ ⁠practical tools to help you respond differently to emotions
•⁠ ⁠greater awareness of feelings, needs, and nervous system responses
•⁠ ⁠simple ways to build more emotional steadiness and self-empathy
This is a warm, supportive space to better understand yourself, connect more deeply with your emotions, and leave with tools you can actually use.
Plus - your ticket includes a plant-based dinner & dessert! You’ll get to eat good food in good company and have a wholesome evening
Meet your host, Chanchala:
Chanchala combines her background in psychology, education, and coaching to help people make sense of their emotions. She loves sharing practical ways to meet feelings, build clarity, and navigate overwhelm with confidence and self-compassion.

If you hear rejection when someone says "no" to you, or if you struggle to say "no" even when you want to - this workshop is for you.

Plus there is an amazing plant-based dinner & dessert included in your ticket! Stay back to continue the connects over a nourishing meal.

This session is interactive, and you will walk away with some understanding of NVC processes and materials to practice in your own time.

You will discover:

What stops you from saying "no" when you really want to

How to connect to what matters (to you and others) and find the needs behind the "no"

How to listen for needs, rather than look for conflict

Meet Helen & Anna, your hosts

Together, Anna and Helen create a safe, engaging, and supportive space where learning feels both empowering and nourishing. Whether you’re completely new to NVC or looking to deepen your practice, you’ll be in very good hands.

Experience Heidi: A.I Medical Scribe for All Clinicians - Wellington, Experience Heidi: A.I Medical Scribe for All Clinicians - Wellington
For practices,clinics & care teams ready to adopt Heidi—the AI scribe for all clinicians. Join us in Wellington. Hosted by Hendrix Health.

About this Event



Experience the Future of Clinical Documentation with Heidi & Hendrix
This event is perfect for practices and clinics looking to bring —the AI medical scribe for all clinicians—into their organisation. Heidi can be used by doctors, nurses, pharmacists, physios, psychologists, vetenarians and more, supporting everything from patient consults and shift handovers to practice meetings and MDMs.
Built with robust data privacy and compliance in mind, Heidi scales to fit how your clinic operates, so you can spend less time on paperwork and more time on patient care. We’ll also discuss safe AI adoption in healthcare, including how Heidi respects data sovereignty in Aotearoa. This session is designed to be straightforward and practical—no hype, just a real look at how AI can transform your everyday workflow.

About Heidi is an AI-powered medical scribe designed to ease the documentation load on clinicians. Already supporting over a million patient interactions every week, Heidi transcribes and processes clinical conversations in real time—helping generate notes, letters, and assessments so clinicians can spend more time with patients and less on paperwork.
Built by a team of doctors and backed by leading global investors, Heidi has become a trusted partner for practices and clinics around the world. The technology is developed to meet international standards including HIPAA, GDPR, NHS and the Australian Privacy Principles, with enterprise-grade certifications like SOC2 and ISO27001.
Heidi never stores session recordings and does not sell or share clinical data. It's designed with clinician wellbeing, patient care, and data safety at its core. Learn more at heidihealth.com.

About
Hendrix Health, Heidi’s official partner in Aotearoa New Zealand , is dedicated to transforming healthcare through life-long learning and human-centred technology. Since September 2024, the Hendrix team have visited over 120 GP clinics, 10 hauora Māori, and 6 Pasifika providers to understand the real challenges on the ground. By working closely with local communities, Hendrix Health ensures that revolutionary innovations like Heidi are culturally responsive and truly effective—already changing the lives of 1000's of healthcare professionals across the country.

Current Pressues in your Work
Info: A quick reflection on everyday challenges—like documentation fatigue, paperwork overload, and time inefficiencies—that impact both workflow and patient care.



🕑: 06:15 PM - 06:30 PM
Heidi Demo
Info: We’ll show how Heidi fits into your clinical workflow, covering:


- Who is Heidi? Background and purpose.


- AI Scribing Basics: Four steps (Transcribe, Customise, Output, Review).


- Live Demo: A clinician–patient consultation, including informed consent and template use.


- SOAP Formatting & Note Review: How Heidi helps structure and refine notes.

Info: Explore data privacy, sovereignty, and compliance in Aotearoa, plus best practices for responsibly adopting AI in clinical settings.

description:
Finding Stability in Turbulent Times, Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars

Finding stability in turbulent times

Pandemic, war, Inflation. Our only problems? Certainly not.

Crisis after crisis slam us in the face.

In the last century it was climate change and world hunger.

This century we are facing newer problems. With the old ones still unresolved.

How is it possible to find peace and stability in a world such as ours? Is it possible?

Albert Einstein said: ' A problem can never get resolved on the same level it originated.'

To find stability, there's need to rise to a higher platform.


Meet your host, Nava

Nava’s natural interest in studying physics blossomed into metaphysics when she arrived in the land of the long white cloud. Originally from Germany, Nava was travelling on a quest to find purpose and answers to the mysteries of life. Did she find anything on this quest? Yes! Join Sri Ganesh for an inspiring Ayurveda talk on how food & senses shape health. Learn 6 tastes, conscious eating, balancing your dominant

About this Event



Food is My Medicine: A Transformative Evening with Sri Ganesh

What you feed your body and mind today shapes your health tomorrow.
Join us for an inspiring and eye-opening lecture with renowned Ayurvedic teacher and bestselling author Sri Ganesh, as he guides us through the powerful connection between physical and mental food—and how they shape our well-being.
In this talk, you’ll discover:
The two types of food we consume: what we eat with our mouths, and what we absorb through our senses.
How to make choices that support both body and mind—using Ayurveda’s six tastes as your guide.
Practical tools to shop wisely, cook from the heart, and eat consciously.
How to align your food and lifestyle with your presently dominant element (PDE) to prevent or heal imbalances at any age.
Whether you’re curious about Ayurveda, seeking to improve your health, or looking to deepen your relationship with food—this lecture will leave you empowered, informed, and inspired.
Sri Ganesh is the author of nine books, including the cookbooks 'Food is my medicine' and 'Food from my village’.




Event followed by a plant-based dinner and dessert, all included in your ticket!



Meet Your Host: Sri Ganesh

Sri Ganesh, the founder of Vaidya’s Ayurveda Village in Kerala, India, is an internationally recognised Ayurveda practitioner, inspirational speaker, and the author of eight widely read health books published in nine languages across the United States, Europe, and India.
Born into a traditional family in South India, Sri Ganesh began his education in Ayurveda in the early years of his life with his grandmother, a well-respected Ayurveda practitioner and poison therapist in their village. He later expanded his knowledge in the subjects of Mana-shastra (psychology), Vedanta (philosophy), Dhyana (meditation), Kalari Marma Chikitsa (Kerala martial art therapy), and Yoga Chikitsa (yoga therapy) through traditional schools in South Indian villages known as gurukulams. Sri Ganesh also holds a bachelor’s degree from Mahatma Gandhi University and a master’s degree in Human Resource Development (HRD).
Drawing on his traditional knowledge and over two decades of experience working as an Ayurveda practitioner around the world, Sri Ganesh has travelled extensively throughout Europe and the United States as an ambassador of Ayurveda, sharing his ancestors’ wisdom through talks, columns, and books. Over the years, Ganesh has delivered hundreds of inspirational talks and has written eight books in the field of health, which have been translated and published in Germany, Sweden, Denmark, Finland, Norway, the Netherlands, the United States, India, and Brazil.

From Freeze to Flow: Somatic Tools to Move Through Emotional Paralysis, From Freeze to Flow: Somatic Tools to Move Through Emotional Paralysis

This will be a gentle Somatic Breathwork workshop designed to help you regulate your nervous system, decompress emotionally, and find embodied clarity. Using nose-dominant breathing techniques, optional mouth exhales, and gentle somatic movements, this session will support you in releasing tension and building to a potential cathartic experience.

Who this is for
This workshop is perfect for:
•⁠ ⁠Those feeling stressed or overwhelmed
•⁠ ⁠Individuals experiencing wired-and-tired fatigue
•⁠ ⁠Anyone struggling with overthinking or racing thoughts
•⁠ ⁠People facing sleep disruptions or insomnia
•⁠ ⁠Those with a heaviness in the chest
•⁠ ⁠Creatives facing blocks in inspiration
•⁠ ⁠Caring parents in need of self-care
•⁠ ⁠Welcome to beginners!

What to expect
•⁠ ⁠Arrival ritual and consent check
•⁠ ⁠Breath demo to guide your experience
•⁠ ⁠Progressive breath arcs using Elebreath 5-Arc
•⁠ ⁠Conservative tracks available throughout
•⁠ ⁠Micro-shakes and unwinding to release tension
•⁠ ⁠Optional arm swings and body sways
•⁠ ⁠Integration rest to reflect on your journey
•⁠ ⁠Journaling to capture insights
•⁠ ⁠Live sound with bowls and curated music

Benefits you may notice
•⁠ ⁠A deeper sense of calm
•⁠ ⁠Softer jaw and shoulders
•⁠ ⁠A steadier baseline of emotional regulation
•⁠ ⁠A clearer mind
•⁠ ⁠Improved sleep quality
•⁠ ⁠A lifted mood
•⁠ ⁠Greater emotional range without feeling overwhelmed

Yoga mats are provided but you are most welcome to bring:
•⁠ ⁠Additional yoga mat
•⁠ ⁠Warm layers and socks
•⁠ ⁠Water bottle
•⁠ ⁠Small towel
•⁠ ⁠Optional eye mask or light scarf
•⁠ ⁠Journal and pen
•⁠ ⁠If you tend to feel cold, consider bringing a blanket

Pre-class prep
•⁠ ⁠Eat a light meal 2 hours before class.
•⁠ ⁠Hydrate well throughout the day.
•⁠ ⁠Avoid alcohol and recreational substances for 24 hours.
•⁠ ⁠Limit caffeine intake 4 hours prior.
•⁠ ⁠Arrive 10 minutes early for intake.
•⁠ ⁠If you have health conditions, check with your provider.
•⁠ ⁠Feel free to share any concerns with Lynn before the session at {{hi@lynofuro.co.nz}}.

Contraindications and safety
Breathwork can alter your breath rate and surface emotions. It may not be suitable for those who are pregnant, have serious cardiovascular issues, uncontrolled blood pressure, or a history of seizures. This practice is not medical care. We offer a conservative track with nasal-only breathing and smaller ranges of motion, along with breaks as needed.

Aftercare
Post-workshop, we encourage you to drink water, eat nourishing food, engage in simple movements or a short walk, and journal any insights. Emotional waves can continue for 24 to 48 hours, so reach out if you need support.

Facilitator
Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach specializing in breathwork and Reiki, focusing on corporate burnout, chronic pain, and stress. Her approach is nurturing and gentle, ensuring a supportive environment for all participants.

It matters that men are able to optimise their wellbeing.  Well men contribute to well whānau, communities, workplaces, economy and society
Drawing on his lived experience and his extensive experience in engaging, assessing and supporting suicidal men of different cultures, age groups, genders and sexualities, he offers practical and time proven approaches to both preventing male suicide, engaging with a suicidal man and effective initiatives to optimise men's wellbeing.

Topics covered:
Overview of suicide in men
The Suicidal Moment - Men's thoughts, emotions and behaviour in the "suicidal moment”
Masculinity for the 21st Century - Are traditional notions of masculinity meeting the needs of men in 2024?  How the changes in men’s roles and identity contribute to suicide in men.
Intergenerational suicide among men and its impact of whānau and hapū
From anxious boys through to lonely old men: Tracking male suicide across the lifespan
A vision for men’s wellbeing: An holistic approach to conceptualising men’s wellbeing and key mental wellbeing messages for men.
Tāne Ora: An Online Masterclass in creating a movement of wellbeing for men by men
Participants would benefit from also registering for this online workshop series which takes a deep dive into the determinants of wellbeing men and what is required to shift very ingrained understandings in men about being a man.  How do we move from a program approach to mens wellbeing to a movement of change that engages men in conversations of the heart and the walrua. Click here for more information and to register
Previous participants’ feedback
"The best and most informative workshop I have attended in 27 years of mental health nursing”  Community Mental Health Nurse
"This workshop should be compulsory for anyone working with men”  Male Family Violence Worker
"It was as if Barry was talking about every young man I see at school”  School Counsellor

An opportunity for a day of learning with award winning suicidologist, Barry Taylor

Barry has worked in mental wellbeing promotion and suicide prevention / postvention for 36 years at the local, national and international levels.
His extensive experience includes sitting on state and national government advisory committees; designing, implementing and evaluating suicide prevention programs; writing suicide prevention guidelines, training packages and community resources; providing technical advice to and evaluating  community based and national mental wellbeing and suicide prevention programmes.
He has led multiple ‘firsts’ in the context of suicide prevention and postvention both in Aotearoa New Zealand and overseas. In recognition of his outstanding contribution to mental wellbeing and suicide prevention, he was awarded in 2016 the NSW Mental Health Commissioner's Community Champion Award. He currently sits one of the Health and Disability Ethics Committees.
As a health sociologist, Barry offers an unique insight into the phenomenon of male suicide in the Aotearoa-New Zealand context, the role of gender construction and the critical social and cultural determinants that have influenced men's distress and impaired wellbeing. Insights that very few others trainers or training programs in this country provide. He has had an interest on the impact of social exclusion, alienation and discrimination on mens's wellbeing and advocates for a human rights based, systems change and person-centred approach to wellbeing.The workshop is enriched by the learnings from Barry's own lived experience of depression and suicidality and his pathway to recovery.
After a number of years overseas, Barry is living back in New Zealand and is passionate about building the knowledge base, competence and capability within our country to effectively respond to the unacceptably high rate of male suicide in this country.

description:
Grey Not Blue: Depression and suicide in older people - Te Whanganui-a-Tara - Wellington (GNB2026/07), Take the opportunity to learn more about suicide in older people, the forgotten population in mental wellbeing and suicide prevention
There are some suicide risk factors that are particular to older people yet rarely are included in suicide risk assessment tools nor covered in suicide prevention training.
Many general population suicide prevention and mental wellbeing campaigns do not or inadequately address the unique contributing factors to depression and suicide in older people.
Studies indicate that the aged care sector is underprepared, the workforce under skilled and there lacks leadership to champion effective prevention strategies and promoting wellbeing in older people.
It is critical that those working with older people are:
knowledgeable about the latest research and understanding of suicide in older people
confident and competent in responding to the depressed or suicidal older person
Suicide in the over-65 age group is more prevalent than commonly understood. Recent statistics indicate a rising trend in suicide among the elderly. Often under-reported, depression and suicide are significant mental health concerns for this demographic.
An emerging mental health concern for Retirement Villages and Aged Care Facilities
As the baby boomer generation ages, many will enjoy reasonable physical health. However mental health issues particularly depression will become more prevalent. This is not just a concern for primary care or aged care facilities but requires serious consideration by management and staff in retirement villages. A study of suicide locations in New Zealand found that aged care facilities and retirement villages were the most common places where older people killed themselves. This has implications for family, staff and other residents.
Older People Suicide vs Assisted Dying
An understanding of the distinction between assisted dying and suicidality in older people is crucial for those working with older people. The workshop will cover the complex interrelationship of factors the between suicidality and assisted dying.

description:
Heal the Cause, Not the Symptom, Overview
Explore the links between astrology, emotions and wellbeing, and discover a holistic perspective on health and inner balance.
Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars:
Heal the Cause, Not the Symptom: An Evening on Astrology, Emotions & Where Disease Really Begins
Have you ever noticed how the body seems to be trying to tell us something, yet our first instinct is often to reach for a pill or a cream instead of listening?
After working one-on-one with hundreds of people, many experiencing a wide range of physical health challenges, I've noticed that emotional patterns, lifestyle, and living out of alignment with one's nature often play a significant role in wellbeing. Skin issues can sometimes reflect unresolved emotions or feeling like things are "getting under your skin." Persistent tension in the legs may be connected to a lack of stability or healthy boundaries. Anger can manifest as inflammation, while fear may be carried in the gut or the joints. These patterns aren't the whole story, but they can offer valuable insights into what the body may be asking of us.
My study of astrology and ancient wisdom traditions has only deepened this understanding. These teachings explore how different planets and zodiac signs are associated with different parts of the body, and how living out of alignment with our nature and purpose may be reflected in our physical and emotional health.
Perhaps that's the deeper meaning of disease: dis-ease—a state of being out of ease, carrying stress or unresolved emotions that the body hasn't yet found a way to release.
Join us at Bhakti Lounge for an evening exploring these fascinating connections. We'll look at which planets and signs govern different areas of the body, why certain health challenges may arise where they do, and how addressing the underlying emotional and energetic patterns can complement caring for the body, rather than simply focusing on managing symptoms.
The seminar will be followed by a delicious plant-based dinner together, all included in your ticket!
Meet your host Gopi
Gopi helps spiritually minded professionals achieve clarity and overcome challenges on their path through his unique integration of hypnotherapy and palmistry. During his former life as a monk, he delved into the timeless wisdom of astrology, palmistry, and the ancient knowledge of the mind and consciousness, gaining deep insights into human psychology. He combines these powerful teachings with modern, effective tools as a certified practitioner in applied hypnotherapy, along with the knowledge he gained through his diploma in psychology and counseling.

description:
Healing Trauma and Nervous System Ancient wisdom for modern resilience, Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars

Healing Trauma and the Nervous System- Ancient wisdom for modern resilience
Stress and struggle leave their mark on both body and mind, sometimes in ways we can’t easily undo. Just as knots form in the body, impressions and tensions accumulate in the mind. While we can’t change the past, the Bhagavad-gita teaches that we can shape our future—what we choose to cultivate now carries us forward.
In this one-hour workshop, we’ll explore how philosophical and spiritual wisdom can help us rise above the tangles of trauma and anxiety. Through practical insights, open discussion, and guidance from the Gita’s philosophy, we’ll look at how to build resilience—not only by steadying the nervous system, but by exploring the deeper self beyond the changing body and mind.

Meet your host, Sivananda

Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. His passion for philosophy, music, good food and community attracted him to the bhakti lifestyle. Having studied and practiced the science of the ‘self’ for six years now, he thrives on drawing insights from contemporary science and combining it with yoga wisdom to encourage others to explore new perspectives.

End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.

Held in Motion - Somatic Movement Series, Held in Motion
A 5-Week Evening Somatic Movement Series for Women
April 13 – May 11
(Monday evenings)
6pm - 7.15 pm

Held in Motion is a five-week somatic movement series for women who want to deepen their relationship with body, expression, and emotion …especially if you feel disconnected, overwhelm, or unsure how to stay in contact with what you’re feeling
At its core, somatic movement is movement guided by internal experience rather than external form.
It is movement led by sensation, impulse, breath, rhythm, and nervous system cues, rather than choreography, performance, or aesthetics.
This space is about listening.
~ Listening to impulse.
~ Listening to instinct.
~ Listening to sensation before it becomes story.
~ Listening to breath, to boundary, to rhythm.
~ Listening to the subtle yes.
~ Listening to the quiet no.
~ Listening to the places that want to soften.
~ Listening to the places that want to move.
Through free movement (without performance), somatic exploration, nervous system awareness, and guided reflection, we explore how to remain in relationship with ourselves while moving.
Each evening is intentionally paced and thoughtfully facilitated, weaving together:
~ Nervous system literacy, gently and accessibly held
~ Nervous system regulation practices integrated throughout
~ Guided somatic movement and free exploration
~ Music that fuels expression
~ Journaling and reflection
~ Moments of softness and moments of wildness
~ Joy. Depth. Integration.

Together we will explore how to:
~ Strengthen internal resourcing
~ Reconnect to sensation
~ Expand capacity for feeling without overwhelm
~ Access playful aliveness
~ Strengthen embodied choice and agency
~ Integrate emotional experience through the body
---
This is for you if…
~ You want to feel more at home in your body.
~ You sense there is more expression inside you than you currently allow.
~ You feel caught in thinking and long for deeper connection with your whole body.
~ You are curious about movement as a pathway to emotional integration.
~ You are ready to listen to your body in a new way.
~~~
REGISTER

Four weeks.
Evenings devoted to the body.
If you are curious about using movement as a way back to yourself, without pressure, without needing to be a “dancer,” without needing to be anything other than human, this space may be for you.

See you soon!

Hi, I am Fiona
I am an Integrative Somatic Facilitator™, Somatic Dance Facilitator, and Therapeutic Yoga Teacher devoted to helping people come home to their bodies. Drawing on somatics, nervous system literacy, and embodied movement, I hold spaces that support regulation, expression, and deeper self-connection.
Alongside my facilitation work, I collaborate with SomaPsych, supporting the expansion of trauma-informed and somatic education into community-centred trainings for vulnerable populations, minority communities, and professionals in demanding, client-facing roles. description:
Hoarding Unpacked - Palmerston North, Variations of this training have been delivered across New Zealand and Australia since 2012. Each year the training is updated to include current research and trends within this very specialised field. Integral to this specialised training is the case examples and strategies that the facilitator has witnessed and used in her time working in the sector as a direct in-home support worker sustaining tenancies, a hoarding support group facilitator, a hoarding behaviour and strategist consultant for government bodies, and as a trainer developer and facilitator in this specialty field. Maire Barron the facilitator and developer of this training has over 20 years experience working in the human services field. Maire holds a Bachelors Degree in Social Sciences Majoring in Counselling among a plethora of other qualifications and trainings.

description:
How to Really Relax - Know your Mind - meditation class, How to Really Relax - Know your Mind - meditation class
How to Really Relax - Know your Mind, meditation class
with Kadam Birgit Saunders

On the surface of a stormy ocean, there are waves and there can be a lot of turbulence.
But the deeper we go below the surface, the more still waters become regardless of the weather at the surface.
By looking within our own mind, we can find similar stillness and refuge from the stress and chaos of our modern life and learn to really relax.

We’ll set off on a gentle voyage of exploration of our mind, developing our understanding of the way in which our mind is the source of our awareness, how thoughts and feelings arise from but always dissolve back into our minds.
We will become more familiar with the deep and profound sense of clarity and peace that arises when our minds are still and undistracted, and which discover our inner potential for peace, happiness and real relaxation.

During this course we will learn and practise meditations that will help us to experience mental clarity and inner peace by meditating of our mind.
We will explore how meditating on our own mind offers us the ability to let go of stress and worry by enabling us to get a clearer, more dispassionate view of our own thoughts and feelings.

DETAILS
Our general programme classes include Dharma teachings along with guided meditations. Each class is self-contained and is also presented as part of a series. Drop into any class you like. These classes are suitable for both beginners and more advanced meditation practitioners. No special clothing is required. Most people sit on chairs. Everyone welcome!

description:
Humans: Why & What To Do, Humans: Why & What To Do
An evening of inspiration & indulgence! Talk by Devamrita Swami followed by a plant-powered dinner & dessert.

We’re the most connected generation in history — and somehow the loneliest. We’ve built more technology than any civilisation before us — and still can’t solve our basic problems. We talk endlessly about progress — while the planet burns and mental health plummets.

What if the trouble isn’t just what we’re doing… but that we’ve forgotten why we’re doing it?

In this bold talk, Devamrita Swami — a world-traveling monk, strategist, and social critic — unpacks the mess we’re in and asks the questions most of us avoid: Why are we here? And what should we actually be doing about it?

Afterwards, stick around for a plant-based dinner and dessert — fresh, colourful, and made to share. Grab a plate, grab a seat, and dive into real conversations with people who are curious, open-minded, and up for something different.

Meet Devamrita Swami, your host
Devamrita Swami is an educator, author, and monk who has spent over forty years exploring and sharing the wisdom of bhakti-yoga. He brings ancient Vedic teachings to life, effortlessly navigating the latest research in archaeology, consciousness, ancient history, neuroscience, social science, and psychology. Author of Searching for Vedic India and Hiding in Unnatural Happiness, he combines philosophy with practical insights on happiness, wellbeing, and personal fulfillment. For anyone seeking to channel the human drive for fulfilment in a meaningful and sustainable way, Devamrita Swami offers clear, engaging, and indispensable wisdom.

description:
Inner infrastructure for Outer Resilience, In times of polycrisis and uncertainty, more people are coming around to the need not for more information, but for integration and presence.
This 90-minute session offers a safe, grounded space to slow down, reconnect with ourselves, and explore the inner terrain of change-making, and of our relational space.
As Rumi reminds us: “Yesterday I was clever and tried to change the world; today I am wise and am changing myself.”
Building our inner infrastructure - our relationship with self, with our feelings, with others and with nature - is foundational to how we show up in the world.
We will begin by discussing research into how distraction or numbing our discomfort is an intelligent and common short-term survival strategy, but in fact is one which limits our long-term capacity to connect, lead and evolve. We will then guide participants in somatic practices to offer accessible ways to reconnect with your agency.
During this session, you will gain tools to increase your inner awareness, expand your bandwidth of awareness, and integrate emotion, sensation, and story. Together we’ll explore the role of perception in our orientation to life and the choices we make, how our narratives can connect us with our agency, the power of curiosity, and dive into how our relational presence can often have more impact than our opinions.
This session is an invitation to restore connection, calm, and courage, to become more whole, more fully human, and more ready for what this moment is asking of us.
About your host
Freda is a curator, engagement practitioner, and connector, who works at the intersection of social change, community-building, and inner development. She is the Founder of the Goodlife Collective, which curates spaces that build connection, wellbeing and collective wisdom.
Drawing on yoga teaching, somatic practices and adult development, Freda is interested in how we build our inner infrastructure - the capacity to work through discomfort, reconnect with our agency, and bring greater presence to relationships. Her background is in psychology, environmental-science and design, and she loves nerding out on ideas and conversations about unlocking our collective potential.

description:
Introduction to Acceptance and Commitment Therapy Workshop - August 2026, Overview




A 2-day introductory, experiential ACT workshop for clinicians.
Over 1000 randomised control trials have clearly demonstrated ACT’s efficacy for a wide range of diagnoses and life problems. ACT helps people make space for their thoughts and feelings while moving towards the life they value. At this experiential workshop you will establish a foundational understanding of Psychological Flexibility, develop skills for using ACT and learn about Relational Frame Theory (RFT).
Over the two days you will learn how to:
meet clients where they are and foster their willingness to change
help clients hold their painful thoughts and emotions gently; identify and actively move towards their values; and develop awareness of the present moment and their capacity to notice it
develop a therapeutic relationship in which support can be provided compassionately and flexibly
formulate life struggles from an ACT perspective
practice ACT exercises and relate the concepts back to your own life and clinical experiences.
This workshop is fully catered with vegetarian food.
Giselle Bahr and Ben Sedley are clinical psychologists and co-founders of ACT Wellington. Since being trained and supervised by many of the world’s leading ACT therapists and researchers, ACT has been the foundation of their practices for many years. Giselle and Ben have both worked at Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services, in Private Practice with adults and adolescents, and trained clinical psychology students at Victoria University of Wellington. Giselle has developed and facilitated groups introducing ACT to parents and adults, and served on the Board of ANZ ACBS. Ben wrote Stuff That Sucks: Accepting what you can’t change and committing to what you can, Holding the Heavy Stuff: making space for critical thoughts and painful emotions, and Stuff That’s Loud: A teen’s guide to unspiralling when OCD gets noisy (with Lisa Coyne). He is also an ACBS Peer Reviewed ACT Trainer.

Please get in touch if you have any questions about this training. You can email us at:
training@actwellington.co.nz
