A 50% refund is available until 14 days before the workshop.
From 14 days before the workshop, your ticket is non-refundable but fully transferrable. To transfer your ticket to another attendee contact us with the new details.

Welcome to the Journey to Serenity Yin Yoga and Sound Healing monthly session!!!

It would be lovely to share this healing, nourishing restorative practice in the special energy and support you to give your life a boost of wellbeing and good feeling!!

INTRODUCING - SPECIAL 20% OFF FOR VALENTINE'S DAY ❤ - TWO PEOPLE FOR $90 (You don't have to be a couple) - Book through bank transfer or message me directly

Unique Yin Yoga, Sound Healing, breathwork and meditation come together to create this specially guided, deeply relaxing and healing experience, held within a unique holistic framework that encourages reflection and self-care.

Take the time and space that this session offers, for yourself, and give yourself a gift of true nourishment.

Bryony Shanti from Heartsong Healing will use a wide range of special healing sound instruments along with her voice to guide you into peace, relaxation and stillness. The healing vibration of the specially chosen sounds will wash over you bringing deep clearing, balance and alignment. There is a experience of gratitude and blessing.

Bryony's sound works to strengthen and deepen the powerful work of Yin yoga teacher Bianca who will guide you through 90-minutes of restorative and uplifting poses that are intended for you relax, heal and to open more to receive the healing vibration of sound.

description:
Katie Knowles PAM, Title:
Self-Disclosure of Sexual Dysfunction to Romantic Partners.

Abstract:
Sexual dysfunctions (e.g., distress about levels of desire, arousal, orgasm, or sexual pain) are linked with poorer individual and relational wellbeing. Disclosing these dysfunctions to a romantic partner helps to mitigate these effects, however, such disclosures also risk rejection or relationship conflict. Existing models of disclosure do not adequately capture the complexities of disclosing sexual dysfunction, such as how costs and benefits are weighed simultaneously, the role of contextual factors, or how partner responses shape future disclosures. Three studies test a model of people’s disclosure of sexual dysfunction. Study 1 reports a thematic analysis of people’s social scripts about disclosing sexual dysfunction. Subsequent studies will test the influence of positive and negative partner responses and develop a scale to measure the anticipated costs and benefits of disclosing dysfunctions. Altogether, these studies build a framework explaining how and when people will disclose sexual dysfunction to romantic partners.
Primary supervisor: Dr Matt Hammond
Second supervisor: Dr Ally Gibson
Staff and postgraduate students are cordially invited to attend. There will be an opportunity at the end of the presentation for audience to observe the panel questioning the candidate about the presentation and proposed research, and for audience members themselves to ask questions of the candidate.

description:
LIFE DRAWING MEETS YOGA!, Connect with your body and your creativity in this all-levels workshop that combines vinyasa yoga practice with a fun and interactive Life Drawing class!
The Life Drawing session is based on the teaching methods of Cecil Collins, a British artist whose non-academic approach to drawing challenges you to leave your inhibitions at the door and work freely from your creative centre...much like yoga!
“But I can’t draw!,” you say. Then even better! This approach is perfect for the artist and non-artist alike as it asks you to drop your expectations of what art should look like, inviting you to express the pose from within…just like we do in yoga.
Drinks & nibbles follow, along with a chance for kōrero and connection.
Guided by JoElle Gragilla from South Coast Studio in Island Bay, who studied Cecil’s methods in London and is an artist, art teacher and AWHI-trained yoga teacher. Co-facilitated by AWHI's Lachlan Broughton.

Practice listening and learn communication skills for life

Become a part of a hearty and diverse community
Have a good time - it’s often uplifting and inspiring.

You practice asana but do you practice YOGA?

This intensive workshop explores the foundational theory, embodied practice, and teaching methodology of pranayama, meditation, and mantra — three profound and transformative limbs of yoga.

Over two full days (plus pre-recorded content to complete in your own time), you'll cover breathing physiology and the subtle body, foundational meditation techniques across multiple lineages, the ethics of mantra, and safe trauma-aware instruction. The workshop includes extensive practice teaching time with peer feedback — so you leave not just informed, but ready to teach.

*Breathing physiology and the subtle body
*Foundational meditation techniques across multiple lineages
*The theory and ethics of mantra
*Trauma-aware instruction for breath and meditation practices
*Practice teaching with structured peer feedback

* Two full-day in-person intensives (9:00 am – 5:00 pm) on Saturday 5th September & Saturday 26th September 2026
*Pre-recorded content to complete between sessions at your own pace
*One optional online wānanga to follow up after the course concludes (date/time TBD)

description:
Master Your Mornings: A Routine That Works, Master Your Mornings: a Routine That Works
Take charge of your mornings and set yourself up for a productive, goal-driven day. A well-designed morning routine can give you focus, fuel your ambition, and create momentum that carries through everything you do. In this workshop, you’ll learn how to build a routine that fits your life and drives your success.

Dive into the science behind effective morning habits, pick up practical strategies for building routines that stick, and explore proven techniques to stay motivated and on track. Whether your goal is to enhance productivity, improve wellbeing, or cultivate mindfulness, this workshop gives you the tools to turn your mornings into a launchpad for long-term achievements.

What you’ll gain:

Understand the psychology behind morning habits and why they matter

Discover how to design a morning routine tailored to your personal and professional aspirations

Learn time-tested strategies for consistency and maintaining motivation

Build a morning routine that sets you up for success, every single day

Leave this workshop with a clear, actionable morning routine that empowers you to take control of your day, and more importantly, your future.

Start each day with intention, clarity, and the momentum to reach your goals

Meet Nava, your host

Nava’s natural interest in studying physics blossomed into metaphysics when she arrived in the land of the long white cloud. Originally from Germany, Nava was travelling on a quest to find purpose and answers to the mysteries of life. Did she find anything on this quest? Yes! After eight exciting years of inquiry, practice, and being immersed in the wonders of bhakti yoga, she is still fully inspired by what she has discovered. Mesmerized by the depth and broad-mindedness that a yoga lifestyle offers, Nava is keen to share with you that wisdom and love, along with her experiences on the road of life. Nava is also an expert vegan chef who specializes in European cuisine and baking, and she is busy spreading that kind of love around Bhakti Lounge too!

When we feel safe in our bodies, everything becomes clearer.

description:
Men's Circle: Authentic Conversations, Men’s Circle: Authentic Conversations

In a world where men are often expected to have everything figured out, this gathering offers a space to be genuine, not perfect.

This is a free event, with an optional plant-based dinner available for $15. While there’s no obligation to stay for dinner, sharing a meal together offers a meaningful way to strengthen connections. Andre and Sri Jiva co-host this circle with a shared passion for creating authentic, supportive spaces where men can connect deeply—offering this gathering simply because they believe in its importance.

The Men’s Circle provides a safe and nurturing environment where men can share openly, express their feelings, and encourage personal growth—free from societal pressures to be stoic or self-reliant. Through honest sharing and collective support, participants build resilience, deepen self-awareness, and strengthen their sense of identity and purpose.

Structure of the Circle

Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.

A short meditation or moment of silence may be included to help everyone arrive and connect.

Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.

Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.

Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.

No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.

Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.

Circle Agreements

Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.

Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.

Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."

No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.

Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group, but keep others' details private.

Meet Andre and Sri Jiva, your hosts

Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human—how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.

Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

Andre and Sri Jiva co-host this circle with a shared passion for creating authentic, supportive spaces where men can connect deeply—offering this gathering simply because they believe in its importance.
The Men’s Circle provides a safe and nurturing environment where men can share openly, express their feelings, and encourage personal growth—free from societal pressures to be stoic or self-reliant. Through honest sharing and collective support, participants build resilience, deepen self-awareness, and strengthen their sense of identity and purpose.
Structure of the Circle
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.
A short meditation or moment of silence may be included to help everyone arrive and connect.
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.
Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group, but keep others' details private.
Meet Andre and Sri Jiva, your hosts
Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human—how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.
Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

description:
Men's Group Tuesday 11 Nov, To join this community, and book your Tuesdays - please sign up here first, and we will email you the event access code. (our venue address will be emailed with your ticket).

Join the event waitlist if meetings are full - a space often comes up!

This is a space for men to talk honestly, listen deeply, and figure some things out together. It’s not about having it all sorted. You don’t need to be a certain type of guy. Just show up as you are, with no pressure to speak or share.
Open group: new faces are welcome
Flexible: book to come when it suits you. Each Tuesday is a new event. Most will try for fortnightly.
Small groups: 8 men + 2 experienced hosts
Inclusive: all ages, backgrounds and identities (18+)
It's about connection and showing up, instead of going it alone. It makes time for meeting our various challenges, while learning and growing us into better friends, partners, dads, sons and humans. 
It isn’t a boys or bros club, therapy or a self-help seminar, religious or new-age. No fixing, preaching, or pressure. It’s not a crisis service or a substitute for professional care. The sign-up form explains this in more detail.
You can expect to:
Practice listening and learn communication skills for life
Discover greater integrity and self-accountability
Be supported in building your emotional intelligence
Become a part of a hearty and diverse community
Have a good time - it’s often uplifting and inspiring.
Joseph and your team of hosts have all been in regular men's groups for many years. The group sometimes offers simple and proven inquiries that draw on NVC, MBSR, active listening, gratitude and more.

description:
Men's Health and Aging, Men's Health & Aging: Take Charge of Your Future

Join us for a no-nonsense, straight-talking session on men’s health and aging. Discover how to stay strong, sharp, and in control as the years go by. It's time to break the silence and tackle the issues that matter most—your energy, vitality, and longevity. Don’t let aging slow you down. Step up, connect with other men, and take charge of your health. (Free for NZ Citizens/Residents, others pay fee of $120)

Aging is inevitable, but how you age is up to you. This essential course offers men a rare opportunity to confront the physical, mental, and social changes that come with age, with a holistic approach to staying strong and engaged.

What We’ll Cover:

Physical Health:

Stay Ahead: Preventive care strategies to keep you at your best.
Fuel & Fitness: Nutrition and exercise tips tailored for men over 40.
Managing Chronic Conditions: Tackle issues like hypertension and diabetes head-on.
Mental Health:

Stay Sharp: Techniques to manage stress, anxiety, and maintain cognitive health.
Mind & Mood: Discover mindfulness and relaxation for a balanced mind.
Movement & Activity:

Keep Moving: Boost flexibility, balance, and strength to stay active.
Strength Training: Simple routines to maintain muscle and vitality.
Your Role in the World:

Purpose & Identity: Redefine your role and find fulfilment in later life.
Community & Connections: Build lasting relationships and a strong support network.
Balance: Master the art of balancing work, life, and leisure.
Fact vs. Fiction:

Media Myths: Challenge aging stereotypes and embrace a positive outlook.
Real Talk: Get the facts about aging and ditch the myths.
Why Join?
This course isn’t offered everywhere, and it’s more important than ever. Take charge of your health, your life, and your future. It’s time to embrace aging with confidence and resilience.

description:
Mental Health First Aid Aotearoa, About 1 in 5 New Zealand adults experience a common mental illness each year. Understanding how to talk about mental health and help someone in need are important skills. This certified Mental Health First Aid course will teach you the skills and knowledge to recognise and respond to someone experiencing mental health challenges. Course fees: If you are a NZ citizen/Permanent Resident Visa the course fee is $199 (evidence of eligibility required). Others pay $499.

Description
Mental Health First Aid is an evidence-based workshop which gives people the skills and confidence to have supportive conversations with their whānau, co-workers and community and help guide them to professional help if needed.

You will learn to recognise common mental health challenges, how to provide initial help to someone experiencing a mental health challenge using a practical, evidence-based action plan, and how to respond in a crisis. During the workshop, you will have the opportunity to practice new skills in a safe environment.

You must be a NZ citizen or resident to qualify for the reduced course fee. A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

Mental health challenges covered in the course include:

Depression
Anxiety
Psychosis
Substance use problems
Mental Health Crisis Covered:

Suicidal thoughts and behaviours
Non- Suicidal self-injury
Panic attack
Traumatic events
Severe effects from Alcohol or other substance use
Aggressive behaviours
People who attend Mental Health First Aid training can complete a short online assessment to be accredited as a Mental Health First Aider. You must attend the full two days to be able to do the online assessment for accreditation. The accreditation is valid for three years.

If you choose not to be accredited, you will receive a certificate of participation if you attend the full course. You will also receive a workbook as part of your course fee.

A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead, so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by emai,l so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Prerequisites
You must be a NZ citizen or resident to qualify for the reduced course fee.

A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

2 days, Sat & Sun 9:30 AM – 4:30 PM
Wellington High School
Presented by Anne Troy

description:
Mental Health and Wellbeing, We warmly invite whānau, carers, community members, and anyone interested in mental wellbeing to join us for an afternoon with Dr Katrina Coleman.

Dr Coleman is a registered nurse, researcher, and health leader with over 20 years’ experience supporting children, families, and communities across Aotearoa. She currently works with Te Whatu Ora’s Mentally Well Team and is passionate about strengthening access to support and improving outcomes for whānau experiencing mental health challenges.

Her work and research focus on the impact of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and the importance of early support, prevention, and community connection in building long-term wellbeing.

This session will be an opportunity to:
Hear practical insights into supporting mental wellbeing

Learn about strengthening whānau resilience and connection
Share kōrero and ask questions in a safe, welcoming space
Explore ways communities can better support those facing mental health challenges
Everyone is welcome. Your ticket will cover a session with Dr Katrina Coleman and afternoon tea.

Mental Wellbeing Impact Assessment Tool Training Programme - Wellington (MWI2026/01), “Facilitating healthy public policy through a systematic wellbeing assessment”
Become more familiar with wellbeing principles and how to undertake a systematic assessment of the impact of policy and programmes on mental wellbeing.
Public policy, the economy, community resilience and assets, the legal and justice systems, urban planning, the environment and human rights all impact on our wellbeing.
Self determination, social agency, mobilisation collective impact, participation and connection, safe and inclusive communities are key determinants for thriving people and economies.
Placing wellbeing at the heart of what we do contributes to a more thriving, inclusive and equitable society.
Register for the Mental Wellbeing Impact Assessment Tool six-day training program. In 2026, TaylorMade will be offering the training program in Wellington.
Mental Wellbeing Impact Assessment Overview
The Mental Wellbeing Impact Assessment (MWIA) provides a structured, evidence-based analysis of how policy development, planning, commissioning and programme delivery impacts on the mental wellbeing of individuals, whānau, hapū, iwi or communities.
With wellbeing and mental health being two areas of social concern in our society, the MWIA provides an ideal methodology for supporting system reform, transformational change and service reorientation using a mental wellbeing lens.
Learn how the MWIA tool can value-add to your work and analysis. The process identifies factors and social determinants that are having, or have the potential to have, a positive or negative impact on mental wellbeing. Once identified, actions and indicators are developed to maximise positive outcomes and provide ways to measure the impact going forward.
MWIA has a key role to play in:
Integrating the promotion of positive mental wellbeing in policy, services and programmes
Enabling a wide range of policy agencies and services to understand and improve their impact on mental wellbeing and preventing adverse impacts.
Developing measures of mental wellbeing to measure outcomes
Community engagement
Commissioning for well-being
An independent first level review of evidence to assess the effectiveness of the MWIA process concluded that there is strong qualitative evidence that the MWIA makes a difference to the way initiatives are implemented.
Utilising this evidence-based tool developed in the United Kingdom to holistically evaluate mental wellbeing in line with the Health Impact Assessment methodology.

description:
Men’s Circle: Authentic Relating, Men’s Circle: Authentic Relating
A supportive space for men to come together, connect, and explore life’s challenges in community. This circle welcomes men at all stages — whether you’re navigating change, looking for connection, or simply want a place to be heard.
Engage in open, honest conversations and experience the kind of connection that’s rare but meaningful. There’s no expectation to speak — your presence alone is valued. The circle follows a respectful, non-judgmental format, prioritizing safety, confidentiality, and authenticity.
Optional Plant-Based Dinner
After the circle, stay for a wholesome plant-based dinner and dessert ($15). Sharing a meal is a simple way to extend the sense of community and connection. This gathering is offered on a non-profit basis.
Meet Andre and Sri Jiva, your hosts
Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. Over the years, Andre has come to value the power of sitting in circle—of men coming together in honesty, vulnerability, and presence to witness and support one another. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human—how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.
Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

description:
Men’s Circle: Real Conversations, Men’s Circle: Real Conversations
A safe, supportive space for men to connect, share openly, and grow—free from pressure or judgment, fostering honesty, resilience, and purpo

About this Event

Men’s Circle: Real Conversations
In a society where men are expected to always have it together, this space is for being honest, not perfect.
This is a free offering but there’s the option to stay for an amazing plant-based dinner ($15). There’s no pressure to join, but sitting down to eat together is a simple, powerful way to deepen the sense of connection. Andre isn’t running this circle for profit and he’s genuinely invested in creating real, meaningful spaces for men to connect.
The Men’s Circle is a gathering where men are able to connect in a safe, supportive space to share experiences, express emotions, and foster personal growth. Free from societal expectations of stoicism or self-sufficiency. Through open sharing and mutual support, participants are empowered to build resilience, self-reflection, and a stronger sense of identity and purpose.
Structure of the Circle
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.A short meditation or moment of silence may be included to help everyone arrive and connect.
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the personholding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is op-tional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking,interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicitedadvice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.
Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fosteringtrust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share whats alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements topromote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicitedadvice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group, but keep others details private.




Meet Your Host: Host: Andre & Sri Jiva

description:
Men’s Health & Aging Workshop, Men's Health & Aging: Take Charge of Your Future
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
Aging is inevitable, but how you age is up to you. This essential course offers men a rare opportunity to confront the physical, mental, and social changes that come with age, with a holistic approach to staying strong and engaged.
What We’ll Cover:
Physical Health:
Stay Ahead: Preventive care strategies to keep you at your best.
Fuel & Fitness: Nutrition and exercise tips tailored for men over 40.
Managing Chronic Conditions: Tackle issues like hypertension and diabetes head-on.
Mental Health:
Stay Sharp: Techniques to manage stress, anxiety, and maintain cognitive health.
Mind & Mood: Discover mindfulness and relaxation for a balanced mind.
Movement & Activity:
Keep Moving: Boost flexibility, balance, and strength to stay active.
Strength Training: Simple routines to maintain muscle and vitality.
Your Role in the World:
Purpose & Identity: Redefine your role and find fulfillment in later life.
Community & Connections: Build lasting relationships and a strong support network.
Balance: Master the art of balancing work, life, and leisure.
Fact vs. Fiction:
Media Myths: Challenge aging stereotypes and embrace a positive outlook.
Real Talk: Get the facts about aging and ditch the myths.
Why Join?
This course isn’t offered everywhere, and it’s more important than ever. Take charge of your health, your life, and your future. It’s time to embrace aging with confidence and resilience.
This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

description:
Mindfulness Meditation, Being mindful can help make us more resilient to life’s challenges and give us more tools for dealing with strong emotions and stress or just enlivening the daily grind.

If you’d like a hand with learning to relax or would like to get fresh insights into why we behave as we do, this course will help. It’s totally secular, practical and takes us all just as we are.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Describe some elements of Buddhism through a secular lens
- Describe practical tips to make your meditation time successful
- Practise guided and silent meditation and the importance of ‘noticing how things are’
- Find resources to support you in a long-term, and even life-long, approach to mindfulness
- Describe three elements of the mindfulness revolution in psychology and mental health

Each session includes practical meditation exercises and opportunities for discussion. Bring a notepad and pen.


Duration 4 weeks

Presented by Jan Rivers.

description:
Mindfulness Meditation, Mindfulness Meditation
Meditation can help us with life’s challenges and is a wise way to work with strong emotions and stress, as well as enlivening the ordinary times. It’s simple and doesn’t need any special resources. Often learning to meditate is presented as something esoteric and mysterious but really it should be a straightforward thing based on our everyday experience.
Come along to this course and learn how to put a meditation practice in place in your life. You’ll be introduced to some different meditation and mindfulness techniques and get an insight into the modern psychology and the ancient wisdom that supports a meditation practice.
The four sessions will provide time to practise different styles of meditation, lots of hints about a fruitful approach to take to set up a regular practice in your life and opportunities to discuss progress with others in the group.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
Describe some ways in which modern psychology and ancient wisdom support meditation
Understand what you need to do to make time for meditation in your life
Describe practical tips to make meditation fruitful
Practise different kinds of guided and silent meditation
Find resources (books, on-line information, other classes and retreats) to support your meditation
Bring a notepad and pen.

Mirimiri Community Clinic Day GLENSIDE, Mirimiri and Romiromi is traditional Māori bodywork and healing. Treatment is holistic and includes body alignment, deep tissue work and release of stress and tension by applying pressure to specific points on the body.
This will be our second Community Clinic Day at our Glenside clinic.
If you have never experienced Mirimiri or Romiromi before, this is your opportunity! Treatment is beneficial for conditions of pain, misalignment, sports or work injuries and relief from emotional distress, stress & tension; while also supporting the body to realign and rebalance energetically.
Sessions: 20mins. COST: $20
Please ensure you are well with no cold or flu symptoms on the day.
One booking per person please (no double appointments)

description:
Mothers Network - Draw It Out morning, Mothers Network - Draw It Out morning
Theme: Self-compassion
Join a special Mothers Network morning tea combined with a Draw It Out workshop - You’ll be guided through wellness drawings that help you support yourself, while connecting with other mums.

About Mothers Network
Mothers Network is a not-for-profit organisation that has been running in Wellington for over 40 years. Run by mums, for mums, we support and connect women facing the changes and challenges of being a mum through discussion groups. We also consider the impact motherhood has on other aspects of life, including relationships, career and sense of wellbeing.
Included in your workshop
You will be guided by Lara Phillips, a trained creative facilitator in Interactive Drawing Therapy, through drawing prompts (similar to a guided meditation or journaling) to draw out where you are at and draw out your own inner guidance. No art skills are needed, more simple mark making.
This gentle yet powerful tool uses drawing and writing as a way to access your subconscious and to listen to your heart rather than your head for guidance. A tool often used in therapy, it is made accessible for self-care and community wellness through these fun and friendly workshops.
About Lara Phillips
Lara Phillips is a creative facilitator trained in Interactive Drawing Therapy. With a 20 year career in creative copywriting in design and communication, she shares drawing and writing as a way of wellness and self-care, to promote preventative and proactive mental health measures through creativity.
“We all have the wisdom within to help ourselves, if given the space.”
For more workshops or to book individual sessions visit www.drawitout.co.nz.
Liability disclaimer
Draw It Out offers creativity for wellbeing. It is not intended as therapy nor does it replace counselling, therapy, or any other medical or clinical professional help. Participants are guided to draw out where they are at, whilst drawing out their own inner resources for support and guidance.
Participants understand it is their own responsibility to manage their mental and physical health during sessions, to opt in and out of activities as they see fit, and make the facilitator aware if further support is required.

description:
Navigating Low Libido - 1 day In-person Course for Women, This one-day intensive course, led by Sexologist and Sex Educator Ilil Lunkry, is for women navigating low desier.
We will explore the underlying causes of your lower libido and learn valuable tools and skills for rekindling desire. This isn't about forcing yourself to have more sex. It's about reawakening parts of you that may have gone quiet, understanding your evolving needs, and honouring what you need to reignite arousal and desire for connection.

Low libido rarely happens overnight. It builds slowly over time, and for good reasons: stress, exhaustion, unmet needs, buildup of resentment, hormonal changes, or simply having sex that doesn't turn you on. The good news? Desire can be rekindled when you understand what's really happening beneath the surface, learn the right tools, and get support from a professional.

Unlike medical approaches that only treat symptoms, this course addresses the root causes – emotional, physical, relational, and psychological.

We will focus on:
* Understanding the underlying causes of low libido.
* Awakening your sensual and sexual self.
* Understand your unique Sexual Blueprint, and integrate it into your sex life.
* Loosen the grip of shame and self-judgement.
* Build a strategy for addressing accumulated resentment.
* Creating a personalised roadmap to continue the work at home.

About Your Facilitator
This course is created and led by Somatic Sexologist and Sex Educator, Ilil Lunkry. Ilil brings a practice-based approach to sex education that focuses on embodied learning and the connection between mind, body, and sexuality.
Over the years, Ilil has worked intensively with women and couples dealing with low libido. Drawing on this experience, she has a created a course that equips participants with the most impactful tools and skills to overcome low libido.

description:
Nervous System Support, Nervous System Support is a gentle, practical introduction to understanding and working with your body’s stress response.

In this 50-minute experiential workshop, you’ll learn simple, science-informed tools to help your nervous system settle and feel safer in everyday life. Together we’ll explore how stress shows up in the body, why “calming down” isn’t always as easy as it sounds, and what actually helps the nervous system shift.

You’ll be guided through a series of accessible practices, including:

- Orienting to your environment for safety and presence

- Squeeze and release to discharge tension

- Havening touch for self-soothing

- The physiological sigh for rapid calming

- Gentle movement to music

- A guided, body-based meditation

- Time to re-orient and integrate


An optional sharing circle to reflect and connect

This is not about “fixing” yourself. It’s about learning to listen to your body, build capacity, and create small moments of safety that accumulate over time.

You’ll leave with tools you can use at home, at work, or in moments of overwhelm — no special equipment or experience required.

Come as you are. Move as little or as much as feels right. You are always in choice.

It would benefit everyone's experience if you arrive before 4:00 pm so we may start on time.


Please bring:

- A yoga mat or blanket for the meditation (bring any other supports that provide you with comfort or safety)

- A journal and a pen

- Water and a snack for after the workshop


Important note:
This workshop is designed for people who are generally resourced and able to self-ground. It is not suitable for anyone currently experiencing a manic episode, in acute crisis, or with untreated complex PTSD.

Nervous system work can sometimes surface uncomfortable sensations, emotions, or memories. This is a natural part of being human and of working with the body. For this reason, participants need to have the capacity to return to a sense of safety on their own and have support available outside the session if needed.

This event is educational and experiential in nature and is not a substitute for therapy or mental health care.

description:
Neural Calm Reset: Tapping for Your Nervous System, If moments of calm slip away as the day goes on, this workshop is designed to change that.

You’ll discover how to take control of your nervous system and cultivate a calm state that feels natural — all through a clear, 3-step framework.

This is not mindfulness. But a practice drawing on principles of memory biology and cognitive reconsolidation to help you interrupt stress signals at their source - the meaning level, where your nervous system responds to life’s challenges.

Calm becomes repeatable, a reliable part of everyday life.

You’ll walk away with a simple, 15-minute daily sequence built around three key steps:

* Tapping to deactivate the stress signal — a gentle, evidence-based technique to reset your nervous system.

* Bright-Side Rewrite Journal — shift your perspective and build empowering mental patterns.

* Inner Dialogue Reframe — transform the way you talk to yourself, supporting lasting calm and clarity.

Plus - your ticket includes a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert

Meet Krishnaloka, your host

Krishnaloka is driven to help others overcome their issues within their mind and psychology. As a mind technician trained in autaptics (Faster EFT), she employs the fastest and most powerful method to create lasting change by addressing the root causes of issues rather than just the symptoms. Her warm and caring nature makes every interaction with her both comforting and transformative.

description:
Nōku te Ao Wellington Regional Wānanga, Nōku te Ao Wellington Regional Wānanga
Nōku te Ao Wellington Regional Wānanga unites voices to drive action against mental distress discrimination in Aotearoa.

About this Event


Overview
Free to attend – registration essential
Limited spots
Morning tea and lunch provided
Following the success of the Nōku te Ao Symposium in Auckland last year, the Regional Wānanga series He reo tini, he wawata kotahi – Many voices, one goal to end mental distress discrimination continues the momentum to create lasting change for people living with mental distress in Aotearoa.
As the final event in a series of four across the motu, the Nōku te Ao Wellington Regional Wānanga will bring together systems change leaders, mental health professionals, and lived experience advocates to focus on practical actions and tools to end mental distress discrimination at every level.
Join us for a day of powerful kōrero, practical learning, and collective action.



Keynote Speakers
We are honoured to welcome Kerri Butler and Paul Rangiwahia as our keynote speakers.
Kerri Butler’s keynote will explore the stigma and discrimination experienced by people living with mental illness or distress – and how each of us can play a role in challenging it. She’ll share practical tools and everyday actions to help foster greater social inclusion, and highlight why it’s so important to keep this social movement alive, visible, and growing.
In his keynote, Paul Rangiwahia will explore the power of art in normalising mental health conversations, and approaches to wellbeing that focus on small, repeatable actions rather than big motivation or hype.



Workshops
The day will include two interactive workshops. The first workshop, led by John Kingi and Heemi Kapa-Kingi from Soften Up Bro, will challenge the perception that experiencing mental distress is a sign of weakness. Through storytelling and reflection, this workshop will explore how vulnerability can strengthen whānau and communities, and how speaking honestly about mental distress can deepen connection and a sense of identity.
The second workshop will be spearheaded by Hannah Whittaker-Komatsu. This workshop will examine how lived experience functions as a continuous loop of influence, shaping the actions we take to create change for our whānau and communities. Together, we’ll reflect, share, and celebrate the many ways we collectively shape our world, moment by moment.



What you’ll gain
Evidence-based tools to challenge mental distress stigma and discrimination in your workplace and community
Connections with sector leaders and lived experience advocates across Wellington and the wider region.
Inspiration and practical steps to help create lasting change.



About Nōku te Ao
Nōku te Ao is a public awareness movement dedicated to increasing social inclusion and ending discrimination against people with lived experience of mental illness or distress.
Grounded in Te Tiriti o Waitangi and led by tāngata whaiora (people seeking wellness), Nōku te Ao works with lived experience communities, whānau, and kaimahi across Aotearoa – to end stigma and discrimination in homes, schools, workplaces, hospitals, and the media.

description:
One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington, We know from ancient wisdom and modern psychology that meditation brings many benefits for our mental and physical wellbeing. It can reduce worry and pain, and improve calmness, focus, sleep, relationships and life satisfaction. The more time we spend meditating, and the more skilled we become, the greater the benefits.
So take a restorative break from your daily life, meet other meditators, and strengthen your practice at this small-group Saturday retreat. Everyone is welcome, whatever their level of meditation experience or preferred style. The retreat is beginner-friendly, and our approach is secular (meaning non-religious) which makes room for diverse beliefs.

The programme
We will begin with introductions, followed by a guided meditation that covers the core skills of both sitting and walking meditation. For the rest of the day, the meditation will be unguided apart from occasional bells to announce breaks, and to remind you to alternate between sitting and walking (if that's what you choose to do).
To help quieten the mind, many participants prefer not to talk again until the discussion circle at the end of the retreat. However some people like to chat with others during the breaks, and there is space allocated for this. The retreat leaders are always available for quiet conversations if you need support with your practice.

The venue
The Innermost Gardens hall is nestled between the central city suburb of Mount Victoria and the green town belt. This provides a peaceful nature-rich setting for the retreat, surrounded by community gardens to enjoy during the breaks or walking meditation.
There will be hot drinks and snacks available throughout the day. For lunch the participants bring a plate of vegetarian food to share. The venue has a full kitchen including cutlery, plates, bowls, fridge, stove, and a microwave.

The leaders
Bryan Royds is an adult educator and registered counsellor with a passion for wellbeing science and leadership development. He has been meditating and teaching meditation skills in groups for many years, including the well-researched methods of Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).
Sarah Jane Barnett is a writer and creative writing teacher at Massey University. She has been a Buddhist for ten years, practicing mostly Vipassana meditation. She also co-facilitates a meditation group for people who practice Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (an evidence-based modern psychotherapy and wellbeing method).
The registration fee is only $20, fully refundable until one day prior. The workshop is limited to 18 participants so register early to reserve your place.

Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars
How do we respond when the mind spirals, when uncertainty clouds our judgement, or when we find ourselves at a personal breaking point? This workshop draws from ancient and time-tested wisdom found in yoga philosophy — especially the Bhagavad Gita — to explore how anxiety and inner conflict can become turning points for insight and conscious action.
Rather than avoiding or suppressing discomfort, the Gita offers a way to meet it — with clarity, honesty, and meaningful direction. Through a blend of philosophical reflection and grounded tools, we’ll explore how to steady the mind and reconnect with deeper purpose in the face of pressure or doubt.

Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. description:
Pelvic Power Workshop, Pelvic floor muscles become weakened, often after childbirth, and can cause incontinence, constipation or frequent urination. These Feldenkrais Method® techniques will help you regain muscle efficiency and tone. For women only.

Description
Apart from assisting with supporting internal organs, and controlling elimination, the pelvic floor is an important part of a woman's overall stability and posture, so you will gain improvement in this respect as well. You'll learn far more than conventional pelvic floor strengthening.

You'll learn to differentiate different parts of the pelvic floor, and also how the pelvic floor functions in conjunction with breathing and spinal movements.

By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:
-Recognise the anatomy of the pelvic floor, where the muscles are and how they work
- Coordinate the pelvic floor muscles with breathing, and with the spine, and recognise its role in overall good posture
- Discover what habits you have which work against your pelvic floor muscles working well
- Practise exercises designed to help you rehabilitate and strengthen your pelvic floor

Please note that instructions are given verbally rather than by demonstration, so good hearing and understanding of English is required. For women only.

We come to know our body and ourselves better through the regular daily practice, practising with full awareness and experiencing the effect of yoga on our body, mind and soul.
Going earlier to bed and not eating too much in the evening are the prerequisites to not giving up after a few days/weeks, though

According to the ancient yoga scriptures, yoga needs to be practised during the period of sunrise, when an immense amount of Prana (cosmic energy) enters our system, nourishing our body, mind, intellect, and soul. Daily practice is crucial if we want to master any skill. You will notice an increased level of energy and positive change in your mood, as well as an improvement in your attention span and concentration. You will experience more inspiration, joy, and love in your daily life.

The Beginners Course teaches the “Sarva Hitta Asanas” from Level 1 - postures that are good for everyone. The Course covers all the foundations you need for an ongoing yoga practice. Loosening your body, the joints, and your mind, the exercises are designed for the complete balance and awakening of energy in body, mind and soul. Experience yoga postures, breath techniques, meditation and relaxation, along with knowledge about basic yoga philosophy and a healthy lifestyle. A wonderful course for new beginners and those looking to deepen their practical experience of yoga.
Some of the many benefits of yoga include: improvement in posture and breathing, increased strength and flexibility, a greater ability to cope with stress, and a feeling of peace and calm.

description:
Qi Gong, Qi gong, pronounced “chi gong,” was developed in China thousands of years ago as part of traditional Chinese medicine. It involves using exercises to optimize energy within the body, mind, and spirit, with the goal of improving and maintaining health and well-being.

Qigong has both psychological and physical components and involves the regulation of the mind, breath, and body’s movement and posture.

In most forms of qigong:

Breath is slow, long, and deep. Breath patterns may switch from abdominal breathing to breathing combined with speech sounds.
Movements are typically gentle and smooth, aimed for relaxation.
Mind regulation includes focusing one’s attention and visualization.
Dynamic (active) qigong techniques primarily focus on body movements, especially movements of the whole body or arms and legs. Meditative (passive) qigong techniques can be practiced in any posture that can be maintained over time and involve breath and mind exercises, with almost no body movement.
Wear loose, comfortable clothing and bring a bottle of water.

[This is a physical activity that involves an element of risk. While all possible measures are taken to prevent accidents or injury, please note that participation is at your own risk].

Raumati / summer yoga in the māra, Join Shaz for Raumati/Summer Yoga in the Māra at Kaicycle Farm on the 28th Hanuere / January and 4th Pēpuere / Febryuary. Class runs 5.30-6.45pm. Koha class - pay what feels good.
Spaces are limited so please register by emailing wildhumannature1@gmail.com or messaging Shaz on Instagram @wildhuman.nature
This vinyasa flow practice focuses on linking breath with movement to help participants slow down, tune in, and settle into the body. With options to scale intensity up or down, the practice welcomes all levels. We’ll explore fluid movement, intentional breath, and moments of stillness that support nervous-system regulation and mental clarity. Come as you are. Leave feeling a little more centered, spacious, and connected.
Please bring:
Yoga mat + a towel (for under your mat for protection if needed)
Warm layers
Water bottle
Cash for koha if you're able to
If you can't pay - still come along! Or if you can pay extra for someone who can't, that's much appreciated. Either bring cash or feel free to do a bank transfer to: S AUDIBERT, 06-0705-0561596-00
Please note that we do have bee-hives on site if these pose a concern for you.
Parking outside the farm is largely reserved for Hospital staff. If you are driving we recommend parking elsewhere in Newtown and walking to the farm so please allow time for this. The undercover parking at the Newtown Woolworths works well.

description:
Real Talk Kāpiti, Real Talk Kāpiti
We are excited to announce that we are bringing Real Talk to Kāpiti. We can’t wait to share space with you all!
🔥Saturday 29th November
🔥11am to 3pm (doors open at 10.30am)
🔥Te Raukura ki Kāpiti, 34a Raumati Road,
Kapiti College, Paraparaumu

This is a FREE event for Rangatahi (14-25years) and also FREE for Rangatahi Service Providers, Kaiako, anyone that works with our rangatahi, Tāngata whaikaha and whaiora.
Click here to register for your tickets:
https://www.eventfinda.co.nz/2025/real-talk-kapiti/paraparaumu

Real Talk Kōrero

We take our audience on a journey, a journey of laughter, a journey of tears, and a journey with absolute passion and purpose.
We create a safe space to speak about what we have experienced in our lives, and that we don’t have to be whakamā, we don’t have to live in silence, we don’t have to hide our secrets anymore.
Because when we speak – we heal, when we speak we free ourselves, and when we speak – we provide inspiration and hope for others.

We provide the following at each event:

❤️Inspiring kaikōrero
❤️Free kai and refreshments
❤️Opportunity to win some incredible prizes on the day
❤️FREE Real Talk pukapuka for every rangatahi in the audience

The subjects covered in our kōrero start with but are not limited to the subjects listed below:

⚫️Suicide and triggers and coping mechanisms
⚫️Mental Health awareness
⚫️Sexual, physical abuse and domestic violence
⚫️Being raised in gang affiliated environments
⚫️Drug and alcohol addiction
⚫️Teen pregnancy & pregnancy loss
⚫️Death & grief
⚫️Takatāpui & tangata whaikaha
⚫️Discrimination – racial, gender, sexual orientation
⚫️Relationship breakdowns
⚫️Career & business aspirations
⚫️Standing strong in who you are

We have a great line up of powerhouse, inspirational kaikōrero/speakers on the day:
🔥Pairama Wright – TikTok sensation
🔥Pania Te Paiho – Wāhine Toa Hunting & Hākuturi
🔥Peleti Oli – Youth Advocate
🔥Elise Niu
🔥Rutu King-Stubbs – Hope Is My Homeboy
🔥Sophie Taylor-Edwards - Kaiwaiata
🔥Kiino Krystal - MC
🔥Hosted by – Tania Carr

description:
Reiki & Rest: An Energetic Circle for Emotional Clarity & Inner Peace, Reiki & Rest: An Energetic Circle for Emotional Clarity & Inner Peace
This is for you if you’ve been “holding it together” for everyone and feel like your inner world is overflowing. You’re intuitive but energetically drained, and you’re longing for a safe space to soften, feel, and reset.

Plus, your event ticket includes an amazing plant-based dinner and dessert, offering space to reconnect and integrate your experience.

Signs you might need this session:
– You feel emotionally heavy or energetically scattered
– You’ve lost touch with your intuition or inner calm
– You’re craving deep rest — not just physical, but soul-level
– You often put others first and find it hard to receive support

Workshop Details:
This 60-minute healing circle offers guided meditation, hands-on or distance Reiki, and gentle somatic grounding practices. It’s an invitation to rest deeply, release energetic tension, and reconnect with your inner stillness. Expect to leave feeling lighter, clearer, and more centered.

What to bring or prepare:
– Dress in layers for comfort and warmth
– Bring a blanket, water, and a journal
– Yoga mat provided
– Optional: crystals, an eye pillow, or anything that helps you relax and drop in

This is your time to receive. There’s nothing you need to do — just arrive, breathe, and allow yourself to be held in stillness.

What’s on the menu?!
Szechuan Noodles with Vegan Mynce
Thai salad with Green Apple
Summer Rolls with Sweet Chilli Sauce
Ginger Pudding with Whipped Coconut Cream

About Lynofuro:
Lynofuro creates trauma-informed, energetically safe spaces where sensitive women can finally exhale. Her intuitive fusion of Reiki, somatic presence, and deep listening invites powerful shifts in a soft, grounded way.

What past participants say:
“The reiki circle was so gentle yet deeply releasing. I didn’t know how much I needed this.”
“I felt held, safe, and completely restored.”

description:
Reiki Alchemy for Energy Retrieval, Overview
Reconnect with yourself through a gentle Reiki journey of healing, grounding and soulful restoration.
Reiki Alchemy for Energy Retrieval
Reiki Alchemy for Soul Retrieval is a gentle, grounded workshop for calling your energy back. The parts of you that went missing in survival mode, over-responsibility, heartbreak, burnout, people-pleasing, or prolonged stress.
In this space, we treat “soul fragments” as protective adaptations, not pathology. We move slowly, with consent, and with the nervous system in mind. You’ll be guided through a somatic + energetic journey to meet a part of you that’s ready to return, and you’ll receive hands-off Reiki to support safe integration.
No prior Reiki experience is required. Come exactly as you are.
What to expect:
Arrival + consent-based orientation (you’ll always have choice)
Breath arrival + gentle body scan to settle your system
Energetic hygiene + boundaries (cord awareness, closing practices, no fear-based language)
Guided “soul retrieval” visualisation (felt-sense + imagery) to meet a younger/exiled part
Hands-off group Reiki transmission for integration + wholeness
Quiet reflection + journaling (optional sharing)
Grounding tea + closing ritual
You might experience:
A deeper sense of calm and internal steadiness
Feeling more “in your body” and present
Less inner fragmentation (less push-pull, less self-abandonment)
Softer jaw/shoulders and more spacious breath
Clearer decisions and boundaries
More capacity to receive love, support, and rest
Emotional release that feels safe and integrated (not overwhelming)
Please bring:
Warm layers + socks (warmth supports safety)
Water bottle
Optional: blanket + eye mask/scarf
Journal + pen
Optional: a small meaningful object for the altar (token, crystal, photo)
Pre-class prep
Eat a light meal ~2 hours before.
Hydrate well throughout the day.
Limit caffeine 4 hours prior (if you’re sensitive).
Avoid alcohol/recreational substances for 24 hours.
Arrive 10 minutes early to settle.
If there’s anything you want me to know beforehand, email hi@lynofuro.co.nz.
Contraindications and safety:
Reiki is gentle and typically safe, but it does not replace medical or mental health care. This workshop is not recommended if you’re currently in acute crisis or unable to stay resourced in your body. You can opt out, pause, or modify at any time. Seated and side-lying options are welcome.
Aftercare:
After the session, your system may feel deeply rested or tender. For 24–48 hours, support integration by:
Drinking plenty of water
Eating nourishing grounding food
Taking a slow walk or gentle movement
Journaling any insights (even a few lines)
Keeping the evening spacious (less stimulation, more softness)
After the Reiki session, share in a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, included in your ticket, a warm way to close the evening together.

Meet Lynn, your host:
Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach, breathwork facilitator, and Reiki practitioner. Lynn supports people who are high functioning on the outside but chronically tense, exhausted, or “stuck” on the inside. Often after seasons of corporate burnout, chronic stress, or prolonged over-responsibility.
Lynn’s work blends three pillars:
Somatic breathwork to help regulate the nervous system, soften protective patterns, and restore a steadier baseline
Reiki to support energetic clearing, heart coherence, deep rest, and integration (hands-off, consent-based)
Coaching to translate insight into grounded change — so what opens spiritually becomes real in relationships, boundaries, and daily choices
Lynn’s approach is trauma-aware, practical, and spiritually spacious. The focus isn’t on forcing catharsis, it’s on creating enough safety for your system to unwind, receive support, and remember your natural capacity for calm, clarity, and connection.
August 1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching (2 spots only)
If you felt a “yes” in your body during this workshop, you’re invited to go deeper. I’m opening 2 private 1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching spots in August for clients ready for nervous system regulation, somatic inquiry, breathwork, and grounded coaching support.
To enquire, email hi@lynofuro.co.nz with the subject line: August 1:1.

description:
Reiki Circle to Align Your Pathways, A soothing Reiki Circle designed to provide gentle biofield support. This session invites relaxation, balance, and heart coherence using a hands-off, consent-based approach. You’ll feel the nurturing energy flowing as you connect with yourself and others in a warm, welcoming space.

Plus - your ticket includes an amazing plant-based dinner & dessert!

This workshop is perfect for anyone experiencing:
•⁠ ⁠Stress and overwhelm
•⁠ ⁠Wired-and-tired fatigue
•⁠ ⁠Overthinking and mental clutter
•⁠ ⁠Sleep disruption
•⁠ ⁠Heaviness in the chest
•⁠ ⁠Creative blocks

Whether you're a beginner or familiar with Reiki, you are warmly welcomed.

What to expect
•⁠ ⁠Arrival Ritual and Consent: Settle into the space and establish your intention.
•⁠ ⁠Guided Breath Arrival: Begin with a gentle breathing exercise to ground yourself.
•⁠ ⁠Group Reiki Session: Experience a soothing hands-off Reiki session accompanied by a soft soundscape.
•⁠ ⁠Quiet Reflection: Take time to integrate your experience in a peaceful environment.
•⁠ ⁠Grounding Tea: Enjoy a cup of tea to nourish and ground you after the session.

What to bring
•⁠ ⁠Warm layers and socks
•⁠ ⁠Water bottle
•⁠ ⁠Small towel
•⁠ ⁠Optional eye mask or light scarf
•⁠ ⁠Journal and pen
•⁠ ⁠If you tend to feel cold, consider bringing a blanket

Pre-class prep
•⁠ ⁠Eat a light meal 2 hours before the class.
•⁠ ⁠Hydrate well throughout the day.
•⁠ ⁠Avoid alcohol and recreational substances for 24 hours prior, ideally 3 days before
•⁠ ⁠Limit caffeine intake 4 hours before class.
•⁠ ⁠Arrive 10 minutes early for intake.
•⁠ ⁠If you have health conditions, check with your provider before attending.
•⁠ ⁠Feel free to email Lynn at hi@lynofuro.co.nz with any questions or concerns.

Contraindications and safety
Reiki is gentle and typically safe, but it's essential to note that it does not replace medical or mental health care. If you have acute psychiatric distress, unmanaged seizures, or are recovering from surgery, please consult your provider first. Inform Lynn if you are wearing a pacemaker or under medications.

Aftercare
After the session, we encourage you to drink plenty of water, nourish yourself with healthy lighter food, engage in simple movement or a short walk, and journal your insights. Emotional waves may continue for 24 to 48 hours, so please reach out if you need support.

Meet Lynn, your facilitator:
Lynn is an integrative somatic coach and Reiki practitioner dedicated to supporting individuals in navigating corporate burnout, chronic pain, and stress. Her approach is gentle and accessible, making spiritual practices approachable and friendly to the nervous system.

Questions before you join? Email hi@lynofuro.co.nz, and Lynn will support you.

description:
Relating in the Dark Wellington, Do you long to explore connection beyond the visuals?

After a wonderful series of events in San Francisco, Portland, Amsterdam, Berlin & Edinburgh, Relating in the Dark is returning to Wellington for a special one-off evening this summer! Grab a blindfold and dive deep into the enriching practices of Authentic Relating, Movement Meditation & Conscious Touch.

By exploring intimacy without sight, we will delve into our intuitive nature, sharpening our capacity for deeper connection. We will use blindfolds to invite you into profound contact with your physical sensations and internal reality, unblocking your inhibition so as to reveal your truest essence.

WHO is this event for?
This event is for anyone who is seeking deeper connection, stronger community, consensual loving touch, or simply a safe space to just be yourself.
If you’re a curious, open, emotional human being and want to enhance your interpersonal relationships and enrich your self love within, this event is for you.
This event is also for you if you’ve been recently feeling blocked, anxious, lacking purpose or direction, and need to reground and remind yourself what's truly important and who you truly are.
My experience includes working with Highly Sensitive People (HSPs); neurodiverse people; people suffering from anxiety and depression; people going through major life shifts; and members of the LGBTQ+ community.
If you have any questions about whether the event would suit you, pop me a message and I’ll get back to you within 24 hours.

WHAT will we explore?
Activities will explore movement, contact and relating, with and without vision and words, by exploring the practices of Authentic Relating, Movement Meditation & Conscious Touch.
Authentic Relating is is a ground breaking social tool that enables you to playfully & courageously dive into open hearted connection, through radical honesty and active listening. The practice invites you to drop deeper into presence, embodied awareness and permission to express whatever is alive within you and the ‘we-space’ between you and other(s).
Movement Meditation is free-form journey of authentic bodily flow. It invites you to surrender to what is arising in your body when deeply in connection with music, inducing a natural state of ecstasy.
Conscious Touch is the practice of bringing full attention and presence into relating physically to another person. In deeper awareness of our desires and boundaries, we will explore the many layers and dimensions of non-sexual touch.
Together, we will create a rich container to explore the many layers of our human experience, to invite loving, consensual touch, and arrive more deeply into present moment awareness.

WHERE will it be?
The event will take place in the beautiful urban sanctuary of Wellington Meditation Centre, 31 Hobson Crescent, Thorndon, Wellington 6011.

The facilitator
Laurie (he/him), is a queer British-Kiwi who’s current home-base is Berlin. His passion is creating spaces that cultivate healthy, thriving human-to-human relationships, helping people take off their masks, feel their sensations and celebrate their aliveness on Earth. Since 2019, he has organised and facilitated hundreds of Authentic Relating, Dating and Embodiment workshops in Oceania and Europe.
His training includes The Embody Lab, Authentic Revolution, Body Electric, World Peace Yoga School and Connection Institute.
He has facilitated at internationally acclaimed festivals such as Stretch and Ignite, and organisations such as ART International and Authentic Bay Area.
His workshops have sparked thousands of nourishing connections, turning many strangers into life-long friends. He looks forward to holding space for you!

For more information, check out itoiauthenticrelating.com.

For his insta, check out: @itoiauthentic.

Here's what others have said about Laurie's workshops (blindfolded & more) :

"This was my absolute favourite authentic relating event. I can't wait for the next one. Removing the clutter and distraction and judgment from my eyes supported me to drop in immediately to my own other senses and hearing and connection with the other. It was incredible."
~ Daniel

"What a wonderful event. The blindfolds encouraged me to stay present and in your body. It was a very sweet and safe space to learn and explore. The connections were very fulfilling. A rejuvenating and enjoyable evening indeed!"
~ Carrie

“It seems funny to say it but I felt so ‘seen’ without being seen”
~ Esther

“I noticed that I was so much more present with myself, and was able to share parts that I would normally find it really hard to share”
~ Elliot

"I love Laurie’s energy, wisdom, execution and light touch. I felt super safe to open up and connect while he was holding the space"
~ Tess

"I live with complex PTSD and anxiety so in the past I have really struggled to open up to people and build meaningful connections. Discovering these workshops has been a life changer and both my therapist and I are thrilled with how my confidence has blossomed in recent months. Laurie's time and generosity really means the world to me"

~ Sarah

HOW MUCH will I invest?
$35 - low income
$45 - medium income
$55 - high income

Why are tickets sold by income?
In order to make the event as accessible as possible, there are three ticket types available. It is up to you to decide which ticket you purchase, depending on your own feelings about your level of disposable income and how much you would like to contribute for the event.
If you would really like to attend but do not have the funds for the lowest ticket option, please get in touch and we can figure something out!

Practicalities:
Location: Wellington Meditation Centre, 31 Hobson Crescent, Thorndon, Wellington 6011.
When: Sunday 1st Feb, 7 - 9.30pm
Dresscode: Comfortable clothing that's easy to move in. Please bring your own blindfold.
Intoxicants: This is a strictly sober space. There will be plenty of tea flowing!
Refund policy: No refunds available, however if you are unable to make it, you may transfer your ticket to someone else or use as credit for a future i to i workshop.

description:
Return to Love - Healing the Divine Masculine & Feminine (Group Shamanic Journeying), Return to Love - Healing the Divine Masculine & Feminine (Group Shamanic Journeying)
✨Return to Love – A Shamanic Journey of Healing the Divine Masculine & Feminine

Relationships are some of our greatest teachers. Whether you are single or partnered, whether your past experiences were harmonious or painful, each relationship reflects the inner dance of the masculine and feminine within us.

Throughout history, these sacred energies—Yin and Yang—were meant to complement and support each other. Yet, distortions, suppression, and separation have created wounds that echo through generations. Many of us carry beliefs such as:

Men cannot be trusted.
Women are not safe.
Love must be earned.
......

Rarely do we pause to sit with these wounds and meet the unhealed parts of our inner feminine and masculine. These energies may hold not only personal pain but also ancestral imprints passed down through time—shaping the way we experience love and connection today.

🌿 In this mini workshop, you will be guided through a shamanic journey to explore and heal your inner archetypes. Together, we will:

✨ Release old wounds and limiting patterns carried by the inner feminine or masculine.
✨ Make peace with the shadow side of our psyche.
✨ Embody the wholeness of the Divine Masculine and Feminine within.

We will close our circle with a sacred forgiveness ritual, bridging the separation and returning to a state of balance, wholeness, and love.

This journey is open to everyone—whether you are new to shamanic work or have walked this path before. All that is required is an open heart and willingness to connect deeply within.

🌸 You’ll leave with:

A renewed sense of love and harmony within yourself.
Greater balance between your inner masculine and feminine.
A deeper connection to spirit, self, and the essence of oneness.

Event Details
📅 Saturday, September 27th
🕒 3:00–6:00 pm
📍 Lotus Yoga Centre – Sanctuary, Paraparaumu
💫 Energy Exchange: $55 per person
🌿 Limited to 12 participants

✨What to bring:
A water bottle, journal, cushion or blanket for comfort.

🚗 Rides from Wellington may be arranged—please contact me if needed.Contact: 0272541272

About Your Guide - Fery Qiu

I am a Shamanic Healer who is committed to the healing path that help people heal from the core of their being. From suicidal depression to shamanic path, my spirituality is not based on how many trainings, meditations, and ceremonies I have done, it’s coming from a deep embodied experience to transform pain into wisdom and empowerment. The shamanic path is a way of being; we allow ourselves to go deeper within to connect all things that come from oneness. I loved my work, which has been proven to help people really change their lives. If you are curious about what this mini workshop could bring, having an open mind and open heart, you will be surprised by how much can be done just in this brief journey within.



With love,
Fery Qiu

description:
Rider Biochemics with Fran from Firmly Fit, Rider Biochemics with Fran from Firmly Fit
Pilates is unique in its total body approach to movement. It gives you balance, strength and flexibility, emphasizing the deep postural muscles of the abdomen and back.
All these skills and principles lay a foundation for good riding – Posture, Postural Support, and Body Awareness and Body Control are tools a rider needs in the saddle.
Through carefully designed movements, the correct abdominal and back muscles engage to align the spine maintaining good posture while the horse is moving.
This allows the rider to stay in self-carriage, balanced over the middle of the horse. Suppleness of shoulders, and minimal gripping with legs is then possible.
Many Pilates exercises also develop balance in the muscles of the hip joints to promote maximal range of motion. Many riders have had falls and injuries that contribute towards imbalance which can be fixed with Pilates.
With the rider being balanced and pain free the horse can perform better making the riding relationship harmonious.

Art of Connection Day Retreat, Reconnect with yourself, improve your communication, and create more ease in your relationships
Come and spend a restorative day on a beautiful rural property in Makara Valley, just 20 minutes from Wellington City (10 minutes from Karori).
This retreat is an invitation to slow down, step away from the noise of everyday life, and reconnect with yourself, with nature, and with a small group of like-minded people.
Understanding your relationship with yourself and how this shapes the way you connect with others. Through guided discussions and self-reflection exercises, you’ll gain insight into self-talk, self-love, your inner and outer worlds, and the ways we mirror what’s happening within us.
We’ll also explore relationships with others, including attachment styles, communication, boundaries, intentions, and simple, practical tools to create more ease, alignment, and connection in your life.
This learning is gently woven into a relaxing and restorative day. You’ll be supported through a guided meditation, cacao, a reflective nature exercise, yin yoga (gentle stretching and reconnecting with your body), a calming sound bath, and time to rest and unwind.
