description:
Sapphic Somatics: A Queer Embodiment Workshop, Sapphic Somatics: A Queer Embodiment Workshop
What does it feel like to exist in a queer body? This workshop aims to help sapphic women and gender minorities find joy, freedom, and connection through somatic exercises that help you embody and embrace your queerness. You will leave feeling confident in your ability to take up space, tapped into your self-expression, and connected to the experiences of your sapphic community.

Here’s a rundown of what to expect:
- Opening Exercise: Guided somatic movements to loosen up your body
- Community Connection: Rotating conversations with other participants about queer embodiment
- Yoga Flow: Creative 30 minute class to explore presence and connect to your self-expression
- Guided Meditation: A relaxing combination of breathwork and visualisation to cultivate safety in your body
- Closing Connection: Gentle and grounding partner stretches (optional) and group reflections

No prior experience with yoga or somatic exercises necessary! All you need to attend is an open attitude, a desire to connect with your body, and a willingness to share your experience with other sapphics. Yoga mats and all other props will be provided. While this workshop dives into your embodied expression of sapphic identity/sexuality, none of the content is sexual in nature and the small amount of physical touch with other participants is completely optional.

The workshop is facilitated by Megan Edwards, creator of Golden Hour Gigs and a 500CYT trauma-informed yoga teacher. This event is intended specifically for queer women and gender minorities. No TERFS no SWERFS.

Content consideration: Because this workshop focuses on finding joy/pleasure/freedom in your body, it might not be suited for anyone experiencing intense dysphoria. With that said, you are welcome to explore discomfort and work on integrating challenging feelings. Megan is trained in movement techniques to lead you away from anything too activating and help you find safety in your body.

Accessibility: Awhi Yoga Studios has an elevator and is wheelchair accessible. There are plenty of gender neutral bathrooms and cosy spaces to rest if you need a break from the workshop at any time. If you want to attend but are concerned about the level of movement required, please email the organiser with any mobility questions at

Self-Hypnosis - Hypnotise Yourself, A practical workshop that will introduce you to a structured and easy-to-follow method to take yourself into hypnosis and use it to your benefit. Let go of old habits and form new ones, brighten your future, excel in your career and create excellence.

Description
Self-hypnosis is a fantastic self-development tool. It can also be used for controlling pain, accelerated healing, letting go of limiting behaviours and a number of other applications. This workshop will provide you with a good insight into the world of hypnosis, demystify it and dispel the myths that surround it.

You’ll learn a structured method of taking yourself into hypnosis (informed by scientific research), some of the classic applications of self-hypnosis and evidence-based skills that will convince you without doubt of your ability to hypnotise yourself.

By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:
- Define and discuss hypnosis
- Practice self-hypnosis
- Create and write hypnosis scripts for personal change
- Use the language of self-hypnosis
- Relax hypnotically to deep levels

Tea and coffee provided but bring your lunch, pen and paper.

description:
Set your focus for 2026 - 2 Events, Set your focus for 2026 - 2 Events
UPDATE: the first workshop is fully booked and I have added another for 9.00am-12.00pm on the same day - 31 January. This event has a few spaces available. DM if you would like to join us.

I am really excited to offer this workshop and in such an amazing space. Let's do it. Let's create a 2026 that is amazing.

Each new year we are encouraged to think about new year’s resolutions. As we know these often don’t play out, we are unable to follow through or we lose momentum or we just make them unachievable.

The purpose of this workshop is to explore what you might want to create, change, or stabilise during 2026 through the exploration and the identification of a word that brings the energy you want for the year.

I have been working with this concept of a word for a number of years now and always when I reflect at the closing of the year, I can identify how this has played out during the year. It works! Reset was my word for 2025!!!

On the day we will have a gentle yoga practice (all levels), meditation and journalling prompted by a framework (you’ll find out on the day) that encourages us to open up to the possibilities of 2026 and to set a clear intention of what we want from the year and how one word can energise that intention.

I will provide some materials for you to create a vision board if that is your intention to do so. I will also provide material (or a framework in corporate speak) to support you in your reflections on what it is that you want in 2026.

Investment is $60. If you want to explore Nga Manu as well, I would definitely encourage that, we can provide you with a discounted access ticket of $15.

description:
She Rises : Lions Gate Edition, Overview

An afternoon to boldly lean into your deepest desires & bring them forward with clarity, decisiveness & momentum.
We are so excited to bring you this She Rises experience, curated especially for the Lions Gate portal, one of the most powerful energetic windows of the year. It is a time to boldly lean into your deepest desires and bring them forward with clarity, decisiveness, and momentum.
This is for the woman who holds it all together. You have built the career, managed the household, and shown up capable for everyone who needs you. You are the creative life force that keeps everything running.
But when you are the anchor and the visionary for everyone else, it is easy for your own dreams to get lost in the shuffle. You rarely stop long enough to ask what you actually want.
On Saturday 8th August, we gather at the peak of Lions Gate (8/8), when the star Sirius rises alongside the Sun in Leo. This brings a season full of courage, leadership, and the demand to be seen in your authentic power.
This afternoon is your intentional pause. It is a chance to step out of the busyness, put down the responsibility, and get honest about what you are really building, so you can lead from clarity instead of exhaustion.
The Experience
Guided by Self-Leadership Coach Sina Mikaio, we will move through three powerful pillars to harness the Lions Gate energy:
Movement (The Release) - Before we can build, we must make space. Through gentle somatic movement, you will arrive in your body, quiet the external noise, and physically release the accumulated tension and pressure you no longer wish to carry.
Mindset (The Courage) - With the noise quieted, we will use guided reflection to examine the heavy expectations, perfectionism, and "good girl" habits that keep you playing small. You will shed the masks you wear for others and reconnect with your deepest truth.
Manifestation (The Illumination) - True manifestation is not magic; it requires both clarity and aligned action. You will step into the high-frequency energy of 8/8 to articulate exactly what you are calling in for your life and leadership. You will leave the room not just with a wish, but with a grounded, courageous commitment to take concrete steps toward your intention.
We don't just hope for things to happen. We get clear, and then we take decisive action.
What's Included:
A fully guided experience of movement, mindfulness, and self-leadership.
A safe, intimate, and non-judgmental container of like-minded women.
Nourishing light refreshments to support your physical body.
A toolkit of grounding rituals you can practice at home.
This room is for the visionary, the high-performer, and the quiet anchor who is ready to tune into her highest frequency and lead with her purpose, presence, and power.

description:
Somatic Breathwork: Returning to Center, Somatic Breathwork: Returning to Center
Returning to Center is a nervous-system-first somatic breathwork workshop designed to support winter resilience, helping you come home to your body, soften protective tension, and build a steadier baseline through the colder months.
“Returning to center” is the practice of reorienting to breath and body when stress pulls you outward - so you can meet winter with more warmth, clarity, and capacity.
Plus - there’s an amazing plant-based dinner & dessert after the event. All included in your ticket!
This workshop is perfect for:
High-functioning people running on tightness, adrenaline, or overthinking
Those feeling wired and tired, emotionally flat, or easily overwhelmed
Those living with chronic tension, persistent pain, or recurring symptoms that feel hard to explain (alongside appropriate medical support)
Anyone craving a gentler way to release without forcing catharsis
People wanting steadiness, boundaries, and self-trust in the body
Beginners looking for a welcoming space to explore somatic breathwork
Pre-class prep
Mats, blankets and pillows will be provided but bring anything extra to support your comfort
Eat a light meal 2 hours before class.
Hydrate well throughout the day.
Avoid alcohol and recreational substances for 24 hours.
Limit caffeine 4 hours prior.
Arrive 10 minutes early for intake.
If you have health conditions, please check with your provider.
Feel free to email Lynn at hi@lynofuro.co.nz if there’s anything you’d like to share before the session.
Contraindications and safety
Somatic breathwork may not be suitable for pregnancy; serious cardiovascular conditions; uncontrolled blood pressure; glaucoma or retinal detachment; epilepsy or seizure history; recent surgery or concussion; or severe psychiatric conditions/active psychosis. A conservative, nasal-only track is always available. This is not a substitute for medical care.
Aftercare
After the session, remember to:
Drink plenty of water
Eat nourishing food
Engage in simple movement or a short walk
Journal your insights
Get an early bedtime
Emotional waves may continue for 24 to 48 hours, so reach out if you need support.
Meet Lynn, your host
Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach, breathwork facilitator, and Reiki practitioner. Lynn supports people who are high-functioning on the outside but chronically tense, exhausted, or “stuck” on the inside—often after seasons of corporate burnout, chronic stress, or prolonged over-responsibility.
Lynn’s work blends three pillars:
Somatic breathwork to help regulate the nervous system, soften protective patterns, and restore a steadier baseline in the body
Reiki to support energetic clearing, heart coherence, and deep rest (in a gentle, consent-based way)
Life coaching to translate insight into grounded change—so what opens in ceremony becomes real in relationships, work, boundaries, and daily choices
Lynn’s approach is trauma-aware, practical, and spiritually spacious. The focus isn’t on forcing catharsis—it’s on creating enough safety for your system to unwind, receive support, and remember your natural capacity for calm, clarity, and connection.

description:
Somatic Sanctuary: Exploring self-care through movement, touch & listening, "The experience and the venue were very restorative for my nervous system. Connectivity through a delicious winding path of interactive games and movement expression experiences lead me to a very open and receptive creative space. Highly recommend. Amazing facilitation." - Lily
“Thanks to this workshop, I was able to let go more than ever before, and really let in touch that was non-sexual, loving, and supportive. Thank you so much for offering another step up the mountain of growth & healing” - Amanda
*****
Imagine a day where you can drop deeply into embodied awareness, show up authentically with other heart-centred humans, and get straight to the core of what truly matters, through connective somatic practices designed to nourish your body & replenish your spirit.
Welcome to Somatic Sanctuary, a full-day experience where you are invited to self-regulate & co-regulate through a range of complementary modalities: Yin Yoga, Authentic Relating & Contact Improvisation.
This February, you are invited to The Wellington Meditation Centre, a beautiful & cosy urban sanctuary complete with a tranquil garden. Come explore the many layers of yourself and others through a journey of deep yet playful communication and contact games.
After taking this precious day for yourself, you are likely to step into the week ahead with a profound sense of well-being, a remarkable connection to your body and an experiential toolkit that you can use right away to make your everyday life even better.
WHO is this day for?
In essence, Somatic Sanctuary is for you if you want to connect on a deeper level with your body, your desires, your boundaries, your emotional reality, your empathy skills and your ability to feel compassion for yourself. This day will enhance your interpersonal relationships and enrich your self love within.
Whether you are a seasoned workshop/retreat goer or it’s your first time ever exploring the bespoke practices, you are sure to get something valuable out of this workshop.
You are also most welcome if you’ve been recently feeling blocked, anxious, lacking purpose or direction, and need to reground and remind yourself what's truly important and who you truly are.
Our experience includes working with Highly Sensitive People (HSPs); neurodiverse people; people suffering from anxiety and depression; people going through major life shifts; and members of the LGBTQ+ community.
If you have any questions about whether the event would suit you, pop us a message and we’ll get back to you within 24 hours.
WHAT will actually happen?
Activities will explore movement, conversation and physical contact, through the modalities of Yin Yoga, Authentic Relating & Contact Improvisation.
Yin Yoga focuses on deeply relaxing the nervous system, by bringing fresh life force (prana) to your connective tissue and vital organs. Through deep stretches, long holds, and mindful breathing, your body is given permission to fully release any tension that has accumulated over time.
Authentic Relating is a ground breaking social tool that invites you to courageously step into open hearted connection, through radical honesty and active listening. The practice invites you to drop deeper into presence, embodied awareness and permission to express whatever is alive within you and the ‘we-space’ between you and other(s), as well as any boundaries that emerge within the connection field.
Contact Improvisation is a dance form that emphasises both self-regulation and co-regulation, through spontaneous movement and physical connection between people, as well as the non-human physical space (such as the floor). It encourages exploration of balance, weight-sharing, and communication through touch, inducing a deeply aware state of surrendered fluidity.
Consent will be emphasised throughout the weekend. You will continually be reminded to listen to your body and only do what is within your personal boundaries. While you will be encouraged to stretch yourself and widen your window of tolerance, you will practice identifying your stress zone and will learn tools to help you self-regulate if you push yourself too far.
There will also be a support team on hand if you need to co-regulate at any point.
WHERE will it be?
The workshop will take place at Wellington Meditation Centre, 31 Hobson Crescent, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand.
The FACILITATORS
Laurie King
Laurie (he/him), is a queer British-Kiwi who’s current home-base is Wellington, NZ. His passion is creating spaces that cultivate healthy, thriving human-to-human relationships, helping people take off their masks, feel their sensations and celebrate their aliveness on Earth. Since 2019, he has organised and facilitated hundreds of Authentic Relating, Dating and Embodiment workshops in Oceania and Europe.
His training includes The Embody Lab, Authentic Revolution, Connection Institute, Body Electric and World Peace Yoga School. He has facilitated at internationally acclaimed festivals such as Stretch and Ignite, and organisations such as ART International and Authentic Bay Area.
His workshops have sparked thousands of nourishing connections, turning many strangers into life-long friends. He looks forward to holding space for you!
For more information, check out itoiauthenticrelating.com.
Laurie’s workshops have already touched & impacted many lives. Here's what others have shared:
“This was a game changer for me. I'm blown away on a daily basis as to how easy communicating and relating has been since doing Laurie's incredible workshop" - Andy
"I live with complex PTSD and anxiety so in the past I have really struggled to open up to people and build meaningful connections. Discovering these workshops has been a life changer and both my therapist and I are thrilled with how my confidence has blossomed in recent months. Laurie's time and generosity really means the world to me" - Sarah
“Laurie created a beautiful, safe space in no time! making it an ideal environment to be present and engage meaningfully with the activities. Even though all participants were strangers to me, I felt a deep sense of belonging developing over the day.” - Julie
“The exercises allowed me to center myself in heartspace - free to be held by others in love and in my own experience while also able to hold them in their experience. As such, it’s a perfect space for co-regulating.” Justin
“I am still digesting the ripples from this profoundly moving workshop, and am beyond grateful for the aligned new connections that have come out of it” - Rachel
“I love Laurie’s energy, wisdom, execution and light touch” - Tess
Sam Baker (she/her)
Sam is an experienced facilitator and has seven years of experience with somatic modalities, including contact improvisation and somatic experiencing. She previously ran ‘Embodied Empowerment’ with Laurie and wrote the ‘Hierarchy of Physical Needs’ (which the workshop was inspired by) based on observations and conversations around “Why does Contact Improv feel so safe & satisfying?”
Here’s what others have shared about Sam’s work:
“Learning about the Hierarchy of Physical Needs really made sense to me. I realise how I’ve impulsively entered into relationships or romantic encounters when really I was just craving playfulness, or connection, or touch” - James
“I really enjoyed the exercises as an opportunity to get out of my mind and into my body. To feel, not just to think” - Meaghan

If you would really like to attend but do not have the above funds available, please get in touch and we can figure something out!

description:
Sound Healing Experience at Lotus Yoga Centre, Sound Healing Experience at Lotus Yoga Centre
We invite you to a special evening of Sacred Harmonic Sound with multi-instrumentalist Claudio Escutia. This immersive sound journey offers a deeply restorative experience that invites you to settle into stillness, reconnect with the heart, and explore a sense of inner spaciousness through vibration

About the event
Claudio skilfully layers the sounds of gongs, crystal and Tibetan singing bowls, Native American flutes, and other traditional instruments, enhanced through high-quality audio equipment so the sound can be both heard and felt throughout your body.Harmonic sound and vibration offer the nervous system a chance to truly rest. In this state of relaxation, the thinking mind softens, and we find connection to citta — the heart-mind. From this place, silence arises naturally through the vehicle of sound.This experience is open to everyone. No previous yoga or meditation practice is needed.


What to bring:Bring your own yoga mat or camping mattress, small pillows, eye pillows and blanket to assure comfort.

Booking is essential — spaces are limited and this event often fills quickly.

About ClaudioClaudio is a multi-instrumentalist musician originally from Mexico City and now based in Wellington. Born into a family of musicians, he began playing music at a young age and later studied classical guitar. His journey led him to Montreal, where he explored jazz, world music, and spiritual sound traditions.

Extensive travels in Asia and Europe deepened his connection with Indian music and yogic philosophy. He studied Tibetan singing bowls in Kathmandu and Varanasi, and has since worked with a wide range of instruments including the sitar, esraj, bansuri, harmonium, flutes, gongs, and voice.

Claudio’s work blends technical skill, deep presence, and a profound respect for the healing power of sound.

description:
Tap for Healing Trauma & the Nervous system, Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars

Tap for Healing Trauma & the Nervous system

Our nervous system is shaped by more than just big life events — hidden wounds and micro-traumas from childhood can leave lasting imprints that show up as stress, anxiety, and repeating relationship patterns. When triggered, these unconscious “programs” hijack our reactions, leaving us feeling stuck even when we want to move forward. In this workshop, we’ll explore how trauma influences the nervous system and why awareness alone isn’t enough to create lasting change.

In this 75 minute workshop, you’ll discover how trauma impacts the nervous system and learn FasterEFT tools to release triggers, reframe old memories, and reset your stress response. You’ll walk away with simple, science-backed practices you can use every day to build resilience and emotional freedom.

“This is an interactive workshop where you’ll connect with others.  It’s a powerful reminder that, beneath the surface, we generally share the same challenges and struggles—and that healing becomes easier when we explore them together.”

Meet your host, Krishnaloka

Introducing Krishnaloka, who is driven to help others overcome their issues within their mind and pyschology. As a mind technician trained in eutaptics (Faster EFT), she employs the fastest and most powerful method to create lasting change by addressing the root causes of issues rather than just the symptoms. Her warm and caring nature makes every interaction with her both comforting and transformative.

description:
Teaching Well - A supportive school for a well staff - Wellington (TWS2025/04), Growing attention to staff wellbeing has resulted in many workplace mental wellbeing initiatives. Nevertheless, the concept of staff wellbeing is rarely well-defined, with programs focusing on either work-related stressors or staff wellness approaches.

As part of a well school, it is just as essential to have a well staff as it is to a well student body. Don't miss out! Discover the key principles of wellbeing and build a sustainable, impactful plan for your staff.

Join this workshop tailored for schools & kura, exploring how to promote staff wellbeing in 2025. Learn the theory and practice of promoting wellbeing in staff!
From Remedial to Sustainable Action
Providing resources or assistance programmes to help staff manage job stress is a single element of an extensive staff wellbeing plan. Schools commonly start at the remedial end of the wellbeing continuum, creating welfare or wellness plans. Learning the differences between welfare, wellness, and wellbeing approaches, including their strengths and weaknesses, is important.

Meta-evaluations reveal that many workplace mental wellbeing programmes lack efficacy due to not addressing organisational and systemic factors that impact wellbeing. Effective staff wellbeing programmes must respond to staff needs and reflect the school's cultural values and character.
Utilizing collective impact, transformational change theory, and Te Whare Tapa Whā, we introduce a conceptual model outlining the eight pillars essential for a staff wellbeing plan. This model's strength lies in its specificity to different settings or occupations, necessitating an in-depth analysis of work nature, dynamics, and inter-relationships.
Based on insights from past workshops and participant feedback, this workshop now provides a comprehensive template for developing staff wellbeing plans.
This workshop does not offer a pre-packaged wellbeing programme. Research indicates that externally imposed wellbeing programmes have limited efficacy in schools. Effective staff wellbeing plans must be rooted in insights gained from reflective analysis and staff consultations. Notably, the consultation process itself is a key wellbeing activity.
Take the opportunity to hear from an award winning wellbeing specialist about:
the wellbeing continuum and the difference between mental illness prevention and wellbeing approaches
the key determinants that impact on staff wellbeing
effective strategies to respond to fatigue, burnout, depression and trauma
why one size doesn't fit all and how to scope and design a staff wellbeing programme responsive to the specific needs of your school
developing a staff wellbeing programme based on proven wellbeing outcomes
making informed decisions on your school’s staff wellbeing policy and activities
Workshop Format:
The content will be delivered over two workshops.
In-Person 1 day workshop in Wellington
Friday 31 October 9am to 4pm
On-Line Workshop
Wednesday 3 December 1 - 3.30pm

Topics covered in this practical workshop:
what is meant by wellbeing and its role in addressing stress and mental distress in staff;
the difference between a welfare and a wellbeing approach;
staff wellbeing as an industrial relations / conditions of employment issue
resilience, coping, thriving? - identifying desired wellbeing outcomes
the interface between personal and professional stressors and distressors
the impact on staff wellbeing from exposure to trauma and poor mental wellbeing within the student body
the key determinants that facilitate wellbeing in the teaching environment
what does and what doesn’t contribute to a supportive environment where staff thrive
the key components that should be in a staff wellbeing programme
designing, implementing and evaluating a staff wellbeing programme
School Group Participation
Schools are encouraged to have more than one staff member participate in the online workshops. Past workshops has shown that having more than one staff member has maximised the benefit of the workshop activities which can then been continued post-workshop. To promote school group participation, there is a 20% discount off the total registration fee when three or more participants per school are registered.
Who should attend: 
Senior leadership team members (especially those with responsibility of staff wellbeing)
OHS representatives or union delegates
Heads of Departments
Boards of Trustees representatives
School Counsellors / EAP providers
In-House Delivery:
This workshop can also be delivered in-house, school clusters, or organisations such as prinicpal assocations or unions. Post workshop consulting services such as mentoring the development of or reviewing a staff wellbeing plan can also be provided.
Post Workshop Consult:
Schools and Kuras have the option of a 90 minute consult with Barry in 2026 to review their staff wellbeing plan.
AN OPPORTUNITY FOR LEARNING WITH INTERNATIONALLY RESPECTED AND AWARD WINNING MENTAL WELLBEING PRACTITIONER AND SUICIDOLOGIST, BARRY TAYLOR
Barry has worked in mental wellbeing promotion and suicide prevention/postvention for 37 years at the local, national and international levels.  His extensive experience includes sitting on state and national government advisory committees; designing, implementing and evaluating suicide prevention programs; writing suicide prevention guidelines, training packages and community resources; providing technical advice to community based and national mental wellbeing and suicide prevention programs.  He has worked extensively with schools both here and overseas supporting management and staff in the event of a suicide. He wrote the first suicide postvention guidelines for schools in 1990, developed the first national suicide prevention guidelines for schools in Australia in 1999 and reviewed and updated the NZ guidelines in 2010.
He has led multiple ‘firsts’ in mental wellbeing both in Aotearoa New Zealand and overseas.  In recognition of his outstanding contribution to mental wellbeing and suicide prevention, he was awarded in 2016 the NSW Mental Health Commissioner's Community Champion Award.
Barry has lectured on wellbeing both nationally and internationally and been appointed to numerous government advisory committees on mental wellbeing and suicide prevention.  He brings to this workshop extensive experience in advising communities and government on post-disaster recovery in terms of both mental wellbeing promotion / community resiliency and suicide prevention.
As a Health Sociologist and Public Health practitioner, Barry has a long-term interest in the social and cultural determinants of wellbeing, especially the role of gender and he brings a wealth of knowledge and passion for promoting wellbeing in men. He has examined the impact of discrimination, internalised stigma, social exclusion or inclusion on mental wellbeing along with the role of human rights as an enabler of wellbeing.
He embraces a holistic understanding of wellbeing and has an interest in the role spirituality and ecology contributes to a person's wellbeing. He uses a population health and systems change approach, drawing on transformational change theory and collective impact.
After a number of years overseas, Barry is living back in New Zealand and is passionate about building the knowledge base, competence and capability within our country to promote well whānau, workplaces and communities and for the incorporation of wellbeing principles in public policy and social outcomes such as education, training and employment.

description:
Teaching Well - Supportive schools for a well staff - Wellington (TWS2025/04), With the growing emphasis on staff wellbeing there is a plethora of workplace mental wellbeing programmes on offer. However what is meant by staff wellbeing is not often clearly defined, with many programmes focusing on work related 'stressors' for staff or using staff wellness approach.  
As part of a well school, it is just essential to have a well staff as it is to a well student body. Take the opportunity to learn the underlying principles of wellbeing that inform a sustainable and impactful staff wellbeing plan.  
Designed specifically for the school context, the workshop examines the theory and the practice of promoting wellbeing through the lens of of being part of a school staff in 2025.
From Remedial to Sustainable Action
Equipping individual staff members skills or resources to cope more effectively with the stressful or distressing aspects of their jobs or providing an employee assistance programme is only one aspect of a comprehensive staff wellbeing plan. It is common for schools to start their development of their plan at the remedial end of the wellbeing continuum. Consequently the plan developed is more a welfare / wellness plan. Learn the difference between welfare, wellness and wellbeing approaches and the strengths and weaknesses of each approach. 

Meta-evaluations of workplace mental wellbeing programmes indicate that there is little evidence around the efficacy of many workplace wellbeing programmes because they do not address the organisational and systemic factors that act as either enablers of or obstacles to wellbeing. Just as it is recognised that supportive environments are foundational to wellbeing of students, so is it also for a well staff. An effective staff wellbeing programmes responds to the needs of the staff and reflects the cultural make-up of the staff, the values and character of the school. 
Drawing on collective impact and transformational change theory and Te Whare Tapa Whā, a conceptual model will be introduced that outlines the eight pou on which a staff wellbeing plan should be based. The strength of this model is that it settings or occupation specific. It requires a depth analysis of the nature, dynamics and demands of the work and the inter-relationships that occur in the work
Building of the learnings from previous workshops and feedback from participants, the workshop now offers a template to guide the development of a staff wellbeing plan
If you are wanting a workshop that will give you a pre-packaged wellbeing programme, then this workshop is not for you. Countless evaluations have shown the limited efficacy of wellbeing programmes that are "inserted" into a school. A staff wellbeing plan must grounded in and responsive to the learnings made out of the reflective analysis and staff consultation stages. In fact, the staff consultation is, in itself, is a wellbeing activity.
Take the opportunity to hear from an award winning wellbeing specialist about:
the wellbeing continuum and the difference between mental illness prevention and wellbeing approaches
the key determinants that impact on staff wellbeing
effective strategies to respond to fatigue, burnout, depression and trauma
why one size doesn't fit all and how to scope and design a staff wellbeing programme responsive to the specific needs of your school
developing a staff wellbeing programme based on proven wellbeing outcomes
making informed decisions on your school’s staff wellbeing policy and activities
Workshop Format:
The content will be delivered over two workshops.
In-Person 1 day workshop in Wellington
Friday 31 October 9am to 4pm
On-Line Workshop
Wednesday 3 December 1 - 3.30pm

Topics covered in this practical workshop:
what is meant by wellbeing and its role in addressing stress and mental distress in staff;
the difference between a welfare and a wellbeing approach;
staff wellbeing as an industrial relations / conditions of employment issue
resilience, coping, thriving? - identifying desired wellbeing outcomes
the interface between personal and professional stressors and distressors
the impact on staff wellbeing from exposure to trauma and poor mental wellbeing within the student body
the key determinants that facilitate wellbeing in the teaching environment
what does and what doesn’t contribute to a supportive environment where staff thrive
the key components that should be in a staff wellbeing programme
designing, implementing and evaluating a staff wellbeing programme
School Group Participation
Schools are encouraged to have more than one staff member participate in the online workshops. Past workshops has shown that having more than one staff member has maximised the benefit of the workshop activities which can then been continued post-workshop. To promote school group participation, there is a 30% discount off the total registration fee when three or more participants per school are registered.
Who should attend: 
Senior leadership team members (especially those with responsibility of staff wellbeing)
OHS representatives or union delegates
Heads of Departments
Boards of Trustees representatives
School Counsellors / EAP providers
In-House Delivery:
This workshop can also be delivered in-house, school clusters, or organisations such as prinicpal assocations or unions. Post workshop consulting services such as mentoring the development of or reviewing a staff wellbeing plan can also be provided.
Post Workshop Consult:
Schools and Kuras have the option of a 90 minute consult with Barry in 2026 to review their staff wellbeing plan.
Barry has worked in mental wellbeing promotion and suicide prevention/postvention for 36 years at the local, national and international levels.  His extensive experience includes sitting on state and national government advisory committees; designing, implementing and evaluating suicide prevention programs; writing suicide prevention guidelines, training packages and community resources; providing technical advice to community based and national mental wellbeing and suicide prevention programs. 
He has led multiple ‘firsts’ in mental wellbeing both in Aotearoa New Zealand and overseas.  In recognition of his outstanding contribution to mental wellbeing and suicide prevention, he was awarded in 2016 the NSW Mental Health Commissioner's Community Champion Award.  He currently sits on the Health and Disability Ethics Committee.
Barry has lectured on wellbeing both nationally and internationally and been appointed to numerous government advisory committees on mental wellbeing and suicide prevention.  He brings to this workshop extensive experience in advising communities and government on post-disaster recovery in terms of both mental wellbeing promotion / community resiliency and suicide prevention. He wrote the first national guidelines for suicide prevention in Australian schools and undertook a review of the NZ guidelines.
As a Health Sociologist and Public Health practitioner, Barry has a long-term interest in the social and cultural determinants of wellbeing, especially the role of gender and he brings a wealth of knowledge and passion for promoting wellbeing in men. He has examined the impact of discrimination, internalised stigma, social exclusion or inclusion on mental wellbeing along with the role of human rights as an enabler of wellbeing.
He embraces a holistic understanding of wellbeing and has an interest in the role spirituality and ecology contributes to a person's wellbeing. He uses a population health and systems change approach, drawing on transformational change theory and collective impact.
After a number of years overseas, Barry is living back in New Zealand and is passionate about building the knowledge base, competence and capability within our country to promote well whānau, workplaces and communities and for the incorporation of wellbeing principles in public policy and social outcomes such as education, training and employment.

description:
Terra Soma Yoga, Terra Soma Yoga
Terra Soma Yoga
You are welcomed to a gentle, invitational yoga experience.

Terra-soma yoga (translating to earth-body) weaves together hatha yoga, somatic inquiry, and nature connection, inviting you into awareness of your inner terrain. This approach encourages you to meet yourself as you are — to listen to the intelligence of your body's own rhythms and sense how they echo the wider rhythms of the earth. Through this listening, we enter a living, evolving conversation about well-being and what it can look like in today’s world.

How is your heart? We often hear “follow your heart” or “listen to your heart,” but what does that actually mean? In this class, you’ll be invited into heart somatic enquiry - locating this intelligent organ, listening into this space, and perhaps allowing it to lead, inform, or express through movement.

The structure of this hour-long class includes:

A gentle lead-in towards the heart

A mixture of supine, seated, and standing asana

Repeated sequences with encouragement to make them your own — add or subtract asana, move in your own time, with your own breath

Optional free movement explorations

This is an invitational practice — everything is a choice, not a must. Tailor the practice to suit yourself. Come as you are; everyone and all of you is welcome.

Your ticket includes a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, making this an evening of movement, heartful awareness, and wholesome connection.

Meet Abbie, your facilitator,
Abbie is a 200-hour certified yoga teacher who trained with Awakening Arts: School of Yoga and Eco Somatics. She deeply values the insight, liberation, inner and collective resources somatic movement practices can offer. Abbie has also completed a 50-hour training exploring how yoga can support trauma awareness, mental health, and body image. She thrives in and intends to create spaces where each person’s pace is honored and the body’s innate wisdom is encouraged to emerge and lead.

description:
The Check-in Men's Group Tuesday 23 Sept, To join this community, and book your Tuesdays - please sign up here first, and we will email you the event access code. (our venue address will be emailed with your ticket).

This is a space for men to talk honestly, listen deeply, and figure some things out together. It’s not about having it all sorted. You don’t need to be a certain type of guy. Just show up as you are, with no pressure to speak or share.
Open group: new faces are welcome
Flexible: book to come when it suits you. Each Tuesday is a new event. Most will try for fortnightly.
Small groups: 8 men + 2 experienced hosts
Inclusive: all ages, backgrounds and identities (18+)
It's about connection and showing up, instead of going it alone. It makes time for meeting our various challenges, while learning and growing us into better friends, partners, dads, sons and humans. 
It isn’t a boys or bros club, therapy or a self-help seminar, religious or new-age. No fixing, preaching, or pressure. It’s not a crisis service or a substitute for professional care. The sign-up form explains this in more detail.
You can expect to:
Practice listening and learn communication skills for life
Discover greater integrity and self-accountability
Be supported in building your emotional intelligence
Become a part of a hearty and diverse community
Have a good time - it’s often uplifting and inspiring.
Joseph and your team of hosts have all been in regular men's groups for many years. The group sometimes offers simple proven inquiries that draw on NVC, MBSR, active listening, gratitude and more.

The Healthy Hospo Stress Reset: Sauna • Ice Bath • Breathwork • Community - Auckland, Healthy Hospo and Hospitality New Zealand are excited to invite you to…
The Hospo Stress Reset: Sauna • Ice Bath • Breathwork • Community
We’re all told that stress is bad. Chronic stress can lead to burnout and serious health issues. But what if stress itself isn’t the enemy? What if learning how to work with stress could actually make it a powerful tool for resilience, energy, and performance?
With hospitality gearing up for peak season, this is your chance to reset, recharge, and equip yourself with the tools to stay calm and in control when things get busy.
Join Healthy Hospo and Hospitality New Zealand for a unique experiential workshop designed just for hospo. Across this 2-hour session, you’ll experience:
·       Interactive Breathwork, led by our resident Breathwork & Physiology expert, Josh Fankhauser, to help you manage stress and shift your state on demand.
·       Hot/Cold Contrast Therapy, a guided community sauna and ice bath experience with Sauna Collective, to boost recovery, improve focus, and leave you feeling re-energised.
·       Practical Tools for Everyday Life. Strategies you can take back to your workplace (and your own wellbeing) to help you thrive through peak season.

 Times: Three sessions to choose from, each capped at 16 people so spaces will go fast!
·       9:00 – 10:45am
·       11:00 – 12:45pm
·       1:15 – 3:00pm
What to Bring
·       Swim suit
·       2 x Towels (one for sauna, one for shower)
·       Change of clothes
·       Notebook & pen
Thanks to funding through Healthy Hospo NZ and Hospitality NZ the cost of $50 per person is fully sponsored.
Spaces are limited and as all spaces are completely funded by Healthy Hospo NZ and Hospitality NZ, you'll need to secure your spot early!

description:
The Inner Blueprint — How the Unconscious Shapes Everything, The Inner Blueprint — How the Unconscious Shapes Everything
Before you could think critically, your mind was already being programmed.
By age 7, you had absorbed a blueprint — beliefs about your worth, your safety, your place in the world — downloaded from the people and environment around you. You didn't choose those beliefs. But you've been living by them ever since.
The Inner Blueprint is a 75-minute transformational workshop exploring the hidden architecture of the mind through the pioneering work of Carl Jung, Bruce Lipton, Joe Dispenza, and Robert Gene Smith.
You'll discover where your patterns come from, why willpower alone can't change them, and experience a practical method to begin rewriting the script — at the level where it actually lives.
The blueprint was written for an earlier version of you. It's time to write a new one.
Meet your host, Krishnaloka
Introducing Krishnaloka, who is driven to help others overcome their issues within their mind and psychology. As a mind technician trained in eutaptics (Faster EFT), she employs the fastest and most powerful method to create lasting change by addressing the root causes of issues rather than just the symptoms. Her warm and caring nature makes every interaction with her both comforting and transformative.
6.15pm Tuesday 2nd June
End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.

description:
The Overthinking Mind - Break Free From Mental Loops, Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars

The Overthinking Mind - Tap to break free from mental loops

This workshop explores why our thoughts get stuck in loops of worry, doubt, and replay.  Drawing on the insights of Carl Jung, we’ll uncover how the unconscious mind, shadow, and how unresolved inner conflicts fuel over-thinking. You’ll also learn how the body and nervous system become conditioned to repeat these mental patterns, creating the familiar cycle of racing thoughts and restless emotions.

Through a guided exercise, you’ll experience practical tools from FasterEFT and the science of neuroplasticity—methods that help rewire the brain and bring the mind back to calm clarity.

By the end of the workshop, you’ll not only understand the deeper roots of over-thinking, but you’ll also walk away with simple, repeatable techniques to interrupt mental loops, ease the nervous system, and create a lasting sense of inner peace.

“This is an interactive workshop where you’ll connect with others and see that many of us face the same challenges beneath the surface—making growth and healing easier when we explore them together :)

“This is an interactive workshop that offers the chance to connect with others on a similar journey. It’s powerful to know, that beneath the surface, we often share the same challenges and struggles—and that healing becomes easier when we explore them together.”

Meet your host, Krishnaloka

Introducing Krishnaloka, who is driven to help others overcome their issues within their mind and pyschology. As a mind technician trained in eutaptics (Faster EFT), she employs the fastest and most powerful method to create lasting change by addressing the root causes of issues rather than just the symptoms. Her warm and caring nature makes every interaction with her both comforting and transformative.

We’re super excited to be collaborating with the lovely Radha Iveta from Heart Awakening. Plus - there will be an amazing plant based dinner included in your ticket!

This will be insightful, down-to-earth and inspiring.

It’s the art of aligning with the natural rhythms. And see how your wellness takes shape with just a few simple adjustments. It’s the small things that compound to develop your wellbeing!

This workshop is an introduction to Dinacharya, the Ayurvedic practice of daily self-care routines that harmonize mind, body, and spirit.

In the workshop, we will cover:

Understanding Dinacharya: What it is and its importance in Ayurveda.

Morning Routine: Simple, effective practices to start your day with balance.

Evening Routine: Techniques to wind down and promote restful sleep.

Eating & Digestion: Ayurvedic recommendations for meal timing and digestion.

Self-Care Practices: How to incorporate oil pulling, tongue scraping, and more into your day.

Seasonal Adjustments: How to tweak your routine according to the seasons.

Meet Radha, your host
Radha Iveta is a meditation and yoga practitioner, certified teacher, Ayurveda practitioner and therapist, cacao lover, and the founder of Heart Awakening and True Nature Ayurveda. Her work was born out of a profound love for these teachings and her desire to invite others on a journey toward more meaning and fulfilment, guided by the direct experience and knowledge that Love is our true nature.

description:
The ultimate gut reset – how to transform your mental and physical health through your microbiome, Autumn is the ideal season to detoxify, reset your gut microbiome, and restore balance to your nervous system — a powerful step toward lasting vitality and emotional resilience.
Join Seleno Health for an inspiring and evidence-informed 2-hour workshop, where you'll discover our transformative 12-Week Gut Reset program. Drawing from ancient Peruvian wisdom (including revered superfoods like maca, cacao, yacon, and tocosh) and modern nutritional neuroscience, this practical guide empowers you to heal your gut, optimize your gut-brain axis, and support profound improvements in mental health, mood, energy, and overall well-being.
The workshop dives deep into the gut-brain axis — the bidirectional communication highway linking your gut microbiome, enteric nervous system, vagus nerve, immune pathways, and brain. Emerging neuroscience shows that a balanced gut ecosystem profoundly influences neurotransmitter production (such as serotonin — with ~90% made in the gut — and dopamine), stress response via the HPA axis, inflammation levels, and even neuroplasticity. Dysbiosis (imbalanced gut bacteria) is increasingly linked to conditions like anxiety, depression, chronic fatigue, brain fog, and mood instability, while nurturing beneficial microbes can promote emotional regulation, reduced stress reactivity, mental clarity, and resilience.
You'll learn science-backed strategies to:
Rebuild a thriving microbiome with targeted prebiotics (e.g., yacon syrup's FOS and inulin to feed good bacteria), probiotics (e.g., fermented tocosh as a wholefood "Penicillin of the Andes" for potent gut repopulation), digestive enzymes, and gut-healing foods (bone broth, collagen, slippery elm, turmeric).
Harness mood-enhancing superfoods: adaptogenic maca for hormone balance, stress management, and vitality; mineral-rich cacao loaded with flavanols, theobromine (a gentle energizer), tryptophan (serotonin precursor), phenylethylamine (the "love chemical" that boosts dopamine reward pathways), and bliss molecules that elevate mood, cognition, and creativity while reducing inflammation — all supporting the gut-brain connection.
Boost detoxification, immunity, and cellular protection with GPx Immune Protect, which enhances your body's natural glutathione peroxidase systems (and related antioxidant enzymes) to combat oxidative stress — a key factor in fatigue, burnout, chronic inflammation, and mood disorders.
Integrate nervous system reset tools: mindful eating, breathwork, gentle movement/yoga, and daily mindfulness practices to calm the vagus nerve, lower cortisol, and enhance parasympathetic "rest-and-digest" mode — directly benefiting both gut function and mental/emotional health.
The session also explores how these interventions tie into the endocannabinoid system (ECS) — your body's master regulator of stress, mood, inflammation, and homeostasis. A healthy microbiome supports ECS signaling (via microbial metabolites and fatty acid precursors), which can help alleviate anxiety, depression symptoms, and anhedonia (lack of pleasure/motivation), creating a virtuous cycle for brain and gut health.
You'll receive actionable tools, including:
The full PDF 12-Week Gut Reset daily planner and holistic guidance.
Personalized ideas for chronic fatigue, autoimmunity, hormonal imbalances, or stress-related conditions.
Tips to reduce reliance on medications through natural, food-first approaches.
Interactive Q&A, real-life case studies (showing gains in energy, mood stability, skin clarity, reduced inflammation, and emotional well-being), and practical integration steps ensure you leave empowered and equipped.
Whether you're seeking preventive wellness, mood optimization, or support for persistent challenges, this gut-centric, neuroscience-informed approach — rooted in wholefoods and ancient remedies — helps you unlock your body's innate healing potential from the inside out.
Spaces are limited — register now to revitalize your gut, brain, and life this Autumn!
Register now to begin your journey to a vibrant, healthier you!

Presenter:
-Dr Corin Storkey (PhD – Med Chem) has over 15 years of academic and research experience, specialising in medicinal antioxidant chemistry, oxidative diseases, cellular protection and health. He has previously struggled with and overcome chronic fatigue syndrome and promotes an integrative and holistic approach to managing chronic health conditions. He currently leads the New Zealand based Maca and cacao research program that studies Andean and Amazonian plant medicines and their bioactives.

Understanding and Supporting Your Neurodivergent Child: A Practical Parent Course, This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
This course is designed for parents and caregivers of neurodivergent tamariki who want practical, evidence-informed strategies to better support their child’s wellbeing, behaviour, and participation at home and school.
Across three sessions, we will explore the foundations of neurodiversity, including different neurotypes, strengths-based perspectives, and neuroaffirming language. You will gain insight into sensory processing, regulation, and the critical role of connection and co-regulation in supporting your child.
The course also provides guidance on navigating Aotearoa New Zealand’s health, education, and disability systems, including how to access supports and advocate effectively for your child. We will explore common challenges such as school refusal, burnout, and meltdowns, with practical strategies for prevention, in-the-moment support, and recovery.
There will be opportunities for discussion, reflection, and shared learning, as well as a Q&A-style panel session incorporating both professional and lived experience perspectives.
This is a group-based learning environment (not individual therapy), with an emphasis on practical tools, connection, and empowerment.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. description:
WELLINGTON BREATHWORK EVENT, Overview


Come for the breathwork. Leave with the breakthrough.
A transformational live experience combining breathwork, nervous system power, guided journaling and coaching, created to get you out of your head, into your body, and into the next version of you.

Join Jacqui Sive, Owaken certified breathwork facilitator and veteran coach, for an afternoon of deep nervous system release and rewiring, personal transformation, and embodied breakthrough.
Throughout the afternoon, Jacqui will guide you through a practical, supportive process to help you quiet the mental noise, identify the patterns that have been holding you back, and create space for a real shift in how you feel, think, and move forward.

This is for you if you’re ready to:
stop overthinking and actually feel the shift
release the old story from your body, not just your brain
reconnect with your power, clarity, and aliveness
be guided through coaching, journaling, and breathwork in one potent experience
walk out feeling like, “Oh. I remember who the hell I am.”
Breathwork is a practical way to release built-up tension, overwhelm, and limiting beliefs, so that everyday life feels more manageable & your creativity can FLOW. If you're feeling blocked or stuck, it's your nervous system on high alert, and in breathwork we get to dissolve limiting beliefs and tap back into your power.
CHANGE THE WAY YOU THINK
Limiting beliefs and self-doubt aren’t just thoughts you need to “fix.” They’re patterns held in your body, your nervous system, and your subconscious, often shaped by past experiences, conditioning, and the ways you learned to stay safe, liked, or in control. When your body is in protection mode, your mind follows.
Breathwork shifts this from the inside out.
By working directly with the breath, you calm the nervous system, open the body, and access deeper subconscious layers where beliefs actually live. This is where stored emotion, old fear, and energetic tension can begin to move, without needing to relive or analyse the past.
This is why people often experience rapid shifts through breathwork. You don’t become someone new. You remember yourself underneath the fear, the doubt, and the conditioning.
During this experience, people may move through emotional release, physical sensation, energetic activation, nervous system recalibration, grief release, insight, breakthrough, clarity, peace and profound reconnection to self. Every experience is unique, but many people leave feeling lighter, clearer, stronger, more open, more grounded and more fully alive.

We’ll begin by sharing cacao and coming together in community, creating space to arrive, connect, and gently open into the experience together.
Then, we move into grounding and nervous system preparation so your body feels supported and ready for the journey. From there, you’ll be guided through a powerful active breathwork experience using breath, music, emotional release and live support in the room. Afterwards, we move into integration, grounding and reflection so your system can land the experience and fully receive what has shifted.
This event may deeply support you if you’ve been:
carrying stress, emotion or pressure for too long
feeling stuck, flat, disconnected or shut down
trapped in overthinking and disconnected from your body
navigating change, grief, burnout or inner tension
craving clarity, release, reset or reconnection
doing inner work but still feeling blocked in your body or patterns
No prior breathwork experience is necessary. Beginners are absolutely welcome.
People often leave feeling lighter, clearer, emotionally released, physically grounded, more energised, more open-hearted and more deeply connected to themselves. Sometimes transformation is not about becoming someone new. Sometimes it’s about releasing what has been sitting on top of who you already are.

IMPORTANT:
Please bring a yoga mat, blanket, pillow or cushion, water bottle, journal, and comfortable clothing you can fully relax in. Creating physical comfort helps the nervous system feel safe enough to open and go deeper into the work.
This is your invitation to breathe, release, move what’s been stuck, & come fully home ot yourself with more clarity, more power and more life inside you.
Please note that breathwork may not be suitable for people who are pregnant or experiencing certain medical or psychiatric conditions including epilepsy, severe cardiovascular conditions, schizophrenia, psychosis or recent major surgery. If you have questions about whether this experience is suitable for you, please reach out privately. Your safety is deeply important to us.

description:
Well Elders: A Masterclass in promoting wellbeing in older people - Te-Whanganui-a-Tara - Wellington (WE2026/03), Aotearoa-New Zealand’s population is ageing rapidly. There are more and more people living into old age. The World Health Organisation has identified that as the baby boomer generation ages, many will enjoy reasonable physical health, however mental health issues, in particular depression and anxiety, will be a prevalent health issue. Therefore promoting mental wellbeing must be a major focus for those working with older people.
A older person's sense of wellbeing is determined by proven social, economic and cultural factors that either positively or negatively impact on older people. It is much broader than a wellness approach. How best to address factors such as loneliness, diminishing physical health, income and food security, significant loss, elder abuse, the invisibility of older people, cultural alienation and impacts of rural to urban migration and immigration from the Pacific Islands in the 1950's and 60's using a wellbeing framework will be a focus of the workshops.
However, while promoting wellbeing is an effective strategy in mitigating the impact of mood and anxiety disorders in older people, it should not be the primary aim of wellbeing promotion. The emphasis must be on ageing well and thriving elders.
Hear from an experienced wellbeing specialist who has lectured and implemented numerous wellbeing programmes at the local, national and international levels.
Over recent years there has been a greater awareness of the fundamental role that wellbeing plays in enabling individuals and communities to thrive. Take the opportunity to learn how older peoples' workers and agencies can put wellbeing at the heart of what they do that enables older people to thrive. This workshop provides a comprehensive overview of the research, evidence and latest international thinking on promoting wellbeing in older people as applied to the Aotearoa-New Zealand context
Well elders: thriving through participating and contributing
Informed by social, cultural and environmental determinants, adopting a wellbeing framework enable workers and agencies to identify how they can be "agents of wellbeing" for older people and how to incorporate wellbeing outcomes into their work. Based on these determinants and frameworks it is possible to develop an evidence-based programme logic with clear wellbeing outcomes and indicators and evaluation tools. An overview of the determinants and outcomes will be covered in the workshop.
Mental wellbeing is not just the responsibility of the health sector, the workshop is ideal training for anyone working with older people in:
aged care facilities
churches
community based older people agencies
local government
older persons' mental health services
primary health care
The training does not offer a ready-made older peoples' wellbeing package but rather helps participants to:
understand the underlying theory, principles and best practice in promoting mental wellbeing,
identify the enablers and disablers of wellbeing in older people,
to move from an outputs to outcomes focus in designing wellbeing programmes or activities

TAYLORMADE TRAINING AND CONSULTING IS PROUD TO BE AN AGE CONCERN DIGNITY CHAMPION 
TAKING A STAND AGAINST AGEISM AND PROMOTING POSITIVE AGEING

After the walk, you’ll have the opportunity to share a meal or snacks of your choice, deepen connections, and continue the conversation in a relaxed setting. As this is a free event, you’ll order and pay for any food and drinks yourself and can choose from the wide range on offer at St John's Bar.
Walking alongside others and taking the time to connect can boost our wellbeing, reduce stress, lift our mood and strengthen our sense of belonging.

Join expert practitioners from The Wellness Collective: Buffy Gill (Nutritionist & Naturopath) and Freda Wells (BSc. Psychology, Yoga Teacher and Somatic Therapist in training) for a powerful, practical masterclass.
In a world where "healthy living" can feel overwhelming, we are bringing it back to basics. Because modern lifestyles and depleted soils mean our food often lacks essential nutrients, this session focuses on using natural whole-food supplements and plant medicine to support your body at a cellular level—restoring balance exactly as nature intended.
In this masterclass, you’ll learn how to:
Boost your energy and improve daily recovery
Get better sleep and build resilience to stress
Improve your digestion and support natural detox pathways
Rebalance your hormones and manage inflammation
Support your health at a cellular level from the foundations up
Whether you’re at the beginning of your health journey and feeling run down, or you're a seasoned natural health lover who wants a simpler, more affordable, and effective regime, this session will help you level up your health across the board with a few simple, consistent daily practices.

description:
What the H***rmones? Pilates & Hormone Health Workshop, What the H***rmones? Pilates & Hormone Health Workshop
When you understand your body, everything changes.

Join Luisa & Eli for a Pilates technique breakdown + hormonal health masterclass, a two-part workshop that will teach you to:

- Move with better technique and less injury risk
- Train in a way that actually fits your hormonal cycle
- Build a more intuitive, sustainable relationship with exercise
- Feel empowered in your body — at every stage of your cycle

*Part 1: Pilates Technique Breakdown with Luisa*
Move beyond simply doing Pilates and learn how to do it well. Luisa will guide you through a detailed breakdown of key Pilates movements. Expect a hands-on, educational experience that sharpens your practice and helps you feel more confident in your body. You'll learn:

- Proper technique and alignment
- Breathwork and pelvic floor activation
- How to build strength safely and effectively
- Progressions that help you get more out of every session

Part 2: Hormonal Health & Training with Eli Hoyos
Eli breaks down how your body's natural rhythms influence your energy, strength and recovery, and what to actually do with that information.

We'll map each hormonal stage to the natural flow of a Pilates class — from breathwork and pelvic floor connection, to warm-up, to higher-intensity phases, and back down to cool-down.

Come away with a framework you can actually use!

WHO THIS IS FOR:

*Anyone who wants to learn more about proper technique & alignment in Pilates movements
*Anyone curious about how Pilates can support hormone health (yours OR the people you know & love!)
*Anyone looking to maximise performance to help you get more out of your Pilates/movement routines.

Haere mai!

About the Facilitators:

*Luisa Gordillo*

Luisa is a Certified Pilates instructor with a passion for holistic wellbeing, specialising in body awareness, injury prevention, and mindful movement. Trained in physiology and anatomy, she creates safe and inclusive classes for all levels. Her classes offer a full-body workout that builds strength, balance, and body awareness. Luisa empowers individuals through movement to improve everyday life.

*Eli Hoyos*

Eli is a Holistic Hormonal Health Coach and the founder of Elivate, a fitness and wellness system built specifically for women. After years of watching women train hard, eat well, and still feel stuck, she made it her mission to give them what the fitness industry never did: a strategy that actually works with their biology. Her approach combines cycle-syncing methodology, movement, and nutrition to help women understand their bodies and finally see lasting results. Learn more at elivatebyeli.com.

description:
When Comfort Isn’t Enough: Finding True Satisfaction, Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars

When Comfort Isn’t Enough: Finding True Satisfaction

We often seek happiness by improving our surroundings, yet true satisfaction comes from within. But what does that really mean, and how can we tap into it? Drawing on the philosophy of the ancient wisdom text Bhagavad Gita, this session explores the key internal shifts that can bring lasting joy, even amidst life’s imperfections.

Meet your host Sivananda:

Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. His passion for philosophy, music, good food and community attracted him to the bhakti lifestyle. Having studied and practiced the science of the ‘self’ for six years now, he thrives on drawing insights from contemporary science and combining it with yoga wisdom to encourage others to explore new perspectives.

6.15pm Tuesday 17th of March

End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.

description:
Women's Circle: To Be Heard, Women’s Circle: To Be Heard

This Women’s Circle is a calm and inclusive space designed to support rest, reflection, and gentle healing.

It’s a space where nothing is required of you. The circle is held in a way that allows women to settle into themselves, whether through quiet listening, reflection, or sharing if that feels right. Healing in this circle isn’t something that’s forced or directed - it’s something that naturally unfolds when there is safety, presence, and care.

The gathering begins with a simple guided experience to settle into the space. Followed by a prompt - everyone will a chance to share, within the circle, their mind and heart.

This is a space to be simply heard in a healing presence - one that supports the nervous system, release, and a sense of being genuinely heard.

There will be a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert to close the night in a grounded and connected way.

Meet Rasesvari, your host

Rasesvari (pronounced Rah-say-shwari) has always remembered feeling connected to healing, the inner world, and what helps people feel well and in alignment. Growing up, she spent many hours tucked away in libraries, reading about philosophy, plants, and anything that felt meaningful or life-giving.

Her path took a few turns away from the usual route, leading her to spend six years in an ashram setting focused on self-development and spiritual life. During that time, she explored meditation deeply and had space to focus on her own healing. This naturally opened the door to learning about Traditional Chinese healing, Ayurveda, sound healing, bioresonance, and a lot of self-study along the way.

Her loving aim is simple: to create spaces where people can finally feel comfortable in themselves again and and have room for their own growth and healing.

description:
Women's Health and Aging Workshop - Johnsonville Community Hall, Women's Health and Aging Workshop - Johnsonville Community Hall
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
An interactive workshop presented by experienced physiotherapist Sara Dore, focusing on how movement and function can be challenging for women as they age. Particularly for women, there is more to the core than abdominal muscles and strength and we explore these broader aspects.  Most importantly, you will come to understand that movement is medicine and we can make a difference.
You will be able to make a positive difference for yourself! The objective of this workshop is to give you knowledge and understanding about how you can manage the effects on your health and wellbeing as we age as women.  Knowledge is power!
In this one-day workshop you will discover:
- The base of the pelvic floor. Anatomy of the pelvic floor, and the common conditions urinary incontinence, and pelvic organ prolapse will be discussed. Education on basic pelvic floor advice and management as well as appropriate exercises will also be covered.
- The middle deep abdominal muscles. Trunk stability versus core strength as we age and the impact on our other core muscles and pelvic floor will be discussed. The principles of Clinical Pilates versus traditional Pilates will be presented together with the key principles of movement is medicine.
-The importance of the diaphragm and breathing well will also be discussed to enhance optimal movement and function for women.
Please wear comfortable clothes and socks as this is an interactive workshop, and bring a yoga mat or beach towel.
Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch and snacks.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

description:
Workshop Series: Vinyasa – Mai i te pō ki te ao mārama, Vinyasa – Mai i te pō ki te ao mārama is a four part workshop series themed on the phases of the Māori creation story (te kore, te pō, te whaiao, and te ao mārama) as a metaphor and framework for confronting the cyclical nature of life. Through vinyasa practice, we explore and embody the phases of the creation story, drawing parallels to yogic wisdom and setting a foundation and spark of curiosity for the wānanga that follows. After a short break, we'll reconvene in a wānanga space to further explore the deep wisdom of the creation story, learn more about the roles of the atua, and begin to unearth the relevance of it all to our own lives.

No prior experience of knowledge required. All are welcome - haere mai!

What to expect:
We will practice vinyasa flow together, sometimes incorporating meditation or breathwork. After a short break for showers/ lunch/coffee, we'll reconvene in a wānanga space to explore the relevant aspects of the Māori creation story for that workshop.

What will people take away from the experience?
A deeper understanding and appreciation of the Māori creation story and how its wisdom can help guide us through life, learned through wānanga and discussion but also through the embodied practice of vinyasa yoga and by drawing parallels with yogic wisdom.

Why Enrol?
To enjoy challenging and fun vinyasa flows themed around the phases of the Māori creation story. To engage in a safe space to ask questions and learn more about the Māori creation story, the phases of creation, the atua, and how the story offers us a framework for moving through the cycles of human life, from darkness to enlightenment.

What to bring:
Bring an open mind, perhaps a journal to gather thoughts down after the workshop. Light kai/food/snacks , as options for buying food are quite limited on the weekends. Mat hire and complementary herbal tea are included in your ticket. Towels can be hired for $3 if needed.

Facilitated by Ani Morris (Ngāti Kahungunu, Te Āti Awa, Rangitāne, Ngāti Mutunga, Rongowhakaata, Ngāti Tūkorehe, Tūhoe, Ngāti Pāhauwera) & Jenny Oliver (RYT 200).

description:
Yin Yoga & Sound Healing, Take an evening to slow down and reconnect. This session weaves together the meditative stillness of yin yoga with the restorative vibrations of sound healing — an immersive experience that invites both body and mind to unwind.

Through long-held yin postures, you’ll be guided to soften rather than strive, creating gentle openings and space for deeper release. The live sound journey adds another layer — resonant frequencies that ripple through the body, calming the nervous system and encouraging inner stillness.

Emma offers a trauma-informed yin practice grounded in compassion and self-awareness, drawing on her own personal growth and understanding of what it means to truly rest. Paired with Alex’s soundscapes, the evening becomes a tender exploration of presence and renewal.

We’ll close with a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert — a simple way to share warmth, grounding, and connection after the practice.

All levels are welcome.

Meet Emma, your yoga teacher
Emma holds a 100-hour trauma-informed Yin Yoga teacher certification, blending her corporate experience with a deep understanding of self-care. Emma's classes are designed to help create a safe space where you can relax and connect with your body. Her approach to teaching yin is purposeful, driven by a strong desire to empower students through mindful and compassionate practices. Her journey is rooted in self-growth and connection, with a strong focus on nourishing the body as an essential part of this.

Meet Alex, your sound healer
Alex is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche—making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from artists such as Deva Premal, The Flying Mystics, Stevin McNamara, and the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

Yoga & Cacao Twilight & Morning Edition - Pop-up Parlour 2025, Yoga & Cacao Twilight & Morning Edition - Pop-up Parlour 2025
Come and join Jenny Allan for a cup of ceremonial grade cacao and then enjoy a gentle and relaxing restorative yoga practice - twilight edition.

Event details

• What - 1.5 hr yoga session
• When -
TWILIGHT EDITION 7-8.30pm Tuesday 23rd September 2025
MORNING EDITION 10-11.30am Saturday 27th September 2025

• Where - St Marks, 98 Rāwhiti Road, Pukerua Bay
• Cost - $30 per person

• What to bring? Most props are provided but feel free to bring your own yoga mat for extra comfort as well as a cushion, blanket, socks and an eye pillow if you have one.

This class is suitable for all - no previous experience is required.

LIMITED SPACES AVAILABLE.
TWILIGHT SESSION - https://tinyurl.com/5a2pad44
MORNING SESSION - https://tinyurl.com/mw82z38u

Restorative yoga is a practice of deep relaxation in which yoga poses (asanas) are held for several minutes with the use of props such as blocks, bolster and blankets to support the body in gentle stretch.

When your body enters a state of relaxation, your mind will also relax. Once you have been guided to let go of any tension held in your body, all that is required is for you to pay attention to your breath, becoming aware of any thoughts that may arise, and then gently releasing them.

This restful practice calms both mind and body, allowing the nervous system to enter its parasympathetic state – the state of “rest and digest”, in which healing is enabled and enhanced.

About Cacao
Cacao is a superfood. It is plant medicine at its finest. Its scientific name, Theobroma cacao, translates to "food of the Gods." Containing many minerals, vitamins and phytonutrients such as flavonoids and antioxidants, it is also an extremely potent adaptogen that encourages the body to come into balance.

Cacao has a particularly strong influence on the heart – both physiologically and energetically. Cacao anecdotally is reported to enhance connection in community, hence its beauty in being shared in circle.

In Jenny's experience, cacao seems to enhance whatever it is that you are doing – be it running a marathon or meditating – cacao can make you go deeper, further, longer, stronger. However she does seem to have a mind of her own so be open to the experience she offers you – it may not always go quite how you planned!

Cacao is very safe and tolerated well by most people. However it is to be used with caution by people who are taking high doses of SSRIs. Cacao releases serotonin, so it works as a mild antidepressant. When taken with SSRIs that release serotonin chemically it can lead to serotonin syndrome. Individuals taking MAOIs (monoamine oxidase inhibitors) should avoid consuming ceremonial cacao due to potential interactions.
