What is yoga?
Yoga is breathing deeply, letting go of anxious thoughts, being kind, stretching the body to reduce tension, being more flexible, focusing and being mindful, and moving into different shapes.

What are the benefits of yoga?
Get stronger, more flexible and learn to relax in these Sunday morning community yoga classes. Reduce your blood pressure, improve circulation, reduce anxiety – and find more ease in your body.

What kind of yoga will I be doing?
A mix of vinyasa, hatha, restorative and mindfulness.

Who is the yoga teacher?
Janie Walker is a trained and experienced vinyasa, restorative and yin yoga teacher. She weaves ancient yoga philosophy and breath work with easy poses. Her classes are for beginners and those who want to deepen their own practice. Janie focuses on relaxation, breath and relaxing the mind.

If you have an injury or want to chat about how to look after yourself during your yoga class, please do contact Janie: or phone 0274539099. If you have any other physical or mental conditions that you’d like Janie to be aware of so she can support you, please contact her.

description:
Yoga Nidra, Unwind from the stresses of the week and start your weekend in a state of relaxation. Yoga Nidra, often referred to as "yogic sleep," is a deeply restorative practice that promotes physical relaxation, mental clarity, and emotional balance. It's the perfect way to rejuvenate your mind, body, and soul: your hinengaro, tinana and wairua.

Yoga nidra is a powerful technique that directly works to heal your mind by removing samskaras - untying knots and mental impressions. This practice of learning to relax consciously is well regarded as an antidote for stress, anxiety, poor sleep amongst other health benefits.

Everyone is welcome to experience the profound benefits of Yoga Nidra, and no prior experience is required. For some people, however, Yoga Nidra’s prolonged stillness or internal focus can bring up strong emotions, memories, and/or sensations. You are encouraged to listen and respond in a way that feels safe for you — adjusting your position, keeping your eyes open, grounding yourself, or stepping out of the room at any time.

Yoga Nidra may not be suitable for everyone. If you are experiencing acute mental health challenges, unprocessed trauma, or conditions that make stillness or internal focus difficult, we recommend seeking guidance from a qualified healthcare provider or speaking with the teacher before participating.

description:
Yoga for All at Kai Tahi, Yoga for All at Kai Tahi
Community yoga is coming to Kai Tahi!

Try Sunday morning yoga classes with local yoga teacher, Janie Walker from BeCalmed Studio. Janie specialises in introducing people to yoga and supporting a life-long practice and love of yoga. Come stretch, breathe and feel good; this is yoga for all bodies and experiences.

$10 per class (cash or internet banking), no bookings required.
Please bring a yoga mat.

Every Sunday 9am (starts 19 October)
Kai Tahi atrium

What is yoga?

Yoga is breathing deeply, letting go of anxious thoughts, being kind, stretching the body to reduce tension, being more flexible, focusing and being mindful, and moving into different shapes.

What are the benefits of yoga?

Get stronger, more flexible and re-learn to relax in these Sunday morning community yoga classes. Reduce your blood pressure, improve circulation, reduce anxiety – and find more ease in your body.

How will I feel after my Sunday Kai Tahi yoga class?

Lighter, more relaxed, stronger, more confident, calmer.

What kind of yoga will I be doing?

A mix of vinyasa, hatha, restorative and mindfulness.

Who is the yoga teacher?

Janie Walker is a trained and experienced vinyasa, restorative and yin yoga teacher. She weaves ancient yoga philosophy and breath work with easy poses. Her classes are for beginners and those who want to deepen their own practice. Janie focuses on relaxation, breath and relaxing the mind.

How much does it cost?

$ 10 per class (cash or internet banking)

Do I need to book?

No bookings necessary. Just turn up. Yoga mats provided or bring your own.

Can I do yoga if I am injured or recovering from illness or don’t feel good?

If you have an injury or want to chat about how to look after yourself during your yoga class, please do contact Janie: or phone 0274539099. If you have any other physical or mental conditions that you’d like Janie to be aware of so she can support you, please contact her.

Find out more about BeCalmed Studio and Janie Walker - www.becalmedstudio.com

description:
Yoga in the Sanctuary, Find peace and tranquility while participating in our Sanctuary Yoga sessions this summer.

Meet at the Visitor Centre and take a calming hīkoi/walk up Lake Road to Tūī Terrace in the heart of the valley. Lay out your mats and be led in a hatha yoga session that is uniquely facilitated with a te ao Māori kaupapa.

Our Wednesday evening sessions run from 5.30-7.30pm, and our morning sessions on Sundays run from 9.00-11.00am.

This experience is outdoors so make sure to dress appropriately. There will be a gentle 15 min walk up and back from the site along an accessible path. These sessions are designed to suit all levels of ability.

If you have your own yoga mat then bring it along, as while Zealandia does have a few to loan out, supplies are limited.

In the event of bad weather the session may be moved indoors but may have a short walk out in the valley before hand, or else cancelled with credit offered to customers for another session.

description:
🧠 The Starving Brain | A Yogic Perspective on Nourishment, Energy & Focus, 🧠 The Starving Brain | A Yogic Perspective on Nourishment, Energy & Focus
We often talk about eating less — but not about what happens when we don’t eat enough.
When the body is under-fuelled, the brain takes priority — quietly redirecting energy away from digestion, hormones, and even mood regulation.

From a yogic lens, this is more than biology.
When energy stops flowing freely (prana), we lose clarity, intuition, and the natural rhythm that keeps body and mind in harmony.

In this 2-hour workshop, we’ll explore:
• Why the brain “steals” energy when under stress or depletion
• The emotional energy of food — and what your cravings might be teaching you
• The science of fasting — when it supports healing and when it harms
• The gut–brain connection and how awareness restores balance
• How nourishment, breath, and rhythm support neuroplasticity and vitality

We’ll finish with Q&A and discussion to help you integrate the insights into your own life.

💰 $40 per person
📍 Yoga Studio, Raumati South
🔗 Book here:

https://35daydetox.simplybook.net/v2/

“In yoga, nourishment isn’t indulgence — it’s how energy becomes consciousness.”

(Now on Sunday) Planetary Parade - Free event, Due to a heavy cloud forecast on Saturday morning, we have changed the date for this event to the following morning, Sunday 24 August.
A rare cosmic event where six of the seven planets are in dawn sky during this final Planetary Parade for 2025. Matariki is also visible at this time close to the line of planets.
Come down to the Wellington waterfront at dawn and see the planets Pareārau (Saturn), Kōpū/Tāwera (Venus), Hine-i-tīweka (Jupiter), Whiro (Mercury), and Matariki (Pleiades) in our skies. Rangipō (Uranus) and Tangaroa (Neptune) are also in the sky but they will be too faint to see. Matawhero (Mars) follows after Te Rā (the Sun) rises so it won't be seen in the sky.
If you want to gaze in wonder at Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, look through our amazing telescopes! We can show you where to find Matariki, but binoculars at better so if you have a pair bring them along. The event is child friendly and free!
If you want to support our Society by becoming a member, please go to https://www.was.org.nz/join-us/

description:
ABBA Day Party: Wellington 💃🕺, ABBA Day Party: Wellington 💃🕺
Book Here → https://www.fatsoma.com/e/faj25ciu/la/mpra

Calling all Dancing Queens and Super Troupers! 🎉

Get ready for a glitter-filled afternoon of pure pop perfection as we celebrate the iconic music of ABBA! Whether you're a lifelong fan or just love a bit of feel-good disco, this is your chance to sing, dance, and party like it's Eurovision '74!

What to Expect:

🎶 Wall-to-Wall ABBA Anthems
From “Dancing Queen” to “Gimme! Gimme! Gimme!”, enjoy all the greatest hits and hidden gems that made ABBA a global sensation.

✨ Disco, Funk & 70s Classics
While ABBA takes center stage, we'll also be spinning a fabulous mix of other dancefloor-fillers from the disco era—think funky grooves, 70s gems, and all the classics that’ll keep you moving from start to finish.

💫 ABBA-Inspired Atmosphere
Think shimmering lights, tinsel wigs and more sequins than you can shake a tambourine at! Step into your own mini-Mamma Mia moment!

🌈 Feel-Good Vibes All Day Long
Celebrate friendship, freedom, and unforgettable tunes with an afternoon of singing, dancing, and joyous nostalgia.

Whether you’re a Fernando or a Chiquitita, this is your Waterloo! don’t miss it! 🎤✨


FAQ’S

🗣️ Why do the tickets come in different price tiers?

Whilst there is no physical difference. There is only a limited amount of tickets we can sell. Therefore we operate a festival style ticketing model. The earlier you buy your ticket the cheaper it will be.

🗣️ Do you do group discount? Stag/Hen etc

Yes, we offer a discounted ticket price for groups of 10 or more. These tickets can be found listed as the “Big Group Package!” above, orders for these tickets are restricted to a minimum of 10.

🗣️ Will there be more tickets available if the event is sold out?

Once this event is sold out, there will not be any additional tickets released. In addiction to this we will be unable to sell them at the door due to maximum capacity and health and safety regulations.

🗣️ Is the venue accessible?

Our events take place at a variety of locations across the UK and Ireland. As each varies please ensure to check the specific venue's website for accessibility information.

🗣️ Can I resell my tickets?

Yes, if you are unable to attend an event you are welcome to sell your tickets on. We do not use names on tickets as a condition for entry.

🗣️ Are your events 18+?

All of our events are strictly 18+. A valid photographic ID may be requested on entry.

🗣️ I have more questions?

If you have additional questions and wish to contact us directly, don’t hesitate to drop us a DM on either Facebook (Daytime Disco) or Instagram (@daytimediscoevents)

Refund Policy:
In-line with normal consumer standards for ticket purchases, tickets for Daytime Disco events are non-refundable, on the condition that we not moved the event or canceled it. If you are no longer be able to attend the event, you are of course welcome to gift or sell your tickets onwards as we do not use names on the tickets as a condition of entry.

description:
Astronomy on Tap, Experience the wonders of the Universe with Astronomy on Tap, Space Place’s after‑hours planetarium series, where great science meets great drinks.
Begin your journey with a drink on arrival and some first‑class in-flight snacks. Then settle into our digital full-dome planetarium as we travel from Pōneke into the vast depths of space. Complete your trip with a visit to the cash bar and our interactive exhibitions.
Whether you’re bringing someone special, catching up with a friend, or exploring solo, raise your glass to the night sky and enjoy a stellar ride.
Tuesday 31 March: Tour of the Solar System (and Beyond!)
Have you ever looked up and wondered what’s really out there? This month, we’re taking you on a grand tour of our cosmic neighbourhood, and then pushing far beyond it.
We’ll begin right here in Pōneke, exploring the night sky and discovering where Earth sits in the vastness of space. Then buckle up for a whistle‑stop journey around our Solar System: planets, moons, oddballs, and everything in between. Finally, we’ll launch thousands of light-years outward into deep space to meet some of the galaxy’s most extraordinary sights.
Come see the night sky as you’ve never seen it before.
Tuesday 28 April: Scale of the Universe
How big is big? How small is small? And where exactly do we fit?
April’s Astronomy on Tap dives into the mind‑bending scales of the cosmos, from our skies over Pōneke to the edge of the observable Universe. After orienting ourselves in the night sky, we’ll journey outward past planets, moons, star‑forming nebulae, and even black holes, until we reach the faint glow of the Cosmic Microwave Background nearly 93 billion light-years away.
It’s a fast, fun, and perspective-shifting ride through space and time, with drinks and nibbles for the trip.
Thursday 28 May: Planets, Exoplanets & Moons
Our Solar System alone is packed with wonders, icy moons, volcanic worlds, and Saturn’s hundreds of orbiting companions. But beyond our Sun lies an even larger menagerie of strange and spectacular exoplanets.
In May, join us for a journey through the planets, exoplanets, and moons both near and far. We’ll visit some of the Solar System’s most dramatic worlds, then leap to distant star systems to explore alien planets that are hotter, colder, larger, smaller, weirder, and wilder than anything we’ve ever seen up close.
What might we discover out there? Come along and find out.
Thursday 25 June: Matatiki
Ka puta Matariki, ka rere Whānui, ko te tohu o te tau.
Matariki appears as Whānui flees; this is the sign of the new year.
The Matariki star cluster appears in our morning sky in midwinter, signaling the transition to spring and eventually to summer. This collection of stars, along with Puanga, te Marama, and other aspects of tō tātou taiao – our environment – are just some of the tohu or signs that tell us we are approaching the New Year. Haere mai, join us for this month’s Astronomy on Tap to learn how to read the signs and celebrate the significance of this time of year.
$45pp | 8PM–10PM | R18 | Space Place

description:
Athol McCredie - Spencer Digby Studio Collection, Athol McCredie is Curator of Photography at Te Papa. He will talk about the Spencer Digby Studio collection held by Te Papa. The studio was founded in 1931 by Spencer Digby and was taken over by Ron and Inge Woolf in 1960, who ran it under the same name until the mid-1970s.
It was a portrait studio where anybody who was anyone in (or visiting) Wellington was photographed, from prime ministers to debutantes.
Athol will also talk about early twentieth-century photographer Leslie Adkin, the subject of his most recent book, ‘Leslie Adkin: Farmer Photographer’.
Thursday, October 9th, Tararua Tramping Club (4 Moncrieff St, Mt Victoria), Doors Open at 7pm
If you’re curious about the Wellington Photographic Society, you’re welcome to attend two meetings for free before deciding whether to join. It’s a great way to meet the community and see what we’re all about!

It’s Halloween and that is true for this month at Bea Adventure! All things spooky and kooky are there for the investigating, rescuing and possibly the running from! Will the witch need saving before the angry mob gets them or is she trying to make you into a casserole? Meet with fellow heroes to save the world against foul monsters and evil enemies … all with a beer* in hand. Join our Professional Dungeon Masters and play D&D the World’s Greatest Roleplaying Game.

In cahoots with Baylands Brewery, Bea D&D the premium gaming store based in Wellington, are running Dungeons & Dragons RPG evening events for adults (R18).

Whether you have played D&D before many times or never, all heroes are welcome to come along. Our professional Dungeon Masters are skilled in helping you have a great time as you learn and still providing a challenging encounter for all the adventurers who have fought many battles before. It’s a great place to bring friends who have been meaning to try the game for a while, get some social time in with friends and try out some amazing locally brewed beers.

We will be providing pre-generated character sheets and everything you need to play. All you need to bring is yourself. Get ready to kick off the new year with Beats by Bingo at The Bond Store! Mistress Viv is here to serve up some winner winner chicken dinners and throwback jams galore.

-When: Thursday 26th March
- Time: 7:30 PM
- Tickets: Grab yours via Eventfinda – spaces are very limited, so snap them up while you can!

What to Expect:
Musical bingo like you’ve never seen it – instead of numbers, your cards are filled with song titles!
Throwback jams, guilty pleasure tunes, and our famous Theme Tunes round featuring songs from film and TV.
Prizes, mini games, and loads of fun!

Seating: Shared seating by default, or contact The Bond Store to book your own table. Make friends, be nice, and enjoy the vibes!

Think you know your music? Come prove it. See you at bingo!

description:
Beer & Spirits Halloween Crawl – Wellington 2025, Beer & Spirits Halloween Crawl – Wellington 2025
Raise your glass to Halloween in Wellington! The Beer & Spirits Crawl brings cocktails, craft beer, costumes, and DJs on November 1st.

About this Event

🍺🥃 BEER & SPIRITS: HALLOWEEN BOOZE CRAWL 2025 – Wellington 🥃🍺 Halloween Saturday in Wellington is about to get boozier. The Beer & Spirits: Halloween Booze Crawl is your pass to explore the city’s best pubs, breweries, and nightlife spots in one epic night of costumes, cocktails, and craft beer.
On Saturday, November 1st, 2025, hundreds of party-ready crawlers will gather to toast the spookiest night of the year. From seasonal ales and spiced lagers to spooky-themed shots and signature cocktails, every stop on the crawl will be serving something worth raising a glass to.



EVENT HIGHLIGHTS
🥃 Beer + Spirits Combo: Enjoy the best of both worlds with craft beer options and premium cocktails at every venue.
🎶 Live Music & DJs: Halloween hits, party anthems, and dance-worthy beats all night long.
📍 Venues: Lulu Bar & Restaurant, El Horno, The Rogue & Vagabond, and BL3 — hand-picked Wellington bars and breweries offering exclusive specials for crawl guests.
🎟 Your Ticket Includes: Wristband for entry, drink specials at each stop, and access to the official crawl map.

HOW TO JOIN THE FUN
1️⃣ Check-In: Pick up your wristband at the starting venue between 7:30–10:30 PM.
2️⃣ Crawl at Your Own Pace: Visit participating middle-stop venues between 8:30–11:30 PM.
3️⃣ Last Call for Halloween: Everyone meets at the final venue at 11:30 PM for the Saturday night send-off party.



PARTICIPATING VENUES The lineup will be released soon — each location is chosen for great drinks, great atmosphere, and great music.
📍 On event day, click the to view the full venue list, drink specials, and schedule.

🎭 Costume Friendly: Whether you’re dressed as a beer-loving ghoul, a whiskey-wielding pirate, or a spooky pop culture icon, you’ll fit right in.

🚨 Saturday-Only Tickets: This is a one-night-only Halloween party. Early bird tickets start at just $15 — secure your spot before they’re gone.

What’s Included in Your Ticket:
🍺 Entry to 4+ pubs, breweries, and clubs in Wellington
🚫 No cover at all participating venues
🎟️ Exclusive Halloween Booze Crawl wristband
📱 Digital crawl map to navigate each stop
🎵 Live DJs & music at every venue
🕺 Closing party to end Halloween Saturday in style



18+ EVENT / GOVERNMENT ISSUED ID REQUIRED


TIPS FOR OUR CRAWL
Pick Up Wristbands On Time: Collect your wristband(s) during the designated check-in time at the scheduled location before 10:30 PM. Late arrivals will not be accommodated — no wristband, no entry.
Assign a Proxy if Needed: Can’t make check-in? Have a friend pick up your wristband for you so they don’t miss out.
Day-Of Updates: Review the Digital Crawl Map on the morning of the event for any last-minute changes or venue updates.
Check Venue Schedule: Each venue’s crawl time is listed in the Digital Crawl Map. Wristbands and drink specials are valid only during these scheduled times.
_______________________________________


IMPORTANT DISCLAIMERS
Age Requirement: You must be 18+ years of age with a valid government-issued ID to participate in this event. No exceptions.
Wristbands: Your wristband is your key to entry. You must present your ticket or QR code at check-in to receive your wristband. Wristbands must be worn at all times to access participating bars and venues. Wristband pickup location and time are listed on the crawl map. If you do not pick up your wristband at the designated location and time, it may not be available, and you will not be able to access crawl venues. No wristband, no entry.
Ticket Policy: All sales are final—no refunds, exchanges, or transfers. In case of event cancellation without a rescheduled date, a refund (excluding fees) will be automatically issued. Event lineup, venues, and specials are subject to change without notice.
Admission & Venue Rights: Participating venues reserve the right to refuse service or entry to any attendee based on intoxication, dress code, inappropriate behaviour, or venue capacity. If refused entry at one venue, you may visit alternative crawl venues available at that time. No refunds will be given if you are denied entry for any of these reasons.
Capacity and Late Entry: Some venues may hit capacity during the event. If a venue reaches capacity or you arrive late, you may have to wait in line to gain entry. There is no guarantee of immediate access or entry to any specific venue once capacity is reached, and no refunds will be provided due to waiting times or access issues.
Self-Guided Crawl: This is a self-guided event with no host leading the group. You must use the digital crawl map to navigate between venues.
Venue Awareness: If bar staff are unaware of the crawl, you must contact the venue representative listed on the crawl map. If you cannot reach them, consider that venue unavailable and proceed to an alternative crawl venue open at that time. Nightlife venues may reach capacity or close early, and not all staff members may be aware of the crawl.
Drink Specials: Drink specials are offered by participating venues and may be modified or discontinued at any time without notice.
Event Time Restrictions: Your ticket is valid only for crawl venues during the scheduled crawl times listed on the crawl map. It is not valid for entry outside these times. If you arrive late or at the wrong venue, refunds will not be issued.
Security Checks: Wristbands do not entitle you to skip venue security checks. All attendees must comply with security screening before entry.
Costume Policy: Do not wear costumes that include items which could be considered or used as weapons. Highly offensive costumes are not tolerated and may result in denial of entry without refund.
Crawl Notifications: Sign up for crawl notification texts to receive updates about when to move to the next venue. There is no host to notify you in person.
Respect & Conduct: Treat others and the event venues with respect. Disorderly conduct, inappropriate behaviour, or damage to the venues will result in removal from the event without a refund. The participating bars reserve the right to refuse entry or remove attendees for inappropriate behaviour at any time.
Liability Waiver: By purchasing a ticket and participating in the crawl, you understand and agree that you are attending entirely at your own risk. You voluntarily assume all risks and dangers incidental to this event, including but not limited to: personal injury, illness, disability, property loss, theft, damage, accidents, death, alcohol-related incidents, and actions of other participants, staff, or third parties. You, on behalf of yourself and your heirs, executors, and assigns, hereby fully release, waive, and discharge Events Per Se, its owners, officers, directors, employees, contractors, volunteers, affiliates, sponsors, participating venues, and their respective representatives from any and all liability, claims, demands, actions, or causes of action whatsoever arising out of or related to any loss, damage, injury, illness, or death — whether caused by negligence, gross negligence, breach of contract, or otherwise — that may occur before, during, or after the event. You agree to indemnify and hold harmless Events Per Se and all released parties from any claims, costs, or expenses (including legal fees) brought by you or on your behalf, or by any third party as a result of your actions during the event. You acknowledge that you have read and understood this waiver, that you are participating voluntarily, and that this waiver is intended to be as broad and inclusive as permitted by applicable law.
Event Changes: Bars and venues may change, but the event will continue rain or shine. Always check the digital crawl map for the latest venue list and updates. Be sure to check your email for any last-minute updates.
*By purchasing a ticket, you confirm that you have read, understood, and agreed to all disclaimers, terms, and conditions stated above, and accept full responsibility for your participation in the event.

description:
Beyond the Bookshelves: Diversity in Austen Retellings, Join Rachel Pilois, passionate Austen lover (owner of over 30 copies of Pride and Prejudice) and Children's Book Buyer at Unity Books, for an illuminating exploration of diversity in contemporary Austen retellings. As a mixed-race, queer, and neurodiverse bookseller, Rachel brings a unique perspective to the rich tapestry of Austen-inspired literature.
In this talk, Rachel will showcase a curated selection of titles—all available through Unity Books—that reimagine Austen's beloved stories through diverse lenses. Discover queer retellings, tales set in other cultures, modern adaptations, and even Regency-era stories that amplify marginalized voices.
Attendees will gain a deeper appreciation for the breadth of the current Austen book market and its resonance with the modern world. Prepare to expand your reading list and discover exciting new perspectives on timeless classics.
Part of the Jane Austen Society of Aotearoa New Zealand's 2026 series on diversity.
Bring a friend: purchase 2 or more tickets and get a 10% discount
Who this event is for:
People who love Austen
People who love books
People who care about diversity
Afternoon tea provided

Image: Pride & Prejudice Pride flag by AmateurAusten (available for purchase on multiple items on Red Bubble)

Do I need to know about Jane Austen?
No. Everyone is welcome.

We aim to provide an accessible and safe environment. Discounts are available for nonwaged members, early birds, volunteers and people buying multiple tickets. Please let us know how we can ensure you're included.

description:
Book Club: Emiko by Chieri Uegaki, Join us in person to discuss Emiko, a contemporary version of Jane Austen's Emma set in Canada.
(Order your copy through us by 20 March 2026 for delivery at the 23 May meeting or couriered in NZ)
About Emiko:
A busybody foodie avoids questions of her own future as she meddles in the love lives of those around her. Has this matcha-maker met her match?

Self-declared matchmaking GENIUS (a la Beyonce) Emiko Kimori has already found success by helping her aunt find true love, so when the new girl in town becomes her new BFF, it's only natural for Emiko to help set her up for social success with a suitable love match.

Emiko lives with her Ojiichan in a small town on BC's West Coast surrounded by friends and neighbors, including her childhood friend Kenzo Sanada, who wishes she'd spend less time playing matchmaker. But Emiko can so clearly see who belongs together, even when her targets don't know it themselves. She simply has to meddle - for the sake of true love!

As for her own romantic life though . . . who has time for that? Emiko is far too busy with her matchmaking schemes, her brunch recipes, volunteering, her bustling social life, keeping up her grades, eating said brunch recipes and making plans for after graduation. Plans she will absolutely decide on soon. Definitely. Maybe? But when Emiko ends up falling for the last person she expects, she finds herself caught in the tangled web of her own love matches. For the first time, instead of arranging from afar, Emiko has to figure out what it means to be in love herself, and that friendship and romance are more complicated than she ever imagined . . .
About the Author:
Chieri Uegaki is a second generation Japanese-Canadian and award-winning children’s author living and writing on Vancouver Island, in the traditional and unceded territory of the lək̓ʷəŋən speaking peoples, today known as the Esquimalt and Songhees Nations.
She graduated with a Bachelor of Fine Arts from the University of British Columbia’s Creative Writing Department and has written a number of stories for children, including the picture books Suki’s Kimono and Rosie and Buttercup (both illustrated by Stéphane Jorisch); Hana Hashimoto, Sixth Violin (illustrated by Qin Leng); and Ojiichan’s Gift (illustrated by Genevieve Simms).
When not reading or writing, Chieri consumes rom-coms and mysteries in any form, chooses appetizers over dessert most of the time, and tries to stay on top of her collecting problem. She is currently working on a number of projects.
Rachel Pilois (Book Buyer) on this selection:
There have been many retellings of Austen’s novels in the last 200 years. Pride and Prejudice easily wins the prize of Austen’s most adapted novel in both film and literature. In the last 20 years there’s been a noticeable growth in culturally (and gender) diverse takes on Austen’s work, with the most popular retellings being of Indian (i.e Bride and Prejudice) or African-American (i.e. Ibi Zoboi’s Pride) heritage. Sadly, some of her less popular novels (Mansfield Park and Northanger Abbey) have few adaptations in both film and literature, faithful or modern retelling.
With the 2026 theme of the JASNZ being diversity it made sense to choose a slightly less popular novel (only in terms of how many adaptations) and a slightly less common culture used in Austen retellings. Thus I settled on the upcoming YA novel Emiko by Chieri Uegaki, a Japanese-Canadian retelling of Emma.
Emma is a much beloved story and a much beloved character, who’s thoughts, actions and motivations are very recognisable in a modern teenager. Adding in the deep cultural etiquette of Japan as a likeness to the rules of regency society, makes Uegaki’s Emiko a brilliant and well thought out modern retelling of the Emma.
As it publishes on 9 September 2025, we can discover and discuss this new and exciting adaptation for the first time together! 
NB: Ticket numbers are limited to ensure ease of discussion. Afternoon tea is provided
FRIEND: bring a friend, get 10% off! Discount automatically applied

NOTE: this ‘April’ meeting is on Tuesday 31 March as the following Tuesday is right after Easter.

Our group reads one Kiwi classic each year; this year we read Smith's Dream...

New Zealand in economic and political crisis. Oil shocks. Industrial disputes. Isolation. The government declares martial law, while opponents of the overnight police state arm themselves and take to the bush... One man, Smith, who thought he was getting away to the Coromandel to escape his personal troubles, is unwillingly dragged into the struggle.

C.K. Stead's short 1971 novel became a prescribed text for thousands of school students and later that decade a major feature film. Sleeping Dogs (1977) was the first New Zealand film released in the United States and stars Sam Neill in his breakout role.

Book Group: The Idiot by Fyodor Dostoevsky, Do you keep meaning to read more of the great classics of literature? At Wellington Classic Literature Club, we read novels that have stood the test of time, whether they were written in 1780, 1880 or even 1980. We meet on the first Tuesday of the month.

We return to Russia for our long summer read! The group's first-ever summer book was Anna Karenina, and we read Dostoevsky's The Brothers Karamazov over the 2018/19 summer. (We were also due to discuss his novel Crime and Punishment, but that was set down for April 2020 and, well, the world had other plans…)

This year, we read another of Fyodor Dostoevsky's masterworks: The Idiot, which was initially published as a serial in 1868-1869. Dostoevsky scholar Joseph Frank said The Idiot "is the most personal of all his major works, the book in which he embodies his most intimate, cherished, and sacred convictions."

The story revolves around Prince Lef Nicolaievitch Muishkin, a young man returning to Russia after spending several years in a Swiss sanatorium for epilepsy. Dostoevsky had set out to create a protagonist with "a truly beautiful soul" and to trace the fate of such an individual as he comes into contact with the brutal reality of contemporary society.

Our November book, and first work of poetry, is Kahlil Gibran's The Prophet (1923). Born in Lebanon in 1883 and later emigrating to the United States, Kahlil Gibran bridged East and West. His writings, poetry and art explore themes of love, spirituality and humanity.

The Prophet, his classic work of prose poetry, has been translated into more than 100 languages and is one of the best-selling books of all time. It has never gone out of print.

Book Group: Uncle Tom's Cabin by Harriet Beecher Stowe, Do you keep meaning to read more of the great classics of literature? At Wellington Classic Literature Group we read novels that have stood the test of time, whether they were written in 1780, 1880 or even 1980. The group has been running for more than a decade and we have a great bunch of regulars as well as readers that come along for particular books or simply when it suits. We meet on the first Tuesday of the month.

Our October book is Harriet Beecher Stowe's 1852 abolitionist novel Uncle Tom's Cabin; or, Life Among the Lowly. The work changed American hearts and minds about slavery.

The influence of Uncle Tom's Cabin was so immense that the story arose that when Abraham Lincoln welcomed Stowe to the White House during the American Civil War he reportedly declared, "So this is the little lady who started this great war."

In the US, it was the best-selling novel of the 19th century and the second best-selling book of all after the Bible.

description:
Braai and get together at Battle Hill - 17 January 2026, Braai and get together at Battle Hill - 17 January 2026
How about just a casual get together and braai? The last one we had at Battle Hill was so nice and we met so many new people. Noting that this is weather dependent.

Where:
We have secured "The Dell" area for semi-exclusive use at Battle Hill. (It will be Wellington Anniversary weekend so may be a bit busy.) This means a large section of grass with trees, toilets and the river close by for the kids to play in and see the eels and we can braai in webers, etc. The bigger kids that want to go and swim in the hole can take a walk there. Unfortunately, there are no concrete slabs that we can make fires on so you will need to bring a braai with.

What to bring?
Well, this is not a catered place so you will need to bring the following:
Gazebo
Chairs and/or blankets
Braai and charcoal/wood i.e. weber, etc 😉
There are gas braais as well but you will need to share it with the rest of the people / campers.)
Meat, drinks, salad and water/ drinks (to drink and to K*ll your fire with)
Balls, bats, etc for the kids to play (If someone is keen on arranging games for the day, we would appreciate it!)

There is no cost to us getting semi exclusive use of the area. However, if you want to extend the night and camp, you will need to pay for that.

Please note that this is a working farm area and unfortunately no dogs are allowed AT ALL.

Also note that the gates are locked at 8pm so if you are not camping, please keep this in mind so you can get out in time.

This is an open invitation so no need to RSVP to me but it would be nice to have an indication on how many people will attend by confirming on the event "Going" or "Interested".

I hope to see LOTS of you there!

Card Merchant Wellington - Catan Settlement Event #1 2026, Card Merchant is excited to be part of the 2026 Catan Organized Play program here in New Zealand, providing an opportunity for players from all over the country to get involved, learn, and enjoy the game in a structured event setting.
These Catan Settlement Events are designed as an accessible entry point into organized play, giving players a chance to experience tournament-style games ahead of more competitive events later in the year.
Event Details:
Store: Card Merchant Wellington
Dates: 9th May 2026
Time: 11:00 AM
Entry Fee: $20
Event Structure:
Players will engage in multiple rounds to determine overall standings for the event.
Preliminary Round:
Each participant will play three separate games of base set Catan.
Opponents will rotate for each game.
At the conclusion of the preliminary round, players will be ranked based on their overall performance across all games.
Final Rounds:
Depending on player numbers, top-performing players may be split into final tables to determine overall placings.
If player numbers are lower, the event may instead consist solely of multiple Swiss-style rounds, with final standings determined by total points or wins.
This event is designed to balance structure with accessibility, giving players a clear tournament experience while keeping the environment welcoming and easy to engage with.
Prizes:
4x Summer Hex Kits
2x Gamegenic Catan Sleeves
2x Exit: Adventures on Catan
1x Catan Seafarers Duel
Whether you’re new to Catan or a long-time player, this is a great opportunity to get involved, meet other players, and take part in organized play. Join us at Card Merchant for a fun and welcoming day of Catan!

description:
Central & Districts Field Days Flyer, Central & Districts Field Days Flyer
Departing Plimmerton and traveling by heritage steam train to the Central Districts Field Days, enjoy a relaxed, hassle-free day out. This special Mainline Steam excursion takes you direct to Feilding, with shuttle transfers to Manfeild Park included in your ticket.

Travel in comfort behind a heritage steam locomotive in our beautifully restored carriages featuring large viewing windows, air-conditioning, comfortable seating, onboard café, and toilets. For fresh-air lovers and photographers, our observation carriage provides open-air viewing of the scenic journey.

Arrival into Feilding is approximately 10:45am, with departure back south at 4:15pm, giving you a full day at Field Days.

🚐 Shuttle Transfers Included
Shuttle buses operate between Feilding Railway Station and Manfeild Park, timed to connect with our train arrival and departure. Shuttle transfers are included with your excursion ticket.

🕒 Indicative Timetable

Outbound
Plimmerton – 07:20
Paraparaumu – 07:55
Ōtaki – 08:45
Levin – 09:35
Shannon – 09:50
Palmerston North – 10:15
Feilding – 10:45

Return
Feilding – 16:15
Palmerston North – 16:55
Shannon – 17:15
Levin – 17:25
Ōtaki – 17:50
Paraparaumu – 18:15
Plimmerton – 18:40

ℹ️ Please note: large Field Days purchases cannot be loaded onto the train

📸 A Great Day Out
Make the journey part of the experience and travel to Field Days in comfort by steam train. Relax, enjoy the scenery, and arrive ready to explore one of the country’s biggest agricultural events.

Club Night - Fireside Chat with Mark and Gavin, it's all about the punt!, Ever wondered what’s really involved in lifting your chains, checking your blocks, and keeping your boat secure inside the harbour?
Come along and hear Gavin and Mark share their knowledge — including Gavin’s tale of installing blocks for Revenue Cutter inside the boat harbour, and how a “mooring muscle boy” became a rocket!
You’ll learn:
How to inspect chains and spot potential issues
Why regular servicing (every 2 years) is the best protection in heavy winds
The story of the Punt — over 100 years old and still servicing moorings in Clyde Quay
The Mooring Punt isn’t a dark art — it’s a simple winch with rollers that does an important job. This is your chance to see how it works, ask questions, and even book a slot to have your mooring serviced so you can sleep well knowing your boat is secure.

description:
Coptic Book Binding Workshop, Coptic binding is one of the earliest forms of creating a book, with raw simplicity you can produce a book of any size with the unique feature of opening out flat. No special tools or materials are needed and yet a wide spectrum of creative results can be created, from a notebook, sketch book and album to a highly crafted artwork. The books themselves can be made from found items, recycled material or quality art papers and card.

In this workshop you will be guided in assembling your chosen materials for your book, create decorative covers and learn Coptic binding - an elegant and simple binding that is unlimited in versatility. You will produce one bound book and one bound album. Once you have Coptic binding in your skill set you can produce your choice of books in any shape or form, for any purpose.

All basic materials supplied.

Half an hour for lunch. Bring a drink bottle and a packed lunch to enjoy in the historic Inverlochy House or explore the cafes in Te Aro. Coffee & tea provided at lunch.

You must be at least 16 years of age to attend this course or attend with a paying adult.

description:
Coven: Butch, For butches and butch lovers! This night sets to make two things clear:

1. We love butches!
2. Get enough sapphics and queers in a room and anything can become a competition

Join us for axe throwing, games, kai, and as always at our events impeccable vibes. Spot prizes for the best butches, drink on arrival, and a room full of hot babes? Need we say more, so get your fits checked and grab your ticket before they go. This event has limited capacity.

Not a butch? No problem, all butch and butch appreciating Coven members of all flavours welcome.

No dress code! Come as you are, celebrate butch fashion or your queer identity and expect a fun chill night with your community.

More info about Coven:

Coming Solo? You’re Not Alone.
Don’t be nervous if you’re planning to come on your own – Coven is built for connection. Whether it’s your first queer event or your hundredth, you’ll be surrounded by a community that gets it. From the moment you arrive, there’ll be friendly faces, welcoming vibes, and plenty of chances to mingle, and connect. Coven is about belonging – and there’s a place here for you.

Coven Kaupapa
For queer women and gender minorities, spaces like this are rare, vital, and sometimes, life-changing. In a world that constantly centers cishet norms, Coven offers a space where we are the default – where you can fully show up as yourself, be seen, celebrated and surrounded by YOUR community.

For many in our Coven, this is one of the only opportunities we feel comfortable enough to experience nightlife free from the male gaze, tokenism, fear, or the need to shrink ourselves to fit in. It’s a space where sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people aren’t just welcomed – we are centered. It’s for those who are often pushed to the margins, who rarely feel represented in “inclusive” spaces that still cater to the mainstream.

This night exists because we need it – and because we create it, together.

Accessibility
This event is located on the ground floor. Have specific accessibility needs? Reach out directly to the Whisky & Wood team at hello@whiskyandwood.co.nz

If you made it this far... Good girl / Good they / Good boy / Good YOU!

description:
Decoding the Arts, Join us at the historic Inverlochy house in discovering and decoding the world of art history. Coffee & tea provided.

Art History is a study of visual arts across time and cultures. It involves analysing artworks to understand visual language in its social, historical, political context, values and human expressions. It helps us to develop critical thinking to interpret how visual culture impacts the society and identity.

The focus this term will be as follows:

The first month will cover briefly the Prehistoric, Ancient, Greco- Roman art followed by the Renaissance period, looking at the works of the great masters like Donatello, Ghiberti, Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Raphael, Albrecht Dürer, Jan van Eyck and Hieronymus Bosch.

In the second month we look at Baroque, Rococo, Romanticism briefly, and then study Modern movements like Impressionism, Surrealism, Expressionism & Cubism, looking at artists like Monet, Degas, Manet, Cezanne, Seurat, Van Gogh to name a few. We also hold discussions on Dali, Matisse, Kandinsky, Mondrian, Rothko, Pollock and end with Picasso, among others.

Recommended materials - writing utensil and notebook

Do It Yourself Framing, Bring along a painting and a suitable frame, either a cheapo from Briscoes or a good second hand frame. We will provide all the tools, process and materials to frame your piece of art.
It’s a practical course where you will learn to prepare the frame, cut with a knife, measure and cut a matt with the matt cutter.

You will walk away with your painting framed, ready to hang and some useful knowledge about framing ready for sale, exhibition standards, D rings, swing tags, acid free archival materials, tape, and how to hang a painting on the wall.

What’s included in this workshop:

- Demonstration steps to framing your work
- Assembling the tools you need
- Choosing and cleaning frames
- How to size and cut an acid free mat
- What sort of tapes to use for each task
- Various fixings for hanging and D-rings
- Replacing acid leaching materials with foam board
- Cutting techniques
- Making and attaching labels and swing tags
- How to photograph your art

This is a hands-on session where you will learn to cut card, cut a window in the matt board, present, secure, tape, screw in D-ring, tie knots etc. All materials will be provided including: knives, metal ruler, cutting board, crescent board for the mat, mat cutter, tape, d-ring, string.

What to bring along:
- your artwork to frame
- a suitable frame for the artwork A4 or smaller

description:
Dungeons & Dragons: Curse of Strahd Campaign - 12th January 2026, Dungeons & Dragons: Curse of Strahd Campaign - 12th January 2026
Outside the tavern, a fog lies across the town. The damp, cobbled pavement glistens as the lights of street lanterns dance across the slick stones. The night chills the bones and shivers the soul of anyone outside.

Yet inside these tavern walls the food is hearty, and the ale is warm and frothy. A fire blazes in the hearth, and the tavern is alive with the voices and laughter.

Suddenly, the tavern door swings open, and you all notice it at the same time. Framed by the lamp-lit fog, a form strides through the doorway. His brightly coloured clothes are draped in loose folds about him, and his hat hangs askew, hiding his eyes in shadows. Without hesitation, he walks up to your table and pulls from his tunic a sealed letter, addressed to all of you in beautiful flowing script. He drops the letter on the table and turns and leaves the tavern, vanishing into the fog.

‘Curse of Strahd’ is a D&D5E gothic horror campaign. It has everything you and your party needs to have a grand experience. It will take you to the mysterious village of Barovia, a realm surrounded by deadly fog and ruled by a wizard, the vampire Count Strahd von Zarovich, the master of Castle Ravenloft. ‘Curse of Strahd’ is a rich narrative story you are part of as it’s unfolding. It’s not just about fighting monsters and hunting for treasure in dungeons; there is a compelling story arc and a richly realized antagonist.

description:
Dungeons & Flagons - An All Ages Adventure, Are you an adult who really wants to introduce your kid to Dungeons & Dragons?
Or are you a kid who wishes your parents would play?
Or are you whānau who want to adventure together?
Then All Ages Dungeons & Flagons is for you.
Whether you’re a seasoned adventurer or you’ve never rolled a die in your life, this two-hour, beginner-friendly D&D experience at Titahi Bay’s own Beer Engine is for you.
Parents and kids can turn up together and be guided through a fast-paced adventure by a professional Dungeon Master. Choose your hero — a silver-tongued bard, a fire-flinging wizard, a sword-swinging fighter, a sneaky rogue, or something else entirely, with all characters, dice, and rules provided.
Parents, this isn’t a drop-off and run situation - you’re at the table too. There are a couple of reasons for that:
1. D&D is for the whole family and...
2. It’s at a bar (and who abandons their kids at a bar?!)
Expect laughs, ridiculous moments, and whānau bonding as you sling spells, swish swords, and roll dice together. And the tavern keeper will have special barbecue and butterbeer for sale for all ages feasting!
No prep. No pressure. Just a great location and a story you’ll still be talking about afterwards. All done in time for dinner!
The inaugural Dungeons and Flagons sold out in a week - so book fast, adventurer!
This is an all-ages event (although we’d suggest that kids under 10 might struggle) but anyone under 18 MUST be accompanied by the holder of an adult ticket. So you can’t just purchase a ticket for a child.
If you don’t have a kid but want to play afternoon D&D, that’s fine too. Just make sure you’re prepared to share a table with some folks who know what 6/7 is about, and that it’s not really cool to reference it anymore.

A freeform, drug- and alcohol-free dance experience where you move however your body wants. The music flows like a wave — starting slow, rising to ecstatic peaks, then softening into stillness. It’s therapeutic, uplifting, and a powerful way to connect with yourself and community.

With over 24 years behind the decks—including 8 years dedicated to Ecstatic Dance—Kimba crafts transformative spaces of joy, release, and connection. Originally from Auckland, she curated Alchemic Dance Floor events for 5 years, now co-runs the Ecstatic Dance Festival, and teaches Alchemic Ecstatic Dance DJ Trainings. She’s thrilled to share her magic and move with you on the dance floor!

Here at Ecstatic Dance Wellington, we believe in using a phat sound system with lots of bass for our dances. We will be bringing an ultra vibey and super bassy experience for you!

description:
F*ck the Small Talk: Wellington #10, Sign up here: https://luma.com/ftstwellington10
F*ck the Small Talk has traveled the world from Berlin, Melbourne, London, Lisbon, and Mexico City, to Lisbon and is now coming to Wellington!

WHAT'S THIS ABOUT?
FTST is a one-of-a-kind social experience where strangers come together for an afternoon of meaningful, fun, and deep conversation. It’s also just a different & cool way of meeting new people by getting a bit out of your comfort zone and skipping the small talk!
Join us for games, talks, and connections with friends you haven’t met yet. Join if you get annoyed after being asked what you do, where you are from, and how long you have been in Wellington every single time you meet someone. If you feel that there are better questions in life then this is the place for you.

HOW DOES IT WORK?
We start with a short & sweet intro talk followed by a few light-hearted group games to warm up. Don't worry, nothing too awkward! After that, we split you up into small groups and start with the conversation rounds (with 3-4 people). We'll have awesome question cards that will guide the flow of the conversation. You’ll never have to speak in public if you don’t want to!

HOW TO JOIN?
Take 2 minutes to fill out our form

https://luma.com/ftstwellington10
Our events are limited to 30 handpicked guests to ensure a cozy atmosphere. We prioritize a balance in gender and cultural diversity, making each gathering a unique blend of perspectives! If you're invited you'll receive an invite with a special link via our ticketing platform Luma

HOW MUCH IS IT?
The cost to attend is NZD 23 (early llama) - NZD 25 (general llama) and includes the following:
3 hours of facilitated and curated activities
Light snacks to keep the energy going (only if outdoors)
A space to meet new people in the least boring way possible
Supporting our mission to slowly eliminate small talk around the world
Also includes those pesky ticket fees!

WHERE IS IT?
We host our events in awesome cafes, rooftops, and bars across the city. We only reveal the location to ticket holders 24 hours before the event.

WHAT THEY SAY
“Great way to connect with people in a more meaningful way. Get to the heart of the matter, dive straight into what really counts!” - Matthias

“This is the kind of activity humanity needs every weekend. Thank you for all.” - Sonya

“F*ck the Small Talk changes the narrative from "Where are you from?" to "When was the last time you laughed uncontrollably?" and I think that's beautiful.” - Monika

“I loved F*ck the small talk, I was a little bit nervous at first but they are pros at making you feel comfortable with the rest of the group, the activities are really fun and I enjoyed every second (consider that the one who's saying this is very, very shy). Give it a try!” - Brenda

"it’s a wonderful experience, it’s like being a kid again, when you were at the park, playing with other kids, and just decided you were going to be best friends for the next hours. Maybe you’ll never see those kids again. But that hour was amazing because you both opened up and trusted each other." - Sara

“Lively, interesting, introspective, completely open and no judgement. Everyone that joined was ready for great conversation and helped with different perspectives. So much fun! I can't wait for the next one! “ - Yaz

Check out our 100+ Google reviews: https://goo.gl/maps/TpZy77bfPFkGoikn7

FAQ
• Can I come alone?
Of course, in fact, we encourage it! 99% of people do.

• I signed up but never got an invite. Why?
We usually get a high volume of sign-ups yet we like to keep it cozy & only about 30 people. We believe this is a good number to ensure an awesome experience! Please try again next time if do not receive an invite - no hard feelings

• Why do you charge?
We value our time and put a lot of love, planning, and effort into creating & designing these experiences.
This is our project/business and what we give to the world and we think everything should be a fair exchange! However, money should never be the reason for people not to attend. If you can’t afford it simply get in touch with us

• I'm digging this! Can I get involved somehow?
Sure thing, send us a message!

• Can I bring my cute dog/llama?
It depends on where the event is! Message us to make sure. But it's always a YES in our hearts.

• Can I get a refund if I can't make it?
Unfortunately, we do not offer refunds or ticket transfers to another event date if you cannot attend with a notice of less than 5 days notice. BUTTTT feel free to pass on your ticket to a friend, provided they also sign up for the form
--

𝘾𝙤𝙢𝙚 𝙘𝙪𝙧𝙞𝙤𝙪𝙨, 𝙡𝙚𝙖𝙫𝙚 𝙘𝙤𝙣𝙣𝙚𝙘𝙩𝙚𝙙.
* Only 30 spots available
* Location is only revealed to ticket holders!
* Age guide, 22-40 years old (only a reference, never a limit
)

This event is a no-phone experience. Keep them tucked in your pocket

We started in Berlin back in 2019 out our frustration of being asked 'where are you from?' 40 times in one week. Now there are chapters in 11 cities around the world including Mexico City, Zurich, Lisbon, London, Berlin and Vancouver.

--

description:
FEBRUARY: The Idiot by Fyodor Dostoevsky, We return to Russia for our long summer read! The group's first ever summer book was Anna Karenina and we read Dostoevsky's The Brothers Karamazov over the 2018/19 summer. (We were also due to discuss his novel Crime and Punishment, but that was set down for April 2020 and, well, the world had other plans…)
This year we read another of Fyodor Dostoevsky's masterworks: The Idiot, which was initially published as a serial in 1868-1869. Dostoevsky scholar Joseph Frank said The Idiot "is the most personal of all his major works, the book in which he embodies his most intimate, cherished, and sacred convictions".
The story revolves around Prince Lef Nicolaievitch Muishkin, a young man returning to Russia after spending several years in a Swiss sanatorium for epilepsy. Dostoevsky had set out to create a protagonist with "a truly beautiful soul" and to trace the fate of such an individual as he comes into contact with the brutal reality of contemporary society.
Photo: The Body of the Dead Christ in the Tomb by Hans Holbein, which features in the novel.
VENUE
We meet in the ‘Games Room’, The Library's private area overlooking Courtenay Place. After you enter the bar, head to your right (up the step) and through a smaller space with booths to the large carpeted space beyond.
SPREADSHEET OF BOOKS READ

description:
FULLY BOOKED - Family Shiny - Akatarawa Forest, Registrations open NOW
What to expect
This is a “Family Shiny” trip into the Akatarawa Forest.
Non members are welcome to join us but must register to obtain details of start time and location.
Vehicles must have a low ratio gearbox and must not be a 4wd car, station wagon or van, and if a soft top must have a roll cage.
Visitor Registration- $20.00 per driver
There is no trip fee for this trip however non-members pay a “Day Membership Fee” of $20. This is payable in Cash to the Trip Leader on the day.
The trip should be relatively easy as it needs to cater for people just starting out and all types of 4wd vehicles – but a good way to see if you want to get into 4wding and a chance to meet some of our club members (if you are unsure if your vehicle is suitable just ask).
No Dogs Allowed sorry
Once you have completed 3 Family Shinys you can join the club but can only participate in Family Shiny or Touring Class trips. Once you have also done a Training Day and had your vehicle inspected by one of our approved inspectors you can come along on our other more adventurous trips. To find out more on how to join our club go to https://ccvcwellington.wildapricot.org/page-1725861.
Like our Facebook page to find out about more trips and club nights.

description:
Feeding Frenzy Halloween Bar Crawl Wellington 2025, Feeding Frenzy Halloween Bar Crawl Wellington 2025
Packed dance floors, killer beats & spooky drinks. The frenzy hits Wellington Nov 1 — and you’re either in it or missing it.

About this Event


🩸🔥 FEEDING FRENZY HALLOWEEN BAR CRAWL – Wellington 2025 🔥🩸

When Halloween Saturday hits Wellington, the streets turn into a party jungle — and the Feeding Frenzy Halloween Bar Crawl is at the top of the food chain. Hundreds of costumed crawlers will be out in full force on Saturday, November 1st, 2025, bouncing from one high-energy bar to the next, chasing the best music, the best drinks, and the wildest crowds in the city.
This isn’t a night where you settle into one place — it’s a moving, breathing, full-costume swarm of energy. Expect packed dance floors, themed drinks that fit the season, and the kind of Halloween madness that only happens once a year.




WHAT’S IN STORE
🍹 Bars and clubs stocked with exclusive drink specials just for the crawl.
🎶 DJs pushing the energy with Halloween remixes, EDM, hip hop, and throwback anthems.
👻 Crowds dressed in everything from elaborate horror make-up to clever pop culture costumes.
📍 Venues chosen for atmosphere, music, and their ability to keep the party moving.


THE PLAN
The party starts at 7:30 PM at the first venue — grab your wristband and you’re in for the night. The feeding frenzy moves through multiple stops, all within walking distance, with each bar serving its own vibe and drink specials. By 11:30 PM, the entire crowd converges for a final blowout party that carries the night until 2 AM.

PARTICIPATING VENUES We’ll reveal the full lineup soon. Every location will be transformed for Halloween and serving themed drinks you won’t find on the menu any other night of the year.
📍 On event day, click the Crawl Map Link to see every participating bar, drink specials, and live music schedule.


🩸 Whether you’re a vampire, witch, demon, or something completely unexplainable, this is your night to roam the city in full costume and let loose with a crowd just as wild as you are.



🚨 Tickets: Starting at $15 — lock yours in now before they’re gone.

Your Ticket Includes:
🎟️ Entry to all participating bars and clubs in Wellington
🚫 No cover charges
📱 Digital crawl map access
🎵 DJs & entertainment at every venue
🍹 Exclusive Halloween drink specials

Age Requirement
Entry is strictly 18+. You must show a valid government-issued photo ID to participate. No exceptions will be made.
Wristbands
Your wristband is your pass for entry. Present your ticket or QR code at the check-in location to receive it. Wristbands must be worn throughout the night to access participating venues. If you miss the pickup window listed on the crawl map, you forfeit your access — no wristband means no entry. Lost or unclaimed wristbands cannot be replaced.
Tickets & Refunds
All sales are final. Tickets cannot be refunded, transferred, or exchanged. If the crawl is canceled without being rescheduled, the base ticket price (minus fees) will be automatically refunded. Participating venues, event hours, and drink specials may be adjusted at any time without advance notice.
Venue Entry
Each participating location has the right to refuse service or entry for reasons including intoxication, violation of dress code, inappropriate conduct, or venue capacity. If denied entry at one stop, you may visit another participating venue. No refunds will be issued under these circumstances.
Capacity & Access
Venues may reach capacity at peak times. Admission is not guaranteed once a venue is full. Late arrivals may face lines or delays. Refunds will not be issued for wait times or inability to enter specific venues.
Self-Guided Crawl
This is a self-directed event. There is no host leading the group. Use the DIGITAL CRAWL MAP LINK to navigate between stops.
Venue Awareness
Not all bar staff may know about crawl logistics. If confusion arises, contact the event representative listed on the crawl map. If that venue cannot accommodate you, move on to another open crawl location.
Drink Specials
Discounts and drink deals are set independently by each bar. They may change, sell out, or be discontinued without notice.
Event Timing
Tickets are valid only during official crawl hours listed on the digital map. Showing up early, late, or outside of the crawl schedule does not guarantee entry.
Security
All venues will conduct their own security screening. A wristband does not bypass checks.
Costumes
Costumes must be safe and respectful. Props resembling weapons or offensive attire will result in denial of entry without refund.
Notifications
To stay updated, sign up for text alerts. These will notify you of venue changes or movement times during the crawl.
Conduct
Respect staff, other attendees, and venues. Disorderly behavior, property damage, or harassment will result in immediate removal without refund.
Liability Waiver
By purchasing a ticket, you acknowledge and accept that participation carries risks. You voluntarily assume all dangers, including but not limited to: accidents, personal injury, illness, disability, property damage, theft, alcohol-related incidents, interactions with other participants, and even serious injury or death.
You, and anyone acting on your behalf, hereby release and discharge Events Per Se, its affiliates, sponsors, contractors, employees, volunteers, and participating venues from any liability for losses, claims, or damages — whether due to negligence, gross negligence, breach of duty, or any other cause — that may occur before, during, or after the crawl.
You further agree to indemnify and hold harmless all released parties against any claims, costs, or expenses (including legal fees) that arise as a result of your actions during the event.
By attending, you confirm you have read and understood this waiver, that you are participating voluntarily, and that this agreement is intended to be as broad as allowed by law.
Event Continuity
The crawl will run rain or shine. Venues may change last minute. Always check your email and the digital crawl map for updates.
Acknowledgment
Purchase of a ticket signifies full acceptance of these disclaimers, terms, and conditions. You accept complete responsibility for your participation.

description:
Field Trip Presents - Paws & Pours (Wellington), We’re turning the park into one giant, dog‑friendly, Field Trip playground.
Paws & Pours is a DJ‑led, social day out where dogs, their humans (and humans that just like dogs) come together for music, beers and sunshine. It's Giant Picnic vibes, but with paws on the grass.
Expect DJs with live sax, styled chill zones, food trucks, dog bakery, cocktails, beers AND games for you and your doggo.
Professional dog trainers and handlers will be on site throughout the day to monitor behaviour and support dog safety. The event is designed to accommodate a range of dog temperaments, with space to move, pause or opt out as needed.
Add in a pet photographer, groomer, pop‑up bars, lawn games and a best‑dressed dog costume competition, and you’ve got a seriously good day out.
This is Field Trip, just a little cuter.
What’s Included
DJs and live music throughout the day
Pop‑up bars with cocktails, wine, beer and non‑alcoholic options
Styled picnic lounges, umbrellas and chill zones
Dog enrichment toys and play areas
Dog treat stations
On‑site dog trainers supporting safety and behaviour
Pet photographer pop‑up
Dog groomer pop‑up
Best‑dressed dog costume competition
Plenty of space to relax, roam and socialise
Dog Safety & Welfare Policy
Dog safety and responsible ownership are taken seriously at this event. Use your common sense. If your dog is not social, comfortable in busy environments, or around other dogs and people, this event will not be suitable.
Dogs must be friendly, social and comfortable around other dogs and people
Owners are responsible for their dog’s behaviour at all times, all dogs must remain under owner control
All dogs must be fully vaccinated
Dogs over 8 months of age must be spayed or neutered
Leads are required on arrival and departure, with designated off‑lead play zones where appropriate
Professional dog trainers and handlers will be present throughout the event to monitor behaviour and step in where required
Dogs showing signs of distress, aggression or overstimulation may be asked to take a break or leave the event
Failure to follow guidance from trainers or event staff may result in removal from the event.
FAQs
Do dogs need to be on a lead?
Yes. All dogs must be on lead at all times, except in clearly designated off-lead areas.
Will there be water and shade for dogs?
But of course. There will be water stations and shaded chill zones available throughout the site.
Are puppies allowed?
Puppies are welcome if fully vaccinated and comfortable in social settings. All dogs over 8 months must be spayed or neutered.
Can children attend?
Children are welcome if accompanied by a parent or legal guardian. They don't need a ticket. Please make sure they know not to pet dogs that aren't theirs without permission

Double the nights, double the chaos. Dance, crawl & party across Wellington Halloween weekend. DJs, shots & finales ‘til 2AM!

About this Event


Fright Night + Screams & Shots Weekend Pass – Wellington 2025 👻🎧
Halloween weekend is built for the bold — and this pass is your all-access ticket.
The Fright Night + Screams & Shots Weekend Pass gets you into both nights of the city’s most electrifying Halloween parties. Friday kicks off with Fright Night, a citywide takeover where DJs, costumes, and neon lights set the stage. Saturday keeps the momentum alive with Screams & Shots, a high-voltage crawl of bars and clubs serving Halloween-themed shooters and nonstop beats.
This isn’t just a bar crawl — it’s a two-night music-fueled Halloween marathon. Think of it as your festival pass to the city’s nightlife: two different lineups, two massive finales, one unforgettable weekend.




WHY GRAB THE WEEKEND PASS?
⚡ Two Nights, One Wristband – Access to both Friday & Saturday events.
🎶 Festival-Level Energy – Back-to-back parties with DJs mixing EDM, hip hop, and Halloween remixes.

📍 Multiple Venues – 4+ stops each night, all within walking distance, ending in a huge late-night finale.


HALLOWEEN CRAWL INSTRUCTIONS
Check-In: Get your weekend wristband at the starting venue (7:30–10:30 PM each night).
Crawl the Clubs: Move between participating venues at your own pace from 8:30–11:30 PM.
Finale Blowout: Meet the full crowd at the closing party from 11:30 PM–2 AM.


YOUR WEEKEND PASS INCLUDES

PARTICIPATING VENUES

👻 Whether you’re chasing bass drops, showing off your costume on packed dance floors, or rallying your crew for back-to-back nights out, the Weekend Pass is your way to experience Halloween without limits.

18 + EVENT / GOVERNMENT ISSUED ID REQUIRED

Check Venue Schedule: Each venue’s crawl time is listed in the Digital Bar List. Wristbands and drink specials are valid only during these scheduled times.

Hailing from Italy and now rooted in Wellington’s vibrant scene, Not My Sister quickly burst onto Aotearoa’s dance floors and has been on a rapid rise ever since. She’s lit up festivals like Twisted Frequency, Kiwiburn, Earthbeat, CubaDupa, Taniwha’s Den and Arkadien and supported international acts including KC Lights.
She currently holds a radio residency on Wellington’s iconic Radio Active, where her show dives deep into house and underground sounds.
Heavily influenced by funk and disco, and driven by a love for vocals, groove and infectious pulse of 90s House, Not My Sister delivers high-energy, uplifting sets that weave together melodic basslines with soulful, tech and deep house sounds. NOT MY SISTER
Not My Sister is a house music DJ born and raised in a little town in the north of Italy. Now based in Wellington, she started this project in 2024, and recently she has been lighting up dance floors across New Zealand, you may have already come across her sets at Twisted Frequency, Kiwiburn, Earthbeat, Cuba Dupa, Arkadien and other events across the country. From the vibrant streets of Wellington, Libby's fascination with music began at an early age with the smooth sultry
sounds of the clarinet and piano. Fast forward to her 20s where she stumbled into the hypnotic world of techno in
Berlin and a passion for 4/4 was ignited.
With a deep appreciation for the power of music to transform, Libby finds the greatest joy on a dance floor, where
the magic of music brings people together and gives us the freedom to be ourselves. Her sets are filled with

Originally from Bristol, UK, Ben was immersed in soundsystem culture from an early age. He started collecting vinyl in his teens and developed a passion for the heavier side of electronic music. With his formative years spent mixing vinyl, studying African percussion and playing drums and recording for rock/rap group Band of Crooks, he moved on to play with some of the best underground DJ's, producers and musicians in Aotearoa, Australia and UK. Ben has played a myriad of parties and events including Newtown Festival, Cuba Dupa, Kiwi Burn, Little Monsters, Insomnia, Toots Suite Festival (Salmonella Dub, Laughton Kora, Pheonix Foundation), Breakaway Magical Doof Bus (Paige Julia, Y, Sorchalula,Young Gho$t, House MD), Cuba Dupa, Sydney Rd Street Festival (Melbourne), Cafe Blue (UK), Castros (UK).

Always armed with bags of bass heavy treats expect a selection of new, classic and surprise music to help you release your spirit into the world.

Gala 2026 Women's Support Motueka, Overview

An inspiring gala with curated art and experiences, raising funds for support services and family violence prevention in our community.

One Night. One Cause. Lasting Impact.
Join us for an inspiring evening of connection and purpose; all in support of building a safer, stronger community for wāhine and whānau.


The Women’s Support Motueka Gala is a special fundraising event dedicated to strengthening our prevention work alongside our essential support services. Every day, we walk alongside women and whānau navigating the impacts of family violence. At the same time, we are deeply committed to creating change before harm occurs; through education, community awareness, and early intervention.

Enjoy a beautiful evening featuring the auction of a range of experiences and curated art, with contributions from generous businesses and talented local artists that reflect the richness and spirit of our region.

All funds raised will support Women’s Support Motueka to continue providing free, confidential services; including advocacy, counselling, and support for healing, while also growing our prevention efforts such as education workshops, and our youth outreach campaign focused on building healthy relationships from an early age.

This is more than a night out. It is an opportunity to stand alongside our community, and to be part of creating lasting change.

description:
Gardens of Aotearoa with Xanthe White, Join Xanthe White for an evening exploring the beautiful gardens her studio has designed around New Zealand. One of the country’s leading landscape designers and a Chelsea Flower Show award winner, Xanthe has worked for nearly three decades on projects ranging from private gardens to larger community spaces, both here and overseas.

Known for her thoughtful, place-based approach that connects people with the natural world, she’ll share a selection of the studio's projects - from coastal and rural sites to urban gardens, including Wellington - and talk through how different climates, conditions, and clients shape each design.

As a relaxed and engaging look at how gardens evolve from their setting, there will be plenty of ideas to take back to your own garden as well as a delicious supper, cash raffles for some fantastic prizes, and signed copies of Xanthe’s newly revised book The Natural Garden for sale at a special price of $50.

Glass Bead-Making Taster - Spring Session!, Join us for this fabulous introduction to working with colourful molten glass at the Winter Special Price!

This class is a great way for absolute beginners to get a taste of working with glass to produce beautiful beads that can be used in a myriad of ways, including making a unique gift for your loved one (or yourself!).

As one of the earliest forms of human adornment, beads have long functioned as a way to express individuality, and what better way to do that than to learn to make your own unique beads?

Students are shown correct lampworking techniques to produce several decorative beads in just 3 hours! How many beads you make is up to you; some students make up to 10 while others make fewer using trickier techniques.

Kids over 12 (or so) are welcome to take the class, but anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

description:
Glow in the Dark Paint Party - A Glowy Night, Ultra violet lights and neon nights in Wellington. Prepare to experience Paintvine like you’ve never experienced it before – in the dark!

Paintvine After Dark is New Zealand’s original glow in the dark paint party – a completely unique night out where creativity, neon paint, and UV lights come together for an unforgettable experience. Watch your artwork come to life as fluorescent colours glow under the lights and your canvas transforms before your eyes.

Our artist guides you step-by-step, so absolutely no art experience is needed. Whether you’re planning a date night, organising a catch-up with friends, or just keen to try something different, Paintvine After Dark is all about good vibes, glowing paint, and outrageous fun from start to finish.

It’s part art class, part neon party, and absolute fun! Who knew you could have so much fun in the dark?

Drinks: No drinks are included in the ticket price, but drinks are available for purchase.

Food: A delicious menu will be available to purchase throughout the event.

What is Paintvine?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality canvas, neon acrylic paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit. All our events are in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip as you create! At the end of the night you will leave with your own fluro painting and a fun memory to go with it.

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website ⇒ paintvine.co.nz

On Friday, October 31st, 2025, the Halloween Nightlife Crawl brings you through a curated mix of Wellington’s top bars, lounges, and clubs. One ticket gives you access to 4+ venues, exclusive Halloween drink specials, and a night full of music and costumes across the city.

Self-Guided Experience

Drink Specials
