Haunted Halloween Weekend Pass 2025 – Wellington, Haunted Halloween Weekend Pass 2025 – Wellington
Two nights, one ticket, endless Halloween chaos in Wellington. Join both crawls with drinks, music, and costume madness.

About this Event


🎃🍺 Halloween Madness Weekend Pass 2025 – Wellington 🎃🍺

Two nights of crawls. One ticket. Zero excuses.
Halloween in Wellington isn’t just one party — it’s a whole weekend. With the Halloween Madness Weekend Pass, you’ll unlock access to two epic bar crawls:
Friday, October 31st → Haunted Halloween Bar Crawl
Saturday, November 1st → Beer & Spirits: Halloween Booze Crawl

Double the venues, double the specials, double the fun. Whether you’re into pumpkin brews, tequila shots, or just want an excuse to rock your scariest (or funniest) costume twice, this pass is your best deal for Halloween weekend.




WHAT’S INCLUDED
✔️ Entry to both Friday & Saturday night crawls
✔️ No cover charges at participating bars & clubs
✔️ Crawl-only drink deals at every stop
✔️ Digital crawl map to guide your night
✔️ DJs, themed parties, and Halloween vibes until 2 AM
✔️ Two big finale parties — one each night


HOW THE WEEKEND FLOWS
👉 Wristband Pickup: Check in between 7:30–10:30 PM each night at the opening venue to collect your pass.
👉 Bar Hopping: From 8:30–11:30 PM, explore multiple walkable venues — pubs, clubs, and breweries — all offering specials.
👉 The Last Stop: Each crawl closes at a featured nightclub from 11:30 PM–2:00 AM with DJs and dance floors packed.




WEEKEND VIBE
👻 Costumes aren’t required but highly encouraged — expect the streets to be packed with zombies, witches, superheroes, and some of the funniest DIY outfits you’ll see all year.
⚡ Early bird tickets start at just $25 for the full weekend. Prices rise as Halloween gets closer — secure your spot now.


PARTICIPATING VENUES
The full lineup of bars and clubs will be released closer to the event. Expect high-energy DJs, themed rooms, and Halloween drink specials at every stop.




⚠️ EVENT RULES & DISCLAIMER

ENTRY REQUIREMENTS
18+ Only: All guests must be 18 years or older with a valid government-issued photo ID. No exceptions.
Wristbands Required: Your wristband is your ticket. Present your Eventbrite ticket/QR code at check-in to claim it. Wristbands must be worn the entire night for access to crawl venues. If you miss the pickup window (before 10:30 PM at the listed check-in), you forfeit entry.


CRAWL GUIDELINES
On-Time Check-In: Arrive during designated hours (7:30–10:30 PM). Late arrivals cannot be accommodated.
Proxy Pickup: If you can’t make it, you may authorize a friend to collect your wristband.
Venue Timing: Specials and entry are only valid during the timeframes listed on the Digital Bar List.
Day-Of Updates: Always check the Digital Crawl Map on event day for the latest venue info, changes, or closures.
Self-Guided Crawl: No hosts will lead groups. Use the crawl map to navigate between bars.
Venue Capacity: If a location is full, you may have to wait. Access is not guaranteed at every bar.


VENUE POLICIES
Right to Refuse: Venues may deny entry or remove anyone due to intoxication, dress code violations, offensive costumes, or inappropriate behavior.
Security Checks: Wristbands do not exempt you from ID or bag checks. Standard venue security applies.
Drink Specials: Offered at the discretion of participating bars; they may change or end without notice.
Venue Awareness: If staff aren’t aware of the crawl, contact the rep listed on the crawl map. If unavailable, proceed to another participating venue.


TICKET & EVENT TERMS
All Sales Final: No refunds, exchanges, or transfers. If the event is canceled outright (without reschedule), refunds excluding fees will be processed automatically.
Rain or Shine: Crawl will proceed regardless of weather. Venues and lineup are subject to change.
Late / Wrong Venue: Tickets are valid only during scheduled crawl hours. No refunds for late arrivals or showing up at the wrong check-in.
Costume Policy: No weapons or weapon-like props. Offensive costumes are prohibited and may result in denied entry.


LIABILITY WAIVER
By purchasing a ticket, you acknowledge that participation is at your own risk. Risks include but are not limited to: injury, illness, property damage, theft, accidents, alcohol-related incidents, or death.
You hereby release, waive, and discharge Events Per Se, its owners, staff, contractors, sponsors, affiliates, and participating venues from all claims or liability, whether caused by negligence or otherwise, for any injury, loss, illness, or death occurring before, during, or after the event.
You further agree to indemnify and hold harmless Events Per Se and all released parties from any expenses, claims, or legal costs arising from your actions during the crawl.
By attending, you confirm you’ve read, understood, and agreed to these terms in full.

Party all weekend in Wellington! The Haunted Hop & Halloween Bar Crawl Weekend Pass gets you into the best bars on Oct 31 & Nov 1.

About this Event






👻🎃Haunted Hop + Halloween Bar Crawl Weekend Pass – Wellington 2025 👻🎃
Two nights. One ticket. The ultimate Halloween takeover. The Weekend Pass gives you entry to both of Wellington’s biggest Halloween crawls — the Haunted Hop Bar Crawl on Friday, October 31st, and the Halloween Bar Crawl on Saturday, November 1st. Back-to-back nights of costumes, cocktails, and chaos, all across the Wellington’s hottest bars and nightclubs.
Friday kicks off with the Haunted Hop, a massive crawl where costumed partygoers pack the streets and every venue becomes a Halloween hotspot. Saturday turns up the volume with the Halloween Bar Crawl, bringing out DJs, dance floors, and spooky specials to close out the weekend in style.
Why settle for one night when you can crawl through both?





WEEKEND PASS HIGHLIGHTS
🎟️ Two Crawls, One Wristband – Admission to both Friday + Saturday events.
🎶 Live Music & DJs – Halloween hits, party anthems, and dance-floor energy all weekend.
🍸 Exclusive Drink Specials – Spooky cocktails, eerie shots, and bar-only deals.
👻 Costumes Everywhere – From scary to sexy to over-the-top — your outfit gets two nights to shine.
📍 Multiple Venues Each Night – 4+ bars and clubs, all within walking distance.



HOW IT WORKS
1️⃣ Check-In: Collect your weekend wristband at the designated starting venue (7:30–10:30 PM, both nights).
2️⃣ Crawl the City: Explore participating bars and clubs between 8:30–11:30 PM at your own pace.
3️⃣ Final Party: Join the crowd at the closing venue from 11:30 PM–2 AM for the ultimate send-off.





WHAT’S INCLUDED
🎟️ Admission to both Friday + Saturday crawls
🚫 No cover charges at any participating venues
📱 Digital crawl maps for both nights
🎶 DJs & live music at every stop
🍹 Themed drink and shot specials
🕺 Huge closing parties each night



PARTICIPATING VENUES
The full lineup of bars and nightclubs will be revealed closer to the event. Each venue offers its own Halloween theme, entertainment, and drink specials for crawl guests.


🎃 Hundreds of Halloween lovers, back-to-back nights, and the best nightlife Wellington has to offer. Whether you’re creeping through the Haunted Hop on Friday or shutting it down at Saturday’s finale, the Weekend Pass is your ticket to experience it all.
🚨 Early bird passes start at just $25. Lock in your plans now before prices rise.



18+ EVENT / GOVERNMENT ISSUED ID REQUIRED


TIPS FOR OUR CRAWL
Pick Up Wristbands On Time: Collect your wristband(s) during the designated check-in time at the scheduled location before 10:30 PM. Late arrivals will not be accommodated — no wristband, no entry.
Assign a Proxy if Needed: Can’t make check-in? Have a friend pick up your wristband for you so you don’t miss out.
Check Venue Schedule: Each venue’s crawl time is listed in the Digital Bar List. Wristbands and drink specials are valid only during these scheduled times.
Day-Of Updates: Review the Digital Crawl Map on the morning of the event for any last-minute changes or venue updates.

Wristbands: Your wristband is your key to entry. You must present your ticket or QR code at check-in to receive your wristband. Wristbands must be worn at all times to access participating bars and venues. Wristband pickup location and time are listed on the crawl map. If you do not pick up your wristband at the designated location and time, it may not be available, and you will not be able to access crawl venues. No wristband, no entry.
Ticket Policy: All sales are final—no refunds, exchanges, or transfers. In case of event cancellation without a rescheduled date, a refund (excluding fees) will be automatically issued. Event lineup, venues, and specials are subject to change without notice.
Admission & Venue Rights: Participating venues reserve the right to refuse service or entry to any attendee based on intoxication, dress code, inappropriate behaviour, or venue capacity. If refused entry at one venue, you may visit alternative crawl venues available at that time. No refunds will be given if you are denied entry for any of these reasons.

There is no guarantee of immediate access or entry to any specific venue once capacity is reached, and no refunds will be provided due to waiting times or access issues.
Self-Guided Crawl: This is a self-guided event with no host leading the group. You must use the digital crawl map to navigate between venues.

If you cannot reach them, consider that venue unavailable and proceed to an alternative crawl venue open at that time. Nightlife venues may reach capacity or close early, and not all staff members may be aware of the crawl.

Event Time Restrictions: Your ticket is valid only for crawl venues during the scheduled crawl times listed on the crawl map. It is not valid for entry outside these times. If you arrive late or at the wrong venue, refunds will not be issued.
Security Checks: Wristbands do not entitle you to skip venue security checks. All attendees must comply with security screening before entry.
Costume Policy: Do not wear costumes that include items which could be considered or used as weapons. Highly offensive costumes are not tolerated and may result in denial of entry without refund.

The participating bars reserve the right to refuse entry or remove attendees for inappropriate behaviour at any time.
Liability Waiver: By purchasing a ticket and participating in the crawl, you understand and agree that you are attending entirely at your own risk. You acknowledge that you have read and understood this waiver, that you are participating voluntarily, and that this waiver is intended to be as broad and inclusive as permitted by applicable law.

description:
Heartland Flyer, Heartland Flyer
Travel with Steam Incorporated north from Kapiti via the spectacular Manawatu Gorge to Woodville for an easy day out. Picking up along the way from Paekakariki, Paraparaumu, Waikanae, Otaki, and Levin, our destination today is Woodville. To get there, we travel through the famous Manawatu Gorge. Now only accessible via rail, you get a unique perspective of the monumental slips which closed the Gorge to road traffic from 2017.

At Woodville, sample the delights of the restored 1960s era station whilst our train is prepared for the run back down the coast. Meridian’s Te Apiti wind farm can also be seen from the station, occupying 1,150ha of land, with enough sustainable renewable energy to power 45,000 kiwi homes.

Fares
Adult (12+yrs) - $139
Child (3-12yrs) - $89
Infant (0-2yrs) - Free

Tickets available at steaminc.org.nz/book-train-trip/heartland-flyer/
label: Hobbies & Interests

description:
Heartland Flyer, Travel behind steam with Steam Incorporated on a special day excursion to Woodville via the spectacular Manawatū Gorge, hauled by one of our majestic coal-fired steam locomotives.
Departing from Paekākāriki and picking up at Paraparaumu, Waikanae, Ōtaki, Levin, and Palmerston North, this journey takes you through a landscape normally hidden from view. With the Gorge road closed since 2017, rail passengers now enjoy the only way to experience this historic route and witness the dramatic slips that reshaped the valley.
At Woodville, step back in time at the restored 1960s-era station while the locomotive prepares for the return journey to Kāpiti. Look out across the ranges and you’ll also spot Meridian’s Te Āpiti Wind Farm, spanning 1,150 hectares and producing enough clean energy to power around 45,000 New Zealand homes.
Our Lounge Car, offering a selection of cool beverages, tea/coffee and some light snacks and food options will be open throughout the day. Please bring cash as the EFTPOS will be in and out of service and may not be available during parts of the trip due to remote locations. All alcohol must be consumed on board, no alcohol is to leave the train. BYO is prohibited. On board services are limited and while stock lasts!
Enjoy a relaxed day out to beat the Autumn blues, and enjoy a day onboard Steam Incorporated's heritage train.
Fares
Departing Paekakariki/Paraparaumu/Waikanae/Otaki/Levin
Adult 13+ yrs - $139
Child 2-12yrs - $99
Departing Palmerston North
Family Pass - $199
Adult 13+ yrs - $69
Child 2-12yrs - $49
Infants under 2 travel free of charge, provided they are on the knee of a full fare paying adult.

Hiwinui Sunflower Field Open Day, Hiwinui Sunflower Field Open Day
We’re thrilled to welcome you back for our 2026 Sunflower Season 🌻
A breathtaking summer experience just 10 minutes from Palmerston North and Feilding. Hiwinui Sunflower Field is a rare and unforgettable destination open for a limited time only.


🌻 ENTRY (CASH ONLY)
🚫 NO EFTPOS facilities on site
• Adults (13 years +): $10
• Children under 13 years: FREE

🌻 PICK YOUR OWN SUNFLOWERS
• Bring your own secateurs or hire for $15 (includes 4 stems)
• $3 per stem
• $1 from every bloom donated to Arohanui Hospice 💛

🌿 EXTRA ACTIVITIES
• Wander our walking and flower track – a brand new field design for 2026
• Stunning photo opportunities & new photo props
• Plenty for the kids including:
– Giant Swing
– Scavenger Hunt
– Lawn Games
• Meet the farm animals: Dior the pony and Poppy & Rambo the pet sheep
• Fonterra Barrel Train Rides – (Gold coin donation)
• Face Painting – (Extra charge $5 per person)
• Extended picnic area with our Hamptons marquee for shade and shelter
• Food Trucks (opening weekend & Food Truck Fridays)
• Real Fruit Ice Cream (opening weekend & Food Truck Fridays)

🕒 OPENING HOURS
📅 Saturday 24 & Sunday 25 January
⏰ 10:00am – 4:00pm

🌻 PRIVATE FIELD HIRE
The sunflower field is available for private hire from 5:30pm – 8:30pm.
Limited spaces available — bookings must be made directly.

📍 LOCATION & PARKING
465 Ashhurst Road, Palmerston North
• Located off the main road — please indicate well in advance
• Follow signage to the main car park
• 🚫 Do not enter via the main entrance of Hiwinui Country Estate
(This is EXIT ONLY)

⚠️ HEALTH & SAFETY
As we are a working farm, please note:
• Leave animals at home (except service dogs)
• Wear suitable footwear — tracks may be uneven
• There are bees and pollen in the field — bring medication if required
• Basic first aid is available at the site office

🌻 We can’t wait to welcome you for another unforgettable sunflower season at Hiwinui

description:
House Candle Holder Clay Workshop, Make a magical clay house which can be used with real or fake candles. We will use my hand drawn templates, slab building and modelling techniques, and imprint with fabrics to produce stunning clear glazed cream houses. This class also includes the option of adding some dashes of colour using underglazes and coloured slips. Add birds, cats, window boxes or whatever inspires to your creation. By themselves they are gorgeous, and when they have a candle inside, they bring warmth and magic to a space.

The house size is approximately 13cm x 7cm x 10cm or 10cm x 6cm x 9cm. If time allows and you're in the flow, extra houses can be made for $40 per house.

Price is $130 per person, which includes all materials, glaze and double firings.

description:
Ice Rink, Wellington Ice Rink at Queens Wharf

Paradice EVENTS returns to Wellington this winter with the Wellington Ice Rink at Queens Wharf. Located on Wellington’s waterfront, the pop-up ice rink transforms Queens Wharf into a seasonal skating destination for visitors of all ages.

Now in its seventh year in Wellington, the event offers a winter skating experience in the heart of the city, featuring music, lighting effects, and sessions suitable for both experienced skaters and first-time visitors.

The rink measures 30 metres by 15 metres and provides approximately 400 pairs of ice skates for hire.
Throughout the season, a range of themed sessions will be held, including:
• Student Wednesdays – Midweek skating sessions with student-focused pricing
• Skate & Date Thursdays – Evening sessions with music and ambient lighting
• Groovy Fridays – Top 40 music sessions to start the weekend

Wellington Ice Rink is suitable for families, groups, students, corporate outings, and casual visitors looking for a winter activity on the waterfront.


Whether visiting for a daytime skate or an evening session under the lights, Wellington Ice Rink offers a seasonal experience in one of the city’s most iconic locations.

Wellington
20 June – 19 July
Location: Queens Wharf
10 am – 10 pm daily
Ice Skating Prices
Adults $26 (13 years plus)
Children $21 (5-12 years)
Pre schoolers $16 (3 and 4 year olds)
Family pass $70
Student night Wednesday 7pm – 10pm $18 Student ID required
Please note: all skaters are required to wear a helmet or Paradice safety approved headband when skating.

Risk Disclosure
Please bear in mind that ice skating and ice sliding is an extreme sport which can result in harm or injury. The risks and hazards include, but are not limited to tripping, falling, collisions and cold exposure. By participating in the activities offered by the Wairakei Estate Ice Rink and MB Century Ice Slide you acknowledge these risks could result in injury and you skate/slide at your own risk.

Keep Yourself Safe
The wearing of a helmet or Paradice approved safety headband is compulsory and we recommend the wearing of gloves. Children 6 years and under only have the option of wearing a helmet not the safety headband. Please follow our rink rules and the advice of staff
Please note minimum age for ice skating is 3 years old.

Tickets are available inside the rink and online www.paradiceevents.co.nz
For more information

description:
Inner Marlborough Sounds Kayak Trip, Hi this is a trip through the Inner Marlborough Sounds, suitable for beginners who have gone to at least one SKISL and be OK with rescues. The focus is on camping, coffee, and having a fun time with relatively short kayaking times on the water.
The schedule for Wellingtonians is: on the Thursday 29th Ferry over to Picton, in at 12:30, launch from Picton beach head over to Kumoto, tents up, Friday - paddle around the Bay of Many Coves, stop for coffee / lunch / chips / shower at Punga Cove, stay at Camp Bay. Maybe a quick trip over to Bumine Island with empty boats. Saturday night at Ratimira for camping / snoozing. Sunday - up early, on water at 8am, paddle back to Picton in by 12, lunch, on 1pm sailing. So 4 days with Blumine as an optional paddle, mostly shortish trips. We might shift the plan around depending on the weather, but that sets out the general plan.
For the ferry you need to book your own tickets and I would urge you to get your ferry tickets now as they go fast. If you are concerned about the weather get the fully refundable tickets. When you buy your ticket select the "kayak" option. Any questions ask them in the comments below.

description:
Jewellery-making In 8 Weeks for Beginners, This class is beginner level only, with each student following the class project.

It starts Tue 25 August and runs for 8 weeks ill Tue 13 October, 5.30pm - 8pm.

Our popular weeknight classes are the best way for beginners to get into jewellery-making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

The stone-setting process teaches you many fundamental techniques in one project!

We start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering.

Then we move on to making a practice ring set with a Cabochon stone (a cabochon has a flat bottom and a smooth, domed top) in a Bezel Setting.

As you work through your practice ring and setting, you can move on to working in silver and produce another ring with a cabochon stone that you really love. This way, you will learn the basics as you go on your practice ring, before taking the next step in costly silver.

This class has all materials included in the class fee!

Each student receives a carefully curated materials pack including copper or brass, sterling and fine silver for your ring-making projects, as well as two stones from our supply so you get a good stone for your level of experience.

We have loads of gorgeous stones of a range of colours, and they are all appropriate for beginner settings.

Our booking system asks for payment to be made via credit card, Afterpay or PayPal on booking. If you do not have access to these payment methods or need to pay your course fee over time, please email us to arrange this ;)
label: Classes & Workshops

description:
Jewellery-making On Thursdays, 8-week Block, Level 2+, Our popular weeknight block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. This class will be held at our new waterfront location, Market Lane!

The course starts on Thursday 27 August and runs for 8 weeks till Thursday 15 October, 5.30pm-8pm.

This class is designed for students who already have some skills and are ready to develop their craftsmanship in a lively, warm, and supportive environment. Guided by our highly skilled tutors, you’ll build confidence, refine your techniques, and gain the satisfaction of making jewellery that reflects your personal style.

If you’re brand new to jewellery making, we recommend beginning with our Tuesday Evening 8-Week Beginners’ Block, which gives a solid foundation in essential techniques before moving on to this class.

At Level 2, the focus is on precision and technique. Students explore the art of chain making, a classic jewellery making project that develops fine soldering skills and accuracy in construction. This project is an excellent way to build confidence with the torch and create a piece of jewellery that is both functional and beautiful. The finished chain can become a pendant, bracelet, or necklace, or you may choose to adapt it into a design of your own.

At Level 3 and above, the emphasis shifts toward creativity and design development. Students at this stage are encouraged to take on more complex projects, experiment with new and challenging techniques, and bring their own design ideas to life. With the guidance of our skilled and supportive tutors, you’ll learn how to push your skills further, problem-solve during the making process, and refine your eye for detail and design.

Evening classes are not just about the technical side of jewellery making - they are also a chance to slow down, enjoy the process, and be part of a creative community. Many students return term after term, finding the rhythm of regular making both mindful and rewarding.

Please note: this class does not include a materials allowance, giving you the flexibility to choose your own metals, stones, or other materials. You only pay for what you use, making it easier to customise your projects and work at your own pace.

Our booking system asks for full payment at the time of registration (via credit card, PayPal, or AfterPay). If you don’t have access to these options or would like to pay in instalments, please email us and we’ll happily arrange an alternative.

description:
Lavender & Flower Farm PYO, Your weekend escape starts at Lavender Magic surrounded by the calming scent of Lavender. As the evening cools, wander through rows of fragrant blooms and gather fresh flowers — the perfect gift for friends and family.

Nestled in a charming country garden, Lavender Magic offers breathtaking views of the Tararua Ranges, creating a stunning backdrop for relaxation and discovery. Whether you’re picking flowers, strolling among the lavender, or simply soaking in the peaceful atmosphere, this is the place to unwind and reconnect with nature.

Come experience the magic. Lavender Magic — where tranquility blossoms and the stars are brighter.

Lavender Magic is a Lavender farm and a Cut Flower Farm. It has about 5000 lavender plants and grows a range of cut flowers. In season you will find pockets roses, lilies, sunflowers, zinnias and dahlias. You can pick lavender and cut flowers!

Since 2007 Lavender Magic has won many awards for the quality of their lavender oil, which can be purchased on site along with balms, creams and sprays in the small farm shop.

We will provide you with everything you need. Cutting nips, rubber band and bucket. We will let you know which flowers are in season and available to cut.

description:
Lavender Magic Flower Farm - Pick your own Lavender, Snap the ultimate summer photo and come and enjoy the best of the Lavender Season from mid-December to mid-January, before the harvesting starts.

Early in the season we start picking English Lavender - short stem but beautifully scented and vibrant in colour. Then we pick the more traditional French Lavender. You can pick your own, take home to dry and enjoy the fragrance all year. Or just wander the garden.

There are rows of lavender and we have pockets of cut flowers nestled in our country garden with magnificent mountain views. The Tararua Ranges and foothills create a stunning backdrop to this romantic relaxing location. Wander through the garden and pick your favorite flowers or just sit and breathe. Ditch the city chaos for some quality time out, picking lavender flowers is relaxing.

Come alone, with a friend or friends to enjoy the experience with others or get a group of together.

At this Magic location you will tune into the sound of nature, see the butterflies flutter, listen to the bees buzz, the birds sing and the river flow.

What do you do?
- Pay on entry or book your on-line ticket (not really necessary)
- Take the scenic drive to Lavender Magic, approximately 75 minutes from Upper Hutt or Palmerston North, take the Mt Holdsworth turnoff from State Highway 2 just south of Masterton.
- Follow the purple signs that lead you to 61 Blakes Rd, Mt Holdsworth, Wairarapa
- When you are ready we will set you up with flower cutters
- We will let you know the cutting areas (which flowers we are cutting as they change throughout the season)
- You will pick a bunch of lavender or two or more!
- You will wander around the colourful, seasonal flowers and pick those if available. Like us on facebook and instagram for up to date details on what is available.
- You can create a bouquet, if available we will help.
- Visit the small lavender shop
- You can test the wonderful natural skincare products we will have for sale in our shop.

Other tips
Wear - Good footwear to explore the flower farm.
Wear - Sunglasses and slip, slop, slap if a sunny day as we get full sun.
Bring - A coffee, a treat or a picnic. BYO food is allowed. Or grab a coffee and something to eat from OUR PLACE CAFE who set up when available, check socials for details.
Bring - A camera to capture some of the magic and create memories.
A toilet is on site.

We accept cash and we have eftpos
Buying tickets online is not necessary, door sales are available.
$5 Entry 13 years and older, children 12 years and under are FREE!
$5 per bunch of lavender
Other flowers are available, priced per flower or per bunch
Ready made bouquets are available.
Bouquets can be pre-ordered to surprise someone special.


****NOTE - the garden is forever changing and different flowers are available for picking throughout the season. Lavender Magic facebook and instagram pages are good resources to show you what is available.

description:
Lavender Magic Flower Farm PYO Dahlias, Enjoy a weekend escape at Lavender Magic. The lavender has been harvested but the sweet calming scent still lingers. We are offically into the flower season - if you love dahlias then this is the place to visit. Wander through our dahlia picking garden and gather fresh flowers — the perfect gift for friends and family.

Nestled in a charming country garden, Lavender Magic offers breathtaking views of the Tararua Ranges, creating a stunning backdrop for relaxation and discovery. Whether you’re picking flowers, strolling among the lavender, or simply soaking in the peaceful atmosphere, this is the place to unwind and reconnect with nature.

Come see the magic. Lavender Magic — where tranquility blossoms and the stars are brighter.

Lavender Magic is a Lavender farm and a Cut Flower Farm. It has about 5000 lavender plants and grows a range of cut flowers. In season you will find pockets roses, lilies, sunflowers, zinnias.

You will find over 100 dahlias in the display gardens, all labelled so you can see the plants in situ. If you intend on buying tubers, rather than checking out catalogues come see for yourself, the size of the plant, the exact colour and size of the bloom. Your visit may save you money from purchasing something that not quite right.

Since 2007 Lavender Magic has won many awards for the quality of their lavender oil, which can be purchased on site along with balms, creams and sprays in the small farm shop.

We will provide you with everything you need to pick blooms from our cutting garden. Cutting nips, rubber band and bucket. We will let you know which flowers are in season and available to cut. If you like we will turn it into a wonderful bouquet to gift or enjoy.

Our Place Cafe will be operating when available so you can pair the best coffee with your visit. Keep an eye on our socials for updates.

Life Drawing Central, UPDATE. We have just finished our sessions for
2025. We intend to start again on 11 February 2026.

Queries - text 021 02510112.

We are usually on the top floor in the room at the end of the foyer. There is an electronic noticeboard showing the location of groups.

Weekly untutored life drawing from a model. Please note you will need to bring your own art materials.

Meet up with others who have an interest in art. We meet each Wednesday evening in a room on the top floor of the St Andrews on the Terrace conference centre.

The conference centre rooms are rented by a range of organisations - we are not affiliated to the church. Our group has been meeting for many, many years - it started at Turnbull House. Some people attend regularly, while others come occasionally as their schedule permits. There is no need to book in advance.

Our group is untutored; please bring your own art materials.
The starting time is 5.30 pm, but if you are delayed, don't worry if you are a few minutes late. We are a small, informal group. Afterwards, some of us usually go to the Old Bailey on Lambton Quay for drinks and dinner. See some of our work on Facebook: St Andrews Wellington Life Drawing Group. We also now have an Instagram page @wgtn_life_art

description:
MOKSHA • 5 Year Anniversary Gathering at Valhalla, MOKSHA • 5 Year Anniversary Gathering at Valhalla
❤️ TEAM MOKSHA PRESENTS ❤️

MOKSHA -5 Year Anniversary Gathering
08 AUGUST 2026 | VALHALLA, WELLINGTON

Five years.

Honestly, it's hard to believe.

What started as a small dream between a few friends has grown into something far bigger than we ever imagined.

Over the last five years, we've shared dancefloors, sunsets, sunrises, laughter, hugs, friendships, and countless unforgettable moments together. We've watched strangers become friends, friends become family, and a community grow around a shared love for music, connection, and freedom.

Our recent gathering, AARANYA , reminded us once again how special this community truly is. Seeing so many beautiful souls come together, dancing under the open sky, sharing smiles and creating memories, filled our hearts with gratitude.

To every artist who has played our stages.
To every volunteer who has helped behind the scenes.
To every person who bought a ticket, shared a post, invited a friend, or danced with us until sunrise...

THANK YOU !

Team Moksha wouldn't exist without you.

As we step into our fifth year, we wanted to celebrate this milestone together.

On Saturday, 08 August, we return to Valhalla Wellington for a special anniversary gathering.

No egos.
No expectations.

Just good music, good people, and the energy that happens when our community comes together as one.

Expect a carefully curated journey through sound, immersive visuals, and the unmistakable atmosphere that has always made Moksha feel like home.

Whether you've been with us since day one or you're about to join us for your very first event, this night is for you.

Let's celebrate five years of music, friendship, growth, and community.

And let's create a few more memories together.

We can't wait to see your faces on the dancefloor again.

With love,

Team Moksha ❤️

Five years later, the music still calls us together.
Welcome home. ❤️✨


📍 Valhalla, Wellington
📅 Saturday, 08 August 2026
🕗 8PM – Late


🎟 Tickets coming soon via PrizmaTix.

description:
Magic: Commander Party Edge of Eternities @ Ceberus Games, Join us for Commander Party! Purchase a booster for entry.
Commander Party is a story-inspired Commander event that immerses players in the setting of the latest set release. The vibe is fun and casual, and the events are outstanding opportunities to welcome in broad groups from your community, from new players to lore enthusiasts to Commander fans.
The event features special rules designed specifically for Edge of Eternities and includes play aids and party cards to support play.
Set up and play follows the regular Commander format rules but players all have these additional abilities:
Special Rules:
Alternate win condition: At the beginning of your upkeep, if you control all five worlds, you win the game.
At the beginning of your end step, if one or more opponents lost 3 or more life this turn, gain control of an unclaimed world or a world controlled by one of those opponents.
Whenever you cast your commander, you get an orbit counter.
, pay an orbit counter: choose left or right. Each player passes control of a world they control to the next player in the chosen direction. Activate only as a sorcery.
Each world card also grants a triggered ability whenever a player gains control of it and at the beginning of their upkeep while it is in their control in their command zone.

description:
Mangatainoka Motors Hot Rod Car Day, Mangatainoka Motors Hot Rod Car Day
Attention all petrolheads! Buckle up for a rip-roaring day at our Car Days, where you can flaunt your sweet ride to fellow enthusiasts and the public alike. Plus, you'll have the chance to compete for some epic prizes that are sure to rev your engine!

Get ready to soak up the atmosphere with live music, delicious grub, and a refreshing ale. Swing by the Histui Museum for a bit of nostalgia, or hit up the Tui Shop for some merch to show off your Tui pride. Or, if you’re feeling laid-back, just kick back, relax, and let the crowd admire your ride while you swap stories with mates and family.

PRIZE CATEGORIES:

We’ve got a treasure trove of fantastic prizes up for grabs! From Most Original to the ever-coveted Star of the Show, there’s something for everyone!

- Most Original – For the ride that makes jaws drop!

- Local Star – Must be from Wairarapa or Tararua (home turf pride, baby!)

- Furthest Travelled – For those brave enough to put some serious miles on the clock!

- People’s Choice – Because the crowd knows best!

- Star of the Show – Walk away with a whopping $500 Tui voucher! (You know you want it!)

KEY TIMINGS FOR THE DAY:

- 09:00 AM - Gates open for cars (let the engines roar!)

- 10:00 AM - Gates open for the public (let the ogling commence!)

- 10:45 AM - All competing cars to be parked (no late arrivals, please!)

- 11:00 AM - Registrations close (don’t miss out!)

- 11:00 AM - 12:00 PM - Judging takes place (bring your A-game!)

- 12:30 PM - Prize giving (who will take home the glory?)

- 4:00 PM - Tui Brewery closes (but we do it all again the following month!)

PRE-REGISTER YOUR VEHICLE:

Why wait? Pre-register your vehicle or bike now for just $10 online. Just jump onto the website and on the day you can just park up, and flash your email confirmation on your dashboard. Easy peasy! Just head to https://www.tuihq.co.nz/mangatainoka-motors/

And if you forget to pre-register? No sweat! You can still sign up on the day.

All proceeds from registrations go towards the Mangatainoka Motors Reserve Restoration Project. It’s a win-win!

So, gather your crew, polish that ride, and join us for a day of laughter, camaraderie, and, of course, some seriously sweet wheels. We can’t wait to see you there!

description:
Mellow Mix, Explore Te Waka Huia Wellington Museum after hours with a special late‑night opening. Wander through the museum in a calm and relaxed atmosphere, check out the exhibits, and enjoy activities on offer.

Slip on a pair of headphones and create your own experience with our silent soundtracks, curated by DJ Marika. Choose your music. Choose your volume. Move at your own pace as you explore the museum after dark.

Get creative with craft activities, join a guided tour of our temporary exhibition, unwind in our chill-out spaces and catch up with old friends or make new ones.

This event is open to anyone wanting to explore the museum in a relaxed and friendly environment. It may feel particularly welcoming to sensory sensitive, neurodivergent and Takiwātanga Autistic visitors. To support visitor comfort, audiovisual displays will run at reduced volume. Sudden sound or visual changes will be clearly signposted.

Whether you’re coming on your own or with friends, you’ll be made welcome by our friendly staff.

Under 16-year-olds must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.

Accessibility maps will be available on the night.

We recommend booking to secure your place.

Friday 15 November | 6PM–9PM

Free entry | Registration recommended | Donations appreciated

description:
Monday Eve 8 Week Block - Mixed Levels, Our popular weeknight block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. This class will be held at our new waterfront location, Market Lane!

The block starts Mon 24 August and runs for 8 weeks till Mon 12 October, 5.30pm - 8pm.

This class is a mixed-level class, allowing beginners to work alongside advanced students. It is the best way for beginners to get into jewellery-making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

Beginners start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering. Then we move on to making a practice-ring set with a Cabochon stone (cabochon means it has a flat bottom and a smooth domed top) in a Bezel Setting. As you work through your practice ring and setting, you can move on to working in silver and produce another ring with a cabochon stone that you really love.

Level 2 students learn to solder more competently on their own using chainmaking as a way to develop their fine soldering skills. They may create a simple stone setting or ring alongside this challenge project so they have something to hone their skills that they are familiar with, as well as taking on a new skill.

Level 3 and above students are encouraged to work on their design skills and try new and challenging techniques. They should prepare to have one or two simple projects they can work on self-directed in class, alongside a challenge project.

This class fee does NOT include materials for any student.

Beginners should expect to spend at least $60 on materials for their ring making project.
All metals and stones as well as quality findings and chains are available for purchase each week in the studio. Students are encouraged to keep their silver scrap and find ways to use it thriftily in future projects!

Natural Textured Rings - Taster Class, Craft a beautiful, personalised ring - a perfect treat for yourself or a thoughtful gift for someone special! This three-hour taster class is designed for absolute beginners, though all skill levels are welcome to join the fun.

You will be guided step-by-step through the core techniques of silversmithing. You'll start by practicing basic texturing, cutting, and shaping with traditional jewellery tools using copper or brass. Once you’re comfortable, you'll move on to crafting your final piece in sterling silver.

In this hands-on workshop, you will learn to:
Measure your finger and cut the metal strip to the perfect length.
Create unique surface textures using a rolling mill, hammers, punches, and even natural elements like feathers or leaves. You can stamp names, dates, whatever you like.
Work safely with a jeweler's torch for heating and soldering the metal.
Finish your ring with sanding and polishing techniques.
By the end of the class, your beautiful, custom-made sterling silver ring will be ready to wear.

This is an ideal activity for individuals, groups of friends, or visitors to Ōtaki looking for a creative experience.

What's Included:
All practice materials (copper or brass).
A strip of sterling silver for your final ring.
All necessary consumables (sandpaper, solder, chemicals).
Use of all tools and equipment.

Important Note for Young Makers: Kids aged 12 and over are welcome to attend, but anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

New Year New Challenge - 1 Million models, STARTING NOW - THIS ENDS 9TH OF MAY!
Help us reach a target of one million miniatures painted in 2026, and Introduce new people to Warhammer to earn rewards!
This year, we've got two great challenges for you - One is about challenging yourself, and the other is aimed at growing the community with friends and family.
Our first challenge is one with a lofty goal – the Million Miniatures Challenge. It’s exactly how it sounds, we want to see one million painted Warhammer miniatures. Taking part is simple: head down to your local Warhammer store from the 17th of January and pledge to paint 25+, 50+, or 100+ miniatures by the 9th of May.
Faction, game system, and size of miniatures doesn’t matter, it’s just how many you can paint. But it’s extra impressive if your numbers include the likes of Fulgrim, Stompas, and Archaon.
Every pledge will be recorded on the store’s hub poster, and you’ll get a bespoke activity card to fill out your commitment and your continuing progress. As you hit your milestones, you’ll be awarded with a series of cool gifts at the Million Miniature celebration event on Saturday 9th May. You’ll get a One Million Miniatures pin badge for 25+ miniatures, a purity seal water pot stand for 50+, and a paint brush tin for 100+*
One million miniatures is a big number to reach, even across every Warhammer store involved. Even with hundreds of prolific painters involved, everyone will need all the help they can get, which is where the second challenge comes in.

About this Event

One weekend. Two worlds. Your Halloween story starts here.
The Nightlife & Horde Weekend Pass unlocks entry to both of Wellington’s wildest Halloween crawls:
Halloween Nightlife Crawl – Friday, October 31st
Zombie Horde Pub Crawl – Saturday, November 1st
Friday night is for the glam. Step into cocktail lounges, rooftop bars, and dance clubs with DJs spinning Halloween remixes and exclusive themed menus. Saturday night is for the horde. Join the undead as the city’s pubs transform into survival zones filled with zombie shots, blood-red cocktails, and a closing party where the living and the undead collide.
Two nights, two vibes — one wristband.





WHY BUY A WEEKEND PASS?
✨ Double the Halloween – Party both Friday & Saturday with one ticket.
🍸 Curated Drink Specials – Classy cocktails Friday, blood-soaked shots Saturday.
🎶 Non-Stop DJs – Hip hop, EDM, party anthems, and spooky remixes across both nights.
🎭 Two Themes, One Crowd – Dress to impress on Friday, then unleash your inner monster on Saturday.
📍 4+ Venues Each Night – From stylish nightlife venues to pub-packed streets, all within walking distance.


HOW THE WEEKEND WORKS
Check-In: Pick up your weekend wristband at the designated start venue (7:30–10:30 PM both nights).
Choose Your Path: Explore any participating bars, pubs, or clubs between 8:30–11:30 PM.
Final Party: Each night ends at a huge closing venue from 11:30 PM–2 AM.


WHAT YOUR PASS INCLUDES
🎟️ Admission to both Halloween Nightlife Crawl (Friday) + Zombie Horde Crawl (Saturday)
🚫 Skip the cover charges at all participating venues
📱 Digital crawl maps for both nights 🎶 DJs + live music at every stop
🍹 Exclusive Halloween drinks and specials each night
🕺 Two grand finale parties to close out the weekend


PARTICIPATING VENUES
Venue lists will be announced closer to Halloween. Expect a curated mix of upscale bars and clubs on Friday, and themed pubs and high-energy party spots on Saturday.
This pass is built for the ones who want it all: Friday for style, Saturday for chaos. Get your crew together, plan your costumes, and claim your spot for back-to-back Halloween madness in Wellington.
🚨 Early bird passes start at $25. Space is limited — secure yours before they’re gone.





EVENT TERMS & CONDITIONS
AGE & ID POLICY
Entry is strictly 18+. You must show a valid government-issued photo ID to join.
No ID = no entry, regardless of ticket purchase.
WRISTBANDS & CHECK-IN
Mandatory Wristbands: A wristband is required for venue access. You’ll receive it at the official check-in by presenting your Eventbrite ticket or QR code.
Check-In Deadline: Wristbands must be collected during the posted hours (before 10:30 PM). If you fail to check in on time, you lose access—no refunds.
Proxy Option: If you can’t arrive in time, you may send someone else to pick up your wristband.
VENUE ACCESS & CONDUCT
Schedule Restrictions: Wristbands and drink deals are valid only during the times listed on the Digital Bar List.
Use the Crawl Map: Always review the Digital Crawl Map Link on event day for updates, venue changes, or closures.
Capacity Limits: Some locations may reach max capacity. You may be required to wait or choose an alternate venue.
Venue Rights: Bars reserve the right to refuse entry based on intoxication, dress code, behavior, or safety concerns. Security screening still applies even with a wristband.
TICKETS & REFUNDS
Final Sale: All tickets are non-refundable and non-transferable. If the event is canceled with no new date, a refund (minus fees) will be issued automatically.
Rain or Shine: The crawl happens regardless of weather. Venue participation and specials are subject to change without notice.
Arrival Issues: Late check-ins or showing up at the wrong venue are not grounds for refunds.
COSTUMES & BEHAVIOR
Costume Guidelines: No items resembling weapons. Offensive or unsafe costumes may lead to denied entry without refund.
Respect the Crawl: Disorderly conduct, damage to venues, or harassment of staff or other guests will result in removal with no refund.
LIABILITY WAIVER
By purchasing a ticket and participating, you voluntarily assume all risks associated with the event, including but not limited to: personal injury, illness, property loss, theft, accidents, alcohol-related harm, and even death.
You fully and forever release and discharge Events Per Se, its owners, partners, contractors, sponsors, employees, volunteers, and all participating venues from any claims, liabilities, or demands connected to your participation—whether caused by negligence, gross negligence, or any other reason.

description:
One Night, Two Lit Events, ONE NIGHT, TWO LIT EVENTS
Bad Diaries Salon + Starling’s 10th Birthday
Verb is thrilled to host two sparkling events in one night this November with our tremendous friends, Bad Diaries Salon and Starling. A fresh batch of bad diaries will start the evening, followed by a line-up of not one, not ten, but twenty poets in celebration of Starling’s 20th issue and 10th birthday.

You have the option of coming to either event but you know you want to come to both. There will be cake! 
___
Friday 7 November at Meow. 
Tickets: $15 for one event / $25 for both. 
Verb Community members receive a 10% discount (check your ReVerb e-newsletter for the discount code, or email community@verbwellington.nz)
BAD DIARIES SALON – STAR 
6pm – 7pm, Friday 7 November at Meow
Tickets: $15 (or purchase the double-bill ticket for $25 and go to Starling’s birthday party, too)
Four courageous, starry writers – Kate Camp, Jo Randerson, Michelle Duff and Elizabeth Knox – read from their unpublished diaries on the salon theme, STAR. This is Verb's eighth annual edition of Bad Diaries Salon, hosted by Tracy Farr. What happens in salon stays in salon, so come, witness, celebrate.
Bad Diaries Salon is raw, raucous, unedited and candid: the written word, rediscovered and shared.
Starling: RELAY
7.30pm–9pm, Friday 7 November at Meow
Tickets: $15 (or purchase the double-bill ticket for $25 and go to Bad Diaries Salon, too)
Join us to celebrate TEN YEARS of Starling with a relay of readers from Issue 20 through to Issue 1. An evening of infectious energy, this is also the sign-off for editors Francis Cooke and Louise Wallace, handing over to the incomparable Tate Fountain and Maddie Ballard. A new chapter of Starling awaits!

description:
Out in the Pool, Our Out in the Pool sessions are regular monthly sessions for all queer, transgender, gender diverse and non-binary folks
We invite our rainbow communities and allies to dive in and swim in a safe and welcoming environment at Keith Spry Pool. These sessions are held on the first Sunday of every month and run 5pm-7pm, starting slightly later in February with our first event on Sunday 8 February 2026.
Out in the Pool evenings at Keith Spry have:
Gender neutral changing rooms and bathrooms, as well as our Men's and Women's changing facilities.
Recreation lanes with inflatables, as well as the Dive board open (as staffing allows).
Lane space will be available to swim some lengths or aqua jog, and the teaching pool will be open as staffing allows.
Spa and Sauna available
Music, swimming and good vibes only.
There is no additional cost for these sessions, simply turn up and pay our regular pool entry fees. There is no need to register, just come on down!

Paint & Sip: Spontaneous Colour, Overview


Spontaneous creative workshop: paint with a credit card using three colours, sip mocktails and connect in a fun relaxed atmosphere.
Paint & Sip: Spontaneous Colour

Join us for this spontaneous creative workshop, where you'll paint, sip delicious mocktails, and connect with like-minded people in a relaxed and creative atmosphere! In this class we will ditch the traditional paintbrush and instead employ a credit card, and only three colours, to skim paints over paper. Because the paint dries immediately, you can easily build up layers, while discovering magical and colourful blends. We guarantee fun and amazement at the colour combinations you create, whether you see yourself as ‘artistic’ or not.

Please note our events now start at 6pm. Please try to be on time.
We’ll close the evening with a nourishing dinner and dessert, all included in your ticket

Kia ora, I’m Rowena and I’ve been teaching art to kids, adults, retirees, and folks on the margins for 15 years. I aim to make art and creativity as inclusive as possible, especially for the people who say, ‘I can’t do art.’

description:
Paint Your Mate with Paintvine!, Paint Your Mate is a fun-filled painting session in the heart of Wellington, where you and your favourite human sit face-to-face and paint a portrait of each other on canvas. No skills required, 100% judgement-free, and abstract, exaggerated masterpieces are very much encouraged!

You’ll be seated opposite your mate while our Paintvine artist guides you with tips, encouragement, and lots of laughs! This event is perfect for couples, dates, best mates, siblings, or anyone who wants a socially acceptable excuse to stare at their mate.

This ticket is a double pass (two people, two canvases) and includes one free Love Potion cocktail (or mocktail) per person, all the painting materials you will need, and a final portrait reveal that will absolutely end in laughter.

What’s included

- Around two hours of painting, laughs, and creative chaos, guided by our Paintvine artist and assistant.
- All painting materials for you and your mate – acrylic paint, brushes, palettes, aprons, the lot.
- Two high-quality stretched canvases (one each!).
- One free Love Potion cocktail (or mocktail) per person to keep the creative juices flowing.
- Photos snapped throughout the session and uploaded to our Facebook page.
- Heaps of laughs while you unleash your chaotic, creative sides.
- Two one-of-a-kind masterpieces to take home.
- and best of all - we clean up!

What is Paintvine?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality canvas, acrylic paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit (or find some at the bottom of a glass). At the end of the night, you will leave with your own painting ready to hang on your wall.

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info, head to [[https://paintvine.co.nz/]

description:
Paint Your Pet with Paintvine!, Introducing our newest event! Paint your Pet, with Paintvine!

Paint Your Pet while enjoying a drink with your human pals. Anyone can Paint your Pet, regardless of art experience. There’s no guesswork and no pressure. Paint your dog, cat, bird or anything – we don’t judge!

Drinks & Food: No drinks are included in the ticket price, but drinks and food are available for purchase throughout the event.

How does Paint Your Pet work?
It’s simple! Guided by your talented Paintvine artist, you'll paint a near-perfect replica of your provided pet photo onto canvas across 2.5 hours. After you purchase your ticket, we'll ask you to bring along a printed copy of a photo of your pet to the event printed out in A3 size. This is for our artists and assistants to help you sketch your pet on your canvas and then we’re ready to go!

Do I have to know how to paint?
No experience is necessary! Whether you’re a regular to Paintvine or haven’t picked up a paintbrush since primary school, you can create an amazing custom portrait of your pet (guided step-by-step but your amazing artist).

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website.

description:
Pick Your Own Apples at Molewood Orchard 2026, Molewood Orchard in Greytown will be opening its gates to the public on weekends for Pick Your Own apples and pears this harvest season.

Long-time Greytown residents Juliet and Ed Cooke returned to operating the Mole Street orchard in 2022, together with son Wendell. Daughter Merran is responsible for marketing and social media, and son Grayson takes care of the website and visual design. The orchard is now run as an independent family business, with the whole family pitching in to support the 2026 harvest season.

The Cooke family is looking forward to welcoming the public to the orchard for the fourth year running, introducing a new generation to the delight of picking fresh, sun-warmed apples off the tree. If the idea of spending an hour or two wandering down rows of trees laden with fresh, delicious apples appeals, we have got your weekend plans covered!

The orchard is only a short walk or bike ride from Main Street, and parking is available in the orchard grounds. Please bring a bucket, basket or bag for the fruit. You’re welcome to bring a picnic lunch as well to enjoy in the orchard's beautiful picnic area, Molewood Meadows. Sunscreen, sturdy footwear and a hat are a good idea too!

Entry to the orchard is free! Prices per kg will be updated on our Facebook page and website.

description:
Planetary Parade - Free event, Six of the seven planets are in dawn sky during this final Planetary Parade for 2025. Matariki is also visible at this time close to the line of planets.
Come down to the Wellington waterfront at dawn and see the planets Pareārau (Saturn), Kōpū/Tāwera (Venus), Hine-i-tīweka (Jupiter), Whiro (Mercury), and Matariki (Pleiades) in our skies. Rangipō (Uranus) and Tangaroa (Neptune) are also in the sky but they will be too faint to see. Matawhero (Mars) follows after Te Rā (the Sun) rises so it won't be seen in the sky.
If you want to gaze in wonder at Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, look through our amazing telescopes! We can show you where to find Matariki, but binoculars at better so if you have a pair bring them along. The event is child friendly and free!
Please note we will postpone the event to if the weather is uncooperative.
If you want to support our Society by becoming a member, please go to https://www.was.org.nz/join-us/

description:
Pop Art and Wine Night in Wellington - POP the Kettle On, Paint Pop Art with Paintvine, and create a vivid painting that evokes a printmaking aesthetic.

In this lively night out, we will entice your inner artist by experimenting with paint in the style of Pop Art. Made popular in the 50s & 60s by artists such as Andy Warhol and Roy Lichtenstein, Pop Art brings popular culture into the realm of art. This painted graphic style adds bold glamour to everyday consumer icons and objects, and really makes them pop!

So smooth out those brushes, buy a glass of your favourite tipple, and paint the night away!

Drinks: No drinks are included in the ticket price, but drinks are available to purchase.

Food: Want to enjoy some delicious food? Food will be available to purchase throughout the event.

What is Paintvine?
It’s a social creative class set in New Zealand’s favourite local bars. Our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the painting materials you need (high-quality canvas, acrylic paint, brushes), all you need to bring is your creative spirit (or find some at the bottom of a glass). All our events are in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip as you create! At the end of the night, you will have a vibrant Pop Art painting that you can hang in your home.

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website ⇒ paintvine.co.nz

Pre-'85 Classic's Trip into Orange Hut, Pre-'85 Classic's Trip into Orange Hut
SAVE THE DATE – PRE-’85 4x4 BBQ at ORANGE HUT!

Saturday, 21 February 2026

Classic 4WDs. Good Food. Great Company.

Dust off those old rigs, fire up your engines, and join us for a laid-back BBQ and catch-up with fellow classic 4x4 enthusiasts!

This isn’t your typical off-road trip — it’s a celebration of the vehicles that built the tracks we love. Whether it’s a bit rusty, beautifully restored, or a bush-basher with stories to tell — if it’s Pre-1985 and 4WD, it’s welcome.


Eligible Vehicles Include:

Toyota's | Series Land Rovers | Patrols | Jeeps | Suzuki's | And all classic off-road legends


️ Proposed Route:

(Subject to change based on weather & group size)

Valley View Road

McGhies Road → McGhies Bridge

Karapoti Road → 3rd Crossing

Pram Track, Dopers Track

Whakatikei Road → Titi Road

Fenceline Track → Hydro Valley Road

Cross the ford to Orange Hut for BBQ lunch

Hydro Road → Pylon

Toi Toi Road → Clearys → Cooks Ridge → Cooks Gate



LUNCH @ ORANGE HUT:

We’ll be firing up the wood BBQ to serve:

Sausages

Build-your-own Burgers
Bring a chair, bring your appetite, and bring your stories!



Post-Trip Dinner (Optional):

Depending on interest, we’re planning a casual dinner catch-up at Brewtown in the evening. Let us know if you're keen!



️ BONUS TRIP – SUNDAY 22 FEBRUARY

We're also planning a Sunday run into Orongorongo Station for those sticking around. Details to follow in the next update.



Tell your mates. Save the date. More info coming soon!

description:
Pride Roller Disco, Come and join us for two hours of joyful resistance on small wheels! Relive the nostalgia of the mid to late 20th Century with a playlist of classic hits! Skate hire and protective gear is available at the Kilbirnie Rec Centre - $4.60 (paid to the venue on entry), or you're welcome to bring your own pair.
Never skated? Most folks haven't before they put a pair of skates on. Think you're too old? The average age of skaters after childhood to mid teens is between 30 and 60 years old!
6:30 - 8:30 at Kilbirnie Rec Center.
101 Kilbirnie Cresent, Kilbirnie Wellington
Proceeds will go directly to New Zealand Junior Roller Derby to assist with their on-going efforts to grow the sport.
Junior roller derby is a body-positive sport which welcomes all youth, including those of marginalised gender.
We are PROUD to support NZJRDA in their efforts to grow the sport here in New Zealand. This includes:
- Plans to organise bootcamps/trainings/game opportunities
- Working with JRDA to develop resources to support leagues wanting to start their own junior programs.
- Building coaching skills, facilitating the development of coaching programs for youth.
- Developing players who will have the skills and experience to join the national team, compete in international competition.
Is there a Junior Derby team near you? Is your roller derby team interested in support developing their junior program? Contact NZJRDA at nzjrda@gmail.com to register interest.
JRDA (Junior Roller Derby Association) does not and will not differentiate between members who identify as female, male, and non-binary / gender diverse (including but not limited to genderqueer, gender fluid, transmasculine, transfeminine, and agender) and JRDA does not and will not set minimum standards of masculinity or femininity for its membership beyond self-identification for divisional play. JRDA does not interfere with the privacy of its players. A player’s self-identification and comfort are the only criteria for the purposes of charter eligibility.

description:
Private Cape Palliser Day Trip from Wellington, Escape to the Dramatic Coast: Private Cape Palliser Day Trip from Wellington
Are you looking for a unique and unforgettable day trip from Wellington?
Imagine yourself surrounded by breathtaking coastal scenery, watching playful seals in their natural habitat, and standing in the shadow of a historic lighthouse with panoramic ocean views.
As your dedicated travel and adventure tour guide, I offer exclusive, low-key private tours to Cape Palliser, perfect for individuals, couples, or families seeking a personalized and enriching experience.
What's in store for you:
Personalized Pick-up & Drop-off: Enjoy the convenience of being picked up and dropped off directly from your Wellington accommodation.
Scenic Coastal Drive: Relax in comfort as we journey through picturesque landscapes, including the stunning Remutaka Hill Road and the rugged Wairarapa coastline.
Marvel at the Putangirua Pinnacles: Explore the otherworldly rock formations made famous by "Lord of the Rings."
Encounter the Cape Palliser Seal Colony: Witness a thriving colony of New Zealand fur seals up close (from a safe and respectful distance).
Discover the Iconic Cape Palliser Lighthouse: Climb (or admire from below) the iconic red and white striped lighthouse and soak in the incredible views.
Flexible & Relaxed Pace: This is your private tour, so we'll move at a comfortable pace and can tailor the day to your interests.
Gourmet Options Available (upon request & additional cost): Elevate your experience with a pre-arranged gourmet picnic lunch or inquire about other bespoke dining options featuring local flavors.
Expert Guidance: Benefit from my local knowledge, insights into the region's history, geology, and wildlife, ensuring a truly engaging experience.
Perfect for Photography Enthusiasts: Capture stunning photos of dramatic landscapes and unique wildlife.
Who is this tour for?
This private Cape Palliser day trip is ideal for:
Individuals seeking a solo adventure.
Couples looking for a romantic and scenic escape.
Families wanting a memorable and educational day out.
Anyone who appreciates beautiful scenery, wildlife encounters, and a relaxed, personalized travel experience.
Those who value quality and are happy to invest in a private tour.
Date & Time: Flexible - Contact me to discuss your preferred dates and times.
Duration: Approximately 8-9 hours (can be adjusted slightly based on your preferences).
Price: Pricing is tailored to the number of people in your group and any additional requests (e.g., gourmet lunch). Please message me for a personalized quote.
Booking:
Send me a direct message to discuss your preferred dates, group size, and any specific interests you may have. I'm happy to answer any questions and create a bespoke itinerary for you.
Don't miss out on this opportunity to experience the magic of Cape Palliser on your own terms!

description:
Pōneke Pump n' Dump - Pinball Tournament, PINBALL TOURNAMENT AT YE OLDE PINBALL SHOPPE
Pōneke's Premier Pinball Tournament for your future career as an internationally ranked pinball player!
Make a hearty pilgrimage through the arcade, trying your hand at a selection of our finely curated games, report your scores to the staff, and watch your ranking on the tournament ladder rise as your scores are stacked up against your competitors. Not happy with a score you got? No problem, you can keep trying until you're
happy with it!
Make it into the Top 16 before the end of Saturday, and you'll be invited to play in the finals round the following Sunday, where 1st - 8th will play in A Division, and 9th - 16th will play in B Division.
This finals round is free of charge, and comes with a whopping prize pool worth $200 in value awarded to the top finishers in each division.
So what are you waiting for? Come and show us your skills!
Qualification Round (7th - 13th September):
Each player is granted access to a token deal of 12 tokens for $20!
- Sunday to Saturday
- Submit at least one score on each of the selected 8 games during open hours.
- Your best score on each game is ranked.
- Take a picture of your score and submit it at the counter.
- Unlimited qualifying! Not satisfied with your score? Grab more tokens and keep playing to improve it!
Scoring System:
- Linear Scoring applies. Score 100pts for the top score on each selected game, 99pts for 2nd, 98pts for 3rd, and so on.
Finals (14th September):
Top 16 qualifiers will battle it out on Sunday from 12pm onwards, with 8 in A-Division, and 8 in B-Division! Keep an eye on our socials if you've participated in the competition throughout the week - those who have qualified for the finals will be announced on SATURDAY night (the 12th).
You could win a share of $200 in Shoppe Credit!
How to Participate:
Simply come to Ye Olde Pinball Shoppe during open hours and submit your scores from Monday to Saturday!
Location:
18A Bond Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011

description:
Rewa Rewa Station - Mini Mill Tours, From fleece to yarn - We welcome visitors of all ages to a personal tour of our Mill and wool Studio shop.

You will learn the entire process from shorn raw wool to our beautifully finished yarn. Visitors will take a tour on our upper mezzanine looking down on the production floor to learn how wool is washed, dried, combed and spun. Afterwards there is an opportunity to purchase natural quality yarn and other woollen products.

Our Mini Mill is located on our working sheep and beef farm in Tinui. You may have the opportunity to see our Corriedale, Polwarth, Gotland and Romney sheep during your visit. All wool processed in our mill is from our own sheep and we can trace the yarn back to a single sheep ensuring the provenance of all our products.

The tour will take approximately 1.5 hours and a minimum of 4 persons are required. Booking is essential and it costs $25pp.
24 hours minimum booking time required and subject to availability

You can book via email pvieno@hotmail.com or telephone 06- 372-6990

description:
River City Express, River City Express
Travel to the beautiful river side town of Whanganui, hauled by both steam locomotive Ab 608 and diesel locomotive Da 1410. Choose between doing your own thing, or jumping on a serene cruise of the Whanganui River onboard the coal fired paddle steamer "PS Waimarie".

Leaving Kapiti as most others are still sound asleep, we quickly escape the coast and delve into the rurality of the Horowhenua. After a stop in Palmerston North we head up the trunk through the townships of Feilding and Marton before turning onto the Marton - New Plymouth railway line for the last stretch into Whanganui. After crossing the 290km long Whanganui River, we proceed slowly down the short 5km branch line taking us to Taupo Quay.

TRAVEL ON THE PADDLE STEAMER WAIMARIE!
Salvaged from the bottom of the Whanganui River where she sat for around 50 years, the Paddle Steamer Waimarie was restored to her former glory and re-launched in 2000. She is now the only one of her kind in operation in New Zealand. Your cruise leaves the Riverboat Centre Wharf and heads upriver taking in the scenery and views of Whanganui which can only be experienced from Te Awa Tupua, the Whanganui River. The commentary shares riverboat history and points of interest along the way. Check out the boiler that powers our paddle steamer, and maybe meet the homing pigeons and send a message with them on their flight back to the Riverboat Centre.

Departing Paekakariki/Paraparaumu/Waikanae/Otaki/Levin
Adult 13+ yrs - $209
Child 2-12yrs - $179

Departing Palmerston North/Feilding
Adult 13+ yrs - $189
Child 2-12yrs - $169

Buses will transport you from your arrival at the station to the Waimarie River Boat Centre.

DO YOUR OWN THING!
There will be a collection of vintage cruiser bikes for hire for a small fee to those keen to take exploring to the next level.

There will be short tours available at the Durie Hill Elevator. It is New Zealand’s only public transport elevator and is still used on a daily basis by locals and visitors.

There are multiple places to go, and things to see on a cruiser bike or on foot. Take a tram ride for a small fee and arrive at the Riverboat museum, be blown away by NZ Glassworks, admire the sculptures and views from the Motua gardens along the river, indulge in local cuisine, or simply shop local.

Departing Paekakariki/Paraparaumu/Waikanae/Otaki/Levin
Adult 13+ yrs - $159

You’ll be transferred by bus to the Riverboat Centre and can explore Whanganui on foot or by hiring a vintage cruiser bike. Attractions include the Durie Hill Elevator, Riverboat Museum, NZ Glassworks, Motua Gardens, and local shops and eateries. A tram ride is also available for a small fee. description:
River City Express, Travel to the beautiful riverside city of Whanganui behind one of our magnificent coal-fired steam locomotives. Once there, you can explore Whanganui at your leisure, or choose to enjoy a relaxing cruise along the Whanganui River aboard the historic coal-fired paddle steamer PS Waimarie.
Departing the Kāpiti Coast while much of the country is still asleep, our journey quickly leaves the coast behind and winds through the rural landscapes of the Horowhenua. After a stop in Palmerston North, we head north along the Main Trunk through Feilding and Marton, before turning onto the Marton–New Plymouth Line for the final stretch into Whanganui. Crossing the mighty Whanganui River, we then roll slowly down the short 5km branch line to Taupō Quay, right in the heart of the city’s riverfront.
Option 1 - Sail On The Queen Of The River - Waimarie
Departing from the Riverboat Centre Wharf, your cruise journeys upstream along Te Awa Tupua – the Whanganui River, revealing spectacular views of Whanganui best experienced from the water. Informative onboard commentary highlights the rich riverboat heritage and key landmarks along the way. Guests can also view the working boiler that powers the paddle steamer, and may even have the opportunity to meet the homing pigeons and send a message back to the Riverboat Centre in true riverboat tradition.

Option 2 - Explore at Your Own Pace
Join us on the banks of the Whanganui River to celebrate the iconic PS Waimarie as she prepares to leave the water for her scheduled dry docking. This relaxed riverside gathering is a chance to celebrate one of Whanganui’s most treasured heritage vessels, with live music, great local food, heritage tram rides, tastings from regional producers, and a vibrant atmosphere at the Riverboat Centre.
If this isn't your cup of tea, browse local shops, enjoy a coffee by the water, or simply relax and take in the scenic river views. You may wish to visit the historic Durie Hill Elevator—New Zealand’s only public transport elevator—or take a leisurely stroll into the nearby town centre to discover more of Whanganui’s charm.

description:
Ruapehu Mountaineer, Ruapehu Mountaineer
After a sold-out run in February, the Ruapehu Mountaineer is back. If you’ve been thinking about it, now’s the time to lock in a seat.

This is a full-day steam-hauled rail journey through the Central North Island to Mt Ruapehu. You’ll travel in comfortable heritage carriages with large viewing windows, an open-air viewing platform, and a café carriage onboard. It’s an easy, relaxed way to take in some of the best scenery on the network, from the Kapiti Coast through the Manawatū and across the Mangaweka viaducts.

At Ohakune, you’ll transfer by coach up to Whakapapa Village, where you’ve got a few hours to do your own thing. Grab lunch, take in the alpine views, or add on the Sky Waka gondola for a trip up the mountain.

It’s a long but rewarding day, and a pretty unique way to experience Mt Ruapehu. Ideal for families, groups, or anyone keen on a proper steam day out.

description:
SOLD OUT: Dark Sky Experience @ Wainuiomata Regional Park, SOLD OUT: Dark Sky Experience @ Wainuiomata Regional Park
Bring the family along for a magical night under the stars at Wainuiomata Regional Park and help us celebrate the opening of the brand-new Dark Sky Museum!

Set away from city lights, Wainuiomata Regional Park offers a superb dark sky location for stargazing. This special FREE dark sky experience begins with the official opening of the Dark Sky Museum, where you’ll learn about the wonders of the night sky and why protecting our dark skies from light pollution matters.

After exploring the museum, step outside to meet expert stargazers from Wellington Astronomical Society who will guide you through the night sky. With the help of telescopes, you’ll be able to spot stars, planets, constellations, and other celestial highlights visible on the night, including favourites of the southern sky.

Marshmallow toasting, hot drinks and a fun glow wall activity will be available to keep everyone warm and entertained between telescope viewings, making this a relaxed and family-friendly evening for all ages.

Come along to discover the beauty of the cosmos, learn something new, and celebrate this exciting new dark sky destination—no experience needed.

Session 1: 6.15pm – 7.45pm (SOLD OUT)
Session 2: 7.45pm – 9.15pm (SOLD OUT)

This event is now SOLD OUT, if you would like to go on the waitlist please email

description:
Silent Reading & Afternoon Tea, Presented by Mrs Blackwell’s Village Bookshop
As part of the Greytown International Cocktail Festival

Sunday, March 22nd
11am - 2pm

Join us for an afternoon of quiet indulgence at the spectacular Wharekauhau Country Estate, perched on the wild Wairarapa coast.

Your experience begins with a perfectly chilled Lighthouse Gin Gimlet on arrival. The gimlet is said to have originated with the British Navy as a tonic to ward off scurvy, so we're serving this classic cocktail as a nod to our venue's location, perched on Wairarapa's dramatic coast.

With gimlet in hand you can explore the lodge and grounds, soaking in the views as a sense of calm washes over you. At 11:30am we’ll gather in the main lounge for a blissful hour of silent reading: bring your own book and enjoy the rare pleasure of uninterrupted reading in a truly exceptional setting.

After our reading hour a gentle bell will signal a move to the dining room for an elegant afternoon tea.

This is a rare opportunity to experience Wharekauhau Country Estate as a day guest and to combine your love of literature and luxury in one special and unforgettable afternoon.

Your ticket includes:

- A silent reading hour at one of New Zealand's most exceptional properties
- A gimlet upon arrival (non alcoholic options available)
- An afternoon tea of sweet and savoury items, prepared by Wharekauhau's award-winning culinary team
- Coffee and tea

Dietary requirements: please inform us when you buy your ticket if you have any dietary requirements. The team at Wharekauhau can accommodate most requests.

Additional alcoholic beverages: these can be purchased on the day. We are at a remote location, please drink responsibly.

Dress code: there is no strict dress code for this event, but consider yourself licensed to wear that very special outfit that doesn't get out of the closet nearly often enough! We may even rustle up a prize for the most fantastic frock!

Come join us for a fun-filled day of sewing and socializing at Karori Arts & Crafts!
