description:
Spring Céilí Dance with The Great Beag Céilí Band, Spring Céilí Dance with The Great Beag Céilí Band
Spring has sprung, the days are getting longer, the rain is falling sideways. Must be about time we had another céilí! Join The Great Beag Céilí Band at St Michael’s Hall in Kelburn for a rousing evening of dancing to foot-stomping celtic tunes. Our Autumn céilí sold out so make sure you get your tickets early!

If you’ve never been to a céilí (or ceilidh) before, fear not - céilí dancing is very easy! No fancy moves or any previous experience required: our caller will explain each dance, and we’ll all walk it through a couple of times before adding the music.

This is social dancing so bring all your friends! No need to bring a specific partner - there’ll be lots of friendly people to dance with.

Discounted online tickets are available on Humanitix until midnight on September 26th: $24 / $16 concession
https://events.humanitix.com/beag-ceili-spring-ceili-2025

Some door sales may be available on the day: $30 / $20 concession (cash only)

—

Doors open 7:30pm

Adults and age 10+ welcome. Under 16s accompanied by an adult.

Light refreshments will be available. We recommend bringing a water bottle to grab a quick drink between dances - hydration is key!
This is an alcohol-free event.

Getting here: St Michael’s Hall is located at 81 Upland Road in Kelburn Village, just behind the church.
There is very limited on-street parking in the village. We recommend public transport: the 4, 18, 21, and 22 buses stop regularly right outside coming up from Te Aro or down from Northland and Karori.

Be safe online: Tickets are only available online from the Humanitix event. Do not buy tickets from other sources such as Facebook comments or resale sites - these are always scams. If you can no longer attend, please contact us via Humanitix, our socials, or email to discuss refunds.

Health notice: Céilí dancing is a great way to meet lots of people. If you are feeling unwell then please stay home and rest this time, we will see you at the next one.

Nam and Amira possess a deep appreciation and respect for Soundsystem philosophy, dedicating their musical selections to the concepts of unity, inclusivity and respect for all sounds sacred and indigenous. Join these two empowered wāhine through sounds of their diaspora. (@nam_chucks on Insta)

Hexadecimal Emerging from the UK underground breakbeat scene in the early 2000s, Scott Reeder quickly established himself as an internationally respected DJ and producer. With 150+ releases to his name and two albums on Distinctive Records, his output has helped shape a generation of forward-thinking club music.
Now based in New Zealand, Hexadecimal remains highly active, delivering genre-blending, dancefloor-driven DJ sets that reflect both his deep roots and global perspective. (@hexadecimalmusic on Insta)

Ché D
Ngāmotu New Plymouth–based visual artist and musician/producer Ché Rogers, aka DJ Ché D, weaves stylish minimal house and techno tunes. Shaken, not stirred, he blends underground classics, originals, and live-improvised remixes with a serving of indie and goth condiments. (@che_rogers_art on Insta)

Lowli
Event co-organiser Laurie and his DJ sets are, in a word: FUN! He’s guaranteed to get carried away and bring anyone, and everyone, on the dancefloor with him. (@lowli_dj on Insta)

The Village Idiot
Longtime Kaibosh supporter, Lee Slater, has been hogging house-party stereos, and sound systems, for over 20 years. Expect flowing, bouncy tunes and a little bit of wonkiness.

DJ Danger
Ange has been dishing up tasty tunes around Pōneke for the past decade. Expect an eclectic, genre-bending collection of tunes in her vinyl-only set.

VJs & sound

Cubeman
VJ Cubeman is an established New Zealand visual artist and live media technician dedicated to turning sound into immersive light environments. Specialising in architectural projection mapping and live video manipulation, Cubeman captures and remixes real-world music moments into what he terms "the new".
If you’re not familiar with his ‘work’ prepare to have your minds blown! (@vjcubeman on Insta)

Metrokorg
A frequent partner-in-pixels, with Cubeman, Kane is a dedicated champion of the underground scene, actively supporting tech crews and behind-the-scenes production. His VJing, custom projection mapping and immersive mood lighting have helped craft hypnotic visual environments for major festivals and events including Bloom, CubaDupa, Sunny Side Up and numerous Kāpiti gigs. (@metrokorg on Insta)

We’re stoked that this epic event will be POWERED BY TORQUE – Pōneke’s brilliant, custom-built Tub’s Audio sound system. (@torque_sounds on Insta)

See you on the dancefloor…

description:
Stitch Hui, Saturday 14th March 2026
10am – 3pm
Johnsonville Community Centre, 3 Frankmoore Avenue
Cost: $5 door fee
All are welcome to attend our Stitch Hui held this year held this year at Johnsonville Comminty Centre!
Bring along a project to work on or bring your tools and use one of our slow stitching packs. If you’d like to partcipate, bring along a piece of completed work to enter into the Diana Parkes award (check out the criteria below). There are two a Stitchbird giftcards for $50 to the Viewers Choice award winners, one for a kit or pattern based work and the other for original work.
We will have traders selling beautiful unique threads, hand dyed fabrics, detailed patterns and fine tools. There will be tea, coffee and baked treats to enjoy all day and we will be opposite the Johnsonville Mall if you need to pop out and grab anything else. We will also have a huge raffle and prizes to be given out on the day!
The Diana Parkes Award:
This award and Stitchbid giftcard for $100 is presented at this event is given to the work that best displays the attributes of Diana herself. A highly valued and skilled past member, who believed that telling a story was paramount.
Show us your creativity and mixed media work. The criteria for the award are as follows:
-An original work, completed in the last two years by a member of a Tararua Guild
-There is no size limitation, can be three dimensional, can be a banner or clothing and can be a joint project.
-Each entry should be accompanied by a short statement describing the inspiration and /or the technique used (no more that 50 words).
-The work may have been exhibited previously.
Check our the link below to see more and learn about Diana.

description:
TOČKA | Fiunary | Veale Moss, TOČKA | Fiunary | Veale Moss
TOČKA beckons Every one to feel carnal and Hollowed. Drawing influence from film, industrial-style production, 00s R&B, and pain, it amalgamates to create a Flayed and Tortured, cathartic club æsthetic. By towing a line between pop femininity and crushing grotesquerie, the artist explores the sensuality in fear, the liberation in disgust, the power in the broken.
-
Fiunary. A terrible and brilliant thing is approaching. A few days ago I felt a weight shift inside me. It happened suddenly, without pause. The air, each footstep, the balance of my head - they all feel different now. No, it's coming from behind my eyes - it's my own gaze that shifted. This is the kind of thing that ruptures you from the inside. What kind of thing is it? I want to be ready to grasp it. fiunary is alive, makes music, and will die.
-
Veale Moss - /viːl/ /mɒs/ , Archivist, unnaturally dense, collected airs of temporary significance.

description:
Taumarunui on the Main Trunk Line 2025, Taumarunui on the Main Trunk Line 2025
Travel over seven viaducts, see the Rangitikei cliffs, the central volcanic plateau, National Park and the Raurimu Spiral ‒ all while travelling on the new Capital Connection carriages to “Taumarunui on the Main Trunk Line” (and back).

Our route begins at Palmerston North and will take us over the Mangaweka viaducts, among the tallest in the North Island, with views seldom matched in New Zealand. You can view the picturesque Rangitikei River below as it flows past the high sandstone cliffs.

Leaving National Park we then travel down one of the rail wonders of the world, the Raurimu Spiral. This magnificently engineered piece of railway, steeped in history with stories of how an engineer with courage, foresight and a brilliant ability overcame one of the most challenging railway engineering assignments of the last century.

here are two options once you get to Taumarunui, a bus tour to Omaka Lodge or the Taumarunui Rail Action Centre.

The bus departs the Taumarunui railway station at 12.30 for Omaka Gardens and will be back at the station by 2.30pm. A pop-up café will be available for you to enjoy lunch while out at Omaka and you will have 3 acres of country excellence to explore at your leisure.
Roses will be in bloom and the rhododendrons in flower. There is even a garden for your wedding hour. There are fantastic views and vistas over the forgotten world.

https://www.omakalodge.nz/ https://gardenstovisit.co.nz/private-gardens/omaka-lodge/

Included are transfers and entrance to the garden for your self-guided tour. Additional guided tours cost an additional $5.00 ‒ please pay to the hosts.

When you buy your train ticket you can choose a shuttle bus that will take you Taumarunui Rail Action Centre where you can view their model railway, trucks, jiggers, tractors and carriages. A hidden little gem, operated by the Taumarunui Rail Action Centre.

If you do not want to take a bus you may wish to visit the railway museum (on the platform) where you can wander down memory lane, or visit the town shops just across the road from the station.

At 2.45 pm it’s “All aboard” for our return journey to friendly Palmerston North!

This train will be hauled by a KiwiRail diesel locomotive.

When Sunday 23rd November 2025
Depart Palmerston North 8.30 am
Depart Marton 9.10 am
Arrive Taumarunui 12.10 pm
Depart Taumarunui 2.45 pm
Arrive Marton 5.55 pm
Arrive Palmerston North 6.30 pm

description:
The Clothes Swap - Wellington CBD, Overview







Fashion waste is one of the Earth's biggest polluters. Let's come together and reduce waste by swapping clothes.
Attend The Clothes Swap and swap up to 10 items that you don't reach for anymore.
How it works:
- Buy a ticket through EventBrite
2 for 1 - $15 (until sold out)
Early bird - $15 (until 30th June or sold out)
General Admission - $20 (1st July until 29th August)
- Bring up to 10 items of clothing that are in good condition - clothing guideline/what to bring below
- Check in your items in 1 hour before the event starts and receive your tokens to swap with. 1 item = 1 token.
- Check in starts at 10am - 11am. The Swap starts at 11:15am - 12:15pm.
- Browse the clothes at the swap event and choose your fabulous new pieces.
- Check out with your tokens and enjoy your new clothes!
- Leftover clothes will be donated
The Clothes Swap Clothing Guidelines
What to bring?
We all want to find good quality clothes to love so we all need to bring good quality clothes to swap.
Please bring garments that are in good condition, not too worn or pilled and with no stains or damage.
Please read our Brand Guidelines via the link below:
https://theclothesswap.mailchimpsites.com/brand-guidelines
Please read our Quality Guidelines via the link below:
https://theclothesswap.mailchimpsites.com/quality-guidelines

When you check in your clothes we’ll have a quick look just to ensure the garments that are coming in are of good quality and are an accepted brand.

Please note: if an item of clothing is an accepted brand but in poor quality, it will not be accepted.
Clothing with no brand labels will also not be accepted.
How to get to Thistle Hall - Upstairs Hall:
The entry to the upstairs hall is around the corner from the entry to the gallery - there'll be a sign. There are stairs inside the door that go up to the upstairs hall which is where the Swap will be or a lift if you need it.

The Digital Minefield: AI, Misinformation, and Detox, This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.

If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

Together, workshop participants will demystify how artificial intelligence actually works, acknowledge some of the harms of this new technology, learn about the characteristics of mis/disinformation, build resilience against fake news, and explore why our brains weren’t built for the infinite scroll. You will walk away from the workshop with a better understanding of the hidden forces shaping your screen, equipped with real-world tools to cut through the digital noise.
 
Dr. Andrew Chen is a leading New Zealand specialist at the intersection of digital technology ethics and public policy. With a PhD from the University of Auckland in Computer Systems Engineering, Andrew brings a deep technical understanding and applies it towards systemic issues and interventions. With extensive experience advising public agencies and private companies on governing emerging technologies, Dr. Chen translates complex technical concepts into clear, accessible insights for the community. He is passionate about helping people understand technology's societal impacts, and thinking more deeply about what’s happening behind the scenes, so we can all navigate today’s complex digital landscape.
 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

The Napier Escape, Saturday 23rd August 2025 – Learn, Indulge or Explore in Napier
Steam Incorporated's Napier Escape excursion in August 2025 offers a captivating diesel-hauled journey through New Zealand's North Island, blending heritage rail travel with the region's stunning landscapes. Departing from Paekākāriki, our beautifully restored heritage train traverses the picturesque countryside, culminating in the Art Deco city of Napier, to showcase the best of the region.
Board the special train at Paekakariki, Paraparaumu, Waikanae, Otaki, Levin, Palmerston North or Woodville.
Passengers will experience the comfort of classic red steel carriages, complete with an open-air viewing platform for unobstructed views of the diverse scenery, hauled by one of our beautifully restored Art Deco-inspired diesel electric locomotives. Onboard amenities include a buffet counter offering a selection of snacks and beverages.
Upon arrival in Napier, passengers can immerse themselves in one of three fantastic options.
A Deco Deep Dive
Influenced by the glamour and optimism of the early 20th century, the new buildings featured bold geometric patterns, sunbursts, zigzags, and elegant façades that have since become iconic. ‘The Art Deco Experience’ includes a visit to the Art Deco Centre and a guided 1hr bus tour of Napier with a tour guide from the Art Deco Trust.

Steam Incorporated's Napier Escape excursion in August 2025 offers a captivating diesel-hauled journey through New Zealand's North Island, blending heritage rail travel with the region's stunning landscapes. Departing from Paekākāriki, our beautifully restored heritage train traverses the picturesque countryside, culminating in the Art Deco city of Napier, to showcase the best of the region.
Board the special train at Paekakariki, Paraparaumu, Waikanae, Otaki, Levin, Palmerston North or Woodville.
Passengers will experience the comfort of classic red steel carriages, complete with an open-air viewing platform for unobstructed views of the diverse scenery, hauled by one of our beautifully restored Art Deco-inspired diesel electric locomotives. Onboard amenities include a buffet counter offering a selection of snacks and beverages.
The journey includes traversing engineering marvels such as the Manawatū Gorge, accessible only by rail, providing a unique perspective of the monumental slips that closed the Gorge to road traffic in 2017, and the famed Ormondville Viaduct, a 280m long and 39m high spectacle in the Central Hawkes Bay.
Upon arrival in Napier, passengers can immerse themselves in one of three fantastic options. Choose from the following to enhance your day:
A Deco Deep Dive
The City’s Art Deco heritage is a defining feature of the city, shaped by a remarkable chapter in its history. After a devastating earthquake in 1931 levelled much of the city, Napier was rebuilt in the architectural style of the time—Art Deco.
Influenced by the glamour and optimism of the early 20th century, the new buildings featured bold geometric patterns, sunbursts, zigzags, and elegant façades that have since become iconic. ‘The Art Deco Experience’ includes a visit to the Art Deco Centre and a guided 1hr bus tour of Napier with a tour guide from the Art Deco Trust.
Sip, Savour, and Soak in the Views
Travel by coach from Hastings through to the Northern reaches of Napier, towards Bay View, and disembark at the Crab Farm Winery to indulge in a special wine tasting and late lunch opportunity from a beautifully crafted set menu.
Crab Farm Winery was established in the early 1980’s with the first vintage under the Crab Farm Winery label released in 1987. The land at Crab Farm has been in the Jardine family for over 100 years. Originally purchased without viewing beforehand – Hamish Jardine’s great grandfather was alarmed to find his new land was actually partially underwater. With tidal pools, rushes and hundreds of Crabs, the family jokingly named it ‘Crab Farm’.
Napier at your Leisure
Enjoy a few hours of free time in Napier’s vibrant CBD—perfect for discovering the city at your own pace. Wander among world-famous Art Deco buildings, stroll the scenic Marine Parade, or relax at a local café with a Hawke’s Bay treat. Visit MTG Hawke’s Bay for a dose of culture, browse boutique shops, or admire the colourful street art. It’s your chance to soak up Napier’s unique charm your way.
For all timetable, pricing & more information - head to www.steaminc.org.nz/book-train-trip/the-napier-escape/

The Napier Escape, Steam Incorporated's Napier Escape excursion in December 2025 offers a captivating diesel-hauled journey through New Zealand's North Island, blending heritage rail travel with the region's stunning landscapes. Departing from Paekākāriki, our beautifully restored heritage train traverses the picturesque countryside, culminating in the Art Deco city of Napier, to showcase the best of the region.

Board the special train at Paekakariki, Paraparaumu, Waikanae, Otaki, Levin, Palmerston North or Woodville.

Passengers will experience the comfort of classic red steel carriages, complete with an open-air viewing platform for unobstructed views of the diverse scenery, hauled by one of our beautifully restored Art Deco-inspired diesel electric locomotives. Onboard amenities include a buffet counter offering a selection of snacks and beverages.

The journey includes traversing engineering marvels such as the Manawatū Gorge, accessible only by rail, providing a unique perspective of the monumental slips that closed the Gorge to road traffic in 2017, and the famed Ormondville Viaduct, a 280m long and 39m high spectacle in the Central Hawkes Bay.

Upon arrival in Napier, passengers can immerse themselves in one of three fantastic options. Choose from the following to enhance your day:

- A Deep Deco Dive: includes a visit to the Art Deco Centre and a guided 1hr bus tour of Napier with a tour guide from the Art Deco Trust.
- Sip, Savour, and Soak in the Views: Travel by coach from Hastings to Crab Farm Winery near Bay View for a curated wine tasting and late lunch.
- Napier at your Leisure: Enjoy a few hours of free time in Napier’s vibrant CBD—perfect for discovering the city at your own pace.

Limited Mobility Disclaimer
Due to the age, design and nature of our heritage carriages, these are not suitable for passengers with limited mobility. If you have any concerns, please contact us on 0800 783 264 to discuss options with our bookings team!

The Spiral Spectacular, Join Steam Incorporated and discover what the Central Plateau has on offer. Experience the Raurimu Spiral first hand, hauled by our beautifully restored diesel locomotive, Da 1410.
Board this special train journey at Paekakariki, Paraparaumu, Waikanae, Otaki, Levin, Palmerston North, Feilding or Marton!
Upon completion the NIMT became important to New Zealand’s economic development, and was also socially significant. The Raurimu Spiral is considered a feat of engineering ingenuity and the success of this solution contributed to the on-going effectiveness of the NIMT. Despite advances in technology and materials in the century since its completion, no feasible alternative to the Spiral has been found. Therefore, the Raurimu Spiral is a lasting tribute to Holmes’ engineering achievements and is of considerable engineering heritage importance.

description:
The Tui Express, The Tui Express
Climb aboard The Tui Express for a spectacular, first-class rail experience. This is our fan-favourite excursion and an unforgettable scenic journey aboard our premium carriages, making it the perfect, easy day out for anyone looking to enjoy a fantastic Sunday on the rails with friends and family. It also falls on Father's Day weekend, offering a wonderful opportunity to treat Dad.

The undisputed crown jewel of this journey is our passage through the spectacular Manawatū Gorge. With the old highway permanently closed, the rail line offers an exclusive, front-row seat to this rugged natural wonder. Watch the dramatic river below and feel the history as we steam through the gorge's tunnels. There is no better place to experience this than from our open-air viewing platform, the ultimate vantage point for taking photos, hearing the thunderous echo of the steam locomotive, and catching the crisp air of the Manawatū Gorge.
Throughout the trip, our onboard licensed café carriage will be open. You can sit back, relax, and purchase a range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic refreshments, hot espresso coffees, and sweet treats right from the rails as the scenery rolls by.

Our tracks lead straight to Mangatainoka Station. Upon arrival, step off the platform and stretch your legs with a flat, leisurely 15-minute walk to the world-famous Tui Brewery, or hop directly onto one of our dedicated transfer buses waiting for you. Once at the brewery, relax and enjoy the iconic historic grounds. Your ticket includes a delicious, hearty BBQ buffet lunch and a complimentary Tui beverage (or non-alcoholic alternative) to wash it down. If you prefer to opt out of the meal, you can do so during booking for a discounted fare.

Your ticket covers your return journey from Plimmerton in beautifully maintained premium carriages alongside exclusive rail-only views of the Manawatū Gorge, rugged cliffs, and historic tunnels. You will have unrestricted access to the open-air viewing platform for unbeatable sightseeing and photography, plus full access to the onboard licensed café carriage selling refreshments, espresso coffees, and snacks. At the destination, you get a freshly prepared BBQ buffet lunch inside the iconic Tui Brewery grounds, one complimentary Tui beer, cider, or non-alcoholic beverage, and free transfer buses between Mangatainoka Station and the brewery.

description:
Trip: Belmont Regional Park at Dry Creek Entrance, Trip: Belmont Regional Park at Dry Creek Entrance
We will climb for 40 minutes up the 4WD Buchanans Road Tramping Track, passing Dendrobium cunninghamii, Earina autumnalis, Helichrysum lanceolatum and Metrosideros colensoi.

From there we’ll walk bait lines and informal unformed tracks for a 90-minute circuit of Syzygium maire (maire tawake, swamp maire). Botanising time will be additional to this. Bring good footwear and gaiters if you have them for waterlogged sites. There is one place with hip-stretching tall steps cut into soil. Areas can be slippery when wet. Hand ropes are beside steep mud steps. This is a 7.5km walk with moving time of around two and a half hours.

There is recent research on Syzygium maire in the Wellington region, published by the School of Biological Sciences at Victoria University. The authors highlight that we ‘need to identify refugia in accessible, albeit sometimes fragmented, habitat’ and recommend ‘leveraging human–nature interactions in areas to create, expand, and protect habitat for [this] rare species in a rapidly changing world’. Syzygium maire has a threat classification of Threatened-Nationally Vulnerable. The research illustrates the preferred habitat of Syzygium maire is waterlogged areas. Such areas are few and shrinking, both nationally and in Wellington region.

This trip will look at thriving Syzygium maire that have fruited and seeded in the rare wetlands below Boulder Hill. We’ll see Ramarama, Threatened – Nationally Critical, and Coprosma rubra, At Risk – Declining and over 100 other plant species observed on iNaturalist. These can be seen in a map view of the proposed quarry Overburden Disposal Area.

Ominously there’s a Fast-track proposal to turn this precious area into a quarry overburden disposal area. This has been reported on by Radio NZ. The Friends of Belmont Regional Park and Wellington Botanical Society have strongly opposed this. The Fast-track application is here.

Non-members are welcome to join, making it an excellent opportunity to explore this region’s native flora.

Meet: Dry Creek Carpark, Hebden Crescent, Kelson, Lower Hutt at 9.30am. This Carpark with toilets is a 10-minute walk from Manor Park Station on the Hutt Valley Line. Trains leave Wellington at 8.35am and arrive at Manor Park Station at 9.08am.

description:
Trip: Raumati South Peatlands, Trip: Raumati South Peatlands
This property was originally held by the Crown as an alternative route for the Kāpiti Expressway. Now planned for housing, large areas are protected SNAs including an area of mostly intact mānukā/kanuka fen which is unusual on the Kāpiti Coast.

Species of note include Scrambling Coral-Fern (Gleichenia microphylla) and Fork-leaved Sundew (Drosera binata). Time can also be spent determining the presence of Kunzea robusta and/or Kunzea amathicola.

Meet: 9:30 am at entrance of Te Rā school. Park at the QEP entrance and cross the road, please don’t park at the school. If travelling by train a pick-up can be organised from Paeākāriki Station, or walk 3.6 km/50min from Paraparaumu Station.

Leader: Andy McKay (Tel 04 296 4653, Mobile 027 555 5653, )

description:
Unity Book Club February 2025 | Service, About the book: 
What's this book about? Is there a restroom? Do you have gluten-free bagels? Do you work here? Do you have a restroom? Do I buy books or rent books or what?
The worst thing about a bookshop is the customers. Then there's the gift-wrapping, the invoicing, the stock takes. The Yelp reviews that inevitably contribute to self-loathing.

In his late forties, Sean is still a frustrated bookseller who should have written his novel already. Instead, he spends his days drowning in his overwhelming sense of contempt -for LA, for its readers, for its casual disdain for service. And what, or whom, is he serving anyway?

Biting, hilarious and self-aware, John Tottenham's debut novel is a razor-sharp dissection of the modern scourges of gentrification, male vanity, jealousy and the worth of literature in a digital age.

You don't have to eat food to know the way to a city's heart is through its stomach. So when a group of deactivated robots come back online in an abandoned ghost kitchen, they decide to make their own way doing what they know: making food—the tastiest hand-pulled noodles around—for the humans of San Francisco, who are recovering from a devastating war.

And now it's Eniiyi's turn - who, due to her uncanny resemblance to her dead aunt, Monife, is already used to her family's strange beliefs, as well as their insistence that she is a reincarnation. description:
Unity Book Club September 2025 | Flesh, About the book: 
A propulsive, hypnotic novel about a man who is unravelled by a series of events beyond his grasp.
Fifteen-year-old István lives with his mother in a quiet apartment complex in Hungary. New to the town and shy, he is unfamiliar with the social rituals at school and soon becomes isolated, with his neighbour – a married woman close to his mother’s age – as his only companion. These encounters shift into a clandestine relationship that István himself can barely understand, and his life soon spirals out of control.
As the years pass, he is carried gradually upwards on the twenty-first century’s tides of money and power, moving from the army to the company of London’s super-rich, with his own competing impulses for love, intimacy, status and wealth winning him unimaginable riches, until they threaten to undo him completely.
Spare and penetrating, Flesh is the finest novel yet by a master of realism, asking profound questions about what drives a life: what makes it worth living, and what breaks it.

description:
Unity Book Club: The Last Living Cannibal, About the book:
Muru is not revenge. Muru is about balance. You put your hands on one of theirs and they had every right to take from you and yours whatever they meant to take, short of a life.
Aotearoa in the 1940s, and the Māori men of Taranaki have refused to join the Māori battalion because of the severity of their land confiscations. Koko is the oldest man in the village, a legend within his community - he's lived through the land wars, Parihaka, imprisonment in Dunedin, and they whisper of him as the Last Living Cannibal. Koko dotes on his grandson Blackie, who has lived with him ever since Blackie's mum left in troubling circumstances years earlier.
But the ghosts of the past are bound to come calling, and when they do, they come with muru in mind.
Richly set in Taranaki during the 1940s, The Last Living Cannibal is the epitome of a classic Aotearoa novel, from one of this generation's most promising writers

WAS October meeting: The Science of Science Fiction - Prof. Jan Eldridge, WAS October 2025 Society meeting
Anyone is welcome to come along to this presentation.
Also accessible online through Zoom.
https://us06web.zoom.us/j/86837857650...
This month's meeting will contain the following:
1. Night sky in October
2. Astronomy News
3. Main talk at 7:50 pm
Title: The Science of Science Fiction - Professor Jan Eldridge
From Lost in Space and The Jetsons to Interstellar, the science behind science fiction films and television series is pretty variable, ranging from rubbish to … quite interesting. Much of it is simply an adjunct to the special effects.The great writers (Jules Verne, H.G. Wells, Isaac Asimov, Arthur C. Clarke, Philip K. Dick, Robert Heinlein, Ursula le Guin, Richard Morgan, William Gibson, and Neal Stephenson) have expanded our views of what could be. Often their work did not survive contact with Hollywood.
A few films and TV series are truly memorable: 'Beam me up, Scotty!’; ‘The red pill’; 'Exterminate!’; and ‘It’s life, Jim – but not as we know it.’ But the books are better.
This month’s speaker is an esteemed astrophysicist (and neither a replicant nor a sleeve) who can provide a detailed rationale for her views.

description:
WCC "Tequila and Salsa night!", Hello again bartenders from all walks of life! Brush up on your Tequila knowledge and your Salsa recipes because the next Wellington Cocktail Competition is just around the corner!
As to the theme for this WCC, it is “Tequila and Salsa food pairing” The hero spirit this time around will be a surprise tequila on the night, but I can tell you it will be a reposado. The catch is, you have to pair it with a salsa that you make yourself. There are no limits on the style of cocktail you want this time around, so get creative!
If you would like to participate, get in touch with me or Dan ASAp as we were running low on time to organize this time around.
Minimum 30ml of Tequila must be used in the drink and as always must be the hero spirit of the night.
You will be making two drinks for the judges to try and 5 minutes to make two servings of your cocktail and serve your salsa.
The judges may also be coerced with bribes and favours during your presentation.
The event will be on 28th of September and the competition will start at 6pm.
If you have any questions about the competition, please ask either me or Dan.
The main aim of this cocktail competition is to help those who may not have entered comps before, gain a bit of confidence and experience, or for people who haven’t entered a comp in a while, to shake off those cobwebs.
It also a chance to meet new people and introduce newcomers to the Wellington bar scene. Most of all the idea is to have fun!
Each competitor will have 5 minutes to make and present two servings of their drink.
All Tequila and corn chips for your salsa will be provided, but you will have to source your own ingredients including citrus and sugar syrup. Glassware and ice will be provided, you are more than welcome to bring specialty equipment and ingredients, however you will be marked on how easy your drink is to replicate.
The competition will be judged by a panel of 3 judges. While knowing your stuff is important, brand knowledge is not the key here. This comp is to engage bartenders in a fun comp environment, so drink and personality are just as important.
Competitors will be first come first serve, so message either me or Dan if you want to be entered, there are 10 spots for the night and there will be prizes for the winner.
There will be drink deals on the night, and make sure you bring your friends, workmates, parents ect ect to cheer you on and heckle the other competitors…
See you all there!

The catch is, you have to pair it with a salsa that you make yourself. There are no limits on the style of cocktail you want this time around, so get creative!
If you would like to participate, get in touch with me or Dan ASAp as we were running low on time to organize this time around.
Minimum 30ml of Tequila must be used in the drink and as always must be the hero spirit of the night.
You will be making two drinks for the judges to try and 5 minutes to make two servings of your cocktail and serve your salsa.
The judges may also be coerced with bribes and favours during your presentation.
The event will be on 28th of September and the competition will start at 6pm.
If you have any questions about the competition, please ask either me or Dan.
The main aim of this cocktail competition is to help those who may not have entered comps before, gain a bit of confidence and experience, or for people who haven’t entered a comp in a while, to shake off those cobwebs.
It also a chance to meet new people and introduce newcomers to the Wellington bar scene. Most of all the idea is to have fun!
Each competitor will have 5 minutes to make and present two servings of their drink.
All Tequila and corn chips for your salsa will be provided, but you will have to source your own ingredients including citrus and sugar syrup. Glassware and ice will be provided, you are more than welcome to bring specialty equipment and ingredients, however you will be marked on how easy your drink is to replicate.
The competition will be judged by a panel of 3 judges. While knowing your stuff is important, brand knowledge is not the key here. This comp is to engage bartenders in a fun comp environment, so drink and personality are just as important.
Competitors will be first come first serve, so message either me or Dan if you want to be entered, there are 10 spots for the night and there will be prizes for the winner.
There will be drink deals on the night, and make sure you bring your friends, workmates, parents ect ect to cheer you on and heckle the other competitors…
See you all there!

Waimeha Camping Village, Cape Palliser, Wairarapa is excited to announce our Waimeha Summer Party 2026, over 2 nights, starting on Friday night March 6th.

Come and enjoy eats and beats in the picturesque surroundings of Palliser Bay with premier New Zealand bands and performers. Waimeha Camping Village is only 45 mins south of Martinborough/Featherston. So party with us Friday night, then visit the Martinborough Fair Saturday morning then back out to dance the night away.

The Waimeha Summer Party has an awesome lineup, starting us off with a rocking Friday night The Wild Hogs, then Saturday we have the legendary The Beat Girls, as well as very popular band Jodie & The Stowaways and our awesome DJ Gravy.

Camping in our front paddock free for ticketholders. We will be cooking up a storm with a variety of food options, along with a range of beers, wines and spirits to purchase.

Please check out our Facebook page “Waimeha Camping Village” for updates and more info.

Gates opening at 12.00 noon Friday 6th.

It will then continue on Saturday afternoon, with DJ Gravy, followed by the Beat Girls and Jodie & the Stowaways.

No B.Y.O. Under 5's free.

description:
Watercolour Paint and Wine Night - It's Wine Time, Looking for a unique night out in Wellington? Join us for a beginner-friendly watercolour painting event where you’ll explore fluid colour mixing, delicate brushwork, and create your own watercolour artwork … in a bar!

Our artist guides you step-by-step through the watercolour process, so absolutely no art experience is needed. You’ll be encouraged to add your own personal touch along the way, making each painting uniquely yours. It’s the perfect excuse to try something new, switch off, and enjoy a relaxed night of creativity and good vibes.

No drinks are included in the ticket price, but drinks are available for purchase.

A delicious menu will be available to purchase throughout the event.


It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality watercolour paper, watercolour paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit. Our events are held in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip on while you paint. At the end of the night, you’ll leave with a watercolour painting you created yourself – you might even surprise yourself with what you can achieve!

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to [https://paintvine.co.nz/]

Watercolour at the Watering Hole, South Coast Studio loves teaming up with our neighbours, the Dub Hub Island Bay, to bring art and craft together (craft beer that is).

Join us for Watercolour at the Watering Hole – a laid-back intro to watercolour painting with a drink in hand and no pressure to be perfect.

Tickets include art tuition, materials and a free drink.

Frocktails: a night of sewcialising, cocktails, delicious snacks and fantastic me-mades!

About this Event

Wellington Frocktails, with our headline sponsor The Fabric Store, celebrates the making of garments. Whether you sew, knit, crochet or stitch, September 6th is the evening to show off your proudest make! Frocktails is a worldwide movement, celebrating me-mades for over 10 years.
Mingle with new sewing friends and say cheers over a shared passion of this craft. Whether you're an expert or beginner, this event is for you.
Included in the ticket price is a welcome cocktail (or non-alcoholic beverage), second beverage, light refreshments, a goodie bag and the chance to win one of the many sewing related prizes. You will need to be 18+ to attend this event.

Please note: A photographer is present at this event. Photos taken may be used for marketing purposes in future event promotions

description:
Wellington Game Review - Play Wellington Indie Games!, It's an in-person playtest of games made right here, in Wellington. As a free event, there’s no registration required or payment!
Anyone can simply come in, try out the games, and fill in a short survey.
The developers will be present to chat and take notes.
Friday, January 30th, at 6pm,
You can play these local games:
- Dream Team Supreme: a co-op roguelike deckbuilder by Big Adventure (https://store.steampowered.com/.../Dream_Team_Supreme/)
- Echo Zero: a survival, base-building, action roguelike by Wildboy Studio (https://store.steampowered.com/app/4028060/Echo_Zero/
- Shape Sender Deluxe: a physics-based puzzler by Dead Teapot (https://store.steampowered.com/.../Shape_Sender_Deluxe/)
Tell your friends about it. Stop by after work, or before going out into town.
Make an evening of it with your mates.
Enjoy all the games (and food) Respawn has to offer and jump into the free playtests as you please. We're easy and we'll be gaming and chatting from 6pm till late.

Wellington Game Review, It's the 1st ever Wellington Game Review!! Try out games for free and support your local dev with feedback.

You can play these games:
- Dream Team Supreme, a co-op roguelike deckbuilder by Big Adventure
- Echo Zero, a survival, base-building, action roguelike by Wildboy Studio
- Shape Sender Deluxe a physics-based puzzler by Dead Teapot

Tell your friends about it. Stop by after work, or before going out into town. Make an evening of it with your mates. Enjoy all the games and food Respawn has to offer and jump into the free playtests as you please. We're easy and we'll be gaming and chatting from 6pm till late.

This is the first time that Wellington game devs have banded together to organise local playtesting in person. These three games have been in development for over a year, and each has something specific that the devs made for this playtest. Respawn is the ultimate gaming hub in Wellington, offering top tier gaming, food, and weekly events. Let's keep the fun going with some games made down the street!

Get ready for the biggest Halloween Bar Crawl in Wellington on Saturday, Nov 1st. Hit the city's top bars & clubs!

About this Event


🎃🕸️ WELLINGTON HALLOWEEN BAR CRAWL 2025 🕸️🎃
Get ready for the wildest Halloween celebration in Wellington. Join the spookiest Halloween Bar Crawl on Saturday, November 1st, 2025, and get access to 4+ of Wellington’s hottest bars and nightclubs!
🎶 Music: Live DJs playing the hottest hits and Halloween classics.
📍 Crawl Stops: Lulu Bar & Restaurant, El Horno, The Rogue & Vagabond, and BL3—Wellington's hottest bars and nightclubs for an unforgettable Halloween celebration!
🕙 Kickoff: Doors open at 7:30 PM. Wristbands must be picked up by 10:30 PM!
🎟 Tickets: Starting at just $15. Prices go up soon, so don’t wait!
Throw on your wildest costume and get ready to crawl through the city with hundreds of partygoers. Whether you're spooky, cute, or covered in fake blood—this is the crawl to be at to celebrate Halloween.🧟‍♀️


⭐ Voted Wellington’s #1 Halloween Bar Crawl Experience!
Gather your friends and take over the city with the Halloween Bar Crawl this Halloween, hitting Wellington’s top bars.
🚨 This event is limited to 500 attendees, so grab your tickets early before they sell out! Don’t miss your chance to celebrate this big holiday—secure your spot before it’s too late!





What’s Included in Your Ticket:
🎃 Join Hundreds of Halloween Partygoers in Wellington
🚫 No Cover at All Participating Venues
🎟️ Exclusive Halloween Bar Crawl Wristband for Entry
📱 Bar Crawl Map to Navigate Each Spooky Stop 🗺️
🎵 Live DJs Spinning Halloween Hits and Party Anthems
🕺 End the Night in Style at the Final Haunted Venue
👻 Costume up and crawl your way through Wellington’s hottest bars. Enjoy eerie drink specials, electric energy, and unforgettable Halloween experience!


🚨 Get Your 2025 Halloween Bar Crawl Tickets Before We Sell Out! 🚨
🦇Wellington’s biggest Halloween bash is just around the corner. Costumes, cocktails, and chaos await across the city's top nightlife spots.
It’s time to show off your best look and turn heads all night long. Whether you're spooky, sexy, or just straight-up wild, this year's Halloween Bar Crawl is your chance to shine. Hit the city’s most popular bars, enjoy themed drinks, and party with hundreds of fellow Halloween lovers. Your costume deserves a crowd, and this is where to find it.
🚫🍸🔑 Celebrate Responsibly!
We DO NOT condone drinking and driving. Use Uber, Lyft, get a Taxi, or a designated driver to ensure a safe ride home. Celebrate responsibly and make it a Halloween to remember!
💀 Let the WELLINGTON HALLOWEEN BAR CRAWL begin!


100% CANCELLATION REFUND GUARANTEE
👌 If the event is canceled for any reason, all tickets will be refunded in full! No vouchers, no credits, just your money straight back to the bank!


WRISTBAND PICKUP INSTRUCTIONS & POLICY
Where and When to Pick Up Wristbands
WRISTBAND VENUE:
Lulu Bar & Restaurant
🕒 7:30 PM – 10:30 PM
📍 31 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington 6011
Details: Please arrive at our first stop to scan your ticket and collect your wristband. You have from 7:30 -10:30 to arrive and pick up your wristband for the night. You can stay at this venue until 10:30PM or explore the other venues.
MIDDLE STOPS:
El Horno
🕒 8:30 PM – 11:30 PM
📍 34 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington 6011
Details: This is a middle slot—you can visit this venue at your leisure anytime between 8:30 PM and 11:30 PM.
The Rogue & Vagabond
🕒 8:30 PM – 11:30 PM
📍 18 Garrett Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011
Details: This is a middle slot—you can visit this venue at your leisure anytime between 8:30 PM and 11:30 PM.
FINAL VENUE:
BL3
🕒 11:30 PM – 2:00 AM
📍8 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington 6011
Details: This is the final stop! Everyone should meet at this final venue at 11:30PM for a massive final Halloween party!


Wristband Policy
This is an open-format crawl. You must start at the first venue to collect your wristband. Once you have your wristband, you can visit any participating venues labeled as “Middle Stops” at your convenience between 8:30 PM and 11:30 PM or stay at the wristband venue until 10:30pm. After 11:30 PM, all participants will meet at the final venue to celebrate at the final party location!
Please remember that you need to collect your wristband at the first stop (wristband venue), as it is required for entry into all venues except the first one. Please also note that wristbands are no longer available after 10:30PM at the first venue. No refunds will be given if you show up late and miss the wristband pick-up window!
This club crawl is a walking bar crawl—all venues are within walking distance of each other. Please plan accordingly for transportation and your walking schedule.
Wristbands for entry will be provided by event staff only. To pick up your wristband, please check in with the event staff at the front reception or host stand.


2025 CRAWL MAP:




🎟️ General Admission – $20
Includes access to all official crawl stops. No frills — just the fun.
───────────────────────────────────────

👑 VIP Ticket – $25
Includes everything in GA plus:
🔥 Access to the VIP-only crawl challenge for free tickets
🚀 First dibs on future crawl drops & pre-sales
───────────────────────────────────────

🤯 Ultra VIP – $35
For the dangerously curious. Includes everything in VIP plus:
🏆 Name on our “Crawl Wall of Fame”
📜 Official “Certified Crawl Legend” digital certificate
🚪 Access to a future exclusive pre-sale drop
❓ A mystery bonus item we legally can’t describe 👀



A SPOOKTACULAR HALLOWEEN PARTY YOU WON'T WANT TO MISS
Skip the overpriced cover charge and long lines at a single bar. With one ticket, you’ll unlock access to multiple Halloween hotspots across Wellington, each with its own theme, music, and party energy. Whether you're rocking a full costume or just out for the night, this is your chance to experience the city’s top nightlife all in one thrilling Halloween themed experience.
THIS IS NOT YOUR AVERAGE HALLOWEEN NIGHT OUT
One bar? One vibe? That’s not how Wellington does Halloween. Grab your crew and bounce between the city’s best bars and clubs, each bringing something different to the table. From spooky cocktails to wild dance floors, the night builds up to one massive end-of-night party you won’t want to miss. 🧛‍♀️
THE BIGGEST HALLOWEEN PARTY NIGHT IN WELLINGTON
This crazy Halloween experience crawl will take you through the city’s top bars and clubs with a line-up built for non-stop fun. Expect packed dance floors, themed drinks, and a crowd ready to party in full costume.
GET YOUR TICKETS BEFORE THEY VANISH!
Spots are filling fast, so now’s the time to lock in your plans. Round up your friends, pick your costume, and get ready to sip, dance, and crawl your way through one of the most exciting nights Wellington has to offer. Halloween only comes once a year... so grab your tickets today! 🎟️



18+ EVENT / GOVERNMENT ISSUED ID REQUIRED


TIPS FOR OUR CRAWL
Pick Up Wristbands On Time: Collect your wristband(s) during the designated check-in time at the scheduled location before 10:30 PM. Late arrivals will not be accommodated — no wristband, no entry.
Assign a Proxy if Needed: Can’t make check-in? Have a friend pick up your wristband for you so they don’t miss out.
Day-Of Updates: Review the Digital Crawl Map on the morning of the event for any last-minute changes or venue updates.
Check Venue Schedule: Each venue’s crawl time is listed in the Digital Crawl Map. Wristbands and drink specials are valid only during these scheduled times.

This event is free for all to attend

Hope to see you there!


IMPORTANT! The puzzle swap operates on an honesty-based system. NZJPA will not be inspecting puzzles and cannot guarantee their completeness or condition. We are providing a space for puzzle enthusiasts to swap puzzles.

Please refrain from bringing puzzles with missing pieces or significant damage (e.g., water damage, severe fraying). It's important to ensure everyone has a positive experience.

Swap puzzles 'like-for-like'. For example, exchange a 1000-piece puzzle for another 1000-piece puzzle, or a 500-piece puzzle for another 500-piece puzzle.

For puzzles with an irregular number of pieces, choose the nearest size available, considering both size and quality. The attendant can help you decide if needed.

Enjoy swapping and updating your puzzle collection!

description:
Women of Pōneke November 2025 Event, Women of Pōneke: Hidden Stories of Our City
6 November | 5:00–7:30pm | The Exchange (The Atrium), Blair & Allen Streets, Wellington
We’re ending the year with an invitation to rediscover the hidden and magical delights that make Wellington the city we love.
Pōneke is a city of contrasts, wild and urban, creative and political. Its hidden stories are all around us, waiting to be noticed and celebrated. We’ll take inspiration from the Wellington Writers Walk; a trail of words and ideas scattered along the waterfront that invites us to pause, notice and listen.
We are delighted to welcome Dame Fiona Kidman as our special guest. As one of the original founders of the Walk, she will share why this project was so important to her and the inspiration behind it. As an esteemed New Zealand author, Dame Fiona brings a wealth of experience in storytelling, creativity, and reflection that we hope will inspire us to all explore our wonderful city.
Join us for an evening of conversation, discovery and connection with Luna Estate wine and delicious food from Monsoon Poon. Our sponsors are our wonderful friends at Inside Recruitment.
Tickets are limited to 150 guests.
Get your tickets now! 
Numbers are limited due to space, so we recommend you get in and quick! We are limited to 150 only. 
We will be serving wine, beer and amazing non-alcoholic drinks, inclusive in the ticket price. Platters will also be shared throughout the evening. 
So grab your ticket now and share with at least one amazing woman (and/or ally) in your life.
To cover our costs, we are charging for this event. We know that things are tough at the moment for many, so if this is a barrier for you to attend, please contact us and we will do everything to support you to attend. 
Help a woman in need
If you wish to support someone else who may have a financial barrier, please buy one of the "Buy-One, Give-One" tickets, so we can support more of the amazing women of Pōneke to attend.
Get in quick!
Tickets for previous events have sold out fast. For this event we are capped at 150 people attending and we will be updating our social media channels on the progress of the ticket sales, so get your tickets quick.  
Accessibility
Access friendly, no stairs, wide entrance and seating for those who need it.
A bit about us 
Me.We.Pōneke is our signature quarterly event designed to inspire, connect and raise the voices of our wonderful community of Wellington women, and people who identify as women. 
We believe that magic happens when women come together. We’ve seen it. We’ve felt it. And we want to create more of it with regular events that are open, welcoming, supportive and empowering for the women of Wellington.
Come along, bring a friend and join us as we continue to raise the voices of Wellington women and invite you all to be part of Me We Pōneke.
You can join our mailing list from our brand new website, thanks to our amazing partner Springload. Check it out here and make sure you sign up to our mailing list: https://www.womenofponeke.org....
We are also on Insta! Follow us here: https://www.instagram.com/wome…

description:
Yu-Gi-Oh!: Saturday Genesys Format (100pt) @ Cerberus Games, WHAT IS GENESYS?
The Genesys rules are simple:
No Link Monsters or Pendulum Monsters are allowed. All other cards are allowed. The original field layout is used, with no Extra Monster Zones nor Pendulum Zones.
The standard Forbidden & Limited Cards list is not used. All those cards can be used, except Link Monsters and Pendulum Monsters. Usual limit of 3 copies max of any card still applies.

The undead rise in Wellington! Join the Zombie Horde Pub Crawl on Nov. 1 for 4+ pubs, specials, & a monstrous finale!

About this Event


Zombie Horde: Halloween Pub Crawl – Wellington 2025 🧟‍♂️

On Saturday, November 1st, 2025, the undead rise in Wellington. The Zombie Horde Pub Crawl takes you through 4+ pubs and bars, each with their own specials and Halloween themes. Walk with the horde, grab exclusive drinks, and end the night at the ultimate zombie party.

Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás – kalandtúra a világ végén, Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás – kalandtúra a világ végén
https://hellovilagvlog.hu/uj-zeland-kiscsoportos-korutazas-kalandtura-a-vilag-vegen/

Készen állsz arra, hogy eljuss a világ egyik legvadabb és legérintetlenebb tájára? Az Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás – kalandtúra a világ végén azoknak szól, akik nem csak látni szeretnének, hanem valóban átélni akarják a természet erejét és változatosságát. Utunkat az Északi-sziget különleges világában kezdjük: Auckland, Hobbiton, Rotorua és Wai-O-Tapu gejzírmezői, gőzölgő hőforrásai és vulkáni tájai már az első napokban megmutatják Új-Zéland nyers arcát. A Lake Taupō partján haladva érkezünk meg a Tongariro Nemzeti Parkba, ahol drámai vulkáni panorámák és alpesi környezet vár ránk — itt nem csak nézelődünk, beleállunk az élménybe. A főváros, Wellington után átkelünk a Cook-szoroson, és megérkezünk a Déli-szigetre. A Picton környéki fjordos partvidéktől az Abel Tasman térség aranyhomokos öblein át vezet az utunk tovább. A vad West Coast mentén elérjük a különleges formájú Pancake Rocks szikláit, majd a lenyűgöző Franz Josef-gleccser világát. A túra csúcspontjai közé tartozik Te Anau és a legendás Milford Sound, ahol hajóra szállva függőleges sziklafalak, vízesések és mély fjordok között haladunk. Ez nem egy klasszikus városnézős túra, hanem egy tartalmas, természetközeli Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás, ahol rövid idő alatt meglepően sok mindent látunk, mégsem rohanunk. Kiscsoportban utazunk, rugalmasan, a legszebb panorámautakon haladva — mert a világ végén nem sietni kell, hanem megélni minden kilométert.

https://hellovilagvlog.hu/uj-zeland-kiscsoportos-korutazas-kalandtura-a-vilag-vegen/

description:
Āio: a Puoro Māori Sound Journey, Āio: a Puoro Māori Sound Journey
Journey inward through Māori sound, pūrākau and crystal bowls, creating a peaceful evening of deep listening, rest and restoration.

About this Event


Āio: a Puoro Māori Sound Journey




Starts at 6pm

Experience a peaceful Māori sound journey blending taonga pūoro, story, and crystal bowls for deep relaxation and inner calm

“Āio” speaks to peace and inner calm. In this immersive evening, pūrākau, taonga pūoro and waiata are woven together with the healing vibrations of crystal singing bowls, creating a space for deep listening, rest and restoration.

The organic tones of traditional Māori instruments including kōauau, pūtōrino, porotiti and pūtātara blend with the resonance of crystal bowls, chimes and ukulele, inviting you to slow down, soften and reconnect with your wairua and body. Through story, sound and vibration, this is a gentle journey inward.


What to bring:

Yoga mats, blankets and cushions will be provided, but you are welcome to bring extra for comfort!









After the sound journey, share in a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, included in your ticket, a warm way to close the evening together.





Meet your hosts & musicians: Smita, Peter, and Alexandra:

Smita (Ngāi Te Rangi) was born and raised in Aotearoa. From a young age she was drawn to music as a means for reflection and self-expression. During her music studies at university, she was introduced to taonga pūoro, and this sparked a personal journey of reconnection to te ao Māori and her own whakapapa. Following university, she lived in an ashram for several years where she was introduced to the wonderful practice of bhakti yoga. She now lives with her husband in the Wellington region, where they regularly participate in kirtan (mantra music meditation) at Bhakti Lounge.

Peter is Pākehā, with grandparents from England and Ireland, and has been on a four-year journey learning the art of taonga pūoro — the traditional Māori musical instruments of Aotearoa. Guided by the wisdom and generosity of expert makers and players, he has learned both to craft and to play these unique instruments. For Peter, taonga pūoro offer a way to connect deeply with sound, story, and the natural world, and he is excited to share their voices as part of this sound bath experience.

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from artists such as Deva Premal, The Flying Mystics, Stevin McNamara, and the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.






Agenda


🕑: 05:45 PM - 06:00 PM
Arrive to Bhakti Lounge

🕑: 06:00 PM - 07:00 PM
Āio: a Puoro Māori Sound Journey
Host: Smita

🕑: 07:00 PM - 08:15 PM
Plant-based dinner and dessert!

2025 Greytown Santa Parade, Celebrate the season with Greytown’s annual Santa Parade - an afternoon of festive fun, community spirit, and creative flair. The parade begins at 2pm on Saturday, 13 December 2025, bringing music, colour, and holiday cheer to the streets of Greytown. This free event is proudly presented by South Wairarapa Rotary.

Local businesses, schools, clubs, and community groups are invited to take part by entering a float. There’s no cost to register, and all entries are welcome. You’ll be greeted by a singing group of talented Pōneke rangatahi and there’ll be live music throughout the evening. description:
Art Classes - Term 4 - Creative Kid's Art Lab - 2025, Art classes & after-school care for children who like to make, create and invent. Located in Raumati, Paraparaumu - Kapiti.

For ages 5-13 on Tues, Wed and Thurs. The kid's art classes are from 3.30 - 5.15pm, however children can arrive from 3pm onwards.


- Qualified primary teacher and artist
- 15 years' experience teaching art to primary-aged children
- Progressive teaching methods
- Lessons based on traditional and modern arts/crafts, developing skills & creativity
- Structured, but in a home-studio setting
- Daily or weekly themes
- A child-friendly, relaxed environment for after-school
- Lots of variety / choice
- Excellent resources

The classes provide an opportunity to play and experiment in a structured but caring, home-studio environment.

Activities are designed and supervised by an experienced primary school teacher and artist.

To meet the needs of active and curious children after school we explore a variety of crafts such as sewing, crochet, pottery, felting, weaving, jewellery and woodwork; and the art forms: painting, drawing, sculpting and printmaking.

The activities utilise a child's growing mathematical skills such as estimating, measuring, scaling up & down, changing 2D to 3D, exploring symmetry, and pattern-making. Natural sciences, such as chemistry, biology, geology and physics are included, as well as history and culture.

See the creativekids artlab website. Phone Helen with any questions.

description:

Join Craig Ross, a sports educator, coach, and mentor with over 35 years’ experience across elite and community sport, for an honest and insightful evening designed specifically for parents and caregivers.
Craig has worked at NZ Youth, Northern Districts, and New Zealand Cricket levels, and through his consultancy Brave & Beyond, he now supports parents, schools, and sporting organisations to create positive, balanced sporting environments where young people can thrive.
During the evening, Craig will share practical tools and strategies to help families support children through trials, selections, and performance pressure. He will explore ways to navigate disappointment, confidence dips, and big emotions at home or on the sideline, while also offering guidance on how to balance encouragement, enjoyment, and performance without adding pressure. description:
Cameraless Photography & Artist's Book - Creative Arts Holiday Program, Explore the historic photographic process of the cyanotype, and stitch your prints into a unique, handmade artist’s notebook.

In this three-day workshop, you’ll explore the beautiful 19th-century photographic process of the cyanotype (often called a blueprint), known for its striking Prussian blue tones. In its earliest form, the cyanotype was used to record botanical specimens. On day one of our workshop, you’ll collect plants or foliage from the garden (or bring your own) to create delicate contact prints on Japanese rice paper and watercolour paper. On day two, we’ll plan your book structure and complete your cyanotypes. On day three, we’ll trim your prints and stitch or construct them into a handmade notebook of your own design.

Course dates are Wed-Fri, 15-17 April, 10 am - 2 pm daily. All materials provided.

Recommended age for this course is tweens & teens ages 10 and above.

description:
Commemorating Purple Poppy Day at Pukeahu, On Wednesday 24 February, tamariki and whānau are invited to come together for a Purple Poppy Day commemoration at Pukeahu.
Purple Poppy Day honours the animals who served alongside people in times of war, companions whose loyalty and courage are woven into New Zealand’s military history.
At this special ceremony, hear stories remembering courageous service animals and meet Paradox the horse and Kingi the dog, who will join the event to represent the heroes in these stories. Guests are invited to lay a purple poppy at the Man and the Donkey Memorial or chalk paint a purple poppy and message of acknowledgement into the park.
Come along to a summers evening at Pukeahu to acknowledge our service animals.
Wednesday 24 February
5pm – 6pm
Pukeahu National War Memorial Park

description:
Drawing & Painting - Creative Arts Holiday Programme for Tween & Teens, Join us for a fun beginner friendly workshop for keen young artists interested in drawing and painting.

Over two sessions, tutor Jake Fairweather will lead participants through a series of exercises designed help improve your drawing and painting.

Workshop goals include:
- Identify the key aspects of a scene to focus on
- How to hatch in various ways to describe the form and express different feelings
- How to tell a story through composition and colour
- How to push the story even further by modifying the lighting and shadows
- Discover your personal drawing and painting style
- Develop greater proficiency with graphite pencil and acrylic paint

Tuesday and Wednesday, 23 & 24 September, 10 am - 1 pm daily.
Suitable for ages 10 and above.

This workshop is part of Inverlochy Art School's September School Holiday Programme. For more teen & tween workshops including photography, jewellery making, animation, sewing and pottery head to the 'Tamariki and Teens' section of our website.

description:
Enchanted Park, Enchanted Park
Free fairy fun in the forest!

Bring the whānau for an enchanting afternoon in the Gums Loop Meadow at Wainuiomata Regional Park. This special summer event invites tamariki to explore nature, get creative, and learn about the native wildlife that calls this forest home.

Help us build a fairy garden in the forest where North Island brown kiwi live. Kids can paint rocks or create their own fairy doors. There will be facepainting and outdoor games. You're encouraged to bring fairy costumes and picnic lunches to enjoy in the meadow.

Our knowledgeable park ranger will be there (with fairy wings on) to answer questions and share stories about the park’s natural heritage.

The Remutaka Conservation Trust and Forest & Bird be on hand to teach tamariki about the kiwi who live in this park and the conservation work happening in the area.

Event Details:

Aimed at: Children aged 4–10

Accessibility: Tracks suitable for prams

Dogs: Allowed on a lead

What to bring: Picnic, costumes, and creativity!


Get the whānau involved in Summer Events

Discover the magic of our regional parks. For 25 years, Greater Wellington has been hosting recreational events that help people connect with nature, get active outdoors, and enjoy time together.

Wainuiomata Regional Park is a special place for conservation. Greater Wellington’s work here protects freshwater sources, preserves ancient native forests, looks after historic sites, and helps build resilience to climate change. Our partners and volunteers, like the Remutaka Conservation Trust, play a vital role in making this park a special place for everyone.
label: Kids & Parents

description:
Fairy Tours, Fairy Tours
Beyond the vials, the Unseen kingdom waits for the day they can meet you again.

I have seen and connected with these races all of my life. There are many, many races that live beyond the veil of our perception. The Green kingdom beings of the Fae and the Elves, the beings of the twigs and leaves. There are the earth-dwelling races of the dwarves and elementals. The “Unseen Kingdom” banner includes the mer people, dragons and the unicorns. In fact, they gave me the term “the Unseen Kingdom” to describe all of the hundreds of races and beings that humans seem incapable of perceiving.
In this experience, we will meet on the margins of the forest. You are invited to bring whatever you need to be comfortable sitting or lying down. We will be inviting whatever beings of the unseen kingdom who wish to, to come and interact with us.
The experience will unfold as it may. I am expecting that it will involve a meditation, lessons in Unseen Kingdom etiquette, and offerings. In my heart, I know more may come, but every time will be unique.
Please come with a calm heart and a gentle voice.
31st January- 4pm- 7pm
Location to be confirmed with the Unseens. - hopefully they have a spot on the Kapiti Coast. lol

description:
Family event: Explore Omnibirding with Giselle Clarkson, We are thrilled and delighted to announce we are going to be hosting a fabulous school holiday event with the multi-award winning Giselle Clarkson to celebrate the release of her latest book Omnibird: An Avian Investigator’s Handbook, a guide to the art and science of omnibirding.
Giselle Clarkson, the author of The Observologist, will be in Tawa for this very special event to explore the inner workings of the book and delights and wonders of the avian world.
Some birds are so commonplace it’s easy to forget how extraordinary they are. These creatures have a secret eyelid, hollow bones and a two-part brain. They dress in feathers. Omnibird, explores what’s remarkable about the birds all around us and the clues we can all use to become avian investigators.
Giselle is an author, illustrator and cartoonist based in Greytown, known for her work on conservation and environmental topics. She has illustrated award-winning picture books and nonfiction and is a 2023 Arts Foundation Laureate, receiving the prestigious Mallinson Rendel Illustrators Award.
This promises to be an unmissable event for bird and nature lovers of any age.
Books for sale thanks to the Children's Bookshop.
We wish to extend our thanks to Gecko Press for helping make this event happen.
This is a free event.
We expect this event to be very popular so to secure your seat early arrival is suggested.

description:
Holiday Programme - Build Your Own Ancient Runes Puzzle Box - CROFTON, Introducing our new updated “Ancient Runes Puzzle Box”. Keep your treasures safe in the coolest way possible. Only you will know the special code to release the catch hidden under the mechanical Iris! This new improved version has 2 code wheels that you can use to set your own unique code, as well as 2 code pins that are stored on the box but have to be inserted correctly to activate the mechanism. If everything is set a hidden push button will then activate a solenoid that releases the catch.

Powered by 4 AAA batteries (provided), you’ll get to solder the components, screw and glue all the intricate pieces together and unwrap the puzzle to learn how it works. And, of course, you'll get to take it home! No previous experience is required and you’re welcome to bring a grown up if you want to.

MakeRoom holiday programmes run every term break as well as over the summer. They are made up of one day workshops focusing on a big build with lots of fun learning along the way. Everyone gets to take the project they have constructed home with them.

- One day sessions
- Only 8 Kids per instructor
- 9am to 3.30pm
- $135 (including GST) for the day
- Open to kids aged 10-15
- Parents and Guardians welcome

On the day:

- Students should bring their own food and water bottle (morning tea and lunch)
- Students should wear closed toed shoes for safety in the workshop
- Students with long hair should have it tied back for safety

Intro to 2D Traditional Animation - Creative Arts Holiday Programme, This is a beginners course in 2D animation where tweens & teens will learn the time-honoured principles of hand-drawn animation and how to apply them to your own animation project. You may work on a project incorporating your own ideas, or if you'd rather, an assigned a project from your tutor.

You can use any device, ipad or laptop you already own (except a mobile – it's really not big enough to do good animation on). The school does not provide any digital equipment.

Your tutor, Ross Payne, is a 30 year veteran of traditional 2D animation, and loves to share his knowledge about it for you to love it as much as he does.

In each lesson there will be examples and demonstrations of the animation principles with follow up exercises to put your new skills into practice. You'll work on your project both during class and at home, applying the animation principles to your individualised project.

You can choose to draw your animation on paper then scan/capture into your device, or choose to draw your animation digitally, directly into an animation programme. which ever you choose, instructions in class will be provided to give you the skills needed for this step.

Bring a water bottle and snack for morning tea.

This workshop is for ages 10 and above. Tuesday - Friday, 30 September - 3 October, 10 am - 1 pm daily.

Chain for pendant is not included but can be purchased for $30.

- Use sizers and jeweller’s callipers to measure ring size
- Use files and sanding to refine and smooth metal edges and surfaces
- Use hammers to form metal
- Use jeweller’s flame torches to solder join metal
- Use Dremel & bench polishers to refine & finish metal casts into wearable jewellery

Minimum age is 13 years

description:
Kathryn Berkett - WHAT’S GOING ON?!, Kathryn Berkett - WHAT’S GOING ON?!
This fundraiser is a little different... and I reckon it's one you won't want to miss!

As some of you know, our whānau is part of the Maidstone Intermediate AIMS Games Rippa Team this year. To help get our team to Tauranga, we're doing a bit of fundraising along the way. Rather than another sausage sizzle, we wanted to bring our community something a little different....an evening that not only supports our tamariki, but also gives you practical, valuable insights to take home and use in your own whānau.

We've been incredibly lucky to secure the amazing Kathryn Berkett to present one of her most popular talks:

🧠 What's Going On? Navigating the Adolescent Years

If you've ever looked at your pre-teen or teenager and thought...
🤯 "What the hecka is going on in that brain?!"

...this night is for you.

Kathryn is one of New Zealand's leading neuroscience educators and has an incredible way of making sense of what is happening in young people's brains. She'll unpack why our rangatahi think, feel and behave the way they do, while sharing practical tools and strategies that parents, caregivers, teachers, coaches and anyone working with young people can put into practice straight away.

(No promises they'll suddenly start washing the dishes... but you'll probably understand why they don't! 😅)

📅 Wednesday 5 August
🕡 6.30pm
📍 Maidstone Intermediate Hall
🎟️ $20 per ticket

Every dollar raised goes directly towards supporting the Maidstone Intermediate AIMS Games Rippa Team on their journey to Tauranga.

Kathryn's book, What's Going On in There? – The Neuroscience of the Adolescent Brain, will also be available for purchase on the night, with a portion of book sales being donated to the team.

If finding a babysitter is the only thing stopping you from coming, bring the kids along. We'll have the school library open with adult supervisors so they can hang out while you enjoy the session. We'd just ask that this option is only used if it's genuinely needed.

🎟️ Grab your tickets here:
👉 https://events.humanitix.com/what-s-going-on-navigating-the-adolescent-years

If you cant make it but know someone raising a tween or teenager (or about to!), please share this post. The more people we can get through the door, the more we support our team—and the more whānau in our community get to hear Kathryn's incredible insights.

Ngā mihi nui for your support!

description:
Kids Do Well If They Can - 'UHub Empower U Session' at St Brendan's School, Kids Do Well If They Can - 'UHub Empower U Session' at St Brendan's School
Kids Do Well If They Can
If we see a child differently, we can see a different child.

Tamariki want to do well.

When behaviour becomes challenging, it can often be a sign that something is getting in the way, rather than a choice to misbehave.

Join us for a practical and encouraging session exploring a different way of understanding behaviour, one that starts with curiosity, connection, and the belief that children do well when they can.

Together we'll explore:
• What behaviour might be telling us
• Why some situations can feel harder for some tamariki
• How to respond with calm, curiosity, and connection
• Practical ways to work alongside your child when challenges arise
• How solving problems together can strengthen confidence, relationships, and wellbeing

Moving from "How do I stop this behaviour?" to "What might my child be finding hard right now?"

Inspired by the work of Ross Greene and Dr Stuart Shanker, this session encourages us to look beneath behaviour, strengthen connection, and better understand what our tamariki may be trying to communicate.

Hosted by St Brendan's School and facilitated by experienced Learning Support Coordinator and proud UHubber, Sharyn Spotswood.

Following the session, our UHub team will be available for one-on-one kōrero if you have any wonderings, worries, or would like to explore possible next steps for your whānau.

💛 Free to attend | Everyone welcome
Bookings preferred via www.uhub.org.nz

description:
Layered Landscapes: Mosaic Horizons, Layered Landscapes: Mosaic Horizons
Create a unique layered landscape using recycled papers in a relaxing, hands-on workshop celebrating creativity and collage.

About this Event


Layered Landscapes: Mosaic Horizons

In this gathering, we will create beautiful landscapes from common materials: magazines, scrap paper, wallpaper, maps, previously hoarded art papers, and even paper towels. Simple or complex, these landscapes come together remarkably quickly, leaving you with a work of art worthy of framing and hanging on the wall.

You're encouraged to bring along any interesting papers you have hanging around at home to incorporate into your artwork.




Please stay for a delicious plant-based dinner and dessert afterwards, included in your ticket!



Meet Rowena, your host

Kia ora, I’m Rowena and I’ve been teaching art to kids, adults, retirees, and folks on the margins for 15 years. I aim to make art and creativity as inclusive as possible, especially for the people who say, ‘I can’t do art.’

The cast of Kiwi's Big Hararei will wow tamariki with a sneak peek of their show, featuring original waiata by Aotearoa singer-songwriter, Benny Tipene. They will also kōrero about the unique adaptations of these manu and how we can all be kaitiaki of them.
