description:
Mindful Kids Summer Holiday Programme, Mindful Kids Summer Holiday Programme
Get your kids ready for a fun, screen-free holiday programme full of mindful, holistic activities. Vegan kai will be provided daily too!

About this Event

At Mindful Kids we will explore nature, get creative cooking and crafting, play music and dance, do mindfulness exercises and more in a peaceful, safe environment. The programme has been crafted with care to give your kids the best experience and will be facilitated by a NZ qualified primary school teacher.
The programme will run for three Fridays over the course of three weeks as per details below.
Times: Drop off time: 8.30am - 9am; Pick up time: 3pm - 3.30pm
Dates: Friday 16th January, Friday 23rd January, Friday 30th January
Location: Bhakti Lounge - 1/175 Vivian Street, Te Aro Wellington
What to bring: A drink bottle, sun protection, weather-appropriate clothing, regular Medic*tion, and walking shoes.
Age range: 7 - 10 year olds
General daily schedule: Each day will run according to the following structure incorporating the daily theme as per below.
8.30 - 9am - Drop off time
9am - Mindful Moment: Roll, 5 mins of breathwork, 5 mins of yoga, story, circle time
9.30am - Activity
10.30am - Morning tea time
11am - Activity
12.30pm - Lunch time
1.30pm - Mindful Moment: Roll, 5 mins of breathwork, 5 mins of yoga, story
1.45pm - Activity
2.30pm - Afternoon tea and pack up time
3 - 3.30pm - Pick up time

Activities for each day: Check out the cool activities we will do each day!

Cooking and Crafts Day -16th January
Vegan cooking class - Learn to make sushi, sweets and more..
Masterchef Jr contest
Table decorating and restaurant designing
Arts and crafts afternoon
Nature Day - 23rd January
Nature treasure hunt at Central Park
Decorating pots and gardening
Nature hike
Fun at the playground and flying fox
Picnic at the park
Music and Dance Day - 30th January
Make your own instruments
Disco dancing with disco ball and lights
Dress up costume play
Music and dance games
Talent quest
Programme Facilitator: Our facilitator has a wealth of experience creating rich, engaging activities for tamariki in Aotearoa. As well as being a qualified primary school teacher for six years, she also has a degree majoring in Psycholgy and Spanish, experience running a yoga and wellbeing student club at Victoria University and experience being a school Sports Coordinator. Additionally, she has taught in schools in Spain, been the Positive Behaviour for Learning Team Leader and has initiated mindfulness sessions for teachers at various schools. She was the second in charge coordinator for a holiday programme in Nelson and is now excited to combine all of her skills and experience to give your kids the best experience possible at Mindful Kids.
We hope to see you and your kids soon! :)

Participants will gain an overview of what disability support can look like, what services are available locally, and how to access and engage with the supports your family may need.

This workshop is free thanks to funding from Wellington City Council.

⚓⚓⚓

The scuttlebutt is true...⛵

The most seaworthy sea shanty band in the South Pacific is releasing their long-awaited 4th collection of new and old maritime bangers:
'Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society'.

All aboard as we set sail for the salty horizon. Prepare to be battered once again by the 4-sailor squall of pure shanty.

ALL SHOWS

WED 3 JUNE - 5Tapped Limited, Waiharakeke/Blenheim
THU 4 JUNE - Scott’s Brewing, Ōamaru
FRI 5 JUNE - Pioneer Hall, Ōtepoti/Dunedin

SUN 7 JUNE - The Dog’s Bone, Whakatū/Nelson

SAT - 1 AUG - Breaker Bay Hall, Pōneke/Wellington #2

Tickets to all shows: https://wellingtonseashantysociety.com/shows

⚓⚓⚓

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).
The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada.

They will be playing new classics from their forthcoming EP 'Never Mind the Rowlocks' as well as your foamy favourites from the 'Sea Shanties of the 70s, 80s, & Today!' EP and their 'Now That's What I Call Sea Shanties' series.

Newlands Tamariki Playcentre Open Week, If you have tamariki aged 0-6, you’re invited to your local centre during Playcentre Open Week to experience early childhood education with a difference.

Come along for a free visit and support your tamariki to learn through play, while you meet other whānau in your community. From sand and water play, arts and music, to outdoor and messy play, there will be a range of resources and experiences on offer.

With over 400 centres across Aotearoa there is one near you. You get three free visits before enrolling, so why not try a few centres in your community to see what suits you best?

Make a booking at newlandstamariki@playcentre.org.nz or 04 478 8470 (phone attended during session hours only)

description:
Newlands messy minis session in the school holidays, we have missed you all and are planning a messy minis session on Thursday 25th September at 10am. a 1hr long session with lots to discover and experience .
this session is at centennial hall 212 Newlands rd newlands.
we will have loads of trays with different taste safe and non toxic product activities, so all the minis are safe to try if desired. we ask all adults to bring a towel and change of clothes. shoe covers provided so you're not taking half of the class home in the grooves of your shoes hehehehe wash tubs are provided to clean off in afterwards. please message us to secure a space . cash paying walk ins accepted on the day if the class isn't full up. paying older siblings welcome

Book at museum reception:

description:
North City Soda Pop Stop, North City Soda Pop Stop
Join us for a burst of bubbly fun these school holidays with our free Soda Pop Stop experience!

About this Event

Join us to discover a playful pop-up soda destination designed just for kids!
Choose your very own North City Soda Pop Tumbler, then make it uniquely yours at our cup customisation station with a range of bright, fun stickers.
Once your masterpiece is complete, head over to the Soda Pop Stop caravan, where our team will fill your tumbler with a delicious fruity sparkling pop drink in your choice of flavour.
It’s the perfect little treat these holidays!

Event Details:
Dates: Monday 06 - Friday 17 April
Time: 10am – 2pm daily (20min session times)
*Please arrive a couple of mins prior to your session start time. If you have not checked in within 5 mins after session start time, spots will be given to those waiting so that session spots are filled. 20 max per session only.
Location: Centre Court, North City Shopping Centre
Cost: Free
Ages: Recommended for children aged 5–12years.
Book your free spot today and join in the fun!
**Please book only one session per child, to allow space for others to join in the fun too.

description:
North Pole Express Kapiti 2025, North Pole Express Kapiti 2025
The North Pole Express is back in 2025!

SUBSCRIBER PRE-SALE 25 JUNE 2025
PUBLIC TICKET SALE FROM 1 SEPTEMBER 2025

description:
North Pole Express Kapiti: 10am - Saturday, 19 December 2026, North Pole Express Kapiti: 10am - Saturday, 19 December 2026
Be whisked away on the North Pole Express to meet Santa, sing, and celebrate this special time of year.

About this Event


'Nice List' presale: 12pm, 25 June 2026 - 5pm, 1 July 2026. Password required.
Public sales commence 1 September 2026.
No tickets will be held during presale, any remaining tickets will be offered to the public from 12pm on 1 September 2026. To join the 'Nice List' visit the .
If you would like to purchase a private carriage for your group on this service, please email prior to 22 June 2026.



Join the magical journey to meet Santa!
Your tickets include:
Entertainers
Carolling
Iced cocoa
Cookies
Souvenir Mug
A special souvenir from Santa
Santa
Extra surprises along the way
Our Candy Class and Claus Class Guests travel in comfort and receive extra treats along the way.


Prepare to be surrounded by the magic and wonder of the Christmas season!
Families will love the magical train ride in one of our specially decorated carriages. You’ll meet Santa, sing, and celebrate this special time of year.
Set to the sounds of carols passengers are invited to join us to be whisked away on the North Pole Express. Delight in the magic of Christmas as the train departs for a journey to collect Santa who has been magically transported to an undisclosed location along the tracks.
From the distance the North Pole Express arrives then the train Conductors invite you and the other passengers to climb aboard shouting “All aboard!”.


All Aboard
During the first leg of the journey wide-eyed children of all ages are invited to engage with characters who are eager to hear what makes the Christmas season special to them.
You’ll meet the conductor, and join in the fun singing and dancing with your hosts and a few other characters who will appear in your carriage on the journey.
At the 'North Pole' Cocoa Class passengers enjoy their iced chocolate from their souvenir mug, and a delicious cookie served by our North Pole Express hosts. Candy and Claus Class passengers will be served aboard the train on the way to the North Pole.
Along the journey Santa appears in your carriage to present each passenger with their very own Christmas ornament. During the trip, characters in each carriage lead passengers in carolling and entertainment as the train makes its way back home.
Children UNDER 2 years (0-23 months) and travelling on the lap of an Adult are FREE. All Passengers 2 years old and over must hold a purchased ticket.

Please note: Seating in our Candy and Claus Classes is strictly limited. Candy and Claus Class Guests receive some extra surprises and treats along the way.
Seating in all carriages is arranged in a configuration of 4 seats as per normal train travel. North Pole Express always endeavour to ensure those who book more than 4 seats are seated in close proximity to each other to ensure they can enjoy the experience together. Children under the age of 2 and travelling on the lap of an adult travel for free.
Wheelchair access: Due to the age and design of the carriages it is not possible to board whist seated in a wheelchair as the entrance is stairs and the doorways are very narrow. However we will be pleased to convey passengers of limited mobility whenever possible provided they can step onto the train from the platform, climbing a step and move to their reserved seats with the help of an able bodied carer. Our crew would assist guiding the passenger up the step onto the train and arrange for the storage of the wheelchair in the guards van. The wheelchair must be able to be folded up and cannot be used on the train. Please let us know when booking if you need wheelchair assistance.

Photo credit: John Bovis
label: Kids & Parents

Children UNDER 2 years (0-23 months) and travelling on the lap of an Adult are FREE. All Passengers 2 years old and over must hold a purchased ticket.

Please note: Seating in our Candy and Claus Classes is strictly limited. Candy and Claus Class Guests receive some extra surprises and treats along the way.
Seating in all carriages is arranged in a configuration of 4 seats as per normal train travel. NPE always endeavour to ensure those who book more than 4 seats are seated in close proximity to each other to ensure they can enjoy the experience together. Children under the age of 2 and travelling on the lap of an adult travel for free.
Wheelchair access: Due to the age and design of the carriages it is not possible to board whist seated in a wheelchair as the entrance is stairs and the doorways are very narrow. However we will be pleased to convey passengers of limited mobility whenever possible provided they can step onto the train from the platform, climbing a step and move to their reserved seats with the help of an able bodied carer. Our crew would assist guiding the passenger up the step onto the train and arrange for the storage of the wheelchair in the guards van. The wheelchair must be able to be folded up and cannot be used on the train. Please let us know when booking if you need wheelchair assistance.

description:
Open Day at Otari Montessori Preschool, Otari Montessori Preschool
Where children grow into confident, capable, and caring people — through play, exploration, and real-world discovery.

We warmly invite Wellington families to come and explore Otari Montessori Preschool at our Open Day.

Come and meet our wonderful teachers, explore our environment, learn about our holistic and well-rounded programme, and see your child in action. Children will have the chance to engage with a variety of discovery activities, as well as explore our purpose-built outdoor deck and playground.
This is also a lovely opportunity to meet our warm parent community and enjoy a conversation over a warm drink and a snack.

At Otari Montessori, we are committed to delivering high-quality early childhood education, supporting our tamariki in their interests and learning about the world around them, while building strong foundations for social-emotional development.

We are also lucky to be situated in one of the most beautiful natural environments in Wellington, with Wilton’s Bush right on our doorstep for children to explore and enjoy.

As a result, our preschool environment supports children to:
• feel happy and secure coming to preschool
• build friendships and connect with others easily
• focus, persist, and stay engaged in what they do
• take initiative and grow in independence
• show kindness, empathy, and care for others

Our programme offers:
• learning through hands-on experiences, purposeful play, time outdoors, and plenty of free play with rich opportunities for social interaction with peers
• a rich and diverse holiday programme featuring arts, environmental exploration, and physical activities, including interactive Kelly Sports games
• weekly music sessions
• weekly bush walks
• a strong transition pathway: Playgroup → Preschool → Primary
• quarterly parent information sessions

This is a relaxed opportunity to visit, ask questions, and get a feel for whether Otari Montessori could be the right fit for your child and family — whether you are new to Montessori or already familiar with its core principles.

Please register your interest if you can, so we can plan for numbers — but you’re also very welcome to pop in on the day, even if you haven’t registered:
https://www.otaripreschool.school.nz/contact-us

We’d love to welcome you.

description:
Our Kids Online Parent Evening 2026, We want our school to be a safe place.

Because of the rapidly changing times, our tamariki are growing up in, and the mounting challenges and harms they are facing online we need to start talking about and tackling this as a community.
As such, Kapiti College has organised Filmmaker, Author and Speaker Rob Cope, producer of the documentary "Our Kids Online" to come and give what promises to be a humorous and eye-opening evening talk to our parent community.

His talk will cover:
Cyberbullying - How bullies can reach our kids 24/7
Social media - How social media is affecting the mental health in 3 out of 5 children. FOMO, depression, anxiety.
Gaming and the developing brain – An oversupply of dopamine leading to dopamine deficiency, synaptic pruning, and the underdevelopment of social skills and empathy
Naked Selfies - The pressure to send nudes from intermediate up through high school
Online predators - The methods they use, how to spot them.
Online porn vs healthy sexuality - How consuming online pornography as a child or teen can create a sexual template where violence, aggression, and dominance are seen as normal and consent can become very blurry
Solutions

Filters - Which filters are best and how to install them
Smartphones - How to lock down a smartphone to make it a safe phone
Boundaries - How to put good boundaries in place around device use
3 golden rules - The 3 golden rules that will keep your kids safe
Talking to your kids - How to have difficult conversations with your kids
Challenging our own phone and device usage - Reconnecting as a family.
"We need to tackle this as a community so that all of our kids are safe. When I protected my kids online, I also protected yours, so please, please protect your kids online so that you are also protecting mine" Rob Cope

description:
Pinhole Photography - Three Day Creative Arts holiday programme, Did you know that any object that can be made light tight can be turned into a camera? Come along to this three-day workshop and choose an object – it could be a tea pot, a book, a coffee jar – to turn into a pinhole camera to then create black and white photographs with.

We’ll work in the darkroom and explore the process of loading your camera with silver gelatin paper, before making exposures in the garden around the historic Inverlochy house, testing different angles and perspectives. We’ll then return to the darkroom to develop your photographic negative, and print it as a positive. You’ll leave the course with a series of atmospheric pinhole photographs, having experienced the magic of hands-on darkroom printing.

Bring a water bottle and morning tea. Recommended age for this course is tweens & teens ages 10 and above.

description:
Printing With Chine Colle - Creative Arts Holiday Programme for Teens, Welcome to mixed media collage, the printmaker's way. Chine Colle is a printing process in which a thin sheet of paper is printed on and, at the same time, mounted on a sturdier sheet, creating a subtle, delicate backdrop to the printed image. Expanded on, this can include contrasting papers, graphic images, select colour shapes and fabric. The mission is just to have fun creating together in the fabulous Inverlochy print studio.

In this one-day workshop for ages 12+, students will:

- Practice traditional and individual Chinese collage techniques
- Explore the use of delicate papers more responsive to ink and hand printing
- Test and practice mixed media chine colle with images, papers and fabric
- How effective Chinese Collage is as a method of adding colour to prints
- Making and using a damp pack
- Recipes for traditional glues

Bring a water bottle and a packed lunch to enjoy in the historic Inverlochy house during break time.

description:
Raising Great Kids In An Overindulgent World, Parenting today delivers unprecedented challenges – are you wondering what went wrong and somehow ended up living with a child you don’t recognise as should be belonging to you? Get a new perspective, an easy-to-understand model to follow and tools to help you to raise likeable and respectful children in an age of over-indulgence.

This workshop will be a confronting one that will expose you to the risks that children face in this modern overindulgent world. Many have become used to being the constant centre of attention and are unable to delay gratification and aren’t competent in everyday skills.

They have few self-care skills and skills relating to others, can’t take personal responsibility and don’t know what is enough or what is “normal” for others – these children end up having a difficult time of it in life and you will too.

You’ll take away new insight and knowledge plus strategies that you can apply that very night to help your child to be a responsible, likeable and respectful person.

By the end of the session, you’ll be able to:
- Reflect on the current context parents are faced with today
- Find the relevant research
- Practise the parenting tools and discuss the model
- Know where to go to get support

Aimed at parents, grandparents and caregivers of children of all ages.

Presented by Madeleine Taylor.

description:
STEAMS School BLENHEIM Term 1 2026, STEAMS is an integrated approach to learning topics of Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Maths, and Society that fosters critical thinking, problem solving, communication and collaboration. Its aim is to teach real world skills through engaging methods whilst allowing individuals to be creative. This involves immersing tamariki into projects and activities that develop innovation and champion curiosity. STEAMS is not ‘play based learning’ but focused learning through an integrated hands-on approach allowing children to take risks and explore their own curiosity in a subject without time barriers.
At the Ministry of Inspiration we offer STEAMS learning each term for Year 1-8 students. Once a week students will attend a class at Waterlea Racecourse, Blenheim on TUESDAY or THURSDAY. STEAMS Jr (ages 7-9) start at 9am and finish at 2:45pm on TUESDAY. Little STEAMerS operates from 9-12 on THURSDAY. STEAMS Sr (ages 10-13) operates on THURSDAY from 9am to 245 pm. 
Inquiry, collaboration, and an emphasis on process-based learning are at the heart of the STEAM approach. Each term the classes will have a focus which drives the learning and our amazing teachers create opportunities to help each student develop their understanding, improve their skills and gain knowledge in a range of topics.
Students who participate in STEAM learning:
· think outside the box
· feel safe to express innovative and creative ideas
· feel comfortable doing hands-on learning
· take ownership over their learning
· work collaboratively with others
· understand the ways that science, maths, the arts, and technology work together
· become increasingly curious about the world around them and feel empowered to change it for the better.
When does it meet, and where?
The school is held during school terms.
STEAMS Jr (ages 7-9) TUESDAY, 9-245.
STEAMS Sr (ages 10-13) THURSDAY, 9-245
Little STEAMerS (ages 5-6) THURSDAY 12-3.
Location:  Waterlea Racecourse, enter off of Linton St.
How much does it cost?
The students come for a paid three-week trial-as a new student you pay for that through Humanitix.
If both family and teacher feel there is a good fit for the child in the class, they continue for the rest of the term. You are then invoiced for the full term less the amount paid for the Trial.
Payment is by term, with a cost of $73 incl. GST We have a limited number of scholarships available that are awarded on a term by term basis for those with financial need for 25% off. 
Little STEAMerS is $30 incl. GST.
Will my child’s school mind that they miss a day per week?
You will need to inform the child’s school that he or she will be at STEAMS School one day per week. To date we have not encountered any issues around accommodating a child’s participation in STEAMS School, and many of the region’s schools are very supportive of the programme. Once enrolled, you are encouraged to inform the teacher and office staff that your child should be marked present for the day they attend STEAMS School, as they will be attending an academic school as opposed to being absent due to illness or other reasons.
label: Kids & Parents

description:
STEAMS School BLENHEIM Term 4 2025, What is STEAMS?
STEAMS is an integrated learning programme covering Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Maths, and Society. It focuses on real-world skills, critical thinking, collaboration, and creativity through hands-on, project-based learning—not play-based, but purposeful exploration without rigid time constraints.
Students are immersed in engaging, age-appropriate activities that encourage curiosity, innovation, and independent learning.
Key Benefits:
Students in STEAMS learn to:
Think creatively and critically
Collaborate and communicate effectively
Connect ideas across disciplines
Take ownership of their learning
Explore without pressure
Understand real-world applications
When & Where?
Weekly classes during school terms, based on age group and location:
Blenheim-Waterlea Racecourse
Class Times:
Little STEAMerS (Ages 5–6): TUES 11:30am–2:45pm
STEAMS Jr (Ages 7–9): TUES 9:00am–2:45pm
STEAMS Sr (Ages 10–13): THURS 9:00am–2:45pm
Cost
Trial (3 weeks): Pay via Humanitix (non-refundable)
Ongoing: $75/day (incl. GST)
Little STEAMerS: $30/day
Scholarships: 25% off for financial need (not available for Little STEAMerS)
School Absence?
Inform your child’s regular school—they’re attending STEAMS School. Most schools are supportive, and students should be marked as justified.

Join Steam Incorporated this School Holidays, as we invite you onboard our heritage train for a brilliant steam train ride for the whole family!

KidzStuff Theatre for Children brings the magic of live performance to your tamariki these July school holidays, a Wellington's family-friendly favourite since 1997. These 45-minute shows are packed with local Kiwi heart, inviting kids to enjoy a high-energy, theatrical escape. Make some memories and join the fun!

Written by the phenomenal Jenny Wake ONZM - a veteran of New Zealand Television and Theatre. In her television career, she wrote, directed and produced ‘Play School’, wrote for ‘Bumble’ and directed ‘What Now’. Jenny has travelled the word championing children's theatre. Street Dance Foundations with Shifting Centre at Māoriland, Manu Wairere is a school holiday programme at the Māoriland Hub in Ōtaki, designed to ignite the creative potential of tamariki and rangatahi Māori aged 5–18.

Rangatahi are invited to join Shifting Centre, a Wellington-based artist collective, for a 3-day Street Dance Foundations Workshop.

The workshop will conclude with a performance for whānau and friends.

A bat who is afraid of the dark encounters a glow worm who thinks she is a star. Themes of courage, friendship, and conservation are interwoven with a heartwarming story that introduces audiences to the unique and endangered short-tailed bat.

Stringendo - Wellington Children’s Orchestra, Stringendo is a training orchestra for school-age string players, founded in 2015 by Donald Maurice and Rupa Maitra. It offers early-level musicians, starting around grade 2, the opportunity to develop their skills in a fun and inclusive environment. Since 2022, the group has been directed by Alex Vaatstra and Hilary Ferral.

Stringendo extends its heartfelt thanks to the wonderful team at Ngaio Union Church for providing an excellent rehearsal space each Saturday afternoon for our weekly rehearsals.

On November 12th, Stringendo will perform a programme including pieces by Vivaldi, Telemann, Handel and more!




Feel free to bring a bag lunch to enjoy during the concert.

description:
StudyTime NCEA Revision Workshops, The upcoming October school holidays are a golden opportunity. While rest is important, these two weeks can also be used wisely to build momentum, fill knowledge gaps, and reduce stress heading into exam leave.
That’s where our holiday workshops come in. After a hiatus, Inspiration Education, in collaboration with StudyTime, is running NCEA Level 2 and 3 revision workshops from 1-3 October at Wellington Girls’ College.
Each session is two hours long and covers an entire external/topic, giving students the chance to:
Go over all the key content they’ll need for the exam
Learn exactly what the exam will be testing
Pick up strategies for tackling the harder Merit and Excellence questions
Receive a workbook to use in the session and keep for revision afterwards
Ask questions and get support from experienced tutors who’ve been through it all before
Why Attend?
These workshops are designed to:
Fill any gaps in knowledge
Build exam confidence
Kickstart motivation heading into Term 4
Spaces are limited and workshops often sell out quickly. Register now to secure your spot and head into exams feeling prepared, confident, and ready to succeed.

description:
Te Papa Whānau Day, This whānau day invites you to explore our deep connections within te taiao (the natural world).

ORO ATUA Wānanga Rongoā Puoro | 11am-12.30pm
A wānanga for all whānau, communities, and ages. Experience Jerome and Ruiha’s whānau practice of Taonga Pūoro Māori (Māori musical instruments) as Rongoā (healing), by coming together to help navigate the challenges of modern life.

Mauri Ora Art Workshop | 10am-2pm (drop-in)
Make your own artwork inspired by nature and pūrākau (Māori stories) with artist Ryan Cassidy. Learn te reo Māori and New Zealand Sign Language as you explore the patterns of the natural world.

Scale of the Universe Interactive | 10am-2pm (drop-in)
Navigate the visible and invisible through the interactive visual tool Scale of the Universe. Explore the scale of different organisms and objects, from the smallest particles to the largest galaxies.

Learn About Lichens | 10am-2pm (drop-in)
Are they fungi, algae, or bacteria? Join Fungi of Aotearoa author Liv Sisson to learn all about the lichens that live among us!

Free face painting by Daizy Designs | 10am-2pm (drop-in)

Gelli plate printing with Lara Shepherd | 10am-2pm (drop-in)
Join Te Papa’s resident evolutionary biologist, Lara Shepherd, to make prints using native plants.

Putting the 'Art' in 'Earth' tours | 11am and 1pm
These tours expand Te Papa's art floors, building dynamic connections between art-making and the environment.

Slow Looking | Times TBC
It’s International Slow Art Day! Take a closer look at a painting in these fun sessions. Local high school students will guide you – the longer you look, the more you’ll see!

Play is not only essential for tamariki and rangatahi development but also supports wellbeing, creativity, learning and social connection. description:
The Royal New Zealand Ballet presents Whānau Day 2026, Bring your whānau and spend the day exploring creativity, discovering the world of dance, and celebrating the joy of being uniquely you at St James.

Join us for a vibrant and inspiring Whānau Day at St. James, a special event designed to bring families together through dance, storytelling, and creativity. For the first time, this much-loved day will take over Theatre’s multiple spaces across Levels 1 and 2, the stage, and the Hospitality Suite, offering a wide range of interactive experiences for all ages.

This year’s event is inspired by the beautiful children’s ballet The Bomb, creating a day full of imagination, movement, and self-expression.

About The Bomb

Based on the award-winning book by Sacha Cotter, illustrated by Josh Morgan, The Bomb tells a powerful and uplifting story about finding your own voice. It follows a young boy determined to master the perfect “bomb” dive. With the help of his Nan, a former champion, and through learning to trust himself, he discovers that true success comes from embracing what makes him unique.

This meaningful story has captured the hearts of readers across New Zealand and has received multiple prestigious awards in 2019, including the Margaret Mahy Book of the Year.

https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=389888618397391

A Day for the Whole Whānau

With most activities completely free and something to engage every age group, Whānau Day is a welcoming and inclusive event for the whole community. Whether your child is trying dance for the first time, getting creative with crafts, or watching live rehearsals, there is something to inspire everyone.

description:
Understanding and Supporting Your Neurodivergent Child, Understanding and Supporting Your Neurodivergent Child: A Practical Parent Course

For parents and caregivers - gain practical, neuroaffirming tools to better understand, support, and advocate for your neurodivergent child/ren. This course explores neurodiversity foundations, sensory needs, regulation and behaviour, connection and co-regulation, and navigating supports in Aotearoa—alongside real-world strategies, advocacy guidance, and a focus on strengths that you can use at home and school. (NZ citizens and residents free with ID, others pay $120)

Description
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents. Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.

If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

This course is designed for parents and caregivers of neurodivergent tamariki who want practical, evidence-informed strategies to better support their child’s wellbeing, behaviour, and participation at home and school.

Across three sessions, we will explore the foundations of neurodiversity, including different neurotypes, strengths-based perspectives, and neuroaffirming language. You will gain insight into sensory processing, regulation, and the critical role of connection and co-regulation in supporting your child.

The course also provides guidance on navigating Aotearoa New Zealand’s health, education, and disability systems, including how to access supports and advocate effectively for your child. We will explore common challenges such as school refusal, burnout, and meltdowns, with practical strategies for prevention, in-the-moment support, and recovery.

There will be opportunities for discussion, reflection, and shared learning, as well as a Q&A-style panel session incorporating both professional and lived experience perspectives.

This is a group-based learning environment (not individual therapy), with an emphasis on practical tools, connection, and empowerment.

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

The StoryWalk® Wairarapa project was instigated by and is managed by Wairarapa Library Service.

Guiding this experience is local Speech Language Therapist Polly Newton, who will share simple, practical tips to help strengthen children’s speech, language, and literacy skills through the way you read with them.

The StoryWalk® is located on a flat, sealed path around the park, making it ideal for prams, wheelchairs, and scooters. Meet by the playground and enjoy a relaxed, family-friendly activity designed for children and their caregivers.

This event is part of the Wairarapa Walking Festival and is proudly supported by REAP Wairarapa, Chatterbox Wairarapa, and Speech Teacher. description:
Wellington Arborists Christmas Tree, Wellington Arborists Christmas Tree
Whilst we were putting the finishing touches on the tree last week we found a note from a chap called Kris Kringle:
****************************************************************
Dear WAL lads,

I had heard from the elven kind
That you had something grand in mind

I recalled your efforts from last year
As the elves gently whispered in mine ear

"Santa; this year's no exception and much like those bygone
A great distance away from North Pole;
a shimmering beacon shone

The WAL lads, they really do admire
A well lit tree and a cheerful shire!
Filled with laughter, joy and cheer
Santa you must go and see for yourself
They even said they'll shout ya a beer!"

So I harnessed up Rudolph and the gang
And off we went with a thundering bang!

Through the thick of night and over velvet snow
My sled flew high and far and then swooped in low
To allow my bespectacled eyes to see
The magnificence that is
The Wellington Arborists Christmas Tree

All across the land there are trees aplenty
But with this effort; you boys deserve a shanty!

To Mrs. Clause we hurried home with a story to tell
Knowing for certain; the Christmas spirit is alive and well!

Ho ho ho!
Kris Kringle
****************************************************************

Now that we have Santa's blessing we'll be officially lighting up the tree with a countdown at nightfall (around 9pm) this Friday 5th of December from 5:30pm onwards. If the weather turns we will push the event out to Saturday or worst case Sunday - hopefully MetService New Zealand can turn it on for us. The tree is on Heath Grove in Waiwhetu, Lower Hutt

description:
Whānau Chine Colle - Creative arts holiday programme for teens & adult, Welcome to mixed media collage the printmakers way. Chine Colle is a printing process in which a thin sheet of paper is printed on and at the same time, mounted on a sturdier sheet, creating a subtle delicate backdrop to the printed image. Expanded on, this can include contrasting papers, graphic images, select colour shapes and fabric.

This is a workshop whereby teens (minimum age 13) are encouraged to learn collectively with one of their favourite adults. Art can be created as a joint or individual project. The mission is just to have fun creating together in the fabulous Inverlochy print studio.

In this one day workshop people will:

- Practice traditional and individual chine colle techniques
- Explore the use of delicate papers more responsive to ink and hand printing
- Test and practice mixed media chine colle with images, papers and fabric
- How effective chine colle is as a method of adding colour to prints
- Making and using a damp pack
- Recipes for traditional glues

The house will be open 10am-4pm with entry by donation, including our current exhibition '75 Tinakori Road: 'This marvel had come to the lane".
From 10am plants from our garden raised by our wonderful volunteers will be sold as a fundraiser for Katherine Mansfield House & Garden. Plants priced from $5. Cash and card accepted, you may like to bring a box or bag to carry your plants home in.
At 11am Gabor Toth, local and New Zealand history specialist at Wellington City Libraries, will give a talk about Thorndon during the years Katherine Mansfield and her family lived on Tinakori Road.

description:

This two-day, self-drive garden tour will feature beautiful and unique gardens in North Wairarapa.

Highlights include…

Scenic Garden Trails
Wander through enchantingly designed gardens adorned with an abundance of native plants, exotic flowers, and captivating sculptures.

Meet the Gardeners
Gain insights from passionate gardeners who have nurtured these landscapes into works of art.

Exclusive Workshops
Learn gardening tips and tricks from experts, and uncover the secrets behind creating and maintaining a stunning garden.

The Market Fair
Indulge in delectable local cuisine and beverages and shop quality local handicrafts amidst picturesque surroundings.

Pick your gardens and choose your route according to whatever tickles your gardening fancy. The tour offers at least a dozen private gardens (not usually open to the public) to choose from. Gardens are revealed in the lead-up to tour weekend.

Locally-sourced and home-made refreshments will be available in selected gardens and BYO picnics are welcome in some gardens. Look for the icons to guide you.

description: 2026 Wairarapa Disability Expo, “Living Our Best Lives” is the tagline for the Wairarapa Disability Expo, which is being held in the Wairarapa Events Centre on Saturday, 28 February from 9.30 to 3.00. The expo will showcase the organisations in our region that are working together to ensure that no matter what the disability, there are services, resources and support to help disabled people lead meaningful lives of their own choosing. As well as exhibitors, there will be workshops and performances throughout the day. The expo is entirely free thanks to sponsorship from Wairarapa Building Society and Carterton District Council. The expo is organised by Good Lives Wairarapa, People First and the FERNZ Wairarapa Community Action Group.

description:
A Marvellous Miramar Christmas: 29 November (3 sessions), We've designed a Christmas experience for the whole family!
Come along and get into the Christmas spirit by joining in a marvellous Miramar Christmas extravaganza! As a family, come along and enter our amazing, indoor, interactive Christmas festival!
Enjoy hands-on crafts and activities together, get into some fun games at your own pace, listen and singalong to live music, let the younger tamariki have their space in a free-play area, tuck into our delish loaded free hot chocolates and cookie bar, get your annual whanau photo in our dress up photobooth, hear Christmas stories, take time to remember someone special at the remembrance tree... and many more merry and marvellous festivities!
Timing note: This year's Christmas event is a 'go-at-your-own-pace' session and you are welcome to leave when needed. Sessions/festival conclude 90mins after the start time.
Market note: While this event is designed to feel like a Christmas market/fair or festival - all experiences and crafts while in your session have no additional cost/are included. The only fee is the initial ticket fee.

TICKET DETAILS:
A Marvellous Miramar Christmas is all about getting into the Christmas spirit - our hope is that we can support families in the Miramar community through this event!
Tickets are $3 per child or adult / $13 for a group of 5.
Please note: if you require more than 5 tickets, please add any additional individual or group tickets to make up your group total.
All proceeds from this event will go towards providing Christmas gifts and support for families in the Miramar community. Thank you for your support!
Simply book tickets for your prefered session using this website! Please reserve tickets for any adults AND kids attending.


SESSION TIMES:
There are three A Marvellous Miramar Christmas sessions over the weekend. Each session is up to 90mins.
Saturday 29 November: 9.30 - 11am
Saturday 29 November: 11am - 12.30pm
Saturday 29 November: 1.30pm - 3pm
Please note: All children under the age of 13 must be accompanied by an adult.

RESERVE YOUR TICKETS ONLINE TODAY!
 Any queries, contact us on Facebook or email miramar.corps@salvationarmy.org.nz or call 04 388 8284

description:
Autumn Open Days and Plant Sales, Due to the wild storm we are currently experiencing we unfortunately need to cancel our first advertised open day on 22nd Feb.
Plants are still available to purchase by messaging me and arranging a collection time. Many varieties have already sold out so please don't wait until our open day to order.
We hope to be able to open from 8th March but will keep this page updated.
We invite you to visit our colourful garden as it transitions from its full summer exuberance of massed sunflowers and colourful perennials to the misty mauves of autumn Michaelmas and rich tones of dahlias and late perennials.
We have a garden of rooms, each with its own unique style. From bountiful borders, to the formality of topiary, the Zen of an Asian tea garden, the warmth of a graveled Mediterranean terrace, the lush jungle of a sub tropical styled garden and everything in between, we have something for you.
We also have many plants for sale, propagated here in our mini nursery.
For a list of plants available please see my earlier post. Plants can be purchased in advance so you don't mis out.
Please come and share in our joy of colour, garden and design at our suburban sized property for 2 Sundays only.
Entry is by donation and part of all collected will be passed on to our charity of choice The Malaghan Institute of Medical Research, Wellington who are making such fantastic advances in cancer treatments and other research.
We look forward to seeing you soon.
PLEASE SHARE THIS POST TO ALL IN WELLINGTON

description:
BOOK LAUNCH! Downstream from Nowhere by Johnny Crawford, Join 5ever books for the celebration and launch of Johnny Crawford's 'Downstream from Nowhere'!
Trades Hall, 124 Vivian Street
Friday 29 August 2025
6:30PM - whenevz
Free entry, all welcome, nibbles and drinks available, accompanied with sentimental words and live serenades.
~~~~~~
In the two centuries since the first Pākehā set foot in what would go on to be known as the Messines Valley, it has seen its fair share of history. Music Festivals. Failed settlements. Paranormal phenomena.
As the stolen land passed through the hands of church and state and capital, each left its mark. ‘Downstream from Nowhere’ follows this course through the eyes of the valley’s least reputable visitors.
~~~~~~
"Crawford sends us running straight into a tornado of intergenerational colonial mindsets, jingoistic historicism, and pop-cultural epochs, with a goat's head in one hand and a kebab in the other" - Jordan Hamel
Art by Miriam Collins, Sam Low and Nabilah Husna Binte Abdul Rahman. Cover designed by Achille Segard.

description:
Beyond the Bookshelves: Diversity in Austen Retellings, Join Rachel Pilios, passionate Austen lover (owner of over 30 copies of Pride and Prejudice) and Children's Book Buyer at Unity Books, for an illuminating exploration of diversity in contemporary Austen retellings. As a mixed-race, queer, and neurodiverse bookseller, Rachel brings a unique perspective to the rich tapestry of Austen-inspired literature.
In this talk, Rachel will showcase a curated selection of titles—all available through Unity Books—that reimagine Austen's beloved stories through diverse lenses. Discover queer retellings, tales set in other cultures, modern adaptations, and even Regency-era stories that amplify marginalized voices.
Attendees will gain a deeper appreciation for the breadth of the current Austen book market and its resonance with the modern world. Prepare to expand your reading list and discover exciting new perspectives on timeless classics.
Part of the Jane Austen Society of Aotearoa New Zealand's 2026 series on diversity.
Bring a friend: purchase 2 or more tickets and get a 10% discount
Who this event is for:
People who love Austen
People who love books
People who care about diversity
Afternoon tea provided

Image: Pride & Prejudice Pride flag by AmateurAusten (available for purchase on multiple items on Red Bubble)
Austen, Maths and Queer nerds unite! A take on Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice but you don't have to be an Austenite to appreciate the sentiment because Pride truly is Greater than Prejudice.
FAQs
Do I need to know about Jane Austen?
No. Everyone is welcome.
Do I need to be a member of the society?
We don't technically have membership, if you turn up we think of you as a member.
I have accessibility or dietary requirements
We aim to meet at venues that are accessible and provide for all dietary requirements. Please check out the accessibility section or contact us if you're unsure. We want you to be there and we want you to be comfortable.

description:
Blue Dragon Book Fair 2026, The Blue Dragon Book Fair 2026 will be held in the Ngaio Town Hall, as usual, on the weekend of 18 and 19 April. We are accepting donations of good-quality books, puzzles and board games from Saturday 21 March to 5pm Tuesday 14 April.
In recent years, we have been receiving huge numbers of donations for which we are very grateful. However, the space in the hall is tight, and our capacity to sort through so many donations needs to be managed. For those reasons, the 2026 book fair will NOT accept donations of:
• CDs, DVDs and records
• Travel guides, self-help books, business books and textbooks
• Food books and gardening books before 2020.
This decision is based on the fact that these books and CDs etc don’t sell very well but take up a lot of space.
We have a much-loved section of quality children's books for only $1 each. That's because the trustees all value reading and know how important it is for children to read.
Drop your donations from Saturday 21 March at Kennards Storage, 19 Hutt Road, in the downstairs area on the right-hand side, labelled 'Blue Dragon'. Please, no books after Tuesday 14 April. Kennards Storage is open M-F 8.30am-6pm; Sat 9am-5pm; Sunday 10am-4pm. It is closed on Easter Friday and open on Easter Monday from 10am to 4pm. Check Kennards’ website for opening hours
If you have any questions or want to help, please email us at bluedragonnz@gmail.com

description:
Bogan Day Out 2026, Bogan Day Out 2026
🚨GET READY FOR THE BIGGEST, BADDEST, BOGAN DAY OF YOUR LIFE!

BOGAN DAY OUT is back for 2026! You are in for the most epic day of the year right here at Brewtown, Upper Hutt – official home of the Bogan!

For just 35 bucks – Get ready for a wild ride with BBQ, Trucks, Chilli Eating, Live Music and all the bogan fun you can handle. Whether you’re an all-out Bogan or just Bogan-curious, if you’re into loud music, drag races, or just living your best life in a flannel shirt, we’ve got it all. Grab your mates, crack a cold one, and come ready for a day full of mayhem, laughs, and top-notch bogan antics!

My Big Bad Bogan Wedding!
This Bogan Day Out at Brewtown, were doing what no sane wedding planner would ever suggest- Brewtown is officially on the hunt for a never been married, 100% authentic bogan couple to tie the knot live at Bogan Day Out in front of other full-blown bogans. Imagine that – thousands of uninvited Bogans at your ceremony watching you bogans marry and cheering you on! This is iconic Upper Hutt.

🍖Our annual Brewtown BBQ comp is back and bigger than ever.
With NZ’s BEST BBQ teams throwin’ down the meatiest, smokiest cook-off you’ve ever seen! Prepare for a sizzling showdown of mouthwatering grills, smoky flavours, and next-level BBQ skills.

🎤Enjoy a full-throttle day of live music on the main stage.
The absolute BEST tribute acts in NZ will be bringing the heat all day long!

LINEUP COMING SOON!

🌶️Think you can handle the heat?
Step up to the Fire Dragon Chillie’s NZ Chilli Eating Champs and put your tastebuds to the ultimate test! This is no ordinary spice challenge—only the brave survive! Grab your guts, gear up for fiery fury, and see if you’ve got what it takes to be crowned the chilli champion!

Limited spaces! Reserve your spot when you purchase your ticket.

Still want more? We got you…
🥩Get ready to master the art of BBQ at the Black Dog BBQ Demo Stage! Learn tips, tricks, and secret techniques from the best pitmasters in NZ, and take your grilling game to the next level. Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just starting out, this is your chance to cook like a legend!

🚛Rev your engines and check out the big rigs at the Truck Displays! Get up close to some of the most massive and impressive trucks on the road, with epic custom builds and roaring engines that’ll leave you in awe. It’s a must-see for truck lovers and gearheads alike!

👚Hit up the market for all your BBQ, spicy food, and bogan essentials! From sizzling spicy sauces and mouthwatering meats to rad gear and bogan merch, you’ll find everything you need to take your BBQ game and bogan style to the next level. Don’t miss out on the best deals and wildest finds!

👑Reckon your Bogan style beats all others? Strut your stuff and be declared the Best Dressed Bogan or Maddest Mullet and win cool sh*t.

🍔Craving some epic eats? Our food trucks have got you covered, with mouthwatering BBQ delights for the true meat lovers and fiery, spice-loaded dishes for the brave! Whether you’re all about smoky, slow-cooked meats, chasing the burn with hot and spicy flavours, or something on the milder side there’s something to satisfy every craving. Come hungry and get ready for a flavour explosion!

🍻Feeling thirsty? A Brewtown event wouldn’t be complete without the Brewtown Bar pumping out the best beers and spirits brewed right here on site, as well as a load of Bogan Specials just for this event and the return of the popular Lion brown Bar!

You don’t wanna miss this – it’s the ultimate day out for all you legends!🤘

All ages event
Pass-outs permitted until 6pm
Last entry is at 6pm
Cashless event for bar and food. Some market vendors may accept cash.

description:
Ceramicus 2025, Now in its 67th year, Ceramicus returns to the Wellington Botanic Garden’s Begonia House from 5–15 November!
Presented by the Wellington Potters’ Association in partnership with Wellington City Council, this much-loved annual exhibition celebrates the creativity and diversity of contemporary ceramics in the Wellington region.
This year we’re thrilled to welcome Aaron Scythe as our Guest Selector and Featured Artist. Known for blending Japanese and New Zealand ceramic traditions, Aaron brings both mastery of technique and a spirit of experimentation to his work. His curatorial eye promises an exhibition that’s thoughtful, dynamic, and full of surprises.
Don’t miss our Pop-Up Pottery Market!
Alongside the exhibition, join us on 8 & 9 November and 15 & 16 November for the Ceramicus Pop-Up Pottery Market, held just outside the Begonia House. Browse and buy directly from local potters, explore a range of handcrafted ceramics—from elegant tableware to unique statement pieces—and take home something special. The market is free and open to everyone, a perfect way to meet the makers and support Wellington’s vibrant ceramics community.
Exhibition: 5–15 November 2025, 9am - 4pm daily
Begonia House, Wellington Botanic Garden
Pop-Up Market: 8 & 9 and 15 & 16 November, 10am - 3pm (weather dependent)
Free entry

description:
Coolmoves gold coin donation garage sale, We will be holding a gold coin donation garage sale once again. We donate our time and resources to collect donations of furniture, toys, tools, household items, craft supplies just about anything you can imagine well maybe not unicorns but you never know. We then donate our time and resources to sort the items and hold a garage sale where all items big or small sell for a gold coin each.
Weather permitting we will be holding a sausage sizzle and there may also be activites for kids and other things this will be updated closer to the time.
All items left over for from the garage sale are then sorted again and donated where possible the last 2 garage sales we have been able to provide Foster hope which copious amounts of books and clothing for children entering the foster system.
All proceeds from this garage sale will be donated to Kitty Kingdom Sactuary.
Kitty Kingdom Sactuary was set up by Alice just over half a decade ago with the aim of front line rescue for one vulnerable cat per month but this quicly grew from one kitty a month to dozens. They do amazing work feeding, caring, rehoming and providing vetenary care for vulnerable cats.
Our Charity garage sale helps out the community fourfold. People get to declutter, people get what they need at a a very low price, a charity gets a financial donation and we reduce the items going to the landfill.
We will start collecting items for the garage sale from the 7th of January so if you have something you believe would be suitable flick us an email with photos to coolmoves@coolmoves.co.nz.
You can find out more about Kitty Kingdom Sanctuary here
https://www.facebook.com/kittykingdomwellington
And Foster Hope here
fosterhope.org.nz
We look forward to seeing you on the 28th of February.
The Team at Coolmoves

Crop Up is Greytown's very own ultra-fresh, ultra-sustainable and ultra-tasty Saturday morning pop-up place to get your fresh food. It's all about crops, coffee and community.

Crop Up brings a blend of small farm suppliers, growers and local backyarders, offering their produce. As well as locally grown fruit and vegetables, there’s coffee, breakfast from The Baker, plus special guest pop-ups offering fresh-caught fish and other tempting products.

Our picnic tables are ready, and umbrellas are up for you and your friends to relax under. Catch up at Crop Up. It’s that kind of friendly place.

Crop Up is zero-waste and plastic-free. Crop Up is at Truckstop Greytown, 102 Main St.

description:
Eastbourne Garden Show, Step into a world of six acclaimed private gardens each a living canvas of colour, design and inspiration from lush natives to sculpted landscapes. Each garden tells a story and provides a visual image of wonderful creations.
One garden, allegedly with the best vista, has not been opened to the public before. One garden has previously featured in the House and Garden magazine. The tour (self-guided) will begin with lunch and an opportunity to buy potted plants in the tranquil St Alban's church garden, 11 Ngaio St Eastbourne, Lower Hutt, Wellington. The tour will end with hors d'oeuvre, wine and live music in the last garden.
This is a chance not just to visit amazing gardens but support the earthquake strengthening of St Alban's historic church and hall for a rejuvenated community hub.
St Albans church garden
The six private gardens all lie within a less than 100 m walk of the 83 Metlink Marine Parade bus route, but a car or bicycle would be more convenient.
A glimpse of the six separate gardens (a-e).

The garden show is in support of earthquake strengthening of the de Jersey Clere designed St Alban's church and adjacent hall to remake this a community hub.
For the last hundred years and more, this beautiful church designed by acclaimed architect Frederick de Jersey Clere has been the heart of Anglican parish life for people in the eastern bays of Wellington. People have rejoiced, prayed and wept in it through happy family milestones and sad occasions, through two world wars and countless celebrations and crises. Along with its parish hall and tranquil garden, it has been the base for social and community services and outreach, and its memorial wall houses the ashes of local residents.
But in 2016 the congregation had to suddenly leave the church, which was deemed an earthquake risk.
Since then, the parish has explored alternatives for continuing its life and service to the people of the eastern bays. In that process it has kept its ministry and worship going through borrowed premises in local schools and other churches. Now, however, the parish has decided it needs to go back to its original base and strengthen both St Alban’s Church and the parish hall so it can continue to serve the community from its heart and home in Ngaio Street, for the next hundred years and more.
Detailed plans for strengthening the church and hall to meet acceptable safety standards have been drawn up, and fund-raising is under way. The parish is a registered charity (CC22188) and tax-deductible receipts will be issued for all donations.
Postponement by 1 day to 30 Nov if weather were to dictate and would be announced on this web site.

The first Fabric-a-brac was held in Wellington 15 years ago - we're sew excited to still be here, bring the sewing community together and raising money for Mary Potter Hospice.
Fabric-a-brac is a fun fabric and sewing supplies market where you can shop for vintage and modern sewing and upholstery fabric, patterns, haberdashery and more. It brings the sewing community together to share stashes, stories and delight in our mutual love of textiles.
Fabric-a-brac is volunteer-run, and is a fundraiser for hospice - in Wellington this is Mary Potter Hospice. All profits from this event are donated to their work. We've raised $80,000 since our first event in 2009.
Selling fabric
If you have a stash you'd like to sell, you can come and take a stall. You pay a stallholder fee (which goes to Hospice) but anything you make on the day is yours to keep. Stalls are allocated via a ballot, which will take place closer to the time. Go to our website to find the form. Closes mid August.

If you have fabric, haberdashery or patterns you'd like to move on, but don't want to have a table, you can donate items. This will all go onto the hospice table on the day, and all profits will go to their wonderful work.
Fabric donation points
- Made Marion
- Mary Potter Hospice - you can take donations to the Mary Potter Hospice in Mein St, Newtown

Pop-up cafe
The fabulous cafe is back with all of its gorgeous volunteers and fab food. There will be tea, coffee and sweet treats for sale, so you can sit down and chat over your new projects and fabric purchases. All proceeds from the cafe also go to Hospice.
Buying fabric
Bring cash - most stallholders and the cafe will be selling by cash only.
We look forward to seeing our fabulous fabric and sewing community soon!
*Saturday September 20 2025
*St Anne's Parish Hall, Emmett Street, Newtown, Wellington

🎄 Support Kāpiti Chorale at the Paekākāriki Christmas Market! 🎄

Kāpiti Chorale has been described as “a jewel of the Kāpiti Coast,” and we’re proud to keep bringing interesting and imaginative music programmes to audiences across the Kāpiti Coast and Wellington region.

As with many community groups, we occasionally run fundraising efforts to help keep our concerts accessible and enjoyable for everyone.

This year, we’ll be at the Paekākāriki Christmas Market on Saturday 13 December, from 10am to 2pm, and we’d love to see you there.

Our stall will be full of festive treats: homemade goodies, jams (including delicious lemon curd), hand-knitted colourful hats and crowns, tissue boxes, and more, all generously donated by talented members and friends of the choir.

💛 Come say hello, pick up something lovely, and help support what we do. Every dollar makes a difference.

We welcome donations of baking and distinctive craft items.
If you’d like to help, please contact Bill Gebbie at 027 677 0180.

Greytown School Country Food Fair, Join us at Greytown School for a country-themed food fair on Opening Night! Just a few steps away from Main St (follow signs through Stella Bull Park), the school children will have delicious, family-friendly food, drinks and sweet treats for sale with proceeds going towards a Shade Solution for the Greytown School Playground.

The event will kick off at 3pm with games, vintage machinery and tractors that kids can sit on - so head into town early to nab a carpark and relax while your kids enjoy their safe, fenced school grounds. The school will have seating, toilets, pram parking for the entire event (if you don’t wish to navigate Main St with it) and even a cosy parents’ room for feeding babies.

Grab a yummy dinner from the stalls, then head to Main Street to watch the Light Up Tractor Parade at 6pm.

description:
Houghton Valley School Fair, Join us for our famous little school fair on Wellington's wild South Coast!

It's a fabulous day out for the whole family. We have something for everyone: bouncy castle, cute bunnies and lambs, candyfloss, pre-loved clothes, toys, book stall, raffles and silent auction, plants and exquisite handmade crafts. description:
Hutt City Night Market - 29 January 2026, Hutt City Night Market – Tomorrow Night!
Lower Hutt, it’s time to eat, explore, and enjoy the sun! Join us tomorrow at Dowse Square from 4 PM – 8 PM for a gorgeous evening filled with incredible food, family fun, and friends.
Here’s the delicious lineup of food trucks you won’t want to miss:
IndoPlus – Savor the rich, aromatic spices of authentic Indonesian dishes, from tender satay skewers to flavorful nasi goreng.
Mao & Co – Comforting Chinese street eats, from dumplings and bao buns to classic stir fried favorites.
Ah Mas Kitchen – Crispy, golden fried chicken with mouthwatering marinades and sides that will keep you coming back for more.
Kai Kart – Taste the best of New Zealand with traditional seafood, succulent burgers, and hearty Kiwi classics.
Gully Food Truck – Crunchy, hand cut potato sticks and refreshing mango lassis perfect for cooling down on a sunny evening.
Habibi Food Truck – Delicious halal food, packed with bold Middle Eastern flavors, from spiced meats to fresh salads.
Paps Tacos – Authentic Mexican tacos with vibrant fillings, zesty salsas, and all the toppings you can dream of.
Greek Food Truck – Mediterranean delights, from juicy souvlaki wraps to creamy tzatziki and fresh Greek salads.
Roti Bay – Savory Sri Lankan curries and roti, full of fragrant spices and hearty flavors.
Cosa Nostra – Hand stretched pizzas and classic pasta dishes, all cooked with love and authentic Italian flair.
Chi-Chi’s Lemonade – Freshly squeezed lemonade, fruity and refreshing, perfect for sipping while you stroll the market.
Acai Me! – Bright and healthy acai bowls and fruit dessert treats that taste as good as they look.
Samoan Taste – Island inspired dishes, from coconut infused delights to tropical flavors that transport you straight to the Pacific.
Pinoy Street Food – Filipino street eats, from sweet and savory skewers to hearty traditional bites that capture the soul of the islands.
Little Bread Loaf – Freshly baked pastries, breads, and sweet treats that smell irresistible and taste even better.
Get Your Crêpe – French style crêpes filled with decadent or fruity goodness, perfect for a sweet evening treat.
Croffle – The ultimate hybrid of croissant and waffle, crisp on the outside, soft and buttery inside.
Chayen Thai Tea – Creamy ice creams and authentic Thai tea drinks that are both refreshing and indulgent.
Berry Lush – Chocolate-covered strawberries that are as beautiful as they are delicious, perfect for sharing… or not!
New this week: Ian Thrift NZ – Explore a treasure trove of vintage and second hand clothing, shoes, and accessories for all ages.
Bring your family, friends, and appetite, soak up the sunshine, and make the most of the last few days of the holidays at Hutt City Night Market!
Dowse Square, Lower Hutt
4 PM – 8 PM

description:
International Cat Day Flash Tattoo Event, The Gallery Tattoo's International Cat Day Event!
In association with Found-A-Feline Cat Rescues, to continue their Support-Search-Rescue-Reunite mission.

Doors open at 9:45am. First tattoo starts at 10am.
First in first served. Get in early to secure your spot!

One off designs, priced between $150 and $350.

Found-A-Feline raffle running alongside the event with tattoo prizes worth over $1000. Be in to win.

Market stalls running all day with amazing items on sale.
Featuring:
Bow wow boutique - The Bow Wow Meow Cat Collection
NZ-Made pet supplies and human accessories.
Showcasing their cat collection for this event. Custom collars, leads and harnesses, and treats galore.

The Gallery
Our very own artists Spectral Grace, Stella Nova, and Ashen Creations are joined by Vibrant Violet creations
offering up a varied selection of art prints, sculptures, stickers, and more.

In Stitches
Kitschy, fun, crochet, yay!
We at In Stitches Crochet NZ love how crochet can make usable art. With an emphasis on fun, In Stitches
delivers high quality, handmade goods (including catnip toys!).
3% of all sales are donated to the NZ Endangered Species Foundation

Spooky Delights
Spooky Delights brings you alternative and mysterious curiosities, jewelry and upcycled pieces. Fun gift ideas,
and special trinkets, ideal for all purveyors of treasures!

Shay Likes Orange
Shay Likes Orange is a Wellington-based Artist and Graphic Designer with a passion for painting cats. You will likely see them at the local art-markets, just look for a bright orange stall.

Enchanted Moon - Cute kitty stuff, cupcakes, temporary airbrush tattoos while you wait for the real thing!

Let's celebrate the joy these beautiful creatures bring to our lives by adorning our bodies and homes with art dedicated to them

* Indoor & outdoor plants

* Ceramics, planters & garden decor
* Natural skincare & eco beauty products
* Seedlings, garden tools & plant accessories

description:
Lightbody Jewellery Pop-Up at Copperfield Collective, Lightbody Jewellery Pop-Up at Copperfield Collective
✨ Lightbody Jewellery Pop-Up at Copperfield Collective ✨

Saturday 6th September · 11am – 2pm · Paraparaumu

For one day only, Lightbody Jewellery is journeying to Paraparaumu.

We’re honoured to be welcomed into Copperfield Collective, bringing with us a collection of our most sought-after treasures.

💫 Meet the maker – learn the stories and symbols hidden in every piece.

💫 Try on sacred treasures – jewellery alive with meaning, energy, and transformation.

💫 Feel the magic woven into silver and gold – creations that choose their keepers.

About Lightbody Jewellery

We are a small New Zealand brand, born from nothing but vision and persistence, built piece by piece, story by story. Lightbody Jewellery grew out of a desire to carry ancient symbols into the present, weaving spirit into matter so that jewellery could once again guide, teach, and protect.

Every pendant, ring, and talisman is handcrafted here in Aotearoa with intention. They are not made to follow trends, they are made to awaken, to empower, to transform.

What began as a spark has grown into a living brand carried by intuition, mystery, and craft. Each piece finds its keeper when the time is right.

This pop-up at Copperfield Collective is more than a display.
It’s a rare chance to meet the maker, hold the work, and feel which treasure has been waiting for you.

✨ Lightbody Jewellery Pop-Up
📍 Copperfield Collective - 17 Seaview Road, Paraparaumu Beach
📅 Saturday 6th September

description:
Nevers (France/Australia) / Jean-Philippe Gross (solo) / Oghum, Nevers (France/Australia) / Jean-Philippe Gross (solo) / Oghum
Nevers
Featuring Clare Cooper (Australia) on guhzeng and Jean-Philippe Gross (France) on electro-acoustic devices, Nevers sometimes sounds like a fire in an electronic flea market, other times like the amplification of an insect funeral march. The duo finds common ground between Clare Cooper’s Chinese guhzeng and Jean-Philippe Gross’ lo-fi microphones, electroacoustic devices and localized speaker system.



Strasbourg’s Jean-Philippe Gross will also perform a solo set, of electronic music using a dedicated feedback system.
https://jeanphilippegross.com/

Clare Cooper is a musician and Design Lecturer from Sydney. Her work in creative community projects includes collaborative composition, speculative design, and critical listening. She co-founded the NOW now (2001), Splinter Orchestra (Sydney 2000), Splitter Orchester (Berlin 2009), and Frontyard Projects (2016).

Jean-Philippe Gross (Strasbourg – France) is a composer and improviser, performing with a dedicated feedback system often utilising multiple small speakers positioned around the performance space. In the studio, he continues his research with a “Serge modular system”. He has composed music for dance and performance, as well as for contemporary ensembles such as Ensemble Dedalus.

Nevers is presented with the support of Rise / La Muse en Circuit - Musica.

---

Oghum is the interstellar duo of Nell Thomas (Orchestra of Spheres, Cookie Brooklyn and the Crumbs) and Jonny Marks (All Seeing Hand, Mean Bones), performing on Synthi AKS, theremin and other assorted items. Oghum blends electronic sounds from times past with an array of acoustic and found sounds, using nuanced improvisation to create detailed and tangible sonic environments, invoking memory and transporting the listener through narrow gaps into wide open otherworldly spaces.

$20 presale tickets via UTR

Special thanks to CNZ for supporting Pyramid Club's programme

Not Your Nana's Craft Market - R18 Art and Craft Market, *Strictly R18*
Are you ready for a unique and thrilling experience? Look no further! We invite you to the most captivating event of the year - the Creepy-Cute, Witchy, Kinky, Sexy, LGBTQIA+ Friendly Alternative Art and Craft Market!

description:
Old St Paul's Craft & Curio Market, Discover Wellington’s Most Enchanting Market!
Set against the breathtaking backdrop of one of Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s most iconic heritage landmarks, the Old St Paul’s Craft & Curio Market is a boutique shopping experience like no other.
As part of this year’s Wellington Heritage Festival, the grounds of Old St Paul’s will be transformed into a vibrant marketplace filled with handpicked stalls offering treasures and treats you won’t find anywhere else. Explore lovingly crafted leather goods, upcycled garments, wellness creations, handmade chocolates, collectibles and curiosities, dyed wool, children’s accessories and clothing, fine embroidery, jams and preserves, artisan breads and baked goods, Christmas decorations, candles, and so much more.
But it’s not just shopping – this is a day steeped in atmosphere. The lawn and forecourt will come alive with heritage-themed games and activities, alongside captivating live demonstrations from the Wellington Embroiderers’ Guild and the Wellington Combined Society of Bellringers.
With its central location just minutes from the Railway Station and bus hub – and plenty of on-street parking – this is your chance to enjoy a heritage day out that’s easy to get to, and unforgettable once you arrive.
Fun for the whole whānau, supporting the ongoing care of this national treasure.
Schedule:
Guided tours of Old St Paul's: 10.30am/11.30am
Wellington Combined Society of Bellringers demonstration: 12.00pm-12.45pm
Wellington Embroiderers' Guild stitching demonstration: 10.00am-2.00pm
Organ performance: 1.00pm-2.00pm
Koha entry. Refreshments available.

Ōtaki Kids Market Pops Up at Coastlands During the School Holidays

The Ōtaki Kids Market is hitting the road these school holidays, bringing its creativity, colour, and energy to Coastlands Shopping Town in Paraparaumu.

The pop-up market will give young entrepreneurs the chance to showcase their talents, products, and business skills to a wider audience – all while inspiring others their age to dream big.

📍 Coastlands Shopping Mall, Paraparaumu
📅 1st, 2nd, 3rd October
🕙 10am-2pm

Otaki Kids Market, Otaki Kids Market
🎨🛍️ Otaki Kids Market is back on Sunday, 5 October 2025 🎉 Rangatahi and tamariki get ready to showcase your creativity.
Let's celebrate the power of young minds and crafts! 🌟👦👧

The Otaki Kids Market is a vibrant and creative event that provides a unique platform for young entrepreneurs to showcase their talents and entrepreneurial spirit.

This special market invites tamariki and rangatahi from 5-19 years old to become stall holders, offering them the opportunity to sell their handmade art and crafts, delicious home baking, toys, and books.

#OtakiKidsCraftMarket #YoungArtistsUnite

description:
Otaki Market - April, Nau Mai Haere Mai, meet you at the Market.
Discover a vibrant outdoor market nestled on State Highway One in Ōtaki, just across from New World. Join us to greet our regular stallholders and special guests from the community.
---
PARKING
There is plenty of free parking available at the Otaki train station.
Main Highway is a perfect spot for customers to the market
60 Minute Parking zone behind Riverstone Cafe.

CASH / ATM
Some vendors have eftpos, and all take cash. There is an ATM located on the main highway.

FOOD VENDORS
And when hunger strikes, our lineup of food trucks and stalls is ready to tantalize your taste buds. From waffles to hangi, seafood chowder to fry bread, sausage sizzles, and a delectable assortment of rice, noodles, and home baking – a feast awaits.

BUSKER
We often have an awesome busker, who'll be playing chilled out middle of the road tunes.

- Art & Craft
- Native trees, flowers and plants
- Candles, soaps and wax melts
- Antiques and collectables
- Produce, including yummy honey!
- Pre-love clothing, shoes and accessories
- Tools for the home and garden
- Toys and books for tamariki

---
STALL HOLDERS
Would you like to be a stall holder?
Join our market family, fill out the enquiry form: www.otakiwomensclub.org/stall-holder

description:
Otaki Women's Community Club Meeting, Come along and join the Ōtaki Women’s Community Club
Meet amazing wāhine, connect with other local women, share a few laughs, feel inspired, and learn together in a warm, welcoming, and safe space with like-minded women. We get together for a club meeting, then have dinner.

Keen to come to a meeting? Email us at otakiwomensclub@outlook.com

The Ōtaki Women’s Community Club is also the heart behind the much-loved Ōtaki Market and Ōtaki Kids Market. Through this, the club supports local businesses, brings people together through community events, and helps strengthen connections across Ōtaki.

Whether you’d love to volunteer, meet new friends, share your skills, or simply be part of something positive in your community, there’s a place for you at ŌWCC.
label: Markets & Fairs

description:
Otaki and Te Horo Producers Market, Otaki and Te Horo Producers Market
We’re teaming up with the Otaki and Te Horo Business Association for a special Producers Market

A vibrant local market showcasing fresh, seasonal produce, handmade goods, and artisan treats from Otaki and Te horo. Brings together the community to support small businesses, enjoy live music, and discover unique, locally made products.


Producers (From Otaki and Te Horo)
🍎 Fresh Fruit & Veggies
💐 Beautiful Blooms, trees and plants
🥚 Free-Range Eggs
🫒 Local Olives & Olive Oil
🌱 Seasonal Produce
☕ Coffee & Tea
🍯 Small Batch Jams, Chutneys & Honey
🍷 Crafted Wine, Cider, Beer, Spirits & Liqueurs
🍹 Juices & Non-Alcoholic Beverages
🍫 Sauces, Chocolates & Sweets
🍦 Ice Cream, Cream, Milk, Cheese & Dairy Products
🍞 Crackers, Breads, Pies & Pastries

ENQUIRE: www.otakiwomensclub.org/producers-market
- All producers must be based within Otaki & Te Horo boundaries.
- Producers must grow or produce their own products


Craft Stalls & Food Trucks:
Art & Craft, jewellery, earrings, soaps, original art, candles. Plants, flowers, trees, garden art. Collectables (limited to five sites). Handmade craft, health and beautify.
ENQUIRE: www.otakiwomensclub.org/stall-holder

description:
Out in the City 2026, Out in the City 2026
We’re celebrating 40 years to the day since the Gay & Lesbian Fair in Newtown on 15 March 1986 began what has become the Wellington Pride Festival. Be part of our all-day family friendly fair event with stalls, stage performances, delicious food and drink and a jam-packed day of LGBTTQIA+ celebration and vibes.

If you’re coming into Te Whanganui-ā-Tara for Pride, you don’t want to miss this event - it’s our biggest, and it’s free! Come down and hang out, can’t wait to see you there.
