description:
Pirates of the CariBlenheim, Pirates of the CariBlenheim
🏴‍☠️ Pirates of the CariBlenheim – Search for the CBD Treasure 🏴‍☠️
📍 The Forum, 54 Market Street, Blenheim CBD
📅 28 February 2026
⏰ Event runs from 10:00am – 12:00pm

Ahoy, young pirates! ⚓
Pirates of the CariBlenheim is a pirate-themed treasure hunt taking place across the Blenheim CBD. Participants will visit CBD store to collect pieces of a puzzle which, once fully assembled, will reveal a destination leading to the infamous Two Pieces of One.

🗺️ How It Works
Meeting point: The Forum
Collect your event map and first puzzle piece
Visit participating store to collect pieces of the puzzle
Assemble the full puzzle to reveal the destination to the treasure
The completed puzzle is the key to open the treasure box

⏰ Important Times
Clue distribution closes at 12:00pm sharp
Final destination open until 2:00pm

☠️ What to Bring
Parents or guardians must bring:
- A3-size or bigger cardboard or firm backing
- Sticky glue or tape
These items are required to help assemble the puzzle pieces as they are collected.

👨‍👩‍👧 Parent / Guardian Guidelines
To ensure a safe and enjoyable event for everyone, please note:

Age Limit
This event is for children aged 13 years and under only.

Map Piece Collection & Assembly
Each participating business will provide one puzzle piece. All pieces must be collected and correctly assembled to complete the challenge.

Prizes
- The first 10 groups to correctly complete the challenge will receive major sponsored prizes.
- Participants will also have the chance to win from a pool of over 250 store vouchers from participating businesses (one voucher per child, maximum of two per group or family).
- All other participants who successfully complete the hunt will be entered into a prize draw for additional prizes.
- A completed puzzle is required to receive any prize.

Costumes
Pirate-themed attire is required to participate 🏴‍☠️

Supervision
Children must be accompanied by a parent or guardian at all times.

Participating Locations
Only visit store displaying the official Pirates of the CariBlenheim poster. Some locations may be mystery stores and clues will be provided.

Conduct & Respect
Please treat staff, volunteers, and other participants with courtesy and follow all instructions.

Responsibility
Parents and guardians are responsible for their child’s safety, supervision, and behaviour throughout the event.

Clayton Knowles – 021 579 533 |

description:
Plant Sale, I have had great success with NZ and imported seed propagation this year so we have a wonderful range of plants ready to go in the ground now.
Some varieties are extremely limited due to the cost of the imported seed and the tiny amount of seeds per packet (only 5 in some cases).
We will be accepting preorders by messenger so get in quick if you don't want to miss out on these special plants.
$7.50 each or multiples of 3 $20
Please note: Our garden will not be open during the plant sale. We aim to open in approximately 5 weeks but it depends how the tulips progress.
As other plants reach maturity we will make them available for sale on our open days. We have decided to have a pre season sale to make room for more beauties.
Abutilon - a range of mixed colours including peach, rose and lemon.
Dwarf Agapanthus - a fine leaved pale blue variety. Great for edging paths and beds. Will not take over.
Aubretia - Lavender trailing plant for rock walls and garden edges.
Arabis - White blooming Spring groundcover
Ajuga - Pink and purple varieties. Great November blooming groundcover for damp areas.
Aster - Early summer flowering variety in blue/lavender
Calamintha - new for us so I shall borrow the Chiltern seeds description. This is a most pleasant plant for your border or herb garden. Heavily scented with a fragrance described as pennyroyal-like, it is an erect perennial with small, somewhat hairy leaves. In summer it bears numerous whorled spikes of tiny blue flowers with long purple bracts. The herb can be used for flavouring. Flowers the first year from seed. 1½ft (45cm).
Campanula glomerata - deep purple
Cerastium - grey trailing leaves smothered in white blooms in Spring. (These have just been cut back)
Cerinthe - By popular demand. Technically an annual but a non invasive self sowing one so once its in your garden you'll have more each year. Glaucous foliage and interesting pendular purple blooms.
Dianthus - Grey leaves and red blooms
Erigeron multiradiatus - A beautiful evergreen groundcover with yellow centred purple/blue daisies from late spring.
Erysimum - a specialty for us as we love them so much. What's not to love? Front to mid border, semi shrubby evergreen perennial, glorious scented blooms and we have individual named colours.
Ivory, Purple bi-colour, Fire King, Vulcan, Ellen Willmott, Primrose, Ruby gem, Siberian allionii and the brand new Tangerine Titan.
Euphorbia - golden foam. Another newbie for us but we love the the chartreuse euphorbias add to the garden so we had to give it a go.
Euphorbia characias - the blue leaved evergreen semi shrubs with huge chartreuse heads that grace our garden every spring.
Geum - Yes, you guessed it, another favourite of ours. We have a good stock of the common types plus some more unusual ones.
Tall - Yellow, Red and Orange (Firestorm).
Dwarf - Deep orange/red, Lemon with hints of pink, blush (very pale pink) and the original geum rivale in a beautiful coppery peach.
Lunaria (Honesty). Two types available. Chedglow the purple leaf version that has taken Chelsea by storm the last couple of years. Variegata - the green leaves become edged in white in their second year before blooming with the typical mauve flowers.
Lysimachia nummularis - yellow creeping jenny. Great lime leaf trailing plant for part shady damp areas. One only.
Orlaya grandiflora - another favourite among designers. A self sowing annual that will provide weeks of beautiful white lacecap flowers. Perfect for filling in border spaces until the summer perennials fill in or to give a light airy feel to meadows and spring plantings. Seedlings will return year after year.
Pelargonium - Deep red
Pulmonaria - Raspberry splash
Romulea - small bulbs grow fine grassy leaves before erupting into a mass of deep rosy purple crocus type flowers in late spring.
Scabiosa - another specialty plant for us as they provide such amazing flower power all summer and autumn. They are not frost hardy but are perennial in sheltered spots for at least 3 years. Enjoy the flowers and at the end of the season collect several packets worth of seed to multiply your stock.
Named varieties available:
Snowmaiden - white, Black Knight - deep maroon, Beaujolias Bonnets - a gorgeous blend of pink, white and burgundy on the same flower, Burgundy beau - a new one this year, Salmon Queen - the most delicious shade of salmon pink. Pale yellow Fata morgana, and blue ones will be available later in the season.
Stachys officinalis - dark pink flowered evergreen groundcover. Perfect for the front of garden beds and rock gardens.
Sissyrinchium blue eyed grass. Low grassy leaves burst in to a mass of blue star shaped flowers in Spring.
Sedum mexicana - a bright lime evergreen succulent groundcover. Perfect for supporting bold tulips in spring and bright perennials in summer.
Sedum Mr Goodbud. A slightly pinker version than the well known Autumn joy.
Sparaxia - very special maroon flowers. Couple only.
Symphytum grandiflora - low-lying evergreen groundcover with medium sized leaves and stunning cream bell flowers all through spring. Excellent spreading plant for difficult to grow areas such as the shade of evergreen trees.
Urospermum - sown last spring and flowered for the first time in summer. Don't be put off by its dandelion looking leaves. This is a beauty with huge lemon flowers ( yes again like a dandelion but oh so much more beautiful). It has survived a wet winter in our gravel garden and also in soil. Definitely not a weed!
Violets - green leaf with white scented flowers and the later flowering purple leaved Viola labadorica with purple flowers.

Sedum mexicana - a bright lime evergreen succulent groundcover. Perfect for supporting bold tulips in spring and bright perennials in summer.
Sedum Mr Goodbud. A slightly pinker version than the well known Autumn joy.
Sparaxia - very special maroon flowers. Couple only.
Symphytum grandiflora - low-lying evergreen groundcover with medium sized leaves and stunning cream bell flowers all through spring. Excellent spreading plant for difficult to grow areas such as the shade of evergreen trees.
Urospermum - sown last spring and flowered for the first time in summer. Don't be put off by its dandelion looking leaves. This is a beauty with huge lemon flowers ( yes again like a dandelion but oh so much more beautiful). It has survived a wet winter in our gravel garden and also in soil. Definitely not a weed!
Violets - green leaf with white scented flowers and the later flowering purple leaved Viola labadorica with purple flowers.

description:
Steiner School Fair 2025, Nau Mai Haere Mai ki te Raphael House Steiner School Fair. The School Fair is our major annual fundraiser hosted by the school community. Its purpose is to celebrate the school’s education and culture with the wider Wellington Community.

Each year students, teachers and parents work together to transform the school environment. Activities, displays, artistic presentations, gift stalls and food offerings provide a venue for community engagement that is a highlight on the school’s annual calendar.

Dive into a world of magic and imagination at our Annual Fair! Join us for a day fueled by holistic education, creative adventures and community togetherness.

Throughout the year, parents, students and teachers get together to transform our school into a mystical, sensory wonderland.

Explore and shop from a delightful array of unique, handcrafted crafts, toys, and Seasonal treats. This is where nature, creativity and heartwarming experiences come together to nurture young minds and inspire families.

Kindergarten parents create small gifts, from natural, materials which the young child will receive in the Little Peoples room. The handwork room is lovingly and thoughtfully prepared with the sensory experiences and impressions of the young child in mind.

Other parents are busy with tasks like creating Christmas crackers and decorations and researching new and exciting tantalizing recipes for the two cafes.

The Teaching faculty gathers students' work, from Kindergarten to Class 12 (Year 13), which are on display in the Eurythmy Room. If you have ever wondered what a main lesson book is you are bound to find one, or more, here!

To ensure there is fun for everyone we even create games to play both indoors and out. Then to add to the atmosphere during the day you will hear the sound of music and singing, and even some dancing while enjoying an organic coffee. The School Fair is a great day for all.

Skip the traffic - There is very limited parking around the school area, so please make use of our Fair Shuttle Bus - every 30 minutes to and from Melling Station. Gold coin per person per trip.

description:
TRI GEAR GARAGE SALE - Support Youth Fund, TRI GEAR GARAGE SALE + CLUB CATCH UP Under the Club tent

Supporting the Tri Wellington Youth Fund
Got tri gear gathering dust. Someone else probably needs it.
On Sunday 1 February 2026 at the Wellington100, we’re turning Tri Club tent into a Tri Gear Garage Sale (don’t worry, free sausages post-race from our awesome sponsor Pak N Save will still be there) . Think pre loved tri gear, good yarns, a sausage in hand, and doing some real good for the future of our sport.
Here’s how it works:
• Members donate tri gear to sell ahead of time (details below). Bikes, shoes, wetsuits, kit, accessories, the lot
• Buyers grab a bargain
• All proceeds go to the Tri Wellington Youth Fund (sellers give 100% of their sale to the fund).
Why it matters

The Youth Fund helps our young triathletes when it counts most. Covering things like race entries, gear, accommodation, and coaching. This is about keeping the sport accessible and backing the next generation of TriWelly legends.
Gear drop off
Please drop donated items by 25 January at either:
• Pedal Project - 158 Victoria Street
Te Aro, Wellington
• Matt’s work - Contact Energy Level 2, Harbour City Tower, 29 Brandon Street
Contact a committee member if you need more details.
We will bring all the gear to the Tri Club tent on race day Feb at the Wellington100, Scorching Bay. Items will be for sale throughout the morning.
The vibe

Come for a sasuage. Stay for a bargain. Leave knowing you’ve helped a young athlete get to a start line they might not otherwise reach.
Give back to the sport that’s given us so much.
Support local young talent.
Clear out your garage for a good cause.
See you at The Wellington100 on Feb 1st

description:
Tawa Community Expo, Tawa Community Expo
There are moments in the life of a community when we get the chance to come together,
stand side by side, and celebrate the people and groups who make Tawa vibrant, connected, and uniquely ours.

Tawa Community Expo 2026 is one of these moments!

This expo is all about celebrating the many local groups, clubs, and organisations that make Tawa a great place to live.
We’ve invited all of Tawa’s community groups to showcase what they have to offer, the diversity and spirit of our community.

Our aim is simple: Connect people, raise Visibility, and Strengthen our Community.

It’s all about people meeting people, discovering what’s happening in Tawa, and finding ways to get involved.

This is a great chance for new and established residents to learn about local opportunities to connect, volunteer, participate, and belong.

The event is not designed for fundraising, selling, or offering catering.

description:
The Bay Express to the Hastings Blossom Festival, The Bay Express to the Hastings Blossom Festival
Welcome spring in style and climb aboard The Bay Express for a magnificent full-day rail adventure. We are heading to Hawke's Bay for the spectacular Hastings Blossom Festival!

Sit back and relax as our majestic steam locomotive takes you through changing landscapes, winding its way toward the sunny Hawke's Bay. There is no better place to experience the sights and sounds of mainline steam than from our open-air viewing platform. It is the ultimate vantage point for taking stunning photos, hearing the thunderous echo of the engine, and catching the fresh spring breeze.

Throughout the entire journey, our onboard licensed café carriage will be open. You can purchase a range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic refreshments, hot espresso coffees, and sweet treats right from your seat as the scenery rolls by.

Our tracks lead straight into the heart of the action. The train will be stopping right in the middle of Hastings, putting you directly in the center of the festival. Upon arrival, you'll step off the train and straight into the vibrant celebrations of the annual Hastings Blossom Festival. Enjoy a fantastic afternoon exploring the famous public parade, live entertainment, market stalls, and beautiful spring blooms. It’s a proud local tradition celebrating the region's rich orchard heritage, and you are perfectly positioned to enjoy it all at your leisure before our return journey home.

What's Included
Your ticket covers your return journey to Hastings in beautifully maintained premium carriages alongside unrestricted access to the open-air viewing platform for unbeatable sightseeing and photography. You will also have full access to the onboard licensed café carriage selling refreshments, espresso coffees, and snacks. Best of all, you get direct arrival right into the heart of Hastings for the Blossom Festival celebrations with plenty of time to enjoy the festival parade, markets, and entertainment.

Approximate Itinerary
Morning Travel – Northbound to Hastings
Plimmerton depart – 5:25am
Paraparaumu depart – 5:55am
Ōtaki depart – 6:30am
Levin depart – 7:00am
Palmerston North depart – 8:10am
Woodville depart – 8:55am
Hastings arrive – 11:55am

Evening Travel – Return Journey
Hastings depart – 4:00pm
Woodville depart – 6:50pm
Palmerston North depart – 7:50pm
Levin depart – 8:45pm
Ōtaki depart – 9:15pm
Paraparaumu depart – 9:45pm
Plimmerton arrive – 10:15pm

Space in these premium carriages is strictly limited, so secure your tickets today for a classic spring day out on the rails!

description:
The Mad Hatter's Market Express, The Mad Hatter's Market Express

Journey with Steam Inc on this return trip to the Woodville Mad Hatter's Market Day!

Bring the family up into the heart of the Manawatu on the steam train, and enjoy a fun filled day at Woodville's famed Mad Hatter's Market Day. Hauled by Ja 1271, our 1956 built steam locomotive. Join the train at Paekakariki, Paraparaumu, Waikanae, Otaki, Levin or Palmerston North. Upon arrival at Woodville, there is the option to walk up to the square, or travel by shuttle bus up.

Woodville 150th Mad Hatter's Day
Since 2017, the local Woodville community have hosted this special event in the heart of the township celebrating all thing's 'mad'! Bring the kids along for a children's tea party and old time games - with a particular focus on steampunk. Featuring live music, over 70 market stalls and most importantly - the annual Crazy Hat Competition! Last year, people on our train took away 1st place!

Spot prizes are to be given out throughout the day for best costumes and hats, and an array of vouchers will also be up for grabs!

Please be at your boarding station minimum 10 minutes prior ready to roll, with your tickets, carriage number and seating allocations at the ready.

Please note that if booking online, our booking system does add on a small percentage to the above fares. Steam Incorporated does not see this revenue.

Mad Hatters Menu
The wonderful team has put together an array of food trucks for all to enjoy at the market, and you can also support the local cafes of Woodville township. There will also be tea/coffee available on board the train, along with some alcoholic beverages and light snacks.

We can cater for larger group bookings - these are best dealt with directly through us by emailing admin@steaminc.org.nz or contacting 0800 783 264.

Book the Mad Hatters Market Express!
All seating is reserved and allocated on these special experiences. Prior booking is essential.

Limited Mobility Disclaimer
Due to the age, design and nature of our heritage carriages, these are not suitable for passengers with limited mobility. If you have any concerns, please contact us on 0800 783 264 to discuss options with our bookings team!

description:
The Moonlit Market at The Atom - A playful experiment in entrepreneurial leadership, Date: Wednesday 15 October
Time: Doors open 5pm, adventure begins 5:30pm sharp. We’ll wrap up around 7:30pm.
Location: The Atom, Rutherford House, Victoria University, Wellington
Cost: Free (but only 25 places - first in, first served)
Step into a fantasy world where business plans mingle with strange enchantments and the market is never what it seems.
This event is designed with entrepreneurial leadership in mind - for anyone curious about the messy reality of building ideas and leading through uncertainty. If you’ve ever wondered what it really takes to test, fail, and adapt on the fly, you’ll feel right at home.
You’ll take on a fantasy character and join a small team of fellow entrepreneurs-in-disguise. Together, you’ll:
Interview strange and unpredictable NPCs to gather intel.
Dream up bizarre products that might just make you rich.
Build your idea with limited time and energy tokens.
Roll the dice and see what magical mishaps or unexpected opportunities change your fate.
The market is chaotic, the customers are fickle, and your product could become a cult sensation - or a village-wide joke.
This playful experience is more than just fun and games. You’ll get a taste of:
Leading through uncertainty
Making decisions with incomplete information
Collaborating under pressure
Turning setbacks into opportunities (or at least good stories)
No business experience required - just bring your imagination, your sense of humour, and your willingness to play.

description:
Toot for Tucker Churton Park, On Tuesday evening 18 November 2025 Johnsonville Rotary is again running our “Toot4Tucker” collection in Churton Park collecting dry and canned food items for our local foodbanks.
You’ll see us coming because we’ll wear hi-viz vests, and you’ll certainly hear us coming thanks once again to the fantastic support from the fire engine and team from the Johnsonville Fire Station.
Beginning at 6:00pm at Mauldeth Terrace to Amesbury Drive, Westchester Drive, Furlong Crescent, Abilene Crescent, Halswater Drive, Lakewood Avenue and finishing at Churton Park New World. Please keep an eye (and ear) out for the very noisy fire engine and the collectors.
There will be opportunities for children and other family members to have their photo taken in the fire engine along the route if you wish. Please have your camera or phone ready, and let us know as we pass.
For those not directly on the collection route, or if you miss us on the night, please ring William Nobelen (Johnsonville Rotary) [027 426 6504] and we’ll arrange to collect separately direct from your home.
On Saturday 6 December the Johnsonville Rotary Christmas Market will again be held at the Johnsonville Shopping Centre between 10:00am and 2:00pm (more news about that soon).
This year, we invite you to also bring your foodbank items, and (new and unwrapped) toys to the collection points at the Market. Kiwi Community Assistance will distribute your generous contributions to those in need in time for Christmas.
Another wonderful project presented by Johnsonville Rotary.

description:
Upper Hutt Gypsy Fair, The Gypsy Fair is a nationwide travelling event, bringing family fun, live music and an unbeatable vibe to each town we visit.
Having been on the road for over 45 years, it’s safe to say our roots run deep. Our people are incredible, and house trucks/buses are pretty cool too! So don’t forget to check out our unique way of living while you’re here
Whether you’re just having a browse, letting the kids loose on our rides, parking up with some food or coffee, or checking out some funky handmade crafts, we would love to see you! Come and hang out for the day, we’re sure to bring smiles to your faces, and create lifelong memories
Free entry for everyone
We pride ourselves on being an affordable event for every family. With free entertainment all day, plenty of chill out zones, and loads of life size games laying around, we truely love to see the community getting amongst it all! Can’t wait to see you there
Follow us on Facebook – ‘Gypsy Fair’ for updates on our travels and creations! We’re always open to anyone who wants to come and live the dream, so please email us if this sounds like a bit of you. – Gypsyfairnz@gmail.com

Upper Hutt Night Market, This vibrant community event promises an exciting evening of entertainment, artisan crafts and delectable food options for attendees of all ages.

Over 80 artisan craft stalls will showcase the talent and creativity of local artists. Attendees will have the opportunity to browse and purchase a wide range of unique handmade products, including artwork, jewellery, candles, home décor, plants, clothing and much more.

description:
Wairarapa Bookshop Hop 2025, The best booksellers in Wairarapa have come together to give you the ultimate book-lovers day out in celebration of New Zealand Bookshop Day.

This year, you can collect stamps from 13 new and used Wairarapa Bookshops and enjoy a range of other bookish events all day long.

One of the (many) great things about Wairarapa is we have 13 fantastic bookshops all within an easy 30 minute drive of one another, so it's entirely possible for you to hop around all 13 bookshops in a single day.

Celebrate NZ Bookshop Day with a Wairarapa wide Bookshop Hop. It's your chance to win lots of prizes and stock up your bookshelf.

STEP 1:
Pick up an official passport from any of the participating bookshops - available from all participating stores from Friday October 10th.

STEP 2:
Collect a stamp from each store you visit and make a purchase. Each stamp is an entry into the prize draws for $1,000 in bookshop vouchers.

STEP 3:
Leave your stamped entry with the last bookshop you visit.

This event happens rain or shine!

Register for free to stay up to date and for an extra chance to win a prize: bookshopday.nz/

description:
Wairarapa Farmers' Market, The Wairarapa Farmers’ Market is held every Saturday from 9am to 1pm (rain or shine!) at the Solway Showgrounds Masterton. Entry is off State Highway 2 or the by pass, onto Judds Rd. There is plenty of car parking and a camping ground for NZMCA Members

Picnic tables are situated underneath the majestic Redwood Tree for you to sit and enjoy a coffee and something to eat while listening to live music. Plus you get to take home quality, delicious produce grown seasonally within the Wairarapa region. It makes for a great morning's outing.

Enjoy breakfast, brunch or lunch and pick up your dinner items with locally produced coffee, eggs, meat, berries, bread, jam, fruit, olive oil, pastries, pies, pickles, slices, cakes, soup, vegetables and more. Shop for plants, seedlings, seaweed, artisan goods including wood turning, Māori weaving, children’s and baby clothes, aprons, peg aprons, tea towels, knitted and crochet toys and hand dyed knitting wools.
Sign up for our regular Wairarapa Farmers' Market newsletter here https://mailchi.mp/d99e1ad65a18/newsletter-sign-up or join us on Facebook to get updates on all the Market goodness! Dogs are welcome to the market and a dog bowl can be provided. See you on Saturday!

"From Paddock to Plate Since 2006"

The entry ticket is non-refundable, but it is transferable so you if you can't attend for whatever reason, you can give the ticket to a friend.

FAQs

Parking is available at the venue, at a cost of $10. Please note parking is card payment only (entry to the Show is card or cash).
2. What is the best time to attend?
Peak visitor times are normally between 11am - 2pm so the crowds are less outside of these times.
3. What days is the ticket valid for?
General Admission entry tickets is for one entry only and is valid for any one of the 3 event days.
Gold Card Special 1/2 price tickets valid for Friday only.
4. Do I have to bring my printed ticket to the event?
A printed ticket or showing the barcode on your phone to the entry staff is required.

description:
'Una Serenata Italiana' - – an intimate evening of Italian opera favourites at the Public Trust Hal, Te Pae Kōkako – The Aotearoa New Zealand Opera Studio (TANZOS) performs for Wellington audiences for the first time this November with Una Serenata Italiana – an intimate evening of Italian opera favourites at the Public Trust Hall.
Directed by Elaine Kidd (Head of the Jette Parker Artists Programme, The Royal Opera House Covent Garden) and accompanied by Caroline Dowdle (Head of Opera, Atelier Lyric Verbier Festival; repertoire coach with the Jette Parker Programme and the Royal College of Music), the concert celebrates the beauty of Italian opera and the new generation of New Zealand opera artists defining the country’s vocal landscape.
Presented in association with Ambasciata d’Italia Wellington, this special performance continues the vision of Dame Malvina Major, whose support for artist development through TANZOS helps nurture Aotearoa’s rising operatic talent.
Featuring Sarah Mileham, Niamh Bentley, Jasmine Jessen, Katherine Winitana, Ridge Ponini, Faamanu Fonoti-Fuimaono, Tomairangi Henare and Samuel McKeever.
About TANZOS:
Te Pae Kōkako – The Aotearoa New Zealand Opera Studio (TANZOS) is directed by internationally recognised soprano Madeleine Pierard, Dame Malvina Major Chair in Opera, and led by Head Vocal Coach Nikki Li Hartliep, an acclaimed performer and teacher who has worked with major opera companies and conservatories around the world.
TANZOS provides full-time, international-level opera training for up to six exceptional New Zealand singers each year, supported by donor-funded scholarships and guided by Dame Malvina Major’s long-held vision for professional opera education in Aotearoa.
Find out more at https://www.tanzos.org/

Active since the late 90s, they've released a huge discography on labels like Celebrate PSI Phenomenon and Pseudo Arcana.
www.thirdoctaveband.bandcamp.com
--
The improvising duo of Bridget Kelly (reeds, harp) & Peter Liley (saxophone & electronics) will combine their unique creative voices and impeccable musicality moving from lyrical melodies to unearthly growls, creating meditative yet visceral compositions in real time.
---
Grant / Winterwood: Erika Grant and Zac Winterwood join forces for a performance utilising hammer dulcimer, shruti box, 12 stringed acoustic guitar, and other various instruments.
Erika Grant is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 30+ years musical experience in bands including Orchestra of Spheres, and Cookie Brooklyn and the Crumbs. Over the past few years Erika has developed a sound bathing practice using gongs, bowls and chimes. She is interested in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing.
Zac Winterwood (NZ/AUS) is a musical outlier whose art lives within the tradition/discipline of minimalism. Since the late 1990s, he has been a purveyor in the art of noise, ambient, drone, field recording and experimental music, whose work has been compared to Low, Terry Riley, Brian Eno and Neil Young.

description:
1TBSP | WELLINGTON | MEOW NUI, 1TBSP | WELLINGTON | MEOW NUI
1tbsp is returning to Wellington for an exclusive NZ show, all his previous NZ dates selling out - get in quick!

PRESALE: Thursday, 2nd of July, 4:30PM NZT
GA ONSALE - Friday 3rd of July, - 4:30PM NZT
PRESALE LINK - https://arep.co/p/1tbsp-bubble-tour-wellington-1

Following a huge run of international touring in the first half of the year, including appearances at Coachella, a North American Bubble Tour and a residency at London's Phonox, 1tbsp jumps the ditch with Bubble Tour - a live show that expands his ever-evolving world.

Across the last few years, 1tbsp, the Meanjin-born, Gadigal-based producer, songwriter, DJ and Dottidot label founder, has quietly assembled one of electronic music's most distinctive universes – a glossy, hyper-coloured landscape where reggaeton drums collide with toy-box synths, club music sparkles with pop sentiment, and every release feels like a portal into somewhere slightly unfamiliar.

Originally known through his Grammy-nominated alt-indie project Golden Vessel, Maxwell Byrne launched 1tbsp in 2021 as an outlet for stranger ideas. What began with the kanashī EP soon evolved into a fully realised creative universe, culminating in the release of his debut album Mosquito Love and later the acclaimed Megacity1000.

Released in 2024, Megacity1000 arrived like a transmission from a parallel metropolis - equal parts club record and pop experiment. Across the album's eight tracks, Byrne fused candy-coated percussion, shimmering vocal fragments and bright, maximalist production into a sound entirely his own. Support quickly followed from Pitchfork, Mixmag, CLASH, The Line of Best Fit and EARMILK, cementing 1tbsp as one of Australia's most forward-thinking electronic exports.

That same spirit extends beyond his own catalogue through Dottidot, Byrne's label and creative platform, which has become home to a growing network of artists and collaborators. Recent releases from label affiliates Soltera and Cherry Chola continue to expand the architecture of this ecosystem.

Now, for the first time, Bubble Tour arrives in Aotearoa this August, Saturday 22nd at Meow Nui.

Tickets on sale: Friday 3rd of July - 4:30pm (Local time) from Tickettek.

🗣️ Why do the tickets come in different price tiers?

Whilst there is no physical difference. There is only a limited amount of tickets we can sell. Therefore we operate a festival style ticketing model. The earlier you buy your ticket the cheaper it will be.

🗣️ Do you do group discount? Stag/Hen etc

Yes, we offer a discounted ticket price for groups of 10 or more. These tickets can be found listed as the “Big Group Package!” above, orders for these tickets are restricted to a minimum of 10.

🗣️ Will there be more tickets available if the event is sold out?

Once this event is sold out, there will not be any additional tickets released. In addition to this we will be unable to sell them at the door due to maximum capacity and health and safety regulations.

🗣️ Is the venue accessible?

Our events take place at a variety of locations across the UK and Ireland. As each varies please ensure to check the specific venue's website for accessibility information.

🗣️ Can I resell my tickets?

Yes, if you are unable to attend an event you are welcome to sell your tickets on. We do not use names on tickets as a condition for entry.

🗣️ Are your events 18+?

All of our events are strictly 18+. A valid photographic ID may be requested on entry.

🗣️ What do I do if I cant find my tickets or confirmation email?

We use Fatsoma to sell tickets for our events. If you’re struggling to find your ticket, you can access their support channels via https://support.fatsoma.com/support/home

🗣️ Are there tickets available on the door?

We always recommend booking in advance as we cannot guarantee on the door entry. However, in certain instances there will be a limited number of tickets on a first come first served basis for sale on the door.

🗣️ I have more questions?

If you have additional questions and wish to contact us directly, don’t hesitate to drop us a DM on either Facebook (Daytime Disco) or Instagram (@daytimediscoevents)

Refund Policy:
In-line with normal consumer standards for ticket purchases, tickets for Daytime Disco events are non-refundable, on the condition that we not moved the event or canceled it. If you are no longer be able to attend the event, you are of course welcome to gift or sell your tickets onwards as we do not use names on the tickets as a condition of entry.

description:
5 And Still Live ! - The Fifth Anniversary of Mouthfull Radio, Five years ago we were in the midst of a global pandemic, visiting digital rooms with friends around the corner, making sourdough, and sort of watching the daily news. We were also making experimental attempts into the world of radio, with the birth of Mouthfull’s first international streaming server, playing music 24/7 (also live events a few times a week).
If we travel even further back in time, 2017 was the debut of the “Mouthfull Radio” episodic series (~20eps) - but we consider the ongoingness the real thing to celebrate.
Moving towards present day ~ through a vast richness of hosts, events, music, shows, zines, selectors, connections, pop ups, and story-times. It is a real joy to help community contemporary radio ripple out from this Pacific Island nation to the world wide web.

5 Years goes so fast, and so we shall honour this time with a great celebration in the capital city of Aotearoa! We will bring together all of the elements of Mouthfull you have known to love; make some books, make up some new dance moves with friends, and make our ears glisten in the sounds of live and selected music.
Whiro // New Moon. The last dark night of winter. A time for reflection; an invitation to come together as friends and whānau and plant intentional seeds for future flowers to bloom, as well as rest in deep listening and shared beingness.

Lineup:
*ºJuniper May
*ºStar Time
*ºajhoneysuckle (tāmaki)
*ºMystery Waitress (duo)
*ºDJ B.Lo (whākatu)
*°Benny Salvador


We are also releasing our first ever compilation. This special event will be opened with a premiere listening session of the full CD, playing the album all the way through. You can purchase a physical copy at the show, or on bandcamp (preorders open September 1st).
5PM sharp CD push play. Some divine collaborators with unique new releases on offer.

This is a fundraiser to support the sustainability of Mouthfull. We are only able to pay the bills due to events like this, and are fundraising to support a long awaited update of our digital infrastructure to enable future support. THANKS FOR YOUR SUPPORT - you can support us by purchasing a ticket (extra donation if you are balling), a tshirt, a raffle ticket, or a zine - it all goes to the same goal of enabling & uplifting one another.

description:
A Celtic Christmas By a Taste of Ireland, “Jingle Jigs, Reels a Treat.” Ken Longworth – The Newcastle Herald

Direct from its Off-Broadway season, A Taste of Ireland – The Irish Music & Dance Sensation, presents its holiday spectacular, A Celtic Christmas. Prepare to be enchanted with some of the world’s finest Irish dancers and musicians bringing the spirit of Christmas to life, in a show that will make you laugh, cry, and sing into the night.

After captivating audiences across the USA and around the world, A Celtic Christmas by A Taste of Ireland returns to New Zealand this festive season following a highly successful 2022 tour. Experience the magic as world-class performers blend melodic folk mash-ups, acapella tap battles, and heart-warming storytelling in one truly unforgettable performance.

Featuring former World Irish dance champions and stars from Lord of the Dance and Riverdance, A Celtic Christmas delivers a holiday spectacular packed with Irish wit, traditional tunes and heartfelt ballads, alongside all your favourite carols. The show’s exciting mix of electrifying rhythms and extraordinary talent promises an evening brimming with Irish charm and enthralling entertainment, all in one powerhouse event.

Immerse yourself in a traditional Celtic landscape and let the magic of an Irish Christmas transport you to a world filled with excitement and wonder, where vibrant music and dance embody the heartbeat of the festive season.

With over one hundred and fifty 5-star Facebook reviews and over 150,000 followers, A Celtic Christmas by A Taste of Ireland promises 100% live singing and dancing as it bridges the gap between energetic folk music, Irish dance, and modern tap styles. Don’t miss your chance to see this magical show as it tours New Zealand for a strictly limited season. Get your tickets now before they sell out.

description:
A Place To Bury Strangers NZ Tour, A Place To Bury Strangers NZ Tour
UTR and Meow Touring presents:

A Place To Bury Strangers return to Aotearoa with their explosive new album Synthesizer — a record built on chaos, colour, and pure DIY spirit. Synthesizer isn’t just the title of their seventh album; it’s also a custom-built instrument created specifically for it. “It’s pretty messed up, chaotic… but it feels really human,” says frontman Oliver Ackermann. The album celebrates spontaneity, collaboration, and the kind of raw noise that can only come from a band locked in together.

Written in the band’s Queens studio after a refreshed lineup — Ackermann with John and Sandra Fedowitz — Synthesizer cracks open and reimagines the signature APTBS sound in vivid new ways. It’s romantic, raw, unsteady, and built for the stage, where the band’s legendary walls of sound hit with full force.

With Support from: Grecco Romank

A Very (late) Wellington Sea Shanty Society Xmas (Sold out), A Very (late) Wellington Sea Shanty Society Xmas (Sold out)
Sold out.

New date! 30 January, 2026. So this will be 'A Very (late) Wellington Sea Shanty Society Xmas'.

NAUTICAL GAMES /// BEST DRESSED PRIZES /// SINGALONG SHANTIES /// XMAS-TYPE STUFF

Your work Xmas-party is going to be lame or cancelled so slap a $2 shop Santa's hat on 2025 and have a sing with Aotearoa's Most Seaworthy Shanty crew.

Prepare to be hit by a wave of joy and merriment as the Full Wellington Sea Shanty Society Experience transform the Abandoned Taproom into a shanty wonderland.

We got shanty booklets for all ye faithful and merch for Xmas presents.

If there's one thing we can all agree on in this country, it's that Xmas needs more sea shanties!

Only Te Upoko o te Ika show for 2025. New EP out in April 2026.

🎅🎅🎅

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).

The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada. Their new EP 'Sea Shanties of the 70s, 80s, & Today!' has just recently surfaced to complement their 'Now That's What I Call Sea Shanties' series. Another must-listen is 'Ahoy!' - a French/English album made with Nantes amis Croche Dedans.

The festivities will begin with Vivaldi’s Gloria, a joyous and uplifting work that will get you right into the Christmas spirit. Then it will be time to get your singing caps on and join us in singing a selection of beloved and well-known carols. From Silent Night in Te Reo to Joy to the World, this is a perfect opportunity to gather and feel the Christmas spirit through music.
Alongside familiar favourites, we’ll showcase a selection of beautiful choral works, including traditional 16th-century carols, as well as pieces by the likes of Arvo Pärt and kiwi composer Jenny McLeod. It’s going to be a night full music and Christmas cheer - the perfect way to end 2025!

A Very Cantoris Christmas, Cantoris would like to warmly welcome you to our final concert of 2025: A Very Cantoris Christmas!
The festivities will begin with Vivaldi’s Gloria, a joyous and uplifting work that will get you right into the Christmas spirit. Then it will be time to get your singing caps on and join us in singing a selection of beloved and well-known carols. From Silent Night in Te Reo to Joy to the World, this is a perfect opportunity to gather and feel the Christmas spirit through music.
Alongside familiar favourites, we’ll showcase a selection of beautiful choral works, including traditional 16th-century carols, as well as pieces by the likes of Arvo Pärt and kiwi composer Jenny McLeod. It’s going to be a night full music and Christmas cheer - the perfect way to end 2025!
We can’t wait to share it all with you. See you there!

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).

The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada. Their new EP 'Sea Shanties of the 70s, 80s, & Today!' has just recently surfaced to complement their 'Now That's What I Call Sea Shanties' series. Another must-listen is 'Ahoy!' - a French/English album made with Nantes amis Croche Dedans.

A.Skills (UK), A.Skillz (UK)
A.Skillz is a master of the decks and a true party rocker, known for fusing Funk, Soul, Hip Hop, Rock, and Bass into an electrifying mix that’s uniquely his own. His sets burst with re-edits, remixes, and original productions, taking crowds on a high-energy journey through sound. description:
ABC, Formed in Sheffield in 1980, the band ABC brought a mix of new romantic, post-punk, and disco-funk to dancefloors. Now, 45 years since they began, they're making their way to New Zealand. Expect a set packed with sharp suits, polished pop, and some of the band’s best-known tracks. 
Charismatic singer Martin Fry fronts ABC. He's likely to serenade you with many of the band's favourites including The Look Of Love, Poison Arrow, All Of My Heart, and When Smokey Sings. All of them made it into the top 20 hits in the New Zealand music charts at the time. ABC’s debut album, ‘The Lexicon Of Love’, reached number one in New Zealand for three weeks and stayed in the album chart for 33 weeks. Even after all this time the songs still draw people to the floor to dance.

description:
ASH ‘1977’ 30th Anniversary Tour, "Ash rule. They are geniuses. Gods maybe."- NME
Ireland’s favourite power pop trio, Ash, finally return to Australia and New Zealand to Celebrate the 30th Anniversary of their iconic debut album, ‘1977’, by performing the album in full. Released in 1996, the album’s title references both the decade the band members were born in and the year Star Wars first hit cinemas.
‘1977’ has sold more than 2 million copies worldwide and was written, recorded and released when most of Ash were still only 19. A cinematic punk-pop soundtrack to binge drinking, chasing girls, youth and frustrated adolescent idealism, the album fused power pop, glam rock, post-grunge and Britpop into a loud, melodic and exuberant sound.
It struck a chord with the hearts, minds and hormones of a generation of like-minded teens, delivering a run of singles including “Girl From Mars”, “Kung Fu”, “Angel Interceptor”, “Goldfinger” and “Oh Yeah” — all of which reached the UK Top 20 and helped cement Ash’s reputation.
The 30th Anniversary Celebration of ‘1977’ will give Ash fans the chance to relive the album that featured “hit after honey-topped hit” and Britpop ruled the airwaves. Oh yeah!

description:
AWE Partnership Concert: Double Helix with Benjamin Baker and Yura Lee, Experience Double Helix with Benjamin Baker and Yura Lee!
NOTICE OF VENUE CHANGE: Venue changed to St Andrew's on the Terrace.
We’ll be hosting an intimate violin and viola recital of international talents Benjamin Baker and Yura Lee at one of Wellington's best-known chamber music venues in the heart of the CBD. Our recent venue change to St Andrew's on the Terrace has opened up more seats than originally planned for this concert, which we are rather excited about!
Opening with Chicago composer Augusta Read Thomas’ Double Helix, this programme explores how two equal spirits intertwine, navigating a shared musical journey like a spiraling helix. International award-winning violin and viola soloist Yura Lee joins AWE Artistic Director Benjamin Baker for an intimate exploration of both instruments — together and apart — through works by Bach, Ysaÿe, Martinů, and Mozart, interwoven with music from Aotearoa by John Psathas and Salina Fisher.
Doors open 5.15pm, concert begins at 6pm. Approx end time 7pm. Tickets $55.
An Incredible Partnership with At The World's Edge Festival!
As part of our 2025 partnership with At the World’s Edge (AWE) Festival, Orchestra Wellington is presenting a three-part series featuring AWE 2025 Festival Artist Yura Lee and AWE Artistic Director Benjamin Baker for a mini-series of concerts and a masterclass here in Wellington in addition to featuring these incredible artists' live performances with us on our subscription series concerts in September and October!

description:
Acoustic Routes December Social Club with Mary Livingston, Featuring guest Mary Livingston. Mary has been part of our local folk scene since she arrived in Wellington 50 years ago, with forays into classical guitar and various choirs. She has sung with many people...in the early days it was with Dave Nicholson & Mary Hubble. Later, she linked up with Sarah Duckworth & then Robin Brew, the Magpies (acapella 4 part), and Dr Livingston and the Presumptions (band with Don and Jill). Her current singing partner is Sue Chamberlain although Mary and Robin are dusting off their voci for an airing in early 2026! Mary loves to harmonise, and aims to not just come up with something that sounds nice, but that actually tries to enhance the sound of the singer with the tune, - a technique learned from her barbershop-Sweet Adeline sojourn. Today however we are going to hear Mary as a soloist. She will share a range of songs that she likes to sing on her own, and puts the harmony in with her guitar work. Some will be her own songs, and the rest is likely to focus on her take on some Celtic favourites using a DADGAD tuning on her guitar. Some of the songs will be familiar to you, but others less so. She is pretty excited about doing this, as it is rare for her to sing alone.
In the second half, we’ll go around the circle and you’re welcome to lead a song or tune if you wish.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Adam McGrath, Gate opens 6.30pm, music starts 7pm

We are SO LUCKY to have Adam McGrath returning to Hilltop – he’s one of the best. Adam has already had a full-on year (and it’s only half way), including touring with the ‘Come Together’ Born To Run – Bruce Springsteen concerts, and then touring with Gary McCormick. Adam is the winner of the 2024 Aotearoa/New Zealand Folk Artist of the Year Award at the Aotearoa/New Zealand music awards. Described by RNZ as a “National Treasure” and the Herald as “NZ’s toughest minded songwriter”, Adam is also widely known as lead singer and songwriter with one of NZ’s most loved roots/country bands The Eastern. Adam’s new album Wrecker Songs was released on May Day 2026 to coincide with the 75th anniversary of the Maritime Union of New Zealand (MUNZ). It hit #1 – Aotearoa Albums Chart and #4 – Official Top 40 Albums (all albums, domestic and international). It also reached #1 on the IMNZ (Independent Music New Zealand) Album Chart. “Wrecker Songs is here, on all the streamers, the cd’s are here the vinyl is late, the spirit is high, the heart is a eye and its wide, the muscle is gristly, the bones brittle, the mind shows grit despite the fog, the fists clenched, the struggle real, the solidarity true.”… Click for the first song on the album -> ‘The Assembly” Adam is a folk singer and yarn spinner stationed, he says, wherever he can get a key! He spends eight months a year on the road between NZ, Australia, Europe and parts beyond. With The Eastern and solo he has shared stages with and opened for Fleetwood Mac, Steve Earle, Old Crow Medicine Show, Paul Kelly, Jimmy Barnes and many, more. His song Hope and Wire was the inspiration behind Gaylene Preston’s TV series of the same name and he is known for his service orientated approach to music in the years since. Described as “maybe part folk singer, part preacher, part boxer, and part rodeo clown he is however all heart”. Raucous, tender, roof and spirit raising, a McGrath show goes straight for the spirit level in all of us, looking deep for the good parts and hoping to reach all the thoughtful bits that matter.

Adam’s first solo album was released December ’23. “It’s called Dear Companions, because of everything I’ve learnt or am learning about the people in the songs and what they help me learn about myself and about the world big and small (especially small). But that kind of conception is just how records start, where they end up is up to whoever gets a copy in their life.”
“One of the best modern roots artists, from any country”
-No Depression magazine

Come along and enjoy this great gig in our special space, up close and personal.

Adrian Cox Trio Club Croco Album Tour, Internationally acclaimed clarinetist Adrian Cox and his trio return to Aotearoa for a series of performances promoting their recently released album 'Club Croco'.

Adrian is a leading authority on New Orleans music, bringing an authentic and electrifying voice to the idiom. As a celebrated exponent of the style, Cox has dedicated his career to preserving and pushing the boundaries of early jazz, earning praise for his masterful technique, deep historical knowledge, and infectious energy on stage. His unrivalled feel and virtuosity for the music he plays have led to concerts with the biggest names in jazz including two concerts with Wynton Marsalis and the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra both in London and New York. Adrian is currently touring with his exceptional Trio featuring the New Zealand born guitarist Honey Boulton and New York based bassist Alex Gilson, a true world class power house that leaves audiences spellbound.

There will be Vinyl, CDs and a super special fanzine (w/ EP download) available for purchase.

description:
Air Force Band Charity Concert tickets, Presented by: Waikanae Lions Club and Royal New Zealand Air Force Band
The much loved Air Force Charity Concert returns for its 18th spectacular year! A firm favourite that regularly sells out, this is not to be missed — secure your tickets early to be part of this unforgettable afternoon.
This year’s concert promises an exciting and uplifting programme, featuring everything from iconic movie themes to timeless classics. Audiences will be treated to the full power and colour of bagpipes, drums, brass and woodwind, together with a stunning performance by the incomparable soprano LAC Barbara Graham.
Adding to the occasion, this concert marks a heartfelt farewell as Director of Music Squadron Leader David Gallaher takes the podium for his final performance with the RNZAF Band before embarking on new adventures back home in Christchurch.
Best of all, thanks to the hard work of the Waikanae Lions Club, every ticket purchased supports a wonderful cause, with proceeds going to Mary Potter Hospice.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Air Force Band Masterworks, Air Force Band Masterworks
Renowned for its breathtaking ensemble playing and military precision, the RNZAF Band will perform music by some of the greatest composers of all time, including Mahler and Strauss.

Returning to the Gillies Group Theatre for the first time in nine years, the band will present a compelling collection of works under the accomplished artistic direction of Bandmaster Warrant Officer Ben Robertson. The programme also features music by Grammy-nominated composer and flautist Valerie Coleman, along with New Zealand composer Georgina Palmer and masters of the concert band genre, Frank Ticheli and James Barnes.

Don’t miss this opportunity to hear New Zealand’s premier military band perform awe-inspiring works in the intimate setting of Whirinaki Whare Taonga.

description:
Air Force in Concert Featuring Hollie Smith, The Royal New Zealand Air Force (RNZAF) Band is set to blast some big sounds in November. The Wellington-based band joins forces with New Zealand soul singer Hollie Smith. Together, they will take over the Michael Fowler Centre with a diverse repertoire. The RNZAF Band will perform hits from symphonic masterworks and marches to jazz standards and pop classics. Hollie will shine with several of her own famous soul songs. 
Hollie Smith is a prodigious songwriter. She has three number-one solo albums and an abundance of awards under her belt. Fat Freddy’s Drop, Trinity Roots, Anika Moa, and Boh Runga are just a few of her many collaborators. 
The RNZAF Band is a reserve force military band. It regularly welcomes dignitaries at Government House and Parliament, and provides music for commemorations at Pukeahu National War Memorial. Many of its members perform in the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, Orchestra Wellington, Shapeshifter, and the Rodger Fox Big Band.
Tickets available to the public from 8am on Monday, 8 September.

description:
Albi & the Wolves, Gate opens 7pm Music Starts 7.30pm Wednesday 1st October 2025
Auckland based Albi and the Wolves set fire to stages and fill hearts with hope with their energetic and relatable alternative indie folk songs. Proud albino frontman Albi (Chris Dent), Pascal Roggen and Michael Young have crafted a stage show brimming with energy yet with pauses for reflection. The trio has a huge sound created simply by acoustic guitar, electric violin, double bass and three voices. Since 2014, Albi & the Wolves have gone from strength to strength touring Australia, New Zealand and Rarotonga. In 2018, they took home the Best Folk Artist Award at the NZVMAs.
What makes the band special is their sense of community. Whether it’s connection through dance, singing or laughter, their performances inspire audiences to keep coming back for more. Just love them!
Come along and enjoy their great gig in our special space, up close and personal.
Not for profit, supporting our dedicated musicians. Suggested donation $40
Teas, Coffee and Snacks provided. You're welcome to bring anything you'd like to eat or drink.
Parking available in the Coupon zones of Upland Rd & Glasgow St free after 6pm weekdays, and free all through the weekends. The Wilson Carpark at the top of the Cable Car charges 24/7.

Alda Rezende, Alda Rezende
The Undercurrent presents Alda Rezende!

Alda will bring to the Undercurrent some of Wellington’s finest musicians to present a vibrant tribute to Brazilian black music of the 1970s - the irresistibly groovy, soulful and dance-driven sound that blends samba with North American soul and funk. Expect high-energy rhythms, classic grooves and an uplifting performance that celebrates the enduring spirit of Brazilian soul.

Brazilian-born Alda Rezende is a celebrated singer and a veteran of Wellington’s music scene, known for her rich vocals and deep musical experience across Brazilian, Latin, jazz and classical traditions. Originally from Brazil, Alda has performed alongside legends like Elza Soares and João Bosco and has been a leading voice in Wellington’s jazz and world music communities for many years, including releasing albums and hosting a long-running world music radio show on Radio Active.

description:
Aldous Harding: Train on the Island, By the time indie/folk singer songwriter Aldous Harding hits Wellington, she will have travelled across the UK and Europe with her Train on the Island tour. By the time the tour reaches the Michael Fowler Centre, it will be a finely oiled machine.   
Named after her fifth studio album Train on the Island, all ten of the album’s songs will appear in the concert, including One Stop, and Venus In The Zinnia.   
Aldous Harding captivates listeners with what Martin Pepperell describes as an ‘elastic and shape-shifting voice’. This, combined with eccentric performances, has catapulted the Lyttelton-born singer to fame. Her second album ‘Party’ won the Taite Prize in 2018, and The Barrel, from her third studio album ‘Designer’, won the 2019 APRA Silver Scroll award.

description:
Aled Jones - My Story, My Songs tickets, Presented by: TEG Live
The My Story, My Songs tour takes Aled Jones on a regional journey across Australia and New Zealand, bringing fans a rare chance to get up close and personal with one of the country’s most loved performers.
A witty raconteur, Aled also performs the hits from his extraordinary career, and a self-penned track from his Number One album Full Circle.
“The response to my most personal tour yet has been incredible. I have absolutely loved sharing some of my most special untold stories and personal photographs.”
“From growing up in Bangor and becoming the world’s most famous choir boy through to present day, as host of Songs of Praise, and appearing on Strictly Come Dancing and The Masked Singer, I’ve loved sharing my journey.
“It’s been wonderful to meet my fans, a golden opportunity to get up close and personal in some of the country’s most beautiful, intimate venues.”
Aled was the boy treble who captivated the world with his angelic voice, most notably voicing the score to Raymond Briggs’s The Snowman. Selling more than seven million albums, he’s equally at home on the classical stage, or starring in musical theatre productions in London West End, his credits include lead roles in Joseph and the Amazing Technicolour Dreamcoat, Chitty Chitty Bang Bang and Irving Berlin’s White Christmas.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Alex Seel and Jon Sanders (UK) @ Wellington Bluegrass Society, Alex Seel and Jon Sanders (UK) @ Wellington Bluegrass Society
“Make no mistake, the audience raved about the sheer scope of musical interplay and different genres… Sanders with his jazz tinged Irish, Arabesque and world music solos, brought the sonorous experience of compositions from the British song-writer’s new album with almost unbelievable changes in tempo, accompanied masterfully by Seel’s impressive guitar… The audience loved Seel’s folk, pop and blues influenced songs and duos with Sanders”
- RheinZeit, Germany

Music has led Alex Seel from Devon to London to Ireland and back to London again. Through his wanderings, Alex has picked up a finely crafted, rootsy songwriting style with thought provoking lyrics and a flare for acoustic guitar finger picking. His influences range from blues, pop and the British folk revival guitarists, but his sound is all his own. He has a growing reputation as a solo performer, having performed around the UK, Ireland, Italy, Germany and Spain.

Jon Sanders is recognised as a virtuoso bouzouki player, tenor ukulele player, drop D and DADGAD guitarist and an internationally acclaimed composer. His compositions draw on elements of jazz, gypsy, funk, Arabic, Latino and Celtic styles, somewhat reminiscent of Sylvain Luc, Pierre Bensusan, Antonio Forcione and James Hill - yet instantly different.

Both were based in Dingle in Kerry, but in different scenes. But only later on started playing in the UK first at the Didsbury Festival, then did couple of other festivals and it went down really well… the chemistry of the duo, complementing each other with symbiotic dynamism, with sensitivity in each others music. Both are long time professional musicians. Jon has been performing in NZ for 20 years, however this is Alex’es first time in NZ.

description:
Alex Trask + 6 (+1), Alex + 6 is a well-seasoned septet that will present a fizzing set of horn-heavy swing. Join us as we explore some new interpretations of familiar melodies and underground favourites. Expect to hear exhilarating tunes from the finest jazz composers, heart-wrenching Broadway ballads, and danceable delights.

Free entry!

We will be joined for this very special gig by the stunning vocalist Ella Dunbar-Wilcox, who is a Wellington-based jazz vocalist. She recorded her debut album "Almost Love" in 2024. Ella is highly in demand and we are very excited to have her appear in both sets.

Inspired by classic albums such as Art Pepper + 11, Oliver Nelson's the Blues And The Abstract Truth, and Oscar Pettiford's Octet and Nonet, the arrangements are appealingly simple and allow all the members to shine through. Look out for our special guest vocalist, who will be singing a couple of lush numbers with us.

Personnel:

Mike Taylor – trumpet
Alex Trask – alto saxophone, arrangements
Oscar Laven – tenor saxophone
Daniel Yeabsley – baritone saxophone
Ayrton Foote – piano
Elijah Mulheron – bass
John Rae – drums

description:
Alex Trask Presents | Coltrane's Soprano, Alex Trask presents a special tribute to John Coltrane, performing tunes that he played on soprano saxophone. ‘Coltrane’s soprano has been hugely influential to me as an alto player and musician. His sound on the instrument is so unique and special, it’s been a touchstone for me for years. I remember being absolutely captivated by his playing on the untitled originals when Both Directions at Once came out, when I was still a beginner player. My Favourite Things is one of my most loved albums, and Everytime We Say Goodbye from that record is some of my favourite saxophone playing ever.’

The band will play classics such as My Favourite Things and Greensleeves, as well as tunes from the albums Both Directions at Once, Duke Ellington & John Coltrane, and Impressions.

Personnel:
Alex Trask – soprano saxophone
Duncan Haynes – piano
Elijah Mulheron – bass
Rick Cranson – drums

Part of the Wellington Jazz Festival 2025

description:
Alex Trask Quintet, Local saxophonist Alex Trask presents original music from his various projects, including a recent recording, his first album, and the Lighthouse Trio setlist. Free improvised sections contrast carefully arranged melodies, allowing creativity and structure to coexist. Old St Paul’s is a stunning example of Gothic Revival architecture, constructed entirely from native timbers and consecrated in 1866. Its soaring wooden arches, stained glass windows, and rich acoustics make it a sought-after venue for a variety of events. The church offers seating for up to 460 guests, with facilities including a grand piano, organ, and a bar licence. While on-site catering isn't available, nearby venues such as Loaves & Fishes Hall, the Royal Society of New Zealand, and the Thistle Inn provide excellent options for receptions and gatherings. Located at 34 Mulgrave Street in Thorndon, Old St Paul’s is easily accessible by public transport and offers a serene setting for weddings, concerts, memorials, and other significant events.

description:
Alphabethead, DISPLEASURE & BIRDPARTY || Meow || Te Whanganui-a-Tara, Alphabethead, DISPLEASURE & BIRDPARTY || Meow || Te Whanganui-a-Tara
TICKETS ARE HERE:
https://meow.flicket.co.nz/events/0cad942c-ea00-4a5a-9ae6-b1523f8ff544

Please join Alphabethead, Displeasure and Birdparty this December as they traverse Aotearoa on a journey to present genre-expanding music that seeks to stimulate the brain, and move the body! These three acts differ widely from one another but are unified in friendship and the shared pursuit of life-affirming, body-moving combinations of rhythms, bass and formidable sound design.

Alphabethead is celebrating the release of “My Name Is David, his debut album of electronic music on Sunreturn. Displeasure release Billionaire Death Drive, their second album of anarcho-dance-punk and Birdparty, having already played some incredible festival shows and gigged in China, tour Aotearoa for the very first time.

ALPHABETHEAD finds himself adrift in the musical cosmos, somewhere between the constellations of Hip Hop, Electronica and Experimental Rock. As a teenager he won the New Zealand DMC DJ Championship and this title sent him performing across the globe. Over the next twenty years he'd go on to make six albums as Alphabethead, five albums as one third of cult genre-shredders All Seeing Hand and two records as half of the psychedelic Hip Hop duo Bad Taste alongside Young Gho$t. He also contributed production or turntable scratching to Home Brew, Tourettes, Death & The Maiden, The Etymologists (featuring Richard Nunns and David Long (The Mutton Birds) and The Village Of The Idiots (a modern jazz ensemble led by Anthony Donaldson (The Front Lawn, Primitive Art Group)). His musical prowess and singular approach to playing the turntable like a musical instrument has led to tours through Aotearoa, Australia, UK and China and performances at festivals like WOMAD, Splore, Laneway and Camp A Low Hum.

Now signed to Sunreturn, Alphabethead's new music is explorative and driving electronica stemming from sound design and synthesis with touches of turntablism and vinyl sampling.

https://alphabethead.bandcamp.com/

DISPLEASURE is the digital subsidiary of Unsanitary Napkin. Their music deals with the swirling mess of scaremongering bullshit rearing its increasingly ugly head in political discourse in Aotearoa. In the year 2025, things have reached the point where disgruntled science-denying farmers are teaming up with perverse public toilet-obsessed transphobes, raging anti-vaxxxers and evangelical megachurch despots in a horrific whirlpool of shit ideas manipulated by white supremacists and alt-right trolls - with all of their delusional social media outrage pumped by cynical algorithms to swell the profits of hypercapitalist billionaires and their colonial space-fantasies. Displeasure highlight the absurdity of this dystopian trajectory, and stresses the urgency of solidarity in dismantling the extractive capitalist core driving the whole enterprise.

https://unsanitarynapkin.bandcamp.com/

BIRDPARTY is the unlikely merger of extreme metal musician William Barrett (Heresiarch) and ambient/electronic dance producer Emma Bernard (Ludus). Constructed with sample-based textures, trippy vocals and drums, the duo build scintillating sci-fi soundtracks for the adventurous listener. Undefinable and unmissable, BIRDPARTY’s live show explores the realms between ambience and uproar — delivering a cathartically noisy spread of cinematic, semi-industrial goods & services.

Since emerging in 2023, BIRDPARTY have established themselves as one of the most exciting live acts in New Zealand, captivating crowds at festivals such as Twisted Frequency, Newtown Festival, Camp A Low Hum and Welcome to Nowhere, as well as the City Gallery of Wellington.

https://birdpartynz.bandcamp.com/

description:
Altared States | Electronic Soundscapes in a Divine Place, Wellington’s iconic Old St Paul’s will play host to a transcendent new series in August, partnering with the Pyramid Club to present Altared States, a unique electronic music experience.
Set beneath the exquisite stained-glass windows of one of Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s most exquisite landmarks, this series promises an immersive sonic experience that invites audiences to explore sound in a deeply personal and transformative way.
Altared States is inspired by Brian Sweeney’s New York-founded Ambient Church, an initiative dedicated to collaborating with artists to create transformative audio performances in architecturally significant spaces. This series will immerse attendees in soundscapes that transcend the ordinary, offering a chance to disconnect for a moment from the modern world.
Each of the evenings will bring a different electronic vibe, conjured by some of Wellington’s most innovative artists. The series lineup includes:
August 1: Ludus
August 8: Stephen Gallagher with David Long and Jules Desmond
August 15: Oghum
August 22: Dream Chambers
Set within the chancel at the altar of the venue, each artist will perform a 60-minute immersive sound experience that redefines ritual in a contemporary light.
Tickets are available from Wednesday 18 June, with limited capacity of 50 for each show of this intimate series.
About the Artists
Ludus
is the captivating musical venture curated by Emma Bernard. Her creative inspiration spans across the worlds of electronic music, audio engineering, sound design, and the written word. Bernard’s artistic journey explores the deep connection between soundscapes and the natural world, with a focus on evoking emotional responses to the environments we inhabit. She is also co-founder of the Pōneke-based collective Tonic.
Stephen Gallagher
is an Emmy award-winning composer and music editor who has worked on an extensive range of projects, from global blockbusters to television and contemporary dance. Most recently, he completed the score for The Lord of the Rings: The War of the Rohirrim, directed by Kenji Kamiyama. Gallagher’s work spans collaborations with Peter Jackson, Brian Eno, Ed Sheeran, Nick Cave, and many more.
David Long
is a composer, performer, founding member of The Mutton Birds, and member of easy listening noise band, Teeth. His career has spanned over 40 years and seen him work on numerous projects to commercial and critical acclaim. In his own words he likes to “mash shit up”, creating orchestral scores that utilise “not only classical instruments but all sorts of things”.
Jules Desmond
is an experimental musician from Wellington who has played in bands including Letterbox Lambs, 1/3 Octave Band, Bachelor of Architecture and Black Boned Angel.
Oghum
is the interstellar duo of Nell Thomas (Orchestra of Spheres, Cookie Brooklyn and the Crumbs) and Jonny Marks (All Seeing Hand, Mean Bones), performing on Synthi AKS, theremin and other assorted items. Oghum blends electronic sounds from times past with an array of acoustic and found sounds, using nuanced improvisation to create detailed and tangible sonic environments, invoking memory and transporting the listener through narrow gaps into wide open otherworldly spaces.
Jess Chambers
is a composer, musician, and educator currently based in Aotearoa New Zealand, and working under the moniker Dream Chambers. From her beginnings as a folk singer to her current explorations in electronic music, she experiments with sound as a practice of attention: to a room, an outer world, an inner feeling. It’s in that space of beholding where transformation and connection occur, and Chambers is a master alchemist, likening that stretch of attention in music to growing a garden: “There’s a lot of searching, reaching and eventual blossoming in my music – it feels like coming up from underground, like a tulip bulb.”
The Pyramid Club, located on Taranaki Street, is an artist-run space dedicated to experimental music and sonic arts, providing a home for innovative sound exploration.

Ravel - Sonatine, M. 40, Modéré and Mouvement de Menuet

Schubert - "Lebensstürme," Allegro in A minor, D 947

Amanda Bunting, piano

Amanda Bunting is a graduate of the New Zealand School of Music, completing her Bachelor of Music with Honours in 2019 in solo piano performance with Dr. Jian Liu; small group ensemble with members of the NZSQ, and performance and embodiment studies with Dr. Hamish Robb and Dr. Margaret Medlyn. Prior to that, she completed a Graduate Diploma in Music in performance piano, performance studies, and pedagogy.

After previously studying with Gillian Bibby at the Conservatorium of Music and graduating in 1996, Amanda chose to return to study, with the guidance of Rosemary Bromley, to further develop performance skills and to gain further knowledge that can inspire and be shared with her piano students. Amanda is an Associate of the Institute of Registered Music Teachers New Zealand and a member of the Wellington Branch. She has an established private piano teaching studio, teaches piano at St Mark’s Church School, and also works as a Human Resources Adviser at Victoria University of Wellington.


Kris Zuelicke, piano

Kris Zuelicke grew up in a theatrical and musical family and began performing from age 5. During school years, she accompanied and sang in choirs and performed in community and Miami University Theatre productions, including on piano, cello and harpsichord. After earning undergraduate degrees in music, linguistics and German in the United States from Miami University and a master's in music theory with a cognate in music education from Indiana University, she taught music along with other subjects at Montessori schools in Bloomington, Indiana and in Landau, Germany. While living in Germany, Kris also enjoyed teaching at the Karlsruhe Teachers College, including developing courses that utilised the arts to teach English.

In New Zealand, Kris obtained a doctorate in harpsichord from the New Zealand School of Music, studying with Douglas Mews and Erin Helyard, and won scholarships to study with Mark Kroll in Boston. She currently teaches in schools around Wellington, while maintaining a private studio for piano and cello lessons, along with accompanying university exams at the NZSM. Kris enjoys playing chamber music with friends, and has performed with the Renaissance Singers, Manawatu Sinfonia, the Queen’s Closet and Stroma, along with a fun stint as a harpsichordist extra in the recently released Time Bandits.

description:
Amici (Saxophone Quintet), Long-established Amici Ensemble performs each year with varying combinations of instruments. In 2026 this is a quintet with the saxophone adding richness to a string quartet. The performers are Donald Armstrong – violin, Anna van der Zee – violin, Nicholas Hancox – viola, Andrew Joyce – cello, and Simon Brew – saxophone. The string players are members of the NZSO, joined by Simon Brew who is much in demand as a saxophonist.

Since Adolf Sax invented the saxophone in the 1840s, composers have been enchanted with its sonorities, combining the saxophone with other instruments in many idioms. Composers such as Debussy and Ravel incorporated its beautiful sweetness in their music, influencing more recent composers such as Ellen Zwilich and Russell Peterson.

This unusual lineup of saxophone and string quartet, while embracing their classical origins, plunge headlong into the evocative sounds, catchy rhythms and soaring melodies that this combination lends itself to.

Russell Peterson, Quintet for Alto Saxophone and Strings
Max Richter, On the Nature of Daylight (string quartet)
Ellen Taaffe Zwilich, Quintet for Alto Saxophone and Strings

Andrew Fagan - Paekakariki, Andrew Fagan - Paekakariki
Andrew Fagan - iconic New Zealand solo sailor, songwriter, and frontman of legendary Kiwi band The Mockers - hits the road with a 20-date nationwide solo tour: Passage Of Time – Songs and Stories from a Swirly World.

The tour charts a course from Invercargill in the deep south to Whangārei in the north, offering fans a rare chance to get up close with Fagan’s extraordinary life in music and at sea.

Picking up from his acclaimed 2024 bestselling book Swirly World: Lost at Sea, the Passage Of Time tour dives even deeper into Fagan’s thrilling and unconventional world.

description:
Andrew London Duo, Andrew London’s quirky songs will make you laugh out loud as you recognise yourself and everyone around you, and all the prejudices, obsessions and weird little habits we put out on display, every day, in this funny little country.

There are songs about politics, social status, shopping habits, teenagers, coffee, neighbours and small town protocol. And insights into the unpredictable and tenuous lives of travelling musicians, based on having played a thousand gigs from the woolsheds of Central Otago to the boardrooms of Queen Street.

Andrew’s songs have contributed to popular trio Hot Club Sandwich, country band The Cattlestops, and numerous collaborations at jazz, blues, folk, country and arts festivals from Queenstown to Auckland, Melbourne to Norfolk Island and Sydney to Saudi Arabia. The enforced isolation of the Covid lockdown saw him and his partner/bass player, Kirsten, rearrange his entire repertoire for duo, the results viewable on eight YouTube episodes called ‘Live at The Londons’.

His current show ‘Songs I Wrote When I Was Cross’ sees the duo tighter than ever, the songs more concise, with the accent on occasionally acerbic satire, self-deprecating humour and astonishing wordcraft. Andrew’s partner, Kirsten, provides bass guitar, vocals and counselling.

‘I’ve never seen anyone sing so many words, so fast, without swallowing his own tongue. These guys are Flight of the Conchords for Rest Homes’ said a Radio NZ caretaker.

Come and have a laugh at yourself.
