description:
Anna Fält - Vocal music from Sweden and Finland, Anna Fält is a versatile singer-songwriter who is passionate about Nordic folk singing. She ́s been touring around Scandinavia, as well as outside Europe, for years with her unique concept of solo vocal concerts. Specializing in different singing traditions from her two home countries Finland and Sweden, she combines the bright Scandinavian and dark East-European tones, performing in churches, museums, festivals, folk music venues, clubs and concert halls.

These concerts are tributes to the human voice, a one woman band, singing like you've never heard it before! Tradition meets vocal arts, avantgarde and story telling in an innovative and personal, intimate way.

Besides her solo concerts, Anna works with performing arts and multidisciplinary art projects, with folk music research and teaching various folk song workshops. She has 3 music degrees and she ́s been studying folk music in 5 different countries. Her main work is, however, being a solo artist and developing the solo a cappella singing.

description:
Anna Fält - Workshop: Nordic Folk Songs, Anna Fält - Workshop: Nordic Folk Songs
Anna Fält (Finland/Sweden) has a degree in pop/jazz singing (2006), folk music education (2011) and a master in Nordic folk music (2017). She's been studying in renowned universities such as The Royal Music Academy in Stockholm and Sibelius Academy in Helsinki.

Anna´s been teaching private lessons since 2008 both in person and online. After graduating as a folk singing teacher 2011, her educational work consists mostly of workshops and courses introducing Finnish singing traditions for non-Finnish people. All material is taught by ear and consists of simple melodies with lots of possibilities for variation - everyone can join, no matter the background! The emphasis is always in Enjoying singing & sounding together.

Anna's specialities are singing traditions from Finland and Sweden, combining the bright Scandinavian and dark East-European tones. She is passionate about the human voice and is known for her innovative ways to use voice as an versatile instrument. She's been teaching workshops at various universities and music schools around the world.

description:
Antipodes, Antipodes is a quintet of musicians from Sydney and Te Whanganui-a-Tara/Wellington that playfully moves between the arty/cerebral and the folksy/earthy elements of jazz and improvised music. Sometimes delicate and considered, sometimes brawny and muscular, the intent that brings their performances together is a commitment to the song: each composition is a glistening artefact, brought to dynamic life by the ensemble.

Originally formed in Berlin and drawing influences from New York to Stockholm, Antipodes has, over 10 years of touring and recording, forged their own identity: a unique triptych of North American, Northern European, and South Pacific sounds that captivates audiences, offering them a shared journey into their dreamlike and evocative co-creations.

Featuring:

Jake Baxendale (saxophone)
Callum Allardice (guitar)
Luke Sweeting (piano)
Tom Botting (bass)
Tim Geldens (drums)

Part of the Wellington Jazz Festival 2025

description:
Antu Marama, The Undercurrent presents Antu Marama!

Wellington band Antü Mārama brings you the vibrant evocative folk music of Latin America, with traditional tunes and original compositions. From Chile, the UK, New Zealand and the Canary Islands the group's ethos is represented by the name - Antü is the Mapudungún word for sun, while Mārama is the Te reo Māori word for Moon.

The group combines both the life-giving energy and vitality of the sun with the deeper emotions and more reflective energy of the Moon. Antü Mārama is a synthesis of the group's diverse backgrounds and musical experiences, united by a love of playing music, and a desire to share the rich folk tradition of Latin America with a local audience.

Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra - The Nutcracker Suite tickets, Witness a defining moment in this country’s jazz scene as the Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra (AoJO) makes its highly anticipated debut at Meow Nui.
Born from a collective vision championed and inspired by jazz legend Rodger Fox, AoJO represents the shared aspirations of the jazz community – honouring our jazz lineage while serving as a platform for its future. This newly formed, and proudly national ensemble brings our country’s jazz talent and legacy into focus.
Led by Musical Director John Rae and Concert Master Oscar Lavën, with Mike Taylor (lead trumpet) and Kaito Walley (lead trombone), this concert features Duke Ellington and Billy Strayhorn’s vibrant reimagining of Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker Suite. A groundbreaking fusion of classical and jazz, it’s hailed as one of Ellington’s most inventive works. Together Strayhorn and Ellington showcase the familiar themes of Tchaikovsky’s ballet through the expressive power of jazz in orchestral form.
Prepare to be captivated by lush orchestration and melodic innovation as the AoJO takes to the stage for the very first time.

description:
Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra tickets, The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra (AoJO) returns to Wellington with a contemporary re-imagining of one of the most influential works of the 20th century: George Gershwin’s Rhapsody in Blue. The performance takes place at Meow Nui on Thursday 6 March at 7.00pm, featuring acclaimed pianist Ben Wilcock.

First heard in 1924, Rhapsody in Blue broke new ground by fusing jazz language with symphonic form. In this performance, AoJO honours the essence of Gershwin’s original while re-examining the work through a modern big band lens — expanding its orchestral colours, rhythmic drive, and improvisational possibilities for today’s audiences.

AoJO Musical Director John Rae says the orchestra approached the piece with both respect and curiosity:

“Gershwin was writing music that looked forward, not backward. Our aim with this version of Rhapsody in Blue is to treat it the same way, to honour the original while allowing it to speak in a contemporary jazz language that feels alive right now.”

The performance features pianist Ben Wilcock, widely regarded as one of Aotearoa’s leading jazz artists, whose international career spans Europe, the UK, and New Zealand.

“Ben brings an incredible combination of authority, imagination, and openness to this music,” says Rae. “He understands Gershwin from the inside out, and he’s not afraid to take risks, which is exactly what this piece demands.”

Wilcock has been praised internationally for his distinctive musical voice: “Wilcock combines dazzling technical command with a rare sense of musical narrative — his playing is both fearless and deeply expressive.” — All About Jazz

Another review described him as “A pianist of remarkable clarity and imagination, equally at home in classical repertoire and cutting-edge jazz.”

Alongside this project, AoJO continues its broader mission of developing large-ensemble jazz in Aotearoa and creating meaningful performance opportunities for local musicians.

“The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra exists to celebrate, develop, and present contemporary large-ensemble jazz in Aotearoa — supporting our musicians, engaging new audiences, and placing this music in a living cultural context rather than a museum one.”

Event details
What: Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra: Gershwin’s Rhapsody in Blue
Featuring: Ben Wilcock (piano)
Where: Meow Nui, Wellington
When: Friday 6 March 2026, 7.00pm

Aroha Quartet and Friends, The popular Wellington-based Aroha String Quartet (violinists Haihong LIu and Konstanze Artmann. violist Zongxian Jin and cellist Robert Ibell) will be joined by four colleagues from the NZSO and Orchestra Wellington to present a rare performance of Schubert's famous Octet for Wind and Strings. This very substantial work of just under an hour's length has six movements, all of them brimming with warmth, charm and glorious melody. There is a wide variety of tonal colour as each of the instruments in turn shares the limelight, with delightful solo lines from violins, viola, cello, clarinet, bassoon, horn and double-bass. The clarinetist will be Nick Walshe, Justin Sun the bassoonist, joined by Alexander Hambleton (horn) and Oleksandr Gunchenko (double-bass).

Also on the programme will be a string quartet by Mozart (No 22 in B flat, K589) and a humorous light-hearted piece by Danish composer Carl Nielsen called "Serenata in Vano" in which a group of musicians attempt. unsuccessfully, to attract the attention of a young woman.

description:
Aroha String Quartet, Founded in 2004, this well-known versatile Wellington-based quartet is Haihong Liu - violin, Konstanze Artmann - violin, Eli Vincent - viola, and Robert Ibell – cello.

Aroha Quartet presents a programme titled “Heart” of heartwarming music from the heart of the chamber music repertoire. It begins with a sparkling piece by the father of the string quartet, Josef Haydn, followed by the Ross Carey’s lovely Toccatina.

American composer Samuel Barber wrote to a friend in 1936 “I have just finished the slow movement of my quartet today (and) its a knockout”. Like a huge inbreath and outbreath, this amazing piece (often performed by string orchestra as the Barber Adagio) is flanked by two wonderful outer movements.

Beethoven’s glorious String Quartet No 10 covers the range of human moods from tranquil calm, to restlessness, heartfelt outbursts and resolute determination. Its nickname, ‘Harp’, comes from the striking pizzicato section in the first movement.

Joseph Haydn, String Quartet in E-flat Op 64 No 6
Samuel Barber, String Quartet in B min Op 11
Ross Carey, Toccatina
Ludwig van Beethoven, String Quartet No 10 in E-flat Op 74 ‘Harp’

description:
Aroha String Quartet, Programme:
Haydn: String Quartet, Opus 64, No 6
Samuel Barber: String Quartet in B minor
Ross Carey: Toccatina
Beethoven: String Quartet, Opus 74 "Harp"

The Aroha String Quartet are popular regular visitors to Waikanae. This time they are joined by a new member, violist Eli Vincent. Australian born, he performed in Germany for some years before joining the NZSO in 2022. Outgoing violist Zhongxian Jin leaves the quartet to allow time for his teaching commitments in China. The remaining long-standing members of the quartet are Haihong Liu and Konstanze Artmann (violins) and Robert Ibell (cello).

The concert opens with a delightfully lyrical quartet by Haydn, Samuel Barber's string quartet follows. Barber is well known for his famous Adagio for Strings but many are unaware that this was originally the slow movement of his only string quartet, written in 1936. Barber arranged the Adagio for string orchestra the same year and later arranged it again as his much-loved and deeply moving choral work Agnus Dei.

After the interval New Zealander Ross Carey's charming Toccatina leads the way to Beethoven's popular Opus 74 quartet, known as "The Harp" because of the striking pizzicato effects in the first movement. A beautiful Adagio and lively Scherzo follow before the quartet ends with a widely varied Theme and Variations movement.

a 10-piece NZ band of varying cultural backgrounds, hence the name.

description:
Auckland Kristallnacht Commemorative Concert 2025, The Holocaust Centre of New Zealand must confirm all tickets generated by the Humanitix ticketing system. Once you register, you'll receive an acknowledgement from Humanitix, followed by a second email directly from the Holocaust Centre of New Zealand.
2025 Annual Kristallnacht Commemorative Concert
Escape & Exile – East & West
Join the Holocaust Centre of New Zealand for a poignant evening of remembrance and reflection. The Te Kōkī Trio, featuring Inbal Megiddo (cello), Martin Riseley (violin), and Jian Liu (piano), will be joined by Professor Kim Cunio, Head of Te Kōkī / New Zealand School of Music, in a powerful performance commemorating Kristallnacht.
 This concert commemorates Kristallnacht, or “The Night of Broken Glass,” the horrific pogroms of 9–10 November 1938, across Germany, Austria, and the Sudetenland. This state-sponsored violence saw the murder of an estimated 91 Jews, the arrest of 30,000, and the destruction of hundreds of synagogues and Jewish businesses. Kristallnacht is widely regarded as a pivotal moment, marking the escalation of Nazi persecution and often described as the beginning of the Holocaust.
 The Nazis sought to silence the music and art of all those they deemed "untermenschen," including six million Jews and other victimised groups. This concert stands as a powerful act of defiance and remembrance, allowing us to hear the voices of those who were murdered, forced into hiding, or exiled. It celebrates their artistic brilliance and ensures their memory lives on.
 This year's theme is "Escape and Exile: East and West." In the tradition of paying musical tribute to all victims, we will honour the music of Jewish composers from across the globe—from the Netherlands and Nazi-occupied Germany in the West, all the way to Iraq and Shanghai in the East.
 The programme will feature pieces that honour:
Erna Weiss Falk, a talented Jewish opera singer from Cologne, whose promising career was cut short by anti-Jewish laws. She and her family ultimately escaped to the Netherlands.
Brigitte Schiffer, a young composer who completed her doctorate in Berlin before fleeing the Nazis to Egypt, where she became the director of the Higher Music Education Institute for women.
The Al Kuwaiti brothers, Jewish pioneers of modern Iraqi music, survived the Farhud, a devastating pogrom inspired by Nazi ideology that targeted Baghdad's Jewish population on June 1-2, 1941, coinciding with the Jewish holiday of Shavuot. Despite their legacy resonating across the Middle East through radio, their contributions were erased from Iraqi history.
Ferdinand Adler, a Hungarian Jewish violinist who miraculously escaped from the Dachau concentration camp, to Shanghai.
 Join us for this important event as we mourn the lives lost and celebrate the resilience of the human spirit. We look forward to welcoming you.

Auckland: Monday, 10 November 2025
Doors Open: 6:00 PM
Concert Begins: 6:45 PM

Get ready, Wellington—one of the most influential figures in house music is landing in the capital for a night of deep grooves, soulful rhythms, and undeniable dancefloor magic at Meow NUI.

===Tickets on sale Friday 22 August at 12.00PM====

Mark Farina is a global dance music icon whose name resonates across the scene. Known for his Mushroom Jazz series, deep house sets, and marathon all-night performances, Farina has built a career on innovation, consistency, and a relentless touring schedule of over 100 shows a year. He has collaborated with legendary venues and record labels, showcasing both classic and new school producers in his sets.

With his recent YouTube series with Defected Records and continued worldwide performances, Farina connects with both longtime fans and new audiences alike, delivering unforgettable journeys through house, jazz-infused grooves, and eclectic beats.

Supporting him is Wellington’s Benny Salvador — one of New Zealand’s most exciting young talents. A DJ, producer, multi-instrumentalist, radio host, and event promoter, Benny has shared stages with Marcellus Pittman and Courtesy and played major festivals including Splore, Beacon, and Catacombs. He has recorded mixes for Planet Trip Records, NTS, Balamii, Related Articles, and Friendly Potential Radio, and released music on Racquet Club, Rush Hour, Love Above Records, Juke Bounce Werk, and his own Aunty Records. Benny’s eclectic sets blend house, techno, disco-funk, dub, and electro, drawing on jazz and funk influences while showcasing his crate-digging, collaborative approach.

description:
BB & THE BULLETS, “An authentic, powerful and generous album, which will undoubtedly place BB & The Bullets among the blues rock revelations of the year.” – Zicazic Magazine, France
It’s been a great couple of weeks for dynamic Whanganui blues band BB & THE BULLETS!
Currently playing their North Island tour, celebrating the international release of their debut album HIGH TIDE from September, the album has achieved impressive traction across Aotearoa’s music soundscape by entering the Official Top 20 Aotearoa Albums at #12 and #5 on the Independent Music NZ Charts!
Landing on both the IMNZ Charts and the Official Aotearoa Music Charts is a cracking result, not just as independent artists, but also for a blues-rock outfit, demonstrating that it’s a genre that can successfully cross both indie and conventional charts, appealing to both grassroots and mainstream audiences – an outcome that the band is thrilled about.
“It’s a great result! We are so proud to be #5 on the IMNZ Chart. Independent artists are the grassroots and lifeblood of Kiwi music. And there’s only been a few local indie blues-rock albums on the Official Aotearoa Music Charts over the last decade – our mate Grant Haua in 2022, and Troy Kingi in 2016, so we’re stoked to be here and rep the Blues in 2025!”
STREAM HIGH TIDE HERE | DOWNLOAD MEDIA + RADIO ASSETS HERE
The tight, three piece blues rock outfit of band members Brad McMillan (drums), Stu Duncan (bass), and Brian Baker (guitar / vocals) have garnered a reputation for their powerful and moving live performances, drawing comparisons to Stevie Ray Vaughan, Johnny Winter, Peter Green and Jeff Beck, while firmly putting their own stamp on the timeless medium that is the blues.
BB & The Bullets have released three well received singles to date off the album: debut single ‘Something In The Water’; album title track ‘High Tide’; and their blues-soaked rendition of the Beatles classic ‘I Want You (She’s So Heavy)’ which is a huge fan favourite at their live shows. To date, all three singles have enjoyed some excellent blues radio attention, including airplay on Radio New Zealand and around the country, as well as in Germany, USA, and Canada, with ‘High Tide’ charting at #4 on Roots Music Charts in Australia, achieving #1 on the Roots Music Report Blues Album Chart, #1 on the Blues Rock Album Chart and three songs on the Blues Singles chart.
Home country of their label Dixiefrog Records has plenty of great things to say about BB & The Bullets, with Paris Move Magazine giving the album a very favourable review, ranking it as a ‘red heart’ favourite, as has French outlet Zicazic Magazine, and the title track single ‘High Tide’ has made the weekly playlist of Rolling Stone Magazine, France.
“This album proves to be a declaration of love to the roots of the blues, driven by striking live energy and unabashed virtuosity.” – Zicazic Magazine, France
Now the trio are continuing to take their killer live show across the motu through October and November. With a well-deserved reputation for their compelling live shows, BB & The Bullets audiences are always wowed by the power and intensity of their performances.
With this chart action, it is evident that the blues scene is alive and vibrant on Antipodean shores, grab your mates and don’t miss your chance to check out a blues-rock experience like no other with BB & The Bullets!

Dec 18th, 7pm. The Underworld Tavern, Pirie St.
Tickets here.

description:
Bach Choir of Wellington present In Stillness, Peace, In Stillness, Peace traces a musical journey through different kinds of stillness and the ways peace can emerge from them. The programme brings together choral music that approaches stillness not as silence or withdrawal, but as an active state shaped by restraint, attention, balance, and trust.

The first half moves from clarity and simplicity towards deeper inward listening. Palestrina’s Sicut Cervus opens the programme with music of balance and transparency, where calm arises through proportion and flow. At the centre of the first half, Ēriks Ešenvalds’ Lux Aeterna invites quiet listening of a different kind, creating a sense of spaciousness in which light and stillness feel closely connected.

The second half is shaped around Michael John Trotta’s For a Breath of Ecstasy, a seven movement cycle for choir, string quartet, and oboe, setting poetry by Sara Teasdale. Written as a sequence of reflections, and heard here in its New Zealand
premiere, the work traces fleeting moments of attentive calm and inward stillness, offering peace not as certainty or arrival, but as something brief, fragile, and deeply felt.

Performed in the resonant space of the Cathedra of the Sacred Heart, this midwinter programme invites listeners to experience how stillness can deepen, shift, and open into peace through sound.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Bach Choir of Wellington present Sounding Boards, Echoes of Friends/Spheres of influence

What happens when composers become each other’s teachers, critics, and friends?
Their music begins to resonate — ideas travelling in widening circles, carried forward through time.

Mendelssohn and Schumann shared a productive working relationship in Leipzig, marked by deep professional respect. A generation later, Schumann’s championing of Brahms as the “future of German music” forged one of the most influential artistic bonds of the Romantic era.

Fauré and Saint-Saëns sustained a remarkable sixty-year friendship, documented in more than a hundred letters. Saint-Saëns taught Fauré, mentored him, and opened the doors of Parisian musical life, shaping his early career.

Mozart and Haydn were kindred spirits across a generation, admiring each other’s craft, playing quartets together, and exchanging works. Mozart dedicated his six “Haydn” quartets to his elder friend — a gesture of profound artistic respect.

Bartók and Kodály discovered a shared passion for Hungarian folk music in 1905, sparking a partnership that transformed ethnomusicology. Their fieldwork shaped two distinct musical voices and left a lasting imprint on 20th-century composition.

Copland, Bernstein, and Barber formed a vibrant American circle. Bernstein regarded Copland as his “only real composition teacher,” while Barber shared their artistic milieu; all three worked closely with the Boston Symphony at Tanglewood.

Holst and Vaughan Williams, the self-styled “committee of two,” were lifelong friends and trusted critics. Their shared ideals and collaboration helped define the sound of English music in the early 20th century.

These are the musical friendships that shaped eras and traditions. Join the Bach Choir for Sounding Boards, featuring music shaped by the artistic relationships that defined their time.

description:
Balinese Gamelan @ The Dell, Balinese Gamelan @ The Dell
Lay out your picnic rug, lie back and enjoy a stunning performance from Gamelan Taniwha Jaya (Balinese gamelan ensemble) in The Dell, behind Begonia House.

The ensemble have kindly donated their time and musicality as a fund raiser for the Begonia House renovation.

Koha will be collected, all donations going towards the renovation.

There will be a food truck onsite for authentic Balinese treats or simply bring your own picnic.

Experience the vibrant sound world of Bali as local musicians Gamelan Taniwha Jaya present an exhilarating programme of traditional Balinese percussion music. The concert features temple music, 20th century compositions by renowned Balinese composers, and music to accompany dance.

Performed on striking, intricately carved bronze instruments, the music is in the Gong Kebyar style - known for its explosive energy, unpredictable rhythms, and dramatic dynamic contrasts. The sound shimmers and pulses, ranging from delicate, high‑tinkling metallophones to the deep resonance of massive booming gongs.

As a special highlight, the event also features a mesmerising performance of Ratoh Jaroe - a traditional Acehnese dance presented by the Indonesian Students Association. Performed in unison by female dancers in a kneeling formation, this visually stunning piece blends rapid hand movements and rhythmic vocalisations to express devotion and grace.

description:
Bar Italia (UK) 'Some Like It Hot' NZ Tour, SATURDAY 13 DECEMBER - HOLLYWOOD AVONDALE, AUCKLAND
SUNDAY 14 DECEMBER - MEOW, WELLINGTON

“...grungy, gritty, and a bit sexy” - Stereogum
“...swaggering and devastatingly cool” - NME

Hot on the heels of announcing their highly anticipated new album Some Like It Hot, the eternally enigmatic UK post-punk darlings bar italia have also unveiled two huge New Zealand shows for this December, brought to you by Strange News Touring and Banished Music. Saturday 13th of December, the band will take the stage at Auckland’s glorious Hollywood Avondale for an all-ages show, playing Meow in Wellington on Sunday 14th December.

After bursting onto the scene with two incredible albums in a single year - the brilliant Tracey Denim and the noisy niceness of The Twits - bar italia spent the next while earning a reputation as one of the best live bands in the game, including a sold out and sweaty show at Auckland’s Neck of the Woods. Since then, the band have been plotting their next move in world domination, dropping fan favourite single Cowbella in June, and this week lifting the lid on Some Like It Hot with accompanying tune Fundraiser - with a video featuring Matt “Super Hans” King.

The London based band, built around the core of Nina Cristante, Jezmi Tarik Fehmi and Sam Fenton, may have looked to be hiding out this year while cooking up this new batch of tunes, but in reality they’ve been anything but dormant. Cristante teamed up with Yves Tumor for a dangerously good duet on We Don’t Count, while Jezmi and Sam dropped another full-length album under their Double Virgo moniker just last month.

With the album dropping on Matador this October, local fans will have a couple of short months to learn the words and get ready to scream and swoon along when bar italia hit our shores this December. Shit yeah!
Tickets on sale now at Banished Music

description:
Baxter Dury tickets, Presented by: Live Nation
Following the release of his latest album, UK alternative artist Baxter Dury is bringing his Allbarone Tour 2026 to Australia and New Zealand. With genre-blurring music that blends post-punk, indietronica and art-rock, his sound leans on sleek synths and a cool, understated aesthetic rooted in a distinctly British sensibility. ‘Allbarone’ can be described as a nine-track tour-de-force, stripping everything away and building Baxter’s most melodically direct, futuristic collection yet.
The Australian leg of the tour will kick off at Melbourne’s Forum on April 28, before heading to Roundhouse in Sydney on April 29, and concluding at The Tivoli in Brisbane on May 1. Dury will then head to New Zealand for performances at The Hollywood Avondale in Auckland on May 3 and Wellington’s Meow Nui on May 4.

description:
Bear's Den New Zealand 2026 | Wellington, Bear's Den New Zealand 2026 | Wellington
British country and indie-folk band Bear’s Den are coming to play their first ever headline shows in Aotearoa. They’ll perform at Auckland’s Tuning Fork on Tuesday 12 May and San Fran Wellington on Wednesday 13 May. Tickets go on sale this Thursday 26 March at midday

Formed in London 2012, Bear’s Den have carved out a global reputation and devoted following for over a decade. Their debut album Islands was certified gold, with the hit single ‘Above The Clouds of Pompeii’ nominated for the Ivor Novello Award for Best Song musically and lyrically. Since then, they’ve created four critically acclaimed studio albums, a collaborative project with screenwriter Paul Frith and a soundtrack album to Season 3 of Apple TV Series Trying.

Their emotive story telling and cinematic sound has made up a catalogue that translates into film and onto live stages, taking them to some of the world’s biggest arenas and festivals, including Reading and Leeds, Glastonbury Festival, Pukkelpop, Lowlands and Bonnaroo.

Consisting of founding member Andrew Davie on vocals and guitar, Christof van der Ven (banjo, guitar, vocals), Marcus Hamblett (synths, horns), and Jools Owen (drums, horns), the band have been on the road celebrating the 10 year anniversary of Islands for the past year and they’re now set to bring it all to New Zealand for the first time.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Beethoven in Kelburn, BEETHOVEN IN KELBURN

An Evening of Chamber Music

Join Koru Trio for an evening of wonderful music in the beautiful surroundings of St Michael’s Church, Kelburn.

We’ll be performing one of Beethoven’s most loved chamber works, the magnificent Archduke Trio—a piece full of soaring melodies, warmth, humour, and brilliance. To begin, enjoy Beethoven’s charming Romance in F Major for violin and piano, a work of lyrical beauty and elegance.

Koru Trio brings together three Wellington musicians who share a love of chamber music and the joy of performing it for others. Whether you are a devoted classical music enthusiast or simply curious to hear live music in an intimate setting, we would love you to join us.

KORU TRIO
Rachel Thomson - Piano
Anne Loeser - Violin
Sally Isaac - Cello

ENTRY BY KOHA
Suggested contribution:
$20 Adult | $10 Student

description:
Beoga New Zealand 2026 | Wellington, Acclaimed Irish band Beoga will make their long-awaited return to New Zealand in January 2026, performing two intimate headline shows in Auckland and Wellington.
Known for their adventurous spirit and willingness to chart new musical territory, Beoga have redefined the possibilities of Irish traditional music. Their global reach was cemented through collaborations with Ed Sheeran on the record-breaking ÷ (Divide) album, including the smash hits “Galway Girl” and “Nancy Mulligan.” The former has now surpassed 1.4 billion streams on Spotify alone.
After a four-year hiatus from touring and releasing music, Beoga made a powerful comeback earlier this year with their new album Phases, released in June. The band went on to perform at Glastonbury and Coachella, where they shared the stage with Shaboozey, Alex Warren, and Ed Sheeran at his now-famous Old Phone Pub pop-up experience.
With a GRAMMY nomination, international tours, and collaborations with some of the biggest names in music, Beoga have established themselves as one of Ireland’s most exciting and genre-blurring acts. Their sound fuses accordion, fiddle, keyboards, guitars, and vocals into a vibrant, modern take on Irish roots music that feels both timeless and new.

description:
Between the Lines: Private Lives with New Zealand String Quartet, This event will take place in Ngā Pou Ruahine on Level 2 of Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, Wellington Central Library.

The theme of our June musical book club is private lives.

Between the Lines is a monthly early-evening chamber music series and book club that brings music and literature into conversation. Presented in the beautiful setting of Ngā Pou Ruahine in Te Matapihi, the series invites audiences to listen, think, and talk. No prior knowledge of music or literature is required, just a curious mind.

Taking place monthly from April to October on the final Thursday of each month, Between the Lines has been co-created by New Zealand String Quartet, Orchestra Wellington, and New Zealand School of Music. Each month these organisations will take turns presenting a talented group of musicians to perform music and host discussion on a different literary theme. From devil’s bargains to language games, the obsessive tortured artist to the intimate private lives of writers and composers, this book club will delve deep into themes that span across artforms.

Each session will feature carefully selected music and a reading list highlighting the theme of the month. So, arrive solo or bring your book club to Te Matapihi for a new kind of conversation.


The theme of our June musical book club is private lives.

Music to be performed:
Amadeus Mozart | String quartet Kv. 465 “Dissonance”, 1st movement
Leoš Janáček | Intimate Letters, 3rd movement
Dmitri Shostakovich | String Quartet No. 8, 1st & 2nd movement
Felix Mendelssohn | String Quartet No.6, Op.80, 1st movement
Pyotr Tchaikovsky | String Quartet No. 1, Op. 11, 2nd movement
Florence Price | "Adoration"

Optional reading list is available on the New Zealand String Quartet website.

Music and literature both have the power to transport an audience deep into the interior private lives of the composer and author. For our June musical book club, Between the Lines, which will take place on the anniversary of the publication of Anne Frank’s diaries in 1947, the New Zealand String Quartet have devised a programme of music that explores the ‘Private Lives’, secret thoughts, and hidden desires of four composers. Mozart, Janáček, Shostakovich, Mendelssohn, Tchaikovsky and Price each encoded their music with secrets, imbuing their music with a personal significance often at odds with their public personas. Now, by reading their letters, alongside performing their music, we can learn more about these composers’ personalities and appreciate their thoughts, fears, and hopes.

The reading list for ‘Private Lives’ brings together a variety of primary sources – the letters and diaries of artists, writers, composers and people living through extraordinary and difficult times – alongside fiction that utilises diary and letter forms.


Explore the rest of the series:

Thursday 28 May, 5:30pm - New Zealand String Quartet - Obsession (first & second sessions to take place on Ngā Paiaka/ Bleachers on Te Papa Whenua/ Ground Floor)

description:
Bic Runga & The NZSO, More than 60 classical musicians will collaborate with Bic Runga and her band for a special concert in Wellington. Bic Runga & the NZSO is a concert of songs from Bic’s much-anticipated new album ‘Red Sunset’. The performance will also feature a selection of hits and best-loved songs spanning the artist’s extraordinary 31-year career.   
This is the only leg of the ‘Red Sunset’ tour featuring orchestra, so expect the songs to be transformed by the powerful accompaniment. Also involved in the show is Bic’s partner, multi-instrumentalist Kody Nielson of The Mint Chicks and Unknown Mortal Orchestra fame.   
Bic Runga (Ngāti Kahungunu) is a multi-award-winning singer-songwriter. The youngest inductee into the New Zealand Music Hall of Fame, she shot to fame in 1996 with the single ‘Drive’. Her 1997 debut album ‘Drive’, including the hit ‘Sway’, won the Tūī for Album of the Year. Over her career, she has won 20 Tūī awards — the most for an Aotearoa solo artist, including Best Female Vocalist four times. 
A New Zealand Order of Merit recipient for services to music. Bic is also acclaimed for her collaborations and live performances with other music icons, such as Tim and Neil Finn, Sir Dave Dobbyn and Anika Moa. She’s also inspired and influenced a new generation of New Zealand musicians. Lorde described her as “New Zealand music royalty” when she performed on stage with Bic in 2019.

James Gray is a contemporary version of an old-school traveling folk singer. In the past decade, Gray has toured Canada, Europe, Australia and New Zealand seeing the world and sharing his beloved songs along the way. A unique finger style guitarist, with a vocal that is hauntingly beautiful, Gray, often accompanied by a rather droll, humorous stage patter, immerses himself in each and every song with a soulfulness and attack that is infectious and disarming.
James is currently touring New Zealand for the second time, with shows up and down the country. For this Wellington show, James is joined by local friends the Bidibids.
With lush harmonies, intricate arrangements, and beguiling melodies, the Bidibids balance soulful ballads that will tug your heart-strings with upbeat numbers which will get your toes tapping. This trio from Aotearoa New Zealand is built around Sarah August's honest, intimate songwriting, driven by Brendan Scheck's blazing mandolin and guitar, and anchored by Simon Carryer on cello-banjo.

BIG COUNTRY, the Legendary Scottish Celtic Rock band, return for the first time since 2019 for The Greatest Hits Tour. Setlist includes – In A Big Country, Chance, Fields of Fire, Look Away, Wonderland plus much more

Featuring the band’s de facto theme song — “In a Big Country”, their debut album, The Crossing, combined anthemic post-punk with folk-inspired guitar sounds to become the leading representative of 80’s Celtic Rock. It was a surprisingly influential mix that would inspire an entirely new wave of British rock artists who openly embraced their Celtic heritage. BIG COUNTRY achieved major international success plus two Grammy nominations and for a time rivalled fellow “big sounding” British guitar rock acts U2 and Simple Minds.

Big guitars, big drums, big checks on their shirts, BIG COUNTRY were well named!

Guitarist, singer and songwriter Bill Lake is one of New Zealand’s most respected and long-serving practitioners. For more than four decades the singer and guitarist led the iconic country-blues band The Windy City Strugglers, as well as playing with pioneering rock group Mammal in the 70s and fronting brassy funk-rockers The Pelicans in the 80s. description:
Bill Lake, “Gentle, sometimes witty and just as often moving reflections at every turn” – Graham Reid

Guitarist, singer and songwriter Bill Lake is a cornerstone of Aotearoa’s musical landscape. With a career spanning more than four decades, Bill has shaped the sound of New Zealand roots music—leading the iconic Windy City Strugglers, co-founding the pioneering rock outfit Mammal, and fronting the brassy, groove-laden Pelicans in the 80s.

A gifted storyteller with a wry lyrical touch, Bill’s songs have been covered by Midge Marsden, Darren Watson, Kokomo, Rag Poets and Marg Layton. His live performances are intimate, soulful affairs—equal parts reflection and revelation.

Bill is joined by longtime friend and Mammal bandmate Steve Hemmens, recently returned from the UK, whose supple bass lines bring warmth and swing. Rounding out the trio is multi-instrumentalist Alan Norman (The Warratahs, Rag Poets), adding colour and texture on accordion, percussion, guitar, and piano.

Together, they offer a rich, rootsy blend of blues, folk, and country music with heart, history, and a touch of Wellington grit.

Black Country, New Road with Ringlets | Meow Nui, Wellington, Black Country, New Road with Ringlets | Meow Nui, Wellington
Handsome Tours are pleased to present the return of Black Country, New Road to Australia + New Zealand in 2026!

Critically acclaimed British collective Black Country, New Road are thrilled to announce their forthcoming Australia + New Zealand tour, set to take place this summer. The announcement arrives in the wake of the band’s most recent studio album, Forever Howlong, which has attracted widespread praise for its recent harmonious reinvention- and recorder solos.

Released earlier this year via Ninja Tune, Forever Howlong marks a bold transformation for the group. Songwriting and vocal duties now shared amongst band members, give rise to a richly collaborative sound and warm communal spirit. ‘Triumph in the face of adversity’ goes some way to explaining the resulting joy.

Described by The Guardian as “a gentler, more bucolic direction” Forever Howlong has made notable chart inroads for the band, revealing new audiences and a revived sense of self.

Now Black Country, New Road are ready to share their evolving sound with Australian and New Zealand audiences. These theatrical live performances are a ‘mustn’t miss’ kind of situation.

Bob McNeill & Emily Roughton in concert, Bob McNeill & Emily Roughton in concert
DATE: Saturday Sept 27
TIME: 7pm
LOCATION: The Offering – 65 Main St, Greytown
AGES:
COST: $25 pp at the door or booking link below

Bob McNeill & Emily Roughton are two of New Zealand’s best-known folk musicians. They bring their deep musical connection to festivals across New Zealand, playing their favourite songs and tunes collected over years of playing together at festivals, stages and late into the night at kitchen tables. Based in Wellington, Bob is one of NZ’s best-known folk songwriters and a favourite with Greytown audiences. His songs have been covered by artists in NZ, Australia, the UK and the USA. New Zealand Musician magazine compared his songwriting to Bruce Springsteen and Mark Knopfler; the Dominion Post likened him to Jackson Brown, James Taylor, Luka Bloom and Dougie Ma¬cLean. A guitarist, he is known for his distinctive open-tuned acoustic fingerstyle and electric guitar playing. He has toured widely in NZ, Australia, Canada, Ireland, the UK and the USA. His latest album, released in June 2024, is Lost Stars, an extended release on CD and download featuring new recordings and rarities, with Emily on violin and piano.

From Whangarei, Emily is a virtuoso violinist inspired by the Scottish tradition and the modern trad movement. Classically trained, she is infinitely adaptable with her gorgeous stylings and fiery tune playing, making her the perfect foil for Bob’s lyrical songs.

Don’t miss a chance to see these two consummate musicians share their foot-stomping collection of banging tunes, favourite songs and stolen moments from the last 20 years.

Book your tickets here:
https://greytownarttown.com/bob-mcneill-and-emily-roughton-in-concert/

description:
Bob McNeill @ Raumati Social Club, Bob McNeill @ Raumati Social Club
One of the most popular New Zealand folk artists of the last two decades, multi award-winning songwriter Bob McNeill brings his acclaimed new album TWELVE DREAMS OF THE RIVER to an intimate concert at Raumati Social Club.

McNeill's songs have been covered by artists in NZ, Australia, the UK and USA. New Zealand Musician magazine compared his songwriting to Bruce Springsteen and Mark Knopfler; the Dominion Post likened him to Jackson Browne, James Taylor, Luka Bloom and Dougie MacLean. A compelling storyteller, his songs paint vivid pictures of the moments of decision in people's lives. He has three New Zealand Music Awards (Tuis), all for Best Folk Album. Known for his many collaborations with some of New Zealand's finest musicians, this is his first solo tour in a decade and showcases his unique songwriting, celebrated guitar playing and gorgeous live sound.

McNeill tours his new album TWELVE DREAMS OF THE RIVER. Featuring his signature rich songwriting, the album explores themes of life, age and transition, re-imagined as a trip down three iconic rivers - the Manuherikia in the South Island, the Waikato in the North Island, and the Kelvin in his native Scotland. It's McNeill's most intimate work to date, with some of his most beautiful songs.

Don't miss this intimate live show from one of New Zealand's great songwriters.

Body Ocean — Live @ Meow, Body Ocean, a dynamic force in the realm of electronic music, specialises in crafting immersive and kinetic house music. Their sonic journey explores the interplay between organic and artificial elements, navigating contrasts between personality and dissolution, as well as the push and pull of extraversion and introspection.

With an impressive catalogue of releases on influential labels such as Size, Black Book Records, Mad Decent, Dirtybird, Box of Cats, and STMPD RCRDS, Body Ocean has firmly established themselves as a notable presence in the electronic music scene. They've also left a lasting mark with remixes for acclaimed artists including Steve Angello, Valentino Khan, Alison Wonderland, Ane Brun, and Mija.

Their commitment to pushing sonic boundaries and exploring diverse musical dimensions sets them apart — fuelling a growing reputation as innovators within the industry.

As they gear up for 2024, Body Ocean is poised to captivate dancefloors with a compelling fusion of sound and a vision that looks firmly to the future of electronic music.

description:
Boy & Bear New Zealand tickets, Presented by: Eccles
Australian indie-folk favourites Boy & Bear announce their return to Aotearoa, playing three consecutive shows in Wellington, Christchurch and Auckland this June. Tickets go on sale Tuesday 7 April at midday.
Off the back of their sixth studio album Tripping Over Time, released in December 2025 and an extensive international tour across Canada, the UK and Europe, the band are set to arrive in peak form.
Boy & Bear emerged onto the global stage with their breakthrough debut album Moonfire, which earned multi-platinum success and five ARIA Awards in 2011. Two years later their follow-up, Harlequin Dream debuted at #1on the ARIA Albums charts, and they went on to amass five consecutive Top 10 albums and more than half a billion streams worldwide.
New Zealand last saw the band in 2024, for their Harlequin Dream 10th Anniversary Tour. That milestone celebrated one of their most beloved records, featuring hit single ‘Southern Sun’ that remains a favourite in New Zealand alongside its music video filmed against a scenic backdrop near Queenstown. Now they return to Aotearoa with a catalogue that spans over a decade and a brand new album.

description:
Brank Bjork Trio: Christchurch, Brant Bjork has spent over a quarter of a century at the heart of California’s desert rock scene. From cutting his teeth as the drummer and songwriter for Kyuss’s legendary early albums to carrying the torch for fuzz-driven rock with Fu Manchu from 1994 to 2001, Bjork’s impact is undeniable. Over the past two decades, he has produced albums for other artists, launched numerous side projects, built an extensive solo career as a singer, guitarist, and bandleader, and founded his own record label. His story is one of relentless, boundary-pushing creativity.

In 2024, Bjork re-formed the Brant Bjork Trio, teaming up with Michael Amster (Nebula, Mondo Generator) on drums and longtime friend—and desert rock pioneer—Mario Lalli on bass.

In 2025, the trio heads to New Zealand for three exclusive shows celebrating their latest album, Once Upon a Time in the Desert. This is a rare chance to catch a true icon of desert rock live—an experience not to be missed.

Joining them on all three dates are Australian rockers Full Tone Generator. Born on the beaches of Australia by Andy Fernando and brought to life in the Californian desert, Full Tone Generator brings the heat with a powerful blend of riff-heavy rock and raw energy.

Secure your tickets today!

Breaking Beats X Frederick Crew

To celebrate Legoman and his family making the move over to Perth, the gang is getting back together for one proper send-off at Wellington’s newest bass music home — Afters.

This one’s for the heads.

----------------------------

THE HISTORY
Both crews came from humble beginnings.

The Frederick Crew built their name through legendary house parties before stepping up to throw iconic nights at Bodega (RIP).

description:
Bret McKenzie - Wellington tickets, Presented by: 95bFM & Eccles Entertainment
Grammy and Academy Award–winning songwriter, composer and performer Bret McKenzie has announced two highly anticipated dates in his homeland of New Zealand in support of his latest album, Freak Out City. Touching down in Wellington and Auckland this April, the shows follow a run of sold-out international concerts and mark McKenzie’s long-awaited return to New Zealand stages. Best known as one half of Flight of the Conchords, Bret McKenzie has built an acclaimed solo career defined by sharp wit, impeccable musicianship and a deep love of classic songwriting. 
Following his solo debut Songs Without Jokes, Bret released his second project, Freak Out City, in August 2025 via Sub Pop Records. Co-produced with longtime collaborator Mickey Petralia, the collection was shaped on the road with his eight-piece band, The State Highway Wonders. The influence of his musical heroes Harry Nilsson and Randy Newman resonates again on this record, where Bret playfully weaves humour and heart into his songs. Hailed as “upbeat, well-made and refreshingly smart” (Daily Mirror) and “superbly crafted with a nod to the greats (God is in the TV), the record highlights Bret’s evolving artistry, blending sharp lyricism, lush arrangements and his unmistakable offbeat charm.
The upcoming shows will feature newly-released songs alongside old favorites, plus hilarious recountings of key moments from his colorful career, songs written on the fly using audience members’ real-life stories, and various other onstage antics.

description:
Bret McKenzie Freak Out City Tour | Wellington SECOND SHOW, Bret McKenzie Freak Out City Tour | Wellington SECOND SHOW
Grammy and Academy Award–winning songwriter, composer and performer Bret McKenzie has announced two highly anticipated dates in his homeland of New Zealand in support of his latest album, Freak Out City. Touching down in Wellington and Auckland this April, the shows follow a run of sold-out international concerts and mark McKenzie’s long-awaited return to New Zealand stages. Best known as one half of Flight of the Conchords, Bret McKenzie has built an acclaimed solo career defined by sharp wit, impeccable musicianship and a deep love of classic songwriting.

Following his solo debut Songs Without Jokes, Bret released his second project, Freak Out City, in August 2025 via Sub Pop Records. Co-produced with longtime collaborator Mickey Petralia, the collection was shaped on the road with his eight-piece band, The State Highway Wonders. The influence of his musical heroes Harry Nilsson and Randy Newman resonates again on this record, where Bret playfully weaves humour and heart into his songs. Hailed as “upbeat, well-made and refreshingly smart” (Daily Mirror) and “superbly crafted with a nod to the greats (God is in the TV), the record highlights Bret’s evolving artistry, blending sharp lyricism, lush arrangements and his unmistakable offbeat charm.

The upcoming shows will feature newly-released songs alongside old favorites, plus hilarious recountings of key moments from his colorful career, songs written on the fly using audience members’ real-life stories, and various other onstage antics.

Following sold-out performances overseas, these intimate New Zealand dates offer a rare opportunity to experience Freak Out City live in two of Aotearoa’s most beloved venues.

Tickets go on sale Friday 16 January at 9am via ticketek.co.nz.

Artist presale begins Wednesday January 14 at 10am local time. Sign up for access via the mailing list at bretmckenzie.os.fan

description:
Bri Louise Album Release Event, Yippee! The time has finally come to celebrate the release of the Bri Louise Album.
Rogue & Vagabond on 24th of January.

Elly Mae and her band will be opening up before the Bri Louise Band takes the stage. The night will also feature some very special friends of ours, including Keira Batten-Copgan, Felix Hilton, Leji, Gala Baumfield, Meihana McGee, the Bri Louise Choir, and the Bri Louise Jazz Orchestra.

Heres a few words about the two bands if you arnt acquainted with them:

Bri Louise blends sultry queerness with smooth love and undeniable groove. Rooted in gospel and neo-soul, their sound expands into a rich fusion of jazz, hip-hop, and R&B. Poetic lyricism is supported by a tight live band that features colourful keys, phatty bass, flashy beats, vibrant guitar, and fruity woodwinds. We will be joined by many guests but our core features Bri Louise (vocals/keys), Molly Wyatt (flute/vocals), Becky Devine (bass), Theo Thompson (guitar), Eloise Edmonds (saxophone), and Jonathan Stolk (drums).

Elly Mae crafts songs that encapsulate the bittersweet ache of growth, the quiet unraveling of time, and the soft glow of nostalgia embedded within. Her music is an amalgamation of folk, dreampop, indie, shoegaze, and anything in between. From lullabies that make you feel weightless to being wrapped in a blanket of sound, Elly Mae’s folk/country melodic guitar style is accompanied by experimental, spatial bass from Arran Cargill-Brown and textured pocket drumming from Sasha Francis-Murray.

Come celebrate this very special night and the release of this cool project with us.
Tickets available via UTR. Poster artwork by Keelin Bell.

Bryn Van Vliet - Wherever You Are Single Release Show, Bryn van Vliet is a Pōneke-based multidisciplinary artist, best known for his work as a saxophonist, his tenure with TOI, and as the creator of the disco collective Boogie Wonderland and the jazz orchestra Brynzilian Big Band. Bryn is a vibrant and dedicated performer who is deeply woven into the Wellington and wider Aotearoa music scene.

An established songwriter and vocalist, Bryn’s songs capture the melancholy of life, with a voice that delivers each lyric with honesty and transparency.

This special performance celebrates the release of his new single, Wherever You Are — a poignant reflection on the cycle of heartbreak, heartache, and the naivety of a former life. It is the first track to be released from his upcoming album and serves as a long-awaited follow-up to his self-titled EP, released in 2019.

Joining Bryn on stage are Callum Allardice (guitar), Leonardo Coghini (keys), Scott Maynard (double/electric bass), and Olivia Campion (drums). Opening the evening is the one and only Iris Little.

If you enjoy poetic songs and thoughtful playing that carry deep meaning and are delivered with grace, join us for this special night celebrating Bryn’s new music.

description:
Brynzilian Big Band (Bryn Farewell!), The Brynzilian Big Band is a 17-piece powerhouse jazz orchestra founded and led by saxophonist Bryn van Vliet. Based in Wellington, Bryn is a multi-disciplinary artist known for his dynamic career as an instrumentalist (saxophone, woodwinds, vocals), performer, composer, arranger, and educator. As a founding member of TOI and former lead alto saxophonist for the Rodger Fox Big Band, he has earned a reputation as a versatile and sought-after musician.

The Brynzilian Big Band presents fresh, vibrant compositions inspired by iconic Brazilian music styles such as Samba, Bossa Nova, and Forró. Bryn’s writing reflects his deep affection for Brazilian music, while honoring its traditional roots and spirit. Featuring 17 of Wellington’s finest musicians, the Brynzilian Big Band promises a performance that will uplift your soul.

Catch this iconic Wellington group for the last time in a while, as Bryn departs his beloved Wellington!

Doors open 7pm for a 7:30pm start. The Shed is an unlicensed seated venue.

Irishman Andrew Kerr (ex. Jacky Tar) and Alan Norman (The Warratahs, The Rag Poets) are now a trio after being joined by Paddy Burgin (The Wooden Box Band, The Zimmermans), and his magical guitars. Paddy, a world-renowned luthier, was a member of The Scarborough Connection, who featured on Andrew and Alan’s critically acclaimed 2023 release ‘For the Record.’

A swampy melting pot of country, folk, americana and blues, they combine a mutual love of story-telling and rhythmic grooves with narratives about the human experience. They perform predominantly original material, with contributions from each member, calling on a wide range of instrumentation including piano, acoustic and Weissenborn guitars, accordion, bodhran, and percussion. They have been performing regularly in the Greater Wellington area and South Island over the past 18 months, most recently at Vogelmorn Upstairs, where they played to a full house.

description:
Burn The Floor — Luminous, Ballroom dance has never been more thrilling. For over 20 years, Burn the Floor has been revolutionising the fast and furious steps of ballroom style. Groundbreaking moves and rebellious energy are brought to the stage every night to create an electrifying experience. For its latest show. Luminous, twenty-six dancers, musicians, and vocalists will take to the stage. You’ll get to witness romantic waltzes, a futuristic foxtrot, and the passion of the paso doble and tango. You’ll also marvel at the footwork of the cha cha, samba, jive, and a smokingly irresistible Rumba. With lights, costumes, and eclectic live music, you’ll want to leap out of your seat to join in.
Director Jason Gilkison sets an uncompromising standard and comments, “From the very beginning, we set out to shatter every expectation of what ballroom dance can be. Burn the Floor has always been about pushing boundaries — and that hunger to evolve is what has kept us alive and thriving.”
Burn the Floor has grown into a global phenomenon, selling more than four million tickets across theatres in over 30 countries. The show is also seen by more than one million people each year through its four permanently installed productions with Norwegian Cruise Line.

description:
Butter Wouldn't Melt, Butter Wouldn't Melt
Gate opens 7pm. Music starts 7.30pm.
Butter Wouldn’t Melt just (15/8) hit Number 3 on the Aotearoa Music Charts with their album Where The Roots Grow Deep. Finalists for the 2023 Best Folk Artist Tūī | Te Kaipuoro Taketake Toa with their first album 1931 Butter Wouldn’t Melt has made a name for themselves around Aotearoa headlining Folk Festivals from Auckland to Dunedin. Their blend of country Americana bluegrass and folk influences with a distinctly New Zealand flavour promises audiences an evocative performance defined by their poetic lyricism powerful harmonies and thought provoking stories. The band includes Andrea Reid (Vocals and rhythm guitar) Nick Burfield (Vocals and lead guitar) Cara Brasted (Fiddle and vocals) Marz Connelly (Double bass and vocals) and Mikey Muggeridge (Mandolin and vocals).On the back of the success of their first Album Butter Wouldn’t Melt got to work in the studio and in 2025 released Where the roots grow deep an ode to all the music that brought them together in the first place. This album turned out to be the first chapter in a two-part album journey and is set to be followed by Beneath the stars above in 2026. Together these albums form a story in contrast—two sides of the same mountain two worlds intertwined: one bathed in light the other steeped in shadow. Both records showcase Butter Wouldn’t Melt’s signature local storytelling and rich harmonies weaving contemporary folk country bluegrass and Americana into a sound that is as timeless as it is deeply personal. Expect these two worlds to collide brilliantly in this performance.

BØLZER - Southern Tempest Tour: Wellington - This week, BØLZER [bœlˈtsr] ~ He who strikes like lightning – with sudden, decisive force or implications.
BØLZER - SOUTHERN TEMPEST TOUR
20/08 - Wellington; Valhalla
21/08 - Auckland; Whammy Bar
Tickets on sale from: https://www.undertheradar.co.nz/gig/97050/BLZER.utr
An intuitive art project born from raw passion;
musical ecstasy fueled by impulsive composition
and enactment. Whilst wielding a lyrical and musical
medium largely inspired by – and seeking to
channel – the primeval essence of the human experience,
flashes of illumination will descend the sky
from which there shall be no shelter.
Forged of an intense understanding between drummer
Fabian Wyrsch and guitarist Okoi Jones, the
project first took physical form in 2008. Before
long, the dualistic significance of their musical partnership
outshone any need for a bass player and
has since served to both challenge and empower the
band’s creativity. Following their 2010 live debut in
Zürich, BØLZER soon made a name for themselves
as the remarkable Swiss-Antipodean duo capable of
conjuring up mighty barriers of sound with nothing
but a ten-stringed guitar and an almost ritualistic
percussion style. The pair describe their own stage
experience as a form of spiritual rapture, an atavistic
vortex woven together from the profound union
of spectacle meeting spectator on a deeper plane.

description:
CHAT PILE (USA) & BEASTWARS, Sludgy noise superstars CHAT PILE have announced their first ever Australia & New Zealand tour for June 2026. Fusing elements of post-punk, nu metal, grunge, they have earned a cult following for their eclectic take on what they simply deem ‘noise rock.’ 
Formed in 2019, the band took their name from piles of chat, byproducts of mining which are commonly found throughout northeast Oklahoma. Their adopted stage names Raygun Busch, Luther Manhole, Stin and Cap’n Ron were conjured as a way of avoiding identification from previous employers.
Following the band’s self-released debut ‘This Dungeon Earth’, they were signed to The Flenser in 2020 and released their debut album ‘God’s Country’. The album received broad acclaim, including ‘Best New Music’ on Pitchfork. 
Their second full-length record ‘Cool World’ was releasing in 2024. They went on to headline Roadburn Festival 2025 and tour extensively, earning a reputation for an incendiary live show.
Joining Chat Pile in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Auckland & Wellington is Kiwi sludge metal band BEASTWARS. The veteran group originally formed in the late 1980s and have abided by one steadfast maxim ever since: obey the riff. It’s time. 
Dig into Chat Pile this June.

description:
CMNZ Series Daniel Müller-Schott – Bach Solo Cello Suites, The six dances that comprise each of the six suites for solo cello provide the musical architecture around which Johann Sebastian Bach has explored the dichotomy of human emotion and intellect, creating some of the most extraordinary music ever composed for a solo instrument.
The cello suites are a touchstone work for cellists and carry with them a high risk-reward ratio. They are exposing, but in the hands of such a virtuoso as German cellist Daniel Müller-Schott, they are transcendent.

Described by the New York Times as “a fearless player with technique to burn”, Müller-Schott has been a soloist with leading international orchestras including the New York and Los Angeles Philharmonics, the Cleveland Orchestra, Boston, Chicago, Philadelphia, San Francisco and London Symphony Orchestras, the Berliner Philharmoniker, the Gewandhausorchester Leipzig, Bayrisches Staatsorchester and Münchner Philharmoniker.

Daniel Müller-Schott studied under Walter Nothas, Heinrich Schiff and Steven Isserlis. He was supported personally by Anne-Sophie Mutter and received, among other awards, the Aida Stucki Prize as well as a year of private tuition under Mstislaw Rostropovich. At the age of fifteen, Daniel Müller-Schott won the first prize at the International Tchaikovsky Competition for Young Musicians in 1992 in Moscow.

description:
CMNZ Series Four Last Songs, Composed in the year before his passing, the 'Four Last Songs' are held by many to be Richard Strauss’ most beautiful, sensuous, and moving composition. They are songs of farewell and of gentle heartbreak. The words of the final song, 'Im Abendrot', speak of an elderly couple walking hand in hand, at rest from their wanderings, away from life. The final verse:

O weiter, stiller Friede! O vast and silent peace!
So tief im Abendrot So deep in sunset glow,
Wie sind wir wandermüde- How weary we are with wandering-
Ist dies etwa der Tod? Could this perhaps be death?

For this special premiere performance, Salina Fisher has arranged the 'Four Last Songs' for NZTrio and celebrated Australian soprano Emma Pearson.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
CMNZ Series From Scratch, New Zealand’s oldest and most avant-garde chamber music ensemble, From Scratch, has been performing nationally and internationally since 1974, principally under the leadership of sound and intermedia artist Phil Dadson.

From Scratch have developed an original and innovative sound/performance style that includes large sculptural invented instruments (primarily percussion), and innovative hocket-style rhythms – where the performers’ individual parts interlock to create complex rhythmic and melodic structures.

The current collective core-group consists of Adrian Croucher, Shane Currey, Phil Dadson, Darryn Harkness and Chris O'Connor.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
CMNZ Series: Four Last Songs - Wellington, CMNZ Series: Four Last Songs - Wellington
This October, Chamber Music New Zealand is proud to tour Aotearoa's own NZTrio (Amalia Hall - violin, Somi Kim - piano, Matthias Balzat - cello) and Australian soprano Emma Pearson in Four Last Songs, a concert reflecting on the nature of goodbyes, endings, and renewals.

Named for Strauss' Four Last Songs which he wrote towards the end of his life — now arranged for piano trio and soprano — the songs reflect on the serene acceptance of mortality and a closeness with nature.

The concert also features Salina Fisher's Kintsugi, about the Japanese art of putting broken ceramics back together with gold and celebrating the beauty of a life not unmarred by difficulty, but made more beautiful by the resilience of overcoming hardship.

PROGRAMME

🎶 Elena Kats-Chernin | The Spirit and the Maiden
🎶 Salina Fisher | Kintsugi
🎶 Amy Beach | 2 Songs Op. 100 A Mirage and Stella Viatoris
🎶 Sergei Rachmaninoff | Vocalise

Symposium Brass members have performed extensively with all of New Zealand’s professional orchestras and with artists and bands ranging from James Morrison and Diana Krall to The Black Seeds and Salmonella Dub.
Their programme will bring together the best of the orchestral and jazz worlds, including the world premiere of "Progression" by Symposium Brass trumpeter and composer Cameron Pearce, which pulls colours from composers Aaron Copland, Steve Reich, and Gabriel Fauré along with trumpeters Kenny Wheeler and Ron Miles, and new material composed by Pearce for this tour.

description:
CMNZ Series: Takács Quartet (Wellington), Celebrating their 50th anniversary in 2025, the Takács Quartet are among the world’s top tier chamber ensembles.
PROGRAMME
* Joseph Haydn | String Quartet in G minor, Op. 74, No. 3 “The Rider”
* Nokuthula Ngwenyama | Flow
* Ludwig van Beethoven | String Quartet No. 9 in C major, Op. 59 No. 3
ARTISTS
Edward Dusinberre, Violin
Harumi Rhodes, Violin
Richard O’Neill, Viola
András Fejér, Cello
Lauded for their recordings of Joseph Haydn’s String Quartets, the Takács Quartet will open their programme with Op. 74, No. 3, known as The Rider – a reference to the galloping licks in the finale, and will finish with Ludwig van Beethoven’s glorious No. 9, Op. 59 No. 3, Razumovsky.
Between these two tōtara of the string quartet repertoire, the Takács Quartet will present a new work - Flow by American solo violist and composer, Nokuthula Ngwenyama, that seeks to express the creation of the universe as it expanded out from a primeval atom 13.7 billion years ago.
Come in and out of silence
Tone swirling in the balance.
Nothing, then everything
Waving into space.
Then light
And after a longer while
Air.
And now sixteen strings manually animated
Vibrating through time.
Nokuthula Ngwenyama

CRYPTOPSY - ALL SO VILE - NZ 2025 - WELLINGTON, +++++ 𝐂𝐑𝐘𝐏𝐓𝐎𝐏𝐒𝐘 - 𝐀𝐋𝐋 𝐒𝐎 𝐕𝐈𝐋𝐄 - 𝐍𝐙 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟓 𝐓𝐎𝐔𝐑 +++++
A vital force in Canadian technical death metal from 1993 onwards, 𝗖𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗼𝗽𝘀𝘆 won the hearts of fans worldwide with the masterful viciousness of their mid-'90s double-punch classics Blasphemy Made Flesh (1994) and None so Vile (1996). Featuring founding member / drumming maestro Flo Mounier alongside gravel-toned vocalist Matt McGachy, guitarist Christian Donaldson (both of whom have been with the group for two decades) and bassist since 2012 Olivier Pinard, 𝗖𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗼𝗽𝘀𝘆's Grammy award-winning album As Gomorrah Burns (2023, Nuclear Blast) signalled a productive new era for the unrepentantly aggressive Montreal four-piece, who have vowed to release a new record every two years.
𝗖𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗼𝗽𝘀𝘆 are bringing their 𝗔𝗟𝗟 𝗦𝗢 𝗩𝗜𝗟𝗘 tour down under this December just before Christmas, blasting local punters with sounds from their ninth studio album An Insatiable Violence and more!

New Zealand’s premier saxophone quartet, Saxcess, delivers a rich kaleidoscope of sounds  swing, classical, tango, cutting-edge NZ contemporary, and much more. For decades, they’ve delighted audiences young and old across Aotearoa and beyond.
Saxcess members:
Debbie Rawson (soprano/alto)
Richard Marin (soprano/alto)
Franz Ombler (tenor)

Let your ears travel the world, from the bold energy of Latin American saxophone pieces to the inventive sounds of New Zealand compositions.
Founded and led by Debbie Rawson, Saxcess is a project-based collective that has toured nationwide for nearly 30 years and have played all major Arts Festivals in Aotearoa, and performed original NZ compositions at Saxophone Congresses in Australia, Belgium, and the USA.

description:
Capital Blues Concert Series: The Carol Bean Ensemble, Capital Blues Concert Series: The Carol Bean Ensemble
Carol Bean brings her encyclopedic blues knowledge and West Coast roots to the Capital Blues stage, fronting a powerhouse ensemble with Deane Hunter (guitar), Andrew Richardson (drums), Elliotte Fuimaono (bass), and Duncan Haynes (keyboard). Showcasing songs from blues legends like Ma Rainey, Elmore James, Memphis Minnie, and Jimmy Reed, alongside contemporary voices such as Etta James (from Carol’s hometown of Los Angeles), Eliza Gilkyson, Debbie Davies, and Angela Strehli from Austin, Texas. And yes—Clarence “Gatemouth” Brown is in the mix.Carol’s sets are known for their depth and feel—steamy slow burners, up-tempo grooves, and tunes you didn’t know you needed. She’s gathered bands like Blue Highways and The Dirty River Band, and has been a fixture in Wellington’s blues scene since 2008. Her credits include Lady Sings the Blues, Wild Women of Wellington, and ALL of the blues festivals in Aotearoa. Born in England and raised in LA, Carol was shaped by the West Coast music of the ’60s and the acoustic blues of Mississippi John Hurt, Mance Lipscomb, and Lightnin’ Hopkins. She studied with Ry Cooder, who helped her acquire the vintage Martin guitar she still plays today.This gig is part of the Capital Blues Concert Series—Sunday afternoons built for listening, relaxing, and reconnecting. Come down, grab a drink, and settle in. Members discounts apply!
Original Photo: Reef Reid

description:
Capital Blues Presents: BB and the Bullets, “An authentic, powerful and generous album, which will undoubtedly place BB & The Bullets among the blues rock revelations of the year.” – Zicazic Magazine, France
It’s been a great couple of weeks for dynamic Whanganui blues band BB & THE BULLETS! 
Currently playing their North Island tour, celebrating the international release of their debut album HIGH TIDE from September, the album has achieved impressive traction across Aotearoa’s music soundscape by entering the Official Top 20 Aotearoa Albums at #12 and #5 on the Independent Music NZ Charts!
Landing on both the IMNZ Charts and the Official Aotearoa Music Charts is a cracking result, not just as independent artists, but also for a blues-rock outfit, demonstrating that it’s a genre that can successfully cross both indie and conventional charts, appealing to both grassroots and mainstream audiences – an outcome that the band is thrilled about.
“It’s a great result! We are so proud to be #5 on the IMNZ Chart. Independent artists are the grassroots and lifeblood of Kiwi music. And there’s only been a few local indie blues-rock albums on the Official Aotearoa Music Charts over the last decade – our mate Grant Haua in 2022, and Troy Kingi in 2016, so we’re stoked to be here and rep the Blues in 2025!”
The tight, three piece blues rock outfit of band members Brad McMillan (drums), Stu Duncan (bass), and Brian Baker (guitar / vocals)  have garnered a reputation for their powerful and moving live performances, drawing comparisons to Stevie Ray Vaughan, Johnny Winter, Peter Green and Jeff Beck, while firmly putting their own stamp on the timeless medium that is the blues.
BB & The Bullets have released three well received singles to date off the album: debut single ‘Something In The Water’; album title track ‘High Tide’; and their blues-soaked rendition of the Beatles classic ‘I Want You (She’s So Heavy)’ which is a huge fan favourite at their live shows. To date, all three singles have enjoyed some excellent blues radio attention, including airplay on Radio New Zealand and around the country, as well as in Germany, USA, and Canada, with ‘High Tide’ charting at #4 on Roots Music Charts in Australia, achieving #1 on the Roots Music Report Blues Album Chart, #1 on the Blues Rock Album Chart and three songs on the Blues Singles chart.
Home country of their label Dixiefrog Records has plenty of great things to say about BB & The Bullets, with Paris Move Magazine giving the album a very favourable review, ranking it as a ‘red heart’ favourite, as has French outlet Zicazic Magazine, and the title track single ‘High Tide’ has made the weekly playlist of Rolling Stone Magazine, France.
“This album proves to be a declaration of love to the roots of the blues, driven by striking live energy and unabashed virtuosity.” – Zicazic Magazine, France
With a well-deserved reputation for their compelling live shows, BB & The Bullets audiences are always wowed by the power and intensity of their performances.
With this chart action, it is evident that the blues scene is alive and vibrant on Antipodean shores, grab your mates and don’t miss your chance to check out a blues-rock experience like no other with BB & The Bullets!
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Capital Blues Presents: Bill Lake's Slow Bake, “Gentle, sometimes witty and just as often moving reflections at every turn” – Graham Reid
Guitarist, singer and songwriter Bill Lake is a cornerstone of Aotearoa’s musical landscape. With a career spanning more than four decades, Bill has shaped the sound of New Zealand roots music—leading the iconic Windy City Strugglers, co-founding the pioneering rock outfit Mammal, and fronting the brassy, groove-laden Pelicans in the 80s.
A gifted storyteller with a wry lyrical touch, Bill’s songs have been covered by Midge Marsden, Darren Watson, Kokomo, Rag Poets and Marg Layton. His live performances are intimate, soulful affairs—equal parts reflection and revelation.
Bill is joined by longtime friend and Mammal bandmate Steve Hemmens, recently returned from the UK, whose supple bass lines bring warmth and swing. Rounding out the trio is multi-instrumentalist Alan Norman (The Warratahs, Rag Poets), adding colour and texture on accordion, percussion, guitar and piano.
Together, they offer a rich, rootsy blend of blues, folk and country—music with heart, history, and a touch of Wellington grit.

description:
Capital Blues Presents: Jamie and the Numbers, Jamie and the Numbers are a Wellington soul‑funk outfit fronted by powerhouse vocalist Jamie Musuvā.
What began as a one‑off recording project quickly grew into a passion for Northern Soul, funk, and inventive covers, all delivered in their own unapologetically loud and soulful style. The band mixes original songs with cleverly re‑imagined classics, drawing praise for their debut album and earning airplay across New Zealand and even the BBC. With Jamie’s voice and a tight line‑up featuring Elliott Fuimaono and the Lerwill brothers, their live shows are renowned for energy, groove, and connection. Collaborations with producer Lee Prebble at The Surgery Studios and releases through Deltaphonic Records have cemented their reputation as one of Wellington’s most compelling soul‑funk acts.
It’s hard to describe how good this band is. You will just have to come and find out.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Capital Blues Presents: Jess and Cam, Jess Deacon is a cross-genre vocalist and songwriter who embodies influences from jazz, folk, soul, classic rock and choral music. She is an engaging performer, has an ear for music that speaks to the soul, and writes songs that connect us as humans and challenge the expectations of the modern musician – following the ebb and flow of life as we know it.
She has fronted a number of bands, been commissioned as a composer, recorded on several projects, performed at a variety of festivals and events across Aotearoa, and has written a variety of original music.
Cam Steel is an amazing drummer and all-round beat master whose ability to produce a soundscape driven by rhythm is next level.
Together, Jess and Cam will give us a lunchtime of easy, groovy blues, a fine way to while away a Sunday afternoon.
10% discount at the bar for food and drinks for members.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Capital Blues Presents: King Oyster, This is one of THE best bands in Wellington.
Driving grooves, classy funk, outstanding musicians. That’s what you get from King Oyster.
The band is Oscar Laven on sax, Blain Fitzpatick on bass, Matthew Fitpatrick on guitar, and Jacob Randall on drums. One look at those names, and you know you are in for some remarkable playing.
A surrealist funk/fusion outfit blending shreddy guitar, sax, bass, and drums into a kaleidoscope of grooves. Their music spins between aggressive funk, jazz fusion, and playful originals, drawing influence from Jaco Pastorius, John Scofield, Primus, Billy Cobham, and George Benson.
This is the first time that King Oyster has played for Capital Blues so come and see why we were so keen to get them.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Capital Blues Presents: Oscar Lavën's RnR Sax, And we’re back! And not just for any new year, but for our 30th. That makes us one of the longest-running blues clubs in the southern hemisphere.
Besides a New Year, we also have a new venue, and lots of other great stuff coming for you in 2026.
Meanwhile, we have an old favourite to open up for us. Yes, Oscar Lavën’s Rock ‘n’ Roll Sax will be our first act of 2026.
They always give us a high-energy show with lots of virtuoso playing. The band remains as popular as ever and is one of the acts people ask us to book again and again.
For those new to their music, they will be bringing you hot, honking, rock ‘n’ roll and R&B sax licks from saxophonists like Sam Butera, King Curtis, and Earl Bostic. Plenty of grooves and easy dancing music.
Come and join us at our NEW, new venue - THUNDER ROAD!
Thunder Road is on Blair St in the CBD, just off Courtenay Place. Besides being a handy location, it is ground level access with parking right outside, and buses are only 30m away. It also has a range of some fabulous beers and wines too. Not your everyday big brewery drinks, but top-quality brews. There are also great bar snacks, and well-trained staff.  It’s everything you asked for.  
Tickets are $20 or $10 for members, and there is a 10% member discount at the bar.
 As Muddy Waters said, “The blues had a baby, and named it rock ‘n’ roll.“
 See you there.

description:
Capital Blues Presents: Ras Judah and Culture Embassy, It's 15 months since Culture Embassy last played for us, so we are really looking forward to welcoming them to our new venue.
The band always gets the audience dancing from their infectious range of beats. From reggae, roots, Cuban, Afro-beat, and more. Dancing is guaranteed along with great music.
The band is led by singer, Ras Judah from Botswana, with two drummers, from Ghana, and Tanzania. Already you can start to get a feel of the rhythms.
Other musicians have Kiwi, Greek, Philippines, and English backgrounds. Add in some jazz influences and you can see why they are called Culture Embassy.
This isn’t just a band but a carnival of diversity.
If you haven’t seen Culture Embassy before, check them out. If you have seen them, then you will surely be back for more.

Free entry, with a pink hat pass-around to support the bands
Come and celebrate the next generation of funky blues and soul: Loud, proud and totally, energetically, live.
