description:
Capital Blues Presents: Simon Donald, Capital Blues Presents: Simon Donald
The recent Ash Grunwald show at meowNui was one of those rare shows where the support act is spoken of in a good way, in a VERY good way.
Lots of people were saying what a great show Simon Donald gave. Gritty blues, played with passion and skill. And played by a local musician too. What more can you ask for? So we booked him.

Simon Donald—understated kiwi brilliance. Chosen to support Ash Grunwald, and now taking the stage at Capital Blues. His online presence is about everyone else. This time, we’re making it all about him.
If you’ve caught him live at meowNUI, Paekākāriki, or the Kapiti Boating Club, you already know: Simon plays from the gut. Blues, Americana, and that rare kind of tone that feels lived-in and honest. He’s shared stages with Ash Grunwald, Sig Wilder, and National Sensation, and the feedback speaks for itself. As Ash put it:
“Hey brother you were amazing. Great to hear some good blues 🔥🔥🔥🔥”

Simon’s sets are all about feel. Deep blues, warm swing, and the kind of playing that makes you lean in and listen. Whether you’re a Thursday regular or just blues-curious, this one’s worth showing up for.
🎫 Members get discounted entry and 10% off at the bar—so come on down, grab a drink, and settle in. Doors open early. Music starts at 7.

description:
Cat Power: The Greatest on Tour, 20 years on from its release, Cat Power’s album, The Greatest, still retains its mesmeric pull. A late-night classic, it still feels as intimate and raw as it did in 2014. Now you get the chance to hear the album in its entirety live at The Opera House in Wellington.   
The concert won’t just showcase this seminal album — it’ll sit alongside favourite songs from Cat’s catalogue over the past three decades. The concert will drift through heartbreak, survival, longing, and grace with the kind of restraint that only makes the emotional weight hit harder. From the slow-burn sway of Living Proof to the bruised beauty of The Greatest, these songs endure because they tell the truth softly.   
The support act for the Wellington concert is Lawrence Arabia. He is known for his sophisticated songwriting and distinctive blend of indie-pop, chamber-pop and psychedelic influences. Lawrence has toured extensively across New Zealand, Europe and North America.

description:
Chamber Dances, Chamber Dances
Wellington-based composer Keith Moss presents the premiere of his new work Chamber Dances, written for marimba, reed quintet, and percussion.

This piece for seven musicians brings two long-held personal wishes to life: to compose a work in collaboration with marimba virtuoso Naoto Segawa, and to create a reed quintet inspired by close friends in Belgium.

The Post praised Keith’s most recent orchestral work, performed by Orchestra Wellington and Arohanui Strings, as “a pleasant, multi-hued piece of tone-painting.” His latest compositions mark a return to a tonal vocabulary that is both approachable and emotionally resonant for audiences.

The concert program will also feature solo marimba works by Peter Klatzow, a marimba duo by Akira Yuyama, and a newly arranged reed quintet version of Grieg’s Holberg Suite. Keith’s fresh take on this beloved classic draws from both Grieg’s original piano score and the composer’s own string arrangement, distilling the spirit of the suite into a sparkling new form for reed quintet.

Taking the stage is marimba specialist Naoto Segawa, Principal Percussionist of Orchestra Wellington. He is joined by fellow OW musicians and NZSO Sub-principal Sam Rich, who brings a vibrant palette of exotic percussion to the performance.

description:
Champion Brass — New Zealand Brass Band Championships 2026, More than 1000 competitors blow into Wellington in April to take part in one of the oldest music competitions in the world. The annual National Brass Band Championships attract competing bands from across Aotearoa, Australia, and beyond. Together, they represent the spirit of community music-making at its pinnacle. This year, 40 bands, including one travelling from Tonga, will compete across four grades. 
The Championships are more than just a competition. They are an annual institution with a huge sense of camaraderie between competing musicians. It is a celebration of everything that is great about live music and therefore attracts a wide audience of supporters. 
The highlight of the week is a gala performance from the National Band of New Zealand. The 12 April concert features top musicians selected from competing bands plus guest soloists. Other events are free and open to the public. This includes solo, chamber, and full-band performances, the Champion of Champions concert, and a masterclass with the principal trombonist of the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, Jorgen Van Rijen.

description:
Chant du Saxophone, Enjoy the lush and mysterious sounds of French music performed by an exciting yet subtle chamber duo.
This concert explores a diverse range of repertoire from household names such as Claude Debussy to lesser known composers such as Paul Bonneau and Paule Maurice. Hear the many moods timbres of the saxophone, from delicately soaring melodies, to dark, enchanting arias and joyful, raucous moments.

Programme:
Francis Poulenc - Flute Sonata FP164
Eugene Bozza - Aria
Claude Debussy - Petite Suite (transcribed by Yukio Nakano)
Paul Bonneau - Caprice en Frome de Valse
Paule Maurice - Tableaux de Provence

About the performers:
Alex Trask is a saxophonist based in Pōneke. He has a keen interest in the classical saxophone and has studied with some of New Zealand's leading player such as Simon Brew and Reuben Chin. He is a member of the Royal New Zealand Air Force Band and has performed with many other significant organizations such as Gallery Orchestra, Saxcess, Wellington Youth Orchestra, and Wellington City Symphonic Band.

Alex is also an accomplished jazz player, and has organized many events both in Wellington and nationally, performing in the Wellington Jazz Festival and the National Jazz Festival many times. Alex was the lead alto saxophone player in the Rodger Fox Big Band from 2024-2025 and has performed as a guest with that band since 2022. His debut album 'Pool of Tears’, which blends folk and classical melodies with jazz performance techniques, was released on Thelonious Records in 2023 and has been featured on RNZ Concert as well as other prominent radio stations.
-
David Codd is a New Zealand-born horn player and pianist. Originally from New Plymouth, New Zealand, David undertook a Bachelor of Music in Classical Performance—Collaborative Piano under Dr Jian Liu at Victoria University of Wellington, as well as secondary studies in French horn with Samuel Jacobs and Sebastian Dunn.

David maintains a busy schedule of performances as a horn player, pianist, and conductor. As well as being a member of the Royal New Zealand Air Force Band horn section, David performs with the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, Orchestra Wellington, Auckland Philharmonia, and the Dunedin Symphony Orchestra.

As a pianist, David has a particular passion for collaborative work, enjoying performing with artists from NZSO and Orchestra Wellington, as well as orchestral keyboard for NZSO and the NZSO National Youth Orchestra.

description:
Choral Connections Concert, NZCF presents Choral Connections, a concert featuring two of New Zealand’s finest youth choirs – the acclaimed New Zealand Secondary Students' Choir, directed by Sue Densem, and the Aotearoa Academy Choir, directed by Rowan Johnston and Elise Bradley.
Set in the soaring acoustics of Wellington’s Cathedral of St Paul, this public concert forms the centrepiece of NZCF’s Choral Connect convention – a bi-annual professional development conference that brings together choral directors from around the country.
At the end of the concert, conference delegates with join with the two youth choirs to form a massed choir of over 150 voices to sing under the direction of international choral clinician Dr Pearl Shankuan.
New Zealand Secondary Students' Choir
Aotearoa's national choir for secondary school students, NZSSC gathers during school holidays to rehearse and perform across the motu. Each two-year cycle culminates in an international tour: in July 2024, the choir travelled to China, where they took part in the Shanghai Oriental Art Centre Chorus Exchange, the Chorus and Conducting Art Conference in Hangzhou, and the China International Chorus Festival in Beijing.
NZSSC is directed by Sue Densem, alongside Assistant Conductor and Accompanist Brent Stewart and Assistant Conductor and Vocal Consultant Ben Madden.

Christine Wang, violin

Christine has been a member of the second violin section of New Zealand Symphony Orchestra since 2022. She holds a Bachelor of Music from Eastman School of Music and Master of Music at Rice University, studying under Oleh Krysa and Kathleen Winkler respectively. Before coming to New Zealand, Christine was Assistant Concertmaster of San Antonio Symphony and has worked in orchestras in the United States and Australia.

Rachel Thomson, piano

Rachel Thomson was born in Dunedin, New Zealand, and grew up in Wellington where she began her piano studies with her mother. She went on to study with Judith Clark, graduating from Victoria University of Wellington before continuing her studies at the Cleveland Institute of Music in the United States, where she gained a doctorate in piano performance. She has toured on numerous occasions for Chamber Music New Zealand and is a member of various chamber ensembles including the Koru Trio. She has worked as an orchestral pianist with the NZSO, Orchestra Wellington, and the Christchurch Symphony Orchestra. Rachel is also active as a teacher, adjudicator and accompanist, and is a music examiner for Trinity College London.

description:
Christof Van Der Ven - “Is This What We’ve Become?” Album Tour, After 5 years Christof is coming back to New Zealand to tour his newly released album.

He plays at the Abandoned Brewery taproom in Petone on the 30th of October.

Christof van der Ven has built a truly impressive CV over the course of his career, from supporting the likes of Bon Iver, The Staves, Mel Parsons, Bear’s Den, Lisa Hannigan, and Nick Mulvey, to playing in front of thousands of fans across the world.

Hailing originally from Holland, Christof van der Ven moved to Galway in 2007 before settling in London. He has released two LPs, Empty Handed (2018) and You Were The Place (2019), alongside multiple EPs. His career has been supported by DIY, Clash, Gold Flake Paint and his music has been played on BBC6 Radio and Radio X.
NEW ALBUM “Is this what we’ve become?”

Throughout ‘is this what we’ve become?’ Christof speaks to loved ones and past selves, reflecting on years of promise, regret and loss. His storytelling is characterized by gentle melodies and rich, textured arrangements, as his younger selves confront him with unfulfilled ambitions and perceived failures. When Christof turns towards friends and family, he finds them too in moments of upheaval, in need of support. Amidst the unpredictable and uncontrollable, community and friendship emerge, providing roots, giving comfort as Christof ruminates on how he came to be - and can come to accept - who he is now.

Written by Christof, ‘is this what we’ve become?’ also features musical contributions from Jools Owen (Bear’s Den, Bess Atwell), Tommy Heap (Billie Marten, Matthew and the Atlas), Marcus Hamblett (Villagers, Bear’s Den), and Estilo String Quartet. The album was produced and recorded by Christof and Ian Grimble (Daughter, Manic Street Preachers, Matt Corby, Fionn Regan), who also mixed the LP. ‘is this what we’ve become?’ incorporates recordings from both studio sessions in London, as well as ad hoc recording sessions engineered by Christof across the UK.

description:
Christoph Gallio / Phil Durrant, Christoph Gallio / Phil Durrant
Phil Durrant (electric mandolin and electronics) and Christoph Gallio (saxophones) are veterans of the international free improvisation scene. Their individual and collaborative projects have helped shape the development of improvised music. They first worked together over 40 years ago, but it wasn’t until 2022 that they started performing as a duo. It is rare that improvisors of their calibre make it out to NZ, so we’re very happy to host them at Pyramid Club for a duo concert plus collaborative sets with local musicians.

Phil Durrant (London, UK) is a multi-instrumentalist improviser, composer and sound artist. As a violinist he was one of the key exponents of the ‘group voice approach’ style of improvised music, performing as a member of the Butcher/Russell/Durrant trio, News From The Shed and the Chris Burn Ensemble. In the late 90s, his influential trio with Radu Malfatti and Thomas Lehn represented a shift to a more reductionist approach. As a synthesiser player, Durrant performs with Bertrand Denzler and Burkhard Beins in Trio Sowari. He is also a member of the international electronic ensemble MIMEO with Keith Rowe, Kaffe Matthews, Thomas Lehn and Rafael Toral. He has performed all over Europe and Canada and released CDs and records on Acta and Emanem Records.

Swiss saxophonist and composer Christoph Gallio studied classical saxophone with Iwan Roth at the Basel Music Conservator and then with Steve Lacy in Paris. He has collaborated with many of the world’s leading voices in improvisation including Irene Schweizer, Urs Blöchlinger, Mani Neumeier, Peter Kowald, Fred Frith, Haco, Tetsu Saitoh, Phil Minton, Pablo Diaz, Marcelo von Schultz, Olie Brice, Andrew Lisle, Cath Roberts, Irene Aebi, William Parker, Rashied Ali, Matthew Ostrowski, Gerry Hemingway, Sven-Åke Johansson, Olaf Rupp, Jan Roder, Oli Steidle, Andrea Neumann, Ernst Thoma, Julian Sartorius, Nicolas Stocker, Paula Shocron, Sergio Merce, Alistair Zaldua, Phil Durrant, Roger Turner, Dominic Lash, Mark Sanders and many more. Gallio has been running his own label PERCASO since 1986.

www.gallio.ch

Durrant and Gallio will perform a duo set, and then be joined by local improvising musicians Tom Callwood (bass), Jake Baxendale (sax) and Daniel Beban (guitar/tapes).

Their tour is sponsored by Swiss Arts Council, Aargauer Kuratorium, City of Baden, SIS (Schweizerische Interpreten Stiftung) and Fondation SUISA.

description:
Classical Tenor Saxophone & Piano Duo Recital "The Art of Time and Sound", Tomomi & Gabriela
Classical Tenor Saxophone & Piano Duo Recital
“The Art of Time and Sound”
Wellington: Karori Anglican Church – Sunday, 30 November, 4 pm
Saxophonist Tomomi Arita-Johnston and pianist Gabriela Glapska warmly invite you to The Art of Time and Sound— a concert that explores how saxophone music travels through the centuries, connecting emotion, colour, and imagination, with a special focus on the classical tenor saxophone.
The programme opens with Jean-Baptiste Singelée’s 4ᵉ Solo de Concert, showcasing the lyrical beauty and virtuosity of the classical tenor saxophone. J. S. Bach’s Sonata in E-flat Major (BWV 1031) follows, where Baroque grace meets the saxophone’s warm resonance. Camille Saint-Saëns’ Sonata Op.168 brings wit, charm, and elegance in a new tonal landscape.
The journey continues with Astor Piazzolla’s “Bordel 1900,” “Café 1930,” and “Night-club 1960,” tracing the sensual evolution of tango, and concludes with George Gershwin’s “Rhapsody in Blue,” a vibrant fusion of classical sophistication and jazz spirit featuring three saxophones.
(FYI: Auckland performance – Lewis Eady, Saturday, 6 December, 5 pm)

Classical in the Chapel -Midwinter Vespers, The second of our Classical in the Chapel series, 'Midwinter Vespers'
Step into the stillness of winter with Midwinter Vespers, an intimate evening of luminous, contemplative music performed by a distinguished string quartet.
The programme weaves together the timeless beauty of Bach’s chorales, the evocative folk-inflected soundworld of the Danish String Quartet’s Last Leaf, the meditative intensity of Arvo Pärt’s Speilgel Im Spielgel , and the intricate elegance of Couperin’s Passacaille/Chaconne. Moody, atmospheric, and deeply reflective, this concert draws on ancient musical traditions to create a rich, immersive listening experience.
Featuring outstanding principal players — Amy Boucher and Jessica Oddie (violins), and Ian Greenberg (cello), with Beatrix Francis (viola) — this promises to be a truly special performance in the unique acoustic of Erskine Chapel.

description:
Cliff Richard - Can't Stop Me Now, British music icon Sir Cliff Richard announced his highly anticipated live tour for New Zealand 2025. These shows offer a rare chance to witness one of Britain’s most celebrated performers in a live setting.
Next year will mark 12 years since New Zealand audiences have seen Cliff Richard live in concert and the 2025 tour will begin in Auckland and make its way to Wellington & Christchurch. Fans will be treated to a setlist packed with timeless classics, including hits such as "Living Doll," "We Don’t Talk Anymore," "Devil Woman," and many more. Known for his energy, charisma, and enduring stage presence, Sir Cliff continues to capture hearts and inspire audiences as he has done across the eight decades.
As one of the greatest hitmakers in British music history, Cliff Richard has sold in excess of 250 million records worldwide, securing his place among the best-selling artists of all time. He remains the only artist to achieve UK Top 5 albums across eight consecutive decades, a remarkable feat recognised by the Official Charts Company. Since his debut in 1958 with “Move It!”, Sir Cliff has delivered a string of chart-topping hits, including 14 number-one singles and seven No. 1 albums, cementing his legacy as a pop legend.
These 2025 performances offer fans a rare opportunity to see one of music’s all-time greats in concert at the age of 85.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Colette Rivers - The Backyard Wonder tour, Colette Rivers - The Backyard Wonder tour
Indie-Folk Artist Colette Rivers and her band will be performing her intimate new album, The Backyard Wonder.

Independent artist Colette Rivers is releasing her second full-length album, The Backyard Wonder, an intimate exploration of healing, change, and the quiet beauty of ordinary moments.

This album holds special meaning for Rivers: after being diagnosed with cancer in July 2023, her planned sophomore release had to take a back seat to recovery. But when the cancer returned in early 2025, she felt compelled to finish and release the album, not just as a legacy project, also as a celebration after hard times, with a focus on how “you can find the wonder in life, even in your backyard.”

A lifelong creative, Rivers records, mixes, and produces in her home studio in Masterton, and plays every instrument heard on The Backyard Wonder. Her debut album, Memory Lake (2020), was shaped by early years spent in the US, and her move to Taupō at age 11; this was followed by a nationwide tour. Now based in the Wairarapa and working as a secondary school drama teacher, Rivers continues to move between solo performance and full band sets, while staying rooted in the acoustic traditions that define her sound.

With her right arm partially paralysed following recent treatment, Rivers has gathered a group of close friends to help bring the songs of The Backyard Wonder to life (especially its intricate fingerpicking parts) for a run of live shows. She’ll be touring the Wellington and Wairarapa regions from August through October, finishing with a set at the Wellington Folk Festival.

For updates, and behind-the-scenes glimpses, visit www.coletteriversmusic.com or follow @colettemusic on Instagram and Facebook.

Opening for Rivers are artists:

Phil Masters
Phil Lively-Masters is an experienced, well travelled singer songwriter who specialises in writing the sort of Sun Kissed West Coast Laurel Canyon Americana that made Neil Young, Stephen Stills and the Byrds famous. With a powerful, honey soaked voice that has won praise and support slots from legendary American country rock pioneers like The Jayhawks and original cosmic cowboy Steve Young, Phil has 20 years worth of road worn original songs to pull on, including tracks from the critically acclaimed CANYON RYDE album 'Free To Be' and some choice country rock covers to weave a spell on any listener.

Saali Marks
A singer, songwriter, guitarist and multi-instrumentalist, Saali Marks hails originally from the
South Island, but has made Wairarapa his home for the last 20 years, where he lives on a farm
with his family and teaches music at Kuranui College.
Saali has played in numerous bands over the years, in a wide range of styles from proto-punk
to psychedelic dub, covers, originals and fully improvised music with no discernible genre, on
stages throughout Aotearoa since 1991. Currently he fronts the Wellington ska band Battleska
Galactica.
Throughout and alongside it all Saali has indulged his love for songwriting and solo
performing, developing a unique style, rooted in folk and blues, and inspired by greats from
across the decades. A skilled guitarist, Saali rarely plays straight ahead chords, and an
education in jazz has informed his ear for harmony, the beauty of dissonance, tension and
resolution, with unconventional song structures, alternate tunings and intriguing melodies.
Although not adverse to penning the odd love song, most of Saali’s lyrics tend to focus on
other aspects of the human condition, from religion and politics to our relationships with the
environment and our own minds.

description:
Come Together - Bruce Springstein, Born to Run, New Zealand’s most successful rock series ever, COME TOGETHER, returns in 2026 with an electrifying trio of landmark albums: Bruce Springsteen’s Born to Run, Radiohead’s OK Computer and Talking Heads’ Stop Making Sense.

Each album will be performed live, in full, by a rotating supergroup of Aotearoa’s most acclaimed rock artists and musicians — followed by a second set of classics and deep cuts that span each artist’s extraordinary catalogue.

From the wall of sound production of Born to Run, to the haunting dystopian brilliance of OK Computer, to the joyful and immersive perfection of Stop Making Sense, the 2026 series celebrates three albums that have cemented their place in music history. Performed in some of the country’s most beautiful venues, Come Together once again promises epic musicianship, emotional punch and the kind of once-in-a-lifetime collaborations that have made the series a cultural phenomenon.

The album that transformed Bruce Springsteen from a struggling artist on the brink of being dropped to a full-blown rock star, Born to Run remains one of the defining records of the 1970s. Sweeping, cinematic and bursting with heart, it delivered immortal tracks including Thunder Road, Born to Run and the epic Jungleland.

Come Together will perform the album in its entirety, followed by a second set diving deep into Springsteen’s vast catalogue — from anthems to hidden gems.

Performed by: Milan Borich, Adam McGrath, Jennie Skulander, Jon Toogood and the Come Together band.

*Booking fees apply
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Come Together - End of Year Big Bash, One stage. Two nations. One unforgettable night of rock.

This December, the Come Together Big Bash 2025 will ignite New Zealand stages with the ultimate Kiwi vs Oz rock showdown. For one massive night in each city, a supergroup of Aotearoa’s best rock musicians will unleash the biggest hits from both sides of the Tasman in an all-out end-of-year rock fest.

Expect wall-to-wall anthems from AC/DC, Split Enz, Cold Chisel, DD Smash, INXS, Silverchair, Hello Sailor and more – the songs that have defined generations, blasted stereos, and packed stadiums.
Joining forces for this epic battle are:

- Jennie Skulander (Devilskin)
- Milan Borich (PLUTO)
- EJ Barnes (Jimmy Barnes)
- Seamus Johnson (Seamouse)
…plus more to be announced.

They’ll be backed by the powerhouse Come Together Band: musical director Jol Mulholland, alongside Brett Adams, Matthias Jordan, Mike Hall, and Alistair Deverick.

For decades, Kiwis and Aussies have traded bands, stages, and stadium tours. Now, it’s time to settle the score the only way that matters — with a night of unrelenting, unapologetic rock.

And the audience isn’t just along for the ride — you’re part of the action. Fans can help shape the setlist by voting for the songs they want to hear in the Kiwi vs Oz showdown.

Head to www.libertystage.com/ct25poll to cast your vote before October 10th.

This is the ultimate end-of-year blowout — a chance to scream, sweat, and celebrate with some of New Zealand’s greatest musicians performing the biggest rock hits of all time.

So, who truly owns rock?

Is it the swagger of Aussie pub rock, or the grit and heart of Kiwi anthems? You decide.

The Come Together Big Bash 2025 caps off an epic year for the juggernaut series, which has already seen thousands of fans pack venues for Neil Young’s Live Rust, Pink Floyd’s Dark Side of the Moon and, next month, the hotly anticipated Led Zep II.

Born five years ago in the isolation of a world turned upside down, Come Together began as a bold celebration of legendary rock albums. It has since grown into one of New Zealand’s most electrifying live concert experiences. With a powerhouse collective of the country’s finest musicians, the series has drawn more than 50,000 fans nationwide and earned critical acclaim, cementing its place as a must-see on the music calendar.
label: Music & Concerts

Performed by James Milne, Anthonie Tonnon, Dianne Swann, Julia Deans and the Come Together band + more to be announced!

Come Together – Led Zeppelin II, New Zealand’s most successful rock series ever, COME TOGETHER, celebrates five amazing years with one of the biggest albums ever!

This isn't just a concert; this is an immersive, once-in-a-lifetime experience where some of the most talented musicians in the country pour everything they have into recreating these albums with absolute precision and passion. Every guitar riff, soaring vocal, thunderous drumbeat, and intricate keyboard melody is delivered with an attention to detail that honours the original recordings while injecting new energy into these classic songs.

description:
Come Together — Kiwi vs Oz Rock Big End of Year Bash 2025, For decades, New Zealand and Australia have sung along to each other’s songs. We’ve traded bands and tunes across the Tasman. The team of famous Kiwi musicians at Come Together are now putting it all to the test. Kiwi vs Oz Rock Big End of Year Bash 2025 packs the biggest hits from both sides of the ditch onto one stage. Some of New Zealand’s most iconic rock musicians will tear through these legendary antipodean tracks in an all-out rock fest. You can decide who truly owns rock. Is it the swagger of Aussie pub rock or the grit and heart of Kiwi anthems? Perhaps it’s both. 
Get ready to hear the biggest tunes from AC/DC, Split Enz, Cold Chisel, The Datsuns, INXS, DD Smash, Silverchair, Australian Crawl, and Hello Sailor. That’s just for starters, so the showdown is set to be epic. Here’s the kicker — you help shape the setlist, and when the amps power down, you vote for which nation takes home the crown. 
This is more than a concert — it’s a massive celebration of the music we grew up to, the songs that built us, and the riffs that still get us moving. Grab your mates, grab your tickets, and get ready to make some noise.

description:
Comfy Concert 5 at The Long Hall - The Chamber Pot Pourri Ensemble performance for Arohanui Strings+, � Join us for an afternoon of beautiful music and community spirit! �
Enjoy Beautiful Chamber Music with a View! Relax with a cuppa while listening to expertly curated chamber music featuring Helene, Rolf, and top musicians at an intimate venue in one of Wellington’s most stunning locations.
Helen Pohl (violin) and Rolf Gjelsten (cello), as the Chamber Pot Pourri Ensemble, are getting together with friends to play a series of intimate concerts that support some of their favourite causes – Arohanui Strings+ included (www.arohanuistrings.org).
Comfy Concert No.5 with Bridget Douglas (flute) and Victoria Jaenecke (viola) on August 30, 2025, playing:
Tabea Squire - Daydream and Dance for violin and cello
JS Bach – Sonata No. 1 in G minor for violin solo
Heitor Villa-Lobos – The Jet Whistle for flute and cello
WA Mozart – Flute Quartet in D Major
(programmes and artists may change - but hopefully not!)
The Comfy Concert series
The Comfy Concerts is a series of four beautiful concert experiences with two dates to benefit Kaibosh (20 September and 16 November) and two dates to benefit Arohanui Strings+ (Saturday 30 August and 18 October).
Thank you to Helene, Rolf and musicians of The Chamber Pot Pourri Ensemble, for generously donating time and talent in support Arohanui Strings+ and Kaibosh!
Learn more about these charities: arohanuistrings.org and kaibosh.org.nz
Location
The Long Hall overlooks Point Jerningham with views of Te Whanganui-a-Tara / Wellington Harbour. See the Google map location.
You can park on Maida Vale Rd or on Roseneath School tennis court and follow the signs. Or on foot or bike, use the footpath up from Carlton Gore Road or from Maida Vale Road near Roseneath School.
Dress warmly, and maybe bring a cushion and some slippers, as it's shoes off to protect the new floor.
It's going to be a wonderful afternoon of fabulous music, while supporting the next generation of musicians through raising funds for two fabulous charities.
label: Music & Concerts

Helen Pohl (violin) and Rolf Gjelsten (cello), as the Chamber Pot Pourri Ensemble, are getting together with friends to play a series of intimate concerts that support some of their favourite causes – Arohanui Strings+ included (www.arohanuistrings.org).

Dmitri Shostakovich – Quartet No. 5
Dmitri Shostakovich – Quartet No. 2

The Comfy Concert series

description:
Concert Pianist Nikolai Saratovsky plays in Paekakariki - JUNE 14, A VERY SPECIAL PIANIST RETURNS TO NEW ZEALAND:
MULLED WINE CONCERTS PRESENTS NIKOLAI SARATOVSKY
Nikolai Saratovsky is an internationally acclaimed Russian concert pianist with an extraordinary repertoire. Mary Gow, organiser of the Paekakariki-based Mulled Wine Concerts discovered Saratovsky in 2018 when he played in Brussels as a young pianist after succeeding in several important piano competitions in Europe. "I was amazed by his virtuosity" says Gow, a concert pianist herself, "He not only had a love for the music, he had all the technical skill-set you need to express yourself fully on the piano". She told him she came from New Zealand and he then told her that he and his Japanese-born wife had always dreamed of visiting New Zealand! As Gow notes, "from there, it was a short step to discussing possibilities..."
His effect on audiences here was remarkable - everyone who heard him knew that they were seeing and hearing something special. Since then, audiences around the world have come to the same conclusion. Saratovsky is now a professor of piano at the huge music school of Taiwan University where he combines teaching and academic research with his performing career, appearing in major concert venues worldwide. He also gives master-classes for aspiring international concert pianists.
Nikolai himself says this of his visits here: "This will be already the fifth time I am coming to NZ, and every time I feel extremely happy to come. I have lived and worked in Taiwan for more than 6 years. I have many memories from NZ. New Zealand is very different from Taiwan, and for me it's very important to "charge my inner spiritual battery". Coming to New Zealand is the ideal choice. Combination of meeting my lovely friends, conversations beside the fire place, fantastic sunsets, and music making makes this trip truly remarkable" He has chosen a wonderful set of music for his recital: "I chose this program by myself, because at this moment of life I prefer to play something that gives me a positive energy. I feel very compassionate with these music works, and they help me to recover during difficult times. I am happy to share this beautiful music with the audience, and I am looking forward for this fascinating musical journey". The concert will start with Western European romantic composers and conclude with pieces by Tchaikovsky and Rachmaninoff.
Mary Gow feels that his visit to New Zealand represents a wonderful opportunity for Kapiti audiences to catch a star already well known in Europe, Russia and the Far East. "This concert I regard as one of the most important and for the North Island, not-to-be-missed!" Mulled Wine Concerts will sponsor his appearance at the Paekakariki Memorial Hall on Sunday, June 14.
==============================
Mulled Wine Concerts presents a piano recital by Nikolai Saratovsky at 2:30 PM on Sunday 14 June, 2026 at the Paekakariki Memorial Hall, The Parade, Paekakariki.
Tickets: $35 adults ($15 students under 14).
Online sales: marygow@gmail.com. Tel: 021 101 9609 .

description:
Cookie Brooklyn & Po Pi Sha / Ceramic / Fizzface, A night of splintered, angular post-punk and fractured suburban boogie from Cookie Brooklyn & Pi Pi Sha, alongside Ceramic’s playful mystical pop and Fizzface’s crumbly twee-noise songs.
-
Cookie Brooklyn & Po Pi Sha is a new project featuring Mark Williams (guitar/vocals) and Derek Champion (drums). Together they render splintered songs of suburban creep with angular boogie and short fuse combustion. Williams' previous projects include Cookie Brooklyn & the Crumbs, Bad Statistics and he currently plays in Dunedin with Living Clipboards. Derek Champion, formerly of Satina Saturnina and numerous other bands and performance art projects in Wellington in the 2000s, spent 12 years living and working in Canada through the 2010s before returning to NZ. Both have previously played with iterations of Bill Direen's Bilders, touring Europe and USA.
-
Ceramic is a multi-media solo project by Tom Heynes that features funky tunes about mystical imaginary stuff like unicorns and mermaids and gender. Ceramic have also composed soundtracks for Mike Heynes' animation.
-
Fizzface is twee noise and unconvincing pop - crumbly songs inspired by k sweets and punk freaks.

Special thanks to Creative NZ and Wellington City Council for supporting Pyramid Club's programme.

Costume Showcase 2026, Overview
Immerse yourself in costume artistry!
Toi Whakaari: NZ Drama School graduating costumiers present their major work costumes on the main stage in this enchanting 40-minute showcase.
The culmination of a year of making, these garments are shown alongside works of millinery, pattern-making and historical costume. Music, lighting and movement bring each garment to life on stage, creating an immersive experience where craft meets performance.

description:
Cotton Daisy Backstep, Cotton Daisy Backstep
The Undercurrent presents... Cotton Daisy Backstep!

Cotton Daisy Backstep play the old ‘hillbilly’ music of the Appalachian Mountains with songs of the pioneers, haunting ballads, old gospels, shotgun totin’ moonshiners and tub-thumping dance tunes with wonderful harmonies and driving rhythms.

Helena spent 10 years in West Virginia steeped in the local music traditions learning from the old folks. Returning to NZ in 2003 she assembled the oldtime band Cotton Daisy Backstep. They have been playing cafes, folk clubs, festivals and square dances around the Wellington area, appearing at events such as Cupa Dupa, Wellington Gardens Magic, Newtown Festival and won the Wellington Folk festival [People’s Choice Award 2018].

Band members include: Helena Faust on banjo/vocals, Philip Muollo on guitar, Bill Vella on double bass, and gifted singer Mili De Mayo recently joining the group.

CDB brings you that old 78 bacon frying sound no dot reading can give; indeed, this is the mountain roots of Americana.

What people say
“Wow you guys are amazing, I love what you do” Anonymous Fan
“I felt transported to another time” Lots of folks say this
“Helena needs no microphone, her voice just sails out and it’s a really different sound” A guy at Wellyfest 2021

description:
Courtney Barnett — Creature of Habit Tour, Australian singer-songwriter Courtney Barnett is heading back to New Zealand five years after her last sell-out tour. The ‘Creature of Habit’ tour coincides with the release of her fourth studio album of the same name. The album is emotionally resonant and explores the central question: how to get out of your own way so you can truly feel your life. With singles Stay in Your Lane, and Site Unseen’ setting the tone, the album and concert mark a decisive new chapter in her musical evolution. Along with the latest music, she will delve into her extensive back catalogue. 
In addition to a Grammy nomination, Courtney has won multiple ARIAs (Australian Recording Industry Awards). She is known for a style that incorporates intimate storytelling with indie rock and bursts of raw grunge-like energy. Her blend of moody guitar, witty, anecdotal lyrics and laconic talk-singing has cemented her as “one of the most distinctive voices in indie music” (The Mancunion).

description:
Cowboy Dan: Dreams That Feel Like Falling Aotearoa Album Tour - Te Whanganui-a-Tara / Wellington, Cowboy Dan: Dreams That Feel Like Falling Aotearoa Album Tour - Te Whanganui-a-Tara / Wellington
Tāmaki Makaurau jangle rockers Cowboy Dan are releasing their debut full length album; Dreams That Feel Like Falling. The album drops 19 September on streaming & vinyl.

Never overblown or overproduced, Dreams That Feel Like Falling is direct and intimate. 11 tracks of warmth, sincerity and brashness that strike a balance of breeze and overdrive.

To celebrate the release, Cowboy Dan are heading out for a run of shows throughout Te Ika-a-Māui in September and October.

This Te Whanganui-a-Tara will be the second outing in the capital for Cowboy Dan, who are delighted to bring Echo Children along for the ride from Tāmaki to share their special tunes and infectous harmoines, along with Te Whanganui-a-Tara local legends Search For Yeti...STACKED!

Once aptly described as The Bats on the right amount of Red Bull, Cowboy Dan has been treating audiences across the motu to energetic, emotionally charged tunes since 2015. Their live shows have consistently delivered good times to fans and new friends alike.

Off the back of two delightful EPs: We Will Hesitate, When We Eventually Wait (2017, Mixed by Jonathan Pearce); Sentimental Now That We're Leaving (2021, Mixed by Rohan Evans), the debut LP, Dreams That Feel Like Falling, is a continuation and a few steps forward, showcasing the bands expansive sonic pallet, with a mix of distortion, introspection, heart and bite.

Search For Yeti draws from a deep range of influences to create a sound that achieves the difficult feat of being hugely atmospheric and diverse while also being hook laden. This is an act that captures people with their onstage energy — and gets them talking afterwards about the songs that they just heard.

Following in the long tradition of innovative Aotearoa indie bands, Echo Children craft a distinctive sound by melding psychedelic pop harmonies with sharp alt-country songwriting.

Gather your pals and get ready for good times! A thursday, sure, but what a chance to digest some upbeat goodness hailing from the big smoke and with some local goodness to boot.

description:
Cushion Concert with Yury Gezentsvey, IAS Cushion Concerts presents local bands in the intimate environment of historic Inverlochy House. Join us as Principal Violinist, Yury Gezentsvey, performs some of Telemann's baroque Violin Fantasias for solo violin, as part of the opening celebration of Inverlochy’s Fundraiser exhibition.


Born in 1952 in Kiev, Ukraine (USSR at the time), Yury Gezentsvey graduated from the Gniessin Institute of Music in Moscow (1974). He emigrated to Chicago, USA (1979) where he was Concertmaster of the Chicago Civic Orchestra, before being engaged as Concertmaster of the Caracas Philharmonic Orchestra in Venezuela (1980), where he also formed a Chamber Ensemble with American pianist Harriet Serr (most acclaimed resident pianist in Venezuela, who also became his mother-in-law). Yury was appointed Principal First Violinist of the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra (1985) and, together with his wife Desirée and their three daughters, he made his new home in Wellington.

Yury has become a valued member of the music world in New Zealand, having taken part in several International Festivals of the Arts in Wellington as a Chamber Music Violinist. As the leader of the Dominion Quartet, he recorded all 17 string quartets by Alfred Hill (NAXOS).

Since his retirement from the NZSO at the end of 2022, he has been enjoying playing with Orchestra Wellington, teaching, and treasuring family life with Desiree, their children and six Kiwi grandchildren.

Visit (violinart.co.nz) for more information about Yury.

DECEITS AOTEAROA TOUR 2026, Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.

Five-time DMC World DJ Championships champion DJ Craze is a true heavyweight of global turntablism, renowned for pushing the boundaries of drum & bass, hip hop and bass music. Founder of Slow Roast Records alongside K*ll the Noise, Craze has played a key role in shaping the US bass music landscape, while touring globally from underground clubs to major festivals. His sets are a masterclass in energy and control - seamlessly weaving rap, dubstep, Miami bass and drum & bass into a high-impact dancefloor experience.

This is more than a DJ set - it’s a chance to witness a battle champion and crowd-destroyer at the top of his game. Don’t miss one of the most technically gifted and influential DJs to ever touch the decks.


Support Ethixx

For the past ten years, Ethixx has operated in the corners of New Zealand’s electronic underground, crafting a style that refuses to be easily categorised. An enigmatic presence behind the decks, he treats genres as fluid boundaries, blending everything from deep tech rollers to low-end club weight with patient, clinical precision. Preferring to let the music speak for itself, Ethixx builds an atmosphere rather than just playing a set -making him the ideal guide to take the crowd into the shadows before DJ Craze takes over.

description:
DJ QBert (USA) + Alphabethead (NZ), DJ QBert (USA) + Alphabethead (NZ)
DJ QBert (USA) + Alphabethead (NZ)
Two titans of the turntables. One night only.

Three-time DMC World Champion DJ QBert is widely regarded as one of the greatest and most influential DJs of all time. His dominance at the DMC World Championships in the early ’90s redefined what was possible with two turntables and he is widely credited with transforming the turntable from a device used to play records into a respected, expressive musical instrument. Decades later, his innovation, technical mastery and cultural impact remain unmatched. Seeing QBert live is not just a show, it is witnessing the evolution of hip hop craft in real time.

Sharing the bill is Aotearoa’s own 2002 New Zealand DMC Champion Alphabethead, a shining star of experimental hip hop and razor-sharp turntablism. "With a career spanning international tours, acclaimed projects both solo and in bands Bad Taste and The All Seeing Hand, Alphabethead represents the very best of New Zealand DJ culture.

This is a rare meeting of eras, styles and legacies at the highest level of turntablism. Miss it, and you will be hearing about it for years to come.

Three-time DMC World Champion DJ QBert is widely regarded as one of the greatest and most influential DJs of all time. His dominance at the DMC World Championships in the early ’90s redefined what was possible with two turntables and he is widely credited with transforming the turntable from a device used to play records into a respected, expressive musical instrument. description:
DJ Vadim, Born in Leningrad and raised in London, DJ Vadim has spent more than two decades carving out a singular place in global underground music culture. A producer, DJ and founder of the influential independent labels Jazz Fudge and King Dada Sounds, Vadim’s sound pulls from hip hop, soul, reggae, dub, jazz and bass music, stitched together with a style that has remained unmistakably his own since the early days of trip hop and Ninja Tune.

Since emerging in the mid-90s, Vadim has built a worldwide reputation as a fearless musical innovator, releasing more than 30 albums and touring relentlessly across clubs, festivals and soundsystems around the globe. His long-running relationship with Ninja Tune helped establish him as one of the defining producers of the era, while collaborations with artists including Stevie Wonder, The Roots, Prince, Public Enemy and DJ Krush further cemented his reputation as a boundary-pushing creative force.

Equal parts crate-digger, beat scientist and veteran selector, Vadim’s DJ sets move fluidly through hip hop, dubwise rhythms, soulful electronics and heavyweight bass pressure, always driven by deep musical knowledge and a lifelong dedication to soundsystem culture. With thousands of performances across nearly 90 countries, he remains one of the underground’s most respected and relentlessly creative figures.

description:
DONAL GUNNING & THE BUCKS - AUTUMN TOUR, By popular demand Dónal Gunning proudly announces the Autumn ‘Don’t Give a Buck Tour’. Leaving Dublin in November 2022 for New Zealand in pursuit of adventure and a full-time music career, his fans are hungry to see him and his band The Bucks live once again.
Following a breakout 2025, his sophomore EP, Zero Bucks Given was exceedingly well received across the globe—earning international radio play, landing prominent playlists, and drawing high praise from critics. The EP catapulted Dónal’s streams and monthly listeners to an all-time high, showcasing a powerful evolution in his sound and songwriting. The release featured a triumphant 15 date tour of New Zealand.
The Irishman is going from strength to strength in 2026, his debut album set to drop this winter. The Don’t Give a Buck Autumn tour promoting the singles off the upcoming album plus new material.
Dónal will be performing in Whanganui, Taupo, New Plymouth, Levin, Napier, Palmerston North, Wellington & Masterton. Joined by the mighty bucks Stan Shepherd (Guitar), Mason J Williams (Drums) & Jake Bergstrom (Guitar).
Tickets via UTR

description:
DYING FETUS w/ 200 Stab Wounds, Armed with undeniably some of the heaviest riffs known to mankind, DYING FETUS has established a reputation for uncompromising integrity with a slew of classical bums and today rides a resurgence of respect and esteem with a new generation. The band continually refines its unique take on death, grind, and hardcore with a combination of virtuosity and ferocity, inescapably catchy hooks, punishing breakdowns and a complete lack of pretension.
After12 horribly long years since their last tour in Australia and in only their second appearance in New Zealand since 2009, DYING FETUS are well overdue to lash us unmercifully with their savage beatdowns and earth-moving grooves and grunt, equally designed to pulverize and mesmerize. 
On their first slog into the antipodes, Cleveland death metal legends-in-waiting 200 Stab Wounds serve up a brutal slab of old school death metal with a contemporary edge. Not for the faint-hearted, 200 Stab Wounds craft classic gore-themed savagery for themselves and like-minded brethren: thrill-seekers, carnage cravers, horror fans, and aficionados of the most extreme of metal.

description:
Dan Hayles Presents | On The Grid, On The Grid is about the marking, passing and embellishing of time. The Grid is life, time, tone, tonality, rhythm, gravity, momentum, and style. 

The musicians work at times together, other times separately as 3 ensembles (horn quintet, string quartet, piano trio), and other times as combinations conversing and improvising amongst themselves. The music covers a selection of different styles and feels within and outside the jazz sound - and it's ready for your participation as a listener of melodies, dancer of beats, expresser of moods, theorist of lore, interpreter of meaning, and feeler of feels.

On The Grid consists of brand new music arranged and composed especially for the Jazz Composer Orchestra series, originally curated and presented by Michael Costeloe with funding from Creative New Zealand in 2025. This show celebrates the release on CD of the group's first ever performance - buy a copy and help us take On The Grid to more audiences around Aotearoa and the world.

Skipping along the intersection of dance music and experimental sounds, Out House aims to get your feet moving, your body shaking and your brain waves oscillating. We are kicking things off with three exciting acts, Benny Salvador, Class war on the Dance Floor and Riki Gooch and Daniel Beban's new duo UMU.

One of the most exciting young talents in his home country's revitalised dance music underground, Benny Salvador is a DJ, multi-instrumentalist and producer from Wellington whose music finds common threads between house, techno, electro, disco-funk, dub, boogie and beyond.
---

description:
Dancing & Drinking Society, DADS return to The Undercurrent!
The Dancing & Drinking Society (or DADS for short), is New Zealand’s premier exponent of authentic 1920s dance Jazz with Rags, Rambles, Shuffles, Drags and Blues from the juke joints, speakeasies, woolsheds and Memorial Halls of 1920s New Zealand.
DADS have been bringing their swing blues sounds to dance floors and craft beer bars across the capital since late 1913. When they take to the stage, guitar, horns, vocals, and kick drum blend as The Society present their favourite old rarities with exactly the sort of vigour you want for some stress relieving dance times. They’ve cultivated a decent reputation for generous and open-hearted live performance.
If you feel like a decent drink and a leg shake or two, this would make for a pretty good option.

description:
Daniel Champagne (Australia) LIVE at Martinborough Town Hall (7pm Show), Show #1
Second show announced by popular demand!
The young virtuoso recently described as “the finest guitar player of this generation” has spent the past few years selling out shows all over the globe and will be bringing his dynamite live act back to New Zealand in 2025 for a series of intimate regional concerts!
Seated show
Family friendly  
Cheaper $15 tickets for under 18s because live music is for everyone!
BYO (non alcoholic) drinks and nibbles 
October 19, 2025 @ Martinborough Town Hall
Doors open from 6:30pm / show starts at 7:00pm (8:10pm finish) 
Tickets are VERY limited. DON'T miss out!
WHAT THE PRESS SAY..
“The word Prodigy seems to entirely fall short of this soft-spoken young man’s skills, he coaxes sounds and melodies out of his instrument that literally drop jaws.”
The Calgary Herald, CANADA

“Today I saw the future of Folk – Festival goers flocking in the thousands towards the main stage to witness a young musical phenomenon from Australia dish out an absolute show-stopper.” The Firefly Column, USA

“Daniel Champagne is a crossroads. Fusing the strong traditions of Blues, Folk and other roots art with pop showmanship and admirable lyrical ability. I firmly believe that he will become an ambassador for roots music in a time where it desperately needs representation.” The Indie Blender, CANADA

“reinventing roots guitar” Rhythms Magazine, AUSTRALIA“Watching Daniel Champagne perform is a once in a lifetime experience. He is a true prodigy that plays like no one else could possibly play unless they spent at least two lifetimes studying the art.” BW Review, NEW ZEALAND

Coupled with an exhilarating guitar talent that transcends mere acoustic playing to replicate a whole band, Champagne is just magical” Themusic.com.au, AUSTRALIA

"You feel as if he just invented the instrument yesterday and was discovering its possibilities afresh” Ted Gioia (American jazz critic and music historian)

It's time to take a nostalgic journey back to the 1950s ‘Skiffle boom’ in England, when the kids turned everyday household items into great music and went on to make rock history.
Without Skiffle, John Lennon wouldn’t have met Paul McCartney – imagine a world without The Beatles!
This interactive show features lots of quirky old-time instruments and a hideous amount of crashing, banging, and chaos. description:
Deafheaven & Nothing | Wellington | San Fran, Deafheaven & Nothing | Wellington | San Fran
American black-metal trailblazers Deafheaven announce their return to New Zealand this July, presented by Banished Music. The band will perform two exclusive headline shows in Auckland and Wellington, joined by special guests Nothing.
‍
Formed in the San Francisco Bay Area in 2010, Deafheaven have spent the past decade and a half pushing at the emotional and sonic boundaries of modern metal. From their debut Roads to Judah, to the genre-defining breakthrough Sunbather, and subsequent records like New Bermuda, Ordinary Corrupt Human Love, and Infinite Granite, Deafheaven have continually redefined the limits of heavy music while confronting themes of alienation, addiction, family history, and self-perseverance.
‍
The tour follows the release of their 2025 album Lonely People With Power. Their sixth album and first for Roadrunner Records arrives as both a culmination and a reckoning , an album that embraces the band’s full identity after years of evolution. Produced by Justin Meldal-Johnsen (Beck collaborator and producer of Infinite Granite), the record captures Deafheaven’s innate ability to merge melody with brutality, and pain with poetry. Through reflections on masculinity, inherited trauma, family, and self-perception, the album grapples with the idea that while we can’t fully escape our past or our nature, we can choose how we move forward. Ultimately, Lonely People With Power stands as one of Deafheaven’s most expansive and human statements.
‍
The album has drawn praise from Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, The Line Of Best Fit, Kerrang and more, and features collaborations with Interpol’s Paul Banks and Boy Harsher’s Jae Matthews.
‍
Revered for their transcendental live shows, Deafheaven have toured the world over, performing at festivals such as Coachella and Primavera Sound, and sharing stages with artists ranging from Slipknot and Knocked Loose to Chelsea Wolfe and Mono. They’ve received a Grammy Award nomination for Best Metal Performance and continue to command a reputation as one of the most compelling live acts in heavy music.
‍
Joining them are American shoegaze outfit Nothing, whose latest release A Short History of Decay has been described by Pitchfork as “fresh and exciting.” Their fifth album and first for Run For Cover Records further expands the band’s sonic scope, delivering the most refined and immersive iteration of Nothing to date.
‍
Deafheaven return to New Zealand at their most expansive and unrelenting. Don’t miss the chance to witness one of heavy music’s most boundary-pushing bands at full force.
label: Music & Concerts

From their debut Roads to Judah, to the genre-defining breakthrough Sunbather, and subsequent records like New Bermuda, Ordinary Corrupt Human Love, and Infinite Granite, Deafhaven have continually redefined the limits of heavy music while confronting themes of alienation, addiction, family history, and self-perseverance.
The tour follows the release of their 2025 album Lonely People With Power. Their sixth album and first for Roadrunner Records arrives as both a culmination and a reckoning , an album that embraces the band’s full identity after years of evolution. Produced by Justin Meldal-Johnsen (Beck collaborator and producer of Infinite Granite), the record captures Deafhaven’s innate ability to merge melody with brutality, and pain with poetry. Through reflections on masculinity, inherited trauma, family, and self-perception, the album grapples with the idea that while we can’t fully escape our past or our nature, we can choose how we move forward. Ultimately, Lonely People With Power stands as one of Deafhaven’s most expansive and human statements.
The album has drawn praise from Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, The Line Of Best Fit, Kerrang and more, and features collaborations with Interpol’s Paul Banks and Boy Harsher’s Jae Matthews.
Revered for their transcendental live shows, Deafhaven have toured the world over, performing at festivals such as Coachella and Primavera Sound, and sharing stages with artists ranging from Slipknot and Knocked Loose to Chelsea Wolfe and Mono. They’ve received a Grammy Award nomination for Best Metal Performance and continue to command a reputation as one of the most compelling live acts in heavy music.
Joining them are American shoegaze outfit Nothing, whose latest release A Short History of Decay has been described by Pitchfork as “fresh and exciting.” Their fifth album and first for Run For Cover Records further expands the band’s sonic scope, delivering the most refined and immersive iteration of Nothing to date.

description:
Debt Club - Foothold Release Tour W/ First Reserve & Dillon Jo - Live @ San Fran, Debt Club - Foothold Release Tour W/ First Reserve & Dillon Jo - Live @ San Fran
Following the release of their recent single, “I Do Mine”, Debt Club announce their first Aotearoa nationwide tour. The tour will celebrate the release of their debut album “Foothold” which is out August 12th & available for vinyl pre-order now!

Debt Club are a Pōneke based indie / folk rock six piece who blend jangling indie rock, folk, alt-country and emo into a sound defined by rich arrangements, soaring saxophone melodies, and emotionally direct songwriting. Since forming in 2023, the band has quickly become a notable presence in Aotearoa’s underground music scene through their dynamic live performances and textured, heartfelt songs. Debt Club have shared stages with Marlin's Dreaming, Phoebe Rings and Australia’s Floodlights, while appearing at festivals including Rhythm and Vines, Twisted Frequency, CubaDupa and Newtown Festival. Following the release of their debut EP, “Taste For Stout,” the band recently unveiled “I Do Mine,” the first single from their forthcoming debut album “Foothold,” due out on August 12th.

Joining Debt Club for the Wellington date is First Reserve & Dillon Jo!

First Reserve is inevitable. Before adopting the moniker in 2023, Ryan Connaghan had been prolifically writing music that communicated their experiences in life, love, and loneliness. These themes are all approached on songs like “Last One” and “Me & My Friends” – the first offerings from First Reserve’s debut EP “There’s A God” set for release on November 14th, 2025. Thanks to their exhilarating live performances joined by a four-piece band, First Reserve has amassed a cult of devoted supporters both in their hometown of Te Whanganui-a-Tara and beyond. On stage, their sound is both intimate and larger-than-life, combining influences from alt-rock, indie-folk, and pop. First Reserve has supported visiting internationals Hot Mulligan (US) and Keli Holiday (AUS), and have toured with Kiwi favourites PARK RD, There’s A Tuesday, and Wet Denim.

Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s staple, Dillon Jo, is a queer, female-fronted four-piece band formed at Massey University in Wellington. Describing their sound as “Dreamy Droppy Rock Pop,”. ‘Dillon Jo’ is the project of Wellington Based artists Betty Smith and Georgie Levien, building paths between the elements of dream pop, shoegaze, folk, alt rock, and indie pop to create their genre defying sound. They have discovered vibrant chemistry over the past few months since making quite a stir in Wellington, playing numerous shows including opening for The Rions, Foley, Wet Denim, Hemi Hemingway and Coast Arcade only to name a few. Having heard of each other through the Reality music TV show Take The Mic 2022 which they were both contestants on, they formed Dillon Jo in early 2025. Releasing their first acoustic single ‘It was you (she’s been waiting for)’ in April 2025 and releasing two more singles later in the year, including ‘Shiver’ and ‘Jo’. The band also consists of Kahu Sanson-Burnett, (a multi-talented musician, producer, and previous member of Parallel Park) and Ruadh Munro, (Drums and previous member of Scarlett crush) Dillon Jo has transformed their live sets into an unbridled big-sound shoegaze experience

description:
Del Amitri tickets, In February 2027, DEL AMITRI return to Australia with Past to Present: Four Decades of Their Greatest Hits a celebratory tour showcasing the songs that defined their remarkable career, from early indie beginnings to international chart success.
Formed in Glasgow in 1982 by Justin Currie, Del Amitri found their long term creative backbone in guitarist Iain Harvie, whose presence has been central to the band’s sound for decades. Their breakthrough came with the 1989 album Waking Hours, featuring the enduring hit ‘Nothing Ever Happens’ and the deliciously catchy ‘Kiss This Thing Goodbye.’ The early ’90s brought further global recognition with ‘Always the Last to Know’ and their biggest US success, ‘Roll to Me,’ which reached Number 10 on the Billboard Hot 100 and remains a worldwide jukebox favourite.
Across seven studio albums, Del Amitri have sold over six million records, earning a reputation for sharp songwriting, wry lyricism and melodic, emotionally resonant rock that continues to connect across generations.
After a hiatus in the 2000s, the band returned for sold out reunion tours and, in 2021, released Fatal Mistakes, their first collection of new music in 18 years, reaffirming their signature sound for both long time fans and new listeners. Del Amitri are currently in the studio recording their new album which is set for a release later this year.
In 2027, the band celebrates their legacy with a powerful, career spanning Australian tour Past to Present: Four Decades of Their Greatest Hits.

description:
Dianne Halliday, Organ, Programme includes works by Carlotta Ferrari, Svitlana Ostrova, Jennifer Bate, Christina Harmon and Fanny Hensel Mendelssohn.


Dianne G Halliday has been active in the organ and church music scene in Wellington since her arrival in 1983. From 1984 - 96 she was Director of Music at the Metropolitan Cathedral of the Sacred Heart, establishing junior and adult choirs and bringing to fruition the expansion of the 1905 Hobday instrument to facilitate its use in contemporary Catholic liturgical practice. During this period she also succeeded in the Fellowship examinations for the American Guild of Organists. In 1997 she began a twenty-three year commitment to St Peter’s Church, Willis Street. Her activities there included the 150 the anniversary of the founding of the parish and continuing the annual Advent Lessons and Carols services. In 2014 she began DMA studies at the New Zealand School of Music at Victoria University, studying with Douglas Mews through 2018. In addition to the Wellington Organists’ Association, of which she is currently president, she has been active in the Royal School of Church Music, of which she was awarded an Associateship in 2023. She formally retired from St Peter’s in 2020 and is now active as a substitute organist and recitalist.

Dilby (Berlin) presented by Mi Casa Su Casa, Dilby (Berlin) presented by Mi Casa Su Casa
We are excited to present an absolute favourite - Dilby returns after a decade in Berlin. Join us for a special evening of world-class house and techno on the dancefloor. His last three Wellington gigs were superb and Sold Out in advance.

Secure your ticket here: https://meow.flicket.co.nz/events/46777ce5-bdc8-468a-a2bc-8ba86f4d4800

Dilby is taking the world by storm with his unique take on underground music. Crafted from a classic house and techno palette but presented with a fresh modern twist. His sound is rich, warm and musical, but aimed squarely at the dance floor. His is a mainstay at the top of the charts where he’s consistently amongst the highest selling artists in House, thanks in part to his No.1 smash hit ‘Remember Me’. In 2022 Beatport named Dilby one of the top trending artists.

Dilby’s passion and talent for electronic music is evident in the creative and innovative sound coming from his studio. A sound that sees him featured on some of the scene’s most iconic and respected labels and as an in-demand remixer, having worked his magic for artists including Mihai Popoviciu, Oliver Schories, Collective Machine, Tom & Collins amongst others. A firm favourite amongst tastemaker DJ’s his music is regularly championed by top-tier artists from Hot Since 82 to Diplo, Hernan Catteneo to Carl Cox, Guy-J to Nicole Madouber.

After making the move to Berlin in 2012 he quickly rose through the ranks to become a regular favourite in the mecca’s top clubs and festivals. In recent years Dilby’s global recognition has seen him develop a global schedule, touring across Europe, Russia, South and Central America and Australasia.

Labels: Saved, 8bit, Crosstown Rebels/Rebellion, Bondage Music, Deeperfect, Toolroom, Glasgow Underground, Bar25 Music, Terms & Conditions, Poker Flat Records.

Dolfin-Lin Duo (Cello/Piano), A chance meeting in Italy in 2021 sparked a partnership between Hungarian cellist Balázs Dolfin and Chinese-New Zealand pianist Tony Chen Lin. Trained in Hungary and Germany, they bring dynamic energy and deep rapport, drawing on global influences while still calling Budapest their enduring musical home. Tony has played solo piano for Sunday Concerts.

Their recital opens with Anton Webern’s evocative Sonata for Cello and Piano, followed by J.S. Bach’s Sonata for Viola da Gamba and Harpsichord, a lively, expressive dialogue. Zoltán Kodály’s Sonata, Op. 4 follows, inspired by Hungarian folk music, answered by Gao Ping’s Sonata No. 2 “Departure”, a Chinese counterpart. Belá Bartók’s Rhapsody No. 1 transforms peasant music into vivid concert form. Nathanael Dejong’s Abandoned Voices reflects on disconnection in the digital age. The concert closes with Johannes Brahms’s Sonata in E minor, a work steeped in contrapuntal textures and homage to Bach, bridging Hungary and the deep roots of the cello-piano repertoire.

Anton Webern, Sonata for Cello and Piano
J S Bach, Sonata for Viola da Gamba and Harpsichord in D major BWV1028
Zoltán Kodály, Sonata Op 4
Gao Ping, Sonata No 2 Departure (2001)
Béla Bartók Rhapsody No 1
Nathanael Dejong, Abandoned Voices
Johannes Brahms, Sonata in E minor Op 38

This concert is presented in association with Chamber Music NZ

description:
Drax Project & Friends, Homegrown Wellington band Drax Project are booked for a very special gig — the grand reopening of Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall. After a 13 year hiatus, the building is back online and who better to christen it than a local band with an international reputation? 
Drax Project fuses pop, R&B, hip-hop, and jazz. They formed in 2014 after meeting in Wellington (members studied Jazz Performance at Victoria University and Whitireia Polytech). After capturing local audiences busking on the streets, they launched a professional career. Since then, they’ve released two albums, toured extensively, and opened for global heavyweights Christina Aguilera, Ed Sheeran, and Camila Cabello. 
Joining Drax Project on the bill is one of the city’s most beloved artists. Oscar-winning Bret McKenzie will open the evening alongside his eight-piece Wellington-based band, The State Highway Wonders. 
When Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall officially reopens in February, it will be 13 years since the iconic venue closed for refurbishment and strengthening. This landmark concert, full of Wellington talent, is the perfect way to honour the city’s rich cultural and musical legacy.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Drax Project and Friends | Town Hall, WELLINGTON, Drax Project and Friends | Town Hall, WELLINGTON
DRAX PROJECT TO HEADLINE GRAND REOPENING OF
TE WHARE WHAKARAUIKA WELLINGTON TOWN HALL SATURDAY 20 FEBRUARY 2027

Hometown heroes Drax Project are set to make history as the first act to perform at Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall when the doors officially reopen on Saturday 20 February 2027, marking the first event in the iconic venue since its closure for refurbishment 13 years ago.

The landmark concert will honour Wellington’s rich cultural and musical legacy, with Drax Project returning to the city where they first captivated audiences as buskers on central Wellington’s streets, before launching a career that would see them become one of New Zealand’s most successful acts.
Joining them on the bill is one of the city’s most beloved global names, Bret McKenzie, who will open the evening alongside his
eight-piece Wellington-based band, The State Highway Wonders.

Tickets go on sale at midday Friday 19 June from ticketmaster.co.nz

The show will also feature a host of surprise special guests throughout the night, including some of Drax Project’s favourite collaborators, inspirations and friends, creating a uniquely Wellington occasion and a celebration of the wider New Zealand
music whānau.

For Drax Project, being invited to reopen the historic 122-year-old building is a true full-circle moment as they explain
“This is going to be a very special gig for us! We all met while at uni here and Wellington is where we got our start. The Town Hall closed before Drax became a thing, but playing there is something we've always dreamt of doing as a band.”

Since emerging from Wellington’s busking scene, Drax Project have built an international career that has seen them amass nearly a billion streams resulting in 34 Platinum certifications globally. Renowned for their live show, they have toured extensively across the world including sharing stages with Ed Sheeran, Christina
Aguilera, Camilla Cabello and George Clinton. Though their music has sustained international success, Wellington remains at the heart of the band's story, making their return to reopen one of the capital’s most treasured venues a fitting homecoming.

Don’t miss your chance to be a part of this historic night. Tickets go on sale midday Friday 19 June from ticketmaster.co.nz

description:
Dusty Lands at Wellington Bluegrass Society, Dusty Lands are an acoustic folk quartet based in Whangarei. Blending American folk with their unique Northland campfire style, Dusty Lands invites you to join them for their first ever performance for an evening of luscious harmonies, soulful songwriting, banjos, mandolins and resonators.

The genesis of the band began with Val and Leah Land, mother and daughter, from their roots in the Hokianga where they have been singing round the fire as long as they can remember - hymns, kapa haka waiata, folk, pop and more. The last ten years have seen them performing as two thirds of the trio Harmony Couch in slots at folk clubs, ceilidhs, Irish pub sessions, oop-up folk gatherings and the Auckland Folk Festival.

Gary Smyth, tugboat captain and one of the greatest songwriters to emerge from Northland, then joined them on stage. Gary is currently working on his debut album inspired by artists like Gregory Alan Isakov and Mandolin Orange.

Rounding out the quartet is Gary's (distant) cousin, singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Dusty Burnell. Winner of the Tui Folk Award twice as a member of both T-Bone and The Frank Burkitt Band, Dusty is a familiar face on stages throughout Aotearoa.

Armed with undeniably some of the heaviest riffs known to mankind, 𝗗𝗬𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗨𝗦 has established a reputation for uncompromising integrity with a slew of classic albums and today rides a resurgence of respect and esteem with a new generation. The band continually refines its unique take on death, grind, and hardcore with a combination of virtuosity and ferocity, inescapably catchy hooks, punishing breakdowns and a complete lack of pretension.

After 12 horribly long years since their last tour in Australia and in only their second appearance in New Zealand since 2009, 𝗗𝗬𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗨𝗦 are well overdue to lash us unmercifully with their savage beatdowns and earth-moving grooves and grunt, equally designed to pulverize and mesmerize.

On their first slog into the antipodes, Cleveland death metal legends-in-waiting 𝟮𝟬𝟬 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗕 𝗪𝗢𝗨𝗡𝗗𝗦 serve up a brutal slab of old school death metal with a contemporary edge. Not for the faint-hearted, 𝟮𝟬𝟬 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗕 𝗪𝗢𝗨𝗡𝗗𝗦 craft classic gore-themed savagery for themselves and like-minded brethren: thrill-seekers, carnage cravers, horror fans, and aficionados of the most extreme of metal.

Warming up the circle pits and necks will be the slamming sonic signature of ORGANECTOMY in New Zealand and the old-school death metal grit and punishing ferocity of ASHEN in Australia.

description:
Dónal Gunning - Free Live Music Wednesdays, Every Wednesday, come down to Moon for FREE live music from 6.30pm, all pizzas $15 from 5.30-9pm
Dónal Gunning is a singer songwriter from Dublin, Ireland. He draws on rock, folk, indie and punk influences.
Now based in Wellington, New Zealand his debut solo single Homesick released in October 2023. Homesick is a song dedicated to the masses who have emigrated their motherland for opportunity and adventure. It tells the story of the struggle in leaving friends and family.
His debut EP Born to Perform released in May 2024. The EP was inspired and written while travelling New Zealand, Portugal and Ireland.
Donal has released two singles in 2025 Your 1 & Losing Weight both of which have received tremendous praise globally. He is set to release a second EP later this year. He knows how to work the crowd and always brings fun, energy and Irish charm through his thought-provoking lyrics and formative sound

Dónal knows how to work the crowd and always brings a fun, energetic, intangible Irish charm to his performances. His lyrics are thought-provoking while his sound is uniquely powerful.
His second EP ‘Zero Bucks Given’ was released in August 2025. The EP features the two singles Losing Weight and Your 1, both of which were exceedingly well received worldwide. He is currently touring New Zealand with 15 dates across the North and South island to promote the EP.
Dónal will be playing some songs from his debut EP Born to Perform, Zero Bucks Given, plus additional acoustic folk songs.

description:
EXHUMED (USA) + ANOXIA (AUS), GORE METAL KINGS EXHUMED (USA) ANNOUNCE AUSTRALIA & NEW ZEALAND TOUR 2026
Gore Metal kings EXHUMED (USA) hit the blood-soaked road in 2026, announcing their long-awaited return to Australia and New Zealand in support of their brand-new album Red Asphalt, out February 20, 2026 via Relapse Records.
The undisputed masters of “Gore” Metal rev their engines and prepare one of 2026’s most frenetic, unhinged slabs of sonic obliteration — a record that finds EXHUMED pushing their trademark deathgrind violence into even more dangerous territory.
“We’re very stoked to be back in your ear-holes with Red Asphalt,” says EXHUMED mastermind Matt Harvey. “Our recent albums have taken you with us through graveyards, operating theaters, video store horror aisles, and our own band history.
This time around, we’re inviting you to a place we spend a disproportionate amount of our lives — the American roadway. Familiar, yet far more dangerous than it feels — a place that can take you to the hospital or the grave in more ways than you can imagine.”
As part of their 2026 Australia & New Zealand tour, EXHUMED will be joined by NSW-based Old School Death Metal band ANOXIA on all New Zealand dates, bringing raw, blood drenched savagery across the Tasman.
For the Australian dates, EXHUMED will be joined by Western Australia’s own ASHEN, one of the country’s most formidable modern death metal acts.
This is the first time EXHUMED (USA) and ANOXIA (AUS) have ever played NZ – DO NOT MISS OUT!
The tour will also see EXHUMED headline Perth Dethfest 2026 (debut appearance) and Sydney Dethfest 2026 (debut appearance), with Sydney featuring a monumental co-headline performance alongside Technical Death Metal pioneers ORIGIN (USA).

description:
Earth Tongue, Fresh off the announcement of their forthcoming third album Dungeon Vision, Aotearoa’s heavy-psych duo Earth Tongue return home this February for a run of six exclusive shows across the country. The tour comes off the back of the band’s whirlwind international touring cycle and gives fans the earliest chance to hear brand-new material. 
The first show lands on the day of Dungeon Vision’s release, playing at the Turner Centre, Kerikeri on Friday 13 February. They’ll follow that up in Auckland’s Double Whammy on Saturday 14 February and then Last Place, Hamilton on Sunday 15 February. The duo then travel south for a run in Dunedin at Pearl Diver on Thursday 19 February, Space Academy in Christchurch on Friday 20 February before heading to Wellington on Saturday 21 February to finish the tour at the iconic San Fran. 
Guitarist Gussie Larkin and drummer Ezra Simmons have been based in Berlin, writing and recording Dungeon Vision with Los Angeles garage-rock icon Ty Segall who together have captured Earth Tongue’s most immersive and ambitious work yet. With anticipation building after unveiling their towering title track ‘Dungeon Vision’ and its handcrafted, cinematic music video - Earth Tongue edge fans toward a set of shows which bring a fully realised Dungeon Vision experience.  
Earth Tongue - Dungeon Vision (Official Music Video)
With their world-building aesthetic, relentless energy and cemented spot as one of our most electrifying psych-rock acts, Earth Tongue are sure to provide an unforgettable show - celebrating the release of their most visionary record to date. Don’t miss them playing in Aotearoa this February.
