description:
Echoes of Home: A Musical Journey Across Time, Event Information
Some days remind us who we are and where we come from — when an entire nation moves as one to honour Independence.
To celebrate the 80th Anniversary of Vietnam’s National Day (2 September), Viet Hub NZ proudly presents
“Echoes of Home – A Musical Across Time”
This free concert is a heartfelt journey through the sounds of Vietnamese history — from nostalgic childhood songs to powerful wartime ballads and modern melodies of pride and hope. All performances will include English subtitles, making it easy for everyone to follow along and connect with the stories.
Whether you’re Vietnamese or simply curious about a different culture, this is a wonderful opportunity to experience the warmth, resilience, and beauty of Vietnam through music and storytelling.
🎁 Raffle with Over $300 in Prizes
Don’t miss our special raffle on the day. Tickets will be available at the venue for $5 and $10. Payment can be made in cash or by bank transfer.
💛 Support Viet Hub NZ
This event is free to attend, but if you believe in what we do and want to help us continue running community workshops, cultural events, and youth-led initiatives — please consider making a donation.
👉 Donate here: https://givealittle.co.nz/cause/viet-hub-nz-rooted-in-culture-powered-by-community

description:
Echoes of Us - WJF 2025, Echoes of Us is a live, improvised music experience where you are the muse. In an evening of deep reflection, spontaneous creativity and genuine musicianship, a house band fronted by saxophonist and woodwind doubler Zoe Ioannou, invites you as the audience to share personal moments, memories, or themes—light-hearted, emotional, joyful, tender–anything you desire. These offerings are then to be transformed into rich, evolving soundscapes created in real-time by the musicians. Perfectly set in the warm, intimate and light atmosphere of Whisky and Wood, this event offers an invitation to slow down, listen deeply, and feel heard in a way words alone often cannot achieve. Come as you are—your story may become the music that moves and echoes us all at Wellington Jazz Festival 2025.
Doors open 4.30pm for a 5pm start.

description:
Elegance - Wellington, Elegance - Wellington
Dynamic British Isata Kanneh-Mason make her NZSO debut in a concert featuring Mozart, Brahms and Andrée.

Programme:
Andrée Andante Recitative
WA Mozart Piano Concerto No. 27
Brahms Serenade No. 1

Isata Kanneh-Mason, the eldest sibling in a dynasty of extraordinary musicians, is being lauded as a pianist who is “the real deal” (classical-scene.com). What a treat to hear her bring such intelligent elegance to Mozart’s last piano concerto. Praised by BBC Music Magazine as capable of making “lines sing beautifully and virtuosic passages dance, finding intimacy and eloquence at telling moments”, Kanneh-Mason is the perfect performer to bring this mature, serenely lovely concerto to Aotearoa New Zealand audiences.

To round out this programme, the NZSO performs two works that deserve a wider audience. Brahms’ Serenade harks back to Mozart’s own delightful serenades, while Elfrida Andrée’s Andante Recitative, written in 1878, was only rediscovered in the 1980s, and “open[s] in broody darkness, but quickly blossom[s] into optimistic, songful melody” (Michael Clive).

description:
Elias Bartholomeo (Aus) at Wellington Bluegrass Society, Elias Bartholomeo is a Solo fingerstyle guitar player hailing from Sydney, Australia. On many occasions, Elias has been titled as one of the top acoustic guitarists around Australia today with his playing being described as "Walking a tightrope between many genres all at once!" with a fearless and energetic approach to his live performances.

Elias embarked on his musical journey at the tender age of four, under the guidance of his grandfather. Immersed in the sounds of The Beach Boys, Jerry Reed, The Shadows, Chet Atkins and Tommy Emmanuel, Elias was inspired to emulate their mastery. Despite being self-taught and unable to read music, he honed his craft through ear training and collaboration with fellow musicians.

At sixteen years old, Elias had the opportunity to live out his dream and perform alongside Tommy Emmanuel in the Maui Cultural Arts Centre, Hawaii - an experience that further fuelled his passion for music. Over the years, he has had the privilege of collaborating with numerous musicians from across the globe, enriching his musical repertoire.

Over the last few years, Elias has toured extensively around Australia, New Zealand and USA. Elias has been has been building a strong profile in the live music and Guitar communities, playing at festivals, theatres and halls as a solo show and collaborating with other great musicians near and far.

In 2020, Elias was recognised as a graduate of the Talent Development Project, marking a significant milestone in his musical career. He has since been carving out his path as a solo artist in Australia, culminating in the release of his debut EP Give to Keep in early 2021 and recording parts of his collaboration project According To History at Sony Music Australia.

His musical journey has led him to crossroads, where in Hawaii, Elias met a fellow Australian guitar player, who has become a driving force in his development as a player. Having done their first show together whilst Elias was still in school, then forming the duo Elias and JJ and released a series of EPs According To History and have performed shows around New South Wales Australia including opening for Daryl Braithwaite at Wests, Tamworth.

Doors 7pm , show starts 7.30pm sharp

After wildly successful sell-out shows across New Zealand, join Cam and Sam for an intimate night out as they wow audiences both young and old performing the greatest hits of Elton John and Billy Joel LIVE! Piano Man, Rocket Man, Uptown Girl, Goodbye Yellow Brick Road, We didn’t start the fire, Bennie and the Jets, She’s always a woman, Crocodile Rock and many many more.

Your favourite Elton and Billy songs are in safe hands with Cam and Sam, these professional touring NZ musicians have performed on live national television, commercial radio and featured in the NZ Music Charts in careers spanning two decades. He has more than fifty Top 40 hits on the UK Singles Chart and US Billboard Hot 100, including seven number-ones in the UK and nine in the US, as well as seven consecutive number-one albums in the US.

American Billy Joel has sold more than 150 million records and ranks as one of the most popular recording artists and respected entertainers in the world. Joel has had 33 Top 40 hits and 23 Grammy nominations. In 1999 he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame and has received the Recording Industry Association of America Diamond Award, presented for albums that have sold over 10 million copies.

description:
Enemy of the State, Enemy of the State
Enemy of the State spans new music, Romantic lyricism, and one of the most incendiary works in Shostakovich’s career, performed by outstanding guest artists.

The concert opens with the NZ premiere of John Psathas’ Next Planet. Commissioned and premiered by the Tonhalle Düsseldorf GmbH (management company for the Tonhalle Düsseldorf in Germany) and the Düsseldorf Symphony as part of their Green Mondays project, Next Planet was premiered in June 2024 as part of a cycle of twelve “Green Pieces.” Read more about the project and John's work here.

The programme continues with Alexander Glazunov’s Violin Concerto in A minor, a Romantic masterpiece notable for its warmth and lyricism. Composed in 1904, the concerto weaves together heartfelt themes across its uninterrupted movements, culminating in a brilliant solo cadenza leading to to the trumpet calls heralding the final Allegro. Orchestra Wellington is delighted to welcome back Benjamin Baker, violinist and Artistic Director of At the World’s Edge Festival, to perform this remarkable work.

Lady Macbeth of Mtsensk, Suite for Soprano and Orchestra, featuring internationally acclaimed lyric soprano Madeleine Pierard, will close the evening. Premiered in January 1934 as a massive success, in early 1936 the Russian newspaper Pravda denounced the opera in an article titled “Muddle Instead of Music,” sending Shostakovich’s life into a tailspin. The work was banned in the Soviet Union for almost thirty years, until 1961. Orchestra Wellington Music Director Marc Taddei has crafted a suite tracing the journey of the opera’s protagonist, Katerina, from isolation and passion to betrayal and despair, combining arias and orchestral interludes into a concentrated symphonic portrait. Alongside the forces of Orchesta Wellington, complemented by one of Wellington's very own A-grade brass bands, Pierard’s powerful voice brings Shostakovich’s heroine vividly to life, illuminating both the work’s humanity and the reasons it provoked such outrage.

description:
Enigma - Wellington, Enigma - Wellington
NZSO Artistic Advisor and Principal Conductor Gemma New with legendary pianist Sir Stephen Hough present a concert of charm, mystery and bold vision.

Programme:
Ross Harris Concerto for Orchestra (World Premiere)
Saint-Saëns Piano Concerto No. 5 Egyptian
Elgar Enigma Variations

Edward Elgar’s greatest masterpiece remains swathed in mystery.

His Enigma Variations, a set of 14 variations on a theme you never actually hear, has been the subject of both intense scrutiny and great love, thanks to the compositional genius and throbbing heart pulsing in these compelling variations.

Similarly, Saint-Saëns’ Fifth Piano Concerto has beguiled audiences with its Eastern-inspired sounds — hence its Egyptian nickname. To weave his own spell on us, legendary pianist Sir Stephen Hough returns to our shores. Praised by Limelight for possessing “an other-worldly stillness and strength [and] the perfect technique combined with the utmost poetic fluency”, Hough promises to transport us to another world.

We proudly premiere Ross Harris’ Concerto for Orchestra. A four-time winner of the SOUNZ Contemporary Award, Harris’ artistry and bold vision electrifies this newly commissioned work, driving the orchestra to new heights.

A self-taught beat-maker, multi-instrumentalist and vocalist, she creates immersive sonic worlds shaped by elastic harmonies, intricate rhythms and playful found-sounds. Her soulful, expressive voice anchors her storytelling, exploring personal, mythical and political themes. 
With three acclaimed albums and an ASMR inspired EP, Estère has earned praise from Elle Magazine France, Afropunk, RNZ, The Guardian and more. Her production credits include collaborations with Jordan Rakei, Deva Mahal and Oddisee, and she placed Top 10 in the global Stonesthrow Records beat-making competition. In 2023 she released “Finer” with Nightmares on Wax on Warp Records. 
A magnetic live performer, Estère has opened for Grace Jones, Erykah Badu, Peaches and Hiatus Kaiyote, and performed at festivals worldwide including Glastonbury, Afropunk Paris, WOMAD, Bushfire and Sori Arts Festival. She has headlined sold-out shows across the UK, France and New Zealand, and was twice nominated for the Aotearoa Music Awards 
Her creative range extends into conceptual performance, including her 2020 show Into the Belly of Capricorn and her role as the first-ever headline artist for the World of Wearable Art Awards Show in 2022. 
Now based in London, Estère is entering a new chapter inspired by reconnecting with her Cameroonian heritage. She has begun weaving her tribal language Bassa and other African languages into her songwriting, themes that shape her forthcoming 2026 album Diaspora Baby. She also founded DiaxXpora, a London-based community and event series celebrating creatives from diaspora backgrounds

Brahms- Symphony No.4 in E minor, Op. 90
I. Allegro non assai
II. Andante moderato
III. Allegro giocoso
IV. Allegro energico e passionato

ETHAN RAWHITI

Wellington-born pianist Ethan Rawhiti graduated in 2025 with a Bachelor of Music (Honours) from Victoria University of Wellington, where he studied with Dr Jian Liu and Emma Sayers. He began learning piano at age seven and has extensive experience as a collaborative musician. In 2025, Ethan was répétiteur for Wellington Opera’s Mate Ururoa by Dame Gillian Whitehead and performed in Brigid Bisley’s In Return concert in Whanganui. In 2024, he was sponsored by Professor Jack C. Richards to attend the Semaine Internationale de Piano in Switzerland. Ethan is committed to collaboration and plans to pursue further study overseas.

WEIRAN CHEN

Chinese pianist Weiran Chen has been a prizewinner in numerous international and national piano competitions, including the “Mido”Concours De Tiano Sino-Francais, the Kingsburg International Piano Competition, the Feis Ceoil in Ireland and the Beethoven International Music Competition.

Chen graduated from the Boston Conservatory at Berklee with a Master of Music degree and is a current DMA student at the NZSM. She is passionate about not only performing piano solos, but also collaborating with other artists and teaching up and coming musicians.

GORE METAL KINGS EXHUMED (USA) ANNOUNCE AUSTRALIA & NEW ZEALAND TOUR 2026
Gore Metal kings EXHUMED (USA) hit the blood-soaked road in 2026, announcing their long-awaited return to Australia and New Zealand in support of their brand-new album Red Asphalt, out February 20, 2026 via Relapse Records.

The undisputed masters of “Gore” Metal rev their engines and prepare one of 2026’s most frenetic, unhinged slabs of sonic obliteration — a record that finds EXHUMED pushing their trademark deathgrind violence into even more dangerous territory.

“We’re very stoked to be back in your ear-holes with Red Asphalt,” says EXHUMED mastermind Matt Harvey. “Our recent albums have taken you with us through graveyards, operating theaters, video store horror aisles, and our own band history.
This time around, we’re inviting you to a place we spend a disproportionate amount of our lives — the American roadway. Familiar, yet far more dangerous than it feels — a place that can take you to the hospital or the grave in more ways than you can imagine.”

As part of their 2026 Australia & New Zealand tour, EXHUMED will be joined by NSW-based Old School Death Metal band ANOXIA on all New Zealand dates, bringing raw, blood drenched savagery across the Tasman.

For the Australian dates, EXHUMED will be joined by Western Australia’s own ASHEN, one of the country’s most formidable modern death metal acts.
This is the first time EXHUMED (USA) and ANOXIA (AUS) have ever played NZ – DO NOT MISS OUT!

The tour will also see EXHUMED headline Perth Dethfest 2026 (debut appearance) and Sydney Dethfest 2026 (debut appearance), with Sydney featuring a monumental co-headline performance alongside Technical Death Metal pioneers ORIGIN (USA).

description:
FLYTE, Acclaimed indie band Flyte bring their signature blend of heartfelt lyricism and melodic craftsmanship to a special run of New Zealand shows this November.

Flyte have earned widespread acclaim for their refined songwriting and emotionally resonant sound, with a catalogue that showcases their evolution from classic British guitar pop to more expansive and introspective arrangements. Their releases have been celebrated for their lyrical honesty and rich harmonies, cementing their place as one of the UK’s most compelling contemporary bands.

Formed in London, Flyte are led by singer-songwriters Will Taylor and Nick Hill, whose close creative partnership underpins the band’s distinctive identity. They broke through with their debut album The Loved Ones and continued to build momentum with subsequent records, including This Is Really Going to Hurt and Flyte, earning praise for their timeless influences and modern sensibility. Their work captures themes of love, vulnerability and connection, delivered with a stripped-back elegance and attention to detail that has resonated with audiences worldwide.
For audiences in Aotearoa, these shows offer a rare opportunity to experience Flyte’s intimate and immersive live performance, bringing their finely crafted songs to life with warmth, precision and emotional depth.

FREE GIG - Andrew Grayson - farewell show, The sound of Wellington band fFolks (pronounced simply, "Folks"), ranges from alt-country to angular punk-pop to atmospheric soundscapes. description:
FUNKIN' DONUTS feat. DJ Audit (AK), FUNKIN' DONUTS feat. DJ Audit (AK)
We’re back for one last jam - and we’re going out with a bang! Join us for an extended party session at Parrotdog, with special guest DJ Audit from Auckland. The last time we teamed up at The Yotty (RIP) in Raglan, it was the stuff of legend. Let’s make it happen again - see you on the dancefloor!

FUNKIN’ DONUTS is a celebration of all things funky on the 7” 45 vinyl format. The brand’s name comes from the records themselves - small, round, and with a large hole in the middle, they’ve long been nicknamed “donuts.” Founded by Flex Webster in 2022, FUNKIN’ DONUTS began as a jam session with fellow 45 heads before evolving into a platform for original edits and future vinyl releases. With an ultimate vision of putting out 7” records, Flex has already released six albums of party edits under the brand, with plans for the first physical release coming soon. Now based in Bali, FUNKIN’ DONUTS is going global - relaunching with a fresh, dancefloor-focused energy.

Joining us from Tāmaki Makaurau: DJ Audit

Since 1998, Audit has been crafting an eclectic sound that transcends genres while staying rooted in Hip Hop culture. A lifelong record collector and open-format DJ, his sets seamlessly weave Disco, Hip Hop, Soul, Cumbia, and Latin rhythms into vibrant journeys. With decades of experience, a deep appreciation for musical diversity, and an instinct for reading the crowd, Audit creates electric atmospheres that keep the audience moving.

Host with the most: Flex Webster

Flex Webster lives and breathes music. A DJ, producer, and record collector with a career spanning almost three decades, his journey has taken him around the globe. Flex’s sound blends Afrobeat, Latin, Funk, Hip Hop, Reggae, Disco, and House, reflecting the soulful rhythms of the African diaspora. Don’t miss this rare B2B with old mate Audit - your last chance to catch Flex for a while, as he returns to Bali to bring his magic back to the Island of the Gods.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Fat Freddy's Drop: Based On A True Story 21st Anniversary Tour | Sun 3 May | MFC, Doing it for the love of music, legendary band Fat Freddy's Drop are returning to the stage in 2026 to perform their ground-breaking debut album Based On A True Story.
The 51 dates across Australia, Aotearoa, Europe & UK will be Freddy’s first shows following the sudden death of founding band member Chris ‘MU’ Faiumu. The band is united in its decision to continue with this long-planned tour.
Lead singer Dallas Tamaira says, ‘It’s important for us to honour the intentions we had with MU and playing
this album live is part of that.’
Based On A True Story was independently released in 2005, an album of 10 fresh slices of future funk, with surprises, fakes & freaky sidesteps. In a historic run, the album became Aotearoa’s Longest-Charting Album with 111 weeks in the Top 40, won eight NZ Music Awards and took out Giles Peterson’s Worldwide Music
Awards in the UK.
‘This was the band’s first full length studio album and its success was the springboard for what has been an incredible journey together’, explains saxophonist Scott Towers. ‘We want to pay tribute to the music, to MU and the band he established. And, of course, to play to our fans around the world who have supported us through everything.’
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Fat Freddy’s Drop, Doing it for the love of music, Fat Freddy’s Drop takes to the Michael Fowler Centre stage in May 2026. They’ll be there for three nights performing their ground-breaking debut album, ‘Based On A True Story’. The tour will mark the first live performances since the sudden death of founding band member Chris ‘MU’ Faiumu.
Lead singer Dallas Tamaira says, “It’s important for us to honour the intentions we had with MU and playing this album live is part of that.” ‘Based On A True Story’ was independently released in 2005. It became Aotearoa’s longest-charting album with 111 weeks in the Top 40. It also won eight NZ Music Awards and took out Giles Peterson’s Worldwide Music Awards in the UK.
Twenty years later, the band’s unique funk and roots style has become a defining sound of Aotearoa. “[Based On A True Story] was the band’s first full-length studio album, and its success was the springboard for what has been an incredible journey together,” explains saxophonist Scott Towers. “We want to pay tribute to the music, to MU, and the band he established. And, of course, to play to our fans around the world who have supported us through everything.”
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Fazed on a Pony - 'swan' Tour - Te Whanganui-a-Tara w/ Welcomer & Tessa de Lyon, Fazed on a Pony - 'swan' Tour - Te Whanganui-a-Tara w/ Welcomer & Tessa de Lyon
Fazed on a Pony is embarking on a nationwide tour to celebrate the release of their new album swan, out January 23 2026 on Melted Ice Cream and Meritorio Records.

Joining FOAP on the night will be Welcomer and Tessa de Lyon.

Tickets at: https://www.undertheradar.co.nz/gig/100103/Fazed-On-A-Pony---Swan---Album-Release-w/-Welcomer-and-Tessa-De-Lyon.utr
_

Fazed on a Pony is the recording project of Tāmaki-based songwriter Peter McCall. Featuring elements of indie rock, alt-country and emo, McCall’s songs address the uncertainties of life with warmth, wit, and emotional immediacy.

swan follows FOAP’s 2022 debut album, it’ll all work out, which featured “nuggets of genius lyricism” (RNZ). This new body of work will see McCall, with bandmates Rassani Tolovaa (Office Dog), Hamish Morgan (Marlin’s Dreaming, School Fair), and Shaun Malloch (Mim Jensen), expand from the Pavement-esque tuneful indie rock of previous releases to include pedal steel, fiddle, drum machines, and synthesisers. While there is a diversity of style, the album is rooted in the hallmarks of McCall’s music: uplifting and catchy guitar lines that serve the song, paired with arrangements that feel both comfortable and surprising. Where the lyrics tell a sad story, the music betrays that it might just be okay in the end.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
First Reserve, Dropper & Elly Mae, Get ready for another memorable night out as First Reserve & Dropper share the bill with rising star Elly Mae. This will be an evening to feast your ears on a diverse soundscape of angular guitars, melodic goodness, and glorious noise.

Here’s the lo-down:

First Reserve is inevitable. Before adopting the moniker in 2023, Ryan Connaghan had been prolifically writing music that communicated their experiences in life, love, and loneliness. These themes are all approached on songs like “Last One” and “Me & My Friends” – the first offerings from First Reserve’s debut EP set for release in late 2025. On stage, their sound is both intimate and larger-than-life, combining influences from alt-rock, indie-folk, and pop.

Dropper combines intuitive songwriting sensibilities with wall-of-sound, guitar.  Blending noise and melody, Dropper is dynamic, song-centred, high-energy indie rock. Often compared to Bob Mould’s work with Hüsker Dü or Lou Barlow's early Sebadoh, they’ve been described by one review as having a "high energy stage performance punctuated by flawless musicianship and songwriting skills that seems beyond the years...Honestly, it’s hard to overstate how impressed I was with Dropper and am eagerly awaiting my next chance to see them live.”

Elly Mae's music encapsulates the bittersweet complexities of growth, relationships, time escaping, and the nostalgia embedded within. Her music is an amalgamation of folk, dreampop, shoegaze and whatnot.

Grab your general release tickets online for just $15! Or, even better, grab an early bird ticket for only $10 and secure your spot for a night of unforgettable live music. Doors at 8pm, first act on at 8:30pm.
label: Music & Concerts

Trained in a jazz conservatory then corrupted in dive bars and on the streets, Aleister James Campbell, with his evergreen love of Charlie Parker & Jimi Hendrix, is known for his spell-binding stage presence and deep connection to the music.

Currently on the run from the Jazz Police for inappropriate Wah Wah use in a straight-ahead jazz context...

For what promises to be a triumphant night, Aleister (on guitar and vocals) will be joined by: Tyson Smith - Electric Bass, Rick Cranson - Drum Kit, Baron Oscar Laven - Alto & Soprano Sax, and Jake Baxendale - Tenor Sax.

description:
Fizzwizard plays T-Bone Walker, Pōneke raised guitar slinger Aleister 'Fizzwizard' Campbell storms home from Tāmaki Makaurau to lead a stellar sextet through a set of sophisticated blues by electric guitar pioneer T-Bone Walker.
At the crossroads where Blues and Jazz meet, you'd be sure to find Aaron Thibeaux Walker. Better known to his fans as 'T-Bone', he pioneered the electric guitar in The Blues, directly influencing every great blues player who came after him, and through Chuck Berry on Rock 'n' Roll. Often performing with jazz musicians, his music was refined and sophisticated, infused with the perfect amount of rough edge and grit, and always devilishly swinging.
Joining Aleister for this one-off gig are a sensational Auckland rhythm section, an exuberant Wellington horn section, and special guest Paul Dyne making a rare outing on keys!

Over a career spanning more than a decade, he has released critically acclaimed albums and collaborated with Kendrick Lamar, Solange, Thom Yorke, and Herbie Hancock. His latest release, the seven-track EP Big Mama (March 2026), was produced entirely in New Zealand while Flying Lotus worked on his debut sci-fi thriller Ash. Accompanied by a short film, he describes the EP as an “experimental, maximalist, hyperfast, electronic burst of energy… unpredictable and alive.”
This winter, experience Flying Lotus live with his Layer³ show - an immersive audiovisual journey blending music and 3D visuals for a striking, unforgettable performance. Don’t miss one of electronic music’s most innovative artists up close.

description:
Folk B*tch Trio - Wellington, Folk Bitch Trio - 'Now Would Be A Good Time' Album Tour with special guest Georgia Knight

Now Would Be A Good Time, the debut album by Folk Bitch Trio, tells vivid, visceral stories. Their music sounds familiar, and it’s built on a foundation of the music they’ve loved throughout their lives–gnarled Americana, classic rock, piquant, clear-eyed balladry. But the songs are modern, youthful, singing acutely through dissociative daydreams and galling breakups, sexual fantasies and media overload, all the petty resentments and minor humiliations of being in your early twenties in the 2020s.

Heide Peverelle (they/them), Jeanie Pilkington (she/her) and Gracie Sinclair (she/her) have known each other since high school, and first started singing together five years ago. Peverelle recalls sending Pilkington a heartbroken—in their words “bad”—song they had written called “Edie”; Pilkington remembers the song differently. “I felt so inspired that my teenage peer had written something so honest and original,” she recalls. It wasn’t long before she messaged Peverelle and Sinclair, asking if they’d be interested in starting a “folk bitch trio.” As soon as they started singing together, their connection deepened, and “the chemistry of being inspired by each other was evident from the get-go,” says Sinclair.

Listening to Folk Bitch Trio, it’s clear that this is a band of three distinct points of view, with contrasting and complementary backgrounds and visions. Pilkington grew up with two musician parents and brings formative memories of watching them perform, of listening to Gillian Welch and Lucinda Williams, and of her own imagined path as a career musician. Peverelle spends their spare time making art and furniture; those hobbies, as well as their love of pop music old and new, articulate a love for the tactile, the home-grown and the hand-made. Sinclair is the self-proclaimed jester of the group, but her taste skews dark, gothic, baroque and dramatic, expressed as a love of opera and ballet as well as musicians as wide-ranging as Patti Smith, Nirvana and Tchaikovsky.

Folk music has a bad habit of being presented as a deathly serious concern. It’s the music you cry to, it’s overly sacred, it’s solemnly considered by critic-historians. But Folk Bitch Trio have a shared sense of humour that is embedded deep in their music and that sets it alight, safe from the self-serious traps of the genre. Now Would Be A Good Time is funny and darkly ironic in the manner of writers like Mary Gaitskill or Otessa Moshfegh. On “Gods A Different Sword” they crack that “My body keeps the score/But if you tell me that you need it/I can get up off my floor,” a nod to the clichéd, over-referenced millennial self-help book, as they wryly sing about sex within earshot of housemates, and wring sexual innuendo from physics terminology

description:
Four Last Songs - Wellington, Four Last Songs - Wellington
One of the world’s most acclaimed conductors, Sir Donald Runnicles, returns to the NZSO in a programme of pure luxury and ravishing beauty.

Programme:
R Strauss Rosenkavalier Suite
R Strauss Four Last Songs
Brahms Symphony No. 3

The sensuous, glittering raptures of the Rosenkavalier Suite evoke the decadence of 18th century Vienna in a dazzling array of complex waltzes.

Then delve deeper into Richard Strauss’ most personal, revealing and achingly beautiful music with his sublime Four Last Songs. These profound songs, performed by silver-voiced soprano Madeleine Pierard, sumptuously evoke a sunset portrait of a wife well loved and a life well lived.

We balance this decadence with the crystalline Symphony No. 3 from Johannes Brahms. In music that plays between light and shadow, the work takes on as its organising motto frei aber froh — free but happy.

Sir Donald Runnicles appears with generous support from Dame Bronwen Holdsworth DNZM.

description:
Freak Slug - Wellington, Manchester based musician Freak Slug - the project of Xenya Genovese - will be welcoming audiences in Pōneke Wellington and Tāmaki Makaurau Auckland into her dreamy indie-pop world this October.

Hugely influenced by ‘90s cult heroes including Ride, Mazzy Star and Stephen Malkmus, Freak Slug is all about hitting a mood. Everything that fuels her creative output is raw, authentic, sometimes weird, but always totally true self-expression. I Blow Out Big Candles is a strong statement of all of this and more. Down there, picking through the curious mix of sounds and feelings, from nostalgic, ‘90s-influenced and dreamy as well as eccentric and experimental, lives Freak Slug.

The 10-track project gives listeners a taste of what they will be in for at her Aotearoa shows, a journey of both soft soulfulness and sonic songwriting, all laid out on the table.

Free Status - Free Live Music Wednesdays (Jazz Fest), Lift your midweek with Moon's Free Live Music Wednesday's! Your weekly escape to into the sonic stratosphere
Every week, we feature a rotating lineup of incredible local musicians
Come by early for our $15 pizza specials, served hot 5.30-9pm
Perfect for date night, catch-ups, or just floating solo through the sound waves. Wednesdays at Moon are the place to orbit
This week we have a Jazz Fest special featuring Free Status!
Free Status is a jazz fusion band blending the melodic richness of Herbie Hancock and 70s jazz-funk with an electronic edge inspired by Moby. Their sound is both nostalgic and forward-looking, offering high-energy grooves and inventive compositions.
At the helm is Tommy David (keys), a rising talent whose original works have earned competition recognition and seen him share stages with acts like Dire Straits Legacy Band, Nazareth, and Hello Sailor. Joining him are seasoned rhythm players Behzad Karakia (drums) and Tyler Diprose (bass), both respected for their work alongside Aotearoa’s jazz greats.
The frontline features James Dawes (alto sax), fresh from selection for an international touring ensemble, and Sam Voyle (keys/sax), a longtime collaborator of Tommy’s with standout performances at the America’s Cup and major festivals.
Together, Free Status delivers a vibrant, genre-bending live experience you won’t forget.
Follow Free Status: https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61575737812566
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Free Status - Jazz Festival, Free Status is a jazz fusion band coming all the way from Auckland for one night only at Otto!
Free Status draws melodic inspiration from iconic artists like Herbie Hancock and 70s jazz/funk legends with electronic flair inspired by artists like Moby.
At the heart of Free Status is Tommy David on keys, an accomplished musician/composer in the early stages of his career. He has earned recognition in numerous jazz competitions and supported legendary rock acts such as Dire Straits Legacy Band, Nazareth, Hello Sailor, and plays with popular rockabilly band, Recliner Rockers. With composition at the center of his artistry, he can’t wait to share the exciting and genuine compositions he has created.
The rhythm section features Behzad Karakia (drums) and Tyler Diprose (bass), both veterans of performances with many of New Zealand’s jazz greats.
On lead alto sax is James Dawes, recently selected for an international touring band on a year-long cruise. His versatility extends well beyond jazz.
On keys is Sam Voyle, whose primary instrument is tenor saxophone. Performing with Tommy since their school days, he has built a strong musical bond that has led to major appearances, including the America’s Cup main stage and high-profile corporate events.

Nam Chucks, known formally as Namnita Kumar, is a DJ, selector, MC, and long time radio host at Radio Active FM.
Few selectors in this scene see critical acclaim, but Nam Chucks is a proud recipient of the Taite Music Prize, alongside the Outstanding Music Journalism Award from NZ on air.

Nam Chucks possesses a deep appreciation and respect for Soundsystem philosophy - dedicating her musical selections to the concepts of unity and inclusivity in rave culture. Soundsystem music serves as a vessel for her to heal others, guide the dance, and respect all things sacred & indigenous.

description:
Friday Launchpad feat. Jen Kyle, Blast off into the weekend with a rotating DJ lineup broadcasting live from Moon Base every Friday 6-8pm.
Commanding the decks this week is Jen Kyle - expect an otherworldly sound journey through disco, techno, acid, house & more
Jen currently hosts a monthly slot on The Late Late Breakfast Show with DJ Coda on RadioActive.FM. Prior to this she gained a cult following for her Drive Show of 12 years where she played everything from techno to disco, punk to funk, soul to hip hop, new wave and beyond. Out and about she's a regular at Taniwha's Den Festival and S-ence nights in the capital.
Having the musical freedom that a place like RadioActive.FM provides combined with living in Glasgow before heading to Aotearoa, working and dancing at legendary Glasgow clubs such as The Sub Club and The Arches has resulted in Jen having a broad musical spectrum. Her sets pull from that whilst being strongly influenced and moulded by her beloved Glasgow.
What to expect? Anything across the realms of disco and the darker side, acid, techno, house, wobbles and wonkiness.
Free entry, happy hour on board!

description:
Frogmeet(s) Noel Meek / Todd Luffa / Leo McKinnon, Frogmeat, also known as Frogmeet in collaboration, is a flexible noise improv performance project venturing explosive forecastings of yet uncapturable crevices. Convened by multimedia artist / musician Sophia Frank/ass Frudd and composer / violinist Mallory Elmo, it lends its name and spirit to their performances as a duo or with occasional and regular collaborators - in this instance, composer, artist and improvisor, Noel Meek.
---
Todd Luffa is the experimental ambient-pop project of Tony Amerman, originally from Minneapolis MN, now based in Pōneke. His releases combine sample based sounds, arpeggios, noise and heavy bass.
https://toddluffa.bandcamp.com/
---
Leo McKinnon creates gentle, ambient, textural works that aim to reflect the beauty he sees in the world.
$15 presale tickets via UTR
$20 door sales ($10 unwaged)
Special thank you to CNZ for supporting Pyramid Club's programme

description:
Funky Fridays Vol. 7 - Not My Sister, Libby K, Ben-Jammin, We're back for another night of house, techno, disco, bass & more at Moon with Funky Fridays Vol. 7!
Created to revive and celebrate the underground electronic scene, Funky Friday is more than just a night out—it’s a space for music lovers, dancers, and creatives to connect through rhythm and energy. Each edition features a rotating lineup of talented DJs, both local and international, ensuring a fresh and unique experience every time.
Come with an open mind and leave with tired feet.
This edition features legends Libby K, Ben-Jammin & our host Not My Sister!
$10 presales available now via UTR, or $15 on the door.
Times:
9-10 Not My Sister
10-11.30 Libby K
11.30-1 Ben Jammin
1-2 Not My Sister
-------------------------------------------------------
NOT MY SISTER
Not My Sister is a house music DJ born and raised in a little town in the north of Italy. Now based in Wellington, she started this project in 2024, and recently she has been lighting up dance floors across New Zealand, you may have already come across her sets at Twisted Frequency, Kiwiburn, Earthbeat, Cuba Dupa, Arkadien and other events across the country. Influenced by funk and disco, with a special focus on vocals and anything groovy, Not My Sister brings high energy and uplifting sets. Constantly developing as an artist, she always brings fun and passion to the dance floors. Expect a delightful fusion of melodic basslines, blending soulful, tech, garage, and deep house sounds.
www.soundcloud.com/not-my-sister
www.facebook.com/notmysista

www.instangram.com/not.my.sister

LIBBY K
From the vibrant streets of Wellington, Libby's fascination with music began at an early age with the smooth sultry
sounds of the clarinet and piano. Fast forward to her 20s where she stumbled into the hypnotic world of techno in
Berlin and a passion for 4/4 was ignited.
With a deep appreciation for the power of music to transform, Libby finds the greatest joy on a dance floor, where
the magic of music brings people together and gives us the freedom to be ourselves. Her sets are filled with
uplifting, emotive and tantalising sounds of downtempo, house and techno. Mixed with intention and a whole lot
of love xx
https://soundcloud.com/libby_k
https://www.instagram.com/libbykdj/
https://www.facebook.com/libbykmusic

https://www.twitch.tv/libbykdj
BEN-JAMMIN
Originally from Bristol, UK, Ben was immersed in soundsystem culture from an early age. He started collecting vinyl in his teens and developed a passion for the heavier side of electronic music. With his formative years spent mixing vinyl, studying African percussion and playing drums and recording for rock/rap group Band of Crooks, he moved on to play with some of the best underground DJ's, producers and musicians in Aotearoa, Australia and UK. Ben has played a myriad of parties and events including Newtown Festival, Cuba Dupa, Kiwi Burn, Little Monsters, Insomnia, Toots Suite Festival (Salmonella Dub, Laughton Kora, Pheonix Foundation), Breakaway Magical Doof Bus (Paige Julia, Y, Sorchalula,Young Gho$t, House MD), Cuba Dupa, Sydney Rd Street Festival (Melbourne), Cafe Blue (UK), Castros (UK).
Ben-Jammin can do what is needed to keep a dancefloor alive, comfortably switching between genres to suit the mood.
Always armed with bags of bass heavy treats expect a selection of new, classic and surprise music to help you release your spirit into the world.
https://soundcloud.com/ben_young_2000

She’s lit up festivals like Twisted Frequency, Kiwiburn, Earthbeat, CubaDupa, Taniwha’s Den and Arkadien and supported international acts including KC Lights.

Crafting sets that can flow through deep, melodic, techy and uplifting terrain she creates the perfect vibe for each time, each place and each crowd, always with a unique journey in mind. Her recent appearances include Flock, Yatra, Newtown Festival and CubaDupa creating magnetic dancefloors wherever she plays.

We're back for another night of house, techno, disco, bass & more at Moon with Funky Fridays Vol. 8!
Created to revive and celebrate the underground electronic scene, Funky Friday is more than just a night out, it’s a space for music lovers, dancers, and creatives to connect through rhythm and energy. Each edition features a rotating lineup of talented DJs, both local and international, ensuring a fresh and unique experience every time.
Come with an open mind and leave with tired feet.
This edition features legends Stolen Tuesday, Kimba Jade, K-otik and Not My Sister
$10 presales available now via UTR, or $15 on the door.

Times:
9-10 Not My Sister
10-11 Stolen Tuesday
11-12 Kimba Jade
12.1 K-otik
1-2 Not My Sister
-------------------------------------------------------

NOT MY SISTER
Hailing from Italy and rooted in Wellington’s vibrant scene, Not My Sister burst onto the scene in 2024 and has quickly become one of Aotearoa’s most exciting rising DJs. In such a short time, she’s already lit up dance floors across the country, playing at festivals like Twisted Frequency, CubaDupa, Taniwha’s Den, and supporting international acts such as KC Lights.

She also holds a radio residency at Wellington’s iconic Radio Active, where her show dives deep into the world of house and underground sounds.

Heavily influenced by funk and disco, and driven by a love for vocals and all things groovy, Not My Sister delivers high-energy, uplifting sets full of passion and playfulness. She weaves together melodic basslines with soulful, tech, garage, and deep house elements, always keeping the crowd moving.

SoundCloud: www.soundcloud.com/not-my-sister
Facebook: www.facebook.com/notmysista
Instagram: www.instagram.com/not.my.sister
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@not.my.sister

STOLEN TUESDAY
Stolen Tuesday started life as a house music club dancer in the UK 20 years
ago, and has spent the last 10 years DJing at Wanaka and Queenstown's best
establishments, bringing her unique energy to create magical dance floors.
Since residing in New Zealand, she has previously split her time living between Great Barrier island and Wanaka, spreading the love through her weekly radio shows on Wanaka Beats and Aotea FM. Not shy of the underground scene, you will also find Stolen Tuesday getting down off grid and playing at bush doofs.
Best known for dropping all things bassy which exude an element of fun matching her own high energy, guest appearances on Base FM (Auckland) alongside well known Auckland DJs have helped showcase her enthusiasm and talent.
With a style ranging from glitter box style disco and funk, to dirty after hours Tech House and all things in between, including the occasional breaks/ghetto funk set, it’s no surprise that She has been a regular on the South Island festival scene where she has been happy warming up or playing after notable international artists. She has also played at Otherlanz and remotely at Great Barrier Island’s new Wingman festival.

Stolen Tuesday now resides in Wellington and whilst fairly new to the city has already played several times for both the 'Open air' brand at Carlucci land and with Wellington renowned 'Little monsters' notably shaking things up at this year's Newtown festival.
Although not one to take herself too seriously, Stolen Tuesday knows it all comes down to the music and having a good time!

Soundcloud: https://soundcloud.com/user-720686581

KIMBA JADE
Kimba Jade has been lighting up dancefloors for over 20 years with her signature blend of deep, funky, and globally inspired grooves. A master of musical journeying, she weaves bass-driven beats with tribal, melodic, and soulful sounds that move both body and spirit.

With a deep passion for Ecstatic Dance and the power of music to connect and uplift, Kimba brings that same vibrant energy into clubs and bars. Her sets fuse Tech House, Indie Dance, and Techno, blending driving rhythms with emotive melodies to create an atmosphere that’s both immersive and electric.

After years in Sydney and Auckland’s underground scenes, Kimba now calls Wellington home—bringing her unique mix of rhythm, soul, and bass to local dance floors.

Soundcloud: https://soundcloud.com/kimba
Facebook: www.facebook.com/kimbadj/
Instangram: @djkimbajade

K-OTIK
Based in Wellington, New Zealand, K-otiK is a multi-genre DJ. His sound spans house, tech house, bass house, and techno — laced with heavy vocals and thumping basslines. With a cheeky stage presence and high energy behind the decks, K-otiK takes crowds on journeys that balance careful curation with unexpected twists. A regular on RadioActive FM and part of Wellington’s Open Air collective, he’s built a reputation for spreading joy through music. For K-otiK, music does not discriminate — it’s the universal language that brings people together.

Instangram: @dj_kotik_nz

description:
Fur Patrol & Dateline - Wellington - Meow, Banished Music are ecstatic to announce the return of one of Aotearoa’s all-time favourite bands, with Fur Patrol returning to the stage for a very special run of shows in March 2026, their first tour since 2024.
From the moment their debut EP Starlifter landed in 1998 until their swansong album Local Kid arrived in 2008, Pōneke’s Fur Patrol carved out an unforgettable legacy in Aotearoa music. Their debut album Pet dominated the New Zealand Albums Chart for an astonishing thirty weeks, while the era-defining single Lydia famously knocked Destiny’s Child off the number one spot. Across three albums, two EPs and hundreds of live shows, Fur Patrol earned a reputation as one of the country’s most formidable and unmissable live acts.
Now, ahead of this year’s Homegrown Festival, Julia Deans (guitar, vocals), Andrew Bain (bass), and Simon Braxton (drums) are hitting the road once more, joined by longtime collaborator and Pet producer David Long (The Mutton Birds). David brings his inimitable guitar wizardry to weave rich sonic layers through the trio’s unmistakable foundation.
Anyone who’s caught Fur Patrol live in recent years will attest they’ve lost none of their potency, power, or energy. These shows promise a celebration of a timeless catalogue, packed with beloved anthems and delivered with the same fire that made the band legendary.
Don’t miss your chance to see one of Aotearoa’s most beloved bands return to the stage this March.

GENERAL KALA LIVE at Le Cafe, Picton, GENERAL KALA LIVE at Le Cafe, Picton
General Kala - Described as "Ultravox meets Kate Bush"
Founded in 2013, Wellington-based General Kala's first live performance was two years later, by which time they had a 90-minute set of original, synthesiser-driven music. The original lineup of Cusiel (vocal and synth), Spence (synths and vocal) and Mathiassen (drums) is still in place for 2025, with six EPs to be released this April and May (plus another six by 2026) through Pulse Science Recordings.
Taking their lead from classic analog-synth acts of the late 1970s and early '80s, as well as progressive and rock luminaries of both decades, Kala infuses visceral, soaring, melodic dance composition with vintage synthesis and syncopated rhythm
Now based in Auckland, the band will bring their singular sound to Le Cafe in Picton.

https://generalkala.bandcamp.com

description:
GIRLS TORQUE, Torque Sounds are back!
Presenting our first Girls Torque here in Aotearoa. Celebrating the wāhine DJs of Te Whanganui-a-Tara. Expect quality selectors playing on the classic Torque Sounds rig that you've heard all over Pōneke and beyond.
Girls Torque is the modern revival of a night that made its mark in London rave scene back in 2004 at the legendary venue; Fridge in Brixton. Two decades on, the scene has transformed. The talent is undeniable, the ranks are deep, and the dancefloor belongs to everyone.This is not a nostalgia trip. It's a resurrection: same name, same energy, new city, new era!
On the line up we have:
M.CAP
Fortuna
Malware
Claire-voyant
Fluffcore
Kicking things off at 9pm with an assortment of electronic music to keep you dancing deep into the night!
Each of the DJ's on this lineup have their names woven into the fabric of Wellington's club scene, each making waves in their own way;
• M.Cap is the founder of 'Nine Oh Nine' who facilitate girls & Femmes only DJ workshops.
• Fortuna is the founder of 'Fortunes' known for their deep/prog/melodic house & techno events.
• Malware is the Co-founder of Venom Events who focus on Techno events here in Pōneke.
• Claire-voyant is one of the founders of Torque Sounds and the original Girls Torque event back in London.
• Fluffcore is the Co-founder of TGF known for their dark techno events.
Come and kanikani to your hearts content amongst friends Saturday August 15th at Valhalla.
Tickets available now via events.humanitix.com/girls-torque

description:
GLM (1985) + TEXTURE, NOYER & WHAEA G B2B OHIMESAMA BREAKS (CUBA DUPA FUNDRAISER #`1), *CUBA DUPA FUNDRAISER #1 - ALL PROCEEDS TO GO TOWARDS VALHALLA @ CUBA DUPA*
Pōneke, we’ve got another one for you…
Ghost Media Presents:GLM (1985/Flexout/Incurzion)
+ Support from Texture, Noyer, Whaea G & Ohimesama Breaks
Get ready to party with Bristol’s finest!
We’ve invited GLM over to lay down his signature flavour of UK bass in Aotearoa for the first time.
Since his first release in 2023, GLM has curated a sound that incorporates elements of dnb, garage, dubstep, grime, and jungle, releasing music on respected independent labels including Incurzion Audio, Helix, Kojiki, Sub:stance Recordings, and 1985 Music. GLM’s sound has received radio support on networks like BBC Radio 1, Kiss FM, and Rinse FM, and he has performed widely across club circuits in the UK. A true don on the tools, we’re excited to welcome him as he showcases his production sound at Valhalla.
On support, we have an all-star lineup including TEXTURE, joining us from Ōtautahi for the first time since 2021.
We’ve been looking for an excuse to bring Texture up for a while, and this felt like a perfect opportunity. A purveyor of a unique sound that elicits an emotional response, fusing elements of bass, breakbeat, jungle and techno, Texture is well-seasoned, having opened for some serious artists including Addison Groove, Machinedrum, Ben UFO and Alix Perez. We can’t wait to host her for the first time either!
From the local sphere, we’ve pulled out the big guns. On opening duties we have NOYER, a man we can always trust to get the floor rocking. One half of Garage Sale, Noyer has been a staple of the capital’s underground dance music scene for the whole of the 2020s. To close out the night in style, we’ve got a blockbuster back to back of two of the capital’s finest jungle selectors - WHAEA G & OHIMESAMA BREAKS. If either of those names are familiar to you, you’ll have some idea of the levels that are about to be effected.
As is standard, we’ve got BANSHEE SOUNDSYSTEM on ear and chest rattling duties. Come on!
Finally, we just want to mention that this event is a fundraiser for our Valhalla stage at Cuba Dupa. So buy a ticket and help support us for the biggest free party of the year!
Tickets available from Humanitix

🚨 AUSTRALIA + NEW ZEALAND we are SO excited for the GLORY album tour!!! With very special guest Darcie Haven !! TJJT Mailing List Pre-sale starts Wednesday 15 October at 1pm local time (check your inbox!) and general on-sale starts at 1pm local time on Friday October 17. Add on a GLORY pre-order to win the chance to come to soundcheck and meet and greet. See you there!! ** 🚨

Presented by: Live Nation & Triple j

ARIA Award-winning indie-rock four piece Teen Jesus and the Jean Teasers - Anna Ryan (they/she; vocals/guitar), Scarlett McKahey (she/her; guitar/vocals), Jaida Stephenson (she/her; bass) and Neve van Boxsel (she/her; drums) - have gone from strength to strength since the release of their debut EP Pretty Good For A Girl Band (2022), with its lead single ‘Girl Sports’ landing at #55 on the triple j Hottest 100. Their debut album I Love You (2023) landed at #6 on the ARIA Charts, placed at #52 on the Hottest 100 (‘I Used To Be Fun’), with its deluxe I Love You Too (2024) featuring new singles ‘Dull’ ft. Softcult and ‘Please Me’ ft. The Linda Lindas - the former landing at #187 in triple j’s Hottest 200 this year.

They have just announced their second album GLORY - which was produced with 3x GRAMMY Award-winning, London-based Catherine Marks (boygenius’ The Record, Wolf Alice) and features the singles ‘BALCONY’, ‘UNSCARRED’, and latest single 'MOTHER' - will be released November 7, 2025 (Community Music)

Teen Jesus and the Jean Teasers have raked in a slew of accolades including nominations and wins at the ARIA Awards, J Awards, APRA Awards, Rolling Stone Awards, AIR Awards and Music ACT Awards, being named one of Spotify’s Artists To Watch, and being hand-picked to open for legendary international heavyweights Foo Fighters and Pearl Jam in Australia and the US.

Now based across Ngunnawal/Canberra, and Naarm/Melbourne, Teen Jesus and the Jean Teasers are just as concerned about issues facing today’s women, non-binary people and young people everywhere as they are with making music that continues to push boundaries and expectations. They are ambassadors for Green Music’s No Music on a Dead Planet, played Rising Tide on Parliament House steps, contributed to the Parliament inquiry into challenges and opportunities within the Australian live music industry and are firm supporters of Michael’s Rule. This is a band never to be pigeonholed, and definitely never underestimated.

description:
GLORY – Kāpiti, GLORY – Kāpiti
Orpheus Choir Wellington hits the road with Vivaldi’s Gloria, bringing this landmark choral work to Kāpiti.

One of the most recognisable works in choral music, Vivaldi’s Gloria unfolds in a rapid series of short movements, moving between full choir and solo voices with an energy and brightness that has made it a favourite for generations.

Glory brings together Vivaldi’s Gloria and Mozart Requiem in a full concert programme.

These performances also feature Orpheus Scholars, emerging singers studying classical voice at Te Kōkī, the New Zealand School of Music, as soloists.

With thanks to Pub Charity and Creative NZ's Creative Communities Scheme, administered by Kāpiti Coast District Council, for their support.

GREAT SOUNDS GREAT 2026, Eyegum Music Collective presents GREAT SOUNDS GREAT, a multi-venue music and arts festival taking over Pōneke's Te Aro precinct for one night only on Saturday 5 September 2026. Showcasing 40 of Aotearoa's best artists across 10 neighbouring venues, this is one big party you shouldn't miss.
Tickets here
Eyegum has worked hard to curate a programme that is sure to offer something for everyone, from first time gig-goers to seasoned live music obsessives. The eclectic lineup includes national treasures like Bic Runga and Savage, heavy-hitting legends Beastwars, Kody Nielson’s enigmatic project Silicon, indie math rockers So So Modern, powerhouse party starter Mokotron, local hip hop sensation MĀ, and everything in between.
Tonic Collective are back with an impeccably curated lineup for their travelling stage, which includes Pitch Black celebrating 30 years as Aotearoa electronica pioneers and award winning sonic explorer Amamelia.
It's not all music, three of our best poets Chris Tse, Dani Yourukova, and Jackson McCarthy will also perform.
Excitingly for 2026, we are adding a new venue, the incomparable Meow Nui, helping make this year's event bigger and better than ever. We are also throwing a warm-up party, The Night Before, across three venues in Newtown village on Friday 4 September. This will showcase 12 incredible up-and-coming artists and is the perfect way to prepare for the main event.
Ticket holders will receive a wristband that will give them access to each of the participating venues throughout the event. Information on how to pick up wristbands will be provided to ticket holders closer to the time.
Limited tickets, including for The Night Before, on sale now from eyegum.co.nz/great-sounds-great
Presented with support from Abandoned Brewery, RadioActive.FM, and Wellington City Council.
Venues: Meow Nui, San Fran, Meow, Valhalla, Rogue & Vagabond, Bedlam & Squalor, Hotel Bristol, St Peter's on Willis, Flying Nun Records, Tonic Travelling Stage.

GUITAR WOLF - MORE JET - AOTEAROA TOUR, Guitar Wolf Rules of Rock and Roll
FIrst ... Band has to have looks
Second ... Fighting spirit
Third ... ACTION!
THere is no fourth or fifth
SIXTH ... Technique
Stir people hearts and your own !!
Tokyo masters of rock&roll mayhem. 30 years young & the foot ain’t ever come off that car crash accelerator pedal. Still swerving, dead man curving, burnin’ out & danger driftin’. Link Wray overdriven guitar rumble fuzz & feedback, Joan Jett warm leatherette aesthetic obsession, locomotive rockabilly rhythms & early Ramones punk chunk thump. Noise, hiss & drone co-opted from fellow Japanese sound assault merchants High Rise & Mainliner. It’s a sonic rendezvous designed to cave in heads & destroy frequencies, while yr dancing yr ass off on that road to oblivion…. Mr Slackjaw
"There are garage-rock bands, and then there’s Tokyo terrors Guitar Wolf... This band’s style of rock’n’roll demands more imposing prefixes, like “jet,” “hurricane,” and “Kawasaki ZII 750.” Much as 1960s British Invasion groups bastardized the blues and sold it back to American teens, Guitar Wolf have spent the past 30(+) years making once-rebellious Stateside sounds—surf, rockabilly, Nuggets, CBGB punk—seem dangerous again, forsaking retro purism for monomania. Your typical garage band might make your ears ring; this one kills zombies." - Pitchfork
Tickets via UTR

description:
Garage Sale Presents: Caru and Brandn Shiraz, Garage Sale Presents: Caru and Brandn Shiraz
AFTER A HUGE RUN OF SHOWS OVER SUMMER, CARU & BRANDN SHIRAZ BRING THEIR MUCH HYPED LIVE SHOW BACK TO THE MIGHTY TE-WHANGANUI-A-TARA. PLAYING AT MOON BAR FOR ONE NIGHT ONLY!

PRESENTED BY GARAGE SALE

JOINED BY AN ALL-STAR CAST OF LOCAL SELECTORS:
⟡ CLOVA
⟡ NOYER & YOUNG GHO$T
⟡ ULTRAVIOLET

⌁₊˚⊹ ⊹˚₊⌁

Caru and Brandn Shiraz join forces to celebrate the sounds of UK Garage. The pair combined their unique musical styles with the 2025 release of their EP ‘Back 2 Back’, a project inspired by the pioneers of pirate radio. Their music combines both artists' respective styles to create a fresh take on the classic 2000’s dance genre, with Brandn Shiraz’s boundary pushing MC skills effortlessly complementing Caru’s refined production. The duo have had notable sets across Aotearoa, with a recent summer tour which showcased the fusion of their energy at festivals such as Northern Bass, The Others Way, Cuba Dupa and Twisted Frequency, and most recently opening for Bakey and Capo Lee.

⌁₊˚⊹ ⊹˚₊⌁

This night will be curated by Garage Sale, one of the capital’s longest running garage nights, who have chosen a range of the finest DJs in town to keep the vibes flowing. Opening things up we have Noyer and Young Gho$t the masterminds of Garage Sale, who will be easing things in with some selections across UKG, funky and grimey beats accompanied by Ghost’s bars.

Warming up for the headliner we have CLOVA, a rising star and local legend who recently released her debut album ‘Spiral’ to widespread applause. For Garage Sale she will hone in some of her favourite tracks, new and old, delivering her unique take on the sound.

Finally on closing duties we have none other than Ultraviolet, making his Garage Sale debut. A seasoned veteran with releases on Big Fresh, Echo Train and Club Unique, UV is one of the country’s best kept musical secrets, and we can’t wait to see what he pulls out the bag for this set.

Tickets are available online for an extremely reasonable $20+bf. Lock in now and prepare for a massive night of big tunes and vibes!

description:
Gardens Magic, The Wellington summer nights just got warmer with the return of Gardens Magic. The capital’s talented musicians are on full display across January. The annual event, brought by Wellington City Council, presents a series of free concerts in the Botanic Garden Soundshell. 
Each year, a huge range of music genres is represented across three weeks. Choose from rock, folk, country and western, soul, jazz, pop, reggae and many more. Come early to grab a good picnic spot and sit back and enjoy the show with the whanau or a group of friends. Prolong your stay in the gardens by exploring the evening light display afterwards. The pathways near the Soundshell will be colourfully illuminated between 9 and 10:30pm every evening. During the day, the Botanic Gardens host a Kids Garden Trail and Kids Explorer Days. 
See the full 2026 programme online and keep an eye out for rain day announcements. This is your chance to join in on a beloved local tradition.

description: Gary Wilby; Reflections, Miniatures and Soundscapes, Gary Wilby has recently retired after nearly 50 years in the classroom. He taught Music both in the classroom and as an Itinerant teacher – mostly in secondary schools. He was fortunate in 1995 to be appointed to the Composer in Schools position which resulted in many works for students to play. Gary graduated from the University of Canterbury with a MA(Hons). He plays piano and cello and while he has in the past sung in choirs, he now enjoys the annual NZCF Wellington May Workshop. Gary has played in many ensembles and has been in the Wellington City Orchestra (formerly Wellington Chamber Orchestra) since 1986. He formerly was for 15 years the Music Director and Conductor of the Capital Performing Arts Orchestra. He has regularly played with “Opus 3 Trio” for the past decade. This will be Gary's third performance in Futuna Chapel.

description: Gaudete! Rejoice! This is an ideal time to mix and mingle with the choir and audience members. We hope you can join us. We look forward to seeing you there.

description:
General Kala, Founded in 2013, Wellington-based General Kala's first live performance was two years later, by which time they had a 90-minute set of original, synthesiser-driven music. The original lineup of Cusiel (vocal and synth), Spence (synths and vocal) and Mathiassen (drums) is still in place, with six EPs released this year (plus another six by 2026) through Pulse Science Recordings.

Taking their lead from classic analog-synth acts of the late 1970s and early '80s, as well as progressive and rock luminaries of both decades, Kala infuses visceral, soaring, melodic dance composition with vintage synthesis and syncopated rhythm (courtesy of Mathiassen, also drummer for Shapeshifter and Kora).

Now based in Auckland, the band will bring their singular sound back to Wellington - performing at the Rogue and Vagabond January the 16th.

Music from 9:30pm, FREE ENTRY

description:
Georgia Knight | Wellington, Banished Music proudly welcomes Georgia Knight back to Aotearoa, following her standout solo performance at The Others Way. After captivating audiences with a spellbinding set that lingered long after the final note, Georgia brings her singular world of sound back to New
Zealand stages, expanded, immersive, and more powerful than ever, this time with her full live band. Naarm-born and sometimes Aotearoa-based, Knight crafts otherworldly pop from autoharp, dusty loops, synth textures, and avant-garde edges. Her 2023 EP Hell on Bent Street established her as a rising force, with appearances at Dark Mofo, Rising, Camp A Low Hum, and shows alongside Blonde Redhead and Mogwai. 
It’s been a big 12 months for Georgia. Her independently released debut album Beanpole, described by KEXP as "an evocative set of dimly-lit, hypnotic, psych-tinted pop", earned praise from Sharon Van Etten, Arab Strap, and BBC Radio 6 Music. Critics highlighted her "shadowy, seductive trip-hop textures" (KCRW), "extraordinary vocal range and graveside poems" (The 13th Floor), and "goosebumps"-inducing live performances (BBC Radio 6). 
Supporting the album, she was booked for a string of highly coveted festivals including The Great Escape (UK), Golden Plains (AU), Phoenix Central Park (AU), The Others Way (NZ), and Port Noise (NZ). 
Now touring her 2025 album Beanpole, recorded with Andrew ‘Idge’ Hehir, Georgia returns with a fuller, immersive live show, intimate, cinematic, and impossible to look away from.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Get Rhythm — The Johnny Cash & June Carter Show, It’s more than just a tribute concert — it’s a live theatrical experience bringing to life the heart, humour, and deep connection of a famous country music couple. Get Rhythm — The Johnny Cash & June Carter Show is coming to Wellington for the very first time in 2026. 
 
Based on the award-winning movie ‘Walk The Line’, Get Rhythm stars real-life married duo Mark and Joanne Caligiuri. Together, they capture the look, sound, and spirit of Johnny and June with remarkable authenticity. Between songs, heartfelt storytelling and charming onstage chemistry, you will be taken on a beautiful musical journey. Authentic, emotional, and unmissable — Get Rhythm stands as a powerful and respectful celebration of Johnny Cash and June Carter’s legacy.

description:
Getdown Services - Australia & New Zealand 2026, Meet Getdown Services – your new favourite band and one of the UK’s hottest word-of-mouth acts! The brilliantly offbeat cult British duo has been turning heads across Britain and Europe with their balls-to-the-walls live shows, tongue-in-cheek wit, razor-sharp lyrics and infectious disco-fuelled grooves, teetering between chaos and genius. And now, after selling out tours across the UK and Europe, they’re bringing their riotous show down under for the first time in May/June 2026 – with shows in Brisbane, Sydney, Melbourne, Auckland and Wellington, presented by I OH YOU and MG Live. 

Tickets go on sale Friday 14 November at 10.00am local time, with MG Live presale commencing Thursday 13 November at 10.00am local time. Sign up for early access to the MG Live presale here.   
            “I reckon we get people asking us to come to Australia probably every day, and everyone in England is moving there, so will be good to see what all the fuss is about.

“Always been one of those places where you’re like, ‘Fair enough, but I can’t be arsed with that. It looks mad – there’s snakes and also it takes 40 hours to get there.’ Will be good fun, though! Went to New Zealand to see a mate of ours get married a few years ago and thought it was a lovely country and I really liked those pies they have. It felt quite similar to the UK in a lot of ways, so playing gigs there should be fun!”
Getdown Services

For those in the know, Bristol-based duo Josh Law and Ben Sadler – aka Getdown Services – are THE must-see new act of the year. And if you don’t know yet, you will soon … and you’ll wish you got in early! Named as “one to watch” at this year’s Glastonbury Festival and dubbed (by the band themselves) “Britain’s Best Band”, their live shows are equal parts smart, sweaty and gloriously unhinged. Their sound is a wild blend of scrappy indie disco, twisted funk and post-punk energy, turning the absurdity of modern Britain into dancefloor gold.        
 
The pair met at school in Minehead, Somerset and now make music together at home in Bristol – churning out what Rolling Stone called “power disco with unrepentant silliness” with a healthy dose of satire and swagger. Their highly lauded debut album Crisps (Breakfast Records, 2023) showcased their eclectic danceable grooves and biting social commentary, and a mix of sharp, funny social observations wrapped in irresistible, funk-fuelled rhythms. Follow-up EPs Your Medal’s In The Post, Crumbs and latest, Primordial Slot Machine, cemented their cult status, alongside an arsenal of red-hot singles – including James Bay’s Hat, Dog Dribble, I Got Views and Eat Quiche, Sleep, Repeat.   

“Getdown Services are unrepentantly silly and constantly deliver one of the most joyously deranged live shows – just one of the best live bands out there!”
 Rolling Stone
“Their live show is as daft and as exhilarating as they come. Five stars.”
 Buzz Magazine
 
 “Genuine contenders to being the most exciting and interesting band in the UK right now.”
 CLASH

Getdown Services look set to gobble up the world, one crumb at a time. Whether you’re into danceable chaos, satirical genius or just want to be ahead of the curve, Getdown Services are the band you didn’t know you needed – until now! Britain’s favourite new band are about to become yours too!  

Supporting Getdown Services are local legends DARTZ.

Proudly from Aotearoa/New Zealand, DARTZ have built their reputation the hard way: relentless touring, chaotic live shows, and singalong anthems that thread the needle between beer-soaked pub classics and earnestly ideological indie punk

DARTZ make rock songs about real lives, all rooted in the strange humour that comes with living at the edge of the world. Vocalist Daniel Vernon, guitarist Christan Pianta, bassist Clark Mathews, and drummer Hakopa Kuka-Larsen formed in 2019, three weeks out from what was only ever meant to be a one-off show. But the New Zealand four-piece hit the ground running, and six years on, DARTZ have never stopped moving at pace.

That sense of speed and urgency still informs their output: scrappy snapshots from the world’s southernmost capital, pulling directly from its run-down rental housing, battered Corollas, and postcolonial political tension. Though lyrics may skate between satire and sincerity, it’s clear that every DARTZ track is written for the people in the room - loud, messy, communal, and impossible not to sing along to.

In the years since, DARTZ have taken those loud, communal anthems as far as Europe and the UK, shared stages with Turnstile and FIDLAR, toured with Australian counterparts The Chats and Dune Rats, and even snagged a 2027 Foo Fighters support slot back home in New Zealand.

The band from Wellington aren’t here to answer life’s big questions: at the end of the day, they lie somewhere between “modern-day folk heroes” and “politically aware class clowns”, depending on who you ask. But beneath the chaos, DARTZ’s core mission remains clear: providing real representation for the place they come from and the people who live there.

description:
Girl Next Door: the next chapter tour - Wellington, Jenni Smith is hitting the road this autumn for her “Girl Next Door: The Next Chapter” Tour - an intimate run of shows celebrating the release of her long-awaited debut album, The Girl Next Door (out March 27).
Fresh from nationwide chart success and years of diary-style storytelling, Jenni invites you into the next chapter of her world - one filled with red lipstick confidence, hopeless romantic daydreams, and the kind of songs that feel like pages torn straight from her journal. Expect heartfelt ballads, kitchen-dance anthems, and the stories behind the songs that built this era.
The tour kicks off in Auckland at Ponsonby Social Club on March 28th - a special album release party the night after the record drops - before heading to Christchurch’s Wunderbar on April 19th, and Wellington’s Moon on April 29th.
Joining Jenni for this run are three incredible artists:
Auckland - Blake Stainton
Christchurch - Steffany Beck
Wellington - Emma Kate
Whether you’ve been here since the first Taylor Swift cover or just found your way to The Girl Next Door, this tour is about celebrating the journey so far - and stepping into what comes next.
The next chapter starts here.

description:
Girls Rock The Boys - Wellington, POWERHOUSE WOMEN SINGERS: CLASSIC ROCK FROM THE BANDS OF MEN: A KICKASS LIVE BAND
Girls Rock the boys is back—bringing powerhouse vocals and legendary rock anthems to the stage.
This time, it’s Ashley Hale-Durham, Georgie Sullivan, and Julie Lamb leading the charge, with a stellar band behind them: Andrew Richardson (drums), Matt Fitzpatrick (bass), Aslan Rowlands (guitar), and Duncan Haynes (keys).
We’re diving deep into the golden era of rock—Journey, Whitesnake, Boston, Foreigner, Rainbow, and Deep Purple, all delivered with the energy of a rugby pitch and the comfort of your favourite dressing gown.
Whether you’re waving your phone torch to Foreigner, headbanging to Rainbow, or playing air guitar to Deep Purple, you’ll find something to do with yourself in every “mini EP” set.

Come and see us - we love it when you do!
🎟️ Early bird tickets just $20. Door sales $30.
💔 A special shout-out to our inaugural bass player, Callum Black, who’s heading overseas. You’ve been an inspiration, Callum. We’ll work to do you proud.

description:
Girls Rock the Boys - Petone, Girls Rock the Boys - Petone
Girls Rock the Boys began as a spark - a half‑joke, half‑challenge tossed around in a rehearsal room: What would happen if women took on the big, swaggering, stadium‑sized rock anthems that were never written with them in mind? Not only as a tribute, but as a full‑throttle, joyous celebration of the songs that shaped generations.

The idea stuck. Because everyone knows those songs - the ones you belt in the car, the ones that must be played too loud, the ones you recognise from the very first riff. Whitesnake. Boston. Foreigner. Deep Purple. Journey. Rainbow. Led Zeppelin. Uriah Heep. The giants.

But what no one expects is how they feel when powerhouse women take the mic.

Girls Rock the Boys brings together a lineup of women with range, grit, soul, and the kind of stage presence that pulls you straight into the mosh pit. Behind them is a kickass live band built for exactly this music. Together, they tear into the classics - honouring the songs, laughing a little at the very male lyrics now being belted by women.

These anthems were always big enough and wild enough to belong to anyone brave enough to claim them. The result is a show that’s nostalgic and fresh at the same time - and loud in all the right ways.

Girls Rock the Boys is a celebration of musicianship, of women in rock and of the timeless songs that still shake the walls decades later. It’s the classics you love, reimagined.

When women take the mic, the classics hit different. Experience it live with Ashley Hale-Durham, Georgie Sullivan, Jude Madill, and Julie Lamb leading the charge, backed by the stellar band: Andrew Richardson (drums), Matt Fitzpatrick (bass), Aslan Rowlands (guitar), and Duncan Haynes (keys).

🎟️ Early bird tickets $20. Door sales $30.

description:
Girls Torque, Girls Torque
Torque Sounds are back!

Presenting our first Girls Torque here in Aotearoa. Celebrating the wāhine DJs of Te Whanganui-a-Tara. Expect quality selectors playing on the classic Torque Sounds rig that you've heard all over Pōneke and beyond.

Girls Torque is the modern revival of a night that made its mark in London rave scene back in 2004 at the legendary venue; Fridge in Brixton. Two decades on, the scene has transformed. The talent is undeniable, the ranks are deep, and the dancefloor belongs to everyone.This is not a nostalgia trip. It's a resurrection: same name, same energy, new city, new era!


On the line up we have:
M.CAP
Fortuna
Malware
Claire-voyant
Fluffcore


Kicking things off at 9pm with an assortment of electronic music to keep you dancing deep into the night!


Each of the DJ's on this lineup have their names woven into the fabric of Wellington's club scene, each making waves in their own way;

• M.Cap is the founder of 'Nine Oh Nine' who facilitate girls & Femmes only DJ workshops.
• Fortuna is the founder of 'Fortunes' known for their deep/prog/melodic house & techno events.
• Malware is the Co-founder of Venom Events who focus on Techno events here in Pōneke.
• Claire-voyant is one of the founders of Torque Sounds and the original Girls Torque event back in London.
• Fluffcore is the Co-founder of TGF known for their dark techno events.


Come and kanikani to your hearts content amongst friends Saturday August 15th at Valhalla.

Tickets available now via events.humanitix.com/girls-torque

description:
Glory, Orpheus Choir Wellington hits the road with Vivaldi’s Gloria, bringing this landmark choral work to Kāpiti.

One of the most recognisable works in choral music, Vivaldi’s Gloria unfolds in a rapid series of short movements, moving between full choir and solo voices with an energy and brightness that has made it a favourite for generations.

Glory brings together Vivaldi's Gloria and Mozart Requiem in a full concert programme.

These performances also feature Orpheus Scholars, emerging singers studying classical voice at Te Kōkī, the New Zealand School of Music, as soloists.

description:
Gnarling, Western Haikus & Serenna, Hey Wellington! New band here.

The internet is a bit of a hell-scape nowadays... so we thought the best way to introduce ourselves would be in person.

You might already know some of us from other bands we've played in, like Lizard Prom, Into Orbit, Opium Eater or any of the other various rock and metal bands we've been part of over the years. We started jamming together and Gnarling mid last year, and have been writing a set of songs drawing from our wide ranging influences from shoegaze and alt-rock to noise and black-metal... so the sound is a bit hard to pin down, but so far most of it is gloomy, doomy and atmospheric.

And where better to share that gloomy doominess with you than at Wellington's gloomiest and doomiest venue, Valhalla? As luck would have it, we're putting on a totally FREE show at Valhalla on Thursday, 29 January, along with two other fantastic local acts, Western Haikus (Screamo) & Serenna (goth/post-punk), who have kindly agreed to give up their Thursday night for us.

Doors will open at 8pm, and Serenna will kick off the night at 8.30.

Looking forward to seeing you there!

Gnarling

description:
Go Folk Yourself - Bottom Bunk Club w/ Departure Party and Finn Madeleine, Go Folk Yourself - Bottom Bunk Club w/ Departure Party and Finn Madeleine
The Industrial Revolution and its consequences have been a disaster for the human race. Make the disaster a little bit more tolerable by coming to a killer gig.

Bottom Bunk Club is a folkpunk/thrashgrass band based in Wellington. The perfect soundtrack for getting dumped, wetting the bed, and small-scale rebellion. You can K*ll the bedbugs, but there's no cure for a catchy chorus.

Departure Party, the solo Folk/Punk Farm/Emo act from Poneke, Wellington. A voice given to all your existential crises and dread, that would like to remind you, Death comes for us all and no one's a main character.

Finn Madeleine is an indie folk songwriter from Australia who has called Aotearoa home for 2 years now. They write raw songs about love and being a person in a longstanding attempt to understand what the hell is going on.

Venue is wheelchair accessible, seated and standing options available.
