description:
Gordo And Teej Present: Craigslist, Craigslist are a party, record label and DJ outfit operated by Colter Carson (Public Possession) and Raffeal Hamblett. Since humble beginnings in 2020, the project aims to create shared moments of joy with an aesthetic centred on obscure records. The success of this manifesto is reflected in the consistently positive response gained from partygoers and label supporters alike, year after year.⁣
⁣
In the DJ booth, Colter and Raffy (Craigslist Soundsystem) strike a delicate balance between eclecticism and danceability that denotes a deep understanding of musical traditions and club culture. Defying the confines of genre and era, the pair bring a refreshing and joyous sound to the dancefloor.⁣

Gordo & Teej are proud to present iconic Ōtautahi due Craigslist, after dancing to these guys all summer at Flux, Smash Palace, Electric Ave and Two Minds festivals we just had to fly 'em up to show the Pōneke whānau how these guys get the dance floor cranking. Expect nothing less than the finest Italo disco grooves, chunky house beats and uptempo club music to transport you to a sun soaked festival light years away from the welly winter.

description:
Goya Live at The Dowse with RadioActive, Goya Live at The Dowse with RadioActive
Goya Live at The Dowse with RadioActive.FM
Friday 10 April, 3-4pm
Free
RSVP appreciated via

Wellington noise-punks Goya take their name from 19th century Spanish painter, Francisco Goya, whose dark imaginative work spanned romanticism, madness and the horrors of war. Goya’s lyrics take aim at the inherent social-pathology of our consumerist lives in the final days of a dying a capitalist system.

Blood is Thicker pairs the heavy metal-inspired works of rocker artist Jason Greig with the darkly sublime works of old masters, including several pieces by Francisco Goya. Creating the effect of a séance across time, with themes of art, music, social criticisms, darkness and chaos, this exhibition provides the perfect backdrop for a live performance in the gallery by Goya.

Join us to hear from curators Chelsea Nichols and Aaron Lister, followed by the live performance by Goya, which will be broadcast live by RadioActive.fm.

Join us to hear from curators Chelsea Nichols and Aaron Lister, followed by the live performance by Goya, which will be broadcast live by RadioActive.fm.

description:
Grace Petrie | POSTPONED. New Date TBC, THIS EVENT IS POSTPONED. NEW DATE TBC

UK protest singer Grace Petrie has become a force on the international folk scene, known for her razor-sharp lyrics, fierce politics and laugh-out-loud wit on stage. Often compared to Billy Bragg, she writes songs that rally, comfort and cut straight to the bone, tackling themes of feminism, queer identity and social justice with passion and bite. 
Since touring New Zealand in 2020 with The Guilty Feminist, Grace has won a loyal following here, drawn to both her firebrand politics and her disarming charm. Her breakout single Black Tie became a queer anthem, streaming over 1.2 million times and drawing praise from MOJO, The Observer and The New Yorker.
Her latest album Build Something Better, produced by Frank Turner, topped the UK folk charts and confirmed what fans already knew: Grace Petrie is one of Britain’s most vital, uncompromising and entertaining songwriters.

Experience the foot-stomping energy of multi-instrumentalist Graeme James as he brings his one-man-band show to the iconic St Peter's Village Hall on the beautiful Kāpiti Coast.

Armed with electric violin, guitar, banjo, bass, piano, baritone ukulele, mandolin, harmonica, and percussion, Graeme builds epic, full-band soundscapes live on stage—layer by layer—creating a loop-driven folk sound bursting with rhythm, melody, and joy.

From his beginnings busking on the streets of Wellington to tours across Europe and North America, Graeme has learned how to turn any room into a shared celebration. Now back in Aotearoa, his music continues to capture the beauty of life’s journeys and the landscapes that inspire them.

description:
Great Sounds Great festival 2026, Eyegum Music Collective presents GREAT SOUNDS GREAT, a multi-venue music and arts festival taking over Pōneke's Te Aro precinct for one night only on Saturday 5 September 2026. Showcasing 40 of Aotearoa's best artists across 10 neighbouring venues, this is one big party you shouldn't miss.
Eyegum has worked hard to curate a programme that is sure to offer something for everyone, from first time gig-goers to seasoned live music obsessives. The eclectic lineup includes national treasures like Bic Runga and Savage, heavy-hitting legends Beastwars, Kody Nielson’s enigmatic project Silicon, indie math rockers So So Modern, powerhouse party starter Mokotron, local hip hop sensation MĀ, and everything in between.
Tonic Collective are back with an impeccably curated lineup for their travelling stage, which includes Pitch Black celebrating 30 years as Aotearoa electronica pioneers and award winning sonic explorer Amamelia.
It's not all music, three of our best poets Chris Tse, Dani Yourukova, and Jackson McCarthy will also perform.
Excitingly for 2026, we are adding a new venue, the incomparable Meow Nui, helping make this year's event bigger and better than ever. We are also throwing a warm-up party, The Night Before, across three venues in Newtown village on Friday 4 September. This will showcase 12 incredible up-and-coming artists and is the perfect way to prepare for the main event.
Ticket holders will receive a wristband that will give them access to each of the participating venues throughout the event. Information on how to pick up wristbands will be provided to ticket holders closer to the time.
Presented with support from Abandoned Brewery, RadioActive.FM, and Wellington City Council.
Venues: Meow Nui, San Fran, Meow, Valhalla, Rogue & Vagabond, Bedlam & Squalor, Hotel Bristol, St Peter's on Willis, Flying Nun Records, Tonic Travelling Stage.

A leading force in the psychedelic techno scene, Greenwolve delivers a powerful sonic journey inspired by cosmic progressions, dark atmospheres, and psychedelic flair into each performance and release.

description:
Greg Crayford's Jazz Night - Twenty Year Anniversary!, Twenty years! Yep, you read that right. This residency has run for two solid decades.
Greg Crayford here. Host and drummer of what’s been billed for some time now as Wellington’s Longest-Running Jazz Residency. And rightly so! Little could we have known when this gig began at The Realm in Hataitai in August 2005 that it’d still be going in 2025. It’s a fantastic achievement. Longer residencies have occurred in our town but nothing currently running holds a candle to that sort of effort by a single artist, at a single venue, in this town (and possibly beyond).
We boast quite the legacy: two Tui-nominated live albums, several bar owners, many managers and staff, hundreds of featured professional musicians and young artists, 500-odd gigs, uncountable numbers of pizzas, beer, whisky, and much laughter and joy. From local music students to top-notch international artists we’ve seen it all.
It’s a huge milestone - 20 years of high quality music played by a massive variety of talented people.
The exciting programme is largely finalised and is pasted below.
Mark the date!
Table bookings 04 974 2207 or info.therealm@nzvenueco.nz or therealm.co.nz and click on ‘book a table’
Great ambience, good company, superb kai and stellar music. What more could a jazz fan want? How about twenty years of quality music?

description:
Greg Crayford's Jazz Night for 20th August - Erna Ferry, Kia ora jazz lover,
This coming week at Wellington’s longest-running jazz residency Greg is thrilled to bring one of Aotearoa’s top vocalists to the stage – the one and only Erna Ferry.
About Erna
Erna, associated primarily with the mighty Rodger Fox Big Band, is a Jazz’n’Blues afficionado from Manawatū.
Erna started her career in amateur musical theatre, discovering, alas, that a thespian she was not - but that she loved to sing! She has performed at all the leading NZ jazz clubs and festivals throughout the country and includes as highlights her ‘tribute to Peggy Lee’ show that toured throughout NZ, and playing support for Al Jarreau and George Benson – not to mention performing at the Monterey Jazz Festival in California with the RFBB.
Erna loves to sing the blues and works regularly with a Whanganui blues band called “Blues Buffet” – and now and then teams up with Wellington vocalist Julie Lamb under the moniker of “Two Bluesy Blondes”.
On a good day she also plays a mean harmonica.
We are SOOOO looking forward to her engagement at The Realm with her ‘A’ team of musicians:
• Oscar Laven (saxophones)
• Duncan Haynes (piano)
• Rory McCartney (bass)
• Greg Crayford (drums and host)
Join us!

description:
Grooverider [UK] tickets, Presented by: Meow Touring
Now at Meow Nui!
Support just announced: DDOG
A foundational figure in the evolution of drum’n’bass, Grooverider is one of the genre’s most respected and influential artists. Emerging from London’s pirate radio and underground party culture in the mid-’80s, his early sets drew from a broad musical palette — funk, soul, hip hop, electro, punk, and early rave — shaping an approach that prioritised musical selection over trends and technique.
Grooverider’s residency at the seminal London club Rage placed him at the centre of a formative period in UK dance music history, where he witnessed — and guided — the transition from acid house and techno into what would become drum’n’bass. During this era, he became known for championing new sounds and supporting emerging artists, playing a key role in defining the genre’s identity and values.
Beyond the club circuit, Grooverider has remained a driving force through his long-standing involvement with Metalheadz, curating line-ups that read like a who’s who of drum’n’bass while continually pushing the music forward. His production work further reflects his wide-ranging influences, blending raw dancefloor energy with funk, experimentation, and musical depth.
Renowned for authoritative, funk-driven DJ sets that balance history with innovation, Grooverider continues to command dancefloors worldwide. This is a rare opportunity to experience one of drum’n’bass’ true originators live at Meow Nui, Wellington.

Guitar Wolf - More Jet - Aotearoa March 2026, Guitar Wolf Rules of Rock and Roll
FIrst ... Band has to have looks
Second ... Fighting spirit
Third ... ACTION!
THere is no fourth or fifth
SIXTH ... Technique
Stir people hearts and your own !!
Tokyo masters of rock&roll mayhem. 30 years young & the foot ain’t ever come off that car crash accelerator pedal. Still swerving, dead man curving, burnin’ out & danger driftin’. Link Wray overdriven guitar rumble fuzz & feedback, Joan Jett warm leatherette aesthetic obsession, locomotive rockabilly rhythms & early Ramones punk chunk thump. Noise, hiss & drone co-opted from fellow Japanese sound assault merchants High Rise & Mainliner. It’s a sonic rendezvous designed to cave in heads & destroy frequencies, while yr dancing yr ass off on that road to oblivion…. Mr Slackjaw
"There are garage-rock bands, and then there’s Tokyo terrors Guitar Wolf... This band’s style of rock’n’roll demands more imposing prefixes, like “jet,” “hurricane,” and “Kawasaki ZII 750.” Much as 1960s British Invasion groups bastardized the blues and sold it back to American teens, Guitar Wolf have spent the past 30(+) years making once-rebellious Stateside sounds—surf, rockabilly, Nuggets, CBGB punk—seem dangerous again, forsaking retro purism for monomania. Your typical garage band might make your ears ring; this one kills zombies." - Pitchfork

Celebrating the 20th Anniversary of If Only You Were Lonely — April 2026

Emo pioneers Hawthorne Heights are set to return to New Zealand in 2026 as part of their global Lonely World Tour, commemorating the 20th anniversary of their influential 2006 album If Only You Were Lonely. The band will perform the album in full, alongside a selection of fan favourites spanning their two-decade career.
Since its release, If Only You Were Lonely has become a defining record of the 2000s emo and post-hardcore movement, featuring anthems such as “Saying Sorry”, “Pens and Needles”, and “This Is Who We Are.” The anniversary tour offers fans the rare chance to experience the album live, in an intimate and high-energy setting.

Hawthorne Heights will play two New Zealand shows only:
Friday 17 April – Auckland | Double Whammy
Saturday 18 April – Wellington | San Fran

Tickets and VIP packages are available now through: waxstartouring.com & hawthorneheights.com

➥ bit.ly/hednon26well
__________________________________________
(HED) P.E. return to shake New Zealand to its very foundations and they are bringing NONPOINT with them
Celebrating the 25th anniversary of their landmark album Broke, the band will deliver a full-throttle set packed with fan favourites like Bartender, Killing Time, and Feel Good; which featured none other than Serj Tankian (System of a Down) and Morgan Lander (Kittie) on the album.
Critics hailed Broke as a “magnum opus of rap, funk, hip hop, and metal” (UnEarthed), while Sputnikmusic praised its “excellent” RATM meets hip-hop genre fusion and raw emotional punch. Whilst RateYourMusic users described the album as “hedonistic, energetic, vulgar, rhythmic, urban, and heavy,” capturing the raw essence of its sound and attitude. With over 450,000 copies sold worldwide, Broke remains a defining moment in the nu-metal era and this tour is your chance to relive it live.
Expect pounding riffs, funk-infused grooves, and the unmistakable flow of frontman Jahred Gomes, whose stage presence turns every show into a riotous celebration of rebellion and rhythm. From their self-titled debut in 1997 to their latest release New and Improved, (HED) P.E. continues to evolve while staying true to their anti-establishment roots.
Debuting in New Zealand for the first time and with an incredible career spanning nearly three decades, Nonpoint has long been a force to be reckoned with in the nu-metal/rap-rock genre. Known for legendary live performances and explosive tracks such as Bullet with a Name, What a Day, Ruthless, and more, the band has consistently captivated audiences with infectious riffs, compelling lyrics, and an uncompromising raw energy. Their discography and stagecraft have made them staples at rock radio and fixtures on festival lineups, earning them a dedicated international following.
This is not nostalgia, it’s a full-blown sonic nu-metal assault. Don’t miss (HED) P.E. and NONPOINT as they rip through Australia with setlists that traverse decades, defy genres, and unleash pure, unfiltered chaos!

description:
Hadestown: Teen Edition, Hadestown: Teen Edition
Kapiti College is excited to present Hadestown: Teen Edition, giving local audiences the opportunity to experience this internationally acclaimed musical live on stage.

Hadestown: Teen Edition blends modern folk and jazz-inspired music with ancient Greek mythology. It follows Orpheus and Eurydice, a young couple trying to make things work in a tough world, alongside Hades and Persephone, who rule over a dark, industrial underworld. When Eurydice is pulled into that world, Orpheus risks everything to bring her back, relying on nothing but his music and his belief in her. It’s a story about love, hope, and the choices we make.

The show is a huge team effort, with around 100 students involved. While many take the stage, others are working behind the scenes on lighting, sound, set design, and stage management. This helps to bring the entire production to life and gives students valuable experience both on and off stage.

Handel's Messiah, Celebrate the festive season with a magnificent performance of Handel’s Messiah on Saturday, 13 December, at 7:30 pm in the Michael Fowler Centre. Presented by Orpheus Choir Wellington in collaboration with Orchestra Wellington, this timeless masterpiece has been a beacon of holiday joy for centuries, blending grandeur, beauty, and drama in equal measure.

Under the direction of Brent Stewart, Music Director of Orpheus Choir Wellington and one of New Zealand’s leading conductors, this performance promises to capture the full brilliance of Handel’s most beloved work. From the exuberance of Worthy is the Lamb to the powerful The Trumpet Shall Sound and the transcendent Hallelujah Chorus, Messiah is a musical journey that inspires and uplifts like no other.

Joining Brent is a stellar lineup of soloists. Emma Pearson, recognised for her captivating performances on international stages, brings brilliance and artistry. Mezzo-soprano Maaike Christie-Beekman adds depth and warmth with her rich, expressive voice. Rising tenor Lila LJ Crichton contributes freshness and flair, while Lexus Song Quest winner Joel Amosa grounds the quartet with his commanding bass.

The Michael Fowler Centre, renowned for its superb acoustics and stunning architecture, provides the perfect setting for this extraordinary concert. With its sweeping choruses, unforgettable arias, and sheer emotional power, Messiah is the ultimate way to mark the festive season.

Come and join us for an evening of musical brilliance that will have you saying, Hallelujah!

Pioneers of the iconic Madchester sound, the 𝐇𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐲 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐲𝐬 are heading back to Australia and New Zealand to celebrate the 35th anniversary of their seminal album, 𝑃𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑠 '𝑛' 𝑇ℎ𝑟𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑠 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝐵𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑦𝑎𝑐ℎ𝑒𝑠.

Fusing funk, rock, psychedelia, and house with the pulsating energy of the UK’s burgeoning rave scene, the 𝐇𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐲 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐲𝐬 became the face of a cultural revolution. Their 1990 release, 𝑃𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑠 '𝑛' 𝑇ℎ𝑟𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑠 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝐵𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑦𝑎𝑐ℎ𝑒𝑠, catapulted them into the mainstream, spending over six months on the UK Albums Chart and earning its place as one of the defining records of the decade.

Fronted by the inimitable 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐮𝐧 𝐑𝐲𝐝𝐞𝐫, with 𝐁𝐞𝐳 ( freaky dancing and percussion), 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤 𝐃𝐚𝐲 (guitar), 𝐆𝐚𝐫𝐲 𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐧 (drums), 𝐌𝐢𝐤𝐞𝐲 𝐒𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐞 (bass) 𝐃𝐚𝐧 𝐁𝐫𝐨𝐚𝐝 (musical director/guitar/keys), and 𝐅𝐢𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐳𝐞𝐡 𝐁𝐞𝐫𝐫𝐲 (backing vocals), the band will perform highlights from the classic album; including anthems like 𝑆𝑡𝑒𝑝 𝑂𝑛, 𝐾𝑖𝑛𝑘𝑦 𝐴𝑓𝑟𝑜, and 𝐿𝑜𝑜𝑠𝑒 𝐹𝑖𝑡, alongside fan favourites such as 24 𝐻𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑃𝑎𝑟𝑡𝑦 𝑃𝑒𝑜𝑝𝑙𝑒, 𝐻𝑎𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑙𝑢𝑗𝑎ℎ, 𝐽𝑢𝑑𝑔𝑒 𝐹𝑢𝑑𝑔𝑒, and 𝑊.𝐹.𝐿.

Their enduring influence on British music was formally recognised in 2016 when they received the prestigious 𝐈𝐯𝐨𝐫 𝐍𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐨 𝐈𝐧𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐀𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐝, a testament to their legacy as one of the UK’s most beloved and groundbreaking bands.

‘Always a great buzz when we play Australia and New Zealand . Looking forward to bringing the Happy Mondays Pills ‘n’ Thrills party there in September’’ - 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐮𝐧 𝐑𝐲𝐝𝐞𝐫

This isn’t just a tour, it’s a full-throttle revival of Madchester chaos, and the year's wildest party is coming.

‘’Funky dancing, maraca shaking, and incredible vocal performances Happy Mondays showed why they were so big in the 90s and have been able to keep that special place in the hearts of the fans for so long.’’ – 𝐌𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐜 𝐍𝐞𝐰𝐬 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐡𝐥𝐲

‘’With Bez and Ryder’s between song banter raising the amusement stakes, the promised Hallelujah was given an airing and its iconic sounds had the crowd bouncing and swaying, it was clear that the Monday’s have lost none of their magic. They are still funky, downright vulgar but so endearing.’’ – 𝐔𝐊 𝐌𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐜 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐢𝐞𝐰𝐬

‘’The show was packed with anthems. Friday night's headline set from the Happy Mondays provided a wonderful dose of nostalgia from one of Manchester's most iconic outfits.’’ – 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐍𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐧 𝐄𝐜𝐡𝐨

description:
Harry Manx (Canada) LIVE at The Little Theatre - Lower Hutt, The “Mysticssippi Blues Man” and one of Canada’s most revered and distinctive musical voices brings his world-renowned live show to New Zealand audiences!
Harry Manx has spent decades carving out a singular musical path. He is known for his extraordinary ability to fuse deep blues grooves with the spiritual depth of Indian classical music. Switching effortlessly between slide guitar, harmonica, banjo, and the remarkable Mohan veena — a 20-stringed instrument taught to him by Indian master Vishwa Mohan Bhatt — Manx creates performances that are immersive, transportive, and deeply human.
“A seamless fit between blues and Indian classical music” - DownBeat Magazine
“Deliciously addictive" - The New York Times
“Canada’s most expressive blues player” - Billboard Magazine
📍 Friday 03 April @ The Little Theatre - Lower Hutt
7pm doors / 7:30pm show
Seated Concert
2 x 45 minute sets with intermission
$59 Early Bird Tickets (very limited)
DON'T miss your chance to see live music at it's finest!

“Watching Harry play tonight I feel like I learned something new …. ”
Bruce Springsteen
Harry Manx is an artist that critics have occasionally had a hard time getting their minds around. His unique amalgam of blues and other American roots music, classical Indian forms, and bits of rock, pop, and folk makes him difficult to pigeonhole, and self-appointed gatekeepers of those traditions sometimes bemoan his lack of purity, stubbornly missing the point. But Manx’s trip is really quite easy to grasp: He’s an accomplished and adventurous lap-slide guitarist – whether playing a National resonator, a solidbody lap-steel, a modified banjo or cigar-box guitar, or his signature 20-string Mohan Veena – and a compelling singer with a rich, warm, and soulful voice who writes intelligent and compassionate songs and puts them over with heartfelt conviction.”
Barry Cleveland, Guitar Player Magazine

There are concerts, and then there are rare musical gatherings that feel quietly profound. Harry Manx creates the latter. This is music that doesn’t rush, doesn’t shout, and doesn’t rely on spectacle — instead, it invites you to listen deeply, feel fully, and leave changed. Audiences don’t just attend a Harry Manx show; they experience it. These nights linger long after the final note fades, becoming the kind of concert people talk about for years. If you value artistry, atmosphere, and the rare magic that happens when a room truly listens, this is a performance you’ll want to be part of.

description:
Harvest Moon: Highways, Heartaches and Harmonies, Wellington Americana band Harvest Moon returns to the Wairarapa Events Centre in August, renewing a relationship with one of New Zealand’s most enthusiastic country music audiences.

The six-piece band has performed in the region on three previous occasions and says Wairarapa audiences have always responded with warmth, enthusiasm and a genuine appreciation for live country and Americana music.

“There has always been a strong country music culture in the Wairarapa,” says band member Wayne Mills. “Every time we’ve played here we’ve been made to feel very welcome, and we’re looking forward to returning.”

Harvest Moon combines guitars, pedal steel, accordion, banjo, dobro and piano with rich vocal harmonies to create an authentic Americana sound inspired by artists including Johnny Cash, Vince Gill, Brad Paisley, Rodney Crowell and The Mavericks.

Fresh from a sell-out show in New Plymouth’s 4th Wall Theatre, and successful recent performances in Whanganui and Feilding, Harvest Moon continues to attract audiences who appreciate outstanding musicianship, memorable songs and an evening of relaxed entertainment.

“Our shows are about more than just the music,” says Mills. “They’re about sharing great songs, having a few laughs and giving people a couple of hours where they can simply enjoy themselves. We know that’s something Wairarapa audiences have always appreciated.”

description:
Helmet 2026 | Wellington, HELMET ANNOUNCE RETURN TO AOTEAROA IN APRIL 2026
"Helmet stripped away the excess, dialled in the precision, and redefined what heaviness could sound like without succumbing to clichés." Pitchfork
NYC Noise Rock Instigators Helmet return to Aotearoa / New Zealand for two shows in April 2026. Playing Wellington’s San Fran on Saturday 11 April, followed by The Powerstation in Auckland on Sunday 12 April. 
Tickets on sale Thursday 2 October 12pm from helmetmusic.com
Helmet has built a reputation as one of the most commanding forces in the underground scene. Born at the dawn of the rage-filled 90’s, Helmet fiercely holds space for multiple generations of alternative fans seeking the vital energy of hostile riffs and inventive metronomic groove. description:
Hiatus Kaiyote tickets, Presented by: Live Nation
Genre-bending future soul visionaries Hiatus Kaiyote return to celebrate their 15th anniversary with an electrifying night of funk, jazz, hip-hop, rock and progressive R&B as only they know how.
Led by singer-guitarist Naomi “Nai Palm” Saalfield, the Melbourne funkateers –featuring bassist Paul Bender, keyboardist Simon Mavin and drummer Perrin Moss –exploded internationally with their 2012 debut Tawk Tomahawk, which drew praise from the likes of Prince, Erykah Badu and Questlove. They landed their first of three Grammy nominations for their Q-Tip collaboration Nakamarra, received their second for their polyrhythmic record Choose Your Weapon (2015), and had their music sampled by no less than Kendrick Lamar, Beyoncé and Drake (with whom Nai Palm also collaborated on 2018’s monster hit Scorpion).
The band’s kaleidoscopic 2021 album Mood Valiant sent them into the national top five and earned them another Grammy nod, while their latest, 2024’s Love Heart Cheat Code, landed them an ARIA nomination for Best Group. Wizards of the shapeshifting live show, Hiatus Kaiyote have built a formidable reputation for their spectacular stage performances – a high-wire mix of musical mastery and thrilling, edge-of-your-seat chaos.

description:
High Dependency Unit with Special Guest W.I.T.C.H - Wellington, After close to a decade away from live stages, the mighty High Dependency Unit return this November announcing their first shows since 2016 including a key festival performance at The Others Way, and an all ages show in Port Chalmers to kick off the tour.
Since their formation in 1993, HDU have carved out a singular space in Aotearoa’s music landscape, fusing and funneling shoegaze and psychedelic noise into hypnotic, sonic power. Their live shows are the stuff of legend, their studio output of essential albums and EPs through the 90s and 2000s have become touchstones for generations of musicians both here and abroad.
The return of Tristan Dingemans, Neil Phillips, and Constantine Karlis to the stage and a rare chance to witness HDU in full flight is nothing short of a seismic event. These November dates will see the band revisit their formidable back catalogue and remind audiences why they’ve long been considered one of New Zealand’s most powerful live acts.
Adding to the magic of the incoming High Dependency Unit NZ tour, HDU’s Wellington Meow Nui show will feature very special guests W.I.T.C.H. on the bill. The legendary 1970s Zamrock pioneers whose psychedelic rock, funk, and African rhythms have made them cult icons around the world, W.I.T.C.H. (We Intend To Cause Havoc) are in the midst of a global renaissance, bringing their irresistible live energy to new generations making this one-off pairing with HDU an utterly unmissable night.

General on sale - Monday 1 September, 10AM

The songwriting is flowing and evolving, new instruments are being acquired, and the band are excited for what might happen next. After a packed out EP launch last year for their EP On A Good Day, they are thrilled to be returning to Wellington Bluegrass Society at Abandoned Petone on Saturday 1st November. Their next dream is to record a full album of their original songs - perhaps on another good day in Wellington!

Hihi and The Stitchbirds are: Elena Saunders - vocals and vibes, Chris Goldsbury - guitar, clarinet and vocals, Tessa Luff - guitar, banjo ukulele and vocals, Matt Hutton - bass ukulele and vocals, and Ellie Stewart - fiddle and vocals.

Two acts will also perform on the night. First is Tessa Luff, who is the main song-writing powerhouse behind Hihi and The Stitchbirds. With natural musicality pulsing through her veins, Tessa experiments with melody and rhythm and brings an ethereal mix of life’s raw highs and lows to her songwriting. Tessa Luff - vocals and guitar, Ellie Stewart - vocals and fiddle, and Elena Saunders - vocals and vibes.

description:
Hobbs & Tucker @ Moon Bar Nov 7th with Miss Leading, Gotal Bournier & Misako Kikuchi (Tokyo), Electronic musician Peter Hobbs presents 'Synthetic Immersionism' with drummer Isaac Levi Tucker at Moon Bar in Newton on Nov 7th. This stunning new visceral audio-visual live show will be preceded by local producer/performer/poet Miss Leading, French Polynesian synth artist Gotal Bournier and Tokyo dancer Misako Kikuchi.
Tickets $18
Earlybirds $15
Students/Beneficiaries $10
Peter Hobbs
Known for his award-winning cinematic and emotional body of work in recordings and immersive art works, Hobbs' new album Panpsychism is a vehicle for his masterful songwriting driven by experimental beats on a highway of synth soundscapes, through an immersive visual-reactive world.
Isaac Levi Tucker
A razor sharp drummer from UK electronic groups Spektrum and Filthy Dukes with monthly residence at Fabric room 1 for the Kill ‘Em All night.. Dj at Sound Architecture London Agency, and locally known for the bands Loungehead, Cuba and Gizmo and Second Child.
Miss Leading
An electronic music producer, singer and poet. Her music aims to widen your mind while moving your body with a mix of pop, hip-hop, spoken ambient and dance tracks with a conscious perspective in relation to race, feminism, sexuality and environment. Her debut album Minor Thing received five-star reviews and gained critical acclaim by independent music magazines across the UK, Brazil, Germany and the USA, including being labelled UK Artist of the Week by The Vinyl District.
Gotal Bournier
Gotal Bournier is a French electronic musician living between Tahiti and Tokyo. Between 2012 and 2017 he released four albums in Japan with the band Lo-shi. Since 2018 he has been based on the island of Raʻiātea, working on solo recordings and various live collaborative projects. His current solo project is a playful and wryly nostalgic live soundtrack to a video collage of Cold War Era science fiction films using the spectral, alien tones of twin modular synthesisers.
Misako Kikuchi
After studying classical ballet at an early age, Tokyo-born dancer Misako Kikuchi went on to explore modern ballet, contemporary dance, street dance and flamenco, while refining her own improvisational approach. Her performances create uncontrived moments of beauty that make you feel that being alive is not irreconcilable with being free

Hogsnort Bulldogs Goodtime Band, Hogsnort Bulldogs Goodtime Band are back with a new show featuring more of their skiffle-pop n’ jug music!

The band, that includes original stars from the sixties and seventies hit bands, Hogsnort Rupert, Bulldogs Allstar Goodtime Band and Dave and the Dynamos, is excited to be back on the Kāpiti coast to perform their energetic and fun-filled show.

Founding members, Dave Luther, Kevin Findlater and Neil Worboys, have collaborated with other great Wellington musicians to develop the “Hogsnort Bulldogs Goodtime Band”. description:
Hudson Freeman, Hudson Freeman is a Brooklyn-based Lofi-folk artist, inspired and forged by the DIY midwest. The 27-year-old Freeman continues to record and perform songs equal-parts resonant, reflective, and poignant. He has quickly emerged as one of indie's most enthralling new voices. His recent full-length, is a Folk Artist, helped solidify his presence as the kind of songwriter unafraid to tackle life's most draining contradictions: modern identity, digital disconnection, and faith.

Born to Evangelical missionaries, Hudson started writing songs upon a radical break at the age of thirteen when his family suddenly moved from the suburbs of Dallas to The Kingdom of Eswatini. The profound influence of indie big-hitters like Sufjan Stevens and Bon Iver as well as college years spent in Springfield, Missouri made a do-it-yourself midwesterner out of Hudson. Now, his new song "If You Know Me" has recently started drawing in attention from the masses, catapulting Freeman into a wider spotlight than ever. It's a moody blend of bedroom pop, folk, slowcore, and post-emo, stitched together by a singular guitar riff and mantra-style lyrics, confirming Hudson's undeniable knack for melody.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
If the Stars would speak & Other stories, If the Stars would speak & Other stories
“If the Stars Would Speak”—a pondering of the starry witnesses above, and the many tales they have silently taken confession of.
Kāpiti local Hannah Goodin, along with her talented jazz ensemble, bring this original musical piece along with a collection of well-loved and thoughtfully reimagined jazz standards and tunes. Nestled amongst them are sparkling poetic tales like “Tell Me” by Rohey. All chosen like one picks out their favourite stories- to share with you in the warmth of the fantastic Raumati Social Club. KOHA entry.

The Hannah Goodin & Friends line up:

Josh Jones (Bass): While supporting on bass for this project, Josh is a jazz and jazz-fusion multi-instrumentalist with a strong reputation as a sideman and studio musician. Known for his skills on saxophone and electric bass, Josh can also be found playing flute, clarinet, double bass, piano, and rhythm guitar. Born and raised in the United States, but currently residing in Wellington, New Zealand, Josh ‘cut his teeth’ playing with jazz ensembles and cover bands all throughout the US, playing bars, hotels, weddings, and festivals of all types. After serving his time aboard Carnival Cruise ships as a stage musician, he began taking on leadership roles in his bands, handling the booking and managing duties. He has a solid reputation in the studio as a performer and composer, with recent sessions and gigs with Defunk’D, the Capital City Big Band, Geoff Culverwell, and Hannah Goodin.

Miles Crayford (Keys): Miles is a talented pianist and musician based on the Kāpiti Coast, with deep roots in Wellington’s vibrant music scene. A graduate of the New Zealand School of Music, Miles has been a regular presence in the capital’s jazz and Latin music circuits since 2007. Growing up in a musical family, he’s developed a rich, diverse sound that spans a variety of genres, though jazz and Latin jazz remain at the heart of his work. Recently expanding his musical horizons, Miles has taken to the Hammond Organ, adding a new layer to his skill set. With years of experience and a passion for pushing musical boundaries, Miles continues to be a prominent figure in New Zealand’s live music scene.

Joanna Devane (Flute): When not in the classroom, Joanna can be seen performing within Orchestral groups. She has played in the Kāpiti Concert Orchestra and in a number of shows with the Ōtaki Players. Joanna will be featuring on a special piece on the night, and her beautiful playing makes the song shine.

Mike Jensen (Drums): Kāpiti based drummer and composer, Mike’s secure and intuitive feel brings so much to the ensemble.

Kathryn Grant (Vocals): Another Kāpiti local, a singer-songwriter in her own right. Kathryn brings her soulful voice on a special piece in the evening. Made all the more special that we get to share the stage as sisters.

Hannah Goodin (Vocals): Originally from further up the Island, Hannah’s now a Kāpiti local who, when not teaching singing, has joined forces with wonderful, talented musicians along the way. Be it performing with a big band, a 9 piece (all hail the glittering Duke Wellington), quintets, or various ensembles of different variations. Featuring at various festivals, musical projects (some her own) and events around the motu.
With a voice that brings warmth to the story, and twists and crafts new paths within the melody, Hannah, along with her ensemble, will bring you a night to remember.

This will be a special gig, for many reasons. We’d love you to be part of it.

description:
Indigenous Voices: A Third Spaces Collective performance, With the ngahere/forest backdrop of Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne, this special performance brings together artists from indigenous and diverse cultural backgrounds to create music grounded in connection, collaboration, and listening.

Third Spaces Collective explores what can emerge when artists share creative space shaped by indigenous values and approaches. Drawing on cultural difference, improvisation, storytelling, and ancestral traditions, the collective creates immersive new music that moves between worlds and traditions while remaining deeply rooted in place and identity.

Audiences can expect an evocative sound journey featuring taonga pūoro, Sámi joik, Brazilian percussion, flute, prepared double bass, and voice. Together, these artists weave contemporary and ancient sound practices into a living conversation about culture, belonging, and collective creativity.

This project is part of the Voice and Justice Third Spaces initiative at the Sibelius Academy, University of the Arts Helsinki, supported by the Erkko Foundation and Paloheimo Foundation.

This event will be held on the Heritage Lawn and is free for all visitors to attend but sanctuary entry fees apply.
Zealandia members get free entry as part of their membership.

POSTPONEMENT:
If the weather is poor this event will be postponed to the same time the next day (Sun 14th). Should poor weather affect both days, the event will sadly be cancelled due to artist travel schedules.

Artist biographies

Hildá Länsman (Sápmi) is an internationally acclaimed Sámi joik singer and songwriter from Utsjoki in northern Finland. Raised within Sámi traditions of reindeer husbandry, duodji, and joik, Hildá combines ancestral vocal practices with contemporary and experimental music. She is known for her uniquely ethereal, shrilling, growling and clear voice and is a proud upholder of the Sámi culture and joik-tradition. Hildá has toured globally with award-winning groups including Solju, VILDÁ, and Gájanas.

Nathan Riki Thomson (Australia / Aotearoa) is a double bassist, multi-instrumentalist, composer, researcher, and Professor of Global Music and Community Engagement, leading the Global Music Programme at the Sibelius Academy in Helsinki. His work spans intercultural collaboration, improvisation, and community arts practice, shaped by decades of performance and teaching across Africa, Europe, Australia, and Aotearoa.

Adriano Itaúna Adewale (Brazil) is a percussionist, composer, educator, and researcher celebrated for his exploratory and deeply collaborative approach to music-making. Blending Brazilian traditions with contemporary improvisation, Adriano is known for his unconventional and exploratory approach to music, and for his ability to create magical soundscapes from the seemingly banal. He has composed for orchestra, theatre, and community projects and collaborated with artists around the world.

Jerome Kavanagh Poutama and Ruiha Turner (Aotearoa) are leading practitioners of taonga pūoro Māori and co-creators of the ORO ATUA, a kaupapa grounded in the healing power of ancestral Māori sound practices. Jerome is a Grammy Award-winning composer and performer whose work has brought taonga pūoro to audiences worldwide. Together, Jerome and Ruiha share deeply immersive performances that balance as taha wahine and taha tane while reconnecting people to whenua, wairua, and sound.

Livia Schweizer (Italy) is a Helsinki-based flutist, improviser, educator, and artistic researcher whose work explores intercultural collaboration through improvisation and experimental notation. Originally from Tuscany, Livia performs internationally across contemporary, experimental, and interdisciplinary music contexts, creating inclusive artistic spaces where diverse voices and traditions can meet.

description:
Into the West: A Choral Journey of Voice, Land and Connection, For its second concert of 2026, Supertonic is thrilled to be joining forces with the renowned Oregon Chorale of Portland for Into the West: A Choral Journey of Voice, Land and Connection. This will be the Supertonic’s first international collaboration with another choir in its twelve-year history. The one-night-only concert, to be presented on Saturday 1 August at St Andrew’s on the Terrace, will see both choirs perform individual sets before joining forces to bring the evening to a memorable close.

Into the West invites audiences on a musical journey celebrating renewal, discovery, and the landscapes—both real and imagined—that shape our sense of home. Drawing inspiration from the Pacific horizon, the programme weaves together New Zealand and Māori folk songs, works by Pacific Northwest composers, global choral favourites, and film-inspired pieces. The result is a concert rich in storytelling and atmosphere, uniting contemporary voices and timeless traditions in a spirit of connection and exploration.

Founded in 1985, the Oregon Chorale is an auditioned community choir based near Portland, Oregon, in the Pacific Northwest of the United States, and is led by Artistic Director Jason Sabino. Guided by its mission to inspire and connect communities through exceptional choral performances and meaningful educational outreach, the Chorale performs a wide range of repertoire, from classical masterworks to contemporary works by living composers.

Supertonic shares Oregon Chorale’s enthusiasm for varied repertoire, striving to push the boundaries of what choral music can be. Since the choir was formed in 2014, it has performed concerts spanning the entire musical spectrum, from Vaughan Williams’ Mass in G Minor, Vivaldi’s Gloria, and Fauré’s Requiem to pop and rock spectaculars celebrating Fleetwood Mac, David Bowie, Elton John, and Queen. For this concert, Supertonic will be directed by Isaac Stone, who is excited to be working with the choir again for the first time since the smash-hit It’s All Coming Back in November 2024.

This promises to be an evening of choral music to remember. Tickets are strictly limited and expected to sell out.

Tickets available from www.supertonic.org.nz from Tuesday 23 June 2026

Irish Musicians for Palestine, Top local Irish musicians play Vogelmorn Upstairs in support of humanitarian aid for Palestine. Get your tickets early for this special night which will sell out.

Featuring Em Griffiths, Paddy McCann, Parcel of Rogues, Pat Higgins and Sláinte, along with special guest Adham and bean an tí Aedeen Boadita-Cormican, there will be some of your favourite Irish songs, along with songs of justice & peace, original music and a poem or two. Saoirse don Phalaistín!

All concert proceeds go to Emily Writes' Aotearoa 2 Gaza Mutual Aid Fund so we've set up ticketing so you can give what you can. Bring a little cash for the raffle! If you can't come to the gig but would like to donate to the Mutual Aid Fund, bank details are Prosean Pictures 06-0574-0906928-00.

Doors open at 6:30pm with a mini market downstairs selling goods and sharing information in support of local Palestine support groups. Entry to the mini market is free.

--------------------------------

The Aotearoa 2 Gaza mutual aid fund was set up last year to directly support families in Gaza. We are a grassroots collective based in Aotearoa standing in unwavering solidarity with Palestinian families in Gaza. Through consistent, direct mutual aid, we send $100 at a time (usually once a week) to families who are living through unimaginable hardship under Israel’s occupation and genocide. These contributions go straight to verified recipients, without intermediaries, ensuring urgent support reaches those who need it most.

Irish Musicians for Palestine is brought to you by Aotearoa Irish for Justice and Peace, a space for those who identify with Muintir na hÉireann, the people of Ireland, and our heritage, grounded in promotion of human rights, justice and peace building. We stand in solidarity with the people of Palestine.

Vogelmorn Upstairs is not a wheelchair accessible building. There is an accessible bathroom in this space. This is an all ages venue but those under the age of 16 must be accompanied by a designated adult after 8pm. The Vogelmorn Precinct is a community space located in a residential area. With that in mind, the team ask that you be kind to others and that when you leave the gig, you do so quietly, to avoid disturbing our neighbours. This gig is seated.

description:
Iron & Wine tickets, Presented by: Handsome Tours
Handsome Tours is proud to present the return of Iron & Wine!
Iron & Wine, the moniker of singer/songwriter and film studies lecturer Sam Beam, returns to Australia for the first time since 2018 – this time as soloist in a captivating run of shows in capital cities and festival appearances, drawing from his transcendent and illuminating folk sounds.
Known for his deeply burnished vocals, keen melodic sensibility, and introspective, free-flowing lyrical point of view, Iron & Wine is one of the preeminent artists and collaborators of the first wave of indie folk. Following his most recent EP release of covers, Making Good Time – a collaboration with Ben Bridwell (Band of Horses), and his 2024 full length album Light Verse, Iron & Wine come to Australia off the back of a huge US tour with award-winning trio I’m With Her and Seattle favourites Band of Horses.
For more than a decade, Iron & Wine has crafted a body of work spanning seven studio albums, numerous EPs and singles, each marked by atmospheric arrangements, poetic storytelling, and Sam Beam’s singular voice. From modest beginnings with The Creek Drank the Cradle, through the rustic beauty of The Shepherd’s Dog, the bold explorations of Kiss Each Other Clean and Ghost on Ghost, to the reflective resonance of Beast Epic and the orchestral sweep of Light Verse, Iron & Wine has earned acclaim for its capacity to move between the hushed and the grand with elegance and emotional clarity.
Iron & Wine will perform solo, playing stripped back music from his expansive catalogue including songs from latest album Light Verse, fan favourites from his collaborations with Calexico and I’m With Her, and the cinematic gems such as the slow dance soundtrack from Twilight.

description:
Jackie Bristow and Barry Saunders @ Wellington Bluegrass Society, Jackie Bristow and Barry Saunders @ Wellington Bluegrass Society
Wow, you're in for a treat with this showcase concert featuring two great singer songwriters who meld perfectly!

Jackie Bristow was brought up in Gore, honed her craft in the pubs and clubs of Sydney, Australia and now lives in Nashville Tennessee, USA. Jackie has released five critically acclaimed studio albums and spent the last few years opening for Chris Isaak, Boz Skaggs, Bonnie Raitt and Tommy Emmanuel, as well as headlining her own shows.

Joined by Barry Saunders, A genuine Kiwi music hero, and singer and principal songwriter for the legendary country band The Warratahs. Barry has also had a parallel solo career spanning six albums, along with collaborations with Sam Hunt and Delaney Davidson.

Jackie's life was turned around in 2020 whilst visiting New Zealand, when the Covid-19 lockdown hit. Unable to return to her home in Nashville, she “made the best of the crazy world” of that time by focusing her creative energy in new directions. A silver lining saw Jackie connecting with Barry Saunders and an amazing friendship and music partnership was made. Jackie and Barry went on to perform shows around New Zealand and releasing their debut single collaboration Good Miles to Go in 2024.

"We're two seasoned songwriters who have teamed up as we love singing together and our voices and songs work so well together.

"We combine our catalogues of songs. We perform as a duo, with two acoustic guitars and two voices, harmonies, harp, including some solo performances and stories.

description:
Jake Baxendale: Trio and Quintet, Jake Baxendale: Trio and Quintet
Two new bands featuring saxophonist and composer, Jake Baxendale:

The trio (with Andy Wright and Isaac Smith) has been working on a vibe for the last 3 years and this will be their first gig!

The quintet will be a happy meeting of awesome musical minds (Ruby Solly, Tom Callwood, Dan Beban & Andy Wright), who will play some of Jake's tunes from a new set called "Sky Meets Country".

As featured in the jazz orchestra composer series, these new compositions utilise tools Jake developed for his Gardening Music ensemble: but where that music takes a granular approach to musical cells, simulating the inward posture of grubbing around in the earth, this new work expands outward to capture the feeling of vastness that open landscapes, bush canopies, and wide, blue skies can inspire.

--

Ruby Solly (Waitaha, Kāi Tahu, Kāti Māmoe) is a musician, taonga pūoro practitioner, and writer living in Pōneke. She has played with musicians such as Yo-yo Ma, Whirimako Black, and Marlon Williams, as well as composed for small group and orchestra such as the Auckland Philharmonia. Ruby is currently working on a book exploring the use of taonga pūoro in hauora, which was the focus of her PhD in Public Health.

https://rubysolly.bandcamp.com/album/p-neke

-

Tom Callwood (double bass) is an improvisor and collaborator who has performed throughout NZ and the UK. He’s a regular in the local experimental and popular music scenes with bands including The Phoenix Foundation, Teeth & Devils Gate Outfit.

-

Andy Wright - Fueled by the Exploration of non verbal shifting time space vector energy zones, Andy is a multidisciplinary visual artist, drummer, keyboardist and regular log on the fire of improv at the Pyramid Club.

-

Daniel Beban is a musician and sound artist who performs on a number of different instruments and builds sound sculptures and invented instruments out of found objects and recycled materials.

-

Isaac Smith is a bassist who also works with electronics. After spending several years in Columbo and Sri Lanka, Isaac is currently based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. Isaac has a strong commitment to improvisation as a vehicle in the pursuit of awareness and balance.


$17.50 presales available via UTR

Special thanks to CNZ for supporting Pyramid Club's programme

description:
James Jin (Violin) and Xing Wang (Piano), The Waikanae Music Society is looking forward to welcoming back the talented Auckland duo James Jin and Xing Wang whose 2025 concert was so popular. With a similar programme format to last year, they will play violin sonatas by Beethoven and Mozart, followed by some charming arrangements of Chinese folk-songs. The most substantial work on the programme will be Grieg’s third Violin Sonata, the best known and most dramatic of the Norwegian composer’s three violin sonatas.

James and Xing are both in high demand as teachers and performers. James is a teaching fellow at the University of Auckland as well as holding leading roles in orchestras throughout the country, both as performer and conductor. Xing, a graduate of the San Francisco Conservatory of Music, is a sought-after collaborative pianist and chamber musician. As a soloist she has appeared with many New Zealand orchestras, and has given numerous solo recitals in New Zealand and overseas.
The concert, in the Waikanae Memorial Hall, will be at 2.30pm on Sunday 7 June. Door sales will be available, or for more information visit www.waikanaemusic.org.nz

Programme:
Beethoven: Sonata for Violin and Piano in D, Opus 12, No 1
Mozart: Sonata for violin and piano in E minor, K304
Guoquan Li: Fisherman's Song
Yuan Mao: Joy of Spring
Grieg: Violin Sonata No 3 in C minor, K304.

description:
James Reyne Wellington New Zealand May 1 Meow Nui, Presented by: The Sound
Everything has a beginning, a middle, and an end. And in February 1986, so it was for Australian Crawl.
It was a wrap. Time to sign off. A swan song, a kiss-off. Sometimes a relief, sometimes a little sad — but always resolute. Put to bed, polished off, and left behind as one of Australia’s most iconic chapters in rock history.
Now, in 2026, we mark The Fall of Crawl — a commemorative run celebrating the music, the memories, and the madness.
The songs you know. The stories you love. A reminder that time really does fly — but the soundtrack stays forever.
We can’t wait to get the band back to NZ !

description:
Jamie Pye Quintet (UK/NZ), Jamie Pye is a London-based jazz guitarist and composer with roots in both Australia and New Zealand. He performs in various line ups and contexts; from intimate duo residencies, to headline performances as a bandleader showcasing his original music. He is often part of house bands for jam sessions around town, or as a sideman on other projects.
In 2023, Jamie completed a 10-date national tour around Aotearoa, including appearances at the Creative Jazz Club in Auckland and Hanover Hall in Dunedin. In between shows, Jamie recorded his debut album ‘Monochrome’, released in November 2024 on Good Twin Records.
As a composer, Jamie draws influence from all music and art forms, paying particular attention to the work of composers and bandleaders Brian Blade, Kendrick Scott, Petros Klampanis and Aaron Parks. Jamie composes music with the intention of honest storytelling and narrative;
creating compositions that are as complex as they are harmonically-rich, while still remaining musically accessible to all ears.
“Guitarist Jamie Pye is establishing himself as a new and dynamic artist coming out of the New Zealand contemporary jazz scene. Displaying a strong compositional voice, he's delivered an exciting debut album and I'm looking forward to seeing his artistry progress into the future”.
-Myele Manzana, Artist, Drummer, Composer
For this Pōneke show, Jamie will be joined by Louisa WIlliamson (Tenor Saxophone), Ayrton Foote (Piano), Seth Boy (Bass) & Hikurangi Schaverien-Kaa (drums)

Jan Boogie Woogie Preston Duo Plays The Shed Lower Hutt, JAN PRESTON is a knockout singer and pianist who has captured audiences around the world.

description:
Jason Bonham's Led Zeppelin Evening New Zealand Tour 2026 | Opera House, Wellington, Jason Bonham's Led Zeppelin Evening New Zealand Tour 2026 | Opera House, Wellington
Jason Bonham’s Led Zeppelin Evening Announces New Zealand as part of the World Tour Celebrating the 50th Anniversary of Physical Graffiti this April 2026

Jason Bonham’s Led Zeppelin Evening/JBLZE is announcing the final dates to Celebrate the 50th Anniversary of the Led Zeppelin classic, Physical Graffiti and what better way to wrap up the World Tour than with dates down under! The landmark tour will let fans experience classics such as “Kashmir” and “The Wanton Song” live alongside deeper cuts like “In The Light” and “Boogie With Stu.” Along with playing the iconic album in its entirety, other Led Zeppelin favourites including “Good Times Bad Times,” “Whole Lotta Love” and of course “Stairway To Heaven” find their way into the setlist.

“For me, this isn’t just an album—it’s the album,” declares Jason Bonham. “Physical Graffiti has always been my ultimate Led Zeppelin record, and I set out to honour its 50th Anniversary with 50 unforgettable shows. That vision now looks more like 80 shows! My last tour of Australia and New Zealand was nothing short of electrifying, and I know the April tour will raise the bar even higher. I’m counting down the days until JBLZE share our final powerful, celebration of Physical Graffiti together.”

Jason prides himself on delivering an authentic Elvis Presley concert experience.

His foster mother introduced him to Elvis gospel records as a young boy, and his appreciation for 'The King' has stuck with him through life.

Jazmine Mary (duo) Hot Sad Summer Tour - WELLINGTON, Jazmine Mary Indie Folk artist is giving us a hot sad summer with a 9 date Duo tour across Aoteroa
“When you step into a
Jazmine Mary gig, be
prepared to be met by either
a clown, a pop star, a pilgrim
farmer, or a nightgown-clad
ghost howling brazenly
onstage. It’s a whimsical
experience that you won’t
want to miss. — VICE
Jazmine Mary is a noir folk artist whose work evokes haunting beauty, poetic grit, and
unflinching vulnerability. They were the 2022 winner of the Auckland Live Best
Independent Debut award for their album The Licking of a Tangerine. Their critically
acclaimed follow-up Dog was named one of Aotearoa’s Top 25 Albums by Rolling
Stone Magazine.
In 2025, Jazmine Mary signed to the iconic Flying Nun Records, marking a new chapter
in their sonic evolution. Their latest album, I Want To Rock And Roll, is raw, transcendent,
and emotionally unguarded. It debuted at #10 on the Oﬃcial NZ Top 20
Jazmine Mary has performed alongside Kurt Vile, Billy Bragg, Hand Habits, and toured
nationwide with Reb Fountain. A standout moment was their show at the Hollywood
Avondale, supported by Julia Deans, praised for its theatrical, spellbinding atmosphere.

description:
Jazz Festival: Alex Keatley's Sounds of the Motherland, An exclusive concert for Wellington Jazz Festival at The Undercurrent.

Double bassist, bandleader and composer Alex Keatley presents Sounds from the Motherland — a vibrant and deeply personal journey into the rich world of South African jazz. Blending the infectious grooves of Cape jazz, the joyous spirit of kwela, and the harmonic sophistication of post-bop, this project pays tribute to the music of Abdullah Ibrahim, Nduduzo Makhathini, Bheki Mseleku, and Winston Mankunku Ngozi while offering bold new compositions inspired by their legacy.

Starting this project while studying his undergraduate degree at the University of Auckland Jazz School, Alex's band consists of friends he has met during his time studying in Auckland and is excited to share with you what they have been working on for the past year. Come along and enjoy the music with us.

Featuring:

- Na'amah Cheiban
- Francesca Parussini
- Jenna Aspeling
- Will Ralph
- Iggy Palmero Epstein
- Ryan Tomov
- Finn McNeill

description:
Jazz Festival: Alex Trask Quartet - Imaginary Folksongs, An exclusive concert for Wellington Jazz Festival at The Undercurrent.
Alex Trask’s ‘Imaginary Folksongs’ blends Earth folk music with a speculative style from an imaginary place. Inspired by bluegrass, Scottish folk music, and jazz performance practice, the tunes have a simplicity in common. Free improvised sections contrast carefully arranged melodies, allowing creativity and structure to coexist. The fiddle-esque melodies and straightforward harmonies create an open and inviting sound that changes depending on the musicians on stage. Performing this music as a group invites each member to paint their private imaginings, creating a unique collective folklore. The quartet will also perform a selection of tunes that inspired the music, including songs by Brian Blade, Gordon Lightfoot, and traditional melodies.

Alex Trask – saxophone
Duncan Haynes – piano
Elijah Mulheron – bass
John Rae – drums

description:
Jazz Festival: Alex Trask Quartet - Imaginary Folksongs, Jazz Festival: Alex Trask Quartet - Imaginary Folksongs
An exclusive concert for Wellington Jazz Festival at The Undercurrent.

Alex Trask’s ‘Imaginary Folksongs’ blends Earth folk music with a speculative style from an imaginary place. Inspired by bluegrass, Scottish folk music, and jazz performance practice, the tunes have a simplicity in common. Free improvised sections contrast carefully arranged melodies, allowing creativity and structure to coexist. The fiddle-esque melodies and straightforward harmonies create an open and inviting sound that changes depending on the musicians on stage. Performing this music as a group invites each member to paint their private imaginings, creating a unique collective folklore. The quartet will also perform a selection of tunes that inspired the music, including songs by Brian Blade, Gordon Lightfoot, and traditional melodies.

Alex Trask – saxophone

Elijah Mulheron – bass
John Rae – drums

description:
Jazz Festival: Daniel Harris Quartet, An exclusive concert for Wellington Jazz Festival at The Undercurrent.

Be prepared for a relaxing evening of traditional jazz music!

Hailing from the (not so) distant city of Christchurch, Daniel and Zachary are joined by locals Ferdinand and Oscar to deliver a wonderful blend of relaxing jazz classics. Featuring quintessential songs from the jazz age, you can rely on a wonderful evening to wash away the worries of the 21st century.

The modern jazz style often incorporates many harsher elements in order to stand out, which can be very engaging. But it often demands attention, and radiates a tense atmosphere. Vintage jazz tends to prioritize an easy listening experience, with lyrical melodies and traditional music harmony.

Settle into a chair, take a sip of wine, and let the smooth harmonies flow over you!

Featuring:

Piano: Daniel Harris
Trombone: Ferdinand Hitchings-Anstice
Bass: Zachary Chyr
Drums: Oscar Garvie

description:
Jazz Festival: Free Status, An exclusive concert for Wellington Jazz Festival at The Undercurrent.

Free Status is a jazz fusion band, drawing melodic inspiration from iconic artists like Herbie Hancock and 70s jazz/funk legends with electronic flair inspired by artists like Moby.

At the heart of Free Status is Tommy David on keys, an accomplished musician/composer in the early stages of his career. He has earned recognition in numerous jazz competitions and supported legendary rock acts such as Dire Straits Legacy Band, Nazareth, Hello Sailor, and plays with popular rockabilly band, Recliner Rockers. With composition at the center of his artistry, he can't wait to share the exciting and genuine compositions he has created.

The rhythm section features Behzad Karakia (drums) and Tyler Diprose (bass), both veterans of performances with many of New Zealand's jazz greats.

On lead alto sax is James Dawes, recently selected for an international touring band on a year-long cruise. His versatility extends well beyond jazz.

On keys is Sam Voyle, whose primary instrument is tenor saxophone. Performing with Tommy since their school days, he has built a strong musical bond that has led to major appearances, including the America's Cup main stage and high-profile corporate events.

On vocals is Melody Lui-Webster, an award-winning singer and accomplished musical theatre performer and actor, with numerous professional stage and television roles.

Thank you for watching!

Jazz Festival: Miro Holland's Ordinance Group, An exclusive concert for Wellington Jazz Festival at The Undercurrent.

After a successful July undercurrent debut, Miro Holland returns -bringing with him stand up locals; Isaac Randel, Evie Patterson, Ateo and Nico Buhne- all brimming with talent. The recent cold months enraging Miro's spirit, he has returned to the light to present his new thinking. The ordinance is about stopping the nullifying wishwash, and getting everyone back to listening to each other! We will swing, dance, we will blow that's sure. There is a tendency for fiction in art that goes often ignored here, but not today! It will be bold and hopefully we will all (you included) be talking to each other, before, after, and during the gig. I think everyone in the band has lots to say and it would be a bummer if you missed out. Come!

Musicians: Miro Holland, Evie Patterson, Ateo Buhne, Nico Buhne and Isaac Randel.

description:
Jazz Festival: The Enigma, An exclusive concert for Wellington Jazz Festival at The Undercurrent.

Get ready for a sonic journey like no other as The Enigma takes the stage at this year’s Jazz Festival! This electrifying organ jazz trio is known for their thrilling original compositions and high-octane performances that keep audiences on the edge of their seats. Featuring Miles Crayford on the mighty Hammond organ, Mike Jensen driving the rhythm on drums, and Aleister Campbell weaving masterful guitar lines, The Enigma delivers a sound that’s both deeply rooted in jazz tradition and fearlessly experimental.

Expect the unexpected—this trio thrives on spontaneity, with compositions that twist, turn, and evolve in real time. Each performance is a living, breathing moment of musical exploration, bursting with energy, groove, and emotional depth. Whether it’s a deep-pocket groove or an explosive burst of improvisation, The Enigma creates music that’s alive with tension, playfulness, and dynamic contrast.

Don’t miss your chance to witness one of the most captivating acts on the scene. The Enigma isn't just a band—it's an experience. Catch them live and be a part of the mystery.

Featuring: Miles Crayford - Organ, Aleister Campbell - Guitar, Mike Jensen - Drums.

Led by Auckland saxophonist, Iggy Nama Ruci, the Iggy Nama Ruci quartet features a powerful interplay of musical conversation through the medium of straight-ahead jazz.

After recently touring around India and South Africa, surrounded by a plethora of Gospel jazz musicians, Iggy brings a fresh perspective and an open playfulness to the bandstand.

Michael Nash, fine-tuned Auckland pianist, draws inspiration from the likes of Brad Meldhau and Keith Jarrett, providing versatile and expressive approach to improvisation.

On double bass, Tyler Diprose acts as a grounding force, laying down a foundation, while providing rich musical intuition and connection in conversation with the band.

Max Crook brings a fiery finesse controlled by creativity and elegance to the drums. His attention to listening and reacting to the band demands constant interactive conversation.

description:
Jazz Orchestra Composer Series Presents Callum Allardice, The eleventh concert in our series of Aotearoa jazz composers features award winning composer and performer Callum Allardice, with a new suite of music for rhythm section and strings; Ode to Sadness.

A collection of songs, old and new, presented alongside some of the works that inspired them. From intimate improvisations and poignant melodies to soaring strings, the music moves through moments of reverence, reflection, and quiet triumph. Sometimes solemn, sometimes radiant, but always beautiful, Ode To Sadness is a celebration of the beauty found in sorrow.

Callum is an award-winning composer and guitarist based in New Zealand. He is a three-time recipient of the APRA Best Jazz Composition award for his works ‘Sons of Thunder’ (2016), ‘Deep Thought’ (2017), and ‘Chungin’ (2019). In 2020 he and his group The Jac, received the Recorded Music NZ Best Jazz Artist award for their album ‘A Gathering’, and in 2022 he was the inaugural Te Kōkī - New Zealand School of Music jazz composer-in-residence.

The Jazz Orchestra Composer Series showcases original music for large jazz ensemble by New Zealand composers. Concerts take place every 1st and 3rd Friday of the month, from May to October, from 7pm. Tickets are $15, door sales $20.

Thanks to Creative New Zealand for their generous support.

description:
Jazz Orchestra Composer Series Presents Louisa Williamson, The ninth concert in this series of Aotearoa composers features the multi-talented saxophonist/composer Louisa Williamson.

Since completing a Masters of Music in Composition in 2020, she has released two albums of original music (What Dreams May Come and Groundwork). In 2023 Louisa won the APRA Best Jazz Composition Award for her piece Dream Within A Dream, and in 2024 Louisa received a composition commission from the Wellington Jazz Festival and headlined the festival with the new work, The Chasm Where We Fall Into Each Other.  Louisa has worked with L.A.B, Bret McKenzie, AJA, The Rodger Fox Big Band, Royal NZ Air Force Band, Trinity Roots and Lord Echo.

"This commission opportunity has come at a perfect time for me to process some recent grief and pain that’s inhabited my circles. Whilst composing this music, I’ve thought about ideas around mental health, specifically with youth in Aotearoa, and also honouring some friends who have passed. I think artists have the ability to turn heartbreak into beauty, and this music is an attempt at that. Although the inspiration which generated the music is heavy, the performance itself will hopefully feel light and reflective (turning heartbreak into beauty = darkness into light!), and will embrace and celebrate the talents of the musicians who are playing. I’ve brought together a beautiful group of people who I know will handle this music with care and fortitude"

description:
Jazz in Martinborough 2025, Big Band Brings Back the Swing
Jazz in Martinborough 2025

Jazz in Martinborough is thrilled to be bringing you the Royal New Zealand Airforce Jazz Orchestra as our feature act on Saturday at the festival for 2025.

“We’re delighted to be able to fill the stage with a full-sized big band of fabulous musicians, and the Town Hall with the fantastic sounds of the big band era,” says Jazz in Martinborough Music Director Lee Quayle.

Jazz in Martinborough is back for their 13th edition during the first weekend in September with ticketed shows on Friday 5th and Saturday 6th and other gigs around town as usual. “The RNZAF Jazz Orchestra will be one of our ticketed gigs, featuring on the Saturday evening,” says Lee. “And on Friday night we invite you to Be Transported back in time to a speak easy club with the superb swing and blues combo that is April’s Fools,” adds Lee.

Staying true to the tradition of swing and improvisation the RNZAF Jazz Orchestra draws on their own rich history dating back to the original ‘swing era’. The Orchestra is a national trailblazer in big band history and features New Zealand compositions, and a classic repertoire from the golden era of big band swing jazz of Ellington and Basie.

The band benefits from a depth of talent that most military bands around the world would only dream of and is made up of Wellington’s most exceptional musicians.

“The line-up will be a who’s who of the Wellington jazz scene,” says Lee. “It’s a while since we had a big band at the festival, so we’re elated to have the Airforce Jazz Orchestra back with us again. They last played at the festival in 2014. Many of the band members have been here since, but not as part of a big band,” says Lee.

Be Transported by April’s Fools
Imagine stepping back in time to a speak easy club. A smoky, dimly lit room where the anticipation is electric but the vibe is laid-back and relaxed. . .

From the stage a jazz swing and blues band begins to play, their instruments blending seamlessly in a harmonious symphony of sound. The rhythm section, with its upright bass and snare drums, lays down a groove that's impossible to resist, while the saxophone punctuates the air with soulful notes.

At. the forefront stands a captivating female singer, her voice rich and velvety, weaving tales of heartache, joy, and everything in between. Her vocal prowess brings both swing and blues to life, effortlessly moving from sultry, slow blues ballads to energetic, foot-tapping swing numbers.

This band doesn't just play music; they create an experience that transports the audience to another era, where the essence of jazz and blues reigns supreme.

Welcome to an evening of superb swing jazz and blues brought to you by the band that is April’s Fools. “We’re absolutely wrapt to be bringing this ultra-talented and experienced combo to the festival,” says Music Director Lee Quayle. “Whenever, and wherever this group of musicians have played reviewers have to search the thesaurus for new superlatives to describe the show, and audiences leave reluctantly, but happy.”

April’s Fools are April Phillips (vocals), Greg Crayford (drums), Zak Dikvert (guitar), Nicholas Bauke-Maunsell (saxophone), Miles Crayford (keyboards) and RoryMacartney (bass). They will be playing at Jazz in Martinborough on Friday 5 September 2025 as the opening of the ticketed festival gigs to be held in the Town Hall.

description:
Jet tickets, Presented by: Live Nation
Originally hailing from Dingley in Melbourne, Jet quickly conquered the world after forming in 2001, selling more than 6.5 million albums globally and securing almost 10 x Platinum certification in Australia and Platinum in the USA and UK for their 2003 debut album “Get Born”. The album produced a string of classic singles in “Are You Gonna Be My Girl”, “Rollover DJ”, and “Look What You've Done” and netted the band 6 x 2004 ARIA awards. Both “Are You Gonna Be My Girl” and “Cold Hard Bitch” peaked at number 1 on the US Modern Rock singles charts and propelled the band to the top of festival bills and charts around the world.

Jet’s follow up album “Shine On” followed in 2006 and was rammed full of another collection of melodic rockers including, “Put Your Money Where Your Mouth Is”, “Bring It On Back” and “Rip It Up”, and achieved platinum status in Australia on the back of stand-out headline shows around the world, and an unforgettable Big Day Out run in 2007.

In 2023, JET celebrated the 20th anniversary of Get Born by returning to the stage after a five-year hiatus, performing the album in full and reminding the world why their songs still pack the same punch two decades on. Reflecting on that era, Nic Cester said, “Get Born was a rare and unique moment of total planetary alignment where we somehow managed to capture lightning in a bottle.”

Their enduring legacy was officially recognised in November 2023, when they were inducted into the ARIA Hall of Fame.

This February see Jet live – raw, loud, and full of the spirit that made them international rock legends.

description:
John Maus NZ Tour 2026 | WELLINGTON, BANISHED MUSIC & STRANGE NEWS PRESENT
JOHN MAUS ~ NEW ZEALAND TOUR 2026
WEDNESDAY 6 MAY - MEOW, WELLINGTON
with CROSSING WATER
THURSDAY 7 MAY - DOUBLE WHAMMY, AUCKLAND
with POWER NAP
Tickets from Banished Music
The musical career of John Maus has been riddled with iconic moments. Now, to celebrate the release of his brand new album Later Than You Think, the synth-tastic American songwriter with the unmistakable baritone is headed to New Zealand for two extraordinary shows next May. Brought to you by Banished Music and Strange News, Mr Maus is set to make good on a long-held promise.
In 2019, after a series of personal tragedies and the stresses of touring his high-intensity show left Maus feeling unable to perform here, he flew home urgently to recover, with shows here cancelled at short notice. Now, with five years of contemplation, retreat and recuperation, and time spent crafting his new record, John Maus is set to make his return.
Throughout his long career, Maus considered himself to have been “constantly fighting the status quo: the Mickey Mouse Club, Coca-Cola, and all the institutions that reduce culture to its lowest common denominator”. Then, in 2020, he was infamously photographed at the January 6 riots, and was himself promptly “cancelled”.
In hindsight, he says, he now knows he should have been a lot clearer about his ethos and political beliefs in the wake of it all. “I thought my legacy would speak for itself,” Maus told Stereogum in a recent interview. Stating he was only at the protest to shoot footage for a new documentary film alongside film-maker Alex Moyer, these days he realises he ought to have stated his position a lot more bluntly. “I should have been clearer that I’m absolutely against Trumpism,” he says. “It wasn’t as forthright a denunciation as it should have been.”
Powered by “genuine emotion and radical sincerity”, the new album includes I Hate Antichrist, a song Maus describes as a sort of sequel to Cop Killer, and features a secular Gregorian chant that embraces French philosopher Alain Badiou’s anti-xenophobic sentiment that “All the people who are here are from here”.
From the death of ego and descent into madness, this is a party we’re all invited to.
label: Music & Concerts

Jonathan Crayford [solo] - Wellington Jazz Festival, Experience an intimate evening of solo jazz piano with internationally acclaimed New Zealand pianist Jonathan Crayford.
Returning home from performances across Europe, Crayford will take to his stunning Steinway D Concert Grand at Meow NUI on Thursday 16 October, weaving an eclectic mix of original compositions and inspired improvisations. Known for his expressive artistry and fearless creativity, Crayford draws on a lifetime of musical exploration across New York, Cuba, Brazil, and beyond. This promises to be a rare chance to hear one of Aotearoa’s finest jazz talents in a powerful and personal setting.
Jonathan Crayford is one of Aotearoa New Zealand’s most acclaimed pianists, composers, and improvisers, with an international career spanning New York, Cuba, Brazil, and Europe. A highly original musical voice, he is celebrated for his adventurous compositions, stunning improvisation, and versatility across jazz, funk, Latin, and classical traditions.
Crayford has written numerous film scores and albums, collaborating with world-renowned artists including Kurt Rosenwinkel, David Binney, Amp Fiddler, Groove Collective, David Murray, Tony Allen, Questlove, Macy Gray, and in Cuba with Bobby Carcassés. His trio album Dark Light (2014) was nominated for Best New Zealand Jazz Album, while its follow-up East West Moon (2016) won the award outright. His film and theatre scores have also earned critical acclaim, awards, and multiple nominations.
Respected both at home and abroad, Crayford has been described by Jazz Times as “exploratory, thoughtful, soulful, focused,” while Jazz Local 32 hails him as “the embodiment of sonic shapes and forms.” Pianist Mike Nock calls him “one of the very finest creative musical talents to have ever come from Aotearoa

KATELYN HENSHALL WITH EXTRA BUTTER AND MAMALOUDER, Katelyn Henshall fuses pop, R&B, and soul into something uniquely her own. Well suited for a whiskey lounge- with a voice described as smoky and rich, like a chocolate stout, that quickly has you craving more.
This December, Katelyn is beyond excited to play alongside a full band, joined by Dónal Gunning, Angus Webb, and Oliver Dudziak. After their debut as headliner in October they are looking forward to getting back up on stage. Stay tuned to hear reimaginings of her singles “Incandescent” and “You’d Be The One (Now I Know It Too)”, in addition to her other originals.
Support by Extra Butter and MamaLouder.
The butter baby was born when three mates teamed up with two beautiful strangers for a jam. Since their 2020 debut, Te Whanganui-a-tara based indie rock/alternative band Extra Butter have evolved into a six piece ear treat consisting of vocals, saxophone, guitar, bass, keys and drums. The soundscape of Extra Butter provides sonic illustrations for a variety of scenarios from cicada season hangs in the backyard and sultry smoke filled speakeasies to gravel pits under peak heat and swamps with both treasures and tricks waiting to be found. The band’s debut EP, Zephyr, released last year, offered the repertoire of the band’s formative years. Their next releases are to be expected in the coming season, offering a smorgasbord of sounds. Drawing on the paradoxical complexities of relationships and the human condition, Extra Butter is an ever evolving unit of introspection as sound and performance.
Mamalouder! Wellington based band of Latin flair and Kiwi soul. This 5-piece band brings you soulful original blues rock, born from the cultural melting pot of Latin America and Aotearoa. Get ready for stirring guitar riffs and soulful vocals that'll move you! Kia ora, vamos a rockear!
