description:
Michaela Tempers & Greta O'Leary (solo) play a Cozy Show at Vogelmorn, Greta O’Leary and Michaela Tempers are banding together for a double bill on Saturday 13 June at Vogelmorn Upstairs. Join Greta and Michaela for a cosy evening of indie-folk music as they celebrate their recent releases, River Dark and Good Woman.
Greta O’Leary
Tāmaki Makaurau songsmith Greta O’Leary writes with a surreal clarity of vision, the line between art and artist, self and image - is razor thin. Raised on rolling hills in northern New Zealand, and coming of age anywhere but here, O’Leary is a writer with her own lens and language. Her breakthrough debut album ‘River Dark’ was released in 2025, landing at #9 on the Aotearoa Album Charts, it received heavy support from RNZ, Rolling Stone AU/NZ, PBS FM, the SRN and toured ten dates through Aotearoa and Victoria.
Michaela Tempers
Michaela Tempers is a writer and musician based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara, Aotearoa. While studying for her master’s in Creative Writing, she began writing a new collection of songs exploring the complexities of womanhood. These songs formed the basis for her debut EP, Good Woman, and feature mediaeval heroines, love, anxiety and death. The record’s six tracks are rich with incisive detail, performed with sincerity and wit.

description:
Moksha - 5 Year Anniversary, TEAM MOKSHA PRESENTS

MOKSHA -5 Year Anniversary Gathering
08 AUGUST 2026 | VALHALLA, WELLINGTON

Five years.

Honestly, it's hard to believe.

What started as a small dream between a few friends has grown into something far bigger than we ever imagined.

Over the last five years, we've shared dancefloors, sunsets, sunrises, laughter, hugs, friendships, and countless unforgettable moments together. We've watched strangers become friends, friends become family, and a community grow around a shared love for music, connection, and freedom.

Our recent gathering, AARANYA , reminded us once again how special this community truly is. Seeing so many beautiful souls come together, dancing under the open sky, sharing smiles and creating memories, filled our hearts with gratitude.

To every artist who has played our stages.
To every volunteer who has helped behind the scenes.
To every person who bought a ticket, shared a post, invited a friend, or danced with us until sunrise...

THANK YOU !

Team Moksha wouldn't exist without you.

As we step into our fifth year, we wanted to celebrate this milestone together.

On Saturday, 08 August, we return to Valhalla Wellington for a special anniversary gathering.

No egos.
No expectations.

Just good music, good people, and the energy that happens when our community comes together as one.

Expect a carefully curated journey through sound, immersive visuals, and the unmistakable atmosphere that has always made Moksha feel like home.

Whether you've been with us since day one or you're about to join us for your very first event, this night is for you.

Let's celebrate five years of music, friendship, growth, and community.

And let's create a few more memories together.

We can't wait to see your faces on the dancefloor again.

With love,

Team Moksha

Five years later, the music still calls us together.
Welcome home.

description:
Monthly Jazz Night: Les Tripes- Parisian Swing Trio, Get ready for a night of irresistible rhythm and sizzling jazz!

Swing clarinetist Oscar Lavën, guitarist Adrian Jensen, and double-bass raconteur Robert Henderson are "Les Tripes" (french for "The Guts") ; a hard-working interpretation of the irresistibly heart-pumping film-noir sound of Django Reinhardt's Quintette du Hot Club de France. Lavën, Jensen and Henderson are professional musicians based in Wellington, and have honed their project through years of performance in venues large and small.

Les Tripes will have you tapping your feet and swinging along as they infuse each performance with passion, precision, and a touch of French flair.

Moon Goose + National Sensation at MOON, Local Wellington darlings NATIONAL SENSATION are joining forces with folk-duo Moon Goose, for a Sunday special at MOON on November 30th. With a view to celebrate their recent friendship, which includes an unlikely combination of kiwiana-indie-folk-celtic-rock-alternative-pop music and a shared love for mullets and bowl-cuts, these strangely adorable creatures will blow your socks off.
Kicking off the evening are alt-folk artists Moon Goose who recently released their debut EP ‘On the island where our shadows lie’, showcasing their dark-yet-bright blend of Celtic-inspired folk music. Their songs include both traditional folk songs from the British Isles and original compositions that celebrate nature, friendship, and the magic of storytelling. With intricate harmonies, deep folk-scapes, glittering guitar and fiddle riffs, Moon Goose will move you deep and good.
Unique creatures of growing renown, NATIONAL SENSATION have been compared to Kate Bush, Bjork, Devendra Banhart, Jefferson Airplane, The Phoenix Foundation, Florence and the Machine, London Grammar, The Topp Twins and various other bands that they are trying really hard to rip off without infringing on copyright. You’ll get bloody good bangers, ballads, banter and more as they sing about the serious stuff, like calling Aotearoa home, your Mum, the bush, death in a funny way, death in a sad way and your local Residents Association. They haven’t peaked yet so see them before they’re washed up.

Danica Bryant is a force to be reckoned with. A pop-folk singer-songwriter with a gritty rock-edge, her music tackles provocative themes from celebrity culture to neurodiversity through an unabashedly queer feminist lens.

Her “playful indie pop” (Rolling Stone) has seen her open for legends like Elton John and Robbie Williams, hit #2 on the NZ Hot Singles Chart with her 2024 release ‘Acid’, and undergo mentorship with Kiwi icon Bic Runga. Bryant has undergone multiple successful New Zealand tours and played festivals including Gardens Magic, Outfield and Cuba Dupa.

With her debut album 'Feast' out this August, Bryant is “venomous yet passionate” (Ambient Light), “cynical but emotional” (NZ Musician), and an unapologetically fresh voice on the pop music scene.

The Weather Machine brings an electrifying blend of soulful longing, theatrical glam, and retro-nostalgic indie rock to the stage. Their live shows are dynamic and heartfelt, weaving together lush arrangements, unexpected instrumentation, and soaring vocal performances. With violin, sax, clarinet, and layered harmonies in the mix, audiences can expect a genre-blurring experience that feels both intimate and cinematic. Whether it’s a delicate folk tune or a full-throttle rock anthem, The Weather Machine delivers each moment with passion, precision, and a deep love for musical storytelling.

The Weather Machine began as the brainchild of Portland, Oregon songwriter Slater Smith. What started as a DIY indie-folk project in the city’s vibrant underground scene has since evolved into a professional, internationally touring band. Over the years, they’ve shared stages with acts like The Lumineers, Alabama Shakes, and Cold War Kids. In 2021, Smith relocated to Te Whanganui-a-Tara, Aotearoa, bringing the project with him and forming a new Wellington-based lineup. Now spanning two continents, The Weather Machine continues to expand its sound with a fresh, collaborative spirit.

This will be their first time headlining at San Fran and their first performance there in more than 6 years - when they opened for The Paper Kites in 2019. It is sure to be a full circle moment.

Mountain Goats | Meow Nui, Wellington - VENUE UPGRADED!, Mountain Goats | Meow Nui, Wellington - VENUE UPGRADED!
UPGRADED TO MEOW NUI DUE TO OVERWHELMING DEMAND

Handsome Tours are proud to present The Mountain Goats!

Veteran indie-rock storytellers The Mountain Goats will make their long-awaited return to Australia and New Zealand in April 2026, with performances in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide, Perth, Auckland and Wellington. This eagerly-anticipated tour represents the band's first visit to Australia in 9 years (2017) and their first trip to New Zealand in 16 years (2010).

Fronted by prolific songwriter and novelist John Darnielle, The Mountain Goats are revered the world over for their sprawling catalogue of twenty-three studio albums released between 1994 and 2023. This tour announcement coincides with the band today unveiling album number twenty-four, 'Through This Fire Across From Peter Balkan' - to be released 7th November 2025 on Cadmean Dawn Records (the band’s own label).

Produced by the Mountain Goats’ multi-instrumentalist Matt Douglas, Through This Fire Across From Peter Balkan is a full-on musical that stands as the most conceptually detailed and musically elaborate project in the band’s ever-expanding catalogue. It features appearances from The Replacements’ Tommy Stinson, harpist Mikaela Davis, musical theatre royalty Lin-Manuel Miranda (Tony Award-winning ‘Hamilton’, Disney’s ‘Moana’ & ‘Encanto’), and the band’s new bassist Cameron Ralston.

Don’t miss one of indie rock’s most enduring and beloved bands as they make their long-overdue return to our shores!

description:
Mozart Requiem and Christopher Tin’s To Shiver the Sky, From the earliest dreams of flight to one of the greatest choral masterpieces ever written — Wellington is in for a treat in April. Wellington’s Orpheus Choir joins forces with Orchestra Wellington to present a mighty programme. Mozart Requiem and Christopher Tin’s To Shiver the Sky explores five centuries of human imagination and purpose.
Mozart’s Requiem stands as one of the greatest choral works ever composed. Written in the final months of his life, it sets the words to the Catholic requiem mass with blazing dramatic power. The oratorio has a depth of feeling that has captivated audiences for more than two centuries. To Shiver the Sky is an epic choral spectacular from Grammy-winning composer Christopher Tin. It draws on texts from da Vinci, Hildegard von Bingen, Ovid, Jules Verne, Amelia Earhart and John F. Kennedy. The work builds a sweeping musical history of human flight from imagined wings to the Moon landing. Orchestra and choir conductor Brent Stewart will also lead four soloists through the concert. They include soprano Emma Pearson, alto Charlotte Secker, tenor Ridge Ponini, and bass Robert Tucker.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Mozart Requiem, Mozart Requiem
Experience two masterpieces in one exceptional concert as Orpheus Choir Wellington present Christopher Tin’s To Shiver the Sky alongside Mozart’s Requiem. This concert spans five centuries of imagination and purpose, from the earliest dreams of flight to one of the greatest choral masterpieces ever written.

To Shiver the Sky is an epic choral spectacular from Grammy winning composer Christopher Tin. Drawing on texts from da Vinci, Hildegard von Bingen, Ovid, Jules Verne, Amelia Earhart and John F. Kennedy, it builds a sweeping musical history of human flight from imagined wings to the Moon landing. Born from a record breaking Kickstarter campaign, the work opens with Sogno di Volare, known worldwide as the main theme of Civilization VI, one of the most celebrated strategy games of the decade. Its sound world spans luminous stillness and immense choral climaxes, evoking the exhilaration and peril of human flight.

Mozart’s Requiem stands as one of the greatest choral works ever composed. Written in the final months of his life, it sets the sacred Requiem Mass with blazing dramatic power and a depth of feeling that has captivated audiences for more than two centuries. From the fierce energy of the Dies Irae to the aching beauty of the Lacrimosa, the music moves with a haunting power that remains unmatched in the choral repertoire.

Together these works form an extraordinary musical journey. One celebrates the daring that pushes humanity forward. The other reveals the full dramatic power of the Requiem tradition at its most intense and expressive. Performed by the mighty Orpheus Choir Wellington with Orchestra Wellington, conducted by Brent Stewart and featuring celebrated soprano Emma Pearson, Charlotte Secker alto, Ridge Ponini tenor, and Robert Tucker bass, this is a night of immense musical colour and emotional impact.

description:
Mudhoney tickets, DUE TO OVERWHELMING DEMAND, MUDHONEY HAS UPGRADED VENUES TO MEOW NUI.
For the first time in over a decade, Mudhoney return to New Zealand for a run of intimate shows. Renowned for their ferocious live performances, the band continue to deliver the same high-voltage mix of sludgy riffs, pounding rhythms and Mark Arm's unmistakable snarl that made them one of the most influential rock bands of their era.
Formed in Seattle in 1988, Mudhoney helped define the sound that would become known as grunge, combining garage rock, punk and heavy distortion into something raw, loud and entirely their own. As one of the cornerstone acts of legendary independent label Sub Pop, the band became a crucial influence on the explosion of alternative rock that followed, with tracks like 'Touch Me I'm Sick' and 'Suck You Dry' remaining enduring underground classics.
More than 35 years on, Mudhoney remain as vital as ever, continuing to release acclaimed new music and proving night after night why they are regarded as one of the greatest live rock bands of their generation.
"When it comes to grunge, or even just Seattle, I think there was one band that made the definitive music of the time. It wasn't us or Nirvana, but Mudhoney. Nirvana delivered it to the world, but Mudhoney were the band of that time and sound." – Eddie Vedder (Pearl Jam)
A rare chance to experience genuine grunge royalty up close.

description:
Muroki - Amber Skies Tour, Muroki, one of Aotearoa’s most distinctive young voices, returns from Berlin with his debut album Amber Skies, written and recorded as he lived a nomadic lifestyle moving between Berlin’s creative underground, the hills of Raglan, the coastline of Portugal and a long overdue reunion with whānau in Kenya.

Amber Skies is released on 30 January 2026, followed by Muroki’s first national tour in three years, running from 6 February to 28 March. He will also make a solo appearance at Te Ahurei Toi o Tāmaki Auckland Arts Festival, where he joins He Manu Tīoriori, a celebration of waiata reo Māori, on Saturday 21 March.

At the centre of Amber Skies is Muroki’s drive for freedom and new experiences. He believes music only really happens when he is fully living, pushing into new environments, meeting people and adding what he calls seasoning to life.

The album was written and recorded between Aotearoa and Berlin, with production by Djeisan Suskov, Justyn Pilbrow and Josh Fountain, and featuring Len Blake and keyboard virtuoso Joe Kaptein.

Muroki is immersed in the Berlin scene, regularly jamming with musicians including members of Parcels, Rikas and the Zen Men, finding grounding in a city that can be both electric and mellow. He filmed the video for latest single Break It Down in Portugal with director Ezra Simons (Earth Tongue), shot entirely on 16mm film in Peniche and Nazaré, and also returned to Kenya for the first time since he was sixteen, reconnecting with whānau and gaining perspective during this chapter.

“I’ve been bouncing between places while working on this album. Living nomadically keeps me open and curious. Nothing beats coming back to Aotearoa, and I can’t wait to play these songs live with the band.”

With platinum success on Wavy, the Triple J topping Love Cocoon with BENEE and collaborations with LEISURE, Young Franco and NASAYA, Muroki returns home ready to take these songs to the stage.

The album was written and recorded between Aotearoa and Berlin, with production by Djeisan Suskov, Justyn Pilbrow and Josh Fountain, and featuring Len Blake and keyboard virtuoso Joe Kaptein. 
Muroki is immersed in the Berlin scene, regularly jamming with musicians including members of Parcels, Rikas and the Zen Men, finding grounding in a city that can be both electric and mellow. He filmed the video for latest single Break It Down in Portugal with director Ezra Simons (Earth Tongue), shot entirely on 16mm film in Peniche and Nazaré, and also returned to Kenya for the first time since he was sixteen, reconnecting with whānau and gaining perspective during this chapter.
“I’ve been bouncing between places while working on this album. Living nomadically keeps me open and curious. Nothing beats coming back to Aotearoa, and I can’t wait to play these songs live with the band.”
With platinum success on Wavy, the Triple J topping Love Cocoon with BENEE and collaborations with LEISURE, Young Franco and NASAYA, Muroki returns home ready to take these songs to the stage.

Music at the Museum, A very full afternoon programme of: The Grey Warblers from 2pm until 3pm - A duo of two vastly experienced and much-loved local jazz musicians. Patrick Bleakley is one of the busiest and most loved jazz musicians in the New Zealand music scene. He began his bass playing career with legendary Kiwi group Blerta and has since performed with a who’s who of New Zealand jazz including Jonathan Crayford, Alda Rezende, The Troubles, Ben Wilcock and many more. Kim Workman's music career started in Greytown round 1954, with a trio that played for local dances and
events. He then spent the next forty years, as a resident piano player, (e.g. Orsinis Restaurant) and pianist/keyboard player in jazz groups in Wellington, Hutt Valley, Rotorua, Whakatane, and Auckland until 2000, when my work responsibilities took over, apart from occasional Jazz Festivals and special occasions. A chance conversation brought them together and now they are enjoying playing the Great American Songbook: the numbers that Frank Sinatra, Tony Bennett, Ella Fitzgerald, and more recently, Diane Krall and Michael Buble made famous, as well as more contemporary numbers and some originals.
12.30pm - The Greytown Songsters: our local community choir will charm us with a programme of well loved favourites.
1pm - 2pm: The Troubador Singers - the community choir from Masterton who love to entertain and sing for the joy of singing together. Gold Coin Koha appreciated Come and enjoy an afternoon of song and music in the beautiful acoustic space of Cobblestones Museum.

description:
Musical Adventure: Celebrate 160 Years | Presented by The Friends of Old St Paul's, Enjoy an afternoon of music, performance and celebration within one of Te Whanganui-a-Tara's most treasured historic buildings. Built in 1866, Old St Paul’s has stood at the heart of the city for 160 years as a place of music, memory, ceremony and community.
The Friends of Old St Paul’s warmly invite the public to celebrate the 160th anniversary of Old St Paul’s, alongside 60 years since the founding of the Friends organisation – the long-standing independent support group dedicated to championing and preserving this much-loved heritage place.
Musical Adventure Programme
Please note there will be no intermission and timings are approximate.
From 1.45pm
Visitors are invited to watch Bell Master Steve Dean and his team ringing peals on the bells. Please note that while the bells are raised, entry to the church will be via the south porch (with a step up into the building).
2.15pm - 4.00pm
Master of Ceremonies Dave Armstrong – playwright, screenwriter, trumpet player and columnist for The Post – will guide audiences through an exciting afternoon of performances.
2.20pm – Max Toth
Sub Organist at Wellington Cathedral and former Richard Prothero Organ Scholar, Max Toth presents a rare solo organ recital before departing for a prestigious Organ Scholarship at Exeter Cathedral in the United Kingdom. Audiences can expect playing that ranges from lyrical delicacy to thrilling, cathedral-filling grandeur.
2.45pm – Hutt City Brass Sextet
Led by horn player James MacKay, a sextet from Hutt City Brass will perform a magnificent medley sure to shake the timbers of Old St Paul’s.
3.10pm – Nota Bene Chamber Choir
Acclaimed chamber choir Nota Bene, directed by Maaike Christie-Beekman, will present a beautiful selection of classical and contemporary works. Many Friends members will remember the choir from their performances at the Friends’ 2025 Carol Service.
3.30pm – Kathryn Mosley & Eleanor Carter
Senior Lecturer in Collaborative Piano at Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington Kathryn Mosley joins NZSO cellist Eleanor Carter for a programme of solo and duet performances for piano and cello.
All welcome! Koha appreciated.
For more information on Nota Bene’s upcoming concert Four Hands, Two Grands, and a Choir, visit their website.

The event takes place monthly at Evaro. It is open to anyone who has a love for music, and no musical experience is required. The venue is wheelchair accessible.

This month we will host famous Afrobeat Maestro Sam Manzanza for a night of African music. Sam will share some of his songs and we will run a drumming circle.

Musical instruments are provided. Come along to meet new people and play music without pressure.
"Musicking Together" is a space to create music together, to dance, to sing or simply listen to others. As long as we are in space, we are musicking.

How to find us? Evaro is located in the James Smith building, at the corner between Manners and Cuba Street. Enter the building and pass Rebel Sports to find the stairs. Go up to level 1 and follow the corridor on the left. You'll find Evaro to your left.

description:
Musos Club Video Premiere, 
Get your best gig gear on and join indie-pop artist Hannah Virk for the premiere screening of the Musos Club music video from her sophomore album Pocket Clocks, including an exclusive live performance, behind the scenes stories and more.
Hannah Virk is an independent musician based in Wellington, New Zealand exploring music on guitar, ukulele and keyboard. Hannah uses her own beats and layers instruments and vocals to create upbeat and captivating songs. Hannah's songs bring together electronic, folk and pop styles to create a truly unique flavour. Described as both quirky and like poetry to music, Hannah's songs are set apart by their vivid imagery and explorative sounds, surprising listeners with every note and melody.
Musos Club is the first single from Hannah's sophomore album Pocket Clocks. The album is an exciting step for Hannah - who began here musical career as an independent artist and producer after getting a guitar at age 30 and letting her creativity bloom. Musos Club dives into the live music scene and her experiences growing up around 'the cool kids' before she started her own musical journey and found her 'wild and free' pathway.
You can find Hannah's music here: https://linktr.ee/hannahvirk

description:
Mystic State (UK) // Wellington // Banshee Soundsystem, Missed Mystic State at Twisted? Here’s your chance to catch them!
Ghost Media x FTF Presents: Mystic State (UK) Powered by Banshee Soundsystem
Support from BOASTEEZE (CHC), Further Sound (DJ Set) & Conna
Hosted by Young Gho$t
Ghost Media and FTF are joining forces to bring you another epic show, this time featuring the one and only MYSTIC STATE
After hitting the New Zealand festival circuit twice, these legends need no introduction, but we’ll give them one anyway.
Hailing from the vibrant city of Bristol, UK, Mystic State is a tour-de-force in electronic music production, forged from the creative minds of Will Marquiss and Mike Holliday. The duo is celebrated for their crystal clear sound, marked by a signature blend that captures the essence of late 90's jungle, dub, and ambient sounds, designed to evoke a rich, textured soundscape. They have released on some of the finest labels in the game, including White Peach, Deep Dark and Dangerous, Chord Marauders and Artikal Music, as well as their own imprints, The Chikara Project and Moth Club. Ghost Media hosted them last time they came here back in 2024, and we can’t wait to welcome them back.
Joining them we have BOASTEEZE from Christchurch, a multitalented selector with a penchant for serious wubs. Boasteeze’s sound is deep and heavy, spanning the full spectrum of the 140 continuum. Ally is one of our favourite DJs in the country, and we’ve been looking for an opportunity to get this legend to the capital, so now seems like the perfect chance!
On closing duties we have CONNA, a skilful DJ and producer from Wellington, showcasing a range of his original dubstep and jungle productions, alongside some of his favourite tunes. Opening up proceedings, we have none other than the FURTHER SOUND crew delivering a workout with some of their favourite dub records, because what’s the point in owning a giant set of speakers if you don’t get to play on it sometimes?
Last but not least we’ve got Young Gho$t on hosting duties, because he just loves playing with the Mystic State boys. They locked in together at Matakanarama and it was something seriously special, so Ghosty is gonna dust off the old mic and try to recapture some of that magic or better yet - make some new magic!
As per, it’s a Banshee Soundsystem install, and you know exactly what that’s gonna sound like.
Limited early birds are available for a cheap as chips $20. Secure yours now and prepare for an evening of serious bass and vibes.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Myths & Legends - Wellington, Myths & Legends - Wellington
Arctic North meets Pacific South in a programme of heart-stirring Finnish works with conductor Pietari Inkinen and NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen.

Programme:
Sibelius Pohjola’s Daughter
Magnus Lindberg Violin Concerto No. 2 (NZ Premiere)
Sibelius Lemminkäinen Suite

Aotearoa New Zealand’s dramatic landscapes chime in kind with a country half a world away: Finland. In this concert, Arctic North meets Pacific South in a programme of heart-stirring Finnish works that resonate with audiences here.

Pietari Inkinen leads the Aotearoa New Zealand premiere of Finnish composer Magnus Lindberg’s Second Violin Concerto, with NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen as soloist. This duo of Finnish talent are the perfect team to evoke the work’s “massive, expansive ... panoramic vista ... of dark clouds over forests and lakes, of repressed passions and baleful desires” (Financial Times).

We pair this contemporary Finnish masterpiece with a past master. Sibelius’ Pohjola’s Daughter and Lemminkäinen Suite were both inspired by the ancient epic the Kalevala. The latter describes the mythological adventures of the wizard Väinämöinen, the hero Lemminkäinen and their entanglement with the primordial forces of nature, death and magic.

*********

Renowned for their explosive blend of rock ‘n’ roll, Irish folk and American gospel, Ireland’s legendary Hothouse Flowers, are set to return to Australia for the first time in 20 long years for a highly anticipated tour in February 2026.

The Dubliner's passionate fusion of rock, folk and gospel has captivated audiences worldwide for the last four decades. From their humble street performing roots in Dublin to global stages, the band continues to deliver electrifying performances that blend cultural storytelling and raw musical spirit with spontaneity and soulful energy.

After winning the Street Entertainers of the Year award in 1985, the band caught the eye of U2’s Bono, leading to a record deal with PolyGram. Their 1988 debut album, People, topped the Irish charts and hit number two in the UK, establishing them as a captivating live band with a dedicated global fanbase. The album features their highest streaming single to date, the utterly sublime, Don't Go.

Home followed in 1990 and featured the band’s gorgeous cover of the Johnny Nash classic, I Can See Clearly Now, which was given a new lease of life and used to stunning affect in the opening scene of 2016's Jeremy Clarkson's Grand Tour TV show. Watch the incredible intro here. Home along with 93’s Songs From the Rain cemented the bands place as one Ireland’s greats. The Australian tour follows the release of their latest album, Let’s Do This Thing (2020)

Known for their unpredictable energy and impromptu improvisation, every Hothouse Flowers show is unique experience. From rock anthems to soulful ballads and traditional songs that evoke the emotional weight of Irish storytelling, the band’s performances are a journey through musical and cultural landscapes. Their shows are marked by humour, raw expression and a deep connection with audiences, making each gig a one of a kind event.

Don’t miss one of the most celebrated returns of the year!

description:
NONCONNAH (U.S.A.) - Live, Nonconnah is an experimental music collective based in Memphis, Tennessee, headed by the husband-and-wife duo of Zachary Corsa and Denny Wilkerson Corsa.

Nonconnah creates haunting soundscapes and collages, often using antique or unusual instrumentation and obsolete recording technology to draw on themes of memory and the past, the supernatural, and the liminal spaces where the man-made and natural worlds meet. Releases such as 2021's Songs for and About Ghosts are filled with warped lo-fi guitars, field recordings, grainy samples, and acoustic instrumentation, arranged into dreamlike sequences. The Corsas draw on a wide range of sonic influences, from shoegaze and post-rock to dark ambient to recurring motifs of old time/Appalachian mountain music. Their work has been widely acclaimed by the likes of Pitchfork, SPIN, The Wire, AllMusic, Fluid Radio, Tiny Mix Tapes, Brainwashed, A Closer Listen, Echoes & Dust, I Heart Noise, and more.

A highly collaborative effort, Nonconnah has collaborated with past and present members of bands like Deerhoof, Swans, Earth, Broken Social Scene, Arcade Fire, A Silver Mt. Zion, Archers Of Loaf, Wolf Parade, Band Of Susans, The Black Heart Procession, Lovesliescrushing, Come, Burning Witch, Vetiver, Cloudland Canyon, Soul Coughing, Lightfoils, Lazy Legs, Skywave, United Bible Studies, and many more.

Official - www.nonconnahdrone.com

Bandcamp - www.nonconnahordeath.bandcamp.com

description:
NZSO From the New World, Eve de Castro-Robinson Aurora
Beethoven Violin Concerto
Dvořák Symphony No. 9, From the New World

María Dueñas appears with generous support from Susan and Donald Best ONZM.
With thanks to the Embassy of Spain in New Zealand.

The winner of the 2021 Yehudi Menuhin Competition at just 18, María Dueñas is swiftly gaining global acclaim thanks to her “luminously radiant and golden-toned, fluidly quicksilver technique” (Gramophone). Her exceptional talent will be brilliantly showcased for the first time in Aotearoa, New Zealand, in a performance of Beethoven’s beloved Violin Concerto — an immense concerto that expanded the horizons of the genre.

Inspired both by memories of his native Bohemia and the majestic North American plains of his new home, Dvořák’s Symphony No. 9, From the New World, is replete with lush, unforgettable melodies that have made it one of the most adored symphonies of our time. It is a work that speaks so powerfully to a sense of place and ideas of home.

We are proud to open our season with a playful tribute to our own NZ skies in Eve de Castro-Robinson’s Aurora — a fanfare of birdsong and momentum.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
NZSO Myths & Legends, Sibelius Pohjola’s Daughter
Magnus Lindberg Violin Concerto No. 2 (NZ Premiere)
Sibelius Lemminkäinen Suite

Aotearoa New Zealand’s dramatic landscapes chime in kind with a country half a world away: Finland. In this concert, Arctic North meets Pacific South in a programme of heart-stirring Finnish works that resonate with audiences here.

Pietari Inkinen leads the Aotearoa New Zealand premiere of Finnish composer Magnus Lindberg’s Second Violin Concerto, with NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen as soloist. This duo of Finnish talent are the perfect team to evoke the work’s “massive, expansive ... panoramic vista ... of dark clouds over forests and lakes, of repressed passions and baleful desires” (Financial Times).

We pair this contemporary Finnish masterpiece with a past master. Sibelius’ Pohjola’s Daughter and Lemminkäinen Suite were both inspired by the ancient epic the Kalevala. The latter describes the mythological adventures of the wizard Väinämöinen, the hero Lemminkäinen and their entanglement with the primordial forces of nature, death and magic.
label: Music & Concerts

description:

Wagner Excerpts from Parsifal

Two familiar faces reunite in this Wagner extravaganza.

Pietari Inkinen is a superlative interpreter of Wagner. His Ring Cycle at Bayreuth in 2023 led to Das Opernglas declaring “he might be remembered as one of the most inspired conductors who ever undertook The Ring in Bayreuth”. Simon O’Neill is undoubtedly the Wagnerian tenor of choice the world over and regularly performs at the Metropolitan Opera, Bayreuth, Covent Garden and the Vienna State Opera.

In this programme, these extraordinary Wagner specialists combine to bring to radiant life excerpts from two of Wagner’s most heroic and magnificent operas: Parsifal and Tannhäuser.

This event is simply not to be missed.

Supported by The Wagner Society of New Zealand.
label: Music & Concerts

description:

Copland Clarinet Concerto
Gabriela Ortiz Antrópolis (NZ Premiere)
Bernstein Symphonic Dances from West Side Story

Gemma New’s signature “strength, clarity and grace” (WTTW News) invigorates this 20th century American classic, Bernstein’s Symphonic Dances from West Side Story. In depicting a New York gangland Romeo and Juliet, Bernstein’s score captures an irrepressible American swagger. Rhythm & Dance also infuses John Adams’ The Chairman Dances, an outtake of Adams’ opera Nixon in China, which imagines the young Chairman Mao dancing the foxtrot with his mistress.

Aaron Copland’s Clarinet Concerto melds Latin American popular music with jazz in this work commissioned by “The King of Swing” Benny Goodman. And we proudly present the Kiwi premiere of Gabriela Ortiz’s Antrópolis. Grammy Award-winning Ortiz is one of Mexico’s hottest contemporary composers, and this work refers to el antro, Mexican slang for a nightclub.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
NZSO Romeo & Juliet, Kenneth Young Douce Tristesse
Barber Cello Concerto
Prokofiev Selections From Romeo And Juliet

Sergei Prokofiev’s Romeo and Juliet is one of the greatest ballet scores of all time. Among the courtly grandeur of Dance of the Knights, the circling, slicing, jabbing music of Death of Tybalt, and the crunching dissonances symbolising the Montagues versus the Capulets, swirls the indescribably sweet lyricism of Romeo and Juliet’s eternal love.

The same emotional depth can be found in Barber’s Cello Concerto, performed by virtuoso Li-Wei Qin. Celebrated for a sound both “incisive and searing, yet filled with tenderness” (Straits Times), Qin will steep Barber’s concerto in deep feeling and passion. Sweet nostalgia reigns in the “drifting, Ravelian waltz” (New Zealand Herald) of Kenneth Young’s Douce Tristesse.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
NZSSC @ Te Raukura ki Kāpiti !, NZSSC @ Te Raukura ki Kāpiti !
NZ’s best young singers to perform first full-length public concert of 2025 at Te Raukura ki Kāpiti this September

The New Zealand Secondary Students’ Choir (NZSSC) will perform their first full-length public concert of 2025 on Saturday 27th September at Te Raukura ki Kāpiti, in the stunning Coastlands Theatre. Concert starts 6pm

The NZSSC has achieved considerable success since its formation in 1986. Bringing their “infectious joy for music-making” to the Kāpiti coast for the first time since 2022, you will see and hear exactly why the NZSSC has won titles such as 'Children's Choir of the World' at Llangollen Eisteddfod and embarked on 16 international tours, including Canada, Singapore, China, USA, South America, Australia and South Africa, during their almost 40 year existence!

Under the direction of Sue Densem, the NZSSC gathers our finest young voices (14–18) throughout Aotearoa and offers a once in a lifetime opportunity – a two-year membership that sees students learning from some of the country’s top choral teachers and composers, as well as performing throughout Aotearoa. The 2-year experience culminates in an exciting international tour in July of the 2nd year, before singers part ways.

As with all their concerts, the repertoire for this Kāpiti concert will be a wonderful mix of cultures, featuring Māori waiata ā-ringa and Pasifika songs with a sprinkling of choral cannon plus some classics like you’ve never heard them before!

Bring the whole family for an evening of choral excellence and entertainment!

description:
NZTrio He Taonga Wairere presents “Groove Café”, Welcome to Groove Café, where the music is strong and the vibe is even stronger. John Psathas’ Island Songs bring sun, surf, and a dash of Kiwi cool - no sunscreen required. description:
NZTrio presents Fantastique, Renowned classical music ensemble NZTrio He Taonga Wairere present their extraordinary programme Fantastique.
Described as a "national treasure" and "New Zealand's most indispensable ensemble" (William Dart, NZ Herald), NZTrio combines warm kiwi stage presence with musicians at the top of their craft.
Amalia Hall (violin), Somi Kim (piano) and Callum Hall (guest cello) explore a lavish tapestry of styles and emotions in Fantastique, a programme of contrasts. Turina's Circulo depicts a single day through dawn, midday and dusk, while brooding disquiet meets stark intensity in Shostakovich's Piano Trio No.1 in C minor. Chen Yi's Tibetan Tunes creates a fusion of traditional Tibetan melodies referencing Buddhist god Du Mu, before the premiere of Angelus, a new commission by one of Aotearoa’s most acclaimed composers, John Psathas. Finally, Franck's youthful Piano Trio No. 1 in F sharp minor is as charming and intimate as it is powerful and explosive.

description:
NZTrio presents Hypnotique, Described as a “national treasure” and “New Zealand’s most indispensable ensemble”, NZTrio He Taonga Wairere is renowned for its eclectic repertoire, outstanding talent and warm kiwi stage presence. Bringing together three incredibly accomplished artists, every NZTrio performance powerfully reaffirms the importance and cathartic nature of a live musical experience in today’s digital world.

Hypnotique presents a diverse array of works that challenges expectations of traditional chamber music. A whirlwind of motion typifies NZ composer Lyell Cresswell's virtuosic Moto Perpetuo, ahead of Fauré's Piano Trio in D minor with lyrical elegance and lush harmonic textures, contrasting with the percussive and electronic influences in Le Boeuf's jazz-adjacent Obliquely Wrecked. Australian composer Elena Kats-Chernin pays homage to Haydn, blending classical and contemporary styles in Calliope Dreaming, then finally, the full Romantic immersion of Schönberg's Verklärte Nacht is structured around the five stanzas of a poem; deeply transcendent and utterly beautiful.

Gabriel Fauré - Piano Trio in D minor, Op. 120
Pascal Le Boeuf - Obliquely Wrecked
Elena Kats-Chernin - Calliope Dreaming
Arnold Schönberg - Verklärte Nacht arr. for piano trio

description:
Nameless and Brainless, ***THIS SHOW IS KOHA ENTRY***
FIRST ACT: 6:30pm
6 piece Soul/Hip Hop Wellington band play Moon for the first time with support from Sam Fowles (solo) and Lucy Summerfield (solo with cello accompanied)
NAMELESS AND BRAINLESS:
What started as some jams for a Master's level project between a couple of the bros has evolved into a soulful, hard-hitting band.
While this project is fresh, each of the musicians either has a degree in music or has vast experience in the industry.
High-energy Kiwi raps in English and Te Reo, accompanied by a powerful band and driven by a locked-in rhythm section.
LUCY SUMMERFIELD:
Lucy Summerfield’s music is threaded through with intention. She explores the full range of human experience in her work with her poignant lyrics. The way she weaves these together with carefully crafted melodies has seen her recognised nationally for her songwriting in both te reo Māori and English.
She is joined onstage by talented cellist Joanna Dann (Boxhill Quartet).
SAM FOWLES:
Sam Fowles is a soul-searcher and sonic adventurer from Pōneke, Aotearoa. His music drifts from smoky, blues-drenched sunrises into funk-filled skies, weaving a tapestry of soulful psychedelia that moves both body and soul.
Live and solo, Sam becomes a guitar-slinging troubadour, wringing the truth from every phrase. Without the full band, the focus falls on his storytelling, the groove in his right hand, and the emotion in his voice. It’s soulful, intimate, and full of heart, showcasing a different side of his music while remaining unmistakably Sam

description:
Nana & Petal @ The RSC, Nana & Petal @ The RSC
The Nana & Petal set comprises an eclectic mix, self-penned songs, several by the prolific O’Dempsey, some co-written with brother Dylan, the pair also have a penchant for songs written by other friends and NZ songwriters such as Reb Fountain and Hammond Gamble. They include covers by the Uppity Blues Women, the Devil Makes Three, Mavis Staples and many by Tom Waits, with lesser-known compositions from songwriters such as the Black Pumas, William Elliott Whitmore, and the eclectic bluesman C.W Stoneking, which are all suited to Paul’s piano style. This duo spans blues, folk, and alt country, with Paul pinning down the groove on piano/organ with some blistering solos and a real sensitivity for accompanying a vocalist, showcasing Celine’s arresting vocal style, charisma and storytelling magnetism.

Friday 17th April
Support from Clova, Young Gho$t, JSwizzle, Ohimesama Breaks & Whaea G

Ghost Media and Rhythm Output are teaming up once again for a spectacular extravaganza of junglism! This time we are elated to welcome none other than NECTAX, in our opinion one of the most exciting jungle producers of modern times!
Nectax exists in the gaps; a breakbeat scientist at heart, never fraternising too heavily with any single sonic blueprint in pursuit of his heterogenous sound. He has released on some of the genre’s most sought after labels, including Over/Shadow, Future Retro, Hooversound, Up Ya Archives and DJ Flight’s Play:Musik.
On support, he will be joined by a classic cast of Poneke’s finest DJs - CLOVA and WHAEA G, both hot off the backs of legendary CubaDupa sets, and OHIMESAMA BREAKS, hot off the back of a massive set at Resonance Festival. Finally, Young Gho$t will open up proceedings, with as an of yet unnamed back to back partner. Who could it be?
Venue will be announced soon… in the meantime score some cheap tix and lock in for a night of serious jungle, breakbeat and hardcore!

Standing show (Seating reserved for those who need it: ).

The wave doesn’t conform to the shape of the rock. It smashes it. The sea doesn’t pretend to be hospitable. It summons courage. And a shantyband never licks the captain's boot. They release another EP!

The best shanties invite us to open our hearts along with the bottle. To draw strength from camaraderie and drown our pettinesses. To seek the rough edge of the wave and savour the salt within. And so, the WSSS have issued a call to arms with their new collection: Never Mind the Rowlocks, Here’s the Wellington Sea Shanty Society.

Never fear if you find yourself adrift on a sea of AI slop, lapping at your hull, lulling you to sleep — Lake Davineer, Vorn dont Le Père Était Marin, Young Nic, Tomas el Largo, and Louis Quatorze are back again to fill your sails and slap the codfish slime clean off your cheeks.

Just when everyone is lamenting the empty galleys of the good ship Wellington, and those ol’ scurvy-mongers are promising renewed bounty if you would only tack five degrees to port or starboard come election time, these songs remind us the sea at least will sustain us, and there’s rum and (metaphorical) guns for them that wants to fight.

Lin Seal | Wellington Nautical History Monthly

⚓⚓⚓

The scuttlebutt is true...⛵

The most seaworthy sea shanty band in the South Pacific is releasing their long-awaited 4th collection of new and old maritime bangers:
'Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society'.

All aboard as we set sail for the salty horizon. Prepare to be battered once again by the 4-sailor squall of pure shanty.


⚓⚓⚓

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).
The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada.

They will be playing new classics from their forthcoming EP 'Never Mind the Rowlocks' as well as your foamy favourites from the 'Sea Shanties of the 70s, 80s, & Today!' EP and their 'Now That's What I Call Sea Shanties' series.

Never fear if you find yourself adrift on a sea of AI slop, lapping at your hull, lulling you to sleep — Lake Davineer, Vorn dont Le Père Était Marin, Young Nic, Tomas el Largo, and Louis Quatorze are back again to fill your sails and slap the codfish slime clean off your cheeks.

Just when everyone is lamenting the empty galleys of the good ship Wellington, and those ol’ scurvy-mongers are promising renewed bounty if you would only tack five degrees to port or starboard come election time, these songs remind us the sea at least will sustain us, and there’s rum and (metaphorical) guns for them that wants to fight.

description:
Nevers (France/Australia) / Jean-Philippe Gross (solo) / Oghum, Nevers
Featuring Clare Cooper (Australia) on guhzeng and Jean-Philippe Gross (France) on electro-acoustic devices, Nevers sometimes sounds like a fire in an electronic flea market, other times like the amplification of an insect funeral march. The duo finds common ground between Clare Cooper’s Chinese guhzeng and Jean-Philippe Gross’ lo-fi microphones, electroacoustic devices and localized speaker system.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vpY7AEVU4mc
Strasbourg’s Jean-Philippe Gross will also perform a solo set, of electronic music using a dedicated feedback system.
https://jeanphilippegross.com/
Clare Cooper is a musician and Design Lecturer from Sydney. Her work in creative community projects includes collaborative composition, speculative design, and critical listening. She co-founded the NOW now (2001), Splinter Orchestra (Sydney 2000), Splitter Orchester (Berlin 2009), and Frontyard Projects (2016).
Jean-Philippe Gross (Strasbourg – France) is a composer and improviser, performing with a dedicated feedback system often utilising multiple small speakers positioned around the performance space. In the studio, he continues his research with a “Serge modular system”. He has composed music for dance and performance, as well as for contemporary ensembles such as Ensemble Dedalus.
Nevers is presented with the support of Rise / La Muse en Circuit - Musica.
---
Oghum is the interstellar duo of Nell Thomas (Orchestra of Spheres, Cookie Brooklyn and the Crumbs) and Jonny Marks (All Seeing Hand, Mean Bones), performing on Synthi AKS, theremin and other assorted items. Oghum blends electronic sounds from times past with an array of acoustic and found sounds, using nuanced improvisation to create detailed and tangible sonic environments, invoking memory and transporting the listener through narrow gaps into wide open otherworldly spaces.
$20 presale tickets via UTR
Special thanks to CNZ for supporting Pyramid Club's programme

description:
New Zealand String Quartet presents: Origins | Wellington, The New Zealand String Quartet presents their 2026 Season: Storytellers.
Across a three-part Wellington series, we'll explore three distinct programmes: Origins, Transform and Legend. We’ll boldly explore more compositional voices than ever before, beginning with classical masterworks that resonate through the centuries, through to modern-day Grammy winners and the distinctive voices of Aotearoa. The three string quartets of Benjamin Britten form the heart of our 2026 Season, to mark the 50th anniversary of the composer’s death.
Storytellers showcases a rich cross-section of our society and celebrates the art of storytelling through music. Join us in 2026 as together we explore these musical stories.
Programme for Origins:
Mika Cornelius - Universal Veil
Franz Schubert - String Quartet No. 10, in E flat major (D. 87)
Gareth Farr - Mondo Rondo
Interval
Missy Mazzoli - Death Valley Junction
Benjamin Britten - String Quartet No. 1, in D major (Op. 25)
‘Origins’ opens with a piece composed especially for the NZSQ: Mika Cornelius’s Universal Veil, an ethereal and atmospheric trip through the lifecycle of fungi.
Schubert’s vibrant E flat major quartet shows the teenage composer finding his voice before Gareth Farr brings us home with the infectious personality of Mondo Rondo.
Grammy nominee and ‘Brooklyn’s post-millennial Mozart’ (Time Out New York) Missy Mazzoli reimagines a harsh desert landscape into something wild and buoyant in Death Valley Junction.
Origins concludes with the cornerstone of our 2026 Season, a tribute to Benjamin Britten as we play all three of his string quartets in the 50th year after his death. His first string quartet, written at 27 years old, prompted musicologist Peter Evans to declare him “a master of tonal architecture with scarcely a rival on the English scene.” It spans the intimate, restless and sublime and forms the perfect ending to our meditation on beginnings.
Explore the rest of the Wellington series:
Transform | Wednesday 12 August, 6:30pm | Prefab Hall, Wellington
Legend | Wednesday 28 October, 6:30pm | Prefab Hall, Wellington

description:
New Zealand String Quartet presents: Transform | Wellington, The New Zealand String Quartet presents their 2026 Season: Storytellers.

Across a three-part Wellington series, we'll explore three distinct programmes: Origins, Transform and Legend. We’ll boldly explore more compositional voices than ever before, beginning with classical masterworks that resonate through the centuries, through to modern-day Grammy winners and the distinctive voices of Aotearoa. The three string quartets of Benjamin Britten form the heart of our 2026 Season, to mark the 50th anniversary of the composer’s death.

Storytellers showcases a rich cross-section of our society and celebrates the art of storytelling through music. Join us in 2026 as together we explore these musical stories.

Programme for Transform:
Henry Purcell - Fantasias
Anthony Ritchie - Perpetual Motion and Last Dance from String Quartet No.3, ‘In Time’
Fanny Mendelssohn - String Quartet in E flat major
Interval
Salina Fisher - Heal
Benjamin Britten - String Quartet No. 2, in C major (Op. 36)

‘Transform’ opens with Henry Purcell's intricately wrought Fantasias, which served as inspiration for Benjamin Britten. Following is Anthony Ritchie, one of Aotearoa’s most eminent composers, celebrating playful melodic lines and infectious rhythm in Perpetual Motion and Last Dance from String Quartet No. 3. Fanny Mendelssohn’s only string quartet showcases her poetic, passionate and introspective voice, too long overlooked in the shadow of her brother, Felix. Salina Fisher’s soothing tribute to grief and loss in Heal serves as a poignant companion to Benjamin Britten’s second string quartet. Written in the immediate aftermath of the Second World War and widely regarded as one of the most extraordinary pieces of the twentieth century, Britten offers a powerful reflection of his inner feelings and a moving tribute to his compositional idol, Henry Purcell.

Explore the rest of the Wellington series:
Origins| Wednesday 6 May, 6:30pm | Prefab Hall, Wellington
Legend | Wednesday 28 October, 6:30pm | Prefab Hall, Wellington

description:
Newtown Rocksteady - Wellington, Newtown Rocksteady - Wellington
The mighty Newtown Rocksteady Return with their massive house of sound.

The bonfire will be lit with bass, dowsed in drums, and then fed with vocals, guitars, keys, horns, dancing, banter, laughter and special guests.

Watch them burn! After years of smash hit, full houses all accross Aotearoa, the boys are hitting the Rogue and Vagabone to shake things up, BIG time!

Did we mention the special guests' Not just guests, special guests! Who will they be' Come find out.

Hear some bangin new tunes alongside some choice rocksteady classics.

It could be the best night of your life! Fullas, you might find a pretty lady in the crowd' Ladies, you might get yourself a cashed-up musician (get in quick -they're flying out the door!)

Whatever happens, it will be hearty good times.

The band has its roots firmly embedded in the traditions of Jamaican rocksteady, ska and reggae music and is further nourished by its connection with its community. They will be spreading this love on their South Island tour in January 2026.

Be sure to bring your dancing shoes for one of Wellington’s biggest, best-loved, longest-running and grooviest vintage reggae bands: Newtown Rocksteady!

Possibly one of the greatest dance bands to have played the Mussel Inn in the past eighteen years. These guys are rock steady in every sense of those two words.
- Andrew, Mussel Inn - Takaka

I love it when I go to a concert expecting to see my favourite band and discover that the openers are almost better than the headline act. Numbering twelve on the stage, Newtown Rocksteady damn near threatened to demolish the stage by sheer force of numbers!

These guys are hard-hitting aficionados of ‘70s dub classics as per Lee Scratch Perry and Augustus Pablo, and their particular delivery quickly fuel up the lukewarm Sunday audience. Story goes that the Black Seeds caught their act at the recent Newtown Festival and were so taken they asked them to open for their Wellington homecoming gigs.

I can see why. Big horns, smatterings of conscious roots, deep, soulful grooves – tunes are well crafted, a little righteous but, ultimately, perfect to wiggle to. Special mention goes to ‘So Long’, with brilliant lines “oil on the water – pain in my soul” – a reference to BP, oil slicks, Nigeria and the evils of the oil industry.

Armed with undeniably some of the heaviest riffs known to mankind, 𝗗𝗬𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗨𝗦 has established a reputation for uncompromising integrity with a slew of classic albums and today rides a resurgence of respect and esteem with a new generation. The band continually refines its unique take on death, grind, and hardcore with a combination of virtuosity and ferocity, inescapably catchy hooks, punishing breakdowns and a complete lack of pretension.

After 12 horribly long years since their last tour in Australia and in only their second appearance in New Zealand since 2009, 𝗗𝗬𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗨𝗦 are well overdue to lash us unmercifully with their savage beatdowns and earth-moving grooves and grunt, equally designed to pulverize and mesmerize.

On their first slog into the antipodes, Cleveland death metal legends-in-waiting 𝟮𝟬𝟬 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗕 𝗪𝗢𝗨𝗡𝗗𝗦 serve up a brutal slab of old school death metal with a contemporary edge. Not for the faint-hearted, 𝟮𝟬𝟬 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗕 𝗪𝗢𝗨𝗡𝗗𝗦 craft classic gore-themed savagery for themselves and like-minded brethren: thrill-seekers, carnage cravers, horror fans, and aficionados of the most extreme of metal.

Warming up the circle pits and necks will be the slamming sonic signature of ORGANECTOMY in New Zealand and the old-school death metal grit and punishing ferocity of ASHEN in Australia.

Armed with undeniably some of the heaviest riffs known to mankind, 𝗗𝗬𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗨𝗦 has established a reputation for uncompromising integrity with a slew of classic albums and today rides a resurgence of respect and esteem with a new generation. The band continually refines its unique take on death, grind, and hardcore with a combination of virtuosity and ferocity, inescapably catchy hooks, punishing breakdowns and a complete lack of pretension.
After 12 horribly long years since their last tour in Australia and in only their second appearance in New Zealand since 2009, 𝗗𝗬𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗨𝗦 are well overdue to lash us unmercifully with their savage beatdowns and earth-moving grooves and grunt, equally designed to pulverize and mesmerize.
On their first slog into the antipodes, Cleveland death metal legends-in-waiting 𝟮𝟬𝟬 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗕 𝗪𝗢𝗨𝗡𝗗𝗦 serve up a brutal slab of old school death metal with a contemporary edge. Not for the faint-hearted, 𝟮𝟬𝟬 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗕 𝗪𝗢𝗨𝗡𝗗𝗦 craft classic gore-themed savagery for themselves and like-minded brethren: thrill-seekers, carnage cravers, horror fans, and aficionados of the most extreme of metal.
Warming up the circle pits and necks will be the slamming sonic signature of ORGANECTOMY in New Zealand and the old-school death metal grit and punishing ferocity of ASHEN in Australia.

PIG DESTROYER boil metal down to its muscle, sinew, and bone - razor-sharp guitar, percussive pummelling, and a lone, stark howl - and use them to commit a vicious assault. The lyrics paint loathsome, frightening images of pitch-black self-hatred and the frailty of the human experience. These musical manifestations only serve to cement their already legendary status. Having not been in Australia and New Zealand since 2008, PIG DESTROYER’s long overwaited return has just one goal. To unnerve the unprepared with a deranged, grisly intensity which very few, if any, can match.

Recently reforming to the original line-up, Singapore’s WORMROT resume their genius in unleashing exquisite noise together, with the announcement of a new album 'TNT'. Grinding faces with the best of them, their performances are intense, spectacular, furious, with a barrage of unrelenting, head-caving abuse, honed by a singular determination to destroy the competition.

description:
Nick Baucke-Maunsell Quintet, Led by saxophonist Nicholas Baucke-Maunsell, the group features Henry Sherris on trumpet — reuniting after a five-year break during which Henry honed his craft in New York.
The two first played together as teenagers in the Young Musicians Programme under the mentorship of the legendary Rodger Fox and now return to the stage for this special performance.
Joining them are Callum Allardice on guitar, Seth Boy on bass, and Abe Baillie on drums — an exceptional rhythm section known for their deep musical connection and expressive interplay.
The quintet will perform a dynamic mix of original jazz compositions. Each piece reflects moments from Nicholas’s recent journey — from touring internationally with the Rodger Fox Big Band to day-to-day insights gained through his work as a teacher.
The set will also feature compositions by Henry, offering reflections on his time living and studying in New York.
Don’t miss the chance to experience this heartfelt performance live.

description:
Nick Cave & The Bad Seeds — Wild God Tour, Their music has long defied classification. For over 40 years, Nick Cave & The Bad Seeds have delivered a sophisticated mix of post-punk, experimental, gospel, and blues to adoring fans. Now, in a New Zealand exclusive, Wellington gets to hear them live at TSB Arena in February. Renowned for their exhilarating and unforgettable performances, the band is regarded as one of the most thrilling to watch on stage. 
In 2024, they released their eighteenth studio album, ‘Wild God’. Now, Nick and the band are circling the globe on the ‘Wild God Tour’. They have finished the North American and European legs, and TSB Arena on Wellington’s waterfront is the next stop off. The band will perform a setlist drawn from the latest album alongside songs spanning the four decades of a storied career.
Brought to you in association with Aotearoa New Zealand Festival of the Arts. 
Tickets will go on sale to the public on Friday, 29 August at 10am.

description:
Nick Herbison Album Release Tour - Wellington 2nd August w/ Joe Cole, Nick Herbison Album Release Tour - Wellington 2nd August w/ Joe Cole
Herbison offers a solo performance in Wellington at Newtowns finest Moon Bar, supported by folk artist Joe Cole. The solo tour marks the release of his self produced album 'Seek and Don't Forget'.



Nick Herbison is a folk-rock artist from Hawke’s Bay, Aotearoa, whose music reflects his philosophical outlook and the internal weather systems he navigates. With acoustic guitar at the core of his songwriting, Herbison crafts introspective, life-affirming songs that explore courage, self-worth, and the ongoing journey toward inner peace. His style has been largely influenced by folk, blues, rock, roots and RnB.



Most recently Nick embarked on a national tour of Aotearoa supporting Melbourne blues troubadour Shaun Kirk during September 2025. Since then Herbison has played as a solo performer at festivals in Auckland and Rotorua (Morph Fest and Sauna Fest).



Herbison's solo performances often demonstrate his sensational ability on the acoustic guitar and his lower toned, smooth vocals. The use of a loop pedal and foot percussion has been a recent addition to his solo set. With influences such as Jack Johnson, Ben Howard, Matt Corby, Ben Harper and Passenger, to name a few, Nick will often include a cover or two during his sets.



'Seek and Don't Forget' is the album that he will be celebrating on his handful of shows around the North Island throughout July and August. Wellington singer songwriter; Joe Cole will support the show with his grandiose style of folk music.

description:
Nicola Mitchell with Jo Moir & Mikey Muggeridge: Valentine's Day Gig, Gate opens 7pm Music Starts 7.30pm

“For the smitten, slightly bitter & the happily single"
Nicola’s warm, magnetic songwriting “swells and tugs at the heartstrings, stirring more than a tear or two“. Rooted in family and storytelling, Nicola Mitchell (Waikato-Tainui, Ngāti Maniapoto) blends folky bluegrass with a touch of te reo Māori.
2025 Country Music Honour winner, Nicola is one half of the Tūī and APRA Best Country Song-nominated duo The Mitchell Twins and regularly tours Aotearoa and Australia alongside her award-winning sister, Jenny Mitchell.
This Valentine’s Day, Nicola brings a special show to Hilltop for “the smitten, the slightly bitter, and the happyily single”. She’s joined by Wellington favourites Michael Muggeridge (Butter Wouldn’t Melt and T-Bone) on mandolin, and Jo Moir (Hobnail) on the violin. An acoustic set designed to move through the many different stories of Valentines Day.
Inspired by artists like Tami Neilson, Marlon Williams, and the Topp Twins, Nicola has shared stages with John Craigie (US), The Warratahs, and Kasey Chambers, following a standout set at the Wellington Folk Festival in 2024.
Come along to catch a show drowning in harmonies with the full spectrum of love this Valentine’s Day.
Come along and enjoy this great gig in our special space, up close and personal.
These are private house concerts, not for profit, supporting our dedicated musicians. Visit www.hilltophouseconcerts.co.nz to reserve a seat. Suggested donation $30. Email confirmation will include address and details.
Teas, Coffee and Snacks provided. You're welcome to bring anything you'd like to eat or drink.
Parking available in the Coupon zones of Upland Rd & Glasgow St free after 6pm weekdays, and free all through the weekends. The Wilson Carpark at the top of the Cable Car charges 24/7.

description:
Niels and the Cartertones an evening of Leonard Cohen, Join us for the special opening night concert of Greytown Art Town weekend. An evening of Leonard Cohen is a collaboration between four extraordinary, Wairarapa-based musicians. They will cover many of Leonard Cohen’s best loved pieces. This performance is an alliance between:
Niels Gedge, fingerstyle guitar and lead vocals, a well-known singer-songwriter on the folk scene, with two albums of original songs. He has also performed extensively in cafes and bars and at events in the UK and throughout NZ. Niels' vocal range is very similar to Leonard Cohen.
Kate Marshall, multi-instrumentalist and vocals. As well as singing in a duo with her partner Bob Cooper-Grundy at clubs, pubs and festivals, Kate is a key member of the much-loved Raven Mavens, the all-woman Boogie/Blues band that plays regularly around the Wellington Region, and beyond.
Bob Cooper-Grundy is an Americana/blues musician who plays finger-picking guitar, mandolin, and slide guitar. Bob has opened for Americana Greats: Guy Clark, Townes van Zandt, Tom Russell, and Jimmy LaFave.
Steve Trotman, vocals and acoustic guitar. Inspired by the bands of the 1950s and 1960s and singer/songwriters, such as James Taylor and Paul Simon, Steve fronted various Wellington groups in the 1970s. He co-founded Verandah Band in the early 2000s, playing a mix of genres in every Wairarapa venue (and beyond) for the past 20-odd years, including Toast Martinborough and Summer Hummer.
The Offering is fully licenced and will be serving snacks and drinks from 6.30pm

description:
Niko Ne Zna Live at Vogelmorn Hall (Wellington), Niko Ne Zna Live at Vogelmorn Hall (Wellington)
Niko Ne Zna returns to Vogelmorn Hall for an unforgettable Saturday night of explosive brass, infectious rhythms, delicious food, and music that's impossible to sit still to.

Drawing inspiration from the rich musical traditions of Serbia, Macedonia, Romania, Greece, and beyond, Niko Ne Zna combines soaring brass, driving percussion, passionate multilingual vocals, and original compositions to create a spectacular live experience. Featuring two trumpets, soprano saxophone, tenor and bass trombones, sousaphone, traditional Balkan bass drum (tapan), snare drum, and powerhouse vocalist Nikkie Rich, the band delivers an exhilarating performance that will have you dancing from the first note to the last.

With more than fifteen years of captivating audiences throughout New Zealand and Australia, appearances at WOMAD New Zealand, and original music featured in What We Do in the Shadows, Niko Ne Zna has earned a reputation as one of New Zealand's premier world music acts.

Doors open at 5:30 pm, giving you plenty of time to enjoy delicious food and a drink from the fully stocked bar before the music begins. Whether you've been following Niko Ne Zna for years or are experiencing the band for the first time, prepare for an unforgettable evening of exhilarating live music, celebration, and dancing.


“It’s like being dropped into the hot and spicy lands of a faraway country.” — wellingtonlivemusic.com

“Straight to the dancefloor.” — Elsewhere

“Driving rhythms, an intoxicating effect.” — Taranaki Daily News

www.nikonezna.com

Saturday 29 August
Vogelmorn Hall, Wellington
Doors: 5:30 pm

Delicious food and a fully stocked bar available

No mans heath album launch celebration, The same moon is the follow up record to the last no mans heath offering ‘ball of string’ that was released in 2017.
This show is a celebration of the finishing of the record.
Tom will be playing songs from the record and a few old favourites. With the help of one of Wellington’s most loved musicians Scott Pilgrim.
No mans heath aka Tom Kane is an English singer songwriter who has made Wellington his home. He songs are insightful and delicate and have been described as a beautiful exercise in restraint.
The wonderful Tessa de Lyon (also of Mystery Waitress) will open the evening with a set of piano songs. Tessa’s songs merge beautiful storytelling with wistful tunes that belong on film soundtracks. "A seemingly endless supply of comforting melodies" (RNZ).

description:
Nonconnah (USA) / 1/3 Octave Band, Nonconnah is an experimental music collective based in Memphis, Tennessee, headed by the husband-and-wife duo of Zachary Corsa and Denny Wilkerson Corsa.
Nonconnah creates haunting soundscapes and collages, often using antique or unusual instrumentation and obsolete recording technology to draw on themes of memory and the past, the supernatural, and the liminal spaces where the man-made and natural worlds meet.
Releases such as 2021's Songs for and About Ghosts are filled with warped lo-fi guitars, field recordings, grainy samples, and acoustic instrumentation, arranged into dreamlike sequences. The Corsas draw on a wide range of sonic influences, from shoegaze and post-rock to dark ambient to recurring motifs of old time/Appalachian mountain music.
A highly collaborative effort, Nonconnah has collaborated with past and present members of bands like Deerhoof, Swans, Earth, Broken Social Scene, Arcade Fire, A Silver Mt. Zion and many more.
http://nonconnahdrone.com
http://facebook.com/nonconnah

http://nonconnahordeath.bandcamp.com
---
1/3 Octave Band is the ambient/noise/drone project of Jules Desmond (Black Boned Angel) and Bill Wood (Birdcatcher) who conjure slow moving walls of eerie and epic electric guitar. Active since the late 90s, they've released a huge discography on labels like Celebrate PSI Phenomenon and Pseudo Arcana.
http://thirdoctaveband.bandcamp.com

description:
Nordic Voice Artist Anna Fält Returns to Aotearoa, Anna Fält is a versatile voice artist, composer and singing teacher with a deep passion for Nordic folk singing. She has toured widely across the Nordic region and beyond with her distinctive solo vocal concerts. Drawing on singing traditions from her two home countries, Finland and Sweden, she blends bright Scandinavian clarity with darker East European colours, performing in churches, museums, festivals, clubs and concert halls.
Her concerts celebrate the power of the human voice: a one woman band creating sound worlds you may have never heard before. Tradition meets vocal art, experimentation and storytelling in a personal and intimate way. Audiences everywhere connect to the honesty of an unaccompanied voice, no matter the language.
Alongside her solo work, Fält collaborates in performing arts and multidisciplinary projects, and is an active teacher and lecturer. She holds three music degrees and has studied folk music in five countries, but her central focus remains developing the art of solo a cappella performance. She has collaborated with several Aotearoa artists over the years, including film composer Karl Sölve Steven and taonga puoro player Rob Thorne.
Fält now returns to Aotearoa for her third tour, bringing her powerful voice and Nordic stories back to local audiences.
Koha entry.

description:
Nui Hui 7 - Fly High Brother Paul, Nui Hui 7 - Fly High Brother Paul
'In Rocking Memory of Paul Norris'
R.I.P Brother'

NUI HUI 7 – LIVE AT 14 WAIU STREET
Wainuiomata, Lower Hutt
Saturday 22 November 2025 | 4PM – LATE

Nui Hui is back – louder, prouder, and more unfiltered than ever. This grassroots music series is built for the people, by the people, shining a spotlight on bands who grind it out, carve their own paths, and keep live music alive.

Nui Hui 7 is a one-night-only collision of sounds and scenes, bringing together rock, reggae, punk, grunge, and soul against a true blue-collared backdrop. No industry machines, no corporate gloss – just raw, rising talent backed by the passion of locals and volunteers who believe in the power of music.

This year’s lineup is stacked with unsigned and upcoming artists from across the region and beyond:

4PM – Munkiez

With a sound as cheeky and chaotic as their name suggests, MUNKIEZ is a bluesy, funk-rock explosion that proves good times and great grooves go hand-in-hand. Hailing from Upper Hutt, this crew is all about embracing the raw energy of rock and roll while slathering on a thick coat of soulful, slinky funk.
They're not here to reinvent the wheel, but to make it spin faster, dirtier, and with a whole lot more swagger. With a dash of that no-nonsense, straight-outta-the-garage Kiwi attitude. MUNKIEZ are a band you feel in your bones, a sound that gets your head nodding and your feet moving before you even realize what's happening. They play it like they mean it, because they do.

5PM – The Groundsmen

Scott Paddock and Shane Martin formed The Groundsmen back in the heady days of 2017 and went through various drummers and bass players before finally finding stability with drummer Rowan Carlyle in 2018.

Since then they’ve played numerous gigs (one supporting Head Like A Hole in Gisborne at Smash Palace 30th anniversary) and released 3 singles on Spotify and other streaming platforms - Black Car, Supanova and Achtung Baby (check them out!).

They’ve recorded their debut album and are just about to mix it and release it.

Playing only original earthen rock punk, we always, always, perform at 110% energy levels and put on a great show with hooky uptempo toons!! With songs commenting on contemporary society and life at large all 3 members throw themselves fully into their performance and leave no energy unused. You will leave one of their shows changed.

See the excerpt from a review of a in Whanganui July 2020:

“After a quick change of equipment, The Groundsmen were next on the agenda. Proclaiming themselves to be Taranaki’s premier rock punk band, the trio wasted no time in belting out a hard and fast set of original, classic punk-inspired tunes that were lapped up by the growing gathering of punters. Bass player Scott Paddock is a tour-de-force; full of noise, energy and an appropriate rock-punk swagger. Along with guitarist Shane Martin and drummer Rowan Carlyle, The Groundsmen powered their way though and energetic set, and it was immediately evident that they were ecstatic to be back on stage and performing again after the recent enforced hiatus. The trio powered through a set of classic, no-frills, original punk inspired tracks that had almost everyone in the room either on their feet or gyrating in their seats. Definitely a crowd-pleaser, there is no doubt whatsoever that The Groundsmen were in their element, and clearly love what they do.”

….from Ambient Light, author Bridget Herlihy, 4th July 2020

6PM – Kaletta Band

Kaletta is a Latin rock band that brings together the rhythms of ska punk and gypsy sounds in Spanish. With musicians from Chile, Colombia, Argentina, Italy, the UK, and New Zealand, our sound is a blend of different beats and roots. We've had the privilege of being two-time national finalists in the Battle of the Bands (BOTB 2024 and 2025) and have performed at festivals like Island Bay and toured the top South Island. We're excited about our upcoming tours in New Zealand next year.

What we're passionate about is creating music that's true to ourselves. Each song is a journey, moving from calm to energetic moments that we hope will keep you engaged. Our lyrics touch on social and political themes, and we hope our performances will inspire thought and conversation. We're looking forward to sharing our music with you and creating memorable experiences through our dynamic sound and energy.

7PM – Burning Embers

Accustomed to breaching anything that requires sociable etiquette they still manage to pull off their unique brand of Wainuiomata rock.

From out of nowhere, they regroup, drink a few, set a plan, and do the complete opposite in tasteful fashion. Burning Embers have an uncanny habit of pulling off a great set, usually unscripted but full of the essence that is Rock n Roll. We're not here long enough to care, but we do love a great audience
Reminiscent of Days of the New and Alice in Chains they're definitely genuine entertainment

8PM – Stretch to Mould

Stretch to Mould is a rock band from Wellington New Zealand who formed in 2012. The band was founded by vocalist and guitarist Darrell Vickers, who has been the only constant member throughout multiple line up changes. Since 2024 the line up has consisted of Vickers alongside Chris Fursdon (bass guitar) and Thomas Fuller (Drums). Stretch to Mould are known for their high energy, hard hitting riffs, powerful vocals and all-round solid musicianship. The band released their debut album Shadows in 2012, EP Painting Faces in 2014 and are currently working on their next release.

9PM – Ras Judah and the Culture Embassy

a 10-piece NZ band of varying cultural backgrounds, hence the name.
The cultural diversity of the band is reflected in the sound of the music
a fusion of African styles, Reggae/Ska, Jazz and Afro-Latin rhythms.

We describe our sound as Afrocentric-World Music as much of what we play is based on African rhythms and songs, which is where our lead-singer ‘Ras Judah’ and two of our master drummers come from (Botswana, Ghana and Tanzania respectively), plus Roots Reggae. Though everyone contributes their own culturally inspired sound, with other band members from Cuba, England and Japan, and others with Greek, Kiwiana and jazz backgrounds. Not just a musical treat representing many parts of the world, but also a visual one; a carnival of ethnic diversity and collaboration on stage!

10PM – The Fabulous Pakehas

Were first conceived in London England, way back in the early 90s whilst on O.E's. Currently working on a album, & after 33 years, still in no rush.
With two of us having roots in WOA TFP are honoured to be playing a set of our originals for NUI HUI 7
The T.F.P original line up are, Antony Maddock, Scott McGill, Leslie Tearne, &
Bevan Ritchie.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

From soul-stirring grooves to fist-in-the-air anthems, Nui Hui 7 is more than just a gig – it’s a celebration of musicians who hustle, create, and share their art on their own terms.

Nui Hui: supporting local, celebrating original, and keeping the fire of live music burning

description:
O FORTUNA (Carmina Burana & Chichester Psalms), O FORTUNA (Carmina Burana & Chichester Psalms)
Prepare for a night of musical grandeur as Orpheus Choir Wellington and Auckland Choral, New Zealand’s largest city choirs, unite to present Orff’s monumental Carmina Burana. With its apocalyptic opening, O Fortuna, this masterpiece explores the capricious nature of fate, the joys and sorrows of life, and the boundless energy of human passion.

This performance will be mighty in scale, with nearly 300 performers on stage, including a children’s chorus, the combined power of two elite choirs, and the dynamic sound of the Wellington Brass Band. Add to this the extraordinary talents of soloists Emma Pearson (soprano), Coco Diaz (countertenor), and James Harrison (baritone), along with celebrated New Zealand pianists Jian Liu and Diedre Irons, and you have a musical event of epic proportions. From the raucous revelry of In Taberna (In the Tavern) to the sensual stillness of In Trutina (In the Balance), Carmina Burana is a visceral and unforgettable experience.

The concert opens with Bernstein’s radiant Chichester Psalms, a joyous blend of rhythmic vitality and heartfelt spirituality, providing the perfect prelude to the drama and intensity of Orff’s masterpiece.

RESERVE YOUR SEAT TODAY FOR THIS EPIC EVENT.
