description:
O Vere Beata Nox – O Truly Blessed Night, Settle into the rich acoustics of Erskine Chapel for this concert of deep listening, sacred voices, and transformation, as we celebrate darkness and the turning of time on the night of the winter solstice.

Featuring the immersive ambient electronica sounds of Tonic Collective; a taonga pūoro quartet with Riki Gooch, Al Fraser, Sam Palmer, and Ruby Solly; and a very special one-off appearance by Orchestra of Spheres performing on gongs, chimes and other instruments.

They are joined by Baroque Voices singing rarely heard works of 12th Century abbess St. Hildegard of Bingen.

This is a vigil of sound, depth and stillness — a space to rest, reflect, and be carried by sound through the depth of winter’s darkest night.

Live visuals created by Erica Sklenars (aka Lady Lazer Light).

– Music Schedule –
Tonic Collective (in the ballroom, between sets, and at close)
Taonga pūoro quartet: Riki Gooch, Al Fraser, Sam Palmer, Ruby Solly (45 mins)
Orchestra of Spheres (45 mins)
Baroque Voices (45 mins)
Grand Finale (15 mins)

Food and drink available at the venue.
This is a licensed event, U18s must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.
The evening will see the audience alternating between live acts in the upstairs chapel and the ambient electronica in the downstairs ballroom.

description:
O'Flynn | Wellington, O'Flynn | Wellington
WELLINGTON! O’Flynn makes his long-awaited New Zealand debut this September, arriving with a new album that captures him at a defining moment. 🌴

TICKET INFORMATION:
Pre-Sale Live: Wednesday 8th July, 10 am (NZT)
General On Sale: Thursday 9th July 10 am (NZT)

THESE TICKETS WILL GO FAST! GET IN EARLY, SIGN UP FOR PRE-SALE NOW.

Meow
Thursday 17th September | 8:00 pm - 12:00 am
Support from: Beccie B, Rydr

For over a decade, O’Flynn has quietly become one of the UK’s most respected producers and DJs, a singular voice in contemporary electronic music, grounded in dexterous production and an instinctive feel for the underground. His catalogue runs deep, shaped by curiosity, and marked by collaborations with artists such as Bonobo and Barry Can’t Swim.

Releasing music across Ninja Tune, Blip Discs, and his own imprint Hundred Flowers, O’Flynn’s work has earned support from tastemakers including Four Tet, Ben UFO, Gilles Peterson, and James Blake.

A pivotal moment came via Bonobo’s Fabric mix, which led to the collaborative track Otomo, a quietly monumental piece, and later saw O’Flynn join Bonobo on tour. Around the same time, he released Shimmer, a collaborative album with Frazer Ray via Ninja Tune’s Technicolour imprint, praised by DJ Mag as “a perfect cocktail of soaring emotions and bottom-heavy bass.”

Live, O’Flynn completed a five-week sold-out residency at London’s Phonox, followed by a sold-out headline show at KOKO, marking a clear step up in scale and demand.

In 2023, O’Flynn became a resident on Rinse FM, further cementing his role as both curator and craftsman. More recently, he delivered the inaugural release on Barry Can’t Swim’s Earth’s Only Paradise label, two tracks that stretched from disco-lit dancefloors to sharp-edged club pressure.

Now, O’Flynn returns with Kairos, his third full-length album, released July 17 via his own Panthus label. Named for the ancient Greek concept of the decisive moment, when conditions align, Kairos feels exactly that: a record where club energy meets patience, detail, and atmosphere. Music built for immersion.

This debut NZ tour marks the arrival of an artist fully in his stride, backed by an album rich in colour, tone, and intent.

description:
OUT IN BREWTOWN, OUT IN BREWTOWN
Wellington Pride Festival and Brewtown are proud to present:
💖OUT IN BREWTOWN

We can't wait to bring you our most fun, fabulous and inclusive night yet, in a super safe and friendly space, where everyone is welcome if they come with love and respect.

Get your glam on, feel gorgeous and bring the good vibes for a full-on party that celebrates our beautiful queer community! With pumping tunes and big energy in a space where we encourage you to express yourself and embrace your identity.

We'll see you on the dancefloor!

(A portion of ticket sales goes to support the excellent work of Wellington Pride Festival and Naming NZ).

🎵LADYHAWKE (DJ Set)
Headlining the night! Award-winning New Zealand artist Ladyhawke makes a long-awaited return to DJing, bringing her trademark mix of infectious energy and impeccable taste back to the dancefloor.

Best known for her genre-bending hits like My Delirium and Paris Is Burning, Ladyhawke’s DJ sets blend nostalgic anthems, Disco House, House and unexpected deep cuts — that will keep you moving all night!

🎵Bec Sandridge (Joining us from Australia)
Discovering Bec Sandridge feels like being let in on a secret.

A queer-pop shapeshifter with sharp angles, step-down black-and-white hair, and a voice somewhere between David Byrne and Kate Bush, Sandridge has been bending pop into performance art for over a decade. Her new single Always A Fan— co-produced with Nick Zaharias (MAY-A, The Buoys)—is the first from her upcoming album Happy Futures, featuring collaborators like Tony Buchen (G Flip, Smashing Pumpkins), Dave Jenkins Jr (Daniel Johns, Vera Blue, and Grammy-winner Cian Riordan (St Vincent, Lana Del Rey).

She’s supported Mitski, St. Vincent, Tegan and Sara, Ladyhawke, Kimbra, Yungblud; played
Reeperbahn, World Pride, Falls Festival; and appeared on The L Word, Q+A, and at Sydney Opera House.

Sandridge’s bold blend of theatre, fuzz pedals, and queer angst earned her Triple J rotation, an ISC finalist nod, and a sold-out 2024 Great Southern Nights show—the first in the series to do so.
Pop—bent, broken, and reassembled into something radically her own.

🎵Ardon England
Ardon England is a high impact live electronic artist from Aotearoa, delivering explosive, dancefloor driven performances that blur the line between club set and pop spectacle.

A proud Māori, queer artist with over two decades in the dance industry, Ardon’s shows are built around movement, precision, and presence — full body performance meets electronic pop at peak energy.

🎵Dateline
Led by bandleader Katie Everingham, Wellington’s stubborn driven indie-rocker’s deliver a performance that oozes emotion by blending earnest harmonies that hark back to early oo's indie pop, with cool burn of UK guitar groups from the 90s.

🎵Tahini Bikini
Pōneke based salad funk band. Dousing Aotearoa with smooth grooves & hummus.
Known for their distinctive sound, a combination of funk, soul and pop rock influences elevated by frontwoman Mads Taylor’s frank, feisty lyrics and smoky voice.

description:
OUT ON THE STREET - Music Posters from NZ and beyond - Thistle Gallery, An exhibition of Music Posters from New Zealand and beyond
Steve Cochrane has been collecting music posters since the late 1970s
By the mid eighties he was importing posters from Europe and selling them mail order through Rip It Up magazine, which evolved into both wholesale and retail
In 1985, Steve joined post punk luminaries Skank Attack and began pasting posters on Wellingtons streets. Eventually realising you could get paid for it, casual work for bars and clubs kept the gas tank full and led to his first poster distribution company The Stick Up!
After a much needed hiatus, Steve returned to the music industry a few years ago, via record and poster retail. Steve now runs Wellington poster company Pasted!, and remains an active musician and promoter
After decades of sporadic trading, Steve still has an extensive poster collection acquired from a vast array of sources. There's Flying Nun gems like Skeptics, The Chills, The Bats and Bailter Space, there's Shihad, Split Enz, and Space Waltz, along with NZ tour posters of REM, Elvis Costello, U2, Mick Jagger, Billy Bragg and many more
With a very small house and a huge collection, its time to start letting this stuff go for others to enjoy - consequently all works are for sale in the gallery or on our Trademe store
https://www.trademe.co.nz/.../stores/Out-On-The-Street

description:
OdESSA - Oak Park Avenue 20th Anniversary Show, Oak Park Avenue 20th Anniversary Show Oct 26th 5pm San Fran

Two decades ago, OdESSA kicked in the back door of the New Zealand
mainstream with their explosive debut Oak Park Avenue – a landmark
Indie-Funk record stacked with classics such as Bring The Money
Back, Baby Don’t Go Home, Promises Promises, Sugarpop, and I Could
Beat You In A Fight, the album captured the raw energy and swagger
of a band unafraid to push boundaries.

Now, 20 years later, OdESSA are back to celebrate the album that
started it all. On Labour Weekend, the band will take the stage at
Wellington’s iconic San Fran for a family-friendly early show,
performing Oak Park Avenue in full – plus a few surprises from their
wider catalogue. Expect high-octane grooves, infectious hooks, and the
kind of live energy that made OdESSA one of Aotearoa’s most beloved
live acts.

Joining them for this milestone event are rising stars of New Zealand’s
alt-pop scene Love Party. Known for their electrifying performances,
Love Party are the perfect complement to OdESSA’s funk-fueled legacy
– bringing fresh fire to a night that promises to be unforgettable.

Whether you were there in 2005 or discovering OdESSA for the first
time, this is a celebration of New Zealand music history you won’t
want to miss.

Tickets available now from moshtix.co.nz.

This very special folk event brings together Chris Priestley and Julian McKean of Acoustic Confusion and Angela Fox for a beautiful evening of song and guitar. Old friends, old favourites: the experience will be sublime listening!

description:
Om Unit (UK) & Roza Terenzi (AUS) at San Fran, GHOST MEDIA & TERMINAL45 PRESENT: OM UNIT (UK) & ROZA TERENZI (AUS) + SUPPORT FROM CURRENT BIA5 & KINDEKEL II 23 JANUARY @ SAN FRAN 

We're firing into 2026 in style! Ghost Media and Terminal 45 are teaming up to present two serious heavyweights of alternative dance music - OM UNIT (UK) and Roza Terenzi (AUS) 
Both of these artists are stalwarts in their own right, and we're seriously excited to present them side by side for the first time, in Pōneke, for a night of undeniable groove, bass, and energy. 
OM UNIT (Jim Coles) is a highly respected electronic music producer and DJ from the UK, known for pioneering genre-bending sounds, fusing jungle, dubstep, footwork, techno, ambient, and hip-hop into a unique style, as well as running the Cosmic Bridge Records label, and pushing boundaries with innovative sound design and releases like his influential "Threads" album and "Acid Dub Studies" project.
ROZA TERENZI (Katie Campbell) is an acclaimed Australian DJ, producer, and label head known for her eclectic, genre-bending electronic sound that blends techno, breakbeat, electro, trance, and jungle with "bush doof" energy. Her music offers futuristic, playful rave vibes, featured on labels like Planet Euphorique and Dekmantel, alongside her own imprint, Step Ball Chain, and since bringing her sound to Berlin she has cemented her status in the global underground scene.
With these two iconic figures in command of the tools, you can expect nothing but pure quality throughout, as we prepare to undergo a true sonic journey across flavours of acid, house, techno, jungle and whatever else the selectors decide to pull out of the bag. 
To begin the journey, we have local hero CURRENT BIAS, peddling their distinctive brand of atmospheric and deconstructed club music. Closing things out we have KINDEKEL II, another talented Pōneke selector with a knack for delivering pulsing, driving techno and rhythmic soundscapes. 
Tickets are available for $40, with a few $30 early birds in the mix. Get yours now and prepare for an absolutely stellar night of sonic vibrations!
label: Music & Concerts

description:
One Giant Leap for Slothkind, It's been a while since Neil Armsloth and Buzz Lightyear set theirs claw onto the surface of the moon... some say the footage was faked. Others even claim it was shot in the Moon Bar green room. All we know is the sloths are ready to blow the lid off the greatest cover-up in cosmic history - with a night of undeniably real tunes and bass heavy enough to shake the craters.

Join the investigation as these slow-moving sound scientists drop interstellar basslines, smoky skanks and lunar licks straight from the sea of tranquility (or maybe Raumati).

Bring your tinfoil hats, your dancing shoes and an open mind - because the truth is out there somewhere... and it sounds incredible.

About Oscar Lavën:
Oscar Lavën is an acclaimed saxophonist, multi-instrumentalist and composer based in Wellington, New Zealand. He has performed/recorded internationally with many artists/ensembles including Dave Weckl, Steve Gadd, Dennis Chambers, Lalah Hathaway, Gregg Bissonette, James Carter, Perter Erskine, Robben Ford, John Beasley's Grammy award winning MONK'estra, New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, Rodger Fox Big Band, Tony Lindsay, Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra, Royal New Zealand Air Force Jazz Orchestra, Rhombus, The Wellington City Shake Em On Downers, and more. His albums 'Questions in Red' and 'Elegant Calamity' received international acclaim with another soon to be released. A lover of jazz and blues, Lavën is also a busy classical performer on bassoon in orchestras, chamber groups and as a soloist, and also teaches in the jazz programme at the New Zealand School of Music at Victoria University.
Oscar Lavën plays Selmer Paris saxophones and clarinets, and is a Thick Records NZ recording artist.

description:
Oscar Lavën’s Rock ‘n’ Roll Sax, And we’re back! And not just for any new year, but for our 30th.
Besides a New Year, we also have a new venue, and lots of other great stuff coming for you in 2026.
Meanwhile, we have an old favourite to open up for us.
Yes, Oscar Lavën’s Rock ‘n’ Roll Sax will be our first act of 2026.
They always give us a high-energy show with lots of virtuoso playing. The band remains as popular as ever and is one of the acts people ask us to book again and again.
For those new to their music, they will be bringing you hot, honking, rock ‘n’ roll and R&B sax licks from saxophonists like Sam Butera, King Curtis, and Earl Bostic. Plenty of grooves and easy dancing music. Featuring Darren Mathiassen on drums, Patrick Bleakley on bass and Dean Hunter on guitar.
Our new venue also ticks all the boxes.
It’s Thunder Road on Blair St in the CBD, off Courtenay Place. Matt, the owner, used to run Jack Hackett’s, so knows Capital Blues and is looking forward to welcoming us back.
Besides being a handy location, it is ground level access with parking right outside, and buses are only 30m away. It also has a range of some fabulous beers and wines too. Not your everyday big brewery drinks, but top-quality brews. There are also great bar snacks, and well-trained staff. It’s everything you asked for.
The time is also what our members asked for, from 7 to 9pm.
Tickets are $20 or $10 for members, and there is a 10% discount at the bar for members.
As Muddy Waters said, “The blues had a baby, and named it rock ‘n’ roll.“
7pm at Thunder Road, see you there.

Other Futures Big Band - Wellington Jazz Festival, OTHER FUTURES BIG BAND is about multi-disciplinary excellence and celebration of our individual and collective voices in new ways. In this episode, anticipate steaming and reverent swing alongside triumphant soul, dark and scenic textures, and dripped-out golden-age hip-hop cuts. We celebrate artistry with dignity, respect and above all, joy. We swing hard. We groove like humanity depends on it. Groove with us at Meow Nui this Wellington Jazz Festival!
=========
OTHER FUTURES BIG BAND is where musical dreams come alive. It’s about the spark of true individuality, nestled in the art and community of ensemble. The thrill and drama of the showband era re-envisioned for our time. Selections that signify deeper meanings and secret codes. Turntablism sensibility on a symphonic scale. Streamlined, momentous, nimble, angular, adapting, shape-shifting, pulsating with relentless joy and emotion.
OTHER FUTURES BIG BAND is an ongoing project by Daniel Hayles that looks to honour elements of the big band tradition while platforming music and artists unexplored within the style. Expect to hear distinct flavour in new interpretations of original music from Aotearoa and the world.

Liszt - Étude in Db major, ‘Harmonie du soir’, S.139, No.11

Chopin - Barcarolle, Op.60

Biography:

Otis Prescott-Mason is one of New Zealand’s leading young pianists. He currently studies in Wellington under Dr Jian Liu and, in the United States, under Professor Boris Berman.

In 2025 Otis was awarded 3rd prize at the National Concerto Competition in Christchurch, performing Prokofiev’s 3rd concerto with the Christchurch Symphony. In 2022 he was awarded 1st prize, Best Performance of a Classical Sonata, and the Audience Choice Award at the Lewis Eady National Piano Competition. In the same year he was awarded 1st prize at the PACANZ National Piano Competition. Otis was also awarded 1st prize at the 2020 New Zealand Junior Piano Competition.

Now finished with undergraduate studies at the New Zealand School of Music in Wellington, Otis plans to pursue graduate study abroad in the near future.

description:
Out In Brewtown, Wellington Pride Festival and Brewtown are proud to present:
OUT IN BREWTOWN

We can't wait to bring you our most fun, fabulous and inclusive night yet, in a super safe and friendly space, where everyone is welcome if they come with love and respect.

Get your glam on, feel gorgeous and bring the good vibes for a full-on party that celebrates our beautiful queer community! With pumping tunes and big energy in a space where we encourage you to express yourself and embrace your identity.

We'll see you on the dancefloor!

(A portion of ticket sales goes to support the excellent work of Wellington Pride Festival and Naming NZ).

**LADYHAWKE (DJ Set)
Headlining the night! Award-winning New Zealand artist Ladyhawke makes a long-awaited return to DJing, bringing her trademark mix of infectious energy and impeccable taste back to the dancefloor.

Best known for her genre-bending hits like My Delirium and Paris Is Burning, Ladyhawke’s DJ sets blend nostalgic anthems, Disco House, House and unexpected deep cuts — that will keep you moving all night!

**Bec Sandridge (Aus)
Discovering Bec Sandridge feels like being let in on a secret.

A queer-pop shapeshifter with sharp angles, step-down black-and-white hair, and a voice somewhere between David Byrne and Kate Bush, Sandridge has been bending pop into performance art for over a decade. Her new single Always A Fan— co-produced with Nick Zaharias (MAY-A, The Buoys)—is the first from her upcoming album Happy Futures, featuring collaborators like Tony Buchen (G Flip, Smashing Pumpkins), Dave Jenkins Jr (Daniel Johns, Vera Blue, and Grammy-winner Cian Riordan (St Vincent, Lana Del Rey).

She’s supported Mitski, St. Vincent, Tegan and Sara, Ladyhawke, Kimbra, Yungblud; played
Reeperbahn, World Pride, Falls Festival; and appeared on The L Word, Q+A, and at Sydney Opera House.

Sandridge’s bold blend of theatre, fuzz pedals, and queer angst earned her Triple J rotation, an ISC finalist nod, and a sold-out 2024 Great Southern Nights show—the first in the series to do so.
Pop—bent, broken, and reassembled into something radically her own.

**Ardon England
Ardon England is a high impact live electronic artist from Aotearoa, delivering explosive, dancefloor driven performances that blur the line between club set and pop spectacle.

A proud Māori, queer artist with over two decades in the dance industry, Ardon’s shows are built around movement, precision, and presence — full body performance meets electronic pop at peak energy.

**Dateline
Led by bandleader Katie Everingham, Wellington’s stubborn driven indie-rocker’s deliver a performance that oozes emotion by blending earnest harmonies that hark back to early oo's indie pop, with cool burn of UK guitar groups from the 90s.

**Tahini Bikini
Pōneke based salad funk band. Dousing Aotearoa with smooth grooves & hummus.
Known for their distinctive sound, a combination of funk, soul and pop rock influences elevated by frontwoman Mads Taylor’s frank, feisty lyrics and smoky voice.

description:
PEBBLE - Free Live Music Wednesdays - Love In Every City, PEBBLE - Free Live Music Wednesdays - Love In Every City
Poems and Songs from the Road

After seasons of wandering through foreign cities, sharing songs with strangers, and capturing stories from the road. PEBBLE has spent the past few years on an open-ended journey: traveling across continents in search of the deepest stories, the wildest love, the purest expression of what it means to be human. From late-night train stations to hidden cafés, from sunlit rooftops to candlelit stages—PEBBLE has been gathering moments and melodies from everywhere he goes, transforming them into songs and poems that reflect a life lived wide open.

“Love in Every City” is the next chapter in that journey—a stripped-back, soul-forward performance that brings those stories home.

Backed by a vision to build a global movement of traveling artists who choose authenticity over perfection, connection over isolation, and creative ownership over compromise, PEBBLE’s work invites us to remember what we’re really here for: to live, to feel, to share.

This show is a moment of reflection and reconnection—
Join us for an intimate night of music, poetry, and storytelling at Moon in Newtown, Pōneke. A suitcase full of songs. A guitar by the table. A heart full of cities.

As always, free entry & all pizzas $15!

Listen >>> https://open.spotify.com/artist/2q9BwdeHhd7cmwTbsdPeil

PRINS | MESSY, YOUNG & ABLE WORLD TOUR, Following a breakout run of releases, international touring, and millions of streams across Spotify and social media, PRINS returns for her biggest headline shows to date.
Now based between Los Angeles and New Zealand, the Auckland-born pop artist has spent the past two years building momentum across New Zealand, Australia, Europe, and the United States, developing a reputation for emotionally charged alternative pop, razor-sharp visuals, and a live show that punches far above its weight. With influences spanning RAYE, Tate McRae, Doja Cat, and Don Toliver, PRINS blends vulnerability, confidence, chaos, and high-energy performance into a sound that feels both intimate and larger than life.
Fresh off performances across Germany, Australia, and the US, PRINS now brings her new era MESSY, YOUNG & ABLE to the stage for the very first time. Built around themes of ambition, imperfection, self-expression, and growing up in the social media era, the show combines full choreography, live performance, and the raw energy that has made PRINS one of New Zealand’s most exciting emerging pop artists.
With multiple chart placements, national radio support, and over 8 million Spotify streams to date, this marks the beginning of PRINS’ boldest chapter yet.

PALEFACE SWISS are the fastest rising force in heavy music today. Anyone who has borne witness to their live shows, critics and fans alike, can attest that their dominance is unassailable. Their trajectory unstoppable.
Hailing from Zürich, Paleface Swiss formed in 2017 and have rapidly climbed the ranks of the global heavy music scene with each album and EP. Frontman Marc “Zelli” Zellweger’s commanding vocals, paired with crushing riffs from guitarist Yannick Lehmann, thunderous bass from Tommy Lee, and pummelling drums courtesy of Luigi Paraventi, delivering a sound that blends old-school hardcore brutality with a full array of modern heaviness.
Joining the fray for this run of shows are Canadian metalcore legends, COUNTERPARTS and Colorado's heavyweight contenders, FOX LAKE.
COUNTERPARTS, fronted by metalcore's irrepressible poet laureate and agent provocateur, Brendan Murphy, are headliners in their own rights having already smashed their way around Australia to sell-out crowds and great acclaim.
Hamilton, Ontario's Counterparts are one of, if not the most respected names in the scene with a well earned a reputation for electrifying live performances and deeply personal songwriting that resonates with fans worldwide.
Putting the icing on this already insane tour are FOX LAKE. Formed in 2017 in Denver, Colorado, Fox Lake fuse heavy riffs, hip-hop, relentless energy and hardcore attitude into a powerful live spectacle. They are a growing global presence and redefining heavy music on their own terms.

description:
Paula Tape + Christopher Tubbs tickets, Paula Tape lands in Wellington at Meow Nui on Saturday 28 February, bringing her unmistakable blend of rhythm-forward house, Balearic warmth and cosmic disco to the dancefloor.
Originally from Santiago, Chile, Paula Tape (Paula Soto Carmona) is a multifaceted DJ, producer and fashion designer whose musical foundations were forged behind the drum kit in metal and indie-electro bands. That percussive instinct still drives her sound today, where classic house meets sun-kissed Balearic moods and left-of-centre club cuts. As the founder of Tempo Dischi, she’s built a platform dedicated to adventurous dance music—championing disco, afro and cosmic influences while spotlighting emerging artists from across the globe.
Joining Paula Tape on the night is Christopher Tubbs, Aotearoa DJ royalty and a recent collaborator with Paula: Christopher’s and Eden Burns’s ‘Drums Are Dangerous’ (feat Paula Tape) came out last year on Germany’s Public Possession, to widespread acclaim.
Christopher Tubbs is a DJ, producer, and broadcaster. More than that he is a true godfather of the New Zealand dance music scene. His productions as Tubbs, Atlantic Conveyor and collaborations with Eden Burns for Public Possession have resulted in strong support from luminaries as varied as Gilles Peterson, Mark Ronson, Zane Lowe, Optimo and Axel Boman.
As a globetrotting DJ, Christopher Tubbs has played at almost every notable club internationally, from Privilege in Ibiza to Fabric in London. Christopher also co-owned the cult vinyl-only record label Untracked (heavily supported by the likes of Mark Ronson and Gilles Peterson), giving debut releases to underground heroes Red Rack’em and NZ’s very own Frank Booker.

description:
Peter Hobbs - Live 3D AV Indietronica with Isaac Levi Tucker, Miss Leading and Gotal Bournier, Peter Hobbs - Live 3D AV Indietronica with Isaac Levi Tucker, Miss Leading and Gotal Bournier
To celebrate the upcoming release of his 11th album, ground-breaking electronic artist and composer Peter Hobbs is touring his new 3D AV show around Aotearoa in Oct-Nov 2025. He is joined in Wellington by drummer extraordinaire Isaac Levi Tucker, producer-performer-poet Miss Leading, Raiatea synth artist Gotal Bournier and dancer Tokyo dancer Misako Kikuchi.

Peter Hobbs
Known for his award-winning cinematic and emotional body of work in recordings and immersive art works, Hobbs' new album Panpsychism is a vehicle for his masterful songwriting driven by experimental beats on a highway of immersive synth soundscapes, through an immersive visual-reactive world.
He is performing his modular synths and immersive AV show alongside legendary percussionist and drummer Isaac Levi Tucker.
Miss Leading
An electronic music producer, singer and poet. Her music aims to widen your mind while moving your body with a mix of pop, hip-hop, spoken ambient and dance tracks with a conscious perspective in relation to race, feminism, sexuality and environment. Her debut album Minor Thing received five-star reviews and gained critical acclaim by independent music magazines across the UK, Brazil, Germany and the USA, including being labelled UK Artist of the Week by The Vinyl District.

Gotal Bournier
Gotal Bournier is a French electronic musician living between Tahiti and Tokyo. Between 2012 and 2017 he released four albums in Japan with the band Lo-shi. Since 2018 he has been based on the island of Raʻiātea, working on solo recordings and various live collaborative projects. His current solo project is a playful and wryly nostalgic live soundtrack to a video collage of Cold War Era science fiction films using the spectral, alien tones of twin modular synthesisers.

Misako Kikuchi
After studying classical ballet at an early age, Tokyo-born dancer Misako Kikuchi went on to explore modern ballet, contemporary dance, street dance and flamenco, while refining her own improvisational approach. Her performances create uncontrived moments of beauty that make you feel that being alive is not irreconcilable with being free

description:
Pianist Michael Endres, TOP EUROPEAN CONCERT PIANIST IN FEATHERSTON and PAEKAKARIKI's MEMORIAL HALL
MULLED WINE CONCERTS PRESENTS MICHAEL ENDRES

Wairarapa and Kapiti classical music enthusiasts have been giving a warm reception to the Mulled Wine Concert series presented by Mary Gow. The series has so far covered concerts ranging from formal piano recitals through harp and flute duos to a full-on big-band jazz session. With valued support from local arts organisations and hopeful of support from commercial sponsors, Gow – a concert pianist herself – is intent on building upon her success to present a further series of concerts in the Wairarapa during 2026.

The highly regarded German pianist Michael Endres will return again to give a piano recital for Mulled Wine Concert in Featherston's Anzac Hall on Saturday 25 July at 4:00 PM and in Paekakariki's Memorial Hall on Sunday 26 July at 2.30 PM
International critics have described Endres as "one of the most interesting pianists recording today". He has released 35 CDs during his career and his extensive prizewinning discography includes the prestigious Diapason d’Or (France) which he was recently awarded for the third time and the Choc du Musique which he has won twice. He has appeared at major festivals and concert-halls all over the world. A prominent academic musician, Endres had a distinguished teaching career in Germany, Norway and New Zealand before he decided to concentrate on performance and recording.

His reviews from music publications have been outstanding: Diapason magazine said of his 2018 release “An acoustic which allows the piano to resonate with a fullness, a brilliance without hardness, and a breadth of sonority which is ideal for Schubert, these works chosen by Michael Endres flow endlessly between jubilation and drama.”

Both Featherston and Paekakariki programmes will include the Mozart Sonata K281, Schubert's Impromptus, Op. 90 and Liszt's Sonata in B minor.

Mulled Wine Concerts organiser Mary Gow says, " We are very excited to be continuing our presentation of concerts in Featherston and Paekakariki. As before, our objective is to present the best music while keeping admission prices at an affordable level. The wonderful ANZAC Hall in Featherston and the Memorial Hall in Paekakariki have excellent acoustics and a splendid piano. What a pleasure it will be to hear exquisite music in such a pleasant settings!"


========= ENDS =========

description:
Pieces of Blue ~ Pieces of Peace - Ian Logan and friends, Pianist, artist, and composer Ian Logan returns with bassist Alistair McLeod for a deeply moving performance inspired by the theme of compassion. Their programme opens with a rich tribute to the blues in all its forms—raw and gutsy, melancholy and joyful.
Tickets: $20
jazzfestival.nz / Ticketmaster / Under the Radar
Door sales
Tickets: https://www.undertheradar.co.nz/.../Pieces-of-BluePieces...
Doors open 7.10pm.

The second half, Pieces of Peace, explores the universal longing for harmony and transformation, drawing inspiration from Bill Evans, Horace Silver, and the eclectic sensibility of Charlie Haden. Blending originals, jazz standards, and works shaped by classical and European singer-songwriter traditions, the set also features the premiere of a multi-media tribute to German expressionist artist Käthe Kollwitz.This will be an original song by Ian Logan interpreted in movement by a guest Aotearoa dancer, echoing Kollwitz's recurring theme of the terrible plight of women protecting children - particularly relevant in today's war-torn world.

Audiences can expect music that revels in emotional depth, from the intimacy of slow adagios to the power of improvisation. Between sets, enjoy light refreshments and an art exhibition—a thoughtful counterpoint to the evening’s music. Koha is welcome to support Island Bay Presbyterian Church’s community outreach.

description:
Pip Payne with Richard Klein and Al Norman, PIP PAYNE, a regular player and founder of Capital Blues is back with another musical variation. Pip has had many artistic guises over the years which shows not only his versatility but also his depth of the music. This time he is joined by two outstanding musicians bring you some Louisiana blues and cajun.
RICHARD KLEIN is a high energy singing fiddler born in Orange, New Jersey. In his early teens he discovered folk and roots music through listening to the likes of Woody Guthrie, Pete Seeger and The New Lost City Ramblers. Travelling to Cape Breton Island in mid 1970s sparked the interest for Celtic music that later brought Richard to travel, live, work and busk extensively through Ireland and the British Isles. A chance meeting with a gang of Swedish fiddlers in Shetland in 1978 introduced another important influence in his fiddle style. But it was being properly introduced to Cajun music later that same year in France that had the most profound impact on his music. Resident in Wellington since 1997, Richard is best known for his collaboration with the Le Blanc Brothers Cajun Band (Melbourne) and the geographically challenged Kiwi Americana band. T-Bone. In 2023 he relinquished his American citizenship. The accent, however, remains.
AL NORMAN has been on the Wellington scene for a while. Early blues club jams and bands, on squeeze box and keys. For this gig it’s the squeeze box or snare. A multi-instrumentalist with a great feel for the groove. He’s been part of a number of well-established groups including Smokeshop, Warratahs, Laura Collins Band and still plays with the Rag Poets and, less regularly, The Hardcore Troubadours. He has also played a number of gigs offshore and toured NZ extensively.
Come and join us for another fine session featuring some virtuoso playing with a twist on the blues.
Tickets are $20 or $10 for members, with bar discounts for paid-up club membership.

Pipe Band Reunion Rehearsal

We look forward to celebrating this historical moment with you!

description:
Postmodern Jukebox [WELLINGTON], Postmodern Jukebox [WELLINGTON]
The world’s foremost purveyors of time-twisting hits, Postmodern Jukebox, have announced their highly-anticipated return to Australia and New Zealand in June and July 2026!

Having previously performed multiple sold-out tours across Oceania, the trailblazing troupe of singers, dancers and instrumentalists will hit our shores with their brand new The Future is Vintage tour.

“In the midst of the AI hype all around us, some folks have gone so far as to proclaim that in the not-so-distant future, all of the music that we listen to will be AI generated – we’ll gladly take the other side of that wager,” says PMJ founder and arranger, Scott Bradlee. “We’re humbly presenting our own unique vision of a spectacular future; one that is built upon the timeless musical genres of the past and the authentically human spirit of creativity that inspired them.”

Concertgoers can expect to enter a parallel musical universe where modern-day earworms and iconic pop tracks alike are reimagined. Expect everything from ’70s rock classics and ’80s Britpop hits, to current chart-toppers, movie and video game soundtracks. Dress in your vintage best, for the full time-travel experience!

A TEG Dainty presale begins on Thursday November 20 at 11am (local). Sign up for access:

https://www.tegdainty.com/tour/postmodernjukebox2026/

Tickets to general public go on sale on Friday November 21 at 11am (local).

description:
Powers / Marrowspawn / Impress, Powers is the current incarnation of Campbell Kneale who has ping-ponged about the nether regions of interstellar sound for close to thirty earth-years aboard sonic spacecraft such as Birchville Cat Motel, Black Boned Angel, and Our Love Will Destroy the World. Known primarily as the captain of his own ship, Campbell Kneale has also collaborated and performed with some of outsider music’s most defiant and diverse experimentalists: Lee Ranaldo and Thurston Moore (Sonic Youth), Merzbow, Stephen O’Malley (Sunn O))), Keiji Haino, Borbetomagus, Phill Niblock, and Tony Conrad to name a few. Whereas the vast majority of Kneale's music revolves around the fastidious manipulation of the multitracking process, Powers pounds on the thin cracking ice of an ‘everything-all-at once’ mindset, performing and recording his immersive blitzkrieg ragas entirely in the moment.
sunsettemples.bandcamp.com campbellkneale.bandcamp.com
Marrowspawn fuses the mechanical precision of drum machine grindcore with black metal, doom and shoegaze. Described as sounding like a 'bulldozer made of hydrochloric acid'. www.marrowspawn.bandcamp.com
Impress is the moniker attributed to the mysterious sound-conjurations of Sam Curtis. What you hear is what you heard.

Pub Sing, Pub Sing - where the audience (you) turns into the choir at the pub, with a live rock band.

No sheet music, no experience needed, and absolutely no solos.

Katy reveals three songs on the night (usually a crowd-pleaser, a ballad, and a banger), and even if you don’t know them, you’ll pick them up fast with colour-coded lyrics on screen.

description:
Public Service Broadcasting tickets, Handsome Tours presents the return of London-based sonic outfit Public Service Broadcasting who return to Australia and New Zealand in May, bringing their powerful, cinematic live show to audiences across the southern hemisphere.
Since emerging into existence in 2009, Public Service Broadcasting – led by instrumentalist-auteur J. Willgoose, Esq. – have forged a singular musical identity, transforming archival narratives into rousing, emotionally resonant works that blend post-rock, electronics and orchestral grandeur.
Across a celebrated catalogue including Inform-Educate-Entertain, The Race For Space, Every Valley, Bright Magic, the spectacular BBC Proms-recorded This New Noise, and their most recent work The Last Flight, the band have explored human endeavour, collective memory and the restless drive to push beyond known limits.
Sonically rich and emotionally expansive, Public Service Broadcasting’s music evokes motion, risk and wonder – from propulsive hymns of flight to moments of haunting stillness. As ever, their meticulous storytelling and immersive live performance elevate history into something urgent and deeply human.
Renowned for their visually arresting shows and ability to turn historical narratives into shared, communal experiences, Public Service Broadcasting’s return to Australia and New Zealand promises an unforgettable live encounter – one that is at once awe-inspiring, moving and exhilarating.

description:
Public performance: New Zealand Secondary Students’ Choir — Part of Mahuru Māori 2025 series, We are delighted to welcome the New Zealand Secondary Students’ Choir and their infectious joy in music-making to Te Whanganui-a-Tara. This will be their first public appearance of the 2025–2026 cycle. Come and hear our nation’s youngest and most talented choral singers as we celebrate Mahuru Māori.
We’re in for another treat this Mahuru Māori at the National Library. Last year, Te Rōpū Rangatahi Waiata o Aotearoa The New Zealand Youth Choir gave a public concert to celebrate this special month, and now the teina — The New Zealand Secondary Students’ choir (NZSSC) — will appear for a public performance as their tuakana did, performing waiata to celebrate te ātaahua hoki o te reo tūturu o Aotearoa.
Bring your hoa, your colleagues and your whānau kia whakanuia ēnei rangatahi me te reo rangatira — this concert is not to be missed!
Nau mai te katoa! Everyone is welcome!
About the choir
The New Zealand Secondary Students’ Choir has achieved considerable success since its formation in 1986. NZSSC has won titles such as Children’s Choir of the World at Llangollen Eisteddfod 2022, and over their near 40-year existence, embarked on 15 international tours, including Canada, Singapore, China, the United States, South America, Australia, and South Africa.
Under the direction of Sue Densem, the NZSSC is a tira waiata of Aotearoa’s finest young voices (14–18) and offers a two-year membership where rangatahi tour throughout the country and learn from some of the country’s top choral teachers and composers. At the end of their two-year cycle, the rōpū rounds out their membership term by embarking on an international tour, performing concerts and competing in choral festivals.
New Zealand Secondary Students’ Choir website: https://www.nzsschoir.com/
Image: Kaiwaiata of the New Zealand Secondary Students’ Choir perform in China (2024).

Pumpkinhead celebrate the 30th anniversary of their critically acclaimed album Sloth this year, performing three exclusive never to be repeated reunion shows.

Sloth entered the New Zealand Album Charts on 30 April 1995, peaked at number 28 and stayed in the charts for 4 weeks. Their single “I Like” made it to number 16 in the Official Top 40 singles chart 10 March 1995.

“Now “Sloth”, Pumpkinhead’s debut album, compresses the quintet’s live energy into a head spinning whirlpool of fierce punky rock, powerful pop, and tempo-hopping Faith No More style metal. Not for the innocent!” – 4.5 stars – NZ HERALD 1995

description:
REforms: Shayne P. Carter and the NZSO, It’s an amalgamation of two musical worlds, and the result is set to be mesmerising. Shayne P Carter has been active on the New Zealand popular music scene since 1979. The singer-songwriter has penned many great tunes. Now, some of those tunes are getting an orchestral treatment thanks to the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra. REforms reimagines ten of Shayne’s songs in magical orchestra colour. 
With arrangements by Tane Upjohn Beatson and conducted by Hamish McKeich, the concert promises to enhance Shayne’s songs through a new lens while keeping their original integrity. Classic songs like Randolph’s Going Home and If I Were You sit alongside new numbers like Left To Defend. Songs from Shayne’s solo album Offsider also feature. 
Shayne is best known for leading indie rock band Straitjacket Fits from 1986 to 1994, and rock band Dimmer (1995–2012). He is a member of the New Zealand Music Hall of Fame and the recipient of several Aotearoa Music Awards.

description:
REforms: Shayne P. Carter and the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, The heft and glory of the NZSO collide with the Shayne P. Carter songbook for the world premiere of this formidable work. Ten tracks ‘reformed’ in orchestral technicolour while maintaining the integrity of the originals.

Classic songs like Randolph’s Going Home and If I Were You spar with new numbers like Left To Defend. Guitar and orchestra do battle on the mighty Crystalator. Songs from Carter’s solo Offsider album expand from their original two-finger piano primitivism into widescreen epicness. Other songs glower with the drama of orchestral restraint.

With arrangements by Tane Upjohn Beatson and conducted by Hamish McKeich, REforms is a singular and purposeful artistic statement; an immersive and all-encompassing performance from a world-class orchestra and one of Aotearoa’s greatest singer/songwriters.

description:
RIVERS OF NIHIL - NZ TOUR, Pennsylvanias progressive death metal progenitors Rivers of Nihil make their first voyage to Aotearoa New Zealand.
The quartets musicianship has been honed to a fine point thanks to an unrelenting touring schedule over the past few years, including headline tours of the U.S. and EU/UK, as well as touring with Cattle Decapitation, Carnifex, Lorna Shore, Between the Buried and Me, and touring with titans of progressive death metal Cynic, Beyond Creation, and Dååth.
Life on the road for Rivers is a treat for fans and band members alike. For the most part, its very mellow, with a lot of laughs and a lot of ball-busting. Andy (Guitar, Vocals), and I have been friends for over 15 years, and Jared (Drums) has been in the fold since 2017 says founding member/guitarist Brody Uttley. Founding bassist Adam Biggs became the bands new lead vocalist/bassist in 2023, which upped the ante and led to the release of self-titled album Rivers of Nihil (2025). Traditionally, a self-titled record can signal a return to basics and/or a fresh beginning, and in 10 powerful songs, its clear that both those factors are in play. I feel like these songs are the perfect blend of all our albums, with all the fat cut away, says Uttley.
River of Nihil have riffs, big choruses, the prog, the solos, the sax and now it will have Aotearoa New Zealand
Tickets vi UTR

This will be the first time either of these artists has been to Aoteaora, and we're honored to be bringing their sounds together for this one-off showcase.
ROHAAN delivers a complex sound that bridges emotional weight and technical precision. His work stretches across drum & bass, halftime, dubstep and experimental club music, with a catalogue that feels equally at home in headphones or on a dark dancefloor. Rohaan can be considered one of the genre's true prodigies, with releases on a broad range of labels including VISION, Hospital Records, Circus Records, Sable Valley, UKF and Shogun Audio.
Alongside him we have ENIGMA DUBZ, another UK-based producer with a style following in the deep dubstep tradition, firmly rooted in atmosphere and groove. With a uniquely warm and melancholic sound, the sound of Enigma Dubz conveys a journey through the spaces between. He has also released on some serious labels, including DUPLOC, Deep Dark and Dangerous, Slime Recordings and his own Morii Records imprint.
Completing the lineup we have two of our favourite local selectors warming things up - leftfield bass maestro PULSE and supreme dubstep selectress BARBWYRE.
High vibes are not only expected but mandatory - cop your ticket now and strap in for a sonic odyssey!

AfroKan plays 100% authentic and totally danceable Afro-Cuban and Latin Jazz with a bit of Salsa and Cha Cha Cha on top, and is a collaboration between resident Afro-Latino and top-end loca jazzl musicians..

Its repetoire includes compositions by Afro-Cuban Jazz greats such as Chucho Valdéz, Carlos “Patato” Valdéz, Poncho Sánchez, Rubén González and Orlando “Maraca” Valle amongst others.

Tonight's ensemble features:

- Rafael Ferrer Noel (Cuba) - vocals and congas

- Mikey Trujillo Rodriguez (Perú) - vocals and bongos

- John Rae (Scotland) - drums and timbales

- Daniel Windsor (Wellington) - trumpet

- Oscar Lavën (Wellington) - Tenor Saxophone

description:
Rain & the Urban Bohemians @ Firebird w/Mercy Lie, Araiyah, Rain & the Urban Bohemians @ Firebird w/Mercy Lie, Araiyah
Join us for a magical evening of music at Firebird Café, Levin.

Three amazing Wellington acts are coming through to present their beautiful sounds and share their heart and soul with you. We warmly invite you to join us and become a part of this collaboration of creativity and connection; spanning triumph and heartbreak, and everything in between, celebrating all it means to be human.

Our wonderful hosts at Firebird Café will be serving their delicious food and creating a warm and inviting atmosphere.

Tickets are $15 online or $20 on the door.

Mercy Lie:

Driving all night under the stars, along the highways of human experience, the original songs of Mercy Lie will haunt, surprise, remind and affirm.

Mercy Lie is the musical guise of Laura Chester-Murphy. An instinctive sound maker from an early age, Laura just wants to keep the music rolling. There’s a lot of sound from that little acoustic guitar and a voice to match. In the songs, you will find fierce independence, crushing vulnerability and a reflective wit that speaks to a life of figuring stuff out along the way.

With influences ranging across and not limited to folk, funk, country, goth, indie and 90’s rave, Laura puts the focus on crafting percussive earworms that won’t leave your head easily. The music of Mercy Lie is a unique soundscape, sculpted with ambience and depth, the silence unforgettably painted by explorations into the motivations of both the self and fellow travellers.

Mercy Lie is about connecting over the foibles of polite society and the ways we are wired to weave around each other.

Hometowns, journeys, mysteries, ghosts, growing up, messing up, speaking out, moving on. If you like getting nostalgic over something and nothing all at once, buckle up.

“Mercy Lie’s novel approach to the guitar and talent for songwriting make for the perfect storm.”
“I did not expect that voice to come from that mouth.”
“An acoustic delight!”

Araiyah & Izzy:

Born in the coastal town of Patea and raised in the vibrant community of Gisborne, Araiyah’s musical journey is as rich and diverse as her heritage. Now based in Wellington, she is not just a musician but a devoted mother of four tamariki and a proud grandmother to one mokopuna. For the past decade, Araiyah has poured her heart into writing, recording, and performing her original compositions, each note resonating with the depth of her experiences.

Araiyah’s music is a poignant reflection of her life’s journey, weaving together themes of love, loss, and resilience. Her deeply moving compositions are rooted in the lessons learned through relationships and the pain that often accompanies them. Through her art, she shares a narrative of healing, transformation, and the strength that comes from embracing vulnerability.

Their support and love provide the foundation upon which her music thrives, making each performance an authentic expression of her gratitude and connection to those who matter most.

With a voice that captivates and lyrics that resonate, Araiyah invites listeners into her world—a place where pain transforms into beauty, and healing becomes a shared experience. description:
Raven Mavens Quartette CD Launch - Upclose & Personal, Raven Mavens CD launch. Be one of the first to hear and see the Raven Mavens Quartette's new music. They will be playing the songs on their new CD as well as some long time favourites.

Since releasing their last album of original songs in 2020 the band has continued to delight audiences throughout Wellington, the Wairarapa and the Kāpiti Coast with their distinctive blend of blues, roots, folk and swing influences.

The Raven Mavens have become renowned for their catchy, blues-infused original songs, written primarily by band leader Cindy Muggeridge. Drawing on her deep roots in blues piano, as well as Latin rhythms and rock ’n’ roll grooves, Cindy's latest collection tells stories of life, love and loss, alongside wry social and political observations. In both performance and recording, she is joined by the exceptional talents of Kate Marshall on vocals, violin, accordion and flute; Marian Carter on vocals, saxophone, clarinet and recorder; and Anje Glindemann on vocals, drums and percussion.

The band is also excited to feature two original compositions by Kate Marshall on this new recording, with Kate taking the lead on piano, supported by the other Mavens.

A unique all-female ensemble, the Raven Mavens Quartette gives every member the opportunity to shine as both instrumentalist and vocalist. Each member is a gifted musician and singer in her own right, but together they create a musical chemistry that is greater than the sum of its parts. Their rich combination of voices and instruments produces a sound more often associated with a much larger ensemble. Audiences can expect humour, passion, warmth and exuberance, all in service of songs that remain firmly at the heart of the performance.

Join the Raven Mavens Quartette for an afternoon celebrating original music, masterful musicianship and the release of a remarkable new collection of songs. Refreshments available for a gold coin.

description:
Raven Mavens Quartette in concert, Raven Mavens Quartette
Suppose you can imagine the sound of the blues, spiced by flavours of the American songbook, folk, country, and even the rock and roll of Jerry Lee Lewis, driven by the unmistakable sound of boogie woogie piano. In that case, you have the Raven Mavens Quartette.  

It is both an accident and it isn’t that this is an all-female group. The group had its genesis a decade ago when piano player and singer-songwriter Cindy Muggeridge encountered the singing and clarinet skills of Marian Carter. They formed the Raven Mavens as a duo that included a core of folk and blues, and exploited the singing talents of the pair through finely crafted harmonies.  

The success of their combination in playing local gigs and folk festivals opened up opportunities with other musicians, and the next step was the inclusion of drummer Anje Glindemann, who has played in a list of local bands, including Tin Pan Alley, Hen Picked and more recently the Salty Hearts. Anje can also be seen performing with Kapiti Coast singer-songwriter icon Andrew London.  And finally, the addition of multi-instrumentalist Kate Marshall. “Kate is an amazing player”, Cindy says. “She can move as easily from piano accordion, to fiddle or flute, depending on what the song calls for - or she feels like playing!” And of course, like the other members of the group, she sings.  

The instrumental diversity of the line-up was now established, but what also distinguishes this group is the addition of Cindy Muggeridge’s original songs to the set. “Writing my own songs has been part of the musical journey for me”, says Cindy, “and it just led naturally to offering some of them to the other singers in the group”. The “fun” of their music and the unmistakable presence of four female musical masters is what they will be sharing when they play at The Offering as part of Greytown ArtTown.

Buy tickets in advance here or txt bookings to 02102361951.

Please note The Offering is fully licensed and will be serving snacks and drinks. Please note this concert replaces Bob McNeill and Emily Roughton due to illness.

UK Indie Rock icons RAZORLIGHT head to New Zealand for the first time ever to perform a headline show in Wellington as part of their ‘’America’’ world tour! The band are celebrating the 20th anniversary of their 5x Platinum self-titled album, a landmark release that cemented their place among the defining acts of the early 2000’s indie scene.
With era-shaping hits like ‘America’, ‘In The Morning’ and ‘Before I Fall To Pieces’, Razorlight became one of the UK’s most successful guitar bands of their generation, delivering three Top 5 albums, multiple Platinum certifications, winning an NME Award, and performing on some of the world’s biggest stages.
Razorlight’s live shows channel the same hook-laden, post-punk-infused energy that defines their sound, but amplified into something harder, tighter and far more intense.
Their melodic swagger of early-2000s indie, driven by a restless passion makes every track feel like it’s about to ignite. Their sets tend to move with a kind of breathless momentum, tight rhythms, bright guitar lines, and delivery that between exposed emotion and a sharp, commanding force. Live, Razorlight animate the entire room.
‘’Razorlight reminded fans why they won their hearts with a masterful performance featuring astonishing electric guitar riffs and impeccable stage craft yet again from Borrell.’’ – The Upcoming

This summer, three of Aotearoa’s most beloved bands hit the road for Ready To Roll, a brand-new touring show celebrating New Zealand music and sun-soaked good times. Featuring the legendary Th’ Dudes, iconic Mockers, and multi-platinum favourites Stellar*, the tour will bring timeless hits and unforgettable live energy to some of the country’s most picturesque summer locations.

Ready To Roll pays homage to the iconic TV music chart show that ran from the 1970s through to the 1990s. As New Zealand’s homegrown version of the Top 40 countdown, Ready To Roll became appointment viewing for generations of music fans, a showcase for both international chart-toppers and breakthrough Kiwi acts. It helped launch and cement countless careers while becoming a cultural touchstone in Aotearoa. Reviving the name for this tour nods to its legacy of celebrating great music and good times, a perfect fit for a summer series featuring three of the country’s most enduring and much-loved groups.

description:
Real Black For Me: Zoe Moon presents the music of Roberta Flack, Roberta Flack made an indelible mark on modern popular music.
Over the course of her career, Flack wrote and performed songs that blended jazz, folk, gospel, and R&B into something uniquely her own — music defined by elegance, intimacy, and emotional depth deeply rooted in celebration of black American culture.
From the quiet intensity of The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face to the gently insistent Killing Me Softly with His Song, her recordings
remain timeless, proven again and again by the ways they’ve been reimagined.
In Real Black For Me, artist Zoe Moon and her band — featuring a live string section — revisit and reimagine this extraordinary body of work through a shared sense of the “strange kind of power” of self defined identity.
These arrangements, which Moon has crafted alongside renowned Wellington big band leader, bass player and composer Seth Boy, bring fresh colour and sophistication to Flack’s most celebrated songs alongside lesser-known but equally captivating gems, tracing the arc of an artist whose voice could fill a room or break a heart with a whisper.
An evening for lovers of great songwriting, luminous vocals, and the enduring legacy of one of music’s finest storytellers.
Doors 6.30pm | Show 7pm

description:
Renaissance Gold - in celebration with Manawatū Sinfonia featuring Bach's Magnificat, Renaissance Gold - in celebration with Manawatū Sinfonia featuring Bach's Magnificat
On Saturday 13 September, at 7.00 pm in the Cathedral of the Holy Spirit on Broadway, PN, the choir under Christine Archer-Lockwood is to be joined by the Manawatu Sinfonia and soloists, Caroline Hickman, Jennifer Little and Lindsay Yeo with choristers Nigel Tongs and Bronté Hodgetts also singing solo in Bach's Magnificat. The Magnificat is a world favourite, arguably Bach's best choral piece that has transcended the ages, celebrating Luke's description of Mary's pregnancy.

In addition, the choir and orchestra perform Ritchie's Then I Understood. When a child of seven to nine, Laura Rangers sketched eight poems centred on summers at Otaki Beach, Ritchie seized the opportunity to add the musical dimension and the result are dual choirs - the Renaissance Singers split - accompanied by the Sinfonia to set off Rangers' delightful insights, so elegantly displayed. The magic that can be childhood.

The concert has a celebratory theme, it being the 50th anniversary of the choir. Thus the inclusion of Forrest's Three Nocturnes that express the wonderment involved when examining the heavens and the universe full of stars. Throughout this piece the percussionists alone from the Sinfonia provide whimsical accompaniment with a celeste providing the heavenly tones - a hit when played on the last occasion the choir sang the piece.

Opening the concert will be Carl Orff's O Fortuna from his popular Carmina Burana. While O Fortuna laments the role of fate it is set in the larger piece that celebrates life with gusto.

With the performers in great form (two choristers just back from singing with the world's best choir) this concert will no doubt build the sense of celebration - full of life and wonderment.

General Admission $25, Concession $20, Secondary School $15,
Under 13 Free.

Revulva Presents: Global Pussy - Get Phoebe To New York! Fundraiser, That’s right - Revulva are reuniting for one final hit in Wellington: a fundraising show to get Phoebe to New York City!

Easing you into summer, Revulva will play two sets at everyone's second home (the Rogue & Vagabond) on Saturday 6th December as a final fundraising effort to get the band’s leader, Phoebe Johnson, to New York to study a masters degree at the New School for January 2026.

After their last sold out home show at Meow in April for the Album Reminder Tour - the band hugged goodbye unsure of when they would reunite next, everyone heading seperate ways for the foreseeable. With international plans delayed, the original Wellington lineup are coming together one last time to see off Phoebe for her next chapter in New York City.

Phoebe began Revulva in 2019 in her final year of jazz performance at Te Kōkī New Zealand School of Music to throw a funky, theatrical, 8-piece hat into the Wellington scene. Since then the band have released two chart topping albums, toured the country up and down with several sold out shows, numerous sweaty festival slots, they’ve opened for international acts such as Mononeon, Snarky Puppy, and Donny Benet, as well as making first ventures overseas with a sold out show in London last month. And now, Revulva will spread its wings to the United States.

There will be guests, merch, maybe a sausage sizzle or bake sale if the Rogue let us. Tickets will go live on UTR on Wednesday 12th November - one last “I Love Pussy” on three!

description:
Rhian Sheehan & Arli Liberman - Traces Album Release Tour - Wellington, Rhian Sheehan & Arli Liberman - Traces Album Release Tour - Wellington
TICKETS FROM https://bit.ly/46xIJWo

ONE WELLINGTON SHOW ONLY - Friday Nov 21, The Great Hall at Massey University

Loop are proud to announce that acclaimed New Zealand musicians, composers and producers Rhian Sheehan and Arli Liberman will bring their collaborative album Traces to life for the first time ever, with a special three-show tour this November.

The tour will see the pair perform the album in its entirety at a series of intimate shows in Auckland, Wellington & Christchurch. These shows will see them accompanied by Ed Zuccollo and Riki Pirihi aka Riki Gooch (TrinityRoots, Orchestra Of Spheres) to bring the album to the stage.

Stream the album here - https://ffm.to/traces-album

This tour marks the long-awaited debut live performance of Traces, an instrumental journey blending electronic, ambient and post-rock soundscapes to create a world unlike anything else — described by filmmaker Sam Kelly as “an ethereal journey through dark and moody worlds.”

For the first time, audiences will be able to experience this collaboration in a live setting. With both artists renowned for their powerful, emotive performances and their ability to craft immersive sound journeys, these shows promise to be as visually striking as they are sonically transporting. Live performances from both Sheehan and Liberman are a rare treat, and this will be only the second-time ever both musicians will be performing together live.

Each show will see Sheehan and Liberman joined by two collaborators on stage to help bring the worlds created in Traces to life. Ed Zuccollo will bring his trademark synth-wizardry to the stage, as he did across a number of tracks on the album. His trademark sound has seen him perform with the likes of Troy Kingi, Kita, The Black Seeds and more, in addition to his own solo work as Zuke. Riki Pirihi aka Riki Gooch is one of NZ’s most celebrated musicians for his work with TrinityRoots, Fat Freddy’s Drop, Cave Circles, and countless others.

The four musicians will combine to perform Traces live, with the second half of the show featuring all four musicians collaborating live on stage with tracks from each artist’s individual catalogues.

These shows will also feature the stunning visuals created for the project by Dunedin-based visual artist Sam Caldwell, which are featured across the album cover and music videos. The Traces live experience will be a richly layered audio and visual feast, unlike anything either artist has performed before..

Tickets go on sale Thursday September 25. Audiences are encouraged to secure theirs early — with only three shows nationwide, these performances promise to be rare, unforgettable events. Presented by Loop, thanks to Manuka Phuel.

description:
Rhythm & Dance - Wellington, Rhythm & Dance - Wellington
Stamp the beat and feel the heat in this concert of pan-American dance, jazz and pizzazz!

Programme
John Adams The Chairman Dances
Copland Clarinet Concerto
Gabriela Ortiz Antrópolis (NZ Premiere)
Bernstein Symphonic Dances from West Side Story

Gemma New’s signature “strength, clarity and grace” (WTTW News) invigorates this 20th century American classic, Bernstein’s Symphonic Dances from West Side Story. In depicting a New York gangland Romeo and Juliet, Bernstein’s score captures an irrepressible American swagger. Rhythm & Dance also infuses John Adams’ The Chairman Dances, an outtake of Adams’ opera Nixon in China, which imagines the young Chairman Mao dancing the foxtrot with his mistress.

Aaron Copland’s Clarinet Concerto melds Latin American popular music with jazz in this work commissioned by “The King of Swing” Benny Goodman. And we proudly present the Kiwi premiere of Gabriela Ortiz’s Antrópolis. Grammy Award-winning Ortiz is one of Mexico’s hottest contemporary composers, and this work refers to el antro, Mexican slang for a nightclub.

In association with New Zealand Herald.

description:
Riki Pirihi - Master Drummer - Night 1, Pyramid Club is excited to present master drummer Riki Pirihi, in a performance residency over 2 nights and an afternoon participatory Conduction workshop.
Riki Pirihi (Ngāti Wai, Patuharakeke, Ngāti Māhanga) is one of the most important musicians of his generation in Aotearoa. As a drummer he has been the rhythmic force behind a huge number of bands and A-list mucisians including Trinity Roots, Fat Freddy's Drop, Connan Mockasin, Anika Moa, Jonathan Crayford, Crowded House, Recloose, Ladi6, Orchestra of Spheres and Dave Dobbyn to name but a few. Working solo under Cave Circles, Riki is constantly reinventing his music, from experimental electronics to taonga pūoro.
Recently Riki completed a Doctor of Musical Arts degree centred on the cultivation of a unique musical language, Rangatuone, which intertwines the principles of Conduction (improvised conducting) with expressive signs and gestures, tailored specifically for the composition and performance of taonga pūoro alongside Western instruments.
Through all this astonishing variety of musical settings, Riki's foundation has always been in improvisation, and it's with pleasure that we welcome him home to Pyramid Club for two nights of improvised collaborations with a diverse lineup of artists from Wellington's creative music family.
Riki will play solo, duo, trio and quartet sets on both the Friday and Saturday night concerts, and will lead a participatory conduction workshop on Saturday afternoon.
SCHEDULE:
Night 1 - Fri 31 July
Riki Pirihi solo
duo w/ Anthony Donaldson
trio w/ Nell Thomas, Simon O'Rorke
quartet w/ Kiva Pirihi, Erika Grant, Jonny Marks

Riki Pirihi solo
duo w/ Alistair Fraser
trio w/ Daniel Beban, David Long
quartet w/ Bridget Kelly, Tom Callwood, Toby Laing

Saturday 1 August 2:30pm - Conduction Workshop

Ringlets EU/UK Fundraiser at San Fran, Wellington, Ringlets are soon heading off. March & April allows them just enough time to pack up an international driving permit, some muesli bars, and a set of guitar strings (can also be used as floss if you don’t mind a little blood) into a polka-dot bindle. May will then see them embark on a five week long tour of Europe & the United Kingdom. They also have a number of bookings later into the year, so they think they’ll stay on.
You can help them out: these two final headline shows – a shameless shake of the tip jar – in Wellington on April 10th, and Auckland on April 11th will be a chance for you to send them off in style. In the bands hometown of Auckland there will also be a garage sale (anything that didn’t fit into the bindle will be flogged off) alongside some actually high-quality merch and small trinkets exclusive to these fundraiser shows (Merch available in both cities).
Presented by Junk Mail & 100% Good

description:
Rivers of Nihil - NZ Tour, Pennsylvanias progressive death metal progenitors Rivers of Nihil make their first voyage to Aotearoa New Zealand.

The quartets musicianship has been honed to a fine point thanks to an unrelenting touring schedule over the past few years, including headline tours of the U.S. and EU/UK, as well as touring with Cattle Decapitation, Carnifex, Lorna Shore, Between the Buried and Me, and touring with titans of progressive death metal Cynic, Beyond Creation, and Dååth.

Life on the road for Rivers is a treat for fans and band members alike. For the most part, its very mellow, with a lot of laughs and a lot of ball-busting. Andy (Guitar, Vocals), and I have been friends for over 15 years, and Jared (Drums) has been in the fold since 2017 says founding member/guitarist Brody Uttley. Founding bassist Adam Biggs became the bands new lead vocalist/bassist in 2023, which upped the ante and led to the release of self-titled album Rivers of Nihil (2025). Traditionally, a self-titled record can signal a return to basics and/or a fresh beginning, and in 10 powerful songs, its clear that both those factors are in play. I feel like these songs are the perfect blend of all our albums, with all the fat cut away, says Uttley.

River of Nihil have riffs, big choruses, the prog, the solos, the sax and now it will have Aotearoa New Zealand

description:
Rivers of Nihil, Pennsylvanias progressive death metal progenitors Rivers of Nihil make their first voyage to Aotearoa New Zealand.

The quartets musicianship has been honed to a fine point thanks to an unrelenting touring schedule over the past few years, including headline tours of the U.S. and EU/UK, as well as touring with Cattle Decapitation, Carnifex, Lorna Shore, Between the Buried and Me, and touring with titans of progressive death metal Cynic, Beyond Creation, and Dååth.

Life on the road for Rivers is a treat for fans and band members alike. For the most part, its very mellow, with a lot of laughs and a lot of ball-busting. Andy (Guitar, Vocals), and I have been friends for over 15 years, and Jared (Drums) has been in the fold since 2017 says founding member/guitarist Brody Uttley. Founding bassist Adam Biggs became the bands new lead vocalist/bassist in 2023, which upped the ante and led to the release of self-titled album Rivers of Nihil (2025). Traditionally, a self-titled record can signal a return to basics and/or a fresh beginning, and in 10 powerful songs, its clear that both those factors are in play. I feel like these songs are the perfect blend of all our albums, with all the fat cut away, says Uttley.

River of Nihil have riffs, big choruses, the prog, the solos, the sax and now it will have Aotearoa New Zealand

description:
Rob Thomas - The All Night Days Tour, Multi-platinum singer-songwriter Rob Thomas today announced three nationwide New Zealand dates on his global The All Night Days Tour, celebrating his forthcoming sixth solo album All Night Days and the 20th anniversary of his acclaimed debut solo record …Something to Be.

The All Night Days Tour will travel to theatres this November, taking in Auckland’s Kiri Te Kanawa Theatre on Tuesday 11th, Te Pae Christchurch Convention Centre on Thursday 13th, before finishing up at Wellington’s Michael Fowler Centre on Saturday 15th.

Promoted in New Zealand by TEG Van Egmond, this highly anticipated tour marks Rob’s first New Zealand solo headline shows, and follows last year’s sold-out tour with Matchbox Twenty.

"After such amazing Matchbox shows in 2024, it’s so great to revisit the solo catalogue, and I can't wait to come back and share these songs with my Kiwi fans. It’s going to be a very special run of shows," said Thomas.

Managing Director of TEG Van Egmond, Christo Van Egmond said “We’re absolutely thrilled to be bringing Rob Thomas back to New Zealand for this incredible run of shows. To see an artist of his calibre in intimate theatre settings is a rare treat, and it’s going to be a truly memorable experience for fans around the country.”

The upcoming tour promises to deliver the captivating live performances that Thomas is known for, and audiences can expect a night filled with timeless hits including “Lonely No More,” “This Is How A Heart Breaks,” “Her Diamonds,” “Street Corner Symphony,” the Grammy-winning Santana collaboration “Smooth,” as well as Matchbox Twenty favourites like “3AM” and “Unwell.” Rob will also perform his powerful new single “Hard To Be Happy,” giving fans a taste of All Night Days.

Romeo & Juliet - Wellington, Benjamin Northey conducts a programme pulsing with the intimate power of love itself, featuring cellist Li-wei Qin.
Programme:
Kenneth Young Douce Tristesse
Barber Cello Concerto
Prokofiev Selections From Romeo And Juliet
Sergei Prokofiev’s Romeo and Juliet is one of the greatest ballet scores of all time. Among the courtly grandeur of Dance of the Knights, the circling, slicing, jabbing music of Death of Tybalt, and the crunching dissonances symbolising the Montagues versus the Capulets, swirls the indescribably sweet lyricism of Romeo and Juliet’s eternal love.
The same emotional depth can be found in Barber’s Cello Concerto, performed by virtuoso Li-Wei Qin. Celebrated for a sound both “incisive and searing, yet filled with tenderness” (Straits Times), Qin will steep Barber’s concerto in deep feeling and passion. Sweet nostalgia reigns in the “drifting, Ravelian waltz” (New Zealand Herald) of Kenneth Young’s Douce Tristesse.

description:
Romi Wrights And Leao, This October, two of Aotearoa’s brightest talents come together for a one-night-only double headline show in Te Whanganui-a-Tara.
On Saturday, October 18th, 60s soul, funk, and R&B revivalists Romi Wrights & the Commotions join forces with fellow "niu-wave" sonic explorers LEAO for their debut headline performances in the capital.

Don’t miss this celebration of era-blending, electrifying Pacific journeys through sound.


LEAO

Formed from a Pacific heart, LEAO is a Samoan musical project led by guitarist/vocalist David Feauai-Afaese, joined by bassist Navakatoa Tekela-Pule, Hawaiian-steel guitarist Levi Gemmell, and drummer Larsen Tito-Taylor. With a deep adoration for Pacific musical reference points and a desire to explore new sonic ground, LEAO synthesises non-traditional tonalities with a fa‘asamoa spirit, creating what some have called “niu wave” and “Pacific neo-psychedelia.” A creative enigma and phenomenal live act since the release of their critically acclaimed debut GHOST ROADS in 2019, LEAO has continued to expand its vision with the 2024 single TAEAO / MEA UMA - a sparkling glimpse into a significant body of alternative Pacific music currently in development. The group is now actively working towards the release of a new full-length album, deepening their bold contribution to contemporary Pacific sound.



Romi Wrights

Although she grew up on the sensibilities of US RnB and Hip-hop, when the Tokelauan singer-songwriter Romi Wrights shares her voice, it’s hard not to feel transported back to the spirit of the late 1960s soul/funk era by her incandescent melodies and stirring stories of love, loss and the confusion that lies in between. Raised between Porirua and the Hutt Valley, Romi started writing diaristic poetry at age eight before beginning to set her words to music during her teenage years.



After finishing high school, she moved to Tāmaki Makaurau (Auckland) to study music at the EXCEL School of Performing Arts and pursue her dreams of being a singer. Several years later she formed the gospel, funk and soul band The Elected, who spent three years performing at venues like Portland Public House, Kings Arms and Golden Dawn.


Since 2021, she has been working alongside Mānuka Recordings co-founder Kenny Sterling and a cast of session musicians and backing vocalists, including Julien Dyne, Cory Champion, Olivia Wilding, JY Lee. In December 2023, Wrights opened for soul legend Lee Fields, at the Hollywood Avondale, and has since performed twice at Pōneke festival CubaDupa. Via Mānuka Recordings, she has released 3 singles; Bring It Back, Without You and Capsized and has an album scheduled for release mid to late 2025.

Rust Your Mind Away, The Undercurrent presents Rust Your Mind Away!
Evie Patterson's grandpa (John Patterson) was a poet who published books filled entirely with four stanza poems, with four lines in each stanza, made up of four words with four letters each. After reading his books, Evie formed an understanding of his way of expression without really ever getting to know him, and from there created a musical concept inspired by it. This year will be 10 years since he passed, and before Evie leaves Aotearoa (to attend music school in Verona, Italy) she would love to celebrate his life by performing this music in tribute to him.
Evie Patterson will be on saxophone, John Rae on drums, Theo Thompson on guitar and Daniel Yeabsley on bass.
Thursday July 30
Doors 7pm
Music 7:30pm
$15
Tickets available online or at the door!
https://www.undertheradar.co.nz/.../Rust-Your-Mind-Away.utr

description:
Ryosuke Kiyasu (Japan) / Ritual Heaps, We are super excited to welcome Japan's Ryosuke Kiyasu back to Pyramid Club for a special one-off performance, following his sold out 2024 show, . Ryosuke Kiyasu has captivated the world with his solo performances. Using only a snare drum, he viscerally explores the sonic complexities of a single instrument.
A driving force in the avant-garde music scene for over two decades, Ryosuke Kiyasu has been a prolific solo performer, while also contributing to the group SETE STAR SEPT and serving as the drummer for Keiji Haino’s legendary ensemble, Fushitsusha. Performing over 200 shows annually across the globe, Ryosuke Kiyasu continues to redefine the very concept of music.
His solo performances have been featured on BBC News and VICE Magazine, and he garnered over 23 millon views on his 2018 performance in Berlin. He has released more than 200 albums, both solo and with his band.
————
Opening the show will be Ritual Heaps, who is psychic defence music. Durational synth fortifications from Whanganui/Te Awakairangi.
