description:
Songwriters' Saturday, Welcome to July Songwriters' Saturday at The Realm!

We have another exciting evening of homegrown music planned for your enjoyment. Things kick off at 6.30 p.m. with the first of three acts. Your host venue, The Realm, is fully seated, with Bar and Restaurant facilities available and is close to bus services. Reservations can be made online or by phone.

Parking is free and, on the street, with easy access from the front of the building. The music ends around 9 o'clock.

About the Artists:

Stephen Hill is a songwriter based in Lower Hutt in Aotearoa New Zealand. Born and raised in Ireland he moved to Wellington in 2008. Stephen performs his folksy songs with an understated delivery but keen pop sensibility, weaving landscapes and emotions with an eye for detail and a refreshing turn of phrase. Inspired by Irish songwriters like Damien Dempsey and Iain Archer, as well as local artists like Delaney Davidson and international heavyweights like Nick Cave and Steve Earle, Stephen’s style is alternately light and dark, silly and serious, calm yet entertaining.

Janine Mitchell is a singer songwriter who performs heartfelt songs in the sixties and seventies era folk tradition. Her writing style often reflects, and is inspired by, folk singers such as Joan Baez, Bob Dylan, Simon and Garfunkel. With her guitar accompaniment and fine lyrical vocals, she sings and writes from the heart, crossing the borders of social, personal and environmental territories.


The Grey Dog band comprises four wizened hamsters who bravely continue to run on the Eternal Wheel of Attrition. Their music is like clear mountain streams, like balm after the cut and thrust of battle, like the sinuous dance of the cobra, like the cold laughter of the galaxies. They have friends in high and low places, so if you don’t like their songs - it’s probably best not to say so.
They are John Broadbent – vocals, guitar and harmonica, Martyn Parlane – vocals and guitar, Graeme “Grey Dog” Sullivan – bass and vocals and Greg Bates - drums.

Organized by Rachel Hird

songwriting muse. Since that time, he has been transitioning from a blues-based artist singing other people's tunes to a singer songwriter who now performs mostly his own tunes.

Soul In Motion (Wellington), SOUL IN MOTION: WELLINGTON

If you’re someone who appreciates the deeper and more soulful side of DNB, this one is for you. Ghost Media and Afters are teaming up to present the Pōneke leg of Soul In Motion’s first ever Aotearoa residency.
Expect a high-octane, full spectrum night of future music straight from the heart, headlined by none other than Soul In Motion’s top dog, NEED FOR MIRRORS.
Joe Moses aka NEED FOR MIRRORS is a true legend of the game, one of the genre’s most prolific and experimental artists, a constant presence in the record crates of many.
Presiding over a distinctly angular and confrontational sound, he has worked with some of the genre’s most esteemed labels, including V Recordings, Souped Up, Metalheadz and Thirtyone Recordings. In 2017, he established his own label - Soul In Motion, which over time has established itself of one of the premier labels and club nights in DNB, with over 40 releases from legends such as Jonny L, Bungle, Mark System, Lynx, Javano and more.
Joining Need For Mirrors we have two of SIM’s brightest stars - Ōtautahi-based pair AUTOMATIC and SINGR.
Both of these producers have been working hard producing tracks for Soul In Motion, receiving all sorts of international recognition and popping up in your favourite DJ’s track listings.
This tour represents an opportunity for them to showcase their sound domestically and demonstrate what the underground of Aotearoa drum n bass really sounds like in 2026.
Opening things up, we have the capital’s busiest selector, PEARLY. Fresh off a run touring with the legendary Shapeshifter, Pearly is an expert in deep and soulful drum and bass, and is planning to open up proceedings with a thoughtfully curated mix of liquid and classic 90s dnb.
On closing duties, we’ve called up Wellington’s very own OG, D-DOG, for a masterclass . After skanking out to him open for Grooverider a couple months ago, we were reminded of D-Dog’s supremacy on the decks, and for a night celebrating drum n bass at its truest and most uncompromising, we couldn’t think of anyone better to close.
On microphone duties of course is Young Gho$t. A man of many genres, he makes no secret about his love for drum n bass, and is exalted for a night that truly celebrates the sound in the way that he perceives it.
Capacity is strictly limited for this one, with $30 early birds available from Humanitix. Secure yours now, and prepare for some serious grooving with these sound providers at the capital’s newest club.

description:
Sounding Boards, Sounding Boards
What happens when composers become each other’s teachers, critics, and friends?

Sounding Boards celebrates the musical friendships that changed history. From Mozart and Haydn trading ideas around a quartet table to Mendelssohn, Schumann, and Brahms inspiring one another across generations, these relationships sparked creativity that continues to resonate today.

Across Europe and beyond, composers shaped each other’s voices through mentorship, collaboration, and shared curiosity. Fauré and Saint‑Saëns sustained a lifelong artistic partnership, Bartók and Kodály transformed folk research into modern composition, and Copland, Bernstein, and Barber forged a distinctly American sound. Holst and Vaughan Williams, trusted companions in craft, helped define English music for a new century.

Join the Bach Choir for Sounding Boards, a concert woven from these remarkable connections.
This programme brings together music born from friendship, respect, and shared artistic vision, inviting audiences to hear how great composers shaped one another and the worlds they lived in.

Soundscape Series: The Weather Machine, The Weather Machine brings an electrifying blend of soulful longing, theatrical glam, and retro-nostalgic indie rock to the stage. Their live shows are dynamic and heartfelt, weaving together lush arrangements, unexpected instrumentation, and soaring vocal performances. With violin, sax, clarinet, and layered harmonies in the mix, audiences can expect a genre-blurring experience that feels both intimate and cinematic. Whether it’s a delicate folk tune or a full-throttle rock anthem, The Weather Machine delivers each moment with passion, precision, and a deep love for musical storytelling.

The Weather Machine began as the brainchild of Portland, Oregon songwriter Slater Smith. What started as a DIY indie-folk project in the city’s vibrant underground scene has since evolved into a professional, internationally touring band. Over the years, they’ve shared stages with acts like The Lumineers, Alabama Shakes, and Cold War Kids. In 2021, Smith relocated to Te Whanganui-a-Tara, Aotearoa, bringing the project with him and forming a new Wellington-based lineup. Now spanning two continents, The Weather Machine continues to expand its sound with a fresh, collaborative spirit.

Australia’s South Summit are coming back to New Zealand in support of their new album ‘RUN IT BACK’ (released 12th June). The ‘RUN IT BACK New Zealand Tour’ see’s South Summit return to Queenstown, Lyttleton, Auckland and Wellington for an epic run of their iconic high energy shows.

‘RUN IT BACK’ marks the bands second album release, and has featured singles ‘TOP OF THE HILL’ and ‘ON THE DASH’. The twelve-track collection of music represents a period of experimentation for the band; one where they found themselves pulled towards threads of funk, hip hop and R&B, while also driven by a desire to galvanise their signature blend of reggae and rock.

The New Zealand tour promises South Summit’s energetic live performance, with tracks from the new album mixed in with some classic fan favourites.

South Summit ‘RUN IT BACK’ New Zealand Tour | Wellington, South Summit are soon to release their sophomore album, RUN IT BACK on June 12 and to celebrate, they have announced RUN IT BACK NZ TOUR.
Coming to Aotearoa this July and August the band will take on Queenstown hotspot Yonder on Thursday 30 July, The Loons, Lyttleton on Friday 31 July, San Fran, Wellington on Saturday 1 August and Auckland’s Double Whammy on Sunday 2 August. 
Run It Back marks the band's second album, featuring stand out singles ‘TOP OF THE HILL’ and ‘ON THE DASH’ which have sent strong signals toward the confident evolution of their sound. The twelve-track record  represents a period of experimentation for the band; one where they found themselves pulled towards threads of funk, hip hop and R&B, while also driven by a desire to galvanise their signature blend of reggae and rock.
In 2024, they released their highly anticipated debut album The Bliss, a reggae-infused indie rock record that showcased both tight songwriting and a willingness to experiment across styles. It debuted at #2 on the ARIA Album Charts and propelled the band into a new tier, with heavy Triple J support, major festival slots and international touring, including appearances at Falls Festival, Groovin The Moo, SXSW Sydney, Vivid LIVE Debut at the Sydney Opera House plus a huge Australasian headline tour.
After a recent visit to Aotearoa to play at Six 60’s new Country & Roots Festival Sweet Home Aotearoa, South Summit now return to New Zealand for their third headline tour in the country. These four shows promise the bands’ renowned live charisma and classic fan favourites, whilst welcoming fans into a brand new era.

The Soweto Gospel Choir is a 30-member ensemble that blends African gospel, spirituals, reggae and American popular music into rousing concerts. For its Wellington concert, the choir will present songs and anthems from Nelson Mandela’s Freedom Movement in South Africa and the Civil Rights Movement of Dr Martin Luther King’s America. There will also be contemporary classics. Hear songs by legendary artists Elvis Presley, Sam Cooke, Cynthia Erivo, Stevie Wonder, and Aretha Franklin. 
Since it formed in 2002, the Soweto Gospel Choir has performed around the world. The choir is dedicated to celebrating the unique and inspirational power of South African Gospel music. It’s won numerous awards, including three Grammy Awards for Best Traditional World Music Album.

description:
Split Enz — Forever Enz Tour, During their recording career, Split Enz released a string of hits across the late 70s and early 80s. Those songs quickly gained notoriety and defined an era for many New Zealanders. Now, for the first time in nearly 20 years, the band has reunited for a New Zealand tour. Featuring original members Tim Finn, Neil Finn, Eddie Rayner and Noel Crombie, the Split Enz — Forever Tour will remind audiences of the band’s huge creative talent. Songs include I Got You, I See Red, Message To My Girl, Six Months In A Leaky Boat, History Never Repeats, One Step Ahead, and plenty more. 
Formed in New Zealand in 1972 before relocating to Australia in 1975, Split Enz is widely regarded as one of the most important antipodean groups of the last five decades. Their number one, 1980 album release, “True Colours”, achieved multiple-platinum status in Aotearoa and was certified five times platinum in Australia, selling over 250,000 copies. In 2005, Split Enz were inducted into the ARIA Hall of Fame. Says founding member Tim Finn — “Aotearoa, rugged individual! We’re looking forward to climbing into our new Noel Crombie suits and seeing you all soon.”

Squeeze tickets, Presented by: Destroy All Lines
British legends Squeeze are returning to New Zealand in April 2027 with their Tried, Tested and Trixies Tour, celebrating 53 years of classic songwriting and standout music hits from one of the UK’s pioneers of Brit-pop music.
Founded in 1974 by Chris Difford and Glenn Tilbrook, Squeeze are one of pop’s best-loved bands with a catalogue of sky-high classics such as ‘Up the Junction’, ‘Tempted’, ‘Cool for Cats’, ‘Another Nail in My Heart’ and ‘Labelled with Love’, whose live shows are legendary and, as The Guardian wrote, “pop perfection”.
Squeeze remain one of the most revered and distinctive music outfits in UK pop history. Led by the unparalleled songwriting duo Glenn Tilbrook and Chris Difford, their legacy spans over five decades of masterful songwriting, stellar live performance, and cultural impact; between 1978 and 1996 they had no fewer than 11 singles in the UK Top 40, with six in the Top 20. Many more of their songs have been woven into the very fabric of the British songwriting tradition – alongside those of The Beatles and The Kinks – influencing everyone from Lily Allen to The Killers.
Coming to New Zealand to mark 50+ years of Squeeze and celebrate the release of their new album, Trixies, will be Glenn Tilbrook, bassist Owen Biddle, percussionist Steve Smith, keyboardist Stephen Large, drummer Simon Hanson, guitarist Leon Tilbrook and backing vocalist Danica Dora.

description:
Stephen Gallagher, David Long & Jules Desmond / Amy Jean Barnett, Formed for the Altared States series, the trio of Stephen Gallagher, David Long & Jules Desmond make long-form cinematic soundscapes with effected cello, electronics and guitar.
Stephen Gallagher is an Emmy award-winning composer and music editor who has worked on an extensive range of projects, from global blockbusters to television and contemporary dance. Most recently, he completed the score for The Lord of the Rings: The War of the Rohirrim, directed by Kenji Kamiyama. Gallagher's work spans collaborations with Peter Jackson, Brian Eno, Ed Sheeran, Nick Cave, and many more.
David Long is a composer, performer, founding member of The Mutton Birds, and member of easy listening noise band, Teeth. His career has spanned over 40 years and seen him work on numerous projects to commercial and critical acclaim. In his own words he likes to "mash shit up", creating orchestral scores that utilise "not only classical instruments but all sorts of things".
Jules Desmond is an experimental musician who has played in bands including Letterbox Lambs, 1/3 Octave Band, Bachelor of Architecture and Black Boned Angel.
https://www.stephen-gallagher.com/
https://www.davidlongnz.com/
---
Amy Jean Barnett is a composer and artist working with sound, performance, installation and acoustic ecology in her practice.
Barnett's live performances weave intricate narratives through sound, drawing on electroacoustic techniques, minimalism, and field recordings. Working with recorded fragments, improvisation, and a tactile engagement with materials, she creates auditory environments of shifting textures that invite deep listening and reveal the subtle complexities of sound unfolding over time.
Barnett is currently pursuing a Master of Musical Arts at the New Zealand School of Music under the supervision of Michael Norris.

description:
Steve ‘Dog’ Hall and Karen Clarke @ The RSC, Steve ‘Dog’ Hall and Karen Clarke @ The RSC
***STEVE 'DOG' HALL & KAREN CLARKE BLUES WOMAN @ RAUMATI SOCIAL CLUB, FRIDAY 6 MARCH***

When these two heavyweight roots artists fire up it’s “groove on” for sure. Steve “Dog” Hall and Karen Clarke Blues Woman bring a powerful, groove-laden blues sound. Individually impressive, together formidable. Guitars weaving, sparring, and locking into a rhythm that just won’t quit. It’s music that lives in the pocket — gritty, warm, and full of pulse — every note feels hand-tooled and every lyric bleeds a little.

Clarke and Hall are seasoned players with miles of road and story behind them. Karen’s soulful vocals and rhythm guitar are steeped in Taranaki grit, while Steve brings decades of blues fire from years on the road. Together they forge a sound that stretches from Mississippi to Chicago to right here at home in Aotearoa — familiar, yet freshly alive and definitely cranking.

Yes-siree their show is raw crankin’ rhythm and good-time groove — songs that sweat, grin, and shake the dust loose. Guitars growl, harmonies soar, and the crowd leans in to the blues stripped back to the bone.

>>>>>Wellington’s Steve “Dog” Hall is a blues guitarist with serious bite — a road-hardened player known for his searing tone, inventive slide work, and grinding rhythm drive.
A songwriter at heart, Hall brings grit, groove, and attitude to every stage he steps on - and there’s been plenty.
Before turning full-tilt toward the blues, Steve spent 17 years in deep with NZ’s premier heavy-metal outfit Confessor, earning his reputation across Australasia as a fearless, high-voltage performer — serving up heavy, groove-laden bass and searing electric guitar night after night.
He later shifted gears into roots and blues, lighting up stages with Swamp Dixie, the Frog and Dog duo, and as a key member of Wellington’s famed Caramello Blues Band, traversing genres with both acoustic and electric flair.
When Dog plugs in, guitars growl, amps snarl, and the blues moan, howl and bite back.

>>>>>From wind-beaten stages in the lower North Island to late-night sessions deep in the Taranaki back blocks, Karen Clarke has been holding down the groove for decades. Now a rising force in Aotearoa‘s indie blues scene, her live show hits like a freight train — one woman, one guitar, and all the damn feelings.
This indie mama owns her own sound — a gritty, groove-driven mix of blues, RnB, alt-country with an occasional jazz dalliance. If you’re after clichéd boy-blues, keep walking.
Clarke’s got pipes. Her powerhouse honeyed vocal oozes warmth and soul, with textures that range from velvet to sass and gravel. Gutsy, driving rhythm guitar work anchors the show.
Live, shes warm and dangerously disarming. A quiet storm — until the fire kicks in. Presence, power and stories that sting. You don’t just watch a Karen Clarke set — you feel her shift the room.
She's a one-woman boil up. Honest. Gutsy. Real.

Dog and KC got a thing, for sure.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Stewart Copeland - Have I Said Too Much, Legendary rock drummer, Stewart Copeland, is returning to Australia & New Zealand for the first time in 18 years. He will bring his ‘Have I Said Too Much? The Police, Hollywood, And Other Adventures’ show to our shores, following dozens of sold out shows across the UK.

Stewart says, “Demand for this intimate new show has surpassed my expectations, and I can’t wait to return to Australia & New Zealand next year and share the stories of my life with even more fans.”

As one of the greatest rock drummers of all time, he drove the all-conquering success of The Police during the 1970s and 1980s, before being inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. A multi-Grammy winner, who followed his work with The Police by composing music for soundtracks for Hollywood movies and operas, Stewart is hitting the road for his most intimate tour to date.

Having played drums for Curved Air from 1975 to 1976, Stewart was the founding member of The Police, recruiting lead singer Sting and guitarist Andy Summers.
His remarkable talent helped drive The Police to world domination between 1977 and 1986, and then again from 2007 to 2008 when the band reunited.

His Hollywood soundtracks include Francis Ford Coppola’s Rumblefish and Oliver Stone’s Wall Street and Talk Radio. He has written books, formed supergroups, made films, and composed music for ballet, opera, and classical concerts.

This special evening with Stewart Copeland will provide a fascinating insight into his incredible life as a performer, musician, entertainer, and writer. All shows will be hosted by acclaimed Perth radio broadcaster, Sarah Tout.

Meet and Greet packages will be available and fans will also be able to submit questions for Stewart to answer on stage.

Strung Out w/ The Vile Maxim, No Sector and Ricky Bobby, Strung Out w/ The Vile Maxim, No Sector and Ricky Bobby
STRUNG OUT (USA) RETURN FOR FULL-BLOWN NZ TOUR —PERFORMING
SUBURBANTEENAGEWASTELANDBLUES IN FULL

Tickets Available now!
https://www.undertheradar.co.nz/.../33281/Strung-Out-USA.utr

Strung Out tore through NZ in 2023, and you lapped it up. You loved them, and they loved
you—so much so that they’re returning this September for a full-blown New Zealand tour, hitting
four locations across both the North and South Island.

And this time, they’re bringing something special.

To celebrate the 30th Anniversary of SUBURBANTEENAGEWASTELANDBLUES, Strung Out
will be playing the album in its entirety.

One of punk’s holy grails, it’s fast, ferocious, and
precise—a record that helped define the genre and influenced generations of bands that
followed.

Released in 1996, SUBURBANTEENAGEWASTELANDBLUES pushed the boundaries of the
genre—faster, sharper, and more intricate than anything that came before. Three decades on, it
still hits hard, and hearing it played live, front to back, is an experience no self-respecting punk
fan can miss.

Hailing from Simi Valley, California, Strung Out are long-standing punk rock royalty and one of
Fat Wreck Chords’ defining “big four.” With decades of touring under their belts, they have a
proven track record of igniting crowds and delivering high-octane, full-throttle punk shows.

Expect a night of relentless energy: razor-sharp riffs, pounding drums, and shout-along
choruses delivered with force.

This is controlled chaos at its best: sweat-soaked rooms, ringing
ears, and intensity that pulls you right in.

Last time Strung Out were here, shows sold out. This run will be no different.

Don’t sleep on it, or you’ll miss it.

Friday September 11th, 2026 — Last Place — Hamilton
Saturday September 12th, 2026 — Whammy Bar — Auckland
Sunday September 13th, 2026 — Valhalla — Wellington
Monday September 14th, 2026 — Loons — Christchurch

description:
Sue Thorby & Mr Moondog, Moondog Blues & Sue Thorby take to the lower North Island in mid-February 2026 with an unforgettable show of heartfelt blues & gypsy soul. Both seasoned and powerful musicians and performers, you are in for a once-in-a-lifetime experience of two of New Zealand’s finest roots musicians.

Moondog, either found based out of Northland, NZ or as the gypsy bluesman touring Australia, channels a gritty, raw style — using metal-bodied guitars (homemade biscuit tins ‘AlleyTyns’), harmonica, a gritty and sometimes dark freight train voice, thumb slappin’ bass, foot-stomping rhythm — to deliver a unique blend of traditional blues, rock n roll, voodoo-infused “Bluz A Billy,” and Mojo-Juju vibes.

Sue Thorby, one of Aotearoa’s finest, brings her exceptional self-titled album and unforgettable live performance, rich with heart and superb musicianship back out on the road. Defying genres fused with blues, rock, celtic, gypsy soul and jazz, driving guitar rhythmns and powerful vocals, Sue weaves unapologetically honest stories of love, humanity, anguish & hope, grit and beauty.

description:
Sumac, Banished Music, Whammy Bar, and Valhalla are proud to present the long-awaited New Zealand debut of experimental post-metal trio SUMAC.

Formed in 2014, the powerhouse trio, comprised of Aaron Turner (guitar, vocals; Isis, Old Man Gloom), Brian Cook (bass; Russian Circles, Botch), and Nick Yacyshyn (drums; Baptists), are renowned for merging crushing heaviness with improvisational freedom, exploring the boundaries between structure and chaos.

SUMAC have built a reputation as a fearsome live band. Visceral and cathartic shows where crushing riffs & sprawling drones collide with extended bursts of wild improvisation. In 2024, the band released their critically acclaimed album The Healer, a sweeping, transformative work spanning four monumental tracks. The record dives deep into themes of regeneration, suffering, and spiritual reconstruction — a testament to the band’s ability to meld raw power with emotional depth.

The experimental metal trio’s four-song, 76-minute album is the peak of their career. It’s dense and invigorating, highlighting the band’s dexterity, creativity, and clarity of purpose. - Pitchfork
Soon after the release, SUMAC teamed up with poet and sound artist Moor Mother to release The Film, a boundary-pushing collaborative album. Released via Thrill Jockey in April 2025, the record unfolds as a cinematic journey across eight “scenes,” merging SUMAC’s heavy, jazz-inflected textures with Moor Mother’s incisive spoken-word commentary.

SUMAC’s work has always been about the transition between different states of being. Our sense of normal, and indeed our sense of life, is now being shaken. We don’t know what is coming next. We are looking for pointers towards the future, as well as things to hold onto in the moment.
  
New Zealanders, don’t miss this rare and powerful journey into uncharted sonic terrain.

description:
Summer Camp Closing Party! | Dillon Jo, Miles Calder & Keira Batten Co, Join us and some of Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s finest artists over five nights across January and February with tickets from $10 or a season pass for $40, featuring drink specials and cocktails thanks to our sponsor Jameson.

Here it is… our final night! Featuring not one, not two, but THREE of Pōneke’s premier acts to close our 2026 series out.

Dillon Jo is the genre defying project of Wellington Based artists Betty Smith and Georgie Levien. Dillon Jo built paths between the elements of dream pop, shoegaze, folk, alt rock, and indie pop to create their genre defying sound. Having recently recruited Kahu Sanson-Burnett and Ruadh Munro, Dillon Jo has transformed their live sets into an unbridled big-sound shoegaze experience.

Miles Calder released his solo debut album Autopilot Life in 2021, a self-reflective delve into waking up from an unexamined life, dressed in a psychedelic folk-rock palette that evoked late-era Beatles as much as contemporaries like Kevin Morby and Father John Misty. The album won over new fans and critics alike & led to a nomination for a prestigious Aotearoa Music Award (Te Kaipuoro Taketake Toa | Best Folk Artist 2022).

Keira Batten Coogan writes raw and messy music for alien listeners. Joined onstage by some familiar Pōneke talent, his earnest earworms pack more punch than ever. Themes of queerness, growing pains, love, and nostalgia shine through his lyricism and captivates audiences.

Summer Camp | BADTAB and Bri Louise, Join us and some of Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s finest artists over five nights across January and February with tickets from $10 or a season pass for $40, featuring drink specials and cocktails thanks to our sponsor Jameson.

Come along for our third night of festivities featuring psychedelic sensations BADTAB and the unbeatable Bri Louise.

BADTAB are carving out their own kaleidoscopic corner of the music world. Weaving together synthesisers and swirling guitar strums with rock and jazz inspired drum beats, BADTAB creates a unique and refreshing sound. The band made their mark in 2024 with a prolific run of releases. September saw the drop of The Pōneke Sessions, collaborative EP with Cellz. Then came December’s Echo Chambers Of…, their full-length debut album that introduced the world to BADTAB’s expansive soundscape. Since the release of their debut album, they have been deep in the works on their sophomore album which is anticipated for a 2026 summer release.

Bri Louise blends sultry queer with smooth love and undeniable groove. Their sound has roots in Gospel and Neo-Soul, evolving into a rich fusion of Jazz, Hip-Hop, and R&B. Bri’s music features a talented live band that supports their poetic lyrics with colourful keys, phatty bass, flashy beats, vibrant guitar and fruity woodwinds.

description:
Summer Jazz in the Gardens, Marine Gardens, Raumati. Saturday 14th February 2026, A Free Community Live Jazz Music Event in Raumati
Kapiti’s summer music scene comes alive with Jazz in the gardens on Saturday 14th from 12:30pm — a vibrant celebration of live jazz music for the whole family. This free event brings together some of the finest jazz musicians, offering an afternoon of soulful rhythms, energetic performances, and a fantastic community atmosphere. We will provide a free Children’s Bouncy Castle for the event.
Event Line-Up
12:30 PM – Hottie Duo
First time performers for Music Festivals and Events NZ. The Hottie Duo will perform a short 20 minute jazz set.
1:00 PM – Jessie Murphy
Jessie is an accomplished musician and vocalist. She will be performing jazz standards and contemporary jazz tunes while playing keys. Jessie brings a polished, soulful performance style and is a fantastic addition to the Summer Jazz line-up.
2:00 PM – Brasso
Kapiti-based large brass ensemble featuring arrangements of the classics by David Langley.
“David is an experienced arranger, infusing charts with a jazz/Latin twist, written for instrumentals or vocals with trumpets, saxophones, and a rhythm section,” said event organiser Chris Craddock.
3:00 PM – Duncan Haynes Quartet
Internationally renowned pianist Duncan Haynes leads his exceptional quartet, bringing world-class jazz to Raumati.
“Again, we have another group made up of professional musicians for the line-up. These cats spend their time in studio work — mostly retired from the touring scene — and have really honed their craft. We are very pleased to have secured them for our event.”
Don’t miss this incredible opportunity to experience the magic of live jazz in a relaxed outdoor setting. This free community event would not be possible without the generous support of Pub Charity.
The forecast is for a beautiful, fine sunny day — bring your picnic hamper.
Wet weather venue Kapiti Boating Club — watch our Facebook page for updates.
For further details, please contact:
Chris Craddock – 027 410 2420

Wellington, join us for a night of Psychedelic & Melodic Techno featuring 2 international artists Kozy ( Canada), Aztoria ( Australia) supported by Aadhi, Blair & Uday. This event will be hosted at the legendary venue, Valhalla on the 24th of January, 8pm onwards.

Kozy will be playing a 2.5 Hour Extended Set, Aztoria will be playing a 1.5hr set & local legends will be playing an hour each.

International DJ Bio's:

KOZY ( CA)

KOZY aka Jeff Koz is a Montreal-based DJ & Entrepreneur specialising in dark & groovy underground techno music.
KOZY's dedication to music is evident in his tight mixes, solid track selection and inclination towards groovy synths and heavy, disruptive bass.

In 2019, he founded AlpaKa MuziK, a Montreal-based record label pushing world-class underground progressive, minimal and psychedelic techno beats. With releases from some of the biggest names in the game, AlpaKa MuziK has been paving the way for this fast emerging genre with relentless quality music and has become one of the most prominent labels in the psychedelic techno sub-genre.

With over 125 releases and over 650 tracks under their belt, AlpaKa has quickly become a powerhouse label in the underground techno community.

Since early 2022, in a little over 2 years, KOZY has gone on 9 international tours, including 5 euro tours, Australia, South Africa Mauritius, India, Mexico and has played over 150 gigs in 24 months in over 30 countries and counting.

Some prominent festivals he has performed at include, Esoteric in Australia, Hadra in France, Texas Eclipse, Boom Festival and many others, bringing to many of them the AlpaKa MuziK takeovers that showcase the cutting edge psychedelic techno sound through countless live sets around the world.

He recently finished his 4-month long 2025 summer euro tour where he performed at Boom Festival in Portugal and many more AlpaKa Showcases all around Europe and beyond. His 2025-2026 world tour is in motion, with Japan and a large Southern Hemisphere schedule in the works. With an unstoppable arsenal of unreleased, cutting edge bangers, he'll leave you wanting more after every set.

AZTORIA ( AU)

Aztoria is the psytech project of Ashley Zadel, also known as Flow Theory.

For more than 16 years, his melodic bush techno sound has evolved through auditory storytelling on stages across the globe, from Cape Town to London, Israel to Brazil, Portugal, New Zealand and Australia.

Rooted in progressive soundscapes with an organic flavour, Aztoria blends melodic deep house grooves with minimal techno to craft psychedelic atmospheres that ignite the imagination.

Aztoria burst onto the scene with his debut EP Reborn (Dense Nebula Records), hitting #4 on Beatport’s Techno charts. His 2024 single Birds of Paradise (Soliq Records) soared to #33, while his Inner Groove remix landed at #23 in Progressive House (Techgnosis Records). With fresh releases on Techgnosis, Recovery Collective and Puzzles Records and more in the works, Aztoria is carving his path in the underground with relentless energy and innovation.

Whether in the depths of a forest or the heart of a concrete jungle, Aztoria’s tunes will captivate and elevate you with his storytelling magic.

This week featuring local saxophonist, back in town briefly from Greece, James Wylie

A modern look at the saxophone-organ trio tradition through the prism of original compositions by James Wylie and Miles Crayford. Joining them will be long-time collaborator, drummer Mike Jensen.

Miles Crayford and James Wylie have been musical brothers since their teenage years and their influence on each other has been central to their artistic worldview. Since that time, their individual paths have diverged, been enriched and new musical identities have been forged. This meeting will be the first time playing together in more than ten years (and Wylie's first appearance in Wellington in as many years) and will feature a range of newly composed orginal music by both musicians. For this performance Crayford will be performing on Hammond organ and Wylie on tenor saxophone - a nod to their childhood trio which was active in and around Wellington in which Mike Jensen held down the drum chair. This is a rare opportunity to hear this group due to James Wylie being based in Europe for the last 15 years. Not to be missed!

description:
Suzanne Vega, Widely regarded as one of the foremost songwriters of her generation, Suzanne Vega emerged as a leading figure of the folk revival of the early 1980s. Four decades later, she is still writing and singing great songs. In her Wellington show, Suzanne will perform a career-spanning set. See her on stage at St James Theatre performing favourites like Tom’s Diner, Luka, Marlene On The Wall, and plenty more. There’ll also be new songs from her 2025 album, ‘Flying with Angels’. Joining her on stage will be longtime guitarist, Gerry Leonard, and cellist Stephanie Winters. 
Since the release of her self-titled, critically acclaimed 1985 debut album, Suzanne Vega has played to sold-out concerts across the world. She is a masterful storyteller who, according to one The New York Times critique, “observes the world with a clinically poetic eye.” Her song lyrics often focus on city life, ordinary people, and real-world subjects. They are notably succinct, understated, and immediately recognisable.

Sven Olsens Play the Wellington Classical Guitar Society, Sven Olsen's Brutal Canadian Love Saga is Wellington's most obscure chamber pop ensemble. They perform songs about the bakers, the fakers, the risk takers who inhabit these shaky isles.
If your hobbies include boogie boarding over the Huka Falls or performing Kung Fu atop an Upper Hutt pizza joint, or just quietly reading, this shows for you. Sven’s creativity is sparked by the songwriting genius of Nigel Beckford and more than seventy members who have contributed to their collective vision of hilarious gloom.
Guitars, harmony singing, strings:
“These songs often have a delicate touch, a lightness of melody and a sympathetic delivery which casts them as love songs to a nation, not a cruel critique.” – Graham Reid in Elsewhere.

description:
System Of A Down, Following the sell-out success of their European summer tour, System Of A Down is heading to Hnry Stadium for its only New Zealand concert. Wellington audiences will also be entertained by warm up act and alternative rock icons Faith No More. 
This concert marks System of a Down's first Wellington show, and their first time playing in Aotearoa in more than a decade. Blending metal with diverse influences including jazz, opera, and Armenian folk, System Of A Down have sold more than 42 million albums worldwide. They released their debut self-titled album in 1998, but it was not until the release of 'Toxicity' in 2001 that their popularity exploded. Heavy music fans can expect a massive career-spanning set filled with the songs that have defined the genre for more than 25 years.
It's been a long time between Wellington shows for Faith No More. The last time the San Francisco-based band played in the capital was 1997. Responsible for such classics as Epic, Midlife Crisis, and a distinctive cover of The Commodores' Easy, they've developed a die-hard following over the last 40 years. 
Together the bands will bring decades of hard rock (and its fans) to Wellington for what promises to be one of the most electrifying nights of heavy music the city's ever seen.

description:
TARN PK - LIVE AT MOON, TARN PK - LIVE AT MOON
~ DON'T GET F.O.M.O ~

Tarn PK is bringing his new EP ’F.O.M.O’ to live audiences in Wellington on the 14th of September 6pm at MOON, with support from Sig Wilder & Friends and Josh Glennie.

With his newly formed 3 piece band, they’re stripping his sound down to the essentials; funky drum breaks, soaring synths and crunchy guitars, bringing a whole new dimension to the sound from the EP.

F.O.M.O, is a reflection on burnout, ambition, and identity in a digitally overwhelmed world. It draws inspiration from urban isolation and the weight of expectations. Tracks from the EP have landed on major Spotify and Apple playlists. Reflecting the office environment, familiar to many, this performance will bring to life the themes from the EP in a host of ways.

With over 2.2 million streams across platforms and 1.8 million on Spotify alone, his impact is growing. Releases have landed on global and regional editorial playlists. His EPs—Fantasy, Monarch, SugarCoated and now F.O.M.O —have consistently showcased his range and evolution as an artist.

Sig Wilder & Friends blend kiwi authenticity with American grit, bringing you a well-worn handwritten journal of lived experiences rendered through metaphor, poetic prose, and the stylistic conventions of folk, alt-country and late-night heartbreak radio.

Josh Glennie is a soulful singer/songwriter based in Wellington, New Zealand. He's made a name for himself playing in bands around Wellington and is now striking out with his own solo material. Together with Tarn, they have produced a new EP of songs that cut to the bone, focused around acoustic guitar and Josh's striking vocals. His New EP is expected late 2025/early 2026.

description:
TCPS The Control Room: Final Transmission, The Control Room: Final Transmission
Presented by The Car Park Society
Saturday 13 December 2025 · 8pm · 149 Victoria Street, Te Whanganui-a-Tara
Final Transmission marks the closing of The Control Room, a social experiment and augmented reality art project by Māori-led collective 'The Car Park Society' that has traced the circuitry of power, colonisation, and collective resistance through the architecture of the city. This final gathering is the end of the broadcast, a chance to power down the system and celebrate the histories of communities buried beneath the streets.
Food and drinks will be served throughout the night, but this is a potluck and you are warmly invited to contribute to the table with kai, inu, or your own creative offering, art work or time. The evening will move between sound, conversation, and ritual, holding space to reflect, reconnect, and close the circuit together. There will be live music, kai, drinks, speakers, interactive Ai media, Māori library and hub of treasure hunts and maps, visual art activities, card and board-games, and decolonial tasks to make you think and feel more connected.
Come share in the final signal, chat to the 'Oracle' and hear what it has to say....Stay until the frequencies fade and always #StayVigilant.

TEIWA — Rob Ruha with the NZSO, Silver Scroll-winning Māori artist Rob Ruha and the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra are joining forces for TEIWA. Here's your chance to experience everything from waiata you’d hear on the marae to exhilarating stadium anthems, The music of Aotearoa is sure to comes to life in a performance of tribal futurism that ignites the senses. Special guests TOA (Te Taumata O Apanui) will bring the unmistakable power of haka to the stage. The Michael Fowler Centre will be bursting with musical confluences and mana .
The NZSO and Rob Ruha will premiere new waiata at the event. Audiences will also hear Ruha’s most loved tracks that will have the whole house moving. After a sell-out Matariki performance with the Auckland Philharmonia, this ‘mighty celebration’ (The New Zealand Herald) is sure to be a programme highlight of Aotearoa New Zealand Festival of the Arts.

description:
TENOR: My Name Is Pati – Wellington Premiere, Hailed as “the next Pavarotti”, the charismatic Samoan singer and Sol3 Mio bandmate Pene Pati has been wowing critics and audiences around the world since his operatic debut.

Directed by Rebecca Tansley, TENOR: My Name Is Pati follows Pene’s journey alongside his brother Amitai — also a rising opera star — from their humble beginnings in the South Pacific to the world’s greatest opera houses.

Weaving intimate family archive footage with behind-the-scenes moments and soaring performances, this music-rich documentary blends humour and heart to reveal how family, cultural pride, and determination can carry an unlikely dream to the world stage.

Watch the TENOR: My Name Is Pati trailer here.

description:
TEST (BRAZILIAN GRINDCORE) W/ WINCE & VORTEKKE, Couldn’t be more thrilled to present legendary DIY grindcore band TEST touring throughout the North Island of New Zealand for the first time this June.
Come see TEST Wednesday 10th at Wellingtons finest venue - Valhalla. Joined by the terrible twins of Vorteke and Wince.
For the uninitiated, TEST is a Brazilian duo formed in 2010 by João Kombi (guitar and vocals) and Barata (drums), two veterans of São Paulo’s underground scene. Known for their intense live performances, notable collaborations with artists like Iggor Cavalera and Deafkids, and a fearless musical approach, the band has established itself as one of the most inventive names in the Brazilian alternative scene.
From the deathgrind band initially known for playing outside of major heavy metal concerts, fueled by a old school VW van-powered generator, Test has gone a long way since 2011, when the band started playing on the streets. Since then, the band has shared stages - inside the venue this time, be it as opening band or headlining - with artists such as Mr Bungle, King Diamond, Napalm Death, Carcass, Cannibal Corpse, Exodus e Brujeria, Mayhem, Mortician, Dillinger Escape Plan, to name a few. Speaking of name-dropping, some famous Test fans include Shane Embury, Napalm Death’s bass player, and the brothers Max and Iggor Cavalera - Iggor, by the way, has chosen Test’s drummer on the top 10 drummers of all time.
Aside from performing with well-know heavy metal artists, Test also took part in two of the major extreme music festivals worldwide: “Obscene Extreme”, in the Czech Republic and Mexico, and “Maryland Deathfest”, in the US. With a steady recording and playing live pace, Test turns sixteen years old with 19 albums (full-lenghts, EPs and split-album with bands from different parts of the world, like Nepal [Chepang], U.S.A. [Cloud Rat, Ixias] and China [Struggle Session]), two feature films, more than ten thousand records sold and more than one thousand shows in all states of Brazil, as well as twenty one foreign tours (Asia, Europe, North America and South America).
Tickets available from Undertheradar.co.nz Presales only $20.

description:
THE BETHS ★ AOTEAROA TOUR – MEOW NUI #1, Globetrotting local four piece, The Beths are thrilled to announce their return home playing seven shows throughout Aotearoa next March in celebration of their recently released fourth album Straight Line Was A Lie.
Released in August this year, Straight Line Was A Lie is the first album released via American label ANTI- , debuting at #1 on the Aotearoa Album Chart and receiving glowing reviews from press around the world.
Last night, The Beths made their late night television debut on Jimmy Kimmel Live! performing Straight Line Was A Lie’s standout opening title track, praised by Stereogum as a “total slam dunk of an opener.”
This performance gives a taste of what to expect on the band’s homecoming tour which kicks off at Meow Nui in Wellington with two nights on Friday 13 and Saturday 14 of March 2026. The band then head south to Dunedin playing Glenroy Auditorium on Friday 20 March, James Hay in Christchurch on Sunday 22 March and Theatre Royal in Nelson on Monday 23 March. The tour wraps up at the iconic Powerstation in Auckland with two shows on Thursday 26 and Friday 27 March. Tickets for all shows go on presale Monday 3 November at 8am and general sale Wednesday 5 November at 8am NZDT.
These shows come on the back of three solid months of touring the world, which kicked off last month in Europe. The North American leg begins this week and includes some of their biggest venues to date in the U.S., including The Wiltern in Los Angeles, The Fillmore in San Francisco, The Salt Shed in Chicago, Brooklyn Paramount in New York City, Union Transfer in Philadelphia, 9:30 Club in Washington, DC and more.

description:
THE POGUES | St James Theatre, Wellington, THE POGUES | St James Theatre, Wellington
The Pogues make their long-awaited return to NZ stages with a special 40th-anniversary celebration of their classic album Rum, Sodomy & the Lash!

The tour brings together original members James Fearnley, Jem Finer, and Spider Stacy, alongside a stellar lineup of guest vocalists Daragh Lynch, Iona Zajac, and John Francis Flynn. They’re joined by musicians Holly Mullineaux, Jordan O’Leary, Fiachra Meek, Jim Sclavunos, Pete Fraser, Daniel Hayes, and Ian Williamson, performing the album in full plus other fan favourites.

Released in 1985, Rum, Sodomy & the Lash remains a cornerstone of alternative music — fusing traditional Irish folk with punk and poetic storytelling. The album features some of The Pogues’ most celebrated songs, including A Pair of Brown Eyes, Dirty Old Town, and A Rainy Night in Soho.

Returning for their first NZ tour in over 35 years, The Pogues promise an unforgettable night honouring one of the most influential albums in modern music.

description:
THUNDERCAT Wellington - May 6th, Meow Nui (SOLD OUT), THUNDERCAT Wellington - May 6th, Meow Nui (SOLD OUT)
Grammy-nominated Bassist, Producer, and Vocalist THUNDERCAT Brings His New Album Distracted To Auckland And Wellington This May.

Known for his jazz-fusion sensibility and elastic funk, Thundercat is bringing his 2026 tour to Auckland and Wellington this May, performing live in support of his new album Distracted. The New Zealand leg of his tour will include a stop at The Powerstation in Auckland on Monday, May 4, 2026, followed by a show at Meow NUI in Wellington on Wednesday, May 6, 2026.

In an age of endless notifications and fractured attention, Thundercat turns the chaos inward on Distracted, his long-awaited new album and one of his most resonant statements yet. Six years on from It Is What It Is, the record captures the restless aftermath of grief and modern overload, balancing existential weight with Thundercat’s unmistakable wit and warmth.

It’s an album that laughs through the noise, folding jazz-fusion virtuosity, elastic funk and late-night introspection into songs that feel like unfiltered inner monologues: tender, funny, and painfully human.

That philosophy carries directly into the live experience. Onstage, Thundercat treats Distracted not as a lecture on modern life, but as a shared release, stretching songs, breaking the fourth wall, leaning into humour and spontaneity as a form of survival.

Thundercats New Zealand shows promise moments of presence inside the noise: music that drifts, refocuses, and reminds you why joy still matters. It’s playful, loose, deeply human, and a rare chance to experience Distracted and all of Thundercat the way it was meant to be felt, not scrolled past.
label: Music & Concerts

description:

The dancefloor is set to light up this October when Wellington's finest soul/funk/roots collective TOI get together with some of their best buds to pay homage to Aotearoa’s criminally overlooked 1970s boogie scene.

The soul/funk/disco magic of the likes of Dalvanius, Mark Williams, Collision, Prince Tui Teka, The Yandall Sisters, 1860 and Tina Cross had a new light shone on it with the release of John
Baker and Alan Perrot’s 2017 compilation Heed the Call: Whakarongo Ngā Tamariki. Now the capital has a chance to celebrate the music live as TOI rediscover and reimagine these sonic taonga.

Comprised of a stellar lineup of Aotearoa’s leading musicians, for over a decade TOI have been bringing crowds together to groove all across New Zealand and Australia in both headline spots and as support for the likes of Red Hot Chili Peppers, Ocean Alley, Fat Freddy’s Drop and Tash Sultana. Don’t miss your chance to see them for this one-night-only exploration of one of Aotearoa’s most interesting and dynamic scenes.

Featuring the vocal stylings of Wellington’s own leading lady of soul Lisa Tomlins, TOI’s Conway Jeune (aka C-Way Green from Fat Freddy’s Drop) and another very special guest to be announced. TOI is Conway Jeune (Guitar, Lead Vocals), Bryn Van Vliet (Saxophone & BVs), Jules Blewman (Lead Guitar), Luther Hunt (Drums & BVs), Kaito Walley (Trombone & Percussion), Daniel Hayles (Keys & Synths) and Johnny Lawrence (Bass).

Tahini Bikini at Moon w/ Nameless and Brainless, Pōneke based funk/soul band Tahini Bikini are performing live at Moon on Saturday, 6th June! Supported by Wellington's freshest soul/hip hop band Nameless & Brainless. Bring your dancing shoes!

Tickets on sale Wednesday, 27th May via UTR - $15 for students/unwaged, $20 GA.

TAHINI BIKINI:

Pōneke-based Tahini Bikini are known for their distinctive sound, a combination of extremely danceable funk, soul and pop influences elevated by frontwoman Mads Taylor’s frank, feisty lyrics and smoky voice.

The seven-piece group released their debut album Fever Dream in 2022, and have since become a fixture at festivals across Aotearoa, performing at Rhythm & Vines, Great Sounds Great, Welcome to Nowhere, Cuba Dupa, Outfield, Twisted Frequency and more. As well as Mads on lead vocals, the band features a talented collective of musicians: Mathew Campbell (Backing Vocals, percussion) Darcy Monteath (Bass), Eric Sebastian (drums), Alex Scott-Billing (Guitar) Cameron Robertson (Trumpet) and Aidan Mcculloch (Saxophone/keys).

In 2025 Tahini Bikini released a run of confident, polished singles, with lines like "tell me does it taste good when you lick those boots?" from 'Mother' emphasising a turn towards a more pointed, critical tone in the Mads’ songwriting.


NAMELESS & BRAINLESS:

Nameless and Brainless are a 6 piece band from Wellington.

What started as some jams for frontman Riva Cowans Masters project between a couple of the bros has evolved into a soulful, hard hitting band.

While this project is fresh, each of the musicians either have degrees in music or have vast experience in the industry.
High energy Kiwi raps in English and Te Reo accompanied by a powerful band and driven by a locked in rhythm section, come party with Nameless and Brainless.

description:
Tap Fusion, 
Tap Fusion is a high energy, percussive Tap Dance show that fuses with Street Dance, Contemporary Dance and Live Original Music.
Creators Brandon & Cameron Carter-Chan, Director and Co Director of Tap NZ, are some of New Zealand's top Choreographers with Brandon winning the National Tap Dance Championship in 2014.  Brandon & Cameron have taught and choreographed in the dance community winning awards across New Zealand, Australia and the United States for over 10 years.  Their Tap Dance Company Tap NZ focuses on Tap Innovation and has recently been invited to perform in Los Angeles and Melbourne to stage their creative works.

Tap NZ is very proud to present Tap Fusion, a show that champions Tap Dance Innovation. The audience are taken on a journey that begins with the roots of Tap, to a future of endless creative possibilities.

Tap Dance originated in the 19th Century with history dating back to 1840's New York, USA. Rhythm and sound have been the foundation as Tap Dance changed and evolved over the years. Tap Fusion is a show designed to push the boundaries of the Tap Dance discipline as well as acknowledging its foundations of exceptional sound and rhythmical composition.

Inspired by famous shows such as Tap Dogs, Riverdance and STOMP, Tap Fusion is a sound and percussion show at the core, designed to entertain the audience through a multi-layered sensory experience.

Tap Shows are rare in the entertainment world with so few that champion Tap Dance at the forefront of the show. Tap Fusion is a platform that showcases Tap as the leading voice of the story where audiences will experience a fresh perspective on what Tap Dance truly represents.  Music of the Sole.

description:
Techno Taster, Techno Taster
This year for the first of our annual pre-parties we’ve gone around the country to gather a lineup of creators working at the intersections of techno, delving into influences from bass, breaks, psychedelia, club music and beyond, all underpinned by elements of dance music's most enduring genre.

We believe each one of these acts is currently pushing the needle forward for underground club culture in Aotearoa, and are thrilled to host them all together at Valhalla to push their vision across the almighty Third Eye Hi-Fi soundsystem.


ELI HØFF — Abyssal Soundworks / PHTM

Producer and DJ, Eli is undoubtedly at the forefront of Aotearoa’s underground dance scene.
Those who have kept their ears tuned to the innovative underground have no doubt stumbled upon the tribalistic, psychedelic, and focused sounds emanating from the mind of Auckland-based producer Eli Høff. With a string of releases on Berlin-based PHTM, Tāmaki Makaurau-based Gypnotica, and an impressive catalog of self-releases, he consistently showcases his singular and original interpretation of dance music.

Instagram.com/e.li
elihoff.bandcamp.com
abyssalsoundworks.bandcamp.com


HUNTER — Hang the Saints / Haven

Raised in Kaikōura, Aotearoa, Hunter's dark and atmospheric sound often contrasts the beautiful environment she grew up in. Her direct approach to techno draws influence from heavy percussion, bold rhythm and industrial soundscapes. After spending two years finding inspiration in clubs overseas, she has returned to Ōtautahi with a refined style that’s ready to make people dance. As the co-founder of “Hang The Saints” and resident of “Haven”, Hunter is all about creating safe, inclusive spaces for people to connect through the music she loves.

https://www.instagram.com/sspoonsnake/
https://soundcloud.com/hunter-mccrory-334790608
https://on.soundcloud.com/bC3qeA6pUxBoMo7P9


LUDUS & RIZZO — Tonic Collective

Tonic Collective is the recent endeavour of Ludus and Rizzo, inspired by the people, places and spaces of their experience touring China with BIRDPARTY and Vera Ellen. Both acts are individually known for their versatile and innovative sound, bringing a wide range of influences and inspirations to the dancefloor. In the short time since establishing the collective, they’ve already hosted Kaishandao and Bone Chapel, established a space, and debuted a monthly radio show on Mouthfull that explores sound from across the genre spectrum, both in the club and out.

https://www.instagram.com/ludus.etc/
https://www.instagram.com/alicerizzoofficial
https://www.instagram.com/tonic.collective/
https://soundcloud.com/l-s-rizzo/416life-support-cl1n1c-chengdu
https://soundcloud.com/racquetclub-info/mix-series-016-ludus


SHLI — Echo Train Records / Warehouse Rave / Holding Hands

Shli is the alias of Ōtautahi-via-Pōneke DJ and Producer Tim Ward. Steadily releasing works over recent years through local labels like Echo Train and the Big Fresh Collective, he is carving out a sound of his own.

Stitching together infectious rhythms layered over low-end pressure, Shli’s sets draw influence from across the hardcore continuum and beyond. Creating dancefloor moments from trippy rhythmic states to unleashing sheer bass weight.

https://www.instagram.com/____shli/
https://echotrainer.bandcamp.com/album/ech009-bracing-set-pace-u-dont

description:
Terrace Dynamics: Pipes & Strings on the Terrace, Kemp English (organ/piano) with Yuka Eguchi (violin).
 
In 2024, renowned Kiwi organist Dr Kemp English gave concerts in the Auckland, Dunedin and Adelaide Town Halls. This year, it’s Wellington’s turn to host this virtuoso solo organist as Kemp comes to town to play the newly restored Croft organ at St. Andrew’s on the Terrace. Kemp is joined by Yuka Eguchi, violinist extraordinaire, who has been Assistant Concertmaster of the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra for the last ten years, combining her orchestral role with a busy chamber music schedule. Before making her home in New Zealand, she was Solo Concertmaster of the Japan Philharmonic Orchestra and Tokyo Mozart Players and a guest Concertmaster throughout Japan.
This concert will include a wide variety of musical treats such as well-known organ music by Bach, Lefébure-Wély and Sousa, music for violin and organ by Mons Takle & W.S Lloyd Weber, and even an early taste of Christmas with an arrangement of Sleigh Ride by Leroy Anderson!

The Wellington Organists Association is delighted to promote this event, which is sure to appeal to anybody with a love of music and an appreciation of fine musicianship, and we are grateful for sponsorship received from the Lion Foundation and The Pelorus Trust.

Admission is free – koha welcome to help offset costs.

description:
Testpot presents - Friend of Friends, Wellington alternative indie rock trio Testpot present Friends of Friends. An afternoon-into-evening celebration of music, community, and connection. From afternoon grooves to electric evening highlights, this is more than just a gig; it’s a gathering, a celebration, and one we'd love you to join us for.
Pack a picnic, bring the whole family, bring your mates, bring drinks, bring a smile.

Friends of Friends is celebrating the connections that hold us together. Every band on the line-up is connected through friendships, side projects, and shared stages, making this a rare chance to see a community of musicians in one place.
So come meet some new friends, old friends, hang out with and get to know:
PLANET
BEANS AND DON
SAM R SAFFERY
BUFFALO BUFFALO BUFFALO
TESPOT
AGATHA PANTHA
KINGSTON HIGH ALL STARS

Experience all of these great bands in the beautiful and iconic setting of Breaker Bay Hall.
BYO friend, food and drinks.
Seatoun village is a stone's throw away, so just nip out, grab some cold ones and some fish and chips or something to bring back to the hall and enjoy.

Can't wait to see you there.

* * * * T E S T P O T * * F R I E N D S * *O F * *F R I E N D S * * * *

PLANET - A mix of traditional bagpipe airs with post punk riffs and a dollop of vaudevillian good humour. It could be world music, it could be underground indie rock. It could be psychedelic folk music. But it's always approachable and certainly a lot of fun.
https://planetband.nz

BEANS AND DON - A dynamic duo beautifully sculpting a path of folky ballads through love, loss, and much, much more.
https://www.facebook.com/people/Don-and-The-Divorcees/61552936937584/

SAM R SAFFERY - From rural New Zealand to the subways and bodegas of New York, Samuel R. Saffery’s musical journey is unquestionably linked to place and movement.
Blending indie folk, alternative rock, and classical influences, his songs are delivered with a distinctive, melodic voice, as haunting as it is sweet.
Instagram: www.instagram.com/slamsafari
Bandcamp: www.samuelsaffery.com
Twitter: @samuelsaffery

BUFFLAO BUFFLAO BUFFLAO - A seven-piece herd of instrument addicts play a mix of electronic and acoustic to produce pop-rock that is equal parts playful and whimsical. Catchy indie-pop licks, lush harmonies, and hooks that stick, the enigmatic, multi-faceted group Buffalo Buffalo Buffalo – so good they named the band three times.
https://www.instagram.com/buffalothree/

TESTPOT - Alternative indie rock trio colliding sonic inspirations from bands such as Radiohead, Animals as Leaders, and Duran Duran. A sonic commentary on social media, corruption, AI, surveillance, and the other goodies we’re all told we have to live with. A side project of Buffalo Buffalo Buffalo member Hayden Overton, joined by the talented Scott Roy and the percussive brilliance of Lachie Kendric, doing whatever it is we do.

AGATHGA PANTHA - Expect the unexpected from Wellington-based Agatha Pantha - a folk/rock four-piece whose sounds range from bouncing rhythms to dark, tangled ballads to anthemic rock numbers. The product of four unlikely allies joined by musical fortitude and lived experience, here to provide a therapeutic soundtrack to the everyday.
https://agathapantha.bandcamp.com

KINGSTON HIGH ALL STARS - The Kingston High All Stars are a Wellington-based band founded by 5 friends who are inspired by the brilliant, hypnotic and incredibly rhythmic music coming out of the Western Sahara. KHAS has since developed their signature style, blending desert blues, psych-rock, middle eastern classical, reggae and funk.

https://on.soundcloud.com/AbWAV1ZLdrs7cgOvf2
https://www.facebook.com/p/Kingston-High-All-Stars-100092946333859/

description:
Thabani Gapara at Wellington Jazz Festival, Award-nominated saxophonist and composer Thabani Gapara presents Dzindza — a powerful celebration of African jazz fusion.
Nominated for Best Jazz Album at the 2025 Aotearoa Music Awards, Dzindza showcases Gapara’s deep connection to his Southern African heritage, blending the sounds of Afrobeat, Highlife, Mbaqanga, and Mbira with influences from across the African diaspora, including Zouk, funk, and soul. This dynamic live show features a high-energy ensemble delivering rich musical storytelling, infectious grooves, and genre-defying improvisation. Dzindza is both a tribute to ancestral roots and a bold expression of contemporary African jazz

description:
The Amber Temple at Vogelmorn Upstairs, Wellington, The Amber Temple marries mysticism with gritty, ghoulish escapades of rogues and renegades. Vignettes of characters similar to you, similar to me, similar to someone you may have been or may one day become, all on the path towards the Amber Temple.
From the bowels of the molten earth, to the jowls of the predatory opportunist, to the angel casting light from celestial constellations, you will find yourself wrapped in a web from a sliver of time, a faraway place, perhaps an unknown space, as musician and dancer weave their tall tales of trials and tribulations, mortal life and looming death, unwavering love and venomous hate, environmentalism and satirical social commentary.
An original music and interpretive dance collaboration between singer-songwriter Julian Temple and contemporary dancer Amber Stephens.
Temple, known mostly for his work in the eponymous Julian Temple Band has written all new works for the project while Stephens, a trained contemporary ballet dancer and choreographer who ran her own dance company in Vienna, has choreographed the interpretive dance for this unique performance.
“A live dancer added a visceral element to an already emotional performance. Having a responsive artist interacting and interpreting the music through movement only heightened the experience. It bridged the gap between performer and audience.”
- Ed Castelow - Dictaphone Blues
“You’ll be a converted fan of The Amber Temple before they’ve even finished their first song. There’s an obvious sense of originality, coupled with carefully crafted dance moments and some of the most intense and outstanding folk songwriting you’ve heard. There’s a feeling though that nothing is premeditated and that improvisation is the star of the show - the kind of performance that requires decades of experience. Luckily for us, Julian and Amber have this in spades. Do yourself a favour, I guarantee you’ve seen nothing like it.”
- Sam Cullen - Singer/Songwriter
“Even having an understanding of the type of show The Amber Temple would be putting on when booking them - I was blown away by the amount of drama, tension and world-building Julian & Amber are able to accomplish in such an agile performance. The Amber Temple is a totally unique and utterly engaging experience which should be seen and celebrated.”
- Chris Scott - Seaside Music
Show starts at 7 Presale tickets $20 (+BF) via undertheradar.co.nz or $25 on the door

description:
The Barker Boys Live at Sprig + Fern Berhampore, The Barker Boys Live at Sprig + Fern Berhampore
The boys are back in town!

Get ready for the annual summer fun of The Barker Boys at the Sprig + Fern Berhampore. Every year the lads bring an evening of fun and sing-alongs. Music kicks off at 7.30pm.

This father and son acoustic duo play songs from the 50’s and 60’s through to modern day including The Beatles, Elvis, Taylor Swift, The Rolling Stones, Coldplay, The Who, REM, Oasis, Foo Fighters, Frank Turner and more...

Sean Barker is a Berhampore local and member of Wellington based bands The Wooden Box Band and Search For Yeti. His dad Geoff Barker is a popular performer across the Dordogne region of France where he lives, after an extensive career on UK radio.

Together Sean and Geoff become The Barker Boys.

They’ve played together over the past 25yrs (when in the same hemisphere!) and this is a chance to catch them during Geoff’s extended holiday in Aotearoa.

Free entry but a good idea to grab the crew and book a table by calling or sending the Sprig a message on Facebook — the gigs are always busy! It's an all ages gig with space inside and outside.

And if you've never seen the boys, here’s some video highlights from a UK gig...


Book a table now, and see you soon!

description:
The Bats celebrating 'Corner Coming Up' w/ Albert River | Wellington, The Bats celebrating 'Corner Coming Up' w/ Albert River | Wellington
Fresh from a triumphant, room-rammed set at The Other’s Way festival, Aotearoa indie legends The Bats are heading out on the road in 2026 to finally deliver the live accompaniment to their much-loved 2025 album Corner Coming Up. Recorded with Tex Houston at Chicks Studio in Port Chalmers, their 11th album Corner Coming Up charted at #1 on the IMNZ chart & #2 on the Aotearoa Music Charts and shows The Bats at their shimmering, melodic best; full of bright guitar lines, warm harmonies, and the band’s unmistakable Bats-ey sweet mystique.

A beloved part of the Flying Nun story, the band have maintained the same lineup since Robert, Kaye and Paul shoplifted Malcolm from The Bilders who played their first gig on New Year’s Eve 1982 in Dunedin.

So behold, nine shows across February and March in The Bats most extensive NZ tour in over 20 years, sharing songs from the record alongside treasured picks from their four-decades-deep knockout catalogue.

Adding to the intrigue, the Auckland headline date at Hollywood Avondale is part of Banished Music & Strange News newly minted Strange Universe show series.

ABOUT THE BATS

Formed in Christchurch in 1982, The Bats - Robert Scott, Kaye Woodward, Paul Kean, and Malcolm Grant - have quietly and loudly endured as one of New Zealand’s most beloved pop bands. An integral cog in the Flying Nun scene alongside friends/ contemporaries The Clean and The Chills, The Bats quickly developed a sound all their own: chiming guitars, melodic bass lines, and songs that unassume while are instantly memorable.

With a lineup that has stayed the same for over 40 years, their chemistry is unmistakable. Albums like Daddy’s Highway, Fear of God, Silverbeet, Free All The Monsters and so many more The Bats have cemented their legendary status at home and abroad, earning them a devoted generation-spanning following.
label: Music & Concerts

An integral cog in the Flying Nun scene alongside friends/ contemporaries The Clean and The Chills, The Bats quickly developed a sound all their own: chiming guitars, melodic bass lines, and songs that are unassuming while being instantly memorable.

With a lineup that has stayed the same for over 40 years, their chemistry is unmistakable. Albums like Daddy’s Highway, Fear of God, Silverbeet, Free All The Monsters, and so many more, The Bats have cemented their legendary status at home and abroad, earning them a devoted generation-spanning following.

description:
The Beatles Dub Club @ The NZ Fringe 2026, Coming to the NZ Fringe for its debut show - The Beatles Dub Club!
A special DJ set showcasing The Fab Four like you've never heard before!
DJ Chris Arnold takes you on a magical mystery tour of his collection of covers, remixes and tracks that sampled arguably the greatest band that ever existed - The Beatles. Expect to hear plenty of reggae, ska, latin, hip hop, dub, funk, house and even drum & bass takes on the wonderful music created by John, Paul, George & Ringo.
Since its explosive debut in 2021, The Beatles Dub Club has packed out stages at Glastonbury, Boomtown, Latitude, Isle of Wight, Camp Bestival, Green Man and far beyond.
The show has been championed by Fatboy Slim, who personally invited Chris to perform with him, and was tipped by Far Out Magazine as one of Glastonbury's "Top 20 Alternative Acts to Watch".
The Beatles Dub Club has since gone truly international, with acclaimed tours across Europe, Australia, New Zealand and Bali, while continuing to light up festivals all over the UK & Ireland - including standout sets supporting UB40, Craig Charles and The Wailers.
"If Sergeant Pepper had been a DJ, this would have been his set..." - Fatboy Slim
"Far from pure novelty, it is a wonderful way to celebrate music in all of its connective guises" - Far Out Magazine
"Loving it!" - Mary McCartney

description:
The Beatniks x IVY - NZ Tour 2025 - Wellington, The Beatniks x IVY - NZ Tour 2025 - Wellington
‘IVY’ and ‘The Beatniks’, two of the biggest independent artists coming out of Ōtepoti, are both known for their highly-captivating live performances. Melancholic in one instance, and packed full of noisy energy the next - now geared up with new material to showcase, the art-rock and surf-punk stylings of each of these young acts are tighter than ever.

‘IVY’ are held in the highest of regards when it comes to emerging kiwi artists. Nestling within the realm of dark and brooding tones, and immense, layered chorus, IVY know how to deliver a powerful and emotionally-resonant set; their sharp growth has quickly turned heads nationwide. From appearing on festival lineups such as Snow machine and OUSA Ori, playing with the Dunedin Youth Orchestra, and earning the SRN 2024 People’s Choice Award, IVY are ready to take their breathtaking art-rock performance around Aotearoa for the first time.

‘The Beatniks’ have been playing together since 2021, and have quickly become a ‘must-see’ live act within Aotearoa. After playing large-scale festivals last year, such as Rhythm & Alps, their recent release has delivered a more mature sound. Yet still soaked in their signature surf-grunge style. Having not toured the North Island since their debut album ‘Archetype’ in 2023, they’re ready to show you a whole new layer of alt-rock spirit on the stage.

description:
The Black Angels tickets, Presented by: Handsome Tours
2026 marks the 20th anniversary of the band’s debut album, Passover (2006), a now-classic record that helped define the 21st-century psych revival. To celebrate, The Black Angels - Alex Maas (vocals/bass), Christian Bland (guitar), Stephanie Bailey (drums), Jake Garcia (guitar), and Misti Hamrick (bass) are returning to the road to perform the album in full, along with their greatest hits.
Formed in Austin, Texas in 2004, The Black Angels have become one of the most influential bands of the modern psychedelic rock movement. Drawing inspiration from forebears such as Syd Barrett, Roky Erickson, Arthur Lee, and The Velvet Underground, the band crafts a sound that is both reverent to the genre’s roots and fiercely forward-looking, hypnotic, heavy, political, and immersive.
Beyond their own recordings, the band’s impact on the global psychedelic community is cemented by their role as founders of Austin Psych Fest, one of the world’s most important gatherings for psychedelic, experimental, and underground music.
Following albums such as Death Song (2017) and Wilderness of Mirrors (2022) on Partisan Records, The Black Angels continue to evolve while remaining unmistakably themselves: a band that channels the spirit of classic psychedelia into a dark, modern, and deeply powerful form.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
The Cowpokers + Tyson Smith, THE COWPOKERS: Foot-tappin' Onekaka Swamp Rock, World Famous in Golden Bay!

Golden Bay's finest local boys are rounding up and riding North to bring their unique brand of rock, blues and ska to the capital. What if swamp rock wasn't born in Louisiana, but in Takaka you ask? What if Iggy Pop and the Stooges had been Marlborough dairy farmers? What if Hendrix had settled in a Tukurua art gallery selling homemade jewellery crafted from shells and bone? The answer to all these questions and more can be found at a Cowpokers gig: a raw, barn-storming, rural-rock-and-roll sensation that 23 years of gigging has utterly failed to hone, polish, or refine.

TYSON SMITH: Wellington-based guitarist/singer/songwriter Tyson Smith will be bringing his unique, original music combining elements of rock, blues, folk, world music and freeform improvisation.

Tyson has worked as a guitarist with acts ranging from the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra to vocalist Hollie Smith, before focusing on his own music in the last few years.
In 2024 he celebrated 10 years since the release of his album The Hollow Tree with Rick Cranson and Ed Zuccollo, and released his new single Wolves. Tyson has been performing regularly around various New Zealand venues and festivals with his raw and exciting sound both with the trio and solo (utilising multiple amps and a bass drum).

description:
The Creation Voyages | NZ String Quartet, The Creation Voyages, from New Zealand Poet Laureate Robert Sullivan’s award-winning children’s book Weaving Earth & Sky is an exciting new performance from the New Zealand String Quartet – Te Rōpū Tūrū o Aotearoa. Through music and storytelling, with imagery by Gavin Bishop, the NZSQ vividly reimagines Aotearoa’s creation myths in an engaging, whānau-friendly performance.

Across 45 minutes, string quartet will meet live storytelling. NZSQ violinist Peter will narrate Ranginui and Papatuānuku’s embrace, their separation and the rise of the Atua, while accompanied by live sound effects and music played by the NZSQ on their unique instruments. Including, Pokarekare Ana, excerpts from Vivaldi’s Four Seasons and Holst’s Planets Suite.

See you at Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Library for a voyage back to creation!

description:
The Darkness tickets, Presented by: SBM
Multi-platinum UK rock royalty The Darkness are set to make their triumphant return to New Zealand in February 2026 with summer shows in Auckland and Wellington.
Following their massive 2024 Permission To Land 20th anniversary tour, the band are bringing their signature high-voltage energy and outrageous fun back to stages, serving up fan favourites like I Believe In A Thing Called Love and Love Is Only A Feeling, alongside new tracks from their latest album Dreams On Toast, including I Hate Myself and The Longest Kiss. This tour marks the first chance for fans to hear the new songs live.
Exploding onto the scene in 2003 with their now-classic debut Permission To Land, The Darkness quickly became one of the UK’s most beloved rock bands, racking up over 1.5 million album sales, a headline set at Reading & Leeds in 2004, and a string of major awards including BRITs, Kerrang!, and an Ivor Novell.
The band’s cheeky, spandex-clad anthems changed the face of British rock and continue to capture hearts and a new generation of fans around the world. Their live shows are pure spectacle: soaring falsettos, outrageous outfits, endless guitar solos, and crowds belting out every word. Don’t miss your chance to experience it all live in 2026 - it’s bold, loud, and gloriously over-the-top fun.
Joining The Darkness on their Australia & New Zealand tour is emerging Australian artist RAGEFLOWER – a magnetic force of cinematic alt-rock whose sound blurs the boundaries of emotion, experimentation and raw power. Her music balances fragility and strength in equal measure. Her live performances are powerful and deeply felt – part confessional, part spectacle – earning her a rapidly growing international audience across the U.S., Japan and Europe, and positioning her as one of Australia’s most compelling new voices.

description:
The Datsuns, Time has rolled on, and so has the clan DATSUN. After years of wrangling riffs across distant lands, marinating in sonic experiments, and rebuilding the clan’s percussive backbone, they return to their homeland with fire in their strings, fury in their rhythms, and rock & roll coursing through every vein.
 This tour marks the clan’s first full assault across Aotearoa since 2018, kicks off in March 2026, promising joyous savagery, riffs honed to perfection, and the raw energy that only The DATSUNS can deliver. The tour sees the clan’s Scandinavian drummer Adam Lindmark (Dead Lord) taking up the thundering seat, joining lead string wrangler Christian, Phil on the rhythmic weavings, and Dolf conjuring hooks across hemispheres, bringing a lifetime of Datsun lessons to the stage.
 Audiences can expect the full sweep of The Datsuns’ catalogue, from the anthems that scorched their early path to the first sparks of their eighth studio album, set to arrive in 2026. The first taste, ‘Ugly Leather’ – accompanied by a blistering video, old fire, new fuel, same unrelenting inferno.
