description:
The Dave Wilson Quintet, Dave Wilson presents his quintet in a special performance of newly arranged material from his two most recent projects: Free, Free: Meditations on Liberation (debuted in 2025), and Ephemeral (Thelonious Records, 2023).  

Free, Free draws from legacies of musical collectivity in an invitation to explore the expansive possibilities for what liberation might sound like. Ephemeral, described as “quite spiritually intense music” by The Guardian, explores the transience of human relationships with one another and the natural world through alternatively floating and driving improvisatory impulses of Wilson and his ensemble.

The quintet for this performance will present the music of Free, Free and Ephemeral in a brand-new configuration: Wilson on saxophone and bass clarinet, Mana Waiariki on violin, Seth Boy on bass, Callum Allardice on guitar, and Abe Baillie on drums.

Dave Wilson is a saxophonist, clarinettist, composer, producer, and interdisciplinary scholar. His music bridges avant-garde and experimental music with various groove-oriented styles from the worlds of jazz, R&B, electronic music, and more. Before relocating to Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington in 2016, Dave grew up in the Chicago area, lived for a decade in Los Angeles, and spent several stints living in Skopje, North Macedonia.

Part of the Wellington Jazz Festival 2025

description:
The Dire Straits Experience, From sold-out arena performances across Europe, the celebrated Dire Straits Experience now heads to Wellington. Personnel for the Long Highway World Tour has been assembled by Dire Straits veteran Chris White, who toured with the original band in the 90s. Prodigious singer-guitarist Terence Reis is also on board, adding further clout to the musical genius on stage.
Delving into Mark Knopfler’s platinum catalogue, this world-class ensemble reignites Dire Straits’ greatest hits with skill and showmanship. Hear classics like Money for Nothing, Walk of Life, So Far Away, Brothers in Arms, Sultans of Swing, Tunnel of Love, Telegraph Road, and plenty more. A seven-piece ensemble will take you on a two-hour odyssey with full concert production values.
Formed in London in 1977, Dire Straits was active until 1988 and then again from 1990 to 1995. Across six studio albums and five live albums, they have sold more than 120 million units worldwide.

description:
The Dire Straits Experience, THE WORLD’S GREATEST DIRE STRAITS SHOW RETURNS TO NEW ZEALAND FOR THREE SHOWS ONLY

The Dire Straits Experience brings the legendary sound of one of rock’s most iconic bands back to Wellington, Christchurch and Auckland this August.

The celebrated and critically acclaimed The Dire Straits Experience is set to return to New Zealand in August for three exclusive shows as part of their highly anticipated Long Highway 2026 World Tour.

Performing the unforgettable music of Dire Straits with stunning authenticity, world-class musicianship and full concert production, the internationally acclaimed seven-piece ensemble will play Wellington’s Michael Fowler Centre on Thursday 20 August, Christchurch Town Hall on Friday 21 August, and Auckland’s Kiri Te Kanawa Theatre on Saturday 22 August.

Assembled by original Dire Straits saxophonist Chris White — a key member of the Brothers In Arms and On Every Street tours — alongside acclaimed singer and guitarist Terence Reis, The Dire Straits Experience delivers a breath-taking journey through Mark Knopfler’s platinum-selling catalogue, bringing one of the greatest songbooks in rock history back to life on stage.

Audiences can expect a two-hour live concert spectacular packed with era-defining anthems including Money for Nothing, Sultans of Swing, Walk of Life, Romeo and Juliet, Brothers in Arms, Private Investigations, Tunnel of Love, Telegraph Road and more.

Handpicked from the highest levels of the international touring circuit, the ensemble features musicians whose collective careers include performances with Paul McCartney, Joe Cocker, Ray Charles, Robbie Williams, ABC, Tears For Fears, Roachford — and Mark Knopfler himself. Together, they recreate the musical power, precision and spirit that made Dire Straits a global phenomenon.

More than 40 years since Sultans of Swing first introduced the world to Mark Knopfler’s unmistakable guitar and songwriting genius, Dire Straits’ music remains a defining force in rock history. With over 120 million albums sold worldwide, the band’s songs continue to resonate across generations.

Dire Straits also holds a unique and enduring bond with New Zealand and Australian audiences. Their monumental 1986 Brothers In Arms tour sold more than 900,000 tickets across Australasia, setting concert attendance records that stood for more than three decades and cementing the band’s place in the musical DNA of the region.

“We absolutely loved our 2024 New Zealand Tour and can’t wait to be returning with The Dire Straits Experience to play for all of our friends in New Zealand. See you in August!” said Chris White.

While Dire Straits officially disbanded in 1995, their music has never faded. The Dire Straits Experience is more than a tribute — it is a powerful celebration of a musical legacy that continues to captivate audiences worldwide.

For Kiwi fans, this is a rare opportunity to relive the songs, the sound, and the spirit of one of rock’s greatest bands — live in concert once again.

*Plus booking fees

description:
The Grogans - 'Stagger' Tour NZ 2025 | Wellington, Ready to take these new tracks on the road, The Grogans new album Stagger is out, plus the band are excited to announce a headline tour across New Zealand. Exploring another side of The Grogans' music, Stagger is a patchwork of different sounds and sonic inspirations that all come together in the one album, "it came from this idea that it was a jagged and stylistically different album track to track", explain The Grogans.
Kicking off their tour at Loons in Christchurch on Wednesday 3 September, the band then head to Yonder in Queenstown on Thursday 4 September, San Fran in Wellington on Friday 5 September before wrapping up at Double Whammy Auckland on Saturday 6 September. Prior to their Aotearoa dates, the trio will also be playing a seven date tour throughout Australia along with stops in LA and New York for North American shows this June.
Capturing the magnetic energy of their live shows, Stagger touches on themes of mental health, taking care of yourself and your loved ones, the occasional love song, and more. As the catchy chorus first single and album opener ‘Oh Boy’ leads into
sonic powerhouse of a tune ‘Come Up (Goes Down)’, ‘In My Heart’ slows it down to a new easy listening direction, followed by ‘Have a Little Dream’ - as dreamy as the title suggests - and the big open echoed instrumentation of ‘Once In A While’. Adding new textural effects in ‘Roll Back’ and last single ‘Roundabout’, ‘Happier Man’ dips into a heavier psych realm with a reminder that "striving to be a better and happier person should be a goal for everyone." ‘Worry About Everything’ is an upbeat tune sure to have you worrying about nothing, and feel good album closer ‘All My Days’ ends on a more serious note that outlines the beauty and the beast of live music and the personal struggles that come with the lifestyle and touring.
Tickets go on sale 12pm, Wednesday 28 May.
label: Music & Concerts

They will also be playing unreleased selections from their recently recorded follow-up album, French Politics, across two sets of original compositions by Hector McLachlan. The music of The Hectet draws from a wide pool of influences, reflecting an open and ambivalent attitude to genre that has given it a unique and broad appeal.

Hector (piano, synth) is a pianist and composer from Te Whanganui-a-Tara who has played across Aotearoa and the world with acts like Revulva, Salvia Palth, Rachel Andie, The Unknot, and The Teskey Brothers. He has also released an album of electronic music on US cassette label Become Eternal.

The Hectet aims to please, and they can't wait share their soulful and expressive stylings with you.

Wild Swiss garage psych punk trio The Jackets - fronted by enigmatic vocalist/guitarist Jackie Brutsche, she of the Love It To Death-style eye makeup - will release their 6th album Essentials on Chaputa Records (Portugal) on March 20.

Serving as an Introduction to the band on the back of their long-awaited first Australian and New Zealand tour, which starts February 25, the album will be available directly from the band at their shows ahead of its official release and is also available to pre-order online now.

description:
The Jesus Lizard - San Fran, Wellington, The Jesus Lizard Return to New Zealand this October:
The quintessential punk band of the 90’s - the Jesus Lizard, returns to New Zealand shores for the first time in 27 years this October! Playing two exclusive shows only at Auckland’s Tuning Fork and San Fran in Wellington on the 11th and 12th respectively.
After initially calling it a day in 1999, the Jesus Lizard officially return full time to save us from the current state of musical mediocrity with their latest album, Rack. A blistering resurgence of the so-called ‘noise rock’ they helped define alongside contemporaries Big Black, Flipper, The Birthday Party, with their previous and most noted albums Head, Goat and Liar. For those of us who live in fear of the reunion album and subsequent tour, the Jesus Lizard thankfully display not only the same chaotic and dark nihilism of their earlier careers but also the maturity and seasoning of a band riding a wave of renewed and reinvigorated form.
Once slated by famed engineer Steve Albini as “the greatest band I’ve ever seen’ the Jesus Lizard not only lived up to this lofty praise in their prime but continue to do so in their advancing years. David Yow still leads the charge as the maniacally possessed frontman entering crowds with reckless abandon and a stamina that much younger vocalists would kill for. The original rhythm section of David Wm Sims and Mac McNeilly further continue to prove why they were and are the best bass & drum combo since Jones and Bonham, anchoring the ship as Captain Yow and first mate Denison navigate the wild seas of their songs. And while he may not always feature (as he rightly should) on many modern music journalists ‘best guitarists lists’, Duane Denison could perhaps be the most innovative and idiosyncratic punk rock guitarist EVER. However, each member is a sum of their parts but combined they are as Albini also once said “the purest melding of the sublime and profane.”
Whether you are a longtime disciple of the Jesus Lizard, seeing them when last here in ‘98, or perhaps your fandom is more recent and have only seen videos of their legendary live performances, you will know that these shows are not to be missed.
Tickets available Thursday 8TH May at 12pm from:
Saturday 11th October 2025 - The Tuning Fork, Auckland (All ages):
https://moshtix.co.nz/.../the-jesus-lizard-nz-tour.../180227
Sunday 12th October 2025 - San Fran, Wellington (R18 unless accompanied by your legal guardian)

description:
The King's Singers, C L O S E H A R M O N Y

For over half a century, The King’s Singers have been synonymous with impeccable blend, radiant tone, and joyful music-making. Formed in 1968 by six choral scholars from King’s College, Cambridge, the group quickly earned an international reputation for their unique approach to “close harmony” — a seamless weaving of voices across centuries and styles. Today, their performances continue to enchant audiences from London to Los Angeles, and now, back in Aotearoa.

This bespoke programme, created especially for their March 2026 tour, offers a journey through The King’s Singers’ remarkable musical history. Beginning with their earliest repertoire from the late 1960s, the evening will move through Renaissance sacred music, English folksong, jazz standards, pop classics, and contemporary works. Expect Byrd alongside Billy Joel, madrigals alongside The Beach Boys, Disney magic alongside dazzling new arrangements from the songwriters of today.

The concert also carries a special significance — it will be one of the final New Zealand appearances for long-standing baritone Chris Bruerton. A proud Kiwi, Chris has been a cornerstone of The King’s Singers for over a decade, touring the world and helping shape their modern sound. His farewell tour offers Wellington audiences a rare chance to celebrate his artistry on home soil.

A highlight of the night will be the “Something Borrowed” segment, where the ensemble will present a pair of songs chosen especially for Wellington — a personal gift to the local audience, performed in their signature style.

With wit, warmth, and unparalleled musicianship, The King’s Singers promise an evening that is both a celebration of their legacy and a showcase of their continuing innovation. Whether you’ve followed their journey for decades or are hearing them for the first time, Close Harmony at Wellington Cathedral will be a night to remember.

The Lighthouse Trio is made up of three of Wellington's busiest players; Alex Trask, Jeremy Grant, and Elijah Mulheron. Alex is a highly regarded alto saxophonist who is seen all around town leading bands and playing for some of the leading musical organisations, including the RNZAF band and formerly the Rodger Fox Big Band. Join Taylor Sol for a 90-minute handpan concert in 432 Hz, offering a deeply immersive listening experience through rhythm, melody, and resonance.
This is a concert-style event where guests are invited to sit comfortably and witness the music as it unfolds. The evening includes a brief spoken opening, one hour of live handpan music, and a gentle closing reflection to complete the journey. The handpan’s warm, organic tones create an ambient soundscape that supports relaxation, nervous system balance, and a sense of connection, both to nature and to the inner listening space. This offering is intentionally simple and inclusive. No participation, movement, or prior experience is required. Just arrive as you are and allow the music to carry you.
WHEN & WHERE
Date: Thursday 26 February 2026
Time: 6:30pm – 8:00pm
Venue: The Polish Association In NZ Inc - 257 Riddiford Street, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
WHAT TO EXPECT
• A 90-minute seated concert experience
• One full hour of live handpan music in 432 Hz
• Opening and closing reflections & storytelling
• Ambient, immersive soundscapes
• A calm, grounded atmosphere
• Space to rest, listen, and receive
WHO IS THIS FOR?
This concert is open to everyone, all ages and walks of life are welcome.
Perfect for those seeking:
• Deep listening and presence

Led by Nigel Patterson, one of New Zealand’s finest keyboardists/composers (The Black Seeds, Fly My Pretties) with support from Blair Latham (The Little Blast Orchestra, Jazz Robots) on tenor saxophone, Johnny Lawrence on bass and Peter Elliot on drums.
Inspired by such greats as Thelonious Monk, Duke Ellington, Mal Waldron, McCoy Tyner and many others, the NPQ creates a contemporary, sophisticated take on the jazz idiom.
From alternative metres through mood ballads and up-tempo swings, the NPQ seeks to bring through the edgier side of jazz while retaining the melodic and emotional character of the music.

description:
The Night Watch: LA NOTTE, The Night Watch presents LA NOTTE
Closing an exciting 2025 Season, LA NOTTE brings to Te Whanganui-ā-Tara a sultry, virtuosic evening of music from the Italian Baroque.
We are thrilled to welcome again guest soprano Carleen Ebbs in intoxicating works by Tarquinio Merula and Barbara Strozzi, and to spotlight our own Kamala Bain in Vivaldi's Recorder Concerto in G Minor 'La Notte'.
We're delighted to present guest violinist Anne Loeser (NZSO), who joins us as a soloist in Vivaldi's Violin Concerto in E Minor 'La Stravaganza' alongside our principal baroque violinist Miranda Hutton, and principal lute/theorbo/baroque guitar George Wills. We are joined again our principal keyboard player Rachael Griffiths-Hughes, viola da gamba Imogen Granwal, and welcome also guest percussionist Benjamin Whitton.
Continuing the theme of our 2025 Season, LA NOTTE explores different facets of the night through music that is, by turns, dream-like, sensual, and vibrantly rhythmic; featuring works by Barbara Strozzi, Isabella Leonarda, alongside many others,
Join us for a vivid, hot-blooded evening of music-making, featuring some of Aotearoa's finest specialists in early music.
THE NIGHT WATCH | co-directed by Luka Venter and Imogen Granwal

Kiwi rock fans are in for the ultimate celebration of grunge history as The Pearl Jam Experience crosses the Tasman to deliver a definitive, career-spanning greatest hits set. This special tour will honour the massive catalog of the Seattle icons, delivering a full-throttle, high-energy performance packed to the brim with Pearl Jam’s biggest anthems and fan favourites.

Widely regarded as the premier tribute to Pearl Jam, the band is renowned for recreating the atmosphere, the madness, and most importantly, the sonically accurate music that defined a generation.

Their commitment to the music’s authenticity goes beyond the stage. In a remarkable nod to Pearl Jam’s golden era, the band recently recorded a collaborative cover of the hit song Go with former Pearl Jam drummer Dave Abbruzzese. Abbruzzese, who drove the rhythm section during the band's peak explosive years, lent his signature powerful drumming to the track and mixed it for the group.

The Pearl Jam Experience also maintains a deep connection to the band's philanthropic legacy. They are proud supporters of the EB Research Partnership (EBRP), the largest nonprofit funding research for a cure for Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB), co-founded by Jill and Eddie Vedder.

For New Zealand fans, this is the ultimate chance to experience a high-octane concert that embodies the true sound and spirit of Pearl Jam, delivered with the energy, precision, and respect this legendary rock catalog deserves.

description:
The Pogues - Rum, Sodomy & the Lash 40th Anniversary, Bringing the spirit of Bluesfest to stages across New Zealand, Bluesfest Tours are proud to present one of next year’s most anticipated Bluesfest artists - The Pogues, who will perform three New Zealand sideshows nationwide, celebrating 40 years of their iconic album Rum, Sodomy & the Lash.

All tickets through Ticketmaster | Access all show tickets from Bluesfesttours.com.au

Now, for the first time in 35 years, The Pogues return to New Zealand to celebrate the 40th Anniversary of their seminal album Rum, Sodomy & the Lash — performed in full alongside beloved favourites.

Featuring original members James Fearnley, Jem Finer and Spider Stacy, this special line-up unites acclaimed guest vocalists Daragh Lynch, Iona Zajac, and John Francis Flynn, bringing one of folk-punk’s most influential albums back to life. Ranked among Rolling Stone’s 500 Greatest Albums of All Time, the 1985 classic features ‘A Pair of Brown Eyes’, ‘Dirty Old Town’, and ‘A Rainy Night in Soho’.

The Pogues are just one of the many world-class artists performing as part of Australia’s Bluesfest 2026 line-up, who have collectively sold tens of millions of albums, earned multiple GRAMMY Awards and Rock & Roll Hall of Fame honours, and defined generations of live music.

The Pogues’ New Zealand tour and Bluesfest return promise a rousing, soul-stirring celebration of one of modern music’s most enduring legacies.

description:
The Rag Poets at Greytown Upclose & Personal, This well-known Wellington band play many of those ‘heady’ Wellington hits from the 60’s & 70’s era, as well as new material they’ve written, and a bunch of covers from the likes of John Prine, Boz Scaggs and Neil Young. The band thrives on big vocal harmonies as they continue to maintain the unique sound they’ve developed over the years. Their audiences love the ‘timeless’ music they play and the stories they tell.
The band features very well-known musicians: Carl Evensen – vocals and percussion (Fourmyula), Rob Clarkson – drums, Alan Norman – accordion and 12 string guitar, who along with Rob played for many years with NZ’s seminal Country band The Warratahs, and Gary Creary on guitar. Gary hails from Toronto including a stint in the fabled Hawks Nest Band. George Barris, on bass, was a member of The Underdogs, Jigsaw, Fresh Air, Highway, and Blerta,
This will be a rocking great afternoon. BYO welcome, refreshments available for gold coin koha.

description:
The Reytons Australian & New Zealand Tour, UK music’s biggest underdogs, indie rock juggernauts The Reytons, keep charging forward on their unstoppable rise. Having flirted with overseas territories successfully over the past 5 years, the band are now heading out on their very first World Tour, and have announced their return to Australia and New Zealand this November and December

Renowned for their raucous live shows, and touted by many as the best live act of their generation, the British 4-piece pride themselves on their honesty and pure energy. Having taken their native UK by storm, with number one albums, sold out park shows and major festival headlines, the lads from Rotherham are taking on the world with their upcoming world tour.

In 2025 alone, they toured the UK, headlined Tramlines Festival and the iconic Wembley Arena. The upcoming world tour is a huge statement for a band who have hurdled every obstacle with nothing other than blue-collar grit and determination. It cements them as a band at the top of British music. The Reytons also recently announced their fourth studio album A Love Letter To A Broken Town - due for release in July.

Rooted in the rough around the edges humour and honesty of everyday life, The Reytons continue to channel their origins into everything they do, and A Love Letter To A Broken Town sees them staying true to those roots while pushing their sound forward with confidence and intent.

“I honestly feel like this album is the best we’ve ever done!” explains frontman Jonny Yerrell. "A lot of bands and artists like to change direction later in their careers, but that’s just not us. We absolutely love the style of music we make, the social commentary aspects and the people who turn up to jump around with us. Why would we change? Expect more, just bigger and better with a few surprises on the side! "

description:
The Rions Everywhere Every Single Day Tour | Wellington, Australian indie-rock four piece The Rions have announced the Everywhere Every Single Day New Zealand tour in support of their debut album Everything Every Single Day. 

Currently midway through their 19-date Australian run, the band are extending the celebration across the Tasman for three consecutive shows this May. They will perform at San Fran, Wellington on Thursday 7 May, Loons, Christchurch on Friday 8 May, and Double Whammy, Auckland on Saturday 9 May. With momentum at an all-time high, these shows welcome Aotearoa fans into The Rions most exciting chapter of their career to date. Tickets go on sale tomorrow, Wednesday 4 March at midday via moshtix.co.nz 

Made up of high school best mates Noah Blockley, Harley Wilson, Asher McLean and Tom Partington, The Rions have rapidly evolved from local Northern Beaches favourites into one of Australia’s most exciting indie-rock exports. They first began gaining traction in 2020, releasing a series of singles that led to their debut EP Minivan in August 2023, followed by Happiness In A Place It Shouldn’t Be in 2024. These early projects were picked up by Australia’s iconic Triple J, with breakout single ‘Night Light’ winning the station’s prestigious Unearthed High competition in 2021 and establishing the foundation for a national following. Their growth has continued to accelerate, translating into relentless touring cycles that quickly found a place in Aotearoa.

Now, the band are in the heat of their success, after the release of their debut full studio album, Everything Every Single Day, released via Community Music in October 2025. The record captures an evolution of their sound, delivering a pensive, contemplative and emotionally-driven collection of pristine indie-rock. It debuted at #1 on the ARIA Australian Artist Albums Chart and stayed familiar to Triple J, taking lead single ‘Tonight’s Entertainment’ to Like A Version, alongside their signature indie-pop rendition of Paramore’s ‘Ain’t It Fun’.

The Saints 73-78, The Saints ’73-’78 announce their New Zealand debut this spring, with concerts at The Powerstation in Auckland on 31 October and Meow Nui in Wellington on 1 November, before they head north to the UK and US.

Feel and Plus1 proudly present the band’s New Zealand tour which follows their hugely successful Australian tour in 2024 to crowds of 12,000 people across 12 shows.

Featuring founding Saints members, guitarist Ed Kuepper and drummer Ivor Hay alongside honorary Saints; singer Mark Arm of Seattle rockers Mudhoney, former The Birthday Party / Bad Seeds guitarist Mick Harvey and bassist Peter Oxley of Australia’s legendary Sunnyboys.

The Saints '73-'78 carry on where the original band left off in 1978 performing the material from their three incendiary albums (I’m) Stranded (1977), Eternally Yours (1978) and Prehistoric Sounds (1978).

“The Saints first three albums rank among the best records ever made. They have been a part of my life since stumbling upon them in the early 80s. Their influence looms large in Mudhoney world. I am stoked, stunned, and humbled that I get to joi in on this Rock ‘n’ Roll Reality Camp with Ed, Ivor, Peter and Mick!”– Mark Arm

The tour also comes off the back of arecent 4 LP box set of 1977’s ground breaking debut (I’m) Stranded which features the original album remastered forvinyl for the first time in over 40 years, the previously unreleased 1976 mix of the album, a 5-song live performance from April 1977 at Sydney’s Paddington Town Hall, a full live show from the London’s Hope and Anchor in November 1977 plus all recordings from the 1977 Top 40 charting This Perfect Day and 1-2-3-4 ep sessions.

“Rock music in the ’70s was changed by three bands—the Sex Pistols, the Ramones and the Saints” – Sir Bob Geldof.

Post Modern Jukebox are a group that samples modern songs and puts an old school twist on them! Their style suits creator Mila Te Whare-Manson perfectly. description:
The Sweet Caroline Tour — A Tribute to Neil Diamond, One of the top singer-songwriters to come out of the United States’ 60s music scene was none other than Neil Diamond. With a career spanning five decades, Neil is behind many hits that have stood the test of time and still woo listeners around the globe. Now you get to hear a tribute to him at The Opera House this November. 
Imbuing long-loved hits with new energy, The Sweet Caroline Tour recreates the feel of the famous man with careful attention to detail. It focuses on recapturing the sound, look and charisma of one of the world’s greatest entertainers. 
At the concert, you’ll hear songs that made numerous top ten lists, won Grammy awards and earned an induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Zac Coombs steps into the shoes of the original performer and brings his own musicality and showmanship to the stage. Don’t worry, you’ll hear all the timeless hits like Sweet Caroline, Song Sung Blue, Red Red Wine, Cracklin’ Rosie, Cherry Cherry, Crunchy Granola Suite, Shilo, Solitary Man, Kentucky Woman, I Am… I Said, and more. 
Relive an era when songs were written with heart, soul and honesty, and melodies stayed with you for a lifetime.

description:
The Temple / Jack Woodbury / Alter Natural, The Temple / Jack Woodbury / Alter Natural
On the heels of their sold-out Lōemis festival show ATOMS, The Temple returns to Pyramid Club with a writhing, distorted reimagining of the atomic sound world. Supported by solo sets from ambient/glitch sound wizard Jack Woodbury, and explorer-of-distant-noises Alter Natural sculpting a live set with his homemade suite of digital granular synthesis tools.

The Temple is a trio composed of producer Jack Woodbury, drummer/percussionist Nathan Carter (aka Alter Natural), and saxophonist Peter Liley, based in Pōneke. The Temple's broad palette of influences reaches into minimalism, electronica, ambient, funk, doom metal, new age, sound art, and jungle, creating a beguiling, kaleidoscopic sound. Their shows explore vast musical territories, and every performance is a ritual devoted to the present moment.

---

Jack Woodbury is a Wellington-based composer and audio engineer. His compositional work focuses on juxtaposing noise and glitch textures against ambient materials. His work has been presented in the UK, USA, Australia and New Zealand.

---

Alter Natural is a New Zealand-based musician, composer/producer of electronic music, and multi-media sonic artist. As a music composer/producer, much of my work takes inspiration from visual art and real-world subject matter, driven by my deep passion to express beauty and philosophical sublimity through sound.

---

Peter Liley is a saxophonist (alto/bass) exploring the far reaches of technique on the instrument, known for unflinching brutalist soundscapes and endless rippling sequences, achieved using circular breathing.

The Veils - Fragile World w/ Jazmine Mary, Following the critically acclaimed release of ‘Asphodels’ in 2025, The Veils quickly return with a bold and invigorated new album titled ‘Fragile World’, out June 19 on V2 Records. Today, The Veils alongside Banished Music announce a 10-date New Zealand tour including 6 band shows featuring the closing show of Strange Universe: Winter in Auckland, and 4 solo performances.

“It feels right to start our Fragile World tour back home in dear Aotearoa. These are some of our favourite towns to play in on earth, and we can’t think of a better way to dust off this moth-bitten black suit and hat and get the show on the road. Come along, be merry, and as always, come up and say hi,” says Finn Andrews.

Arriving just over a year after their last release, ‘Fragile World’ marks a striking shift in tone and energy for the band. Recorded live to tape in New Zealand by Paddy Hill, with production by Tom Healy (Tiny Ruins, The Chills, Folk Bitch Trio), ‘Fragile World’ captures The Veils in an urgent and instinctive mode.

The album’s title is both a reflection of the present moment - a time in which many institutions appear to be crumbling before our eyes - and a metaphor for the act of creation itself. The process of making music, Andrews notes, is a delicate and fragile undertaking where thousands of small decisions gradually coalesce into a finished whole.

“We went into the studio with a lot of songs, but very little idea of the arrangements or instrumentation. It was truly exciting, having no idea what this record would sound like and only a few weeks to figure it out. It’s mostly Tom and me playing everything, with Joseph McCallum coming in at times. It was all very instinctual, quite full-on, and scary at times - but a good kind of scary, not scary like the real world out there.”
‍
With its immediacy, intensity, and emotional clarity, ‘Fragile World’ stands as one of The Veils’ most compelling releases to date.

description:
The WBS presents: The Raven Mavens Quartette CD Launch Concert, The Raven Mavens Quartette return to the Wellington Bluegrass Society for the launch of their eagerly anticipated new CD.

Since releasing their previous album of original songs in 2020 — also celebrated at the Bluegrass Society — the band have continued to delight audiences throughout Wellington, the Wairarapa and the Kāpiti Coast with their distinctive blend of blues, roots, folk and swing influences.

The Raven Mavens have become renowned for their catchy, blues-infused original songs, written primarily by band leader Cindy Muggeridge. Drawing on her deep roots in blues piano, as well as Latin rhythms and rock ’n’ roll grooves, Cindy's latest collection tells stories of life, love and loss, alongside wry social and political observations. In both performance and recording, she is joined by the exceptional talents of Kate Marshall on vocals, violin, accordion and flute; Marian Carter on vocals, saxophone, clarinet and recorder; and Anje Glindemann on vocals, drums and percussion.

The band are also excited to feature two original compositions by Kate Marshall on this new recording, with Kate taking the lead on piano, supported by the other Mavens.

A unique all-female ensemble, the Raven Mavens Quartette gives every member the opportunity to shine as both instrumentalist and vocalist. What began in 2011 as a duo, with Cindy on boogie and blues piano and Marian contributing soulful vocals and clarinet, expanded to a trio with the addition of drummer Anje Glindemann, and later became a quartet when multi-instrumentalist Kate Marshall joined the group.

Each member is a gifted musician and singer in her own right, but together they create a musical chemistry that is greater than the sum of its parts. Their rich combination of voices and instruments produces a sound more often associated with a much larger ensemble. Audiences can expect humour, passion, warmth and exuberance, all in service of songs that remain firmly at the heart of the performance.

Join the Raven Mavens Quartette for an evening celebrating original music, masterful musicianship and the release of a remarkable new collection of songs.

The Warratahs at MEOW, The Warratahs are one of New Zealand’s best loved bands and have just been inducted into the NZ Music Hall of Fame.
For nearly 40 years they have toured their iconic NZ music to audiences in New Zealand and Australia, from large festivals to small country towns and just about everywhere else in between.
They have released 8 charting studio albums, winning gold and platinum awards for the songs that have become part of this country's musical culture since 1987 when the band formed.
Their last album "Runaway Days" won the 2017 Tui Music Awards Country Album of the Year. Their latest album “Burning Daylight” will be released in July.
They have supported several international artists, including John Cash and The Highwaymen, Billy Joel, Jackson Brown and Lucinda Williams during their shows in New Zealand.
The Warratahs have 3 times been music video finalists at the International TV & Film Awards in New York. Their latest singles and supporting videos are “Silver Train” and “Goin’ Up North”.

The Wooden Box Band at Greytown Upclose and Personal, The Wooden Box Band in concert 4pm 19 October in Cobblestones Museum new gallery.
The Wooden Box Band has some of Wellington’s best known musicians getting together and having fun playing the kind of music they love.


Songster Jessie Moss came from Jessie James and the Outlaws which was a staple of the Newtown scene a few years back. Newtown Rocksteady musician Jeremy Desmond has been in the Wooden Box band for many years bringing an array of guitar tones on his bright red Gibson 335 and effects pedals. On bass is the busiest bassist in town, Murray Costello, who cut his musical teeth in the Mockers during the eighties and has been playing hard ever since.

He plays an electric upright to bring bottom end to the urban folk sound. Together with Jessie Moss the other main songwriter in the band is local luthier Paddy Burgin, who’ s also busy with the Zimmermans and other acoustic and electric groups around the capital. He features on acoustic guitar, slide guitar and keyboards. The front row of singers is completed with Emily Clemmett who also brings her trumpet and fiddle to the party, and together with Jessie and Paddy these three produce thrilling harmonies reminiscent of the Mamas and the Papas.

On drums we have Search for Yeti man Sean Barker who keeps a very lively beat going behind the rest of the musicians. He’s also on quips and humour.
Their music has a sixties vibe with the tones and harmonies. They believe in adventurous tuneful songs with universal themes that people can relate to. And they perform them in a very engaging manner. Expect to be toe- tapping and even singing along!
The Wooden Box Band’s latest album, Broken River, was released over the winter. You can find them on Spotify for a preview.

Your Favourite Band (YFB) is proud to present The Music of Kendrick Lamar: Reimagined Live.
Titans of Aotearoa music celebrating one of hip hop’s most influential voices.
Kendrick Lamar (K-Dot, Kung Fu Kenny, Cornrow Kenny, oklama) is known for pushing boundaries—blending sharp storytelling with jazz, funk, soul, and experimental hip hop, and unquestionably reshaping the sound of modern hip-hop.
This show flips Kendrick’s catalogue into a live setting, reworking key tracks with new textures, live vocal samples, heavy grooves, and room to stretch out and improvise. Performed by members of renowned boundary pushing bands in their own right Avantdale Bowling Club and Yoko-Zuna.
Don’t miss out on this homage to one of modern music’s most important voices at Wellington’s own Meow Nui.
Support to be announced.

description:
Third Chapter, 
D, Muss & JLaw is a jazz trio that embodies the spirit of creative rebellion, their music a potent fusion of genre-bending experimentation and emotional intensity. Comprised of pianist James 'Muss' Illingworth, drummer Darren 'D' Mathiassen, and bassist Johnny 'JLaw' Lawrence, this trio has forged a unique sound that defies categorization. Soundscapes oscillate between heavy jazz and thumping hip-hop beats, soaring to emotionally powerful improvisations and dissolving into moments of sublime euphoria.
Their compositions are a testament to their collective creativity, weaving together intricate polyrhythms, hypnotic melodies, and explosive improvisations that conjure the raw energy of a live performance. Illingworth's piano playing is a masterclass in dynamic range, shifting seamlessly from delicate nuance to thunderous crescendo, often augmented by his deft use of synthesizers and electronic textures. Mathiassen's drumming is a force of nature, his polyrhythmic wizardry propelling the music forward with unstoppable momentum, while Lawrence's bass lines provide the foundation, his earth-shaking tones anchoring the trio's sonic explorations.
The trio's connection is palpable, their synergy born of years of collaboration and experimentation. They've worked with some of the biggest names in music, from Shapeshifter to Bliss n Eso to Louis Baker to Allen Stone, and their experience has honed their craft, allowing them to push the boundaries of jazz and beyond.
When D, Muss & JLaw takes the stage, the energy is electric. Their performances are a testament to their deep connection, their music a living, breathing entity that evolves and adapts in the moment. They're not just playing notes - they're conjuring emotions, telling stories, and transporting their audience to a realm of sonic wonder. This is their Third Chapter.

description:
This Silent Divide EP Release Show With Kaletta and Adult Friends, Wellington rock band This Silent Divide celebrate the release of their new EP with a show at Moon in Newtown with locals Kaletta and Adult Friends in support.

This Silent Divide mix driving drums, wall-of-sound guitars and melodic overtones to create catchy, high-energy songs. The band released their single City Lights in July, with Loud Enough? Magazine labelling it a lively piece of modern rock with a twist of punk attitude. A gritty, energetic music video accompanied the release of City Lights, filmed in Wellington's Eastern Suburbs and featuring fellow musicians and fans.

Following time in the studio in early 2025, again working with local producer Toby Lloyd at Tiny Triumph Recordings, the band has played a range of live shows. Upcoming single 'Rockets' is out in September, ahead of the release of their new 4-song EP in October.

In 2024 the band released single 'In This World' which Flash-Trax labelled “an absolute belter of a track” and 2023 singles 'Outside', 'Beautiful Creature' and 'Morning', received positive reviews and radio play in New Zealand, the US & UK, taking the band's music to a wider audience.
Check out the City Lights music video on YouTube, and the band's music on your favourite music streaming platform.

Kaletta
Kaletta is a high-energy band that blends Latin rhythms with punk rock and ska influences, creating a unique sound that's infectious and danceable.
Kaletta's been making waves on the live scene playing the Island Bay Festival, embarking on a tour of the top of the South, and reaching the national finals of the Battle of the Bands competition twice. The band is currently working on new material and a music video.The band's momentum is building and they're grateful for the support of their fans and the music community.

Adult Friends
Adult Friends are a Wellington-based guitar-centric, post-punk/post rock act, inspired by bands like At The Drive In, Failure, and The Cure. 2025 has seen the band release their album Find Me In The Inferno, along with a music video for single 'Greyhounds'. Regulars on the local scene, the band recently supported Toronto punks Pup at their Wellington show.

Throwing Muses, Throwing Muses - one of the most acclaimed US college bands of the 1990s - will perform two New Zealand shows in December.


The band has announced concerts at San Fran, Wellington on 9 December, and Double Whammy in Auckland on 10 December.
Throwing Muses' Aotearoa tour is part of New Zealand promoter Plus1 Touring's 25th anniversary celebrations.
These are Throwing Muses' first shows in New Zealand since 1994.
Formed by Kristin Hersh with high school friends, the band pioneered a new alternative sound, releasing a string of critically celebrated albums and touring the world.
Throwing Muses - featuring Kristin Hersh, David Narcizo and Bernard Georges - recently released new album ‘Moonlight Concessions’ which has been described by Pitchfork Magazine as: “A stunning return to form”.
‘Moonlight Concessions’ goes back to basics, a return for Throwing Muses to their esoteric off-kilter best courtesy of Kristin’s pin-sharp sketches and their suitably abrasive musical arrangements. The album follows ‘Sun Racket’ from 2020, a heady set filled with tough and tender tales spiked with surreal imagery.
Don't miss Throwing Muses performing their career-spanning concerts in Auckland and Wellington in December.

description:
Thundercat tickets, Presented by: Bench Music
Known for his jazz-fusion sensibility and elastic funk, Thundercat is bringing his 2026 tour to Wellington this May, performing live in support of his new album Distracted. See his show at Meow NUI in Wellington on Wed, 6 May 2026.
In an age of endless notifications and fractured attention, Thundercat turns the chaos inward on Distracted, his long-awaited new album and one of his most resonant statements yet. Six years on from It Is What It Is, the record captures the restless aftermath of grief and modern overload, balancing existential weight with Thundercat’s unmistakable wit and warmth. It’s an album that laughs through the noise, folding jazz-fusion virtuosity, elastic funk and late-night introspection into songs that feel like unfiltered inner monologues: tender, funny, and painfully human.
That philosophy carries directly into the live experience. Onstage, Thundercat treats Distracted not as a lecture on modern life, but as a shared release, stretching songs, breaking the fourth wall, leaning into humour and spontaneity as a form of survival.
Thundercat's New Zealand shows promise moments of presence inside the noise: music that drifts, refocuses, and reminds you why joy still matters. It’s playful, loose, deeply human, and a rare chance to experience Distracted and all of Thundercat the way it was meant to be felt, not scrolled past.

description:
Tim Rogers @ Moon, Tim Rogers (You Am I) performs live at Wellington venue MOON for an exclusive one-off solo NZ performance.
As the frontman of You Am I, one of the essential Australian rock n’ roll bands which has released ten studio albums to date. Three of these releases debuted at number one on the ARIA charts in consecutive order –1995’s “Hi Fi Way”, 1996’s “Hourly, Daily” and 1998’s “#4 Record”– with the Albums also receiving multiple Platinum and Gold status for commercial sales.
Tim Rogers musical career has also produced side projects, collaborations and solo albums which include the release of his first solo album in 1999 (with backing band The Twin Set) “What Rhymes With Cars And Girls”.
Following releases included ‘Spit Polish,” “Dirty Ron/Ghost Songs,” “My Better Half”(with Tex Perkins), Rogers Sings Rogerstein,” “The Rules Of Attraction”(with the Bamboos)and 2017’s incredible “An Actor Repairs”. Tines Of Stars Unfurled was released in early 2023, the companion record and bookend to Tim’s Debut 1999 record What Rhymes With Cars and Girls. It debuted at #4 in the ARIA charts and was seen as his strongest solo record in a over a decade.
Whether as part of You Am I or as a solo artist since 1999, Tim Rogers has received 13 ARIA Awards, including Male Artist of the Year, Best Group, Best Independent Release and Album Of The Year.
In 2025 seminal You Am I record Hi Fi Way celebrated turning 30 years old with a top 10 charting deluxe reissue and a massive sold out national tour capped off by Tim Rogers and You Am I being inducted into the ARIA Rock and Roll Hall Of Fame.

Shenanigans are one of New Zealand's most accomplished and sought-after bands in Irish Traditional Music today. This young and exciting group creates a sound that is full of energy & innovation, whilst all the time remaining true to their traditional roots.

“Shenanigans was THE breakout band at the Gardens Magic in Wellington NZ".Their energy was infectious and the crowd response was incredible. They were able to connect to all ages, from Mohawked teenagers, to their grandparents. I had heard good things about them, but the musicianship, and stage presence playing live exceeded every expectation I had.” – Alan Thompson Director of Irish music Appreciation society 2013.

Shenanigans garnered much critical acclaim in recent years, even being compared to super groups such as by respected New Zealand Musician Magazine. Their meteoric rise in the music world was given a massive boost in 2011 when they were released their album Live 2005!. Shenanigans subsequently went on to receive the “Best live act on the Good Morning show” from well-respected Tv Presenter and were also named “Best Jokers” at The New Zealand Jokers Awards in 2012.

Following the tremendous success of their debut album “ballyscullymuckery”, the group’s profile was further raised with the release of their follow up title, “Live in your Lounge” in 2018.Nz Musician Magazine described it as having “so many good tracks, so much energy, a band in full control and having such fun yet well able to bring things down to a tearful pause”. Most recently Shenanigans was awarded “Top Band of few” by the a guy down the pub.


Shenanigans is one of New Zealand's hottest bands. Specializing in elegant live preformances, Shenanigans is the perfect choice for your event. Although based in Wellington, we perform regularly throughout the country; including Auckland, Christchurch, and Masterton. Shenanigans is a band seriously worth considering for the best possible wedding music that inspires non-stop dancing. In addition to weddings, we often play at charity events, corporate functions, catered affairs, and private parties. Shenanigans plays the best dance music ever written from the 1930's - present, which includes Irish Classics, Country, Rock-n-Roll, Ethnic, Group Participation, and much more. In addition, we keep our repertoire as cool as we can by constantly learning everyone's favourite songs. This hardworking Wellington wedding band spends a tremendous amount of time learning, reviewing, and ultimately perfecting the music required for each engagement. We play everything live without the artificial computerized support that most of our competitors rely on these days. You will notice that Shenanigans performs every song with a celtic fun twist. There is no better choice for wedding music.

description:
Titan - Wellington, Violinist James Ehnes performs Korngold’s dazzling, brilliant Violin Concerto before NZSO Artistic Advisor and Principal Conductor Gemma New leads the orchestra in Mahler’s magnificent Titan symphony.
Programme:
Thomas Adès The Origin Of The Harp (NZ Premiere)
Korngold Violin Concerto
Mahler Symphony No. 1, Titan
We begin in a mythical world, where a sea nymph is transformed in Thomas Adès’ haunting and atmospheric The Origin of the Harp.
From such exquisitely misty transfiguration, we emerge into the dazzling, technicolour brilliance of Korngold’s Violin Concerto. Performed by James Ehnes, Gramophone’s 2021 Artist of the Year, his extraordinary spectrum of colour and articulation finds its perfect match in this beautiful neo-Romantic score.
At the time of writing his first symphony, Mahler was best known as a conductor. Titan emphatically announced his arrival as a composer of extraordinary talent, bursting, sun-like, above the horizon. From primordial strings, to clarinet cuckoo calls heralding a sumptuous dawn, to the work’s mercurial moods of joy, gloom, hell and heaven, this magnificent symphony is the sound of the boundless universe itself being born.
Generously supported by Bill Falconer CNZM.

description:
Tom Callwood | Ant Donaldson | Lucien Johnson | Jonny Marks | Dayle Jellyman, Five of Pōneke's finest improvisors converge on the Pyramid Club to channel "electronic space jazz"!
-
Tom Callwood (double bass) is an improvisor and collaborator who has performed throughout NZ and the UK. He’s a regular in the local experimental and popular music scenes with bands including The Phoenix Foundation, Teeth & Devils Gate Outfit.
-
Anthony Donaldson is one of this country's great drummers and a pioneer of improvised music in Aotearoa. He has been a creative force in Wellington music for over four decades and continues to push the boundaries of accepted musical norms.
-
Lucien Johnson is a New Zealand saxophonist, composer, and theatre maker. In recent years he has focussed on creating his own unique jazz sound, shrouded in wonder and mystique. His last album, “Wax///Wane” received rave reviews internationally, with France Musique calling it “Bewitching and Astonishing” and London Jazz News describing it as “Mystical, a touch retro and increasingly spellbinding”.
-
Dayle Jellyman is a keyboardist, guitarist, composer and man of many bands - from regular jazz sessions to the positive punk of Love Party and the apocalyptic metal of Fvkvshima.
-
Vocalist and electronic musician Jonny Marks has been a key figure in the creative music scene in Wellington since the early 2000s. Modulating his vocal chords like a synthesizer, Jonny moves between sub-bass drones to ring modulated whistle tones with his voice alone - and now in a spellbinding combination with a beloved Synthi AKS.

Performing for years under the name Lost Bird, Ali built a reputation for writing heartfelt, melancholic folk-pop, playing everywhere from Wellington bars to stadium stages — including opening for Ed Sheeran in Auckland in 2018.

Now, after years of performing behind an alias, Ali is stepping forward under his own name, embracing his identity as an artist with an invigorated sense of purpose, and tackling his artistry with newfound confidence and clarity.

description:
Tom Cunliffe & Ali Whitton, Ali Whitton is a New Zealand-based singer-songwriter. Born in Aotearoa and raised in rural North Yorkshire, his music blends introspective folk, alt-country, and acoustic storytelling, drawing inspiration from artists like Nick Drake, Bright Eyes, Johnny Cash, and Bob Dylan.
With poetic lyrics rooted in nature and emotional honesty, his songs explore themes of longing, resilience, and cosmic wonder. After an early career touring the UK and France – including sharing stages with Ed Sheeran – Ali settled in Aotearoa New Zealand, where salty sea winds and bush covered landscapes continue to shape his sound.
-----------------
Tom Cunliffe returns with 'Spit Out Your Gum' – his fourth album and most intimate release to date. Vivid, offbeat, and full of heart, the record captures Cunliffe at his most direct, delivering a collection of songs that glow with warmth and humanity.
Across its tracks, Cunliffe takes listeners on a journey from the streets of London to the bright lights of Karangahape Road, and out into the cold green waves of the Irish Sea. Each song feels alive – steeped in imagery, character, and a quiet intensity that rewards deep listening.
Recorded live-to-tape at Roundhead Studios, 'Spit Out Your Gum' carries the unmistakable warmth of that hallowed room and the people within it. With Paddy Hill engineering, Cunliffe was joined by Dave Khan (violin, piano) and Cass Basil (bass, clarinet).
Together, they captured performances that unfold in real time – no edits, no digital polish, just songs recorded in single takes, preserving the intimacy, imperfection, and energy of the moment.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Tom Scott tickets, Presented by: Live Nation
Off the back of the release of his Aotearoa Music Chart topping album ANITYA, Tom Scott brings his self untitled tour to Wellington to play Meow Nui on Friday, 8 May.
Raw as exposed nerves after a car crash, and as tender as the final kiss goodbye, ANITYA is the first solo album from Tom Scott, one of the most acclaimed New Zealand artists of his generation, hip-hop or otherwise. Recorded with a cast of 30 of the most versatile musicians, beatmakers and vocalists in his contact list and the award-winning studio engineer and producer Ben Lawson, it represents a significant creative breakthrough for one of Avondale’s finest. A tale told in two halves, ANITYA is a collect call from the void, offering redemption as you gaze into the house fire. Rendered through a nocturnal blend of progressive soul, dream-pop, jazzy psychedelic folk and ambient R&B, the album’s ten songs confirm Scott’s status as a preternaturally gifted lyricist with an ear for a unifying hook, revelling in the expansive possibilities of who he is still becoming as a songwriter, producer and melodist.
It’s not all pretty, but it’s high art. After all, much like the truth, art can be very ugly.
Born of the blood, sweat, and tears shed with Homebrew, @Peace, Average Rap Band, and Avantdale Bowling Club, Scott’s craft as a music maker and performer is second to none.

Tommy Emmanuel CGP - Living In The Light Tour | Opera House, Wellington, Tommy Emmanuel CGP - Living In The Light Tour | Opera House, Wellington
Tommy Emmanuel CGP - Living In The Light Tour
NEW ZEALAND 2026

Special guest: Mike Dawes

World-renowned guitarist and master entertainer TOMMY EMMANUEL, CGP is thrilled to announce what is sure to be an unforgettable tour of New Zealand in May 2026.

The five-date tour takes in Auckland, Hamilton, Palmerston North, Wellington and Christchurch.

TOMMY EMMANUEL, CGP is a living legend in the world of acoustic guitar, celebrated for his jaw- dropping technique, innovation, and boundless musicality. He has enthralled audiences around the globe with his dazzling fingerstyle performances, and now, New Zealand will have the privilege of witnessing his mastery up close and personal.

“I feel like the Indiana Jones of the guitar world,” says the globe-trotting fingerpicker. “I’m on this wild journey, just making it up as I go, and I’m thrilled that so many people are having fun joining along with me.”

TOMMY EMMANUEL Hailed as “one of the best acoustic guitarists in the world” by NPR’s World Cafe, Tommy Emmanuel got his start at the age of six, when he first began touring his native Australia with his family’s band. As a teenager, he earned a reputation as a highly sought after sideman and session player, and by his early twenties, Emmanuel was playing on chart-topping hits and performing with acts like Air Supply and Men at Work.

TOMMY EMMANUEL, CGP, Living in the Light Tour

Sunday 17 May - Town Hall, Auckland
Tuesday 19 May - BNZ Theatre, Hamilton
Thursday 21 May - Regent Theatre, Palmerston North
Friday 22 May - Opera House, Wellington
Saturday 23 May - Isaac Theatre, Christchurch

description:
Tommy Emmanuel CGP — Living In The Light Tour, He’s a world-renowned guitarist and master entertainer. Tommy Emmanuel, CGP, is bringing his beloved Maton guitar to The Opera House stage in Wellington. He is considered a living legend in the acoustic guitar world. The Australian musical legend has enthralled audiences around the globe with his dazzling technique. The concert promises to be an inspiring journey as Tommy strums and plucks his way through jazz, rock, country and pop music. Fans will be captivated by the diverse musical landscape he creates. 
Since his career began in the 1960s, Tommy has toured with luminaries like Eric Clapton and John Denver. He has won a Grammy Award and performed for a televised audience of more than two billion at the 2000 Sydney Olympics. Collaborations include guitar greats like Les Paul, Mark Knopfler, Joe Walsh, and Richard Thompson. 
Tommy’s hero, legendary guitarist Chet Atkins, bestowed the title of Certified Guitar Player (CGP) on him. He is one of only four players in the world with the title. Tommy Emmanuel CGP continues to push the boundaries of what is possible on the acoustic guitar.

description:
Tony As Robbie Williams Tribute, For over two decades, Tony Lewis has been turning heads and wowing audiences worldwide with his incredible portrayal of Britain’s greatest entertainer — Robbie Williams. Since debuting in Legends in 2002, Tony has performed across the globe, leaving crowds asking, “Is that really…?”
Based in Manchester, England, Tony first met Robbie in 2005, earning his idol’s approval when Robbie said, “I think it’s great, I’m really flattered! It’s bloody hard work being me!”
Three years later, Tony reached the finals of BBC One’s The One and Only, performing to over 7 million viewers each week. His uncanny resemblance and spot-on performance have led to countless TV appearances, promotional campaigns, and even official work for Robbie’s album Rudebox.
Tony has also appeared alongside stars like Simon Cowell, Olly Murs, Stephen Fry, and Ant & Dec — even helping prank Robbie himself on Saturday Night Takeaway!
His show captures all the greatest hits, from the early classics and swing favourites to modern anthems and a touch of Take That. With the looks, the moves, the voice, and the attitude — Tony Lewis truly is Robbie Williams!

description:
Tony Lee, solo piano, Join us for a recital of Scriabin and Rachmaninoff given by Australian pianist Tony Lee.

Scriabin -

Prelude Op. 11, No. I in C major
Prelude Op. 17 No. 5 in F Minor
Prelude Op. 16 No. 1 in B major
Etude Op. 2 no. 1 in C# minor

Rachmaninov -
Sonata No. 1 in D minor, Op. 28

Sydney-born pianist and educator Tony Lee has gained a reputation as one of Australia's finest young pianists. He seeks to transmit the essence of music and his understanding of it through his performances and teaching. Tony was an artist in residence at the Chapelle Musicale Reine Elisabeth in Belgium and worked closely with the renowned Portuguese Swiss pianist Maria-João Pires between 2014-2019.

In 2023, Tony served on the Piano Faculty at the Zhejiang Normal University and Emporia State University Undergraduate Joint Program and now holds the position of Artistic Advisor for the Rising Stars Program at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

Tony has performed across the Asia Pacific, Europe, the USA and has appeared as soloist with the BBC Philharmonic Orchestra, Brussels Philharmonic Orchestra, National Ballet of China Symphony Orchestra, Shanghai Philharmonic Orchestra, Lanzhou Symphony Orchestra, Chengdu Philharmonic Orchestra, Guangxi Symphony Orchestra, Samara Philharmonic Orchestra, Queensland Symphony Orchestra, Adelaide Symphony Orchestra, Tasmanian Symphony Orchestra, and New Zealand Symphony Orchestra.

Do not miss this one.

description:
Too Many Chiefs at Kapiti Playhouse, Wayne Mason, Andrew London and Rob Joass work regularly with their own respective groups but come together several times a year to collaborate, sharing songs, complaints about the music industry, gossip about other musicians, and irreverent banter with audiences around the country. Their individual influences and performing styles range from blues and jazz to Americana-infused country and folk, often with an element of social commentary, personal reflection and occasional satire.

Andrew’s reputation stands mostly on his satirical and comedic songs which lampoon many of New Zealand society’s obsessions, foibles and taboos. They have had audiences all over Australasia in stitches, and have contributed to a Correspondence School English Syllabus, several feature films, over 20 recorded albums and a stage musical.

Rob Joass is well known throughout New Zealand through his work with Hobnail, The Shot Band, and The Hard Core Troubadours. He writes compulsively, tours incessantly, teaches guitar and produces albums for other artists. Rob is a 3 time finalist at the NZ Music Awards.

Patriarch of the group Wayne Mason has been instrumental in the formation and success of some of the most revered names in Kiwi music history. Rocking Horse, the Fourmyula and the Warratahs all owe their inception to Mason, who shows no signs of slowing the pace, or lowering the standard he set back in 1969 when he penned the song ‘Nature’, named by APRA in 2004 as ‘Best Kiwi Song of the Century’.

Sophie Songbird makes her solo debut this spring, stepping into the spotlight with a voice and vision all her own. Known for her work with the beloved band Dr. Reknaw, Sophie now unveils a fresh chapter — touring in celebration of her first solo release and sharing a collection of unreleased, vintage-inspired originals that blend nostalgic charm with a modern twist.

Drawing from the rich traditions of jazz, blues, and country — with a touch of psychedelic flair — Sophie’s songwriting is both timeless and distinctly her own. Her stories are laced with wit, warmth, and a hint of mischief, offering a refreshing take on classic genres.

Her debut single, “Topless Picking Flowers” — set for release on September 19th — is a dreamy fusion of classic country and smooth Hawaiian tones. On stage, Sophie captivates with exceptional rhythm guitar work and a honey-toned voice that soars effortlessly.

with support from ABBEY EVE
label: Music & Concerts

Transvision Vamp - Meow Nui, Wellington, NZ, Transvision Vamp - Meow Nui, Wellington, NZ
UK pop rockers Transvision Vamp are bringing those glorious hits to NZ in February - their first tour here since 1991!

Formed in 1986, Transvision Vamp quickly rose to fame. Their songs Baby I Don’t Care, Revolution Baby, I Want Your Love, The Only One, and If Looks Could K*ll, were all NZ chart hits.

Joining original Transvision Vamp's Wendy James and Dave Parsons onstage are guitarist Alex Ward (The Thurston Moore Group) and James Sclavunos (Nick Cave and The Bad Seeds) on drums.

Says Wendy James: "I am so very excited to be coming back to New Zealand to play the songs which started my whole musical journey! I remember vividly so many incredible moments gigging in New Zealand, moments of enormous success, enormous love and enormous fun."

description:
Transvision Vamp, Transvision Vamp announce first New Zealand tour in 31 years!
British pop rock band Transvision Vamp are bringing their hits down under for the first time in almost three decades. With shows in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch lined up for February 2026, the group will be playing their nostalgia-filled favourites.
‍
Formed in 1986, Transvision Vamp quickly rose to fame. Their songs 'Baby I Don’t Care', 'Revolution Baby', 'I Want Your Love', 'The Only One' and 'If Looks Could Kill' all hit the Top 50 in the New Zealand singles chart from 1988 - 1991. Wendy James, the lead singer and focal point of the group, attracted media attention with her sexually charged and rebellious image.

Transvision Vamp became known for their collision of brash punk and commercial pop, and joining James on this tour are some musical luminaries: Alex Ward (The Thurston Moore Group) on guitar, Dave Parsons (Transvision Vamp) on bass, and James Sclavunos (Nick Cave and The Bad Seeds) on drums.

Wendy James went on to pursue a successful solo career spanning an additional seven studio albums, including a notable collaboration with Elvis Costello. She served as a feminist symbol in the 80’s for unapologetic self-expression and fearless leadership.

James says, "I am so very excited to be coming back to New Zealand to play the songs which started my whole musical journey! I remember vividly so many incredible moments gigging in New Zealand, moments of enormous success, enormous love and enormous fun. I’m bringing with me a set full of music that will thrill and musicians who will amaze!"
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Traskforce! Ft. Eugene Wolfin, Starring Eugene Wolfin on vocals, the octet will present a fizzing set of big band swing, Broadway hits, and gorgeous ballads. Hear the fine lyricism of the 20th century sung by one of Wellington’s most exciting performers.

Free entry! Koha encouraged.

For the last 8 years vocalist Eugene Wolfin has been a regular of Wellington music scene performing in a wide variety of genres including Jazz, Blues, and Rock ’n’ Roll. He has had a hand in a few local Musical Theatre productions performing lead roles in ‘Chess’ and the modern hit ‘If/Then', and is a regular in front of Jazz Orchestras including the Royal New Zealand Air Force Band and the Rodger Fox Big Band.

Traskforce! is bandleader Alex Trask’s most swinging musical organisation. They play fresh arrangements of original compositions, classic swing, and Broadway ballads. This includes songs from the Basie repertoire, Bob Mintzer, Oliver Nelson, Quincey Jones, and Lionel Bart's Oliver! to name a few. The five horn arrangements allow for the power of a big band and the subtlety of a quartet to shine side by side. The band is made up of Wellington’s top players, including members of the Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra, the RNZAF band, NZSM faculty, and rising stars.

Photo by Oscar Laven
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Triske, Triske are a Wellington-based folk trio blending Celtic traditions with a modern energy. Drawing on Irish, Scottish and Breton influences, their music moves easily between lively dance tunes and reflective songs, creating performances that are warm, intimate and richly melodic.

The band features Em Griffiths on vocals, fiddle and whistles, whose expressive playing and clear, engaging voice sit at the centre of the group’s sound. With a background in classical violin and traditional music, Em brings both precision and emotional depth. Ceara McAuliffe Bickerton shapes the music’s character on flute and whistles, adding lift and lyrical colour. On guitar and vocals, award-winning Bob McNeill provides rhythmic drive and harmonic foundation, drawing on many years in New Zealand’s folk scene.

Their debut EP, Flightless (2023), showcases both original songs and traditional arrangements.

Come along and enjoy this great gig in our special space, up close and personal.

description:
Tudor Consort presents Prophetiae Sibyllarum, The Tudor Consort is thrilled to present Orlande de Lassus' Prophetiae Sibyllarum, one of the greatest works of the sixteenth century.
The twelve motets that comprise the work are written in a style known as ‘musica reservata’ or ‘musica secreta’, featuring highly chromatic chord progressions for greater emotive and expressive effect. In the very first bars Lassus breaks the rules of accepted harmonic practice to produce the sort of music that will not be written again for hundreds of years.
As the name suggests, this style of music was considered very specialised and just for performance to an educated and initiated audience. Prophetiae Sibyllarum is seen by many as the apex of this style, blending expressionism with breathtaking beauty.
This incredible work provided the basis of our sold out performance of Michael Norris’ SoundCathedral at the Aotearoa Festival of the Arts, and we can't wait to perform it in its entirety.
We round out the programme with our favourite Tudor works by Tallis, Byrd and Gibbons, alongside Ross Harris’ Vobiscum in aeternam which was written for The Tudor Consort in 2011.
This will also be our final solo concert in the Lower North Island this year, we hope to see you there!

Twisted Frequency - Techno Taster, This year for the first of our annual pre-parties we’ve gone around the country to gather a lineup of creators working at the intersections of techno, delving into influences from bass, breaks, psychedelia, club music and beyond, all underpinned by elements of dance music's most enduring genre.
We believe each one of these acts is currently pushing the needle forward for underground club culture in Aotearoa, and are thrilled to host them all together at Valhalla to push their vision across the almighty Third Eye Hi-Fi soundsystem.

ELI HØFF — Abyssal Soundworks / PHTM
Producer and DJ, Eli is undoubtedly at the forefront of Aotearoa’s underground dance scene.
Those who have kept their ears tuned to the innovative underground have no doubt stumbled upon the tribalistic, psychedelic, and focused sounds emanating from the mind of Auckland-based producer Eli Høff. With a string of releases on Berlin-based PHTM, Tāmaki Makaurau-based Gypnotica, and an impressive catalog of self-releases, he consistently showcases his singular and original interpretation of dance music.
Instagram.com/e.li
elihoff.bandcamp.com
abyssalsoundworks.bandcamp.com

HUNTER — Hang the Saints / Haven
Raised in Kaikōura, Aotearoa, Hunter's dark and atmospheric sound often contrasts the beautiful environment she grew up in. Her direct approach to techno draws influence from heavy percussion, bold rhythm and industrial soundscapes. After spending two years finding inspiration in clubs overseas, she has returned to Ōtautahi with a refined style that’s ready to make people dance. As the co-founder of “Hang The Saints” and resident of “Haven”, Hunter is all about creating safe, inclusive spaces for people to connect through the music she loves.
https://www.instagram.com/sspoonsnake/
https://soundcloud.com/hunter-mccrory-334790608
https://on.soundcloud.com/bC3qeA6pUxBoMo7P9

LUDUS & RIZZO — Tonic Collective
Tonic Collective is the recent endeavour of Ludus and Rizzo, inspired by the people, places and spaces of their experience touring China with BIRDPARTY and Vera Ellen. Both acts are individually known for their versatile and innovative sound, bringing a wide range of influences and inspirations to the dancefloor. In the short time since establishing the collective, they’ve already hosted Kaishandao and Bone Chapel, established a space, and debuted a monthly radio show on Mouthfull that explores sound from across the genre spectrum, both in the club and out.
https://www.instagram.com/ludus.etc/
https://www.instagram.com/alicerizzoofficial
https://www.instagram.com/tonic.collective/
https://soundcloud.com/l-s.../416life-support-cl1n1c-chengdu
https://soundcloud.com/racquetclub-info/mix-series-016-ludus

SHLI — Echo Train Records / Warehouse Rave / Holding Hands
Shli is the alias of Ōtautahi-via-Pōneke DJ and Producer Tim Ward. Steadily releasing works over recent years through local labels like Echo Train and the Big Fresh Collective, he is carving out a sound of his own.
Stitching together infectious rhythms layered over low-end pressure, Shli’s sets draw influence from across the hardcore continuum and beyond. Creating dancefloor moments from trippy rhythmic states to unleashing sheer bass weight.
https://www.instagram.com/____shli/
https://echotrainer.bandcamp.com/.../ech009-bracing-set...

description:
ULCERATE + Vicissitude, Via Debemur Morti:
“After triumphantly casting off the shackles of claustrophobic dissonance on 2020's lauded ‘Stare Into Death and Be Still’, New Zealand unorthodox Death Metal legends ULCERATE up the ante even further with mind-bending 7th album ‘Cutting the Throat of God’.
An acknowledgement that the band's most powerful and affecting material leans to the melodic side, this refined and hook-laden new record is a self-sufficient universe unto itself, a conflagration of inventively visceral Death/Black Metal where dizzying experimentation meets head-nodding abandon - obscenely twisted and addictive, heart-stopping in its depth of feeling.”
To complete the touring cycle for ‘Cutting…’, the band will undertake seven Australasian headlining dates in 2026. Special guests for the New Zealand leg are the utterly deadly Vicissitude.

description:
UPCHUCK: Australia & New Zealand 2026, If you’ve been waiting for a band that hits hard, means it and leaves nothing behind, this is it. I OH YOU and MG Live are pumped to announce provocative punk powerhouse Upchuck are bringing their explosive live show down under. The ferocious five-piece from Atlanta will make their Australian and New Zealand debut next March, with shows in Brisbane, Sydney, Melbourne, Auckland and Wellington, as well as a featured set at Victoria’s Golden Plains festival.
The tour follows the release of their blistering third album – and Domino debut – I’m Nice Now, out now here. Produced and mixed by Ty Segall, the album is a bold evolution of their sound – a raw, urgent and emotionally charged statement of survival and resistance. Formed in 2018 by a crew of Atlanta skaters in their early 20s – KT (vocals), Mikey Durham (guitar), Hoff (guitar), Ausar Ward (bass) and Chris Salado (vocals/drums) – they quickly became hometown legends. Their debut Sense Yourself (2022) and Ty Segall-produced follow-up Bite The Hand That Feeds (2023) cemented their fearless reputation. Early singles Freaky and Facecard earned praise from punk icons Iggy Pop and Henry Rollins, who both played tracks on their radio shows, while support slots for Faye Webster (who calls Upchuck “her favourite band”), Amyl and the Sniffers, Soul Glo, Osees, King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard and a breakout Coachella 2024 performance further solidified their status.
A fierce lineup of local acts will join Upchuck around Australia and New Zealand. Captivating fourpiece Blue Diner kick things off in Brisbane on Wednesday 4 March; Post-punk rockers Xiao Xiao open in Sydney on Friday 6 March with secret guests in tow! Punk Naarm trio CLAMM bring their raw and visceral sound to Melbourne on Wednesday 11 March, while Aotearoa rockers DARTZ take over Auckland on Friday 13 March and Wellington on Saturday 14 March with their signature fiery live set! Like your punk loud, honest and unfiltered? This is the tour you’ve been waiting for. Don’t miss Upchuck’s debut down under.

description:
Uncle Acid and The Deadbeats AUS / NZ Tour, UK psychedelic heavyweights Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats return to Australia and New Zealand this December, bringing their dark, hypnotic live show to stages across the country.
The brainchild of Kevin Starrs, Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats have spent over a decade carving out a singular space within the global heavy music landscape. Since emerging in 2009 from the depths of the British underground, the band have built a reputation for their unmistakable fusion of warped psychedelic pop, downer blues and doom-metal intensity.
Too bold and idiosyncratic to be easily defined, Uncle Acid’s sound is steeped in haunting melodies, layered vocal harmonies and eerie, cinematic arrangements, offset by crushing riffs and a persistent sense of unease. It’s a sonic world that feels both deeply nostalgic and completely otherworldly, cementing Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats as one of the most compelling live acts in contemporary rock.
With their last visit to our shores in 2020, Australian audiences can expect a set that traverses the band’s cult catalogue, delivered with the immersive intensity that has made them a must-see worldwide.

description:
Unwrapping Beethoven with the Elouan Quartet, Unwrapping Beethoven is an intimate musical experience that invites audiences inside the world of
Beethoven’s string quartets. Intertwining performance with conversation, the Elouan Quartet
explores this extraordinary genre - from its structural brilliance to its emotional depth through a
series of musical examples, reflections, and insights from the players themselves.

Rather than a traditional concert, this event weaves together discussion and live performance to
illuminate Beethoven’s compositional voice, the evolution of the quartet, and the interpretive
decisions that bring this music to life.

Along the way, audiences will encounter stories, ideas, and moments of discovery that
deepen their connection to the music and offer a fresh perspective on these remarkable works.

The Elouan Quartet, formed in 2025, comprises New Zealand Symphony Orchestra players with a
special love of chamber music and performing in informal and intimate settings.

Violinist Jessica Oddie studied at the Juilliard School, Yale University, and the Yale School of Music.
She returned to New Zealand in 2020 when she was engaged as Guest Assistant Concertmaster of
the NZSO. She was delighted to join the orchestra as Assistant Principal Second in 2022. Jessica has
recorded albums of chamber music for the Naxos and Tactus recording labels, including the
premiere recording of twentieth-century Italian composer Gino Gorini’s chamber works. She has
performed in festivals including the Venice Biennale, the Norfolk Chamber Music Festival in the US,
the Toronto Summer Music Festival, and in Fontainebleau, France.

Originally from Paeroa, Anna van der Zee is a member of the first violin section of the NZSO. Trained
in Wellington, Germany and USA, Anna co-founded the Tasman String Quartet. The quartet ventured
to Boulder, Colorado for two years to study under the renowned Takacs Quartet. Alongside her work
with the NZSO, Anna runs Karori Classics - a series of monthly chamber music concerts supporting
local charities. She plays regularly in chamber music groups with her NZSO colleagues and is a core
member of contemporary ensemble Stroma.

New Zealand violist Alexander McFarlane is Associate Principal Viola with the New Zealand
Symphony Orchestra. Equally at home in a solo, chamber or orchestral idiom, he has performed
internationally in venues including the Wigmore Hall, the Barbican Hall, the Musikverein in Vienna
and the Concertgebouw in Amsterdam. As a chamber musician, he has collaborated with artists
including Steven Isserlis, Janine Jansen, and the Doric String Quartet, and performed at festivals
including IMS Prussia Cove, Yellow Barn, ‘At the World’s Edge’ Festival, the ‘Mendelssohn on Mull’
Festival, and ‘Musique à Marsac’ in France.

London-born cellist Ken Ichinose was appointed Associate Principal Cello of the New Zealand
Symphony Orchestra in 2014. He is the cellist of the Ghost Piano Trio and also performs regularly
with contemporary music group Stroma. Ken returns to London regularly to perform chamber music
with his siblings and work with orchestras such as the London Symphony and Royal Philharmonic.
Before moving to New Zealand, Ken was a founding member of the Galitzin Quartet with whom he
performed for ten years,
