description:
VEGYN (DJ SET) | WELLINGTON | MEOW, Sprawling with obtuse bass lines, sharp digital peaks and asymmetrical drum machines, Vegyn’s music doesn’t walk a straight line so much as trip over itself beautifully.
The London-born producer, artist, DJ and label head returns to Australia and New Zealand this October for a rare run of headline shows, supported by NYC producer amr*.
Across everything he touches - from surreal club sets to production work for Travis Scott, JPEGMafia and Frank Ocean - Joseph Thornalley makes music that’s hard to pin down and harder to forget. His productions are jagged and abstract, built from negative space, ambient haze and rhythms that never quite resolve. There’s hip hop in the DNA, but it never plays by the rules, always veering towards something stranger, softer, rawer.
Through his label PLZ Make It Ruins, Vegyn has built an entire world. His 2019 debut Only Diamonds Cut Diamonds felt like a manifesto; the 71-track Text While Driving If You Want To Meet God! followed as a chaotic, genre-agnostic statement of intent. Since then, he’s ventured further leftfield, releasing The Head Hurts but the Heart Knows the Truth under the alias Headache, followed by the 2024 masterpiece The Road to Hell Is Paved with Good Intention, and the unexpected arrival of Blue Moon Safari - an output that feels made more for himself than for any audience. Dreamlike, disjointed and deeply personal.
As a DJ, Vegyn shifts between industrial breaks, ambient drift and warped club memories. This October, he returns to Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane, Wellington and Auckland - a rare chance to slip through the cracks and step inside his world.
label: Music & Concerts

Iron & Wine, the moniker of singer/songwriter and film studies lecturer Sam Beam, returns to Australia for the first time since 2018 – this time as soloist in a captivating run of shows in capital cities and festival appearances, drawing from his transcendent and illuminating folk sounds.

Known for his deeply burnished vocals, keen melodic sensibility, and introspective, free- flowing lyrical point of view, Iron & Wine is one of the preeminent artists and collaborators of the first wave of indie folk. Following his most recent EP release of covers, Making Good Time – a collaboration with Ben Bridwell (Band of Horses), and his 2024 full length album Light Verse, Iron & Wine come to Australia off the back of a huge US tour with award-winning trio I’m With Her and Seattle favourites Band of Horses.

description:
Vera Ellen - Heave Knows What Time | Wellington, Vera Ellen - Heave Knows What Time | Wellington
Aotearoa Music Award-winning and Taite Award-winning artist Vera Ellen releases her new album Heaven Knows What Time. on May 1 via Flying Nun Records. Alongside the album release, Vera Ellen returns to Aotearoa in July for a six-date national tour in celebration of Heaven Knows What Time.

The title Heaven Knows What Time. arrived while Vera was lying on the top bunk of a house truck in Buenos Aires, nearly two years after writing the record and almost a year after completing the mix. After multiple working titles, it surfaced with clarity and immediacy - less a decision than a moment of recognition. It reflects the album’s central tension: frustration and surrender to forces outside of control. As Vera describes it, creativity cannot be demanded - it can be nurtured, but ultimately arrives in its own time, “like a baby”.

The album was written during a two-week songwriting residency in Greytown, awarded through the NZ Pacific Studio Artist Residency Programme. The residency provided space and solitude away from touring and performance, culminating in a performance at Studio 73 for fellow residents and members of the local community.
‍

In her residency application, Vera wrote: “After the heaviness of Ideal Home Noise, I feel it is pressing that I now create an uplifting record that has a guiding message of hope, but from a matured perspective.” While that intention is present, Heaven Knows What Time. resists neat resolution, moving through themes of love, joy, self-assurance, humour, moodiness, and heartbreak - positioning Vera as an observer of both inner and outer worlds.

Alongside extensive touring in Aotearoa — including the 2025 Laneway Festival — Vera has performed internationally with her band, including a 14-date tour of China, a sold-out run in Australia supporting Crowded House, appearances at New Colossus Festival and SXSW (Austin and Sydney), and a full UK/EU support tour with Yumi Zouma. She is set to support Aldous Harding on her full UK/EU tour and perform at The Great Escape in Brighton. The Guardian described her performance as: “Arising New Zealand empress Vera Ellen and band were a revelation, a shimmering reminder that pop’n’roll can still nudge one’s soul.”
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Violet Hirst Summer Tour: Hataitai Bowling Club Wellington, Contemporary singer-songwriter Violet Hirst tours small Aotearoa venues this summer. An evening of layered vocals, familiar melodies and unique songwriting supported by Madeleine Dove.
Born and raised in Tāhuna Queenstown, Violet's musical journey began the day she was born: opening night of her mother's musical Kitchens. Her songs and live performance embody the theatrics and ballads that surrounded her childhood. Gaining comparisons to Aldous Harding and Julia Jacklin, Hirst’s songs combine hypnotic vocal melodies with meditative rhythms and poignant lyrics from a young woman. After touring the USA as a support musician for Flying Nun rockers Office Dog, Hirst is back on the road to share her own new works.
Her debut album Donegal was recorded in Central Otago with De Stevens (Roundhead Studios, Marlin's Dreaming) and Reuben Scott (Saltwater Criminals, Molly Payton). The album received a Student Radio nomination for Best Album, charting on both SRN and Radioscope charts. Followed with a nationwide tour and sold-out shows, Hirst is excited to return to the road for the first time since then. Joined by Madeleine Dove (vocals, keys) the duo will perform new contemporary meditations and vocal experiments.
“(Donegal) is brimming with the confidence of an artist fully inhabiting their own sound; wistful and slightly heartbroken, but unencumbered by expectation." - RNZ
“Evident to everyone present was how special that rainy night was, how flawless, nuanced and emotive Hirst’s singing and songwriting. The real deal, with the crowd standing in the rain outside afterwards, not ready to leave, raving.” - NZ Musician
https://violethirst.bandcamp.com/

description:
Vocal Blokes NOT Over the Hill and Still Singing, Wellington Vocal Blokes are NOT going to Greytown as we first thought– Older, Bolder, and Still Singing, but we are having a workshop and concert in Wellington.
An afternoon of music, laughter, and good company on Saturday, 22 November.
Our end-of-year concert is bigger and better. This time we’re adding a singing workshop led by our young and inspiring music director, Paddy Shanahan, before rounding the day off with the 4:00 pm concert NOT Over the Hill and Still Singing at the Old Salvation Army Hall, 209 The Parade, Island Bay.
Workshop: Singing Together (2:00 – 3:30 pm)
Once you’ve warmed up, it’s time to build harmony. Drawing inspiration from Jacob Collier’s version of Coldplay’s Fix You, Paddy will guide the group in shaping simple “oohs” into rich, layered sound. It’s less about perfection and more about listening, blending, and feeling the joy of shared music.
You can take part in this workshop, and join the Vocal Blokes at the afternoon concert — a true “community choir” moment.
Workshops cost just $15 or $25 for both workshop and concert.
NOT Over the Hill and Still Singing is a playful nod to our cancelled journey from Wellington to Greytown and to the fact that most of us are, well, not exactly in our twenties anymore.
But that’s the beauty of it — we sing for the sheer love of it. Expect songs about travel, friendship, and meeting new people, all delivered with our trademark mix of heart and humour.
We love performing for audiences because you listen, laugh, and sing along in all the right places. There’s something special about our venue — the warmth, the curiosity, the way the hall fills with energy before the first note.
Come Join the Chorus. So, whether you’re a shower-soloist, a closet crooner, or simply someone who enjoys good company and great music, come spend the day with us. Bring your voice, bring a friend, and rediscover how good it feels to sing together. Workshop 2:00 pm. Concert at 4:00 pm.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Voices New Zealand presents: Ara Hura — A Visionary Journey, Aotearoa’s most influential choral conductor has made her mark across multiple choirs in New Zealand and beyond. The huge contribution of Dr Karen Grylls is celebrated in ‘Ara Hura — A Visionary Journey’. 
It’s fitting that this Aotearoa Festival of the Arts concert involves the choir Dr Grylls founded 28 years ago. Voices New Zealand debuted with a concert at the same festival in 1998. It has gone on to build a reputation for excellence in the music world. For this celebratory concert, the choir is joined by taonga pūoro artist Horomona Horo, leading instrumentalists, and a chamber ensemble from the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra. 
The concert centrepiece is Robert Wiremu’s Re-imagined Mozart: Erebus. The programme also features a new commission from Takerei Komene, as well as waiata by Ngāpō and Pimia Wehi. This highlights Dr Grylls’ pioneering collaborations that reshaped Aotearoa’s choral landscape. Her expertise as a choral clinician is sought internationally, and she regularly conducts masterclasses and workshops in Wales, England, North America, Canada and Australia. 
This marks Dr Grylls’ final appearance as Music Director of Voices New Zealand. It’s a rare opportunity to celebrate her vision, artistry, and legacy.
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Vorn and his Prog Consort / Thagomizer, Vorn and his Prog Consort / Thagomizer
Wellington legend Vorn Colgan has been writing and releasing extraordinary and odd popular music from bedrooms across Aotearoa and the world since 1999, a career which was scheduled to be cut short in 2019 by a terminal cancer diagnosis. 2023 saw him release his surprisingly non-posthumous hit The Late Album, and given his demonstrated inability to die he was left with maybe the world's most wonderful problem: what to record for his 10th album?

The answer is The Aeronaut, a 60ish minute meditation on Wellington, the universe, and everything, hewn from purest regionally-sourced prog rock and presented in a single baffling and hopefully pleasant serving. The Aeronaut is currently still a work in progress; this evening offers keen punters a chance to watch Vorn and his frighteningly good band (Nick Brown - Drums; Charley Davenport - Bass, Thomas Liggett - Violin) iron out the final kinks on a future Kiwi classic. Be there so you can say you were!

https://vornpowertool.bandcamp.com/

Thagomizer is the dino synth project (dinosaur themed dungeon synth) of Caspar Kneale (yes, he is related, in fact mr Birchville Cat Motel is Caspar's Dad). Inspired by the vibe of retro dinosaur media, Thagomizer aims to summon a Mesozoic mood to transport you back in time. As far as we know, Thagomizer is the only dino synth project in the country.


$17.50 presales available via UTR

Special thanks to CNZ for supporting Pyramid Club's programme

WELCOMER 'CALENDARS' RELEASE TOUR W/ BELLADONNA & KING HIT, Welcomer are embarking on their first nationwide headline tour to celebrate the release of their debut album Calendars, out June 12 via trusted DIY stalwarts, Papaiti Records.
Calendars follows a string of European shows in 2025 and a self titled EP which was described by Under the Radar as ‘melancholic splendour.. in swirls of harmonious goodness, each packed with presence and perfectly placed’. Single Nothing of You Remaining was described by Rolling Stone AU as “blending folk influences with strings for a warm, layered pop sound”.

Belladonna is the musical project of Bella Cook, a songwriter with a well-honed knack for musical storytelling, capturing the quirk and romance of everyday life. The debut Belladonna album, Arcus Way, was released in 2025 - a stunning collection of sharp and affecting songs with paired back arrangements.
https://belladonnamusicnz.bandcamp.com/album/arcus-way
King Hit is a Pōneke-based four piece melding the abrasiveness of shoe-gaze and punch of hardcore with the melancholy of Midwest-emo. Originally conceived as a three-piece by principal songwriter, guitarist and frontman Stefan Jenkins, King Hit cut their teeth in the Wellington underground scene for the first half of 2025 before adding Caitlin Gabb on guitar and vocals, joining bassist Felix Bird and drummer Sebastian Bell as architects of the band’s formidable wall of noise.

description:
WELLINGTON, NZ - Coal Miners Daughter - 7.30pm, Coal Miner’s Daughter celebrates the incredible life of the late great Loretta Lynn.
Amber Joy Poulton (Loretta Lynn), Lizzie Moore (Patsy Cline) and The Preacher Denis Surmon (Conway Twitty & Willie Nelson), along with kickin' band The Holy Men, will sing the story of and celebrate Loretta Lynn. In floor length gowns adorned with tassels and rhinestones, with hair as close to country music heaven as possible, where country music started and still should be, in the theatre, just like the Grand Ole Opry, and it's coming to New Zealand!
This inspiring show was a smash hit at the 2025 Tamworth Country Music Festival and has played to packed theatres across Australia since its debut in 2017, but it's New Zealand that has been screaming out for a tour and the cast couldn't be more excited for their first New Zealand tour in October 2025. They will have you tappin' your toes, tilting your head and falling in love with country music all over again with hits like 'Coal Miner's Daughter', 'You Ain't Woman Enough To Take My Man', 'Crazy', 'You're Lookin' At Country', 'Walkin' After Midnight', 'One's On The Way', 'Stand By Your Man', 'Faded Love' and more.
This is a show not to be missed!
"Loretta Lynn paved the way for women like me in country music to take centre stage" - Amber Joy Poulton star of Coal Miner's Daughter

description:
WJC presents The Louisa Williamson Quintet, Louisa Williamson presents music from her latest album, Groundwork, plus more recent compositions.
Louisa Williamson is a saxophonist, flutist, composer and arranger based in Wellington. Since completing a Masters of Music in Composition in 2020, she has released two albums of original music (What Dreams May Come and Groundwork). In 2023 Louisa won the APRA Best Jazz Composition Award for her piece Dream Within A Dream, and in 2024 Louisa received a composition commission from the Wellington Jazz Festival and headlined the festival with the new work, The Chasm Where We Fall Into Each Other. Louisa has worked with L.A.B, Bret McKenzie, AJA, The Rodger Fox Big Band, Royal NZ Air Force Band, Trinity Roots and Lord Echo. In 2016 Louisa was the first New Zealander to successfully audition for the JMI Jazz World Orchestra (consisting of the best young jazz musicians from around the world, aged 18-25), touring Germany, Belgium, Switzerland, Slovenia and Croatia.
Featuring: Louisa Williamson 9saxophone), Callum Allardice (guitar), Daniel Hayles (piano), Johnny Lawrence (bass), Max Sheehan (drums).

Andrews' ensemble will present a series of original compositions developed during his time as the 2024 Jazz Composer-in-Residence at Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington. These works reflect a compositional approach shaped by both the harmonic and improvisational sensibilities of contemporary jazz pianists such as Brad Mehldau, Robert Glasper, and Aaron Parks, and the rhythmic, melodic, and resonant qualities of indigenous Samoan music, drawn from my own cultural heritage. This synthesis seeks to articulate a distinctly Pasifika jazz sound. This performance marks the live debut of the full suite of compositions, which have been recorded and are set to be released later this year.

Wahine In Jazz X The Listening Collective Collaborative Jam, Rooted in the values of connection, care, creativity and community, Wāhine in Jazz (AKL) and The Listening Collective (WLG) are two kaupapa-driven initiatives, aimed to uplift women and gender diversity in improvised musical spaces across Aotearoa. They invite you to join, improvise and collaborate this Wellington Jazz Festival.
The jam will weave influences from Wellington-based saxophonist, composer and educator, Dave Wilson’s model for improvisation; Finding Common Ground - fostering environments for musicians of all abilities to come together and improvise. Let this session invite you to a space where improvisation becomes a language of belonging.
Wāhine in Jazz is a Tāmaki Makaurau based organisation that advocates for and promotes the development of female and gender diverse jazz musicians in Aotearoa.
The Listening Collective is a Te-Whanganui-a-Tara based group of female and gender diverse musicians that aim to create spaces that uplift and empower individuals in the presentation of their creative work

description:
Wairarapa Youth Orchestra: Around The World With Music, Get ready for a global classical musical journey as the Wairarapa Youth Orchestra presents their special concert, “Around the World with Music”!
The vibrant sounds of violins, flutes, cellos, trombones, and more will fill the Wairarapa Events Centre, Carterton as our young musicians from across the Wairarapa share their hard work. These talented tamariki and rangatahi are now ready to take you on an unforgettable adventure through sound.

Under the expert guidance of conductor Andrew Atkins and our dedicated tutors, the Wairarapa Youth Orchestra has been diligently preparing a diverse program that celebrates music from various continents. Prepare to be captivated by everything from the rhythmic pulse of African drums to the sweeping melodies of European symphonies, including the grandeur and pomp of Tchaikovsky’s 1812 Overture, and evocative folk tunes echoing the sounds of Asia. It’s a unique opportunity to experience a rich tapestry of sounds, all brought to life by the passion and talent of our local youth.

This inspiring event is more than just a performance; it’s a vital fundraiser. The Wairarapa Youth Orchestra offers free orchestral music learning to young people throughout the Wairarapa, and we rely entirely on fundraising and donations to keep this invaluable program thriving. Your attendance directly supports the continued musical education of our community’s youth.

description:
Waltz of My Heart, Step into a world of sweeping melodies, soaring voices, and the graceful rhythm of the waltz in this unforgettable concert Waltz of My Heart, a celebration of one of the most beloved musical forms in history.

From the iconic Viennese waltzes of Johann Strauss to modern interpretations such as The Anniversary Waltz and The Tennessee Waltz, this enchanting programme showcases the enduring beauty and emotional power of the waltz across generations and genres. Whether heard in grand ballrooms or intimate theatres, this music continues to captivate and enchant.

Taking centre stage are our four magnificent tenors whose rich, expressive voices breathe new life into classic and contemporary waltzes alike. Joining them is fabulous baritone John Bayne plus stunning Amanda Atlas, whose powerful soprano and magnetic presence bring depth and drama to every note.

This is a concert of melody, magic, and masterful singing — where every phrase is infused with passion and every performance is unforgettable. Let yourself be swept away by the romance, elegance, and enduring charm of the waltz.

Featuring:
Bonaventure Allan-Moetaua

description:
Warehouse Rave ft. Coki (UK), SYLC & Ghost Media Presents: WAREHOUSE RAVE FT. COKI
Friday 5th September
Secret Central Wellington Location (TO BE REVEALED ON EVENT DAY)
Powered by Banshee Soundsystem
7pm-1am
R18
Strictly limited capacity
Get ready Welly, because this one is about to be serious. We have secured the one and only COKI for an intimate warehouse rave at an inner city location.
This legend of bass needs no introduction, but we’ll give him one anyway. As one half of DIGITAL MYSTIKZ, Coki has made sine waves move like no other, architecting much of the sonic blueprint that modern dubstep has become known for. Alongside Mala, he helped forge the DMZ sound and is now making his way to Wellington for a rare showcase of pure low-frequency warfare. Expect heavyweight pressure, bone-rattling subs, and that unmistakable Coki wobble - this is dubstep in its rawest form.
On support we have drawn for the best of the best. Opening up proceedings we have BABETECH, champion selector and vibe master. Since murking opening slots for Loefah, Filth and Kahn & Neek as well as spreading the gospel of bass for countless evenings on RadioActive, we can’t think of a better opener for this night.
Following that, we have dubstep extraordinaire DUSTY warming things up with his signature and gruelling take on the classic dubstep sound. With releases on Infernal Sounds and Leather Kennel, Dusty has proven himself to be a force to be reckoned with, and is surely one of the most exciting young producers in the game today.
On closing duties we have the Support Your Local crew going b2b with Young Gho$t to round out the night with a bit of silliness.
We’ve managed to secure an all-new inner city warehouse location for this one, and its Further Sound on soundsystem duties this time, heating things up with their BANSHEE SOUNDSYSTEM, preparing for only its second full rollout after Cuba Dupa this year.
We’re unbelievably excited to share this space with you all for a dance and are expecting this to be one for the books.Secure your tickets now and don’t miss out on this momentous and legendary dance music event!
Tickets: https://events.humanitix.com/coki-uk-warehouse-rave

Join us for a night of warm rhythms, deep cuts, and pure analog sound, no sync buttons in sight, no USBs, just records. Expect everything from funk and disco to techno and eclectic breakbeat gems, handpicked and mixed live by an incredible lineup of wāhine DJs who know how to get the dancefloor banging.

Odette aka Gimpgirl, a subversive selector and true audio provocateur, returns with her signature breaks, and attitude that challenged every lazy beat around her.
Kimba Jade, vinyl devotee and groove alchemist, has been lighting up dancefloors for over two decades. Founder of Divinyl in Auckland and a master of soulful basslines.
All vinyl. All night.

Waypeople Album Release Tour - Wellington, Wellington-based saxophonist and composer Jake Baxendale brings together a remarkable collective of Aotearoa’s leading jazz and contemporary musicians for Waypeople, a luminous new album inspired by Ursula K. Le Guin’s English-language version of the Tao Te Ching. Drawing from jazz, Chinese classical music and improvisation, the project fuses lyrical storytelling with meditative textures and powerful ensemble interplay.

Featuring Chelsea Prastiti (voice), Jia Ling “Jessie” (guzheng), Callum Passells (saxophones), Daniel Hayles (piano), Seth Boy (double bass), and Rick Cranson (drums), Waypeople transforms the timeless Taoist philosophy of harmony, balance, and paradox into sound. The result is a work of shimmering beauty — grounded in jazz but alive with the rhythm of ancient poetry and the pulse of contemporary life.

description:
Wednesday 'Bleeds' NZ Tour - Wellington, Wednesday 'Bleeds' NZ Tour - Wellington
BANISHED MUSIC & STRANGE NEWS PRESENT
WEDNESDAY ‘BLEEDS’ NZ TOUR

FRIDAY 22 MAY - SAN FRAN, WELLINGTON
SATURDAY 23 MAY - LOONS, LYTTELTON
SUNDAY 24 MAY - HOLLYWOOD AVONDALE, AUCKLAND

When North Carolina’s noise makers Wednesday first visited Aotearoa off the back of their album RAT SAW GOD, audiences were taken by surprise in the best possible way. A 95bFM review called the band’s Whammy show “a sold out countrygaze extravaganza”, and everyone who came left with big hearts and even bigger smiles.

Now, with the band’s unbelievable sixth album ‘Bleeds’ out in the world, it’s high time that Banished Music and Strange News had their fun pals from Asheville down for a repeat visit, with three shows across Wellington, Lyttelton, and Auckland happening this May.

Bleeds is the album the band are calling “not only the best Wednesday record—it’s also the most Wednesday record”, with all the elements that make the Southern rock magic of this rare group so special. NME put it beautifully in their five-star review of the album, heaping well deserved praise on Wednesday’s “blown-out distortion, weirdo-country slide guitar and serrated melodies”.

Fronted and founded by the fierce and fun Karly Hartzman, whose songs are at once confessional and crack-up, Wednesday have built a reputation for being one of the best - and most dynamic - live bands on the circuit. Joining Karly will be the inimitable and animated Xandy Chelmis on lap steel and pedal steel, beat-keeper extraordinaire Alan Miller on drums, brilliant bassist Ethan Baechtold, and the band’s scorching touring guitarist Jake Pugh.

If you caught them last time, there’s no way you’re missing this. If you missed them the first time, it’s not too late to join the cult. Good times guaranteed.

“There's an ever-present joy, even during the most harrowing songs… this is catharsis personified” - Exclaim!

Welcomer 'Calendars' release tour w/ Belladonna & King Hit, Welcomer are embarking on their first nationwide headline tour to celebrate the release of their debut album Calendars, out June 12 via trusted DIY stalwarts, Papaiti Records.

Calendars follows a string of European shows in 2025 and a self titled EP which was described by Under the Radar as ‘melancholic splendour.. in swirls of harmonious goodness, each packed with presence and perfectly placed’. Single Nothing of You Remaining was described by Rolling Stone AU as “blending folk influences with strings for a warm, layered pop sound”.

https://welcomer.bandcamp.com/album/calendars

Joined in Pōneke by Belladonna and King Hit

Belladonna is the musical project of Bella Cook, a songwriter with a well-honed knack for musical storytelling, capturing the quirk and romance of everyday life. The debut Belladonna album, Arcus Way, was released in 2025 - a stunning collection of sharp and affecting songs with paired back arrangements.

https://belladonnamusicnz.bandcamp.com/album/arcus-way

King Hit is a Pōneke-based four piece melding the abrasiveness of shoe-gaze and punch of hardcore with the melancholy of Midwest-emo. Originally conceived as a three-piece by principal songwriter, guitarist and frontman Stefan Jenkins, King Hit cut their teeth in the Wellington underground scene for the first half of 2025 before adding Caitlin Gabb on guitar and vocals, joining bassist Felix Bird and drummer Sebastian Bell as architects of the band’s formidable wall of noise.

https://kinghit.bandcamp.com/track/sap

description:
Wellington Bluegrass Society presents: Forty Years In Harmony, Three friends Chris Priestley, Julian McKean and Angela Fox, who have been creating music for over forty years, come together to perform their first ever concert!

Julian McKean and Chris Priestley first met and played together in 1981 when they formed Acoustic Confusion with Denny Stanway and were later joined by Brendan Power. The four were guests at many NZ festivals including the 1983 National Folk festival in Wellington, and recorded the legendary LP Hazy Days in 1985.

After the group split up, they remained in contact and often performing and recording over the years. Chris recorded his first solo LP Argentina to Invercargill, during which he met Angela Fox and realised what a fabulous harmony singer she was. Angela also recorded two CDs of her fabulous songs. Julian continued to write great songs including Far Far Away which became a NZ folk classic. Angela and Julian individually helped Chris on most of the many LPs and CDs he recorded over the years. However Angela had never sung on any of Julians songs, likewise for Julian with Angela's songs.

"though the three of us have been playing together for more than fourty years, we have never done a concert together, so we’re looking forward to creating some magic at the bluegrass club"
- Chris Priestley

BENT HORSESHOE AND THE HOKOWHITU BOWLING CLUB PRESENTS
WELLINGTON HEADS ON SATURDAY THE18th OF OCTOBER AT 7.30 AT A COST OF $25

Wellington Heads have been playing for us for many years and always put on a great show.
and with a frontman like Neil Worboys how could they fail to.
They are also one of the few bands that have a brass section which is always great to hear.
They have a great time on stage and that comes across in their nusic.
If you have not seen them before take this opportunity ,you won't be disappointed.
Named after the striking features on Wellington’s rugged southern coastline, Wellington Heads have been playing in and around the capital city, and in venues further afield, for over 20 years.



Wellington Heads consists of three core songwriter-musicians (Geoff Keith, Neil Worboys, and Bill Wood) who combine with key musicians to form a larger live and recording band. Their songs comment on life experiences with a distinctive Wellington and New Zealand flavour.



Wellington Heads have evolved their own sound through the influences of Kansas style blue jazz, the swinging rhythm n blues of Louis Jordan and Ray Charles, Chicago blues and infused with Pacific/Hawaiian rhythms, New Orleans grooves and Latino feels.



Sharp and energetic, Wellington Heads entice people to the dance floor, regularly delighting audiences at Wellington venues, and playing festivals, corporate and private functions. They are frequently invited to perform outside of Wellington, and over the years have played Auckland, Tauranga, Manawatu, Nelson and Wellington Jazz and Blues Festivals.



Wellington Heads have recorded six albums, their latest, ‘World Keep On Turning’ was released in December 2023. This album continues their unique sound with a mix of rhythm n’ blues, swing, soul and latino grooves. In combining this with their previous albums, Wellington Heads have built an extensive repertoire of eclectic original songs.



Wellington Heads’ regular six piece line up is: Neil Worboys – vocals, guitar, harmonica, Bill Wood – guitars, Geoff Keith – bass, Nic Deighton – drums, Phil Costello – saxophone, Andy Weir – trumpet.



For more information about the band and to check out photos, videos and Wellington Heads music please visit our website www.wellingtonheads.co.nz

Since his breakout album Liquid Spirit on Blue Note Records, which sold over a million copies and earned him his first GRAMMY Award for Best Jazz Vocal Album in 2014, he’s captivated audiences worldwide with his soulful baritone vocals and dynamic storytelling.

Seamlessly blending the elegance of jazz’s golden age with a modern touch, be sure to secure your seats to see the unforgettable Samara Joy.

description:
Wendyhouse / DSLB / vegetable.machine.animal, Wendyhouse / DSLB / vegetable.machine.animal
Wendyhouse are Bryce Galloway and Daniel Powell (AKA Mr Pudding and EE monk). The pair met at the Elam School of Fine Arts. Wendyhouse got their name from debut performances at Art Space (Tāmaki Makaurau) where they sang songs set in the year 2032 from inside a Wendy house (Soundwatch ’92). A prolific creative period followed before EE monk relocated to Europe in 1995. Wendyhouse output has been somewhat sporadic ever since, but with EE monk’s recent return, the pair have returned to performing live.

Wendyhouse music was initially played on toy musical instruments, the kind that fit inside a Wendy house. Real instruments were added as the band moved out of the house and onto the stage.

The music is best described as lo fi inverted pop music, with lyrics about unlikely topics. For example, the two newest songs in the Wendyhouse are an existential treatise on real estate and a love/hate ode to Futurist Luigi Russolo. Guitar, toy keyboard and vocals are the Wendyhouse instruments of choice.

---


DSLB

DSLB is the solo project of Chrissie Butler (the shouty bass playing half of the now sleeping duo, mr sterile Assembly). An offshoot from Chrissie's other band Ditzy Squall, DSLB (Ditzy Squall's Lunch Box) is a showcase for a love of long endings and the hum things make when you hold them close to your ear. Performed live, DSLB is an improvised mash-up of ancient record players, purring keyboards, kitchen utensils and found objects. Soundtracks for short films and hand drawn comics are also residents in the lunch box. Recordings are released by skirted Records.

https://skirtedrecords.com/dslb/

---

vegetable.machine.animal

New solo project courtesy of Mr Sterile, in which living fungal and plantlife inform a modular synthesiser with biofeedback. This signal acts upon the synth changing the pitch, tone, rate and more in the delivery of sound. These ‘curated’ sounds are then responded to with percussion. VMA explores the intersections between spontaneous playing, electronic music, and science-informed inter-species collaboration.

https://mrsterileassembly.bandcamp.com/album/my-daughter-the-spider


$17.50 presales available via UTR

description:
Wilkie Mac and Penni Feather at Acoustic Routes, Monday 20 April, Johnsonville Club, 1 Norman Lane (off Johnsonville Road), Johnsonville, Wellington, 7:30 pm. Parking up the drive at the venue, bus and train nearby.
Entry: $20/$15 for members. Cash only (no eftpos facilities).
Raglan musicians WilkieMac and Penni Feather have been touring as a double bill and bring their combined show to Acoustic Routes, performing separately and together.
Penni Feather
From English trad and blues, to her originals in a contemporary folk style, Penni loves to connect with an audience through song. Known for her interpretive skills, she brings a wide vocal range and emotional depth to her performances.
After starting out in folk music in Hamilton and Auckland, in the 2010s Penni was again active on the North Island folk circuit and guested at Wellington, Aongatete and Hamilton folk festivals. More recently Penni has had a one-woman cabaret show in the Hamilton Arts Festival and performed solo in the inaugural Raglan Blues Festival.
WilkieMac
WilkieMac are Lynne Wilkins and Michael Mackinnon. The duo has a deserved reputation in NZ’s folk scene for their arrangements, with their original songs and Celtic roots to the fore. Recent highlights include being the featured concert guest at the 2025 Te Rangi Festival in Hawkes Bay and opening for Australian band Ukulele Death Squad for one of their pre-WOMAD tour gigs.
Michael provides the solid backdrop on guitar, while Lynne brings a varied soundscape with harmonica, flutes, whistles, guilele (a six-string ukulele) and guitar. Topped with their blended vocals, a WilkieMac performance is bound to leave you wanting more.
Penni Feather and WilkieMac collaborated for sets at the 2025 Hamilton Arts Festival. They enjoyed weaving instruments and harmonies on each other’s songs so much, they teamed up again for gigs that have since been taking them around the North Island.
Note: The concert will be on the first floor, with access via stairs or the lift. (We are told the lift is back in action!) You may have to press the button at the side of the door to gain access to the building.

Supper is not provided, but you’re welcome to purchase drinks, tea and coffee and snacks at the bar. If you want to purchase alcohol, a member of the Johnsonville Club will need to sign you in. Feel free to make your purchases on the way in and bring them up to the room.

description:
Wilson Blackley 'Remain' Tour With Oscar Ladell, Wilson Blackley returns to Aotearoa alongside Oscar LaDell and King Leo this summer to celebrate the release of his new song 'Remain' (Co-written by Troy Kingi).

Wilson Blackley is an Australian multi-instrumentalist and producer currently based in Melbourne. Born and raised in Poowong (Victoria), Wilson was surrounded by music from an early age. At just 2 years old he started playing the drums along to his mother’s music collection consisting of old soul, funk and r&b from the 60’s and 70’s. He started learning the guitar as soon as he could, and had the habit of making anything he could get his hands on into an instrument. Growing up far from the city instilled a strong sense of curiosity and work ethic in him from a young age, leading him to produce his first batch of demos in his teenage years. A stand-out among these demos was the song ‘Home’. ‘Home’ found its way to Sam Teskey (The Teskey Brothers) who would go on to co-produce the song alongside Wilson when he was just 18.

Following the release of ‘Home’, he went on to sell out The Gasometer and play a string of festival slots alongside a variety of artists including The Teskey Brothers and Boy and Bear. At this time, Wilson moved to St Kilda and in the heart of Melbourne began collaborating with Sensible J (Sampa The Great, Remi, Immy Owusu) on his debut EP ‘Material Plane P1’ which was released to critical acclaim in August 2022. After that, he co-produced Oscar LaDell’s EP ‘No Blue’ and subsequently embarked on a co-headline tour of Aotearoa and Australia with LaDell. After a three year break from releasing music, Wilson Blackley returns to Aotearoa alongside Oscar LaDell and King Leo this summer to celebrate the release of his new song 'Remain'
label: Music & Concerts

description:
Wooden Box Band at Whirinaki Whare Taonga, Wellington’s Folk Treasures "The Wooden Box Band" to Play Whirinaki Whare Taonga

Acclaimed six-piece ensemble The Wooden Box Band bring their signature "urban folk" sound to Upper Hutt on February 20th for a special performance at Whirinaki Whare Taonga.

Known for their storytelling and rich, organic textures, the band features a unique blend of soaring harmonies, rhythmic acoustic guitars, and the occasional "blast" of trumpet and violin. Fronted by world-renowned luthier Paddy Burgin, the group includes members from iconic NZ acts like The Mockers and Balkanistas.

The performance follows the success of their latest album, Broken River, which saw the band named as finalists for the Aotearoa NZ Folk Awards. Fans can expect a journey through Aotearoa-centric narratives— true and imagined — delivered with a "chilled Americana vibe" and virtuosic playing.

Part of the Late Nite Sound Bite series, this koha-entry event offers an intimate evening of live music, art galleries, and food from Dough Bakery.

For more information, visit woodenboxbandmusic.com
(https://woodenboxbandmusic.com).

TICKETS: https://bit.ly/wh25_tktnz

Handsome Tours are pleased to present Wunderhorse in Wellington with support from Dropper!

Wunderhorse are Jacob Slater, Harry Fowler, Peter Woodin & Jamie Staples. 2022 saw the release of their debut album Cub, a collection of songs which found fans in Zane Lowe, NME, and BBC Radio 1, and took the band on tour with the likes of Fontaines D.C., Pixies, Sam Fender, and Foals, whilst also selling out their own headline slots along the way. Midas is out now.

Adopting an organic, unpolished recording process, Midas captures the visceral atmosphere of Wunderhorse’s raucous live performances. “We wanted it to sound like your face is pressed up against the amp,” frontman Jacob Slater told The Guardian. “No frills, no polish – just pure, uncut rock’n’roll.”

Indeed, the album’s rugged hooks, unfiltered noise, and fierce melodic sensitivity set Wunderhorse up for a year that will see them firmly established as an endlessly addictive and rousing generational talent.

description:
Wāhine In Jazz X The Listening Collective Present New Standards, Celebrate the New Standards of tomorrow with the vibrant force of Wāhine in Jazz (AKL) and The Listening Collective (WLG) joining forces to showcase female and gender minority musicians that are shaping the sound of jazz in Aotearoa.
Taking inspiration from Terri Lyne Carrington’s New Standards: 101 Lead Sheets by Women Composers, this showcase will feature original works, and arrangements that highlight the breadth of voices often underrepresented on the bandstand.
WIJ and TLC invite you to collaborate with them in whatever capacity you are moved to. Charts can be found via this link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1jQju30yLpi54QPdfRGnZ2x4FZBIUnjUz?usp=drive_link
Wāhine in Jazz is a Tāmaki Makaurau based organisation that advocates for and promotes the development of female and gender diverse jazz musicians in Aotearoa.
The Listening Collective is a Te-Whanganui-a-Tara based group of female and gender diverse musicians that aim to create spaces that uplift and empower individuals in the presentation of their creative work.

WIJ and TLC are also hosting a jam on Thursday 16th October at 4pm. All welcome, koha entry, more info here: https://events.humanitix.com/wahine-in-jazz-x-the-listening-collective-collaborative-jam

XYZZY Album Release, Celebrate the release of the XYZZY soundtrack on vinyl with a special evening at Space Place.

Experience the award-winning planetarium show and hear from video artist Simon Ward about the making of the visuals and enjoy live performances from Stef Animal, Eyeliner and Lachlan Anderson. You can pre-order the limited-edition vinyl and collect it on the night.

Make the most of the event:

UK’s breakout rap sensation YT hits Australia & New Zealand this October.

YT has carved out a lane entirely his own — a sound built on electrifying jerk beats, autotuned hooks that stick in your head, and a razor-sharp lyrical style that’s as witty as it is unapologetic.
From his cult SoundCloud tape #SWAGRENAISSANCE to his viral hit “Black and Tan” with Lancey Foux, he’s established a distinctive British sound that’s turning heads worldwide.

This October, YT lands in Auckland, Wellington, Melbourne, Sydney and Perth for his debut shows in Australia & New Zealand.

Expect raw energy, chaos, and the sound of rap’s next wave coming alive on stage.

2025 is already moving at full speed — and YT is only just getting started.

description:
Yoko-Zuna: A Live Tribute to KAYTRANADA, This October, Aotearoa electronic/progressive hip-hop powerhouse Yoko-Zuna will make their long anticipated return to Pōneke, presenting the music of KAYTRANADA in the city's magnificent Meow NUI.
Over the past decade Yoko-Zuna have firmly established themselves as one of the country’s most exciting live acts and a favourite on the festival circuit. Just back from a world tour with hip-hop multihyphenate CHAII, the four piece made up of Swap Gomez, J.Y Lee, Kenji Iwamitsu-Holdaway, & Frank Eliesa once again join forces to perform their live tribute to a genre-defying beat wizard.
Louis Kevin Celestin aka KAYTRANADA is a Haitian-Canadian record producer and DJ. He first made waves in 2010 with a steady stream of mixtapes, remixes, and original tracks released under the name Kaytradamus. By 2013, reintroducing himself as KAYTRANADA, he was turning heads across the global music scene. The momentum only grew—by 2014, he landed a deal with the influential label XL Recordings. In 2016, he dropped his debut studio album, 99.9%, which was met with widespread critical acclaim. 2019’s Bubba—a genre-blurring triumph earned him two Grammy Awards, including Best Dance/Electronic Album, solidified his place as one of the most innovative voices in contemporary music.
Tickets on-sale 12.00PM Friday 4th July from meownui.com
label: Music & Concerts

description:
You, Me, Everybody - Midnight Album Tour, You, Me, Everybody hit the road in 2026 for a national tour celebrating Midnight, their new album exploring the moment where one day ends and the next begins. Recognised as finalists for Best NZ Folk Artist at the 2021 Aotearoa Music Awards, the group has earned widespread acclaim, including a global audience after their song “Stranger” featured in Netflix’s Sweet Tooth.

Founded by brothers Laurence (vocals and guitar) and Sam Frangos-Rhodes (mandolin, fiddle and vocals) and featuring Nat Torkington on Banjo, Rob Henderson on double bass and Kim Bonnington on vocals and guitar, You, Me, Everybody has built a reputation for pushing bluegrass beyond its borders, blending virtuosic musicianship with contemporary folk and modern string-band innovation. Midnight captures the tension and possibility of life’s turning points, brought to life onstage through rich harmonies, bold instrumental interplay, and great storytelling.

“Acoustic, drumless, genius” - Roger Bowie

The Midnight Tour sees the band bring their new album to Whāngarei as part of a 12-date run across Aotearoa.

Yurt Party are back, fresh out of hibernation and revving up for their biggest Spring tour yet - and a special Halloween show at Meow! (dress up if ya feelin spooky!)

The Ōtautahi crew are hitting the road to celebrate their second album 200, bringing the trademark mash-up of Balkan, Latin and Dub that’s turned backyards, clubs and festivals into full-blown dance floors. There's something about their sound that just makes people lose it in the best way possible.

Honestly, if you haven't experienced the chaos of a Yurt Party show, you're missing out. Pure joy, ridiculous energy, and guaranteed sore legs the next day.

description:
Yīn Yīn - New Zealand Tour | Wellington, Dutch groove-explorers YĪN YĪN are bringing disco, funk, psychedelia and dance to Wellington’s San Fran Friday 27 November and Auckland’s Tuning Fork on Saturday 28 November. 
Made up of Erik Bandt on guitar, Kees Berkers on drums, Jerôme Schere on keyboards and Remy Scheren on bass, YĪN YĪN are the kaleidoscopic instrumental quartet from Maastricht, Netherlands, renowned for their genre-bending records and transportive live experience. 
Emerging out of an experimental jam session in a remote ballet school village in 2017 that resulted in the making of their debut album The Rabbit That Hunts Tigers, the band have since created another three critically acclaimed albums and spent the better part of the last decade chasing rhythm across continents. 
With relentless international touring and performing everywhere from Fuji Rock Festival and Lowlands to North Sea Jazz Festival and Clockenflap they have been collecting sounds, textures and musical flavours like souvenirs, drawing from a multitude of influences such as ‘70s Thai Funk, Japanese City Pop and crate-dug global disco. Each project has evolved alongside the eager exploration to immerse their worldly experience into a sonic universe of their own.
Their latest of which,Yatta!, arrived in January 2026. A defining influence on Yatta! Is the cosmic allure of Italo Disco - the psychedelic futuristic dance music that emerged in Italy during the late 1970s and flourished throughout the 80s. “It has something of a mystique,” the band explains. 
“Because all the producers were using new recording techniques and effects and stuff like that, but there are not many pictures or videos of how they were creating things in the studio.You have to use your own fantasy and create your own story about how that music is created.”
This one sees the band into their most realised selves yet, translating into an unmissable live experience. “We tried to make a mix of songs that are very energetic and danceable and are party starters, but also have songs that take you on trips and are more easy. People can also just chill and relax and listen to the music and enjoy it.” - YĪN YĪN 

Aotearoa, get ready to move. YĪN YĪN are set to take on Aotearoa for the first time for two shows this November.


San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

description:
Ziggy Alberts - 'New Love' Tour - Wellington, ARIA-accredited and APRA Award-winning artist Ziggy Alberts will return to New Zealand this November as part of his New Love World Tour, following three years of extensive touring across Europe, the UK, North and South America, Asia, and regional Australia. Celebrating the release of his seventh studio album, New Love, Ziggy will return to New Zealand for the first time since 2023, with a special show in Wellington.
From his early days busking the streets of Byron Bay to selling out venues like London’s Royal Albert Hall, Ziggy’s journey has been defined by grassroots touring, heartfelt songwriting, and an unwavering independent spirit.
Fans can look forward to favourites like ‘Days in the Sun’ and ‘Runaway’, which recently surpassed 100 million streams, alongside new tracks from New Love - an album crafted for live performance. Featuring hit singles 'New Love’, 'Where Does the Love Go?' and latest single, ‘I’m With You’ the record marks a return to simplicity and authenticity, blending folk, rock, and country influences to create a cohesive yet dynamic listening experience.
Alberts’ year of New Love is not one to miss. This leg of the world tour will celebrate connection, authenticity, and music’s ability to bring people together. Don’t miss the chance to see Ziggy Alberts live on the New Love World Tour 2025.

description:
[OFFSITE] Jim White (Aus) & Marisa Anderson (US) with Motte + UMU, [OFFSITE] Jim White (Aus) & Marisa Anderson (US) with Motte + UMU
Offsite at Meow, 9 Edward Street, Wellington

Jim White & Marisa Anderson
The collaboration between renowned drummer Jim White (Dirty Three, PJ Harvey, Bonnie Prince Billy, Cat Power) and acclaimed US guitarist Marisa Anderson is a natural union of two of the most intuitive players and listeners working in music. White and Anderson are both in high demand as collaborators, in no small part because of their mastery, versatility and highly expressive playing. The duo have amassed an impressive body of work together (including their 2020 debut The Quickening and 2024’s Swallowtail), and each remain at the vanguard of their practices due to an insatiable curiosity and delight in exploration of new avenues of expression.

---

Marisa Anderson channels the history of the guitar and stretches the boundaries of tradition. Her playing is fluid, emotional, and masterful, featuring compositions and improvisations that re-imagine the landscape of American music. Her work applies elements of minimalism, electronic music, drone and 20th century classical music to compositions based on blues, jazz, gospel and country music.

---

Drummer Jim White first come to attention in the mid-1990s with the acclaimed Australian instrumental trio Dirty Three, and is now recognised internationally as one of the most creative and expressive drummers on the planet. His unique playing style and deft way with sound and rhythm has seen him become the go-to drummer for a huge number of alt-A-list vocalists with collaboration in mind. PJ Harvey has said there is ballet in White’s light, precise touch. And the other collaborators that he’s mesmerised, including the likes of Bonnie Prince Billy, Smog, Nick Cave, White Magic, Beth Orton, Marianne Faithfull, Kurt Vile, Cat Power and the iconic Cretan lyra player Psarantonis, all know that there’s more to White’s drumming than mere accompaniment. His intuitive beats and singular approach have created sparks in his collaborations. Whoever White is playing with, he is right there, present in the most inspirational sense.

---

Motte is the solo project of violinist and composer, Anita Clark. Riding the thin line between beauty and devastation, Motte weaves together a richly textured world with a violin, delay pedal, sampled sound and voice. Creating a world solely her own, the sound is modern classical, ambient, alt/experimental pop and improvised noise. Her musical gifts and skilful reach across genres makes her an indispensable collaborator with The Phoenix Foundation, Luke Buda, Marlon Williams, Don McGlashan, the Renderers, Nadia Reid, Lawrence Arabia, Delaney Davidson and plenty of others. As Motte, she dances around the shining candescence of her culture like a night insect, always seeking a better vantage point to the light.

---

UMU is a duo of Riki Gooch and Daniel Beban. Silver Apples meets Kuduro with Riki's deep grooves played on an 80s Roland electronic drum kit which are manipulated and dubbed out by Dan on two Tama Techstar drum synths.

etu is a Tongan-American singer, songwriter, and storyteller whose music bridges cultures and generations. Blending island harmonies with mainstream aura, etu’s sound is deeply rooted yet powerfully contemporary. His debut album ‘Sunflower’ is a heartfelt exploration of identity, belonging, and gratitude — a celebration of Pacific pride and resilience. etu’s performances are more than just about the music — they’re tailored spiritual & personal experiences that uplift, connect, and inspire. From concerts in the South Pacific to major festival stages, etu is on a mission to bring light to his people and share their stories with the world.


"This tour is more than me playing songs – it’s about bringing the spirit of the islands to every stage," says etu. "I want people to leave feeling seen, uplifted, and part of something bigger than themselves." 

With songs in English, Tongan, Samoan, Fijian, and Chuukese, Sunflower is a rich tapestry of sound and storytelling – a heartfelt exploration of belonging, gratitude, and resilience.

description:
mHz : Brutalist Noise Ensemble v2 / Te Tumu, Mo H. Zareei aka mHz is an Iranian sound artist and researcher based in New Zealand. His practice spans electronic compositions, kinetic sound-sculptures, and audiovisual installations. Using custom-built software and hardware, his work often aims to uncover the beauty in the fundamentals of sound and light production, and reductionist audiovisual elements that draw inspiration from physical and architectural principles.
Brutalist Noise Ensemble v2 involves a series of electromechanical instruments built to extend the territory of noise and glitch beyond the digital realm, while paying conscious homage to Brutalism: an unapologetic celebration of raw material through rigorous formalism, where noise replaces concrete. Despite its experimental raw materials, the formal structure of the work is established through purely grid-based and club-style rhythms and repetition is used to bring accessibility to noise.

the end of 2025 is approaching fast, and what better time to gather with others to celebrate this shift than a new moon??
with several live solo electronic artists this new moon at moon gig will be the perfect opportunity to reflect and celebrate your progress this year, (or to dance away blocks stopping you from moving forward!) and connect with others.

hazel elder

modern dialogue
beet-wix

koha tarot readings

description:
the Jesus Lizard, After initially calling it a day in 1999, the Jesus Lizard officially return full time to save us from the current state of musical mediocrity with their latest album, Rack. A blistering resurgence of the so-called ‘noise rock’ they helped define alongside contemporaries Big Black, Flipper, The Birthday Party, with their previous and most noted albums Head, Goat and Liar. For those of us who live in fear of the reunion album and subsequent tour, the Jesus Lizard thankfully display not only the same chaotic and dark nihilism of their earlier careers but also the maturity and seasoning of a band riding a wave of renewed and reinvigorated form.

Once slated by famed engineer Steve Albini as “the greatest band I’ve ever seen’ the Jesus Lizard not only lived up to this lofty praise in their prime but continue to do so in their advancing years. David Yow still leads the charge as the maniacally possessed frontman entering crowds with reckless abandon and a stamina that much younger vocalists would kill for. The original rhythm section of David Wm Sims and Mac McNeilly further continue to prove why they were and are the best bass & drum combo since Jones and Bonham, anchoring the ship as Captain Yow and first mate Denison navigate the wild seas of their songs. And while he may not always feature (as he rightly should) on many modern music journalists ‘best guitarists lists’, Duane Denison could perhaps be the most innovative and idiosyncratic punk rock guitarist EVER. However, each member is a sum of their parts but combined they are as Albini also once said “the purest melding of the sublime and profane.”

Whether you are a longtime disciple of the Jesus Lizard, seeing them when last here in ‘98, or perhaps your fandom is more recent and have only seen videos of their legendary live performances, you will know that these shows are not to be missed.

Saturday 11th October 2025 - The Tuning Fork, Auckland (All ages)

Sunday 12th October 2025 - San Fran, Wellington (R18 unless accompanied by your legal guardian)

vegetable.machine.animal (vma) is an interspecies improvisational trio from Te Whanganui-a-Tara/Wellington, Aotearoa New Zealand. Led by drummer Kieran Monaghan [he/him] (ex-mr sterile Assembly), vma transforms the electrical signals of living plants and fungi into sound, fusing modular synths and live percussion in performances that are spontaneous, rhythmic, and unpredictable. This is music as a living system - a real-time collaboration where non-human organisms shape the sonic outcome alongside human performers. No two sets are the same. A Visiting Scholar at Te Kōkī / New Zealand School of Music, Monaghan brings decades of experience across punk, free jazz, and experimental scenes, with vma performing at festivals, residencies, and venues across Aotearoa and internationally.

Kiwi rock fans are in for the ultimate celebration of grunge history as The Pearl Jam Experience crosses the Tasman to deliver a definitive, career-spanning greatest hits set. This special tour will honour the massive catalog of the Seattle icons, delivering a full-throttle, high-energy performance packed to the brim with Pearl Jam’s biggest anthems and fan favourites.
Widely regarded as the premier tribute to Pearl Jam, the band is renowned for recreating the atmosphere, the madness, and most importantly, the sonically accurate music that defined a generation.
Their commitment to the music’s authenticity goes beyond the stage. In a remarkable nod to Pearl Jam’s golden era, the band recently recorded a collaborative cover of the hit song Go with former Pearl Jam drummer Dave Abbruzzese. Abbruzzese, who drove the rhythm section during the band's peak explosive years, lent his signature powerful drumming to the track and mixed it for the group.
The Pearl Jam Experience also maintains a deep connection to the band's philanthropic legacy. They are proud supporters of the EB Research Partnership (EBRP), the largest nonprofit funding research for a cure for Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB), co-founded by Jill and Eddie Vedder.
For New Zealand fans, this is the ultimate chance to experience a high-octane concert that embodies the true sound and spirit of Pearl Jam, delivered with the energy, precision, and respect this legendary rock catalog deserves.

description:
2026 Francis Gurry Lecture on Intellectual Property - WELLINGTON, 2026 Francis Gurry Lecture on Intellectual Property - WELLINGTON
"The Future of IP Dispute Resolution" by Sir Colin Birss, Chancellor of the High Court of England and Wales

About this Event




5.30pm | Pre-event refreshments
6.00pm | Public lecture




The Future of IP Dispute Resolution

The legal landscape is changing before our eyes. The advent of AI and digital assets, the internationalisation of dispute resolution, and the changing expectations of users, all pose challenges, and intellectual property has always raised issues of its own.

This lecture will examine the state of intellectual property litigation today in the wider context, consider where it needs to be in future, and look at how we need to adapt to meet the challenges.

The topics include the major legal problems in IP which will need to be addressed; the legal and practical impact of artificial intelligence; the importance of digital assets and tokenisation; and the emergence of alternative modes of resolving dispute resolution.






Colin Birss is the Chancellor (Head of the Chancery Division) of the High Court of England and Wales. Called to the English Bar in 1990, he practised intellectual property law. In 2010 he became judge at the Patents County Court (now IPEC), in 2013 he went to the High Court, and in 2021 to the Court of Appeal. He was Deputy Head of Civil Justice 2021-25, and appointed Chancellor in 2025. He sits in the Court of Appeal and in the High Court.




If you are a University of Melbourne alumni, information about your participation may be shared with the Advancement team, as explained in our privacy notice.

A Voyage to the Moon by Offenbach: A NZSM Opera Production, Classical Performance students from the New Zealand School of Music – Te Kōkī present four performances of Jacques Offenbach's delightful comic opera A Voyage to the Moon, directed by Sara Brodie with musical direction by Kathryn Mosley.

Inspired by this year's space exploration milestones, including NASA's Artemis II mission, this production celebrates Offenbach's imaginative 1875 opera, which was a sensation in Paris, running for an impressive 185 consecutive performances during its first run.

Loosely based on Jules Verne's novel From the Earth to the Moon, A Voyage to the Moon takes audiences on a adventure filled with fantastical lunar landscapes, eccentric characters, and Offenbach's trademark comedic twists. The story follows King V'lan, his adventurous son Prince Caprice, and their companions—including Microscope and Rhombus—as they journey to the Moon, where they encounter Cosmos, Princess Fantasia, Flamma, and other curious inhabitants of the lunar world.

Directed by Sara Brodie, who also led last year's fantastic production of L'enfant et les sortilèges, the opera features vocal numbers performed in French with English surtitles. The spoken dialogue is presented in English, bringing the comedy vividly to life for contemporary audiences.

This production showcases the talents of students across the Classical Performance programme, with NZSM voice students performing all roles and in ensembles, and the NZSM piano students taking part as rehearsal pianists (répétiteurs) and playing for the performances. Musical direction is provided by Head of Collaborative Piano Kathryn Mosley, and the production is coordinated by Head of Classical Voice Jenny Wollerman.

Join us for an imaginative, entertaining, and truly 'out there' operatic adventure!

Programme:
Dame Gillian Karawe Whitehead Hoata
Beethoven Symphony No. 9

Its audacious juxtaposition of styles, sounds and forces, including the revolutionary inclusion of a choir, marked the Ninth as a landmark work, not just for Beethoven but for music itself. Its monumental achievement and undeniable emotional power will be brought to stunning life with the help of Orpheus Choir Wellington and City Choir Dunedin.

Our essential need for community and connection is also at the heart of Dame Gillian Karawe Whitehead’s Hoata. Named for the Māori phase of the moon where the moon is barely visible, Hoata was written in 1979 during a cold northern hemisphere winter and evokes the icy blizzards and intense isolation that swirled around the composer as she wrote.

description:
Cacao & Connection Circle, Overview

Share ceremonial cacao, heartfelt conversation and a nourishing dinner in an evening of authentic connection and presence.

Cacao & Connection Circle
Starts at 6pm

This evening is an invitation to slow down, be present, and experience genuine human connection. Together we'll share ceremonial cacao, meaningful conversation, and a welcoming space where there's no need to perform, impress, or have all the right words. Just come as you are.

What to Expect

We'll begin with a gentle grounding practice to help everyone arrive. This is an opportunity to pause, settle into the present moment, and reconnect with yourself before connecting with others.

From there, we'll gather in a circle to share ceremonial cacao. 

We'll then move into a heart-sharing circle. A thoughtful question will be offered as a prompt, and you're warmly invited, but never expected to share your experience. There is no advice-giving or fixing here. Instead, we practise honest expression, deep listening, and creating space for one another to simply be witnessed.

What Heart-Sharing Can Offer

 Authentic Connection

Experience the kind of connection that comes from being seen, heard, and accepted exactly as you are.

Meaningful Conversation

Step beyond everyday small talk into conversations that invite honesty, curiosity, and presence.

Greater Self-Awareness

Sharing and listening often brings unexpected clarity about your own thoughts, emotions, and life experiences.

Gentle Personal Growth

Speaking from the heart and listening without judgement can quietly shift perspectives and deepen understanding.

A Sense of Belonging

Being part of a supportive circle can ease feelings of isolation and remind us that we all share common human experiences.

 

After the circle, we'll enjoy a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert together, both included in your ticket. It's a relaxed time to continue conversations, connect naturally, and simply enjoy each other's company.

Meet Andre, your host:

Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human, how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.

description:
Can Electricity Markets Deliver the Clean Energy Transition?, Can Electricity Markets Deliver the Clean Energy Transition?
A global perspective on investment, reliability, and the risks of getting it wrong.

About this Event



Three recent shocks to electricity markets - cheap renewables, declining storage costs, and the return of demand growth - have led some to conclude that electricity markets as we know them have run their course. Drawing on thirty years of restructured markets abroad, this presentation will argue that these developments actually strengthen the case for markets — and will explore what reliability means, and how it should be provided, in a greener electricity system.

Professor James Bushnell – Biography

Professor James Bushnell is a distinguished scholar whose research and policy contributions have helped shape modern understanding of electricity markets, energy regulation, and climate policy, making him one of the most influential voices in energy economics. He is an internationally recognised expert in energy economics, electricity markets, environmental policy, and industrial organisation.The event is being facilitated by ERGANZ and will be hosted at the Wellington offices of Russell McVeagh

Date and Time: Thursday 3 September, 4pm - 6pm @Russell McVeagh, 157 Lambton Quay, please join us for a drink and nibbles from 4pm, presentation to start at 4:30pm with a Q&A to follow.

Please email with any dietary requirements.

Wellington Chamber of Commerce and Pax8 are proud to host the Prime Minister, Christopher Luxon.

About this Event



Join Business Central and the Wellington Chamber of Commerce for an exclusive breakfast event featuring Prime Minister Rt Hon Christopher Luxon in conversation with Hayley Horan, Chief Executive of Business Central.

Set within the iconic Banquet Hall at Parliament, this special event offers members and the wider business community a rare opportunity to hear directly from New Zealand's leader in a professionally moderated fireside chat.

Unlike a traditional keynote speech, this event has been designed as a genuine conversation. The discussion will be informed by the experiences, perspectives, and questions submitted by Business Central and Wellington Chamber members, helping to ensure the topics explored reflect the realities, opportunities, and challenges facing our business community today.

Designed to be engaging, insightful, and business-focused, the discussion will explore the opportunities and challenges shaping New Zealand's future. From economic growth, productivity, trade, infrastructure, workforce development and artificial intelligence, through to geopolitics and New Zealand's long-term competitiveness, the conversation will focus on the issues that matter most to businesses across our region.

Following the fireside chat, attendees will have the opportunity to participate in a live audience Q&A, providing further engagement with the Prime Minister and valuable insight into the Government's priorities and vision for New Zealand.

Your Ticket Includes:

Shared breakfast at a round table with fellow business leaders
Exclusive access to a one-hour conversation with the Prime Minister
Opportunity to submit questions that may shape the discussion
Live audience Q&A
Networking with business, government, and community leaders before and after the event

Agenda:

7.00 am - Guest arrival & networking

A first level qualification in Lego Serious Play with its usual twist of change magic added into the learning experience

This workshop will focus on building your skills as a Lego® Serious Play® (LSP1.0) facilitator.
In day 1 you will be introduced to the benefits of the approach and learn the three core elements of LSP: challenge, build and share for individual, group and connected building. We will also explore the needs for clarity of challenge and using LSP to help define that challenge as well as potential for coaching and facilitating others through change.
In day 2 you will learn how to apply the day 1 learning through practical application of the learning as well as define a workshop and practice facilitating an activity individually and with others. Certification will be awarded to attendees who complete the workshop content and successfully deliver a short, facilitated workshop event at the end of Day 2.
All attendees will go away with an information booklet and guide for undertaking LSP themselves and a Lego Exploration pack.

description:
Christian Leotta piano recital, Overview

From Scarlatti to Schubert: The Evolution of the Piano Sonata. Acclaimed pianist Christian Leotta in a remarkable recital.

The Italian Embassy is delighted to present internationally acclaimed pianist Christian Leotta in a recital exploring the remarkable evolution of the piano sonata through the music of Domenico Scarlatti, Ludwig van Beethoven, and Franz Schubert.

Spanning more than a century of musical innovation, the programme traces the transformation of the sonata from Scarlatti's elegant miniatures to Beethoven's groundbreaking masterpieces and Schubert's poetic lyricism. Featuring Beethoven's celebrated "Waldstein" Sonata and his final Piano Sonata in C minor, Op. 111, this recital offers a compelling journey through some of the greatest works ever written for the piano.

Renowned for his interpretations of the Classical and Romantic repertoire, Christian Leotta rose to international prominence at the age of 22 after performing the complete cycle of Beethoven's 32 Piano Sonatas. Since then, he has appeared in more than 50 countries and performed with leading orchestras in many of the world's most prestigious concert halls.

You might see a first-timer stepping up for their debut. You might see a seasoned comic testing fresh material. You might see someone absolutely smash it. You might see someone realise, in real time, that jokes are harder than they look. That’s the magic.

Discover the science behind better health with Presidential Director Marcia Schaefer.

Join us for a special First Look event with Presidential Director Marcia Schaefer, DC, a licensed Chiropractor and passionate health educator, as she explores The Missing link in health

We all strive to make healthier choices, eating well, staying active and looking after our wellbeing. But what if the key isn't simply doing all the right things, but understanding what's missing and putting the pieces together in the right order?

In this engaging session, Marcia will explore the science behind healthy ageing, glycans and the vital role they play in supporting communication at the cellular level. Discover why providing your body with the right nutritional foundation may be the missing link to helping you get the most from your overall health and wellness journey.

Since partnering with Mannatech in 2010, Marcia has been dedicated to educating practitioners and communities on the importance of nutrition, preconception health and creating the conditions for healthier generations. Her ability to simplify complex science into practical, everyday knowledge has inspired audiences around the world.

Whether you're new to Mannatech, wanting to learn more about glycans, or looking to better understand the science behind healthy ageing, this is an event you won't want to miss.

Join us for an inspiring and educational evening that may change the way you think about health and discover why glycans are considered by many to be the missing link.

Foundations, The Music Managers Forum Aotearoa (MMF) is proud to announce FOUNDATIONS, a refreshed evolution of its long running Back to Basics seminar series. Presented in collaboration with Ka Korokī Ka Maranga | Māori Music Industry Collective, FOUNDATIONS is a free two hour workshop for artists and self managers in the early stages of building a music career.

For this session, we will be joined by Mikee Carpenter (Manager - Georgia Lines) and AJA (Artist)

SECURE YOUR SPOT HERE: https://www.mmf.co.nz/news-pages/2026/7/16/vgjzb0thbu20b6fey3l2uvqk9ihm51

FOUNDATIONS was born out of a moment of reflection for MMF. With the loss of long time Back to Basics presenter Lorraine Barry in 2025, the team felt it was the right time to relook at the programme she had shaped for so many years. Lorraine was a dedicated advocate for emerging artists and managers, and FOUNDATIONS carries her commitment to helping the next generation navigate the industry with confidence.

The workshop covers the building blocks every artist needs from day one, including the NZ music ecosystem and funding pathways, rights and royalties, finding and growing a real fanbase, releasing music with a team around you, understanding the business side of the industry, patience in building a career, and the financial realities of a life in music. Each section is followed by open Q&A, giving attendees the chance to bring their own questions to experienced guests.

“Lorraine Barry was a mentor to me for over eight years and someone I always turned to for advice, as well as being a great friend. It’s an honour to carry on the work she was so passionate about in artist development, on behalf of the MMF.” - Mikee Carpinter

description:
French Pastry for Beginners, French Pastry for Beginners
A 4-Week Hands-On Series

Step into the world of French pâtisserie with our beginner-friendly four-week course designed to teach you the essential techniques behind some of France's most iconic pastries. Guided by Le Ciel's experienced pastry chef and owner, Shuchi, you'll build your confidence week by week as you learn the foundations of classic French baking.

This progression-based course is perfect for anyone who loves baking, wants to develop professional techniques, or is looking to begin their pastry journey. Each class focuses on a new skill while building on what you've learned in previous weeks, making it easy to continue growing as a baker.

Week 1 – French Macarons

Take on one of France's most famous pastries with confidence. Learn how to create smooth macaron shells, perfect feet, balanced fillings, and troubleshoot common problems so you can recreate them successfully at home.

Week 2 – Choux Pastry

Master the fundamentals of pâte à choux as you learn to mix, pipe, bake, fill, and finish classic French favourites including profiteroles and éclairs. You'll also learn how to make silky pastry cream and achieve perfectly crisp shells.

Week 3 – French Tarts

Discover the secrets to beautiful French tarts by learning sweet pastry dough, blind baking, creamy fillings, fruit finishing, and professional presentation techniques.

Week 4 – Mille-Feuille

Complete the course by creating the elegant Mille-Feuille. Learn how to work with puff pastry, prepare rich vanilla crème pâtissière, assemble delicate layers, and finish with a professional glaze.

What's Included
Four hands-on classes
Step-by-step instructions from professional pastry chefs
All ingredients and equipment are provided
Recipe booklet to take home
Your creations to enjoy and share
Small class sizes for personalised guidance

Who is this course for?

This course is ideal for complete beginners and enthusiastic home bakers. No previous baking experience is required—just bring your enthusiasm and a love of French pastries.

By the end of the four weeks, you'll have mastered a range of foundational pastry techniques and be ready to continue into our future intermediate pastry workshops.

Spaces are limited to ensure every participant receives plenty of individual guidance. Early booking is recommended.

Many people find it difficult to talk about dying, yet dying is an important stage of life and is inevitable. We plan for the birth of a child, yet when it comes to the end of life, we don’t often want to think about it or talk about it.
