description:
Greentea Peng tickets, Presented by: Astral People & Handsome Tours
Neo-soul artist Greentea Peng arrives in Australia and New Zealand this November, delicately infusing hypnotic dub with seductive hip-hop swings and jazzy neo-soul excursions.
The South London born Greentea Peng is an artist whose work is guided by self-inquiry, shaped by the dualities she inhabits: pain and pleasure, engagement and withdrawal, expression and stillness. Her emotional literacy is transformed into a blend of neo-soul, dub and jazz, all draped in psychedelic textures.
After rediscovering her love for music while travelling - where she joined a local band in Mexico - a renewed sense of self-confidence propelled her return to London and the release of her 2018 EP, Sensi. The project marked the beginning of a distinctive sound carved from heavy, weighty narration, dubby grain, hissy textures and sparse arrangements. The six-track release is anchored by negative space that sits tightly side-chained to the kick, creating a breathing, pumping feel, while minimal melodic movements allow tension to build and swell around her earthy, soulful voice.
This early foundation continued to evolve, punctuated by notable moments such as her performance of "Downers" on COLORS, which garnered millions of views, as well as her television debut on Later... with Jools Holland on the BBC, where she performed her breakout track "Hu Man". These milestones paved the way for her 2021 debut album, MAN MADE, which she described as a record designed to resonate "more in your heart space, and less in your headspace".
Her latest offering, TELL DEM IT'S SUNNY, dives deeper into her enduring practice of self-witnessing - a work of affirmation, emotional maturity and radical self-acceptance. From "BALI SKIT PT. 1", a soundscape that rises and falls like the ribcage of a shadowy spirit, to "RAW", where we're once again met with Peng's poignant voice notes, the album showcases an artist continuing to explore her inner world with clarity and conviction.
Now, the psychedelic R&B soulstress returns to Australia and New Zealand this November, bringing her rich catalogue of deeply personal, genre-defying music to audiences once again.

The primary distinction of HealthX is our active sourcing model. We do not rely solely on open invitations; we build the candidate pool around the specific needs of the attending organizations.
How the "Custom Sourcing" Works:
Reserve Your Spot: Secure your organization's attendance.
Share Your Needs: Submit your open requisitions—whether for clinical staff, allied health, or administrative roles.
We Source: Upon your registration, our recruiting team launches a targeted campaign to identify and invite professionals who specifically match your credentialing and experience requirements.
Healthcare Professionals of All Specializations
We cater to the full spectrum of the healthcare industry. Whether you are looking to fill high-volume clinical roles or specialized leadership positions, we source the talent you need each event highlights a specific fous.

The Format
In a competitive healthcare market, top talent is rarely active on public job boards. We provide access to a pre-vetted pool of professionals in a format designed for speed and impact.
Invite-Only: Every attendee is reviewed to ensure they hold valid credentials and relevant experience.
Accelerated Interviews: Our "speed-dating" format allows you to conduct intro interviews with dozens of qualified candidates in a single session—volume that would typically require weeks of scheduling.
Active Talent: Engage with 100+ motivated professionals who are actively seeking new opportunities.

Candidates
To ensure you can maximize your time, we provide complete transparency regarding who is in the room. Participating employers receive:
Full Candidate Roster: Names and background details provided in advance.
Professional Profiles: Direct links to LinkedIn or professional bios.
Credentials: Visibility into licensure and work history.
Direct Contact Info: Verified email addresses to facilitate immediate follow-up.

Please Note: To maintain a balanced candidate-to-employer ratio, participation is strictly limited.

How To Write A Romance Novel: A Workshop, Overview






A workshop that will take you through the A to Z of writing a character driven romance novel from bestselling author George Penney.
Do you have dreams of typing “The End” on a romance novel you’ve written but don’t know where to start?
Have you always dreamed of being a writer but find the actual process of becoming one intimidating?
Or maybe you’re a forever-writer just looking for pointers for how to shape your ideas into a structure that’ll sell to readers.
This three hour workshop will take you from initial character creation, through romance story structure and then to practical tips on getting your romance novel finished.
You’ll be taken through different romance genres, how to come up with three-dimensional, interesting characters, how to built tension and conflict, tips on writing good sex scenes and how to write that truly satisfying Happy Ever After ending.
This is a practical workshop designed to leave attendees motivated, excited and equipped with the tools to go on and finish that book!

*Please note: This is an AI free writing workshop. We believe that writing should be a messy, wonderful, exasperating, rewarding process that explores the depth of human creativity rather than a test on how well someone can type a prompt into a LLM. If you'd like to argue this point, please send us a non-AI hardbound treatise of no less than one hundred thousand words, hand-written in iambic pentameter.

For all other Beautiful Words events, go to www.beautifulwords.net

INSPIRE Festival, Overview


INSPIRE Festival is for all tamariki aged 8-13 (up to year 8) who are interested in STEAMS learning.
Public ticket sales open on 7 August. Early access is currently available by invitation only.

INSPIRE Festival is 4-5 Sept 2026!
$60 per child per day for a full day of STEAMS learning!
INSPIRE Festival 2026 offers two days of student selected challenging discussions and hands-on workshops all focused around STEAMS (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Maths, and Society). This year the festival is being hosted at Nayland College!
• Friday: 1- or 2-hour workshops
• Saturday: 2-4 hour, in-depth workshops. Perfect for students to get really stuck in to topics.
INSPIRE offers thought-provoking discussions and hands on experiments for AGES 8-13 (up to Year 8). Students choose up to 4 sessions to attend, all based on the STEAMS model of education and delivered by New Zealand's top professionals, scientists, businessmen, and mentored college students.
INSPIRE will develop the connection between classroom theory and some very exciting and ground-breaking real careers which make a difference in our world. The inaugural INSPIRE was in 2012 and massive demand has led to it being hosted annually with over 650 students attending and has continued to grow. The energy and enthusiasm of the students is wonderful and, with their feedback, demonstrates the necessity and benefits of INSPIRE. All attendees will be our future leaders and creative thinkers and they have told us they want more; more challenge, more connections and more opportunities to grow and learn.
It is recommended that students attending INSPIRE Festival have a teacher/adult 'in-charge' of them. Students left at the venue without an adult 'in-charge' are left at their own risk.

In Conversation: The Rt. Hon. Helen Clark & Hon. Philip Woollaston, Overview
The people, politics and ideas that shaped New Zealand’s conservation legacy, hosted by West Coast-Tasman Labour candidate, Rory Paterson.
As New Zealand debates proposed changes to our conservation laws, there has never been a better time to hear from two people who played a pivotal role in shaping our conservation history.
Join former Prime Minister and former Conservation Minister, the Rt. Hon. Helen Clark, and former Minister of Conservation and former Nelson mayor, Hon. Philip Woollaston, for a special lunchtime conversation exploring the people, politics and ideas that shaped modern conservation in New Zealand.
Helen and Philip were New Zealand’s second and third Conservation Ministers, respectively.
Drawing on their first-hand experience, they will reflect on the vision, challenges and decisions behind some of New Zealand's most significant conservation legislation and discuss the legacy it continues to leave today.
The conversation will be facilitated by Johny O'Donnell and hosted by West Coast-Tasman Labour candidate, Rory Paterson.
Bring your lunch, bring your curiosity, and enjoy an engaging discussion, with plenty of time for audience questions.
Admission is free. Koha at the door is appreciated.
We’ll also have raffles and a silent auction, so bring some cash if you’d like to support our West Coast-Tasman campaign.
Seating reservations on a first-come, first-served basis.

description:
Investing through the AI revolution, Investing through the AI revolution
Join RIVAL Wealth for a small, interactive session exploring the rise of AI and what it could mean for your investments.

About this Event



Artificial intelligence is changing how businesses operate, how markets move, and where capital is being invested, so what does that actually mean for your investments in practice?

This session steps away from the headlines and focuses on the practical side of investing in a world shaped by AI. Matt Logan, a Portfolio Manager at Fisher Funds, will walk through how AI is influencing portfolios today, and where we are seeing real impacts in markets and investment decisions. With almost 20 years' experience at Fisher Funds, Matt is a senior member of the investment team and brings extensive experience analysing markets, managing risk and identifying investment opportunities.

He will cover:
• How AI is affecting global markets and investment returns
• Where opportunities may sit, and where risks are building
• How your KiwiSaver or investment portfolio may already have exposure
• What a considered, long-term approach looks like in this environment

This is an opportunity to ask questions and understand how this fits into your wider financial plan, and what it may mean for your own situation.

A light lunch and refreshments will be provided.

You are welcome to arrive from 11.30am for a coffee and a chat, with the presentation starting at 12.00pm. If you are joining us for your lunch break, feel free to arrive closer to the start time. We will be in the Te Papa Noho room at the BNZ Partners Centre, Wellington.

We are keeping this session small, so we recommend registering early to secure your place.

Parking is available at Stout Street, Wellington and Queens Warf Waterfront parking, both a short walk to the BNZ Partners Centre.


RIVAL Wealth is a Financial Advice Provider (FAP) licenced by the Financial Markets Authority to provide financial advice. Our disclosure document is located at rivalwealth.co.nz or a written copy is available on request

Just A Drink Speed Dating (Age Range Mid-20s – Mid-30s), Overview








Apps are shit. This is less shit. Everyone comes with a single friend they think is worth meeting. 6-10 dates. ~5 mins each. Drink included.

Just A Drink Speed Dating
We put on events so that the single people worth meeting can meet each other without having to open an app.

How This Event Works
This event works by asking everyone to come in pairs. We do this for two key reasons:
You’ve both got someone to go with. Good company is guaranteed and moral support is built-in.
If someone has been brought along by a friend, they’re probably all good. We love that everyone at our events is someone another person there can vouch for.

What We're Trying To Help With
It's hard for the single people worth meeting to find each other.
Out and about, you can’t always tell who’s single.
The apps have helped – you’ve probably met some good people through them – but it can still be hard to tell who’s actually worth leaving the house for.
So, here’s another way to meet people.
Come along. It’s just a drink.

description:
Leadership: Escape the Drama Triangle, Overview

Create a team that communicates better, takes ownership, and solves problems together.

Every team experiences tension.

A conversation goes sideways. Someone starts blaming. Another person steps in to fix everything. Before long, the real issue has been lost and the same pattern begins again.

This free leadership session will help you recognise those patterns and respond differently.

Leadership: Escape the Drama Triangle is a practical 90-minute workshop for business owners and team leaders who want their people to communicate clearly, take greater ownership, and solve problems together.

During the session, we will explore how workplace conversations can fall into the roles of Victim, Rescuer and Villain, and how leaders can help shift those conversations from blame, excuses and denial towards responsibility, accountability and ownership. This reflects the workbook’s movement from the “Victim Cycle” to the “Victor Cycle” and its focus on improving the quality of words, conversations, relationships, collaboration and achievement.

You will learn how to:

Recognise the Drama Triangle in everyday team conversations
Identify when people are operating below the line
Avoid rescuing, blaming or taking over
Reframe conversations so people can take responsibility
Create clearer, more productive team discussions
Help your team move from problems towards practical next steps

This is not about removing every disagreement from your workplace.

It is about giving you a simple way to recognise unhelpful patterns early and guide the conversation towards a better outcome.

You will leave with practical language and ideas you can begin using with your team straight away.

Who is this for?

This session is suitable for:

Business owners
Managers and team leaders
People responsible for workplace culture
Leaders dealing with repeated communication issues
Anyone who finds themselves stepping in to solve everyone else’s problems

description:
Men's Circle & Breathwork, Overview
A welcoming men’s circle for honest conversation, breathwork and meaningful connection in a space of trust and support.
Men's Circle & Breathwork 
Starts at 6pm
In a world where men are often expected to have everything figured out, this gathering offers a space to be genuine, not perfect.
This is a free event, with an optional plant-based dinner available for $15. While there’s no obligation to stay for dinner, sharing a meal together offers a meaningful way to strengthen connections.
Andre and Sri Jiva co-host this circle with a shared passion for creating authentic, supportive spaces where men can connect deeply, offering this gathering simply because they believe in its importance.
The Men’s Circle provides a safe and nurturing environment where men can share openly, express their feelings and encourage personal growth. Through honest sharing and collective support, participants build resilience, deepen self-awareness, and strengthen their sense of identity and purpose.
 Structure of the Circle
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.
Breathwork is a powerful practice to help ground the nervous system and connect to a deep presence. 
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.
 Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group but keep others' details private.
Join us after this free event for an optional plant-based dinner and dessert for only $20 (or $10 for students).
Meet Andre, your host:
Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human, how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.
Meet Sri Jiva, your host:
Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

description:
National Dog Database, National Dog Database
Using the NDD to its full potential. Get hands-on and use realistic scenarios to explore and learn the functionality of the NDD website.

About this Event


Description

The National Dog Database went live 1 May 2006 and provides a countrywide overview of dog control in New Zealand.

It brings great benefits to the animal control industry including the ability to;

track classified owners and dogs
monitor the national infringement count of owners
look up out of district dog and owner details
locate dogs when only limited information is available;
and contribute accurate data to ongoing policy analysis.







Outline

Using the NDD training environment (it looks just like the live NDD system but contains fictional data), the NDD training workshop will explore the following areas:

Background – the history of the NDD project – from 2003 to present
TA Extracts – how information gets from your local system to the NDD and the feedback the NDD will give you as well as the different types of files you can send
Searching – how to get the best out of the search screen and how to interpret the results of your search
The ToDo List – what are errors, warnings, information and system notifications? Detailed discussion about what you need to do with them.
Automated and Manual Linking – National Duplicates – comparing dogs and owners that look similar but are in different districts, and how to manually search for other duplicates.
Security – passwords, adding new users or expiring old accounts, as well as the owner protected status.
Reports – what reports you can run and how to use them in your TA. Did you know there are 18 different kinds of reports that you can generate from the NDD and that you can use some of them to compare your TA’s data to a national summary?







Learning outcomes

With a focus on maintaining data quality, participants in the workshop will learn to use the NDD as a tool for animal control and further understand the importance of administrative roles at the local level. Following the completion of the NDD training workshop, NDD users will have the confidence to use the database to its full potential.







Audience

This course is suitable for managers, team leaders and users with animal control administrator responsibilities.







Prerequisites

To participate in the NDD training workshop you must be a registered user of the National Dog Database (employee or contractor). You are required to bring your own laptop.

description:
Ngā Mokopuna Tour, Ngā Mokopuna: A Living Building Story Tour

Join us for an introductory guided tour of Ngā Mokopuna, Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington's pioneering regenerative building project.

This experience explores the vision, values, and aspirations behind a building designed to tread lightly on the environment while creating lasting benefits for people and place. Grounded in principles of kaitiakitanga and inspired by mātauranga Māori, Ngā Mokopuna reflects a commitment to caring for our natural world and future generations.

During the tour, you'll learn about the Living Building Challenge, one of the world's most ambitious sustainability frameworks, and discover how Ngā Mokopuna has been designed to meet its rigorous standards. The project represents a significant step towards becoming one of Aotearoa New Zealand's next recognised Living Buildings.

From outside the building and surrounding precinct, you'll hear the stories behind its design, sustainability features, and cultural foundations. You'll also meet staff and student ambassadors who work and study within Ngā Mokopuna and learn firsthand how the building supports teaching, learning, wellbeing, and community.

The tour also provides an opportunity to view Te Tumu Herenga Waka Marae and hear how the marae and Ngā Mokopuna together express values of sustainability, kaitiakitanga, belonging, and connection.

Whether you're interested in sustainable design, Māori worldviews, education, architecture, or the future of the built environment, this tour offers a unique insight into a project that seeks to demonstrate what regenerative design can achieve.

Come and discover how sustainability and kaitiakitanga are being brought to life at Ngā Mokopuna.

😼 Totally Chonkers Collective are heading back to Blenheim for a heavyweight night of underground bass music, bringing one of Aotearoa’s most established Dubstep and Drum & Bass artists, Optimus Gryme, to The Yard Bar on 29 August. 🔥

Driven by a lifelong passion for music, Charlie B—better known as Optimus Gryme—has spent more than two decades helping shape New Zealand’s bass music landscape. His journey began in the 1990s with hip hop, progressing from schoolyard performances to playing in front of thousands alongside artists such as Che Fu and King Kapisi.

In 2009, Optimus Gryme made history by releasing New Zealand’s first Dubstep 12-inch record. He went on to release a solo album and create official remixes for some of the country’s biggest names, including Shapeshifter, Shihad, Six60, Tiki Taane and Dub FX.

Across his career, he has performed more than a thousand shows and appeared at major festivals including Homegrown, Rhythm & Vines and Northern Bass. Following a two-year hiatus, he returned in 2020 with his Drum & Bass EP, Welcome to the Streets, continuing a musical journey that shows no sign of slowing down.

Now, Optimus Gryme is bringing that experience to The Yard Bar for a headline set packed with Dubstep, Drum & Bass, heavyweight low-end pressure and unmistakable sound system energy.

Physical Oceanography Workshop 2026, Overview












The physics of the ocean in the age of multiple stressors.




Welcome to the biannual New Zealand Physical Oceanography Workshop (POW).
As climate change fundamentally reshapes our marine environments, understanding the fluid dynamics, heat distribution, and structural dynamics of our oceans has never been more critical. This year, our community gathers under a vital, unifying theme: The physics of the ocean in the age of multiple stressors.

We invite abstracts and presentations exploring the fundamental physical processes driving—and reacting to—global environmental change:
Coastal Oceanography of New Zealand
High-Latitude and Polar Dynamics
Next-Generation Ocean Modelling & Data Integration
Cross-Disciplinary Climate Solutions
How to do oceanography in the age of gestures broadly

Call for Abstracts & Registration Details
Oral Presentations: Standard 15-minute slots (including Q&A).
Lightning Talks: Project snapshots—ideal for introducing preliminary findings, novel scripts, or new field deployments.
How to Submit: Please email your presentation title, authors' list, a brief abstract (max 250 words), and your presentation preference directly to the organising committee at oceanography.newzealand@gmail.com.
Abstract Submission Deadline: 20 August 2026
Registration Deadline: 20 August 2026
Hybrid Registration Deadline: 1 September 2026
Registration is $100 for general attendees and free for students. We also have a free hybrid attendance option with the ability to present. Early-career researchers are highly encouraged to present.

We are planning a fun dinner on Wednesday, and we aim to finish early on Thursday.
We're looking forward to seeing you in September!

Concert pianist Lưu Hồng Quang presents a remarkable programme from Franz Liszt's Years of Pilgrimage, Third Volume – a deeply spiritual and reflective work from the composer's later years.

This performance forms the final public presentation of Lưu Hồng Quang's Doctor of Musical Arts research at the New Zealand School of Music | Te Kōkī. description:
Power Up Central Hutt, Power Up Central Hutt
Come to the first of the new 2026 Power Up The Hutt information sessions in the Hutt Bowling Club, Myrtle Street on the evening of Thursday 29th October at 7:30pm.

Power Up the Hutt is a free five-part community event series bringing together Hutt Valley residents who want to cut their power bills, reduce their carbon footprint, and future-proof their homes.

New Zealand has reached an electrification tipping point — households can now save money and significantly reduce their emissions by switching their appliances and vehicles to electric. But knowing where to start can feel overwhelming.

These friendly, practical evenings — hosted by local volunteers with experience in electrification and drawing on the research of Rewiring Aotearoa — will walk you through the real options available right now: solar panels and home batteries, electric vehicles, heat pump hot water systems, induction cooking, and making the switch from gas to electricity.

Businesses, schools, or community organisations interested in electrification are also welcome. No jargon. No sales pitch. Just straight talk from your neighbours about what works, what it costs, and how to get started.

description:
Propagandhi tickets, Presented by: SBM
Propagandhi will make their long-awaited return to Australia and Aotearoa in early 2027, marking their first shows in the region in nearly eight years.
The ever-evolving standard-bearers of politically charged punk have actively kicked against musical confines and bro-punk conservatism, promoting a message of anti-fascism since 1986. Distilling their DNA of breakneck riffs, hardcore ethos, and radical consciousness, their message remains as vital, and volatile, as ever.
The tour comes in support of the Manitoba, Canada-based outfit’s eighth album, *At Peace*. In true Propagandhi fashion, it’s smart music for dangerous times. “Everything I’m singing about is still coming from being the same person that wrote and sang our first record *How to Clean Everything* in 1993,” Chris Hannah states, recalling the band’s snarky skate-thrash origins.
“But what we’re putting into the songs now, probably reflects more despair than 30 years ago when we had similar perspectives, but with strands of hope and naivete. Now it’s the existential dread of eking out a life worth living in this completely failed society.”
Propagandhi are set to bring their incendiary live show back to Australia and Aotearoa, drawing from a body of work that continues to challenge, confront, and inspire.
New album "At Peace" out now Propagandhi.com

Requirements Elicitation, Overview



Gain a core understanding of requirements elicitation, the importance of planning, and coverage of many valuable elicitation techniques.
Description
This one-day course provides a core understanding of elicitation, the importance of planning, and coverage of many valuable elicitation techniques. Emphasis is also placed on the need to verify requirements with the business to confirm that an accurate understanding has been elicited. During the afternoon session course participants undertake a realistic elicitation exercise, to reinforce the principles and techniques learnt during the course.
Greater emphasis is being placed on skilled business analysts who have the ability to communicate strongly, engage with stakeholders, and elicit a clear understanding of business requirements. Requirements elicitation skills have never been more important for business analysts and IT professionals.

The Requirements Elicitation course is delivered by seasoned Equinox consultant practitioners who apply the techniques and practices presented in this course on a daily basis.

Outline
Introduction to Requirements Elicitation
Goals of elicitation
Elicitation in the analysis process
Requirements elicitation methodology
Plan
The need for planning
Common elicitation problems
Requirements elicitation techniques
Requirements election patterns
Selection criteria
The requirements elicitation plan
Do
Preparing for the elicitation session
Performing elicitation
Managing the elicitation session
Presenting the elicitation results
Check
Communicate the requirements set
Check elicitation results
Check elicitation process
Act – corrective action
Requirements elicitation exercise

Learning outcomes
Following the completion of this course, students will be able to:
Identify where requirements elicitation fits within the broader requirements process
Understand and adopt an elicitation methodology
Select appropriate elicitation techniques for the situation
Plan and manage a requirements elicitation session
Understand the need for verification of elicitation results

Audience
The primary audience for this course is business analysts and systems analysts of all levels of experience. The course will also be of value to any project team members who are involved in elicitation or requirements activities.

Prerequisites
It is recommended that participants have some experience with requirements in project environment before attending.

Somatic Breathwork: Spring Renewal, Overview

Refresh body and mind with a gentle spring breathwork journey to release winter heaviness and reconnect with your natural aliveness.

Somatic Breathwork: Spring Renewal




Event starts at 6pm

September is a threshold month, a natural invitation to spring clean.

Not just the space around you, but the space inside you too.

Spring Cleansing is a somatic breathwork session designed to help you gently shift some of the heaviness that can build up over the colder months. Think sluggishness, brain fog, tension, low energy, or simply that feeling of being a little stuck in your body.

Through a consent-led, trauma-aware breathwork journey, we’ll create space to:

move stagnant energy and emotions
warm and reconnect with the body
release some of the heaviness that winter can leave behind
return to your breath, presence, and natural sense of aliveness

A chance to pause, breathe, and make room for something new.

You’ll leave feeling lighter, clearer, and more connected to your body, like opening the windows and letting fresh air move through.

This session is for you if:
you’ve felt heavy, puffy, sluggish, or “damp” after winter
your chest/breath has felt tight, shallow, or restricted
you’ve been waking up tired, unmotivated, or mentally foggy
you’ve been indoors more, moving less, and can feel it in your body
you want a reset that’s embodied, not performative
you want a welcoming, choice-based space to explore breathwork
What to expect
Arrival (consent + information) chair, side-lying, and low-intensity options available
Nervous system primer: clearing and activation safely
Breath demonstration + choice of intensity tracks (including a gentle nasal-only option)
A guided somatic breathwork arc. clearing, warming, and releasing what’s been holding on
Optional movement to support circulation (micro-shakes, shaking, or gentle unwinding)
Integration rest + grounding
Closing reflection (brief journaling prompt or quiet pause)
Benefits you may notice

You might experience:

a lighter body and clearer head
more warmth and circulation through chest/shoulders/hips
improved mood and motivation
emotional release without overwhelm
deeper, easier breathing
a renewed sense of momentum that feels steady (not forced)
Please bring:
Yoga mat
Warm layers (we’ll warm up, but your body may cool during rest)
Water bottle
Small towel
Optional eye mask or light scarf
Journal and pen
If you run cold, bring a blanket
Pre-class prep
Eat a light meal 2 hours before class.
Hydrate well throughout the day.
Avoid alcohol and recreational substances for 24 hours.
Limit caffeine 4 hours prior.
Arrive 10 minutes early for intake.
If you have health conditions, please check with your provider.
Feel free to email Lynn at hi@lynofuro.co.nz if there’s anything you’d like to share before the session.
Contraindications and safety

Somatic breathwork may not be suitable for pregnancy; serious cardiovascular conditions; uncontrolled blood pressure; glaucoma or retinal detachment; epilepsy or seizure history; recent surgery or concussion; or severe psychiatric conditions/active psychosis. A conservative, nasal-only track is always available. This is not a substitute for medical care.

Aftercare

After the session, remember to:

Drink plenty of water
Eat nourishing food
Engage in simple movement or a short walk
Journal your insights
Get an early bedtime

Emotional waves may continue for 24 to 48 hours, reach out if you need support.

You’ll also receive a guided audio breathwork aftercare to support you in the 24–48 hours after the session (gentle regulation, grounding, and integration).

Please stay for a delicious plant-based dinner and dessert afterwards, included in your ticket!
September 1:1 Somatic Coaching — 2 spots available

If this session lights something up in you and you’re ready for deeper support, I’m opening 2 private 1:1 coaching spots in September.

This is for you if you want nervous-system-led guidance to:

regulate stress and restore steady capacity
soften chronic tension patterns in the body
build embodied boundaries and self-trust
move through stuckness with breath, somatic tools, and grounded coaching

To enquire, email hi@lynofuro.co.nz with the subject line: September 1:1.

Meet Your Host: Lynn

Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach, breathwork facilitator, and Reiki practitioner based in Aotearoa, New Zealand. Her work combines somatic breathwork, Reiki, and life coaching to support nervous system regulation, emotional wellbeing, and grounded personal transformation in a practical, trauma-aware way.

Speak with Confidence, Speak with Clarity, Speak with IMPACT - Wellington, Overview

Get ready to boost your confidence, and your speaking game, and learn how to leave a lasting impression every time you talk.

Speak with Confidence, Speak with Clarity, Speak with Impact




How we communicate shapes how people experience us, how well our ideas are understood and, ultimately, the influence we are able to have.

In this practical and highly interactive workshop, communication specialist and keynote speaker Monique Bradley helps participants develop the confidence to use their voice, the clarity to know what they want to say, and the skills to communicate in a way that connects with other people and creates impact.

Participants will explore some of the most common challenges around speaking and presenting, including nerves, uncertainty about what to say, how to structure a message, how to keep an audience engaged and how to deliver with greater confidence and presence.

Monique introduces simple, practical techniques for managing nerves, structuring presentations, strengthening vocal delivery and using stories to make ideas more engaging and memorable. The session also explores communication as a form of influence and challenges participants to think intentionally about how they want to be experienced and remembered by others.

The focus throughout is not perfection. It is building competence through practice, developing greater self-belief and learning how to communicate with confidence, clarity and genuine human connection. The workshop closes on Monique’s core principle: confidence is built through competence, and competence is built through repetition.

Participants will leave with:
practical tools for managing nerves and speaking anxiety
a simple way to structure what they want to say
techniques for improving pace, pitch, projection and pronunciation
greater awareness of how stories create connection and influence
practical experience speaking and practising their delivery
a clearer understanding of the impact they want their communication to have

1-4 Sept, and 6-11 Sept
Botanic Garden ki Paekākā

Gather your friends, whānau, or neighbours who might find it tricky to access the gardens, and enjoy a relaxing, self-guided drive through a spectacular spring floral display at Wellington Botanic Garden ki Paekākā.
Simply drive along the one-way route past the Display Garden and soak in the colours of tulips, forget-me-nots, dianthus, primulas, chrysanthemums, daffodils, and more.

How it works:
- No registration needed — just turn up and enter through the Glenmore Street gates.
- Follow the designated one-way route through the gardens, keeping within your vehicle at all times.
- Exit through the West/White Gate to return to Glenmore Street.
- Feel free to enjoy the route as many times as you like during opening hours.

Please note:
- Drive slowly (maximum 10 km/h), and watch carefully for pedestrians, especially children.
- Stay in your vehicle for the entire tour to keep everyone safe and comfortable.
- Follow all signage and do not turn around within the garden grounds.

This event is self-guided and unstaffed. If you need assistance during your visit, please call 04 499 1400.
For enquiries, email treehouse@wcc.govt.nz or call 04 499 1400.

description:
State-Market Tensions & Geopolitical Rivalry in the Semiconductor Industry, Overview
Why are semiconductors central to global power? This keynote explores state-market tensions, supply chains, and geopolitical rivalry.
Using the global semiconductor industry as a case study, this lecture explores ‘decoupling’ amidst the complex web of state-market relations.
Most studies of decoupling focus on the United States and China. In contrast, I focus on the relationship between the United States and the full range of key semiconductor producers (Taiwan, South Korea, Japan, and China). I ask when, and how, states intervene in semiconductor markets and propose that while the main actors in the semiconductor supply chain are not hegemonic powers, their high production capacities mean that their power is ‘pivotal’.
I argue that while technology production chains reflect the conflicting interests of states, because production chains also embody key shared interests, states cannot completely ‘decouple’ from one another. Meanwhile, key stakeholders are not always states, but also private companies and skilled workers. These actors have their own interests as well, meaning that production chains become further intertwined, rendering true decoupling impossible. Their resistance to decoupling means that this ‘stickiness’ will be a feature of any state-led attempt to forge supply chain independence.

What if creating a better future starts with rethinking the way we live today?

FREE EVENT: Join us for an evening of conversation, connection, kai, and practical ideas for building more sustainable and resilient communities.

Who is this for? Anyone interested in creating a more sustainable and resilient future, whether you're already taking action or simply wondering where to start.

We'll bring together leaders, changemakers, and community voices to explore:

🌿 What can we actually do at home?
🌏 How can we build stronger, more resilient communities?

Talanoa for Tomorrow is taking place across four Wellington sessions, with a different panel of speakers at each event.




We are excited to announce for this session we have:

Andrew Wilks is the Manutaki (Director) of Sustainability at Te Herenga Waka – Victoria University of Wellington, leading efforts to embed sustainability and climate action across the University. He is passionate about helping people and organisations take practical action on climate change, build resilience, and create positive futures for their communities.

Dr. Nate Rigler is the Project Lead for the collaborative Kia Mouriora Te Kaiwharawhara Sanctuary to Sea initiative, led by Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne. With a PhD in Pacific Studies and a deep passion for urban biodiversity, Nate works to connect local communities and businesses with native ecosystem restoration in Te Kaiwharawhara water catchment.

Inangaro Vakaafi - Pacific Climate Warriors

Joshua Peauafi is a Pacific leader, social impact advocate, and co-founder of Potplant Studio. Passionate about relational leadership, diversity, equity, and inclusion, Joshua uses nature and plants as a vehicle to spark meaningful conversations around wellbeing, mental health, and community connection across Aotearoa New Zealand.

The Pharcyde tickets, Presented by: Meow Touring
*VENUE UPGRADE*
Due to overwhelming demand, The Pharcyde has been upgraded to Meow Nui!
All existing tickets remain valid. If you haven't grabbed yours yet, now's the time.
Few groups have had a greater impact on alternative hip hop than The Pharcyde.
Emerging from South Central Los Angeles in the early '90s, they rewrote the rules with their wit, originality and unmistakable chemistry, delivering two of the most influential albums of the era.
From the platinum-selling Bizarre Ride II the Pharcyde to the genre-defining Labcabincalifornia, classics like "Passin' Me By," "Runnin'," "Drop," "Otha Fish" and "Ya Mama" continue to inspire generations of artists and remain essential listening more than 30 years later.
The Pharcyde's legacy extends far beyond their own catalogue. They helped open the door for a more playful, soulful and inventive style of hip hop, collaborated with a then- emerging J Dilla, worked with visionary director Spike Jonze, and proved that creativity could be just as powerful as bravado. Their influence can still be heard across modern hip hop, while their timeless live show continues to win over audiences around the world.
Featuring Imani, Slimkid3, Fatlip and DJ Cee Brown, this is your chance to experience one of hip hop's defining groups live.
Secure your tickets early and don't miss the opportunity to see true pioneers of alternative hip hop when they return this December.

Have you ever bitten into an apple and wondered where it came from?

Not the orchard.

Not the supermarket.

But the very first idea that eventually became the fruit in your hand.

Creating a new apple or pear variety isn't something that happens overnight. It can take years of research, testing, patience and innovation before a single piece of fruit reaches consumers.

Join Tony Martin, Chief Executive of Prevar, for a fascinating behind-the-scenes Learning Lunch exploring how New Zealand is helping shape the future of fruit.

From understanding changing consumer tastes to developing entirely new varieties, Tony will reveal the remarkable journey from seedling to supermarket shelf and the science, strategy and creativity that make it possible.

You'll discover how some of New Zealand's most successful apple and pear varieties were developed, what makes a fruit variety stand out in global markets, and why innovation in horticulture requires both long-term thinking and bold decision-making.

Best of all, this isn't just a conversation.

Guests will enjoy a guided tasting of different apple and pear varieties, offering a rare opportunity to experience firsthand the flavours, textures and characteristics that breeders spend years developing.

This is a wonderful opportunity to look at something familiar in a completely new way.

Meet Tony 🎤

Tony Martin is Chief Executive of Prevar, the innovation and commercialisation company behind many of New Zealand and Australia's leading apple and pear varieties. With more than two decades of leadership experience across agribusiness, innovation and international markets, Tony works at the intersection of science, consumer insight and global horticulture, helping bring world-class fruit varieties from concept to consumers around the world.

What We'll Explore
• How new apple and pear varieties are created
• The science and strategy behind fruit innovation
• What consumers really want from future fruit varieties

description:
Treasury Guest Lecture with Sir Peter Gluckman: IN-PERSON attendance, Overview

A provocation from inside and outside: addressing New Zealand’s systems challenges

Join us for the next lecture in our current seminar series

Over recent decades, New Zealand policy making in most areas has been focused on the short-term: often political claims for solutions have been over-simplified. This has contributed to citizen’s cynicism and a decline in institutional trust which puts at risk the social cohesion which has been one of New Zealand’s greatest assets. Most evident is the continued failure to really lift productivity and reach a trajectory like other small, advanced economies.

The challenges ahead of us include: a big demographic shift in age and composition and the need for a more complete population strategy, the failure to systematically understand the opportunities in the rapid technology revolution underway in both the digital/AI and life sciences, an inevitable shift in the nature of higher education, a persistent failure of Auckland to demonstrate a comparative agglomeration effect, a failure to maximise international partnerships beyond trade and security, and a continued naive exceptionalism with regard to science and research. At the policy level this is reflected in a relative lack of the use of the tools of long-term thinking including anticipatory foresight and formative evaluation and continued siloed and short-term biases in the budget process.

Our guest speaker - Sir Peter Gluckman, founder of Koi Tū: Centre for Informed Futures and the President of International Science Council - will address each of these provocations.

About this event

This will be a hybrid event. Please use this site to register if you plan to attend it in person.

If you would like to attend it virtually, please use THIS LINK to register.

About the presenter

Sir Peter Gluckman ONZ KNZM FRSNZ FRS is founder of Koi Tu: Centre for Informed Futures (a non-partisan thinktank focused on long-term and complex issues facing New Zealand), president of the International Science Council and member of the Prime Minister’s Science, Innovation and Technology Advisory Council. Former President of the International Network for Government Science Advice and chief science advisor to the Prime Ministers of New Zealand (2009-2018). He chaired both the recent Science System Advisory Group and the University Advisory Group.

He is a biomedical and clinical scientist who has published over 750 scientific papers and was awarded the Rutherford Medal in 2001 and has written extensively on the science policy and science diplomacy interfaces. He is the recipient of the American Association for the Advancement of Science medal for science diplomacy.

About this seminar series

New ideas, robust evidence, and insights from leading thinkers are crucial to strengthening the Treasury’s economic analysis and policy advice. Our new guest lecture theme — Navigating Global Shifts: Resilience, Challenges and Opportunities for New Zealand — invites us to reflect on how Aotearoa New Zealand can navigate an increasingly complex and interconnected global environment.

This series explores the major global forces that shape our economic landscape, including evolving trade relationships, geopolitical developments, and the global movement of people, capital, and ideas. Through these discussions, we aim to deepen our understanding of how New Zealand can build economic resilience, respond effectively to uncertainty, and harness our regional and international partnerships to support economic performance, productivity, and our living standards.

Our speakers explore strategies for mitigating the impacts of global disruptions — from pandemics and climate‑related events to geopolitical tensions and supply‑chain shocks – while also examining potential opportunities presented by rapid technological shifts, digital economy, and global innovations, to name a few. The series considers the role of government in supporting economic transitions, strengthening national resilience, and ensuring that New Zealand remains well‑positioned to meet emerging global opportunities. By bringing together diverse perspectives, this series seeks to inspire new ways of thinking about New Zealand’s economic future and to support informed, forward‑looking policymaking.

Please note that the views, opinions, findings, and conclusions expressed in the Treasury Guest Lecture Series are those of the individual presenters. They do not necessarily reflect the views of the New Zealand Treasury or the New Zealand Government.

For updates and our latest research visit: www.treasury.govt.nz

Keep in touch

If you would like to be the first to hear about our upcoming events in the Treasury Guest Lecture Series, please SUBSCRIBE to stay up to date.

description:
Āio: a Puoro Māori Sound Journey, Overview

Journey inward through Māori sound, pūrākau and crystal bowls, creating a peaceful evening of deep listening, rest and restoration.

Āio: a Puoro Māori Sound Journey




Starts at 6pm

Experience a peaceful Māori sound journey blending taonga pūoro, story, and crystal bowls for deep relaxation and inner calm

“Āio” speaks to peace and inner calm. In this immersive evening, pūrākau, taonga pūoro and waiata are woven together with the healing vibrations of crystal singing bowls, creating a space for deep listening, rest and restoration.

The organic tones of traditional Māori instruments including kōauau, pūtōrino, porotiti and pūtātara blend with the resonance of crystal bowls, chimes and ukulele, inviting you to slow down, soften and reconnect with your wairua and body. Through story, sound and vibration, this is a gentle journey inward.

What to bring:

Yoga mats, blankets and cushions will be provided, but you are welcome to bring extra for comfort!




After the sound journey, share in a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, included in your ticket, a warm way to close the evening together.

Meet your hosts & musicians: Smita, Peter, and Alexandra:

Smita (Ngāi Te Rangi) was born and raised in Aotearoa. From a young age she was drawn to music as a means for reflection and self-expression. During her music studies at university, she was introduced to taonga pūoro, and this sparked a personal journey of reconnection to te ao Māori and her own whakapapa. Following university, she lived in an ashram for several years where she was introduced to the wonderful practice of bhakti yoga. She now lives with her husband in the Wellington region, where they regularly participate in kirtan (mantra music meditation) at Bhakti Lounge.

Peter is Pākehā, with grandparents from England and Ireland, and has been on a four-year journey learning the art of taonga pūoro — the traditional Māori musical instruments of Aotearoa. Guided by the wisdom and generosity of expert makers and players, he has learned both to craft and to play these unique instruments. For Peter, taonga pūoro offer a way to connect deeply with sound, story, and the natural world, and he is excited to share their voices as part of this sound bath experience.

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from artists such as Deva Premal, The Flying Mystics, Stevin McNamara, and the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

description:
A Day in the Heart - One Day Silent Yoga and Meditation Retreat, A Day in the Heart - One Day Silent Yoga and Meditation Retreat
An invitation to press "pause" for a day, and just Be.

To drop from the busy mind into the silence of the Heart.

And to remember the freedom of who you are, when you're not in a role.


This lovingly crafted offering is a day immersion into practice, providing a glimpse of what the experience of silence can offer.

Suitable for complete beginners in meditation and yoga, as well as for advanced practitioners who'd like to unplug and enjoy retreat-time.


The schedule will include:

- Multiple seated meditation sessions with guidance

- Walking meditation

- Mindful Hatha Yoga and Restorative Yoga sessions

- Yoga Nidra

- Cacao to open the Heart

- Time to journal, walk in nature, or just be


Cost for a whole day program + 2 meals: $195


Food:

breakfast and lunch - nutritious vegan meals prepared with love + tea and cacao


Location:

the Lotus Yoga Centre in Paraparaumu


Date: 22nd August 2026 Saturday

Duration: 7.30am - 5.30pm

please arrive at 7.15am to settle in and start on time


To book, please purchase your ticket below or email Radha for more info at


*WHY IS THIS A SILENT RETREAT? A silent retreat means that everyone participating observes mauna, noble silence (apart from the teacher/ the guide). This means no casual chats and conversations, but also no use of phone or any devices during the day. The practice of silence allows the the mind to quieten down significantly, it is a very unique, deeply purifying and enlightening experience. It creates space for a deep insight and a proper reset, even in the short span of one day.


*WHY MEDITATION? Meditation is known for thousands of years as one of the most powerful practices, within and outside of spiritual context. It is good not only for creating a state of calm or relaxation, but also is the best known path to self-knowledge and self-love. When we retreat into silence beyond mind, there is an unmistakable feeling of being back home, in the heart of being, a sense of connection and purpose.


*WHY "A DAY IN THE HEART"? The Heart/ Hridaya in Sanskrit is a synonym of awareness or presence. According to the great yogis and the non-dual philosophy, the Heart is a place to centre in our meditations, but also an organ of knowledge and the seat of our true Self. When the mind is quiet and we centre within, the Heart can awaken - bringing a sense of being back home, back to what truly matters, back to our Self.

As Rumi said, "Close your eyes, fall in love, stay there"

A Weekend of Qi — with Dr Margaret Macky | Strathean, Kāpiti, A Weekend of Qi — with Dr Margaret Macky | Strathean, Kāpiti
Qigong is a practice people discover and then quietly wonder where it's been all their lives. You'll leave this weekend with a practice that actually calms your nervous system — and one that you'll keep using.

Dr Margaret Macky is a retired medical doctor who came to qigong through her own chronic back pain — and stayed for the 25 years since. She has trained with Zhineng Master Wei Qi Feng and taught internationally, but she rarely offers in-person retreats in New Zealand. This July is one of those rare occasions.

The setting is Strathean Retreat Centre — 10 acres of open farmland edged with native tōtara forest near Ōtaki, just 50 minutes north of Wellington. A genuinely quiet place.

Over two days you'll learn the beautiful flowing qi forms of the Zhineng tradition and sit in guided qigong meditation — a practice that works with the body's own energy in a way that's hard to describe and easy to feel. No experience required. No particular fitness level. Just two days away from your usual pace.

If you've been curious about qigong, or you simply need two days that feel genuinely different, this is the one.

Places are limited and the weekend is fully catered — all meals, accommodation, and sessions included. Choose the option that suits you:


✦ Shared room: $430

Questions:


About Dr Margaret Macky

Dr Margaret Macky came to qigong in the late 1990s through her own experience of chronic back pain. As a medical doctor, she was well-placed to be sceptical — and well-placed to recognise, once the pain was gone, that something real was happening.
She has since trained closely with Zhineng Master Wei Qi Feng, qualifying as a Mingjue Gongfu teacher — a practice rooted in a deep consciousness state that she describes as qigong's most profound dimension. For four years she has taught an international audience through the World Consciousness Community, with intensive retreats in China and online courses reaching students across the globe.
Now retired from medicine and living near Takaka in Golden Bay, Margaret devotes her time to practice and teaching.

description:
Bach Choir, Nota Bene, Chiesa Ensemble - Bach's Christmas Oratorio, The Bach Choir of Wellington, in collaboration with Nota Bene and the Chiesa Ensemble, presents Bach’s Christmas Oratorio (Parts I, II, III & VI).

Bach’s Christmas Oratorio, BWV 248, is a spiritually rich masterpiece composed during 1723 and 1724 and first performed in its entirety during the Christmas season of 1734–1735 while Bach was serving in Leipzig. Drawing on earlier secular cantatas and a now-lost church cantata (BWV 248a), this oratorio weaves together a vibrant tapestry of sacred music celebrating the birth of Christ.

This performance features four of the six cantatas:

Part I opens with a dazzling transformation of secular music into sacred celebration. Drums, strings, winds, and triumphant trumpets set the stage for the Evangelist’s narration and a sequence of expressive recitatives and arias, including the beloved “Bereite dich, Zion” and the majestic “Großer Herr, o starker König.” Chorales, including the Passion Chorale, frame the cantata with solemn beauty.

Part II begins with a pastoral, tender tone, portraying the shepherds’ encounter with the angel. The sinfonia evokes a rustic charm with oboes and flutes, leading into serene chorales and the exquisite slumber aria, where the flute hovers like a halo above the alto voice. The cantata concludes with a joyful “Glory to God” and a reprise of “Vom Himmel hoch.”

Part III returns to grandeur with trumpets and drums, as the shepherds journey to Bethlehem. The Evangelist’s narration is interwoven with contemplative chorales, a duet for soprano and bass, and an aria reflecting Mary’s inner thoughts. The cantata closes with a reprise of its opening chorus, reinforcing its celebratory tone.

Part VI, written for Epiphany, shifts to a darker mood as the story turns to Herod’s treachery. The music is dramatic and unpredictable, mirroring the tension of the narrative. The arias and recitatives explore divine power and moral conflict, culminating in a triumphant final chorus embedded with the Passion Chorale—symbolically linking Christ’s birth to his eventual sacrifice.

This is the first time in over a decade the Christmas Oratorio is being performed in Wellington, making this a special opportunity to experience one of Bach’s most joyful and profound creations. We hope you will join us for an evening of radiant music and festive spirit.

description:
Cacao & Connection, Cacao & Connection
This evening is about real connection - the kind that happens when guards soften, and we don’t have to perform or impress.

We will all share cacao, and have conversations that feel a little more meaningful than everyday small talk.

How the evening unfolds:

We’ll begin with a short grounding exercise to help everyone arrive and settle. Life is hectic, and this is a moment to pause and land before moving into connection.

We’ll then share a cacao ceremony in a circle. Cacao is known for gently opening the heart space and supporting presence and openness. It’s subtle and grounding rather than dramatic.

From there, the circle opens for a heartshare experience. A reflective question will be offered as a prompt, and each person is invited (but never expected) to share from their own experience. This is not about fixing or advising - it’s about speaking honestly, listening deeply, and being witnessed.

The evening ends with a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, included in your ticket. Conversations can continue!

What heartsharing can offer

A sense of true connection
Being seen and heard as you are can soften feelings of loneliness and remind you that you’re not alone in what you carry.

Honest, meaningful conversation
Heartsharing moves beyond small talk, creating space for authenticity, vulnerability, and real presence.

Deeper self-understanding
Listening and sharing with others often brings clarity around your own feelings, needs, and experiences.

Gentle personal growth
There’s something quietly powerful about speaking from the heart and listening without judgement - it often opens new perspectives in unexpected ways.

Emotional support and wellbeing
Sharing in a respectful, non-judgemental space can feel grounding, relieving, and deeply human.

A few things worth knowing

You’re very welcome to come alone - many people do. There’s no expectation to know anyone, and no pressure to speak if you don’t want to.

You don’t need to be experienced with cacao ceremonies or heartsharing, or “good at talking.” Curiosity, openness, and presence are more than enough.

The evening concludes with a plant-based dinner & dessert - all included in your ticket.

Meet Andre, your host
Andre has been exploring the art of authentic connection since his teens, when a rite of passage in Golden Bay first sparked his passion for circle work. description:
Challenges in a Changing World – what kind of future do we want?, Challenges in a Changing World – what kind of future do we want?

Humanity is at a crossroads

One path into the future leads to increasing social and economic division, environmental destruction, war and planetary peril. The other path leads to increasing social harmony, economic and environmental balance, and a golden era of peace.

Throughout history, especially at times of crisis, great spiritual teachers have emerged to show humanity the next step forward.

According to British artist, author and esotericist Benjamin Creme, a group of such spiritual teachers is now living in the modern world ~ Maitreya, the World Teacher and The Masters of Wisdom ~ to help and inspire humanity in its task of global transformation ~ to create a civilisation based on sharing, justice and peace; for humanity to act - to share and save our world.

From ancient times, a body of spiritual teachings known as the Ageless Wisdom has been handed down from generation to generation. A systematic and comprehensive account of the evolution of consciousness in humanity and nature, it describes how the universe came to exist, how it operates, and humanity’s place within it.

As humanity matures, further aspects of this previously hidden knowledge are released in a wider, more open manner. Throughout the last 100 years, the Ageless Wisdom Teachings have been communicated through individuals such as Helena Blavatsky, founder of the Theosophical Society, and later by Alice A. Bailey and Helena Roerich, followed by Benjamin Creme.

Along the lines of these teachings, humanity is once again at a critical point in its further development, now with a growing awareness of the necessity for unity, justice and peace.

According to these teachings, Maitreya – known as the Teacher for this coming Age of Aquarius – will emphasise the utter necessity for peace, and that the complete renunciation of war can only be achieved by trust. Sharing alone, Maitreya will affirm, can engender that trust.

~ followed by a short Transmission Meditation session ~

description:
Deep Listening Soundbath at Erskine Chapel, Deep Listening Soundbath at Erskine Chapel
For the first time, a Deep Listening Soundbath inside the sublime acoustics of Erskine Chapel

Tickets available here: https://events.humanitix.com/deep-listening-sound-bath-at-erskine-chapel/tickets

Limited door sales for $50

*Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable. Dress comfortably*

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1.5hr-hour sound bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs and taonga pūoro, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs and other instruments can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the sounds, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1.5hr-hour soundbath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life.

There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

*THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY**

Disclaimer
Sound baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.
Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first

About Us

Alistair is a practitioner of ngā taonga pūoro. He has performed, composed, and collaborated with many of Aotearoa's finest artists, across genres of music and alongside various artistic disciplines since 1999.


Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 35+ years musical experience. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

🌟✨ Ecstatic Dance Wellington – Summer Solstice Celebration ✨🌟

With DJ Codaraan & Kimberley Jade @ St Peters Village Hall, Paekākāriki.

Kimba Jade & Bernie Cruise are thrilled to be hosting a special Summer Solstice Ecstatic Dance — a night to move, release, and celebrate the turning of the seasons. 🎉

☀️ Summer Solstice Celebration
As we gather close to the longest day of the year, we honour the light, abundance, and life that the Sun brings. The Solstice marks a time of illumination, gratitude, and renewal — a powerful moment to celebrate all that has blossomed, and to release what no longer serves as we prepare to turn toward the next cycle.

Together, we’ll weave a simple solstice honouring and meditation before the dance to ground into our intentions and connection with the elements. We’ll close the evening with chai, chocolate, and community — a warm space to share reflections, smiles, and heart connection.

🎶 What is Ecstatic Dance?
A freeform, drug- and alcohol-free dance experience where you move however your body wants. The music flows like a wave — starting slow, rising to ecstatic peaks, then softening into stillness. It’s therapeutic, uplifting, and a powerful way to connect with yourself.

Please note, this Ecstatic Dance is not verbally guided — we let the music guide you 😊. Dance freely, how your body moves you.

🎶 The Dance Floor
Guided by DJ Codaraan (Bernie Cruise), expect an immersive journey through deep bass, tribal rhythms, and global soundscapes that awaken both body and spirit. His music will invite you to move and connect with your body, expect an enticing groove-focused journey that builds slowly, allowing you to find your flow at your pace.

🎶 The Sound System
Here at Ecstatic Dance Wellington, we believe in using a phat sound system with lots of bass for our dances. Expect an ultra-vibey, deeply immersive experience!

Limited door sales for $25
*Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket for maximum comfort and warmth*
Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1-hour gong bath experience.
During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.
Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy, particularly gong baths, in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and frequencies of the gongs can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.
Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the gongs, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.
Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1-hour gong bath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.
**THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 20 PEOPLE ONLY**
About Me
Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 30+ years musical experience. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

Gong Bath at Vogelmorn Hall, $20
Limited door sales for $25
Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable
Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1-hour gong bath experience.
During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.
Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy, particularly gong baths, in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.
Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the gongs, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.
Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1-hour gong bath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.
THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY
About Me
Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 35+ years musical experience. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice
