description:
Āio: a Puoro Māori Sound Journey, Āio: a Puoro Māori Sound Journey
Āio: a Puoro Māori Sound Journey

“Āio” speaks to peace and inner calm. In this immersive evening, pūrākau, taonga pūoro and waiata are woven together with the healing vibrations of crystal singing bowls to create a space of deep listening and restoration.

The organic tones of traditional Māori instruments — including kōauau, pūtōrino, porotiti and pūtātara — blend with the resonance of crystal bowls, chimes and ukulele, inviting you to slow down, soften, and reconnect with your wairua and your body. Through story, sound and vibration, this is a gentle journey inward.

After the sound journey, share in a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, included in your ticket — a warm way to close the evening together.


What to bring:

Yoga mats, blankets and cushions will be provided but you are welcome to bring extra for comfort!



Meet your hosts & musicians: Smita, Peter, and Alexandra

Smita (Ngāi Te Rangi) was born and raised in Aotearoa. From a young age she was drawn to music as a means for reflection and self-expression. During her music studies at university, she was introduced to taonga pūoro, and this sparked a personal journey of reconnection to te ao Māori and her own whakapapa. Following university, she lived in an ashram for several years where she was introduced to the wonderful practice of bhakti yoga. She now lives with her husband in the Wellington region, where they regularly participate in kirtan (mantra music meditation) at Bhakti Lounge.

Peter is Pākehā, with grandparents from England and Ireland, and has been on a four-year journey learning the art of taonga pūoro — the traditional Māori musical instruments of Aotearoa. Guided by the wisdom and generosity of expert makers and players, he has learned both to craft and to play these unique instruments. For Peter, taonga pūoro offer a way to connect deeply with sound, story, and the natural world, and he is excited to share their voices as part of this sound bath experience.

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche—making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from artists such as Deva Premal, The Flying Mystics, Stevin McNamara, and the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

✨Seeking new horizons and self-discovery? Try Kundalini energy awakening in 21 Days with- Free Online Guided Meditation- live & recorded

About this Event

Why 21 days of meditation for Kundalini Awakening?
Seeking new horizons and self-discovery? Use the New Year 2026- as an opportunity to challenge ourselves to rise higher with one journey we always missed- 'Journey Inside'. Be a part of the 21-day Kundalini Awakening community on Live & Recorded from 25th January (Sunday) 2026, to 14th February (Saturday) 2026 @ 2:45 PM every day. Link shared after signup.YouTube will have daily recordings in case you are unable to join live meeting at the scheduled time. We will schedule additional workshops on Sundays to enable you to join a live meeting. We cleanse our inner subtle system using the powerful yet gentle techniques of Sahaja Yoga Meditation. This is a spiritual meditation in which we awaken the inner energy called Kundalini that gently brings positive change within us-- making us more balanced, peaceful, and joyful. As you participate in daily classes, you will notice physical, emotional and spiritual healing. With pure desire, you may also feel Kundalini energy movement and its working on your fingertips and other physical manifestations. It will enable you to raise your consciousness to a higher dimension. Sahaja Yoga Meditation is volunteer-run, always free, and practiced in more than 100 countries.
No prior meditation or Kundalini awakening experience is needed.
Are you seeking awakening from the heart?

Who is organizing this course?
A team of Sahaja Yoga meditation volunteers has been practicing and teaching 'Sahaja Yoga' meditation for decades. Sahaja Yoga meditation was invented by 'Shri Mataji Nirmala Devi' in 1970, who, in a very Motherly fashion, helped people to take to true meditation easily. The goal of this meditation is to reconnect us to Divinity and experience the universal consciousness within us. It is practiced in more than 100 countries and is always free. description:
10th Grade Tournament, 10th Grade Tournament
10th Grade Tournament

Timona Park, Feilding | Hosted by Feilding United AFC Juniors

Feilding United AFC invites all 10th Grade teams registered to play in Central Football Manawatū to attend the 2026 10th Grade Festival in Feilding.

There is a 10th Grade Cup to be won, with runner-up medals awarded for second place. A minimum of eight teams is required for both awards to be presented.

No academy teams or tournament specific teams to enter.

WHEN & WHERE

The festival will be held on: Sunday 21 June 2026
(Postponement date: Sunday 28 June 2026)

📍 Timona Park, Feilding – Home of Feilding United AFC Juniors

· 8:30am – Coaches Meeting at the Feilding AFC Gazebo

· 9:00am – First games kick off

REGISTRATIONS

Registrations must be completed via Tournify using the link below:

https://tournifyapp.com/live/feildingafc10thgradetournament

Registration fee: $110 per team

The first 16 teams registered by 8th June 2026 will secure a place in the tournament.

RULES

Tournament rules will follow the current Central Football Regulations for Youth Leagues, which can be viewed here:

https://www.sporty.co.nz/asset/downloadasset?id=7eabcc5d-0023-4a42-9383-cb93c07e4814

DRAW & FORMAT

· Teams will play a minimum of four games.

· Games will consist of:

o 2 x 10-minute halves

o 2 -minute halftime

Points System

· Win = 3 points

· Draw = 1 point

The team with the most points will win their group.

If teams are tied on points, placings will be determined by:

1. Goal difference

2. Most goals scored

3. Toss of a coin

If a semi-final or final ends in a draw, the match will go directly to a penalty shootout. No extra time will be played.

REFEREES

Referees will be provided for most games. However, if a referee is unavailable, teams may be asked to provide a suitable person to control one half of the game.

The referee’s decision is final.

POSTPONEMENTS / CANCELLATIONS

The tournament will proceed regardless of weather conditions unless:

· Manawatū District Council closes the grounds, or

· A Health & Safety risk is identified by the Feilding United AFC Junior Football Committee.

Please remember that everyone involved in organising and refereeing this tournament are volunteers. Without them, this event could not take place.

Enjoy the day and the opportunity to watch the kids play the beautiful game!

CONTACT

For any questions or concerns, please email Blair at:

2-Day Kali Seminar with Stephen Brown from Inosanto Academy in CA, 2-Day Kali Seminar with Stephen Brown from Inosanto Academy in CA
Want to learn the exact martial art skills as used in the Bourne films? Wellington this is your chance...

Tactical Survival Academy is hosting Senior Instructor Stephen Brown from the renowned Inosanto Academy of Martial Arts in Marina Del Rey, Los Angeles!

With over 40 years of martial arts experience and 36 years training under Guro Dan Inosanto, Stephen is one of only two instructors currently teaching Kali classes at the academy alongside Guro Dan Inosanto himself.

Stephen specializes in the Filipino Martial Art of Kali, as passed down through Guro Inosanto’s lineage. His training background also includes extensive experience in Muay Thai, Silat, Western Boxing, Jeet Kune Do, Savate and Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu.

Over the decades, Stephen has worked with:
* Multiple branches of Law Enforcement, Military units and Special Forces.
* Actors, stunt performers, and executives in the film and television industry.
* As a fight choreographer for screen productions.

Known for his precision, adaptability, and deep respect for the cultural roots of the arts he teaches, Stephen brings a wealth of knowledge and embodied experience to every seminar.

Currently based in Marina Del Rey, CA, Stephen is excited to share the Kali method of Guro Inosanto with the New Zealand martial arts community.

• Location: Mt Cook School Hall, 160 Tory Street, Te Aro
• Dates: Sat Sept 6 + Sun Sept 7
• Time: 1:30pm – 4:30pm (both days)
• Cost: One Day Only (Sat or Sun) $140 / Both Days $260

description:
2025 Corporate Challenge Wellington, Team work makes the dream work at Corporate Challenge Wellington! join us on Wednesday, 12th November for a fun-filled night of team building, fitness and friendly competition.
Nestled between Te Papa and Chaffers Dock, right in the centre of the city, our event HQ at Waitangi Park unlocks the gorgeous Wellington waterfront. The course takes in all the sights - Te Papa, Whairepo Lagoon and the Well_ngton sign - as it follows the wide public esplanade around the harbour. Views forever and usually (always) a decent wind to chase you to the finish line.
After you finish your 5k - running or walking a flat, two-lap course around the waterfront - grab a banana and water or sport drink before heading back to your tent to see how your mates did. The best performances of the day - plus our amazing team managers - are acknowledged at the Awards Cermony at 7:30pm. Spot prizes wrap up around 8pm and there's time to exchange war stories as you pack down.

description:
24-hour Squash Marathon for Wayne, 24 Hours on Court for Wayne.
This time I’m picking up my squash racket for a challenge like no other: 24 hours of nonstop squash. Why? Because someone I care for has been facing a far tougher battle.
My father-in-law was recently diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL). For years he lived undiagnosed, pushing through symptoms without answers. Now that we finally know what he’s fighting, I want to turn my energy into something that can help him—and others—on their journeys.
According to CLL Advocates NZ, only 10-15 people out of 250 on average per year benefit from the budget allocation. And many are not even able to receive the same treatment options here in NZ.
Squash has always been a sport of endurance, resilience, and determination. Playing for 24 hours is my way of honoring his fight, raising awareness, and bringing people together to support the cause.
You can help by:
Donating: Any amount you would like to.
Predicting: Predicting how many points and games will be played in 24 hours.
Joining me on court: Book a slot to play a game, cheer from the sidelines, or come be part of the atmosphere.
Buy raffle tickets, or sponsor a prize towards the raffle.
We would like to give a shout out to our current sponsors;
Hair Phoria,
Aimee Photography,
X-Potential,
Mitchells,
Meaters,
CBD Eatery,
Forrest Wines and
Fat Tony's
No matter how small, your contribution will make a difference. Together we can transform his story of late diagnosis into one of community, awareness, and action.
I’ll be pushing myself through the night, but I won’t be alone—your support will keep me going with every serve, rally, and game. Let’s make this 24 hours count.

description:
Blenheim Trail Runners Presents - Crush The Vernon - V2, Blenheim Trail Runners Presents - Crush The Vernon - V2
The Second coming of the "Crush the Vernon" Vert Day is just around the corner, We had such a great time last time and its smack bang into the point where everyone needs elevation for events so i thought it would be silly not to bring it back!

"Crush the Vernon" is a couple of fun endurance challeges to get us up into the Wither Hills for a big vert day!
This event will push you to the red line, boasting both as much high-level uphill suffering as you can possibly endure whilst building a steady accumulation of regret over 6 hours on the trails.
It’s an event that's built to stretch the boundaries of what you think you can do uphill, but overall, it’s a chance to get out there and have some fun, whether solo or in a team. Whilst there is some faster efforts needed to come out on top of any of these “disciplines”, the aim of the game is just to get out there and enjoy yourself at whatever pace suits you.

The added extra this time is not only an extra hour, explained below, but the plan is to tie this into the elevation for a group effort for a BTR Everest Challenge, more details around this when I can get a team entry together, but really keen to try and pudh the limits of what has been done before.

Details:
Date: 26th October - Backup date is the week after
Time: 6am-1pm - (1 hr per week it too Hialry to conquer everest!)
Location: The Wither Hills, Basecamp: Sutherland Stream picnic area - this will be where we have the whiteboard & a bit of an "Aid station/Bag drop" situation going on.

Disciplines:
- "Vernon Vert Masters" Highest total elevation (solo/team) - pretty self explanatory, but between the hours of 6 am- 1pm any elevation in the Wither hills farm park accumulated within these hours on this day (solo or in a team) counts towards your total for the “Total Elevation” part of the challenge

- “Crush the Covenant” loop (solo/team) - Crush the covenant Loop is a 3.75km, 300m vert loop running from Sutherland Stream Picnic Area to the Mt Vernon Summit & then back down again, the loops can be run in whichever direction you would like, just be aware that this is a 2-way track and there will be a bit more traffic than you would usually see up on it. The aim of the game here is to get as many laps in as possible between 6 am-1pm; this will also count toward your elevation total for the "Vernon Vert Masters"

The Basics:
- This is an open event to anyone who wants to participate
- The event is open from 6am-1pm - any elevation in the Wither hills farm park accumulated within these hours on this day counts towards your total for the “Total Elevation” part of the challenge
- We will have a basecamp/aid station at the Sutherland stream picnic spot. This will be the hub for the meet-up and the start/finish line for the laps of “Crush the Covenant”.
- No minimum time, you can start whenever you like in the 6 am-1pm timeframe and go for as long as you would like.
-You can do as many laps/summits/cumulative elevation as you like/can within the timeframe.
- Teams - Teams can be between 2-5 people for the overall elevation challenge, and your total elevation will be your total accumulated. You will need to pre-register your team with Mikey before the day so that we can have you on the scoreboard.
- You will need to confirm your solo/teams total elevation with Basecamp by 1.30pm on the day, in person. If you are unable to do this for whatever reason, you will need to confirm and prove details via message or screenshots so we can add them to the total tally.


Who's up for some hills?



Disclaimer
We at Blenheim Trail Runners don’t see ourselves as event organisers and as such, do not have any consent or insurance; we deem this as a “Club Meet-up”.
With that, the expectation is that you are 100% responsible for yourself and take part at your own risk.
Be aware, as this isn't a formal event, there won't be any official timekeeping, marshals or trail markers. There will be DIY DIY-type whiteboard to note down your shared laps & elevation, and we will provide details via trail maps for the “Crush the Covenant” loop.
We are unable to provide any/can not be held responsible for: Urgent medical attention (we will however, assist wherever possible, there will be a first aid kit at base camp), nutrition, hydration ( there is public access throughout the hills and in two points on the “crush the Covenant” loop), the condition of the trail on the day or the weather.
label: Sports & Fitness

Card Merchant Wellington - Catan Cities Event 2026, Card Merchant Wellington - Catan Cities Event 2026
​Card Merchant is incredibly excited to be working with CATAN Studio and Asmodee to bring official CATAN Organized Play to New Zealand.

As part of the 2026 Organized Play program, Card Merchant stores across the country will be hosting 10 CATAN Cities Events. These events represent the next step up in competitive play and serve as regional qualifiers for the New Zealand CATAN National Championship.

Each represented city will host a single Cities Event, with 10 events taking place nationwide. The winner of each Cities Event will earn a seeded place in the Top 16 of the New Zealand Catan National Championship, to be held in Wellington later this year.

Whether you're an experienced Catan player or looking to test your skills in a larger tournament environment, Cities Events provide the opportunity to compete against players from your region and take the next step on the road to Nationals.

Event Details

Store: Card Merchant Wellington

Date: 22nd August 2026

Time: 11:00am

Entry Fee: $20

Event Structure

Players will compete across multiple rounds of base game CATAN to determine overall standings.

Preliminary Round

• Each participant will play three separate games of base set CATAN.

• Opponents will rotate between games.

• At the conclusion of the preliminary rounds, players will be ranked based on their overall performance.

Final Rounds

• Depending on attendance numbers, top-performing players may advance to final tables to determine overall placings.

• If attendance numbers are lower, the event may instead consist solely of multiple Swiss-style rounds, with final standings determined by total points or wins.

This structure is designed to provide a competitive tournament experience while remaining approachable and enjoyable for players of all experience levels.

Prizes

In addition to qualification opportunities, a range of official Catan Organized Play prizes will be awarded on the day.

Prizing includes:

8x Summer Hex Sets

Christmas Race Day, Christmas Race Day at the historic Tauherenikau Racing and Event Centre, 1498 SH2, Featherston, 1pm – 6pm, Sunday. Get your families and friends together for an afternoon of thrilling horse racing and fun at the historic Tauherenikau Racecourse. Free entry. For more information, go to: https://www.tauherenikau.co.nz/

The Wairarapa Racing Club was officially formed on the 21st of April 1864. For ten years the club held meetings in other parts of the Wairarapa and in 1874 shifted to its current location at Tauherenikau.

Work began on the Tauherenikau Racecourse in 1866 and was completed in 1874, with the first meeting being held at Tauherenikau on January 26th/27th, 1874. The first buildings were erected in 1892 with the building of a Grandstand, Weighing Room, Stewards Room, 4 boxes and 8 stalls.

A Featherston Heritage Festival Event.

Three wide, staggered rows, with 2m between the rear of the bike in front and the front of the bike behind.

Pits
Pit site allocation TBC closer to the time.

Officials for the weekend
Clerk of Course: Alysha Sands
Steward of Meeting: Dane Foster
Friday and Saturday night support crew (so far!): Georgia Lynn, Quentin, John Busby and Matt Clarke

We NEED an army of volunteers for both Friday and Saturday night! There will be lights on the track, sure, but we can't underestimate the safety risk of running at night! We need eyes... everywhere... we can't do this without extra hands. Calling all parents, friends and acquaintances – if you can spare some time either night, please reach out to Alysha!

✨ Light it up! ✨
It's a NIGHT race! So we're going to join our karting counterparts and allow some decorative lighting on your bikes!! Get creative, just make sure you follow the rules in the SuppRegs!

Machine examination will include checking your light setup, and the examiner's decision is final – so make it good, but make it compliant!

Wanna camp at the track?
Parking will be available Friday and Saturday in the far carpark on the western side of the track complex. Self-contained motorhomes and caravans only! Cost: TBC

Does racing make you hungry? Or thirsty?
The Club Café will be serving dinner both nights plus snacks and drinks. Alcoholic drinks available after racing only.

Not a member?
If you're not a BRNZ, MNZ or KSW member you can still race! Reach out and we'll give you the info you need.

Don't wanna race but wanna watch?
Spectators are free to come along and enjoy the racing – everyone's welcome! Just keep your wits about you and stay safe around the track.

More info to follow closer to the event – keep an eye on this page!

See you there!

Please note: the track is closed Friday through Sunday for any activity other than the on-track times listed above.

This is a double elimination format tournament. Teams must lose twice to be eliminated. Matches are played according to standard shuffleboard rules as can be read here:
https://www.theshufflehouse.com/.../how-to-play...
EXCEPT:
- There is a 10 MINUTE time limit each match.
- Matches are played FIRST TO TEN.
- In the event of a draw after the 10 minute time limit, a "Golden End" will be played. The winner of the Golden End wins the match.
- Pucks that do not pass the foul line are removed from play.
- The shuffleboard will be reset and resanded after each match.
- No sand will be added during a match.
- The final match is played first to 15 with no time limit - if time allows.
- Every "Hanger" is rewarded with a sweet treat!

description:
Double Trouble @ Moonshine, Double Trouble @ Moonshine
Welcome to the first edition of Double Trouble @ Moonshine Park!

What?
Double Trouble is a one-day, two round Doubles disc golf tournament. The modified best-shot doubles rule applies where only two tee shots in a row from the same player can be taken.

There are two divisions available:
1) Open (no rating caps or restrictions)
2) Mixed

Mixed division is for teams of:
* male + female
* female + female
* adult + junior
* junior + junior.
The guideline for entry to the Mixed division is that the total PDGA rating for the team is less than 1700.

Registration is capped at 54 teams, so get in quick so you don't miss out (there will be a wait-list if needed).

Where?
Moonshine Park in Upper Hutt.
Parking, bathrooms and water are available on site.

When?
Saturday 31 January 2026.
Player briefing at 8:45am, with round one starting at 9:15am.
Lunch will be one hour from 12pm to 1pm, with round two starting at 1:15pm.
Timings may vary depending on speed of play.

How to enter?
This is a UDisc event. Registration is now open.

If you have a partner, complete the below form and make a team payment of $20 no later than Friday 30th January 2026, 5pm.


If you would like a randomly assigned partner, complete this form and make a payment of $10 no later than Friday 30 January 2026, 5pm. You will be notified of your partner via email by Friday 30 January, 8pm.



Catering?
Thank you to Eve Chin who has offered to provide catering for this event. description:
Fairy Tours, Fairy Tours
Beyond the veils, the Unseen Kingdom waits for the day they can meet you again.

I have seen and connected with these races all of my life. There are many, many races that live beyond the veil of our perception. The Green kingdom beings of the Fae and the Elves, the beings of the twigs and leaves. There are the earth-dwelling races of the dwarves and elementals. The “Unseen Kingdom” banner includes the mer people, dragons and the unicorns. In fact, they gave me the term “the Unseen Kingdom” to describe all of the hundreds of races and beings that humans seem incapable of perceiving.
In this experience, we will meet on the margins of the forest. You are invited to bring whatever you need to be comfortable sitting or lying down. We will be inviting whatever beings of the unseen kingdom who wish to, to come and interact with us.
The experience will unfold as it may. I am expecting that it will involve a meditation, lessons in Unseen Kingdom etiquette, and offerings. In my heart, I know more may come, but every time will be unique.
Please come with a calm heart and a gentle voice.
31st January- 4pm- 7pm
Location to be confirmed with the Unseens. - hopefully they have a spot on the Kapiti Coast. lol

Faultline Ultra, Calling all athletes on foot or bike. National and international competitors are invited to test their endurance at Faultline Ultra. For runners and mountain bikers, it’s a dream come true — the ultimate stamina challenge set against the wildly beautiful Wellington landscape. 
In April 2026, the hills and trails around Wellington offer six possible routes for athletes to push their limits. Beginning with 6-kilometre and 12km tests, the routes grow in length to 25km, 53km, 103km, and a colossal 161-kilometre challenge. You choose the length depending on your ability.

Tournament Rules:
This is a double elimination format tournament. Teams must lose twice to be eliminated. Matches are played according to standard shuffleboard rules as can be read here:
https://www.theshufflehouse.com/.../how-to-play...
EXCEPT:
- There is a 10 MINUTE time limit each match.
- Matches are played FIRST TO TEN.
- In the event of a draw after the 10 minute time limit, a "Golden End" will be played. The winner of the Golden End wins the match.
- Pucks that do not pass the foul line are removed from play.
- The shuffleboard will be reset and resanded after each match.
- No sand will be added during a match.

Grand Opening Lucas Oil Superstock & Super Saloon Series, Grand Opening Lucas Oil Superstock & Super Saloon Series
The days are getting longer and that can only mean one thing - Speedway is about to roar back into life! The 2025/26 season at Robertson Prestige International Speedway thunders back into action on Saturday 25th October at 6:30pm with a HUGE night of entertainment.

The midnight oil is being burned in sheds and workshops all over the country, as competitors and crews race to be ready for the massive summer of speedway action ahead. With new cars and new drivers plus all your favourites, the opening night is going to be huge on the dirt oval at the Robertson Prestige International Speedway.

The familiar roar of Superstocks hitting the dirt is an institution in Palmerston North and a quality field of these fearless drivers are ready to set the tone for the season racing in the Lucas Oil SuperStock Shootout Series! Metal crunching Stockcars never disappoint with plenty of new cars, new paint schemes, and wild designs - these are the backbone of the sport and always are dedicated to putting on a sensational show for the fans!

Spectacular Super Saloons will hit the dirt for the Lucas Oil Super Saloon Shootout Series and put on a thrilling show racing side by side! The return of your favourite Historic Stockcars from yester-year will bring back all the memories of the days gone by. Add in Minisprints and the future of Speedway Youth Ministocks round out what is expected to be a massive, high adrenaline filled opening night of the 2025/26 Speedway Season.

Its double points night, which is an excellent chance for competitors to get some early runs on the board in the Travel Managers Group Season Points Chase. Points are awarded for a top six placing in every non-championship race throughout the season, and overall victory in any of the classes is a major achievement, and a tribute to a driver's consistency throughout the season.

Classes in action are Superstocks, Stockcars, Super Saloons, Minisprints, Historic Stockcars, and Youth Ministocks – PN Registered Cars only.

Drivers, please follow the below link to register your intention to compete at the Opening night of the 2025/26 season. Please note Youth Ministocks are only open to Palmerston North Speedway registered competitors only.

description:
Greater Wellington Centurion - 2026, Summer is here and that means it is birdie season for Greater Wellington Disc Golf! As such, the club is once again organizing Centurion on Wellington Anniversary.
What is "Centurion"?
It's a social event where teams known as "Car-horts" complete over 100 holes across the Greater Wellington region trying to collect as many birdies as possible. "Car-horts" consist of 2-4 players (or as many as you can fit in your car). Bragging rights are awarded for best individual birdie performance, best total Car-Hort birdie performance, and overall score.
*Can anyone beat Johnny Wake's 58 birdie/2 ace performance?
**Yes, aces/eagles count as 2 birdies!
***Who will hit double digits underpar?
Where is it?
This year, the 108 Holes will be played at Harcourt Park, Hikoikoi Reserve, Poole Crescent Reserve (Wainuiomata), and the Berhampore Hills.
- Holes 1 to 36 are at Harcourt Park (2x Short/"Main Tees")
- Holes 37 to 54 at Poole Crescent Reserve (2x "Main Tees")
- Holes 55 to 72 are at Hikoikoi Reserve (2x "Main Tees")
- Holes 73 to 108 are at Berhampore Hills (2x "Black Tees")
Car-Horts may complete the event in any sequence they wish, but must score the round on UDisc using the hole allocations above.
All disc golfers are welcome to compete, so if you're interested/plan on competing, please post in the event discussion who's in your Car-Hort, as well as your Car-Hort name.
Don't have a Car-hort? No worries! Make a post about seeking a Car-Hort, or reach out to Brady Kuech who is organizing the event.
For those posting on social media (Instagram, Facebook, and Stories), tag @greaterwellingtondiscgolf and #gwcenturion to be featured on our socials. We'd love to share all the action throughout the day.
So charge your phone. Pack a lunch. Slather on your suncream, and nab them birdies!
label: Sports & Fitness

description:
Greg Rust: Life in the Fast Lane – Stories from Behind the Microphone, Greg Rust: Life in the Fast Lane – Stories from Behind the Microphone
What happens when you're standing trackside as the world's fastest drivers hurtle past at 300 kilometres an hour?

Or when you're interviewing champions moments after victory, heartbreak or controversy?

Most of us only see the finished broadcast.

The highlights.

The interviews.

The polished moments on screen.

But behind every major sporting event are extraordinary stories, fascinating personalities and split-second moments that rarely make it into the final broadcast.

Join renowned motorsport broadcaster and storyteller Greg "Rusty" Rust for a lively and entertaining Learning Lunch packed with behind-the-scenes stories from a remarkable career spent at the heart of international sport and media.

From Formula One and MotoGP to Bathurst, the Winter Olympics and the Commonwealth Games, Greg has spent decades meeting extraordinary people and witnessing history unfold from the best seat in the house.

But this isn't just a conversation about motorsport.

It's about curiosity, human performance, great storytelling and what we learn when we spend time with people pursuing excellence at the highest level.

Expect humour, fascinating stories, unexpected insights and plenty of memorable moments from life behind the microphone.

Meet Greg 🎤

Greg "Rusty" Rust is one of Australia and New Zealand's best-known motorsport broadcasters, presenters and commentators. Over a career spanning almost 30 years, he has covered Formula One, MotoGP, Supercars, World Rally, the Winter Olympics, Commonwealth Games and major sporting events around the world. Based in Hawke's Bay, Greg is also the host of the award-winning Rusty's Garage podcast.

What We'll Explore
• Behind-the-scenes stories from major sporting events
• What really happens when the cameras are rolling
• Conversations with drivers, riders and champions
• The art of storytelling, interviewing and staying curious
• Lessons from a lifetime spent around remarkable people

Wellington gets to celebrate with them when they visit in July. The team will take over TSB Arena and again revel in 100 years of thrills, laughs, and sheer basketball joy. If you aren’t already a fan, then sit back and watch their combined athleticism, sense of theatre, and comedy play out on the court. The gravity-defying dunks and dexterous tricks will have you roaring for more. 
The team has travelled the world visiting more than 120 countries and territories. Their 26,000 exhibition games continue to win new fans wherever they go. From the epic pre-game magic to unforgettable post-game interactions — come and experience their most legendary tour yet.

description:
Hutt River Trail, Wellington, Distances: 7km , 9.5km , 14km
Tucked alongside the Hutt River and winding its way through the heart of Upper Hutt, this trail offers a beautiful mix of riverside serenity and lush greenery. The course follows the river’s edge, weaving past native bush, open parkland, and peaceful swimming spots, with the crystal-clear water never far from view. Keep an eye out for local birdlife as you cross small bridges and enjoy the changing scenery, from shaded forested sections to wide open spaces framed by the surrounding hills. Easily accessible yet rich in natural beauty, this trail is a favourite for both locals and visitors seeking a refreshing riverside escape.
More info: https://kiwiwalkrun.co.nz/event/hutt-river-trail-wellington/

description:
Inter-Club Football Match: 30th Anniversary of the Aldo Cuccurullo Memorial Trophy, This year marks the 30th anniversary of the annual football game between Club Garibaldi (Wellington) and Club Italia (Nelson).
We would like to invite past and present players to be a part of this event.
Please save the date. Details to follow in due course, including the time and location of the game and the after match function.
***
Aldo Cuccurullo Memorial Trophy
Each year Club Garibaldi of Wellington and Club Italia of Nelson interact through a soccer game between representatives of the two clubs.
The game is in memory of Aldo Cuccurullo, a young member of Club Italia who tragically died at a very young age.
Aldo was known as a gentle giant who gave of his time not only to play rugby league himself, but also to coach children.
The game, as you would expect of Italian football, is a tense one. Member supporters of each club travel to be at the game but the weekend is as much an opportunity to socialise and build friendships as it is to play football.

description:
James Marsh Memorial, Join us for the annual James Marsh Memorial Game, a Kāpiti Coast Softball Club tradition.
This special event honours the memory of James Marsh, who was a cherished member of our softball family, alongside his family and father Tom.
The day is more than a game, it's a time to come together, celebrate James’s life, and remind ourselves of the strength and unity in our community. It also highlights the importance of looking out for one another and supporting mental health awareness.
Game plan:
11.00: U17 invitational game
1.00: Game, open to all skill levels—come play or cheer from the sidelines. We will put you in teams on the day.
1.00-2.00: Shared Kai, bring a plate if you can.
Let’s honor James’s legacy and continue the conversation about mental health, ensuring that no one feels alone.
This event is for everyone—friends, family, and community members. Whether you’re part of the softball world or simply want to show support, we’d love to see you there.
For more information, please contact us at info@kapitisoftball.co.nz

description:
Kāpiti Run for Youth 2026, Kāpiti Run for Youth 2026
We’ve checked the tide timetable – Anchor your calendar now to take part in the 2026 Web Genius Kāpiti Run for Youth on Sunday 29 March 2026 – Raising funds for rangatahi in Kāpiti since 2011 while having fun strolling or running along the beautiful Kāpiti coastline. Kāpiti Run for Youth is a lively, family-friendly event focused on fostering community spirit and supporting organisations that encourage and uplift local young people. RAIN or SHINE, get ready to have fun!

We know Kāpiti Run for Youth helps to support amazing community work done by local fundraising partners. We have 13 incredible fundraising partners you can choose to support and raise funds for. We are very proud of them all and the work they do to uplift the youth of Kāpiti. Each partner brings something unique to the table, from providing essential resources and mentorship to creating spaces where young people can thrive. By supporting rangatahi through education, creativity, employment, and well-being initiatives, they ensure our youth are not just supported but empowered to reach their full potential. Our partners are creating a brighter tomorrow for the young people of Kāpiti!

In the beginning Kāpiti Run for Youth was created by Web Genius as their way as a local business to ‘give back’ to the community so, more than a decade on we can proudly say the event is sustainable and is popular with all sorts, young and old, the fit and not so fit. Kāpiti Run for Youth has raised $280,003 for rangatahi since inception in 2011. In 2025 the event raised $25,531 which was remarkable.

Kāpiti Run for Youth will be open for sign up early in January 2026 >> https://www.kapitirunforyouth.co.nz/signup

At that time, we will be seeking individuals and teams to get together to walk or run from Paraparaumu Beach (Maclean Park) to Raumati Beach and back. For those choosing the 12km walk or run, they will do two circuits of the course.

Choose your adventure – a 6km or 12km run or walk along the beautiful Kāpiti coastline. Whether it's a leisurely stroll or a mad dash to be the first across the finish, you choose the event that suits you best, and which of our amazing fundraising partners you're going to raise funds for. On race day grab your dog and your mates and head down to the beach for fun, family and fitness. Registration takes place from 8.30am to 9.45am with a briefing at 9.45am and all walkers and runners starting together at 10am.

Once your profile is set-up online, let your family, friends and work mates know so they can sponsor your efforts. We encourage every participant to raise $20 through sponsorship instead of paying an entry fee. All entrants receive regular campaigns to motivate their sponsorship efforts along the way.

Kāpiti Run for Youth prides itself on being a sustainable, family-friendly event that is all about supporting each other and having fun. Join your community for a feel-good morning on the beach. Your fundraising makes a difference in the lives of our young people! BYO sunhat, sunscreen, and water on the day, and there are sponsored spot prizes, treats for the kids, certificates for participating and free Paekākāriki Mini Pops for everyone at the end.

Checkout our FAQs over on our website >> https://www.kapitirunforyouth.co.nz/faqs

Closer to the event, go to our website to sign up or sponsor someone that you know who is participating >>
https://www.kapitirunforyouth.co.nz/search

All registrations and sponsorship are handled securely and confidentially on the Kāpiti Run for Youth website that is powered by Raisley and supported by Stripe online payments.

---------------------------------------------

BUSINESS SPONSORSHIP
Platinum $1,000+, Gold $500, Silver $250, Bronze $125 is available for businesses who want to support the underlying work of this event and rangatahi youth of Kāpiti. In 2025 we were grateful to 58 local business sponsors to the value of $15,125 that can be viewed on our website >> https://www.kapitirunforyouth.co.nz/sponsors

Sponsorship for the 2026 campaign will open late in January 2026

---------------------------------------------

FUNDRAISING MODEL
We focus on returning as much money as we can back to the Kāpiti community to those working with rangatahi. All funds raised are split 70% to the official Fundraising Partner chosen by the participant at the time of registration and 30% is retained towards running and promotion of the event.

FUNDRAISING PARTNERS
Birthright Kāpiti, Challenge for Change Kāpiti, Kāpiti Basketball Association, Kāpiti College, Kāpiti Kindness Trust, Kāpiti Youth Support, No 49 Squadron Air Cadets Kāpiti, Ōtaki College, Paraparaumu College, The Shed Project Kāpiti, Whirlwind Kāpiti, Work Ready Kāpiti, ZEAL Kāpiti >>
https://www.kapitirunforyouth.co.nz/fundraising-partners

---------------------------------------------

WELLNESS UPDATE
We operate within the Event Sector Voluntary Code. Please don’t attend if you are feeling unwell.

REGISTRATION DISCLAIMER
Kāpiti Run for Youth carries comprehensive Public Liability event insurance for a period of 48 hours that includes set-up, pack-down and during the event. We maintain an Accident & Incident Register at the Registration Gazebo and local GP, Paraparaumu Medical Centre, handle any medical emergency on the day of the event. We dial 111 if there is an incident beyond their resources.

We remind participants to take self-responsibility and those they are with when on the beach course and to alert officials as needed. It is important to listen to all instructions given on the day of the event at the pre-course briefing, and to report any incidents however minor they may seem. To report an incident, dial 027 244 9585.

PHOTOGRAPHY DISCLAIMER
Kāpiti Run for Youth reserves the right to use any image captured by our official photographer for promotional purposes in any media, in perpetuity without compensation, unless not consented.

---------------------------------------------

IN-KIND EVENT SPONSORS
24/7 Fitness, Beach FM, Captured By Friday Photography, Coffee to Die For, Kāpiti Business Projects, Kāpiti Chocolate Factory, Kāpiti Law, Kāpiti Party Hire, NZME, Paekākāriki Pops, Peter Jackson Plumbing, R-Line, Shoe Clinic, SignCraft Kāpiti, Speedy Signs Kāpiti-Porirua, Wellington Water Filters & Kāpiti Pure Water and Founder, Web Genius.

description:
Looking for a New Sport? Try Ultimate Frisbee, Looking for something active and social to try on a Thursday night?

Come along to our free beginner Ultimate Frisbee taster sessions at Ākau Tangi Recreation Centre. These relaxed games are designed for people who have never played before or want a casual introduction to the sport.

Ultimate frisbee is a fun, fast-moving team sport played with a flying disc. It is easy to pick up, very social, and a great way to meet new people while getting some exercise.

Each Thursday night is a stand-alone session, so you can drop in whenever it suits you. You do not need to have attended earlier weeks, and there is no commitment to come every week.
These sessions focus on beginners and newer players, with guidance available to help people learn the basics, build confidence, and enjoy their first games.

Most people who attend are in their 20s and 30s, but anyone curious to try ultimate frisbee is welcome.

Bring a friend, try something new, and see why so many people love ultimate.

Event Details
What: Beginner Ultimate Frisbee “Taster” Sessions
When: Thursdays, 7:00pm
Dates: 16 April – 18 June
Where: Court 1, Ākau Tangi Recreation Centre, Kilbirnie, Wellington
Cost: Free
Who: Beginners and anyone curious about trying ultimate frisbee
What to bring: Comfortable sports clothes and running shoes

No experience needed. Just show up and join in.

This game is for people over the age of 18, all genders, all abilities.
$6.50 towards court hire. Drink bottles are a must as are cool, comfortable clothing at this time of the year.
Come as an individual, a couple, or a group.

description:
MX-5 Rally, MX-5 Rally
MX-5 Rally - Sunday 15th Feb

Please note that this is a rally, and not a race. So, you need to follow provided instructions, and answer questions along the way correctly to win a prize. There is no prize for being the fastest. This rally has been organized for the Kapiti chapter of the MX-5 Club of NZ, but any other MX-5 drivers are welcome. Details below:

We will be meeting at the same place as last time - the Park 'n' Ride carpark at Manor Park, Lower Hutt, at 9am. Don't worry - we'll be doing completely different roads this time!

There is no breakfast at the start, but if people are interested, we could informally meet at Town & Country in Stokes Valley for breakfast beforehand,then all drive to the Park 'n' Ride together in convoy.

You will need to bring a pen or pencil, and something to press on, such as a clipboard, or a hardcover book. You will also need something you can take evidence photos with - a cellphone or digital camera will be fine.

I also highly, highly recommend that you bring a co-driver, as it will make things infinitely easier for you. Call Russell on 021 0269 3224 if you have trouble finding a co-driver, as I can assist with that!

Like last time, there will be prizes for 1st, 2nd & 3rd, but the prizes are based on who gets the most answers correct, and NOT on who is fastest to complete the course.

Lunch will be at the end point, so bring some $$$ with you.

Snacks will again be provided along the way. This event is free for members of The Kapiti Chapter of the MX-5 Club of NZ, or $2 per car for non-members of that club. This will cover the cost of the provided snacks, plus the photocopying. Thanks.

Further instructions on the day, but if you attended the last rally I organised, then you'll know what to expect. You'll need about 1/2 a tank of gas.

Please RSVP to Russell by texting 021 0269 3224 by Friday 13 Feb, so I can ensure that there are enough printed instructions for everyone.

ONLINE PRICES

Trails Wellington/WMTBC Members – $35

Under 13s – $25
The WMTBC has a reciprocal arrangement with the MMBC and PNP allowing discounted entry to this race if you are a member. Contact your club administration for the entry code.

INCLEMENT WEATHER

Refunds & Cancellation Policy

In the event that you are no longer able to attend (and notify us by Friday the 29th by 9am) or the event is cancelled due to bad weather or unforeseen circumstances—we are unable to provide refunds, so instead we will credit your WMTBC account. You can use the credit to pay for future events, WMTBC membership or as a donation to Wellington trails.

I am personally responsible for ensuring my bike is securely on the shuttle transport (if part of this event) and will not hold the Wellington Mountain Bike Club Inc liable to any damage.

If you need to stop on a trail, pull to the side and ensure both you and your bike are well off the trail.

You may injure yourself or come across an injured rider, if it is serious, someone should remain stationary with the injured rider and then the next rider must notify a marshal as soon as possible.

I agree to abide by all rules set out by the Wellington Mountain bike Club Inc.

I agree to a fee of $100 in the event that the race timing token allocated to me is not returned to WMTBC at the end of the event.

Ebiker's are permitted to use one bike and one battery per entrant, smaller capacity batteries are allowed an extender.

description:
Manawatu Saloon Champs + Sidecar Best Pairs, Manawatu Saloon Champs + Sidecar Best Pairs
Speedway action this Saturday night at the Robertson Prestige International Speedway where the Manawatu Saloon Championship is decided along with the exhilarating side-by-side Sidecar racing action for the AFC Motorcycles Sidecar Best Pairs. Saturday night will also see the return of V8 Modifieds racing wheel to wheel around the Robertson Prestige International Speedway. Fantastic SuperStocks, metal crunching Stockcars and eye-catching Minisprints add to a massive night of entertainment.

A quality field of drivers is expected for the sought after Manawatu Saloon Championship adding to a packed show at the Robertson Prestige International Speedway in the form of Corvettes, Camaros and Mustangs racing wheel-to-wheel. The wide tyres and thundering V8 engines add another style of speedway racing which is proving popular not only with drivers but the spectators alike. The Saloon racing this season has been competitive at the Robertson Prestige International Speedway with local drivers including 7p Clayton More, 57p Calvin Honore, 81p Jonathan Mason, and 242p Ashleigh King all looking to be in contention for the title.

Adding to the exciting programme is the AFC Motorcycles Sidecar Best Pairs which will see some of the country’s best sidecar combinations pair up and battle it out. With 14 combinations confirmed including 5p Wingnut & Sam McNaught, 8p Rob Miller & Jaxon Hannan, 17p Tony Hislop & Aidan Foothead, recent Ray Tarrant Sidecar Memorial winners 27b Craig Boaler & Kayla Meehan all included in the sensational field. The Robertson Prestige International Speedway has seen some spectacular Sidecar racing and this best pair championship is set to deliver this high calibre of entertainment for the fans once again!

With the return of the V8 Modifieds to the Robertson Prestige International Speedway, expect a high calibre of side-by-side racing from these v8 powered race cars with replica fiberglass car bodies and big wings! Drivers including Newton Gordge from Taranaki, Cody Hata from Auckland, 28w Ricky Dykstra and 9e Sheldon Arapere have indicated that they will be in attendance for this momentous return of Modified racing to the Robertson Prestige International Speedway.

Adding to the packed programme this Saturday night, the Superstocks will hit the track with grit, steel, and determination to be at the front of the pack. Metal crunching Stockcars will be battling it out for the chequered flag as well. Both classes race Side-by-side and bumper-to-bumper, these drivers in both classes mean business, with their fearless attitude and willingness to put on a show its anyone’s guess who will carry the chequered flag at the end of the race! Rounding out what is set to be a massive night the Minisprints make their return ahead of their Oval Superstars Tour first round the following weekend.

Classes in action are SuperStocks, Stockcars, Saloons, Sidecars, Modifieds, Minisprints

Drivers, please follow the below link to register your intention to race on the 22nd November
https://www.pnspeedway.co.nz/forms/22-11-2025

Please Note: Entries in other classes will determine whether Youth Ministocks are added to the programme later in the week.

Admission prices are $30 for an Adult (16 years and over), $10 for Children aged 8-15, and $70 for a Family pass of 2 adults and up to four children. Kids aged 7 and under are FREE.

Tickets are available to pre-purchase online from www.eventfinda.co.nz , (tickets purchased incur an additional service fee) or on race day from Gate 1 (Waldegrave Street), Gate 2 (Cuba Street - Bridge) and Gate 3 (Cook Street) from 5.30pm.

Racing Starts 6.30pm.

description:
Mills Albert Wellington Saints 2026 Season, The Mills Albert Wellington Saints take to the court for what is sure to be a massive 2026 season. After taking out the 2025 season with a nail-biting win over the Southland Sharks, can they defend their championship title? Kiwi coach Aaron Young takes to the helm again after winning coach of the year. Hutt Valley local Jordan Hunt returns to the team after representing New Zealand in the Tall Blacks, and Melbourne’s Akech Aliir joins the Saints, bringing 6’9” of power and athleticism. 
The 2026 regular season features eleven home games at the TSB Arena. Saints’ fans can expect high-energy basketball and a family-friendly atmosphere. Tip-off times have been optimised to make it easier for young fans to witness their heroes in action. 
Join the game court-side and put your lungs to the test as you cheer on your favourite Wellington side.

description:
Morrisons Bush Camping Weekend & Rally, Morrisons Bush Camping Weekend & Rally
Friday 13th - Sunday 15th Feb
NOTE If you are not a member and want to be part of this epic weekend then click here https://www.jbnz.co.nz/join-jbnz and you are good to go!
Morrison's Bush is a beautiful camping area on the banks of the Ruamahanga River. Central Districts provides Porta loo's, and will cover the cost for those who wish to camp. If your crew doesn't like the idea of camping you can still take part and seek accommodation at nearby Martinborough or Greytown.
When you arrive: Please register before setting up your camp site
Friday 13th: You are welcome to arrive and set up your camp. Scrutineering for Saturdays Rally will be available from 3pm. There will be no shortage of good company and stories that evening.
Saturday 15th: This is Rally Day, with eight family friendly events which will test your boating skills and your ability to bribe the time keepers. Once the boating has finished there will be a lollie scramble for the children, tug of war (for big kids too) and a few games prior to prize giving.
Sunday 16th: There will be a short run up the Ruamahanga river, with most people starting to make their way home from around midday.
Directions: From the southern end of Greytown, drive 6km towards Martinborough. The road takes a sharp right hand bend at the foot of the hills, but don't take the bend. Instead, travel straight ahead up and over the hill on the track (look for the signage). Keep driving towards the river for another 3.5km.
The Rally: All boats must be scrutineered. Those who arrive Friday will be done that evening.
Scrutineering will be from 8am - 9.30am Saturday morning. Please have your boat in the water no later than 10am ready for the briefing.

description:
NPC: Wellington Lions x Hawke's Bay Magpies, NPC: Wellington Lions x Hawke's Bay Magpies
The 2026 NPC season starts here!
Don’t miss the Wellington Lions’ opening clash of the season against our rivals and neighbours, the Hawke's Bay Magpies. Join us for what promises to be a thrilling start to the campaign.

It's Old Timers Day — an opportunity to celebrate the legends who have shaped our game, left a lasting legacy, and made a profound impact on rugby and our wider community.

To honour our Old Timers, we encourage fans to wear their retro or vintage jerseys — whether club, school, or representative and proudly #WearYourHistory.

We will also commemorate the remarkable service of Major William James Hardham VC — Wellington Rugby representative, member of the original Wellington team that won the Ranfurly Shield in 1904, and Victoria Cross recipient. His courage and sacrifice are enduring part of the region's rugby heritage.

We will also recognise the links between Wellington and Hawke's Bay and the Battle of Chunuk Bair, fought on 8 August 1915, one of New Zealand's most significant actions at Gallipoli, where soldiers and former players from both provinces played a pivotal role in one of the defining battles of the campaign.
Be there as we kick off the 2026 campaign and celebrate the people, stories, and traditions that make our game so special.

Pre Game Activations include: William James Hardham, VC Frame Presentation

Be Gold, Be Black, Be There! Grab your tickets today!!!
Wellington. My Home. Our Lions!

description:
New Zealand Cricket: Summer Season, It looks like New Zealand Cricket (NZC) has smashed it for six. The 2026-27 international home season of cricket promises an exciting few months of action across the country. Wellington has scored six major opportunities to see the BLACKCAPS and WHITE FERNS in action. Three formidable opponents are travelling to New Zealand’s shores. The Indian, Bangladeshi, and Sri Lankan teams have booked their tickets for Aotearoa and will play tests, ODIs, and T20 matches against the Kiwi women’s and men’s teams. 
The Indian men’s team will be particularly busy during their visit. With twelve matches booked against the BLACKCAPS, it will be the most internationals scheduled for an Indian men’s tour in NZC history. Fans will get their chance to see them duke it out in all three formats across the capital, beginning with a T20 at Hnry Stadium on 27 October. 
Make sure you don’t miss the WHITE FERNS. They host Bangladesh in Wellington in a T20 and ODI, during their only home tour of the summer. The Wellington schedule finishes with a visit from Sri Lanka for an ODI against the BLACKCAPS on 19 January at the Cello Basin Reserve.   
With games split across Hnry Stadium and Cello Basin Reserve, the city will be bouncing with life. The 2025/26 season saw bumper crowds, and our men's and women's sides are set to build on this exciting momentum.

description:
New Zealand Pinball Championships 2025, Welcome to the New Zealand Pinball Championships 2025!
This is part of a 4 day event - Fri/Sat/Sun/Mon - 16/17/18/19 Jan 2026.
The top 48 performers over 2025 qualify to play in the NZ Champs at Ye Olde Pinball Shoppe in Wellington.
Upstairs from Ye Olde Pinball Shoppe, our good mates at Fork & Brewer have opened up their bar to us for the event. To spread out the large number of players, we will have banks of games located upstairs, this will be a great spot to wind down and enjoy some food and drink.
Saturday 17th:
New Zealand Champs Qualifying - 9am-9:30pm (estimate)
This event is for the top 48 performers over 2025 and has a 150% points boost.
- Doors open 9am, tournament starts at 9:30am
- 7 rounds of 4 player match play
- 3 games per round
- Software will choose a bank of three games from the banks available.
- Player order will automatically rotate each game.
- Top 24 make finals
- Top 8 receive 1 bye
- One hour lunch break
Sunday 18th:
New Zealand Champs Finals - 9am-2pm (estimate)
Top 24 play off, best of 5 matches head to head.
- Top 8 receive one bye.
- Highest seed picks a bank of games and has games 1,3,5.
- Lower seed picks a bank of games, and has games 2 and 3.
- Games in each bank can be played in any order, but not more than once in a 5 game match.
The winner of the NZ National Championship receives qualification to the IFPA World Championship (along with the #1 ranked NZ player as of December 31st). Top 16 place getters will receive prize money, gathered from the $1 IFPA fee you have been paying to play in tournaments over the 2025 year. These amounts will be announced prior to the event.

description:
Official Round the Bays (RTB) Shake Out Run - Wellington, Official Round the Bays (RTB) Shake Out Run - Wellington
Get ready to shake out those legs and join the fun run before the big Round the Bays race in Wellington!

About this Event


Official Round the Bays (RTB) Shake Out Run - Wellington
For the Love of Running 💙
Get ready to loosen up, shake out the legs, and soak up the good vibes before race day with the Official Round the Bays Shake Out Run – Wellington.
Because it’s Valentine’s Day, we’re leaning into the theme For the Love of Running. This one’s about movement, connection, and celebrating why we run in the first place.
We’ll start with an easy, social shake-out run at a relaxed pace. No pressure, no pace expectations. Just a cruisy run to get the body moving and the legs feeling fresh.
After the run, we’ll guide everyone through a short yoga flow designed to help loosen up tight muscles, release any lingering tension, and leave you feeling relaxed and race-ready.
We’ll then head to Aye Empanadas for a post-run coffee, connection, and pre-race chats.
We’ll also have lululemon joining us with a couple of product cards for selected individuals.
What to expect:

Easy, social shake-out run
Short post-run yoga flow to loosen up and reset 
All paces and experience levels welcome
Community vibes and good chats
Post-run coffee at Aye Empanadas
lululemon product cards

Come solo, bring a friend, or bring your race nerves. Leave feeling lighter, looser, and ready for Round the Bays.

description:
PADI Open Water Diver Course, PADI Open Water Diver Course
“Ever Since I Was A Kid I’ve Wanted To Learn To SCUBA Dive…”

PADI is by far the largest and most popular Scuba diver certifying system in the world and for good reason. Courses are fun safe relevant and packed with excitement! No matter what country you are in your PADI qualification will be recognised.

To learn to dive first complete the medical questionnaire to make sure you are medically fit to dive. Next pay your deposit and select your course dates. You will receive your PADI eLearning theory which must be completed before you attend the first practical session. This simple and fun eLearning program will give you the knowledge you need to understand the reason for the skills you will learn.

The practical part of your Open Water Scuba Diver course takes just four days! During the first weekend we make it very easy and convenient for you with our on-site dive pool (the only one in the Wellington Region). Our pool is where you learn to dive so we can go at your pace no matter how long it takes. During the first weekend you learn and practice all the necessary dive skills. Once completed you will be ready for the sea dives.

During the second weekend you complete four sea dives two per day. This is where we confirm and practice the skills you learnt in our pool – all under direct supervision. You will also complete a simple 300m swim (no time limit and wearing wetsuit mask snorkel and fins).

Once you are a certified diver you will receive an eCard on your PADI App showing your qualification – and any PADI Dive Centre will be able to confirm your certification online. You will also be qualified to attend the PADI Advanced Open Water Diver course and our regular Dive Days.
Our aim is to prepare you for the fascinating adventure of diving. We want to make your diving safe and enjoyable. Welcome to the exciting world of Scuba diving!

If you have any questions please call email or stop by our Dive Store.
 

PPADI Open Water Diver course at a glance
Digital theory: Open Water Diver eLearning Course (allow 8-14 hours)
Practical: One weekend pool training one weekend with four sea dives
Options: One-on-one or unscheduled dates – additional costs apply.
Start Time: Be at NZ Sea Adventures by 8.30am each day.

Location
We are located at 9 Marina View Mana Porirua; just north of the Paremata bridge on SH1. Look for the big yellow building. Our Location

Prerequisites
Be at least 10 years old (special conditions apply for 10 and 11-year-olds)
Be able to swim 300m (mask snorkel and fins no time limit) and swim/float for 10 minutes.
Be medically fit to dive. Check the Diver Medical Participant Questionnaire. If you answer YES to any of the questions or have any doubts a visit to your doctor is required.
eLearning must be completed before your pool training can begin.
Complete the Optional RDP Tables Quiz and Exam after the final exam if you don’t have a dive computer.

What to Bring
Completed Diver Medical Participant Questionnaire.

description:
Paekākāriki Escarpment Track, Join us for a walk along the Paekākāriki Escarpment Track. This track is best suited to people with a good level of fitness, as there are steep sections and a couple of swing bridges.
We’ll meet at St Peter’s Hall in Paekākāriki and walk together to the start of the track. The walk takes around 3–4 hours including breaks and is one way only. We’ll return by train from Pukerua Bay. No dogs, sorry.
If it’s too windy, the walk may be postponed, so please check this page for updates.
If you’d like, you’re welcome to bring your togs and a towel for a swim at the beach afterwards.
Please bring:
sunscreen
drinking water
a packed lunch
suitable footwear

description:
Porirua Parkrun, What is Porirua parkrun? It is a free 5km walk or run event - It’s not about coming first or winning. You can go at your own pace and just enjoy being with other people. It is inclusive and the perfect way to start your weekend in the outdoors chatting to people.

The start occurs just upstream of the Bothamley Park carpark. This car park is off Champion street, opposite the intersection with Windley Street. Head to end of carpark where the concrete ends and there is a gate. For location see https://goo.gl/maps/wEohfp9bRu82.

The course is following the old coach road (circa 1870's) established for the early farms in the area. Today this historic track is located within a park, away from cars and now used by walkers, runners and cyclists.

The track is generally 3 metres wide with a gentle gradient and a compacted gravel surface beside the Kenepuru Stream through a picturesque wooded wild valley. (Note there is a pinch point for a short section after the 2km marker where participants need to go single file each direction for approx 30 metres)

The valley runs east-west with mature trees which means this has to be one of the most sheltered places, out of the wind to exercise in Wellington.

What does it cost to join in? Nothing - it's free! but please register before your first run or walk, so you can get your timing results. You only need to register with parkrun once, to participate at any of the parkrun events around the world. Don't forget to bring a copy of your barcode. If you forget it, you won't get a time.

How fast do I have to be? Walking is fine as long as you can finish the 5km. Please come along and join in whatever your pace!

One dog per adult is welcome, as long as it is on a short hand held lead.

Children welcome but those 10 years and under need to be kept within arms reach of a supervising adult.

Note there is no toilets in the park, so go before you go.

We're friendly! Every week we grab a post park run/walk coffee/tea at Get Fixed within Kai Tahi at 20 Parumoana Street, to mix exercise with socialising.

There are volunteering opportunities even week. So those doing Duke of Edinburgh or similar challenges can get volunteer credits. Ensure you contact us well in advance at "porirua@parkrun.co.nz"

description:
RETHINK Fundraising Wellington 2026, INTRODUCING AOTEAROA'S NEWEST FUNDRAISING EVENT: RETHINK
RETHINK Fundraising 2026 invites you and your team to look at your fundraising programme from a fresh perspective.
Join us for a full day of inspirational talks, panel discussions and practical workshops that will leave you energised, AND armed with a toolkit of actionable learnings to take your fundraising to the next level.
Date: Thursday, 5 March
Venue: Mākaro Room, Wharewaka Function Centre
Time: 8am-5pm
Cost: $249NZD (exc GST)*
Contact: Anna Shere anna@changeand.co
*If you prefer to pay via invoice, please email accounts@changeand.co.
THE PROGRAM
For those of you who joined us for RETHINK Auckland 2025, please note that RETHINK Wellington will feature many of the same sessions from that event, with a few additions to the program and two new guest speakers.
Branding blindspots 
In a sector focused on campaigns, conversion, and compliance, brand is often overlooked. But brand isn’t just a logo or a nice story. It’s how people feel about supporting you. And if it's not clear, engaging, or modern – you’re leaving both money and meaning on the table. This presentation from Tim Dove at re:brand will challenge a few norms and show some examples of it being done well. He’ll get you thinking about your organisation and how you can ensure you’re avoiding the ‘brand blindspot’. 
Rethinking charity comms 
When it comes to getting people enthused about our cause, too often we focus on the what rather than the why. Worse, we risk boring our audience to death with earnest, organisation-centric communications which neither inspire nor instruct. Dominique Antarakis from Change&Co will show you a new and fun way to look at your charity comms for maximum engagement and donor retention.  
Workshop 1 
Facilitated workshop which will provide the opportunity to take the learnings from the morning sessions and give you the practical branding and comms tools to take back to your organisation - and transform your fundraising! 
Lunch break  
Take a break, mix and mingle, and enjoy a fabulous lunch selection.
Data, behaviour, and hyper-personalisation 
This presentation from MIMO/DATAM will show you how to transform raw data into meaningful, multi-channel interactions across email, SMS, voice, and direct mail - all from a single platform. This session will challenge how you think about personalisation - it’s not just about names in subject lines or open rates in eDMs, it’s about burning down the old school campaigns and rebuilding around behaviour, context and connection. 
Lessons from the legacy frontlines 
Based on interviews with practitioners from organisations large and small, this session shares unfiltered insights from Gift in Will managers who are doing the work every day—what's actually generating pledges, where they're getting stuck, and what they wish they'd known sooner. Through their collective wisdom, and guided by TEDIREX’s Martin Ruane, we'll explore the biggest challenges facing legacy programs today, the opportunities hiding in plain sight, and tactical takeaways that work for both beginners and experienced practitioners. 
Workshop 2 
Facilitated workshop which will provide the opportunity to take the learnings from the afternoon sessions and give you the practical personalisation and AI tools to ramp up acquisition and retention.  
CFRE ACCREDITATION
Full participation in RETHINK Fundraising is applicable for 7 points in Category 1.B -Education of the CFRE International application for initial certification and/or recertification.
EVENT PARTNERS
Change&Co, DATAM, mimo, re:brand and Tedirex. Special thanks to FIA/FINZ for their support of the day.
RETHINK has been designed by fundraisers for fundraisers, and we’re keen to make sure you get the most out of the day. We promise no hard-sell, no product placement, and a 100% satisfaction guarantee.
The idea is for you to leave at the end of the day with a roadmap to greater donor engagement – and a sense of renewed energy for what lies ahead.

Run Manu Run & Community BBQ, Run Manu Run & Community BBQ
Invite to the 5th Annual Run Manu Run and Community BBQ

Hi all. Run Manu Run this year will be (weather permitting) on Saturday 6th December. Starting/finishing at 74 Hill Rd with community BBQ to follow.

Run Manu Run is a unique group adventure run (everyone stays together during the event). The course takes in the 3 most famous Pareraho swimming holes: the taniwha pool, the Mighty Kelson Waterfall, and the Hill Road swimming hole, as well as some of the quirky Pareraho trails and the charming Crikey Canyon.

The event involves repeated full immersion and some slippery scrambling on slimy stones, but has been successfully conquered by staunch nine year olds with their parents, or other designated adults. The event takes approximately 2 1/2 hours.The run finishes down a slip in slide at 74 Hill Road.

The Community BBQ/potluck starts as Run Manu Run finishes and continues into the evening. All welcome! Bring a plate/contribution if you can. BYO beverages.

Run Manu Run start: 2pm (please arrive 15min before)
Community BBQ start: 4pm

This is the final Round of a 3 Round Rubber Duck Series and is a WMSA Kim Naylor Round!
Online entries via Motorsport NZ and are open!
If you don't have a Motorsport NZ Login, get in touch and we'll be happy to help you out, nearer the event time we will upload a form you can fill out.
Treaded tyres only, so semi slicks are okay. No full slicks!
Helmet and overalls requirements haven't changed for events of this level. Just make sure you're wearing cotton or wool under it, and leather shoes please.
To avoid any refuelling rule headaches we suggest you bring your car with enough fuel already in it. There is a few choices of petrol stations close by in Masterton.
No competition licence required.
Car club membership required unless this is one of your first two events ever.
Please follow official guidance when travelling over the drag strip, and do so at low speed and maximum care when entering the track.
The pits are our usual spot on the grass. We are not to use the concrete pads.
$60 entry plus to possibility of some lunch provided. Will confirm nearer the day.

description:

Shuffleboard pairs tournaments are 6pm to 9.30pm at the latest (usually earlier), the last Wednesday of each month.
Check out the league over at Challonge.com
https://challonge.com/communities/meanshuffle
Tournament Rules:
This is a double elimination format tournament. Teams must lose twice to be eliminated. Matches are played according to standard shuffleboard rules as can be read here:
https://www.theshufflehouse.com/.../how-to-play...
EXCEPT:
- There is a 10 MINUTE time limit each match.
- Matches are played FIRST TO TEN.
- In the event of a draw after the 10 minute time limit, a "Golden End" will be played. The winner of the Golden End wins the match.
- Pucks that do not pass the foul line are removed from play.
- The shuffleboard will be reset and resanded after each match.
- No sand will be added during a match.
- The final match is played first to 15 with no time limit - if time allows.
- Every "Hanger" is rewarded with a sweet treat!
PRIZES
1st place: $60 of Taproom Vouchers + 1st place ribbon + Your team name immortalised on the honours board
2nd place: $40 of Taproom Vouchers + 2nd place ribbon

description:
Shea McAleese: The Evolution of a Four-Time Olympian, Shea McAleese: The Evolution of a Four-Time Olympian
What does it take to perform on the world's biggest stage?

And perhaps more importantly, what happens when the cheering stops, the jersey comes off, and it's time to reinvent yourself all over again?

Join four-time Olympian and New Zealand hockey legend Shea McAleese for an inspiring Learning Lunch exploring the highs, challenges and lessons of a life spent pursuing excellence.

From a young Hawke's Bay athlete with a dream to representing New Zealand at four Olympic Games and four Commonwealth Games, Shea's journey offers a fascinating insight into commitment, resilience and what it really takes to perform at an elite level.

But this isn't simply a story about sport.

It's about leadership, teamwork, personal growth and learning how to evolve through different chapters of life.

Today, Shea works as an international coach and leadership mentor, helping individuals and teams perform at their best. Drawing on lessons from elite sport, he shares a practical and human perspective on building trust, developing culture and creating environments where people thrive.

Expect honest stories, valuable insights and a fascinating look behind the scenes of life as an Olympian, coach and leader.

Meet Shea 🎤

Shea McAleese is one of New Zealand's most celebrated hockey players and a proud son of Hawke's Bay. Over a 16-year international career he represented the Black Sticks 320 times, competing at four Olympic Games and four Commonwealth Games. Since retiring from international hockey, he has transitioned into international coaching and leadership development, working with elite teams and building a global following through his coaching platform, Inside Hockey.

What We'll Explore
• The realities of competing at four Olympic Games
• Lessons from elite sport that apply to everyday life
• Leadership, trust and building high-performing teams
• The transition from athlete to coach
• Resilience, growth and adapting through life's different chapters

🕙 Time: 11:00am – 1:30pm
☕ Refreshments: Lunch included

description:
Steps To Success - The recipe to competing at your best, Steps To Success is a seminar, helping you become the best athlete possible. No matter your level, weather you are a beginner, an amatuer or a pro, this workshop has the recipe to start competing at your best. You don't even have to be competing! You could just want to do better.
What:
This seminar is a fundraiser to get the Rocking Robins Top team to Nationals this year in Rotorua.
When: August 29th 2025 6pm
Where: Tawa Fitness Portal
Cost: $25 Per ticket
Purchase your ticket here: https://docs.google.com/.../1FAIpQLSfMyBy9iQsriz.../viewform
Bonus: Each ticket comes with a $5 voucher to the Fitness Portal Cafe.
Sausage Sizzle: There will be a sausage running during the sausage sizzle so you won't go hungry.
Please make payment into the following account:
Account Name: Rocking Robins Rock N Roll Club
Account #: 06-0773-0877111-00
Particulars: STS
Reference: First + Last Name

What is this event?
Rotate through each 20–30 min session (with 5-min breaks between):
1. Mindset & Visualization – Mental prep and performance focus with Jordan
2. Injury Prevention - Progressive load and how to avoid injury with Devin Glover
3. Fuel your body right - Talking fueling and supplements thanks to Scorpion Supplements with Rebekah Glover and Liz Monrad
BBQ will be running on the night so be sure to bring your loose coins!!
Proceeds from this event go towards helping the Rocking Robins top team get to national in October!!
Meet your hosts:
Jordan Shearer: Coach. Trainer. Space-holder for rebels, dreamers, and high end performers.
Jordan is the founder of Being You, a coaching practice grounded in authenticity, connection, courage, simplicity, and going rogue. She blends her background in mental health, life coaching, and human behavior with no-fluff, deeply human approach to performance. Having competed herself, Jordan understands the pressure that comes with stepping out, showing up, and giving your best when it counts. Jordan has coached competitive gymnasts, doctors, dancers, and first responders (to name a few) - people who need to stay mentally strong in high-performance spaces.
Devin Glover: Owner and Founder of The Fitness Portal Limited. Devin has been a personal trainer for 10+ years, and has competed either Nationally or Internationally in the following sports: Underwater Hockey, Olympic Weightlifting, Rock N Roll Dancing, CrossFit, Swimming and has dabbled in endurance sports like Ironman and Road cycling.
Rebekah Glover: Rebekah has gone through a huge lifestyle transformation. After losing over 30kgs and keeping it off, she became a Weight Watchers coach, then she started personal training in 2021. Rebekah has learnt through trial and error, about how important it is to fuel correctly to achieve your goals and that it isn't always about weight loss. If you you want to perform you need to fuel correctly. She is now an avid runner and competes Nationally in Rock n Roll Dancing, after only three years of dancing she holds one national title, and two regional titles.
