description:
Stockcar Teams Invasion, Stockcar Teams Invasion
Last week saw SuperStock Teams Racing return, this week it’s time for the Metal Crunching Stockcar Teams Racing to take to the track at the Robertson Prestige International Speedway for the Machinery Specialists Stockcar Teams Invasion! One of the best Stockcar Teams Racing nights this season on the calendar with many drivers looking to solidify their places in their home track teams in preparation for the New Zealand Stockcar Teams event at Rotorua in March.

The Stockcar Teams Invasion will see teams from around the North Island descend on Robertson Prestige International Speedway for one night of metal crunching, stockcar teams racing. Racing for pride of their region with grit and determination, it will be all left on the track so expect plenty of action from the drop of the flag!

Making their way to battle it out are the Waikato Raiders, Gisborne Gladiators, Whanganui Vulcans, Wellington Young Guns, and the local hero Stockcar teams Palmerston North Pumas & Palmerston North Colts it is a massive line-up of Stockcar Teams ready to battle!

Add in Consolation Stockcar races for the Stockcar drivers who are not competing in the Teams event, Saloons, and the dare devil Sidecars plus the future of speedway Youth Ministocks – PN Registered Cars only, you couldn’t ask for a better night of spectacular speedway entertainment!

Please Note: No SuperStocks this weekend.

Classes in action are Stockcar Teams Racing, Consolation Stockcars (non-team), Saloons, Sidecars, Youth Ministocks – PN Registered Cars only.

Drivers, please follow the below link to register your intention to race on the 13th of December 2025:

https://www.pnspeedway.co.nz/forms/13-12-2025

Admission prices are $30 for an Adult (16 years and over), $10 for Children aged 8-15, and $70 for a Family pass of 2 adults and up to four children. Kids aged 7 and under are FREE.

Tickets are available to pre-purchase online from https://www.eventfinda.co.nz, (tickets purchased incur an additional service fee) or on race day from Gate 1 (Waldegrave Street), Gate 2 (Cuba Street - Bridge) and Gate 3 (Cook Street) from 4:30pm.

Racing starts 6pm.

description:
Superstock Teams Extravaganza, Superstock Teams Extravaganza
SuperStock Teams Racing makes a return to the Robertson Prestige International Speedway on Saturday 6th December with an earlier start time of 6pm, on a night which will have something on the programme for everyone. Palmerston North Panthers, Manawatu Mustangs, Gisborne Giants, Stratford Scrappers and Wanganui Warriors will all take to the track in a round robin of SuperStock Teams Races. Add to the programme Stockcars, Sidecars and Non-Teams consolation SuperStock races, and it’s going to be one epic night at the Home of SuperStock Teams Racing!

The SuperStock teams are all eager to get another chance to refine their skill in anticipation of the 2026 ENZED SuperStock Teams Championship event in February. With all teams featuring new drivers to their squads, it’s certainly going to be entertaining teams racing on Saturday Night. The local Palmerston North Panthers and Manawatu Mustangs teams will have plenty of anticipation from the fans to start their teams racing season off successfully, but formidable competition from the Gisborne Giants and Wanganui Warriors will look to place a halt on these plans and have something to prove. Fresh from the recent Huntly SuperStock Teams racing event, the Stratford Scrappers will be looking to further advance their skills with another great chance to team’s race in the lead up to the main event of the ENZED SuperStock Teams Championship in February. With new drivers and team pride on the line, it will be an entertaining night at the Robertson Prestige International Speedway.

To add to what is going to be a spectacular Superstock night at the Robertson Prestige International Speedway, for non-team SuperStock drivers there will be Consolation races included in the programme, along with the metal crunching Stockcars battling it out on track - these drivers love to put on the action for their fans, plus the daredevil Sidecars will be back out on the track. What a night it is going to be!

Classes in action are SuperStock Teams Racing, Consolation SuperStocks (non-team), Stockcars, Sidecars

Drivers, please follow the below link to register your intention to race on the 6th of December 2025:
https://www.pnspeedway.co.nz/forms/06-12-2025

Admission prices are $30 for an Adult (16 years and over), $10 for Children aged 8-15, and $70 for a Family pass of 2 adults and up to four children. Kids aged 7 and under are FREE.

description:
The Web Genius Kāpiti Run for Youth 2026, We’ve checked the tide timetable – Anchor your calendar now to take part in the 2026 Web Genius Kāpiti Run for Youth on Sunday 29 March 2026 – Raising funds for rangatahi in Kāpiti since 2011 while having fun strolling or running the beautiful Kāpiti coastline. We are a lively, family-friendly event focused on fostering community spirit and supporting organisations that encourage and uplift local young people. RAIN or SHINE, get ready to have fun!

We know Kāpiti Run for Youth helps to support amazing community work done by local fundraising partners. We have 13 incredible fundraising partners you can choose to support and raise funds for. We are very proud of them all and the work they do to uplift the youth of Kāpiti. Each partner brings something unique to the table, from providing essential resources and mentorship to creating spaces where young people can thrive. By supporting rangatahi through education, creativity, employment, and well-being initiatives, they ensure our youth are not just supported but empowered to reach their full potential. Our partners are creating a brighter tomorrow for the young people of Kāpiti!

Sign up opens early Jan 2026 - Individuals & teams walk or run from Paraparaumu Beach (Maclean Park) to Raumati Beach and back. For those choosing the 12km walk or run, they do two circuits. Choose your adventure – 6km or 12km run or walk. Whether it's a leisurely stroll or a mad dash to be the first across the finish, choose the event that suits you best, and which of our amazing fundraising partners you're going to raise funds for. On race day grab your dog & your mates and head down to the beach for fun, family & fitness. Registration 8.30am to 9.45am, briefing at 9.45am and all walkers & runners starting together at 10am.

Once your profile is set-up online, let your family, friends & work mates know so they can sponsor your efforts. We encourage every participant to raise $20 through sponsorship instead of paying an entry fee. All entrants receive regular campaigns to motivate their efforts. Join your community for a feel-good morning on the beach. Your fundraising makes a difference in the lives of our young people! BYO sunhat, sunscreen, and water on the day. Sponsored spot prizes, treats for kids, certificates for participating & free Paekākāriki Mini Pops for everyone.

Business Sponsorship
Platinum $1,000+, Gold $500, Silver $250, Bronze $125 is available for businesses who want to support the underlying work of this event and rangatahi youth of Kāpiti. In 2025 we were grateful to 58 local business sponsors for $15,125 that can be viewed on our website. Sponsorship for the 2026 campaign will open late January 2026.

Fundraising Model
We focus on returning as much money as we can back to the Kāpiti community to those working with rangatahi. All funds raised are split 70% to the official Fundraising Partner chosen by the participant at the time of registration and 30% is retained towards running and promotion of the event.

Fundraising Partners
Birthright Kāpiti, Challenge for Change Kāpiti, Kāpiti Basketball Association, Kāpiti College, Kāpiti Kindness Trust, Kāpiti Youth Support, No 49 Squadron Air Cadets Kāpiti, Ōtaki College, Paraparaumu College, The Shed Project Kāpiti, Whirlwind Kāpiti, Work Ready Kāpiti, Zeal Kāpiti.

In-kind Event Sponsors
24/7 Fitness, Beach FM, Captured by Friday Photography, Coffee to Die For, Kāpiti Business Projects, Kāpiti Chocolate Factory, Kāpiti Law, Kāpiti Party Hire, NZME, Paekākāriki Pops, Peter Jackson Plumbing, R-line, Shoe Clinic, Signcraft Kāpiti, Speedy Signs Kāpiti-Porirua, Wellington Water Filters & Kāpiti Pure Water and Founder, Web Genius.

Kāpiti Run for Youth reserves the right to use any image captured by our official photographer for promotional purposes in any media, in perpetuity without compensation, unless not consented.

7am - Marathon

Website: tiptrackmarathon.co.nz
Rego: https://tip-track-marathon.lilregie.com/boo.../attendees/new
COURSE DETAILS:
Tip Track Marathon (TTM) –
Tip Track Marathon is an out-and-back, out-and-back, out-and-back, out-and-back, out-and-back, out-and-back type course that has proven popular with participants. Each of the six laps is slightly over 7km, with around 400m in elevation (2500m in total). Try not to trip on a loose rock while taking in the aromatic smells emanating from the tip. Ignore the gale-force northerly. It makes for a challenging marathon but you can find comfort in the other runners suffering too.
Recommended donation: $40
Half Marathon -
For those that hate themselves but not as much as the marathoners. Same course as above but three laps instead of six,
Recommended donation: $25
Tip Track Marathon (TTM) is a low-key, no frills trail running race that takes place at the Tip Track in Wellington each year - all in the name of charity. TTM is all about hard hills, high-fives, and doing something stupid for the sake of it. There are no prizes. Your workmates will not understand why you did this. It’s not even that fun.
This is a race for those that want a little more from life than the ordinary. Those that question the monotony of their daytime jobs and wonder, "isn't there meant to be more to life than this?" Enter TTM... I mean, you won't find any answers here but those are the people that tend to be attracted to it.
DONATIONS:
All entry fees charged go to our charities for 2025:
Youthline Wellington
Social Supermarket
There is a recommended donation amount for each race of $40 (TTM) or $25 (Half). These are recommended only. If you are not in a position to donate, then give whatever you can, if you earn a bit more then feel free to pop in a bit more.
Previous years we have raised:
2024 - $5,500 for the Social Supermarket and OMF
2023 - $5,125 for the Social Supermarket
2022 - $3,600 split between Trailblazers and Wellington Women's Refuge
2021 - $3,770 split between Trailblazers and Wellington Women's Refuge
2020 - $3,376 split between Challenge 2000 and Wellington Women's Refuge

Tip Track Marathon is an out-and-back, out-and-back, out-and-back, out-and-back, out-and-back, out-and-back type course that has proven popular with participants. Each of the six laps is slightly over 7km, with around 400m in elevation (2500m in total). Try not to trip on a loose rock while taking in the aromatic smells emanating from the tip. Ignore the gale-force northerly. It makes for a challenging marathon but you can find comfort in the other runners suffering too.
Recommended donation: $40

Half Marathon -
For those that hate themselves but not as much as the marathoners. Same course as above but three laps instead of six,
Recommended donation: $25

Tip Track Marathon (TTM) is a low-key, no frills trail running race that takes place at the Tip Track in Wellington each year - all in the name of charity. TTM is all about hard hills, high-fives, and doing something stupid for the sake of it. There are no prizes. Your workmates will not understand why you did this. It’s not even that fun.

This is a race for those that want a little more from life than the ordinary. Those that question the monotony of their daytime jobs and wonder, "isn't there meant to be more to life than this?" Enter TTM... I mean, you won't find any answers here but those are the people that tend to be attracted to it.

DONATIONS:
All entry fees charged go to our charities for 2025:
Youthline Wellington
Social Supermarket

There is a recommended donation amount for each race of $40 (TTM) or $25 (Half). These are recommended only. If you are not in a position to donate, then give whatever you can, if you earn a bit more then feel free to pop in a bit more.
Previous years we have raised:

2024 - $5,500 for the Social Supermarket and OMF
2023 - $5,125 for the Social Supermarket
2022 - $3,600 split between Trailblazers and Wellington Women's Refuge
2021 - $3,770 split between Trailblazers and Wellington Women's Refuge
2020 - $3,376 split between Challenge 2000 and Wellington Women's Refuge


The day is a celebration of the Wellington running community. It is a social, unofficial event. Come along for a run, to support, and meet some new friends along the way.

description:
Track Day- 2025, Track Day- 2025
🚗💥 START YOUR ENGINES! 💥🚗

We are beyond excited to announce Forged Development's First Ever Track Day at Manfeild Motorsport Park-Circuit Chris Amon!

📅 SAVE THE DATE: 27th September 2025!

In celebration of our founder and owner, Sameer Kumar’s 40th birthday, we’re kicking things into high gear with an action-packed PlayDay on Track event!
Forged Development, in collaboration with PlayDay on Track, we’ve been working tirelessly to deliver an unforgettable track experience. Whether you're a seasoned track enthusiast or just looking to enjoy a fun day on the tarmac, we’ve got you covered.

What’s in store:

A thrilling day on the iconic Manfeild Motorsport Park.

Designed for all skill levels, with three distinct Speed Groups to ensure a safe, exciting experience for everyone.

Maximum track time with minimal racing traffic, so you can make the most of every lap!

Track Entry Tickets now available:

Show and Shine Entry: Now Live

Spectator entrance free!


Competitor Information:

WOF or Reg aren't required, however 3rd Party insurance is preferred as Forged Development Limited and PlayDay on Track takes no liability for any damages or loss at the event.

What you need to bring: (You will not be allowed on track without the minimum safety requirments)
- Driver’s license
- Overalls (minimum 1 layer Cotton)
- Closed top shoes
- Helmet

Not mandatory however highly recommended:
- Neck Restraints/Hans device
- Fire extinguisher

No passengers unless a full MSNZ approved caged. (Expect in familiarization laps for non-caged vehicles)
Passengers wishing to go in a caged car must sign an indemnity form available from the documentation/registration area.

Garage sheds are on a first come, first serve basis.

Pitlane Garages are available for hire, limited available for purchase along with your ticket.

Vehicle Safety:
Participants are responsible for ensuring their car is safe. This includes:
- No fluid leaks (oil, fuel, coolant, brake fluid)
- Brakes in good working condition with sufficient pad material
- Tires in good health
- Lug nuts torqued to spec; all must be present
- Battery securely mounted
- Seat belts or harnesses in working condition
- No loose items inside the vehicle (tools, bottles, etc.)
You will be asked to sign a self-tech form during registration.

On-Track Rules:
- Passing allowed only in designated zones (straights) and with ownership on the driver overtaking to execute a safe pass.
- No hard-overtaking under braking/corners.
- Yield to faster vehicles; use mirrors frequently.
- If you spin or leave the track, rejoin only when safe or return to the pits.
- When on track, do not leave your vehicle unless if fire.
- Aggressive driving, unsafe behaviour, or reckless manoeuvres (e.g., drifting, tailgating) will result in ejection from the event.
- Obey all flag signals and track officials immediately.
- Pitlane Speed limit: 10 kph
- No tire burnouts, speeding, or aggressive driving in paddock/pit areas.

Weather Policy:
- Track day runs rain or shine unless deemed unsafe by organizers.
- Participants must adjust driving style to suit conditions.

Liability Disclaimer:
- All participants must sign a waiver of liability.
- You are responsible for any damage you cause to your vehicle, other vehicles, or track property.
- The track and organizers are not liable for injuries, mechanical failures, or accidents.

Refunds:
There are no refunds but you can transfer your entry to someone else (You can do this via contacting us directly)

Advertising release:
As a condition of entry, each entrant for themselves, as agent for accompanying adult and as parent or guardian for an accompanying child, grant the event promoter, Forged Development Limited, the exclusive right to photograph, video or film, or portrayal without names or credits as the event promoter may in their absolute discretion think fit.

Selection starts earlier, competition runs deeper, and pressure moments arrive before many athletes have the skills to cope. When this gap exists, confidence wavers, enjoyment fades, and potential remains untapped.

In this keynote, Dr Craig Harrison reveals what’s really happening under pressure, and what it takes to thrive within it. Drawing on developmental science, lived stories from youth sport, and practical tools, this session shifts the conversation from “handling pressure” to working with it.

First, you’ll learn how the adolescent brain, stress response, and social dynamics influence behaviour under pressure. Then, you’ll discover how to build the skills to meet pressure moment by moment, and create the conditions for confident, adaptable performance.

Who is this talk for?
- Parents of youth athletes wanting to better support their child
- Coaches of youth athletes wanting to develop more resilient players
- Teen athletes wanting to perform under pressure

Bond-Murray Room - Doors open 645 PM for a 7 PM start

About Dr Craig Harrison:
With over 20 years’ experience working with developing athletes, coaches, and families, Craig is one of New Zealand’s leading voices on helping young people thrive in sport. His work blends cutting-edge research in long-term athlete development and child psychology with real-world stories from schools, clubs, and academies around the world.

WHAC Presents: Honest 10 - 21 September 2025, Join us at 8:30am on Sunday 21 September for the next edition of the Honest 10 taking in Wellington's beautiful waterfront. The Honest 10 is the perfect chance to test your 5km or 10km fitness and maybe have a go at walking or running PB.
EVERYONE IS WELCOME NO MATTER WHAT YOUR LEVEL OF FITNESS. The is an optional 8:15am early start for those who think they might need more time (eg over 70 mins for 10k)
Organised by WHAC, the Honest 10 provides a fast, fun and friendly environment. The race course has been officially measured and there will be pacers running 40min, 45min, 50min, 55min and 60min to help you run your best.
Cost: Just $10 for 10km, $5 for 5km!!
How to enter:
1. Pre-register by email (recommended) BEFORE 5PM on Saturday 20 Sept. Payment methods for pre-registrations include online bank transfer (an email with your reference will be sent back to you) or pay cash on the day.
Account Name: Wellington Harrier Athletic Club
Account Number: 12-3493-0058553-00
Use "H10 [your race number]" as your reference. Eg "H10 #23"
OR
2. Sign up on the day from 8am (cash only).
Photos are free of charge and posted online (on the WHAC website) alongside results after the race. https://whac.org.nz/wp/honest-10/
Where: At the Whale's Tail next to Freyberg Pool, Oriental Bay
When: Registration from 8am. Race starts at 8:30am Sunday morning. Let us know when you register, if you request an early 8.15am start, eg if you are walking the 10km or are likely to run slower than 70mins.
***Pre-registration details***
Email the following details to honest10@whac.org.nz BEFORE 5pm Saturday 20 Sept
You will receive a confirmation email back with your race number. If you select 'N' for prepaid, just bring cash to the race with you. If you select 'Y' for prepaid, pay via WHAC's bank account details below.
- Name
- Age
- 5km or 10km
- M, F or D (unfortunately we are currently unable to give age-calculated results for the gender-diverse (D) category, as our source currently only provides age-calculated result data for M and F)

using "H10 [your race number]" as your reference. Eg "H10 #23"

description:

Hi everyone - welcome to the WSKN Christmas SKISL / Paddle to Mana!

On Saturday 13th December we will have a Christmas event on Mana Island, departing Titahi Bay at 10am (so arriving at 9:30) getting to Mana around 10:40, keen ones can do stuff prior to lunch around 12:00, then there might be groups that head back at different time slots, but we can work that out on the day. Return could therefore either be 1:30 or 2:30 with the latest return to Titahi Bay being 3pm.

We've made this event later than the normal SKISL so that it's easier for folks to drive down from Palmerston North, and also because it is a lunch event.

The lawn on Mana is really nice, sheltered and pleasant and there are also good walks. Mana is of course a sanctuary so you must check your boats for any wildlife especially ants that may have gotten in past the hatches. Also we cannot have any fires

Plan B: If weather nukes Mana, we'll try for Green Point or Onehunga Bay in Whitireia Park by driving there.

Plan C: We will postpone to 21 December

Wairarapa A & P Show, This year will be Wairarapa A&PI s 146th annual show, and the only one of its type remaining in the Wairarapa/Wellington region. It is deeply embedded in the culture and history of the area and is accessible to people of all ages and capabilities.

The A&P show has something for all ages, with a focus on learning and family enjoyment. It provides connectedness between town and country, and the opportunities that the rural sector provides.

There is something for everyone, visitors can enjoy the typical animal classes and competitions including sheep shearing, wool handling, pet lamb and calf judging, and equestrian sports, as well as the beloved Goldpine pet corner where attendees can see farm animals up close.

The woodchopping, fencing and dog trials competitions are always highlights, as are the children’s art, scavenger hunt and lawnmower racing. Tickets are available either through Eventbrite or at the gate on the day.

Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Duntulm Farm Dog Walk, Wairarapa DogWalk Group invites friendly dogs and their owners to enjoy a special walk on private land at beautiful Duntulm Farm in the Mangatārere Valley. This is a wonderful opportunity to explore stunning scenery, meet fellow dog lovers, and let your canine companions stretch their legs.
Dogs must be under control at all times, whether on or off-leash, and owners should bring a leash and clean up after their dogs.

We’ll pause mid-walk for a relaxed morning tea, with hot drinks and nibbles provided.

The Wairarapa DogWalk Group meets every month for a friendly, sociable walk somewhere new in our region — and we’d love you to join us.

Walk Format:
There will be two options: a cardio walk up to the top with an elevation gain of 300m, or a much flatter option. Both will start at 9:30am and finish at 12:30pm. There may be shallow stream crossings. Note there are patches of no cellphone reception during this walk.

Images: Credit to Wairarapa DogWalk Group
label: Sports & Fitness

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Gladstone Wine and Olive Walk, Back by popular demand, the much-loved Gladstone Wine & Olive Walk is a relaxed, sensory journey through one of Wairarapa’s most celebrated wine-growing areas. Stroll the river terraces above the Ruamāhanga, where award-winning vineyards and olive groves flourish, and enjoy tastings of wines, olive oils, and seasonal nibbles along the way.

Guided through vines and groves, you’ll gain insights into why Gladstone wines are consistently praised for their complexity and elegance, shaped by the region’s unique soils and growing conditions. Highlights include a stop at the stunning Urlar Vineyard cellar door, recently awarded Gold at the 2025 Master Builders Commercial Project Awards, and stories of Gladstone’s history shared en route. This walk is led by local Gladstone legend John Booth, in partnership with the Go Carterton business group.

This walk is via bus only, due to parking restrictions and road safety. The bus will leave the Wairarapa Events Centre at 2pm and return at 5pm. Plan ahead - Please ensure you organise safe transport home from the Wairarapa Events Centre.
label: Sports & Fitness

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Homewood Airstrip| Roast by the Coast, Enjoy a day out on the Wairarapa Coast with a family-friendly walk and a hearty roast lunch. Situated on working farmland, the Homewood Airstrip walk is a 5km return track that follows a gradual incline to the top, offering sweeping views of land and sea, before an easy downhill return. The gravel track is usually straightforward, but can be slippery or muddy in wet conditions—good footwear and wet-weather gear are recommended. Gates will be open and stock fenced off for the day. Thanks to Tranzit sponsorship the bus fare is significantly reduced for participants.

After your walk, return to the Homewood Storeroom to refuel with a traditional roast lunch of slow-cooked lamb, crispy roast potatoes, and seasonal salad, with an optional slice for dessert.

Walk Format
Travel: 1 hour each way from Masterton (2 hours total)
Arrive: Café at 10am (time for the loo and to collect maps—navigation support by Gavin, our seasoned guide!)
Walk: Depart up the airstrip by 10.30am; allow 2 hours including time to enjoy the views
Lunch: Return to the Storeroom by 12.30pm for a roast lunch
Return: Bus departs from the café at 2pm

This outing is ideal for fit trampers, casual walkers, families, pre-schoolers, and school groups (minimum age 4+). Expect moderate hills and potentially muddy conditions if it rains—but with the right gear, light rain and wind will only add to the adventure.
label: Sports & Fitness

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Pōhatu Farm Riversdale Beach Hike, From the Summit to the Sea – The Riversdale Beach Farm Hike is your gateway to experiencing New Zealand’s stunning rural landscapes and is the perfect way to reconnect with rural life.

Ideal for hikers with a moderate to high fitness level, this self-guided, catered one-day hike covers 17-km, taking you along the historic Orui Station coast, the Whareama River, and the rolling hills of Pōhatu Farm. Perched between land and sea, Pōhatu is a family-run, 1,200-hectare sheep and beef farm, rich in raw beauty and natural abundance.

Located just five minutes from Riversdale Beach, 45 minutes from Masterton, and just over two hours from Wellington and Palmerston North, this hike is an adventure you’ll never forget. Enjoy a Wairarapa Walking Festival special of $40pp (50% off!) which includes a generous packed lunch.

Walk Format:
Your adventure begins by meeting your host and driving in convoy along a well-maintained 5-km forestry road, offering scenic views of native bush, pine forests, and the Pacific Ocean. You'll arrive at a designated carpark where your host will provide a health and safety briefing and hand out your generous packed lunch. Once the briefing is complete, your 17-km self-guided journey begins with a gentle downhill walk to the breathtaking Orui Station coastline. From there, you’ll follow the coast for approximately 7-km before crossing back over to Pōhatu Farm where you’ll walk alongside the beautiful Whareama River. At the 11-km mark, you’ll begin your first and only ‘spicy’ ascent to the top of the Pōhatu Farm ridges - where panoramic views await - before completing the loop back to your vehicle. Take your time to enjoy the hike at your own pace. This self-guided experience is designed for adventurers who value a mix of challenge and leisure.

Important:
You are responsible for your own travel here. A moderate-high level of fitness is required. This walk takes approximately 5hrs, including stops. Strictly no dogs allowed. Please note there is only a bathroom at the lunch stop. Please email pohatufarm@gmail.com for any dietary requirement queries.
label: Sports & Fitness

description:

Take time to enjoy the sunshine, the tranquil setting, and the calls of the ducks and birds that make Henley Lake their home. After the walk, stay on for a shared picnic—just bring along your own lunch.

This walk is designed to be welcoming and accessible, offering a chance to connect with others. Under 18s are welcome to attend with a caregiver.

description:
Weightlifting NZ Masters Nationals, Weightlifting NZ Masters Nationals
We're proud to be hosting the 2026 Weightlifting New Zealand Masters Nationals right here at Fitness Portal Tawa.

This is one of the highlights of the NZ weightlifting calendar — a two-day national championship where Masters athletes from across the country come together to compete in the Snatch and Clean & Jerk.

Masters weightlifting is for athletes aged 30 and over, competing in age and bodyweight categories. It's a sport that rewards technical skill, consistency, and years of dedication — and watching it live is genuinely impressive.

Whether you're here to compete, support a friend, or just curious what Olympic weightlifting actually looks like up close — come down and check it out. Entry to spectate is free and everyone is welcome.

What to expect:
Two full days of competition across multiple sessions, with athletes lifting in a range of weight categories.

Competing?
Registrations are managed through Weightlifting New Zealand. Head to weightlifting.nz for entry details and qualifying information.
Entries open 1st of August.

Questions?
Get in touch with us at or message us here on Facebook.

We're looking forward to welcoming the NZ weightlifting community to Tawa. It's going to be an epic weekend!

We look forward to seeing you all at the Club at 9:30 for Lotto 8’s (weather permitting).
Following the meetings, a light lunch will be provided. This is also WRC’s opportunity to unveil the Function Space renovations to the membership.

Information about the AGM
The WRC AGM will commence at 12noon, in the WRC Function Centre. There will be provisions for online attendance.
At this year’s AGM, we have several board and committee positions that we will be seeking to fill. Many hands make light work, and we all depend on volunteers to keep the club growing and thriving. A variety of experience levels, skill sets, and perspectives are needed for a well-functioning club.
The positions to be filled this year are:
-Club Captain (2-year term, Officer role)
-Vice President (2-year term, Officer role)
-Club Treasurer (2-year term, Officer role)
-Club Secretary (2-year term, Officer role)
-3 Committee roles (1-year term, non-Officer role)
-3 Board members (2-year term, Officer role)
Officers of the must consent in writing to being an officer and certify that they are eligible and not disqualified from holding office as described under section 36B of the Charities Act 2005.
The Club by-laws outline the current role descriptions, can be found here, note that the roles can be tailored to suit individuals’ skill sets and experience. Mentoring and support can be provided to develop individuals in these positions.
If you are interested, but have further questions- please reach out to the people holding the current role or any of the board or committee members to discuss.

description:
Welly On Wheels Karori - Confidence & Skills for Biking, Keen to build your biking confidence? Join us for Welly On Wheels: Karori edition!
Thinking about biking more, but not quite confident on city streets? Join us and Pedal Ready for a free, social bike tour between Karori, the Botanical Gardens and the waterfront. Get to know the route and street changes, build cycling confidence and skills, and learn about interesting features such as murals and fix it stands along the way!
This ride starts and ends at Switched On Bikes on the waterfront near Waitangi Park. The route leads along the scenic waterfront, past the Botanical Gardens, with the "Gardens magic" in full swing, up to Karori and Karori Park, and into South Karori to the starting point of Mākara Peak mountain bike trails. We will then retrace our tracks back to Karori Park and use the separated cycle lane to travel through Karori, and back down past the Botanical Gardens and on to the waterfront. The ride will finish at Switched-on-Bikes.
Wednesday 21 January
5.30pm - 7.30pm (arrive 30 minutes early if renting a bike)

description:
Welly On Wheels: Waterfront to Karori and back, Wellington City Council and Pedal Ready are teaming up to run a guided bike tour along the cycle route between Karori, the Botanical Gardens and the waterfront! Get to know the route and street changes, build cycling confidence and skills, and learn about interesting features such as murals and fix it stands along the way!

This ride starts and ends at Switched On Bikes on the waterfront near Waitangi Park. The route leads along the scenic waterfront, past the Botanical Gardens, with the "Gardens magic" in full swing, up to Karori and Karori Park, and into South Karori to the starting point of Mākara Peak mountain bike trails. We will then retrace our tracks back to Karori Park and use the separated cycle lane to travel through Karori, and back down past the Botanical Gardens and on to the waterfront. The ride will finish at Switched-on-Bikes.

For alternative arrangements for the end of this bike tour, please see details below!

An electric bike is strongly recommended to participate due to the hilly nature of this ride. Thanks to Switched on Bikes and Wellington City Council, you can rent an electric bike for just $10 if you don't have access to one. Please book your rental e-bike separately here: https://switchedonbikes.rezdy.com/642002/electric-bike-hire-welly-on-wheels

Allow 2 hours.
Please arrive 30 minutes early (by 5pm) if you are renting a bike.

These rides are suitable for people who:
- know how to ride a bike but aren't yet cycling in the city; or
- are cycling in the city but would like to gain confidence; or
- want to learn how to use new cycling infrastructure.

Open to riders aged 18+ (or 13+ if accompanied by an adult). Families are also welcome to bring younger children on cargo bikes or bike seats provided themselves. Please enquire directly with Switched on Bikes if you'd like to borrow a bike seat for the tour.

Alternative arrangements for the end of this bike tour:
- If you're feeling extra enthusiastic and want to extend your bike hire, you're welcome to hold onto the bike overnight and return it before 10am to Switched on Bikes at no extra charge!
- There's also the option to hold onto the bike all day the following day for a discounted cost of $39.
Please discuss your intentions with us on the day.

If this tour is not quite for you and you would like to learn to ride a bike away from the road instead, please check out the free Pedal Ready courses on their website https://www.pedalready.org.nz/. Any pātai (questions) about these tours please get in contact: info@pedalready.org.nz
PRIVACY STATEMENT: The information you shared in signing up for this ride is used for booking and safety purposes. Within 14 days after the tour, your name and emergency contact details will be deleted. Other information provided may be stored anonymously to support our project evaluation. Your email address will be stored for up to 4 months following the tour. Within that time, we may contact you with follow-up information about biking in Pōneke, as well as feedback opportunities about the ride and the impact it has had on your travel around Pōneke. You have the right to ask for a copy of any personal information we hold about you and to ask for it to be corrected if you believe it is incorrect. If you would like to ask for a copy of your information or to have it corrected, please contact us at tours@wcc.govt.nz.

description:
Women's Amateur Asia-Pacific Championship, Royal Wellington Golf Club will host the eighth edition of the Women's Amateur Asia-Pacific Golf Championship and is inviting the public to come witness the golf stars of tomorrow and enjoy hospitality and entertainment in our Royal Village.

This championship brings together the Asia- Pacific region's elite amateur women golfers who will complete for starts in three major championships. The goal of the championship is to build a long-term pathway for women's golf across the Asia Pacific region.

Free to spectators, this event is ideal for families and sports enthusiasts of all ages. There will be opportunities for people to get to know more about the game of golf. If you've wanted to give golf a go, you will want to check out the hugely popular "She Loves Golf programme" (developed by New Zealand Golf).

Please consider using public transport. If you catch the train, Heretaunga Railway Station is about a 5-minute walk to the Club. The number 110 bus from Petone to Emerald Hill (both ways) stops near Golf Road. If you're driving, parking is available in the Heretaunga area. Please note that there is no parking available at the Club.

Save the date (February 12 to 15) and we’ll see you there!

description:
Women's Football Training, Try Football This Summer — Free Sessions for All Women*!

Ever wanted to try football but didn’t know where to start?
Or keen to get back into the game after a break?

The Women’s Football Centre is hosting free, beginner-friendly football lessons for women aged 18+ (no upper age limit!), designed to help you build skills, confidence, and community this summer.
No experience? No worries, this is for you!

You’ll learn the basics of the game — passing, dribbling, movement, teamwork — in a supportive and empowering environment created specifically for new and returning players. You'll also have a chance to socialise and meet new people! All sessions are run by women coaches and supported by an awesome volunteer crew.

Stay after the session for Extra Time, where you can try goalkeeping or get one-on-one guidance from our coaches.

Bring a bottle of water and your sports shoes or football boots, and get ready to give football a go in a fun, inclusive space.

No sign ups or registrations! Just turn up to any session and we'll see you there!

*including cis women, transfeminine and trans women

We will play various versions of tag games: such as Ultimate Tag (which involves multiple evaders), Flight Club (which involves king of the hill format), and Chase-Off (the team version, as seen in World Chase Tag competition videos).
World Chase Tag was formed by Christian Devaux in 2012 after a game of Tag with his son in their back garden. A year later, he was joined by his brother, Damien, and together they set about turning the oldest game into the newest sport.

description:
XTrail Spring - Battle at Boulder Hill, Boulder Hill offers up a classic slice of Wellington trail running - rugged, scenic, and deeply rewarding. Set in the Belmont Regional Park, the three courses take you through a mix of lush native bush, open ridgelines, and rolling farmland with epic views across the Wellington harbour, Hutt Valley, and out to the coast. The short course is a compact loop with punchy climbs and flowing descents, while the long course gives you the full Boulder Hill experience — a steady climb from the valley floor to the summit, followed by sweeping downhills and one final sting in the tail before you loop back to base. A true taste of the terrain that makes this region so special.
https://barefootxtrail.co.nz/

Rangituhi serves up a lush and leg-burning journey through one of Porirua’s most scenic spots. Starting from Spicers Botanical Park, all three courses wind their way up through the peaceful, green trails of Spicers Forest before breaking into the rugged beauty of the Colonial Knob Reserve. The short course offers a more forgiving climb with playful zig zags and a fun descent, while the long course takes you all the way to the summit of Rangituhi, a proper challenge rewarded with stunning views over Porirua Harbour and beyond. With a mix of forest trails, farm tracks, and fast-flowing descents, this one’s a true highlight of the region.

The short course offers a rewarding climb and scenic descent, while the long course adds a little extra vert and extends your adventure along the iconic Skyline Track, with sweeping views over the city, coast, and beyond. With flowing trails and plenty of natural beauty, it’s a proper taste of Wellington’s wild backyard.

🏏 Girls’ Cricket Open Day – Come Give Cricket a Go!, 🏏 Girls’ Cricket Open Day – Come Give Cricket a Go!
Come along to North City Cricket Club's women and girls cricket open day to learn more about getting involved in cricket.

We have opportunities for girls aged 5+ to participate in girls only teams, mixed teams, hardball or softball cricket.

Cricket is a fantastic sport to play! It's fun, engaging and it helps build resilience, teamwork and patience.

Now is an awesome time for girls and women to get into cricket - the pathways into senior and representative cricket are stronger than they've ever been - and North City Cricket Club has produced more than it's fair share of White Ferns (New Zealand's women's cricket team) and Wellington Blaze (Wellington representative women's cricket team) players.

Come along on the day to learn more about the different options to get involved, participate in some fun activities, learn some important cricket skills and meet some of our champion Wellington Blaze players.

There will be prizes to give away on the day to participants, a free sausage sizzle and awesome prize packs up for grabs!
